title: Doc comments and help strings that contradict the code (M1 audit)
description:
## Background

A code audit for the README rewrite found doc comments, descriptions and help strings that contradict what the code does. Each misleads the next agent that reads them.

- `src/resolve/select.rs` (lines 6-8) and `src/sources/release_json.rs` (lines 7-9) use WeakAuras as an example of a mainline build. Its 5.22.1 `release.json` lists no mainline flavor, and `catalog/catalog.toml` says so.
- `src/resolve/catalog.rs` (lines 8-10) says `families` narrows target choice. It is only displayed by `info`; no selection reads it.
- `src/engine/ownership.rs` (line 3) says `--force` resolves case collisions. The code and tests say it never does.
- `src/engine/blobs.rs` (lines 12-14) says retained and planned blobs are pinned. Only blobs of installed releases are.
- `src/politeness.rs` (around line 55) says exceeding `MAX_REDIRECTS` is `http_status`. It is `network`.
- The `limits.snapshot_max_bytes` config description says "Largest snapshot"; it is the per-target total beyond the 24-hour window.
- The published limits registry in `src/limits.rs` names config keys `tx_retention` and `default_check_interval`. `config.toml` uses `limits.tx_retention_count`, `limits.tx_retention_days` and `check_interval_hours`.
- `src/discover/mod.rs` (lines 10-11) and `src/discover/registry.rs` (lines 11-12) describe running processes as a discovery source. Production never feeds them (see the companion bead on process hints).
- The bare help title says "World of Warcraft addon manager (CLI + Omarchy plugin)", but the Omarchy plugin does not exist until M3.
- `src/model.rs` (around line 141): `MutableFolderName`'s doc says every mutating API takes it; none does.

## Technical Approach

- Correct each comment and string to match the code, and cite the evidence where the original claimed something verified.
- The help title becomes "World of Warcraft addon manager for Linux" until the widget ships. Update the help snapshots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every item above is corrected or removed.
- `argc gate` passes with the help snapshot updated.

## Test Plan

- `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` bare-help snapshots updated for the title.
- No behavior change: the full suite passes unchanged otherwise.

## Considerations

- Do not change behavior in this bead. Where a comment describes intended behavior that should exist, file a bug instead of deleting the intent silently.
acceptance_criteria: every listed comment and string is corrected or removed; the bare help title no longer claims an Omarchy plugin; argc gate passes with help snapshots updated
close_reason: Every listed doc comment and string matches the code

title: The discovery cache ignores products and version_families overrides and binary upgrades
description:
## Background

The discovery cache (`src/discover/cache.rs`) reuses a root's parsed targets while its stamped files (`.build.info`, `.flavor.info`, exes, `Config.wtf`, `realmlist.wtf`, `product.db`) are unchanged (around lines 104-119). On a hit, only the client-rules row is re-picked (around lines 184-192), so `[client_rules.*]` patches and `family_ranges` apply at once. Family, interface, product, default id and kind come from the cached parse.

So two inputs that change those values are ignored until a stamped file changes or `targets --rescan` runs:

- a `[rules]` edit in `config.toml` to `products`, `version_families` or a row's `interface_includes_patch`;
- a binary upgrade whose built-in tables changed (a new product row, a new version → family rule).

`status --cached` has the same issue by design, but a normal command does a full scan anyway, so it should not serve stale identities.

Found while auditing discovery for the README rewrite. README.md documents it under Known limitations ("run `targets --rescan`").

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `omaddons status` once (the cache is written).
2. Add `[[rules.version_families]]` mapping the custom 3.3 client to another family, or a new product row.
3. `omaddons status` still shows the old family; `omaddons targets --rescan` shows the new one.

## Technical Approach

- Add a fingerprint of the effective rules table (built-in plus overrides, e.g. SHA-256 of its canonical JSON) and the tool version to the cache header. A mismatch invalidates every root's parse, which is the same as `--rescan` for that run.
- Keep the per-root stamps for everything else.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a rules override changes, the next normal command re-parses every root and reports the new family/interface/id without `--rescan`.
- After a version bump, the cache is re-parsed once.
- An unchanged config and binary still reuse every root (cache hit counted in the `-v` debug log).
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/discover_cache.rs`: the reproduction above, before and after; a tool-version change in the header forces a re-parse; an unrelated config change (`default_channel`) does not.

## Considerations

- `status --cached` must not scan. It can warn that the cache was built from other rules, and its fix is `omaddons targets --rescan`.
- Remove the Known-limitations line from README.md when fixed.
acceptance_criteria: a products or version_families override or a tool-version change re-parses every root on the next normal command; unchanged config and binary still reuse every root; argc gate passes
close_reason: The discovery cache re-parses every root once when the rules or the binary change

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: claim: src/discover/cache.rs, tests/discover_cache.rs, README Known limitations

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: DiscoveryCache 1.1 gains basis (serde default, empty in 1.0) = SHA-256 of CARGO_PKG_VERSION and the effective RulesTable's JSON (builtin plus [rules] and [client_rules.*]); a cache on another basis reuses no parse (Cached and NoScan still only look at the cached roots, re-parsing them; NoScan still writes nothing). decided: hash the whole effective table rather than only products/version_families/interface_includes_patch, so a client_rules or family_ranges edit also re-parses once (cheap, never stale); the version covers parser changes without a table change. README: Known-limitations line removed, the rules reference and discovery paragraph say what the cache rests on. Gate green (1278).

title: Epic: M1 — Working slice
description:
## Background

M1 is the working slice of omaddons (vision bead omad-vision-8qa, §7). When it closes, omaddons installs, reinstalls-to-update, removes and undoes addons from keyless GitHub, git, URL and local sources into every discovered target, including WoW: Forever and legacy private-server clients. Everything goes through the final transaction engine and the core CLI contract.

The timing matters. WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04. M1 alone delivers keyless Forever support:
- the `release.json` flavor `forever`;
- the `_Forever`/`_Camelot` TOC suffixes;
- the guard against a Forever client loading a retail-only `_Mainline.toc`;
- 1.60.x family detection for both `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_`.

M1 also carries the riskiest engine work (journaled per-folder swaps, recovery, undo), so the beads are ordered to put the Forever-critical path first.

M1 is split into seven area epics:

| Epic | Area |
|---|---|
| E1 | Domain model and CLI contract core (envelope, error registry, exit dictionary, clap skeleton, constants) |
| E2 | fsx single writer, locks and state (paths, Op enum, mutate, prune, locks, schema-versioned state, records, history, config) |
| E3 | Client discovery and target identity (BPSV, product.db, dosdevices, Battle.net and custom roots, scan, launchers, cache, running detection, registry) |
| E4 | ClientRules, TOC engine and folder inventory |
| E5 | Network layer and keyless sources (Http, allowlist, net.log, retry, fixtures, refs, local/url/GitHub/git sources, selection, catalog) |
| E6 | Transaction engine (blob cache, archive inspection, staging, ownership, planning, journal, swap, commit, running policy, undo, retention) |
| E7 | M1 commands, the contract conformance suite, fuzzing and checkpoint verification |

## Goals

- Every installed WoW client is discovered with no configuration. Each gets a stable target identity: a ULID key, a human id and a marker.
- Addons install from keyless sources and are verified against the client's own TOC load rules (`ClientRules`). Wrong-flavor builds never install.
- Every mutation is a journaled transaction that is crash-recoverable and undoable, with the "wholly old or wholly new" folder invariant.
- The core CLI contract holds for every M1 command:
  - one stdout envelope under `--json`, on success and on failure;
  - `fix` plus `fix_argv` on every error;
  - NDJSON on stderr when stderr is not a TTY;
  - the general exit dictionary (0–6).
- Privacy is verifiable: a host allowlist checked on every redirect hop, `net.log` covering HTTP and git subprocesses, and `--offline`.

## Success Criteria

All seven area epics are closed, and every M1 checkpoint from the vision is met with recorded evidence (the m1-checkpoint bead under E7 runs them):
- On the development machine, `omaddons status --json` reports `retail` (12.1.x, from `product.db` and `.build.info`) and the 3.3.5a target (`wrath-legacy`, interface 30300, label "localhost", 23 protected folders). Both get stable keys and markers on their first mutation.
- Synthetic trees resolve correctly for:
  - every product, including `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_` at 1.60.x;
  - every legacy `ClientRules` row;
  - a game on a mapped drive letter outside `drive_c`;
  - a custom client outside any prefix;
  - each launcher config;
  - an unknown `_xyz_` folder.
- TOC load-rule tests cover every suffix, the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` case, comma Interface lists and every legacy row.
- Keyless installs of WeakAuras, DBM, BigWigs, Plater and Bartender4 into real retail and a synthetic Forever target are TOC-verified. A legacy addon installs into 3.3.5a from git and from a GitHub release. `Blizzard_*` folders are untouched.
- Installing `release.json` publishers on the stable channel makes zero GitHub REST requests (asserted from `net.log`).
- Failure injection at every engine step leaves each folder wholly old or wholly new. Recovery happens only under the lock, and a reader during a live swap reports `tx_in_progress`.
- Two concurrent installs into one target both complete without `locked`. Lock hold time per commit is under 50 ms.
- `undo` restores folders byte-for-byte, follows the SavedVariables policy, raises `undo_conflict` across transaction kinds, and `--last-by agent` reverts only that actor's transaction.
- The hostile archive suite is rejected, and `blizzard_auctionui/` beside `Blizzard_AuctionUI/` is refused.
- Non-allowlisted hosts fail with `host_blocked`. `net.log` has every request and no credentials.
- The contract core checks pass, the local gate passes, and each fuzz target runs for at least 10 minutes without crashes.
- README.md describes exactly what exists.

## Non-Goals

- `outdated`/`update --all`, WoWInterface and Tukui sources, dependency resolution, adoption, drift checks, `export`/`sync`/`copy` and `search` belong to M2. In M1, `--no-deps` is accepted and ignored.
- The Omarchy widget, `errors` (BugGrabber), `backup` and `--progress json` streams for long operations belong to M3.
- `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, intent inference beyond the closest-command fix, the wire-name golden test, stored plans (`plan_id`, `apply`) and the `doctor` surface belong to M4. M1 ships the engine-guarding warnings (`journal_pending`, `state_version_older`/`state_version_newer`) as plain warnings.
- CurseForge, Wago and release engineering belong to M5.

## Considerations

- The Forever launch layout (`wowf`/`_forever_`/16001) is pre-launch data. Detection is data-driven (D15), and fixtures cover both the beta and launch layouts.
- `product.db` field layout and Proton process naming are UNVERIFIED. Both have fallbacks, and a miss degrades to scanning or a warning, never to data loss.
- Decisions made while decomposing M1 (DEC-1 to DEC-16) are recorded as a comment on omad-vision-8qa. They include these contract additions: errors `scope_denied` and `state_too_new`, and warnings `state_version_older` and `state_version_newer`.
- Parallel agents share one working tree on `main`. The module skeleton and the up-front `Cargo.toml` dependencies exist to keep edits from colliding. Each command bead adds its own clap subcommand.
acceptance_criteria: All seven M1 area epics (E1-E7) are closed; every M1 checkpoint from the vision is met with recorded evidence in the m1-checkpoint bead; the local gate passes; README.md describes exactly what exists
close_reason: All children completed

title: Epic: M1 foundation — domain model and CLI contract core
description:
## Background

omaddons is a single Rust binary whose product is its CLI contract (vision omad-vision-8qa, D2, D17): coding agents drive `omaddons … --json` directly, and the Omarchy widget only renders the same output. Every later M1 area (fsx, state, discovery, sources, the transaction engine, the commands) returns typed outcomes and typed errors, so the vocabulary they share has to exist first:

- the domain types (`Target`, `FolderName`, ids, refs, release sets, addon records);
- the error and warning code registries, with each code's exit code and retryability;
- the JSON envelope, the human renderer and the stderr event stream;
- the clap skeleton: global flags, bare help, usage-error mapping and the panic hook;
- the politeness and safety constants (D22).

The scaffold bead omad-scaffold-fjq (closed, commit 942a1d1) is part of this epic. It created the Cargo package, lints (`unsafe_code` forbidden; clippy `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `print_stdout`, `print_stderr`, `dbg_macro` denied), `deny.toml`, the module skeleton, `argc gate` and README v1.

This epic is first in the M1 delivery order ("contract core, fsx, state"). WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04, and M1 is scoped to land before then.

## Goals

- Domain types in `src/model.rs` that encode safety invariants at the type level: a folder name that cannot escape `AddOns/` and a mutable-folder type that cannot name a `Blizzard_*` folder (D14, D27).
- One closed registry of error codes (code → exit code → retryable) and warning codes in `src/error.rs`. Every error carries a non-empty `fix` plus `fix_argv` (D17, D31).
- The §5.9 envelope: exactly one JSON document on stdout under `--json`, on success and on failure. Human output otherwise, with stdout empty on error. Diagnostics on stderr (NDJSON when stderr is not a TTY).
- A clap skeleton that every command bead extends (DEC-1). Bare `omaddons` prints help and exits 0. Usage errors become `usage` envelopes (exit 2) with a suggested fix. A panic still yields a well-formed `internal` envelope.
- Every §5.13 constant defined exactly once, typed, and listed in a registry that M4's `capabilities.limits` and the config overrides read.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:

- `omaddons` (no arguments) prints concise help on stdout and exits 0. `omaddons --json` prints one envelope with `"ok":true,"command":"help"`.
- `omaddons hepl --json` exits 2 and prints one envelope with `error.code == "usage"`, a non-empty `fix` and `fix_argv == ["omaddons","help"]`.
- A panic injected with the debug-only failpoint `cli.panic` under `--json` exits 1 and prints one envelope with `error.code == "internal"` and `fix_argv == ["omaddons","status"]` (DEC-5).
- When stderr is not a TTY, every stderr line parses as JSON and carries an `event` key in `progress|log|warning|error`.
- `ErrorCode` covers every code in vision §5.9 plus the DEC-4 additions (`scope_denied`, `state_too_new`), and a table-driven test checks each code's exit code and retryability.
- `src/politeness.rs` and `src/limits.rs` define every §5.13 constant, and a test checks that the registries list each one, with the config-overridable set matching the vision's "(config)" markings.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Non-Goals

- `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, full intent inference (verb aliases, misplaced target names), `completions` and the wire-name golden test are M4. This epic only provides the registries and serialization they will read.
- The doctor exit dictionary (0–6 plus 64/66/73/74) is M4.
- Real commands (`status`, `install`, …) are E7. Each command bead adds its own subcommand (DEC-1), and there are no stubs.
- Stored plans and `plan_id` are M4.
- `--progress json` events for long operations are emitted by the engine and command beads. This epic defines the event stream and its modes.

## Considerations

- The contract freezes only at M4's first tag, so codes and keys may be added during M1. Each addition is recorded on the vision bead (DEC-4).
- Determinism: under `--json`, struct keys appear in declaration order and map keys are sorted (`BTreeMap`). Data is serialized generically, never round-tripped through `serde_json::Value`: without serde_json's `preserve_order` feature a `Value` object sorts its keys and would break declaration order.
- Data structs derive `Serialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema` from day one (DEC-3).
- Lints deny `print!`/`eprint!`. All output goes through `src/output/` using locked `std::io::Write` handles.
- Children: model, error-registry, constants, output-envelope, cli-skeleton, plus the closed scaffold bead omad-scaffold-fjq.
acceptance_criteria: bare omaddons prints help on stdout and exits 0, and omaddons --json prints one ok:true envelope with command help; omaddons hepl --json exits 2 with error.code usage, a non-empty fix and fix_argv ["omaddons","help"]; the debug failpoint cli.panic under --json exits 1 with one internal envelope whose fix_argv is ["omaddons","status"]; with stderr not a TTY every stderr line is JSON with an event key; ErrorCode covers every vision §5.9 code plus scope_denied and state_too_new, and a table-driven test checks exits and retryability; every §5.13 constant is defined once and listed in its registry; argc gate passes
close_reason: M1 foundation complete: domain model (1.4), error/warning registries (1.3), constants and limit registries (1.2), output envelope and stderr stream (1.5), CLI skeleton (1.1), plus the scaffold

comments.author: BoldKettle

Bare help and the --json help envelope: tests/cli_skeleton.rs. hepl usage fix and cli.panic internal envelope: tests/cli_skeleton.rs. NDJSON stderr lines with an event key: checked on every E2E run and in src/output tests. ErrorCode table test: src/error.rs. §5.13 constant registries: src/limits.rs and src/politeness.rs. argc gate passes at c1eef90 · found: none

title: clap skeleton, global flags, bare help, usage-error mapping and panic hook
description:
## Background

"The first command an agent guesses should work" (vision omad-vision-8qa §5.9, D17, G4). Bare `omaddons` prints concise help to stdout and exits 0. That help lists the most common verbs and the exit-code table, and the program never runs an action, opens a pager or TUI, or prompts. Bare `omaddons --json` prints the same information as JSON.

Beyond help, the parse step must keep the contract intact:
- an unknown command or flag becomes a `usage` error (exit 2) whose `fix`/`fix_argv` is the closest valid command;
- a panic still emits a well-formed `internal` envelope (exit 1) on stdout under `--json`, mirrored on stderr.

This bead builds the clap skeleton that every command bead extends. DEC-1: each command bead adds its own subcommand and `src/app/<cmd>.rs`, and there are no stub subcommands. This bead ships only the global flags, bare help, `help [<command>]`, usage-error mapping, the panic hook and the `Context` (DEC-2) that commands receive.

Depends on: output-envelope (rendering), model (`Actor::resolve`), constants (`REASON_MAX_CHARS`), fsx-primitives (`fsx::failpoint`, used to trigger a test panic).

## Technical Approach

**Files:**
- `src/main.rs`: `fn main() -> ExitCode { omaddons::cli::run(std::env::args_os()) }`.
- `src/cli.rs`: clap derive definitions, `GlobalArgs`, `Context`, `run`, usage-error mapping and the panic hook.
- `src/app/mod.rs`: the `Command` enum dispatch.
- `src/app/help.rs`: the help outcome.

**Global flags.** Copied from vision §5.9, all declared with clap `global = true` so they work before or after the subcommand:

```
global: --json | --format json|human | --robot · -t/--target (alias --flavor) · --dry-run (mutating) ·
        --actor A · --reason "…" · --offline · --while-running · --no-color · --no-progress ·
        --progress json|human|none · --quiet · -v
```

- `--json`, `--robot` and `--format json` are equivalent. `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json` sets the default; flags win.
- `-t/--target <T>` (visible alias `--flavor`) stores the raw value. The registry bead resolves it (id, key, family, product code, flavor folder, install root or AddOns path).
- `--dry-run` is accepted globally. Decided: read-only commands ignore it, because nothing would be previewed and erroring would make the first guessed command fail. Mutating commands return their plan (DEC-16).
- `--actor human|agent|widget` (env `OMADDONS_ACTOR`) is resolved with `model::Actor::resolve(flag, env, stdin_is_tty)`. An invalid value is `usage`.
- `--reason "…"` is stored verbatim. Decided: longer than `REASON_MAX_CHARS` (200, counted in chars) is a `usage` error rather than silent truncation, because history stores the reason verbatim. Its `fix_argv` is the original argv with the reason cut to 200 chars at a char boundary.
- `--offline` (or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`), `--while-running`, `--no-color`, `--no-progress`, `--progress json|human|none`, `--quiet` and `-v` (a count, `ArgAction::Count`).

**Context** (DEC-2), passed by reference to every command:

```rust
pub struct Context {
    pub output: OutputConfig,      // output/stderr/progress modes, color, verbosity (output-envelope bead)
    pub actor: Actor,
    pub reason: Option<String>,
    pub argv: Vec<String>,         // verbatim, lossy UTF-8, argv[0] normalized to "omaddons"
    pub offline: bool,
    pub dry_run: bool,
    pub while_running: bool,
    pub target: Option<String>,    // raw -t value
    pub started: std::time::Instant,
}
```

`argv` is what history records and what `fix_argv` suggestions are built from. Decided: argv[0] is normalized to `omaddons`, because the widget substitutes its configured binary path for `argv[0] == "omaddons"` (vision §5.9).

**`run(argv) -> ExitCode` pipeline:**
1. Install the panic hook.
2. Pre-resolve the output mode from raw argv and the environment (`output::resolve_output_mode_from_argv`), so even a parse failure honors `--json`.
3. `Cli::try_parse_from`.
4. Build the `Context`.
5. `app::dispatch(cmd, &ctx)` returns the outcome.
6. `output::emit` turns it into an `Exit`, then `ExitCode`.

Commands never print. All exit statuses come from `error::Exit`.

**Bare help** (no subcommand). This is a help outcome, not clap's auto-help.
- Human: one line saying what omaddons is, usage, the common verbs, `omaddons help <command>` for details, `omaddons status` as the triage entry point, and the general exit-code table:

  | Code | Name | Meaning |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0 | `ok` | Success, including partial success (`partial: true`) |
  | 1 | `failed` | Runtime failure; see `error.retryable` |
  | 2 | `usage` | Unknown command or flag, bad argument, bad ref syntax |
  | 3 | `not_found` | Target, ref, addon, plan or transaction not found, or ambiguous |
  | 4 | `refused` | Safety refusal; `fix` names the flag or command |
  | 5 | `locked` | Lock held past the acquire timeout; retryable |
  | 6 | `check_failed` | An opt-in assertion (`--check`, `--strict`) failed |

- Decided: the verb list is generated from the live clap subcommand tree, ordered by a fixed "common verbs" list (`status, install, update, remove, undo, list, targets, info, history, config`) with any others after it. Only commands that exist in this build appear, so each command bead's addition shows up automatically and help never advertises a command that would fail. The vision's discovery trio (`capabilities --json`, `doctor --json`, `robot-docs guide`) arrives in M4 and appears through the same mechanism.
- JSON (`omaddons --json`): an envelope with `command: "help"` and data `{ "name", "version", "usage", "commands": [{"name","about","aliases"}], "global_flags": [{"name","short","takes_value","about"}], "exit_codes": [{"code","name","meaning","retryable"}] }`, built from the clap tree and `error::Exit::ALL`. Data structs derive `Serialize` and `JsonSchema` (DEC-3).
- `-h/--help` on any command and `-V/--version` render through the same outcome path on stdout, exit 0. `--version --json` gives data `{"version"}`.

**`help [<command>]`**: the command's long help (clap-rendered, no ANSI when color is off), exit 0. With `--json`, data `{ "command", "about", "usage", "args": [...], "flags": [...] }`. An unknown command name is a `usage` error with the closest-command fix.

**Usage-error mapping.** Every `clap::Error` becomes `ErrorCode::Usage` (exit 2) with message = clap's message without ANSI codes, trimmed to its first lines. Fixes by error kind:
- `InvalidSubcommand`: the closest subcommand by Levenshtein distance ≤ 2 replaces the bad token in the original argv (`omaddons hepl` → `omaddons help`; `omaddons stauts -t retail` → `omaddons status -t retail` once status exists).
- `UnknownArgument`: the closest long flag of that command or the globals, distance ≤ 2 (`--jsno` → `--json`).
- `MissingRequiredArgument`, `InvalidValue`, `ValueValidation`, …: `omaddons help <command>`.
- Otherwise `omaddons help`.

Decided: a 20-line Levenshtein function in `src/cli.rs` rather than clap's built-in suggestions, which use Jaro similarity; the vision specifies distance ≤ 2. Other close matches go into `alternatives[]`. Full intent inference (verb aliases, misplaced target names such as `omaddons retail update`) is M4.

**Panic hook.** `std::panic::set_hook` builds `Error::internal("internal error: <payload> at <file:line>")`, whose fix is `omaddons status` with argv `["omaddons","status"]` (DEC-5).
- In Json mode it writes the failure envelope to stdout, unless the output layer reports stdout was already written.
- It always mirrors the error to stderr (an NDJSON event or the human form).
- A static `AtomicBool` ensures it renders only once, even when a scoped worker thread's panic is re-raised on join.
- `run` wraps dispatch in `std::panic::catch_unwind` and returns `Exit::Failed` (1), so the process exits 1, not Rust's default 101.
- Test trigger: `fsx::failpoint::hit("cli.panic")` at the start of dispatch. With `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=cli.panic=panic` (DEC-7, debug builds only) it panics.

**tests/smoke.rs** is replaced by `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons` with no arguments exits 0. Stdout contains the usage line, the verb list and the exit-code table, and stderr is empty. It never prompts or pages (no TTY is needed for the test).
- `omaddons --json`, `omaddons --robot`, `omaddons --format json` and `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json omaddons` each print exactly one JSON document with `ok:true`, `command:"help"`, and `data.exit_codes` listing codes 0–6.
- `omaddons help help` and `omaddons help help --json` exit 0.
- `omaddons hepl --json` exits 2, and stdout holds one envelope with `error.code:"usage"`, a non-empty `fix`, and `fix_argv:["omaddons","help"]`. `omaddons --jsno` exits 2 with a fix that uses `--json`. In human mode, stdout is empty and stderr has `error[usage]: …` and `fix: …` lines.
- `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=cli.panic=panic omaddons --json` (debug build) exits 1. Stdout holds exactly one envelope with `error.code:"internal"` and `fix_argv:["omaddons","status"]`, and stderr holds exactly one `{"event":"error",…}` line.
- With stderr captured (not a TTY), every stderr line in these tests parses as JSON and has an `event` key.
- `--reason` with 201 characters exits 2. `--actor robot` exits 2. Global flags are accepted both before and after `help`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/cli.rs`):
  - Levenshtein distances;
  - closest-command and closest-flag selection, including no match (falls back to `omaddons help`);
  - argv rewriting for fixes;
  - `--reason` boundary (200 accepted, 201 rejected, multibyte chars counted as chars);
  - `Context` construction from parsed flags and an injected environment.
- E2E (`tests/cli_skeleton.rs`, `assert_cmd`, HOME and XDG_* set to tempdirs per DEC-6):
  - bare help, human and JSON, plus the three JSON flag spellings and `OMADDONS_FORMAT`;
  - `help help`;
  - `-V` and `--version --json`;
  - unknown subcommand and unknown flag, JSON and human;
  - the panic failpoint;
  - an NDJSON stderr check over every test's stderr;
  - `--actor` and `--reason` validation.
- Snapshot: insta snapshot of the bare `--json` help envelope (meta redacted) and of the human bare help text.
- Log full argv, stdout and stderr on failure.

## Considerations

- Added dependency `fsx-primitives` (not in the plan's line for this bead): the panic test needs the DEC-7 failpoint facility, which lives in `src/fsx/failpoint.rs`. The alternative, a separate env check here, would duplicate the facility.
- clap's own help and version output and its error exits must never reach the terminal directly. Use `try_parse_from`, map every error kind, and disable clap's color in Json/Ndjson modes.
- Non-UTF-8 argv elements: clap parses `OsString`. `Context.argv` stores a lossy copy for history and fixes, and path arguments keep `PathBuf`.
- Out of scope: real subcommands (E7 and the config bead add them per DEC-1), verb aliases and misplaced-target inference (M4), `completions` (M4), and `capabilities` (M4, which will read the same clap tree).
- The help text must stay concise (well under a screen), because agents read it on every first contact.
acceptance_criteria: bare omaddons exits 0 with usage, the verb list and the exit-code table on stdout and nothing on stderr; omaddons --json, --robot, --format json and OMADDONS_FORMAT=json each print exactly one ok:true envelope with command help and data.exit_codes listing 0-6; omaddons help help exits 0 in human and JSON modes; omaddons hepl --json exits 2 with error.code usage, a non-empty fix and fix_argv ["omaddons","help"], omaddons --jsno exits 2 with a fix using --json, and human-mode usage errors leave stdout empty and print error[usage] and fix lines on stderr; OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=cli.panic=panic omaddons --json exits 1 with exactly one internal envelope on stdout (fix_argv ["omaddons","status"]) and exactly one error event on stderr; every captured stderr line is JSON with an event key; a 201-character --reason and --actor robot exit 2; global flags work before and after the subcommand; argc gate passes
close_reason: omaddons now answers its first guessed commands: bare help (human and every JSON spelling), help <command>, -h, -V, usage errors with closest-command and closest-flag fixes (Levenshtein ≤ 2), validated --actor and --reason, and a panic hook that emits one internal envelope and exits 1

comments.text: **fsx-primitives landed.** The panic-hook test can arm `cli.panic` with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=cli.panic=panic` (debug builds only) and call `crate::fsx::failpoint::hit("cli.panic")` at the chosen point. `hit` returns io::Result and panics for the `panic` action. In-process unit tests use `failpoint::with_spec("cli.panic=panic", || …)` instead of the environment.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **output-envelope landed (src/output/).** Wiring: fill `output::OutputFlags` from the global clap flags and call `output::resolve(&flags, &TermEnv::from_process())` to get the OutputConfig for Context. When clap fails, use `resolve_output_mode_from_argv(&argv, &env)` to choose the usage-error envelope format. Render with `output::emit(&cfg, &mut Reporter::stderr(&cfg), command, started, offline, result)` → Exit, then convert with `ExitCode::from(exit)`. Help goes through `output::emit_help(&cfg, &mut stdout, started, &data, &text)`. The panic hook checks `output::stdout_written()` before writing a failure envelope (`Envelope::failure(command, &Error::internal(..), &[], &[], meta)`) and mirrors the error with `Reporter::error`. Failpoint `cli.panic` exists via `crate::fsx::failpoint::hit`.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: claim: src/cli.rs, src/main.rs, src/app/{mod,help}.rs, src/error.rs (Exit::retryable), tests/cli_skeleton.rs (replaces tests/smoke.rs).

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/cli.rs, src/app/{mod,help}.rs, tests/cli_skeleton.rs).**
(1) Bare help, `help [<command>]`, `-h` and `-V` all render a normal Outcome (`app::help::HelpOutcome`, data = untagged `HelpData` Bare/Command/Version) through `output::emit`. This supersedes the 1.5 note: `output::emit_help` was removed so help has one path. clap's own help/version flags and help subcommand are disabled, and `-h`/`-V` are our global flags. `-V` wins over everything and its envelope command is `version`. `-h` with a subcommand renders that command's help.
(2) A usage-error envelope's `command` is the canonical subcommand when one was recognized, else `omaddons`.
(3) `fix_argv` drops presentation flags (--json, --robot, --format, --progress, --no-color, --no-progress) so the consumer keeps its own format; this is what makes `hepl --json` → `["omaddons","help"]`. A corrected token survives even when it is one of them (`--jsno` → `--json`), and `--flag=value` keeps its value. When nothing is within distance 2 the fix is `omaddons help [<subcommand>]`.
(4) The subcommand the user reached for is the first positional argument, skipping the values of value-taking flags, including short clusters ending in one (`-vt retail`).
(5) An invalid `--actor` gets the argv without --actor as its fix. An invalid OMADDONS_ACTOR gets a text fix with no argv. OMADDONS_OFFLINE enables offline only when it is exactly `1`.
(6) Per-command help puts global flags under a 'Global options' heading, so each command's own flags come first.
(7) The `cli.panic` failpoint is hit after parsing and before Context validation. The panic hook reads (OutputConfig, command, started) from a Mutex updated after the raw-argv pre-resolution and again after parsing. It renders the full failure envelope unless `output::stdout_written()`, in which case it only mirrors to stderr. It renders once per process, and `catch_unwind` maps the panic to exit 1.
(8) Added `Exit::retryable() -> Option<bool>` for `data.exit_codes[].retryable` (null for ok and failed).
(9) The JSON help snapshot is a serde_json::Value (sorted keys) with version and elapsed masked; key order is covered by the output unit tests. The E2E helper also asserts that help and usage errors create nothing in the isolated HOME.

comments.author: BoldKettle

title: Politeness and safety constants in src/politeness.rs and src/limits.rs
description:
## Background

D22 (vision omad-vision-8qa §5.13): how omaddons behaves toward upstream hosts and toward the user's machine must be auditable, so every network and filesystem-scan politeness default is a named constant in `src/politeness.rs`, and every safety limit is a named constant in `src/limits.rs`. Values change in one place or not at all, and changing a value means updating the vision tables in a comment on the vision bead.

Only constants marked "(config)" may be overridden in `config.toml`. M4 publishes all of them in `capabilities.limits`.

Nearly every other M1 area reads these constants: net (timeouts, retries, concurrency), discovery (scan depth, skip dirs, dir cap), archive inspection (entry, size and ratio caps), locks (acquire timeout), retention (snapshot and blob caps), the CLI (`--reason` length) and the TOC parser (line limit). This bead has no open dependencies.

Placeholder used below: `<home>` is the user's home directory.

## Technical Approach

**`src/politeness.rs`** (copied from vision §5.13):

| Constant | Rust type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `USER_AGENT` | `&str` | `concat!("omaddons/", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))` | All requests |
| `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` | `usize` | 6 | Global worker pool |
| `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST` | `usize` | 3 | Also protects the github.com web endpoints' undocumented secondary limits |
| `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | `Duration` | 10 s | |
| `API_READ_TIMEOUT` | `Duration` | 30 s | JSON API calls |
| `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` | `Duration` | 300 s | Whole archive download |
| `MAX_RETRIES` | `u32` | 3 | Idempotent GET only; 429, 5xx, timeout or connection reset |
| `BACKOFF_BASE` / `BACKOFF_MAX` | `Duration` | 500 ms / 8 s | Exponential ×2, full jitter |
| `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` | `Duration` | 60 s | A longer `Retry-After` fails with `rate_limited` and the reset time |
| `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` | `Duration` | 15 min | `outdated` (M2) reuses the last per-source result inside the window unless `--refresh` |
| `DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL` | `Duration` | 6 h | Widget background check (config) |
| `WOWI_FILELIST_MIN_AGE` | `Duration` | 1 h | Or the server's `max-age`, whichever is larger (M2) |
| `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE` | `u32` | 5 | For the REST-only paths (beta/alpha, repos without release.json, search): at or below this `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, stop and return `rate_limited` with the reset time |
| `CURSEFORGE_BATCH_SIZE` | `usize` | 50 | `POST /v1/mods` ids per request (server maximum UNVERIFIED; M5) |
| `WOWI_DETAILS_BATCH_SIZE` | `usize` | 50 | `filedetails` ids per request (server maximum UNVERIFIED; M2) |
| `DISCOVERY_MAX_DEPTH` | `usize` | 4 | Under each `drive_c` and under `<home>/Games` |
| `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS` | `&[&str]` | `["windows", "users", "ProgramData"]` | Under `drive_c`, matched case-insensitively. `ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db` is read directly as a hint |
| `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS` | `usize` | 50 000 | Directories visited per scan before stopping with a warning |
| `MAX_REDIRECTS` | `usize` | 5 | Redirect hops followed per request before failing (`http_status`); every hop is checked against the allowlist. Decided during M1 decomposition (net-core bead); not in the vision's §5.13 table, recorded in the vision comment |

**`src/limits.rs`** (copied from vision §5.13):

| Constant | Rust type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES` | `u64` | 20 000 | (config) |
| `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED` | `u64` bytes | 1 GiB | (config) |
| `ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO` | `u64` | 200 (meaning 200:1) | Zip-bomb guard (config) |
| `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` | `u64` bytes | 512 MiB | (config) |
| `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` | `Duration` | 5 s | Then `locked` (exit 5); `concurrency_lost` in the M4 doctor |
| `TX_RETENTION` | `TxRetention { min_age: Duration, keep_last: usize, window: Duration }` | min_age 24 h, keep_last 10, window 7 days | Snapshots are always kept at least 24 h; beyond that, the last 10 transactions within 7 days per target (config) |
| `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` | `u64` bytes | 2 GiB per target | Applies beyond the 24 h protection window (config) |
| `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` | `u64` bytes | 1 GiB | LRU with pins (config) |
| `PLAN_TTL` | `Duration` | 24 h | Stored plans (M4) |
| `REASON_MAX_CHARS` | `usize` | 200 | `--reason`, counted in Unicode scalar values |
| `NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES` | `u64` bytes | 10 MiB | Rotate once, keep one previous |
| `SAVEDVARIABLES_MAX_BYTES` | `u64` bytes | 64 MiB | Lua parser input cap (`errors`, M3) |
| `TOC_LINE_MAX` | `usize` | 1024 chars | Client rule: the client reads only the first 1024 characters of each TOC line |
| `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET` | `Duration` | 5 ms | Doctor `--quick` / `health` (M4) |

Constants that serve later milestones are defined now anyway, so the tables stay complete and auditable in one place.

**Registry.** Each module also exports `pub const REGISTRY: &[LimitInfo]`, one entry per constant, for M4's `capabilities.limits` and for the config overrides:

```rust
pub struct LimitInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,          // "DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES"
    pub value: LimitValue,           // typed default, rendered for humans and JSON
    pub unit: &'static str,          // "bytes" | "ms" | "count" | "ratio" | "chars" | "text" | "list"
    pub config_key: Option<&'static str>, // Some("download_max_bytes") only for "(config)" constants
    pub notes: &'static str,
}
pub enum LimitValue { Count(u64), Bytes(u64), Millis(u64), Ratio(u64), Text(&'static str), List(&'static [&'static str]), Retention { min_age_ms: u64, keep_last: u64, window_ms: u64 } }
```

`LimitInfo` and `LimitValue` derive `serde::Serialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema` (DEC-3).

**Effective values.** `EffectiveLimits` holds the eight config-overridable values: `DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL`, `ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES`, `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED`, `ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO`, `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES`, `TX_RETENTION`, `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` and `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`.
- `EffectiveLimits::default()` uses the constants.
- `EffectiveLimits::apply(key: &str, value: &toml::Value) -> Result<(), LimitOverrideError>` validates the type and the range (positive and non-zero), and rejects keys that are not config-overridable.
- Decided: overrides live under a `[limits]` table in `config.toml`, keyed by the lowercase constant name (e.g. `[limits] download_max_bytes = 268435456`; `tx_retention = { keep_last = 20, window_days = 14 }`). One naming rule means the registry, the config bead and M4's capabilities cannot drift. The config bead reads the table and calls `apply`. The 24 h minimum age of `TX_RETENTION` is not overridable, because age protection always wins.
- Subsystems receive limits as parameters (an `&EffectiveLimits`) rather than reading globals, so tests can shrink them, for example to build a small zip bomb.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/politeness.rs` defines all 19 politeness constants and `src/limits.rs` all 14 limits, with the types and defaults in the tables above, each with a doc comment carrying the table's note.
- `politeness::REGISTRY` and `limits::REGISTRY` together list every constant exactly once. A test compares them against a hand-written name list taken from the vision tables.
- `config_key` is `Some` for exactly the eight "(config)" constants and `None` for every other.
- `USER_AGENT` equals `omaddons/` followed by the crate version.
- `EffectiveLimits::apply("download_max_bytes", 1000)` changes only that value. `apply("lock_acquire_timeout", …)` returns an error naming the key as not overridable. `apply("archive_max_ratio", 0)` and wrong-typed values are rejected.
- `serde_json::to_string(&limits::REGISTRY)` succeeds and is deterministic.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/politeness.rs`, `src/limits.rs`):
  - a registry-completeness test against the hand-written name list;
  - a test that the config-overridable set matches exactly the eight names above;
  - value spot checks: 1 GiB is `1 << 30`, 512 MiB is `512 << 20`, 10 MiB, 64 MiB, `TX_RETENTION` fields;
  - `EffectiveLimits::apply` accept and reject table;
  - `USER_AGENT` prefix.
- Snapshot: an insta JSON snapshot of both registries, to catch accidental value changes in review.

## Considerations

- Changing a default after this bead lands requires a comment on the vision bead that updates the §5.13 table (D22). Mention this in the module doc comments.
- `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS` matching is case-insensitive because Wine paths are; the discovery scan bead applies it.
- `ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO` is stored as the integer N of N:1. The archive-inspect bead compares the total uncompressed size against `N × compressed size`, both per entry and in total.
- Out of scope: reading `config.toml` (config bead), publishing `capabilities.limits` (M4), and the doctor's use of `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET` (M4).
acceptance_criteria: src/politeness.rs defines all 19 politeness constants and src/limits.rs all 14 limits from vision §5.13 with the specified types and defaults, each documented; politeness::REGISTRY and limits::REGISTRY list every constant exactly once, checked against a hand-written name list; config_key is Some for exactly the eight (config) constants (DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL, ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES, ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED, ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO, DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES, TX_RETENTION, SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES, BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES) and None otherwise; USER_AGENT is omaddons/<crate version>; EffectiveLimits::apply changes only the named overridable value and rejects non-overridable keys, zero values and wrong types; both registries serialize deterministically to JSON; argc gate passes
close_reason: src/politeness.rs (20 constants incl. MAX_REDIRECTS) and src/limits.rs (14 limits) define every §5.13 value with its note, both REGISTRYs list each constant once with config_key on exactly the eight (config) ones, and EffectiveLimits applies validated [limits] overrides

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: claim: src/politeness.rs, src/limits.rs (+ src/snapshots/ registry snapshot). Defining the §5.13 constants, LimitInfo registries and EffectiveLimits.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/politeness.rs, src/limits.rs).** (1) Count: the bead text says 19 politeness constants, but its table (vision §5.13 plus MAX_REDIRECTS) has 20, and all 20 are implemented; the 14 limits match. The completeness test checks both hand-written lists. (2) `LimitInfo`, `LimitValue`, `TxRetention` and `EffectiveLimits` live in limits.rs; politeness.rs builds its REGISTRY with the shared `limits::limit` const fn and `limits::ms`. (3) TX_RETENTION's unit is `retention`, which is not in the bead's unit list but names the structured value. (4) `[limits]` value forms: integers for byte, count and ratio limits. `default_check_interval` takes a duration string parsed by `jiff::SignedDuration` ("6h", "90m", "PT6H"); a bare integer is rejected because its unit would be ambiguous. `tx_retention = { keep_last, window_days }` accepts either key alone and rejects any other inner key, min_age included. (5) `LimitOverrideError` separates `Unknown` (not a limit at all) from `NotOverridable` (a real constant without "(config)"), plus `WrongType` and `NotPositive`; a rejected apply leaves every value unchanged. (6) The registry snapshot masks the crate version in USER_AGENT, so a version bump does not churn it.

title: Error and warning code registries, Error/Warning/Suggestion types in src/error.rs
description:
## Background

The CLI contract (vision omad-vision-8qa §5.9, D17, D18, D31) requires:

- every failure to be a typed error with a stable snake_case `code`, a human `message`, a `fix` that is never empty, and `fix_argv`, the argv that runs the fix;
- every error code to map to exactly one exit code in the general exit dictionary, with a published retryability;
- every executable suggestion (the `fix`, each `alternatives[]` entry, each `commands[]` entry) to carry `argv`, so programs execute argv and never shell-parse a display string. The widget executes only entries whose `argv[0]` is `omaddons`. Non-CLI fixes such as `/reload in game` carry `argv: null`.

Warnings use a second registry. The reference implementation this project replaces printed a traceback and no JSON on an unexpected error (vision §3 R3). The registry exists so that every failure path has a code, an exit status and a fix.

This bead builds both registries and the error, warning and suggestion types in `src/error.rs`. It has no open dependencies; the output-envelope bead renders these types.

## Technical Approach

**Exit dictionary.** `Exit` is the general dictionary, used by every command except the M4 `doctor` tree:

| Code | Name | Meaning | Retryable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `ok` | Success, including partial success: per-item failures are listed in `data`, mirrored in `warnings`, and flagged `partial: true` | — |
| 1 | `failed` | Runtime failure: network, source, archive integrity, I/O, state, internal | per `error.retryable` |
| 2 | `usage` | Unknown command or flag, bad argument, bad ref syntax | no |
| 3 | `not_found` | Target, ref, addon, plan or transaction not found, or ambiguous | no |
| 4 | `refused` | Safety refusal: running client, protected folder, ownership or case conflict, unsafe archive, wrong flavor, undo conflict, blocked host | no (`fix` names the flag or command) |
| 5 | `locked` | Another omaddons process held the lock past the acquire timeout | yes |
| 6 | `check_failed` | An opt-in assertion failed (`--check`, `--strict`) | no |

`Exit` provides `code() -> u8`, `name() -> &'static str`, `meaning() -> &'static str`, `ALL: &[Exit]` (M4's capabilities publishes it) and `impl From<Exit> for std::process::ExitCode`. Decided: the process exit status is only ever derived from an `Exit` value; no literal integer passed to `std::process::exit`/`ExitCode::from` appears anywhere else, which the E7 contract suite's exit-site test enforces.

**Error codes.** `ErrorCode` is a closed enum. Each variant provides `wire() -> &'static str`, `exit() -> Exit`, `default_retryable() -> bool` and `ALL: &[ErrorCode]`. The table, copied from vision §5.9 plus the DEC-4 additions:

| Code | Exit | Retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `usage`, `ref_invalid` | 2 | no |
| `target_not_found`, `target_ambiguous`, `ref_ambiguous`, `not_found`, `not_managed`, `plan_not_found`, `no_compatible_release` | 3 | no |
| `game_running`, `protected_folder`, `ownership_conflict`, `unmanaged_folder`, `case_collision`, `wrong_flavor`, `unsafe_archive`, `archive_too_large`, `undo_conflict`, `host_blocked` | 4 | no |
| `scope_denied` (DEC-4: fsx refused a write outside the write-scope table or onto the deny-list, other than a protected folder, which stays `protected_folder`) | 4 | no |
| `state_too_new` (DEC-4: a state file's `schema_version` is newer than this binary; writes refused; fix display "upgrade omaddons", `argv: null`) | 4 | no |
| `locked` | 5 | yes |
| `check_failed` | 6 | no |
| `network`, `rate_limited` (details carry the reset time), `download_failed` | 1 | yes |
| `http_status` | 1 | yes for 5xx only |
| `hash_mismatch` | 1 | yes, once |
| `plan_stale` | 1 | yes when raised by engine step-6 re-planning; no when raised by `apply` (M4; fix = the stored dry-run argv) |
| `offline`, `bad_archive`, `distribution_disabled`, `source_disabled`, `auth_required`, `auth_rejected`, `state_corrupt`, `io`, `internal` | 1 | no |

Per-instance retryability: `Error.retryable` starts from `default_retryable()` and is set by dedicated constructors where the table says it depends on context:
- `Error::http_status(status, …)` sets `retryable = status >= 500`;
- `Error::plan_stale(raised_by: Replan | Apply, …)`;
- `Error::hash_mismatch(attempt: u8, …)` is retryable only on the first attempt.

**Suggestions.**
- `Suggestion { display: String, argv: Option<Vec<String>> }`.
- `Suggestion::command<I, S>(argv: I)` (argv[0] must be `"omaddons"`, checked by `debug_assert!`) sets `display = shell_words::join(&argv)`, so display strings are shell-quoted.
- `Suggestion::text(display)` is for non-CLI fixes (`/reload in game`, "upgrade omaddons") and sets `argv: None`.
- A display can never be empty: an empty `text` falls back to the DEC-5 fix.

**Command hints.** `CommandHint { action: String, command: String, argv: Vec<String>, destructive: bool }`, built by `CommandHint::new(action, argv, destructive)` with `command = shell_words::join(argv)`. The wire field order matches the vision envelope example: `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo 01JB…","argv":["omaddons","undo","01JB…"],"destructive":false}`.

**Errors.**
- `Error { code: ErrorCode, message: String, fix: Suggestion, alternatives: Vec<Suggestion>, retryable: bool, details: serde_json::Value }`, derived with `thiserror::Error`, displaying as `error[<code>]: <message>`.
- Constructors: `Error::new(code, message, fix)`, builder methods `.alternative(Suggestion)`, `.details(serde_json::Value)` and `.retryable(bool)`, and per-domain helpers where useful (`Error::internal(msg)`, `Error::io(path, &std::io::Error, fix)`).
- `details` defaults to an empty JSON object `{}`.
- `type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>`.
- DEC-5: until `doctor` exists (M4), `Error::internal` uses fix `omaddons status`, argv `["omaddons","status"]`. M4 switches it to `omaddons doctor`. Keep this in one function, `internal_fix()`.
- Decided: no blanket `From<std::io::Error> for Error`. Every I/O failure goes through `Error::io` with the path and a fix, because a bare conversion would lose the context the fix needs.

**Wire serialization** (an `ErrorBody` view, field order exactly as the vision failure example): `{"code","message","fix","fix_argv","alternatives":[{"display","argv"}],"retryable","details"}`. `fix` is the display string, `fix_argv` the argv or `null`.

**Warnings.**
- `WarningCode` is a closed enum with `wire()` and `ALL`.
- `Warning { code, message, fix: Option<Suggestion> }` serializes as `{"code","message","fix","fix_argv"}`. Decided: both `fix` and `fix_argv` are always present, `null` when absent, so the shape is stable for consumers.
- The initial codes from vision §5.9: `journal_recovered`, `journal_pending`, `tx_in_progress`, `atomic_swap_unavailable`, `reload_required`, `saved_variables_deferred`, `snapshot_cap_exceeded`, `out_of_date`, `missing_dependency`, `toc_comma_on_legacy`, `client_not_launched_since_patch`, `widget_outdated`.
- DEC-4 adds `state_version_older` (state is migrated forward on the next write) and `state_version_newer` (writes refused).
- Other M1 beads add the warning codes they introduce here, in the same file, keeping the enum closed. Codes already claimed by M1 beads: `config_unknown_key` (config), `unknown_flavor`, `discovery_truncated`, `target_key_duplicate` (discovery and registry), `catalog_override_invalid` (catalog), `ownership_transferred` (ownership). This bead may add them all up front so later beads only use them. The contract is not frozen until M4, and each addition is listed in the comment recorded on the vision bead.
- Decided: a per-item failure that is mirrored into `warnings` during partial success (exit 0, `partial: true`) uses the item's error code as its warning code. `WarningCode` has a variant `Item(ErrorCode)` whose `wire()` is the error's wire name, so `install a b` where `b` has no compatible release yields a warning `{"code":"no_compatible_release",…}` alongside the per-item entry in `data`. Wire names stay unique: no plain warning code may reuse an error code's name.

All public wire types derive `serde::Serialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema` (DEC-3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ErrorCode::ALL` contains exactly the 38 codes in the table above (the 36 vision §5.9 codes plus `scope_denied` and `state_too_new`). A table-driven test asserts each code's `wire()`, `exit().code()` and `default_retryable()`.
- `Exit::ALL` lists codes 0–6 with the names `ok, failed, usage, not_found, refused, locked, check_failed`.
- Every wire name (errors and warnings) is unique and matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.
- `Error::http_status(503, …).retryable` is true and `Error::http_status(404, …).retryable` is false. `plan_stale` raised by re-planning is retryable and raised by apply is not. `hash_mismatch` is retryable on attempt 1 only.
- `Suggestion::command(["omaddons","install","my addon","-t","retail"]).display == "omaddons install 'my addon' -t retail"`, and `shell_words::split(display)` returns the argv unchanged, for argv containing spaces, `!`, `$(…)`, quotes and backslashes.
- No `Suggestion` can carry an empty display. `Error::internal(…)` has fix `omaddons status` with argv `["omaddons","status"]`.
- An `Error` serializes with keys in the order `code, message, fix, fix_argv, alternatives, retryable, details`, and a `Warning` as `code, message, fix, fix_argv`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/error.rs`):
  - a table test that iterates a hand-written copy of the table above and compares it to `ErrorCode::ALL` (catches a code missing from either side);
  - wire-name uniqueness and format;
  - the retryability constructors;
  - `Suggestion` quoting round trips through `shell_words::split`, including argv `["omaddons","install","a b","$(rm -rf x)","it's","!x"]`;
  - empty-display fallback.
- Snapshot: insta JSON snapshots of a `target_ambiguous` error with one alternative and `details.candidates`, and of a `reload_required` warning with a text fix (`fix_argv: null`).
- Property: proptest over arbitrary argv vectors checks that `shell_words::split(Suggestion::command(argv).display) == argv`.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- This bead fixes wire names that M4 freezes and the wire-name golden test pins. Choose spellings exactly as in the tables above.
- Not here: the M4 doctor dictionary (0–6 plus 64/66/73/74) and finding ids `fm-<subsystem>-<slug>`; rendering of errors and warnings (output-envelope bead); the exit-site enforcement test (E7 contract suite).
- `rate_limited` errors put the reset time in `details.reset_at` (RFC 3339). Name the key here so the net beads use it.
- Where a refusal can be overridden, its `fix` must name the overriding flag or command (exit-dictionary row 4), e.g. `game_running` → `--while-running`, or `unmanaged_folder` → `--force` until M2's `adopt`.
acceptance_criteria: ErrorCode::ALL contains exactly 38 codes (the 36 vision §5.9 codes plus scope_denied and state_too_new), and a table-driven test checks each wire name, exit code and default retryability; Exit::ALL lists 0-6 named ok, failed, usage, not_found, refused, locked, check_failed; all error and warning wire names are unique and match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$; http_status is retryable for 5xx only, plan_stale is retryable from re-planning but not from apply, and hash_mismatch is retryable on the first attempt only; Suggestion::command display strings are shell-quoted and round-trip through shell_words::split for argv with spaces, !, $(...), quotes and backslashes; no Suggestion has an empty display and Error::internal has fix omaddons status with argv ["omaddons","status"]; Error serializes as code, message, fix, fix_argv, alternatives, retryable, details and Warning as code, message, fix, fix_argv; argc gate passes
close_reason: src/error.rs holds the general exit dictionary, the 38-code error registry and the 20-code warning registry (plus Item(ErrorCode)), Suggestion/CommandHint with shell-quoted displays and argv, and the Error/Warning types with their wire bodies; all acceptance criteria are covered by tests

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: claim: src/error.rs (+ src/snapshots/ for error/warning snapshots). Building Exit, ErrorCode, WarningCode registries, Suggestion, CommandHint, Error, Warning.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/error.rs).** (1) Each registry is one `macro_rules!` table (`error_codes!`, `warning_codes!`), so a code's wire name, serde rename, exit and default retryability come from a single row. (2) Default retryability for context-dependent codes: `http_status` false, `hash_mismatch` true, `plan_stale` true. Their constructors decide per instance: `Error::http_status(status, …)` (also sets details.status), `Error::hash_mismatch(attempt, …)` (attempts count from 1), `Error::plan_stale(PlanStaleSource::{Replan,Apply}, …)`. (3) Added `Error::rate_limited(reset_at: jiff::Timestamp, …)`, which writes `details.reset_at` (RFC 3339) as the bead asks; `Error::io` puts the path in `details.path`. (4) `Suggestion` and `CommandHint` keep their fields private behind accessors, so an empty display is unconstructible; `argv[0] == omaddons` is a debug_assert. Suggestion has no Deserialize, since that would bypass the invariant. (5) schemars derives the deserialize contract by default, so `#[serde(into = "ErrorBody")]` did not shape Error's schema; `JsonSchema for Error` is written by hand and delegates to ErrorBody. (6) `Warning` derives Deserialize through WarningBody, because the discovery cache persists warnings; a blank fix loads as None. Added `Warning::with_fix` and `Warning::item(&Error)` for partial-success mirroring. (7) All six later-claimed warning codes are added up front (config_unknown_key, unknown_flavor, discovery_truncated, target_key_duplicate, catalog_override_invalid, ownership_transferred): 20 plain codes plus `Item(ErrorCode)`.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: done: argc gate passes (62 lib tests incl. argv round-trip proptest; snapshots target_ambiguous_error and reload_required_warning match the vision envelope example; strict cargo doc clean; ubs 0 critical); decisions in comment above; notes on 1.5, 5.2, 2.4, 5.5 · found: none

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Post-close change (found while doing paths, ejl.2.6):** `Error` was 136 bytes, so clippy's default `result_large_err` (128-byte threshold) rejected every function returning `error::Result<T>`. Error is now `pub struct Error(Box<ErrorData>)` with `Deref`/`DerefMut` to `ErrorData { code, message, fix, alternatives, retryable, details }`, so `err.code` and `err.message` still work and `Result<T>` is one pointer wide (guarded by the test `errors_stay_one_pointer_wide`). Constructors, builders, Display and the wire shape (ErrorBody) are unchanged; struct-literal construction and destructuring of Error are no longer possible.

title: Define the core domain types in src/model.rs
description:
## Background

Every M1 subsystem (fsx, state, discovery, sources, resolution, the engine, the commands) passes the same domain values around: targets, folder names, transaction and plan ids, actors, refs, release sets, candidates and addon records (vision omad-vision-8qa §5.1). Several safety invariants are meant to be enforced by these types rather than by checks scattered through the code (vision §3 language note, D14, D27):

- a folder name can never escape `Interface/AddOns/`: no `/`, `\`, `..`, leading `.`, empty name or NUL;
- folder identity is case-insensitive, because Wine resolves names case-insensitively, so `Blizzard_AuctionUI` and `blizzard_auctionui` are the same folder;
- a folder whose case-folded key starts with `blizzard_` is protected and can never enter the mutable namespace, even with `--force`.

DEC-13: `Family`, `InstallKind`, `TargetKind`, `ClientRules` and the client version type live in `src/rules.rs` (the rules-tables bead, which depends on nothing). This bead depends on rules-tables and defines everything else in `src/model.rs`.

## Technical Approach

All types live in `src/model.rs`. Data types derive `Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema` (DEC-3). Struct field order is the wire order. Maps are `BTreeMap`. Wire names are snake_case lowercase. Use `#[schemars(with = "String")]` for ULIDs, timestamps and paths, because schemars does not know those types without extra features.

**Folder names**
- `FolderName`: a validated `AddOns/<Name>` entry name that keeps its original spelling. `FolderName::new(&str) -> Result<FolderName, FolderNameError>` rejects:
  - empty names, `.` and `..`, and names with a leading `.`;
  - names containing `/`, `\` or NUL, or any ASCII control character (0x00–0x1F, 0x7F);
  - names longer than 255 bytes (NAME_MAX).
- `key(&self) -> &str` returns the ASCII case-folded name (`to_ascii_lowercase`), computed once at construction. `as_str()` returns the original spelling.
- `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash` and `Ord` compare by key, so `BTreeMap<FolderName, _>` treats case variants as one folder. Code that must detect two on-disk spellings of one key (the inventory) collects into a `Vec` and groups by key.
- `is_protected()` is true when `key()` starts with `blizzard_`.
- `MutableFolderName`: a newtype that only `FolderName::into_mutable(self) -> Result<MutableFolderName, FolderName>` can construct, and only when the name is not protected. Every API that creates, replaces, renames or removes an AddOns folder (fsx scope checks, engine ops, ownership) takes `MutableFolderName`. Decided: two types rather than one checked type (D14), so a protected folder cannot reach a mutation API without a compile error.
- Serialize as a plain string. Deserialize through `FolderName::new`, so a persisted record holding an invalid name fails to load (`state_corrupt`).

**Ids**
- `TargetKey(Ulid)`, `TxId(Ulid)` and `PlanId(Ulid)`, each with `new()` (`Ulid::new()`), `Display`, `FromStr`, and serde as the 26-character Crockford base32 string (the ulid crate's `serde` feature is enabled). The JSON Schema is a string with pattern `^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`.
- Keys are immutable once assigned; the registry bead owns assignment.

**Small enums** (lowercase wire names):
- `Actor { Human, Agent, Widget }`, plus a pure `Actor::resolve(flag: Option<&str>, env: Option<&str>, stdin_is_tty: bool) -> Result<Actor, ActorError>`. Precedence: the `--actor` flag, then `OMADDONS_ACTOR`, then `human` when stdin is a terminal and `agent` otherwise. An invalid value is an error that the CLI maps to `usage`. Decided: stdin, not stdout, decides the default, because a human piping `omaddons list | jq` still has a TTY on stdin while agents run with no TTY on any stream.
- `Channel { Stable, Beta, Alpha }`, default `Stable`, ordered so `Stable < Beta < Alpha`. `Channel::includes(release_channel)`: beta includes stable, alpha includes everything.
- `TxKind { Install, Update, Remove, Undo, Adopt, Sync, Restore, Repair, Backup }`, with `is_undoable()` false only for `Backup`. The history records WTF backup creation as `kind: backup` (M3); the variant exists now so the history schema does not change later.
- `ReloadRequired { None, Reload, Restart }`, ordered so `max()` merges per-op requirements into a per-target value.
- `VersionConfidence { Release, Toc }`, `AddonReason { Explicit, Dependency }`, `AddonState { Ok, Degraded }`.

**`Target`** (vision §5.1), one client dir plus its identity:
- fields in this order: `key: Option<TargetKey>` (None until registered), `id: String` (human alias), `install_root: PathBuf`, `client_dir: PathBuf`, `flavor_dir: Option<String>` (e.g. `_retail_`; None for custom roots), `product: Option<String>` (e.g. `wow_classic_era`), `install_kind`, `family`, `kind` (`live|test`), `version` (the rules client-version type), `interface: u32`, `exe_name: String`, `label: Option<String>` (e.g. `localhost` from realmlist), `rules: ClientRules`;
- `rules` is `#[serde(skip)]` and excluded from the schema. Decided: the row is large and not useful in token-frugal output; commands that need rules data build their own view;
- helper `addons_dir()` returns `client_dir/Interface/AddOns`. Paths are produced here and never created here.

**`AddonRecord`** (vision §5.1), fields in order: `ref` (serialized as its canonical string), `name`, `version: String`, `version_confidence`, `release_id: Option<String>`, `channel`, `pinned: bool`, `reason`, `required_by: Vec<String>`, `folders: Vec<FolderName>`, `state`, `installed_at` (`jiff::Timestamp`, RFC 3339), `tx_id: TxId`. The per-file index is not part of the record; it lives in `targets/<key>.files.json` (state-records bead).

**`Ref`**, the canonical `source:id`:
- `GitHub { owner, repo }` ↔ `gh:Owner/Repo`
- `Wowi { id: u64 }` ↔ `wowi:5108`
- `Tukui { slug }` ↔ `tukui:elvui`
- `CurseForge { id: u64 }` ↔ `cf:61284`
- `Wago { id }` ↔ `wago:<id>`
- `Git { url, rev: Option<String> }` ↔ `git:<https-url>[#<rev>]`
- `Url { url }` ↔ `url:<https-url>`
- `File { path }` ↔ `file:<path>`

Behavior:
- `Display` and `FromStr` handle only these canonical forms. Pasted URLs, catalog names and installed names are the refs bead's job.
- `FromStr` errors are typed, and the refs bead maps them to `ref_invalid` (exit 2). Checks: GitHub owner and repo match `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+` and are not `.`/`..`; wowi and cf ids are decimal; git and url schemes must be `https`; file paths are non-empty.
- `RefKind` (`Gh, Wowi, Tukui, Cf, Wago, Git, Url, File`) with `prefix()`. The sources layer maps kinds to sources.
- Equality and hashing for `GitHub` compare owner and repo ASCII-case-insensitively, because GitHub treats them that way and the fetch-once orchestrator must not fetch `gh:weakauras/weakauras2` twice. Display keeps the given spelling. Serialize as the canonical string.

**Release types** (vision §5.1; field lists are the minimum, and later beads may add `Option` fields):
- `ReleaseSet { ref, releases: Vec<Release> }`: everything one fetch learned about one ref.
- `Release { release_id, version, channel, published_at: Option<Timestamp>, assets: Vec<Asset>, changelog_url: Option<String> }`.
- `Asset { filename, location: AssetLocation, size: Option<u64>, expected_hash: Option<ExpectedHash>, flavors: Vec<AssetFlavor>, name_flavors: Vec<FlavorHint>, nolib: bool }`.
- `AssetLocation { Url(String) | LocalZip(PathBuf) | LocalDir(PathBuf) | GitCheckout { url: String, rev: String, sha: String } }`. Decided here, once, because four source beads and three engine beads route on it: `Url` is downloaded into the blob cache; `LocalZip` is hashed and opened in place (user files are not copied into the cache); `LocalDir` is read through a directory `FolderView`; `GitCheckout` is materialized by the git-hosts source into a temp dir and then treated like `LocalDir`.
- `AssetFlavor { flavor: String, interface: Option<u32> }` (release.json metadata).
- `FlavorHint { Mainline, Classic, Bcc, Wrath, Cata, Mists, Titan, Forever, ClassicAny }`: flavor guesses from asset file names, filled by the GitHub REST source's name heuristics for repos without `release.json`. Variant names follow the packager's release.json flavor names.
- `ExpectedHash { Sha256(String) }`, lowercase hex. Decided: M1 has only SHA-256; the MD5 (WoWInterface, M2) and SHA-1 (CurseForge, M5) variants and their crates arrive with those sources.
- `Candidate { release_id, version, channel, asset: Asset, rank: RankReason }`, where `RankReason { MetadataInterface, MetadataFlavor, NameHint, Unannotated, NameHintMismatch, MetadataMismatch }` records which tier of the select bead's ranking proposed it. Selection logic is the select bead's job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/model.rs` defines every type above. `cargo doc` shows each with a one-line doc comment.
- `FolderName::new` rejects `""`, `"."`, `".."`, `".hidden"`, `"a/b"`, `"a\\b"`, `"a\0b"`, names with control characters and names over 255 bytes, and accepts `"WeakAuras"`, `"!BugGrabber"` and `"Blizzard_AuctionUI"`.
- `FolderName::new("Blizzard_AuctionUI").key() == "blizzard_auctionui"`, and that name `is_protected()`. `into_mutable()` fails for it and for `"BLIZZARD_x"`, and succeeds for `"WeakAuras"`.
- Two `FolderName`s differing only in ASCII case are equal and hash equally. `as_str()` keeps the original spelling.
- Every canonical `Ref` form round-trips through `Display` and `FromStr`. `gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2 == gh:weakauras/weakauras2`. `git:http://…` and `url:http://…` are rejected.
- `Actor::resolve` follows flag > env > TTY default, and rejects unknown values.
- ULID ids serialize as 26-character strings and parse back.
- Every data type derives `JsonSchema`, and `schemars::schema_for!` succeeds for `Target`, `AddonRecord`, `ReleaseSet` and `Candidate`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (in `src/model.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`):
  - table tests for `FolderName` accept and reject cases, `key()`, `is_protected()` and `into_mutable()`;
  - `Ref` round trip for each variant, plus rejection cases;
  - `Actor::resolve` precedence matrix;
  - `Channel::includes` matrix;
  - `ReloadRequired` max-merge.
- Property (proptest):
  - for arbitrary strings, `FolderName::new` never returns a name containing `/`, `\`, NUL or `..` as a component, and never one starting with `.`;
  - `key()` is idempotent and case-insensitive (`new(s.to_uppercase())` and `new(s)` have equal keys when both are valid ASCII);
  - every `Ref` built from generated valid parts round-trips.
- Serde: insta JSON snapshots of a sample `Target` (`rules` absent) and an `AddonRecord`; deserializing a record with folder `"../x"` fails.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (proptest prints the minimal failing case).

## Considerations

- `key()` folds ASCII only, as the vision specifies ("ASCII case-folded"). Wine folds non-ASCII case too, so two non-ASCII names differing in case are treated as distinct here. Addon folder names are ASCII in practice; revisit only if a real collision appears.
- Trailing dots and spaces are legal on Linux, but Windows path semantics may strip them under Wine. They are accepted for now; the archive-inspect bead's case-folded collision check is the place to tighten this if needed.
- `Target.version` is `rules::ClientVersion { major, minor, patch, build: Option<u32> }` from the rules-tables bead; do not define a second version type here.
- Out of scope: Ref parsing beyond canonical forms (refs bead), id/alias assignment (registry bead), plan, journal and history types (engine and state beads), `Finding` (M4 doctor).
- Dependency: rules-tables provides `Family`, `InstallKind`, `TargetKind`, `ClientRules` and the version type.
acceptance_criteria: src/model.rs defines FolderName, MutableFolderName, TargetKey, TxId, PlanId, Actor, Channel, TxKind, ReloadRequired, Target, AddonRecord, Ref, ReleaseSet, Release, Asset, Candidate, each with a doc comment; FolderName::new rejects empty, ., .., leading-dot, slash, backslash, NUL, control-character and over-255-byte names and accepts WeakAuras, !BugGrabber and Blizzard_AuctionUI; Blizzard_AuctionUI has key blizzard_auctionui, is_protected() is true and into_mutable() fails (also for BLIZZARD_x) while WeakAuras converts; case variants of a FolderName are equal and hash equally while as_str keeps the spelling; every canonical Ref form round-trips through Display/FromStr, gh refs compare case-insensitively, and non-https git:/url: refs are rejected; Actor::resolve follows flag > OMADDONS_ACTOR > stdin-TTY default and rejects unknown values; ULID ids serialize as 26-character strings; schemars::schema_for! succeeds for Target, AddonRecord, ReleaseSet and Candidate; argc gate passes
close_reason: src/model.rs defines every domain type in the bead: FolderName/MutableFolderName with case-insensitive identity and type-level protection, ULID ids, the small enums, Target, AddonRecord, Ref with canonical parsing, and the release/candidate types; all acceptance criteria are covered by unit, property and snapshot tests

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/model.rs, plus two additions in src/rules.rs).**

- **`Target.exe_name` is `Option<String>`**, not `String`. discover-battlenet step 7 yields `None` when a flavor folder has no exe.
- **`Target.version` stays `ClientVersion`** as specified. It is `0.0.0` when no version could be read, which pairs with family `unknown` and interface 0, the verdict's "unknown" sentinel. The field doc says so.
- **`Target.rules` is `#[serde(skip)]`**, so deserializing needs a default.
  - rules.rs gains `impl Default for ClientRules`, which returns the conservative `fallback-custom` row.
  - `Target::refresh_rules(&RulesTable)` re-derives the row; call it after loading a target (discovery cache) and after a config family override.
  - It uses the new `RulesTable::rules_for_family(family, version, kind)`. `rules_for` now delegates to it, so a decided family picks that family's row and an uncovered version falls back by install kind.
- **Ids** (`TargetKey`, `TxId`, `PlanId`) come from one `ulid_id!` macro: `new()`, `from_ulid`, `ulid()`, `Display`/`FromStr` (`IdParseError`), serde as the 26-character string, and a JSON Schema string with the Crockford pattern.
  - ulid 3.0 renamed `Ulid::new()` to `Ulid::generate()`, so `new()` calls `generate()`.
  - `new()` carries `#[expect(clippy::new_without_default)]`: a default id would be random or nil, and both would surprise.
- **`Ref`.**
  - `Eq`/`Hash`/`Ord` all derive from one identity string: the canonical form with GitHub owner and repo lowercased. `Ord` was added so refs can key a `BTreeMap` deterministically.
  - Validation beyond the bead, each closing an injection or URL-safety gap:
    - a `git:` rev must be non-empty, must not start with `-` (it reaches git's argv) and has no whitespace or control characters;
    - tukui slugs and wago ids use the same `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` charset as GitHub segments (they are interpolated into URL paths), never `.`/`..`;
    - https URLs need a host and no whitespace or control characters.
  - `RefKind` serializes as its prefix.
- **`Actor`.**
  - `FromStr` ignores ASCII case.
  - An empty `OMADDONS_ACTOR` counts as unset.
  - `ActorError { value, origin }`, where `origin` is `--actor` or `OMADDONS_ACTOR`.
- **Folder names.**
  - `FolderNameError::Protected` exists only for deserializing a `MutableFolderName`; `FolderName::new` never returns it.
  - `NAME_MAX = 255` is a private const in model.rs. It is the Linux limit, not a §5.13 policy limit, so it does not belong in limits.rs.
- **Small additions.**
  - `ExpectedHash::sha256(hex)` normalizes to lowercase and validates 64 hex digits.
  - `Channel` (stable) and `ReloadRequired` (none) implement `Default`.
  - `AssetLocation` serializes externally tagged in snake_case: `{"url": …}`, `{"local_zip": …}`, `{"git_checkout": {url, rev, sha}}`.
