title: Battle.net root discovery: flavor folders to targets
description:
## Background

A Battle.net WoW root (`<root>`, e.g. `<prefix>/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/`, where `<prefix>` is a Wine prefix) holds `.build.info` and one flavor folder `_<x>_/` per installed product. Each flavor folder is a *client dir* (it holds `Interface/` and `WTF/`) and becomes one target (vision §5.1, §5.2 step 3). This is the Forever-critical path: M1 must detect product `wowf` in `_forever_` and the Forever beta in `_classic_beta_`, both version 1.60.x and family `forever`, before the 2026-11-04 launch. Detection is data-driven (vision D15): any new `_x_` folder must become a usable target without code changes.

Facts this bead relies on (vision §4.1):

| Product | Folder | Exe | Version (Oct 2026) | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wow | `_retail_` | WoW.exe | 12.1.5.70391 | live |
| wowt | `_ptr_` | WoWT.exe | 12.1.0 | test |
| wowxptr | `_xptr_` | WoWT.exe | 12.1.5 | test |
| wow_beta | `_beta_` | WoWB.exe | 12.0.1 | test |
| wow_classic | `_classic_` | WoWClassic.exe | 5.5.4 (Mists) | live |
| wow_classic_ptr | `_classic_ptr_` | WoWClassicT.exe | 5.5.4 | test |
| wow_classic_beta | `_classic_beta_` | WowB.exe | 1.60.1.70374 (Forever beta) | test |
| wow_classic_era | `_classic_era_` | WoWClassic.exe | 1.15.9 | live |
| wow_classic_era_ptr | `_classic_era_ptr_` | WowClassicT.exe | 2.5.6 (Anniversary PTR) | test |
| wow_anniversary | `_anniversary_` | WoWClassic.exe | 2.5.6 (TBC) | live |
| wow_classic_titan | `_classic_titan_` | WoWClassic.exe | 3.80.2 (China) | live |
| wowf | `_forever_` | Wow.exe | 1.60.1.70245 | live |

- The product code does **not** determine the game family: `wow_classic_era_ptr` runs TBC 2.5.x and `wow_classic_beta` runs Forever 1.60.x. Family comes from the version; the product is a label and a fallback. Exe names vary in case; match case-insensitively. Folder names are not derivable by pattern (`wowf` → `_forever_`).
- Version → family (Battle.net): major 1 & minor < 50 → `vanilla`; major 1 & minor ≥ 50 → `forever`; 2.5 → `tbc`; 3.4 → `wrath`; 3.80 → `titan`; 4.4 → `cata`; 5.5 → `mists`; major ≥ 6 → `mainline`. This table lives in `src/rules.rs` (rules-tables bead); call it, never re-implement it.
- Interface = major×10000 + minor×100 + patch for every current Battle.net client (12.1.5 → 120105, 1.60.1 → 16001, 3.80.2 → 38002), computed by `rules::interface_for`.
- `.flavor.info` (BPSV, header `Product Flavor!STRING:0`) is the authoritative folder → product mapping. `.build.info` rows carry `Product`, `Version`, `Active`, `Branch`, `Tags`, parsed by header name (bpsv bead).
- `WTF/Config.wtf` holds `SET lastAddonVersion "<interface>"`, written by the client. On Battle.net targets the `.build.info` interface wins, and a differing `lastAddonVersion` yields the warning `client_not_launched_since_patch`.
- Default human ids (vision §5.1): `retail` (wow), `classic` (wow_classic), `era` (wow_classic_era), `anniversary` (wow_anniversary), `forever` (wowf), `ptr` (wowt), `xptr` (wowxptr), `beta` (wow_beta), `classic-ptr` (wow_classic_ptr), `classic-beta` (wow_classic_beta), `era-ptr` (wow_classic_era_ptr), `titan` (wow_classic_titan). Read them from the rules-tables product table's `default_id` column; do not keep a second list here. `kind` is `test` for PTR/XPTR/beta products and `live` otherwise. Unknown flavor folders become targets with family `unknown`.

## Technical Approach

- New files: `src/discover/battlenet.rs`, `src/discover/config_wtf.rs`, `src/discover/target.rs`; declare them in `src/discover/mod.rs` and re-export `DiscoveredTarget`, `DiscoverySource`.
- **`src/discover/target.rs`** (shared by every discovery bead; this bead defines it):
  ```rust
  pub struct DiscoveredTarget {
      pub target: crate::model::Target, // key: None; id: the default id suggestion
      pub default_id: String,           // unqualified default id, e.g. "retail"
      pub qualifier: String,            // used by the registry for collisions, e.g. "battlenet", "steam"
      pub source: DiscoverySource,
  }
  pub enum DiscoverySource { ProductDb, Launcher(String), Process, ExtraRoot, Scan, Manual }
  ```
  Derive `Serialize` + `JsonSchema` (DEC-3); field order is wire order.
- **`src/discover/config_wtf.rs`**: `pub fn last_addon_version(client_dir: &Path) -> Option<u32>` reads `WTF/Config.wtf` (read-only), finds a line matching `SET lastAddonVersion "<digits>"` case-insensitively (quotes optional, surrounding whitespace tolerated), returns the number. Also `pub fn cvar(client_dir, name) -> Option<String>` for the realmlist fallback used by `discover-custom`. Missing file → `None`.
- **`src/discover/battlenet.rs`**:
  - `pub struct BattlenetHints { pub product_by_folder: BTreeMap<String, String>, pub version_by_product: BTreeMap<String, String> }` — filled by `discover-scan` from product.db entries; empty when there is no hint. Decided: hints are plain data passed in, so this bead does not depend on the product-db bead.
  - `pub fn is_battlenet_root(dir: &Path) -> bool` — `dir/.build.info` is a regular file.
  - `pub fn discover_root(root: &Path, hints: &BattlenetHints, qualifier: &str, source: DiscoverySource) -> (Vec<DiscoveredTarget>, Vec<Warning>)`:
    1. Read `.build.info` (lossy UTF-8) → `bpsv::build_info_rows`. A parse failure yields no rows (versions then come from hints) plus a debug diagnostic, never an error.
    2. List `root` (read-only); flavor folders are directories whose name matches `^_.+_$`. Sort by name for determinism.
    3. Product per folder: `.flavor.info` → `hints.product_by_folder` → the built-in product table's folder column (via `src/rules.rs`) → `None`.
    4. Version: the `.build.info` row whose `Product` equals the folder's product (prefer `Active == 1` when several); else `hints.version_by_product`; else, if `.build.info` has no `Product` column and exactly one row, that row. Parse into the version type defined in `src/rules.rs`.
    5. Family, interface, `ClientRules`: `rules::family_for(version, InstallKind::Battlenet)`, `rules::interface_for`, `rules::rules_for`. No version is special-cased here.
    6. Kind: the product table's kind when the product is known; otherwise `test` if the product code or folder name contains `ptr` or `beta`, else `live` (decided: heuristic for unknown products, matches every row of the table).
    7. Exe name: the folder entry matching the product table's exe case-insensitively; otherwise the first entry (sorted) matching `wow*.exe` case-insensitively, excluding `wowerror.exe`; otherwise `None`. Store the file name with its on-disk case.
    8. Unknown family (no version, or a version the table does not map) → family `unknown` with `rules::rules_for` returning the most permissive modern row, and warning `unknown_flavor` naming the folder (the target stays usable).
    9. Default id: the table above by product; unknown products → folder name with the surrounding underscores removed (`_xyz_` → `xyz`).
    10. `lastAddonVersion` from `config_wtf` differing from the computed interface → warning `client_not_launched_since_patch` (message names the target; fix: display "launch the client once", `argv: null`). The computed interface is kept.
    11. Label: `"<default id> (<qualifier>)"`, e.g. `retail (battlenet)` (decided: Battle.net clients have no realmlist host; the widget shows family, version and kind separately).
    12. `Target` fields: `key: None`, `id: default_id`, `install_root: root`, `client_dir: root/<folder>`, `flavor_dir: Some(folder)`, `product`, `family`, `kind`, `version`, `interface`, `exe_name`, `label`, `rules`.
- Add warning code `unknown_flavor` to `WarningCode` in `src/error.rs` (additive contract change before the M4 freeze; recorded on the vision bead with the other DEC-4 additions). `client_not_launched_since_patch` is already in the initial list.
- Read-only: nothing in this bead writes. Paths in messages use the target id, not full paths, unless `-v`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A synthetic root with all twelve products from the table yields twelve targets with the right product, family, interface, kind, exe name and default id; `_forever_` (1.60.1) and `_classic_beta_` (1.60.1.70374) are family `forever` with interface 16001; `_classic_era_ptr_` (2.5.6) is family `tbc`; `_classic_titan_` (3.80.2) has interface 38002.
- A folder without `.flavor.info` gets its product from `BattlenetHints`, then from the folder table.
- An `.build.info` with reordered columns or without `Product` (single row) still yields versions.
- An unknown `_xyz_` folder with a `.flavor.info` of `wowz` and a `.build.info` row at 13.0.0 becomes a `mainline` target with id `xyz`; with no version it becomes a usable `unknown` target and emits `unknown_flavor`.
- Exe matching is case-insensitive (`wowclassic.EXE`).
- `lastAddonVersion "120100"` on a 12.1.5 client emits `client_not_launched_since_patch` and keeps interface 120105.
- Discovery of a root writes nothing (tree hash unchanged).

## Test Plan

- Unit (`battlenet.rs`, `config_wtf.rs`): tempdir roots written inline in the test module (plain `std::fs` in tests is allowed): each table product; missing `.flavor.info`; reordered/old `.build.info`; two rows for one product (active wins); unknown folder with and without version; mixed-case exe names; `Config.wtf` variants (quoted, unquoted, different case, missing).
- Integration: the full-tree cases (every product at once, Forever beta and launch layouts side by side) are covered by the `discover-matrix` bead using the `test-trees` builders.
- Log the discovered target list (as JSON) on failure.

## Considerations

- Forever's launch layout (product `wowf`, `_forever_`, interface 16001, `_Forever` TOC suffix) is pre-launch data; nothing here may assume it beyond the table rows, so a different launch layout still works through `.flavor.info` + version.
- A flavor folder can exist half-installed (no exe, no `Interface/`). Still emit the target; the inventory and engine handle a missing `Interface/AddOns` (the engine creates it under fsx scope at first install, never discovery).
- Do not read `product.db` here; `discover-scan` passes the hints.
- Out of scope: id collision qualification and keys (registry bead), the scan that finds roots (`discover-scan`), custom clients (`discover-custom`).
- Dependency added beyond the plan: `error-registry`, because this bead emits `Warning` values and adds `unknown_flavor` to `WarningCode`.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic root with all twelve vision §4.1 products yields twelve targets with correct product, family, interface, kind, exe name and default id; _forever_ and _classic_beta_ at 1.60.x are family forever with interface 16001, _classic_era_ptr_ 2.5.6 is tbc and _classic_titan_ has interface 38002; a folder without .flavor.info gets its product from hints then the folder table; reordered or Product-less .build.info still yields versions; an unknown _xyz_ folder becomes a usable target (mainline with a 13.0.0 version, unknown plus warning unknown_flavor without one) with id xyz; exe matching is case-insensitive; a lastAddonVersion that differs from the computed interface emits client_not_launched_since_patch and keeps the computed interface; discovery writes nothing
close_reason: Battle.net roots become one target per flavor folder: product from .flavor.info, hints, then the folder table; version from .build.info by product, active row first; family, interface and rules from the rules table; kind, exe, default id and label; unknown_flavor and client_not_launched_since_patch warnings; reads only, each read bounded

title: Discovery cache keyed by file stats, and --rescan
description:
## Background

Discovery re-reads `.build.info`, every `.flavor.info`, PE headers and realmlists on each call. `status --cached` must answer in under 5 ms with no network and no scan (vision §5.8), and the widget calls it on every doorbell. The vision specifies a discovery cache (§5.2 step 6):

- The cache key per root is the (path, size, mtime) of `.build.info`, each `.flavor.info`, `Wow*.exe` and `product.db`, plus the root directory listing.
- A directory mtime does not change when `.build.info` is rewritten in place, which is why the files are keyed individually.
- `targets --rescan` forces a full rescan.
- Unknown flavors and version/interface disagreements produce warnings, not failures.

Placeholders: `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache` under the home directory).

The cache is derived data. Deleting it is always safe; a corrupt or old-format cache is discarded, never an error.

## Technical Approach

- New file `src/discover/cache.rs`; declare it in `src/discover/mod.rs`.
- Location: `<cache>/omaddons/discovery.json`. Add `Paths::discovery_cache()` to `src/state/paths.rs` (additive; the §5.6 table does not list this file). Decided: the cache lives with the other derived data (`<cache>` is writable by every command per the write-scope table).
- Format (`Serialize`/`Deserialize` + `JsonSchema`, DEC-3):
  ```rust
  pub struct DiscoveryCache {
      pub schema_version: String,          // "1.0"
      pub roots: Vec<CachedRoot>,          // sorted by path
  }
  pub struct CachedRoot {
      pub path: PathBuf,                   // canonical root
      pub kind: RootKind,                  // battlenet | custom
      pub source: DiscoverySource,
      pub qualifier: String,
      pub stamps: Vec<FileStamp>,          // sorted by path
      pub listing_sha256: String,          // sha256 of the sorted root entry names, NUL-joined
      pub targets: Vec<DiscoveredTarget>,
      pub warnings: Vec<Warning>,
  }
  pub struct FileStamp { pub path: PathBuf, pub size: u64, pub mtime_ns: i128 } // missing file: size 0, mtime_ns -1
  ```
- Stamped files per root:
  - Battle.net: `.build.info`; each `_x_/.flavor.info`; each flavor folder's exe; each flavor folder's `WTF/Config.wtf` (it feeds `client_not_launched_since_patch`); the prefix's `product.db` when the root came from a product.db hint.
  - Custom: every `wow*.exe` in the root; `WTF/Config.wtf` (feeds the `lastAddonVersion` override); each realmlist location checked by discover-custom (feeds the label).
  - Decided: `Config.wtf` and realmlist files are stamped in addition to the vision's list because they feed target fields; leaving them out would serve stale interfaces and labels.
- Modes (`pub enum DiscoveryMode { Cached, Full, Rescan }`, passed through `DiscoveryInput` or a sibling parameter):
  - `Full` (default for non-cached commands): run the scan to find roots; for each found root, if a cached entry with the same path has identical stamps and listing hash, reuse its targets and warnings; otherwise parse the root. Write the new cache if anything changed.
  - `Cached` (`status --cached`): do **not** scan. Re-stat each cached root's stamps; unchanged roots reuse cached targets; a changed root is re-parsed (cheap, one root); a vanished root is dropped from the result with a diagnostic (see Considerations; no new warning code). New roots are found only by a `Full` run. No cache file → behave like `Full`.
  - `Rescan` (`targets --rescan`): ignore the cache entirely, run `Full` parsing for every root, then overwrite the cache.
- Writes go through fsx: `fsx::mutate(&mut WriteSession::untracked("discovery-cache"), &path, Op::WriteFile{..})` (DEC-10: derived data uses an untracked session; unique temp + fsync + rename). A write failure is a diagnostic, never a command failure.
- Read: tolerant `serde_json` decode; `schema_version` other than `1.x` or any decode error → treat as no cache.
- Discovery itself still never writes to game directories; the only write is the cache file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A second `Full` discovery of an unchanged tree reuses every cached root (asserted via a parse counter exposed to tests) and produces output identical to the first.
- Rewriting `.build.info` in place with a new version (same directory mtime, different size or mtime) invalidates that root and the new version appears.
- Adding a new `_xyz_` flavor folder invalidates the root through the listing hash.
- Changing `WTF/Config.wtf` `lastAddonVersion` on a legacy client invalidates its root.
- `Cached` mode performs no directory scan (asserted: a new root added after the cache was written is not reported until a `Full` run) and completes in under 5 ms for a cache of 10 roots on the development machine (measured, recorded in the close comment).
- `Rescan` ignores a deliberately poisoned cache entry.
- A corrupt `discovery.json` is ignored and rewritten; the write goes through fsx into `<cache>/omaddons/`.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`cache.rs`): stamp comparison, listing hash stability (order-independent input, sorted), decode of corrupt and future-version files.
- Integration (`tests/discover_cache.rs`, with `tests/common/` trees and the DEC-6 env helper): the invalidation cases above; mode behavior; poisoned cache under `Rescan`.
- Timing: a `#[ignore]` benchmark-style test for `Cached` mode, run at the checkpoint (hyperfine on `status --cached` belongs to the E7 checkpoint bead).
- Log the cache JSON before and after on failure.

## Considerations

- mtime granularity: compare `mtime_ns` and size; a rewrite within the same nanosecond with the same size is not detectable, which is acceptable for a cache (the next `--rescan` fixes it).
- `Cached` mode intentionally misses new installs until a non-cached command runs; the widget's background `outdated` check and any terminal command refresh it.
- Vanished roots in `Cached` mode: decided to drop them silently from the cached result and leave reporting to the registry/status layer (a registered target whose root is gone is a status concern, `target-root-missing` in the doctor catalog for M4), so no new warning code is introduced here.
- Out of scope: the `--rescan` flag on the `targets` command (E7 `cmd-targets`), `status --cached` itself (E7 `cmd-status`).
acceptance_criteria: A second Full discovery of an unchanged tree reuses every cached root and gives identical output; an in-place .build.info rewrite invalidates that root; a new flavor folder invalidates the root through the listing hash; a changed lastAddonVersion invalidates a legacy root; Cached mode performs no directory scan and runs in under 5 ms for 10 roots on the development machine; Rescan ignores a poisoned cache entry; a corrupt discovery.json is ignored and rewritten through fsx into <cache>/omaddons/
close_reason: Discovery reuses each root's parse while every file feeding it (stamped by path, size and mtime) and the root's listing are unchanged; Cached mode skips the scan, Rescan ignores the cache; the cache is derived data written through fsx and discarded when corrupt or newer; the command pipeline uses it

comments.text: **model landed (src/model.rs).** `Target.rules` is `#[serde(skip)]` and deserializes as the conservative `ClientRules::default()` (the fallback-custom row). After loading cached `DiscoveredTarget`s, call `target.refresh_rules(&table)` with the live (override-applied) RulesTable, so a cached target never runs on the placeholder row. A test covering cache load → rules row would catch a missed refresh.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **discovery scan landed (src/discover/mod.rs, scan.rs).** `discover(&DiscoveryInput { home, extra_roots, extra_prefixes, launcher_hints }, &RulesTable) -> Discovery { targets (sorted by install root, then flavor folder), warnings (sorted by code, then message), diagnostics }`; `discover_with(.., ScanLimits)` exists for tests. `DiscoveredTarget { target (key None), default_id, qualifier, source }` is what the registry assigns keys and ids to. A full run takes about 1 ms warm on the development machine.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/discover/cache.rs; discovery split into collect/parse_root/finish in src/discover/mod.rs; tests/discover_cache.rs).**
(1) `discover_cached(input, &table, &paths, ScanLimits, DiscoveryMode::{Cached, Full, Rescan}) -> (Discovery, CacheStats { scanned, parsed, reused, written })`. CacheStats is the parse counter tests use; it is returned beside Discovery so Discovery stays byte-identical across runs.
(2) `DiscoveryCache` is Versioned ('discovery_cache' 1.0, listed in store::KINDS). schema_version comes from store::encode. A cached root also stores canonical path, kind, source, qualifier, product.db hints and hint_files. A hit requires all of these plus the stamps and the listing hash to match, so a root reached by a different route is re-parsed.
(3) Stamps, missing files as (0, -1): Battle.net roots stamp .build.info, plus each flavor folder's .flavor.info, wow*.exe files and WTF/Config.wtf; custom roots stamp wow*.exe, WTF/Config.wtf, root realmlist.wtf and each Data/<locale>/realmlist.wtf; the product.db files that gave a root its hints are stamped too. A newly added exe appears as a new stamp, so per-folder listings are not hashed; the root listing is. mtime_ns is i64 (good until 2262).
(4) Cached targets are deserialized with placeholder rules, then `refresh_rules(&table)` runs. The 'identical output' test compares rules too.
(5) The cache is written only when the encoded bytes change, through an untracked Writer::Derived session ('discovery-cache') with ensure_dir_all on <cache>/omaddons. A failure is a diagnostic. A newer, corrupt or undecodable cache counts as no cache, then gets overwritten.
(6) A Cached-mode root that is gone, or no longer a root, is dropped with a diagnostic ('… is gone').
(7) **Wiring:** `app::world::World::load()` now uses Full mode, and `World::load_with(mode)` exists for status --cached and targets --rescan. So any command may write the derived cache. This **supersedes 7.3's 'list writes nothing' cache-dir check**; tests/list.rs now asserts home, state and config are unchanged and that the cache file exists.
(8) **Measured on this machine (release):** Cached mode about 60 µs for its 2 roots, against the 5 ms budget; warm Full 0.9 ms; first Full 19 ms including the cache write. The synthetic 10-root Cached test passes the 5 ms release budget. The measurement's real ~/.cache/omaddons/discovery.json was removed afterwards.

comments.text: done: argc gate passes. tests/discover_cache.rs has 8 tests: an unchanged tree reuses every root with identical output; an in-place .build.info rewrite; a new flavor folder through the listing; a legacy lastAddonVersion change; Cached never scanning, dropping vanished roots and falling back to Full; Rescan beating a poisoned cache; a corrupt cache rewritten; 10 cached roots under 5 ms in release. 2 unit tests. Measured about 60 µs Cached on this machine (details above) · found: none

title: Custom and legacy client discovery: PE version, realmlist label, lastAddonVersion
description:
## Background

Private-server clients are first-class targets (vision G1, D29). They have no `.build.info`, no flavor folder and no multi-TOC support. Layout (vision §4.2):

- `<root>/Wow.exe` (any case), `<root>/Interface/AddOns/`, `<root>/WTF/`.
- `<root>/Data/<locale>/realmlist.wtf` containing `set realmlist <host>` (this location is valid for clients 3.0.2–5.0.4).
- `<root>` is the custom client root. It may sit inside a Wine prefix (`<prefix>/drive_c/WoW`) or outside any prefix (`<home>/Games/<name>/Wow.exe`, run by Lutris, Heroic or Bottles). `<prefix>` is a Wine prefix, `<home>` the user's home directory.

Versions in use: 1.12.1 (e.g. Turtle WoW, likely the largest private-server population; its exe version is UNVERIFIED), 2.4.3, 3.3.5a (build 12340), 4.3.4, 5.4.8.

Rules (vision §4.1, §4.2, §5.2 step 4):
- Version source: the `Wow.exe` PE `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` **numeric** fields, read with `pelite`. The version *string* form is UNVERIFIED and must not be used.
- Custom clients below the multi-TOC era get `-legacy` families: 1.12.x `vanilla-legacy`, 2.4.x `tbc-legacy`, 3.3.x `wrath-legacy`, 4.3.x `cata-legacy`, 5.4.x `mists-legacy`. This mapping lives in `src/rules.rs` (rules-tables bead) keyed by install kind `custom`.
- Legacy clients omit the patch digit from the interface number: 3.3.5 → 30300, 1.12.1 → 11200, 2.4.3 → 20400, 4.3.4 → 40300, 5.4.8 → 50400 (`ClientRules.interface_includes_patch = false`).
- `WTF/Config.wtf` `SET lastAddonVersion "<interface>"` is written by the client. On legacy targets it is the most reliable interface source and **overrides** the computed interface when present.
- The label comes from the realmlist host; `127.0.0.1` becomes "localhost".
- Private-server packs may ship extracted `Blizzard_*` addons inside `Interface/AddOns`; those are protected (handled by the inventory bead and fsx, not here).

Development machine (vision §4.7): a custom client at `<home>/Games/wow-335/drive_c/WoW/`; `Wow.exe` is 3.3.5a; `Interface/AddOns` holds 23 `Blizzard_*` folders and nothing else; `Data/enUS/realmlist.wtf` is `set realmlist 127.0.0.1` (a local AzerothCore server). The M1 checkpoint expects it as `wrath-legacy`, interface 30300, label "localhost".

## Technical Approach

- New files `src/discover/pe.rs`, `src/discover/realmlist.rs`, `src/discover/custom.rs`; declare them in `src/discover/mod.rs`. Reuse `DiscoveredTarget`, `DiscoverySource` (`src/discover/target.rs`) and `config_wtf` from the discover-battlenet bead.
- **`pe.rs`**: `pub fn exe_version(path: &Path) -> Option<ExeVersion>` where `ExeVersion { major, minor, patch, build: u16 }`.
  - Open with `pelite::FileMap` (memory map, read-only) and wrap in `pelite::PeFile` (handles PE32 and PE32+).
  - `pe.resources()?.version_info()?.fixed()` → `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO`. Use `dwFileVersion` (Major, Minor, Patch, Build). Decided: if the file version is all zeros, fall back to `dwProductVersion` (which field legacy clients populate is unknown; trying both costs nothing).
  - Any pelite error → `None` (the root is then reported with family `unknown` and warning `unknown_flavor`, still usable).
  - Convert to the version type defined in `src/rules.rs`.
- **Exe selection** (`custom.rs`): entries of `<root>` matching `wow*.exe` case-insensitively, excluding `wowerror.exe` (the crash reporter). Prefer `wow.exe`, then `wow-64.exe` (5.4.8 ships both), then the remaining names sorted. Keep the on-disk case in `exe_name`. Decided: this preference order is a heuristic recorded here; any matching exe with a readable version works.
- **`realmlist.rs`**: `pub fn realmlist_host(root: &Path) -> Option<String>`:
  1. `Data/<locale>/realmlist.wtf` for every locale dir (sorted; first hit wins).
  2. `<root>/realmlist.wtf` (older clients before 3.0.2 keep it in the root — UNVERIFIED, harmless to check).
  3. `WTF/Config.wtf` `SET realmList "<host>"` via `config_wtf::cvar` (clients after 5.0.4 — UNVERIFIED, harmless to check).
  - Line grammar: `set realmlist <host>` case-insensitive, value optionally quoted, trailing whitespace and `\r` stripped; the first matching line wins.
  - `pub fn label_for(host: Option<&str>, root: &Path) -> String`: `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1` → `"localhost"`; another host → the host verbatim (e.g. `logon.example.org`); no host → the root directory's basename.
- **`custom.rs`**:
  - `pub fn is_custom_root(dir: &Path) -> bool` — no `.build.info`, has a matching exe and an `Interface/` directory (case-insensitive names).
  - `pub fn discover_custom_root(root: &Path, qualifier: &str, source: DiscoverySource) -> (Option<DiscoveredTarget>, Vec<Warning>)`:
    1. Exe + version (above). Family via `rules::family_for(version, InstallKind::Custom)`; rules via `rules::rules_for`; interface via `rules::interface_for` (no patch digit for legacy rows).
    2. If the rules row is `legacy` and `config_wtf::last_addon_version(root)` is `Some(n)`, the interface becomes `n` (override, no warning).
    3. Default id: the family-based id: `vanilla-legacy` → `vanilla`, `tbc-legacy` → `tbc`, `wrath-legacy` → `wotlk`, `cata-legacy` → `cata`, `mists-legacy` → `mists`. A non-legacy family on a custom client (e.g. a later private-server version) uses the family name; `unknown` uses the root basename (lowercased, non `[a-z0-9-]` → `-`).
    4. Kind `live`. `product: None`, `flavor_dir: None`, `install_root = client_dir = root`.
    5. Label from `realmlist.rs`.
  - Read-only throughout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- PE stubs built by the `test-trees` PE builder for 1.12.1, 2.4.3, 3.3.5.12340, 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 yield families `vanilla-legacy`, `tbc-legacy`, `wrath-legacy`, `cata-legacy`, `mists-legacy`, interfaces 11200, 20400, 30300, 40300, 50400, and default ids `vanilla`, `tbc`, `wotlk`, `cata`, `mists`.
- A 3.3.5a root with `Data/enUS/realmlist.wtf` = `set realmlist 127.0.0.1` gets label "localhost"; a host `logon.example.org` is used verbatim; no realmlist → root basename.
- `WTF/Config.wtf` `SET lastAddonVersion "30300"` is honored and a different value overrides the computed interface on a legacy target.
- `WOW.EXE`, `wow.exe` and `Wow.exe` are all found; `WowError.exe` alone is not a client.
- A directory with a `.build.info` is never a custom root; a directory with an exe but no `Interface/` is not one.
- A corrupt or non-PE exe yields a usable `unknown` target plus `unknown_flavor`, not a failure.
- Nothing is written to the scanned tree.

## Test Plan

- Integration (`tests/discover_custom.rs`, using `tests/common/` builders from the test-trees bead): one root per legacy version with a PE stub, realmlist variants (each of the three locations, quoted, mixed case, CRLF), `Config.wtf` variants, exe case variants, 5.4.8 with both `Wow.exe` and `Wow-64.exe`, a non-PE `Wow.exe`.
- Unit: `realmlist.rs` line grammar and `label_for` table; exe selection ordering on a synthetic listing.
- Assert the tree hash is unchanged after discovery. Log the discovered target JSON on failure.

## Considerations

- Turtle WoW's exe version is UNVERIFIED; it may not report 1.12.1 in `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO`. If a real sample is available at checkpoint time, record its version in a comment; until then `lastAddonVersion` covers the interface.
- The vision says only the `Data/<locale>/realmlist.wtf` location is verified (3.0.2–5.0.4); the other two locations are best-effort lookups and stay marked UNVERIFIED.
- Hostnames from realmlists are user data; they appear in labels but never in logs beyond what output already shows.
- Out of scope: protected-folder handling (inventory/fsx), id collisions (registry), finding roots (discover-scan).
- Dependencies added beyond the plan: `discover-battlenet` (this bead reuses its `DiscoveredTarget` type and `config_wtf` reader, and Battle.net detection comes first in the M1 delivery order) and `test-trees` (its PE builder produces the VS_FIXEDFILEINFO fixtures; building PE files in two places would duplicate ~150 lines).
acceptance_criteria: PE stubs for 1.12.1, 2.4.3, 3.3.5.12340, 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 yield families vanilla-legacy, tbc-legacy, wrath-legacy, cata-legacy, mists-legacy with interfaces 11200, 20400, 30300, 40300, 50400 and ids vanilla, tbc, wotlk, cata, mists; set realmlist 127.0.0.1 labels the target localhost, another host is used verbatim and a missing realmlist falls back to the root basename; WTF/Config.wtf lastAddonVersion overrides the computed interface on legacy targets; exe names match case-insensitively and WowError.exe alone is not a client; a directory with .build.info or without Interface/ is never a custom root; a non-PE exe yields a usable unknown target plus unknown_flavor; nothing is written to the scanned tree
close_reason: Custom and legacy clients are discovered: exe version from VS_FIXEDFILEINFO (file version first), legacy families and patch-less interfaces from the rules table, lastAddonVersion overriding on legacy rows, realmlist labels with loopback as localhost, ids from the family table; unreadable exes stay usable with unknown_flavor; reads only

(b) `pelite::pe32::PeFile::from_bytes` rejects a buffer that is not 4-byte aligned in memory (Error::Misaligned). A `Vec<u8>` from the global allocator is malloc-aligned on Linux, so read the file into a Vec, never a sub-slice at an odd offset. **Implementation decisions (src/discover/{custom,pe,realmlist}.rs; tests/discover_custom.rs).**
(1) `pe::exe_version(path) -> Option<ClientVersion>` returns the rules version type (build Some); there is no separate ExeVersion type. The file version wins, and the product version is used only when the file version is all zeros. **Verified on this machine's real 3.3.5a Wow.exe:** file 3.3.5.12340, product 3.3.0.0. A stub with exactly that pair is tested (`pe_stub_with`).
(2) The exe is memory-mapped with `pelite::FileMap` (never read whole; a 3.3.5a exe is 7.3 MiB) after `discover::open_regular` confirms a regular file. `pelite::PeFile` handles both PE32 and PE32+ (5.4.8's Wow-64.exe).
(3) `discover_custom_root(root, &RulesTable, qualifier, &DiscoverySource) -> (Option<DiscoveredTarget>, Vec<Warning>)` has the same shape as Battle.net discovery and returns (None, []) for a non-custom root.

(5) The default id is `RulesTable::default_id_for_family` (wotlk, tbc, …; plain family names for non-legacy custom versions). Unknown falls back to the root's directory name, lowercased, with anything outside [a-z0-9-] replaced by '-'; it is 'custom' for '/'.
(6) Labels: 127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1 and [::1], each with an optional :port, read 'localhost'. Any other host is used verbatim, port included. With no host the directory name is used.

(8) `.build.info` and `Interface` are found ignoring case; Interface must be a directory.
(9) Custom targets never emit `client_not_launched_since_patch`: on legacy rows lastAddonVersion is authoritative, and the bead specifies no check for non-legacy custom clients.
(10) Robustness fix to the shared helpers: `read_text` and `read_bytes` now go through `open_regular`, which checks the file type before opening, so a FIFO planted under a metadata name cannot block discovery.
(11) **M1 checkpoint item verified:** `OMADDONS_REAL_CUSTOM_ROOT=<this machine's wow-335 WoW dir> cargo test --test discover_custom -- --ignored` finds wrath-legacy, interface 30300, label localhost, with nothing written. title: Launcher config readers: Lutris, Heroic, Steam, Bottles (native and Flatpak)
description:
## Background

Many WoW installs on Linux are run by a launcher rather than Battle.net under Omarchy's default prefix (vision §1, §5.2 step 1b). Their prefixes and executables are recorded in launcher config files. Reading those configs finds clients the bounded scan would miss: prefixes outside `<home>/Games`, Steam libraries on other disks, and custom clients outside any prefix. Each format gets a small tolerant reader that extracts keys; there is **no general YAML or VDF dependency** (vision §5.2).

Placeholders: `<home>` = the user's home directory; `<config>` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config` under the home directory); `<data>` = `$XDG_DATA_HOME` (default `.local/share` under the home directory).

Formats and locations (vision §5.2 step 1b; locations not given by the vision are marked UNVERIFIED and must be checked on a real install when available):

| Launcher | Files | Keys | Locations |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lutris | `games/*.yml` | `exe`, `prefix` (under `game:`) | `<config>/lutris/games/`; newer releases may use `<data>/lutris/games/` (UNVERIFIED) — check both |
| Heroic | `GamesConfig/*.json` | `winePrefix` (per game object) | native `<config>/heroic/GamesConfig/`; Flatpak `<home>/.var/app/com.heroicgameslauncher.hgl/config/heroic/GamesConfig/` (UNVERIFIED path) |
| Steam | `steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf` | `"path"` per library | native `<data>/Steam/` (and `<home>/.steam/steam/`, usually a symlink to it); Flatpak under `<home>/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/` (`.local/share/Steam/`, UNVERIFIED subpath) |
| Bottles | one directory per bottle (the bottle dir is the Wine prefix) with `bottle.yml` | `Name`, `Path` (UNVERIFIED keys) | native `<data>/bottles/bottles/`; Flatpak `<home>/.var/app/com.usebottles.bottles/data/bottles/bottles/` (UNVERIFIED paths) |

Each Steam library contributes `<library>/steamapps/compatdata/*/pfx` prefixes (WoW is typically a non-Steam shortcut with its own compatdata id).

## Technical Approach

- New files `src/discover/launchers/{mod.rs,lutris.rs,heroic.rs,steam.rs,bottles.rs}`; declare `pub mod launchers;` in `src/discover/mod.rs`.
- Output type `LauncherHint { launcher: String, flatpak: bool, prefix: Option<PathBuf>, exe: Option<PathBuf> }` (already declared in `src/discover/mod.rs` by the discover-scan bead; extend only additively).
- `pub fn collect_hints(home: &Path) -> (Vec<LauncherHint>, Vec<String> /* diagnostics */)` runs every reader. `discover()` calls it and appends the results to `DiscoveryInput.launcher_hints` before scanning (edit `discover()` in `src/discover/mod.rs`; the input slot already exists).
- **Lutris** (`lutris.rs`): for each `*.yml` in both directories, scan lines for `^\s*(exe|prefix|working_dir)\s*:\s*(.*)$`; strip surrounding single or double quotes and trailing comments (` #…`); expand a leading tilde or `$HOME` path prefix against `home`. `prefix` → hint prefix; `exe` → hint exe (a custom client outside a prefix is found through its exe's directory). Lutris also runs other games; decided: keep every existing `prefix` (scanning a non-WoW prefix is bounded and harmless), and keep `exe` only when its basename matches `wow*.exe`, `world of warcraft launcher.exe` or `battle.net launcher.exe` (case-insensitive).
- **Heroic** (`heroic.rs`): parse each JSON file with `serde_json::Value` (already a dependency); walk all objects and collect every string value under a `winePrefix` key. Invalid JSON → diagnostic, skip.
- **Steam** (`steam.rs`): read `libraryfolders.vdf` line by line; collect values of lines matching `^\s*"path"\s+"(.*)"\s*$`, unescaping `\\` → `\`. Libraries = those paths plus the Steam root itself. For each library, list `steamapps/compatdata/*/pfx` directories → hints with launcher `steam`. De-duplicate libraries by canonical path (the native `.steam/steam` symlink and `<data>/Steam` usually point at the same place).
- **Bottles** (`bottles.rs`): each directory under the bottles dir that contains `drive_c/` is a prefix (hint with launcher `bottles`); read `bottle.yml` only to pick up a `Path:` override (tolerant line reader, same grammar as Lutris) when present.
- Qualifiers: the discover-scan bead derives the qualifier from `launcher` (`lutris`, `heroic`, `steam`, `bottles`); Flatpak variants use the same qualifier (decided: users think of "Steam", not "Steam Flatpak"; the registry adds `-2` on a real collision).
- **Never fail discovery**: any unreadable, missing or malformed file yields a diagnostic string and is skipped. Readers never panic on arbitrary bytes. Read-only: no writes anywhere.
- Hints feed discover-scan as candidate prefixes (scanned under `drive_c` with the normal bounds) and as candidate roots (the parent directory of a hinted exe, classified with the normal Battle.net/custom checks).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Lutris yml with `game:\n  exe: <path>/Wow.exe\n  prefix: <path>/pfx` (quoted and unquoted, CRLF) yields both hints; the exe's directory is discovered as a custom root.
- A Heroic GamesConfig JSON with `winePrefix` nested in a per-game object yields the prefix; invalid JSON is skipped with a diagnostic.
- A Steam `libraryfolders.vdf` listing two libraries (one on another tempdir "disk") yields every `compatdata/*/pfx`, and a WoW root inside one of those prefixes is discovered with qualifier `steam`.
- A Bottles directory with two bottles yields two prefixes.
- Native and Flatpak locations are both read for Heroic, Steam and Bottles; both Lutris directories are read.
- Truncated, binary or empty config files never fail `discover()` and never panic (proptest over each reader).
- No file is written.

## Test Plan

- Unit (each reader module): inline fixture strings for well-formed, quoted, commented, CRLF, truncated and binary inputs; property tests feeding arbitrary bytes.
- Integration (`tests/discover_launchers.rs`, using the `tests/common/` launcher builders from the test-trees bead): a synthetic home with one config per launcher (native and Flatpak) pointing at synthetic prefixes containing a Battle.net root or a custom client; assert targets and qualifiers.
- Log the collected hints and diagnostics on failure.

## Considerations

- Several locations and keys are UNVERIFIED. When a real install is available (checkpoint time), record the observed paths in a comment and update the reader; keep the old candidates too, since launchers move files between releases.
- Never read secrets: Heroic and Steam directories contain account data; the readers open only the named config files.
- Expanding `~` in Lutris paths is the only path expansion; environment variables other than `$HOME` are left as-is.
- Out of scope: launching games, Lutris Flatpak (not listed in the vision), Heroic sideload library files.
- Priority 2: the M1 delivery order puts launcher hints after the Forever-critical path.
acceptance_criteria: A Lutris yml (quoted, unquoted, CRLF) yields exe and prefix hints and the exe's directory is discovered as a custom root; a Heroic GamesConfig JSON yields its nested winePrefix and invalid JSON is skipped with a diagnostic; a Steam libraryfolders.vdf with two libraries yields every compatdata/*/pfx and a WoW root inside one is discovered with qualifier steam; a Bottles directory with two bottles yields two prefixes; native and Flatpak locations are read for Heroic, Steam and Bottles and both Lutris directories are read; malformed or binary configs never fail discover() or panic (proptest); no file is written
close_reason: Lutris, Heroic, Steam and Bottles config readers (native and Flatpak) feed discovery as prefix and exe hints

comments.text: **discovery scan landed (src/discover/mod.rs, scan.rs).** `discover(&DiscoveryInput { home, extra_roots, extra_prefixes, launcher_hints }, &RulesTable) -> Discovery { targets (sorted by install root, then flavor folder), warnings (sorted by code, then message), diagnostics }`; `discover_with(.., ScanLimits)` exists for tests. `DiscoveredTarget { target (key None), default_id, qualifier, source }` is what the registry assigns keys and ids to. A full run takes about 1 ms warm on the development machine. The launcher slot is `DiscoveryInput.launcher_hints: Vec<LauncherHint { launcher, flatpak, prefix, exe }>`. A hinted prefix is scanned under its drive_c with qualifier slug(launcher) and source Launcher { name }. A hinted exe resolves through its flavor folder's parent, else its own directory. Only the default Steam library's compatdata is scanned today; add the other libraries as hint prefixes. Paths that are not prefixes become diagnostics.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Verified on a real native Steam install (2026-10-15):** <data>/Steam/steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf (an identical copy in config/; read only as a fallback), tab-separated quoted VDF with one "path" per library; ~/.steam/steam and ~/.steam/root are symlinks to <data>/Steam; compatdata/<id>/pfx/drive_c for each Proton app, including id 0. No Lutris, Heroic or Bottles install exists on the development machine, so their locations and Bottles' keys stay as planned and are marked unverified in the module docs; Flatpak Steam is read from both .local/share/Steam and data/Steam under its private home. **Decisions:** (1) The Steam reader replaces the hard-coded default-library compatdata scan: every library (the root, the vdf's paths, ~/.steam/{steam,root,debian-installation}, the Flatpak root) is read once by canonical path, so default-library prefixes now report found_by launcher:steam instead of scan, with the same qualifier steam. (2) Readers run inside discovery's collect(), ahead of explicit DiscoveryInput.launcher_hints, from new DiscoveryInput.config_home/data_home (None = the XDG defaults under home); Paths gained data_home () and a config_home accessor, and World passes both. (3) Lutris: the first exe/prefix/working_dir line wins; a relative exe resolves against working_dir, then prefix, preferring one where the file exists; only wow*.exe, World of Warcraft Launcher.exe and Battle.net Launcher.exe exes are kept; a non-WoW exe is silently ignored. (4) Bottles: only an absolute top-level (unindented) Path: is a custom location. (5) Heroic: strings under winePrefix at any depth, depth first in key order. (6) Missing files are silent; unreadable ones and invalid Heroic JSON are diagnostics. Dev machine: targets --rescan finds the same two clients (retail via product.db, wotlk via scan) in 19 ms.

title: Discovery test matrix over synthetic trees (M1 checkpoint 2)
description:
## Background

M1 checkpoint 2 (vision §7 M1 Checkpoints) requires that synthetic trees resolve correctly:
- every product in §4.1, including `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_` at 1.60.x;
- every legacy `ClientRules` row;
- a game on a mapped drive letter outside `drive_c`;
- a custom client outside any prefix;
- each launcher config;
- an unknown `_xyz_` folder (yields a usable `unknown` target).

Each discovery bead tests its own piece; this bead is the end-to-end matrix that proves the pieces compose through `discover()` + registry reconciliation, and that discovery never writes (vision defect R10, §5.2 step 7). It is also the Forever launch guard: WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04, and both the beta layout (`wow_classic_beta` in `_classic_beta_`, 1.60.1.70374) and the launch layout (`wowf` in `_forever_`, 1.60.1.70245) must resolve as family `forever`.

Expected values (vision §4.1; interface = major×10000 + minor×100 + patch for Battle.net, patch omitted for legacy):

| Folder / client | Family | Interface | Kind | Default id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_retail_` 12.1.5 | mainline | 120105 | live | retail |
| `_ptr_` 12.1.0 | mainline | 120100 | test | ptr |

title: Bounded discovery scan and hint aggregation
description:
## Background

Discovery must find every WoW root on the machine with zero configuration (vision G2, §5.2 steps 1–2) and stay cheap enough to run on every non-cached command. This bead owns the entry point `discover()`: it collects hints, picks candidate prefixes, runs a bounded scan, classifies each root as Battle.net or custom (via the discover-battlenet and discover-custom beads), de-duplicates, and returns targets in a deterministic order. Discovery never writes to game directories (vision defect R10).

Placeholders: `<home>` = the user's home directory; `<prefix>` = a Wine prefix (a directory with `drive_c/`).

Hints, in order (vision §5.2 step 1):
- (a) Battle.net `product.db` per prefix at `<prefix>/drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db`, parsed by the product-db bead; install paths mapped through `<prefix>/dosdevices/<letter>:` symlinks. A parse failure falls through to scanning.
- (b) Launcher configs (Lutris, Heroic, Steam, Bottles) — added by the discover-launchers bead; this bead provides the input slot.
- (c) Running processes (`WINEPREFIX` and exe paths) — computed by the running-detection bead; the caller passes them in.
- (d) `extra_roots` from `config.toml` — passed in by the caller.

Bounded scan (vision §5.2 step 2, constants from `src/politeness.rs`, vision §5.13):

| Constant | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `DISCOVERY_MAX_DEPTH` | 4 | Under each `drive_c` and under `<home>/Games` |
| `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS` | `windows`, `users`, `ProgramData` | Under `drive_c`. `ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db` is read directly as a hint |
| `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS` | 50 000 | Directories visited per scan before stopping with a warning |

Candidate prefixes: `<home>/Games/*`, `<home>/.wine`, Steam compatdata `*/pfx` in every library, and prefixes from (b). The scan runs under each prefix's `drive_c` and under `<home>/Games` itself (for custom clients outside prefixes), looking for `World of Warcraft/` or any directory containing a `Wow*.exe` (case-insensitive).

## Technical Approach

- New file `src/discover/scan.rs`; `discover()` lives in `src/discover/mod.rs`.
- Input/output types (in `src/discover/mod.rs`, `Serialize` + `JsonSchema` per DEC-3 where they reach output):
  ```rust
  pub struct DiscoveryInput {
      pub home: PathBuf,
      pub extra_roots: Vec<PathBuf>,          // config extra_roots + registry manual roots
      pub extra_prefixes: Vec<ExtraPrefix>,   // running processes, etc.
      pub launcher_hints: Vec<LauncherHint>,  // filled by discover-launchers; empty here
  }
  pub struct ExtraPrefix { pub path: PathBuf, pub qualifier: String, pub source: DiscoverySource }
  pub struct LauncherHint { pub launcher: String, pub flatpak: bool, pub prefix: Option<PathBuf>, pub exe: Option<PathBuf> }
  pub struct Discovery { pub targets: Vec<DiscoveredTarget>, pub warnings: Vec<Warning>, pub diagnostics: Vec<String> }
  pub fn discover(input: &DiscoveryInput) -> Discovery
  ```
  `diagnostics` are debug notes (unreadable files, skipped hints) rendered as stderr `log` events at `-v`; they are not warnings.
- **Prefix collection** (`scan.rs`): `<home>/Games/*` entries that contain `drive_c/`; `<home>/.wine` if it has `drive_c/`; `<home>/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/*/pfx` (default library only — discover-launchers adds every library from `libraryfolders.vdf`); `extra_prefixes`; prefixes from `launcher_hints`. Each prefix carries a qualifier: the launcher name for launcher/Steam prefixes (`steam`, `lutris`, `heroic`, `bottles`), otherwise the prefix directory's basename lowercased with non `[a-z0-9-]` characters replaced by `-` (e.g. `battlenet`, `wow-335`).
- **Hint (a)**: for each prefix, `product_db::read_product_db(prefix)`; map each `install_path` with `dosdevices::map_windows_path`; mapped directories become root candidates with source `ProductDb`; collect `flavor_folder → product` and `product → version` pairs into the `BattlenetHints` passed to `battlenet::discover_root` for that root.
- **Scan** — one bounded breadth-first walk per base directory, sharing one visited-directory budget:
  - bases: each prefix's `drive_c` (with `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS` applied to its direct children, matched case-insensitively), `<home>/Games` itself, and each `extra_roots` entry;
  - depth is counted from the base (`drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft` is depth 2); stop descending past `DISCOVERY_MAX_DEPTH`;
  - when walking `<home>/Games`, do not descend into directories that are Wine prefixes (contain `drive_c/`), because their `drive_c` is scanned as its own base (decided: avoids walking every prefix twice and walking `drive_c/windows` without the skip list);
  - at each directory, list entries once (read-only) and classify:
    - contains `.build.info` → Battle.net root (`battlenet::is_battlenet_root`); record it and do not descend further;
    - is a custom root (`custom::is_custom_root`: exe matching `wow*.exe`, an `Interface/` dir, no `.build.info`) → record, do not descend;
    - contains a `wow*.exe` and its parent contains `.build.info` → it is a flavor folder; record the parent as a Battle.net root (covers roots not named `World of Warcraft`);
  - directory symlinks are followed, with a visited set of `(dev, ino)` pairs as the loop guard; each directory counts once against `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS`;
  - reaching `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS` stops the scan and adds warning `discovery_truncated` (message: how many directories were visited and the base being scanned; fix: display "add the client with: omaddons targets add <path>", argv null). Add `discovery_truncated` to `WarningCode` in `src/error.rs` (contract addition before the M4 freeze).
- **Classification and de-duplication**: canonicalize every root (`std::fs::canonicalize`, read-only) and keep the first occurrence in hint order (product.db, launchers, processes, extra roots, scan), which decides `DiscoverySource` and qualifier. Battle.net roots → `battlenet::discover_root`; custom roots → `custom::discover_custom_root`. For custom roots found under `<home>/Games` outside any prefix, the qualifier is the root's basename.
- **Order**: sort targets by `(install_root, flavor_dir)` as byte strings; sort warnings by code then message. Same filesystem → identical output.
- Never writes: no fsx, no `std::fs` mutation; the whole module is read-only. Errors reading a directory (permission denied, vanished) become diagnostics, never failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `HOME` pointed at a synthetic home, `discover()` finds: a Battle.net root in `<home>/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft`; a root reached only through `product.db` + a `d:` drive mapping outside `drive_c`; a custom 3.3.5a client at `<prefix>/drive_c/WoW`; a custom client directly under `<home>/Games/<name>/` outside any prefix; a root listed in `extra_roots`.
- A root reachable by two routes (product.db hint and scan, or a symlinked path) appears once, with the product.db source.
- `drive_c/windows`, `drive_c/users` and `drive_c/ProgramData` (any case) are never descended into; directories deeper than depth 4 are not visited.
- A symlink loop under `<home>/Games` terminates.
- Setting the directory budget to a small value in a test hook stops the scan and yields `discovery_truncated`.
- Running `discover()` twice on the same tree returns byte-identical serialized output.
- The scanned trees are unchanged afterwards (tree hash before == after).

## Test Plan

- Unit (`scan.rs`): depth counting, skip-list matching (case-insensitive), prefix detection, qualifier normalization, root classification on synthetic listings.
- Integration (`tests/discover_scan.rs`, using `tests/common/` builders from the test-trees bead): the trees in the acceptance criteria; a symlink loop; a permission-denied directory (chmod 000 in the tempdir; skipped with a diagnostic); a budget-limited run via a `#[cfg(test)]`/debug-only override of the directory budget (decided: the constant stays in `src/politeness.rs`; tests use an internal `ScanLimits` struct defaulting to the constants).
- Determinism: run twice, compare serialized `Discovery`.
- Log the visited-directory count and the target list on failure.

## Considerations

- Discovery cost matters for every command; budget it at tens of milliseconds on the development machine (two prefixes). The discovery cache (discover-cache bead) removes the per-root parsing cost, and `status --cached` skips the scan entirely.
- A game installed on a drive letter outside `drive_c` is found only through product.db or launcher hints or `extra_roots`; the scan does not follow `dosdevices`.
- Steam libraries beyond the default one come from the discover-launchers bead.
- Out of scope: launcher readers (discover-launchers), caching (discover-cache), keys and ids (registry), running detection (running-detection; the caller converts running prefixes into `extra_prefixes`).
acceptance_criteria: discover() finds a Battle.net root under <home>/Games/battlenet/drive_c, a root reached only through product.db and a d: mapping outside drive_c, a custom client at <prefix>/drive_c/WoW, a custom client under <home>/Games outside any prefix, and an extra_roots entry; a root reachable two ways appears once with the product.db source; windows, users and ProgramData under drive_c are skipped case-insensitively and nothing deeper than depth 4 is visited; a symlink loop terminates; exhausting the directory budget yields warning discovery_truncated; two runs give byte-identical output; scanned trees are unchanged
close_reason: discover() finds every WoW root with zero configuration: product.db hints mapped through dosdevices, launcher and process hints, extra roots, then a bounded breadth-first scan with skip dirs, depth, a shared directory budget and a symlink loop guard; roots are de-duplicated by canonical path in route order and output is deterministic; reads only

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/discover/{mod,scan}.rs; tests/discover_scan.rs).**
(1) `discover(input, &RulesTable) -> Discovery` takes the table so config overrides apply. `discover_with(input, table, ScanLimits)` and `ScanLimits` (Default = the politeness constants) are public, because integration tests cannot reach a cfg(test) hook; the constants stay in politeness.rs.
(2) Route order decides which source and qualifier a root keeps. Order: product.db (every prefix, with its prefix's qualifier), launcher exes, launcher prefixes, extra (process) prefixes, extra_roots, the scanned prefixes (`<home>/Games/*`, `~/.wine` as 'wine', and the default Steam library's compatdata pfx as 'steam'), then `<home>/Games`. product.db hints still merge into a root first reached some other way, since one product.db lists each product of a root separately. De-duplication uses canonical paths, and the first route's path is kept as given.
(3) Each directory is listed once and classified from that listing; there are no per-root helper calls during the walk. Order: a flavor folder (a client exe whose parent has .build.info) becomes its parent; else .build.info means Battle.net; else exe + Interface/ means custom.
(4) **Bug found and fixed:** a flavor folder (WoWClassic.exe + Interface/, with no .build.info of its own) looked like a custom root. A launcher exe hint or an extra root pointing inside a Battle.net root turned `_anniversary_` into a custom TBC client. `custom::is_custom_root` now rejects any directory whose parent is a Battle.net root, and both `root_of_exe` and the walk check the parent first. Regression tests are in both suites.
(5) Qualifiers use one `discover::slug` (lowercase, non [a-z0-9-] → '-'), which custom ids now share. Roots under `<home>/Games` or an extra root are qualified by their own directory name.
(6) Diagnostics: unlistable directories, product.db paths that do not resolve, hinted prefixes that are not prefixes, and exes outside any root. They are collected in order, never fail discovery, and the scan's diagnostics follow the hint diagnostics.
(7) `discovery_truncated` reports the visited count and the base being scanned. Its fix is text ('add the client with: omaddons targets add <path>'), with no argv.
(8) **Measured on this machine:** about 1 ms warm. It finds retail (mainline 120100, via product.db, qualifier battlenet) and wotlk (wrath-legacy 30300, localhost, via scan, qualifier wow-335) with no diagnostics.
(9) Housekeeping: `src/fsx/failpoint.rs` now allows dead_code in non-debug builds (the parser is debug-only by design), so `cargo build --release` is warning-free.

title: Tolerant product.db protobuf reader and dosdevices drive mapping
description:
## Background

The Battle.net Agent keeps a protobuf database of installed products at `<prefix>/drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db` (vision §4.1, §5.2 step 1a). `<prefix>` is a Wine prefix such as Omarchy's `<home>/Games/battlenet` (`<home>` = the user's home directory). It is discovery's first and best hint: it names install paths directly, including installs on another drive letter that a scan of `drive_c` would never reach.

Facts:
- On the development machine product.db contains the install path `C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft`, the flavor folder `_retail_` and the version `12.1.0.69933`.
- The field layout follows WowUp's reader and is **UNVERIFIED**. A tolerant wire-format reader is sufficient; a parse failure falls through to scanning.
- Install paths are Windows paths. They map to Linux paths through `<prefix>/dosdevices/<letter>:` symlinks. The development machine has `c: → ../drive_c`, `s: → /home`, `w: → /mnt`, `x: → <home>`, `z: → /`. A game installed on another letter lives outside `drive_c`.
- `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS` skips `ProgramData` during the scan precisely because product.db is read directly as a hint.

No protobuf crate is used (vision §5.12: the protobuf wire reader is implemented inline, ~100 lines).

## Technical Approach

- New files `src/discover/product_db.rs` and `src/discover/dosdevices.rs`; declare both in `src/discover/mod.rs`.
- **Wire reader** (`product_db.rs`, private module section):
  - Decode varints (max 10 bytes; overflow → stop), tags (`field << 3 | wire_type`), and wire types 0 (varint), 1 (fixed64), 2 (length-delimited), 5 (fixed32). Wire types 3/4 (groups) and anything else end parsing of that message.
  - Every read is bounds-checked; a truncated or malformed message returns what was decoded so far. No `unwrap`, no indexing that can panic, no recursion deeper than 16 levels.
  - `fn fields(buf: &[u8]) -> Vec<Field>` where `Field { number: u32, value: Value::{Varint(u64), Bytes(&[u8]), Fixed32, Fixed64} }`.
- **Shape-based extraction** (layout-agnostic, because the layout is UNVERIFIED):
  - Treat each top-level length-delimited field as one candidate "product install" entry (in WowUp's layout these are the repeated `product_installs`).
  - Within an entry, walk length-delimited values recursively: try to decode as a nested message (accept it if it decodes cleanly to at least one field and consumes the whole buffer); otherwise, if it is valid UTF-8, collect it as a string.
  - Classify the entry's strings:
    - install path: matches `^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]` (e.g. `C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft`);
    - product code: matches `^wow[a-z0-9_]*$` (all WoW product codes start with `wow`);
    - version: matches `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`;
    - flavor folder: matches `^_[a-z0-9_]+_$`.
  - Keep only entries that have an install path and either a `wow*` product code or an install path containing `World of Warcraft` (case-insensitive); product.db also lists the Agent and other Blizzard games.
  - Output: `pub struct ProductDbEntry { pub product: Option<String>, pub install_path: String, pub flavor_folder: Option<String>, pub version: Option<String> }` and `pub fn parse_product_db(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<ProductDbEntry>` (empty on any failure; never errors).
  - `pub fn read_product_db(prefix: &Path) -> Vec<ProductDbEntry>` reads `drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db` (read-only, size-capped by refusing files over 16 MiB; decided: a product.db is a few KiB, and the cap keeps a corrupt file from being slurped — it is a parse guard, not a §5.13 safety limit).
- **dosdevices mapping** (`dosdevices.rs`):
  - `pub fn map_windows_path(prefix: &Path, win: &str) -> Option<PathBuf>`:
    1. Normalize `\` to `/`; split `X:` drive letter (case-insensitive) from the rest.
    2. Read the symlink `<prefix>/dosdevices/<x>:` (lowercase letter). Resolve a relative target (`../drive_c`) against `<prefix>/dosdevices/`; absolute targets are used as-is.
    3. Join the remaining components. Wine resolves names case-insensitively, so when an exact component is missing, match it case-insensitively against the directory listing (read-only). If several entries differ only in case, pick the exact match if present, else the lexicographically first, and continue.
    4. Return `None` when the letter has no mapping or a component cannot be found.
  - `pub fn drive_map(prefix: &Path) -> BTreeMap<char, PathBuf>` for diagnostics and for `running-detection`, which maps process exe paths the same way.
- Discovery integration is done by `discover-scan`: for each candidate prefix it calls `read_product_db`, maps each `install_path` with `map_windows_path`, and treats the result as a Battle.net root hint; the `flavor_folder` → `product` pairs become the product.db fallback that `discover-battlenet` uses when a flavor folder lacks `.flavor.info`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A synthetic product.db encoding WowUp's layout (entries with uid/product code, a nested settings message holding the install path, a nested state message holding the version) parses into `ProductDbEntry { product: Some("wow"), install_path: "C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft", flavor_folder: Some("_retail_"), version: Some("12.1.0.69933") }`.
- The same strings placed at different field numbers and nesting depths are still extracted (layout-agnostic).
- Non-WoW entries (e.g. product code `agent` with a non-WoW path) are dropped.
- Truncated, random and empty inputs return an empty or partial list and never panic (proptest, 10 000 cases).
- `map_windows_path` resolves `C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft` through `c: → ../drive_c`, resolves a `D:/Games/WoW` path through `d: → <some dir outside drive_c>`, matches components case-insensitively, accepts backslashes, and returns `None` for an unmapped letter.
- Neither module writes anything (no `std::fs` write calls; read-only APIs only).

## Test Plan

- Unit (`product_db.rs`): a small `#[cfg(test)]` encoder (varint + length-delimited helpers, ~30 lines) builds:
  - the WowUp-shaped database with `wow` and `wow_classic_era` installs plus an `agent` entry;
  - a shuffled-field-number variant;
  - a database with a truncated final entry.
- Property: arbitrary bytes and arbitrary mutations of the valid fixture never panic; decoding a valid fixture is deterministic.
- Unit (`dosdevices.rs`): tempdir prefix with `dosdevices/c:` → `../drive_c`, `dosdevices/d:` → an absolute tempdir path outside `drive_c`, `dosdevices/z:` → `/`; directories created with different case (`program files (x86)`); assert mapping results.
- Fixture: if the development machine's product.db contains no personal data (only product codes, paths and versions), copy its bytes to `tests/fixtures/product_db/retail.db` and assert the retail entry. If it contains anything personal (account names, emails), do not copy it; keep only the synthetic fixture and say so in the close comment.
- Log the decoded field tree on assertion failure.

## Considerations

- WowUp's exact field numbers are UNVERIFIED; do not hard-code them as the only path. The shape-based classifier is the contract; field numbers may be used as a tie-breaker only.
- A string field that happens to decode as a valid nested message (short ASCII strings sometimes do) can be misclassified; the "consumes the whole buffer and every field is well-formed" rule plus checking both interpretations (collect the string too when it is valid UTF-8) keeps paths from being lost.
- Multiple installs of the same product in one prefix are possible; return all entries, de-duplication happens in `discover-scan` by canonical root path.
- Out of scope: turning entries into targets (`discover-battlenet`), choosing which prefixes to read (`discover-scan`), the fuzz target (E7 `fuzz-targets`).
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic WowUp-shaped product.db yields product wow, install path C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft, flavor folder _retail_ and version 12.1.0.69933; the same strings at different field numbers and nesting depths are still extracted; non-WoW entries are dropped; truncated, random and empty inputs never panic (proptest); map_windows_path resolves C: through a relative ../drive_c link and D: through an absolute link outside drive_c, matches components case-insensitively, accepts backslashes and returns None for an unmapped letter; neither module writes to the filesystem
close_reason: Tolerant inline protobuf reader for product.db, with shape-based extraction of WoW installs (path, product, flavor folder, version), and dosdevices mapping of Windows paths into the prefix; reads only, bounded

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/discover/{product_db,dosdevices}.rs).**
(1) Size guard: `read_product_db` reuses limits::DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES (1 MiB) through a new `discover::read_bytes`, which refuses an oversized file rather than truncating it. This replaces the bead's separate 16 MiB guard: constants live in limits.rs, and a product.db is ~1 KiB.
(2) Only printable UTF-8 (no control characters) counts as a string. This keeps a nested message whose bytes happen to be ASCII from being classified as a path. Each class takes its first match in depth-first order.
(3) An entry without a `wow*` code is kept only when its path contains 'World of Warcraft' (product None).
(4) **Layout verified** against this machine's product.db: install path at settings(3).1, flavor folder at settings(3).13, version at cached_state(4).base_state(1).7. That matches WowUp's layout. Field numbers are recorded here only; the code stays shape-based.
(5) Fixture `tests/fixtures/product_db/retail.db` is that file (1259 bytes). It contains product codes (agent, bna, wow), Windows install paths under C:/, versions, public build-config hashes and region/locale tags (us/USA/US, enUS). It has no account names, emails, usernames or home paths (checked with strings and grep). It parses to exactly the expected retail entry.
(6) `map_windows_path`: a relative dosdevices link is resolved lexically, so `c:` maps to `<prefix>/drive_c` (clean paths for dedup). A `..` component in the Windows path returns None; empty and `.` components are skipped; a non-Windows path returns None. Case-insensitive components use `discover::find_child` (exact match first, else the sorted first).
(7) The decoder function is `decode_message`: ubs flags any function named `decode` as a JWT risk.
