title: Epic: M1 network layer and keyless sources
description:
## Background

omaddons must install addons without any account (vision goal G2, decision D4). The most-used addons ship on GitHub releases with a BigWigs-packager `release.json`, and legacy private-server addons live in plain GitHub repos, other git hosts, direct https zips and local files. Milestone 1 delivers the keyless half of the source story: the network layer every source shares, and the `local`, `url`, `github` and `git` sources.

The network layer is where the privacy promise (G5, D13) becomes checkable by the user: one HTTP client, a hard host allowlist enforced on every request and every redirect hop, a local `net.log` that records every HTTP request and every git subprocess, and an `--offline` switch. The GitHub source follows D28: refs are fetched once per run no matter how many targets want them, selection is a pure function that is table-tested without I/O, and the stable channel for `release.json` publishers uses github.com web endpoints (a 302 `Location` header, `release.json`, release-asset downloads) so it performs zero GitHub REST requests and the 60 requests/hour unauthenticated REST budget stops mattering.

This epic holds the network layer (net-core, net-resilience, net-fixtures), the ref parser and fetch-once orchestrator (refs), the four keyless M1 sources (source-local-url, source-github-stable, source-github-rest, source-git-github, source-git-hosts), pure candidate selection (select) and the built-in catalog (catalog).

## Goals

- One `Http` trait with a ureq + rustls (ring provider) implementation, used by every source. Per-hop host allowlist, https only, `host_blocked` on violation.
- `net.log` at `<state>/omaddons/net.log` (`<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME`, default `.local/state` under the home directory): one JSON line per HTTP request and per git subprocess, with credentials and query secrets stripped.
- `--offline` / `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` makes every network attempt fail fast with `offline`.
- Retry with exponential backoff and full jitter, `Retry-After` handling, ETag/Last-Modified validators, and bounded parallelism, all driven by the constants in `src/politeness.rs`.
- Deterministic tests: HTTP fixture replay, a record mode that rewrites fixtures with secrets stripped, and live probes run only at milestone checkpoints.
- Ref parsing for canonical refs, pasted URLs, local paths, installed names and catalog names, plus a fetch-once orchestrator that fetches each distinct ref exactly once per run.
- Keyless sources: `file:` and `url:`; GitHub stable via redirects and `release.json`; GitHub REST only for beta/alpha channels and repos without `release.json`; `git:` refs for GitHub (commits atom + codeload) and for configured non-GitHub hosts (git binary).
- Pure `select()` ranking candidates per target and channel.
- Catalog v1 so `omaddons install weakauras` works with no account, plus verified repos for each legacy family.

## Success Criteria

- Installing `release.json` publishers on the stable channel performs zero `api.github.com` requests, asserted by reading `net.log` in fixture-replay tests (vision M1 checkpoint).
- A request, or any redirect hop, to a non-allowlisted host fails with `host_blocked` (exit 4) before any bytes are sent to that host. Every HTTP request and git subprocess appears in `net.log` without credentials (vision M1 checkpoint).
- `--offline` produces `offline` (exit 1) for any command that would touch the network, and `net.log` gains no lines.
- Each distinct ref is fetched once per run regardless of how many targets request it (asserted with a counting fake source and from `net.log`).
- `select()` is table-tested for every family, including `forever`, `titan` and every legacy family, with no I/O.
- The catalog parses at build time, every entry's ref parses, names and aliases are unique, and every entry's repository was verified against a recorded fixture.
- Live probes (`OMADDONS_LIVE=1`) pass at the M1 checkpoint: one request per keyless endpoint, decoded by the production decoders.
- Every leaf bead in this epic is closed and the local gate passes.

## Non-Goals

- WoWInterface and Tukui sources (M2). Their refs parse in M1 and fail at fetch with `source_disabled` (DEC-12).
- CurseForge and Wago sources and credentials (M5). Their hosts are never contacted in M1.
- `search`, `outdated`, changelogs, `auth github`, GraphQL batching (M2).
- Dependency resolution (M2). The catalog folder index is built now so M2 can use it.
- Downloading into the blob cache, archive inspection and TOC verification (E6 beads blob-cache, archive-inspect and plan). Sources describe assets; the engine downloads and verifies them.
- Proxy support. ureq runs with no proxy.

## Considerations

- github.com web endpoints have undocumented secondary rate limits. `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST` (3), backoff and live probes at checkpoints mitigate this (vision §8).
- `release.json` metadata is unreliable in practice: WeakAuras' current file has no `mainline` entry. Selection therefore never excludes a candidate on metadata alone, and the engine's TOC verification decides (D5).
- Legacy clients have no metadata anywhere. Every candidate for a legacy target is "unannotated", and the `ClientRules`-based verification in E6 is what keeps a modern build out of a 1.12.1 client.
- Sharp edges between beads: the engine (E6 plan/blob-cache) downloads `Asset` URLs, reads local `file:` directories through `FolderView`, and materializes non-GitHub git checkouts through a function source-git-hosts provides. Each source bead states the asset shape it emits.
- Placeholders used in this epic's beads: `<state>`, `<cache>` (= `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`, default `.cache`) and `<config>` (= `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, default `.config`), all under the user's home directory by default.
acceptance_criteria: Installing release.json publishers on the stable channel performs zero api.github.com requests (asserted from net.log in fixture replay); a request or redirect hop to a non-allowlisted host fails with host_blocked (exit 4) and every HTTP request and git subprocess appears in net.log without credentials; --offline yields offline (exit 1) with no net.log lines; each distinct ref is fetched once per run; select() is table-tested for every family including forever, titan and all legacy families with no I/O; the catalog parses, every ref parses, names and aliases are unique, and every entry was verified against a recorded fixture; live probes pass at the M1 checkpoint; all child beads closed and the local gate passes

title: Built-in addon catalog v1 with user overrides and a folder index
description:
## Background

`omaddons install weakauras` should work with no account and without the user knowing the GitHub repository (vision G2, G4: "the first command an agent guesses works"). The vision (§5.4) gives the catalog this shape:

- **Sources:** `catalog/catalog.toml`, embedded in the binary with `include_str!`, plus user overrides in `<config>/omaddons/catalog.d/*.toml`.
- **Entry shape:** `{name, aliases[], ref, families[], folders[], notes}`.
- **Coverage:** popular keyless addons, and verified repositories for each legacy family. Legacy ecosystems have no registry, so catalog entries plus git/url sources are the realistic ceiling (vision §8).
- **Folder index:** the entries' `folders[]` give the index used later by dependency resolution and adoption (M2).

M1's catalog must cover the GitHub `release.json` publishers listed in vision §4.5 (as of October 2026): WeakAuras2, DBM, BigWigs, LittleWigs, Plater, Bartender4, Questie, OmniCC, Dominos, Masque, RaiderIO, MythicDungeonTools, AllTheThings. It must also hold at least one verified repository per legacy family: 1.12.1 (vanilla-legacy, Interface 11200), 2.4.3 (tbc-legacy, 20400), 3.3.5a (wrath-legacy, 30300), 4.3.4 (cata-legacy, 40300) and 5.4.8 (mists-legacy, 50400).

Placeholder: `<config>` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `catalog/catalog.toml` (data) and `src/resolve/catalog.rs` (loader, lookups, folder index).

**File format** (built-in file and override files alike):

```toml
schema_version = "1.0"

[[addon]]
name = "WeakAuras"
aliases = ["weakauras", "wa"]
ref = "gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2"
families = ["mainline", "vanilla", "tbc", "wrath", "cata", "mists"]
folders = ["WeakAuras", "WeakAurasOptions"]
notes = "release.json lacks a mainline entry; TOC verification decides"
```

The folder list and families above are illustrative and must be replaced with verified values.

**Field rules.**
- `name`: required, unique case-insensitively across all names and aliases.
- `aliases`: optional, also unique.
- `ref`: required, must parse with the model's canonical `Ref::from_str`.
- `families`: wire names from `src/rules.rs` (`mainline`, `vanilla`, `forever`, `tbc`, `wrath`, `titan`, `cata`, `mists`, `vanilla-legacy`, `tbc-legacy`, `wrath-legacy`, `cata-legacy`, `mists-legacy`). It lists where the entry is known to work and lets the install command narrow "the single compatible target"; it never replaces TOC verification.
- `folders`: valid `FolderName`s, none protected (`blizzard_` keys rejected).
- `notes`: optional free text.
- Optional `remove = true`, override files only: drops a built-in entry with the same name.

**Loading.**
- `Catalog::load(paths: &Paths) -> (Catalog, Vec<Warning>)`. Parse the embedded file first; a parse failure there is a build-breaking bug, caught by a unit test.
- Then read `<config>/omaddons/catalog.d/*.toml` in lexical filename order. An entry whose name matches an existing entry case-insensitively replaces it wholesale, `remove = true` deletes it, and new names are added.
- An override file that fails to parse or validate is skipped as a whole, with a warning naming the file and line. Decided: introduce the warning code `catalog_override_invalid` (DEC-4 style contract addition, recorded on the vision bead with the others), because a bad user file must never break install or status.
- The catalog is read-only and writes nothing.

**Lookups.**
- `by_name(&str) -> Option<&Entry>`: case-insensitive on name and aliases. It feeds `RefContext.catalog` in the refs bead.
- `by_folder(&FolderName) -> &[EntryId]`: keyed by `FolderName::key()`. It serves M2 dependency resolution and adoption, and the list command's hints.
- `entries()`: in file order, for `info` and future `search`.

**Verification of entries (mandatory, no guessing).** For every built-in entry the implementer:
1. confirms the repository exists and publishes installable zips, with one live check per repository, recorded with net-fixtures' record mode into `tests/fixtures/http/catalog/`;
2. takes `folders[]` from the actual archive's addon roots, not from memory;
3. for each `release.json` publisher, confirms the file exists. Entries whose repository lacks it still go in, with `notes` saying so;
4. for each legacy family, finds a real addon repository or release whose TOC carries that family's legacy Interface (11200/20400/30300/40300/50400), records the archive's TOC line in the fixture, and uses a `gh:` ref (release assets) or a `git:` ref (repository is the addon) as appropriate.

If no repository can be verified for a family, leave that family without an entry and say so in the bead's close comment. An empty slot is better than a wrong ref. Record the verification evidence (repository, tag or sha, TOC Interface line) in the close comment.

A replay test walks every catalog entry through its source's `fetch` (github-stable, github-rest or git-github fixtures) and asserts a non-empty release set. That test lands with or after those sources: write it with `#[ignore]` and a note until they exist, then enable it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `catalog/catalog.toml` is embedded with `include_str!` and parses. Every entry's `ref` parses canonically. Names and aliases are unique case-insensitively. `folders` are valid non-protected `FolderName`s. `families` are valid family wire names.
- It holds entries for all 13 `release.json` publishers named above, with repositories and folder lists verified against recorded fixtures.
- It holds at least one verified entry per legacy family, with the TOC Interface evidence recorded, or an explicit note in the close comment for any family that could not be verified.
- `catalog.d/*.toml` overrides apply in lexical order: replace by name, add new, `remove = true` deletes. An invalid override file is skipped with warning `catalog_override_invalid`, and the built-in entries stay intact.
- `by_name` resolves names and aliases case-insensitively, and `by_folder` returns the entries owning a folder key.
- The catalog performs no writes and no network access at load time.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - embedded catalog validation (parse, refs, uniqueness, FolderName validity, family names);
  - override merge semantics with tempdir `catalog.d` (replace, add, remove, lexical order, invalid file skipped with warning);
  - `by_name` case-insensitivity and aliases;
  - `by_folder` with a folder shared by two entries (both returned, in file order).
- Integration (replay; enabled once the sources land): every entry's ref fetches a non-empty release set from `tests/fixtures/http/catalog/`.
- E2E (in cmd-install): `omaddons install weakauras --dry-run` resolves through the catalog with no account.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (entry name, ref, failing rule).

## Considerations

- Catalog data rots: repositories move and folders change. The replay test catches structural drift against recorded fixtures, and the live probes at milestone checkpoints catch upstream moves.
- `catalog/**` is an embedded asset, so it counts as a code change for the local gate (D16).
- Aliases must not shadow installed-addon names in a confusing way. The refs bead already reports `ref_ambiguous` when an installed name and a catalog name disagree.
- CurseForge-only or WoWI-only addons (e.g. Details!, which has no usable GitHub releases) are out of M1's catalog. WoWI entries arrive with the WoWI source in M2.
- Out of scope: search ranking (M2) and dependency resolution through the folder index (M2).
- Dependency added beyond the plan: `paths` (for the `catalog.d` directory) and `net-fixtures` (entry verification is recorded with its record mode).

title: GitHub source: stable channel without REST via redirects, atom and release.json
description:
## Background

The most-used keyless addons publish GitHub releases built by the BigWigs packager, which uploads a `release.json` asset describing each zip's flavors (vision §4.5). As of October 2026 the publishers include WeakAuras2, DBM, BigWigs, LittleWigs, Plater, Bartender4, Questie, OmniCC, Dominos, Masque, RaiderIO, MythicDungeonTools and AllTheThings.

Unauthenticated GitHub REST allows only 60 requests per hour per IP, so with dozens of addons and several targets REST would be exhausted quickly. The vision's answer (D28, §5.4) is a stable-channel path that uses only github.com web endpoints, which carry no REST rate limit. M1's checkpoint requires that installing `release.json` publishers on the stable channel performs zero GitHub REST requests, asserted from `net.log`.

Facts this bead relies on (vision §4.5, verified 2026-10-14):
- `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/latest` returns a 302 to `/releases/tag/<tag>`. Read the tag from `Location` without following it.
- `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases.atom` supports conditional GET with ETag and returns no rate-limit headers. Atom feeds do not carry the prerelease flag.
- `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>/<file>` returns a 302 to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` or `objects.githubusercontent.com`.
- `release.json` format: `{"releases":[{"name","version","filename","nolib":false,"metadata":[{"flavor":"mainline","interface":120100}]}]}`. An additional entry with `nolib:true` may exist. Only `filename`, `nolib` and `metadata` are reliable: Questie omits `name`/`version` and adds extra keys.
- Packager flavor names: `mainline, classic, bcc, wrath, cata, mists, titan, forever`. The packager maps tbc→bcc, vanilla→classic, wotlkc→wrath, camelot→forever.
- WeakAuras' current `release.json` has no `mainline` entry, so metadata is unreliable and TOCs must be verified. Details! has no usable GitHub releases (latest 2021).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/sources/github.rs` (`GithubSource`, `SourceId::Github`), `src/sources/release_json.rs` (decoder), `src/sources/atom.rs` (a minimal shared Atom decoder, also used by source-git-github).

**fetch(refs, http):** refs are `gh:<owner>/<repo>`. Each ref is processed independently with `net::pool::run_bounded(…, MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS)`. Per ref:

1. **Stable tag.** `GET https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/latest` with `RedirectMode::Manual`, purpose `release-latest`.
   - 302 with `Location` ending `/releases/tag/<tag>` → tag = last segment, percent-decoded.
   - 302 to `…/releases` (the repository has releases but none marked latest, e.g. only prereleases) → for the stable channel `no_compatible_release` (3), with fix `omaddons install gh:<o>/<r> --channel beta` (argv).
   - 404 → no releases at all → `not_found` (3), with fix `omaddons install git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>` (argv), since the repository may still be installable as a git ref.
   - Other statuses → `http_status`, through net-resilience's retry.
2. **Pinned version.** With an explicit version (from `--version` or a URL `version_hint`), skip step 1 and use it as the tag. If its `release.json` is 404 and the value does not start with `v`, retry once with `v<version>`.
3. **release.json.** `GET https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>/release.json` with `Follow`, purpose `release-json`. The 302 goes to an allowlisted asset host. Decode tolerantly:
   - unknown keys ignored;
   - `releases[]` entries without `filename` skipped, with a log event;
   - `nolib` defaults to false;
   - `metadata` defaults to empty;
   - flavor strings lowercased and kept even when unknown (a future flavor simply matches nothing);
   - `interface` optional;
   - `version` taken when present, else the tag.
   - Decided: a malformed `release.json` is treated like a missing one (fall through to step 5), with a warning logged, because a broken manifest should not block an installable zip.
4. **Release set.** One `Release`:
   - `release_id = "gh:<o>/<r>@<tag>"`, `version`, `channel: Stable`, `published_at: None`;
   - one `Asset` per `release.json` entry: `name = filename`, `location = Url("https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>/<filename>")`, `flavors = metadata[{flavor, interface?}]`, `nolib`, `expected_hash: None`.

   The engine downloads assets later through `Follow`. Both hops (github.com → asset host) are allowlisted.
5. **No release.json (404) or a malformed one.** Delegate to the REST fallback seam `GithubSource.rest: Option<Box<dyn GithubRestFallback>>`, filled by source-github-rest. Until that lands, return `no_compatible_release` (3) with fix display `download a release zip, then: omaddons install <path>` (`argv: null`) and an alternative `omaddons install git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>` (argv).
6. **Beta/alpha channel requested.** These need the prerelease flag, which only REST or GraphQL provide. Delegate to the same REST seam. Until it lands, return `no_compatible_release` with fix `omaddons install gh:<o>/<r> --channel stable` (argv).

**releases.atom.** Implement `GithubSource::recent_tags(o, r, http) -> Result<Vec<AtomEntry>>`: a conditional GET (`Request.validators = true`) on `releases.atom` that returns entries (tag from the entry link, `updated`) and reports `Revalidated` on 304. Decided: the M1 install path does not use it. `releases/latest` already gives the stable tag in one request, and atom cannot tell stable from prerelease. It is built here so M2's `outdated` can short-circuit unchanged repos, and because `src/sources/atom.rs` is shared with source-git-github. Keep the Atom decoder minimal: `feed/entry/{id,title,updated,link@href}`, tolerant of namespaces and unknown elements, with no XML crate. Decided: a small hand-written tag scanner, since the format is fixed and tiny and adding a crate is not justified.

**Zero REST.** Nothing in this file may build a URL on `api.github.com`. A unit test greps `src/sources/github.rs` and `release_json.rs` for `api.github.com` and fails if it appears. REST lives in source-github-rest's file.

**Fixtures.** Record with net-fixtures' record mode (`OMADDONS_RECORD=1`) into `tests/fixtures/http/github-stable/`: the `releases/latest` redirect, `release.json` and one small asset zip for WeakAuras2 (`WeakAuras/WeakAuras2`, the vision's example ref; its `release.json` has no `mainline` entry), DBM, BigWigs, Plater, Bartender4 and Questie (no `name`/`version`). The implementer looks up and confirms each repository's owner/name while recording; do not guess repository paths. Add a decoder-level live probe for `release.json` to `tests/live_probes.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GithubSource::fetch` resolves the stable tag from the `releases/latest` 302 `Location` without following it, downloads and tolerantly decodes `release.json`, and emits one stable release with one asset per entry (URL, flavors and nolib populated).
- Repos with only prereleases yield `no_compatible_release` with the `--channel beta` fix. Repos without releases yield `not_found` with the `git:` fix.
- Pinned versions skip `releases/latest` and retry once with a `v` prefix on 404.
- Missing or malformed `release.json`, and beta/alpha channels, go through the REST seam, or return `no_compatible_release` with the documented fixes when the seam is empty.
- `recent_tags` performs a conditional GET on `releases.atom` and decodes its entries. The shared `src/sources/atom.rs` decoder exists and is unit-tested.
- Fixture-replay tests for the six recorded publishers produce correct release sets, and `assert_no_github_rest` passes on their `net.log`. The checkpoint "zero GitHub REST requests for `release.json` publishers on the stable channel" holds.
- WeakAuras2's release set has no `mainline` metadata, and the source does not invent any.
- No `api.github.com` URL appears in this bead's files (grep test).

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - `release.json` decoder over:
    - the documented example;
    - Questie-style (no name/version, extra keys);
    - entries with and without `nolib`;
    - unknown flavor names;
    - missing `filename`;
    - malformed JSON;
  - `Location` parsing: absolute, relative, percent-encoded tags (`v1.2%2Bbuild`), `…/releases`;
  - Atom decoder against a recorded feed and a synthetic feed with namespaces;
  - the grep test.
- Integration (replay, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=tests/fixtures/http/github-stable`):
  - each recorded publisher fetches correctly;
  - `fetch_once` over the six refs requested by three targets produces 6 `releases/latest` requests and 6 `release.json` requests, no duplicates (`assert_each_url_once`) and zero REST (`assert_no_github_rest`);
  - synthetic scenarios: 404 `releases/latest`, a 302 to `/releases`, 404 `release.json`.
- Live (`#[ignore]`, `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`): decode WeakAuras2's live `release.json` with the production decoder.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (ref, request URLs, decoded release set).

## Considerations

- github.com web endpoints have undocumented secondary limits. Concurrency is bounded by net-resilience (3 per host), and failures back off. If GitHub ever stops sending the `releases/latest` redirect, the live probe catches it at the checkpoint.
- Tags may contain `/` (rare). Percent-decode the `Location` segment, and percent-encode again when building download URLs.
- Prefer `nolib:false` entries; select does the ranking, not this bead.
- Release `published_at` and changelog bodies are not available without REST. Changelogs are M2 (`info --changelog`).
- The opt-in GitHub token and GraphQL batching are M2 (`auth github`). This source sends no credentials to github.com web endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: GithubSource::fetch resolves the stable tag from the releases/latest 302 Location without following it, downloads and tolerantly decodes release.json, and emits one stable release with one asset per entry (URL, flavors, nolib); prerelease-only repos yield no_compatible_release with the --channel beta fix and repos without releases yield not_found with the git: fix; pinned versions skip releases/latest and retry once with a v prefix on 404; missing or malformed release.json and beta/alpha channels go through the REST seam or return no_compatible_release with the documented fixes; recent_tags performs a conditional GET on releases.atom and the shared src/sources/atom.rs decoder is unit-tested; fixture-replay tests for six recorded publishers produce correct release sets and assert_no_github_rest passes on their net.log; WeakAuras2's release set has no invented mainline metadata; no api.github.com URL appears in this bead's files
close_reason: gh: refs resolve on the stable channel with two github.com web requests (releases/latest redirect, then release.json), with tolerant manifest decoding, pinned versions with a v-prefix retry, exact errors for prerelease-only and release-less repos, a REST fallback seam, and an atom decoder; six real publishers replay with zero REST

**Implementation decisions (src/sources/{github,release_json,atom}.rs, tests/sources_github.rs, tests/fixtures/http/github-stable/).**
(1) **Source trait change:** `Source::fetch(&self, wanted: &[Wanted], http)` where `sources::Wanted { ref, channel, version: Option<String> }` (Ord/Hash; `Wanted::stable(ref)`). The bead needed the channel and pinned version inside fetch. Deduplicating on the whole wish keeps D28 (three targets wanting gh:x on stable is one fetch). fetch_once now returns BTreeMap<Wanted, Result<ReleaseSet>>.
(2) Order inside fetch: a pinned version wins over the channel. Pinned: release.json at <version>; on a 404, and only if the version has no leading v, once more at v<version>. A pinned version with an empty, '.' or '..' segment is not_found without a request. Beta/alpha without a version go straight to the seam, with no web request.
(3) releases/latest: 3xx with /releases/tag/<t> gives the tag (percent-unescaped; '/' and '+' kept). 3xx to …/releases is no_compatible_release with fix '--channel beta'. **A 3xx to another …/releases/latest (a renamed repo) is followed, up to 3 times, and downloads use the new owner/repo.** 404 is not_found with fix `omaddons install git:https://github.com/o/r`. Any other non-3xx is http_status. **Real-world fact: Questie's latest tag is bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6.** Location carries it raw; the atom link percent-encodes it as bundle%2Fwago%2F…. Download URLs encode each '/'-separated segment (+ → %2B) and keep the slashes; GitHub accepts the raw, fully-encoded and segment-encoded forms.
(4) release.json: a 404 counts as missing. An unusable manifest (not JSON, no releases array, or no entry with a safe filename) goes through the same seam, with the reason carried in the message ('has an unusable release.json (…)'). There is no logging facility, so the reason travels in the error, which is what the user sees when the seam is empty. **Entries whose filename contains '/', '\\', a control character, or is '.'/'..' are skipped** (defense against a hostile manifest). The interface accepts a number or numeric string. The release version is the first entry's version, else the tag. changelog_url is the release page.
(5) Seam: `github::GithubRestFallback { fn fetch(&self, &Wanted, &RestReason, &dyn Http) -> Result<ReleaseSet> }`, `RestReason::{NoReleaseJson { tag, why: Option<String> }, Prerelease}`, `GithubSource { rest: Option<Box<dyn …>> }`. Without a seam: Prerelease is no_compatible_release with fix '--channel stable'. NoReleaseJson is no_compatible_release with fix display 'download a release zip, then: omaddons install <path>' (argv null) and alternative `omaddons install git:https://github.com/o/r` (with #<tag> when the version was pinned).
(6) `sources::SourceRegistry::builtin()` registers GithubSource; later source beads add theirs there.
(7) recent_tags is a conditional GET (purpose releases-atom). It takes the tag from the entry link (percent-unescaped), else the title. revalidated=true when the Validating layer answered from a 304.
(8) **Fixtures:** recorded 2026-10-14 by the ignored test `record_github_stable` (`OMADDONS_RECORD=1 cargo test --test sources_github -- --ignored record`; delete the directory first). It holds 6 repos × (latest 302, release.json 302, asset-host 200), 164 KB, with no asset zips: the engine downloads assets, and zip structure is archive-inspect's synthetic job. **Questie's release.json was hand-trimmed** to one changelog entry per block, with the author set to 'contributor' and content-length adjusted, to keep third-party contributor names out of the repo. Its extra keys (questie, questiedb) stay, so the tolerance is still exercised. The atom-decoder test uses a synthetic feed with GitHub's 2026-10 shape and placeholder authors; the real feed is covered by the live probe.
(9) **Bug found in 5.3 record mode and fixed here:** RecordTransport returned the secret-stripped Location upward, so the live redirect lost its jwt and the asset CDN answered '618 jwt-not-provided' (intermittently: 3 of 6 failed). It now stores stripped headers but returns the originals. Covered by the record unit test.
(10) ubs's JWT rule matches any `decode(`, so the decoder entry point is `release_json::parse` and the percent helper is `github::percent_unescape`.

title: local and url sources
description:
## Background

Some addons are not published anywhere omaddons can track: a zip someone sent, a folder the user unpacked, a private server's addon pack, or a direct https download. The vision (§5.4, §4.2) names `file:` and `url:` sources for these, and for legacy clients they are often the only option, since "no `release.json` flavor and no WoWInterface compatibility tag covers legacy clients". M1 needs both so that every target can receive an addon even when no registry knows it. They also give the engine tests (engine-tests) a network-free way to drive installs.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/sources/local.rs` (`LocalSource`, `SourceId::Local`) and `src/sources/url.rs` (`UrlSource`, `SourceId::Url`). Both implement the `Source` trait from the refs bead and are registered in the M1 `SourceRegistry`.

**`file:<path>` (LocalSource).**
- The path is absolute (the refs bead resolved it). Cases:
  - **zip file**: a regular file whose first four bytes are `PK\x03\x04` (an empty archive `PK\x05\x06` is rejected later by inspection);
  - **directory**: a directory holding one or more addon folders, or one that is itself an addon folder.
  - Anything else (missing, a device, a non-zip file) → `not_found` (3) or `bad_archive` (1), with a message naming the path.
- Decided: directories are read through the `FolderView` trait directly and never re-zipped (DEC-14, plan decision), so no copy of the user's working tree is made before staging.
- The source emits a `ReleaseSet` with exactly one stable `Release`:
  - `release_id = "file:" + sha256` of the zip bytes, or a hash of the sorted `(relative path, size, mtime_ns)` listing for a directory, so an unchanged input re-plans as "already current";
  - `version: None` with `version_confidence: toc`. The engine fills the version from the loaded TOC's `## Version` after inspection.
  - One `Asset` whose location is `LocalZip(path)` or `LocalDir(path)`, with no flavor metadata and no expected hash.
- `fetch` performs no network I/O and writes nothing.

**`url:<https-url>` (UrlSource).**
- Decided: url: hosts must be on the hard allowlist (vision §5.7: only git hosts are user-configurable), so a non-allowlisted host fails with `host_blocked` (exit 4). The fix has display `download the file in a browser, then: omaddons install <path>` and `argv: null`, because the user must act outside the CLI.
- `fetch` does not download the archive; the engine downloads assets into the blob cache. It validates the URL against the allowlist (net-core's `Allowlist::permits`) so the error appears at plan time, and emits:
  - one stable `Release` with `release_id = "url:" + url` (the URL is the identity; content changes are detected by the blob hash at download time);
  - `version: None` (`version_confidence: toc`);
  - one `Asset { name: <last path segment>, location: Url(url), flavors: [], nolib: false, expected_hash: None }`.
- With `--offline`, a `url:` ref whose blob is not already cached fails with `offline` when the engine downloads it. `fetch` itself needs no network.

**Asset shape.** If the model bead's `Asset` lacks a location enum that distinguishes `Url`, `LocalZip` and `LocalDir`, this bead adds it (`AssetLocation`). The engine (blob-cache, plan, archive-inspect) consumes it:
- `Url` → download into the blob cache;
- `LocalZip` → hash the file and open it in place, with no copy into the blob cache. Decided: user files are not duplicated into the cache, because the user owns them; undo uses snapshots;
- `LocalDir` → inspect through `FolderView`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `LocalSource::fetch` turns an existing zip into one stable release with an `LocalZip` asset and a content-derived `release_id`, and turns an existing directory into a `LocalDir` asset with a listing-derived `release_id`. In both cases it performs no network I/O and no writes.
- A missing path gives `not_found` (3). A non-zip regular file gives `bad_archive` (1).
- `UrlSource::fetch` turns an allowlisted https URL into one stable release with a `Url` asset and does not download it.
- A non-allowlisted host gives `host_blocked` (4) with the documented fix display and `argv: null`.
- Both sources leave the version empty with `version_confidence: toc`.
- Fetching the same unchanged zip or directory twice yields the same `release_id`; changing one file changes it.
- Both sources are registered in the M1 `SourceRegistry`.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - zip detection by magic bytes (zip, empty file, text file, directory);
  - `release_id` stability across two fetches of the same tempdir tree, and change after touching a file's content;
  - allowlist check for `url:` with `github.com` (ok), `objects.githubusercontent.com` (ok) and `example.org` (`host_blocked`).
- Integration (`tests/common/archives.rs` builds zips, DEC-8): `fetch_once` with a `file:` zip, a `file:` directory and a `url:` GitHub asset URL returns three release sets, and the fake `Http` records zero requests.
- E2E coverage comes from engine-tests, which install through `file:` sources only.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (path, detected kind, release id).

## Considerations

- A directory input can change between planning and staging, because the user may be editing it. The engine's revalidation step re-checks generations, not user input. Staging reads the directory once and hashes what it copies, so the per-file index matches what was installed.
- Symlinks inside a `file:` directory are rejected by inspection exactly like symlink entries in a zip (archive-inspect). This bead does not special-case them.
- Large local zips are opened in place, not copied, so `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` does not apply to them. `ARCHIVE_MAX_*` limits still apply during inspection.
- `install <ref> --file <zip>`, installing a manually downloaded archive as another ref's release, is the install command's job (cmd-install). It reuses `LocalSource`'s zip handling.
- Out of scope: downloading (blob-cache), inspecting (archive-inspect), and hash verification of source-provided hashes. Neither source provides hashes.
acceptance_criteria: LocalSource::fetch turns an existing zip into one stable release with a LocalZip asset and a content-derived release_id, and a directory into a LocalDir asset with a listing-derived release_id, with no network or writes; a missing path gives not_found (3) and a non-zip file gives bad_archive (1); UrlSource::fetch turns an allowlisted https URL into one stable release with a Url asset without downloading it; a non-allowlisted host gives host_blocked (4) with the documented fix display and argv null; both leave version empty with version_confidence toc; unchanged inputs keep the same release_id and a changed file changes it; both sources are registered in the M1 SourceRegistry
close_reason: file: zips and directories and url: https downloads are sources: content-derived release ids, no network or writes at fetch, hard-allowlist refusal for url hosts, versions read from the TOC at planning

Parallelize inside fetch with `net::run_bounded(refs, MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS, …)`; the Http stack enforces per-host caps.

**Implementation decisions (src/sources/{local,url}.rs, TOC versions in src/engine/plan.rs).**
(1) **Version:** Release.version is a String in the model, so 'no version' is the empty string. **Planning fills it** from the addon's own folder TOC (the folder named like the addon, else the first, through loaded_toc with the target's rules) as `## Version`, with version_confidence Toc, or 'unknown' when none. Tested: a file: directory with ## Version 2.5.1 records version 2.5.1, confidence toc, name MyAddon.
(2) Release ids follow the --file convention: `<ref>@sha256:<zip hash>` for zips, `<ref>@listing:<hash>` for directories (sorted path\0size\0mtime_ns lines, .git skipped as inspection does). url: refs use the ref itself as the id.
(3) Zip detection is by magic: PK\x03\x04, or PK\x05\x06 for an empty archive, which inspection then rejects. A missing path gives not_found (exit 3); a regular file that is not a zip, or a device, gives bad_archive (exit 1, reason not_a_zip).
(4) **UrlSource uses the hard allowlist** (`Allowlist::new(false, false, &[])`: no CurseForge, no Wago, no user git hosts), with userinfo and port stripped and the host lowercased. A blocked host gives host_blocked (exit 4) with details.host and the fix text 'download the file in a browser, then: omaddons install <path>' (argv null). The asset filename is the last path segment without query or fragment.
(5) Both are registered in SourceRegistry::builtin() beside GitHub. Neither does network I/O nor writes: fetch_once over a zip, a directory and a url: asset makes zero requests (tests/plan.rs).

title: Http trait, ureq client, per-hop host allowlist, offline mode and net.log
description:
## Background

Every network request omaddons makes must go through one HTTP client, so the privacy promise can be checked rather than taken on trust (vision goal G5, decisions D9 and D13). This bead builds that client and the guard around it: an `Http` trait, a ureq 3 implementation on rustls with the ring provider, a hard host allowlist checked on every request and on every redirect hop, https only, an offline switch, size and time limits, and a local `net.log` that records every request with credentials and query secrets stripped.

The reference project passed API URLs around unchecked (vision §3, R11) and had no request log. Here a request to a host outside the allowlist fails with `host_blocked` before any bytes reach that host, and the user can read every request omaddons ever made with `omaddons net-log` (that command lands in cmd-info-netlog).

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/net/mod.rs` (trait, request/response types, stack constructor), `src/net/client.rs` (ureq transport), `src/net/guard.rs` (allowlist, https, offline, size cap, logging layer), `src/net/allowlist.rs`, `src/net/log.rs` (net.log writer and reader).

**Types.**
- `trait Http: Send + Sync { fn send(&self, req: Request) -> Result<Response>; }` (`Result` is `crate::error::Result`).
- `Request { method: Method, url: String, headers: Vec<(String, String)>, purpose: Purpose, timeout: TimeoutKind /* Api | Download */, redirect: RedirectMode /* Follow | Manual */, validators: bool }`. `purpose` is a short static label written to net.log (`"release-latest"`, `"release-json"`, `"asset"`, `"commits-atom"`, `"rest-releases"`, `"download"`, …). `validators` is consumed by net-resilience; net-core ignores it.
- `Response { status: u16, headers: Vec<(String, String)>, final_url: String, body: Body }` with `Body` readable either fully into bytes (API calls) or as a streaming reader (`Response::into_reader()` for downloads, DEC-11). Helpers: `header(name)` (case-insensitive), `location()`, `error_for_status(context) -> Result<Response>` mapping non-success statuses to `http_status` (exit 1; retryable only for 5xx).
- Layering, outermost first: `Redirecting<Guarded<T>>` where `T` is a transport (`UreqTransport` here; `ReplayTransport`/`RecordTransport` come from net-fixtures). net-resilience wraps this stack further. `net::stack(&NetConfig) -> Box<dyn Http>` builds it; it exposes a hook for net-fixtures to swap the transport in debug builds (DEC-7).

**Guard layer (`Guarded`).** Every request that reaches the wire passes through it, including each redirect hop:
1. If offline (`NetConfig.offline`, set from `--offline` or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`), fail immediately with `offline` (exit 1, not retryable). Nothing is logged because nothing was sent.
2. Parse the URL. Scheme must be `https`; anything else is `host_blocked`.
3. Host must be on the allowlist (exact, case-insensitive host match; no implicit subdomains). Otherwise `host_blocked` (exit 4, not retryable). `details` names the host, and the message says whether it was the first request or a redirect hop.
4. Send through the transport, measure duration, and write one net.log line. Downloads log when the body is fully read or dropped (a counting reader), so `bytes` is the real byte count.
5. Enforce `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB): reject up front on a larger `Content-Length`, and abort the counting reader when the stream passes the cap. Both fail with `archive_too_large` (exit 4).

**Allowlist (vision §5.7).**
- Always: `api.github.com`, `github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, `api.mmoui.com`, `cdn.wowinterface.com`, `api.tukui.org`.
- Only when the CurseForge source is enabled: `api.curseforge.com`, `edge.forgecdn.net`, `mediafilez.forgecdn.net`. Only when Wago is enabled: `addons.wago.io`. Neither is ever enabled in M1, but `NetConfig` carries the flags so M5 adds no new mechanism.
- Plus the git hosts the user configures (`NetConfig.git_hosts`). Those hosts are allowed for git subprocesses (source-git-hosts), which use the same allowlist check through `Allowlist::permits(host)`.
- `NetConfig` is built by the command layer from config and flags. net-core does not read `config.toml` itself.

**Redirects (`Redirecting`).** ureq is configured with zero redirects (`max_redirects(0)`) and `http_status_as_error(false)`. With `RedirectMode::Manual` the 3xx response is returned as is: the GitHub source reads the tag from `releases/latest`'s `Location`. With `Follow`, 301/302/303/307/308 are followed up to `MAX_REDIRECTS` hops. Each hop is a fresh request through `Guarded`, so it is allowlist-checked and logged. A relative `Location` resolves against the current URL. Exceeding the hop limit gives `network` (retryable: false). Decided: add `MAX_REDIRECTS = 5` to `src/politeness.rs` (no other place may hold it). Recording the new constant on the vision bead is part of this bead's close-out, because §5.13 requires every politeness value to appear there.

**Transport (`UreqTransport`).** One `ureq::Agent` built once per process:
- user agent `USER_AGENT` (`omaddons/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>`);
- `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` 10 s;
- a whole-call timeout of `API_READ_TIMEOUT` (30 s) for `TimeoutKind::Api` and `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` (300 s) for `Download`;
- rustls with the ring provider (the crate's `rustls` feature) and webpki roots;
- no proxy. Decided: proxies are not supported in M1, because the vision does not call for them and CurseForge's terms forbid proxy access.

Transport errors map to `network` (exit 1, retryable): DNS, connect, TLS, timeout, reset.

**net.log (`src/net/log.rs`).** Path `<state>/omaddons/net.log`. Each request appends one JSON line through an fsx untracked session (`Op::AppendFile`, DEC-10), in this field order: `{"time": RFC 3339 UTC, "method", "host", "path", "status": u16|null, "bytes": u64|null, "duration_ms", "purpose", "via": "http"|"git", "error": code|null}`.
- Decided: the query string is never logged, only the path. This strips tokens, `api-key`/`key`/`access_token` parameters and the signed parameters on GitHub release-asset redirect URLs in one rule.
- Request headers are never logged, so `Authorization` and `x-api-key` cannot leak.
- `status` is null and `error` holds the error code when no response arrived.
- Rotation: before appending, if the file is larger than `NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (10 MiB), rename it to `net.log.1` with `Op::Rename{mode: Replace}`, keeping exactly one previous file.
- `NetLog::record_git(GitLogEntry)` lets source-git-hosts log subprocesses: `via: "git"`, `method: "GIT"`, `status` = exit code, `purpose` = `"ls-remote"`/`"clone"`/`"fetch"`.
- A reader `NetLog::read(since: Option<Timestamp>) -> Vec<NetLogEntry>` covers `net.log.1` and `net.log` in order and skips a torn last line. It serves `net-log` and the test helpers.

**Credentials.** Never placed in a child process's argv and never logged. Headers carrying credentials are set by the caller (source-github-rest adds `Authorization` for `api.github.com` only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Http` trait, `Request`/`Response`, `Guarded`, `Redirecting`, `UreqTransport` and `net::stack()` exist in `src/net/`. ureq runs on rustls with ring and no redirects of its own.
- Requests to a non-allowlisted host fail with `host_blocked` (exit 4) before any connection to that host. A redirect hop to a non-allowlisted host fails the same way, and the hops before it are logged.
- Non-https URLs fail with `host_blocked`.
- With offline set, every request fails with `offline` (exit 1) and net.log is unchanged.
- Every request that reaches the transport produces exactly one net.log line with the documented fields. The query string and all request headers are absent from the line.
- Downloads larger than `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` fail with `archive_too_large`, whether announced by Content-Length or discovered while streaming.
- `MAX_REDIRECTS` exists only in `src/politeness.rs`, and `Follow` stops after that many hops.
- net.log rotates to `net.log.1` above `NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, keeping one previous file.
- `NetLog::record_git` and `NetLog::read` exist, and the reader tolerates a torn last line.
- All writes go through fsx; the single-writer test stays green.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - allowlist matching: case-insensitive; `evil-github.com` and `github.com.evil` rejected; CF/Wago hosts rejected unless their flags are set; configured git hosts accepted.
  - Redirect resolution of relative and absolute `Location`.
  - Hop counting.
  - net.log line serialization: field order; query stripped from `/x?token=abc&sig=def`; no header text present.
  - Rotation threshold.
  - Reader skips a torn last line.
- Integration (a scripted in-process fake transport that returns canned responses; no network):
  - 302 from github.com to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` is followed and both hops are logged.
  - 302 to `example.org` yields `host_blocked`, with one logged hop.
  - Offline yields `offline` with zero lines.
  - The size cap applies via Content-Length and via a streaming body.
  - Manual mode returns the 302 with its `Location`.
- Live (`#[ignore]`, `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`): one GET to `https://github.com/` succeeds through `UreqTransport` and is logged. This proves rustls/ring works on the machine.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (request URL, response status, the net.log line).

## Considerations

- Concurrent processes append to the same net.log. Each line is a single `write` on an `O_APPEND` descriptor, so lines do not interleave on local filesystems. Rotation is best-effort, and a process still holding the old descriptor writes into `net.log.1`; that is acceptable because no line is lost.
- Host matching is exact. If GitHub moves release assets to a new host, downloads fail with `host_blocked` until the allowlist is updated. That is the intended trade-off.
- Retries, validators and the concurrency limits are net-resilience. Fixture replay, record mode and the live-probe harness are net-fixtures. This bead only provides the transport-swap hook.
- `api.mmoui.com`, `cdn.wowinterface.com` and `api.tukui.org` are on the always-list now, but no M1 source contacts them.
- Adding `MAX_REDIRECTS` changes the §5.13 politeness table. Post the updated row as a comment on omad-vision-8qa when closing this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Http trait, Request/Response, Guarded, Redirecting, UreqTransport and net::stack() exist in src/net/ with ureq on rustls+ring and no internal redirects; requests and redirect hops to non-allowlisted hosts fail with host_blocked (exit 4) before connecting, earlier hops logged; non-https URLs fail with host_blocked; offline makes every request fail with offline (exit 1) and leaves net.log unchanged; every wire request writes exactly one net.log line with the documented fields and no query string or headers; downloads over DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES fail with archive_too_large via Content-Length or streaming; MAX_REDIRECTS lives only in src/politeness.rs and Follow stops at it; net.log rotates to net.log.1 above NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES keeping one previous; NetLog::record_git and NetLog::read exist and the reader tolerates a torn last line; all writes go through fsx and the single-writer test stays green
close_reason: src/net provides the Http trait, Request/Response, the Guarded layer (offline, https+allowlist per hop, size cap, one net.log line per wire request), the Redirecting layer (MAX_REDIRECTS, credential stripping across hosts), UreqTransport on rustls+ring with no redirects or proxy, net::stack/stack_with, and NetLog with rotation, record_git and a torn-line-tolerant reader

comments.text: **error-registry landed (src/error.rs).** Error constructors for the net layer: `Error::http_status(status, msg, fix)` (retryable for 5xx, details.status), `Error::rate_limited(reset_at: jiff::Timestamp, msg, fix)` (details.reset_at RFC 3339), and `Error::new(ErrorCode::{Network, HostBlocked, Offline, DownloadFailed}, msg, fix)` (default retryability from the registry). There is no From<io::Error>; I/O failures use `Error::io(path, &err, fix)`.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: claim: src/net/{mod,client,guard,allowlist,log}.rs, src/fsx/scope.rs (net.log ancestors creatable by every writer).

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/net/{mod,client,guard,allowlist,log,tests}.rs).** (1) Security beyond the bead text: `Redirecting` drops Authorization and x-api-key when a hop leaves the original host, and the guard refuses URLs with userinfo or a non-443 port (host_blocked). (2) A blocked or offline request writes no net.log line, because nothing was sent. Every request that reaches the transport writes exactly one line: on transport error (status null), when the body hits EOF, on a body read error, at the size cap, or when the response is dropped unread (best effort). (3) If writing the line fails inside a body read, the io::Error carries the crate Error and `net::body_error` recovers it, so it is not misreported as network. (4) Writes go through fsx: an untracked `Writer::Derived` session with `ensure_dir_all` and AppendFile. TLS is rustls+ring via the crate feature. (6) Methods are GET and HEAD in M1; POST arrives with CurseForge (M5). Error messages redact URLs to scheme://host/path. (8) The live probe (`OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test -- --ignored live_github_request`) ran once on this machine and passed: rustls/ring reached github.com, and the request went through the allowlist and was logged. title: HTTP fixture replay, record mode and live-probe harness
description:
## Background

Tests must never touch the network (vision §5.12 testing strategy), yet the sources have to be exercised against real upstream responses: GitHub's 302 `Location` headers, atom feeds with ETags, `release.json` files with their real quirks, and zip downloads. This bead provides three pieces:

- A **replay** transport that serves recorded responses.
- A **record** mode that captures real responses into fixture files with credentials and query secrets stripped.
- A **live-probe** harness, run only at milestone checkpoints, that hits each keyless endpoint once.

It also provides the test helpers that read `net.log`, so tests can assert facts such as "zero GitHub REST requests" (vision M1 checkpoint).

All three hooks are debug-only (DEC-7): compiled in, active only when `cfg!(debug_assertions)`, and ignored by release builds.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/net/replay.rs`, `src/net/record.rs`, the selection hook in `net::stack()` (`src/net/mod.rs`), `tests/common/netlog.rs`, and `tests/live_probes.rs`.

**Transport selection (DEC-7).** `net::stack()` picks the bottom transport through `select_transport(env, debug: bool)`:
- `debug && OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=<dir> && OMADDONS_RECORD != "1"` → `ReplayTransport::load(dir)`.
- `debug && OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=<dir> && OMADDONS_RECORD == "1"` → `RecordTransport::new(dir, UreqTransport)`.
- Otherwise, including every release build → `UreqTransport`.

The transport always sits under net-core's `Guarded` layer. Replayed and recorded runs therefore still enforce the allowlist and https-only rule, honor offline mode, and write normal `net.log` lines. This is what lets fixture tests assert REST counts from `net.log`.

**Fixture layout.** `tests/fixtures/http/<scenario>/<host>/<method>-<path-slug>-<hash8>.json`, plus an optional sibling `.body` file. `<hash8>` is the first 8 hex digits of the sha256 of the normalized request key. File shape:

```json
{"schema_version":"1.0",
 "request":{"method":"GET","url":"https://github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/releases/latest"},
 "responses":[{"status":302,"headers":[["location","https://github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/releases/tag/5.19.0"]],"body_file":null}]}
```

The tag value above is illustrative, not a fact. `responses` is consumed in order and the last entry repeats, which lets one scenario express "first 200 with ETag, then 304". Header names are stored lowercase. A scenario is a directory, and one test points `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` at one scenario.

**Request normalization (shared by record and replay).** The key is `METHOD scheme://host/path?query`, where:
- secret query parameters are removed: `token`, `api-key`, `api_key`, `key`, `access_token`, `jwt`, `sig`, `signature`, `se`, `sp`, `sv`, `sr`, `skoid`, `sktid`, `skt`, `ske`, `sks`, `skv`, `hmac`, and every `X-Amz-*` parameter;
- the remaining parameters are sorted.

Record applies the same stripping to every stored URL and to stored `location` headers. A replayed redirect therefore points at the normalized URL, which replay can then match.

**ReplayTransport.**
- Loads every `*.json` in the scenario directory tree at construction. Two files with the same key are a load error.
- `send` normalizes the request and serves the next response for its key, with the body streamed from the `.body` file when present.
- An unmatched request returns `internal` with the message `replay: no fixture for <METHOD> <normalized url>` (DEC-5 fix). A distinct code prevents an error-path test from passing by accident.
- `ReplayTransport::unmatched()` returns the misses for in-process tests.
- Never opens a socket.

**RecordTransport.**
- Wraps `UreqTransport` and forwards every request.
- Writes or overwrites the fixture for the normalized key, with the response body saved verbatim to `.body`.
- Never writes request headers, so `Authorization` and `x-api-key` cannot reach a fixture.
- Strips `set-cookie` from stored response headers.
- Writes go through fsx. Decided: in debug builds only, while `OMADDONS_RECORD=1`, the fsx write-scope table gains one entry, "the directory named by `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`", writable by `RecordTransport` alone. This bead adds that row to the scope table built by fsx-mutate. It keeps record mode inside the single-writer rule instead of letting `src/net/` call `std::fs`.

**net.log helpers (`tests/common/netlog.rs`, DEC-8).**
- `read_net_log(state_dir) -> Vec<NetLogEntry>` (wraps `omaddons::net::log::NetLog::read`).
- `count_host(&entries, host)`.
- `assert_no_github_rest(&entries)`: fails, listing the offending lines, if any entry has host `api.github.com`.
- `assert_each_url_once(&entries)`, which feeds the fetch-once checks.

**Live probes (`tests/live_probes.rs`).**
- Every test is `#[ignore]` and also returns early unless `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`.
- One request per keyless M1 endpoint, against `gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2` (the vision's example ref):
  1. `https://github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/releases/latest` returns 302 with a `Location` containing `/releases/tag/`.
  2. `releases.atom` returns 200 with an `ETag`. A conditional re-request returns 304.
  3. `releases/download/<tag>/release.json` redirects to an allowlisted host and decodes as JSON with a `releases` array.
  4. `commits/<default branch>.atom` returns 200 atom.
  5. `https://codeload.github.com/WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/zip/<sha>` returns 200 with a zip signature (`PK\x03\x04`).
- These probes check raw shape only. Each source bead adds its own decoder-level probe to this file (source-github-stable decodes `release.json`, source-git-github decodes commits atom), because the decoders live in those beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In debug builds, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` selects replay, and adding `OMADDONS_RECORD=1` selects record. `select_transport` ignores both when `debug == false` (unit-tested).
- Replay serves recorded status, headers and body for a normalized request key, consumes `responses` in order with the last repeating, never opens a socket, and returns `internal` naming the URL for an unmatched request.
- Record writes fixtures in the documented layout with secret query parameters stripped from URLs and `location` headers, never stores request headers, and drops `set-cookie`.
- Record writes go through fsx under the debug-only fixture scope, and the single-writer test stays green.
- Replayed requests still pass through `Guarded`: allowlist enforced, offline honored, `net.log` lines written.
- `tests/common/netlog.rs` provides `read_net_log`, `count_host`, `assert_no_github_rest` and `assert_each_url_once`.
- `tests/live_probes.rs` exists with the five probes. They are skipped unless run with `--ignored` and `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`, and they pass against live GitHub at the checkpoint.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - normalization strips each secret parameter, sorts the rest, and is idempotent;
  - fixture JSON round trip;
  - duplicate keys rejected at load;
  - `responses` sequencing;
  - `select_transport` truth table, including `debug=false`.
- Integration:
  - a scenario with a 302 chain (github.com → release-assets) replays through the full `net::stack()`, and `net.log` shows both hops;
  - a scenario hop to a non-allowlisted host still yields `host_blocked`;
  - an unmatched request yields `internal` with the URL;
  - record mode against a fake inner transport (not ureq) writes the expected files into a tempdir scenario, with `token=` and `X-Amz-Signature=` stripped and no request headers.
- Live (`#[ignore]`, `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`): the five probes above.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (normalized key, the fixture path looked up).

## Considerations

- Record runs real commands against the network. Use it only with throwaway `HOME`/`XDG_*` directories (DEC-6), and review the diff of `tests/fixtures/http/` before committing: fixtures are tracked and may become public. They must contain no tokens, cookies or personal data.
- Fixture bodies for large zips bloat the repository. Prefer the smallest real release that exercises a case, or build synthetic zips in `tests/common/archives.rs` (archive-inspect) for structural cases.
- Signed asset URLs change on every request. Stripping their query makes replay deterministic, at the cost of the fixtures no longer holding the exact signed URL. That is intended.
- Fixture files under `tests/fixtures/**` count as code changes for the local gate (D16).
- Out of scope: source-specific fixtures (recorded by each source bead), and the decoder-level live probes (added by the source beads).
acceptance_criteria: In debug builds OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES selects replay and OMADDONS_RECORD=1 selects record, and select_transport ignores both when debug is false; replay serves recorded status, headers and body for a normalized request key, sequences responses with the last repeating, never opens a socket, and returns internal naming the URL for unmatched requests; record writes fixtures in the documented layout with secret query parameters stripped from URLs and location headers, never stores request headers and drops set-cookie; record writes go through fsx under the debug-only fixture scope and the single-writer test stays green; replayed requests still pass through Guarded (allowlist, offline, net.log); tests/common/netlog.rs provides read_net_log, count_host, assert_no_github_rest and assert_each_url_once; tests/live_probes.rs holds the five probes, skipped unless --ignored with OMADDONS_LIVE=1, and they pass live at the checkpoint
close_reason: Debug builds replay recorded HTTP fixtures (or record new ones with secrets stripped, through fsx) underneath the full guarded stack, tests have net.log assertion helpers, and live probes of the five keyless GitHub endpoints exist and pass

title: Retry with backoff, HTTP validators cache and bounded parallelism
description:
## Background

Upstream hosts throttle, time out and fail. omaddons has to be polite to them (vision §5.13, D22) and dependable for the user: retry transient failures with backoff, honor `Retry-After`, avoid re-downloading unchanged feeds through ETag/Last-Modified validators, and cap concurrency both globally and per host. github.com's web endpoints, which the GitHub source relies on for its no-REST path, have undocumented secondary limits, and `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST` exists partly to stay under them (vision §8).

This bead adds three `Http` decorators on top of net-core's stack, plus a bounded worker helper that sources use to fetch many refs in parallel.

Placeholders: `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/net/retry.rs`, `src/net/validators.rs`, `src/net/limit.rs`, `src/net/pool.rs`. The decorators wrap net-core's stack in this order (outermost first): `Limited<Retrying<Validating<Redirecting<Guarded<Transport>>>>>`. `net::stack()` (net-core) gains the three layers here.

**Constants used (all from `src/politeness.rs`, never literals):**

| Constant | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` | 6 | global in-flight request cap and worker-pool size |
| `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST` | 3 | per-host in-flight cap |
| `MAX_RETRIES` | 3 | retries after the first attempt, idempotent GET/HEAD only |
| `BACKOFF_BASE` / `BACKOFF_MAX` | 500 ms / 8 s | exponential ×2 with full jitter |
| `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` | 60 s | a longer `Retry-After` fails with `rate_limited` and the reset time |

**Retrying.**
- Only `GET` and `HEAD` are retried. Retryable outcomes:
  - HTTP 429;
  - any 5xx;
  - transport `network` errors (timeout, connection reset, connect failure).
- Delay before retry *n* (n = 0, 1, 2) is `random(0, min(BACKOFF_MAX, BACKOFF_BASE × 2^n))` (full jitter).
- If the response carries `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP-date, parsed with `jiff`):
  - a value ≤ `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` replaces the computed delay;
  - a longer value fails at once with `rate_limited` (exit 1, retryable). `details.reset_at` holds an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- Primary rate limits: a 403 or 429 carrying `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` fails at once with `rate_limited`. `reset_at` comes from `X-RateLimit-Reset` (epoch seconds). These responses are never retried.
- When retries are exhausted, the last outcome maps to its error:
  - 429 → `rate_limited`;
  - 5xx → `http_status` (retryable: true);
  - transport → `network` (retryable: true).
- Each attempt is a separate wire request, so each appears as its own net.log line (net-core logs them).
- Only failures that happen before the response is handed to the caller are retried. A body-read failure on a streamed download surfaces as `download_failed` (exit 1, retryable); the downloader (E6 blob-cache) may retry the whole download once.
- Randomness: a small inline xorshift64* generator seeded from the system time and pid. Decided: no new crate, because jitter needs no cryptographic quality.
- `Sleeper`, `Rng` and `Clock` are injectable traits, so tests run instantly and deterministically.

**Validating (ETag / Last-Modified).**
- Only requests with `Request.validators == true` take part: atom feeds and, later, the WoWI file list and REST release lists. Downloads never do.
- Cache directory: `<cache>/omaddons/http/`, two files per URL keyed by the sha256 of the full URL:
  - `<sha>.json` = `{"schema_version": "1.0", "url", "etag": str|null, "last_modified": str|null, "status": 200, "headers": [[k, v], …], "stored_at"}`;
  - `<sha>.body`.
- Before sending, add `If-None-Match` and/or `If-Modified-Since` when cached values exist.
- On `304`, return the cached response (status 200 and the cached body) with `Response.cache = CacheState::Revalidated`.
- On `200` with an `ETag` or `Last-Modified`, store body and metadata.
- Writes go through an fsx untracked session (DEC-10). The cache is derived data and safe to delete. A corrupt or missing cache entry means "no validators", never an error.
- net.log records the real 304, so revalidations are visible.

**Limited (concurrency).**
- A global counting semaphore of `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` permits plus one semaphore per host of `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST`, built from `Mutex` + `Condvar`.
- A permit is held for the duration of `send` and, for streamed downloads, until the body reader is dropped.
- The host comes from the request URL. Redirect hops run inside the same permit, because redirects are followed below this layer.

**Pool (`run_bounded`).** `pub fn run_bounded<T, R>(items: Vec<T>, max_workers: usize, f: impl Fn(T) -> R + Sync) -> Vec<R>` uses `std::thread::scope` with at most `max_workers` threads pulling from a shared queue, and returns results in input order (determinism, DEC-3). Sources call it with `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`. The per-host cap is still enforced by `Limited`, so a pool of 6 hitting github.com never has more than 3 requests in flight there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Retrying` retries GET/HEAD on 429, 5xx and transport errors, up to `MAX_RETRIES` times, with full-jitter exponential delays between 0 and min(`BACKOFF_MAX`, `BACKOFF_BASE`×2^n). It never retries POST.
- `Retry-After` ≤ 60 s is honored as the delay. A longer value returns `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at` and no retry.
- A 403 or 429 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` returns `rate_limited` with `reset_at` from `X-RateLimit-Reset` and is not retried.
- Exhausted retries map to `rate_limited`, `http_status` (retryable) or `network` (retryable), as appropriate.
- `Validating` sends `If-None-Match`/`If-Modified-Since` for opted-in requests, turns a 304 into the cached 200 body with `CacheState::Revalidated`, stores validators under `<cache>/omaddons/http/` through fsx, and treats a corrupt cache entry as absent.
- `Limited` never has more than 6 requests in flight in total, or more than 3 to one host (asserted with a blocking fake transport and counters).
- `run_bounded` preserves input order and never runs more than `max_workers` closures at once.
- All delays use the injected `Sleeper`; no test sleeps in real time.
- Every value comes from `src/politeness.rs`.

## Test Plan

- Unit (fake transport plus a recording sleeper):
  - 500 → 500 → 200 succeeds on the third attempt with two recorded delays inside the jitter bounds;
  - four 503s → `http_status` retryable after exactly 4 attempts;
  - 429 with `Retry-After: 2` → one 2 s sleep, then success;
  - `Retry-After: 120` → immediate `rate_limited` with `reset_at` = now + 120 s (injected clock);
  - HTTP-date `Retry-After` parsing;
  - 403 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` → `rate_limited`, no retry;
  - POST never retried;
  - a transport timeout is retried.
- Validators:
  - first fetch stores the ETag;
  - second fetch sends `If-None-Match`, fake returns 304, caller sees the cached body and `Revalidated`;
  - `Last-Modified`-only path;
  - corrupt `<sha>.json` → plain GET;
  - downloads never send validators.
- Limits: a transport that blocks until released, 20 parallel requests to 2 hosts; assert max global in flight = 6 and max per host = 3.
- Pool: order preserved; concurrency bound respected (atomic counter high-water mark).
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (attempt count, delays, statuses).

## Considerations

- Body-read retries for large downloads are deliberately left to the downloader, because the layer cannot replay a half-consumed stream into the caller's writer.
- The validator cache is not size-capped in M1. Atom feeds are small, and the WoWI file list (about 5.6 MB) arrives in M2, which may add a cap. Deleting `<cache>/omaddons/http/` is always safe.
- GitHub REST conditional requests return free 304s only when authenticated (vision §4.5). Unauthenticated, a 304 still costs a request against the 60/hour budget. source-github-rest accounts for that.
- `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 min) applies to `outdated` and belongs to M2, not here.
- Out of scope: the fixture transports (net-fixtures) and the `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE` budget logic (source-github-rest).
acceptance_criteria: Retrying retries GET/HEAD on 429, 5xx and transport errors up to MAX_RETRIES with full-jitter exponential delays bounded by BACKOFF_BASE/BACKOFF_MAX and never retries POST; Retry-After <= 60 s is honored and longer values return rate_limited with details.reset_at without retrying; 403/429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 returns rate_limited with reset_at from X-RateLimit-Reset and is not retried; exhausted retries map to rate_limited, http_status (retryable) or network (retryable); Validating sends If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since for opted-in requests, maps 304 to the cached 200 body with CacheState::Revalidated, stores validators under <cache>/omaddons/http/ through fsx, and treats corrupt entries as absent; Limited never exceeds 6 in-flight requests globally or 3 per host; run_bounded preserves input order and bounds concurrency; all delays go through the injected Sleeper; every value comes from src/politeness.rs
close_reason: The net stack now retries transient failures with full-jitter backoff and Retry-After, fails fast on rate limits with the reset time, revalidates opted-in feeds with ETag/Last-Modified from an fsx-written cache, caps requests at 6 in flight overall and 3 per host, and offers run_bounded for ordered parallel fetches; all values from politeness.rs

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **net-core landed.** Wrap the `Box<dyn Http>` from `net::stack`/`stack_with` (outermost). `Request.validators` is carried but ignored by net-core. `Response.headers` is Vec<(String, String)> with case-insensitive `header(name)`. Retries must re-send a cloned Request (Request: Clone). Note that each attempt is a separate wire request and writes its own net.log line.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/net/{retry,validators,limit,pool}.rs; net::stack now takes &Paths).**
(1) `stack(config, log, paths)` / `stack_with(config, log, paths, transport)` build Limited<Retrying<Validating<Redirecting<Guarded<…>>>>>. The new `core_stack_with(config, log, transport)` is the old Redirecting<Guarded> core: net-core tests use it so scripted 5xx and transport errors are not retried with real sleeps.
(2) `Response.cache: CacheState { Network (default), Revalidated }` was added.
(3) net has only GET and HEAD (Method), so every request is idempotent and 'never retry POST' holds by construction.
(4) Retried: a response with 429 or 5xx, and Err with code `network`. Final at once: other errors (host_blocked, offline, archive_too_large), every other status (4xx is the caller's to judge), and primary limits (403/429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, reset from X-RateLimit-Reset epoch seconds, else now). The response is dropped before sleeping, so its net.log line is written.
(5) Retry-After: delta-seconds or an HTTP-date via jiff::fmt::rfc2822 (a past date means no delay). Above RETRY_AFTER_CAP it is rate_limited with reset = now + value. When attempts run out: 429 gives rate_limited (reset = now + Retry-After or now), 5xx gives http_status (retryable, after MAX_RETRIES+1 attempts), and a transport error returns the last network error.
(6) Backoff: uniform in 0..=min(BACKOFF_MAX, BACKOFF_BASE·2^attempt) ms from an inline xorshift64* (seeded with time ^ pid). Sleeper, Clock and Rng are public traits for injection (`Retrying::with`).
(7) Validators: only GETs with `req.validators`. Metadata is a Versioned 'http_validators' 1.0 JSON (url, etag, last_modified, status, headers, stored_at) plus a .body file, keyed by the sha256 of the URL under <cache>/omaddons/http. A stored entry must name the same URL and carry at least one validator. The body is written before the metadata. A 200 with validators is read fully (feeds are small) and returned from memory. Writes go through an untracked Writer::Derived session; any failure leaves the cache unchanged.
(8) Limited: per-host permit first, then global, so requests queued on a busy host never hold global slots. Permits ride in the response body (`Held`) until it drops; poisoned mutexes are recovered. Hosts come from `guard::parse_target`, lowercased.
(9) run_bounded(items, max_workers, f): scoped threads (max_workers clamped to 1..=len) pull from a queue, and results return in input order.
(10) Live probe re-run through the full stack: passes.
