Live probe passes through the full stack. ubs 0 critical · found: none

title: Ref parsing, the Source trait, ReleaseSet and the fetch-once orchestrator
description:
## Background

Users and agents name addons many ways: a canonical ref (`gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2`), a URL pasted from a browser, a git URL with a branch, a local zip, the name of an installed addon, or a catalog name such as `weakauras`. The vision (§5.4) requires all of these to work, and an ambiguous input to fail with the candidates rather than a guess. Every source also shares one contract. `fetch` does all the network work for a batch of refs. Selection and verification are pure and live elsewhere. A run fetches each distinct ref exactly once, however many targets want it (D28: "requests no longer multiply by target count").

This bead provides the user-facing ref parser, the `Source` trait, the source registry, and the fetch-once orchestrator. The model bead owns the canonical `Ref` type and its `source:id` round trip; this bead builds on it.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/sources/mod.rs` (trait, `SourceId`, registry, `fetch_once`), `src/sources/refs.rs` (user-input parsing).

**Canonical forms (owned by the model bead, restated here):** `gh:<owner>/<repo>`, `wowi:<id>`, `tukui:<slug>`, `cf:<id>`, `wago:<id>`, `git:<url>[#<rev>]`, `url:<https-url>`, `file:<path>`.

**Parsing, `parse_user_ref(input: &str, ctx: &RefContext) -> Result<ParsedRef>`.** `ParsedRef { r#ref: Ref, version_hint: Option<String>, asset_hint: Option<String>, matched_by: MatchKind }`, where `MatchKind` is one of `Canonical | Url | Path | Installed | Catalog | Shorthand`. Steps, in order:

1. **Canonical prefix** (`gh:`, `wowi:`, `tukui:`, `cf:`, `wago:`, `git:`, `url:`, `file:`): delegate to the model's `FromStr`, then validate:
   - `gh` owner/repo use GitHub's charset (`[A-Za-z0-9-]` for owner; `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` for repo, which is never `.` or `..`);
   - `wowi`/`cf` ids are numeric;
   - `tukui` slugs are `[a-z0-9-]+`;
   - `git:` URLs are https, with an optional `#rev` that may not be empty;
   - `url:` is https (no extension requirement; the engine verifies the content is a zip);
   - `file:` paths are made absolute against the current directory.

   Violations are `ref_invalid` (exit 2).
2. **https URL:**
   - `github.com/<o>/<r>` (with or without a trailing `/` or `.git`) → `gh:<o>/<r>`.
   - `…/releases/tag/<tag>` → `gh:<o>/<r>` with `version_hint = tag`.
   - `…/releases/download/<tag>/<file>` → `gh:<o>/<r>` with `version_hint = tag` and `asset_hint = file`.
   - `…/tree/<branch>` → `git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>#<branch>`.
   - `wowinterface.com/downloads/info<id>-<slug>.html` or `download<id>-…` → `wowi:<id>`.
   - `tukui.org` addon pages → `tukui:<slug>`.
   - `curseforge.com/wow/addons/<slug>` and `addons.wago.io/addons/<slug>` → fail at once with `source_disabled` (exit 1), saying CurseForge/Wago arrive in M5, with fix `omaddons help install`. Decided: these URLs carry a slug, not the id a `cf:`/`wago:` ref needs, so they cannot become a canonical ref. Failing at parse time gives the same observable result as DEC-12.
   - A URL whose host is a configured git host (`RefContext.git_hosts`), or whose path ends in `.git` → `git:<url>`.
   - Any other https URL → `url:<url>`.
   - `http://` URLs → `ref_invalid` with the https form as the fix.
3. **Local path** (starts with `/`, `./` or `../`, or names an existing file or directory): an existing `.zip` file or a directory → `file:<absolute path>`. A missing path that starts with `/`, `./` or `../` → `not_found` (exit 3).
4. **`<owner>/<repo>` shorthand** (exactly one `/`, both halves valid GitHub names):
   - → `gh:<owner>/<repo>`;
   - if a relative path of that name also exists on disk → `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3), with candidates `./<owner>/<repo>` and `gh:<owner>/<repo>`, each with an exact `omaddons install …` fix argv.
5. **Bare name:**
   - Look up installed addons via the injected `RefContext.installed(name) -> Vec<InstalledMatch { name, r#ref, target_id }>`. It is case-insensitive on record name and folder key and is fed from state records by the caller.
   - Look up the catalog via the injected `RefContext.catalog(name) -> Option<CatalogMatch { name, r#ref }>`. It is case-insensitive on name and aliases and is fed by the catalog bead.
   - If every match resolves to one ref, use it.
   - If matches resolve to different refs → `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3). `details.candidates` lists each canonical ref and where it came from, and `alternatives` carries one `omaddons install <canonical ref>` argv per candidate.
   - No match → `not_found` (exit 3), with fix `omaddons help install`.

Injected lookups keep this bead free of dependencies on state-records and catalog. The command layer wires them.

**Source trait (vision §5.4):**

```rust
pub trait Source: Send + Sync {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId;
    /// Network; batched; called once per run with every distinct ref of this source.
    fn fetch(&self, refs: &[Ref], http: &dyn Http) -> Vec<Result<ReleaseSet>>;
}
```

`SourceId` is one of `Github | Git | Url | Local | Wowi | Tukui | Curseforge | Wago`, with wire names `github, git, url, local, wowi, tukui, curseforge, wago`. Results are positional: result *i* belongs to `refs[i]`. Decided: `search` is left out of the M1 trait. M2's search bead adds it with a default implementation, so M1 sources carry no stub.

**Registry and fetch-once.**
- `SourceRegistry` maps `SourceId → Box<dyn Source>`. The M1 registry holds `local`, `url` and `github`; `git` is added when source-git-github lands. Refs whose source is not registered (`wowi`, `tukui`, `cf`, `wago`) yield `source_disabled` per ref (DEC-12). The message names the milestone (WoWI/Tukui: M2; CurseForge/Wago: M5), and the fix is `omaddons help install`.
- `fetch_once(refs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Ref>, registry: &SourceRegistry, http: &dyn Http) -> BTreeMap<Ref, Result<ReleaseSet>>`:
  1. deduplicate by canonical ref (`Ref: Ord`);
  2. group by `SourceId`;
  3. call each source's `fetch` exactly once with its group;
  4. run the groups concurrently with `net::pool::run_bounded` (net-resilience) capped at `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`.

  Sources that fetch many refs parallelize inside `fetch` with the same helper. The per-host limit is enforced in the `Http` stack.
- Errors are per ref, so one bad ref never fails the others. Partial success becomes `partial: true` in the command layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `parse_user_ref` handles every input class above, with the documented results and error codes: `ref_invalid` (2), `ref_ambiguous` (3), `not_found` (3), `source_disabled` (1).
- GitHub repo, release-tag, release-download and tree URLs map to the documented refs and hints. WoWI `info<id>-…` URLs map to `wowi:<id>`.
- CurseForge/Wago project URLs fail with `source_disabled`, naming M5.
- Every ambiguity error carries `details.candidates` and one executable `alternatives[].argv` per candidate.
- `Source` and `SourceId` exist as specified, with no `search` method.
- `fetch_once` calls each registered source's `fetch` exactly once per run with deduplicated refs, returns one result per distinct ref, and yields `source_disabled` for unregistered sources without touching the network.
- Per-ref failures do not affect other refs.
- No network or filesystem writes in the parser. Its only filesystem access is reading whether a path exists and what kind it is.

## Test Plan

- Unit, table-driven over about 60 inputs with expected `ParsedRef` or error code:
  - canonical forms of every source;
  - GitHub URLs with and without `www`, trailing slash, `.git`, `/releases/tag/v1.2`, `/releases/download/v1.2/Foo.zip`, `/tree/main`;
  - WoWI URLs;
  - CurseForge/Wago URLs;
  - `http://` URLs;
  - configured git host URLs;
  - arbitrary https zip URLs;
  - existing and missing local paths (tempdir);
  - `owner/repo` with and without a colliding local directory;
  - bare names hitting installed only, catalog only, both agreeing, both disagreeing, neither.
- Proptest: `parse_user_ref` never panics on arbitrary strings, and every canonical ref it returns round-trips through `Display`/`FromStr`.
- fetch-once:
  - a counting fake source receiving the same ref from three "targets" is called once with one ref;
  - two sources run concurrently (fake sources with barriers);
  - an unregistered `wowi:` ref yields `source_disabled` and the fake `Http` records zero requests;
  - one failing ref leaves the others `Ok`.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (input string, parsed result).

## Considerations

- The parser reads the filesystem to decide whether a path exists. That is the only side effect, and it never follows symlinks out of an explicit path the user gave.
- Version and asset hints from URLs are hints. The install command turns `version_hint` into the equivalent of `--version` and fails if it conflicts with an explicit `--version`.
- Branch names that look like versions (`#v2`) are handled by the git sources, not here. The parser only splits on the first `#`.
- Catalog and installed-name lookups are injected, so this bead can land before catalog and state-records. The fuzz bead (fuzz-targets) adds a fuzz target for `parse_user_ref`.
- Out of scope: the GitHub, git, url and local sources themselves; candidate selection (select); WoWI/Tukui fetching (M2).
- Dependency added beyond the plan: `net-resilience`, because `fetch_once` runs source groups through `net::pool::run_bounded`.
acceptance_criteria: parse_user_ref handles canonical refs, https URLs, local paths, owner/repo shorthand and bare names with the documented results and codes ref_invalid (2), ref_ambiguous (3), not_found (3), source_disabled (1); GitHub repo, release-tag, release-download and tree URLs map to the documented refs and hints and WoWI info<id> URLs map to wowi:<id>; CurseForge/Wago project URLs fail with source_disabled naming M5; ambiguity errors carry details.candidates and one executable alternatives[].argv per candidate; Source and SourceId exist without a search method; fetch_once calls each registered source's fetch exactly once per run with deduplicated refs, returns one result per distinct ref, and yields source_disabled for unregistered sources without network; per-ref failures do not affect other refs; the parser performs no network access or writes
close_reason: User refs parse from canonical forms, GitHub/WoWI/Tukui/git/https URLs, local paths, owner/repo shorthand and installed or catalog names, with ambiguity reported as exact candidate commands; the Source trait, SourceId, registry and fetch_once give every source one batched fetch per run with per-ref errors and source_disabled for later milestones

title: Pure candidate selection per target
description:
## Background

One fetch of a ref produces a `ReleaseSet`. Each target then needs its own ordered list of candidate assets to try. The vision (§5.4, D28) makes this a pure function, `fn select(set: &ReleaseSet, t: &Target, ch: Channel) -> Vec<Candidate>`, with no I/O, so it can be table-tested for every family. Fetching stays once per ref while selection runs once per target.

Selection only orders. The engine downloads each candidate in order, inspects it, and verifies its TOCs against the target's `ClientRules`. The first compatible candidate wins, and a failing one falls back to the next. Metadata is a hint, never a verdict (D5): WeakAuras' current `release.json` has no `mainline` entry, yet its zip contains a Mainline TOC and works on retail. Legacy clients have no metadata at all.

Facts used here:
- BigWigs packager flavor names: `mainline, classic, bcc, wrath, cata, mists, titan, forever`. The packager maps tbc→bcc, vanilla→classic, wotlkc→wrath, camelot→forever.
- Family to `release.json` flavor comes from the rules-tables bead (`Family::release_flavor() -> Option<&str>`):

  | Family | Flavor |
  |---|---|
  | mainline | mainline |
  | vanilla (Classic Era) | classic |
  | tbc (incl. Anniversary and the 2.5.x era PTR) | bcc |
  | wrath | wrath |
  | titan | titan |
  | cata | cata |
  | mists | mists |
  | forever (incl. the `_classic_beta_` 1.60.x client) | forever |
  | every `-legacy` family and `unknown` | none |

- Channels: `stable` (default) | `beta` | `alpha`. A GitHub prerelease is beta.

## Technical Approach

File: `src/resolve/select.rs`. Public API:

```rust
pub fn select(set: &ReleaseSet, target: &Target, channel: Channel, pin: Option<&str>) -> Selection;
pub struct Selection { pub candidates: Vec<Candidate>, pub empty_reason: Option<EmptyReason> }
pub enum EmptyReason { NoEligibleRelease, PinnedVersionNotFound, NoAssets }
```

`Candidate` (model bead) carries `release_id`, `version`, `channel`, the `Asset`, and a `rank: RankReason` enum used by `--verbose` output and tests. The vision's three-argument signature gains `pin`. Decided: a pinned version is part of selection, so the "which release" logic lives in one pure place.

**Step 1: choose the release.**
- With `pin`: the release whose `version` or tag equals `pin`, also matching after stripping a leading `v` from either side. If none matches, return no candidates with `PinnedVersionNotFound`.
- Without `pin`: filter by channel (`stable` = stable releases only; `beta` = stable + beta; `alpha` = all), then take the newest by `published_at`, falling back to set order (sources emit newest first). None left → `NoEligibleRelease`.
- Decided: candidates come only from that one release. Older releases are never tried automatically, because silently installing an old version would mask a broken release. The user can pin with `--version`.

**Step 2: rank that release's assets, best first.** Tiers, stable sort within each tier by original asset order:
1. **Metadata match.** The asset's `release.json` metadata has `flavor == target family's release flavor`. Within the tier, exact `interface == target.interface` first, then same major/minor family digits, then the rest.
2. **Name-hint match.** No metadata, but `name_flavors` (from source-github-rest) contains the target family, or `ClassicAny` for any classic family.
3. **Unannotated.** No metadata and no name hints. Every asset for `file:`, `url:` and `git:` refs falls here.
4. **Name-hint mismatch.** Hints present, none matching.
5. **Metadata mismatch.** Metadata present, none matching. Decided: kept as last-resort candidates rather than dropped, because metadata is wrong in practice (WeakAuras has no `mainline` entry). TOC verification decides.

Within every tier, `nolib: false` comes before `nolib: true`. Non-zip assets never reach select; sources filter them.

**Legacy and unknown targets.** `release_flavor()` is `None`, so nothing can be a metadata match. A modern `classic` metadata entry is a mismatch (tier 5) for a `vanilla-legacy` target. It stays a candidate only so verification can reject it with a precise reason, and it is ranked after everything unannotated. A modern Classic Era build (Interface 11509) never verifies against a 1.12.1 client (Interface 11200); that guarantee belongs to toc-loaded and is tested in toc-matrix.

**Purity.** No filesystem, network, clock or environment access. Deterministic output for identical inputs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `select` is pure and deterministic, with no I/O. A test asserts that it compiles without any `std::fs`/`net` imports in the module.
- Release choice follows the channel rules: stable excludes beta/alpha, beta includes stable, alpha includes all. Candidates come only from the newest eligible release.
- A pin selects the matching release (with `v` prefix tolerance) or returns `PinnedVersionNotFound`.
- Assets rank in the five documented tiers, with `nolib: false` first inside each tier.
- Metadata mismatches are kept last, not dropped.
- Table tests cover every family:
  - mainline, vanilla, tbc, wrath, titan, cata, mists and forever, including a `_classic_beta_` 1.60.x target as forever;
  - each legacy family: vanilla-legacy, tbc-legacy, wrath-legacy, cata-legacy, mists-legacy;
  - unknown.
- A WeakAuras-shaped release set (metadata without `mainline`) still yields its zip as a candidate for a mainline target.

## Test Plan

- Unit, table-driven (`tests` module in `src/resolve/select.rs`, built from synthetic `ReleaseSet`s):
  - multi-flavor BigWigs-style set (one zip per flavor plus nolib variants) × every family → expected first candidate;
  - single multi-flavor zip with metadata listing several flavors;
  - WeakAuras-shaped set for mainline;
  - interface tie-break (two `mainline` entries, 120100 vs 120105, target 120105);
  - name-hint-only REST set (`Foo-classic.zip`, `Foo-mainline.zip`, `Foo-3.3.5.zip`) for wrath-legacy, mainline and vanilla;
  - `git:`/`url:`/`file:` single unannotated asset for every family;
  - channel matrix over a set with stable 1.0, beta 1.1-beta and alpha 1.2-alpha;
  - pin hits `1.0`, `v1.0` and misses;
  - empty asset list → `NoAssets`.
- Proptest: output is a permutation of the chosen release's assets, so no asset is invented or lost.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (family, channel, candidate order with rank reasons).

## Considerations

- Fallback across candidates, downloading and verifying are the planner's job (E6 plan). This bead never decides compatibility.
- `published_at` is missing for no-REST GitHub releases, which yield a single release anyway, so set order is the fallback.
- If the packager adds a flavor name (as it did with `forever`), only the rules table needs a new mapping (D15). Unknown flavors in metadata simply never match.
- Out of scope: dependency candidates (M2) and CurseForge `gameVersionTypeId`/`releaseType` mapping (M5).
acceptance_criteria: select is pure and deterministic with no I/O; release choice follows the channel rules (stable excludes beta/alpha, beta includes stable, alpha includes all) and candidates come only from the newest eligible release; a pin selects the matching release with v-prefix tolerance or returns PinnedVersionNotFound; assets rank in the five documented tiers with nolib false first inside each tier and metadata mismatches kept last, not dropped; table tests cover mainline, vanilla, tbc, wrath, titan, cata, mists, forever (including a _classic_beta_ 1.60.x target), every legacy family and unknown; a WeakAuras-shaped release set without mainline metadata still yields its zip as a mainline candidate
close_reason: Candidate selection is a pure, deterministic per-target ordering of one release's assets (pinned or newest on the channel) in five documented tiers, never dropping metadata mismatches, table-tested for every modern, legacy and unknown family

Register in `SourceRegistry::builtin()`. Test helpers: tests/common/http.rs (`fixture`, `replay`, `record`, `scenario`).

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/resolve/select.rs).**
(1) API as specified: `select(&ReleaseSet, &Target, Channel, pin: Option<&str>) -> Selection { candidates, empty_reason: Option<EmptyReason::{NoEligibleRelease, PinnedVersionNotFound, NoAssets}> }`. EmptyReason serializes snake_case.
(2) Pin: matches the release version or the tag after the last '@' of release_id, with a leading v/V stripped on both sides. **A pin ignores the channel** (it is explicit). Without a pin, the newest eligible release is chosen by published_at when every eligible release has one (ties go to set order), else the first in set order.
(3) **Metadata flavors compare through `Family::from_release_flavor`**, so packager aliases (tbc, vanilla, wotlkc, camelot) match; unknown flavors match nothing. Tier 1 closeness: an exact target.interface gives MetadataInterface; otherwise MetadataFlavor ordered same interface/100, then other (and None interfaces). For a legacy or unknown target, any metadata is a tier-5 mismatch.
(4) **Name hints:** FlavorHint maps to the release-flavor names (Classic→classic, Bcc→bcc, …). ClassicAny fits every modern non-mainline family. Hints never match legacy or unknown targets. FlavorHint has no legacy variants (e.g. 3.3.5): a legacy-named zip without hints is Unannotated (tier 3), which ranks it ahead of mismatched hints for a 3.3.5 target.
(5) Sort key: (tier, nolib, closeness, original index). nolib false comes first within a tier, before interface closeness, as the bead orders it.
(6) Purity: a test scans the non-test part of the file for std::fs, std::net, crate::net, std::env, SystemTime and Timestamp::now.
(7) Tests: every modern family takes its BigWigs flavor first with the nolib twin second and the 14 others kept as MetadataMismatch; every legacy family and unknown has no metadata match; WeakAuras-shaped mainline; interface tie-break; name hints for retail, era and 3.3.5; unannotated git asset for every family; channel matrix and pins (v-prefix, tag vs version); published_at; a proptest that candidates are a permutation of the release's assets.

title: git refs for GitHub-hosted repos via commits atom and codeload
description:
## Background

Many legacy private-server addons have no releases at all: the repository is the addon, and users track a branch. The vision (§5.4) adds `git:` refs, `git:<url>[#<tag|branch|sha>]`. For GitHub-hosted repositories it avoids both the `git` binary and REST:
- branch heads come from `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/commits/<branch>.atom`, an in-process request that is allowlisted and logged;
- archives come from `codeload.github.com`.

The M1 checkpoint requires "a legacy addon installs into the 3.3.5a target from a git repo".

## Technical Approach

File: `src/sources/git_github.rs`, registering `SourceId::Git` in the M1 `SourceRegistry` and handling refs whose URL host is `github.com`. source-git-hosts later adds non-GitHub hosts to the same `SourceId::Git` implementation through a dispatch on host. This bead creates `src/sources/git.rs` as that dispatcher and routes `github.com` here.

**Accepted refs.** `git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>[.git][#<rev>]`. Owner and repo are validated (the refs bead already checked the charset), and a trailing `.git` is stripped.

**Rev resolution (in-process, purpose `commits-atom`).**
1. `rev` is 40 hex characters → treat it as a commit sha. No request is needed to resolve it.
2. `rev` is present otherwise → try it as a branch first: `GET https://github.com/<o>/<r>/commits/<rev>.atom`.
   - 200 with at least one entry → head sha = the newest entry's commit sha, taken from the entry `id` (`tag:github.com,2008:Grit::Commit/<sha>`) or the link `…/commit/<sha>`.
   - 404 → treat `rev` as a tag. No resolution request is made; the archive is fetched by tag name.
   - Decided: branch first, then tag, because tracking a branch is the main reason to use a git ref over a release. Document that a branch and a tag sharing a name resolve to the branch.
3. No `rev` → the default branch. Decided, per the plan: the implementer verifies with one live probe, recorded as a fixture, whether `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/commits.atom` with no branch tracks the default branch. If it does, use it. Otherwise try `commits/main.atom`, then `commits/master.atom`. Record which behavior was confirmed in this bead's close comment and in the code comment.

The Atom decoder is the shared `src/sources/atom.rs` from source-github-stable.

**Release set.** One `Release`:
- **Branch or default**: `release_id = "git:<url>@<sha>"`, `version` = the first 7 characters of the sha, `version_confidence: release`, `channel: Stable`.
- **Tag**: `release_id = "git:<url>@<tag>"`, `version` = tag.
- **Sha**: `release_id = "git:<url>@<sha>"`, `version` = short sha.
- One `Asset { name: "<repo>-<rev>.zip", location: Url("https://codeload.github.com/<o>/<r>/zip/<resolved>"), flavors: [], nolib: false }`, where `<resolved>` is the resolved sha for branches and default, the tag name for tags (`zip/refs/tags/<tag>`), or the sha itself.

Pinning the archive URL to the resolved sha guarantees the plan installs exactly what was resolved, even if the branch moves before download.

**Archive layout.** codeload zips wrap everything in `<repo>-<rev>/`. The repository may be the addon itself (`<repo>-<sha>/<Addon>.toc`) or contain addon folders (`<repo>-<sha>/<Addon>/<Addon>.toc`). archive-inspect normalizes both by TOC name, and this bead does nothing special. If the repository root is the addon, its folder name comes from the TOC name, not the `-<sha>` suffix.

**Updates.** Re-running install resolves the branch again. A new head sha gives a new `release_id`, so the planner records `kind: update`. The same sha means "already current".

**Channels and versions.** Git refs have no channels, so `--channel` is ignored for them. An explicit `--version` on a git ref is treated as a rev, identical to `#<rev>`. A conflicting `#rev` plus `--version` is `usage` (exit 2).

**Zero REST.** Nothing here touches `api.github.com`. The tests assert it through `assert_no_github_rest`.

**Fixtures.** Record into `tests/fixtures/http/git-github/`:
- the commits atom and a small codeload zip for one real legacy 3.3.5a addon repository with no releases (implementer picks and confirms it; do not guess);
- the default-branch probe result;
- a tag-resolution scenario (branch atom 404).

Add a decoder-level live probe for commits atom to `tests/live_probes.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `git:https://github.com/<o>/<r>[#rev]` refs fetch through `commits/<branch>.atom` and codeload only, with no REST and no git subprocess.
- Branch revs resolve to the newest commit sha, and the archive URL is pinned to it. Tags resolve after a branch-atom 404. 40-hex revs are used without a resolution request.
- The default-branch behavior is verified live once, recorded as a fixture, and implemented as confirmed.
- The release set has the documented `release_id`, `version` (short sha or tag) and a single codeload asset.
- Re-fetching after the branch moves yields a new `release_id`; an unchanged branch yields the same one.
- `--version` on a git ref acts as a rev, and conflicting with `#rev` is `usage`.
- Replay tests for the recorded legacy repository pass with `assert_no_github_rest`.
- `src/sources/git.rs` dispatches `github.com` URLs here and rejects other hosts with `source_disabled` until source-git-hosts lands.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - commit sha extraction from atom entry `id` and `link` forms;
  - rev classification (40-hex vs other);
  - codeload URL construction for branch, tag (`refs/tags/…`) and sha, including a tag containing `/`;
  - `release_id` and version formatting.
- Integration (replay):
  - default branch;
  - explicit branch;
  - tag fallback after 404;
  - explicit sha;
  - branch moved (two scenarios with different heads → different release ids);
  - `net.log` shows only `github.com` and `codeload.github.com` lines.
- E2E (in m1-checkpoint / engine-tests): installing the recorded legacy repository into a synthetic 3.3.5a target verifies by TOC (`## Interface: 30300`).
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (ref, atom URL, resolved sha, asset URL).

## Considerations

- GitHub could stop serving commits atom for some repositories (very large ones, or archived ones). The live probe at the checkpoint watches for it, and the fallback is a `gh:` ref or a `url:` codeload link.
- Short shas as versions can collide in display only; identity uses the full sha in `release_id`.
- Private repositories return 404 on atom, so they are treated as "branch not found" and then fail at archive download with `http_status` 404. The error message says private repositories are not supported in M1.
- Out of scope: non-GitHub hosts and the `git` binary (source-git-hosts).

title: git refs for non-GitHub hosts through the git binary
description:
## Background

Some legacy addons live on git hosts other than GitHub: Codeberg, a self-hosted Gitea or GitLab. The vision (§5.4) handles them with the `git` binary: "Other hosts use `git ls-remote` with https only, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `-c http.followRedirects=false`, logged as a `via: git` entry in `net.log`", and archives come from `git clone --depth 1 --branch` of the working tree.

Two privacy rules from §5.7 apply:
- Git subprocesses are restricted to allowlisted https hosts with redirects disabled.
- Every git subprocess is logged.

A git subprocess is the one place where bytes reach the disk without passing through fsx, so this bead also defines exactly where git may write.

Placeholders: `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache` under the home directory), `<config>` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config`).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/sources/git_hosts.rs`, plus dispatch in `src/sources/git.rs` (created by source-git-github) for non-GitHub hosts.

**Configured hosts.** Add the config key `git_hosts`, a list of hostnames (e.g. `git_hosts = ["codeberg.org"]`), to the config schema (config bead): typed, validated as bare hostnames without scheme or path, and settable with `config set`. The command layer passes the list into `NetConfig.git_hosts` (net-core), which adds the hosts to the allowlist. A `git:` URL whose host is neither `github.com` nor in `git_hosts` fails with `host_blocked` (exit 4). The fix is `omaddons config set git_hosts <host>` as display, with `argv: null` because the value must be merged into the existing list by the user. Only `https://` URLs are accepted; anything else is `ref_invalid` (2).

**Subprocess hygiene.** Every invocation goes through one helper, `run_git(args, purpose, timeout) -> Result<Output>`:
- `std::process::Command::new("git")` with argv only, never a shell.
- `env_clear()`, then set only:
  - `PATH` and `HOME`;
  - `LC_ALL=C`, so output parsing is stable;
  - `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`;
  - `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, so the user's `url.<x>.insteadOf`, proxy or credential settings cannot redirect a fetch to a non-allowlisted host;
  - `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https`.
- Always pass `-c http.followRedirects=false -c credential.helper= -c core.askPass= -c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always`.
- Credentials are never placed in argv. Repositories that need authentication fail fast because prompts are disabled, giving `download_failed` (exit 1, not retryable) with a message saying private repositories are not supported.
- Timeouts: `API_READ_TIMEOUT` (30 s) for `ls-remote`, `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` (300 s) for clone/fetch. On expiry the child is killed and the result is `network` (retryable).
- Before running, the URL host is checked with `Allowlist::permits`.
- After running, one net.log line via `NetLog::record_git`: `via: "git"`, `method: "GIT"`, host, path (no query), `status` = exit code, `bytes: null`, `duration_ms`, `purpose` ∈ `ls-remote|clone|fetch`.
- `--offline` makes `run_git` fail with `offline` before spawning anything.
- A missing `git` binary (spawn `NotFound`) gives `source_disabled` (exit 1) with fix display `install git (pacman -S git)` and `argv: null`.

**fetch (resolution only).** `git ls-remote --symref <url> [<rev>]`:
- No rev → read `ref: refs/heads/<b>\tHEAD` for the default branch and the HEAD sha.
- Branch → the sha of `refs/heads/<rev>`.
- Tag → the sha of `refs/tags/<rev>^{}` when peeled, else `refs/tags/<rev>`.
- 40-hex rev → used as-is.
- Nothing matches → `not_found` (3).

Branch is checked before tag, matching source-git-github. The release set has one release, `release_id = "git:<url>@<sha>"` and `version` = short sha (or the tag for tags), with one `Asset { location: GitCheckout { url, rev, sha } }`. `fetch` writes nothing.

**Materialize (download step).** `pub fn materialize(asset: &GitCheckout, dest: &Path) -> Result<()>` is called by the engine's planner/download step (E6 plan), which knows the transaction id. Decided, per the plan: git writes only into a fresh directory `<cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/git/` that the caller creates through fsx. That directory is the one sanctioned subprocess write, and it is pruned with `prune(PostCommitCleanup)` after commit or by orphan cleanup when the transaction's in-flight lock is free. Steps:
- branch or tag: `git clone --depth 1 --branch <rev> --single-branch --no-tags <url> <dest>`;
- sha: `git init <dest>`, then `git -C <dest> fetch --depth 1 <url> <sha>`, then `git -C <dest> checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD`. Servers that refuse fetching by sha produce `download_failed` with a message suggesting a branch or tag;
- after checkout, verify `git -C <dest> rev-parse HEAD` equals the resolved sha, else `plan_stale` (1, retryable), meaning the branch moved between resolution and clone.

The engine reads `<dest>` through `FolderView` as a directory input, with `.git/` excluded, so the tree is never re-zipped.

**Asset shape.** Add the `GitCheckout { url, rev, sha }` variant to `AssetLocation` (introduced by source-local-url) if it is missing. The E6 plan bead must route this variant to `materialize`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `git_hosts` config key exists, is validated, and feeds the allowlist. `git:` URLs to unlisted non-GitHub hosts fail with `host_blocked`, and non-https URLs with `ref_invalid`.
- Every git invocation runs through `run_git` with the cleared environment, the listed `-c` options and env vars, no shell and no credentials in argv, and writes exactly one `via: "git"` net.log line.
- `ls-remote` resolution handles the default branch, branch, peeled tag and sha, branch before tag. Unknown revs give `not_found`.
- `materialize` clones branch/tag shallowly, or fetches a sha, into a caller-provided fsx-created directory under `<cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/`, and verifies HEAD matches the resolved sha (`plan_stale` otherwise).
- Missing git gives `source_disabled` with the package fix. Offline gives `offline` without spawning. Timeouts kill the child and return `network`.
- `src/sources/git.rs` routes non-GitHub hosts here.
- No git subprocess can follow redirects or read the user's global or system git config (asserted by inspecting the constructed `Command`).

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - `ls-remote --symref` output parsing over recorded samples: default branch, branches, peeled and unpeeled tags, empty output;
  - host validation for `git_hosts` values;
  - the `Command` builder has the exact env and `-c` set, with no `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GIT_*` leakage from the parent (set junk vars in the test and assert they are absent).
- Integration (local, no network). Production refuses every protocol except https, so decided: test against a local bare repository through a test-only seam. `run_git` takes a `ProtocolPolicy`; `ProtocolPolicy::FileForTests` exists only under `cfg(test)`, so these are in-crate tests in `src/sources/git_hosts.rs`. They cover resolution, clone into a tempdir, sha fetch, branch moved → `plan_stale`, and timeout via a fake `git` script on `PATH` that sleeps. The production path never allows `file://`.
- Live (`#[ignore]`, `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`): `ls-remote` and a shallow clone of one real public repository on a non-GitHub host (implementer picks one), logged in net.log with `via: "git"`.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (argv, env keys, stdout/stderr of git, resolved sha).

## Considerations

- `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` needs git 2.32 or later (2021). The minimum supported git version is checked at first use (`git --version`); older versions give `source_disabled` with an upgrade fix.
- git's own HTTPS stack does not go through omaddons' `Http` trait, so retries and per-host limits do not apply to it. Each subprocess is still bounded by its timeout and logged.
- `git clone --depth 1` downloads the whole tree at that commit. Large repositories are bounded only by `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT`; the inspection limits still apply to what is installed.
- Out of scope: GitHub-hosted git refs (source-git-github), SSH URLs (not supported, since https is mandatory), and submodules (not fetched).
- Dependency added beyond the plan: `config`, because this bead adds the `git_hosts` key to the config schema.
acceptance_criteria: A git_hosts config key exists, is validated and feeds the allowlist; git: URLs to unlisted non-GitHub hosts fail with host_blocked and non-https URLs with ref_invalid; every git invocation runs through run_git with the cleared environment, the listed -c options and env vars, no shell and no credentials in argv, and writes exactly one via: git net.log line; ls-remote resolution handles default branch, branch, peeled tag and sha with branch before tag and unknown revs give not_found; materialize clones branch/tag shallowly or fetches a sha into a caller-provided fsx-created directory under <cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/ and verifies HEAD equals the resolved sha (plan_stale otherwise); missing git gives source_disabled with the package fix, offline gives offline without spawning, and timeouts kill the child and return network; src/sources/git.rs routes non-GitHub hosts here; no git subprocess can follow redirects or read the user's global or system git config
close_reason: git refs to configured non-GitHub hosts through a hygienic git runner, with checkouts materialized by the engine

comments.text: **net-core landed.** Check git hosts with `NetConfig::allowlist().permits(host)`; the user's configured hosts come from `NetConfig.git_hosts`. Log each subprocess with `NetLog::record_git(GitLogEntry { host, path, exit_code, duration_ms, purpose: "ls-remote"|"clone"|"fetch", error })`. Never put credentials in the path.

Register in `SourceRegistry::builtin()`. Test helpers: tests/common/http.rs (`fixture`, `replay`, `record`, `scenario`).

comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/sources/git_hosts.rs).** GitRunner (allowlist + offline from NetConfig, a shared NetLog clone, ProtocolPolicy::Https; FileForTests only under cfg(test)) is attached by the command layer with SourceRegistry::builtin().with_git(..) in app/engine.rs and app/info.rs; GitSource gets it as an Arc and routes github.com to git_github, everything else to the runner, and without a runner other hosts are source_disabled. GitRunner::command: argv only, env_clear then PATH, HOME, LC_ALL=C, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https; -c http.followRedirects=false, credential.helper=, core.askPass=, protocol.allow=never, protocol.https.allow=always; stdin null; its own process group, so a timeout kills git-remote-https too (rustix gained its 'process' feature for kill_process_group; no new crate, cargo deny clean). URLs with credentials are ref_invalid; unlisted hosts host_blocked (exit 4, display fix naming config set git_hosts, argv null); --offline refuses before spawning; a missing git is source_disabled 'install git (pacman -S git)'; git older than 2.32 (probed once with --version, which touches no repository and is not logged) is source_disabled. Every run that touches a repository logs one via: git line whose purpose is the subcommand (ls-remote, clone, fetch, and the local init, checkout, rev-parse: §5.7 says every git subprocess is logged). Resolution: ls-remote -- <url> refs/heads/<rev> refs/tags/<rev> refs/tags/<rev>^{} (branch, then peeled tag, then tag), or ls-remote --symref -- <url> HEAD for the default branch; 40-hex revs need no run. Materialize: clone --depth 1 --branch=<rev> --single-branch --no-tags, or init + fetch --depth 1 <sha> + checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD; then rev-parse HEAD must equal the resolved sha, else plan_stale (replan, retryable). **Engine:** the planner's GitCheckout arm creates cache_tmp(tx)/git/<n>/<repo>-<sha> through fsx (Writer::Derived), checks out into it and reads it with inspect_dir (.git skipped); the existing post-commit cleanup prunes cache_tmp(tx). The <repo>-<sha> name lets a repository-root addon be named by its TOC (the wrapper rule from 5.7). **Config:** git_hosts values must be bare DNS host names (no scheme, port, path or user), checked in Config::parse, so config set refuses them too. **Tests:** in-crate against local bare repositories (default branch, branch, peeled and lightweight tags, sha, unknown rev, clone of branch/tag/sha, moved branch → plan_stale, a TxScene install of a checkout with the temp dir gone after commit), the Command's env and -c set, the spawned environment, refusals before spawning, and a sleeping stand-in killed with its child; the live probe resolves and checks out tullamods/Dominos on Codeberg in about 2 s. title: GitHub REST fallback: prerelease channels, asset listing and rate-limit handling
description:
## Background

The no-REST GitHub path (source-github-stable) covers stable releases that carry a `release.json`. Two cases need the GitHub REST API (vision §5.4):

- **Beta and alpha channels.** Only REST and GraphQL expose a release's `prerelease` flag (atom feeds do not), and GraphQL always needs a token. A GitHub prerelease counts as beta.
- **Repositories without `release.json`.** Most legacy private-server addons publish plain zip assets, and listing them needs REST. The M1 checkpoint requires "a legacy addon installs into the 3.3.5a target … from a GitHub release".

Unauthenticated REST allows 60 requests/hour per IP, 5000/hour with a token. Conditional-request 304s are free only when authenticated (vision §4.5). The vision (§5.13) sets `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE = 5`: on the REST-only paths, at or below that `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, stop and return `rate_limited` with the reset time. The token is strictly opt-in (D12): `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` is read, `GITHUB_TOKEN` is never read implicitly, and `gh auth token` is read only by the M2 `auth github --from-gh` command.

## Technical Approach

File: `src/sources/github_rest.rs`, implementing the `GithubRestFallback` seam that source-github-stable defines on `GithubSource`. The REST-only budget logic lives here.

**Endpoints** (all `https://api.github.com`, headers `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` and `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`, purpose `rest-releases`):
- `GET /repos/<o>/<r>/releases?per_page=20` lists recent releases with `tag_name`, `name`, `prerelease`, `draft`, `published_at`, and `assets[]` with `name`, `browser_download_url`, `size`, `content_type`.
- `GET /repos/<o>/<r>/releases/tags/<tag>` returns one release, for the asset listing of a known stable tag whose `release.json` is missing.

Decode tolerantly: `#[serde(default)]`, unknown fields ignored, optional fields as `Option`.

**Channel semantics.**
- `stable`: the newest non-draft, non-prerelease release.
- `beta`: the newest non-draft release, prerelease or not ("beta includes stable").
- `alpha`: identical to beta on GitHub, which has no separate alpha. Decided, and documented in the source's capabilities notes later.

**Release to assets.**
- If the chosen release has an asset named `release.json`, download it via its `browser_download_url`, a github.com URL that needs no REST, and decode it with source-github-stable's decoder. Assets then come from its entries exactly as on the stable path.
- Otherwise, list the release's `.zip` assets. Asset name heuristics annotate each with `name_flavors: Vec<FlavorHint>` (a field this bead adds to `Asset` if the model bead lacks it). On the lowercased name, without the extension:

  | Name contains | Hint |
  |---|---|
  | `mainline`, `retail` | Mainline |
  | `vanilla`, `era` | Vanilla |
  | `classic` (alone) | ClassicAny |
  | `bcc`, `tbc` | Tbc |
  | `wrath`, `wotlk` | Wrath |
  | `cata` | Cata |
  | `mists`, `mop` | Mists |
  | `forever` | Forever |
  | `1.12`, `2.4.3`, `3.3.5`/`335`, `4.3.4`, `5.4.8` | the matching legacy family |

  `-nolib` and `nolib` mark `nolib: true`. Non-zip assets are ignored. Hints only order candidates. TOC verification in the engine decides compatibility, and select ranks hint mismatches last rather than dropping them.
- `release_id = "gh:<o>/<r>@<tag>"`; `version` = tag; `channel` = `Beta` when `prerelease`, else `Stable`; `published_at` from the API.

**Budget (`RestBudget`, shared across a run).**
- Updated from every REST response's `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`.
- Before sending a REST request, if the last known remaining is ≤ `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE` (5), do not send. Return `rate_limited` (exit 1, retryable) with `details.reset_at` (RFC 3339 from `X-RateLimit-Reset`) and a fix suggesting the opt-in token: display `export OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN=…`, `argv: null`.
- The first REST request of a run is always allowed, because the remaining count is unknown.
- A 403 or 429 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` is mapped to `rate_limited` by net-resilience.
- REST list requests set `Request.validators = true`. Authenticated, a 304 costs nothing; unauthenticated, it still counts, and that cost is accepted.

**Token.** If `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set and non-empty, send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on `api.github.com` requests only, never to github.com web endpoints or asset hosts. The token is never logged (net-core logs no headers), never placed in a child process's argv, and never echoed in errors. `GITHUB_TOKEN` is never read; a unit test asserts that setting only `GITHUB_TOKEN` sends no `Authorization` header.

**Fixtures.** Record into `tests/fixtures/http/github-rest/`:
- one real legacy addon repository whose releases carry only zip assets and no `release.json`. The implementer picks a real repository for a legacy family (3.3.5a preferred), confirms it, and records it; do not guess;
- one repository with a prerelease newer than its latest stable release (for beta selection);
- a synthetic scenario with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 4` on the first response, to test the reserve stop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GithubSource` delegates beta/alpha requests and stable tags without `release.json` to this fallback.
- Stable picks the newest non-prerelease, non-draft release. Beta and alpha pick the newest non-draft release.
- A release with a `release.json` asset uses its metadata, and that file is fetched from github.com without REST. A release without one yields zip assets with `name_flavors` hints and `nolib` flags per the table.
- After a response with `X-RateLimit-Remaining` ≤ 5, the next REST request is not sent and the call returns `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at`.
- `Authorization: Bearer` is sent only to `api.github.com` and only when `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set. `GITHUB_TOKEN` alone sends nothing. The token never appears in `net.log`, errors or fixtures.
- Replay tests for the legacy zip-only repo and the prerelease repo produce the expected release sets.
- The legacy repo's zip asset is a candidate that the engine can verify against a 3.3.5a target. The end-to-end proof lands in m1-checkpoint.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - asset-name heuristics table over about 30 real-world-style names (`ElvUI-3.3.5.zip`, `Foo-classic.zip`, `Foo-bcc-nolib.zip`, `Foo-Mainline.zip`, `Foo_v1.2.zip`);
  - channel selection over a synthetic release list (draft, prerelease, stable orderings);
  - budget state machine: unknown → allow, 6 → allow, 5 → stop, with the reset time carried;
  - token header presence and absence (`OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` vs `GITHUB_TOKEN`).
- Integration (replay):
  - legacy zip-only repo end to end through `GithubSource::fetch` (stable `releases/latest` → `release.json` 404 → REST listing);
  - prerelease repo with `--channel beta`;
  - reserve stop scenario;
  - `net.log` shows exactly the expected `api.github.com` lines and none for repos that have a `release.json`.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (ref, channel, chosen release, hints).

## Considerations

- 60 requests/hour unauthenticated is tight for M2's `outdated` across many beta-channel addons. The reserve stops early with an honest error instead of burning the budget. M2's `auth github` and GraphQL batch relieve it.
- Heuristics misfire: names like `Foo-classic.zip` say nothing about era versus progression classic. That is why they are hints and verification decides.
- `per_page=20` covers the common case. A repository whose newest stable release is older than 20 prereleases is not handled in M1, and the error says no stable release was found within the listing.
- Search through REST is M2.

title: Epic: M1 transaction engine
description:
## Background

The transaction engine is the core of omaddons and the main fix for the reference implementation's worst defect (vision §3, R2): it deleted old addon folders and then copied new ones in, so any failure mid-loop left an addon half-installed, with stale records. omaddons instead runs every mutation (install, update, remove and undo in M1; adopt, sync, restore and repair later) as one journaled transaction per target. Each transaction is snapshotted, attributed to an actor, and reversible with `omaddons undo`.

The engine follows vision §5.5. The steps that need no lock (plan, download, inspect, stage) run concurrently with other omaddons processes. The global lock is held only for the commit window: revalidate, journal, swap, commit. That window takes milliseconds, so the widget, a terminal and an agent can mutate at the same time without hitting `locked` (D24). Liveness is proven only by held flocks (D23): recovery of a left-over journal happens only while holding the global lock, and an artifact counts as orphaned only when its per-transaction in-flight lock is free. Each folder is swapped with `RENAME_EXCHANGE` or `RENAME_NOREPLACE`, so at every instant an AddOns folder is either the complete old version or the complete new version. Where the filesystem lacks those flags, the engine falls back to two renames under the journal and reports `atomic_swap: false` honestly (D25). SavedVariables of touched folders are reflink-snapshotted, restored conditionally on undo, and never written while the client runs (D33). A `safe` running policy lets the common "alt-tab, update, /reload" flow work and reports `reload_required` (D30).

Placeholders used in this epic and its children: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache`); `<client dir>` = the directory that holds `Interface/` and `WTF/` (a flavor folder such as `<root>/_retail_/`, or a custom client root).

## Goals

- A content-addressed blob cache under `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/`, LRU-capped and pinned by references (blob-cache).
- Archive inspection that finds addon roots by TOC, normalizes wrapper layouts, rejects hostile archives, and verifies candidates against the target's `ClientRules` (archive-inspect).
- Same-filesystem staging under `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/`, producing the per-file index during extraction (stage).
- The ownership model: `ownership_conflict`, `protected_folder`, `unmanaged_folder`, `case_collision` and the `--force` semantics (ownership).
- Planning that resolves refs to verified candidates and computes folder ops against a generation snapshot; its output is the `--dry-run` plan (plan).
- A phased journal with step records, and recovery only under the global lock (journal).
- Per-folder atomic swaps with snapshots, SavedVariables reflink snapshots and an honest fallback (swap).
- The transaction driver: lock, revalidate with generations, journal, swap, commit, post-commit cleanup (commit).
- The running policy and `reload_required` (running-policy).
- Undo with conflict detection, `--last-by` and the `--saved-variables` policy (undo).
- Age-protected, size-capped retention via `fsx::prune()` (retention).
- The failure-injection and concurrency test matrix that proves the invariant (engine-tests).

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- A failure injected at every engine step leaves each AddOns folder wholly old or wholly new, and recovery happens only under the lock.
- A reader running during a live swap reports `tx_in_progress` and changes nothing.
- Two concurrent installs into the same target both complete without `locked`, or one becomes a no-op. Lock hold time per commit is under 50 ms on fixtures.
- `undo` restores folders byte-for-byte. SavedVariables follow the policy: unchanged files are left alone, changed files are cloned and then restored, and a running client defers the SavedVariables part. `undo_conflict` is raised across transaction kinds, and `undo --last-by agent` reverts only that actor's transaction.
- The hostile archive suite (including case-folded collisions) is rejected and nothing is written outside staging. Creating `blizzard_auctionui/` beside `Blizzard_AuctionUI/` is refused.
- The `RENAME_EXCHANGE` fallback (injected `EINVAL`) and the reflink fallback both work and are reported.
- No code path renames or deletes the global lock file.

## Non-Goals

- Dependency resolution and installs of required dependencies (M2). M1 accepts `--no-deps` and ignores it.
- Stored plans, `plan_id` persistence and `apply <plan_id>` (M4). M1 `--dry-run` returns the plan with `plan_id: null`.
- `adopt`, `sync`, `restore` and `repair` transaction kinds (M2–M4). The engine's `TxKind` already names them, but only install, update, remove and undo are driven in M1.
- CurseForge and Wago archives (M5). The blob cache exposes `cacheable: false` so they never land in it.
- Doctor detectors and fixers such as `orphan-inflight` and `journal-pending` (M4). In M1 the engine reports `journal_pending` and `tx_in_progress` as plain warnings.
- Drift detection over the per-file index (M2). M1 only writes the index.

## Considerations

- The vision's §5.5 step order is the contract. Do not move work into or out of the lock window without recording why on the bead.
- Every write goes through `src/fsx/` (the single writer). The engine never calls `std::fs` mutation functions directly.
- Lock hold time is a checkpoint (< 50 ms on fixtures). Work that can happen outside the lock (download, inspection, extraction, hashing) must stay outside it.
- `atomic_swap` and `reload_required` are reported per target in every mutation outcome. They are part of the M1 `data` schema and derive `Serialize` + `JsonSchema` (DEC-3).
- The engine's failpoints (debug builds only, `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`) are published as a constant list so the test matrix covers every one.
- Account, realm and character names appear on disk inside snapshot paths but never in any output.
acceptance_criteria: A failure injected at every engine step leaves each AddOns folder wholly old or wholly new and recovery happens only under the lock; a reader during a live swap reports tx_in_progress and changes nothing; two concurrent installs into one target both complete without locked or one becomes a no-op, with lock hold under 50 ms per commit on fixtures; undo restores folders byte-for-byte and SavedVariables follow the auto/restore/keep policy; undo_conflict is raised across transaction kinds and undo --last-by agent reverts only that actor's transaction; the hostile archive suite is rejected with nothing written outside staging, and blizzard_auctionui beside Blizzard_AuctionUI is refused; RENAME_EXCHANGE and reflink fallbacks work and are reported; no code path renames or deletes the global lock file
close_reason: All children completed

title: Archive inspection: addon roots, normalization, hostile-entry rejection, verification
description:
## Background

Step 3 of the transaction engine (vision §5.5) inspects each downloaded archive before anything touches the client. Two reference-implementation defects motivate it (vision §3):
- R5: zip top-level directories were used verbatim, so `Foo-main/` and `Foo-main/Foo/` layouts installed broken.
- The reference checked path traversal but nothing else. omaddons must also reject every hostile shape: absolute paths, drive letters, `..`, symlinks, devices, case-folded collisions, entry-count bombs and zip bombs.

Inspection also produces what verification needs. Upstream metadata is wrong in practice: WeakAuras' `release.json` has no `mainline` entry, so the client's own load rules applied to the actual archive contents are the ground truth (D5). Inspection exposes the archive as a `FolderView` (DEC-14), so the toc-loaded bead's `loaded_toc` and `verdict` run unchanged on archive contents. That gives `verify(&Inspected, &Target) -> Verdict`, the pure check from vision §5.4.

Wine resolves names case-insensitively, so two archive entries that differ only in case would make the installed result undefined. Folder identity is the ASCII case-folded key (D27).

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/inspect.rs`; `inspect(blob: &Path, limits: &ArchiveLimits) -> Result<Inspected>`. No lock and no writes: it only reads the blob.
- Directory inputs: `inspect_dir(dir: &Path, limits) -> Result<Inspected>` handles `file:` directories and materialized git checkouts (`AssetLocation::LocalDir` / `GitCheckout`, model bead). It applies the same addon-root detection, normalization, wrapper descent, FolderName validation, entry-count and total-size limits and case-folded collision checks. Symlinks inside the directory are never followed: a symlink entry → `unsafe_archive`, same as in a zip. `blob_sha256` is `None` for directory inputs; files are hashed while walking.
- Open the archive with the `zip` crate (deflate only; stored entries are also allowed). Not a readable zip → `bad_archive` (exit 1, not retryable).
- Entry path normalization, before any other check:
  - Treat `\` as a separator (`/`), because Windows tools produce such entries and `..\` traversal must be caught.
  - Drop `.` components and empty components.
  - Reject the whole archive with `unsafe_archive` (exit 4) when an entry: is absolute (`/x`); starts with a drive letter (`C:`, any case); contains a `..` component; contains NUL or ASCII control characters; is a symlink (unix mode `S_IFLNK` in external attributes); is a device, FIFO or socket (`S_IFCHR`, `S_IFBLK`, `S_IFIFO`, `S_IFSOCK`); or collides with another entry after ASCII case folding, including a file-versus-directory collision (`Foo` file and `Foo/` dir).
- Limits, all from `src/limits.rs` and overridable in config (the caller passes an `ArchiveLimits`):
  - more than `ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES` (20 000) entries → `archive_too_large` (exit 4);
  - total uncompressed bytes above `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED` (1 GiB) → `archive_too_large`;
  - compression ratio above `ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO` (200:1), per entry or overall → `unsafe_archive` (decided: a ratio that high is a crafted zip bomb, which is a safety refusal, not a size problem).
  - Header sizes can lie. Sizes and ratios are enforced on the bytes actually decompressed, through a counting reader that aborts as soon as a limit is crossed. Header values are only used for an early reject.
  - `details` carries the measured value and the limit.
- Addon-root detection:
  - A directory `D` is an addon root when it directly contains a TOC whose basename, minus a recognized suffix, equals `D`'s name case-insensitively. Recognized suffixes are the union of every ClientRules row's game, family and legacy suffixes, with `-` or `_` as the separator (rules-tables bead).
  - Normalization: when `D`'s name is `<N>-main`, `<N>-master` or `<N>-<version>` (a version is a token starting with a digit or `v<digit>`) and `D` directly contains a TOC named `<N>` (plus an optional suffix), `D` is an addon root installed as `<N>`.
  - Descend through single wrapper directories: if no addon root is found at a level and that level holds exactly one directory (loose files are ignored), descend into it. Multi-addon layouts (`Repo-main/AddonA/AddonA.toc`, `Repo-main/AddonB/AddonB.toc`) yield several roots.
  - Loose files at the archive root (README, LICENSE) are ignored.
  - The whole subtree of an addon root belongs to it. Nested directories with their own TOCs, such as embedded libraries, are not separate roots.
  - Every resulting root name must parse as `FolderName` (model bead). A name that does not parse → `unsafe_archive`. A name whose key starts with `blizzard_` is returned as a root; the ownership bead refuses it with `protected_folder`.
  - Two roots that normalize to the same folder key → `bad_archive` (decided: malformed rather than hostile; it cannot be installed either way).
  - No addon root at all → `bad_archive` with `details.reason = "no_addon_root"`. The planner treats this as a failing candidate and falls back to the next one.
- Output: `Inspected { blob_sha256: Option<String>, folders: Vec<InspectedFolder> }` with `InspectedFolder { name: FolderName, archive_prefix: String, files: Vec<InspectedFile { rel_path, size, sha256 }> }`. Hashes and sizes are computed while reading with the counting reader. These become the per-file index entries that the stage bead completes with `mtime_ns` after extraction.
- `ArchiveFolderView` implements `FolderView` (toc-loaded bead) over one `InspectedFolder`: case-insensitive entry lookup and file reads from the zip. It reads only TOC files and the files TOCs reference, never the whole archive into memory.
- `verify(inspected: &Inspected, target: &Target) -> Vec<(FolderName, Verdict)>`: runs `toc::verdict` per folder. The archive is compatible when at least one folder is `Compatible` and none is `WrongFlavor`; `NoToc` sub-folders cannot occur for roots by construction. An out-of-date folder is compatible, and the planner surfaces the `out_of_date` warning.
- `Inspected` and `InspectedFolder` derive `Serialize` + `JsonSchema` (DEC-3) because the plan output lists folders and file counts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every hostile fixture is rejected with the documented code before any byte is extracted: traversal (`../x`, `..\x`), absolute, drive letter, symlink, device, zip bomb (ratio), entry-count bomb, total-size bomb, case-folded collision, file/dir collision.
- A zip whose headers understate uncompressed sizes is still stopped at the real limit.
- `Foo-main/Foo.toc` installs as folder `Foo`; `Foo-1.2.3/Foo/Foo.toc` (wrapper) installs as `Foo`; `Repo-main/A/A.toc` + `Repo-main/B/B.toc` yields folders `A` and `B`; loose root files are ignored.
- A folder's nested library sub-directory with its own TOC is not reported as a separate root.
- `verify` on a WeakAuras-style archive with only `_Classic`/`_Vanilla`/`_Mists` TOCs returns `WrongFlavor` for a retail target and `Compatible` for the matching Classic family.
- `verify` on an archive whose only TOC is `Foo_Mainline.toc` with `## Interface: 120105` returns `WrongFlavor` for a Forever target (the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` guard).
- Per-file sizes and SHA-256 hashes in `Inspected` equal those of the extracted bytes.
- Inspection performs no filesystem writes (asserted by the fsx actions log staying empty and by hashing the temp dir before and after).

## Test Plan

- Unit: path normalization table (backslashes, `.` components, drive letters in any case, NUL/control characters).
- Unit: root detection table: plain, `-main`, `-master`, version-suffixed (`Foo-1.2.3`, `Foo-v1.2`), single and double wrappers, multi-addon repos, loose files, nested library TOCs, case-variant TOC names (`foo.TOC`, `Foo_mainline.toc`).
- Integration: hostile archive builders in `tests/common/archives.rs` (DEC-8). Each builder writes raw zip records where the `zip` crate refuses to produce the hostile shape (symlink and device modes via external attributes, lying size headers). Cover traversal, absolute, drive letter, symlink, device, ratio bomb, entry-count bomb (20 001 empty entries), total-size bomb, case-folded collision, file/dir collision.
- Integration: verify against synthetic targets for retail, Forever, a Classic family and 3.3.5a (wrath-legacy), using small fixture archives built in the test.
- Property: proptest over random entry name lists never panics and never returns a root whose name fails `FolderName` parsing.
- Log the entry list and the verdicts on failure.

## Considerations

- `bad_archive` (exit 1) versus `unsafe_archive`/`archive_too_large` (exit 4): malformed archives are runtime failures, hostile or oversized ones are safety refusals. Keep the mapping in one function so the contract suite can assert it.
- The client reads only the first 1024 characters of each TOC line (`TOC_LINE_MAX`); the toc-parser bead handles that, and inspection must not pre-truncate.
- Unicode folder names: case folding is ASCII-only, matching `FolderName::key()`. Non-ASCII names are allowed if `FolderName` accepts them.
- Version-suffix detection is a heuristic. When it is ambiguous (for example `Foo-Bar/Foo-Bar.toc`), the exact-name rule wins, because the TOC basename equals the directory name.
- Fuzzing of this function is owned by the fuzz-targets bead (E7). Keep `inspect` callable on an in-memory `&[u8]` (via `Cursor`) for that.
- This bead creates `tests/common/archives.rs` (normal and hostile archive builders reused by the stage, plan and engine-tests beads). If `tests/common/mod.rs` does not exist yet (the test-trees bead creates it), create it with just `pub mod archives;` and let test-trees extend it.
- Out of scope: extraction (stage bead), ownership checks (ownership bead), choosing between candidates (plan bead).
acceptance_criteria: Every hostile fixture (traversal with / and \, absolute, drive letter, symlink, device, ratio bomb, entry-count bomb, total-size bomb, case-folded collision, file/dir collision) is rejected with the documented code before any byte is extracted; a zip whose headers understate sizes is stopped at the real limit; Foo-main/Foo.toc installs as Foo, a single wrapper is descended, a multi-addon repo yields one folder per addon, and loose root files are ignored; nested library TOCs are not separate roots; verify returns WrongFlavor for a WeakAuras-style classic-only archive on retail and Compatible on the matching Classic family; verify returns WrongFlavor for a Mainline-only archive with Interface 120105 on a Forever target; per-file sizes and sha256 in Inspected equal the extracted bytes; inspection performs no filesystem writes
close_reason: Zips and directories are inspected before extraction: hostile names, modes, collisions, duplicate entries, size, count and ratio bombs (including lying headers) are refused with the documented codes; addon roots are found through branch, version and wrapper layouts; files are measured from their real bytes; nothing is written; verify applies each target's TOC load rules

comments.text: **rules-tables landed (src/rules.rs).** For addon-root detection use `RulesTable::toc_suffixes()` rather than the bare const: it returns `KNOWN_TOC_SUFFIXES` (Standard, Forever, Camelot, Mists, Cata, Wrath, TBC, Vanilla, Plunderstorm, WoWLabs, WoWHack, Mainline, Classic, BCC, WOTLKC), then any other suffix a row lists (override rows included), de-duplicated ignoring case. comments.text: **FolderView landed (src/toc/loaded.rs).** Implement `toc::FolderView { folder_name(), root_files(), read_toc(file) }` over an archive folder, using `toc::read_bounded(reader)` for each entry. Then `toc::verdict(&view, &rules, family, target_interface, &table)` gives the same VerdictReport as on disk. Archive symlink entries must never become root files.

comments.text: claim: src/engine/inspect.rs, tests/common/archives.rs, tests/inspect.rs

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/engine/inspect.rs, tests/common/archives.rs, tests/inspect.rs).**
(1) **Signatures take the rules table:** `inspect(blob, &ArchiveLimits, &RulesTable)`, `inspect_zip<R: Read+Seek>(reader, ..)` (in-memory, for fuzzing), `inspect_dir(dir, ..)`, `verify(&Inspected, &Target, &RulesTable) -> Result<Vec<FolderVerdict { folder, report: VerdictReport }>>`, `compatible(&[FolderVerdict]) -> bool`. Root detection needs `table.toc_suffixes()`, and verdicts need the table. `ArchiveLimits::from(&EffectiveLimits)` carries config overrides.
(2) **New limit ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR = 1 MiB (not configurable):** the 200:1 ratio applies only once an entry, or the whole archive, has expanded past 1 MiB. A flat per-entry ratio rejects legitimate small repetitive files (10 KB of padding deflates over 300:1), and every real bomb expands far past 1 MiB. Exactly 200:1 is allowed. The limits registry and snapshot are updated.
(3) **Duplicate entry names are hostile:** the zip crate silently keeps one entry per name, so inspect reads the entry count from the end-of-central-directory record (the signature whose comment length runs to the end, so a decoy in the comment is ignored). When it exceeds the crate's distinct count, the archive is unsafe_archive with details.reason duplicate_entry. The entry limit uses the larger of the two counts.
(4) Headers are checked first (names, modes, collisions, encryption, compression method, declared total and per-entry ratio), before any byte is decompressed. Then every entry is decompressed once and hashed, with running checks on the total and overall ratio, then the per-entry ratio. **The zip crate itself caps output at the declared size**, failing with InvalidData '…larger than its declared uncompressed size'. That is mapped to unsafe_archive ('expands past the size its header declares'), so a lying header stops at its declared size, earlier than the limit. Other read failures (CRC, corrupt deflate) are bad_archive (reason corrupt). Only Stored and Deflated are read; others are bad_archive (unsupported_compression), as are encrypted entries (encrypted). A non-zip is bad_archive (not_a_zip).
(5) Modes: no unix mode, type 0, regular and directory are fine; symlink, char and block devices, FIFO and socket are unsafe. A zip directory is a trailing '/' or '\\', the crate's is_dir, or a directory mode. Normalization: '\\' becomes '/', '.' and empty parts are dropped, then refusals for absolute paths, '<letter>:' at the start, '..' anywhere, and ASCII control characters (NUL, DEL). ':' later in a name is allowed.
(6) Collisions: every path and implicit parent is registered by its ASCII-folded key. Two spellings, file vs directory, or the same file twice are unsafe. Explicit and implicit directories with the same spelling agree.
(7) Roots: an exact TOC match (the TOC stem, or the stem minus a known suffix after '-' or '_', equals the directory name ignoring case) installs under the directory's spelling. A wrapped name (<N>-main, -master, or -<digit…|v<digit…>, leftmost '-' first) installs under the TOC's spelling, so weakauras-main/WeakAuras.toc gives WeakAuras. Loose files never stop the descent; a level with several directories and no root is no_addon_root. Roots are never searched inside. An invalid FolderName for a root is unsafe; two roots with one key are bad_archive (duplicate_folder).
(8) **inspect_dir treats the directory itself as a candidate root** (`omaddons install ./MyAddon` works), descends wrappers like a zip, **skips any '.git' directory**, refuses symlinks, devices, non-UTF-8 names, control characters and backslashes in names, and enforces count and total size. blob_sha256 is None.
(9) Output: `InspectedFile { rel_path, size, sha256, source: FileSource::{ZipEntry(index), Disk(path)} }`. The source is serde-skipped and is for staging. Each folder keeps its root files and line-bounded TOC bytes (serde-skipped), and `folder.view()` is the FolderView.
(10) **New WrongFlavorReason::NoLoadableToc:** `verify` maps judge's NoToc to WrongFlavor{no_loadable_toc}, because a root has a TOC by construction and a client that loads none of them is the wrong flavor. That is what makes the WeakAuras-style classic-only archive WrongFlavor on retail. The on-disk inventory keeps NoToc.
(11) Error fixes: bad_archive and unsafe_archive have text fixes (nothing installed; report to the author). archive_too_large names `omaddons config set <details.config_key> <value>`. `archive_error(ArchiveFault, message, details)` is the single fault→code mapping.
(12) Archive builders: tests/common/archives.rs has `zip_of`, `zip_text` and `RawEntry::{stored, deflated}.mode().declared_size().raw_name()` with `raw_zip` (any unix mode, lying sizes, raw name bytes).

title: Same-filesystem staging under Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>
description:
## Background

Step 5 of the transaction engine (vision §5.5) extracts the inspected addon folders to a staging directory before the global lock is taken. The stage dir is `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/`. It is:
- on the same filesystem as `Interface/AddOns/`, so the later swap is a rename (`RENAME_EXCHANGE` / `RENAME_NOREPLACE`), not a copy (D7);
- outside the directory the client scans, so a half-extracted folder is never visible to the game;
- unique per transaction, so concurrent transactions never share a stage dir.

Staging is also where the per-file index for new folders is produced. The vision's `targets/<key>.files.json` holds `{path, size, mtime_ns, sha256}` per managed file, "computed during extraction" (§5.5 commit step, §5.6). M2's drift check depends on it.

The transaction holds its in-flight lock (`<state>/omaddons/inflight/<tx>.lock`, fsx-lock bead) from planning until cleanup. A crash during staging therefore leaves a stage dir whose in-flight lock is free, which is the one and only signal that it is orphaned (D23).

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = the directory that holds `Interface/` and `WTF/`; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/stage.rs`; `stage(tx: &TxCtx, target: &Target, blob: &Path, inspected: &Inspected) -> Result<Staged>`.
- Precondition: the caller holds `InflightLock` for `tx` (asserted in debug builds).
- Ensure `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/` and `stage/<tx>/` exist via `fsx::mutate(.., Op::CreateDir)`. The `Interface/.omaddons/` scope row of the fsx write-scope table permits this for the install engine.
- Extract only the normalized addon roots listed in `Inspected`. Each entry is written to `stage/<tx>/<FolderName>/<rel_path>` (normalized names from archive-inspect; `Foo-main/` becomes `Foo/`). Loose files and anything outside the roots are never extracted.
- Writes and durability. Decided (performance and durability together): staged files are written with `Op::WriteFile` in an fsx untracked session scoped to the stage dir (DEC-10: stage contents are derived data, reproducible from the blob). The session uses deferred durability (no per-file fsync). After the last file, one `fsx::sync_filesystem(stage_dir)` (`syncfs(2)` via rustix) makes everything durable before the transaction moves on to the lock.
  - Why: per-file fsync plus a per-file `actions.jsonl` line would take seconds for addons with thousands of files (for example AllTheThings).
  - The authoritative record of what entered AddOns is the directory-level `Rename` action at swap time, which carries the folder's tree hash computed from this bead's index (vision §5.5: "directory ops record tree hashes derived from the per-file index: computed during extraction for new folders").
  - fsx-mutate provides both pieces: `mutate_with(…, MutateOpts { durability: Durability::Deferred, .. })`, which is accepted only under the stage dir, and `fsx::sync_filesystem(path)`. Call `sync_filesystem` once after the last staged file, before handing `Staged` to the commit driver.
- Verify while extracting: each written file's size and SHA-256 must equal the `InspectedFile` values. A mismatch (the blob changed underneath, or the disk misbehaved) → `bad_archive` (exit 1) with the path in `details`.
- File modes: regular files 0644, directories 0755. Never preserve archive modes (no setuid, no exec bits) and never create symlinks (inspection already rejected them).
- After writing, stat each file and record `mtime_ns`. Output: `Staged { tx, stage_dir, folders: Vec<StagedFolder { name, path, files_index: Vec<FileIndexEntry { path, size, mtime_ns, sha256 }>, tree_hash }> }`. `tree_hash` = SHA-256 over the sorted `path\0size\0sha256\n` lines (decided: path-sorted with a fixed line format, so the same folder content always yields the same hash; the format is documented in the module so fsx and drift agree).
- Failpoints (debug builds, DEC-7): `engine.stage.begin`, `engine.stage.file` (after the first file), `engine.stage.synced`.
- Staging never touches `Interface/AddOns/`. Failure leaves only the stage dir. The transaction driver (commit bead) prunes the stage dir on any error after staging (`PruneReason::PostCommitCleanup`). If the process dies, the orphan is recognized by its free in-flight lock (retention bead in M1; doctor `orphan-inflight` in M4).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Staging a multi-folder archive produces `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/<Folder>/…` for exactly the inspected roots, with normalized names, and nothing under `Interface/AddOns/` changes.
- Every staged file's size and SHA-256 match the inspection, and `files_index` contains `path, size, mtime_ns, sha256` for every file.
- `tree_hash` is deterministic: staging the same archive twice into different tx dirs yields equal tree hashes.
- Staged files have mode 0644 and directories 0755 regardless of archive modes.
- Exactly one `syncfs` happens per stage call (asserted through a test counter on the fsx primitive), with no per-file fsync.
- An injected `error` failpoint mid-staging returns an `io` error, leaves AddOns untouched, and leaves a stage dir that the caller's cleanup prunes.
- All writes go through fsx (the single-writer test passes).

## Test Plan

- Unit: tree-hash format and determinism; mode normalization.
- Integration (a synthetic target from `tests/common/trees.rs`, or a minimal `<client dir>` with `Interface/AddOns/` built inline if the test-trees bead has not landed; archives from `tests/common/archives.rs`): multi-folder archive; `Foo-main/` normalization; an archive with 5 000 small files (assert a time budget, generous enough to stay stable, for example under 2 s in a debug build on tmpfs, and log the timing).
- Integration: hash-mismatch path, using a blob altered between inspect and stage → `bad_archive`.
- Integration: failpoint `engine.stage.file=error` → error returned, AddOns unchanged (hash the AddOns tree before and after).
- Integration: two transactions staging into the same target concurrently, using different tx ids, never interfere.
- Log the stage dir listing on failure.

## Considerations

- `syncfs` flushes the whole filesystem. That is acceptable: it happens once per transaction, outside the lock.
- Same-filesystem placement is what makes the swap a rename. If `Interface/` is a symlink to another filesystem, the later rename fails with `EXDEV`. Detect it here by comparing `st_dev` of `stage/<tx>` and `Interface/AddOns` and fail early with `io` (decided: no cross-device fallback in M1; the error message names the condition).
- The stage dir sits inside `Interface/`. The client scans only `Interface/AddOns/`, so `.omaddons/stage/` is invisible to it (D7).
- Out of scope: the swap itself (swap bead), the lock and revalidation (commit bead), and orphan sweeping (retention bead).
acceptance_criteria: Staging a multi-folder archive produces Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/<Folder>/ for exactly the inspected roots with normalized names and nothing under Interface/AddOns changes; every staged file's size and sha256 match the inspection and files_index has path, size, mtime_ns and sha256 for every file; tree_hash is deterministic across two stagings of the same archive; staged files are 0644 and directories 0755 regardless of archive modes; exactly one syncfs and no per-file fsync per stage call; an injected error failpoint mid-staging returns an io error, leaves AddOns untouched and leaves a stage dir that cleanup prunes; all writes go through fsx and the single-writer test passes
close_reason: Inspected folders stage under Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/ with normalized names, verified sizes and hashes, fixed 0644/0755 modes, the per-file index and a deterministic tree hash, using deferred writes and one syncfs, never touching AddOns
