**Implementation decisions (src/engine/stage.rs, fsx sync counters, tests/stage.rs, tests/common/targets.rs).**
(1) **Signature:** `stage(inflight: &InflightLock, scopes: &ScopeTable, target: &Target, blob: Option<&Path>, inspected: &Inspected) -> Result<Staged>`. There is no TxCtx type yet, so holding the InflightLock proves liveness at the type level and gives the tx. scopes must include the target's client dir. blob is required when any file's source is ZipEntry; directory inputs pass None.
(2) Output: `Staged { tx, stage_dir, folders: Vec<StagedFolder { name: FolderName, path, index: state::files_index::FolderIndex } }> }`. **The existing FolderIndex supplies files (path, size, mtime_ns as i128, sha256) and tree.** That tree is fsx's TreeDigest: SHA-256 over path-sorted `path\0size\0sha256\n` lines, written 'tree:sha256:<hex>'. mtime and order do not affect it (unit-tested against a hand-built digest).
(3) Directories: `Interface/.omaddons/stage/` is created with ensure_dir_all at Immediate durability, a one-time cost per client. stage/<tx> and every folder and subdirectory are a deferred CreateDir followed by Chmod 0755 (umask-proof). Files are WriteFile from a streaming reader, deferred, mode 0644. Archive modes such as setuid and exec are never applied (tested with 0o104755 and 0o100600 entries). Hashing goes through a tee reader, because untracked sessions do not return the written hash. A size or sha256 mismatch is bad_archive with details {reason: changed, path: '<Folder>/<rel>', expected, actual}. The blob is reopened by entry index.
(4) **fsx gained thread-local durability counters:** `fsx::sync_counts() -> SyncCounts { fsync, syncfs }`. Every sync_all in sys.rs goes through one counting fsync helper, and sync_filesystem counts syncfs. Thread-local because tests run in parallel. Measured: a second staging of 61 files makes exactly 1 syncfs and 0 fsync.
(5) Same filesystem: st_dev of stage/<tx> is compared with Interface/AddOns, or with Interface/ when AddOns does not exist yet. A mismatch is an io error whose message names the condition, with a text fix. There is no cross-device fallback.
(6) Failpoints: engine.stage.begin (before anything), engine.stage.file (after the first file), engine.stage.synced (after syncfs). Each maps to an io error. The failpoint test is a lib unit test, because `failpoint::with_spec` is cfg(test)-only and the environment spec is read once per process. It also proves prune(PostCommitCleanup) removes the partial stage dir.
(7) Measured: 5 001 small files stage in about 0.3 s (debug, tmpfs). The test budget is 5 s to absorb parallel load.
(8) Test helpers: tests/common/targets.rs (`battlenet(env, code)`, `legacy_335(env)`), shared with tests/inspect.rs.

title: Per-folder atomic swaps with snapshots, SavedVariables reflink snapshots and fallback
description:
## Background

The swap is the instant at which an addon changes on disk. Vision §5.5 step 8 and the invariant: at every instant, each AddOns folder is either the complete old version or the complete new version. Without per-folder `RENAME_EXCHANGE` and `RENAME_NOREPLACE`, that claim would be false for the moment between two renames (D25). Where the filesystem does not support those flags (NTFS via ntfs-3g, some FUSE filesystems return `EINVAL`), the engine falls back to two renames under the journal and reports `atomic_swap: false` for that target. That keeps the claim honest.

Step 7 snapshots, taken just before swapping (vision §5.5, D33):
- `CloneFile` the touched folders' SavedVariables into `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/WTF/…`: the account and per-character `SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua` and `.lua.bak`. On btrfs and xfs (reflink) this is instant and uses no extra space; elsewhere it falls back to a byte copy.
- Snapshot the target's state files into `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`.

SavedVariables paths (vision §4.4):
- account: `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/SavedVariables/<Addon>.lua`;
- character: `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/<Realm>/<Char>/SavedVariables/<Addon>.lua`;
- Blizzard's own `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/SavedVariables.lua` is never touched;
- the client writes `<Addon>.lua.bak` beside each file.

`<ACCT>` is for example `123456#1` (Battle.net) or a legacy account name. Account, realm and character names are personal data and never appear in output.

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/swap.rs`. It runs inside the commit window: the caller (commit bead) holds the global lock and has created the journal (`prepared`).
- `snapshot_saved_variables(tx, client: &ClientPaths, folders: &[FolderName]) -> Result<SvManifest>`:
  - For each touched folder (added, replaced or removed), find matching files case-insensitively: `WTF/Account/*/SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua` and `.lua.bak`, plus `WTF/Account/*/*/*/SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua` and `.lua.bak`. Skip `SavedVariables.lua` itself.
  - `CloneFile` each into `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/WTF/<same relative path>` via `fsx::mutate` (the `Interface/.omaddons/` scope).
  - `SvManifest` lists every candidate path relative to `WTF/`, with its pre-transaction SHA-256 or `absent`. Decided: absent files are recorded too, because undo must be able to restore "absent" when new addon code created a SavedVariables file (undo bead).
  - The manifest is written as `snapshots/<tx>/WTF.manifest.json`. It contains account, realm and character names (local only); they are never copied into history, output or logs. Output reports counts only.
  - Records whether reflink or a byte copy was used. The byte-copy fallback costs I/O and is reported in a debug log event.
- `snapshot_state(tx, key) -> Result<()>`: `CloneFile` `targets/<key>.json`, `targets/<key>.files.json` and `registry.json` (when present) into `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`.
- `swap(journal: &mut Journal, ops: &[PlannedOp], staged: &Staged, client: &ClientPaths) -> Result<SwapReport>`, per folder in a deterministic order (folder key ascending):
  - **Replacement**: append step `exchange stage/<tx>/<F> ⇄ AddOns/<F>` (purpose `swap_in`), then `fsx::mutate(Rename { mode: Exchange })`. The live path now holds the new version and the stage path holds the old one. Then append step `rename stage/<tx>/<F> → snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/<F>` (purpose `old_to_snapshot`) and rename with `NoReplace`.
  - **New folder**: append step `noreplace stage/<tx>/<F> → AddOns/<F>`, then rename with `NoReplace`. If a folder with that name (any case; the ownership check ran under the lock, but this is the last line of defense) appeared after planning, the kernel returns `EEXIST` and the transaction fails with `plan_stale` (exit 1, retryable). A folder created after planning is never overwritten.
  - **Removal**: append step `rename AddOns/<F> → snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/<F>` (purpose `remove_to_snapshot`) with `NoReplace`.
  - The live spelling is preserved on replacement (the exchange keeps the path). The managed record stores the archive's spelling for display only (ownership bead).
  - Each rename's `actions.jsonl` line records the folder's tree hash before and after. The new tree hash comes from the stage bead's `tree_hash`; the old one comes from the existing files index for managed folders, or is computed on demand (vision §5.5).
  - After each phase (all exchanges, all snapshot moves, all removals), fsync the parent directories involved: `AddOns/`, `stage/<tx>/`, `snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`.
  - **Fallback**: when `Exchange` or `NoReplace` returns `Unsupported` (fsx-primitives maps `EINVAL`/`ENOSYS`), switch the whole target to two-rename mode for the rest of this transaction:
    - replacement = step `rename AddOns/<F> → snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/<F>` (`fallback_live_to_snapshot`), then step `rename stage/<tx>/<F> → AddOns/<F>` (`fallback_stage_to_live`);
    - new folder = an existence check followed by a plain rename (the race window is reported, not hidden).
    - Set `atomic_swap: false` for the target and emit the warning `atomic_swap_unavailable` (fix display "the AddOns filesystem does not support atomic renames; omaddons stays crash-safe through its journal", `argv: null`).
  - After the last folder, `journal.mark_swapped()`.
- Failpoints (debug builds, DEC-7), published in the engine's failpoint list: `engine.snapshot.sv`, `engine.snapshot.state`, `engine.swap.before_rename` (before every rename, after its step line), `engine.swap.after_exchange` (between exchange and snapshot move), `engine.swapped`. Fallback is forced in tests with the fsx failpoint `fsx.renameat2.einval`.
- `SwapReport { atomic_swap: bool, folders: {added, replaced, removed}, sv_files_snapshotted: usize, reflink: bool }` (derives `Serialize` + `JsonSchema`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a successful swap, every replaced folder's live tree hash equals the staged tree hash, the old version sits in `snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/<F>` with its old tree hash, and removed folders sit in `snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/<F>`.
- Every rename is preceded by a fsync'd step line in the journal, in order.
- A new folder whose name (any case) appeared after planning is never overwritten; the swap fails with `plan_stale`.
- With `fsx.renameat2.einval` injected, the swap completes with two renames per folder, `atomic_swap: false` and one `atomic_swap_unavailable` warning, and the journal records the fallback steps.
- SavedVariables of every touched folder (account and per-character `.lua` and `.lua.bak`, matched case-insensitively) are cloned into `snapshots/<tx>/WTF/…`, and the manifest lists absent candidates too. `SavedVariables.lua` is never touched.
- With the reflink fallback forced, SavedVariables are byte-copied and the report says `reflink: false`.
- Output and history contain counts only, never account, realm or character names (asserted by searching the envelope for the fixture's names).
- State files are cloned into `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/` before the swap.

## Test Plan

- Unit: path matching for SavedVariables (case variants, `.bak`, Blizzard's own file excluded).
- Integration (tempdir client dir with a synthetic `WTF/Account/123456#1/…` tree containing fake realm and character names): replacement, add and remove in one transaction; compare tree hashes and journal step lines.
- Integration: a race test that creates `foo/` in AddOns after planning and before the swap → `plan_stale`, `foo/` untouched.
- Integration: EINVAL fallback via failpoint; reflink fallback via the fsx failpoint that forces a byte copy (add `fsx.reflink.unsupported` in fsx-primitives if missing).
- Integration: failpoint `engine.swap.after_exchange=error`, then journal recovery (journal bead) restores the old tree.
- Log journal lines, tree hashes and directory listings on failure.

## Considerations

- Ordering by folder key keeps journals deterministic and makes the failure-injection matrix reproducible.
- Multi-folder addons are consistent across crashes through the journal. A `/reload` while a running-client transaction is mid-swap may briefly see mixed folders; the outcome reports `reload_required` (running-policy bead).
- `RENAME_EXCHANGE` and `RENAME_NOREPLACE` are supported on btrfs, ext4, xfs and tmpfs (vision §4.8). Test both the native and the fallback path on the tempdir's filesystem.
- Dependency added beyond the plan: `stage`, because the swap consumes `Staged` (stage paths and per-folder tree hashes).
- Out of scope: lock acquisition, revalidation, record writes and cleanup (commit bead); recovery logic (journal bead); restoring SavedVariables (undo bead).
acceptance_criteria: After a swap every replaced folder's live tree hash equals the staged tree hash and the old version sits in snapshots/<tx>/AddOns with its old tree hash, and removed folders sit in snapshots/<tx>/AddOns; every rename is preceded by a fsync'd journal step line in order; a new folder whose name appeared after planning is never overwritten and the swap fails with plan_stale; with fsx.renameat2.einval injected the swap completes with two renames per folder, atomic_swap false and one atomic_swap_unavailable warning; SavedVariables of every touched folder (account and per-character .lua and .lua.bak, case-insensitive) are cloned into snapshots/<tx>/WTF with absent candidates listed in the manifest and SavedVariables.lua never touched; with reflink forced off SavedVariables are byte-copied and reported; output and history contain counts only, never account, realm or character names; state files are cloned into the state snapshots dir before the swap
close_reason: Staged folders swap into AddOns per folder with RENAME_EXCHANGE or RENAME_NOREPLACE under the journal (new folders first, then old versions and removals to the snapshot), never overwriting a folder that appeared after planning, with an honest two-rename fallback; touched SavedVariables and state files are snapshotted first, reporting counts only

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/engine/swap.rs, src/engine/testing.rs, fsx clone-kind reporting, FolderIndex::digest).**
(1) **API:** `swap(&mut s, &mut journal, &[SwapOp], &staged, &client) -> SwapReport { atomic_swap, folders: SwapCounts { added, replaced, removed }, warnings (serde-skipped) }`. `SwapOp::{Add { name }, Replace { name, live, old_tree: Option<TreeDigest> }, Remove { live, old_tree }}`. (2) **SavedVariables are reported separately:** `snapshot_saved_variables(&mut s, &tx, &client, &folders) -> SvReport { sv_files_snapshotted, reflink }` and `snapshot_state(&mut s, &paths, &tx, &key)`. The driver calls both before `swap` and merges the counts into its outcome. reflink is true only when every clone was a reflink (or nothing needed cloning).
(3) **Phases:** (a) swap in, in folder-key order: Add is NoReplace after a case-insensitive absence check; Replace is Exchange. (b) Exchanged old versions (now at the stage path) move to snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/<live>. (c) Removals move AddOns/<live> there too. Then mark_swapped. Every rename is journaled first; the failpoint engine.swap.before_rename sits between the step line and the rename.
(4) **plan_stale (retryable, PlanStaleSource::Replan):** a folder of the same name in any case appeared in AddOns (pre-checked before any rename, re-checked in fallback), a live folder to replace or remove disappeared, or a swap-in rename fails a precondition (exact-name race). Tested: AddOns/bar created after staging Bar leaves bar untouched and Foo still old.
(5) **Fallback:** the first Unsupported from a flagged rename (that step is journaled, never ran, and recovery's identity check skips it) switches the rest of the transaction to plain renames. title: Undo: revert transactions with conflict detection and the SavedVariables policy
description:
## Background

Cheap, precise undo is what makes agent autonomy safe (D6, D31): an agent can update everything, and a human (or the agent) can revert exactly what happened. Vision §5.5 "Undo":

- `omaddons undo` reverts the most recent transaction. `undo <tx>` reverts an older one only if no later transaction of any kind (including `repair` and `adopt`) touched the same folders; otherwise `undo_conflict` (exit 4). `undo --last-by <actor>` reverts that actor's most recent transaction.
- The output always names the transaction being reverted.
- Undo is itself a transaction, snapshotted, so it can be undone.
- Folders and state records are restored. SavedVariables follow `--saved-variables auto|restore|keep`:
  - `auto` (the default), per file:
    - unchanged since the transaction ⇒ nothing to do (the new code never ran);
    - changed ⇒ the current file is cloned into the undo transaction, then restored, so nothing is lost;
    - client running ⇒ the SavedVariables part is skipped and reported as `saved_variables_deferred`, with `fix: omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` once the client exits. Folders follow the running policy.
  - `restore`: like `auto`, but refused with `game_running` instead of deferred while the client runs.
  - `keep`: SavedVariables are never touched.
- SavedVariables are never written while the target's client runs, under any policy or flag (D33).

Write scope (fsx table): `<client dir>/WTF/Account/**/SavedVariables/<owned folder>.lua[.bak]` (account and per-character) is writable by the install-engine undo only. The rest of `WTF/` is off-limits (the whole-tree row belongs to `backup restore`, M3).

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/undo.rs`; `engine::undo(req: UndoRequest, ctx) -> Result<TxOutcome>`, where `UndoRequest { selector: Latest | Tx(TxId) | LastBy(Actor), sv_policy: Auto | Restore | Keep, dry_run, while_running }`.
- Selecting the transaction, from `history.jsonl` (state-records reader; torn lines skipped):
  - `Latest` = the newest entry with `result: ok` whose kind is undoable. Undoable kinds are install, update, remove, undo and (later) adopt, sync, restore and repair. `backup` entries are not undoable (vision §5.1).
  - `LastBy(actor)` = the newest such entry with that actor.
  - `Tx(id)` = that entry; absent → `not_found` (exit 3).
  - `Latest` with an empty history → `not_found` with fix `omaddons history`.
- Conflict check, decided: by folder key per target, over every later history entry of any kind. Any later entry touching a folder key that the selected transaction touched → `undo_conflict` (exit 4), with `details: {tx, conflicting: [{tx, kind, folders}]}` and fix `omaddons undo <newest conflicting tx>` (argv set). Undoing the most recent transaction never conflicts.
- Snapshot availability: the transaction's snapshots (`<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/` and `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`) must exist. Pruned by retention → `not_found`, message "snapshot for <tx> was pruned by retention".
- Building the undo as a transaction: undo reuses the commit bead's driver with `TxKind::Undo`. Undo needs no network and no staging from an archive, so it uses a "restore" source: the folders to bring back are in `snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`.
  - Decided: undo first `CloneFile`s each snapshot folder tree into `stage/<undo-tx>/` and swaps from there. The original snapshot stays intact (it may still be needed, for example to undo the undo's undo), and the undo transaction gets its own snapshot of what it replaces. The swap and journal are the same code as any transaction.
  - Inverse op per original op: an original add → undo removes the folder (moved into `snapshots/<undo-tx>/AddOns/`); an original replace → undo replaces the live folder with the snapshot's old version; an original remove → undo adds the folder back from the snapshot (`NoReplace`; if a folder with that key exists now, that is a later transaction's doing and the conflict check already refused).
  - State records: restore `targets/<key>.json` and `targets/<key>.files.json` contents from `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`, with the generation set to current + 1 (generations never go backwards), written through the commit payload. Records of other addons changed by the original transaction (for example a degraded previous owner after `--force`) are restored too.
  - History: the undo entry carries `kind: undo` and `undoes: <tx>`.
- SavedVariables, using the original transaction's `WTF.manifest.json` (swap bead), per file in the manifest:
  - `keep` → skip all files.
  - Compute the current state (hash or absent). Equal to the manifest's pre-transaction state → nothing to do.
  - Changed, and the client is not running: clone the current file into `snapshots/<undo-tx>/WTF/…` (so the undo is undoable), then restore. Restoring means: pre-transaction hash present → `CloneFile { from: snapshots/<tx>/WTF/… }` into a unique temp name beside the live file, then `Rename { mode: Replace }` onto the live path (both fsx ops, so the live file is replaced atomically); pre-transaction absent → rename the live file into `snapshots/<undo-tx>/WTF/…` (deletion is not an fsx op).
  - Changed, and the client is running: `auto` → skip the SavedVariables part entirely and emit `saved_variables_deferred` with fix `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` (argv set). `restore` → refuse the whole undo with `game_running` (exit 4) before any change. Running state is evaluated again under the lock (running-policy bead, `RestoreSavedVariables` op).
  - A deferred follow-up `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` after the original undo, decided: allowed and SavedVariables-only. If `<tx>` was already undone by an undo transaction whose SavedVariables part was deferred, this restores only the SavedVariables (folders are already reverted) as a new `undo` transaction with no folder ops. It is recognized from history: a later `undo` entry with `undoes: <tx>` and `sv_deferred: true`.
- Folders follow the running policy (running-policy bead). For example, undoing an install while running removes a folder with a loaded TOC, which is refused under `safe` unless `--while-running`.
- `--dry-run` returns the undo plan with `dry_run: true`, `tx: null` (DEC-16).
- The outcome's `data` names the reverted transaction (`undoes`), plus `changes`, `reload_required`, `atomic_swap` and `sv: {restored, deferred, unchanged}` counts. Never file paths inside `WTF/` and never account or character names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `undo` after an install, update or remove restores every folder byte-for-byte (tree hashes equal the pre-transaction trees) and restores the target record contents with a new, higher generation.
- `undo` of an `undo` re-applies the original change.
- `undo <older tx>` when a later transaction of any kind touched the same folder fails with `undo_conflict` (exit 4) naming the conflicting transaction. When the later transactions touched other folders, it succeeds.
- `undo --last-by agent` reverts only the newest agent transaction and leaves later human transactions in place (when they touch other folders).
- SavedVariables: unchanged files untouched (mtime and hash unchanged); changed files cloned into the undo snapshot and then restored; files created by the new code renamed away; `keep` touches nothing.
- Client running: `auto` reverts folders (subject to the policy) and defers SavedVariables with `saved_variables_deferred`; `restore` refuses with `game_running` and changes nothing; a later `undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` with the client stopped restores only the SavedVariables.
- A pruned snapshot yields `not_found` with the retention message.
- Output never contains account, realm or character names.

## Test Plan

- Integration (synthetic targets with a `WTF/Account/123456#1/Realm/Char/SavedVariables/` tree; `file:` refs; fake `/proc` for running state):
  - install → undo → compare trees; update → undo; remove → undo; undo → undo;
  - the conflict matrix: install A, update A, undo the first install → conflict; install A, install B, undo A → ok;
  - `--last-by` with mixed actors;
  - the SavedVariables matrix (unchanged, changed, created, `.bak` files) × policy (auto/restore/keep) × running (yes/no);
  - the deferred follow-up flow;
  - a pruned snapshot.
- Unit: conflict detection over synthetic history lists; inverse-op computation.
- Log history lines, manifests and tree hashes on failure.

## Considerations

- Undo restores folders from snapshots, never from blobs (vision §5.5 retention: "CurseForge/Wago undo uses snapshots, never blobs"). That works offline and for any source.
- `sv_deferred` and `undoes` are new history fields. Coordinate the history record schema with the state-records bead; both derive `JsonSchema` (DEC-3).
- Undoing a transaction that registered a target does not unregister it. Registration is identity, not addon state.
- Out of scope: the `undo`/`history` CLI surface (cmd-undo-history bead) and `doctor undo` (M4, which resolves to `omaddons undo <tx>`).
acceptance_criteria: undo after install, update or remove restores every folder byte-for-byte and restores the target record with a new higher generation; undo of an undo re-applies the original change; undo of an older tx whose folders a later tx of any kind touched fails with undo_conflict (exit 4) naming the conflicting tx, and succeeds when later txs touched other folders; undo --last-by agent reverts only the newest agent tx; unchanged SavedVariables are untouched, changed ones are cloned into the undo snapshot then restored, files created by the new code are renamed away, and keep touches nothing; with the client running auto defers SavedVariables with saved_variables_deferred, restore refuses with game_running and changes nothing, and a later undo <tx> --saved-variables restore restores only SavedVariables; a pruned snapshot yields not_found with the retention message; output never contains account, realm or character names
close_reason: engine undo: selection, folder-key conflicts, snapshot-staged inverse swap, per-addon record restore, SavedVariables policy with journaled restore and deferred follow-up

**Implementation decisions (src/engine/undo.rs).**
(1) **API:** `engine::undo(&UndoRequest { selector: Latest | Tx(id) | LastBy(actor), sv_policy: Auto | Restore | Keep, dry_run, while_running, reason, targets: Vec<DiscoveredTarget> }, &EngineCtx) -> Result<UndoOutcome { undoes, #[flatten] outcome: TxOutcome, sv: SvCounts { restored, deferred, unchanged, kept } }>`. The engine picks the target whose key the reverted entry names from `targets` (`target_not_found` if it is gone). `kept` was added to the bead's counts: under `keep`, changed files are neither restored nor deferred.
(2) **Selection/conflicts:** Latest/LastBy = newest `is_undoable()` entry (by actor); Tx absent or a backup → `not_found` (fix `omaddons history`). Conflicts by folder key on the same target over every later entry; details `{tx, conflicting: [{tx, kind, folders}]}`, fix `omaddons undo <newest>`; when the newest conflicting entry is an undo of this tx the message says "already undone by".
(3) **Folders:** inverse ops from the history ops against AddOns now: add → Remove (already gone → record-only), replace → Replace from the snapshot (live gone → Add), remove → Add from the snapshot (a folder put back outside omaddons → `undo_conflict`, fix: move it away). The snapshot folders are cloned into `stage/<undo-tx>/` by a new `stage::stage_trees` (reflinks, symlinks recreated, same index as archive staging), then the normal journal + swap run with `Writer::Undo`. A missing snapshot (client or state side, or a needed folder) → `not_found` "snapshot for <tx> was pruned by retention".
(4) **Record/index:** per addon, not wholesale: every addon in the reverted ops comes back from `<state>/snapshots/<tx>/<key>.json` (or goes, if absent there); an owner the transaction took folders from with `--force` gets them back with its old state; all other addons stay as they are now; generation = current + 1. Files index per touched folder key: the snapshot's entry, else removed. Changes: install/update/remove per addon with from/to versions and the folder lists.
(5) **SavedVariables:** classified against `snapshots/<tx>/WTF.manifest.json`; the undo snapshots its own SavedVariables first (so it is undoable), then after `swapped` restores each changed file by cloning the old version into `snapshots/<undo-tx>/sv-restore/<attempt>/…` and renaming it over the live file (the SV scope admits only `<Folder>.lua[.bak]`, so no temp file beside it); a file the new code created is renamed into `snapshots/<undo-tx>/sv-created/…`. The list rides in a new optional journal field `CommitPayload.sv_restore`, and roll-forward re-applies it idempotently (files already at their target hash are skipped). Errors never name a SavedVariables path.
(6) **Running:** folder ops go through `running::evaluate` like any transaction (undoing an install while running is refused under safe without --while-running). auto + running → SavedVariables deferred, warning `saved_variables_deferred` with fix argv `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore`, history `sv_deferred: true` (new field). restore + running → `game_running` before any change. The follow-up `undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` is SavedVariables-only (no folder ops; history ops are `record` ops on the reverted folders so later undos see it). A plain `undo <tx>` after a deferred undo is `undo_conflict` with that follow-up as fix and `omaddons undo <deferring tx>` as alternative.
(7) **fsx changes:** `sys::clone_file` takes a `Durability`; `CloneFile` may be deferred in untracked staging sessions (one syncfs per stage, as archive staging). `snapshot_saved_variables` errors no longer name files.

title: Content-addressed blob cache with LRU cap and pins
description:
## Background

Step 2 of the transaction engine (vision §5.5) downloads every selected archive into a content-addressed cache before anything else happens. Because blobs are keyed by their SHA-256, the same archive is stored once no matter how many targets or transactions use it, and reinstall, undo and cross-target copies work offline. The cache must stay bounded: `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` (1 GiB, overridable in config) with least-recently-used eviction. Blobs that are still referenced are pinned and never evicted. A pinned blob is one referenced by an installed addon record, a retained transaction, or an unexpired plan.

CurseForge and Wago archives must never be cached or persisted (their API terms forbid it; vision §5.7, D4). Those sources arrive in M5, but the cache API has to make the rule enforceable now: CurseForge/Wago downloads go to the transaction's stage dir only.

Placeholders: `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache` under the home directory); `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state`).

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/blobs.rs`, type `BlobCache` built from `Paths` (paths bead): root `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/`.
- Layout: `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/<sha256-hex>` (64 lowercase hex chars, no extension). Temporary downloads live at `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/.tmp-<tx>-<n>` and carry the transaction id, so an orphaned temp blob can be recognized: its in-flight lock (`<state>/omaddons/inflight/<tx>.lock`, fsx-lock bead) is free.
- `BlobCache::store_stream(tx: TxId, reader: impl Read, expected: Option<ExpectedHash>, cacheable: bool) -> Result<BlobRef>`:
  - Streams the reader into the temp file through `fsx::mutate` with `Op::WriteFile { content: Content::Reader(..) }` in an untracked session (DEC-10, DEC-11), hashing SHA-256 while streaming.
  - Enforces `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB, from `src/limits.rs`) while streaming. Exceeding it aborts with `archive_too_large` (exit 4).
  - On success renames the temp file to `<sha256>` with `Op::Rename { mode: NoReplace }`. If a blob with that hash already exists, the temp file is pruned (`PruneReason::PostCommitCleanup`) and the existing blob is used, so identical content is never stored twice.
  - `cacheable: false` (CurseForge/Wago, M5) writes into the caller-provided stage path instead and never under `blobs/`. Decided: the flag is a required parameter, not a default, so a future source cannot forget it.
- `ExpectedHash` is a non-exhaustive enum with a single M1 variant, `Sha256(hex)`. SHA-256 is the blob identity. Decided: the `Md5` (WoWInterface, M2) and `Sha1` (CurseForge, M5) variants are added by the beads that add those sources, together with the `md-5`/`sha1` crates, so no unused crate or dead variant lands now. When an expected hash is given, it is checked against the streamed digest. A mismatch prunes the temp file and returns `hash_mismatch` (exit 1, retryable once: the caller may re-download a single time).
- `BlobCache::get(sha) -> Option<BlobRef>` and `BlobCache::open(&BlobRef) -> Result<File>` for the planner and undo. Every `get` that returns a blob updates its last-use time.
- Last use: decided — recorded in `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/index.json` (`{sha256: {size, last_used_ns}}`, written via an fsx untracked session), not file atime, because atime is often disabled (`noatime`, `relatime`). The index is derived data. If it is missing or corrupt it is rebuilt from a directory listing, with last use set to file mtime.
- `BlobCache::evict(pins: &BTreeSet<Sha256>) -> EvictReport`: if total size exceeds `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, remove unpinned blobs oldest-last-use first until under the cap, each via `fsx::prune(PruneReason::Retention, path)`. Pinned blobs are never removed even if the cap stays exceeded; the report says so. The pin set is computed by the caller (retention bead) from installed records, retained transactions and unexpired plans (plans are M4; M1 passes none).
- Orphan temp blobs (`.tmp-<tx>-*` whose in-flight lock is free) are removed by `evict` as part of the same pass.
- The configured cap comes from `config.toml` when overridden (the config bead exposes overridable limits); this bead takes the cap as a parameter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Storing the same bytes twice yields one file `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/<sha256>` and the same `BlobRef`.
- A stream larger than `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` fails with `archive_too_large` and leaves no temp file behind.
- A provided expected SHA-256 that does not match fails with `hash_mismatch` (exit 1, retryable) and leaves no temp file behind.
- `cacheable: false` never creates anything under `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/`.
- `evict` brings the cache under the cap by removing least-recently-used unpinned blobs, never removes a pinned blob, and removes orphan temp blobs whose in-flight lock is free.
- All writes and removals go through `fsx::mutate` and `fsx::prune(PruneReason::Retention | PostCommitCleanup)`; the single-writer test passes.
- A missing or corrupt `index.json` is rebuilt without error.

## Test Plan

- Unit: hash-while-streaming equals `sha2::Sha256` of the same bytes; dedupe of identical content; size cap enforcement using a reader that yields `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES + 1` bytes lazily (do not allocate 512 MiB; make the cap injectable for tests and assert the production default separately).
- Unit: `ExpectedHash::Sha256` match and mismatch; the mismatch leaves no temp file.
- Unit: LRU order with an injected clock; pinned blobs survive; cap smaller than pinned total leaves the cache over cap and reports it.
- Integration: two threads storing the same content concurrently end with one blob and no temp files.
- Integration: an orphan `.tmp-<tx>-0` with a free in-flight lock is removed by `evict`; one whose in-flight lock is held is kept.
- Log test inputs (sizes, hashes) and the directory listing on failure.

## Considerations

- Downloads run without the global lock (vision §5.5 step 2). Uniqueness of temp names comes from the tx id plus a counter, never a fixed name (the reference implementation's fixed `.tmp` name was defect R4).
- Renaming the temp file onto the hash name with `NoReplace` makes concurrent stores of the same content safe: the loser sees `EEXIST`, prunes its temp file and uses the winner's blob. Contents are identical by construction.
- The blob cache is derived data. Deleting the whole directory is always safe, except that undo of a transaction then needs its snapshot (undo uses snapshots for folders, so it still works).
- Eviction runs outside the global lock except for the trash rename inside `fsx::prune`.
- Out of scope: the pin computation (retention bead), source hashes for WoWI/CurseForge (M2/M5), plan pins (M4).
- Dependencies added beyond the plan: `fsx-lock`, because recognizing orphan temp blobs requires probing the per-transaction in-flight lock (`InflightLock::is_live(tx)`); and `fsx-prune-guard`, because every removal here goes through `fsx::prune()`, which that bead provides.
acceptance_criteria: Storing the same bytes twice yields one blob file named by its sha256 and the same BlobRef; a stream larger than DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES fails with archive_too_large and leaves no temp file; a mismatching provided hash fails with hash_mismatch (exit 1, retryable) and leaves no temp file; cacheable false never writes under the blobs dir; evict brings the cache under the cap by removing least-recently-used unpinned blobs, never removes a pinned blob, and removes orphan temp blobs whose in-flight lock is free; all writes and removals go through fsx::mutate and fsx::prune and the single-writer test passes; a missing or corrupt index.json is rebuilt without error
close_reason: Archives are stored once by SHA-256 under the cache with streaming hash, size cap and expected-hash checks that leave nothing behind on failure, uncached storage for terms-restricted sources, LRU eviction that never touches pins, and an orphan sweep of dead transactions' temp dirs, all through fsx

comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/engine/blobs.rs, tests/blobs.rs).**
(1) **Temp layout follows prune-guard, not the bead text:** downloads stream into `<cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>/blob-<n>` (paths.cache_tmp, n from a per-cache atomic counter). prune can only remove whole tmp/<tx> dirs, and skips them while the transaction lives, so no individual temp file is ever pruned.
(2) **No temp file survives any outcome:** the write is fsx's atomic WriteFile, fed by a guarding reader. The reader fails the stream past the size cap, and at EOF when an expected hash does not match. The failed atomic write discards its own temp, and the guard's typed error (archive_too_large or hash_mismatch) is returned instead of the io error. Success renames into blobs/<sha256> with **RenameMode::Replace instead of NoReplace**: a file already there has the same bytes by construction (SHA-256 identity), so replacing it is harmless and leaves no losing temp file. 4 concurrent stores end as one blob and zero temp files (tested).
(3) **API:** `BlobCache::new(&paths).with_max_download(n).with_clock(fn)`, `store_stream(&scopes, &tx, reader, Option<&ExpectedHash>, &Storage) -> BlobRef { sha256, size, path }`, `get(&scopes, sha) -> Option<BlobRef>` (case-insensitive; marks it used), `open(&BlobRef)`, and `evict(&scopes, &pins, cap) -> EvictReport { evicted, freed_bytes, remaining_bytes, over_cap, orphans_removed }`. **The cacheable flag is an enum:** `Storage::{Cache, Uncached { dest }}`, a required parameter, so a source must state it. Uncached writes go to dest (a client stage path, Writer::Mutating) and never touch <cache>.
(4) hash_mismatch is always attempt 1 (retryable); the caller marks a second failure `.retryable(false)`. archive_too_large carries details {limit, config_key: limits.download_max_bytes}. ExpectedHash comparisons ignore case.
(5) Index: blobs/index.json {sha: {size, last_used_ns}}, written atomically with Writer::Derived after every store and get. A missing or corrupt index is rebuilt from a listing using mtimes. Concurrent writers may lose a last-use update, which is acceptable for derived LRU data.
(6) evict lists 64-hex blobs, orders by last use (ties by name), and skips pins until the total is at most the cap, reporting over_cap when pins prevent that. It sweeps tmp/<tx> dirs whose in-flight lock is free. One GlobalLock::acquire covers both prune calls (Retention for blobs, PostCommitCleanup for tmp dirs) and is only taken when something is to be removed.
(7) The download cap is injectable for tests; the production default is asserted to be 512 MiB. A lazy reader proves the cap without allocating.

Unit (6): dedupe plus get, open and uppercase, the cap with a lazy reader (production 512 MiB asserted), expected hash match and mismatch, Uncached writes only dest, LRU with pins and over_cap, corrupt and missing index rebuild. tests/blobs.rs (2): 4 concurrent identical stores give 1 blob and 0 temp files; the orphan sweep spares live transactions · found: none

title: Lock, revalidate and commit: the transaction driver
description:
## Background

This bead is the transaction driver: it runs vision §5.5 steps 5–9 in order and is the only code that holds the global lock for a mutation. The lock is held only for revalidate → journal → swap → commit (milliseconds), never across network I/O (D24), so concurrent omaddons processes practically never see `locked`. The vision's steps:

5. **Stage** (no lock), under `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/`.
6. **Lock and revalidate.** Acquire the global lock and run recovery. If any affected target's `generation` changed since step 1, re-check ownership and folder state without network (the archives are already staged) and re-plan once. If it still conflicts, fail with `plan_stale` (exit 1, retryable).
7. **Journal and SavedVariables snapshot.** Write the journal `prepared` (fsync), clone touched SavedVariables, snapshot the target's state files.
8. **Swap**, per folder, with step records.
9. **Commit.** Write the target record with `generation + 1` and the per-file index; append `history.jsonl`; mark the journal `committed`; release the lock. Afterwards: rewrite `status.json` (monotonic), delete the journal, prune the stage dir, run retention.

Each transaction also holds an in-flight lock (`<state>/omaddons/inflight/<tx>.lock`) from planning until cleanup. A held flock is the only proof of liveness anywhere in the program (D23). Targets are registered (ULID key and marker) by the first mutating command that touches them, and only under the global lock (vision §5.1, §5.2 step 7).

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`.

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/tx.rs`; entry point `engine::run(req: TxRequest, ctx: &EngineCtx) -> Result<TxOutcomes>`. Commands (install, remove, undo) call it; they never sequence engine steps themselves.
- Sequence:
  1. Create `TxId` (ULID) and acquire `InflightLock` (fsx-lock bead).
  2. Call `plan::plan` (plan bead). With `dry_run`, return the plan as the outcome (DEC-16) and release the in-flight lock. A plan with no ops returns `ok` with an empty change list and no transaction (idempotence).
  3. Per target with ops: `stage::stage` (no lock).
  4. `GlobalLock::acquire(LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT)` (5 s) → on timeout `locked` (exit 5, retryable, `details.holder` from the lock file contents).
  5. `journal::recover_all(&guard)`. Recovered transactions add `journal_recovered` warnings to this outcome.
  6. Registration: for each affected target without a key, `registry.ensure_registered(target, &guard)` assigns the ULID and writes the registry entry and the `Interface/.omaddons/target.json` marker via fsx.
  7. Revalidate: reload each affected `TargetRecord` and compare its `generation` with `plan.generations`. On a change: re-read the inventory, rebuild folder ops from the already-inspected and staged folders, re-run `ownership::check` and `running::evaluate` (fresh running state), and re-plan once. Ops that became unnecessary (for example the same release already installed by a concurrent transaction) drop out; an empty result means a no-op (vision checkpoint: "or one becomes a no-op"). Any conflict → `plan_stale` (exit 1, retryable) with `details.cause` holding the underlying code (`ownership_conflict`, `case_collision`, `game_running`, …). Without a change, still re-run `running::evaluate`, because running state is live and may differ from plan time.
  8. Per target: build the `CommitPayload` (new record with `generation + 1`, files-index entries from `Staged`, history record), call `Journal::create` (prepared), `swap::snapshot_saved_variables`, `swap::snapshot_state`, then `swap::swap`.
  9. Write `targets/<key>.json` (generation + 1, updated `AddonRecord`s with `tx_id`, `installed_at`, `folders`, `state`; degraded previous owners on forced transfers) and `targets/<key>.files.json` (entries for removed folders dropped, new ones added) via state-records. Then append `history.jsonl`: `{tx, kind, at, target, actor, reason?, argv, ops[], result}`, where `ops` lists folder ops with folder names and tree hashes and `result` is `ok`. Then `journal.mark_committed()`.
  10. Release the global lock. Measure the hold time from acquire to release and emit a `log` event `{"msg":"lock released","tx","lock_held_ms"}` through the Reporter when `-v` is given (the engine-tests bead asserts < 50 ms from it).
  11. After the lock: rewrite `status.json` (state-records' monotonic writer), `journal.finish()`, prune the stage dir (`PruneReason::PostCommitCleanup`), run the retention hook (retention bead; a no-op until it lands), release and prune the in-flight lock file.
- Multi-target requests: one transaction per target, in target-key order. Each target commits independently. A failure in one target is a per-item failure (`partial: true`, exit 0; `--strict` → exit 6 via the command layer); targets already committed stay committed and each remains undoable.
- Error paths: any error after staging and before `prepared` prunes the stage dir and releases the locks with no journal written. An error after `prepared` but before `swapped` triggers immediate in-process rollback through the same code path as recovery (`journal::rollback(&guard, tx)`), then returns the error. An error after `swapped` rolls forward. The invariant holds either way.
- `TxOutcome` per target (derives `Serialize` + `JsonSchema`; this is the M1 `data` core for install, remove and undo): `{target, key, tx, kind, dry_run, changes: [Change], atomic_swap, reload_required, warnings}`. `commands` gains `{action: "undo", command: "omaddons undo <tx>", argv: ["omaddons","undo","<tx>"], destructive: false}`.
- Failpoints (debug builds, DEC-7). The canonical list is `pub const FAILPOINTS: &[&str]` in `src/engine/mod.rs`, so the engine-tests bead iterates over it: `engine.plan.done`, `engine.stage.synced`, `engine.lock.acquired`, `engine.recovered`, `engine.registered`, `engine.revalidated`, `engine.journal.prepared`, `engine.snapshot.sv`, `engine.snapshot.state`, `engine.swap.before_rename`, `engine.swap.after_exchange`, `engine.swapped`, `engine.record.written`, `engine.history.appended`, `engine.committed`, `engine.unlocked`, `engine.cleanup.done`. The swap and stage beads contribute their names to the same list.
- `TxKind` values driven in M1: `install`, `update`, `remove`, `undo` (undo bead).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A successful install produces: folders swapped; `targets/<key>.json` with generation incremented by exactly 1; `targets/<key>.files.json` covering every managed file; one `history.jsonl` entry with actor, reason (when given) and the verbatim argv; journal and stage dir gone; in-flight lock released; `status.json` rewritten.
- The global lock is never held during plan, download, inspect or staging (asserted by a failpoint-`sleep` test: a second process acquires the lock while the first is in `engine.stage.synced=sleep:1000`).
- A generation change between plan and lock triggers exactly one re-plan. A concurrent install of the same release becomes a no-op. A conflicting change fails with `plan_stale` (exit 1, retryable) with `details.cause`.
- The lock timeout yields `locked` (exit 5, retryable) with holder details.
- An `error` failpoint at each step before `swapped` leaves every folder wholly old; at each step after `swapped` leaves every folder wholly new with the records written. Both are verified in-process.
- First mutation of an unregistered target assigns its key and writes the marker under the lock.
- `-v` emits a `lock released` log event with `lock_held_ms`.
- `FAILPOINTS` lists every failpoint name hit in `src/engine/` (a test greps the source for `failpoint::hit("engine.` and compares against the list).

## Test Plan

- Integration (in-process, `error`-mode failpoints, `file:` refs from fixture archives, synthetic targets from `tests/common/trees.rs`): happy path install, update and remove; a failpoint at every name in `FAILPOINTS` with the invariant checked by tree hashes; generation-change re-plan, using a second thread that commits in between (synchronized by failpoint `sleep`); `plan_stale` cause propagation; registration on first mutation.
- Integration: a lock-not-held-during-staging test using two processes (the test binary re-invoking itself through a helper test, or the CLI once cmd-install lands; until then a helper thread with its own open file description, since flock is per open file description).
- Unit: `CommitPayload` construction; files-index merge (removed folders dropped).
- Crash (`abort`) tests across processes live in the engine-tests bead.
- Log the failpoint name, journal lines and tree hashes on failure.

## Considerations

- Keep everything that can run outside the lock outside it. Hashing, extraction and SavedVariables enumeration (not cloning) can be prepared before acquiring the lock. If the hold time misses the 50 ms target on fixtures, move preparation work out first, and never weaken the journal's fsyncs.
- Dependency added beyond the plan: `registry`, because registration of unregistered targets must happen under the global lock this bead holds.
- `status.json` is written after the lock is released and is monotonic. A lost race only delays the widget's doorbell (vision §5.6).
- Out of scope: undo semantics (undo bead), retention policy (retention bead), command-level rendering and target selection (E7 command beads).
acceptance_criteria: A successful install swaps folders, increments the target generation by exactly 1, writes the files index for every managed file, appends one history entry with actor, reason and verbatim argv, removes journal and stage dir, releases the in-flight lock and rewrites status.json; the global lock is never held during plan, download, inspect or staging; a generation change between plan and lock triggers exactly one re-plan, a concurrent install of the same release becomes a no-op, and a conflicting change fails with plan_stale (exit 1, retryable) carrying details.cause; lock timeout yields locked (exit 5, retryable) with holder details; an error failpoint before swapped leaves every folder wholly old and after swapped leaves every folder wholly new with records written; the first mutation of an unregistered target assigns its key and writes the marker under the lock; -v emits a lock released log event with lock_held_ms; FAILPOINTS lists every engine failpoint name in the source
close_reason: The transaction driver runs plan, stage, a short lock window (recover, register, offline re-check, journal, snapshots, swap, record, index, history, commit), status and cleanup, one transaction per target, recovering any in-window error in process so folders are always wholly old or wholly new

Each target is one transaction (one journal, one stage dir, one history entry, independently undoable). Per-target errors are PlanFailures (target only); committed targets stay committed.
(3) **Under the lock:** recover_all (warnings returned in TxOutcomes.warnings), register via LockedRegistry::ensure_registered when the key is None, then **rejudge every planned addon offline** (plan::rejudge) against the current record, inventory and running state. A change that became unnecessary drops out; if none remain the outcome has tx None and kind None (a no-op). A rejudge error becomes plan_stale (retryable, details { cause, cause_message }) when the generation changed since planning, otherwise the error itself (for example game_running because the client just started). Then Journal::create(prepared), snapshot SV and state, swap (marks swapped), save the record and files index, append history, mark_committed. The session is a Tx session logging to <state>/snapshots/<tx>/actions.jsonl.
(5) **In-process recovery:** any error after Journal::create calls `journal::recover_tx` (new: the owner's recovery without the liveness check). If it rolled forward (phase swapped), the transaction stands and the outcome is success; otherwise the original error is returned. An error before prepared just propagates; cleanup prunes the stage dir.
(6) Cleanup (best effort, one prune with LockUse::Acquire after dropping the in-flight lock): journal, stage dir, cache_tmp(tx) and the in-flight lock file, for each target tx and for plan_tx. status.json is rewritten after unlock from this record plus other targets' records and metadata taken from the existing status file. Retention is a no-op until 6.8.

JournalLine now has a hand-written Deserialize over a JSON value, plus a round-trip test with a non-empty index. (b) --file installs all had release_id <ref>@local, so a different zip looked already current. A local zip's identity is now sha256:<content>, and a directory gets a fresh dir:<ulid> (always reinstalls). (c) stage() tolerates an existing stage dir (several addons per transaction).
(8) `engine::FAILPOINTS` lists all 22 engine failpoints; a unit test scans src/engine for failpoint::hit("engine.…") and compares.
(9) Tests (unit, src/engine/tx.rs with engine::testing::TxScene: --file zips, a NoNetwork Http, injected running set): first install (registration marker, generation 1, files index, history with reason/argv/actor, no leftovers, status.json); update with replace and drop, then remove, reinstall, no-op; **the failpoint matrix** (every FAILPOINTS name except plan.downloaded and recover.step: before swapped is wholly old with generation unchanged, from swapped on is wholly new with record and one history line, and a rerun converges with no leftovers); the lock free during staging (another handle acquires it during engine.stage.synced=sleep); concurrent same release becomes a no-op; a concurrent change makes plan_stale with cause unmanaged_folder; a held lock gives locked (exit 5, retryable, holder command). title: Engine failure-injection matrix and concurrency tests (M1 checkpoints)
description:
## Background

The engine's reliability claims are high-confidence only because each is proven by a specific test (vision §9). This bead is the companion test suite for E6. It covers the M1 checkpoints that need real processes: crashes, concurrent invocations, and a reader racing a live swap. The individual engine beads carry their own in-process tests with `error`-mode failpoints. This bead adds the cross-process matrix. The vision's M1 checkpoints it proves (§7):

- A failure injected at every engine step leaves each folder wholly old or wholly new; recovery happens only under the lock; a reader running during a live swap reports `tx_in_progress` and changes nothing.
- Two concurrent installs into the same target both complete without `locked` (or one becomes a no-op). Lock hold time per commit is < 50 ms on fixtures.
- `undo` restores folders byte-for-byte. SavedVariables follow the policy (unchanged → untouched; changed → cloned then restored; client running → deferred). `undo_conflict` is raised across transaction kinds. `undo --last-by agent` reverts only that actor's transaction.
- The fallback tests (vision §5.12): the `RENAME_EXCHANGE` fallback path (injected `EINVAL`) and the reflink fallback path.
- The concurrency tests (vision §5.12): concurrent staging by two processes; a reader during a live swap never recovers; lock-hold time measured; no lost records; the lock file is never renamed or deleted by any code path.

Test hooks are debug-build only (DEC-7): `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>[=abort|=error|=sleep:<ms>|=panic][,…]`. `abort` calls `std::process::abort()`, which simulates a crash: the kernel releases the process's flocks exactly as it would for a real crash. The failpoint names are published in `engine::FAILPOINTS` (commit bead) and in the fsx failpoint list, so this matrix iterates over them instead of hard-coding names.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`.

## Technical Approach

- Test files: `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, `tests/engine_undo.rs`, `tests/engine_fallbacks.rs`. Each test builds an isolated world: HOME and the XDG dirs set to tempdirs (DEC-6), a synthetic retail target, a synthetic Forever target and a synthetic 3.3.5a target from `tests/common/trees.rs`, and fixture archives from `tests/common/archives.rs` installed through `file:` refs. There is no network: `--offline` is passed and no `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` is set.
- Tests drive the real binary (`assert_cmd`) through the M1 commands: `install`, `remove`, `undo`, `history` and `status` with `--json`. Dependencies added beyond the plan: `cmd-install`, `cmd-remove`, `cmd-undo-history` and `cmd-status`, because crash and concurrency checkpoints are defined in terms of separate processes and CLI-visible outcomes.
- Invariant oracle (`tests/common/invariant.rs`): before a transaction, record the tree hash of every AddOns folder (old state) and compute the expected new tree hashes from the fixture archive. After any crash and recovery, every folder must hash to its full old or its full new tree, never a mix. All folders of one transaction must be on the same side after recovery (multi-folder consistency through the journal).
- **Crash matrix**: for each name in `engine::FAILPOINTS` plus the stage and swap names, and for install-new, update (replace with a folder dropped) and remove:
  1. run the command with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>=abort` and expect abnormal termination;
  2. assert that `status --json` (a reader) reports `journal_pending` when a journal exists, changes nothing (hash `<state>` and the client dir before and after) and does not recover;
  3. run a mutating command that reaches the lock (install a different small fixture addon into the same target; a no-op install returns before taking the lock and does not recover) and assert a `journal_recovered` warning when a journal existed;
  4. check the invariant oracle, the record generation (old or old + 1, consistent with the folder side) and that history has at most one entry for the tx.
- **Recovery only under the lock**: hold the global lock from a helper process (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.lock.acquired=sleep:3000` on an unrelated install), then run `status`: it reports `tx_in_progress` and the journal from an earlier crash is untouched.
- **Reader during a live swap**: run an install with `engine.swapped=sleep:2000`. While it sleeps (holding the lock, after the swap, before the commit), run `status --json`: expect `tx_in_progress`, exit 0, no writes. Then let the install finish and assert the final state.
- **Concurrent installs**: two processes install the same addon into the same target at the same time (synchronized with `engine.stage.synced=sleep:500` on both). Both exit 0 and neither reports `locked`. Either both report `kind: install` against different generations (the second re-plans) or the second reports an empty change list. Records are not lost: the final record contains the addon exactly once and the generation equals the number of committed transactions. Repeat with two different addons: both end installed.
- **Concurrent staging**: two installs of different addons into the same target with overlapping staging (sleep failpoints) never share or corrupt stage dirs.
- **Lock hold time**: run 20 installs with `-v` and parse the `lock released` NDJSON log events (`lock_held_ms`). Assert every value is below 50 ms on fixtures. Log the distribution. Decided: tests run on the tempdir's filesystem; if CI-like slowness makes this flaky locally, the threshold stays and the test reports the measured values for diagnosis, rather than being relaxed silently.
- **Lock file immutability**: record the inode and existence of `<state>/omaddons/lock` at the start of the suite file and after every test in it (including crash tests); they never change. A source scan asserts no `prune(`/`Rename` call can target the lock path (a fsx deny-list unit test exists; this is the end-to-end confirmation).
- **Undo matrix** (`tests/engine_undo.rs`): byte-for-byte restore after install, update and remove; undo of undo; `undo_conflict` across kinds (install then update of the same addon, then undo of the install); `--actor agent` and `--actor human` interleaved, then `undo --last-by agent`; SavedVariables policy, with a synthetic `WTF/Account/123456#1/Realm/Char/SavedVariables/` tree and a fake `/proc` showing the client running: unchanged, changed, created × auto, restore, keep × running yes/no; the deferred follow-up `undo <tx> --saved-variables restore`.
- **Fallbacks** (`tests/engine_fallbacks.rs`): `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=fsx.renameat2.einval=error` → install succeeds with `atomic_swap: false` and an `atomic_swap_unavailable` warning, and a crash matrix subset in fallback mode keeps the invariant; the reflink fallback failpoint → SavedVariables byte-copied, undo still restores them.
- **Hostile archives end to end**: installing each hostile fixture through `file:` fails with its documented code (exit 4 or 1) and nothing is written outside `<cache>` and the stage dir, which is pruned. `blizzard_auctionui/` beside `Blizzard_AuctionUI/` on the 3.3.5a target → `protected_folder`.
- Helpers live in `tests/common/` (process spawning with failpoints, NDJSON stderr parsing, tree hashing).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The crash matrix passes for every failpoint name in `engine::FAILPOINTS` (plus stage and swap names) across install, update and remove: invariant holds, readers never recover, the next mutating command recovers with `journal_recovered`.
- A reader during a live swap reports `tx_in_progress`, exits 0 and writes nothing.
- Two concurrent installs into one target both succeed without `locked`, or one is a no-op. No record is lost and the generation equals the number of commits.
- Every measured `lock_held_ms` is under 50 ms on fixtures.
- The global lock file keeps the same inode across the whole suite.
- The undo matrix passes: byte-for-byte restore, undo of undo, `undo_conflict` across kinds, `--last-by agent`, and the SavedVariables policy matrix including deferral and the follow-up restore.
- The EINVAL fallback and the reflink fallback pass, with `atomic_swap: false` reported in the first.
- Hostile archives are refused end to end with nothing written outside staging, and `blizzard_auctionui/` beside `Blizzard_AuctionUI/` is refused.
- The whole suite runs without network access and within `cargo test` (no `#[ignore]`), in under 2 minutes on the development machine. If it is slower, crash-matrix cases are parallelized across tempdirs, never skipped.

## Test Plan

- This bead is the test plan. Each scenario logs, on failure: the failpoint name, the command argv and env, stdout/stderr, the journal lines, the folder tree hashes (expected old and new versus actual), and the lock file inode.
- Run the suite three times in a row before closing to catch flakiness; record the timings in the close comment.

## Considerations

- `abort` leaves no destructors running, which is the point. Tempdir cleanup happens in the parent test process, never the aborted child.
- flock locks belong to open file descriptions. A helper thread that opens the lock file separately contends correctly, but crash semantics need a separate process. Use processes for crash tests.
- Timing-based synchronization (`sleep` failpoints) must use generous margins (≥ 500 ms) and assertions on final state, not on interleavings, to avoid flakes.
- The 50 ms lock-hold budget is a checkpoint, not a micro-benchmark. Measure only the window between acquire and release.
- Out of scope: real-machine smoke tests and keyless network installs (m1-checkpoint bead), and the CLI contract shape (contract-suite bead).
acceptance_criteria: The crash matrix passes for every failpoint in engine::FAILPOINTS plus stage and swap names across install, update and remove, with the invariant holding, readers never recovering, and the next mutating command recovering with journal_recovered; a reader during a live swap reports tx_in_progress, exits 0 and writes nothing; two concurrent installs into one target both succeed without locked or one is a no-op, with no lost record and generation equal to the number of commits; every measured lock_held_ms is under 50 ms on fixtures; the global lock file keeps the same inode across the suite; the undo matrix passes (byte-for-byte restore, undo of undo, undo_conflict across kinds, --last-by agent, SavedVariables policy with deferral and follow-up restore); the EINVAL and reflink fallbacks pass with atomic_swap false reported; hostile archives are refused end to end with nothing written outside staging and blizzard_auctionui beside Blizzard_AuctionUI is refused; the suite runs offline inside cargo test in under 2 minutes

title: Transaction journal: phases, step records and recovery under the lock
description:
## Background

The journal is what makes a transaction crash-safe across several renames. Vision §5.5 "Journal phases and recovery":

- Phases run `prepared` → one step record per rename → `swapped` → `committed`.
- Before each rename, a step record is appended and fsync'd.
- Recovery rolls forward from `swapped` and rolls back from anything earlier. It reads the step records instead of inferring progress from which directories exist.
- A journal counts as left over only when the process examining it holds the global lock. A held flock proves the writer is alive; a free one proves it is gone (D23). Mutating commands recover right after acquiring the lock and report the warning `journal_recovered`.
- Read commands never recover. They list `journal/`, probe the lock with a non-blocking `try_lock`, and add the warning `journal_pending` (lock free) or `tx_in_progress` (lock held), each with a `fix`.
- Journals in phase `committed` are complete. Their writer or the next lock holder deletes them, and they are never reported.

This bead owns the journal format, the writer API used by the swap and commit beads, recovery, and the reader-side reporting. The engine-guarding warnings ship in M1 as plain warnings; the doctor's `journal-pending` fixer is M4.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<client dir>` = the directory that holds `Interface/` and `WTF/`.

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/journal.rs`. File `<state>/omaddons/journal/<tx>.jsonl`.
  - Decided: JSON Lines, appended with `Op::AppendFile` plus fsync, instead of rewriting a `<tx>.json` document per step. Each rename is preceded by exactly one small append and one fsync, which keeps the commit window short (the lock-hold target is under 50 ms). This changes the vision §5.6 file name from `journal/<tx>.json` to `journal/<tx>.jsonl`; the paths bead must use the `.jsonl` name, and the vision bead gets a comment recording it.
- Line types (each line one JSON object with `"type"`; all derive `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `JsonSchema`):
  - `{"type":"prepared","schema_version":"1.0","tx","target_key","client_dir","kind","started_at","commit": CommitPayload}`. `CommitPayload` holds everything roll-forward needs without re-planning: the new `TargetRecord` (generation + 1), the new files-index entries for affected folders, the `history.jsonl` record to append, and the stage dir path. Decided: embedding the payload makes roll-forward mechanical and keeps recovery free of network and planning logic.
  - `{"type":"step","n","op":"exchange|noreplace|rename","from","to","purpose":"swap_in|old_to_snapshot|remove_to_snapshot|fallback_live_to_snapshot|fallback_stage_to_live"}`, appended and fsync'd before the rename it announces.
  - `{"type":"swapped"}` after the last rename and the parent-dir fsyncs.
  - `{"type":"committed"}` after the records, the files index and history are written.
- Writer API (used by the swap and commit beads; the caller must hold the global lock; debug-asserted):
  - `Journal::create(tx, payload) -> Journal` writes `prepared` via fsx (`WriteFile` with fsync) in the transaction's `WriteSession`.
  - `journal.step(StepRecord)` appends and fsyncs.
  - `journal.mark_swapped()` and `journal.mark_committed()` append and fsync.
  - `journal.finish()` removes the file via `fsx::prune(PruneReason::PostCommitCleanup)` after the lock is released.
- Reading: parse line by line. A torn last line (no trailing newline, or invalid JSON) is ignored. Decided, because it is safe: a step record is fsync'd before its rename starts, so a torn step line means that rename never happened. The phase is the last `swapped`/`committed` marker, else `prepared`. A file without a valid `prepared` line was created but never prepared: there is nothing to undo, so recovery just prunes it.
- Recovery: `recover_all(lock: &GlobalLockGuard, ctx) -> Vec<Recovered>`. It takes the guard as proof the lock is held, so recovery cannot run without the lock (enforced by the type).
  - For each journal in `<state>/omaddons/journal/`, skip any whose in-flight lock (`<state>/omaddons/inflight/<tx>.lock`) is held: its writer is alive. The only legitimate case is a writer that has released the global lock and is still in post-commit cleanup, so its journal is `committed` and the writer deletes it itself. A held in-flight lock with an uncommitted journal cannot occur while we hold the global lock; if seen, it is logged as an internal inconsistency and left alone.
  - `committed` → prune the journal and the tx's stage dir. Not reported.
  - `swapped` → roll forward: write `commit.record` and the files index via state-records (idempotent; skipped when the record's generation already equals the payload's), append the history record unless an entry with that `tx` already exists, append `committed`, then prune the journal and the stage dir.
  - Anything earlier → roll back: replay the step records in reverse. `exchange` is undone by exchanging again. `noreplace from→to` and `rename from→to` are undone by renaming `to`→`from` with `NoReplace`. A step whose effect is not present (the rename never ran, checked as "source exists at `from` and `to` is absent or holds the other side") is skipped. That is the one place we look at the filesystem, and only to decide whether a recorded step completed. Then prune the stage dir and the journal. State files were never written before `swapped`, so they need no restore. SavedVariables snapshots are copies, so nothing to restore.
  - Each recovered transaction yields the warning `journal_recovered` `{tx, target, action: rolled_forward|rolled_back}` with fix `omaddons history --limit 5` (argv set).
  - Failpoints (debug builds, DEC-7): `engine.recover.step` (between replayed steps), so a crash during recovery is itself recoverable (recovery is idempotent).
- Reader reporting: `pending_warnings(ctx) -> Vec<Warning>`, never writing anything:
  - list `journal/`; ignore `committed` journals;
  - `probe_global()` (fsx-lock bead) without blocking: Free → `journal_pending` per journal, fix `omaddons status` (decided: in M1 the next mutating command recovers it; `status` is the read-only way to see it; M4 switches the fix to `omaddons doctor --fix --only fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending`); Held → `tx_in_progress`, fix display "wait for the running omaddons command to finish" with `argv: null`.
  - Warning details carry the tx id and target id, never paths inside WTF.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `recover_all` cannot be called without a global-lock guard (it does not compile otherwise).
- For a journal left at each phase (prepared with 0..n steps, swapped, committed), recovery restores the documented outcome: roll back leaves every folder exactly as before the transaction (tree hashes equal); roll forward leaves every folder as after the transaction, with records, files index and one history entry written.
- Recovery is idempotent: a crash injected mid-recovery followed by a second recovery reaches the same final state.
- A torn last line is ignored and recovery still succeeds.
- `committed` journals are deleted and never reported.
- A read command with a pending journal and a free lock reports `journal_pending`; with the lock held it reports `tx_in_progress`; neither writes anything (asserted by hashing the state dir before and after).
- Each recovery emits one `journal_recovered` warning with the action taken.
- Every journal line round-trips through serde, and the `prepared` payload is enough to roll forward with no network access (the test runs with `--offline`).

## Test Plan

- Unit: parsing (torn line, missing prepared, unknown `type` ignored with a log event); phase determination; reverse-step computation for every op/purpose pair.
- Integration (tempdir client dir and state dir; real renames): construct journals at every phase by running the swap sequence step by step and stopping, then call `recover_all` and compare tree hashes against the old and new trees. Include the two-rename fallback steps.
- Integration: reader reporting with the lock held by a second process (or a second open file description in a helper thread, since flock is per open file description) → `tx_in_progress`; lock free → `journal_pending`.
- Integration: failpoint `engine.recover.step=error`, then recover again → same final state.
- Log the journal lines and the directory listings on failure.

## Considerations

- Recovery only under the lock is the D23 rule. Never add a code path where a reader "helpfully" recovers.
- The journal lives in the state dir, while the renames happen inside the client dir. Both are fsync'd: step lines via the journal file's fsync, renames via parent-dir fsyncs (swap bead).
- Dependencies added beyond the plan: `state-records`, because roll-forward writes the target record, files index and history entry from the embedded payload; `fsx-prune-guard`, because journals and stage dirs are removed through `fsx::prune()`.
- The `.jsonl` name change must be mirrored in the paths bead and recorded on the vision bead.
- Out of scope: performing the swap (swap bead) and orchestrating the transaction (commit bead).
acceptance_criteria: recover_all cannot be called without a global-lock guard; for a journal left at every phase recovery rolls back to the exact old trees or rolls forward to the new trees with records, files index and one history entry written; recovery is idempotent across a crash injected mid-recovery; a torn last line is ignored; committed journals are deleted and never reported; a read command reports journal_pending when the lock is free and tx_in_progress when it is held, writing nothing; each recovery emits one journal_recovered warning naming the action; every journal line round-trips through serde and the prepared payload rolls forward with no network access
close_reason: Transactions journal every rename with fsync'd JSON Lines; recovery under the global lock rolls forward from swapped with an embedded payload or rolls back exactly by recorded file identities, idempotently across crashes; read commands report pending or in-progress transactions without writing

Use Free + leftover journals → `journal_pending`, Held → `tx_in_progress`. Recovery takes `&GlobalLockGuard` as proof of holding the lock. Acquire with `GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, command)`; it is not re-entrant, so pass the guard down.

comments.text: **prune-guard landed.** Delete committed journals with `fsx::prune(&scopes, PruneReason::PostCommitCleanup, &[paths.journal(&tx)], LockUse::Held(&guard))`. The victim must be `journal/<tx>.jsonl` (ULID stem), and only src/engine/journal.rs is allowlisted to call prune for this (tests/single_writer.rs PRUNE_CALLERS). In-flight locks `inflight/<tx>.lock` prune the same way, after the owner dropped its InflightLock; a held one is skipped.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/engine/journal.rs, World wiring in src/app/world.rs, tests/journal.rs, tests/list.rs).**
(1) **Step records carry identities:** `StepRecord { n, op: exchange|noreplace|rename, from, to, purpose, from_id, to_id: Option<FileId { dev, ino }> }`. `Journal::step` takes them itself just before appending. The bead's 'skip a step whose effect is not present' cannot work for exchange from existence alone, since both paths exist before and after. Identity decides exactly: the before state means it never ran (skip), the after state means it ran (undo), anything else is an error left for manual repair. This also makes rollback idempotent.
(2) API: `Journal::create(&mut s, &paths, &GlobalLockGuard, Prepared)`, `step(&mut s, Step { op, from, to, purpose }) -> StepRecord`, `mark_swapped`, `mark_committed`, `finish(scopes, LockUse)` (prune). Every line is one `Op::AppendFile` (write plus fsync, and a dir fsync on creation) in the caller's session. `JournalLine` is internally tagged by "type" (prepared|step|swapped|committed); Prepared is boxed.
(3) `CommitPayload { record: TargetRecord, index: IndexChanges { upsert: Vec<FolderIndex>, remove: Vec<folder key> }, history: HistoryEntry, stage_dir }`. **The index is a delta, not the full files index**, to keep the prepared line, which is written under the lock, small. `IndexChanges::apply` is idempotent.
(4) Parsing: a torn last line (no newline, or invalid JSON) is ignored. Invalid JSON before the last line is an internal error (corruption; the journal is left alone). Valid JSON with an unknown type is skipped and counted. A swapped or committed marker without a prepared line is Unprepared.
(5) `recover_all(&GlobalLockGuard, &paths, &scopes) -> Result<Vec<Warning>>`. It skips journals whose in-flight lock is live. Unprepared and committed journals are pruned silently. Swapped rolls forward: ensure targets/, save the record only if its generation is behind, apply the index delta, append history only if no entry has this tx, then append committed. Earlier phases roll back in reverse; an undo of noreplace/rename tries NoReplace and falls back to a plain rename when unsupported. **The engine.recover.step failpoint fires after each undo** (between steps), so a crash leaves a half-rolled-back state; the next run completes it (unit-tested). Then it prunes the stage dir, the journal and the in-flight lock file, all with LockUse::Held. Recovery writes in an untracked 'recovery' session. **status.json is not touched by recovery**: the mutating command that recovered refreshes it.
(6) Warnings carry the tx and target key in the message, because Warning has no details field. journal_recovered says 'completed it (rolled forward)' or 'undid it (rolled back)', with fix `omaddons history --limit 5`. pending_warnings: journal_pending with fix `omaddons status` when the lock is free or missing; tx_in_progress with a text fix when it is held.
(7) **Wired into World::load**, so every command (list now, status later) reports unfinished transactions without recovering. tests/list.rs asserts `list` reports one, leaves the journal in place and writes nothing.
(8) No network exists in the recovery path; the payload alone drives roll-forward.
