title: Ownership model: conflicts, protected and unmanaged folders, case collisions, --force
description:
## Background

Before any folder is swapped, the engine has to decide whether it is allowed to write that folder at all. Vision §5.5 step 4 defines the ownership model. It runs at plan time without the lock and again under the lock during revalidation (step 6). The rules:

- `FolderName` (model bead) cannot represent `/`, `\`, `..`, a leading `.`, or an empty name, so traversal is impossible by type. Its key is the ASCII case-folded name, which matches Wine's case-insensitive lookup (D27).
- A folder owned by another managed addon → `ownership_conflict` (exit 4).
- Any protected key (key starts with `blizzard_`) → `protected_folder` (exit 4). There is no override, not even `--force` (D14). Private-server client packs ship extracted `Blizzard_*` addons inside `Interface/AddOns`; the development machine's 3.3.5a client has 23 of them and nothing else.
- An unmanaged folder → `unmanaged_folder` (exit 4). The vision's fix is `omaddons adopt`, which lands in M2.
- A new folder whose key matches an existing folder with a different spelling → `case_collision` (exit 4). The `fix` names the existing folder plus `adopt`/`remove`.
- `--force` on `ownership_conflict` moves the folder to the new addon and marks the previous owner `degraded` (doctor finding `ownership-transferred`). Both records are part of the same transaction, so undo restores both.
- `--force` on `unmanaged_folder` snapshots the unmanaged folder and replaces it.

The M1 checkpoint requires that creating `blizzard_auctionui/` beside `Blizzard_AuctionUI/` is refused (vision §7 M1 checkpoints).

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/ownership.rs`. Pure function over inputs; no I/O:
  `check(ops: &[FolderOp], inventory: &Inventory, records: &TargetRecord, installing: &AddonName, force: bool) -> Result<OwnershipOutcome>`.
  - `FolderOp` is `Add(FolderName) | Replace(FolderName) | Remove(FolderName)`, as computed by the planner. The planner first maps each incoming archive folder to `Add` or `Replace` by key lookup in the inventory.
  - `Inventory` comes from the inventory bead: every entry of `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns` with its key and class (protected, managed, linked, unmanaged, invalid, `case_duplicate`).
- Rules, evaluated per folder in this order (the first match wins):
  1. Key starts with `blizzard_` → `protected_folder`. `details: {folder}`; fix: display "this folder belongs to the game client and is never modified", `argv: null`. `--force` ignored.
  2. The live entry is `linked` (a symlink, e.g. a developer's working copy) → `unmanaged_folder` with `details.class = "linked"`; fix display "remove or rename the symlink yourself", `argv: null`. Decided: reuse `unmanaged_folder` rather than add a code, because the remedy is the same kind (the user acts on the folder). omaddons never mutates or follows links (vision §5.1), and `--force` does not override this.
  3. The live entry is `invalid` (its name fails `FolderName`) → cannot be the target of an op by construction. Skip it.
  4. Incoming key equals a live entry's key but the spelling differs → `case_collision`. `details: {incoming, existing}`; `fix` = `omaddons remove <owner>` when the existing folder is managed, else display "rename or remove <existing> first, or rerun with --force to replace it" with argv = the original argv plus `--force`. `--force` turns a case collision with an unmanaged folder into a replacement under the existing spelling (decided: the live spelling is kept, so the client never sees two spellings; the managed record stores the archive's spelling for display only).
  5. Live entry managed by a different addon → `ownership_conflict`. `details: {folder, owner}`; fix = argv plus `--force`; alternatives: `omaddons remove <owner>`. With `--force`: the outcome lists `transfers: [{folder, from, to}]`, the previous owner's record becomes `state: degraded`, and the warning `ownership_transferred` is emitted. Wire name decided: snake_case like every warning code; the doctor finding id `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` is M4.
  6. Live entry unmanaged → `unmanaged_folder`. `details: {folder}`; fix: argv plus `--force` until `adopt` exists (M2), at which point M2 switches the fix to `omaddons adopt <folder>`. With `--force`, the folder is replaced; the swap snapshots the old one like any replacement, so undo restores it.
  7. Live entry managed by the same addon → allowed (replacement).
  8. No live entry → allowed (add).
- `Remove(folder)` ops: protected → `protected_folder`; not owned by the addon being removed → never planned (the planner only removes folders owned by the record).
- `OwnershipOutcome { allowed_ops, transfers, replaced_unmanaged, warnings }`. It feeds the plan's data and the commit's record updates.
- All refusals are typed `Error`s from the error-registry bead with exit 4. The error carries every conflicting folder in `details.folders` (decided: report all conflicts at once, not just the first, so one fix covers them).
- The same function runs twice: at plan time against the snapshot inventory, and under the lock against a fresh inventory (commit bead). A difference between the two is what makes the commit re-plan or fail with `plan_stale`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Planning an archive containing `blizzard_auctionui/` into a target that has `Blizzard_AuctionUI/` fails with `protected_folder` (exit 4), with or without `--force`, and no file is written.
- Any op whose folder key starts with `blizzard_` in any case (`Blizzard_X`, `BLIZZARD_X`, `blizzard_x`) is refused with `protected_folder`.
- A folder owned by addon A, planned for addon B, fails with `ownership_conflict`, whose fix argv is the original argv plus `--force`. With `--force` the outcome contains the transfer, marks A degraded, and emits `ownership_transferred`.
- An unmanaged folder fails with `unmanaged_folder`; with `--force` it becomes an allowed replacement.
- An incoming `foo/` beside a live unmanaged `Foo/` fails with `case_collision` naming both spellings; with `--force` it replaces under the live spelling.
- A symlinked folder is never planned for mutation, even with `--force`.
- All conflicting folders are reported in one error's `details.folders`.
- The function is pure: unit tests run without a filesystem.

## Test Plan

- Unit: a table over (live class, spelling relation, owner relation, `--force`) → expected outcome or error code, covering every rule above. Assert each error's `fix.argv` and `alternatives`.
- Unit: multi-folder archive with one protected and one unmanaged folder → a single error listing both, with protected taking precedence in `code`. Decided: the error code is that of the highest-precedence violation, protected > linked > case_collision > ownership_conflict > unmanaged.
- Integration: a synthetic 3.3.5a target (`tests/common/trees.rs`, 23 `Blizzard_*` folders) plus an archive containing `blizzard_auctionui/` → planning fails with `protected_folder`. Hash the AddOns tree before and after.
- Log the inventory and the planned ops on failure.

## Considerations

- `ownership_transferred` is a new warning code, not in the vision's initial warning list. It must be added to the error-registry's `WarningCode` (coordinate with that bead; the vision bead's contract-additions comment should list it alongside DEC-4).
- The precedence order for multi-violation errors is a decision recorded here. Keep it in one place so the contract suite can assert it.
- `adopt` (M2) changes the `unmanaged_folder` fix. Keep the fix construction in a single function.
- Out of scope: discovering which folders an archive contains (archive-inspect), and building the inventory (inventory bead).
acceptance_criteria: Planning blizzard_auctionui beside Blizzard_AuctionUI fails with protected_folder (exit 4) with or without --force and writes nothing; any blizzard_ key in any case is refused with protected_folder; a folder owned by another addon fails with ownership_conflict whose fix argv adds --force, and with --force the outcome transfers the folder, marks the previous owner degraded and emits ownership_transferred; an unmanaged folder fails with unmanaged_folder and becomes a replacement with --force; foo beside unmanaged Foo fails with case_collision naming both and replaces under the live spelling with --force; a symlinked folder is never planned for mutation even with --force; all conflicting folders are reported in one error's details.folders; the check is pure and unit-tested without a filesystem
close_reason: Ownership is a pure, single-error check that refuses protected, linked, case-colliding, foreign and unmanaged folders with exact fixes and precedence, lets --force transfer or replace where allowed, and returns allowed ops with live spellings for the swap

title: Engine planning: resolve refs to verified candidates and compute folder ops against a generation snapshot
description:
## Background

Step 1 of the transaction engine (vision §5.5) produces the plan: every requested change, resolved against a snapshot of state that records each target's `generation`, turned into concrete folder adds, replaces and removes. No lock is held, so planning runs concurrently with other omaddons processes. The commit bead later takes the lock and revalidates the plan against the generations recorded here (optimistic concurrency, D24).

Planning includes resolution (DEC-15), because the folders an install touches are only known after the selected archive has been downloaded and inspected. The pipeline is the vision's fetch/select/verify split (§5.4, D28):

1. `fetch_once` (refs bead): each distinct ref is fetched once per run, across all targets.
2. `select` (select bead): pure, per target. It returns candidates best-first.
3. Download (blob-cache bead): each candidate archive, into the content-addressed cache.
4. Inspect and verify (archive-inspect bead): the client's own load rules applied to the archive (D5).
5. A failing candidate falls back to the next one. No compatible candidate → `no_compatible_release` (exit 3). A user-specified file, URL or zip that does not verify → `wrong_flavor` (exit 4).
6. Ownership (ownership bead) and the running policy (running-policy bead) are applied to the resulting folder ops.

The plan is exactly what `--dry-run` returns. M1 has no stored plans: `plan_id` stays null and `apply` arrives in M4 (DEC-15, DEC-16). The vision's Plan shape (§5.1) is `{plan_id, created_at, expires_at, argv, actor, generations{key: n}, ops[], releases[{release_id, url, expected_hash}]}`.

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/plan.rs`.
  `plan(req: &PlanRequest, ctx: &PlanCtx) -> Result<Plan>`, where:
  - `PlanRequest` holds `changes: Vec<RequestedChange>` per target, with `RequestedChange = Install { ref, channel, version: Option<String>, file: Option<PathBuf> } | Remove { addon } | Reinstall { addon }` (update in M1 is reinstall-to-update of the newest compatible release), plus `force: bool`.
  - `PlanCtx` holds the `Http` impl, `BlobCache`, the state snapshot (`TargetRecord` per target via state-records; unregistered targets have none), the inventory per target (inventory bead), running state per target (running-detection) and the `RunningPolicy` (from config, passed in), `actor`, `argv` and the `Reporter` for progress events.
- Generations: `generations: BTreeMap<String, u64>`, keyed by target key. Decided: an unregistered target (key null, vision §5.1) is keyed by its provisional id with generation 0. If the target was registered by another process before commit, its record exists with a generation of 1 or more, so the commit's revalidation sees a change and re-plans.
- Install resolution per target:
  1. Collect all `Install` refs across targets and call `fetch_once` once.
  2. `select(release_set, target, channel, pin)` (select bead), where `pin` is `--version V` (matched against version or tag, leading `v` ignored). When `--file <zip>` is given, the candidate is that local archive, attributed to the ref's release (M1: verified by TOC; the expected hash is checked when the source supplies one).
  3. For each candidate in order: obtain the archive according to its `AssetLocation` (model bead) — `Url` → download into the blob cache (`cacheable: true` for every M1 source); `LocalZip` → hash and open in place; `LocalDir` → inspect the directory directly; `GitCheckout` → `sources::git_hosts::materialize` into a fresh temp dir under the tx, then inspect it as a directory — then `inspect`, `verify`. A `--version V` that matches no release maps the select bead's `PinnedVersionNotFound` to `not_found` (exit 3). Record why each rejected candidate failed (for `details.tried`). The first compatible candidate wins.
  4. No candidate verifies → `no_compatible_release` (exit 3), with `details: {ref, target, tried: [{asset, reason}]}` and a fix suggesting the other compatible targets when any exist. A user-specified `--file`, `url:` or `file:` ref that fails verification → `wrong_flavor` (exit 4).
- Idempotence and update:
  - The addon is already installed with the same release id and folder set → no op. The result is `ok` with an empty change list (vision §5.9 "Idempotent").
  - Installed with an older release → `kind: update`, replacing its folders. Folders present in the old version and absent in the new one become `Remove` ops.
  - Not installed → `kind: install`.
- Remove: `not_managed` (exit 3) when the addon has no record in that target. Otherwise every folder in the record becomes a `Remove` op.
- Folder ops: map each incoming folder to `Add` or `Replace` by key lookup in the inventory, then run `ownership::check` (may raise `protected_folder`, `ownership_conflict`, `unmanaged_folder` or `case_collision`, and applies `--force`). Then build `PolicyOp`s (loaded TOC before, via toc-loaded on the live folder; TOC names after, from `Inspected`) and run `running::evaluate`. Refusals surface here, before any staging.
- Warnings collected in the plan: `out_of_date` (verdict), `ownership_transferred` (forced transfers), `reload_required` (when the client runs).
- Dependencies are M2. `--no-deps` is accepted and has no effect in M1, with no warning.
- `Plan` (derives `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `JsonSchema`; DEC-3; field order = wire order):
  `{schema_version, plan_id: null, created_at, expires_at: null, argv, actor, dry_run, generations, targets: [TargetPlan]}` with
  `TargetPlan { target (id), key (or null), kind: install|update|remove, changes: [Change], ops: [PlannedOp], releases: [{release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256}], reload_required, warnings }`,
  `Change { addon, ref, from_version, to_version, folders: {added, replaced, removed} }`, and
  `PlannedOp { op: add|replace|remove, folder, addon, staged_from: Option<InspectedFolder ref> }`.
  Decided: `plan_id` and `expires_at` are present as null in M1, so M4's stored plans only fill them (an additive change, no rename).
- Partial plans: when several refs are requested, a failure for one ref in one target is recorded as a per-item failure (`failures: [{ref, target, error}]`) and the rest proceeds. The command layer turns that into `partial: true` (exit 0) or `--strict` exit 6 (vision §5.9). Errors that apply to the whole request (`target_ambiguous`, `offline` before any fetch) fail the call.
- `--dry-run`: the command returns the `Plan` as `data` with `"dry_run": true` and `tx: null` (DEC-16). Downloads still happen, because verification needs the archive, so `--dry-run` warms the blob cache. Nothing outside `<cache>` is written (placeholder: `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`, default `.cache` under the home directory).
- Failpoints (debug builds, DEC-7): `engine.plan.fetched`, `engine.plan.downloaded`, `engine.plan.done`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Installing a ref that is already current yields `ok` with an empty change list and no transaction.
- Installing a newer release of an installed addon yields `kind: update`, with folders removed by the new version planned as `Remove`.
- A WeakAuras-style release whose first candidate is the wrong flavor falls back to the next candidate; when none verifies, the call fails with `no_compatible_release` (exit 3) listing every tried asset and its reason.
- A `--file` zip that fails verification fails with `wrong_flavor` (exit 4).
- Ownership and running-policy refusals surface at plan time with their codes and nothing is staged or written outside `<cache>`.
- Each distinct ref is fetched once even when installed into several targets in one call (asserted with the replay `Http` impl's request log).
- `generations` records each target's generation (0 and the provisional id for unregistered targets).
- `--dry-run` returns the same `data` schema as the real run with `dry_run: true`, `tx: null` and `plan_id: null`; an insta snapshot pins the shape.
- One failing ref among several yields per-item `failures` while the other refs still plan.

## Test Plan

- Unit: idempotence and update classification over record/release combinations; old-versus-new folder-set diffing.
- Integration (replay `Http` from net-fixtures, synthetic targets from `tests/common/trees.rs`, fixture archives from `tests/common/archives.rs` served as release assets):
  - fallback across candidates; `no_compatible_release`; `wrong_flavor` for `--file`;
  - one ref into a retail and a Forever target: fetched once, a different candidate selected per target;
  - ownership refusal (a protected folder in the archive) and running-policy refusal (fake `/proc` showing the client running, removing a folder) are both raised before staging;
  - a `--dry-run` envelope snapshot.
- Log the candidate list, the verdicts and the request log on failure.

## Considerations

- Planning can be slow (network, downloads), which is why it holds no lock. Long plans racing with other commits are handled by the commit bead's revalidation.
- The plan holds the transaction's in-flight lock from planning onward (the commit bead creates the `TxId` and `InflightLock` before calling `plan`), so the temp blobs it creates are never mistaken for orphans.
- Plans include URLs but never credentials (M1 has none; M5 must keep it that way).
- Dependencies added beyond the plan: `net-fixtures` (the integration tests replay HTTP) and `test-trees` (synthetic targets). `inventory` is reached through `ownership`.
- Out of scope: staging and the commit (stage, commit beads), stored plans and `apply` (M4), dependency resolution (M2).
acceptance_criteria: Installing an already-current ref yields ok with an empty change list and no transaction; installing a newer release yields kind update with dropped folders planned as Remove; a wrong-flavor first candidate falls back to the next, and when none verifies the call fails with no_compatible_release (exit 3) listing every tried asset and reason; a --file zip that fails verification fails with wrong_flavor (exit 4); ownership and running-policy refusals surface at plan time and nothing is staged or written outside the cache; each distinct ref is fetched once across several targets; generations records each target's generation (0 and the provisional id for unregistered targets); --dry-run returns the real-run data schema with dry_run true, tx null and plan_id null, pinned by an insta snapshot; one failing ref among several yields per-item failures while the rest still plan
close_reason: Planning resolves requested installs, updates and removals per target without the lock: one fetch per ref, per-target selection with download, inspection and verification fallback, idempotence before download, ownership and running-policy refusals as per-item failures, and a serialized Plan plus everything the commit needs

title: Snapshot retention and blob eviction via prune()
description:
## Background

Every transaction leaves snapshots behind. Old folder versions and SavedVariables clones go to `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`, and pre-transaction state files go to `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`. Downloaded archives accumulate in `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/`. Without retention these grow forever. Vision §5.5 "Retention" fixes the policy:

- Snapshots younger than 24 h are never pruned.
- Beyond that, keep the last 10 per target within 7 days, capped at `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` per target, oldest first, and never the most recent transaction.
- Age protection wins over the size cap. If young snapshots alone exceed the cap, the warning `snapshot_cap_exceeded` is raised.
- The blob cache is LRU-capped at `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`. Blobs referenced by retained transactions, installed records or unexpired plans are pinned.
- CurseForge/Wago undo uses snapshots, never blobs.

Limits (`src/limits.rs`, both overridable in config): `TX_RETENTION` = always at least 24 h, and beyond that 10 transactions within 7 days per target; `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` = 2 GiB per target; `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` = 1 GiB.

Deletion is not an fsx `Op`. `fsx::prune()` is the only deletion path, and retention pruning is one of its few allowed callers (`PruneReason::Retention`). Pruning first renames the victim into the owning `trash/` directory under the global lock, then deletes outside the lock (fsx-prune-guard bead).

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache`).

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/retention.rs`; `retention::run(ctx, targets: &[TargetKey]) -> RetentionReport`. Called by the commit bead's post-commit hook (outside the global lock) for the target just committed, and callable for all targets.
- Inputs per target: history entries for that target (state-records reader), snapshot directories on disk for that target, and their sizes (`du`-style walk of each `snapshots/<tx>/`, counting both the client-dir and state-dir parts; reflinked SavedVariables count at their apparent size; decided: apparent size, because shared-extent accounting is not portable and over-counting only prunes earlier).
- Selection, per target:
  1. Order the target's snapshot-bearing transactions newest first by commit time from history.
  2. Protected: the most recent transaction, and every transaction younger than 24 h.
  3. Retained: protected ones, plus the newest transactions younger than 7 days, up to 10 in total (protected ones count toward the 10).
  4. Prune: every non-retained transaction.
  5. Size cap: if the retained set's total exceeds `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES`, prune the oldest non-protected retained transactions until under the cap. If only protected ones remain and the total is still above the cap, keep them and emit `snapshot_cap_exceeded` (`details: {target, bytes, cap}`; fix display "raise snapshot_max_bytes in config or wait 24 h", argv `["omaddons","config","set","snapshot_max_bytes","<value>"]` only if that key exists in config, else `argv: null`).
- Pruning a transaction removes both `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/` and `<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/` via `fsx::prune(PruneReason::Retention, path)`. Its history entry stays (history is append-only). A later `undo <tx>` reports `not_found` "snapshot pruned" (undo bead).
- Orphan sweep, decided: retention also prunes stage dirs (`<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/`) and in-flight lock files (`<state>/omaddons/inflight/<tx>.lock`) whose in-flight lock is free, which have no journal in `<state>/omaddons/journal/`, and which are older than 1 h. Why: in M1 nothing else removes them (the doctor's `orphan-inflight` quarantine fixer is M4), and a free in-flight lock proves no live process owns them (D23). A stage dir that has a journal is never swept; journal recovery owns it. The 1 h floor is a safety margin against clock or racing surprises.
- Blob eviction: compute the pin set as the `blob_sha256` of every installed record's current release, plus every blob referenced by retained transactions' history ops. Plans add none in M1 (stored plans are M4). Then call `BlobCache::evict(&pins)` (blob-cache bead) with `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, which also removes orphan temp blobs.
- `RetentionReport { pruned_tx: usize, freed_bytes, kept_tx, cap_exceeded: bool, orphans_swept: usize, blobs_evicted: usize }` is attached to the transaction outcome only under `--verbose`. The `snapshot_cap_exceeded` warning is always attached.
- Failure isolation: retention runs after the transaction committed. Any retention error becomes a log event plus warning and never fails the command (the transaction already succeeded).
- Injectable clock for tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Snapshots younger than 24 h and the most recent transaction's snapshot are never pruned, even when over the size cap. In that case `snapshot_cap_exceeded` is emitted.
- With 15 transactions older than 24 h and within 7 days, exactly the newest 10 snapshots remain. Snapshots older than 7 days are pruned unless protected.
- The size cap prunes the oldest non-protected snapshots first until the target is under `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES`.
- Both the client-dir and the state-dir parts of a pruned transaction's snapshot are removed. History entries remain.
- Orphan stage dirs and in-flight lock files (lock free, no journal, older than 1 h) are swept; anything with a held lock or a journal is left alone.
- Pinned blobs survive eviction; unpinned least-recently-used blobs are evicted to the cap.
- Every removal goes through `fsx::prune(PruneReason::Retention, …)` (the prune call-site test passes).
- A retention failure never changes the committed transaction's exit code.

## Test Plan

- Unit: the selection function over synthetic transaction lists (ages, sizes, most-recent flag) with an injected clock, covering every rule including cap-exceeded-by-young.
- Integration: create snapshot dirs for fake transactions in a tempdir client dir and state dir, run retention, assert what remains. Orphan sweep with a held in-flight lock held by a helper (kept) versus a free one (swept), with and without a journal.
- Integration: blob pins from records and retained history.
- Log the selection input table and the remaining directories on failure.

## Considerations

- Undo depends on snapshots. Retention is the only thing that makes old transactions non-undoable, and the 24 h floor guarantees at least a day of undo.
- Retention runs outside the global lock except for the trash rename inside `prune`. Two concurrent retention runs must be safe; `prune` renaming into trash is atomic and the second one sees the victim gone.
- Dependency note: the orphan sweep needs `fsx-lock` (probing in-flight locks), reached through `commit`.
- Out of scope: the doctor's `orphan-snapshot-dir` and `orphan-inflight` detectors (M4), and backup pruning (M3).
acceptance_criteria: Snapshots younger than 24 h and the most recent transaction's snapshot are never pruned even over the size cap, which then emits snapshot_cap_exceeded; with 15 transactions between 24 h and 7 days old exactly the newest 10 snapshots remain and older-than-7-days snapshots are pruned unless protected; the size cap prunes the oldest non-protected snapshots first until under SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES; both client-dir and state-dir parts of a pruned snapshot are removed while history entries remain; orphan stage dirs and in-flight lock files with a free lock, no journal and older than 1 h are swept while held or journaled ones are left alone; pinned blobs survive eviction and unpinned LRU blobs are evicted to the cap; every removal goes through fsx::prune(PruneReason::Retention); a retention failure never changes the committed transaction's exit code
close_reason: snapshot retention, orphan sweep and pinned blob eviction after every commit

title: Running policy and reload_required
description:
## Background

Players often alt-tab out of a running game, update addons, and type `/reload`. A guard that refused every mutation while the client runs would fire constantly and turn into noise, so the vision chooses a `safe` running policy by default and reports what the player must do afterwards (D30). The facts it rests on (vision §4.4):

- A Linux rename never disturbs files the client already has open.
- Modern clients pick up new files, new addons and TOC changes on `/reload` (since 9.0.1 retail / 1.14.0 Era). Deleting or renaming a TOC that is already loaded needs a client restart.
- 3.3.5a, and legacy clients generally, likely need a full restart for new addons or TOC changes (UNVERIFIED).
- SavedVariables load just before `ADDON_LOADED` and are written on logout, disconnect, quit and `/reload`. External edits made while the client runs are overwritten. So SavedVariables are never written while the target's client runs, under any policy or flag (D33).

The policy (vision §5.5 "Running policy"): `running_policy = "safe" | "refuse" | "allow"` in `config.toml`, default `safe`.
- While a target's client runs, `safe` allows replacing folders whose TOC basenames are unchanged, and adding folders.
- `safe` refuses with `game_running` (exit 4): removing or renaming folders with a loaded TOC; SavedVariables restores; any mutation on a `legacy` client.
- `--while-running` overrides the folder rules but never the SavedVariables rule.
- Every mutation outcome carries `reload_required: none|reload|restart` per target.

Running state comes from the running-detection bead and is computed live on every call (`/proc` scan, about 1–2 ms).

## Technical Approach

- Module `src/engine/running.rs`. Pure functions, no I/O:
  - `evaluate(policy: RunningPolicy, running: bool, rules: &ClientRules, ops: &[PolicyOp], while_running: bool) -> Result<PolicyOutcome>`
  - `PolicyOp` describes each planned op with what the policy needs:
    - `AddFolder { folder }`
    - `ReplaceFolder { folder, loaded_toc_before: Option<String>, toc_names_after: BTreeSet<String> }` (TOC file names case-folded; `loaded_toc_before` is the file name `loaded_toc` picks in the live folder, None when nothing loads)
    - `RemoveFolder { folder, loaded_toc_before: Option<String> }`
    - `RestoreSavedVariables { files: usize }` (undo; later `backup restore`).
  - `RunningPolicy` is `Safe | Refuse | Allow`, deserialized from config (`safe`, `refuse`, `allow`); default `Safe`.
- Definitions:
  - A replacement keeps its TOC basename when `loaded_toc_before` is None, or when that file name (case-insensitively) is still present in `toc_names_after`. Otherwise the replacement deletes or renames a loaded TOC and is treated like a removal of a loaded TOC.
  - A folder "has a loaded TOC" when `loaded_toc_before` is Some.
- Rules when `running == false`: everything is allowed and `reload_required = none`. A client that is not running loads the new state at its next start.
- Rules when `running == true`:
  - `RestoreSavedVariables` → always refused with `game_running`, whatever the policy or `--while-running` (the SavedVariables rule). The undo bead turns this into a deferral for `--saved-variables auto`; this function only reports it.
  - `Refuse` policy: any folder op → `game_running`, unless `while_running`.
  - `Safe` policy:
    - `rules.legacy == true`: any folder op → `game_running` unless `while_running`.
    - Otherwise: `AddFolder` and TOC-preserving `ReplaceFolder` are allowed. `RemoveFolder` with a loaded TOC, and a `ReplaceFolder` that drops the loaded TOC → `game_running` unless `while_running`.
  - `Allow` policy: every folder op is allowed.
  - `while_running` overrides every folder rule under every policy. Decided: the flag is the explicit per-invocation consent and wins over `refuse` as well as `safe`, because the configured policy is a default and the flag is a direct instruction.
- `reload_required` per target when running, taking the maximum over its ops (`none < reload < restart`):
  - legacy client, any folder op → `restart` (UNVERIFIED; conservative);
  - removal of, or a replacement that drops, a loaded TOC → `restart`;
  - any other add or replace → `reload`.
- `game_running` error: `details: {target, ops: [..], reason}`; `fix` = the original argv plus `--while-running` (when a folder rule refused) or display "quit the game client, then rerun" with `argv: null` (when the SavedVariables rule refused); `alternatives` includes the other one where it applies. The message names the target id but never account or character names.
- `PolicyOutcome { reload_required: ReloadRequired, refused: Vec<..> }`. `ReloadRequired` comes from the model bead and serializes as `none|reload|restart`.
- When `reload_required != none`, the outcome also yields the warning `reload_required` with fix display "/reload in game" (or "restart the game client" for `restart`) and `argv: null`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Not running: every op is allowed and `reload_required` is `none`, under every policy.
- Running, `safe`, modern client: adding a folder → allowed, `reload`; replacing with the loaded TOC kept → allowed, `reload`; removing a folder with a loaded TOC → `game_running` (exit 4) whose fix argv adds `--while-running`; with `while_running` → allowed, `restart`.
- Running, `safe`, legacy client: any folder op → `game_running`; with `while_running` → allowed, `restart`.
- Running, `refuse`: any folder op → `game_running`; with `while_running` → allowed.
- Running, `allow`: folder ops allowed with the computed `reload_required`.
- Running, any policy, any flag: `RestoreSavedVariables` → `game_running` with fix display "quit the game client, then rerun" and `argv: null`.
- A replacement that renames `Foo_Mainline.toc` to `Foo.toc` while running under `safe` is treated as dropping the loaded TOC.
- The functions are pure and fully table-tested.

## Test Plan

- Unit: one table over (policy × running × legacy × op kind × TOC kept/dropped × while_running) → expected allow/refuse and `reload_required`, covering every row above.
- Unit: `reload_required` maximum over mixed ops; warning text and argv for both fix kinds.
- Unit: config deserialization of `running_policy` (`safe`, `refuse`, `allow`; an unknown value is the config bead's usage error).
- Log the input row and the outcome on failure.

## Considerations

- "Running" means a client of that target is running. Mapping processes to targets is the running-detection bead's job (by `WINEPREFIX` and exe path); this bead takes a boolean per target.
- Legacy reload behavior is UNVERIFIED. If it is later verified that 3.3.5a picks up changes on `/reload`, change the legacy rule in one place and record it on the vision bead.
- Out of scope: reading the policy from config (the command layer passes it in); the SavedVariables deferral flow (undo bead); refusing at commit time with fresh running state (the commit bead calls `evaluate` again under the lock).
acceptance_criteria: When the client is not running every op is allowed and reload_required is none under every policy; running under safe on a modern client allows adds and TOC-preserving replacements with reload, refuses removal of a folder with a loaded TOC with game_running (exit 4) whose fix argv adds --while-running, and allows it with while_running and restart; running under safe on a legacy client refuses any folder op unless while_running, then restart; running under refuse refuses any folder op unless while_running; running under allow permits folder ops with the computed reload_required; RestoreSavedVariables while running is refused under every policy and flag with fix 'quit the game client, then rerun' and argv null; renaming the loaded TOC under safe counts as dropping it; the functions are pure and table-tested
close_reason: The running policy (safe, refuse, allow plus --while-running) is a pure, table-tested evaluation that refuses unsafe changes while a client runs with exact game_running fixes, never allows SavedVariables writes while running, and reports reload_required with a warning

A target is running iff its client_dir has an entry. PrefixOnly can be a false positive (shared WowClassic.exe in one prefix), which is safe for the 'safe' policy.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text:
**Implementation decisions (src/engine/running.rs, RunningPolicy default in src/state/config.rs).**
(1) **Signature:** `evaluate(&PolicyContext { target_id, argv }, policy, running, &ClientRules, &[PolicyOp], while_running) -> Result<PolicyOutcome { reload_required, warnings }>`. The context was added because the game_running fix repeats the original argv plus --while-running and the message names the target id. Refusals are Err(game_running) with details {target, reason, ops: [{op, folder}]} listing only the refused ops. reason is one of saved_variables, policy_refuse, legacy_client, loaded_toc.
(2) **RunningPolicy now derives Default = Safe** (config keeps Option; callers use `config.running_policy.unwrap_or_default()`). Config deserialization of the three values is already covered by the config bead's tests.
(3) Rules as specified. The SavedVariables rule is checked first and wins over everything: its fix is the text 'quit the game client, then rerun' (argv null), with no alternative, since --while-running cannot help. A folder refusal's fix is `<argv> --while-running` with the alternative 'quit the game client, then rerun' (text). --while-running overrides refuse as well as safe.
(4) **reload_required per op:** legacy client is restart; dropping a loaded TOC (a remove with a loaded TOC, or a replace whose new TOC names lack the loaded one, case-insensitively) is restart; **removing a folder with no loaded TOC is none**, because nothing the client loaded changes (the bead text did not cover this case); any other add or replace is reload. The maximum across ops is reported, with one reload_required warning (fix text '/reload in game' or 'restart the game client', argv null).
(5) Table test: 18 rows over policy × running × legacy × op × kept/dropped × while_running, plus SV-always-refused under every policy and flag, fix and alternative shapes, max-plus-warning, and TOC-rename detection.
(6) Test flake found and fixed in engine::testing (6.11's crash test): flock locks are shared across fork, so a child that a concurrent lib test forks (config credential commands) briefly keeps a dropped InflightLock alive. Scene.inflight is now Option and `release_inflight()` waits (bounded) until is_live is false. This is correct production behavior, not an engine bug.

title: Epic: M1 commands and checkpoint verification
description:
## Background

M1 ("working slice", vision omad-vision-8qa §7) ends when a user or an agent can install, reinstall-to-update, remove and undo addons from keyless GitHub, git, URL and local sources into every discovered target, including WoW: Forever and legacy private-server clients, through the final transaction engine and the core CLI contract. The other M1 epics build the parts: the contract core and domain model (E1), fsx, locks and state (E2), discovery and target identity (E3), ClientRules and the TOC engine (E4), the network layer and sources (E5), and the transaction engine (E6). This epic turns those parts into the commands people and agents actually run, then proves the milestone against its checkpoint list.

The M1 command set (vision §7 M1 "Commands"): `install` (including reinstall-to-update), `remove`, `undo`, `history`, `status` (offline triage: targets, records, running state, warnings), `list`, `targets`, `info` (no changelog), `config` (owned by the E2 config bead), `net-log`, and `--dry-run` on every mutating command (plan output only; stored plans and `apply` are M4).

Every command follows the contract core from E1: under `--json` (or `--format json`, `--robot`, `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json`) stdout carries exactly one envelope, success or failure; stderr carries NDJSON events when it is not a TTY; every error has a non-empty `fix` plus `fix_argv`; exit codes come from the general dictionary (0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 not_found, 4 refused, 5 locked, 6 check_failed). Each command bead adds its own clap subcommand and `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (DEC-1); commands receive a `Context` and return an `Outcome`, and never print (DEC-2).

WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04. M1 is scoped to land before it, so the Forever-critical commands (`install`, `remove`, `undo`, `status`) are P1.

## Goals

- Ship `install`, `remove`, `undo`, `history`, `status`, `list`, `targets`, `info` and `net-log` with defined `--json` `data` schemas and human renderers.
- Make the target-default rules concrete: read commands default to all targets; `install` uses the configured default target, else the single compatible live target, else `target_ambiguous` with exact fix commands.
- Prove the CLI contract across every M1 command with one conformance suite (one stdout envelope, `fix` + `fix_argv`, NDJSON stderr, exit codes match the dictionary, every exit site maps to a published code).
- Fuzz every M1 parser and the archive inspector.
- Run the M1 checkpoint list from the vision against fixtures, synthetic trees, live endpoints and the development machine, and update README.md to describe exactly what exists.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- Every vision §7 M1 checkpoint is checked off with recorded evidence (test names, command output, timings) in the m1-checkpoint bead's close reason and a comment on omad-vision-8qa.
- `omaddons <cmd> --json | jq -e .ok` distinguishes success from failure for every M1 command.
- The contract suite, discovery matrix, TOC matrix and engine failure-injection suite pass inside `argc gate`.
- Each fuzz target has run for at least 10 minutes without a crash.
- README.md describes the M1 command set as it exists, and nothing more.

## Non-Goals

- `outdated`, `update`, `pin`/`unpin`, `adopt`, `search`, `export`/`sync`/`copy`, dependency installs, WoWInterface and Tukui sources, `info --changelog` (M2).
- The Omarchy widget, `errors`, `backup`, `--progress json` streaming for long operations (M3).
- `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, verb aliases and intent inference beyond the CLI-skeleton's closest-command fix, stored plans and `apply`, the wire-name golden, the `doctor` surface (M4).
- CurseForge, Wago, `auth`, release engineering (M5).

## Considerations

- Commands are thin: resolution, planning, locking and committing live in the engine (E6); the command layer parses arguments, resolves targets through the registry, calls the engine, and shapes the outcome. Logic that belongs in the engine must not be duplicated in a command.
- `data` structs derive `Serialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema` from day one (DEC-3), so M4's `robot-docs schema` and the wire-name golden need no retrofit. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
- The contract freezes at M4's first tag. Until then, renaming a `data` key is allowed but must update the insta snapshots and the bead that owns the schema.
- Real-machine checks touch the development machine's real AddOns folders. They must undo every transaction they create and leave the machine as they found it, apart from target keys and markers, which M1 expects to be written on first mutation.
- Public-safe bead text: paths are written with placeholders (`<home>`, `<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`).
acceptance_criteria: Every vision §7 M1 checkpoint is checked off with recorded evidence in the m1-checkpoint close reason and a comment on omad-vision-8qa; omaddons <cmd> --json | jq -e .ok distinguishes success from failure for every M1 command; the contract suite, discovery matrix, TOC matrix and engine failure-injection suite pass inside argc gate; each fuzz target has run at least 10 minutes without a crash; README.md describes exactly the M1 command set that exists
close_reason: All children completed

title: Implement the info and net-log commands
description:
## Background

Two small read commands round out M1:

- `info <ref|addon>` answers "what is this addon and what would I get?": the installed records across targets, the catalog entry, and the latest stable release from its source. Changelogs (`--changelog`) arrive in M2 with the WoWInterface and Tukui sources (vision §7 M1 "Commands": `info` without changelog).
- `net-log` makes the privacy claim verifiable by the user rather than asserted (vision G5, D13, §5.7): every HTTP request and git subprocess omaddons makes is logged to `<state>/omaddons/net.log`, with credentials and query secrets stripped at write time, and `omaddons net-log [--since]` renders it.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/info.rs`, `src/app/net_log.rs`, `Info` and `NetLog` subcommands in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

### info

Synopsis (vision §5.9, minus M2's flag): `omaddons info <ref|addon> [-t T]`.

- Resolution through the refs bead: canonical refs, pasted URLs, installed addon names, catalog names and aliases. Bad syntax → `ref_invalid` (2); ambiguity → `ref_ambiguous` (3, candidates); nothing matches → `not_found` (3) with fix `omaddons list` (argv form).
- Installed: every managed record matching the resolved ref or name, across all targets (or the `-t` target): target id/key, version, `version_confidence`, channel, pinned, state, folders, `installed_at`, `tx`.
- Catalog: the catalog entry if the ref or name is in the catalog (name, aliases, families, folders, notes).
- Latest: one fetch through the source (`fetch_once` with a single ref), then `select` per target to report which targets have a metadata candidate. Metadata only: no archive download, no verification (so `targets` here means "has a candidate", not "verified"; the install path verifies).
- `--offline`: decided — no fetch is attempted; `latest` is null and `data.offline` is true, exit 0 (why: info's local part is still useful offline, and `offline` errors are for commands that need the network).
- Fetch failure (network, `rate_limited`, `source_disabled` for `wowi:`/`tukui:`/`cf:`/`wago:` per DEC-12): decided — partial success: exit 0, `partial: true`, `latest: null`, and the error mirrored in `warnings` with the error's own code and fix (same rule as install's per-item failures). If the ref resolves to nothing local and the fetch fails, the fetch error is the command's error.

`--json` `data` schema (`InfoData`):

```
{
  "query": string,
  "ref": string,
  "name": string | null,
  "catalog": {"name": string, "aliases": [string], "families": [string], "folders": [string], "notes": string | null} | null,
  "installed": [
    {"target": {"id": string, "key": string}, "version": string, "version_confidence": "release" | "toc",
     "channel": string, "pinned": bool, "state": "ok" | "degraded", "folders": [string], "installed_at": string, "tx": string}
  ],
  "latest": {"version": string, "release_id": string, "channel": "stable", "flavors": [string], "targets": [string]} | null,
  "offline": bool
}
```

`flavors` are the release.json flavor names (`mainline`, `classic`, `bcc`, `wrath`, `cata`, `mists`, `titan`, `forever`) when present; `targets` are ids of targets with a candidate. `-v` adds asset URLs and record paths.

Human output:

```
WeakAuras  gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2
  catalog: folders WeakAuras, WeakAurasOptions, … · families mainline, mists, vanilla, …
  retail: 5.19.1 (release, stable) installed 2026-10-20
  latest: 5.19.2 · candidates for retail, forever
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3.

### net-log

Synopsis: `omaddons net-log [--since D]`.

- Reads `<state>/omaddons/net.log` and the one rotated previous file kept by the net-core bead (rotation at `NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES` = 10 MiB, keep one previous; use the file name net-core defines), oldest first.
- Each line is one JSON object written by net-core: `{time, method, host, path, status, bytes, duration_ms, purpose, via}` where `via` is `"http"` or `"git"`. Secrets were stripped at write time; this command adds no filtering of its own beyond parsing.
- `--since D`: a duration (`30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `2w`) or RFC 3339 timestamp (jiff). Invalid → `usage` (2) with fix `omaddons net-log --since 1d`. Without `--since`, every entry in both files is returned (bounded by the two 10 MiB files).
- Unparseable lines are skipped and counted (`skipped`), never fatal. A missing log is an empty result, not an error.
- `summary`: request counts per host and per `via`, so "did anything talk to a host I did not expect?" is one glance.
- Never performs network I/O; works under `--offline`.

`--json` `data` schema (`NetLogData`):

```
{
  "entries": [{"time": string, "method": string, "host": string, "path": string, "status": int | null,
               "bytes": int, "duration_ms": int, "purpose": string, "via": "http" | "git"}],
  "summary": {"by_host": {string: int}, "by_via": {string: int}},
  "skipped": int,
  "since": string | null
}
```

Human output: one line per entry (`2026-10-20T14:02:11Z  GET 302  github.com  /WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/releases/latest  0 B  85 ms  latest-tag`), then the summary.

Exit codes: 0, 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons info weakauras --json` with HTTP replay fixtures returns the catalog entry, `latest.version` from the fixture's release tag, `latest.flavors` from its release.json, and `latest.targets` listing the synthetic targets that have candidates.
- After installing it, `installed` lists the record for that target.
- `info weakauras --offline` returns `latest: null`, `offline: true`, exit 0, and net.log is unchanged.
- `info wowi:5108` with no local match exits 1 `source_disabled` (DEC-12) with fix `omaddons help install`.
- For an installed addon whose latest fetch fails (a replay fixture returning 503 on every retry), `info` exits 0 with `partial: true`, `latest: null`, the installed record, and the `http_status` error mirrored in `warnings`.
- `info nosuchaddon` exits 3 `not_found` with a fix.
- After a fixture install, `omaddons net-log --json` lists the GitHub requests with `via: "http"`, `summary.by_host` counts them, and no entry contains a token, `api-key`, `access_token` or an Authorization value (the test plants one in the request and asserts it is absent).
- `net-log --since 1h` filters by time; `--since nonsense` exits 2; a log with a corrupt line reports `skipped: 1`.
- `net-log` reads the rotated previous file too.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `--since` parsing (shared helper with history); net.log line decoding; summary aggregation; info partial-success folding.
- Integration (`tests/info_netlog.rs`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` replay, synthetic trees, HOME/XDG_* tempdirs): the cases above; a rotated log pair written by the test.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per case.

## Considerations

- Added deps beyond the plan's list: `source-github-stable` (fetching `latest` for `gh:` refs needs a real source) and `select` (per-target candidates). Both are P1 beads; this bead stays P2.
- `info --changelog` (GitHub release body, WoWI `UIChangeLog`, Tukui `changelog_url`) is M2.
- `net-log` output can be long; agents should pass `--since`. Pagination is not in the M1 contract.
- Verb alias `show` → info is M4.

(2) Add its canonical name to `app::COMMANDS`, so usage errors name it. (3) Add arms to `app::command_name` and `app::dispatch` that call `src/app/<cmd>.rs`, returning `Result<impl output::Outcome, Error>`; dispatch renders it with `output::emit`. `Context` provides: output, actor, reason, argv (argv[0] = omaddons, for history and fix_argv), offline (flag or OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1), dry_run (read-only commands ignore it), while_running, target (raw -t value), started. comments.text: **registry landed (src/discover/registry.rs, src/state/registry.rs).** Pipeline for a command: `discover(&input, &table)`, then `reconcile(&load_registry(&paths)?.value, &found.targets)` gives `Resolved { targets (key and id filled, key None when unregistered), warnings, missing }`. Then `resolve_one(selector, &resolved.targets, &ctx.argv)` gives target_not_found / target_ambiguous with argv fixes. To register (mutating commands, inside the transaction): `GlobalLock::acquire`, then `LockedRegistry::load(&guard, &paths)?`, then `.ensure_registered(&mut session, &target)?`. The session's ScopeTable must include the target's client dir. Read paths never write.

title: Verify the M1 checkpoints: real-machine smoke, keyless installs, fuzz, probes and README
description:
## Background

Each milestone ends in a usable state: the local gate passes, README.md describes exactly what exists, and contract snapshots are updated (vision §7). This bead closes M1 by running every M1 checkpoint from the vision, recording evidence, adding the real-machine smoke tests, running the checkpoint-only checks that are not part of the per-commit gate (fuzz runs, coverage, live probes, real-machine smoke tests, benchmarks; vision §5.12), and updating README.md.

WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04; M1 is scoped to land before it. M1 alone delivers keyless Forever support: the `release.json` flavor `forever`, the `_Forever`/`_Camelot` TOC suffixes, the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` guard, and 1.60.x family detection for both `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_`.

Placeholders: `<home>` = the user's home directory; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under `<home>`).

## Technical Approach

### Development machine facts (vision §4.7, the real-world oracle)

- Retail: `<home>/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/` (Omarchy's Battle.net prefix, installed with umu-launcher and GE-Proton). `product.db` and `.build.info` both report product `wow`, version `12.1.0.69933` (interface 120100; live is 12.1.5). Only `_retail_` is installed, and its AddOns folder is empty. `dosdevices` maps `c:`, `s:`, `w:`, `x:`, `z:`.
- Custom: `<home>/Games/wow-335/drive_c/WoW/`. Wow.exe is 3.3.5a. `Interface/AddOns` holds 23 `Blizzard_*` folders and nothing else. `Data/enUS/realmlist.wtf` is `set realmlist 127.0.0.1`, a local AzerothCore server.
- Filesystems: the games directory, the XDG state dir and the XDG config dir are btrfs (reflink and `RENAME_EXCHANGE` capable).
- Toolchain present: cargo/rustc (stable pinned by the repo, nightly installed), cargo-deny, cargo-audit, cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-fuzz, hyperfine, ubs.

### Real-machine smoke tests

- `tests/real_machine.rs`, every test `#[ignore]` and additionally gated on `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1` (decided name; vision §5.12 says "ignored by default, enabled by an environment variable"). These tests use the real HOME and XDG dirs, never tempdirs.
- They must leave the machine as they found it: every transaction they create is undone at the end (`omaddons undo` per tx, newest first), and the test asserts each touched AddOns folder's tree hash equals its value before the test. Target keys and markers written on first mutation are expected and stay.
- Live network: the keyless install checks run with `OMADDONS_LIVE=1` against real endpoints, once, at the checkpoint.

### M1 checkpoint list (vision §7 M1, copied verbatim; each item is checked off with evidence)

- [ ] On the development machine, `omaddons status --json` reports:
  - `retail` (from `product.db` and `.build.info`; 12.1.x);
  - the 3.3.5a target (`wrath-legacy`, interface 30300, label "localhost") with 23 protected folders.

  Both receive stable keys and markers on their first mutation.
- [ ] Synthetic trees resolve correctly:
  - every product in §4.1, including `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_` at 1.60.x;
  - every legacy `ClientRules` row;
  - a game on a mapped drive letter outside `drive_c`;
  - a custom client outside any prefix;
  - each launcher config;
  - an unknown `_xyz_` folder (yields a usable `unknown` target).
- [ ] TOC load-rule tests cover every suffix in §4.3, the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` case, comma Interface lists, and every legacy `ClientRules` row (1.12.1, 2.4.3, 3.3.5a, 4.3.4, 5.4.8). A modern `classic`-flavor build never verifies against a 1.12.1 client.
- [ ] Keyless installs into the real retail target and a synthetic Forever target: WeakAuras, DBM, BigWigs, Plater, Bartender4. Every resolved file is verified by TOC load rules; WeakAuras never installs a wrong-flavor build. A legacy addon installs into the 3.3.5a target from a git repo and from a GitHub release. `Blizzard_*` folders are untouched.
- [ ] Installing `release.json` publishers on the stable channel performs zero GitHub REST requests (asserted from `net.log` in fixtures).
- [ ] Failure injection:
  - a failure injected at every engine step leaves each folder wholly old or wholly new;
  - recovery happens only under the lock;
  - a reader running during a live swap reports `tx_in_progress` and changes nothing.
- [ ] Two concurrent installs into the same target both complete without `locked` (or one becomes a no-op). Lock hold time per commit is < 50 ms on fixtures.
- [ ] `undo`:
  - restores folders byte-for-byte;
  - SavedVariables follow the policy (unchanged → untouched; changed → cloned then restored; client running → deferred);
  - `undo_conflict` is raised across transaction kinds;
  - `undo --last-by agent` reverts only that actor's transaction.
- [ ] The hostile archive suite (including case-folded collisions) is rejected; nothing is written outside staging. Creating `blizzard_auctionui/` beside `Blizzard_AuctionUI/` is refused.
- [ ] A request or redirect to a non-allowlisted host fails with `host_blocked`. Every HTTP request and git subprocess appears in `net.log` without credentials.
- [ ] Contract core:
  - bare `omaddons` prints help;
  - every M1 command accepts `--json` and emits exactly one stdout envelope on success and on failure (`cmd --json | jq -e .ok` distinguishes failure);
  - every error has a non-empty `fix` and a `fix_argv`;
  - stderr is NDJSON when it is not a TTY;
  - exit sites match the general dictionary.
- [ ] The local gate passes; fuzz targets each run ≥ 10 min without crashes.

### Where each item's evidence comes from

| Item | Evidence |
|---|---|
| status on the development machine | `tests/real_machine.rs::status_reports_retail_and_335` output (JSON attached to the close reason, with home paths replaced by `<home>`) |
| synthetic trees | discover-matrix suite (`cargo test` names) |
| TOC load rules | toc-matrix suite |
| keyless installs | `tests/real_machine.rs::keyless_installs_retail` (live), a synthetic Forever tree run live with `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`, plus the fixture versions in the source and install suites; legacy addon via a catalog legacy entry from git (`git:` ref) and from a GitHub release; a before/after hash of every `Blizzard_*` folder |
| zero REST | fixture test counting `api.github.com` lines in `net.log` |
| failure injection, concurrency, lock hold | engine-tests suite; lock hold time printed by the debug log and recorded |
| undo | engine-tests and cmd-undo-history suites |
| hostile archives | archive-inspect suite and ownership tests |
| allowlist, net.log | net-core suite |
| contract core | contract-suite |
| gate, fuzz | `argc gate --all` output; `argc fuzz-all --time 600` output |

### Other checkpoint-only checks

- Live probes: `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored` (net-fixtures bead); every keyless endpoint used in M1 decodes with the production decoders.
- Coverage: `cargo llvm-cov --summary-only`, recorded (no threshold in M1).
- Benchmarks: `hyperfine 'omaddons status --json --cached'` on the development machine (target < 5 ms, vision §5.8), recorded.
- Lock hold time per commit on fixtures (< 50 ms), recorded.

### README.md

Update README.md to describe exactly what exists after M1: what the tool does today, the M1 commands with one example each, the `--json` contract in brief, the exit-code table, the safety model in plain words (transactions, undo, protected `Blizzard_*` folders, running-client policy), privacy (host allowlist, `net-log`, `--offline`, no telemetry), the gate, and what is not there yet (M2–M5). Nothing that does not exist. Run the de-slopify pass on it.

### Recording

- Close this bead with a reason that lists each checkpoint item and its evidence (test names, timings, command outputs with home paths replaced by placeholders).
- Add a comment on omad-vision-8qa ticking M1 in "§10 Milestone status" and recording any deviations (do not edit the vision body).
- File beads for anything that failed or was deferred, with `--deps discovered-from:<this bead>`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every item in the M1 checkpoint list above is checked off with evidence recorded in the close reason.
- `tests/real_machine.rs` exists, is ignored by default, runs only with `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1`, and leaves every touched AddOns folder hash-identical to its starting state.
- `argc gate --all` passes; `argc fuzz-all --time 600` completes with no crash for every target.
- Live probes pass with `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`.
- Coverage summary, `status --cached` timing and lock hold time are recorded.
- README.md describes exactly what exists after M1.
- A comment on omad-vision-8qa ticks M1 and lists deviations; follow-up beads exist for every failed or deferred item.

## Test Plan

- Unit: none new.
- E2E: `tests/real_machine.rs` (status on the development machine; keyless installs into real retail with undo; legacy installs into the 3.3.5a target with undo; `Blizzard_*` hash check).
- Checkpoint runs: discovery matrix, TOC matrix, engine-tests, contract-suite, live probes, fuzz-all, coverage, hyperfine, all logged with full output.

## Considerations

- The real-machine tests modify the user's real AddOns folders while they run. They must never run in the gate, must undo what they did, and must refuse to run if the target's client is running (check running state first and skip with a message).
- Upstream data changes between fixture recording and the live run (for example a new WeakAuras release) are expected; the live run asserts verification, not exact versions.
- If Forever's launch layout (`wowf` / `_forever_`) changes before 2026-11-04, the discovery tables are data (D15); update the fixtures and record the change here.
- Legacy addon choice: use a catalog entry verified by the catalog bead for the 3.3.5a family that offers both a git repo and a GitHub release; if none offers both, use two entries and say so in the close reason.

title: Implement the install command with target defaulting, partial success, --strict and --dry-run
description:
## Background

`install` is the command M1 exists for: put an addon from a keyless source into a target, verified against that client's own TOC load rules, through the journaled transaction engine, reversible with `omaddons undo`. In M1 it also covers updating: installing an addon that is already installed, when the source has a newer release, replaces it (`kind: update`). `outdated`/`update` arrive in M2.

The engine (E6: `plan` → `stage` → `commit`) does the work. This bead is the command layer: argument parsing, target defaulting and registration, calling the engine, partial-success semantics, `--strict`, `--dry-run`, the `data` schema and the human renderer. Vision references: §5.9 (contract, behavior), §5.4 (refs, selection), §5.5 (engine), §5.1 (records).

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/` for a target; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/install.rs` (command), a `Install` subcommand added to `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1), human renderer in the same module or `src/output/human/install.rs`.

Synopsis (vision §5.9):

```
omaddons install <ref|url|path>... [-t T] [--channel C] [--version V] [--file <zip>] [--no-deps] [--force] [--strict]
global flags that apply: --dry-run --actor --reason --offline --while-running --json/--format/--robot -v --quiet
```

Arguments:
- Each positional is parsed by the refs bead (`src/sources/refs.rs`): canonical refs (`gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2`, `git:<url>[#rev]`, `url:<https-zip>`, `file:<path>`), pasted GitHub URLs, https zip URLs, local paths, installed addon names, and catalog names/aliases (`omaddons install weakauras`). `wowi:`/`tukui:`/`cf:`/`wago:` refs parse but fail at fetch with `source_disabled` (DEC-12). Bad syntax → `ref_invalid` (exit 2); ambiguity → `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3, candidates in `details`).
- `--channel stable|beta|alpha` (default: the addon's recorded channel, else config `default_channel`, else `stable`). The chosen channel is stored on the record. beta/alpha for `gh:` refs use REST (source-github-rest); until that bead lands the GitHub source reports the limitation as its own error.
- `--version V`: install that exact release. Honored for `gh:` (tag) and `git:` (rev); for `url:`/`file:` it is a `usage` error (exit 2). An unknown tag → `not_found` (exit 3).
- `--file <zip>`: install a manually obtained archive as the release of the single given ref. Decided: exactly one positional ref is allowed with `--file` (more → `usage`). In M1 no source provides an expected hash for manual files, so the archive is verified by TOC load rules only; the record keeps the ref, takes its version from the TOC `## Version` (`version_confidence: "toc"`) and sets `release_id` to null. When a later source provides an expected hash (CurseForge, M5), a mismatch is `hash_mismatch`.
- `--no-deps`: accepted and ignored in M1 (dependency resolution is M2), with no warning.
- `--force`: overrides `ownership_conflict` (moves the folder to the new addon, previous owner becomes `degraded`, warning `ownership_transferred`) and `unmanaged_folder` (snapshots and replaces the unmanaged folder). It never overrides `protected_folder` or `case_collision` (vision §5.5 step 4, D14).
- `--strict`: a partial success becomes exit 6 `check_failed` with `ok: false` and `data` still populated.

Target defaulting (vision §5.9 "Target defaults"):
1. `-t T` given → resolve through the registry's `-t` resolver (id, key, family name, product code, flavor folder name, install root, AddOns path). Not found → `target_not_found` (3); more than one match → `target_ambiguous` (3).
2. Else the configured default target (config `default_target` or the registry default).
3. Else the single compatible target. Decided: compatibility is decided by planning each requested ref against every discovered `live` target (fetch once, select, download into the blob cache, inspect, verify); `test` targets (PTR/XPTR/beta) are only ever chosen with an explicit `-t` (why: otherwise every machine with a PTR installed would make every install ambiguous; this matches `sync`'s rule that test targets are addressed only explicitly).
4. More than one compatible live target → `target_ambiguous` (3) with `details.candidates` (ids), `fix` = the original argv with `-t <first candidate>` appended, `alternatives` = the same for each other candidate. Example: `{"code":"target_ambiguous","message":"weakauras is compatible with 2 targets","fix":"omaddons install weakauras -t retail","fix_argv":["omaddons","install","weakauras","-t","retail"],"alternatives":[{"display":"omaddons install weakauras -t forever","argv":["omaddons","install","weakauras","-t","forever"]}]}`.
5. No discovered targets → `target_not_found` (3) with fix `omaddons targets add <path>` (argv null because `<path>` must be filled in). No compatible live target → `no_compatible_release` (3) listing the targets checked.

Execution:
- One transaction per command run (one target). Per-item failures discovered during planning (fetch, select, verify, ownership) are excluded; the remaining items commit atomically in one transaction. Decided: the transaction kind is `update` when every changed item is an update, else `install`.
- Registration: the first mutating run on an unregistered target assigns its key and writes its marker under the global lock (registry bead API, called from the commit path). `--dry-run` never registers.
- Idempotent: an already-current addon is `status: "unchanged"` with an empty folder change list. If nothing changes at all, no transaction is created (`tx: null`), exit 0.
- `--dry-run` (DEC-15, DEC-16): runs fetch, select, download, inspect, verify and ownership; writes only derived data (blob cache, HTTP validators); never stages into the client dir, never takes the global lock, never writes state. Output is the same `data` schema with `dry_run: true` and `tx: null`.
- Partial success (vision §5.9 exit dictionary): if at least one item succeeded or was unchanged and at least one failed, exit 0 with `partial: true`; each failure appears in `data.items[].error` and is mirrored in `warnings`. Decided: a mirrored per-item failure is a warning whose `code` is the failing item's error code (for example `no_compatible_release`) and whose `fix`/`fix_argv` are that error's fix; the `Warning` type must accept an error code as its code (coordinate with the error-registry bead; add the variant here if it is missing). If every item fails, the command fails with the first failing item's error (argument order), `details.items` listing every item's error, and that error's exit code.
- Outcome extras: when a transaction committed, `commands` contains `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo <tx>","argv":["omaddons","undo","<tx>"],"destructive":false}`. When `reload_required` is `reload`, add warning `reload_required` with fix display `/reload in game` and `fix_argv: null`; when `restart`, the same warning with fix display `restart the game client`. If the engine reported `atomic_swap: false`, the engine's `atomic_swap_unavailable` warning passes through. Engine warnings (`journal_recovered`, `out_of_date`, `toc_comma_on_legacy`, `ownership_transferred`) pass through unchanged.

`--json` `data` schema (`InstallData`, field order is wire order):

```
{
  "dry_run": bool,
  "target": {"id": string, "key": string | null},   // key null only under --dry-run on an unregistered target
  "tx": string | null,                                // ULID of the committed transaction
  "kind": "install" | "update" | null,                // null when nothing changed
  "items": [
    {
      "request": string,                              // the positional exactly as given
      "ref": string | null,                           // canonical ref, null if parsing failed
      "name": string | null,                          // addon name (record key)
      "status": "installed" | "updated" | "unchanged" | "failed",
      "from_version": string | null,
      "to_version": string | null,
      "version_confidence": "release" | "toc" | null,
      "channel": "stable" | "beta" | "alpha" | null,
      "folders": {"added": [string], "replaced": [string], "removed": [string]},
      "error": {"code": string, "message": string, "fix": string, "fix_argv": [string] | null} | null
    }
  ],
  "reload_required": "none" | "reload" | "restart",
  "atomic_swap": bool | null                          // null when no swap happened
}
```

Folder lists are sorted by key; `items` keep argument order. `-v` adds `paths` (client dir) and the release asset URL per item; default output stays token-frugal.

Human output (stdout):

```
retail: installed WeakAuras 5.19.2 (3 folders)
retail: DBM-Core unchanged (11.2.5)
retail: failed BigWigs: no_compatible_release: no release verifies for mainline 120105
tx 01JB… · /reload in game · undo: omaddons undo 01JB…
```

Errors in human mode leave stdout empty; the error goes to stderr per the output bead.

Exit codes this command can return: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons install <ref> -t <id> --json` against fixtures installs the addon, prints exactly one envelope with `ok: true`, `data.tx` set and `data.items[0].status == "installed"`, and the folders exist in `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns`.
- Re-running the same install prints `status: "unchanged"`, `tx: null`, exit 0, and changes nothing on disk.
- With a newer fixture release, the same install reports `status: "updated"`, `kind: "update"`, `from_version`/`to_version` set.
- With two compatible live targets and no default, the command exits 3 `target_ambiguous` with `fix_argv` ending in `-t <id>` and one `alternatives` entry per other candidate; running that `fix_argv` succeeds.
- A `test`-kind target is never chosen implicitly.
- Mixed success and failure exits 0 with `partial: true`, the failure in `data.items[].error` and mirrored in `warnings`; with `--strict` the same run exits 6, `ok: false`, `error.code == "check_failed"`, `data` populated.
- When every item fails, the envelope is the first item's error with its exit code.
- `--dry-run` returns the same schema with `dry_run: true`, `tx: null`, writes nothing under the client dir or `<state>/omaddons`, and does not register the target.
- `--file <zip>` installs a local archive under the given ref with `version_confidence: "toc"`.
- `protected_folder`, `case_collision`, `ownership_conflict`, `unmanaged_folder`, `wrong_flavor`, `game_running` each produce exit 4 with a non-empty `fix`; `--force` resolves only the two documented cases.
- `commands` contains an undo hint with argv after every committed transaction; a `reload_required` warning appears when the engine reports reload or restart.
- The first mutating install on an unregistered target writes its registry entry and marker; key and id are stable on later runs.
- Insta snapshots cover the success, unchanged, partial and ambiguous envelopes (meta stripped).

## Test Plan

- Unit: target defaulting (default target set, single compatible live target, two compatible → ambiguous with exact argv, test targets skipped, no targets); partial-success folding (some fail, all fail, all unchanged); `--strict` mapping; transaction kind selection; argument validation (`--file` with two refs, `--version` with `url:`).
- Integration (`tests/install.rs`, synthetic trees from `tests/common/trees.rs`, archives from `tests/common/archives.rs`, HTTP replay via `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`): install from `file:` zip; install from `gh:` with release.json fixtures (WeakAuras2 without a mainline entry must pick a verified build or fail with `no_compatible_release`, never a wrong-flavor build); reinstall-to-update; idempotent re-run; `--dry-run` writes nothing (hash the client dir and state dir before and after); `--file`; `--force` on an unmanaged folder then `omaddons undo` restores it; `blizzard_auctionui` vs `Blizzard_AuctionUI` refused.
- E2E contract: every case above run with `--json` asserts exactly one stdout JSON document and the exit code; stderr lines parse as NDJSON.
- Log test inputs (argv, env) and full stdout/stderr on failure.

## Considerations

- The compatibility probe for implicit targets downloads candidate archives for every live target. It is bounded by fetch-once and the blob cache; with many targets it is slower than an explicit `-t`, which the ambiguous-target fix steers users toward.
- `--file` with a ref whose source later provides hashes must switch to hash verification; keep the verification step behind the source's `expected_hash` so M5 only supplies the hash.
- The `<home>/Downloads` lookup after `distribution_disabled` is CurseForge-only (M5); out of scope here.
- Verb aliases (`add` → install) are M4.
- Dependency installs (`reason: dependency`) are M2; `--no-deps` is accepted now so scripts written against M1 keep working.
- Added coordination point, not a new dep: the mirrored-failure warning needs `Warning` to carry an error code (error-registry bead).
acceptance_criteria: install <ref> -t <id> --json installs from fixtures with exactly one envelope, ok true, data.tx set and status installed; re-running reports unchanged, tx null, exit 0, no disk change; a newer fixture release reports status updated and kind update; two compatible live targets without a default exit 3 target_ambiguous with fix_argv ending in -t <id> and one alternative per other candidate, and running fix_argv succeeds; test-kind targets are never chosen implicitly; mixed success exits 0 partial true with failures in data.items[].error mirrored in warnings, and --strict turns it into exit 6 check_failed with data populated; all items failing returns the first item's error and exit code; --dry-run returns the same schema with dry_run true and tx null, writes nothing under the client dir or <state>/omaddons and does not register; --file installs a local archive with version_confidence toc; protected_folder, case_collision, ownership_conflict, unmanaged_folder, wrong_flavor and game_running exit 4 with non-empty fix and --force resolves only ownership_conflict and unmanaged_folder; committed transactions add an undo hint with argv and reload/restart adds a reload_required warning; the first mutation registers the target with a stable key and marker; insta snapshots cover success, unchanged, partial and ambiguous envelopes
close_reason: install command with target defaulting, compatibility probe, partial success, --strict, --dry-run, --file and catalog naming

An item failing on every live target does not decide either; if every item fails everywhere the command fails like an all-failed run (first item's error; a purely client-specific failure becomes `no_compatible_release` listing the checked targets). A target-level commit failure fails every changed item. Partial success mirrors each failure as `Warning::item` (message prefixed with the request unless it already names it).
