title: Implement the list command over records and folder inventory
description:
## Background

`list` shows what is in each target's AddOns folder: the managed addons with their versions and sources, and, on request, the folders omaddons does not manage. The reference project only listed unmanaged folders and exposed `Blizzard_*` folders of custom clients as if they were mutable (vision §3, R9); omaddons classifies every folder by its case-folded key and never offers protected or linked folders for mutation.

The inventory bead (E4) does the classification and TOC reading. This bead is the command layer: argument parsing, per-target assembly from records plus inventory, the `data` schema and human output.

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = a target's directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/list.rs`, a `List` subcommand in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons list [-t T] [--unmanaged] [--protected]`. Read-only: no lock, no writes, no network.

- Targets: all discovered targets by default (read commands default to all targets), including unregistered ones (`key: null`, provisional id, no managed addons). `-t T` narrows to one via the registry resolver (`target_not_found` / `target_ambiguous`, exit 3).
- Managed addons come from `<state>/omaddons/targets/<key>.json`: name, version, `version_confidence` (`release` | `toc`), canonical ref, channel, pinned, state (`ok` | `degraded`), folders.
- Folder classes come from the inventory bead, by `FolderName::key()` (ASCII case-fold, matching Wine's case-insensitive lookup):
  - `protected`: key starts with `blizzard_`;
  - `managed`: owned by exactly one managed addon;
  - `linked`: a symlink (for example a developer's working copy); listed, never mutated, never followed outside AddOns;
  - `unmanaged`: everything else;
  - `invalid`: an entry whose name fails `FolderName` validation; listed, never mutated.
  Two folders whose names differ only in case are flagged `case_duplicate: true` on both entries (which one the client loads is undefined under Wine).
- Default output: managed addons per target plus counts of every class. `--unmanaged` adds the `unmanaged`, `linked` and `invalid` entries. Decided: linked and invalid entries ride on `--unmanaged` (why: they are not managed, and a separate flag per class would bloat the surface). `--protected` adds the `protected` entries.
- Unmanaged entries carry the TOC metadata the inventory reads (Title, Version, Interface, and the TOC-load verdict against the target: `compatible`, `out_of_date`, `wrong_flavor` or `no_toc`), so an agent can see what an unmanaged folder is before M2's `adopt`. Protected entries carry only the folder name (token-frugal; a 3.3.5a client pack has 23 of them).
- A managed record whose folder is missing on disk is reported with `missing_folders: [..]` on that addon (the doctor finding `record-folder-missing` arrives in M4).
- Token-frugal by default (vision §5.9): ids, names, versions and counts. `-v` adds folder lists per addon, `client_dir`, and TOC metadata for managed folders.

`--json` `data` schema (`ListData`):

```
{
  "targets": [
    {
      "id": string,
      "key": string | null,
      "addons": [
        {
          "name": string,
          "version": string,
          "version_confidence": "release" | "toc",
          "ref": string,
          "channel": "stable" | "beta" | "alpha",
          "pinned": bool,
          "state": "ok" | "degraded",
          "folders": int,                       // -v: [string]
          "missing_folders": [string]
        }
      ],
      "counts": {"managed": int, "unmanaged": int, "protected": int, "linked": int, "invalid": int},
      "unmanaged": [ {"folder": string, "class": "unmanaged" | "linked" | "invalid", "title": string | null, "version": string | null, "interface": int | null, "verdict": "compatible" | "out_of_date" | "wrong_flavor" | "no_toc" | null, "case_duplicate": bool} ] | null,
      "protected": [ {"folder": string} ] | null
    }
  ]
}
```

`unmanaged` is null without `--unmanaged`; `protected` is null without `--protected`. Targets sort by id; addons by name (case-insensitive); folders by key.

Human output:

```
retail (12.1.0.69933, mainline)
  WeakAuras   5.19.2   gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2   stable
  DBM-Core    11.2.5   gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods  stable  degraded
  2 managed · 1 unmanaged · 0 protected · 0 linked
wotlk (3.3.5.12340, wrath-legacy, localhost)
  0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 23 protected · 0 linked
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a synthetic retail target with two installed addons, one unmanaged folder and one symlinked folder, `omaddons list --json` reports both addons with name, version, ref and channel, and counts `managed 2, unmanaged 1, protected 0, linked 1`; `unmanaged` and `protected` are null.
- `--unmanaged` adds the unmanaged folder with its TOC Title, Version, Interface and verdict, and the linked folder with `class: "linked"`.
- On a synthetic 3.3.5a target, `--protected` lists 23 `Blizzard_*` folders; a lowercase `blizzard_custom` folder is also classified protected.
- Folders `Foo` and `foo` side by side are both flagged `case_duplicate: true`.
- A record whose folder was deleted reports it in `missing_folders`.
- `list` writes nothing and performs no network I/O (hash check of state, cache and client dirs; net.log unchanged).
- `-t unknown` exits 3 `target_not_found` with a fix.

## Test Plan

- Unit: assembly of records plus inventory into `ListData`; flag handling (`unmanaged`/`protected` null vs populated); sorting.
- Integration (`tests/list.rs`, synthetic trees, `file:` installs for managed records, a symlink created in the test, a 3.3.5a tree with 23 `Blizzard_*` folders): the cases above, plus `-v` output containing folder lists.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per case.

- `adopt` (bringing unmanaged folders under management by confidence tier) is M2; the verdict and TOC metadata shown here are what M2's adoption will build on.
- Reading TOCs for many unmanaged folders costs a little I/O; it happens only with `--unmanaged` or `-v`.
- Verb alias `ls` → list is M4.
- Symlinks are never followed outside AddOns; a symlink pointing at a non-directory is still `linked`.

title: Implement the remove command as an undoable transaction
description:
## Background

`remove` takes managed addons out of a target. Like every mutation it is a journaled, snapshotted transaction (kind `remove`) attributed to an actor and reversible with `omaddons undo` (vision §5.5, §5.9). Removal never deletes: the engine renames each live folder into the transaction's snapshot directory (`<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`), so undo can rename it back. SavedVariables are not touched by remove; the engine still snapshots the touched folders' SavedVariables so undo can apply its policy.

This bead is the command layer on top of the engine (E6 `commit`): argument parsing, resolving names to a target and its records, calling the engine with remove ops, partial-success semantics, `--dry-run`, the `data` schema and the human renderer.

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/` for a target.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/remove.rs`, a `Remove` subcommand in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons remove <addon>... [-t T]`, plus the global `--dry-run`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--while-running`, `--json`.

Name resolution:
- Each positional matches a managed addon record by record name (ASCII case-insensitive), by canonical ref (`gh:Owner/Repo`), or by the key of a folder the addon owns (removing `DBM-Core` removes the addon that owns it). Two addons matching one positional inside a target → `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3) with candidates.
- With `-t T`: resolve the target with the registry's `-t` resolver (`target_not_found` / `target_ambiguous`, exit 3); names are looked up in that target only.
- Without `-t`: each name is looked up across all registered targets. Decided: all names must resolve to one target. If a name is managed in more than one target, or the names span targets, fail with `target_ambiguous` (exit 3), `fix` = the original argv with `-t <first candidate>` appended and `alternatives` for the rest (why: a removal is one transaction on one target; silently picking a target, or fanning out, would surprise people).
- A name not managed anywhere (or not in the given target) → item error `not_managed` (exit 3). Unregistered targets have no records, so nothing there is removable.
- Protected (`Blizzard_*`), linked (symlink) and unmanaged folders are never removable by this command; naming one yields `not_managed` with a message saying which class the folder is.

Execution:
- One transaction per run on the resolved target, containing a remove op for every folder of every resolved addon. The engine applies the running policy: while the target's client runs, removing a folder whose TOC is loaded is refused with `game_running` (exit 4) under the default `safe` policy unless `--while-running`; on a `legacy` client any mutation while running is refused. `reload_required` comes from the engine (removing a loaded TOC means `restart`).
- The engine deletes the addon records, increments the target's `generation`, updates the per-file index, appends `history.jsonl` (`kind: remove`, actor, reason, argv), and rewrites `status.json`.
- Dependents warnings and orphan reporting arrive with dependency resolution in M2; M1 removes exactly what was named.
- Partial success: at least one addon removed and at least one item failed → exit 0, `partial: true`, failures in `data.items[].error`, mirrored in `warnings` (warning `code` = the item's error code, as decided in the install bead). Every item failing → the first item's error and exit code, `details.items` listing all. `--strict` is not offered on remove (vision lists it on install, update, sync and copy only).
- `--dry-run`: resolves names and computes the ops and the running-policy verdict; takes no lock, writes nothing. Same schema with `dry_run: true`, `tx: null` (DEC-16).
- After a commit, `commands` holds the undo hint `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo <tx>","argv":["omaddons","undo","<tx>"],"destructive":false}`, and a `reload_required` warning is added when reload or restart is needed (fix display `/reload in game` or `restart the game client`, `fix_argv: null`).

`--json` `data` schema (`RemoveData`):

```
{
  "dry_run": bool,
  "target": {"id": string, "key": string},
  "tx": string | null,
  "items": [
    {
      "request": string,
      "name": string | null,
      "ref": string | null,
      "status": "removed" | "failed",
      "version": string | null,
      "folders": [string],                         // folders moved into the snapshot, sorted by key
      "error": {"code": string, "message": string, "fix": string, "fix_argv": [string] | null} | null
    }
  ],
  "reload_required": "none" | "reload" | "restart",
  "atomic_swap": bool | null
}
```

Human output:

```
retail: removed Bartender4 4.15.2 (1 folder)
retail: failed Questie: not_managed: Questie is not managed in retail
tx 01JB… · restart the game client · undo: omaddons undo 01JB…
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons remove <addon> -t <id> --json` removes every folder of the addon from `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns`, moves them under `Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`, deletes the record, increments `generation`, appends a `kind: remove` history entry, and prints one envelope with `status: "removed"` and an undo hint with argv.
- `omaddons undo` immediately afterwards restores the folders byte-for-byte and the record.
- Removing by folder key (for example `DBM-Core`) removes the owning addon; removing by canonical ref works.
- A name that is not managed yields `not_managed` (exit 3) with a non-empty fix; naming a `Blizzard_*`, linked or unmanaged folder yields `not_managed` and never touches it.
- Without `-t`, a name managed in two targets fails with `target_ambiguous` (exit 3) whose `fix_argv` adds `-t <id>`.
- Mixed results exit 0 with `partial: true` and mirrored warnings; all failing returns the first item's error.
- While the client runs (fake /proc), removing a loaded folder is refused with `game_running` (exit 4) under `safe`; `--while-running` allows it and reports `reload_required: "restart"`.
- `--dry-run` reports the ops with `tx: null` and leaves the client dir and state untouched.

## Test Plan

- Unit: name resolution (record name case-insensitive, ref, owned folder key, ambiguous within a target, spans targets without `-t`, not managed, protected/linked/unmanaged folder named), partial-success folding.
- Integration (`tests/remove.rs`, synthetic trees, `file:` installs to set up records, fake /proc tree for the running client): remove then undo round-trip comparing folder hashes; remove by folder key; refused removal while running; `--while-running`; `--dry-run` writes nothing (hash before/after).
- E2E contract: every case under `--json` has exactly one stdout document and the documented exit code.
- Log argv, env and full stdout/stderr on failure.

## Considerations

- Removing a required dependency, dependents warnings and `orphan` reporting are M2.
- Verb aliases (`uninstall`, `rm`, `delete`) are M4.
- SavedVariables of the removed addon stay in `WTF/` (the client owns them); removal does not offer to delete them, and backups are M3.
- Retention eventually prunes the snapshot holding removed folders (24 h minimum); after that, undo of the removal is impossible, and the undo bead reports it as `not_found` for the snapshot.

close_reason: remove command: name/ref/folder resolution, one-target rule, not_managed classes, partial success, engine running policy, undo round trip

title: Implement the status command as offline triage with --cached and --check
description:
## Background

`status` is the triage command and the first call for orientation (vision §5.8, §5.10, D19). The full version reports every target, pending update counts, doctor findings by severity, recent Lua error counts, live running state, journal warnings and a `commands` list of recommended next actions. Updates arrive in M2, Lua errors in M3 and doctor findings in M4, so the M1 version is offline triage only: targets, records, folder counts, live running state, journal and state-version warnings.

`status --cached` is the Omarchy widget's authority from M3 onward (`omaddons status --json --cached`): local state only, under 5 ms, no network. M1 sets that contract now so the widget can rely on it later. The first M1 checkpoint is also a `status --json` run on the development machine.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache`); `<client dir>` = a target's directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/status.rs`, a `Status` subcommand in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons status [-t T] [--cached] [--check]`. Default: all targets (read commands default to all targets). `-t T` narrows to one (registry resolver; unknown → `target_not_found`, exit 3).

Sources of truth:
- Targets: discovery (`discover()`, E3) merged with the registry (`<state>/omaddons/registry.json`). Registered targets carry their ULID `key`; discovered-but-unregistered targets carry `key: null` and the deterministic provisional id from the registry bead. Registered targets whose client dir no longer exists are listed with `missing: true`.
- Records: `<state>/omaddons/targets/<key>.json` (managed addons, `generation`, addon `state: ok|degraded`).
- Folder counts: the inventory bead's classification of `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns` by case-folded key: `managed`, `unmanaged`, `protected` (`blizzard_` prefix), `linked` (symlinks), `invalid` (names that fail `FolderName` validation). Status uses classification only, without reading TOC metadata: call the inventory with `Depth::Classes`, which opens no TOC files, to stay inside the 5 ms `--cached` budget.
- Running state: computed live on every call, including `--cached`, by the running-detection bead (reads `/proc`, ~1–2 ms).
- Journal: the journal bead's reader API: list `<state>/omaddons/journal/`, probe the global lock without blocking, and produce `journal_pending` (lock free) or `tx_in_progress` (lock held) warnings with their fixes. Status never recovers journals.
- State versions: loading state files may yield `state_version_older` or `state_version_newer` warnings (state-store bead); status passes them through.

`--cached` (vision §5.8): reads local state only and never scans. It uses the registry, the discovery cache (`<cache>/omaddons/discovery.json`, discover-cache bead) and the records; it never runs the bounded scan and never reads TOCs. Decided: when the discovery cache is absent, `--cached` lists registered targets only and adds a `commands` entry `omaddons status` (why: the full scan costs more than the 5 ms budget, and the widget must never block on it). Budget: under 5 ms on a warm machine with a handful of targets (hyperfine at the checkpoint).

Decided: status never writes, with or without `--cached` (it is a read command). `status.json` is written by commits only.

Without `--cached` M1 status is still fully offline: it runs discovery (which uses the discovery cache when valid) and inventory classification. No network in M1 at all.

Attention (per target, M1 definition): a target needs attention when any of these hold, listed in `attention` as a status-local enum (pinned in M4's wire-name golden):
- `journal_pending` — an unrecovered journal touches this target (lock free);
- `state_version_newer` — the target record is newer than this binary (writes refused, `state_too_new`);
- `target_missing` — registered, but the client dir is gone;
- `addon_degraded` — at least one addon record has `state: degraded` (for example after `--force` transferred a folder).

`tx_in_progress` is a warning, not attention: another process is working.

`--check` (vision §5.9): exits 6 when any target needs attention, returning `ok: false`, `error.code = "check_failed"`, `data` still populated. The `fix` is the fix of the first attention item in target order (journal pending → the journal bead's fix; target missing → `omaddons targets rm <id>`; degraded → `omaddons list -t <id> -v`; state newer → display "upgrade omaddons", `fix_argv: null`).

`commands` (recommended next actions, deterministic order): one entry per attention item using the fixes above; for a target with unmanaged folders, `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged` (`destructive: false`). M2 adds update and adoption recommendations.

`--json` `data` schema (`StatusData`):

```
{
  "cached": bool,
  "targets": [
    {
      "id": string,
      "key": string | null,
      "registered": bool,
      "default": bool,
      "family": string,                       // e.g. "mainline", "forever", "wrath-legacy", "unknown"
      "kind": "live" | "test",
      "install_kind": "battlenet" | "custom",
      "product": string | null,               // e.g. "wow", "wowf"; null for custom clients
      "version": string,                      // e.g. "12.1.0.69933", "3.3.5.12340"
      "interface": int,                        // e.g. 120100, 30300
      "label": string | null,                 // e.g. "localhost" from realmlist
      "running": bool,
      "missing": bool,
      "folders": {"managed": int, "unmanaged": int, "protected": int, "linked": int, "invalid": int},
      "addons": {"total": int, "degraded": int},
      "attention": [string]
    }
  ],
  "journal": {"pending": int, "in_progress": bool},
  "needs_attention": bool
}
```

Targets sort by id. `-v` adds `client_dir`, `install_root` and `exe_name` per target (paths are verbose-only, vision §5.9 "token-frugal").

Human output:

```
retail   mainline      12.1.0.69933  live  running    0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 0 protected
wotlk    wrath-legacy  3.3.5.12340   live  localhost  0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 23 protected
warning: journal_pending: an interrupted transaction for retail awaits recovery
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 3, 6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a synthetic machine with a Battle.net root (`_retail_` 12.1.0.69933) and a custom 3.3.5a root with 23 `Blizzard_*` folders and `set realmlist 127.0.0.1`, `omaddons status --json` reports `retail` (family `mainline`, interface 120100) and the 3.3.5a target (family `wrath-legacy`, interface 30300, label `localhost`, `folders.protected == 23`), both with `key: null` before any mutation.
- After one install into each, both report stable keys on every later run.
- `status` writes nothing: hashes of `<state>/omaddons`, `<cache>/omaddons` and every client dir are identical before and after, with and without `--cached`.
- `status --cached` never runs the bounded scan (asserted via a debug log event or a scan counter) and performs no network I/O (net.log unchanged; works with `--offline`); with no discovery cache it lists registered targets only and recommends `omaddons status`.
- Running state is live under `--cached`: starting and stopping a fake process in a fake /proc tree flips `running` without any other change.
- A leftover journal with the lock free yields warning `journal_pending`, `attention` containing `journal_pending`, and `status --check` exits 6 with `ok: false`, `error.code == "check_failed"`, `data` populated and a non-empty fix; with the lock held (failpoint sleep in another process) status reports `tx_in_progress` and changes nothing.
- A registered target whose client dir was deleted shows `missing: true` and attention `target_missing`.
- `--cached` completes in under 5 ms on the fixture machine (measured at the checkpoint with hyperfine; recorded, not asserted in the gate).

## Test Plan

- Unit: attention computation per condition; `--check` fix selection; `commands` ordering; target merge of discovered and registered (registered missing, unregistered provisional, default flag).
- Integration (`tests/status.rs`, synthetic trees from `tests/common/trees.rs`, fake /proc tree, HOME/XDG_* tempdirs per DEC-6): the two-target machine above; registration after install; leftover journal (write a `prepared` journal fixture); lock held by a second process using `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swapped=sleep:2000`; deleted client dir; `--cached` with and without a discovery cache; write-nothing hash check.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per case, exit codes 0/3/6 as documented.
- Log argv, env and outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- Added deps beyond the plan's list: `inventory` (folder counts come from its classification) and `discover-cache` (`--cached` reads the discovery cache). discover-cache is P2 while this bead is P1; it is size S, so the inversion costs little, and the plan owner may want to raise its priority.
- Pending update counts, `outdated` results, drift results (M2), Lua error counts (M3) and doctor findings by severity (M4) are added to this schema by those milestones as additive keys.
- The provisional id for unregistered targets must be deterministic across runs (registry bead), or agents will chase changing ids.
- Account, realm and character names never appear; status does not read `WTF/` beyond what discovery needs (`Config.wtf` on legacy targets).

title: Implement the targets command: list, add, rm, rename, default and --rescan
description:
## Background

A target is one WoW client directory (the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`) plus its identity: an immutable ULID `key`, a human `id` alias, family, kind, version, interface and `ClientRules` (vision §5.1). Discovery finds targets with no setup (§5.2); the registry (`<state>/omaddons/registry.json`) remembers registered ones, and a marker at `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` lets a moved install be re-linked. `omaddons targets` is the user-facing surface over all of that: list what exists, add a client discovery cannot find, remove, rename, choose a default, and force a rescan.

The registry bead (E3) owns keys, aliases, markers, registration under the lock and `-t` resolution; the discover-cache bead owns the cache that `--rescan` bypasses. This bead is the command layer.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<config>` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config`); `<client dir>` as above; `<root>` = a WoW install root.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/targets.rs`, a `Targets` subcommand with `add`, `rm`, `rename`, `default` sub-subcommands in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons targets [add <path> [--name N] | rm <id> | rename <id> <new> | default <id>] [--rescan]`.

Decided: the envelope `command` for sub-subcommands is the space-joined path (`"targets add"`, `"targets rm"`, `"targets rename"`, `"targets default"`); bare listing is `"targets"` (why: one string per distinct `data` schema keeps envelopes self-describing; coordinate with the output-envelope bead so every command family follows it).

### targets (list)

- Runs discovery (using the discovery cache when valid; `--rescan` bypasses and refreshes it) and merges registered targets. Read-only apart from the derived discovery cache.
- Each target reports: `id`, `key` (null when unregistered), `registered`, `default`, `family`, `kind` (`live` | `test`), `install_kind` (`battlenet` | `custom`), `product` (null for custom), `version`, `interface`, `label`, `client_dir`, `missing` (registered but the directory is gone), `found_by` (`product_db` | `scan` | `launcher:<lutris|heroic|steam|bottles>` | `extra_root` | `manual`).
- Decided: `client_dir` is always included, unlike other commands where paths are verbose-only (why: a target is its client dir; a target list without it is useless). `-v` adds `install_root`, `flavor_dir`, `exe_name`, the `ClientRules` row name, and the alias list.
- Discovery warnings (unknown flavor folders, version/interface disagreement, `client_not_launched_since_patch`, `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS` reached) pass through as warnings.

### targets add <path> [--name N]

- Accepts a Battle.net root, a flavor folder (`<root>/_retail_`), a custom client root, an `Interface` directory or an `Interface/AddOns` directory, and normalizes to client dir(s) by running the discovery recognizers on that path.
- Decided: a Battle.net root registers every flavor folder under it (one target each); `--name` is then allowed only when exactly one target results, otherwise `usage` (exit 2) with fix naming the flavor-folder form (why: one name cannot label several clients).
- A path that does not exist, or contains no recognizable client → `target_not_found` (exit 3), message saying what was looked for (`.build.info`, `Wow*.exe` + `Interface/`), fix `omaddons targets` (argv form).
- The path is stored in the registry as a manual root so later discovery includes it even outside the bounded scan.
- `--name N`: Decided: ids match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,31}$`, must not parse as a ULID, must not contain `@` (reserved for qualified collisions such as `retail@steam`), and must not already be taken; violations → `usage` (exit 2) naming the target that holds the id and suggesting `omaddons targets rename`.
- Already registered → idempotent, `changed: false`, exit 0.
- Registration (key assignment, registry write, marker write) happens under the global lock via the registry API.

### targets rm <id>

- Decided: removes the registry entry and leaves the client dir untouched, marker included, so a later `add` (or the next mutation touching it) re-links the same key. State files `targets/<key>.json` and `.files.json` are kept for the same reason.
- If it was the default target, the default is cleared.
- Data reports how many managed addons the target had (`managed_addons`) so a caller notices it unregistered a target with content. No warning code.
- Unknown id → `target_not_found` (3).

### targets rename <id> <new>

- Gives the target a new primary id; the old id is released. Same validation as `--name`. Renaming an unregistered target registers it first (vision §5.1: keys are assigned by the first mutating command or by `targets add|rename|default`).

### targets default <id>

- Sets the default target in the registry (registering it if needed). The default is used by `install` when `-t` is absent.
- Decided: config `default_target` in `<config>/omaddons/config.toml`, when set, overrides the registry default (explicit configuration wins); `targets default` still writes the registry and reports `overridden_by_config: true` so the caller knows why nothing changed in behavior. Flagged to the plan owner as a two-sources-of-truth problem worth revisiting.

Mutating sub-subcommands take the global lock (`LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` 5 s → `locked`, exit 5) and write through fsx via the registry API. They are not transactions (they are not in the transaction kind list) and are not undoable; they are idempotent and cheap to reverse by hand. `--dry-run` reports what would change and writes nothing.

`--json` `data` schemas:

```
targets:          {"targets": [Target], "default": string | null, "rescanned": bool}
targets add:      {"changed": bool, "targets": [Target]}
targets rm:       {"id": string, "key": string, "managed_addons": int, "was_default": bool}
targets rename:   {"key": string, "from": string, "to": string}
targets default:  {"id": string, "key": string, "overridden_by_config": bool}

Target = {"id": string, "key": string | null, "registered": bool, "default": bool, "family": string,
          "kind": "live" | "test", "install_kind": "battlenet" | "custom", "product": string | null,
          "version": string, "interface": int, "label": string | null, "client_dir": string,
          "missing": bool, "found_by": string}
```

Human output (list):

```
* retail   01JB…  mainline      12.1.0.69933  live  <client dir>
  wotlk    01JC…  wrath-legacy  3.3.5.12340   live  localhost  <client dir>
  ptr      -      mainline      12.1.0        test  (unregistered)  <client dir>
```

(`*` marks the default; in real output `<client dir>` is the actual path.)

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a synthetic machine, bare `omaddons targets --json` lists every discovered target with `client_dir`, `found_by`, `registered: false` and `key: null` before any mutation.
- `targets add <custom root> --name pserver` registers it with a ULID key, writes `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` containing that key, and a second identical call returns `changed: false`.
- `targets add <Battle.net root>` with two flavor folders registers both; adding `--name` there exits 2.
- `targets add` on a directory with no client exits 3 `target_not_found` with a fix.
- `targets rename retail main` makes `-t main` resolve and `-t retail` fail; invalid ids (`Main`, a ULID, `a@b`, a taken id) exit 2.
- `targets rm <id>` removes the registry entry, leaves the marker and state files in place; `targets add` of the same path restores the same key.
- `targets default <id>` makes `install` without `-t` use that target; with config `default_target` set to another id, the output reports `overridden_by_config: true`.
- `--rescan` ignores the discovery cache: with a cache entry whose stored target data was edited in place by the test (stat keys left valid), bare `targets` shows the cached data, `targets --rescan` shows the on-disk truth with `rescanned: true` and rewrites the cache.
- A mutating sub-subcommand with the lock held by another process for longer than 5 s exits 5 `locked` with `retryable: true`.
- `--dry-run` on add/rm/rename/default writes nothing.

## Test Plan

- Unit: path normalization (root, flavor folder, custom root, `Interface`, `Interface/AddOns`); id validation; default precedence (config vs registry).
- Integration (`tests/targets.rs`, synthetic trees, HOME/XDG_* tempdirs per DEC-6): the cases above; lock contention using a second process holding the lock via `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swapped=sleep:<ms>` (or the fsx-lock test helper); marker contents checked as JSON.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per sub-subcommand, success and failure, with the documented `command` string.

## Considerations

- Two live markers with one key (a copied install) are handled by the registry: the original path keeps the key, the copy gets a new one; `targets` surfaces the registry's warning.
- `extra_roots` in config and `targets add` overlap: config is declarative (dotfiles), `add` is imperative and recorded in the registry. Both feed discovery.
- Family names, product codes and flavor folder names are also accepted by `-t`; an id equal to one of those could be confusing. The registry bead defines resolution precedence; this bead only rejects ids that are already taken.
- Removing a target never deletes anything in the client dir.
acceptance_criteria: Bare targets --json lists every discovered target with client_dir, found_by, registered false and key null before any mutation; targets add <custom root> --name pserver registers a ULID key, writes Interface/.omaddons/target.json with that key, and repeating it returns changed false; add on a Battle.net root with two flavor folders registers both and --name there exits 2; add on a directory with no client exits 3 target_not_found with a fix; rename makes the new id resolve and the old fail, and invalid ids (uppercase, ULID-shaped, containing @, taken) exit 2; rm removes the registry entry but leaves marker and state files, and re-adding the path restores the same key; default <id> makes install without -t use it and reports overridden_by_config true when config default_target differs; --rescan ignores the discovery cache (an in-place edited cache entry is shown by bare targets, while --rescan shows on-disk truth with rescanned true and rewrites the cache); a mutating sub-subcommand with the lock held past 5 s exits 5 locked retryable; --dry-run on add/rm/rename/default writes nothing
close_reason: omaddons targets lists every client (registered or provisional, with found_by, missing and default) and adds, removes, renames and chooses targets under the global lock; --rescan bypasses the discovery cache; --dry-run writes nothing; nested help and usage errors work for its subcommands

title: Implement the undo and history commands
description:
## Background

Undo is what makes agent autonomy safe (vision D6, D31): every mutation is a snapshotted transaction attributed to an actor, and `omaddons undo` reverts it. `history` is how humans and agents see what happened and who did it, and it feeds the canonical intent "undo what the agent did today" (`history --actor agent --since 1d`, then `undo --last-by agent`).

The undo engine (E6 `undo` bead) implements reverting, conflict detection and the SavedVariables policy. The records bead (E2 `state-records`) implements `history.jsonl` reading with filters. This bead is the command layer for both: argument parsing, transaction selection, `data` schemas and human output.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/undo.rs`, `src/app/history.rs`, `Undo` and `History` subcommands in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

### undo

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons undo [<tx> | --last-by <actor>] [--saved-variables auto|restore|keep]`, plus global `--dry-run`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--while-running`, `-t`, `--json`.

Selection:
- No argument: the most recent transaction in `history.jsonl` across all targets. Decided: a global `-t T` narrows "most recent" to that target (why: `-t` is a global flag, and "undo my last change to retail" is a natural request).
- `<tx>`: a full ULID, or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters. Unknown → `not_found` (exit 3, fix `omaddons history`); an ambiguous prefix → `not_found` with the matching ids in `details.candidates` (the general dictionary maps "not found or ambiguous" to 3).
- `--last-by <actor>`: the most recent transaction whose `actor` is `human`, `agent` or `widget`. Another value → `usage` (exit 2). None found → `not_found` (exit 3).
- `<tx>` and `--last-by` together → `usage`.
- Empty history → `not_found`, message "nothing to undo", fix `omaddons history`.

Rules the engine enforces (restated so the command maps them correctly):
- `undo <tx>` reverts an older transaction only if no later transaction of any kind (including `adopt` and `repair` in later milestones) touched the same folders; otherwise `undo_conflict` (exit 4) naming the later transaction(s) in `details`, with fix `omaddons undo <later tx>`.
- Undo is itself a transaction (kind `undo`), snapshotted and undoable. The output always names the reverted transaction.
- `--saved-variables` (default `auto`), per SavedVariables file of the touched folders:
  - `auto`: unchanged since the transaction → nothing to do; changed → the current file is cloned into the undo transaction, then restored; the target's client running → the SavedVariables part is skipped and reported as warning `saved_variables_deferred` with fix `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` (argv form) to run once the client exits. Folders still follow the running policy.
  - `restore`: like `auto`, but while the client runs it is refused with `game_running` (exit 4) instead of deferred.
  - `keep`: SavedVariables are never touched.
  - SavedVariables are never written while the target's client runs, under any policy or flag.
- `--dry-run`: reports what would be restored and the SavedVariables decisions per file count; takes no lock and writes nothing (DEC-16).

After a commit, `commands` holds the undo-the-undo hint `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo <undo tx>","argv":[...],"destructive":false}`, and a `reload_required` warning when needed.

`--json` `data` schema (`UndoData`):

```
{
  "dry_run": bool,
  "reverted": {"tx": string, "kind": string, "at": string, "target": {"id": string, "key": string}, "actor": "human"|"agent"|"widget", "argv": [string]},
  "tx": string | null,                          // the new undo transaction
  "folders": {"restored": [string], "removed": [string]},   // removed = folders the reverted tx had added
  "saved_variables": {"policy": "auto"|"restore"|"keep", "restored": int, "unchanged": int, "deferred": int, "kept": int},
  "reload_required": "none" | "reload" | "restart",
  "atomic_swap": bool | null
}
```

Counts only: account, realm and character names never appear in output (vision §4.4). `-v` adds the reverted transaction's `reason` and the folder paths.

Human output:

```
reverted 01JB… (install by agent, 2026-10-20 14:02) on retail
restored 3 folders, removed 1 · SavedVariables: 2 restored, 4 unchanged
tx 01JC… · /reload in game · undo this: omaddons undo 01JC…
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

### history

Synopsis: `omaddons history [-t T] [--limit N] [--actor A] [--since D]`. Read-only; never takes the lock; never writes.

- Newest first. Decided: default `--limit 20` (token-frugal; agents can raise it). `--limit 0` → `usage`.
- `--actor human|agent|widget`; another value → `usage`.
- `--since D`: a duration (`30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `2w`) relative to now, or an RFC 3339 timestamp, parsed with `jiff`. Anything else → `usage` (exit 2) with fix `omaddons history --since 1d`.
- `-t T`: resolve with the registry resolver; unknown → `target_not_found` (3).
- A torn last line in `history.jsonl` is skipped by the records reader; the command emits one stderr `log` event about it and no warning code (the doctor finding `history-torn-line` arrives in M4).

`--json` `data` schema (`HistoryData`):

```
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "tx": string,
      "kind": "install"|"update"|"remove"|"undo"|"adopt"|"sync"|"restore"|"repair",
      "at": string,                                   // RFC 3339 UTC
      "target": {"id": string, "key": string},
      "actor": "human" | "agent" | "widget",
      "reason": string | null,
      "argv": [string],
      "changes": {"added": int, "replaced": int, "removed": int},
      "result": string                                // as stored by the engine
    }
  ],
  "truncated": bool                                   // more entries matched than --limit
}
```

`-v` replaces the `changes` counts with the stored `ops[]`. Target ids are resolved from the registry at render time; a key no longer registered shows `id` = the key.

Human output: one line per entry, `01JB…  2026-10-20 14:02  agent  install  retail  +3 ~0 -0  "reason"`.

Exit codes: 0, 2, 3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After an install, `omaddons undo --json` reverts it, names the reverted tx in `data.reverted`, creates a new `kind: undo` transaction, and the folders are byte-identical to before the install.
- `omaddons undo` on the undo transaction re-applies the install (undo is undoable).
- `undo <tx>` with a later transaction touching the same folders exits 4 `undo_conflict`, naming the later transaction; with disjoint folders it succeeds.
- `undo --last-by agent` reverts only the most recent `actor: agent` transaction even when a newer human transaction exists.
- Unique 8-character prefixes resolve; unknown ids and ambiguous prefixes exit 3 with a fix.
- `--saved-variables` policies behave as specified; while the client runs (fake /proc), `auto` defers with warning `saved_variables_deferred` whose fix argv is `["omaddons","undo","<tx>","--saved-variables","restore"]`, and `restore` exits 4 `game_running`.
- No output, JSON or human, contains account, realm or character names from the synthetic `WTF/` tree.
- `omaddons history --actor agent --since 1d --json` lists only matching entries newest first, with `truncated` correct for `--limit`.
- `history` with an invalid `--since` or `--actor` exits 2 with a fix.

## Test Plan

- Unit: tx selection (latest, latest with `-t`, prefix resolution, ambiguous prefix, `--last-by`, conflicting arguments), `--since` parsing (durations, RFC 3339, invalid), history filtering and `truncated`.
- Integration (`tests/undo_history.rs`, synthetic trees with a `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/…` layout using fake account/realm/character names, `file:` installs, fake /proc for the running client): install → undo → byte comparison; undo of undo; conflict across install then remove of the same folder; `--last-by agent` with `OMADDONS_ACTOR=agent` and `--actor human` transactions interleaved; SavedVariables matrix (unchanged, changed, running × auto/restore/keep); grep all outputs for the fake names (must not appear).
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per case; exit codes as documented.
- Log argv, env and full outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- Undo after retention pruned the reverted transaction's snapshot cannot restore folders; the undo engine reports that case and this command passes its error through unchanged.
- `history` reads the whole `history.jsonl`; it grows by one line per transaction, so this is fine for M1. If it ever becomes slow, read from the end.
- Verb aliases (`revert`, `rollback` → undo; `log` → history) are M4.
- `doctor undo <run>` resolving to `omaddons undo <tx>` is M4.
acceptance_criteria: undo --json after an install reverts it, names the reverted tx in data.reverted, creates a kind undo transaction and leaves folders byte-identical to before the install; undoing the undo re-applies the install; undo <tx> with a later transaction touching the same folders exits 4 undo_conflict naming it, and succeeds for disjoint folders; undo --last-by agent reverts only the latest agent transaction even when a newer human one exists; unique 8-character prefixes resolve and unknown or ambiguous ids exit 3 with a fix; --saved-variables auto defers with saved_variables_deferred and fix argv omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore while the client runs, and restore exits 4 game_running; no output contains account, realm or character names; history --actor agent --since 1d --json lists only matching entries newest first with truncated correct for --limit; invalid --since or --actor exits 2 with a fix
close_reason: undo and history commands over the engine undo and the history reader

title: Build the M1 CLI contract conformance suite and the exit-site test
description:
## Background

The CLI contract is the product (vision D2, D17): agents drive `omaddons` directly, so every command must behave the same way at the edges. Individual command beads test their own cases; this bead is the cross-command conformance suite that proves the M1 contract-core checkpoint (vision §7 M1):

- bare `omaddons` prints help;
- every M1 command accepts `--json` and emits exactly one stdout envelope on success and on failure (`cmd --json | jq -e .ok` distinguishes failure);
- every error has a non-empty `fix` and a `fix_argv`;
- stderr is NDJSON when it is not a TTY;
- exit sites match the general dictionary.

It also implements the vision's "a test asserts that every exit site in the source maps to a published code" (§5.9 publication rules).

Placeholders: `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` = the XDG state, cache and config dirs, which tests point at tempdirs (DEC-6).

## Technical Approach

Location: `tests/contract/` as one integration-test crate (`tests/contract/main.rs` with modules), using `assert_cmd`, `insta` (json feature), synthetic trees from `tests/common/trees.rs`, archives from `tests/common/archives.rs`, and HTTP replay via `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` (DEC-7). No network: a test fails if the replay layer sees an unknown URL.

Contract facts the suite asserts (restated from vision §5.9 so the suite is self-contained):

- Envelope (stdout under `--json`), one shape for success and failure, keys in this order: `ok`, `schema_version` (`"1.0"`), `tool_version`, `command`, `exit_code`, `partial`, `data` (success) or `error` (failure), `warnings`, `commands`, `meta` (`elapsed_ms`, `offline`). Under `--check`/`--strict` failures (exit 6) both `error` (`code: "check_failed"`) and `data` are present.
- `error` = `{code, message, fix, fix_argv, alternatives: [{display, argv}], retryable, details}`. `fix` is never empty. `fix_argv` is an array, or null only for non-CLI fixes (for example "/reload in game", "upgrade omaddons"). When `fix_argv` is an array its first element is `omaddons` and `shell_words::join(fix_argv) == fix`.
- Every `warnings[]` entry has `code`, `message`, and when it has a `fix`, a `fix_argv` (array or null) following the same rule. Every `commands[]` entry has `action`, `command`, `argv`, `destructive`.
- `--json`, `--format json`, `--robot` and `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json` are equivalent.
- stderr is NDJSON when stderr is not a TTY, or `CI` is set, or `TERM=dumb`: every line parses as a JSON object with `event` ∈ `progress|log|warning|error`. Every error is mirrored to stderr as exactly one `{"event":"error",…}` line.
- Human mode (no JSON flag): stdout is empty on error.
- General exit dictionary: 0 `ok` (including partial success), 1 `failed`, 2 `usage`, 3 `not_found`, 4 `refused`, 5 `locked`, 6 `check_failed`. `exit_code` in the envelope equals the process exit code, and equals the error code's registered exit.
- Determinism: running the same command twice on the same state produces byte-identical stdout once `meta` is removed.

Command matrix (each row is at least one success and one failure case, all run under `--json`):

| Command | Success case | Failure case |
|---|---|---|
| (bare) | `omaddons` → help on stdout, exit 0; `omaddons --json` → envelope with `command: "help"` | `omaddons --bogus` → `usage` (2) |
| `help` | `help install` | `help nosuch` → `usage` (2) with closest-command fix |
| `status` | two-target synthetic machine | `-t nosuch` → `target_not_found` (3); leftover journal + `--check` → 6 |
| `targets` | list; `targets add <root>` | `targets add <empty dir>` → `target_not_found` (3); `targets rename x Bad` → `usage` (2) |
| `list` | after a `file:` install | `-t nosuch` → 3 |
| `info` | catalog name with replay fixtures | `info nosuchaddon` → `not_found` (3) |
| `install` | `file:` zip; `gh:` with fixtures | `ref_invalid` (2); `target_ambiguous` (3); `protected_folder` (4); partial + `--strict` → 6 |
| `remove` | installed addon | `not_managed` (3) |
| `undo` | after install | empty history → `not_found` (3); `undo_conflict` (4) |
| `history` | after install | `--since nonsense` → `usage` (2) |
| `config` | `config get`, `config set`, `config path` | `config set nosuch.key 1` → `usage` (2) |
| `net-log` | after install | `--since nonsense` → 2 |

Additional cases:
- `locked` (5): hold the global lock in a second process (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swapped=sleep:<ms>` on a concurrent install) past `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` and run a mutating command; assert exit 5, `retryable: true`.
- Panic: `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=cli.panic=panic` (DEC-7) → stdout holds one envelope with `error.code == "internal"`, exit 1, fix `omaddons status` (DEC-5), and one stderr error line.
- `--offline` on a command that needs the network (`install gh:…`) → `offline` (1).
- `CI=1` and `TERM=dumb` each force NDJSON stderr even when stderr would otherwise be human (simulate by setting them; the suite cannot allocate a TTY, so the TTY-human path stays covered by the output bead's unit tests).

Snapshots: `insta::assert_json_snapshot!` of each envelope with `meta` removed and ULIDs/timestamps redacted (`insta` redactions on `.data.tx`, `.data..at`, etc.), stored under `tests/contract/snapshots/`.

Exit-site test (`tests/contract/exit_sites.rs`):
- Scan `src/` for every `ErrorCode::<Variant>` construction and assert each variant appears in the registry's published table (the registry exposes an iterator over all codes with `wire()`, `exit()`, `retryable()`).
- Assert every registry entry's exit is in the general dictionary (0–6), and every wire name is unique snake_case.
- Assert `std::process::exit` appears nowhere in `src/`, and `ExitCode::from` appears only in `src/main.rs`/`src/cli.rs`, where the value is derived from `Exit` (why: one exit path means every exit maps to a published code).
- The doctor dictionary (64/66/73/74 etc.) does not exist in M1; the test is written so M4 can add the second dictionary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/contract/` covers every row of the command matrix plus the locked, panic, offline and CI/TERM cases, and passes in `argc gate`.
- For every case: stdout is exactly one JSON document (parsing stdout as a stream yields one value), `.ok` matches success/failure, the process exit code equals `exit_code` and the registered exit of `error.code`.
- Every error and every warning with a fix has a non-empty `fix`; `fix_argv` is null only for the documented non-CLI fixes, otherwise starts with `omaddons` and round-trips through shell-words to `fix`.
- Every stderr line in non-TTY runs parses as JSON with a valid `event`; each failing run has exactly one `error` event.
- Human-mode failures leave stdout empty.
- `--json`, `--format json`, `--robot` and `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json` produce identical stdout (meta removed).
- Repeated runs produce identical stdout (meta removed).
- The exit-site test fails if a new `ErrorCode` variant is used without a registry entry, or if `std::process::exit` is added anywhere in `src/`.
- Envelope snapshots are committed and reviewed.

## Test Plan

- This bead is itself the test plan for the contract. Structure: `tests/contract/main.rs` (shared harness: env setup per DEC-6, run helper returning parsed stdout/stderr/exit, assertion helpers `assert_envelope`, `assert_ndjson_stderr`, `assert_fix_argv`), one module per command, `exit_sites.rs`, `snapshots/`.
- Self-test the harness: feed it a known-bad stdout (two JSON documents; empty fix) and assert the helpers fail.
- On failure, log argv, env, full stdout and stderr.

## Considerations

- The suite depends on every M1 command bead; command beads should already have per-command e2e tests, so this suite focuses on uniformity, not behavior depth.
- `fix_argv` placeholders: fixes that need user input (for example `omaddons targets add <path>`) carry `argv: null`; the suite's allowlist of null-argv fixes must stay small and explicit, listed in the harness.
- M4 extends this suite with `capabilities`, the wire-name golden (`tests/contract/wire_names.txt`), the doctor dictionary, intent inference and `robot-docs schema` validation of every snapshot.
- TTY behavior (human stderr lines, colors, progress bars) cannot be exercised without a pseudo-terminal; it is covered by unit tests in the output bead.
acceptance_criteria: tests/contract/ covers every command-matrix row (bare, help, status, targets, list, info, install, remove, undo, history, config, net-log) plus locked, panic, offline and CI/TERM cases and passes in argc gate; every case prints exactly one stdout JSON document whose .ok matches the outcome and whose exit_code equals the process exit code and the registered exit of error.code; every error and fixed warning has a non-empty fix, and fix_argv is null only for documented non-CLI fixes, otherwise starts with omaddons and round-trips through shell-words; every non-TTY stderr line parses as JSON with a valid event and each failure has exactly one error event; human-mode failures leave stdout empty; --json, --format json, --robot and OMADDONS_FORMAT=json give identical stdout with meta removed; repeated runs are byte-identical with meta removed; the exit-site test fails on an unregistered ErrorCode variant or any std::process::exit in src/; envelope snapshots are committed
close_reason: CLI contract conformance suite and exit-site test

comments.text: **Implementation (tests/contract/: main.rs harness, matrix.rs, special.rs, exit_sites.rs, 21 snapshots).** support::check asserts on every --json run: one stdout JSON document (streaming parse), top-level keys in wire order (ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, partial, data, error, warnings, commands, meta; read with an order-preserving visitor), exit_code == process exit == the registered exit of error.code (deserialized as ErrorCode), ok == (exit 0), data kept under check_failed, non-empty fix with fix_argv starting with omaddons and shell_words::join(fix_argv) == fix (alternatives too), or null only for a short documented TEXT_FIXES prefix list (or a fix that is not a command at all); warnings with fixes follow the same rule; commands[] argv joins to command; every stderr line is a JSON event in progress|log|warning|error, with exactly one error event per failure and none on success. Matrix rows: bare/help, status (+ -t nosuch, + crashed journal --check → 6), targets (list, add, add empty dir → 3, rename to an invalid id → 2), list, info (catalog + replay, not found), install (--file, catalog via replay, ref_invalid, target_ambiguous via the two-client probe, protected_folder, partial --strict → 6), remove, undo (empty → 3, conflict → 4, ok), history, config (get/set/path, unknown key → 2), net-log. Special: locked (exit 5, retryable, via a concurrent install sleeping at engine.swapped past LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT), cli.panic → internal (exit 1, fix omaddons status), --offline install → offline (1), CI=1 and TERM=dumb, the four JSON spellings identical without meta, repeated runs byte-identical without meta, human-mode failures with empty stdout. exit_sites: every ErrorCode::<Variant> in src/ is in ErrorCode::ALL, wire names unique snake_case, exits in the 0–6 dictionary and never 0, no std::process::exit, ExitCode::from only in cli.rs/error.rs/main.rs. A harness self-test feeds two documents, an empty fix and reordered keys and expects failures. Snapshots redact the tempdir (<root>), ULIDs and RFC 3339 times; reviewed, no paths leak. Runs in about 8 s (the locked case waits the 5 s lock timeout).

title: Add cargo-fuzz targets for every M1 parser and archive inspection
description:
## Background

Every parser in M1 reads bytes omaddons does not control: `.build.info` and `.flavor.info` (BPSV), Battle.net's `product.db` (protobuf, layout UNVERIFIED), launcher configs (Lutris YAML, Heroic JSON, Steam VDF, Bottles YAML, all read by small tolerant hand-written readers), TOC files, addon archives from the internet, and user-typed refs. The vision's goal G3 says upstream drift yields typed errors, never crashes; the testing strategy (§5.12) lists property tests and fuzz targets for exactly these inputs, and the M1 checkpoint requires each fuzz target to run for at least 10 minutes without a crash.

Property tests live in each parser's own bead. This bead adds the cargo-fuzz harness, the targets, seed corpora and the recipe, and runs nothing in the per-commit gate (fuzz runs happen at milestone checkpoints, vision §5.12 "Not in the per-commit gate").

## Technical Approach

- `fuzz/` is its own cargo-fuzz crate (`fuzz/Cargo.toml` with `[package.metadata] cargo-fuzz = true`, its own `[workspace]` table so the main package's build, clippy and tests never include it, `libfuzzer-sys`, and a path dependency on `omaddons`).
- Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins stable 1.97.1; cargo-fuzz needs nightly sanitizer flags, so targets run with `cargo +nightly fuzz run <target>` (a nightly toolchain is installed on the development machine). Decided: no nightly pin in the repository (why: nightly is only for fuzzing; the product builds on stable).
- Targets (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/<name>.rs`), each calling the production entry point on arbitrary bytes and asserting only "returns, never panics, never allocates without bound":
  - `bpsv` → the BPSV parser (`src/discover/bpsv.rs`).
  - `product_db` → the protobuf wire reader (`src/discover/product_db.rs`).
  - `lutris`, `heroic`, `steam_vdf`, `bottles` → the launcher-config readers (discover-launchers bead).
  - `toc` → the TOC parser (`src/toc.rs`), with lossy UTF-8 input.
  - `archive` → archive inspection on in-memory zip bytes (`std::io::Cursor`); the inspection API must accept `Read + Seek` so no file is needed. Limits (`ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES`, `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED`, `ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO`) must keep memory bounded.
  - `ref_parse` → the user-ref parser (`src/sources/refs.rs`), with lossy UTF-8 input.
- Entry points must be reachable from outside the crate. If a parser is private, expose it through a `#[doc(hidden)] pub mod fuzzing` re-export in `src/lib.rs` rather than widening module visibility.
- Seed corpora: decided — committed under `fuzz/seeds/<target>/` (why: `fuzz/corpus/` is gitignored for generated inputs). Seeds come from the existing test fixtures (`tests/fixtures/…`, the hostile archives from `tests/common/archives.rs` written out once, the `.build.info` example header from vision §4.1). Each target gets at least three seeds, including one malformed.
- Recipe in `Argcfile.sh`: `argc fuzz <target> [--time <seconds>]` (default 600) running `cargo +nightly fuzz run <target> fuzz/corpus/<target> fuzz/seeds/<target> -- -max_total_time=<seconds> -rss_limit_mb=2048`, plus `argc fuzz-all [--time]` looping over every target. Use the argc DSL correctly (`@cmd`, `@arg target![...]` with a `_choice_target` function listing `fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs`, `@option --time`), shellcheck-clean, `@meta require-tools cargo-fuzz` on those recipes.
- Crash triage: a crash writes an artifact under `fuzz/artifacts/<target>/`; the fix is a regression test in the owning parser's unit tests using that input, then the fuzz run is repeated.
- Gate interaction: files under `fuzz/` count as code changes (vision §5.12), so commits touching them run `argc gate`; the gate itself does not build the fuzz crate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fuzz/` exists as a separate cargo-fuzz crate excluded from the main package; `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` in the repository root do not compile it.
- Nine targets exist: `bpsv`, `product_db`, `lutris`, `heroic`, `steam_vdf`, `bottles`, `toc`, `archive`, `ref_parse`, each with at least three committed seeds under `fuzz/seeds/<target>/`.
- `argc fuzz <target> --time 30` runs each target for 30 seconds without a crash on the development machine (smoke run recorded in the close reason).
- `argc fuzz` and `argc fuzz-all` are shellcheck-clean and pass `argc --argc-export Argcfile.sh`.
- Any crash found while building the targets is fixed in the owning parser with a regression unit test.
- The 10-minute-per-target run is left to the m1-checkpoint bead (documented in the recipe help).

## Test Plan

- Smoke: 30-second run per target (above).
- Regression: every crash input becomes a unit test in the owning module.
- Check that the main package is unaffected: `argc gate` passes with `fuzz/` present.

## Considerations

- The `archive` target can find slow inputs rather than crashes (decompression of near-limit entries); `-timeout` defaults are fine, but report slow units if libFuzzer flags them.
- The Lua SavedVariables parser (M3) and the WoWI/Tukui decoders (M2) add their own targets later.
- If `cargo +nightly fuzz` is unavailable on a machine, the recipe must fail with a message naming `cargo install cargo-fuzz` and a nightly toolchain, not a cryptic error.

title: Epic: Post-M2 audit fixes (gaps in milestones 1 and 2)
description:
## Background

On 2026-10-16, right after milestone 2 closed, an independent audit compared the vision bead (`omad-vision-8qa`), README.md and the code at `53b54e6`. Seven read-only investigations covered discovery and rules, the transaction engine, sources and the network layer, the CLI contract, the gate and test suite, the beads-versus-vision coverage, and a read-only smoke test on the development machine.

The result: M1 and M2 are real. The gate passes 1,288 tests with 0 failures, and every M1/M2 command works on the development machine's six clients. But the audit found defects inside that "done" work, and none of them was tracked:

- correctness bugs in the engine's failure paths: recovery, the journal, SavedVariables;
- contract holes an agent will hit, e.g. a usage-error fix that turns `uninstall` into `install`;
- integrity and privacy statements the code does not fully keep;
- discovery and rules fields that do nothing;
- test-suite blind spots;
- README statements that no longer match the code;
- real-world facts that have only ever been checked against synthetic fixtures.

On 2026-10-18 the owner decided these gaps are fixed before any milestone 3 work is planned. This epic holds them. Each leaf bead was re-verified against `53b54e6` before filing, with exact file:line anchors and, where possible, a reproduction in an isolated HOME.

## Goals

- Every defect the audit found in M1/M2 code is fixed, with a regression test.
- Every promise in README.md is true of the code, or the README says exactly what the code does.
- The real-world assumptions the safety model rests on are observed on real clients, not only on fixtures: running detection under Proton, in-game loading, legacy client behaviour.

## Success Criteria

- Every child area epic is closed (`br epic close-eligible`).
- `argc gate` passes at the closing commit.
- The pinned vision bead has comments recording every contract addition these fixes made (DEC-4, before the M4 freeze).
- README.md's numbers and claims match the code at the closing commit.

## Non-Goals

- No milestone 3, 4 or 5 work: no Omarchy widget, `errors`, `backup`, `doctor`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, skill, stored plans/`apply`, completions, full intent inference, wire-name golden file, CurseForge, Wago, GraphQL or packaging. Where a fix touches one of those areas, the leaf bead scopes itself to what M1/M2 promised and names the boundary.
- No refactors beyond what each fix needs.

## Considerations

- Several engine fixes touch the same recovery code (`src/engine/journal.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/engine/undo.rs`). Their `blocks` edges order them so they do not collide.
- Contract additions (new warning or error codes, data keys) are allowed until the M4 freeze, but each must be registered in `src/error.rs`, documented in README.md and recorded on the vision bead.
- The real-world verification beads wait on external events or on owner-supplied clients and sessions. They are deferred with the exact ask, so they do not hold up the code fixes.
acceptance_criteria: every child area epic is closed (br epic close-eligible); argc gate passes at the closing commit; the vision bead has a comment for every contract addition these fixes made; README.md's numbers and claims match the code
close_reason: Success criteria met at the closing commit. (1) Every child area epic yegz.1-.7 is closed. (2) argc gate --all passes at 7fb0a2c, the last code change: 1592 tests passed, 0 failed, 53 ignored; cargo deny clean after the TLS advisory bump (omad-rquq); the closing commit changes only README.md and .beads/. (3) Vision comments cover every contract addition: an audit of 75 closed descendants found 6 unrecorded groups and 1 partial record, now comments 1016-1022 on omad-vision-8qa. (4) README.md was audited section by section against the code (8 parallel read-only audits plus an adversarial review of the diff): about 100 corrections and additions, a client-rules table, current test counts and M3 state. Every place the code still differs from the README is a filed bug listed under README 'Known issues': omad-rnk8 (P1), omad-ck0h, omad-oxxv, omad-zwl3 (P2), omad-npec, omad-o3gd, omad-peud, omad-hp8r (P3).
