title: Fixes that are omaddons commands are written as prose with fix_argv null
description:
## Background

Vision §5.9: "Every `fix`, `alternatives[]` entry, `commands[]` entry … carries `argv`"; "Non-CLI fixes such as `/reload in game` carry `argv: null`". README "Fields": `fix_argv` is "`null` when the fix is prose", and "For coding agents": "fix_argv is null when the fix is prose (read error.fix)". The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that many fixes that ARE omaddons commands are built with `Suggestion::text` (`src/error.rs:342-353`), so agents cannot execute them, and that the contract suite cannot notice:

- `tests/contract/main.rs:232-241`: a null-argv fix passes when its display does not start with `omaddons` (so "add it to git_hosts: omaddons config set git_hosts …" passes), or starts with one of 37 allowlisted prefixes (`TEXT_FIXES`, `tests/contract/main.rs:48-91`).

Census at HEAD (non-test code, `#[cfg(test)]` blocks and `tests.rs` files excluded): **146** `Suggestion::text(` call sites (the audit's ~169 counted tests and doc comments). Classified:

| Class | Count | Meaning | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| R | 9 | a complete omaddons command, every value known at the site | convert to `Suggestion::command` |
| N | 4 | "run the command again" for an immediately retryable error (`plan_stale`, `locked`) | the failing argv, set at the command boundary |
| O | 5 | "run without --offline …" | the failing argv without `--offline`, at the boundary, when the flag (not the env var) made the run offline |
| P | 20 | an omaddons command that needs a value only the user has (`<path>`, `<ref>`, `<addon>`, `<client>`) | stays prose with a `<placeholder>` display; add a runnable read-only alternative where one exists |
| S | 10 | deliberately prose: a secret piped on stdin, or raising a safety limit | stays prose (an agent must not run these unasked) |
| L | 20 | "retry later; if it persists …" (time-dependent) | stays prose: `retryable` and `details.reset_at` say when; an argv invites a tight retry loop against the sources' politeness limits |
| X | 75 | not an omaddons command: quit the game, `/reload`, edit a file, `chmod`, install git, wait | stays prose (vision: argv null) |
| F | 3 | pass-through of another fix (`src/app/outcome.rs:202`, `src/app/outdated.rs:746`, `src/net/guard.rs:279`) | follows its source |

R (convert):
- `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:203` (`host_blocked`): "add it to git_hosts: omaddons config set git_hosts '["<host>"]' (keep any hosts already listed)" → argv `["omaddons","config","set","git_hosts", <TOML array of the configured hosts plus this one>]` (the allowlist's configured `git_hosts` are at hand; serialize with `toml_edit`'s array formatting). Exit-4 refusal fixes already carry the overriding argv (`--force`, `--while-running`), so this is consistent; the message keeps "(this lets omaddons contact <host>)".
- `src/engine/plan.rs:1287` (`missing_dependency`, `--no-deps`): → the failing argv without `--no-deps` (`cli::without_switch`, `src/cli.rs:770-772`; `PlanCtx` has `argv`).
- `src/engine/plan.rs:1259`, `:1266`, `:1273`, `:1283` ("install the one you use", "install it yourself"; reached only when no top candidate exists), `:1293`, `:1299` → `omaddons search <folder>` (read-only; the same fix README already documents when no keyless source ships the folder, and `src/engine/plan.rs:1248-1253` already uses it).
- `src/app/remove.rs:333` (`ref_ambiguous`, a folder or ref several addons share) → fix `omaddons list -t <id>`, alternatives one `omaddons remove <name> -t <id>` per candidate (as `target_ambiguous` lists one command per candidate).

N (boundary): `src/engine/swap.rs:500`, `src/engine/tx.rs:872`, `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:338` (`plan_stale`, Replan), `src/fsx/lock.rs:156` (`locked`). Four commands already override `locked` by hand (`src/app/auth.rs:283-287`, `config.rs:291`, `export.rs:402`, `targets.rs:346`); engine commands do not, so `install` under a held lock says "wait for the other command to finish, then retry".

O (boundary): `src/engine/plan.rs:4051`, `src/net/guard.rs:104`, `src/resolve/cache.rs:435`, `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:196` (error `offline`), `src/sources/wowi/index.rs:234` (warning `stale_check`).

P (stay prose; standardize; alternatives): `src/app/adopt/apply.rs:73`, `:456` (alt `omaddons search <folder>`); `src/app/copy.rs:167` (when both `--from` and `--to` were given, R: the argv without `-t`); `src/app/install.rs:909`; `src/app/status.rs:826` (`journal_pending`: no command recovers without changing something; `doctor` is M4); `src/app/sync.rs:374`, `:376` (alt `omaddons help sync`); `src/app/targets.rs:459`, `src/discover/registry.rs:614`; `src/app/update.rs:462`; `src/discover/battlenet.rs:105`, `src/discover/custom.rs:108` (display `omaddons config set targets.retail.family <family>` with the real id filled in: `config set` accepts `targets.*.family`, `src/state/config.rs:309`; only the family is the user's to choose); `src/discover/mod.rs:279`; `src/engine/plan.rs:4072` (alt `omaddons info <ref> -t <id>`); `src/net/guard.rs:61` (see omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.14); `src/resolve/updates.rs:203`; `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:560`, `src/sources/github.rs:258`, `src/sources/github_rest.rs:258`, `src/sources/url.rs:62`.

S (stay prose): `src/app/auth.rs:207`, `:244`, `:254`, `:259`; `src/engine/blobs.rs:486`; `src/engine/inspect.rs:183`; `src/engine/retention.rs:181`; `src/sources/github_rest.rs:144`; `src/sources/github_search.rs:120`; `src/state/files_index.rs:173`.

## Technical Approach

1. **Placeholder rule (decided).** A fix that needs a value only the user can supply stays `Suggestion::text`, and its display is the exact command with each missing value as a lowercase `<placeholder>` in angle brackets (`omaddons targets add <path>`), optionally after a short lead ("download the file, then: omaddons install <path>"). Rejected: argv with placeholder tokens (README tells agents to run argv as is; `<path>` would be executed literally), and a `requires_input` flag on suggestions (a new contract field for a corner case; D17 mentioned it for `commands`, M4 capabilities can define it). README "Fields", `error` row, and "For coding agents": "fix_argv is null when the fix is prose or needs a value only you can supply; such a fix shows the command with `<placeholders>`."
2. **R conversions** as listed above, each with its existing message kept.
3. **Boundary retry fixes.** In `Out::emit_as` (`src/app/mod.rs:176-190`; give `Out` the argv and the `--offline` flag alone, `cli.global.offline`), rewrite an `Err`'s fix when it is the generic text for its code: `plan_stale` with `retryable: true` and `locked` → `Suggestion::command(fix_argv(&argv))`; `offline` → `fix_argv(&argv)` without `--offline` when the flag set it and `OMADDONS_OFFLINE` is not `1`, else unchanged prose. Same for `stale_check` warnings in the outcome. Remove the four hand overrides of `locked`. Keep `locked`'s `details.holder`.
4. **Alternatives for P** as listed (each runnable and read-only).
5. **Guard the prose side.**
   - Contract (`tests/contract/main.rs:232-241`): a null-argv display passes only if it contains no `omaddons ` word, or contains a `<…>` placeholder, or matches an explicit S/X allowlist of the few displays that mention a command without being one (the `echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set` pipeline and its gh variant; the GitHub rate-limit "wait until …, or store a GitHub token with omaddons auth github set …"; the `--dry-run` reminders `src/engine/plan.rs:700`, `:756`; `src/app/sync.rs:779`'s "regenerate the file with `omaddons export`"). Shrink `TEXT_FIXES` to that list plus the placeholder prefixes.
   - Source scan (new test in `tests/contract/exit_sites.rs`, beside `every_error_code_used_in_src_is_registered`): every string literal passed to `Suggestion::text(` in `src/` (outside `#[cfg(test)]`) that contains `omaddons ` must contain `<` or be in the same allowlist. This catches sites the matrix never triggers.

Contract (DEC-4): changed fixes only (no codes, no keys); README text as in step 1; record the placeholder rule and the boundary retry rule on omad-vision-8qa.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The 9 R sites build `Suggestion::command`; their argvs parse (omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.2's check) and run.
- `install` under a held lock, a `plan_stale` retry, and an `--offline` failure (flag given, env unset) all carry the failing argv (minus `--offline`) as `fix_argv`; with `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` the offline fix stays prose.
- P displays follow the `<placeholder>` rule; the listed alternatives exist.
- The contract check and the source scan pass and reject a planted `Suggestion::text("omaddons status")`.
- README and the vision comment updated; argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/engine/plan.rs` tests for `missing_dependency` under `--no-deps` and with no top candidate; `src/sources/git_hosts.rs` tests for the merged `git_hosts` argv (none configured, one configured, the host already present cannot happen since it would be allowed).
- Integration: `tests/net_replay.rs` (where `host_blocked` is exercised today) for a `git:` ref on a non-allowlisted host, asserting the merged `git_hosts` argv and that running it lets the next attempt pass the allowlist; `tests/deps.rs` for `--no-deps`.
- Contract: `tests/contract/special.rs::a_held_lock_is_locked_and_retryable` asserts `fix_argv` equals the held command's argv; `offline_refuses_the_network` asserts the argv without `--offline`; the new source scan; snapshots whose fixes change (review each).

## Considerations

- Size: at the top of size-M. If it runs long, split into (a) R + boundary rewrites + tests, (b) P standardization + alternatives + the prose guard.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.14 changes `src/net/guard.rs:61`'s neighbour (`ref_invalid` for `http://`); coordinate the url `host_blocked` display.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.2's parse check covers every argv this bead adds.
- The census is a snapshot at HEAD; the source scan keeps it honest afterwards.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.2`: The contract suite never checks that a suggested argv parses
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.14`: The fix for an http:// ref suggests an https URL that then fails host_blocked
acceptance_criteria: the 9 derivable command fixes become Suggestion::command; plan_stale, locked and offline fixes get the failing argv (minus --offline) at the command boundary; placeholder fixes keep fix_argv null with a documented <placeholder> display and a runnable read-only alternative where one exists; a contract check and a source scan reject any null-argv fix that embeds a runnable omaddons command outside an explicit allowlist; README documents the placeholder rule; argc gate passes
close_reason: Part (a): every fix that is a complete omaddons command is now argv (git_hosts, missing_dependency, remove ref_ambiguous), and the command boundary gives plan_stale, locked and offline the failing argv; part (b), placeholders, alternatives and the prose guard, is omad-4bkg.

title: auth github set --dry-run says it stored the token although nothing is written
description:
## Background

README "Global options": `--dry-run` shows "the plan without changing anything (mutating commands)", and every other mutating command's data says so: `dry_run` in `install`/`remove`/`undo`/…, `config set` (`src/app/config.rs:95`, `:335`, `:339`), each `targets` action (`src/app/targets.rs:139`, `:151`, `:161`, `:172`, rendered "would register"/"would make", `:630-666`). The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found `auth github` is the exception:

- `src/app/auth.rs:279-282`: `write` returns `Ok(())` at once under `ctx.dry_run`, so nothing is written (correct).
- `src/app/auth.rs:65-70`: `AuthData` is `{configured, source, rate_limit}`, with no `dry_run`.
- `src/app/auth.rs:102-108`: `render_human` prints "stored the GitHub token in <path>" for `Set` and "cleared <path>" for `Clear`, whatever `dry_run` is, and then (`:120-127`) reports the token state read back from disk, which under `--dry-run` is the old state, so the output contradicts itself.

User-visible consequence: a human (or an agent reading human output) is told the token was stored when it was not; JSON gives no way to tell a dry run from a real one.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment, empty HOME:

```
echo ghp_x | omaddons auth github set --dry-run
# stored the GitHub token in <config>/omaddons/credentials/github
# no GitHub token: GitHub's API allows 60 requests an hour (the main path needs none)
ls <config>/omaddons/credentials            # does not exist (nothing written: correct)
echo ghp_x | omaddons auth github set --dry-run --json
# {"ok":true,…,"command":"auth github",…,"data":{"configured":false,"source":"none","rate_limit":null},…}
omaddons auth github clear --dry-run        # "cleared <path>", same contradiction
```

Expected: "would store the GitHub token in <path>" and a data object that says it was a dry run.

## Technical Approach

1. `AuthData` (`src/app/auth.rs:65-70`) gains `dry_run: bool` as its last field, as the other settings commands place it (`SetData`, `src/app/config.rs:88-96`; `AddData`/`RmData`/`RenameData`/`DefaultData`, `src/app/targets.rs:136-173`). Set it from `ctx.dry_run` in `run` (`src/app/auth.rs:188-197`).
2. `render_human` (`src/app/auth.rs:102-141`): under `dry_run`, "would store the GitHub token in <path>" / "would clear <path>". Then describe the state the write would produce, not the unchanged disk: for `set`, the token that would be used afterwards (`OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` first, then a config.toml credential, then the file, the `TokenSource` order) — compute it by resolving with the would-be file content, i.e. `configured: true, source: file` unless an env or config credential outranks the file (then the existing "<VAR> is set, and is used instead of the file" line). For `clear`, `configured`/`source` as they would be with an empty file.
3. JSON: `configured` and `source` follow step 2 under `--dry-run` (decided: the data describes the result of the command, as `install --dry-run` describes the planned result; `dry_run: true` marks it).
4. `--from-gh --dry-run` still runs `gh auth token` (it validates the token and that `gh` works) but writes nothing; say so in the help text (`AUTH_HELP`, `src/cli.rs:440-448`): "--dry-run checks the token and writes nothing".

Contract (DEC-4): additive data key `dry_run` on `auth github`. README `auth github` paragraph (`README.md:1134`): "`data` is `{configured, source, rate_limit, dry_run}`". Record on omad-vision-8qa.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `echo ghp_x | omaddons auth github set --dry-run` prints "would store the GitHub token in …", then "GitHub token: from …" as it would be; writes nothing.
- `--json` data has `dry_run: true` and the post-write `configured`/`source`; without `--dry-run`, `dry_run: false` and behaviour unchanged.
- `auth github clear --dry-run` says "would clear".
- README and vision comment updated; argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

title: search install hints break ties by target id, ignoring the default target
description:
## Background

README `search` promises: "`commands` holds `omaddons install <ref> -t <client>` for up to three results, each on its best client, never for `no`, `unlikely` or `abandoned`." The human output prints the first as `Install: …`.

`install_hints` (`src/app/search.rs:527-550`) picks, per result, `min_by_key(|(id, c)| (**c, id))` over the suggestible `compat` entries: the strongest hint (`Compat` orders `Yes < Likely < Unknown`), then the target id. On a machine with several clients, most results tie: the catalog says `yes` for every family it lists, and GitHub is `unknown` everywhere. The tie goes to the alphabetically first id, usually `anniversary`. That holds even when the user made `retail` the default target (`targets default retail`, or `default_target` in `config.toml`), and even when every installed addon is on retail. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit saw it on the development machine. Verified in an isolated HOME with five Battle.net clients: with `retail` registered as the default, and an addon installed only on retail, `search dbm --offline` still suggests `omaddons install gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods -t anniversary`.

An agent following `commands[0].argv` installs into a client the user does not play.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a synthetic Battle.net root with `_retail_`, `_classic_`, `_classic_era_`, `_anniversary_` and `_forever_` (one `.build.info` row and one `.flavor.info` per product).
2. `omaddons targets default retail`, then `omaddons install ./Foo -t retail` (any local addon folder).
3. `omaddons search dbm --offline --json | jq -c '[.commands[].command]'` (the catalog alone is enough offline).

Expected: `omaddons install gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods -t retail`.

Actual: `… -t anniversary`, and the same for every other hint (`wowi:… -t anniversary`).

## Technical Approach

1. **Define the best client.** Among a result's `compat` entries that are `suggestible()` (never `no`, `unlikely` or `abandoned`), the best is the first by:
   1. hint strength: `yes`, then `likely`, then `unknown`;
   2. the install default target. That is `config.toml`'s `default_target` resolved with `resolve_one`, else the registry default (`world.registry.default`), exactly as `install`'s `choose_target` (`src/app/install.rs:748-768`) reads it. Factor the first two steps of that function into a shared `World::default_target(&self, argv) -> Option<&DiscoveredTarget>` so both agree. A `default_target` that resolves to nothing is ignored here: `install` reports it.
   3. a live client before a test one (`TargetKind::Live`);
   4. the client with the most managed addons (`world.records()`: the client the user actually uses);
   5. the mainline family (retail) before others;
   6. the target id.
2. **Implementation.** In `run` (`src/app/search.rs:278`), compute once a preference order of the selected targets' ids by keys 2–6. Pass it to `install_hints(results, &preference)`, which picks the suggestible entry minimising `(compat, position in preference)`. `install_hints` stays pure, and the tests feed it a preference list. With `-t` naming one client, nothing changes.
3. **Docs.** README `search`, replacing the `commands` sentence: "`commands` holds `omaddons install <ref> -t <client>` for up to three results, each on its best client: the strongest hint (`yes`, then `likely`, then `unknown`), and among equals the default target, then a live client before a test one, then the client with the most managed addons, then retail, then by id. Never for `no`, `unlikely` or `abandoned`." Update the doc comment at `src/app/search.rs:525-526`.
4. **Contract.** No key changes. Which target `commands[].argv` names changes, which is allowed before the M4 freeze (DEC-4). A one-line vision-bead comment records the tie-break order.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Omitting `-t` and letting `install` choose.** `install`'s fallback probes every live client and can end in `target_ambiguous`. A hint must be one runnable command.
- **One hint per suggestible client.** It multiplies `commands` and is no longer "up to three".
- **The most recently used client.** Nothing records it apart from history. The managed-addon count is local, cheap and stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In the reproduction the hint is `-t retail`. Without a default target and with no addons anywhere it is `-t retail`, by the mainline rule.
- With `default_target = "era"` and a catalog entry that is `yes` on era and retail, the hint is `-t era`. For a Tukui hit that is `likely` only on retail, it stays `-t retail`, because the stronger hint wins.
- A test client (PTR) is chosen only when it alone has the strongest hint.
- README documents the order.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit, `src/app/search.rs`: `install_hints` with a hand-built preference list. Cover a tie on `yes` (preference order decides), a stronger hint beating preference, no suggestible entry (no hint), and the three-hint cap.
- Unit, `src/app/world.rs`: `default_target` matches `install`'s choice for config default, registry default and neither.
- Integration, `tests/search.rs`: a two-client home (retail and classic) with `targets default classic`. The catalog result's hint is `-t classic`. Without the default and with an addon installed on classic, it is still `-t classic` by addon count.

## Considerations

- `world.records()` reads every target record. `status` and `list` already do so per run, and the records are small.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.7 changes which results reach the top three. The two are independent.
- The choice stays a hint: `install` verifies every TOC and may still refuse.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.7`: search ranks unrelated GitHub repositories first and misses WoWInterface duplicates
acceptance_criteria: each search install hint names the result's best client: strongest suggestible hint first (yes, likely, unknown), then the install default target, then a live client before a test one, then the client with the most managed addons, then retail, then id; with a default target the hint uses it whenever its hint ties the best; README says how the client is chosen; argc gate passes
close_reason: search's install hints go, among equal hints, to the default target, then a live client, then the one with the most addons, then retail, then by id, instead of the alphabetically first client.

title: The fix for an http:// ref suggests an https URL that then fails host_blocked
description:
## Background

README "Sources and refs": "`http://…` | | refused (`ref_invalid`), suggesting the https form", and "any other `https://` link | `url:` | refused at plan time unless its host is allowlisted". The vision's agent contract (§5.9, D31) is that agents run `fix_argv`.

`parse_user_ref` (`src/sources/refs.rs:80-87`) answers every `http://` input with `Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "install", <https form>])`. `aimed_at` (`src/app/resolve_args.rs:34-50`) then re-aims that fix at the running command. It never checks whether the https form is fetchable. For a host off the hard allowlist (`src/net/allowlist.rs:7-16`; `url:` refs use exactly that list, `src/sources/url.rs:24-30`), the suggested command fails with `host_blocked` at once (`src/sources/url.rs:56-64`). An agent following the fix loops into a second error whose own fix is prose.

The canonical forms are inconsistent besides. `url:http://…` and `git:http://…` go through `canonical()`, fail the model's parse with "the URL must start with https://", and get `omaddons help install` as the fix, with no https suggestion at all. Found by the 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated HOME with a synthetic retail client, offline:

```bash
omaddons install http://example.com/a.zip -t retail --json
# error.code ref_invalid, fix "omaddons install https://example.com/a.zip -t retail" (argv given)
omaddons install https://example.com/a.zip -t retail --json
# error.code host_blocked, message "example.com is not a host omaddons downloads from",
# fix "download the file in a browser, then: omaddons install <path>" (argv null)
omaddons install url:http://example.com/a.zip -t retail --json
# ref_invalid, fix "omaddons help install"
```

Expected: the first command's fix is the host_blocked advice. The https URL is never offered, because it is not fetchable.

## Technical Approach

1. **Look at the https form before suggesting it** (`src/sources/refs.rs:80`). Rewrite `http://` to `https://` and run the existing `url(&https, rest, ctx)`, then decide from what it returns:
   - `Ok` with `Ref::Url { url }` whose host is not permitted by the hard allowlist: the error stays `ref_invalid`, with
     - message `"<input>" is not https, and <host> is not a host omaddons downloads from`;
     - fix `Suggestion::text("download the file in a browser, then: omaddons install <path>")`, the same wording as `src/sources/url.rs:62`;
     - `details: {"host": <host>}`.
   - `Ok` with any other ref (`gh:`, `wowi:`, `tukui:`, `git:` on GitHub or a configured `git_hosts` host, `url:` on an allowlisted host): the fix stays the https form, as now. `aimed_at` keeps aiming it at the running command.
   - `Err`: the https form is malformed too (for example a bad GitHub owner). The error is that one, so the user sees the real problem, with the message prefixed `"<input>" is not https; and with https: `.
2. **One host check.** Move the host extraction and allowlist test out of `UrlSource::release_set` (`src/sources/url.rs:47-56`) into `pub fn url_host_allowed(url: &str) -> (String, bool)`, so `refs.rs` and the source agree by construction. The hard allowlist is `Allowlist::new(false, false, &[])`, which the `url:` source uses today.
3. **The canonical forms.** In `canonical()` (`src/sources/refs.rs:111`):
   - `url:http://X` is handled like the bare `http://X`, through the same branch, so its fix is the https `url:` form or the host advice;
   - `git:http://H/…` gets the fix `git:https://H/…` when H is `github.com` or listed in `git_hosts`. Otherwise it gets the same `host_blocked` wording the git source uses for an unlisted host (`src/sources/git_hosts.rs:203`, "add it to git_hosts …", which omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.11 turns into an argv).
4. **README.** In the refs table, `http://…` row: "refused (`ref_invalid`), suggesting the https form when omaddons can fetch it; for a host it does not download from, the fix is to download the file and install the local path". Error table, `ref_invalid` row: unchanged.
5. **Contract.** The fix and the message change, and `details.host` is new for this case. Allowed before the M4 freeze (DEC-4). Record it in a vision-bead comment. No new code.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Returning `host_blocked` (exit 4) for the http input.** The input is first of all a malformed ref (exit 2), and the user should learn both rules from one message.
- **Fetching the http URL.** The https-only rule is a hard safety property (§5.7).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `install http://example.com/a.zip -t retail` gives `ref_invalid` with the prose download advice, `fix_argv: null` and `details.host: "example.com"`.
- `install http://github.com/o/r -t retail` still suggests `omaddons install https://github.com/o/r -t retail`. The same holds for `http://www.wowinterface.com/downloads/info123-x.html` and for a `git_hosts` host.
- `url:http://example.com/a.zip` and `url:http://github.com/o/r/archive/x.zip` get the matching fixes. `git:http://github.com/o/r` suggests `git:https://…`.
- `info http://example.com/a.zip` and `adopt X --ref http://example.com/a.zip` behave the same, through `aimed_at`.
- No `ref_invalid` fix argv, run as is, fails with `host_blocked`. A unit test checks this over a table of inputs.
- README updated. The vision comment is posted.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit, `src/sources/refs.rs`: extend the table at `src/sources/refs.rs:541-569` with the http cases above (expected code, fix text or argv, `details.host`). Add a check that every suggested argv's ref parses to a ref whose host passes `url_host_allowed`, or is not a `url:`.
- Unit, `src/sources/url.rs`: `url_host_allowed` for allowlisted, unlisted, userinfo and port cases, so `release_set` is unchanged.
- Integration, `tests/install.rs`: the three commands of the reproduction under `--json`.
- Contract: `tests/contract/main.rs` `TEXT_FIXES` needs no entry, because the prose does not start with `omaddons`.

## Considerations

- The advice "download the file in a browser" assumes an interactive user. That is the existing `host_blocked` wording, and omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.11 decides how such prose fixes are represented.
- `git_hosts` is user configuration: an http link to a configured git host becomes a `git:https://` fix that works.
- Keep the message under one line: agents read `error.fix`, humans read `error[ref_invalid]: … / fix: …`.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.11`: Fixes that are omaddons commands are written as prose with fix_argv null
acceptance_criteria: an http:// ref (bare, url: or git:) whose https form omaddons can fetch keeps an https fix aimed at the running command; one whose https form is a url: on a host off the hard allowlist gets the host_blocked download advice instead (prose, fix_argv null, details.host), and a git: host outside git_hosts gets the git_hosts advice the git source gives (an argv once omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.11 lands); no ref_invalid fix ever names a ref that fails host_blocked; README's refs table says so; argc gate passes
close_reason: An http ref (bare, url: or git:) suggests its https form only when omaddons can fetch it; otherwise the fix is the source's own advice with details.host, so no fix runs into host_blocked.

title: Dry-run human output reads as past tense ("would be installed Baz", "restored 6 folders")
description:
## Background

DEC-16: a dry run uses "the real run's `data` schema with `dry_run: true`"; the human text should then say what *would* happen. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found dry-run lines in past tense or ungrammatical:

- `src/app/outcome.rs:1034-1112` (`header`, shared by `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`): under `dry_run` it prefixes the past-tense summary with "would be " (`:1090-1091`), giving "retail: would be installed 1 addon", "would be unpinned 1 addon", "would be changed 2 addons (1 installed, 1 updated)".
- `src/app/outcome.rs:1137-1158` (`status_detail`): item lines say "Baz  1 (installed)", "Foo  1 → 2", "(removed)", "(adopted)" whatever `dry_run` is.
- `src/app/install.rs:285-298` and `:348-357`: `install`'s own lines use the same "would be {verb}" pattern: "retail: would be installed Baz 1 (1 folder)", "would be updated Foo 2 (1 folder)". `remove` is already right ("retail: would remove Bar 2 (1 folder)").
- `src/app/undo.rs:208-235` (`render_undone`): the header says "would revert …" but the counts line says "restored 0 folders, removed 0 · SavedVariables: 0 restored, 0 unchanged" under `--dry-run`.
- `src/app/sync.rs:729-735`: "nothing to do (1 client match <file>)": the verb does not agree with a count of 1.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment, synthetic retail client with local addons `<dir>/v1/Foo`, `<dir>/v2/Bar`, `<dir>/v3/Baz` (Baz not installed), and an `addons.toml` listing Baz for `family.mainline`:

```
omaddons install <dir>/v3/Baz -t retail --dry-run   # retail: would be installed Baz 1 (1 folder)
omaddons unpin Foo --dry-run                        # retail: would be unpinned 1 addon / Foo  unpinned at 1
omaddons sync --dry-run                             # retail: would be installed 1 addon / Baz  1 (installed)
omaddons undo --dry-run                             # would revert … on retail / restored 0 folders, removed 0 · SavedVariables: 0 restored, 0 unchanged
omaddons sync; omaddons sync                        # second run: nothing to do (1 client match <config>/omaddons/addons.toml)
```

Expected: "would install Baz 1 (1 folder)", "would unpin 1 addon", "Baz  1 (would install)", "would restore 0 folders, remove 0 · SavedVariables: would restore 0, 0 unchanged", "1 client matches".

## Technical Approach

1. A verb table on `ItemStatus` (`src/app/outcome.rs`): `fn verb(self, dry_run: bool) -> &'static str` returning the past form for a real run (`installed`, `updated`, `removed`, `adopted`, `pinned`, `unpinned`, `edited`) and `would install`, `would update`, `would remove`, `would adopt`, `would pin`, `would unpin`, `would edit` for a dry run. `header` (`:1066-1092`) builds `what` from it ("would install 1 addon", "would change 2 addons (1 install, 1 update)" — under dry run the breakdown uses base verbs). The adoption special case keeps "(N folders)".
2. `status_detail` (`:1137-1158`) gets `dry_run`: "(would install)", "(would remove)", "(would adopt)", "would pin at V", "would unpin at V", "(would edit)"; `from → to` and "(unchanged)" stay. `item_detail` and every caller pass `dry_run` through (`update`, `sync`, `copy`, `pin` renderers).
3. `install`'s renderer (`src/app/install.rs:285-298`, `:348-357`): use the table (`would install`, `would update`, `would reinstall`, and for the records-only statuses `would pin` / `would unpin` / `would edit`).
4. `undo` (`src/app/undo.rs:221-235`): under `dry_run`, "would restore N folders, remove M" and "SavedVariables: would restore N, M unchanged" (deferred/kept keep their words).
5. `sync` (`src/app/sync.rs:731-735`): "1 client matches", "N clients match".
6. README's Quick start dry-run example (`README.md:294-295`, "retail: would be installed HelloWorld 1.0.0 (1 folder)") becomes "retail: would install HelloWorld 1.0.0 (1 folder)"; the `copy` example (`README.md:831-836`) is a real run and keeps "(installed)".

No JSON change: `status` values stay the past-tense wire names (`installed`, …) with `dry_run: true` (DEC-16).

## Acceptance Criteria

- No human line under `--dry-run` contains "would be " followed by a past participle, or a bare past-tense count line (`restored N folders`).
- The Steps-to-Reproduce commands print the expected text.
- JSON output is byte-identical before and after (only human text changes).
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/app/outcome.rs` tests for `header` and `status_detail` with `dry_run` true/false over every `ItemStatus`; `src/app/undo.rs` render test for a dry run.
- Integration: the human-output assertions that match "would be " (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, `tests/install_first_launch.rs`, found by grep) and any in `tests/sync.rs`, `tests/copy.rs`, `tests/pin.rs`, `tests/undo_history.rs`; `insta` snapshots of human output under `src/app/snapshots/` (`omaddons__app__outcome__tests__targets_human_*.snap`) and `tests/snapshots/` (review each diff).
- Contract: `tests/contract/special.rs::m2_outputs_are_byte_identical` keeps JSON unchanged.

## Considerations

- Keep "would revert …" (already right) and "would register"/"would make" in `targets` (`src/app/targets.rs:630-666`).
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.16 changes other human tables; land in either order, both touch snapshots.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.16`: Human tables misalign labelled targets, and list and history show look-alike columns
acceptance_criteria: every --dry-run header and item line uses "would <verb>" with the base verb (install, update, reinstall, remove, adopt, pin, unpin, edit, change, restore); item suffixes say "(would install)" etc.; undo --dry-run's counts read "would restore N folders, remove M"; sync's footer says "1 client matches"; human snapshots updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: Dry-run human output says what would happen ('would install 1 addon', 'Foo  2 (would install)', 'would restore N folders'), and sync agrees '1 client matches'; JSON is unchanged.

title: Human tables misalign labelled targets, and list and history show look-alike columns
description:
## Background

The human output's convention is header-less aligned tables (`output::table`, `src/output/human.rs:48-78`) whose cells say what they are: `status` puts the label in its own column with "-" when there is none (`src/app/status.rs:238`); `outdated` writes "Foo  v1  → v2" and "Pin  v1  pinned (latest v2)" (README `outdated`). The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found three tables that break it, and verification found a fourth problem in the same code:

1. **`targets`** (`src/app/targets.rs:590-616`, `rows`): the label, "(unregistered)", "(missing)" and the client path are joined into one last cell (`notes.join("  ")`, `:614`), so a row with a label (or a note) pushes its path right of the other rows' paths.
2. **`list`** (`src/app/list.rs:443-451`): each addon row is name, installed version, latest version, ref, flags. The latest column is the raw remembered version (blank when unchecked or static), so a current addon shows the same version twice side by side ("Foo  1.2  1.2  gh:o/foo"), with no header saying which is which.
3. **`history`** (`src/app/history.rs:140-172`): the first two columns are the tx and the run, both shortened by `short_id` (`:333-336`) to their first ten characters. A ULID's first ten characters are its millisecond timestamp, and a run id is minted in the same millisecond as its first transaction, so the two columns look alike ("01M5822F89…  01M5822F88…").
4. **Short ids are timestamps only** (found while verifying 3): because of the same ULID layout, the ten-character prefix that `history`, the `update`/`pin`/`sync` headers (`src/app/outcome.rs:1093-1100`, `full.get(..10)`) and `undo`'s header (`src/app/undo.rs:213`) show carries no random part. Transactions of one multi-client run, committed within a millisecond, show the same prefix, and `omaddons undo <that prefix>` is ambiguous (`not_found`, `src/app/undo.rs:391-420`).

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment, synthetic Battle.net root with a retail and a Classic Era client, two local installs and a pin on retail, `<config>/omaddons/config.toml` with `[targets.retail] label = "localhost"`:

```
$ omaddons targets
  era     -        Classic Era · Hardcore · Season of Discovery  1.15.7.61582  live  era (wow)  (unregistered)  <home>/Games/WoW/_classic_era_
  retail  01M582…  mainline                                      12.1.5.70391  live  localhost  <home>/Games/WoW/_retail_
$ omaddons history
01M5822F89…  01M5822F88…  2026-10-18 12:48  agent  pin      retail  +0 ~0 -0 =1
01M5822F7D…  01M5822F7D…  2026-10-18 12:48  agent  install  retail  +1 ~0 -0
01M5822F6J…  01M5822F6H…  2026-10-18 12:48  agent  install  retail  +1 ~0 -0     "first one"
```

`list` with a remembered latest release equal to the installed one shows the version twice (code: `src/app/list.rs:443-451`; reproducing needs a release memo, e.g. `tests/list.rs` fixtures).

## Technical Approach

1. **`targets`** (`src/app/targets.rs:590-616`): columns id (with the default marker), key, family or modes, version, kind, label ("-" when none, the same filter as today for the "<id> (battlenet)" default), notes ("(unregistered)", "(missing)", joined; blank when none), path (last, so unpadded). Same `rows` serve `targets add` (`render_add`, `:628-636`).
2. **`list`** (`src/app/list.rs:443-451`): the latest cell, from `a.latest.status`: `update_available` → "→ <version>"; `pinned` (a newer release exists) → "→ <version>" (the flags column already says "pinned"); `blocked` → "→ <version> (blocked)"; `failed` → "check failed"; `current`, `ahead`, `unchecked`, `static` → blank. JSON is unchanged (`latest {version, status}`). README `list` (`README.md:919`): "the column is blank when the addon is unchecked or static" becomes "the column shows `→ <version>` when a newer release is known (`update_available`, `pinned`, `blocked`), and is blank otherwise".
3. **`history`** (`src/app/history.rs:140-172`): the run cell is "run <short id>" when that run has two or more transactions in the history read (count over all entries before `--limit`), blank otherwise and for pre-M2 lines (today "-"). Decided over a header row: no other human table has headers, and the cell then names itself.
4. **Short ids**: one helper, `output::short_id(&str) -> String`, the first 16 characters (10 of time, 6 of randomness: about 2^30 values per millisecond) plus "…"; used by `history` (`src/app/history.rs:329-336`), `outcome::header` (`src/app/outcome.rs:1093-1100`), `undo` (`src/app/undo.rs:213`) and any other `get(..10)` of a tx or run (grep). The `undo` hint lines keep the full id.
5. README examples with short ids ("(tx 01M5Q2VA0J…)", `README.md:684-724` and others; grep `…)`) move to 16 characters.

No JSON change. Rejected: header rows (inconsistent with every other table), full ids in history rows (26 characters twice per row is noisy; the 16-character prefix is unique in practice and `undo` accepts any unique prefix of 8+).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `targets` with one labelled and one unlabelled client prints every path starting in the same column.
- `list` never shows the installed version twice; an update reads "Foo  1.1  → 1.2  gh:…".
- `history` rows of a single-transaction run have a blank run cell; a multi-client `update` shows "run <id>…" on each of its rows.
- Every short tx id shown in human output is 16 characters plus "…", and passing it to `undo` selects that transaction even when several transactions share a millisecond.
- README updated; argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/app/targets.rs` render test with a labelled, an unlabelled and a missing target (column positions of the path); `src/app/list.rs` render test over every latest status; `src/app/history.rs` render test with a two-transaction run and a single one; `src/output/human.rs` test for `short_id`.
- Integration: `tests/undo_history.rs`: two transactions in one run (a two-client `update` fixture, `tests/engine_multi_target.rs` style), `undo <16-char prefix>` reverts the right one.
- Snapshots: human snapshots under `src/app/snapshots/` and `tests/snapshots/` that contain short ids or these tables (review each).

## Considerations

- `table()` pads by character count; the "(missing)" note is colored (`style.warn`), and ANSI codes count as characters, so keep colored cells in the last-but-one column only when every row's cell is colored or blank, or pad before painting.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.15 changes dry-run wording in the same renderers; either order works.
- Agents read JSON; this is human output only.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.15`: Dry-run human output reads as past tense ("would be installed Baz", "restored 6 folders")
acceptance_criteria: targets gives label, notes and path their own columns ("-" for no label, as status does); list shows the latest release as "→ <version>" only when it differs; history shows the run as "run <id>" only for runs of two or more transactions; every short id is 16 characters so a shown tx prefix works with undo; README examples updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: Human tables align and say what they are: targets' label and notes have columns of their own, list's latest shows only a newer release, history names a run only when it has several transactions, and short ids are 16 characters so one run's transactions differ.

title: net-log prints every logged request with no default limit
description:
## Background

Vision §5.9: "Token-frugal by default. JSON contains ids, names, versions and counts; `--verbose` adds evidence, changelogs and paths." `history` follows it with a default `--limit 20` in every output mode (`src/app/history.rs:22-23`, `:177-184`) and `truncated` in its data. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found `net-log` returns everything:

- `src/app/net_log.rs:21-27`: the only flag is `--since`.
- `src/app/net_log.rs:127-152`: every entry of `net.log` and `net.log.1` (`src/net/log.rs:171`) goes into `data.entries` and into the human table (`:84-123`).
- `net.log` rotates at `NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES` = 10 MiB (`src/limits.rs:56`), so the two files can hold tens of thousands of lines; on the development machine plain `net-log` printed 1,037 lines.

User-visible consequence: the command an agent is told to use to audit the network ("net-log shows every request that reached the network", README "For coding agents") can return megabytes of JSON.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment; write 120 valid lines to `<state>/omaddons/net.log` (one JSON object per line: `time`, `method`, `host`, `path`, `status`, `bytes`, `wire_bytes`, `duration_ms`, `purpose`, `via`, `error`), then:

```
omaddons net-log | wc -l            # 121 (120 rows and the hosts line)
omaddons net-log --json             # data.entries has 120 items; data keys: entries, since, skipped, summary
```

Expected: the 50 most recent rows by default, a hint that more exist, and `truncated: true`.

## Technical Approach

1. `NetLogArgs` (`src/app/net_log.rs:21-27`) gains `--limit N` ("At most this many requests, the most recent (default 50)"); `0` is a usage error with fix `omaddons net-log --limit 50`, as `history` does (`src/app/history.rs:177-184`). Default 50, a local `const DEFAULT_LIMIT: usize = 50;` (not a safety limit, so not in `src/limits.rs`; `history` keeps its own 20 the same way). Decided 50 over history's 20: one `outdated` or `update` across a few clients makes tens of requests, and the point of `net-log` is to see a whole run.
2. Keep oldest-first order, and keep the *last* N matching entries (the most recent). `--since` filters first, then the limit applies.
3. `NetLogData` (`:29-39`) gains `truncated: bool` (more matched than shown), placed after `entries` as in `HistoryData`. `summary` keeps counting every matching entry, not only the shown ones (it is the per-host total), and `skipped` is unchanged.
4. Human output: after the table, when truncated, "(N earlier requests: --limit N or --since)" in the style of history's "(older entries: --limit N)" (`src/app/history.rs:166-168`).

Contract (DEC-4): new flag, additive data key `truncated`, default behaviour change (50 entries). README `net-log` (`README.md:1136-1143`): add `omaddons net-log --limit 200` to the examples and "By default the 50 most recent requests (`--limit N`); the host summary counts every request that matched; `truncated` says more matched." README "For coding agents" line becomes "net-log shows the requests that reached the network (the 50 most recent; --limit N)". Record on omad-vision-8qa.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `net-log` with 120 logged requests shows the last 50, oldest first, and "(70 earlier requests: …)"; `--json` has 50 entries, `truncated: true`, and `summary.by_host` totals 120.
- `--limit 200` shows all 120 with `truncated: false`; `--limit 0` is `usage`.
- `--since 1d --limit 5` applies the window first.
- README and vision comment updated; argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/app/net_log.rs` tests): selection of the last N after `--since`, `truncated`, summary over all matches.
- Integration (`tests/info_netlog.rs`): a written `net.log` with 60 lines; default, `--limit`, `--limit 0`.
- Contract: `tests/contract/snapshots/contract__matrix__net_log_ok.snap` gains `truncated` (review).

## Considerations

- Reading still parses both files whole (bounded by 2 × 10 MiB); only output is limited. A streaming tail is not needed at these sizes.
- Torn or unreadable lines stay counted in `skipped`.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.16`: Human tables misalign labelled targets, and list and history show look-alike columns
acceptance_criteria: net-log gains --limit N (default 50, N >= 1) showing the N most recent matching requests oldest first, in human and JSON output; data gains truncated; summary still counts every matching request; human output ends with a hint when truncated; README updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: net-log shows the 50 most recent requests by default (--limit N, after --since), says truncated when more matched, and still counts every match in its host summary.

title: Document that read-only commands accept --dry-run and --reason as no-ops, and test it
description:
## Background

`--dry-run` and `--reason` are global clap flags (`src/cli.rs:68-76`, `global = true`), so every command accepts them; read-only commands ignore them silently. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit asked whether that should be a warning or a usage error. README "Global options" says only "`--dry-run` | Show the plan without changing anything (mutating commands)" and "`--reason <TEXT>` | Why, recorded verbatim in history" (`README.md:573-575`), which leaves the read-only case unstated.

Verified in an isolated HOME (synthetic retail client, two installs): `status`, `list`, `history`, `info Foo`, `outdated`, `search foo`, `net-log`, `targets`, `config`, `export`, `adopt` and `help`, each with `--dry-run --reason why --json`, succeed with `ok: true` and no `dry_run` field.

## Technical Approach

Decided: silent and documented. D17 and vision §5.9: "The first command an agent guesses should work"; README "For coding agents" tells agents to use `--dry-run` "first for anything destructive", and an agent that adds it to a read-only command, or passes `--reason` on every call, has done nothing wrong. A usage error would break those first guesses; a warning would add noise to every such run and teach agents to ignore warnings. Rejected both.

1. README "Global options" (`README.md:573-575`): `--dry-run`: "Show the plan without changing anything. Every command accepts it; one that changes nothing ignores it." `--reason`: "Why, recorded verbatim in history (at most 200 characters) by every command that changes something; others accept and ignore it." (omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.5 makes "every command that changes something" true.)
2. The clap help strings (`src/cli.rs:68`, `:74`) match: "Show the plan without changing anything (ignored by commands that change nothing)".
3. A contract test (`tests/contract/special.rs`, beside `a_dry_run_leaves_the_state_directory_as_it_was`, `:127-181`): for each read-only path in `omaddons::app::COMMANDS` (`mutates == false` once omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1 adds it; until then a local list), run it with and without `--dry-run --reason x` and assert `support::without_meta` of both envelopes is equal, and that `state_tree(<state>)` (`:103-125`) is unchanged by the `--dry-run` run beyond derived files the command writes anyway.

No contract change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- README Global options and the clap help state the no-op rule.
- The contract test covers every read-only command and passes.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Contract: the new test above; `cargo test --locked --test contract special`.

## Considerations

- A mutating command that ignored `--dry-run` would be a real bug; omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.12 is the one case of wrong wording found, and `tests/contract/special.rs::a_dry_run_leaves_the_state_directory_as_it_was` guards the writes.
- `--actor` stays a filter on `history` (README), not a no-op there.
- Derived writes (release memo, download cache, `net.log`) still happen under `--dry-run` for `outdated`, `search`, `info` and `adopt`; README already says what each writes.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1`: Usage-error fixes come from the root command list and can name a different mutating verb
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.12`: auth github set --dry-run says it stored the token although nothing is written
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.5`: config set, targets changes, auth github set/clear and export --write record no history
acceptance_criteria: README Global options says --dry-run and --reason are accepted by every command and ignored by those that change nothing; a contract test shows each read-only command's data is identical with and without --dry-run --reason, and writes nothing to state; argc gate passes
close_reason: --dry-run and --reason are documented as accepted everywhere and ignored by commands that change nothing; a contract test proves it for every read-only command.

title: The contract suite never checks that a suggested argv parses
description:
## Background

README "For coding agents": "Run fix_argv / alternatives[].argv / commands[].argv as argv arrays; never parse the display strings." README "Stability" says the contract suite checks "that every `fix_argv` and `commands[].argv` round-trips through shell quoting to its display string", and nothing more. The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found suggested argvs that do not parse at all (omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1: `omaddons targets pin a b`, `omaddons config list k v`, `omaddons targets --reason`), which the suite cannot catch:

- `tests/contract/main.rs:232-255` (`support::fix`): checks that a non-null argv starts with `omaddons`, joins back to the display, and carries no presentation flag.
- `tests/contract/main.rs:198-207`: the same for `commands[]`, without parsing.
- `tests/contract/main.rs:189-197`: warning fixes go through `support::fix` too.
- Nothing calls `omaddons::cli::Cli::try_parse_from` (the crate exports `cli` publicly, `src/lib.rs:12`).

Also stale: README "Stability" and the Tests table (`README.md:1322`, `:1829`) say "24 snapshots"; `tests/contract/snapshots/` holds 60.

## Technical Approach

1. **Parse every suggestion.** In `tests/contract/main.rs`, add `fn parses(argv: &[String], ctx: &str)` that asserts `omaddons::cli::Cli::try_parse_from(argv).is_ok()` (with the clap error rendered in the failure message). Call it from `support::fix` for every non-null argv (error fix, alternatives, warning fixes) and from the `commands[]` loop. This runs on every envelope the matrix, `special.rs` and `recommendations.rs` produce, so every existing case becomes a parse check. A parse check, not an execution: semantic failures (an addon that is not installed) are fine.
2. **A corpus of wrong invocations.** New test file `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` (registered in `tests/contract/main.rs` beside `mod special;`), with a table of argvs, each run as `s.json(argv, 2)`:
   - root verbs: `instal dbm`, `uninstall dbm` (now an alias: exit per command, not 2; assert it is `remove`), `plan`, `unpn x`, `statsu`, `lst`, `serch x`, `outdate`, `hepl`, `reinstall x -t retail`;
   - nested: `targets rn a b`, `targets ad /x`, `targets remov x`, `targets list`, `config st k v`, `config gt k`, `config ls`, `auth github st`, `auth gihub`, `auth github show`;
   - flags: `install x --dry-rn`, `targets --rescn`, `targets add /x --nme foo`, `undo --last-bi agent`, `--jsno`, `status --cachd`, `history --limt 5`;
   - values: `install x --channel betaa`, `search x --source wowii`, `undo --saved-variables restor`, `--format jsno status`.
   For each: the fix and every alternative parse (step 1 already asserts it); and a **verb rule**: let `typed` be the canonical path the typed word resolves to through aliases and the omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1 synonym table (`None` for a pure typo); the fix's command path (via `omaddons::cli::command_path`) must be `typed`, a path whose `omaddons::app::COMMANDS` entry has `mutates == false`, or `help …`. A table of expected fixes pins the decided outputs from omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1's acceptance list.
3. **A generated sweep.** In the same file, for every path in `omaddons::app::COMMANDS` (root and nested) build one-edit typos of the last word (drop a letter, swap two adjacent letters) and assert the same two properties on `cli::usage_error(&err, &argv)` directly (in-process, no binary run, so the sweep stays fast). Skip a typo that happens to be another real name or alias.
4. **Docs.** README "Stability" (`README.md:1322`): "... and that every `fix_argv`, `alternatives[].argv` and `commands[].argv` parses as an omaddons command line and round-trips through shell quoting to its display string; a corpus of mistyped commands checks that a fix never names a different command that changes addons. Snapshots pin representative envelopes." The count is dropped (decided: a number in prose drifts, as 24 → 60 shows). Same change in the Tests table row (`README.md:1829`).

No contract change: this is a test of the existing promise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `support::fix` and the `commands[]` loop assert `Cli::try_parse_from` succeeds on every suggested argv.
- `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` exists with the corpus and the generated sweep; both pass after omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1.
- The verb rule uses `COMMANDS[].mutates` (added by omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1), not a second hand-kept list.
- README Stability and the Tests table describe the parse check and no longer say 24 snapshots.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Contract: `cargo test --locked --test contract` (the whole suite, since step 1 tightens every existing case).
- Self-test: extend `the_harness_rejects_broken_envelopes` (`tests/contract/main.rs:527-555`) with an envelope whose `fix_argv` is `["omaddons","targets","pin","a","b"]` and assert `check` panics.
- Unit: none beyond omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1's.

## Considerations

- Fails until omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1 lands (the corpus encodes omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1's decisions); land omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1 first, or land this with the corpus marked expected-to-fail only if omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1 is split. Decided: land after omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1 (depends_on).
- Some fixes are deliberately prose (`fix_argv: null`); step 1 only touches non-null argvs. omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.11 tightens the prose side.
- A fix that parses only with input on stdin (`auth github set`) still parses; stdin is not part of argv.
- `Cli::try_parse_from` treats `--help`/`-h` as a flag (`disable_help_flag = true`, `src/cli.rs:33`), so `omaddons help …` and `… --help` both parse.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.11`: Fixes that are omaddons commands are written as prose with fix_argv null
acceptance_criteria: support::check parses every error fix_argv, alternatives[].argv, warnings[].fix_argv and commands[].argv with omaddons::cli::Cli::try_parse_from; a corpus test of wrong invocations (root, targets, config, auth github, flags, values) asserts each fix parses and is never a different mutating verb; README Stability describes the check and the real snapshot count; argc gate passes
close_reason: The contract suite parses every suggested argv (error fix, alternatives, warning fixes, commands[]) with Cli::try_parse_from, and a corpus plus a generated one-edit sweep check that usage fixes never name a different mutating command.

The contract-suite corpus check this bead adds can assert the same through the binary.

title: Failure envelopes and stderr drop every warning the run raised before it failed
description:
## Background

README "The JSON contract": the envelope has `warnings` on success and on failure (`README.md:1175-1184`, `:1198`), and vision §5.9 says the run's diagnostics go to stderr. A failure is exactly when an agent most needs to know that `config.toml` has an unknown key, that an interrupted transaction is pending (`journal_pending`), or that a state file was written by a newer omaddons (`state_version_newer`). The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found that every failure drops them.

Where the code is:

- `src/output/mod.rs:139-145`: `Err(error)` renders `Envelope::failure(command, &error, &[], &[], meta)`: warnings and commands are always empty, and `reporter.warning` is never called, so stderr drops them too.
- Commands return `Result<O, Error>`; warnings live only inside a successful outcome. `World::load_with` (`src/app/world.rs:53-122`) gathers config (`:57`), registry (`:62`), discovery (`:101`), reconciliation (`:103`), `journal_pending` (`:107`) and GitHub credential (`:110`) warnings into `world.warnings`, and each command clones them into its outcome (`src/app/status.rs:376`, `remove.rs:255`, `install.rs:414`, … 17 sites). Any `?` after `World::load` loses them.
- The same loss happens on some successes, because their outcomes never copy `world.warnings`: `undo` (`src/app/undo.rs:442`, warnings start empty), `targets add|rm|rename|default` (`src/app/targets.rs:410`, `:438`, `:541`, `:572`), `config set` (`src/app/config.rs:337`).

User-visible consequence: an agent sees `ok:false, warnings: []` and fixes the error it was given, never learning that `journal_pending` or `config_unknown_key` explains or accompanies it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment (empty HOME), `<config>/omaddons/config.toml` containing `bogus_key = 1`:

```
omaddons status --json                     # warnings: ["config_unknown_key"]; stderr: one warning event
omaddons remove nothing -t nowhere --json  # ok:false target_not_found, warnings: []; stderr: only the error event
omaddons install nosuchaddon --json        # ok:false not_found, warnings: []
```

With a synthetic retail client, one install, then the same config.toml:

```
omaddons undo --dry-run --json             # ok:true, warnings: []    (status/history show config_unknown_key)
omaddons targets default retail --json     # ok:true, warnings: []
omaddons config set default_channel beta --dry-run --json   # ok:true, warnings: []
```

A pending journal (debug build), synthetic retail client, no config.toml:

```
OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.journal.prepared=abort omaddons install <dir>/Foo -t retail --json   # aborts (exit 134)
omaddons list --json            # ok:true,  warnings: ["journal_pending"]
omaddons list -t nosuch --json  # ok:false target_not_found, warnings: []
```

Expected: `config_unknown_key` (or `journal_pending`) in every one of these envelopes, and one `warning` event on stderr before the `error` event.

## Technical Approach

1. **A run-scoped sink.** Add `pub struct RunNotes` in `src/output/` (beside `ProgressSink`, `src/output/stderr.rs:79-157`): an `Arc<Mutex<…>>` holding `warnings: Vec<Warning>` and `commands: Vec<CommandHint>`, `Clone`, with `warn(Warning)`, `warn_all(&[Warning])`, `hint(CommandHint)` and `snapshot() -> (Vec<Warning>, Vec<CommandHint>)`; a poisoned lock is used as is (as `stderr::lock` does). `Context` (`src/cli.rs:186-205`) gains `pub notes: RunNotes`, created in `Context::new`.
2. **Feed it where warnings are found.** `World::load_with` takes `&Context` (`World::load(ctx)`, `World::load_with(ctx, mode)`; 19 call sites, mechanical) and pushes each batch into `ctx.notes` as soon as it exists (after `Config::load`, after `load_registry`, after discovery, after reconciliation, after `pending_warnings`, after `GithubToken::resolve`), so a later `?` inside `load_with` keeps the earlier ones. `world.warnings` stays as it is for the outcomes. `config::read` (`src/app/config.rs:160-168`) and `auth::run`'s `Config::load` (`src/app/auth.rs:172`) push their config warnings too. Commands that load records later (`load_record(...).warning(...)`, e.g. `src/app/list.rs:211`) push those as well.
3. **Render them.** `output::emit_to` (`src/output/mod.rs:81-147`) takes the snapshot (pass `&RunNotes` through `emit`/`Out::emit_as`, `src/app/mod.rs:171-190`; usage errors and the version/help paths pass an empty one):
   - `Err(error)`: `Envelope::failure(command, &error, &warnings, &[], meta)`, and `reporter.warning(w)` for each before `reporter.error(&error)`.
   - `Ok(outcome)`: emitted warnings are the run's first, then each `outcome.warnings()` entry not equal to one already emitted (dedup by `PartialEq`, run warnings win their position). Today every outcome clones `world.warnings` first, so order is unchanged for every command that already reported them. `commands` on success stay the outcome's own.
   - `check_failed`: same merge as success.
   The `commands` channel is filled by omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.9 (commit hints for the panic path); this bead only defines it and keeps failure `commands` empty.
4. **Docs and contract.** README "Fields", `warnings` row: "`{code, message, fix, fix_argv}`. On a partial run, each failed item is mirrored here. On a failure, it holds what the run found before it failed (a `journal_pending`, a `config_unknown_key`)." Add to the Failure paragraph that `commands` is empty on failure other than `check_failed`. Record on omad-vision-8qa as a DEC-4 behaviour change (no new code, no new key). The envelope's key order is unchanged (`src/output/envelope.rs:20-38`; the contract ORDER list `tests/contract/main.rs:34-46`).

Rejected: a `warnings` field on `Error` that each command fills with `.map_err(|e| e.with(&world.warnings))` (every `?` site must remember, and errors inside `World::load` still lose earlier batches); returning `(warnings, Result<O>)` from every command (invasive, same forgetting problem); a process-global collector (crosstalk between in-process unit tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The three failure reproductions carry `config_unknown_key` in `warnings` and print one stderr `warning` event before the single `error` event.
- `undo`, `targets add|rm|rename|default` and `config set` successes carry it too.
- A `journal_pending` warning (a crashed install, as `tests/contract/matrix.rs::status` makes one) appears in the envelope of a following failing read command (`list -t nosuch`).
- No warning is emitted twice on success; snapshot order of existing successes is unchanged.
- README updated, vision comment recorded; argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/output/tests.rs`): `emit_to` with an `Err` and a non-empty `RunNotes` renders the warnings in the envelope and on the NDJSON reporter before the error; with an `Ok` whose outcome repeats a run warning, it appears once.
- Integration: `tests/cli_config.rs` (unknown key, then a failing command and `config set`); `tests/undo_history.rs` (undo success carries a config warning).
- Contract: a matrix case `list -t nosuch` after a crashed install (journal pending) asserting `warnings[].code` contains `journal_pending`; `support::check` already validates warning fixes. Review the failure snapshots: those whose scene has no world warnings stay `"warnings": []`.

## Considerations

- `--quiet` still drops stderr warnings (only errors); the envelope keeps them.
- Warnings found before the failure only: a failure inside `Config::load` itself has none to report.
- The panic path (omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.9) should read the same sink from the panic state; omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.9 depends on this bead.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.10 changes the HOME error, which happens before any warning exists.
- Performance: one mutex per push, a handful per run.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.9`: The panic path can print two envelopes, none, or a malformed one, and loses the undo hint
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.10`: A missing HOME, or an internal error inside status, gets the failing command as its fix
acceptance_criteria: a run-scoped warning sink on Context collects World/config/registry/discovery/journal/credential warnings as they are found; a failure envelope's warnings and the stderr warning events carry them; successes merge them without duplicates, so undo, targets add/rm/rename/default and config set stop dropping them; README Fields documents warnings on failure; argc gate passes
close_reason: Context.notes (output::RunNotes) collects the run's warnings as they are found (World::load batches, late record warnings, config set, auth github, targets rm, undo's history_lines_skipped). A failure envelope and stderr carry them before the error; successes merge them first without duplicates, so undo, targets and config set stop dropping them. README Fields documents warnings on failure and empty failure commands; vision comment added.

Why it matters: the warning matters most when undo fails because the transaction's line was skipped (undo <tx> answers not_found, bare undo picks an older one). How: once failure envelopes keep warnings raised before the failure, raise it into that channel before select() runs. Risk: double reporting if both the success path and the new channel add it. title: A JSON flag spelling that fails to parse gets no stdout envelope
description:
## Background

README "The JSON contract": "`--json` (or `--robot`, `--format json`, `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json`) makes every command print **exactly one JSON object on one line on stdout**, on success and on failure, including usage errors and panics." When clap cannot parse argv, `cli::run_with` (`src/cli.rs:285-310`) renders the usage error with `fallback_output`, which reads presentation flags token by token in `output::flags_from_argv` (`src/output/term.rs:183-216`). The 2026-10-16 post-M2 audit found spellings the fallback misses:

- `src/output/term.rs:192-193`: only the exact tokens `--json` and `--robot` set JSON; `--json=1`, `--json=true`, `--robot=yes` (clap: "unexpected value '1' for '--json'") fall through to `other` and are ignored.
- `src/output/term.rs:194-195`: `--format` and `--progress` take `args.next()` unconditionally, so `status --format --json` makes `--json` the format value and JSON is never set (clap itself reports "a value is required for '--format'").
- `src/cli.rs:56` and `:90`: clap's `value_parser = ["json", "human"]` is case-sensitive, while `output_mode` (`src/output/term.rs:159-172`) and `OMADDONS_FORMAT` accept any case, so `--format JSON` is a usage error although `OMADDONS_FORMAT=JSON` works.

What already works (verified): `--format=json` and `--format JSON` with a later parse error, `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json` with a parse error, `--json --format` (missing value), `--format=xml --json`.

User-visible consequence: an agent that passes `--json=true` (a common spelling for boolean flags) gets an empty stdout and has to parse stderr.

## Steps to Reproduce

Isolated environment, empty HOME:

```
omaddons status --json=1        # stdout: empty; stderr: {"event":"error","code":"usage","message":"unexpected value '1' for '--json' found; ...","fix":"omaddons help status",...}
omaddons status --json=true     # stdout: empty
omaddons status --robot=1       # stdout: empty
omaddons --robot=yes status     # stdout: empty
omaddons status --format --json # stdout: empty (a value is required for '--format')
omaddons status --progress --json   # stdout: empty
omaddons status --format JSON   # stdout: one envelope, but a usage error (invalid value 'JSON')
```

Expected: exactly one envelope on stdout for each; `--format JSON` succeeds.

## Technical Approach

1. **Fallback reads every JSON spelling** (`src/output/term.rs:183-216`): in the `other` arm, `--json=<anything>` sets `flags.json = true` and `--robot=<anything>` sets `flags.robot = true`. Decided: the user named the JSON flag; its value is what is wrong, so the error is rendered as JSON. Rejected: accepting `--json=false` as "human" (no clap flag here takes a boolean value; inventing one adds a contract surface for nothing).
2. **Never swallow a flag as a value**: `--format` and `--progress` take the next token only when it does not start with `-`, matching clap's own refusal; otherwise the value is `None` and the next token is read normally.
3. **Case-insensitive values in clap** (`src/cli.rs:56`, `:90`): `value_parser = clap::builder::PossibleValuesParser::new(["json", "human"])` with `ignore_case = true` (and the same for `--progress`'s `json|human|none`), so `--format JSON` parses; `output_mode` already compares case-insensitively and `resolve`'s progress match should lowercase too (`src/output/term.rs:131-139`).
4. **A useful fix**: for a clap error whose invalid argument is a presentation flag (`--json`/`--robot` with a value, `--format`/`--progress` with an invalid or missing value), the fix is the argv without that flag (`fix_argv` already drops presentation flags, `src/cli.rs:701-735`): `omaddons status`, which the consumer reruns with its own `--json`. The "never the failing command itself" check (`src/cli.rs:581-588`) compares presentation-stripped argvs, so it must not apply to this case (the stripped argv is a different, valid command line). Today the fix is `omaddons help status`.

Contract: behaviour only (no new code); README needs no change beyond omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.2's Stability text, since it already promises this. Note it in the vision-bead comment that records omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1's usage-fix rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `status --json=1`, `--json=true`, `--robot=1`, `--robot=yes status`, `--format --json`, `--progress --json` each print exactly one envelope (`ok:false`, `usage`, exit 2) and one stderr `error` event.
- Their fix is `omaddons status` (argv `["omaddons","status"]`).
- `status --format JSON` and `--progress JSON` succeed.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/output/term.rs` tests): extend `raw_argv_finds_the_output_mode` with `--json=1`, `--robot=yes`, `--format --json`, `--progress --json`, `--json=` (empty value).
- Unit (`src/cli.rs` tests): `a_usage_error_renders_as_its_argv_asks` gains `--json=1`; a new case asserting the fix for `status --json=1` is `["omaddons","status"]`; the "never itself" loop (`a_usage_error_never_suggests_itself`, `src/cli.rs:935-983`) already includes `--json=1` and must keep passing with the exemption scoped to presentation flags.
- Contract (`tests/contract/special.rs::every_json_spelling_prints_the_same_envelope`): add a failing-spelling companion test: each of the Steps-to-Reproduce argvs through `support::check(run, 2)` (exactly one envelope, one error event).

## Considerations

- Arguments after `--` stay ignored by the fallback (`src/output/term.rs:191`).
- `--json=1` remains a usage error on purpose: the fix tells the agent the right spelling.
- omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1 changes the generic usage fixes; this bead's presentation-flag case runs before them.

## Related

- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.1`: Usage-error fixes come from the root command list and can name a different mutating verb
- `omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.2`: The contract suite never checks that a suggested argv parses
acceptance_criteria: the raw-argv fallback treats --json=<v> and --robot=<v> as asking for JSON and never takes a following flag as the value of --format/--progress; --format and --progress values are case-insensitive in clap; the usage fix for a bad presentation-flag value is the argv without it; status --json=1, --robot=1, --format --json and --progress --json each print exactly one envelope; argc gate passes
close_reason: Every JSON flag spelling clap refuses still prints one envelope, its fix is the command without the refused or misspelled presentation flag, and --format/--progress values are case-insensitive.

It leaves out the presentation-flag typos this bead owns. Today 'omaddons --jsno --json' gets fix 'omaddons --json', which the harness rejects as a suggestion carrying a presentation flag; under this bead's step 4 it should be 'omaddons' (status --jsno → 'omaddons status'). Add (&["--jsno"], None), (&["status", "--jsno"], Some("status")) and (&["--format", "jsno", "status"], Some("status")) back to CORPUS when this lands.
