title: Records-only engine work: Records mode, RecordEdit, RecordGuard, record history ops, kind override and TxKind::Pin
description:
## Background

Adoption (E5.2), pin/unpin (B7), channel and reason edits (A4.3, F3.1), `required_by` bookkeeping (C4.1, C6) and removing an addon whose folders are already gone all change records without touching an AddOns folder. The engine cannot express that. Line numbers are as of `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.
- `rejudge` (`src/engine/plan.rs:411-462`) arms: `(Some(template), Some(inspected))` → no-op check or `build_install` (428-453); `_ if !record.addons.contains_key(..) => Ok(None)` (454-459); `_ => planner.remove(..)` (460). A work with a record and no inspected archive is dropped under the lock, or turned into a remove.
- `history_ops` (`src/engine/tx.rs:716-734`) derives ops from `SwapOp`s only, so a swap-less commit writes `ops: []`. Undo and `check_conflicts` (`src/engine/undo.rs:507-555`) read `ops`, so such a commit is not undoable and invisible to conflict detection.
- `next_record` (`tx.rs:654-688`) inserts each work's full record, the last for an addon wins (661-674), and restamps `installed_at` for every work (666).
- `TxRequest` (`tx.rs:84-92`) has no kind; `target_kind` (`plan.rs:538-548`) knows Install, Update and Remove and is recomputed in `locked()` (`tx.rs:480`); `TxKind` (`src/model.rs:408-419`) has no `Pin`.
- **Latent defect 1:** `TargetPlanner::remove` (`plan.rs:861-898`) gets no allowed op for a folder with no live entry (`src/engine/ownership.rs:159-163`). A remove whose folders were all deleted out of band writes `ops: []`, its undo restores nothing, and the gone folders' index entries stay.

Without this, each feature would hand-roll an un-undoable state write, breaking G-M2-7 (every mutation is a transaction) and starving G-M2-4 (adopt without replacing folders), G-M2-5 (sync converges) and G-M2-1 (pins protect updates). First child of epic A4 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4`).

## Technical Approach

Builds on A3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.3`): `Install` carries `channel_explicit`, `pin: PinIntent { Keep, Pin, Unpin }`, `reason`, `reinstall`; `Reinstall` is renamed `Update`; `AddonWork` keeps the intent; `carry_over` runs in `build_install` at plan time (snapshot) and under the lock (current record). Add `RequestedChange::Edit { addon: String, edit: RecordEdit }`.

**1. Work shapes.** `AddonWork { addon, mode }`:
- `Folders { record, blob, inspected, skipped, swap, transfers, degraded, intent: Option<InstallIntent>, edits: Vec<RecordEdit> }`: today's install, update, remove (A3's `intent` moves here from `AddonWork`), plus folded edits.
- `Records { before: Option<AddonRecord>, after: Option<AddonRecord>, edits, index_upserts: Vec<(FolderName, FolderIndex)>, index_removals: Vec<FolderName>, guard: RecordGuard }`: no folder ops, nothing staged.

`edits` is kept because the rules run again under the lock: `rejudge` recomputes `after` by applying `edits` to the **current** record, so a concurrent change to another field survives (`Adopt` keeps the spec's record, `Forget` keeps `None`). Read `w.record`/`w.inspected` through accessors (`stage_all`, `creates_addons_dir`, `src/app/install.rs:795`).

**2. `RecordEdit`:** `SetPinned(bool)`, `SetChannel(Channel)`, `SetReason(AddonReason)` set the field; `AddRequiredBy(String)`/`RemoveRequiredBy(String)` add or remove a name, kept sorted and de-duplicated by `TargetRecord::addon_key`; `Forget` drops a record whose folders are all missing (with a folder present, the item fails `usage`, fix `omaddons remove <name> -t <id>`); `Repoint(Ref)` sets `ref`, clears `release_id` and sets `version_confidence: toc`, so the next `update` installs from the new ref (E5.2); `Adopt(AdoptSpec)` creates a record, `AdoptSpec { record, folders: Vec<(FolderName, FolderIndex)>, stats }` with per-file plan-time `(size, mtime_ns)` (E5.2 fills it via `index_live_folder`). An edit that changes nothing plans no work (unchanged, no transaction). An edit on an unrecorded addon is the item failure `not_managed` (except `Adopt`).

**3. One work per addon per transaction.** Two works for one addon would roll its record back to whichever `next_record` inserts last (an update of BigWigs plus an `AddRequiredBy` on BigWigs). So an edit to an addon that already has a work is folded into it: into a `Folders` work's carry-over (applied after `carry_over`, at plan time and in `rejudge`) or merged into its `Records` work. Folding is order-independent: a `Folders` work planned after a `Records` work for the same addon absorbs its edits and replaces it, change included. `Records.after` comes from the snapshot plus the works already planned in this target; A5 replaces that with the working view, so keep folding in one function A5 can rewire.

**4. `RecordGuard`**, re-checked by `rejudge` under the lock, offline, per edit kind so an unrelated concurrent change does not abort the target:
- `SetPinned`, `SetChannel`, `SetReason`, `Repoint`: still recorded with the same `release_id`.
- `AddRequiredBy`, `RemoveRequiredBy`: still recorded, at any release.
- `Forget`: still recorded, and its folders still absent.
- `Adopt`: every folder still present, unmanaged and not a symlink; a re-listing finds exactly the indexed paths; every file keeps its plan-time `(size, mtime_ns)`; no record has taken the spec's name.

Several folded edits take the strictest guard. Failure rules: **an adopt guard failure is always `plan_stale` (retryable), whatever the generation**, because a file edited between hashing and the lock never bumps it, and dropping the work would lose the request. For edits, a failed guard with the generation changed is `plan_stale` with `details.cause` via `tx::stale()`, as for folder work (cause: an existing code such as `not_managed`; no new code). With the generation unchanged the edit is dropped as no longer needed (only a `Forget` whose folder came back by hand). Give `rejudge` the plan-time generation, or a typed failure `locked()` maps.

**5. History, `rejudge`, `remove`.** `history_ops` also emits one `HistoryOp { op: FolderOp::Record, folder, addon }` per folder (before ∪ after) of every `Records` work. Undo already turns `record` ops into "no swap" (`undo.rs:647`) and restores the addons named in `ops` from the snapshot, which undoes pin, channel, reason, repoint, adopt and forget. `rejudge` becomes mode-aware: `Folders` arms stay byte-identical; `Records` works check the guard, then return the recomputed work or apply the failure rules, and are never dropped or turned into a remove while the guard holds. `TargetPlanner::remove` plans a `Records` work when every recorded folder is absent: `before` = the record, `after: None`, `index_removals` = its folders, guard `Forget`, `Change { kind: Remove, folders.recorded }`, no running policy. That fixes latent defect 1. A partly absent remove stays a `Folders` work (M1 behaviour).

**6. Kind.** `TxRequest.kind: Option<TxKind>` (override), carried into `PlanRequest`. `TxTarget.default_kind: TxKind` (what the app means: install → Install, remove → Remove, update → Update) is copied into `TargetRequest.default_kind`. Both feed `plan()` and the recomputation in `locked()`. Add **`TxKind::Pin`** (wire `pin`, undoable). `target_kind(changes, override, default_kind)`, in order:
1. no changes → no transaction;
2. an override wins: `Adopt` (adopt, repoint), `Pin` (pin, unpin), `Sync`;
3. all changes are `Edit`s that changed only `pinned` → `pin`;
4. all changes are `Edit` or `Adopt` → `default_kind`;
5. in a mix, `Edit`/`Adopt` changes are ignored and today's rule applies: `remove LittleWigs` plus `RemoveRequiredBy` on BigWigs is `remove`.

Undo of any kind is an ordinary `undo`. Update the literals in `src/app/install.rs:406` and `:592` (probe), `src/app/remove.rs:225`, `src/engine/testing.rs:367`, `tests/plan.rs`.

**7. Commit.** The journal already handles zero swap steps: `swap()` still writes `swapped` (`src/engine/swap.rs:338`). A crash while Prepared rolls back nothing, and once Swapped it rolls forward record, index and history idempotently. No new phase or payload field. Records-only transactions still take the state snapshot and write an empty `WTF.manifest.json` (`snapshot_saved_variables` with no folders); undo requires both (`undo.rs:412-414`, `:871-872`), so do not optimise them away. Merge `index_upserts`/`index_removals` into the swap-derived `IndexChanges`, so they ride in the journal payload. `next_record`: a `Records` work inserts `after` (or removes the key), sets `tx_id`, keeps `installed_at`; an `Adopt` (no previous record) takes the commit time; `Folders` works restamp as today. Records-only works skip staging and the running policy, report `reload_required: none`, and commit while the client runs.

**8. Output.** `ChangeKind` gains `Adopt`, `Edit` (wire `adopt`, `edit`). Keep it a `Copy` string enum and add `Change.fields: Vec<EditField>` (wire `fields`: `pinned|channel|reason|required_by|ref`, sorted, omitted when empty) so existing change JSON is byte-identical. Example: `{"addon":"Foo","ref":"gh:o/foo","kind":"edit","fields":["pinned"],"from_version":"1","to_version":"1","folders":{"added":[],"replaced":[],"removed":[],"skipped":[],"recorded":["Foo","FooOld"]}}`. `FolderSummary.recorded: Vec<FolderName>` (folders whose ownership record changed without a swap; sorted, always serialised; update `install.rs` `sorted()`). `src/app/history.rs` `ChangeCounts.recorded` counts `record` ops, shown in the human line when non-zero.

**Why (M2-D6):** done once in the engine, every records-only change is journaled, snapshotted, attributed and undoable, and M4's `repair` gets it free. **Crash safety:** the folder oracle cannot see records-only work. Record oracle: after a crash and recovery, the record holds the edit **iff** `history.jsonl` holds the transaction, the generation matches, and AddOns is byte-identical. A4.4 runs it cross-process (`abort`); this bead in process (`error`).

**Files:** `src/engine/{plan,tx,undo,testing}.rs`, `src/engine/journal.rs` (verify only), `src/model.rs`, `src/state/history.rs` (doc), `src/app/{history,install,remove}.rs`, `tests/plan.rs`, `tests/engine_undo.rs`, snapshots `tests/snapshots/{install__*,plan__plan_dry_run}.snap` and `tests/contract/snapshots/contract__matrix__{history_ok,install_*}.snap`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Edit(SetPinned(true))` via the engine API commits kind `pin` with one `record` op per folder; `undo` unpins it (generation +1); AddOns stays byte-identical.
- `remove Foo` after its folders were deleted out of band commits kind `remove` with `record` ops and drops record and index entries; `undo` restores both.
- Updating D plus `Edit(AddRequiredBy("R"))` on D, in either order, writes one record (new release, R in `required_by`) and one change.
- Guards: a pin still commits after a concurrent install of another addon; a `RemoveRequiredBy` survives a concurrent update of its addon and keeps that release; a concurrent update breaking a pin guard is `plan_stale` (retryable, `details.cause`); a changed adopted file is `plan_stale` even at an unchanged generation.
- `TxKind::Pin` serialises `pin` and is undoable; `target_kind` follows the five rules, including `remove` + `RemoveRequiredBy` → `remove`.
- A no-op edit creates no transaction; records-only transactions report `reload_required: none` and commit while the client runs under `safe`.
- An `error` at each commit-window failpoint leaves the edit present iff its history line exists, folders untouched.
- The existing crash, concurrency and undo suites pass unchanged; install/remove output changes only by `folders.recorded`; reviewed snapshots committed.

## Test Plan

- Unit `plan.rs`: `target_kind` table; `apply_edit` per variant; fold order independence; guard checks and the strictest-guard rule.
- Unit `tx.rs` (`TxScene`): `history_ops` with mixed works; `next_record` with `Records` works; an `error` matrix over `FAILPOINTS` for a pin, modelled on `an_error_at_any_failpoint_leaves_folders_wholly_old_or_wholly_new`; two-thread races with `failpoint::with_spec("engine.plan.done=sleep:400", …)` against a competing `TxScene::run` (pin vs other install; `RemoveRequiredBy` vs update; pin vs update → `plan_stale`).
- Unit `undo.rs`: undo of a pin, a forget, and a hand-built `Adopt` (record and index entries go; folders untouched).
- E2E: `tests/engine_undo.rs` forget-remove then `undo` via the CLI; `tests/plan.rs` dry run showing `kind: "edit"`, `fields`, `folders.recorded`. Unit `app/history.rs`: `recorded` counted.

## Considerations

- Keep install and remove byte-identical; the M1 suites are the regression net. Change `rejudge` only by adding mode-aware arms.
- **`required_by` edits keep M1 snapshot-restore undo until A4.2.** Undoing a requester after its dependency was updated would raise `undo_conflict` or roll the dependency's record back under new folders. Nothing outside tests may produce `AddRequiredBy`/`RemoveRequiredBy` before A4.2; C4.1 and C6 wait for it.
- Command statuses for edits belong to A4.3, B7, E5.2, F3.1. One exception, owned by A6 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.6`): if A6's `src/app/outcome.rs` is already on `main`, map the new kinds in its `build` as A6 specifies (`Adopt` → `adopted`; an `Edit` whose `fields` are only `pinned` → `pinned` or `unpinned` by the new value; any other `Edit` → `edited`), because whichever of A6 and A4.1 lands second adds that mapping. `FolderOp::Record` exists since M1; `HistoryOp` is unchanged here.
- Hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x), `src/engine/undo.rs` (A4.x, A12, E1), `src/error.rs`.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.

title: Reversible required_by edit ops in history and undo
description:
## Background

Dependencies make one addon's record carry another addon's name. Installing LittleWigs (R) adds `LittleWigs` to BigWigs' (D) `required_by` in the same transaction (C4.1). Removing R, or an update of R that drops the dependency, takes it out again (C6). After A4.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1`), such an edit is a `Records` work on D whose history ops are plain `record` ops on D's folders. Undo treats them like any other op. Line numbers are as of `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

- `check_conflicts` (`src/engine/undo.rs:507-555`) collects the folder keys of every op of the reverted transaction and refuses when any later transaction touched one.
- `FolderPlan::inverse` (`undo.rs:626-727`) pushes every op's folder into `touched` (`:638`). `record` ops become "no swap" (`:647`).
- `restored_state` (`undo.rs:756-848`) builds its `direct` set from every op's addon (`:776-782`). It restores each direct addon's **whole record** from the transaction's state snapshot (`:808-815`), and upserts the snapshot's files-index entry for every touched folder (`:840-846`).
- `FolderPlan::record_only` (`:609-623`), used for the SavedVariables follow-up, copies every op as a `record` op.

**The failure.** Install R (D gains R in `required_by`), then update D, then undo R's install:
1. `check_conflicts` sees D's folders replaced by the later update, so the undo is `undo_conflict` and R's install can never be undone while D stays updated.
2. Without the conflict, it would be worse: D's record would be restored from the snapshot taken before R's install. That means D's pre-update release, with the new folders still on disk, and D's files index rolled back to pre-update entries.

This bead makes `required_by` edits reversible in place (M2-D35). Dependency installs then stay undoable (G-M2-2, complete installs, undone together), and undo stays trustworthy (G-M2-7). C4.1 and C6 are the only producers of these edits, and both wait for this bead.

## Technical Approach

**1. The history op field.** In `src/state/history.rs`, `HistoryOp` gains an optional, additive `edit`:

```rust
#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
pub edit: Option<HistoryEdit>,

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum HistoryEdit { RequiredByAdd(String), RequiredByRemove(String) }
```

On the wire, an op is `{"op":"record","folder":"BigWigs","addon":"BigWigs","edit":{"required_by_add":"LittleWigs"}}` or `{"required_by_remove": …}`. Ops without an edit serialise exactly as today. The history line format stays `schema_version` 1.0 under M2-D36: never bump an existing state file's version for an additive optional field. `store.rs` treats any newer `(major, minor)` as Newer and refuses to write it, so a bump would lock older binaries out. `HistoryOp` has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so M1 binaries ignore `edit`. Update every `HistoryOp` literal (`tx.rs` `history_ops`, `undo.rs`, tests) with `edit: None`.

**2. Emitting it** (`history_ops` in `src/engine/tx.rs`):
- A `Records` work whose edits are **only** `AddRequiredBy`/`RemoveRequiredBy` emits one `record` op per (folder of the addon, edit), each with `edit` set (`required_by_add` / `required_by_remove`, carrying the requester's name).
- An addon with any other change in the same transaction emits ops without `edit` and keeps snapshot-restore semantics. Other changes are a folder change, or a pin, channel, reason, repoint or adopt edit folded into the same work. Those are deliberate acts on that addon, reverted as one; per M2-D35 they keep snapshot restore and normal conflict detection.

So the ops of one addon in one transaction either all carry `edit` or none do.

**3. Undo** (`src/engine/undo.rs`). Ops carrying `edit` are handled apart from every other op:
- **Conflicts.** `check_conflicts` builds `keys` only from reverted ops **without** `edit`, and ignores later transactions' ops **with** `edit`.
- **Folders.** `FolderPlan::inverse` skips them: no swap, no policy op, not in `touched`, no history op from the folder loop. `FolderPlan::record_only` skips them too, so a SavedVariables follow-up does not claim D's folders.
- **Records.** `restored_state` leaves them out of `direct`. Because they are not in `touched`, D's files-index entries are never rewritten. **This exclusion is what keeps D's index intact**: without it, undoing the LittleWigs install would roll BigWigs' files index back to its pre-update entries.
- **Inverse edit.** For each distinct `(addon, edit)` among the reverted ops, newest first, apply the inverse to that addon's record in the undo's resulting record, **when the addon is still recorded** (otherwise skip it):
  - `required_by_add: R` → remove R;
  - `required_by_remove: R` → add R back, sorted and de-duplicated by `TargetRecord::addon_key`.
- **The undo's own ops.** One `record` op per (folder named by the reverted ops, inverse edit), carrying the **inverse** `edit`. A later undo of the dependency then sees no spurious conflict, and an undo of this undo re-applies the original edit.
- **The undo's `changes`.** One `Change { kind: edit, fields: ["required_by"], folders.recorded }` per addon edited in place, from/to its current version.
- **Stale names.** Whenever a record is restored from a snapshot (direct addons, and previous owners given folders back), drop every `required_by` name that is no longer recorded on the target in the undo's resulting record. Example: undoing D's update after R was undone must not bring R back into D.

**4. Unchanged.** Pin, channel, reason, repoint and adopt edits keep snapshot restore and normal conflict detection. The journal needs nothing new: the undo's record and history ride in its commit payload as computed, and roll forward idempotently.

**Who produces these edits:**
- C4.1 emits `AddRequiredBy` when a required dependency is satisfied by a managed record or by another work in the same transaction.
- C6 emits `RemoveRequiredBy` on `remove` and on an update that drops a dependency.

After this bead lands, both may ship.

**Files:** `src/state/history.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs` (`history_ops`), `src/engine/undo.rs` (`check_conflicts`, `FolderPlan::inverse`, `FolderPlan::record_only`, `restored_state`), `src/app/history.rs` (`-v` ops show `edit`; counts unchanged), `src/engine/journal.rs` (literals in tests only), `src/engine/testing.rs` (helpers).

## Acceptance Criteria

The scenario runs through the engine API with an explicit `Edit(AddRequiredBy)`; no CLI command emits one yet. Given D installed (explicit):
- tx1 = `[Install R, Edit { addon: D, edit: AddRequiredBy("R") }]`. tx1's history holds `add` ops for R's folders and `record` ops on D's folders with `edit: {"required_by_add": "R"}`.
- tx2 updates D to v2.
- `undo tx1` succeeds with no `undo_conflict`:
  - R's folders and record are gone;
  - D keeps its v2 release, folders and record, minus R in `required_by`;
  - **D's files-index entries are byte-identical** across the undo;
  - the undo's history holds `remove` ops for R's folders and `record` ops on D's folders with `edit: {"required_by_remove": "R"}`.
- A following `undo tx2` succeeds: D is back at v1, and R is not in its `required_by`, because the stale name was dropped.

The remaining criteria:
- An undo of the undo of tx1 re-adds R, and R again in D's `required_by`.
- A transaction removing R with `RemoveRequiredBy("R")` on D is undone with R restored and D's `required_by` exactly as before.
- `check_conflicts` ignores ops carrying `edit`, both in the reverted transaction and in later ones.
- A records-only work on D that combines `SetPinned` with `AddRequiredBy` writes ops without `edit` and undoes by snapshot restore.
- History lines without `edit` (M1 lines and A4.1 lines) parse, render and undo exactly as before. The existing undo, history and crash suites pass unchanged, and the history line `schema_version` stays 1.0.

## Test Plan

- **Unit (`src/state/history.rs`):** serde round trip with and without `edit`; an M1 line parses; the JSON shape of both variants.
- **Unit (`src/engine/undo.rs`, `TxScene`):**
  - the acceptance scenario, comparing D's serialised `FolderIndex` entries before and after the undo;
  - undo of the undo;
  - the remove-plus-`RemoveRequiredBy` undo;
  - stale-name dropping;
  - the mixed pin + `required_by` case;
  - `check_conflicts` over synthetic histories containing edit ops on both sides.
- **Unit (`src/engine/tx.rs`):** `history_ops` emits `edit` only for `required_by`-only works.
- **E2E:** `history -v --json` shows `ops[].edit` for a line written through the engine API.

## Considerations

- **Exclude edit ops from `touched`, not only from `direct`.** Missing the `touched` exclusion silently rolls the dependency's files index back. That is the bug the index-identity criterion catches.
- An M1 binary would read edit ops as plain `record` ops: snapshot restore plus conflicts. That is safe, since M1 cannot produce them, and it is what the history format promised.
- Several `required_by` edits on one addon in one transaction give one op per (folder, edit). Undo applies each distinct inverse once.
- Names compare by `TargetRecord::addon_key` (lowercase), as record keys do.
- Hot spots: `src/engine/undo.rs` is also edited by A12 (run-level undo) and E1 (undo's index source); `src/engine/tx.rs` and `src/engine/plan.rs` by A5, C4.x and others. Rebase before each gate run.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1` (Records-only engine work): defines `AddRequiredBy`/`RemoveRequiredBy`, the `Records` work and the `record` history ops this bead annotates.

Unblocks:
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (Dependency rounds on install): emits `required_by_add` edits when a dependency is satisfied by a managed record. Without this bead those installs could not be undone after the dependency updates.
- C6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.6` (Dependency bookkeeping on update and remove; orphans): emits `required_by_remove` edits, and its "undoing the remove restores `required_by` exactly" depends on the in-place inverse.
acceptance_criteria: Through the engine API, installing R with Edit(AddRequiredBy("R")) on an installed D writes record ops on D's folders carrying edit {"required_by_add": "R"}; after updating D, undoing R's install succeeds without undo_conflict, removes R, keeps D's updated release, folders and record minus R in required_by, leaves D's files-index entries byte-identical, and records record ops with the inverse edit; a following undo of D's update succeeds and does not bring R back (stale required_by names are dropped on snapshot restore); undoing that undo re-adds R to D; undoing a remove of R that carried RemoveRequiredBy("R") on D restores required_by exactly; check_conflicts ignores ops carrying edit on both sides; ops carrying edit are excluded from undo's direct set, touched folders and index changes; an addon with any non-required_by change in the transaction keeps edit-free ops and snapshot-restore undo; history lines without edit parse and undo as before, the history schema_version stays 1.0, and existing undo, history and crash suites pass unchanged
close_reason: Reversible required_by edits landed

**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Shared dependencies make records point at each other. With plain snapshot-restore undo, one ordinary sequence breaks undo: install LittleWigs, which marks BigWigs as required by it, then update BigWigs, then try to undo LittleWigs. Either the undo is refused forever (`undo_conflict` on BigWigs' folders), or it rolls BigWigs' record and files index back to a release that is no longer on disk. Both would make `undo`, the feature that makes agent autonomy safe, untrustworthy as soon as dependencies exist. This bead keeps dependency installs (G-M2-2) undoable without touching the dependency's own state, which the thesis of a safe, undoable sole authority requires.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D35:** `required_by` edits are recorded as history ops with an `edit` field. Undo reverses them in place on the current record, and conflict detection ignores them.
  - Why: otherwise updating a dependency makes its requester's install un-undoable, and a snapshot restore would roll the dependency's record back under new folders.
  - Rejected: snapshot restore for every records-only change, which is the M1 behaviour A4.1 leaves in place for `required_by` until this bead.
- **M2-D36:** never bump an existing state file's `schema_version` for an additive optional field. `store.rs` treats any newer `(major, minor)` as Newer and refuses to write it, so a bump would lock older binaries out and wedge journal recovery. `HistoryOp.edit` is therefore optional, and the history line format stays 1.0. Rejected: bumping the format.
- **Review-round fix, `required_by` undo semantics** (the plan's third, consistency review pass): ops carrying `edit` are excluded from undo's `direct` set, from its `touched` folders **and** from its index changes. The plan names `undo.rs:636-647` (every op pushed into `touched`) and `undo.rs:840-846` (old index entries written back for touched folders). The undo writes its own op with the inverse `edit`, and stale `required_by` names are dropped on snapshot restore.
- **Decided while splitting, recorded here:**
  - Ops of one addon in one transaction either all carry `edit` or none do. Any non-`required_by` change on that addon (a folder change, or a folded pin, channel, reason, repoint or adopt edit) keeps snapshot-restore semantics.
  - Several `required_by` edits give one op per (folder, edit), and undo applies each distinct inverse once.
  - The undo reports an `edit` change with `fields: ["required_by"]` for each addon edited in place.
  - `FolderPlan::record_only` (the SavedVariables follow-up) also skips edit ops.

**Facts verified during planning** (at `e902d36`):
- `check_conflicts` compares the folder keys of every op (`src/engine/undo.rs:507-555`).

title: Record-only differences become records-only transactions (pin, promote to explicit, SetChannel)
description:
## Background

A3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.3`) carries an installed addon's `pinned`, `channel` and `reason` through `carry_over`. Some requests then choose the installed release yet change the record: `install X --version <installed>` (pin), `update X --channel beta` when the newest beta is installed, `install <a dependency>` (promote to explicit), and `sync` converging a channel or pin. The planner returns "unchanged" whenever the chosen release equals the record's and every folder is present: `src/engine/plan.rs:659-667`, and under the lock `rejudge` at `plan.rs:428-439` (line numbers as of `e902d36`; symbol names are what matter). A3 detects the difference but, until this bead, reports `unchanged` with a `-v` note. So the intent is lost, and `sync` never converges because it sees the same channel difference on every run.

A4.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1`) supplies the records-only `Records` work, guards and kind rules. This bead connects the two. It serves G-M2-1 (pins and channels give control over updates) and G-M2-5 (`sync` converges and its re-run is a no-op).

## Technical Approach

**The rule (from the record carry-over design).** When the chosen release equals the record's and all its folders are present, but the carried-over `pinned`, `channel` or `reason` differs from the record, the planner emits a `Records` work with those edits instead of returning unchanged:
- one `SetPinned`, `SetChannel` or `SetReason` per differing field;
- `before` = the record;
- `after` = the record with the edits applied;
- guard "still recorded with the same `release_id`" (A4.1's guard for those three edits);
- `Change { kind: edit, fields }`, with `folders.recorded` = the addon's folders and from/to = the installed version.

Its kind is **`pin` if only `pinned` changed, otherwise the request's kind**. A4.1's `target_kind` rules already give exactly that: rule 3 makes pinned-only edits `pin`, and rule 4 gives edit-only changes the target's `default_kind`. That is `install` for install, `update` for update, and `sync` under sync's override. In a mix with folder changes, the edit is ignored for the kind.

Apply it in both places that return unchanged:
- **Plan time:** the no-op check in `TargetPlanner::install` (`plan.rs:659-667`).
- **Under the lock:** `rejudge`'s no-op arm (`plan.rs:430-439`). A Folders work whose release a concurrent transaction already installed must still record its intent. Otherwise an `install X --version V` racing an unpinned install of V would lose the pin. Per the carry-over design, the rules run again under the lock against the current record.

It also covers A3's rule that **a pin intent never moves the release by itself**. `Pin`/`Unpin` with no `version` on an installed addon keeps the installed release, reaches this point, and becomes a `SetPinned` work.

A repeat request finds no difference and stays `unchanged`, with no transaction.

**Cases:** `install X --version <installed>` on an unpinned X → a `pin`-kind transaction (same for `pin X --version <installed>` once B7 exists). `install <current dependency>` → an `install`-kind `SetReason(Explicit)`; promoted addons are never orphans (C6). `install X --channel beta` with the newest beta installed → an `install`-kind `SetChannel`; under `update --channel` the kind is `update`, under sync `sync`.

**Install's output** keeps its M1 shape. A records-only change maps to an item `status` from A6's multi-target vocabulary: `pinned` (only `pinned` changed, to true), `unpinned` (to false; unreachable through `install` today), otherwise `edited`. Add these to install's `ItemStatus` additively, or reuse A6's enum if it exists. `data.kind` may now be `pin`. `from_version` and `to_version` are both the installed version, and `folders.recorded` lists the addon's folders. The human line names the change (`retail: pinned Foo at 1.2 (tx …)`), and the undo hint is emitted as for any commit.

**Files:** `src/engine/plan.rs` (both no-op sites), `src/app/install.rs` (item status mapping and human line), `tests/install.rs`, `tests/plan.rs`, install snapshots if the shape example changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `install X --version <installed>` on an unpinned X writes a `pin`-kind transaction with `record` ops that sets `pinned: true`. The item status is `pinned`, folders are byte-identical, and `undo` unpins it.
- `install X --version <installed>` on an already pinned X is `unchanged` with no transaction.
- `install <current dependency>` writes an `install`-kind records-only transaction promoting the record to `reason: explicit`. The release and folders are unchanged.
- `install X --channel beta`, when the newest beta is the installed release, writes a records-only `SetChannel` edit (item `edited`, `fields: ["channel"]`). An immediate repeat makes no change and creates no transaction.
- A `Pin` intent with no version on an installed addon never changes the release.
- Under the lock, an install whose release was installed meanwhile by a concurrent transaction still records its pin, channel or reason difference as a records-only edit.
- Install's JSON changes only additively: the new status values and `kind: pin`. Existing install tests pass.

## Test Plan

- **E2E (`tests/install.rs`):** each acceptance case with `gh_release` fixtures (`tests/common/http.rs`, `Home::scenario`). Set the dependency record up with an engine-API `Edit(SetReason(Dependency))` or by writing it. For the channel case, use a beta REST release-list fixture (as `tests/sources_github_rest.rs` builds them), or an `--file` install with `--channel beta` over the same zip. Assert history `kind` and `ops`, record fields, AddOns tree hashes, and a repeat that commits nothing.
- **Unit (`plan.rs`):** the record-only-difference function over every combination of differing fields → expected edits and fields. The kind for pinned-only versus mixed edits.
- **Concurrency (in process, `TxScene`):** an install of V paused with `failpoint::with_spec("engine.stage.synced=sleep:400", …)` while another thread installs V unpinned. The paused one commits a `pin` edit.
- If B6 has landed: `update X --channel beta` with the newest beta installed records `SetChannel` under kind `update`.

## Considerations

- Only `pinned`, `channel` and `reason` count as record-only differences. `required_by` is never carried by a request (A3's table), and version or `release_id` differences are real updates.
- The no-op check keeps M1's rule that every recorded folder must be present. A pinned addon with a missing folder is a reinstall case (B9), not an edit.
- B6 (update) does not depend on this bead. Whichever lands second wires `update --channel` to the edit (B6 reports `unchanged` until then).
- Hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x). `src/app/install.rs` is also changed by A6, B9 and C5.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1` (Records-only engine work): provides the `Records` work, the same-release guard, `ChangeKind::Edit` with `fields`, and the `target_kind` rules that make pinned-only edits `pin`.

Unblocks:
- B7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` (pin and unpin): `pin <addon> --version V` with V already installed must become a records-only `pin` transaction, which this conversion provides.
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): a channel difference is planned as an install on the new channel. It becomes a `SetChannel` edit here when that release is installed, which is what makes the next `sync` a zero-request no-op.
acceptance_criteria: When the chosen release equals the record's and all folders are present but carried-over pinned, channel or reason differ, the planner emits a records-only Records work with SetPinned/SetChannel/SetReason edits instead of unchanged, at plan time and under the lock in rejudge; its kind is pin when only pinned changed, otherwise the request's kind; install X --version <installed> on an unpinned X writes a pin-kind transaction with record ops, item status pinned, folders byte-identical, and undo unpins it; the same request on a pinned X is unchanged with no transaction; install <current dependency> writes an install-kind edit promoting it to explicit; install X --channel beta when the newest beta is installed writes a records-only SetChannel edit (item edited, fields [channel]) and an immediate repeat makes no change; a Pin intent without a version never moves the release; an install whose release a concurrent transaction installed meanwhile still records its pin, channel or reason difference; install JSON changes only additively (statuses pinned/unpinned/edited, kind pin)
close_reason: Same-release pin, channel and reason differences commit as records-only transactions at plan time and under the lock; argc gate passes

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Pins exist to protect a working setup, and channels say which line of releases an addon follows. If `pin X --version <installed>` or a channel switch whose newest release is already installed were silently a no-op, the owner's intent would be lost, and `update --all` could later move a "pinned" addon. Without this conversion, `sync` (G-M2-5) would also see the same difference on every run and could never reach its zero-request no-op re-run. Recording these as records-only transactions keeps them journaled, attributed and undoable, consistent with the project's thesis that every mutation is a transaction.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D5:** pin and unpin are records-only transactions of the new kind `pin`; channel changes ride on `install`/`update --channel`.
  - Why: undoable and attributed like every mutation, with no extra `channel` command.
  - Rejected: plain state writes (not undoable), and reusing the `adopt` or `update` kinds (misleading history).
  - Here, pinned-only differences produce kind `pin`, and other differences keep the request's kind.
- **M2-D29:** `install X` of a pinned X is a no-op with `addon_pinned` (A3), and `install X --version V` re-pins.
  - Why: pins protect working setups.
  - Rejected: silently unpinning, which is M1's behaviour.
  - This bead makes the re-pin record itself when V is already installed.
- **Record carry-over design (A3's table):** "Record-only differences are changes, not no-ops", "A pin intent never moves the release by itself", and "The rules run again under the lock". All three are applied here at both no-op sites.
- **Review-round fix, pin-kind derivation:** the kind comes from A4.1's `target_kind`. Rule 3 makes pinned-only edits `pin`, rule 4 gives the request's `default_kind`, and in a mix the edit is ignored for the kind.
- **Decided while splitting, recorded here:**
  - `rejudge`'s no-op arm applies the same conversion, so an install racing a concurrent install of the same release still records its pin, channel or reason.
  - Install items for a records-only change use the A6 status values `pinned`, `unpinned` or `edited`, added to install's item status enum. Install's `data.kind` may be `pin`.
  - These are additive wire values for H6 to record.

**Facts verified during planning** (at `e902d36`):
- The plan-time no-op check is `src/engine/plan.rs:659-667`, and the under-lock one is `rejudge` `plan.rs:430-439`. Both return unchanged on an equal `release_id` with all folders present.
- Install's item status enum (`src/app/install.rs:129-134`) is `installed|updated|unchanged|failed`, mapped from `ChangeKind` at `install.rs:809`.
- A `--file` candidate's `release_id` is `<ref>@sha256:<hex>` of the zip (`plan.rs:1252`). That is why the same zip with `--channel beta` is a fixture-free way to exercise the rule.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A conversion that fires too eagerly would create spurious transactions. Only `pinned`, `channel` and `reason` count, and the "repeat makes no change" criteria guard idempotency.
- Folding into a `Folders` work is not involved: these cases have no folder work by definition.
- The plan rates the engine changes **medium-high** confidence. This bead is small, built on A4.1's tested path.

**Siblings.**
- A4.1 provides the `Records` work, the same-release guard and the kind rules. This bead adds no engine machinery.
- A4.2 (reversible `required_by` edits) is unrelated: `required_by` is never a record-only difference of a request.
- A4.4 covers crash safety of the records-only path these transactions use.
- B7 and F3.1 wait for this bead. B6 does not; whichever of B6 and this bead lands second adds the `update --channel` test.

title: Records-only crash matrix with the record oracle, and records-only concurrency
description:
## Background

M1 proved its crash invariant with a cross-process matrix. `tests/engine_crash.rs` runs every engine failpoint (`omaddons::engine::FAILPOINTS`) as a real crash (`<name>=abort`: no unwinding, and the kernel releases the flocks) for `Op::{Install, FirstInstall, Update, Remove}`. After each crash it checks:
- every folder is wholly old or wholly new;
- a reader (`status`) reports `journal_pending` and writes nothing;
- the next locking command recovers (`journal_recovered`);
- all folders sit on one side consistent with the generation and history, and the lock file keeps its inode;
- at least 10 failpoints actually crashed.

Its oracle decides whether the transaction committed by comparing folder tree hashes with a reference run. A records-only transaction (A4.1, `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1`) never changes a folder, so that oracle cannot tell a committed pin from a rolled-back one. `tests/engine_concurrency.rs` likewise covers only folder-changing installs.

Records-only transactions are about to carry user intent: pins (B7), adopt (E5.2), sync edits (F3.1) and dependency bookkeeping (C4.1, C6). The crash and concurrency evidence must exist for them as it does for installs. That is G-M2-7 (no regression of M1 guarantees) and the A4 design's crash-safety requirement.

Line numbers are as of `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

**1. The record oracle** (for every records-only op). After an abort at failpoint F and the recovery command:
- the target record contains the transaction's edits **if and only if** `history.jsonl` contains the transaction;
- the generation equals the old value plus that (plus one for the recovery command's own commit);
- every AddOns folder is byte-identical to before, because records-only transactions never touch folders.

**2. Driving a pin before `pin` exists.** B7 adds the `pin` command later, so `Op::Pin` goes through a test-only `Edit` request into the engine API, in a child process that can really abort. Follow the `child_holder` pattern in `tests/fsx_lock.rs` (`spawn_holder`):
- Add an `#[ignore]` helper test in `tests/engine_crash.rs`, for example `child_engine_edit`. It does nothing unless its own environment variable is set, named like `OMADDONS_LOCK_TEST_HOME` in `fsx_lock.rs`. It is read only by the test binary, never by `omaddons`.
- When set, the helper loads `World::load()` from the same isolated environment `Home` gives CLI children, and selects target `retail`. It builds an `EngineCtx` as `src/app/engine.rs` `Engine::ctx` does, offline, then calls `omaddons::engine::run` with `TxRequest { kind: Some(TxKind::Pin), targets: [TxTarget { changes: [Edit { addon: "Foo", edit: RecordEdit::SetPinned(true) }], default_kind: TxKind::Install, … }], … }`. It exits 0 when the transaction committed.
- Add `Scene::run_engine_edit(failpoints) -> Run` in `tests/common/engine.rs`. It spawns `std::env::current_exe()` with `child_engine_edit --exact --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`, the `Home` environment (`env.apply_to`) and `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`. A signal death reports code -1, as `Home::exec_with` does.
- Once B7 lands, `Op::Pin` may switch to the `pin` CLI. H2 makes that switch only if B7 is already on `main` when H2 runs; neither this bead nor H2 waits for B7, so the engine-API child must keep working on its own.

**3. New ops in `tests/engine_crash.rs`:**
- **`Op::Pin`.** Prepare: `s.install("gh:o/foo", "v1")`. Command: the child edit. Committed means Foo's record has `pinned: true` and the same `release_id`, and history gained a `pin` line whose `ops` are only `record` ops on `Foo` and `FooOld`.
- **`Op::Forget`.** Prepare: install v1, then delete `Foo` and `FooOld` from AddOns in the test (test code may use `std::fs`). Command: `remove Foo -t retail --offline --json`. Committed means Foo's record and its files-index entries are gone, and history gained a `remove` line with only `record` ops. The folders stay absent either way.

**4. `record_matrix(op)`,** alongside the existing `matrix(op)`, for each failpoint in `FAILPOINTS`:
1. Take a fresh `Scene` and prepare it.
2. Capture the folder tree hashes (absent included), generation, history, Foo's record and index entries, and the lock inode.
3. Run the command with `<F>=abort`. Exit -1 counts as a crash; anything else must exit 0.
4. Reader check, as today: `status --json` reports `journal_pending` iff a journal is unfinished, the state and client trees are unchanged, and the journals are untouched.
5. Recovery: `install gh:o/bar --file bar.zip`. It warns `journal_recovered` iff a journal was pending and leaves no journals.
6. Apply the record oracle. `committed` = history holds a new `op.kind()` line before Bar's. The edit is present iff `committed`. The generation is old + `committed` + 1. Foo's and FooOld's trees equal the old ones. AddOns holds nothing but `Foo`, `FooOld` and `Bar`. The lock inode is unchanged.
7. Print the crashed failpoints as `matrix` does, and assert at least 10.

On the records-only path the expected crashing failpoints are these; verify them by running and record the actual list in the close comment:

`engine.plan.fetched`, `engine.plan.done`, `engine.lock.acquired`, `engine.recovered`, `engine.registered`, `engine.revalidated`, `engine.journal.prepared`, `engine.snapshot.sv`, `engine.snapshot.state`, `engine.swap.after_exchange`, `engine.swapped`, `engine.record.written`, `engine.history.appended`, `engine.committed`, `engine.unlocked`, `engine.cleanup.done`, `engine.retention`.

Staging, `engine.swap.before_rename`, `engine.addons_dir.created`, `engine.plan.downloaded` and `engine.recover.step` are off the path. Extend `the_reference_runs_change_what_they_should` with Pin (pinned, folders unchanged) and Forget (record gone, folders still absent).

**5. Concurrency (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs`):** a records-only transaction racing an install of a **different** addon on the same target. Both orders, real processes, `sleep` failpoints with generous margins, assertions on final state only (the file's own rule):
- **Pin sleeps.** Start the pin child with `engine.plan.done=sleep:1500`. Poll until its in-flight lock appears under `<state>/omaddons/inflight/`. Run `install gh:o/bar --file bar.zip -t retail --offline` to completion, then wait for the child.
- **Install sleeps.** Spawn the Bar install with `engine.stage.synced=sleep:1500`, poll until its stage dir exists under `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/stage/`, run the pin child to completion, then wait for the install.
- **In both:** both exit 0. Foo is pinned with an unchanged `release_id`. Bar is installed. The generation is +2. History holds one `pin` and one `install` line (order not asserted). Foo's and FooOld's trees are unchanged, and no journal is left.

**Files:** `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/common/engine.rs`, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `crash_matrix_pin` and `crash_matrix_forget` pass. Each crashes at 10 or more failpoints, and the record oracle holds at every failpoint:
  - edit present iff the history line exists;
  - generation consistent;
  - every AddOns folder byte-identical;
  - the reader reports `journal_pending` iff unfinished and writes nothing;
  - recovery reports `journal_recovered` and leaves no journal;
  - the lock inode is unchanged.
- The committed `pin` and `remove` lines carry only `record` ops.
- The four existing matrices and `the_reference_runs_change_what_they_should` pass, extended but otherwise unchanged.
- The records-only race passes in both orders: both transactions commit, and neither is `plan_stale`.
- The existing concurrency tests pass unchanged, including the lock-hold budget.

## Test Plan

These are the test suites themselves:
- `cargo test --test engine_crash` (debug build: failpoints are debug-only, DEC-7);
- `cargo test --test engine_concurrency`;
- then `argc gate`.

On failure, log the journals, history lines, records and tree hashes, as the existing `context` closure does.

## Considerations

- The child helper must not change production code. If building an `EngineCtx` from a test needs a small public constructor, add it to `src/app/engine.rs` with a doc comment, and do not add a hidden CLI command (DEC-1: no stubs).
- Keep each new matrix under about 5 s, which H2 also asks of its ops. Scenes are tempdirs, and records-only runs do no staging.
- Do not assert interleavings, only final state. Polls time out at 10 s, as `support::poll` does.

- The plan's collision hot spots do not include `tests/engine_crash.rs`, but H2 edits it later. Keep helpers in `tests/common/engine.rs`.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1` (Records-only engine work): provides the records-only commit path, `Edit(SetPinned)`, `TxKind::Pin`, and remove's `Forget` conversion that these matrices crash.

Unblocks:
- H2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` (Crash and concurrency coverage for M2 transactions): builds `Op::Adopt` and the mixed-transaction checks on the record oracle, the child helper and `Op::Pin` added here.

**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** M1 earned trust by proving, at every failpoint and with real crashes, that a transaction is all or nothing. M2's records-only transactions carry intent the owner cares about: a pin that protects a working setup, an adoption, a sync, dependency bookkeeping. That same proof has to cover them before user-facing commands rely on them in the field. The folder oracle cannot see a records-only transaction, because folders never change, so a new oracle is needed. This bead keeps G-M2-7 (no regression of M1 guarantees) true for the new transaction shape, and it gives H2 the oracle and harness it builds the rest of M2's crash coverage on.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D6:** records-only work, the per-target working view and folder handover are first-class in the engine. Adopt, pin, dependency bookkeeping, sync and M4's repair all need them, so there is one implementation and **one crash matrix**. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature, each of which would need its own unproven crash story.
- **The record oracle** comes from the plan's testing strategy. After an abort at F and recovery, the record holds the edits iff `history.jsonl` holds the transaction, the generation matches, and every AddOns folder is byte-identical. Mixed transactions (H2) add the folder oracle per folder on top.
- **Decided while splitting, recorded here:**
  - The plan's single A4 task ran the crash matrix itself. The split moves it here, and A4.1 keeps an in-process `error` matrix so `main` has crash evidence in between.
  - `Op::Pin` runs through the engine API in a child process that re-executes the test binary. That follows the existing `child_holder` pattern in `tests/fsx_lock.rs`, so no production code or hidden CLI command is added before B7 (DEC-1: no stubs).
  - `Op::Forget` uses the real `remove` CLI, because A4.1 turns an all-absent remove into a `Forget` work.

**Facts verified during planning** (at `e902d36`):
- `tests/engine_crash.rs` loops over `FAILPOINTS` with `=abort`. It asserts ≥10 crashes per op, reader silence, recovery with `journal_recovered`, an empty journal dir and lock-inode stability, and it decides commit by folder hashes. That last check does not work for records-only work.
- `Home::exec_with` reports a signal death as code -1, and `Home.env.apply_to` gives a child the isolated environment.
- With zero swap ops, `swap()` still writes `swapped` and hits `engine.swapped` (`src/engine/swap.rs:338-339`).
- `engine.swap.after_exchange` is hit outside the per-op loop.
- Staging failpoints are skipped, because `stage_all` stages only works with an archive (`src/engine/tx.rs:377-395`).

That is why about 17 failpoints are expected on the path.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Flaky races are avoided by asserting final state only, with generous sleeps and 10 s polls, as the M1 suite does.
- The child helper is guarded by its own environment variable, so a normal `cargo test` skips it (`#[ignore]`).
- If an `EngineCtx` cannot be built from a test without a small public constructor, add one with a doc comment in `src/app/engine.rs`, never a CLI command.
- The plan rates the engine work **medium-high** confidence. The new record oracle is one of its named mitigations.

**Siblings.**
- A4.1 provides the path, the in-process error matrix and the guard tests.
- A4.2 and A4.3 add no new commit paths, so their transactions are covered by this matrix's shape. H2 adds `Op::Adopt` and the mixed ops later.

title: Per-target working view, folder handover and intra-transaction claims
description:
## Background

`TargetPlanner` judges every addon against one fixed snapshot of the record and the inventory. Line numbers below are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

- `plan()` loads each target's record (`src/engine/plan.rs:271`) and inventory (`:311`) once. `TargetPlanner { record, live, … }` (`:576-585`) hands every work the same pair. `judge()` calls `ownership::check(changes, self.live, addon, force, argv)` (`:901-956`).
- Two works in one transaction that touch the same folder are therefore **not detected at plan time**. They collide later:
  - at staging: `stage_all` stages every work into one stage dir (`src/engine/tx.rs:377-395`), and the second `create_dir` hits an existing folder;
  - or at swap: `absent()` (`src/engine/swap.rs:476-490`) fails with `plan_stale`.

  `plan_stale` is **retryable**, so an agent would retry it forever.
- A folder handed from one addon to another in one transaction cannot work as a separate remove plus add:
  - `swap()` runs every add and replace before any remove (`swap.rs:268-336`: step 1 adds and replaces, step 3 removes), so the add's `absent()` check fails;
  - a history line holding `remove Old` plus `add Old` cannot be undone, because `FolderPlan::inverse` refuses a `remove` whose folder is live (`src/engine/undo.rs:681-695`).
- `next_record` inserts each work's full record and the last one wins (`tx.rs:654-688`), so two works for one addon roll the record back to whichever was computed last.
- Under the lock, `locked()` calls `rejudge` once per work (`tx.rs:462-478`). Each call reloads the record and inventory (`plan.rs:417-418`), so one work never sees another's effect.

M1 never had two addons in one transaction claiming overlapping folders. M2 does, through:
- dependencies (C4.1: a requester and its dependency);
- `sync` (F3.1: installs, removes and edits on one target);
- `update` (a new release that starts shipping a folder another managed addon drops);
- adopt groups (E5.2).

This serves G-M2-2 (a dependency installs in the same transaction as its requester), G-M2-5 (`sync` applies a mixed change set at once) and G-M2-7 (no retryable error that can never succeed). It implements **M2-D6** (below).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/engine/plan.rs` (`WorkingView`, two-phase target planning, duplicates, handover), `src/engine/tx.rs` (`locked()` replays in order over one fresh view; `next_record` skips `degraded` for handovers), `src/engine/ownership.rs` (`Transfer.handover`, within-transaction conflicts), `src/app/install.rs` (the duplicate item), `tests/plan.rs`, `tests/install.rs`, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, `tests/engine_undo.rs`.

**The design (authoritative).**

The target planner keeps a **working view**: the snapshot record plus every change already planned in this target, and the live inventory plus the folders planned to appear or disappear:

```rust
struct WorkingView { record: TargetRecord, live: LiveView }   // cloned from the snapshot per target
struct LiveView {
    present: BTreeMap<String /* folder key */, FolderEntry>,
    planned_add: BTreeSet<String>,
    planned_remove: BTreeSet<String>,
}
```

Keep its API small: `claim`, `release`, `owner_of`, `apply(work)`. After each planned work, `apply` its effect:
- record upsert or removal;
- folders added or removed;
- records-only edits: A4.1's `Records { before, after, … }` works. An adopt work claims its folders, and `Forget` releases the record but no folder, because its folders are already absent.

`Records.after` is computed from the working view. This replaces A4.1's interim rule (the snapshot plus works already planned in this target).

**Order.** Works are planned deterministically: explicit requests in argument order, then dependency rounds in resolution order (C4.1 supplies the rounds).

**Ownership is judged only after every round-0 work on the target has been inspected.** Planning a target becomes two passes.
1. Resolve, select, download, inspect and verify every round-0 request in argument order, without judging ownership.
2. **Release** every folder whose current owner has a work in this transaction that omits it: an update dropping it (`build_install`'s `dropped`, `plan.rs:791-806`), or a remove. Do this before any claim is judged, whatever the argument order.

`install B A`, a bare `update` where the claiming addon sorts first, and a `sync` whose install comes before the update all behave the same. Each work is then judged against the working view.

- **Conflicts.** A folder claimed by an earlier work in the same transaction is "owned by addon N (in this transaction)". The later work fails with `ownership_conflict`:
  - `details.within_transaction: true`, with the existing per-folder entries (`details.folders[].owner` = the earlier addon);
  - a message naming both addons.

  **`--force` does not override an intra-transaction conflict.** Nothing on disk could be degraded to make room; the two releases simply disagree. Fix: a text that does not start with `omaddons` (for example "choose one of A and B: both ship Shared"), so it needs no `TEXT_FIXES` entry. Conflicts with folders owned by addons that have no work here keep M1's rules, including `--force` transfers.
- **Handover.** Suppose a work releases a folder and another work claims it. The pair is **merged into one `SwapOp::Replace` owned by the claiming work, plus a `Transfer { folder, from, to, handover: true }`**, and the releasing work's `Remove` op for that folder is dropped (from its swap ops, its `PlannedOp`s and its `FolderSummary.removed`).
  - The claimant's summary lists the folder under `replaced`.
  - This reuses the existing `--force` transfer path (`ownership.rs:221-246`; `next_record`'s transfer handling, `tx.rs:675-679`).
  - History records a single `replace` op, owned by the claimant, which undo already reverses, transfers included (`undo.rs:817-837` puts lost folders back on their previous owner).
  - **A handover transfer is marked `handover: true`.** It sets no `degraded` state and raises no `ownership_transferred` warning, because the previous owner's new release dropped the folder legitimately. Today `next_record` marks a transfer's previous owner degraded (`tx.rs:680-684`); that path now applies only to `--force` takeovers.
  - The merged op is judged by the running policy as a `ReplaceFolder` (`running::evaluate`, unchanged).
  - `Transfer` (`ownership.rs:66-71`) derives no `Serialize` and does not reach the journal or history, so `handover` is an internal field unless it later reaches a serialised shape.
  - **Why not a separate remove and add:** `swap()` would fail the add's `absent()` check, and the resulting history line could never be undone (both explained above).
- **Duplicates.** Two requests for the same ref (by `Ref` identity) collapse into one work, the first in order. The duplicate item is `skipped` with `skip_reason: duplicate`.
  - Install's item (`InstallItem`, `src/app/install.rs:109-125`) gains the additive status `skipped` and the field `skip_reason`. If A6 has landed, reuse its `SkipReason`; otherwise add the enum with `duplicate`.
  - The plan also asks for `duplicate_of` (the first request's string) under `details`. Install items and A6's items have no `details` object; `ItemError` carries none. Decided: the item carries `duplicate_of` as an optional key, serialised only on duplicates, and its `error` stays `null`. A skip is not a failure and does not make the run partial. If A6 has landed, add the same optional key to its `ItemResult` and map the collapse to `skipped/duplicate` in its `build` (A6 states the same rule: whichever of A5 and A6 lands second does it).
- **Folded edits.** An edit to an addon that already has a work folds into that work's carry-over (A4.1's one-work-per-addon rule), looked up through the working view.

**Under the lock.** `rejudge` replays the **planned works** (dependency works included) in the same order against **one fresh working view**, built from the current record and inventory, so a concurrent transaction is detected the same way.
- Change `locked()` to build the view once and pass it to each `rejudge`. The release pass runs first, then the claims, applying each result.
- The rules for the result are unchanged:
  - a refusal with the generation changed is `plan_stale`, with `details.cause`;
  - a work that is no longer needed is dropped.
- Rejudge is offline: it never resolves new dependencies and never fetches. Dropping a dependency work whose every requester dropped out belongs to C4.1, which introduces dependency works. The replay must keep each work's identity and order so C4.1 can add that rule.

**Output order.** The plan's `changes`, `ops` and `work` follow planning order, so `--dry-run` output is deterministic.

**M2-D6 (decision).** Records-only work, a per-target working view and folder handover are first-class in the engine. Why: adopt, pin, dependency bookkeeping, sync and the M4 doctor's repair transactions all need them, so there is one implementation and one crash matrix. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature. A per-target view is the smallest change that makes multi-addon transactions sound. A global claim registry across targets is unnecessary, because folders are per target.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two refs whose archives both contain folder `Shared`, in one `install` command:
  - the second is an item failure `ownership_conflict` with `details.within_transaction: true`, naming both addons;
  - the first commits, and the run is `partial: true`;
  - `--force` gives the same result.
- **Handover.** An update of A that drops folder `Old`, plus an install of B that ships `Old`, in one transaction, commits **in both argument orders**.
  - History holds one `replace` op for `Old`, and B owns it.
  - A stays `state: ok`, and no `ownership_transferred` warning is raised.
  - **Undo** of that transaction restores A (with `Old`) and removes B, byte-for-byte (tree hashes).
- `install a a` (or a catalog name plus its canonical ref) installs once and reports the second item `skipped` with `skip_reason: duplicate` and `duplicate_of`.
- The plan's `changes` order matches the planning order, and repeated `--dry-run` output is byte-identical apart from `meta`.
- A concurrent transaction that lands between plan and lock is detected by the replay. An unrelated install lets both commit. One that takes a folder a planned work claims makes the commit `plan_stale` with `details.cause: ownership_conflict`.
- M1's plan, ownership, install, crash, concurrency and undo suites pass unchanged.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (`src/engine/plan.rs` tests): `WorkingView::apply` for each work kind (install, update, remove, records-only edit, adopt claim, forget); handover detection in both orders; a within-transaction conflict; duplicate collapse by ref identity; two claimants for one released folder (the first gets the handover, the second conflicts).
- **E2E** (`tests/install.rs`, `tests/plan.rs`, synthetic `gh_release` fixtures):
  - `gh:o/a` v1 ships `A` and `Old`, and v2 ships only `A`; `gh:o/b` ships `B` and `Old`. Install a v1, switch to the v2 scenario with `home.scenario(...)`, and run `install gh:o/a gh:o/b` on one home and `install gh:o/b gh:o/a` on another.
  - The `Shared` conflict, with and without `--force`.
  - `install a a`.
  - Dry-run determinism.
- **Undo** (`tests/engine_undo.rs`): undo the handover transaction and compare tree hashes with the pre-transaction trees, and records with the snapshot.
- **Concurrency** (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs`): run the handover command with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.plan.done=sleep:2000`. While it sleeps:
  1. an unrelated install commits, and both transactions commit, with one `replace` op for `Old`;
  2. separately, an install that takes `B`'s folder commits, and the handover command fails `plan_stale` with cause `ownership_conflict`.

  Assert final state only.

## Considerations

- Keep the M1 single-addon path fast. Cloning the record per target is cheap. Do not re-read the inventory per work.
- A releasing work whose only swap op was the handed-over folder (removing A, whose single folder B claims) must still appear in history, or undo cannot restore A's record. A4.1's `history_ops` emits `record` ops only for `Records` works, so this bead extends it: a `Folders` work whose record changed but which has no swap op left after the handover merge emits one `record` op per folder of its previous record (here `Old`, with `addon: A`), so undo's `direct` set includes A and restores its record from the snapshot. Test it.
- Case: a claimant whose spelling of a released folder differs from the live spelling still meets M1's `case_collision` rule. A handover does not relax it.
- B6 documents an interim degradation (a handover across two addons in one `update` fails the second with `ownership_conflict` until this task lands). Remove it by making that case one transaction.
- Collision hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x), `src/engine/tx.rs` and `src/engine/ownership.rs` (E5.3 changes the `unmanaged_folder` fix there). Rebase before each gate run.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- A4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1` (Records-only engine work): the view must apply the `Folders`/`Records` work shapes, folded edits and `Forget` that A4.1 defines, and replaces A4.1's interim `Records.after` computation. A5 does **not** need A4.2's reversible `required_by` history and undo ops: they change only how a committed edit is recorded and reversed, not how planning sees it.

**Unblocks:**
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (Dependency rounds on install): rounds plan into this view, a dependency installed by another work in the same transaction counts as satisfied, and two dependencies shipping one folder must conflict clearly.
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): a sync transaction mixes installs, removes and edits on one target, and must not depend on entry order.
acceptance_criteria: Each target is planned against a WorkingView (record plus planned changes, LiveView present/planned_add/planned_remove) in argument order, and ownership is judged only after every round-0 work is inspected, with folders that an owner's own work omits released first; two refs whose archives both ship folder Shared in one install make the second an item failure ownership_conflict with details.within_transaction true naming both addons, --force does not override it, the first commits and the run is partial; an update of A dropping Old plus an install of B shipping Old commits in both argument orders as one replace op for Old owned by B plus a handover transfer, A stays state ok, no ownership_transferred warning is raised, and undo restores A with Old and removes B byte-for-byte; install a a installs once and reports the duplicate skipped with skip_reason duplicate and duplicate_of; plan changes follow planning order and --dry-run output is deterministic; rejudge replays planned works in order over one fresh working view, so an unrelated concurrent install lets both commit and one taking a claimed folder yields plan_stale with cause ownership_conflict; M1 plan, ownership, install, crash, concurrency and undo suites pass unchanged
