comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead, and how it serves M2.** M1 transactions held one addon, or several that never shared a folder. M2 puts several addons in one transaction as a matter of course: a requester and its dependency (`install littlewigs` brings BigWigs), a `sync` that installs, removes and edits on one client, an `update` whose new release starts shipping a folder another addon just dropped, and adopt groups. Against today's fixed snapshot those collide at staging or at swap with `plan_stale`. That is the worst possible failure for an agent, because it is retryable and never succeeds. The thesis says every mutation is one sound, undoable transaction. The working view makes overlapping claims an explicit, non-retryable item failure, turns a legitimate handover into one `replace` that undo already knows how to reverse, and lets dependency rounds (C4.1) and `sync` (F3.1) plan into a view that already contains the other works.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D6: records-only work, a per-target working view and folder handover are first-class in the engine.** Why: adopt, pin, dependency bookkeeping, sync and the M4 doctor's repair transactions all need them, so there is one implementation and one crash matrix. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature, which would not be journaled, snapshotted or undoable. Also rejected: a global claim registry across targets, which is unnecessary because folders are per target.
- **Handover is a merged `Replace` plus a `Transfer` with `handover: true`**, never a remove plus an add. This was a design blocker in review pass 1: swap order makes the add fail `absent()`, and undo refuses a remove whose folder is live.
- **Order independence** (review pass 3). Releases are computed after every round-0 work is inspected and before any claim is judged, so `install B A`, `install A B` and a sync with any entry order behave the same.
- **No `--force` inside a transaction.** Nothing on disk could be degraded to make room, because the two releases disagree. `--force` keeps its M1 meaning across transactions.
- **Decided in this bead.**
  - `duplicate_of` becomes an optional item key, because install items, A6 items and `ItemError` have no `details` object.
  - The within-transaction conflict's fix is a text that does not start with `omaddons`.
  - Dropping dependency works whose requesters all dropped is left to C4.1, which introduces dependency works; the replay preserves work identity and order so C4.1 can add it.
  - `Transfer.handover` is internal, because `Transfer` is not serialised at `e902d36`.

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`).
- `swap()` runs adds and replaces before removes (`src/engine/swap.rs:268-336`), and `absent()` fails with `plan_stale` (`:476-490`).
- `FolderPlan::inverse` refuses a `remove` whose folder is live (`src/engine/undo.rs:681-695`), and restores lost folders to their previous owners (`:817-837`).
- `ownership::check` builds `Transfer`, `degraded` and the `ownership_transferred` warning in one block (`src/engine/ownership.rs:221-246`). `next_record` applies transfers and degraded (`src/engine/tx.rs:675-684`), and the last record per addon wins (`:661-674`).
- `locked()` rejudges per work, and each `rejudge` reloads record and inventory (`tx.rs:462-478`, `src/engine/plan.rs:417-418`).
- `install` maps items to plan changes by ref (`src/app/install.rs`, item mapping around `:745-850`). Today `install a a` makes two works for one addon.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *A handover fails at swap or becomes un-undoable* (plan risk table: medium likelihood, high impact). Mitigation: reuse the transfer path that undo already reverses; test undo byte-for-byte in both argument orders.
- *Regressing install and remove* through the restructured planner. Mitigation: M1's plan, ownership, crash, concurrency and undo suites are the regression net. H2 adds a `Handover` crash op with the folder oracle (exactly one record owns the folder after recovery).
- *Many agents editing `plan.rs`.* Mitigation: claim with file lists, keep commits small, rebase before each gate run.
- Confidence: medium-high, the plan's level for the engine changes (A4, A5, C4, A12). The code review confirmed that journal, swap and undo behave as this design assumes.

title: Shared multi-target outcome and multi-target commit coverage
description:
## Background

The engine can already commit several targets in one run, but nothing in production has ever done it. `engine::run` (`src/engine/tx.rs:151`) plans every `TxTarget`, then commits them one at a time in key order (the sort at `tx.rs:214-220` is `(key.is_none(), key, target id)`, so unregistered targets come last, in id order). Each target gets its own `commit_target`: its own tx id, in-flight lock, stage dir, lock window, journal, snapshots and history line. A commit error becomes a `PlanFailure` with `ref: None, addon: None` (`tx.rs:235-241`), and targets already committed stay committed.

`install` and `remove` build one `TxTarget` (`src/app/install.rs:406-415`, `src/app/remove.rs:225`), and install's outcome reads `done.outcomes.first()` (`install.rs:423`). The only multi-target run is install's dry-run probe (`install.rs:586-605`), which never commits. The plan rates "the multi-target commit path has never run in production" medium likelihood, high impact. Five M2 commands return per-target results (`update` B6, `sync` F3.1, `adopt --apply` E5.2, `pin`/`unpin` B7, `copy` F4); without one shape and one renderer they drift apart, and agents read `data.targets[].items[].status` from all of them.

A partial-run test needs a failure on exactly one target, which the failpoint grammar cannot express: `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>[=abort|=error|=sleep:<ms>|=panic]` fires on every hit (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:1-55`). In-process tests cannot arm failpoints either: the spec is read once into a process-wide `OnceLock` (`failpoint.rs:95-100`), and Rust 2024 makes `std::env::set_var` unsafe, which `unsafe_code = "forbid"` (`Cargo.toml` `[lints.rust]`) rules out. The thread-local override `with_spec` (`failpoint.rs:116-129`) is `#[cfg(test)]` in a `pub(crate)` module (`src/fsx/mod.rs:5`), and integration tests link the library compiled **without** `cfg(test)`.

This serves the M2 goals "current by default" (update every client with one command, undo it with one) and "no regression of M1 guarantees" (every mutation a transaction, one envelope), and lands the multi-target test before B6 relies on the path.

Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** new `src/app/outcome.rs`; `src/app/mod.rs` (module); `src/app/install.rs` (shared types and renderer); `src/fsx/failpoint.rs` and `src/fsx/mod.rs` (`@N` grammar, `with_spec` for integration tests); new `tests/engine_multi_target.rs`; new snapshots under `tests/snapshots/`.

### The shared multi-target outcome (the whole rule, inlined)

`update`, `sync`, `adopt --apply`, `pin`/`unpin` and `copy` all return per-target transaction results through one data shape and one human renderer:

```json
"dry_run": false,
"run": "01M…",
"targets": [
  {"target": {"id": "retail", "key": "01M…"}, "tx": "01M…", "kind": "update", "no_section": false,
   "items": [{"request": "DBM", "name": "DBM", "ref": "gh:…", "status": "updated", "skip_reason": null, "reason": "explicit",
              "from_version": "12.1.14", "to_version": "12.1.15",
              "folders": {"added": [], "replaced": ["DBM-Core", "…"], "removed": [], "skipped": [], "recorded": []},
              "required_by": [], "error": null}],
   "reload_required": "reload", "atomic_swap": true, "creates_addons_dir": false}
],
"summary": {"targets": 2, "changed": 3, "unchanged": 12, "skipped": 1, "failed": 0}
```

Item fields:
- **`status`** is one of: `installed`, `updated`, `removed`, `adopted`; `pinned`, `unpinned` (was just pinned or unpinned by this command); `edited`; `unchanged` (planned, but nothing to do: M1's existing value, kept; covers an already-current addon, or an already-pinned one passed to `pin`); `skipped`; `failed`.
- **`skip_reason`** (null unless `skipped`) is one of: `pinned` (left alone because it is pinned), `ahead`, `blocked`, `static`, `unchecked`, `already_installed`, `no_build_for_target`, `local_source`, `duplicate`. Update-status names never appear in `status`.
- **`summary` buckets:** `changed` (installed, updated, removed, adopted, pinned, unpinned, edited), `unchanged`, `skipped`, `failed`. `targets` is the number of targets listed.
- **`request`** is the user's argument. For dependency installs it is the required folder name (`"BigWigs"`), so the M1 type (`String`) is unchanged.
- **Dependency fields** (C5): `reason`, `required_by`, `bridge_dependencies`, `unresolved`.

Target fields:
- **`no_section`** is true for sync targets without a desired set.
- **`dry_run`** lives only at `data.dry_run`. Per target, `tx` is null under a dry run.

Per-item errors: planning failures (`game_running` on a running legacy client under `safe`, `ownership_conflict`, …) are items with `status: failed`. A target-level error (`TargetResult.error`, for example `locked` at commit time) means none of that target's work committed. Either makes the run `partial`.

Order: targets commit in key order (the engine's deterministic order), but are rendered sorted by target id, consistent with `status`, `list` and `outdated`. Within a target, items keep request order. Where order is not meaningful, sort by target id, then addon name (case-insensitive), then folder key.

Default output omits `unchanged` items; `summary` counts everything, and `-v` lists all items.

Undo commands: `commands` lists `undo --run <run>` (action `undo_run`) first when more than one transaction committed, then one `undo <tx>` (action `undo`) per transaction, all `destructive: false`.

`install` keeps its M1 single-target JSON shape for compatibility, as a one-element special case of the same renderer. Its JSON is unchanged except for additive item fields that later beads add (`reason`, `required_by`, `bridge_dependencies`, `unresolved` from C5; status `skipped` with `skip_reason: duplicate` and `duplicate_of` from A5).

The full `update` envelope, with keys binding and values as examples:

```json
{"command":"update","partial":false,
 "data":{"dry_run":false,"run":"01M…","targets":[
   {"target":{"id":"forever","key":"01M…"},"tx":null,"kind":null,"no_section":false,
    "items":[{"request":"Questie","name":"Questie","ref":"gh:Questie/Questie","status":"skipped","skip_reason":"pinned",
              "from_version":"bundle/v12.1.0+v1.0.6","to_version":null,"error":null}],
    "reload_required":"none","atomic_swap":null,"creates_addons_dir":false,"error":null},
   {"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M…"},"tx":"01M…","kind":"update","no_section":false,
    "items":[{"request":"DBM","name":"DBM","ref":"gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods","status":"updated","skip_reason":null,"reason":"explicit",
              "from_version":"12.1.14","to_version":"12.1.15",
              "folders":{"added":[],"replaced":["DBM-Core","DBM-GUI"],"removed":[],"skipped":[],"recorded":[]},"required_by":[],"error":null}],
    "reload_required":"none","atomic_swap":true,"creates_addons_dir":false,"error":null}],
  "summary":{"targets":2,"changed":1,"unchanged":11,"skipped":1,"failed":0}},
 "commands":[{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo 01M…","argv":["omaddons","undo","01M…"],"destructive":false}]}
```

The 11 `unchanged` items are omitted by default and listed with `-v`. `pin`/`unpin` items use `status: "pinned"|"unpinned"`; `adopt --apply` items use `status: "adopted"` with `folders.recorded`; `sync` targets without a section have `no_section: true` and no items; `copy` skips use `skip_reason: "already_installed"|"no_build_for_target"|"local_source"`.

### Types and mapping (`src/app/outcome.rs`)

- `TargetsData { dry_run, run: Option<RunId>, targets: Vec<TargetResult>, summary: Summary }`; `TargetResult { target, tx, kind, no_section, items, reload_required, atomic_swap: Option<bool>, creates_addons_dir, error: Option<ErrorBody> }`; `ItemResult { request: String, name, ref, status, skip_reason, reason, from_version, to_version, folders, required_by, error }`; enums `ItemStatus` and `SkipReason` with the snake_case spellings above. All derive `Serialize + JsonSchema`; field order is the wire order shown. `reason`, `folders` and `required_by` are omitted (`skip_serializing_if`) for items that never got a planned record, as in the skipped item above.
- Move install's `TargetRef { id, key: Option<TargetKey>, mode }`, `ItemStatus` and `ItemError { code, message, fix, fix_argv }` into `outcome.rs` and use them from install. Install's emitted values do not change.
- `folders` reuses `engine::plan::FolderSummary`. Its `recorded` key appears when A4.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1`) adds `FolderSummary.recorded`; that is additive.
- `fn build(outcomes: &TxOutcomes, run: RunId, requested: &[ItemRequest]) -> TargetsData`, with `ItemRequest { request: String, target: String, addon: Option<String> }` (the plan's signature plus the run id, which lives on A12's `TxRequest.run`). It maps per target:
  - each `Change` in the target's outcome (or its plan under `--dry-run`) to an item: `ChangeKind::Install` gives `installed`, `Update` gives `updated` and `Remove` gives `removed`;
  - `PlanFailure`s carrying a ref or addon become `failed` items;
  - a `PlanFailure` with no ref and no addon on a target (`tx.rs:235-241`) becomes `TargetResult.error`, and that target's planned items are reported `failed` with the target's error, as M1 install's `build_items` does (`install.rs:732-736`);
  - requested items with neither a change nor a failure become `unchanged`.
- Commands add the items they decide without the engine (update's `skipped/pinned`, copy's `skipped/already_installed`) and targets that never reached the engine (sync's `no_section`) through `TargetsData::push_item` and `push_target`, which keep `summary` consistent.
- `skipped/duplicate` items come from the engine's duplicate collapse (A5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.5`: two requests for one ref become one work), and such an item carries the optional key `duplicate_of` (the first request's string, serialised only on duplicates). Whichever of A5 and A6 lands second maps the collapse in `build` and adds `duplicate_of` to `ItemResult`.
- `ChangeKind::{Adopt, Edit}` do not exist yet. Whichever of A6 and A4.1 lands second maps them: `Adopt` gives `adopted`; an `Edit` whose `fields` are only `pinned` gives `pinned` or `unpinned` by the new value; any other `Edit` gives `edited`.
- `run` is the command's run id when at least one transaction committed, else `null` (dry runs, nothing to do).
- **Partial rules:** any failed item or target error sets `partial: true`. When every item failed and nothing changed, stayed unchanged or was skipped, the command fails with the first failure's error, its exit code and `details.items`, the rule M1 install already follows.

### Human renderer

- One `TargetsOutcome { command, data, warnings, commands, notes }` implementing `Outcome`. Targets are sorted by id.
- Per target, a header names the change: `retail: updated 2 addons (tx 01M5…)`, plus ` — /reload in game` or ` — restart the game client` from `reload_required`. Mixed statuses read `changed 3 addons (2 installed, 1 removed)`. With nothing changed: `forever: nothing to update (Questie is pinned)`.
- Then indented items (`DBM  12.1.14 → 12.1.15`, failures with their code and fix). `unchanged` items are omitted unless `-v`.
- A final undo line: `Undo all of it with: omaddons undo` when more than one transaction committed, else `undo: omaddons undo <tx>`.
- Commands append their own notes (adopt's "no folder was changed", sync's "sync does not update; run `omaddons update`") through `notes`.
- `install` renders through the same code as a one-target case. It keeps its mode note, its `created Interface/AddOns` line and its skipped-folders line (`install.rs:214-305`).

### Failpoint `@N` grammar and in-process arming

- Grammar: `name=<action>@N` (N ≥ 1) fires on the Nth hit of `name` only and is inert on every other hit. The suffix is parsed on every action, so one rule covers all of them; the multi-target test uses `error@N`. `N = 0`, or a suffix that is not a number, is malformed and dropped like other malformed entries. Debug builds only (DEC-7: test hooks are honoured in debug builds only).
- Hit counting: each spec entry keeps a hit counter. The process-wide spec built from `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS` uses an atomic counter. The `with_spec` override keeps its counter in its thread-local spec.
- `with_spec` becomes a debug-only `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn` that integration tests can call (a `#[cfg(debug_assertions)] #[doc(hidden)] pub use` from `fsx`, or a `pub` module). The override lookup (`overridden`) must also move from `#[cfg(test)]` to `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`, or integration tests would install an override that `configured` never reads. Release builds keep ignoring both the environment and overrides.
- The override is thread-local, so it affects only failpoints hit on the calling thread. `engine.lock.acquired` is hit in `locked()` on the caller's thread (`tx.rs:422`), because `engine::run` commits targets sequentially on that thread.

### The new test (`tests/engine_multi_target.rs`)

Drive `omaddons::engine::run` in-process with three `TxTarget`s on three synthetic Battle.net clients (`tests/common/targets.rs` `battlenet`), installing one fixture `gh:` ref (`tests/common/http.rs` `gh_release`, `replay`), with `EngineCtx.running: Some(&empty set)` so no real `/proc` is read. Run it inside `with_spec("engine.lock.acquired=error@2", …)`:
- the targets committed first and third in key order commit; the second reports a target-level error;
- the two history lines share one run id (A12);
- each transaction undoes independently through `omaddons::engine::undo` with `UndoSelector::Tx`, leaving the other target byte-identical.

A8 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.8`) adds its download-once tests to this file. If A8 lands first, it creates the file and A6 adds to it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A three-target in-process run with `engine.lock.acquired=error@2` commits two targets and reports the remaining target's error (the second in key order) at target level (`TargetResult.error`), with `partial: true`, `commands[0]` = `undo --run <run>` (action `undo_run`), then two `undo <tx>` commands.
- Each committed target has its own tx id, history line and snapshots (`<state>/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/` and `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`), and no journal is left over. Undoing one transaction leaves the other committed target's AddOns tree hash unchanged.
- Both history lines of the run carry the same `run` id.
- `TargetsData` serialises exactly the keys and order shown above. Renderer output for 0, 1 and 3 targets is snapshot-tested in human and JSON form, with targets rendered in id order, and `unchanged` items hidden without `-v` while `summary` counts them.
- The `@N` parser accepts `error@2` and `abort@3`, drops `error@0` and `error@x`, and a `name=error@2` failpoint errors on the second hit only.
- `install`'s JSON is byte-identical to before for every existing `tests/install.rs` case and contract snapshot (single target), apart from additive fields other beads add.
- Release builds ignore `@N` specs and `with_spec` overrides, as today.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`outcome.rs`): `build` for success, item failure, target failure, dry run, pushed skips, summary buckets, the all-failed rule, `undo_run` ordering.
- Unit (`failpoint.rs`): the `@N` parser and per-entry hit counting.
- Integration: `tests/engine_multi_target.rs` (the first integration test calling `engine::run` in-process); renderer snapshots for 0, 1 and 3 targets.
- Regression: `tests/install.rs`, the contract matrix and `tests/engine_crash.rs` pass unchanged.

## Considerations

- Run ids are attribution, not atomicity: each target commits and undoes on its own, by design (one lock window per target).
- Do not change the M1 failpoint semantics: an entry without `@N` still fires on every hit, and an entry without an action still aborts.
- `ChangeKind::{Adopt, Edit}`, `FolderSummary.recorded` and the dependency item fields come from A4.1 and C5; this bead only leaves room for them. Do not add flags or commands here (DEC-1: no stubs).
- Collision hot spots: `src/app/install.rs` is also edited by A8, A9, B1, B3, B9, C4.1, C5 and F1. Keep the type moves mechanical and small.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A12 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.12` (Run ids and run-level undo): `TargetsData.run`, the `undo --run <run>` command hint and the "history lines share one run id" check all need `TxRequest.run` and the history `run` field that A12 adds.

Unblocks:
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): renders its per-target results through this outcome and relies on the multi-target commit path tested here.
- B7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` (pin and unpin): one pin transaction per target, rendered with `pinned`/`unpinned` items.
- C5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.5` (Dependency results in command output): adds `bridge_dependencies` and `unresolved` to these items and to install's.
- E5.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2` (adopt --apply): renders `adopted` items with `folders.recorded`, one transaction per target.
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): renders per-target results, including `no_section` targets.
- F4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.4` (The copy command): renders its `skipped` reasons through this outcome.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** `update` is the milestone's most-used command, and it will be the first production code to commit more than one target in one run. M1 built that path (`engine::run` commits each target in its own lock window) but only install's dry-run probe ever exercised it. This bead tests the path before anything depends on it, with one target made to fail mid-run, and gives the five fan-out commands (update, sync, adopt --apply, pin/unpin, copy) one data shape and one renderer. Agents then read the same `targets[].items[].status` everywhere, and the owner sees the same "what happened, and how to undo it" layout after every multi-client change. That keeps the project's promise that every mutation is a visible, undoable transaction (G-M2-7) while M2 multiplies the number of transactions per command (G-M2-1).

**Decisions applied.**
- *One transaction per target, sharing a run id* (with A12, M2-D38). Each target keeps its own lock window, so one client's failure never rolls back another, and the run id makes "undo all of it" one command. Rejected: one transaction spanning targets, which would need a cross-target journal and longer lock holds (vision D24: lock only for the commit window).
- *Item `status` versus `skip_reason`.* Statuses say what this command did; update-status names (`ahead`, `blocked`, …) only ever appear as skip reasons. `unchanged` keeps M1's meaning. A newest release that does not load on a client is `skipped/blocked`, not a failure (M2-D41), and copy's missing builds are `skipped/no_build_for_target` (M2-D30), so `partial` keeps meaning "retryable work failed".
- *Contract additions are additive* (M2-D32): install keeps its M1 JSON, and the new keys and enum values are recorded on the vision bead by H6.
- *In-process failpoint arming* rather than environment mutation: `set_var` is unsafe in Rust 2024 and the crate forbids `unsafe`, and the env spec is cached in a `OnceLock`. A debug-only, hidden `with_spec` is the smallest change that lets integration tests fail one target out of three. Rejected: a cross-process test, which cannot fail the second commit only without `@N`, and a second env variable, which the `OnceLock` would also freeze.
- *Risk-table mitigation folded in:* the plan's risk table lists "the multi-target commit path has never run in production" (medium likelihood, high impact) and names this bead's `error@N` test, landing before B6, as the first mitigation; A12's run-level undo and H2's crash case are the others.

**Staging decisions made while writing this bead.** `build` takes the run id as a parameter (the plan's signature had no source for it). `run` is null when nothing committed. Commands add engine-free items through `push_item`/`push_target`. `folders` reuses `FolderSummary`, so `recorded` appears when A4.1 adds it. Whichever of A6 and A4.1 lands second maps `ChangeKind::{Adopt, Edit}`. The all-failed rule follows M1 install. `@N` is accepted on every action, not only `error`.

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `e902d36`): `engine::run` sorts commits by `(key.is_none(), key, id)` (`tx.rs:214-220`) and records commit errors as `PlanFailure { ref: None, addon: None }` (`tx.rs:235-241`); `engine.lock.acquired` is hit on the calling thread in `locked()` (`tx.rs:422`) and also in undo's commit (`undo.rs:214`); `with_spec` is `#[cfg(test)]` (`failpoint.rs:116-129`) and the spec cache is a `OnceLock` (`failpoint.rs:95-100`); install reads `outcomes.first()` (`install.rs:423`).

**Risks and mitigations.** Moving install's types could change its JSON by accident: the install suite and contract snapshots are the guard, and any diff must be reviewed. A thread-local override does not reach failpoints hit on worker threads; the test arms only `engine.lock.acquired`, which runs on the caller's thread. Plan confidence for the engine area (A4, A5, C4, A12, and this multi-target coverage) is medium-high: the code is delicate, but M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites are the regression net.

title: MD5 expected hashes and tagged planned-release hashes
description:
## Background

Two M2 sources publish MD5, not SHA-256, and both facts were verified live on 2026-10-15. WoWInterface's `filedetails` gives `UIMD5`, which equals the MD5 of the downloaded bytes (BugSack: `683278e9d6e1cbc1514c3066d3d347b2`). Tukui's download response carries an `ETag` that is the MD5 of the zip. Today the code can check neither:

- `ExpectedHash` (`src/model.rs:952-967`) has one variant, `Sha256(String)`, and its doc comment already says MD5 arrives with WoWInterface.
- Two closures destructure it irrefutably and will stop compiling once a second variant exists: `plan.rs:754` (`.map(|ExpectedHash::Sha256(h)| h.clone())`, building the plan's release entry) and `blobs.rs:125` (`expected.map(|ExpectedHash::Sha256(hex)| …)`, the download guard).
- `PlannedRelease.expected_hash` (`src/engine/plan.rs:212`) is a bare `Option<String>` that does not say which algorithm it is.
- The download guard (`blobs.rs:329-387`) hashes SHA-256 only, and there is no hook that turns a response header into an expectation.

Without this bead, D3 (WoWInterface) and D4 (Tukui) would install unverified archives. That breaks the M2 goal "more keyless sources … install, update and verify like GitHub (MD5 where the source provides one)", and the checkpoint items "a tampered WoWI fixture fails with `hash_mismatch`" and "ElvUI's MD5 is checked against the response `ETag`".

Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `Cargo.toml` (`md-5 = "0.11"`), `src/model.rs`, `src/engine/blobs.rs`, `src/engine/plan.rs`, `tests/blobs.rs` (or unit tests in `blobs.rs`), an engine-level test (in `tests/plan.rs`), and `tests/snapshots/plan__plan_dry_run.snap` if its output changes.

### Expected hashes (the design, inlined)

- **`ExpectedHash` gains `Md5(String)`**: lowercase hex, 32 characters, with constructor `ExpectedHash::md5(hex) -> Option<Self>`, mirroring `ExpectedHash::sha256` (`model.rs:961-967`: validates length and hex digits, stores lowercase).
  - Add the `md-5` crate (RustCrypto) at version **0.11**. It shares `digest` 0.11 with the `sha2` 0.11 already in use (`Cargo.lock`: `digest` 0.11.3, `sha2` 0.11.1). Then run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny).
- **`PlannedRelease.expected_hash` changes from `Option<String>` to `Option<ExpectedHash>`**, tagged on the wire as `{"md5": "…"}` or `{"sha256": "…"}`. `ExpectedHash` is already `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` and externally tagged, so the variants serialise that way.
  - This is M2's one deliberate **type change** to an existing key (decision M2-D32: contract additions are additive except this one change in dry-run plan output; all are recorded in one vision comment, and `schema_version` stays 1.0 until the M4 freeze). It affects only dry-run plan output, because plans are not stored until M4.
- **Hashing:** `BlobCache::store_stream` and its guard always compute SHA-256 (the blob key), plus MD5 when an MD5 is expected. A mismatch fails `hash_mismatch`, retryable once, as today (`plan.rs:1145-1146`: the first mismatch is retried, the second is marked not retryable). The mismatch message names the algorithm ("the download's MD5 is …, but the source published …"). `details` keep their existing keys `{expected, actual}`.
- **The blob cache stays keyed by SHA-256.** The cache fast path at `plan.rs:1123` (`if let Some(ExpectedHash::Sha256(sha)) = expected && let Some(blob) = ctx.blobs.get(…)`) matches only SHA-256 expectations, so it silently does not apply to MD5. That is intended: memo candidate facts (B3, `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3`) provide the fast path for MD5 sources.
- **Header-derived hashes:** add `HashFromHeader { EtagMd5 }` next to `ExpectedHash`. When the download is asked to use `EtagMd5` (A8's `ResolvedAsset.hash_from_header`, used by Tukui in D4), it treats a quoted 32-hex `ETag` on the 200 response as the expected MD5 for that stream. An absent `ETag`, a weak one (`W/"…"`), or one that is not 32 hex digits means no check, plus a `-v` log line.
  - Read the header from the response before streaming the body (`Response::header`, `src/net/mod.rs:173`).
  - The guard checks every expectation it has: a declared hash (either algorithm) and a header-derived MD5 when no MD5 was declared.
  - No engine code can write a `-v` log line today: the only debug log lines come from `src/app/mod.rs`, using outcome fields such as `lock_held_ms`. Carry the note out the same way, as a `#[serde(skip)]` list of debug notes on the plan or outcome that the app logs at `LogLevel::Debug`. If B1's memo diagnostics have already added such a channel, reuse it.
- **MD5 is for corruption detection, not security.** SHA-256 remains the identity. Say so in the doc comments on `ExpectedHash::Md5` and `HashFromHeader`, so nobody later "upgrades" trust in MD5.
- **Fix the irrefutable patterns** by matching both variants: `plan.rs:754` becomes a clone of the whole `Option<ExpectedHash>`, and the guard at `blobs.rs:125` keeps the expectation with its algorithm.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A blob download with a correct MD5 expectation stores the blob under its SHA-256. A wrong one fails `hash_mismatch` and stores nothing in `blobs/`. A second mismatch on retry is not retryable.
- `ETag: "<md5>"` with `EtagMd5` verifies, and a wrong `ETag` MD5 fails `hash_mismatch`. A weak or wrong-length `ETag` skips the check, with a `-v` log line.
- `releases[].expected_hash` in plan output serialises as `{"md5": "…"}` or `{"sha256": "…"}` (asserted in a test for both), and `null` when the source gives none.
- `ExpectedHash::md5` accepts 32 hex digits in either case and stores them lowercase; it rejects other lengths and non-hex input.
- `cargo deny check` passes with `md-5` 0.11 and no second `digest` version in the tree.
- Existing SHA-256 behaviour is unchanged: the GitHub REST digest path (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:355-359`) and the cache fast path still work.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/model.rs`): MD5 hex validation and normalisation; serde round trip of both variants.
- Unit (`src/engine/blobs.rs`): `store_stream` with SHA-256, MD5 and header-derived MD5 expectations (match, mismatch, weak, absent and wrong-length `ETag`), in the style of the existing `expected_hashes` test (`blobs.rs:547`).
- Engine-level (`tests/plan.rs`): the test builds its own `SourceRegistry` and registers a fake source under `SourceId::Wowi` (`wowi:` refs already parse). The fake returns an asset with `expected_hash: Some(Md5(…))` served by a replay fixture. Check a correct body, then a tampered body (`hash_mismatch`, nothing installed).
- Snapshot: `tests/snapshots/plan__plan_dry_run.snap` shows `"expected_hash": null` today (GitHub `release.json` assets carry no hash), so it may not change. Review it if it does.

## Considerations

- Do not key the blob cache by MD5 or skip the SHA-256: the cache, retention pins and `blob_sha256` on records all depend on SHA-256 identity.
- WoWI may serve an empty `UIMD5`; D3 then passes no expectation. That is D3's rule, not this bead's.
- Collision hot spot: `src/engine/plan.rs` is also edited by A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3 and C4.x. The `download()` signature changes in A8 and B3 too, so keep this bead's edit to the hash plumbing.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: none (can start immediately).

Unblocks:
- A8 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.8` (Deferred asset locations and per-command download de-duplication): `ResolvedAsset` carries `expected_hash: Option<ExpectedHash>` and `hash_from_header: Option<HashFromHeader>`, both defined here, and its retries rely on the guard's `hash_mismatch`.
- D3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.3` (The WoWInterface source): every WoWI asset carries `expected_hash = Md5(UIMD5)`.
- D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4` (The Tukui source): Tukui downloads are verified through `HashFromHeader::EtagMd5`.
acceptance_criteria: ExpectedHash gains Md5 (32 lowercase hex digits, constructor ExpectedHash::md5 that accepts either case and rejects other lengths or non-hex); a blob download with a correct MD5 expectation is stored under its SHA-256, a wrong one fails hash_mismatch and stores nothing, and a second mismatch on retry is not retryable; HashFromHeader::EtagMd5 turns a quoted 32-hex ETag on the 200 response into the MD5 expectation, a wrong ETag MD5 fails hash_mismatch, and a weak, absent or wrong-length ETag skips the check with a -v log line; the plan's releases[].expected_hash serialises as {"md5": ...} or {"sha256": ...} (asserted for both) and null when the source gives none; the blob cache stays keyed by SHA-256 and the SHA-256 cache fast path and the GitHub REST digest path behave as before; md-5 0.11 shares digest 0.11 with sha2 and cargo deny check passes; an engine-level test with a fake source serving an MD5-carrying asset installs the correct body and rejects a tampered one
close_reason: MD5 expected hashes, ETag MD5 checks and typed planned-release hashes; gate --all green

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** WoWInterface and Tukui are M2's two new keyless sources, and both publish MD5 rather than SHA-256. M1's promise is that nothing is installed unverified when the source offers a hash. Keeping that promise for the new sources needs MD5 in the expected-hash type, in the download guard, and in a header hook for Tukui's `ETag`. Doing it as a small root task lets D3 and D4 start on a verified download path instead of each inventing one. It also fixes the two irrefutable `ExpectedHash::Sha256` patterns before a second variant breaks the build in someone else's bead.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D32.** Contract additions are additive, with one exception: `PlannedRelease.expected_hash` changes from a string to a tagged object (`{"md5": …}` / `{"sha256": …}`). It is the only way to say which algorithm a hash is. It is acceptable because plans are dry-run output only and are not stored until M4. The change is recorded on the vision bead (H6), and `schema_version` stays 1.0 until the M4 freeze. Rejected: bumping the schema now; a parallel `expected_md5` key, which would leave two keys meaning "the expected hash".
- **MD5 is corruption detection, not identity.** The blob cache, retention pins and `blob_sha256` stay SHA-256, so trust never depends on MD5.
- **The SHA-256 cache fast path does not apply to MD5.** That is deliberate: B3's memo candidate facts (SHA-256 of a `(release_id, asset)` already downloaded) give MD5 sources the same "no second download" benefit.
- **M2-D13 (applied here only as the header hook).** Tukui's download URL is a short-lived token, so the hash cannot be known before the download; the `ETag` on the download response is the only MD5. A8 adds the deferred-URL mechanics.

**Staging decisions made while writing this bead.** The `-v` "ETag skipped" note travels out as a `#[serde(skip)]` debug-note list that the app logs, because the engine has no log channel. `hash_mismatch` keeps its `details` keys `{expected, actual}`, and only the message names the algorithm. A header-derived MD5 applies only when no MD5 was declared, and a declared hash is always checked.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- Live, 2026-10-15: the MD5 of a WoWI download equals `UIMD5` (BugSack `683278e9d6e1cbc1514c3066d3d347b2`); the Tukui download response's `etag` is the MD5 of the bytes.
- Code, as of `e902d36`: `ExpectedHash` has only `Sha256` (`src/model.rs:952-967`); irrefutable patterns at `plan.rs:754` and `blobs.rs:125`; `PlannedRelease.expected_hash: Option<String>` (`plan.rs:212`); the SHA-256-only fast path at `plan.rs:1123`; `md-5` 0.11.0 exists and depends on `digest` 0.11, the version `sha2` 0.11.1 already pulls in.

**Risks and mitigations.** The guard is on every download path, so a mistake would break all installs: the existing blob tests and the install suite are the regression net. A weak or odd `ETag` must never fail a download, only skip the check, because Tukui's header behaviour is outside our control (the plan's risk table: "the `ETag` MD5 check is skipped when absent"). Plan confidence for the WoWI and Tukui sources is high: every API fact used here was verified live.

title: Deferred asset locations and per-command download de-duplication
description:
## Background

Two download problems block M2's update economy and the Tukui source.

**Token URLs.** Tukui's download URL is a short-lived token, verified live on 2026-10-15. `GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addon/<slug>` returns `url = https://api.tukui.org/v1/download/<slug>/<50-char token>`, with a fresh token on every call. One token was refused with 403 about 20–40 s after it was issued, and HEAD on it returns 404. The download itself comes straight from `api.tukui.org` with no redirects. An asset's URL therefore has to be obtained right before downloading, obtained again on retry, and never stored. Today `AssetLocation` (`src/model.rs:904-917`) has only `Url`, `LocalZip`, `LocalDir` and `GitCheckout`, and the `Source` trait (`src/sources/mod.rs:85-90`) has only `id` and `fetch`.

**Repeat downloads.** `TargetPlanner::download` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1121-1150`) skips the network only when the asset carries an expected SHA-256 whose blob is cached (`plan.rs:1123`), and only the GitHub REST path supplies one (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:355-359`). So one DBM release installed on three Classic clients is downloaded three times in one run. `install` also runs the engine twice: a dry-run probe across every live target (`src/app/install.rs:586-605`), then the real run (`install.rs:406-416`). Each `engine::run` builds a fresh `PlanCtx` (`src/engine/tx.rs:180`), so a memo kept per plan would be dropped between the probe and the real run, and the real run would download again.

This bead serves the M2 goal "current by default": one download per distinct archive per run, however many clients take it. It also serves "more keyless sources" (Tukui installs through deferred assets, D4) and the checkpoint item "`net.log` shows … each distinct asset downloaded once per run".

Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/model.rs` (`AssetLocation::Deferred`); `src/sources/mod.rs` (`resolve_asset`, `ResolvedAsset`, `Deserialize` on `SourceId`); `src/engine/plan.rs` (`download`, `PlanCtx`, `try_candidate`, the `PlannedRelease` URL at `plan.rs:746-756`); `src/engine/tx.rs` (`EngineCtx` and both `PlanCtx` constructions, `tx.rs:180` and `tx.rs:444`); `src/app/engine.rs` (`Engine` owns the memo); `src/engine/testing.rs` and `tests/plan.rs:97` (struct literals); `tests/engine_multi_target.rs` (created by A6, or here if A8 lands first); `tests/install.rs`.

### Per-command download de-duplication (the design, inlined)

`app::engine::Engine` (one per command, `src/app/engine.rs:21-33`) owns a `DownloadMemo`, a `Mutex<BTreeMap<(String /*release_id*/, String /*asset*/), Result<PathBuf /*blob*/, Error>>>`, and passes it into every `PlanCtx` it creates (through a new `EngineCtx` field). `install` runs the engine twice (a dry-run probe across live targets, then the real run), so the memo lives at command level, not per plan.
- The first plan to need an asset downloads it, and every later plan or target in the command reuses the blob path.
- It stores `Error`, not `ErrorBody`, so exit codes survive (`PlanFailure.cause`).
- Failures are memoised within one command only.
- Assets without a `(release_id, asset)` identity (`LocalZip`, `LocalDir`, `GitCheckout`) are not memoised: they are local already.

Together with B3's candidate facts (the SHA-256 of an asset already downloaded, kept in the release memo), each distinct archive is downloaded at most once per command, and not at all when an earlier command cached it. This is decision M2-D28: per-command de-duplication plus blob facts in the memo, instead of re-downloading per target as today.

### Deferred assets (the design, inlined)

`AssetLocation` gains `Deferred { source: SourceId, key: String }`.
- **At download time,** the planner calls `registry.get(source).resolve_asset(key)` to get a fresh URL and hash rule, then downloads as for `Url`.
- **Retries:** a 403 or 404 from the resolved URL, or a `hash_mismatch` retry, calls `resolve_asset` **again**, once, before retrying the download. Tokens die quickly, and a retry must not reuse a dead one.
- **The resolved URL is never stored** in the memo, a record, history or a plan. `PlannedRelease.url` holds `ResolvedAsset.canonical_url`, the stable metadata URL (for example `https://api.tukui.org/v1/addon/elvui`), or `null`.

Only Tukui uses this in M2 (D4). This is decision M2-D13: Tukui assets are `Deferred`; the token URL is fetched right before download, re-resolved on retry, never persisted, and redacted in `net::redact` (D4); the `ETag` MD5 is verified (A7's hook). Storing the `url` from the list call was rejected: tokens expire within seconds, so a stored URL breaks later downloads and leaks tokens into logs.

The trait addition (the default keeps every existing source compiling unchanged):

```rust
/// The concrete URL and hash rule of a Deferred asset, fetched immediately before download.
fn resolve_asset(&self, _key: &str, _http: &dyn Http) -> Result<ResolvedAsset> { Err(internal) }
pub struct ResolvedAsset { pub url: String, pub expected_hash: Option<ExpectedHash>,
                           pub hash_from_header: Option<HashFromHeader /* EtagMd5 */>, pub canonical_url: Option<String> }
```

The default error is `internal` and names the source ("the <id> source cannot resolve deferred assets").

### Implementation notes

- `SourceId` (`sources/mod.rs:31-43`) derives `Serialize` and `JsonSchema` only. Add `Deserialize`, because `AssetLocation` (and so `Release`, `ReleaseSet` and B1's memo) is deserialisable.
- `download()` gains the `release_id` and asset filename (B3 needs the same parameters; whichever bead lands first adds them). Its order becomes:
  1. look up `(release_id, asset)` in the `DownloadMemo`: a hit returns the stored blob path or error;
  2. take today's SHA-256 cache fast path;
  3. look up B3's memo fact for `(release_id, asset)` (B3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3`): a recorded SHA-256 whose blob still exists in `blobs/` is used without downloading (an evicted blob counts as a miss). Sources with no SHA-256 up front, such as Tukui, skip the network only through this step. If B3 has not landed yet, this step is absent and B3 inserts it here;
  4. resolve a `Deferred` location just in time;
  5. download, then record the blob path, or the `Error`, in the memo.
- Retry rule: one retry per download, as today. It is triggered by a 403/404 from a resolved deferred URL or by the first `hash_mismatch`, and for deferred assets it re-resolves first. `resolve_asset` therefore runs at most twice per download.
- The resolved `expected_hash` and `hash_from_header` feed A7's guard. Tukui's rule is `hash_from_header: Some(EtagMd5)`.
- `try_candidate` (`plan.rs:1024-1040`) handles `Deferred` like `Url` after resolution. `plan.rs:746-756` sets `PlannedRelease.url` to `canonical_url` for deferred assets, and A7's tagged hash where one is known. `install -v`'s `asset_url` reads `PlannedRelease.url` (`install.rs:737-746`), so it shows the canonical URL too.
- Every `match` on `AssetLocation` gains the `Deferred` arm. `info`'s `asset_urls` (`src/app/info.rs:330`) lists `Url` locations only and skips `Deferred`.
- Planning is sequential within a command, so the mutex only guards lookups and inserts. Never hold it across a network call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fake source whose `resolve_asset` returns a fresh URL per call, with the fixture answering the previous URL with 403: installs succeed, `resolve_asset` is called once per download, and once more after an injected 403.
- `engine::run` with three `TxTarget`s installing one `gh:` ref downloads its asset once (`net.log` has one `asset` line).
- `install` without `-t` on a home whose probe covers several live targets (the addon loads on one of them) downloads the asset once across the probe and the real run.
- A failed download is not retried for a second target in the same command, and reports the same error code and exit code. A new command retries it.
- No resolved deferred URL appears in the record, history, plan JSON, `--json` output, or (once B1 has landed) the release memo (a test greps them all for the token).
- `LocalZip`, `LocalDir` and `GitCheckout` installs behave as before, with no memo entries.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `DownloadMemo` hit and miss; error memoisation within a command (same error and exit code for the second target); the retry-and-re-resolve rule (403, 404, `hash_mismatch`); `Deserialize` round trip of `AssetLocation::Deferred`.
- Engine-level: a fake source registered under `SourceId::Tukui` in a test-built `SourceRegistry` (`tukui:` refs already parse), returning `Deferred` assets. Its `resolve_asset` counts calls with an atomic and returns `https://api.tukui.org/v1/download/fake/<n>` (an allowlisted host); replay fixtures answer token 1 with 403 and token 2 with the zip.
- E2E: the three-target engine test in `tests/engine_multi_target.rs`; the install probe-plus-run test in `tests/install.rs`, counting `asset` lines with the `net.log` helpers in `tests/common/netlog.rs`.

## Considerations

- Never memoise failures across commands: the memo lives in memory and is never persisted.
- A memo hit whose blob file has disappeared, for example evicted by retention after an earlier target's commit in the same run, SHOULD be treated as a miss and downloaded again, rather than failing at staging.
- Token redaction in `net.log` and error messages (`/v1/download/<slug>/<token>` becomes `/v1/download/<slug>/…`) is D4's job in `net::redact` and the guard's logged path. Do not log resolved URLs at `-v` here.
- Collision hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` is also edited by A3, A4.x, A5, A7, B3, B9, C3 and C4.x; the `download()` signature is shared with B3. `src/app/install.rs` is edited by several M2 beads.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.7` (MD5 expected hashes and tagged planned-release hashes): `ResolvedAsset` carries `Option<ExpectedHash>` (with the `Md5` variant) and `Option<HashFromHeader>`, both defined by A7, and the re-resolve-on-`hash_mismatch` retry relies on A7's guard.

Unblocks:
- D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4` (The Tukui source): Tukui assets are `Deferred { source: tukui, key: slug }`, resolved through `resolve_asset` right before each download, and D4's "downloads ElvUI once across three targets" criterion relies on the `DownloadMemo`.
- H3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.3` (Performance budgets and bench recipes): its request-economy assertions ("assets once per run") and `update --all` timings depend on per-command de-duplication.
acceptance_criteria: AssetLocation gains Deferred { source, key } and Source gains resolve_asset returning ResolvedAsset { url, expected_hash, hash_from_header, canonical_url }, with a default that is an internal error naming the source; with a fake source whose resolve_asset returns a fresh URL per call and a fixture answering the previous URL with 403, installs succeed, resolve_asset is called once per download and once more after an injected 403 (one retry per download, re-resolving first); engine::run with three TxTargets installing one gh ref logs exactly one asset request in net.log; install without -t downloads the asset once across its dry-run probe and its real run; a failed download is not retried for a second target in the same command and reports the same error code and exit code, and a new command retries it; no resolved deferred URL appears in records, history, plan JSON, --json output or the release memo (grep test), and PlannedRelease.url holds canonical_url or null; LocalZip, LocalDir and GitCheckout assets are never memoised and behave as before
close_reason: Deferred assets resolve just in time with one re-resolving retry; each archive downloads once per command; gate green

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** M2's headline economy claim is "each distinct archive is downloaded once per run, however many clients take it". The first checkpoint criterion asserts it from `net.log` for an `update --all` across about 30 addons on three targets. Today one DBM release installed on three Classic clients downloads three times, and `install` downloads twice when its compatibility probe runs. Tukui, which brings ElvUI (one of the most-used UI replacements), cannot work at all without just-in-time URLs, because its download URLs expire within seconds. This bead gives the engine both mechanisms in one place, so D4 only has to write the source and H3 can assert the economy.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D28.** Per-command download de-duplication, plus blob facts in the memo (B3). Each distinct archive downloads once per command, and not at all when an earlier command cached it. Rejected: re-downloading per target, as today.
  - *Why a per-plan memo is not enough:* `install` runs the engine twice, a dry-run probe across every live target (`install.rs:586-605`) and then the real run (`install.rs:406-416`), and each `engine::run` builds a fresh `PlanCtx`. Only a memo owned by `app::engine::Engine`, which lives for the whole command, spans both runs.
  - *Why failures are memoised only within one command:* within a command, a download that just failed would fail the same way for the next target seconds later; retrying it wastes requests and could give one run two different answers for one asset. Keeping the `Error` (not `ErrorBody`) keeps its exit code. Across commands the next invocation must retry, because network failures are transient and tokens are re-issued, so the memo is in-memory only and never persisted.
- **M2-D13.** Tukui assets are `Deferred`: the token URL is fetched right before the download, re-resolved on retry, never persisted, and redacted in `net::redact` (D4). The `ETag` MD5 is verified (A7). Why: tokens expire within seconds (verified), so persisting them would break later downloads and leak them into logs. Rejected: storing the `url` from the list call.
- `PlannedRelease.url` shows the stable `canonical_url`, so dry-run plans and `install -v` still say where a release comes from without exposing a token.

**Staging decisions made while writing this bead.** One retry per download in total (403/404 or the first `hash_mismatch`), re-resolving first, so `resolve_asset` runs at most twice. `SourceId` gains `Deserialize`, because `AssetLocation` must stay deserialisable for B1's memo. A memo hit whose blob was evicted mid-run SHOULD count as a miss. Whichever of A8 and B3 lands first adds the `release_id` and asset parameters to `download()`.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- Live, 2026-10-15: Tukui's `GET /v1/addon/<slug>` returns a fresh `https://api.tukui.org/v1/download/<slug>/<50-char token>` per call; a token was refused with 403 about 20–40 s after issue; HEAD returns 404; the download is served directly by `api.tukui.org` with no redirect, and its `etag` is the MD5 of the bytes.
- Code, as of `e902d36`: the download cache fast path covers SHA-256 expectations only (`plan.rs:1123`); only GitHub REST supplies one (`github_rest.rs:355-359`); `SourceId` lacks `Deserialize` (`sources/mod.rs:31`); `Engine` is built once per command (`install.rs:371`).

**Risks and mitigations.** The plan's risk table: "Tukui token behaviour changes (longer or shorter life, HEAD support)", medium likelihood, low impact. Resolving right before the download, and again on retry, works for any token lifetime, and the `ETag` check is skipped when the header is absent. A memo that hands out a stale blob path is the main new failure mode; treating a missing blob as a miss closes it. Plan confidence for the WoWI and Tukui source work is high: every API fact was verified live.

**What landed:**

- **`BlobCache::download_resolving(…, resolve, refreshable, …)`** in `src/engine/blobs.rs`, with `DownloadTarget { url, declared, from_header }`:
  - `resolve` runs before each attempt.
  - There is still one retry per download. It follows the first hash mismatch, or, when `refreshable` (deferred), a 403 or 404, so `resolve` runs at most twice.
  - `download(url, …)` is a wrapper with `refreshable = false`, so a fixed URL's 403 still fails at once.
  - The unusable-`ETag` note now prints `net::redact(url)`, not the raw URL.
- **`DownloadMemo`** (`engine::plan`, `Mutex<BTreeMap<(release_id, asset filename), Result<Downloaded>>>`, in memory only):
  - `app::engine::Engine` owns one per command and passes it in through the new `EngineCtx.downloads: Option<&DownloadMemo>`. `install`'s probe and real run share it.
  - `engine::run` with `None` makes one per run, so a run's targets still share downloads.
  - `PlanCtx.downloads` is the new field. Re-judging gets an empty memo; it never downloads.
- **`TargetPlanner::download(release_id, asset) -> Downloaded { blob, canonical_url }`**, in order:
  1. the memo: a hit returns its blob, or the same `Error` again. A hit whose blob is gone (evicted) is a miss.
  2. the declared-SHA-256 cache;
  3. B3's candidate fact;
  4. `Deferred`: `registry.get(source).resolve_asset(key)` just in time; else the `Url`.
  5. the download. Its result, blob or error, goes into the memo.

  Local, dir and git assets never reach it.
- **`try_candidate`** handles `Url` and `Deferred` alike. `Winner.canonical_url` carries the canonical URL to `PlannedRelease.url` for deferred assets (`null` when the blob came from the cache without resolving). `install -v`'s `asset_url` therefore shows it, and the token is never stored.

**Tests:**
- **Unit:**
  - `a_resolved_download_resolves_again_before_its_one_retry` (`blobs`):
    - a 403, a 404 or a hash mismatch resolves again: 2 resolves, then success;
    - dead twice is `http_status` after 2 resolves;
    - a mismatch twice is `hash_mismatch` and not retryable;
    - a fixed URL's 403 fails after 1 resolve.
  - `a_deferred_location_round_trips` (`model`).
  - `a_source_without_deferred_assets_cannot_resolve_one` (`sources`).
- **Engine, `tests/engine_multi_target.rs`:**
  - Three `TxTarget`s installing `gh:o/foo` make exactly 1 `asset` line.
  - The asset answering 404 fails all three targets with the same code and exit code from 1 `asset` line, and a new run asks again (2).
  - A fake `SourceId::Tukui` source returns `Deferred` assets; its `resolve_asset` counts and hands out `https://api.tukui.org/v1/download/foo/TOKEN-000n`. Token 1 answers 403, token 2 the zip with its `ETag` MD5.
    - All three targets install, with 2 resolves and 2 `asset` lines.
    - `PlannedRelease.url` is the canonical URL on every target.
    - No `TOKEN-` appears in the serialized plan or outcomes, nor in any file under the state, cache and config dirs except `net.log`. That includes the records, history, files index and the written `releases.json`.
- **E2E, `tests/install.rs`:** `the_single_compatible_live_target_is_chosen` (no `-t`, the probe covers retail and classic) now asserts 1 `asset` line. With the command-wide memo switched off it saw 2, so the assertion is meaningful.

**decided:**
- The download memo keys on `(release_id, asset filename)`, as B3's facts do.
- Failures are memoised for the command only: every error from the fetch step, so later targets report the same code and exit code.
- A deferred asset whose source is not registered fails `source_disabled` through `SourceRegistry::unavailable`, with the same fix as a ref of that source.
- **Tokens stay in `net.log` paths for now.** Redacting them in `net::redact` and the guard's logged path is D4's, as the bead says.

**Wire names:**
- New: the `AssetLocation` variant `deferred` (`{source, key}`), which reaches the memo and release sets.
- No new error codes and no constants.

title: Progress plumbing for long commands
description:
## Background

The progress surface exists but nothing can reach it. The global flags `--progress json|human|none` and `--no-progress` are parsed (`src/cli.rs:85-90`) and resolved into `OutputConfig.progress` (`src/output/term.rs:131-139`). `Reporter::progress` writes the event (`src/output/stderr.rs:153-196`). But the `Reporter` is created inside `app::dispatch` (`src/app/mod.rs:81`) after the command's `Context` was built (`src/cli.rs:271`), and `Context` (`src/cli.rs:152-164`) carries no handle to it. The engine has no hook either. No command emits a single progress event today.

M2 adds the first commands that take seconds cold: `update` across about 30 addons, `outdated` cold, `adopt` verifying archives, `sync`, and `search` with GitHub. Without feedback they look hung on a terminal, and the M3 widget, which runs commands with `--json --progress json --actor widget`, has nothing to drive its progress bar.

This bead serves the M2 goals "current by default" (long update and check runs that stay legible) and "no regression of M1 guarantees" (stderr stays NDJSON events only, stdout stays one envelope). It lands early (wave 1) because it has no blockers and every long command needs it.

Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/output/stderr.rs` (`ProgressSink`, `Phase`), `src/output/mod.rs` (re-export), `src/output/term.rs` (verify only), `src/cli.rs` (`Context.progress`, built at `cli.rs:271`), `src/app/mod.rs` (`dispatch` shares the reporter), `src/app/engine.rs` (passes the sink), `src/app/install.rs`, `src/engine/plan.rs` (`PlanCtx.progress`; fetch, download and verify events), `src/engine/tx.rs` (`EngineCtx.progress`; stage and commit events), `src/engine/testing.rs` and `tests/plan.rs:97` (struct literals), `tests/install.rs`.

### Progress (the design, inlined, adjusted to the code)

- **Plumbing.** `Context` gains `progress: ProgressSink`, a cheap clonable handle to the existing stderr `Reporter`.
- **Events.** Long commands (`outdated`, `update`, `sync`, `adopt`, `search`, and `install` with dependencies) emit progress for the phases `fetch|download|verify|stage|commit`, with a running count, a total and the item (a ref or a target id), at most one event per item per phase.
- **Precedence,** consistent with `src/output/term.rs`:
  - an explicit `--progress json|human` wins over `--json`, `--no-progress`, `CI` and a non-TTY stderr, so the M3 widget's `--json --progress json` gets NDJSON;
  - without it, `--json`, `--no-progress`, `CI` or a non-TTY stderr mean no progress;
  - on a TTY in human mode, progress is a single rewritten line.
- **Rollout.** A9 adds events to every listed command that exists when it lands. Every later command bead includes "emits progress events" in its acceptance criteria.
- **Decision M2-D26** (departs from the vision): the vision bead §7 puts "`--progress json` NDJSON events for long operations" in M3. M2 adds the plumbing and the events because M2 introduces the first multi-second commands, and a silent multi-second run reads as a hang. Waiting for M3 was rejected.

**Two points where the plan and the code differ; this bead follows the code:**
- **Event shape.** The plan sketched `{"event":"progress","phase":…,"done":n,"total":m,"item":…}`. The existing `Reporter` already emits, and unit-tests, `{"event":"progress","phase":"download","message":"WeakAuras","current":1,"total":3}` (`stderr.rs:292-295`). Keep that wire shape: `message` carries the item (ref or target id), and `current` carries the done count. Do not add a second progress shape.
- **`--quiet`.** `Reporter::progress` returns early under `--quiet` even when `--progress json` is explicit (`stderr.rs:161-163`), and the test `quiet_drops_everything_but_errors` (`stderr.rs:313-319`) pins M1's rule that `--quiet` drops everything but errors. Keep it. An explicit `--progress` beats `--json`, `--no-progress`, `CI` and non-TTY, but not `--quiet`.

### Implementation

- `pub enum Phase { Fetch, Download, Verify, Stage, Commit }`, with lowercase wire names.
- `ProgressSink` is `Clone + Debug + Send + Sync`. It wraps either nothing (`ProgressSink::none()`, a no-op that takes no lock, used when progress is off, in unit tests and by in-process test callers of the engine) or an `Arc<Mutex<Reporter<Stderr>>>`. It offers `fn event(&self, phase: Phase, done: u64, total: u64, item: &str)`, which calls `Reporter::progress(phase.wire(), item, Some(done), Some(total))`.
- **One reporter.** Build the shared `Reporter` where `Context` is built (`cli.rs:271`), and let `dispatch` use the same instance for `output::emit` and its log lines. The `Reporter` tracks whether a human progress line is on screen (`progress_line`, `stderr.rs:30-31`, cleared in `clear_progress`, `stderr.rs:213-217`). Two reporters would leave a half-drawn progress line in front of a warning or error. Lock the mutex only for each write; `dispatch` MUST NOT hold the lock while the command runs, or the first event would deadlock.
- **Engine hooks.** `EngineCtx` and `PlanCtx` gain `progress: &ProgressSink`. `app::engine::Engine` takes the sink from `Context`.
  - In planning: `fetch` per distinct `Wanted` fetched (total = the distinct count), `download` per archive actually downloaded, `verify` per candidate verified.
  - In the commit loop of `engine::run`: `stage` and `commit` per target (total = targets with work).
  - Count each phase in one place under the sink's lock, so `current` is monotonic even when fetches finish on worker threads (`fetch_once` runs sources in parallel).
- **Commands.** `install` is the only existing long command. It passes `ctx.progress` into its `Engine`, so the dry-run probe and the real run both report. Dependency rounds (C4.1) will add fetch rounds to the same counters. `status`, `list`, `info` and the other quick commands emit nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons install A B -t retail --progress json --json` (fixtures) writes progress events to stderr that the contract test's stderr check accepts (`event: progress`, `tests/contract/main.rs:187`), alongside exactly one stdout envelope.
- Per phase, `current` is monotonic, never exceeds `total`, and `total` is constant. No item appears twice in one phase.
- With `--json` alone, or in human mode with a non-TTY stderr (every test run), no progress event is emitted. With `--quiet --progress json`, none either.
- The human-mode single rewritten line is cleared before any warning or error line (unit test with a `Vec` sink).
- Existing stderr and term tests (`ndjson_lines_are_events`, `quiet_drops_everything_but_errors`, `progress_resolution`) pass unchanged.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `ProgressSink::none()` is a no-op; `event` maps to the existing wire shape; the shared reporter clears a human progress line before a warning.
- E2E (`tests/install.rs`): a two-addon fixture install with `--progress json --json` (event set, monotonic counts, one stdout envelope); absence checks for `--json` alone and `--quiet --progress json`.
- Regression: the contract matrix's stderr NDJSON check over every command.

## Considerations

- At most one event per item per phase keeps the volume bounded; never emit per file or per byte.
- Progress goes to stderr only. stdout stays exactly one envelope under `--json`.
- Collision hot spots: `EngineCtx` and `PlanCtx` also gain fields in A8 (`DownloadMemo`) and C4.1 (catalog, default channel); `src/engine/plan.rs` is edited by many M2 beads. Keep the hook calls one line each.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: none (can start immediately).

Unblocks:
- B5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.5` (The outdated command): emits fetch and verify progress through `Context.progress`.
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): emits fetch, download, verify, stage and commit progress across targets.

- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): reports per-target planning and commits.
- F4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.4` (The copy command): reports one fetch per copied ref and the commit on the destination.
- G1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7.1` (The search command): reports its per-source lookups, including the GitHub request.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** M2's batch commands (`update`, `outdated`, `sync`, `adopt`, `search`) are the first that take several seconds cold. A terminal that shows nothing for five seconds looks hung, and an agent or the M3 widget running `--json --progress json` needs machine-readable progress to show a bar. The flag, the resolution rules and the `Reporter` event already exist from M1. Only the plumbing is missing: a handle on `Context`, and hooks in the engine. Doing it once, early, means every later command bead adds one acceptance line ("emits progress events") instead of building its own channel.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D26 (departs from the vision's timing).** Progress plumbing and events land in M2; the widget consumes them in M3. Why: M2 adds the first multi-second commands, and a silent multi-second run reads as a hang. Rejected: waiting for M3, which would ship M2's slowest commands with no feedback.
- **Precedence follows `src/output/term.rs`.** The vision makes `--progress json|human|none` "the explicit control" and says `--json` implies `--no-progress`; the code resolves an explicit `--progress` over `--json`, `CI` and non-TTY, which is what the widget's `--json --progress json` needs.
- **At most one event per item per phase**, to bound volume for agents reading stderr.

**Where the plan and the code differ (written the code's way).**
- The plan sketched event keys `done` and `item`. The M1 `Reporter` already emits and unit-tests `message` and `current` (`src/output/stderr.rs:292-295`), so this bead keeps that one wire shape rather than introducing a second.
- The plan listed `--quiet` only among the "without an explicit flag" conditions. The code drops progress under `--quiet` even with `--progress json` (`stderr.rs:161-163`), and M1 pins that in `quiet_drops_everything_but_errors`. The bead keeps M1's rule: `--quiet` means errors only.

**Staging decisions made while writing this bead.** `ProgressSink` lives next to `Reporter` in `src/output/stderr.rs`, and the engine takes it through `EngineCtx` and `PlanCtx`. One shared `Reporter` (behind a mutex) replaces the two-reporter risk. `install`, the only long command that exists today, is wired in this bead.

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `e902d36`): `Context` (`src/cli.rs:152-164`) has no reporter handle; `dispatch` builds its own `Reporter` (`src/app/mod.rs:81`); `--progress` resolution is at `src/output/term.rs:131-139`, with a resolution table test at `term.rs:309`; the contract suite accepts `progress` events on stderr (`tests/contract/main.rs:187`).

**Risks and mitigations.** A shared reporter behind a mutex can deadlock if `dispatch` holds the lock while the command runs: lock per write only. Counters updated from parallel fetch threads could report out of order: count under the sink's lock. The plan's confidence section does not single out this area. It is sized S and has no blockers: small plumbing over existing, tested output code.
