title: The dependency resolver (pure)
description:
## Background

omaddons verifies every archive against the client's TOC load rules, but it ignores what those TOCs require. `install littlewigs` installs an addon the game will not load, because LittleWigs' TOC says `## Dependencies: BigWigs`. Line numbers below are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

- `verify` computes each folder's required dependencies (`FolderVerdict.dependencies`, `src/engine/inspect.rs:839`), but planning throws them away: `Winner` keeps only `Loadable` (`src/engine/plan.rs:596-611`).
- `missing_dependency` is declared (`src/error.rs:249`) and never emitted. `install --no-deps` is accepted and ignored (`src/app/install.rs:56`).
- `Catalog::by_folder` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:150`) returns every entry shipping a folder, in file order, with no family filter.
- `primary_folder` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1318`) can only use a GitHub repo name, so it cannot prefer the right folder of a `wowi:` or `tukui:` archive.

Which folders' dependencies to follow, when one is already satisfied, and where to get it involve ranking heuristics and safety guards: WoWInterface alone has 781 folder names shared by several projects (many junk, such as `__MACOSX`, `Interface`, `WTF`) and many stale projects. This bead is the **pure** layer (no I/O, no clock, no fetching), so it is table-testable and reusable by the engine's rounds (C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1`), by status and by the M4 doctor.

It serves the M2 goal **complete installs**: required projects arrive in the same transaction, from a keyless source, verified like any install, and nothing the TOC marks optional is installed unasked.

## Technical Approach

New module `src/resolve/deps.rs`, registered in `src/resolve/mod.rs` (whose doc already names dependencies). Everything that reaches the wire (reasons, candidates, bridge entries) derives `Serialize + JsonSchema` with snake_case spellings.

### Which folders' dependencies are followed

- **Needed folders.** An addon's needed folders are its primary folder plus every folder of the same archive that the primary transitively requires.
- **Required dependencies of needed folders** are resolved and installed.
- **Required dependencies of other folders** (bridge or plugin folders, such as a `Masque_<Addon>` that integrates with an optional third-party addon) are **reported, not installed**:
  - the item carries `bridge_dependencies: [{folder, requires}]`, computed **after all dependency rounds** against the final working view, so a bridge whose target is installed in the same transaction is not reported;
  - the first install of the addon adds an informational warning `bridge_dependency` ("Masque_Dominos works with Masque, which is not installed"), with `commands` holding `install Masque -t <id>`;
  - updates never repeat it, because the item data keeps it.

Why: the primary folder is what the user asked for. Pulling in every project a bridge folder mentions would install addons the user never wanted, such as Masque for everyone installing Dominos. The TOC author's intent for bridge folders is "works with X if present" (M2-D7). The separate warning code keeps "optional integration" visibly distinct from `OptionalDeps` (never warned) and from `missing_dependency` (needed and absent).

This bead provides the two functions; C4.2 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.2`) computes bridges after the last round and C5 emits the warning.
- `needed_folders(primary: &FolderName, folders: &[FolderVerdict]) -> BTreeSet<FolderName>`: the primary plus the transitive closure of its required dependencies that are folders of the same archive (present in `folders`). The caller passes the folders the client installs and the primary among them (the folder `try_candidate` names the addon after, `plan.rs:1075-1077`).
- `bridge_dependencies(needed: &BTreeSet<FolderName>, folders: &[FolderVerdict]) -> Vec<BridgeDependency { folder, requires }>`: required dependencies outside the archive, of folders outside `needed`. Raw: C4.2 drops those that `is_satisfied` against the final working view.
- Both read `FolderVerdict.dependencies`: a `Vec<FolderName>` of required dependencies today, a `DepList` whose `.required` is that list once C1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.1`) or C4.1 introduces it. Whichever lands later updates the reads.

### When a dependency is satisfied

A required folder `D` is satisfied, and nothing is installed, when any of these holds:
1. `D` starts with `Blizzard_` (case-insensitive; `FolderName::is_protected`, `src/model.rs:81`). The client provides it.
2. `D` is a folder of the same archive that this target installs.
3. A folder whose key equals `D`'s key exists in the target's AddOns:
   - **3a, managed:** the owning record gains the requester in `required_by`. This is an `Edit(AddRequiredBy)`, folded into that record's work when it has one (one work per addon per transaction).
   - **3b, unmanaged, linked or protected:** satisfied, with no record change. When unmanaged, the item adds a hint in `commands`: `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged` until the `adopt` command exists, then `omaddons adopt D -t <id>` (E5.3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3` makes that change).
4. Another work in the same transaction installs `D`. The planner's working view knows. That work's record gets the requester in `required_by`.

Wrong-flavor or out-of-date presence is not judged here. That is the M4 doctor's `wrong-flavor` finding.

Implement `is_satisfied(dep, archive, view) -> Option<Satisfier>` over a small trait, so this bead needs neither A5's working view nor the engine:
- `trait DepView { fn folder(&self, dep: &FolderName) -> Option<ViewFolder>; }` answers for the target **after the works already planned**: `Planned { addon }` for a folder a planned work installs, else the present folder's inventory class and, when managed, its owner. C4.1 implements it over A5's `WorkingView`; tests use fakes.
- `Satisfier` (internal): one variant per rule, e.g. `Client`, `SameArchive`, `Managed(owner)` (caller adds `AddRequiredBy`), `Present(class)` (caller hints only for `Unmanaged`), `Planned(addon)`. Only `Managed(owner)` is a fixed name.
- Folder identity is the case-folded key (`FolderName` equality).

### Resolution chain

```rust
pub fn resolve(missing: &FolderName, target: &Target, lookups: &DepLookups<'_>) -> DepResolution;
pub struct DepLookups<'a> {
    pub managed: &'a TargetRecord,
    pub catalog: &'a dyn CatalogLookup,            // by_folder(D), filtered by family
    pub tukui: Option<&'a dyn TukuiDirs>,          // directories → tukui:<slug>
    pub wowi: Option<&'a dyn WowiDirs>,            // UIDir → projects, ranked with guards
    pub now: Timestamp,                            // for the age guard; keeps resolve pure
}
pub enum DepResolution {
    Resolved { r#ref: Ref, via: DepVia /* catalog | tukui | wowi */, name: Option<String> },
    Ambiguous { candidates: Vec<DepCandidate>, reason: AmbiguityReason },
    Missing { reason: MissingReason },
}
```

Wire spellings: `AmbiguityReason` = `several_catalog_entries`, `wowi_ambiguous`, `wowi_abandoned`; `MissingReason` = `no_source`, `managed_folder_missing`. C5 serialises these, plus the reasons C4.1 adds (`unknown_condition`, `out_of_date` for the out-of-date guard, `limit_reached` past `DEPENDENCY_MAX_DEPTH` or `DEPENDENCY_MAX_ADDONS`), as `unresolved[].reason`. `DepCandidate` holds at least the ref, a display name and `via` (and the WoWInterface date when known, so a warning can say why); its field names are new wire names for the close comment. `name` in `Resolved` is the catalog name, the Tukui name or the WoWInterface `UIName`, which C4.1 uses to name the new record.

Lookups are trait objects so C7 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.7`) can plug in the real indexes and tests use fakes. `Catalog` implements `CatalogLookup`. `WowiDirs` returns per project: uid, `UIName`, sanitised `UIDir`, the families its `UICompatibility` maps to, `UIDownloadTotal` and `UIDate`.

In order, the first unique hit wins:
1. **Managed but missing.** A record lists `D` among its folders while `D` is absent on disk. This is **not** auto-repaired: the result is `Missing { reason: managed_folder_missing }`, and the warning's fix is `omaddons install <owner> --reinstall -t <id>`. Report and recommend; don't act. Carry the owner's name in the result so the caller can build that fix.
2. **Catalog.** `by_folder(D)`, filtered to entries whose `families` include `target.family` or are empty. Exactly one gives `Resolved (via: catalog)`. With several, prefer the entry whose name equals `D` case-insensitively. If several still remain, `Ambiguous { reason: several_catalog_entries }` with those entries as candidates. Zero after filtering falls through.
3. **Tukui.** The list's `directories` contain `D`, giving `tukui:<slug>` (`via: tukui`). Decided here: more than one hit is not unique and falls through to WoWInterface (today's two entries have disjoint directories).
4. **WoWInterface.** Projects whose sanitised `UIDir` contains `D` are ranked by:
   1. single-folder project (`UIDir == [D]`);
   2. `UIName` normalised equals `D` normalised;
   3. `UICompatibility` maps to the target's family (a hint only);
   4. `UIDownloadTotal`;
   5. `UIDate`.

   Auto-resolve only when the top candidate is strictly better than the second on criterion 1 or 2, **and** its `UIDate` is within `DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE` (new limit, 730 days). Otherwise the result is `Ambiguous { reason: wowi_ambiguous | wowi_abandoned }`, with the top three as candidates: `wowi_abandoned` when the top candidate would have won but is too old, `wowi_ambiguous` otherwise. Decided here: a sole candidate counts as strictly better only if it meets criterion 1 or 2 itself (a lone multi-folder project named differently from `D` bundles `D`; it is not `D`'s project).
5. **Anything else** is `Missing { reason: no_source }`. The warning's fix is `omaddons search <D>`. Its message says the folder may only be distributed on CurseForge or Wago, which arrive in M5.

Normalisation for criterion 2 and for the primary-folder hint: ASCII-lowercase and drop every non-alphanumeric character. One helper with a doc comment; E4.1's Title/Author normalisation is a superset and SHOULD reuse it.

### The out-of-date guard (applied by C4.1, not here)

After resolution, the dependency is planned like any install, with one extra guard: if TOC verification yields `Compatible { out_of_date: true }`, the dependency is **not** auto-installed. The run reports `missing_dependency` with the candidate and the reason "out of date for this client". Out-of-date loads need the "load out of date AddOns" checkbox in game, and silently installing a stale build to satisfy a dependency would be wrong. The 2020-era Details! on WoWInterface is exactly this case (M2-D8). The guard needs a verified archive, so C4.1 applies it after verification; this pure layer does not.

### `primary_folder` gains a name hint

`primary_folder(r#ref, folders, name_hint: Option<&str>)` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1318`):
- with a hint (a catalog name, WoWInterface `UIName` or Tukui slug), prefer the folder equal to it, normalised and case-insensitive;
- otherwise keep today's order: the folder named like the GitHub repo, the folder the others extend (`WeakAuras` for `WeakAurasOptions`), the single `*-Core`/`*_Core` folder, then the shortest.

Update every caller: `try_candidate` (`plan.rs:1044`), `addon_name` (`plan.rs:1310-1313`), the unit tests (`plan.rs:1382-1404`) and `tests/inspect.rs:60`. Decided here: existing callers pass `None`, so behaviour stays byte-identical; D3 and D4 carry `UIName` and the slug from their releases into `try_candidate`. This bead adds no carrier on `Release`: whichever of D3 and D4 lands first adds the optional `Release.name_hint` and passes it at the `primary_folder` call.

### Limit

`DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE` (730 days, not configurable) in `src/limits.rs`, with a `REGISTRY` row (`LimitValue::Millis`, unit `ms`, no config key), an entry in the test's `LIMIT_NAMES`, and the reviewed `src/snapshots/omaddons__limits__tests__limit_registries.snap`. G1's search reuses it for `abandoned`.

**Files:** new `src/resolve/deps.rs`, `src/resolve/mod.rs`, `src/engine/plan.rs` (`primary_folder` signature and callers), `tests/inspect.rs`, `src/limits.rs` and its registry snapshot.

## Acceptance Criteria

Table tests cover:
- `Blizzard_*`: satisfied; same-archive: satisfied; planned by another work: satisfied (`Planned`);
- present managed: satisfied, plus `Managed(owner)` (the caller's `AddRequiredBy`);
- present unmanaged: satisfied, plus the hint signal; present linked or protected: satisfied, no hint;
- managed record with a missing folder: `Missing { managed_folder_missing }` with the owner for the reinstall fix;
- a unique family-filtered catalog hit; an entry for another family only falls through;
- two catalog hits resolved by the name tie-break, and two that remain `several_catalog_entries`;
- a Tukui directory hit;
- a unique, recent WoWInterface single-folder project; an ambiguous WoWInterface result (top three candidates);
- a WoWInterface project older than the max age: `Ambiguous { wowi_abandoned }`;
- nothing: `Missing { no_source }`.

Also:
- `needed_folders` follows in-archive chains (A requires A_Lib requires A_Core) and excludes bridges; `bridge_dependencies` reports only external requirements of non-needed folders.
- `primary_folder` with a name hint picks `BugSack` from `[BugSack, BugSack_Extras]`, and a hint overrides today's order where they differ (hint `MyAddon` over `[Lib, MyAddon]`, where the shortest-name rule picks `Lib`).
- Existing `primary_folder`/`addon_name` tests and `tests/inspect.rs` pass unchanged with `None`.
- `DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE` is registered and the registry snapshot is reviewed.

## Test Plan

Unit tests only, in `src/resolve/deps.rs`: fakes for the four traits, a fixed `now`, `Target`s from `RulesTable::builtin()` rows, `FolderVerdict`s built directly (public fields). Hint cases go beside the `addon_names` test in `src/engine/plan.rs`; the limits test covers the registry.

## Considerations

- Keep it pure: no I/O, no clock, no fetch, no warnings built here. The engine (C4.1), C5 and C7 own I/O, messages and fixes.
- Two fixes named above need commands later beads add: `--reinstall` (B9) and `search` (G1). A bead never emits a fix for a command that does not exist yet. C4.1 builds these fixes and owns their interim forms: `managed_folder_missing` gets `omaddons list -t <id> -v` until B9 lands, and `no_source` gets the text fix "no keyless source ships <D>; it may only be on CurseForge or Wago, which arrive in M5" until G1 lands. B9 and G1 switch them to the final forms when they land after C4.1.
- Sanitising `UIDir` (empty, `.`-prefixed, `__MACOSX`, `Interface`, `WTF`, invalid and case-duplicate names) is D2's job; the `WowiDirs` adapter hands over sanitised lists.
- `src/engine/plan.rs` is a collision hot spot (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x). Keep this bead's edit there to the `primary_folder` signature and its call sites.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: none (can start immediately).

Unblocks:
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (Dependency rounds on install: collect, resolve, plan, fixpoint, failure semantics and --no-deps): its rounds call `needed_folders`, `is_satisfied` and `resolve`, and its out-of-date guard follows this resolution.
- C7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.7` (Wire the WoWInterface and Tukui indexes into dependency resolution): it implements `TukuiDirs` and `WowiDirs`, which this bead defines.
- D3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.3` (The WoWInterface source): it passes `UIName` as the primary-folder name hint, which needs the new `primary_folder` signature.
- D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4` (The Tukui source): it passes the slug as the primary-folder name hint, likewise.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** "Complete installs" is the M2 goal that M1's TOC verification cannot reach on its own: verification proves a folder loads, not that the projects it needs are present. The risky part of dependency handling is not the engine plumbing but the judgement calls: which folders' requirements count, when a requirement is already met, and which upstream project a bare folder name means. Putting all of those in one pure module makes every call table-testable, keeps the engine (C4.1) a thin loop over it, and lets status and the M4 doctor reuse the same answers. Conservatism here is what keeps omaddons trustworthy as the sole authority: a dependency it cannot place with confidence is reported with candidates, never guessed.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D7:** auto-install only the required dependencies of the primary folder, and of the folders it transitively requires inside the archive. Bridge-folder dependencies are reported once. `OptionalDeps` are never installed. Why: it matches user intent with no surprise installs (Masque for every Dominos user). Rejected: following every folder's dependencies.
- **M2-D8:** resolution chain catalog → Tukui → WoWInterface (unique, recent, not out of date) → `missing_dependency`. A managed record with a missing folder is reported, not repaired. Why: deterministic and conservative; WoWInterface's 781 shared folder names and stale projects (Details! from 2020) make blind lookups dangerous. Rejected: taking the most-downloaded WoWInterface project, which would install stale builds.
- **M2-D9** (applied by C4.1, shaped here): a dependency that resolved but failed to install makes the run partial; one that resolved to nothing is a warning. That is why `resolve` separates `Resolved`, `Ambiguous` and `Missing` cleanly.
- **M2-D10:** the dependency checkpoint is LittleWigs → BigWigs (a real required cross-project dependency between two catalog addons), not BugSack → `!BugGrabber` (optional, and without an official release).
- The out-of-date guard (a resolved dependency that verifies only as out of date is not auto-installed) is part of M2-D8 but needs a verified archive, so C4.1 applies it; this layer stays pure.
- Staging decisions made when writing this bead (not specified elsewhere): `is_satisfied` works over a small `DepView` trait so C3 has no edge to A5's working view; `resolve` takes `now` in `DepLookups` to stay pure; a Tukui step with several hits falls through; a lone WoWInterface candidate auto-resolves only if it is single-folder or name-matched; existing `primary_folder` callers pass `None` and D3/D4 supply real hints. `DepCandidate`'s field names become wire names through C5.

**Facts verified during planning** (line numbers as of `e902d36`; live facts 2026-10-15):
- `Winner` keeps only `Loadable`, so per-folder dependencies are discarded (`src/engine/plan.rs:596-611`); `FolderVerdict.dependencies` is filled in `verify` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:880`).
- `missing_dependency` is registered and never emitted (`src/error.rs:249`); `--no-deps` is a no-op (`src/app/install.rs:56`).
- `Catalog::by_folder` exists with no family filter (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:150`); built-in entries always list families, overrides may not.
- `primary_folder` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1318`) prefers the GitHub repo name, then the extended folder, then a single `*-Core`, then the shortest; callers are `try_candidate`, `addon_name` and `tests/inspect.rs`.
- LittleWigs' TOC: `## Dependencies: BigWigs`, `## LoadOnDemand: 1`. BugSack v12.1.7 lists `!BugGrabber` under `OptionalDeps`.
- WoWInterface filelist: 8,218 projects; 781 `UIDir` names belong to more than one project; junk names include `__MACOSX` (119), `""` (56), `Interface` (60), `WTF` (23). `!BugGrabber`, LibStub, ElvUI and Auctionator are not listed. Details! (UID 23056) is stale, from 2020.

**Risks and mitigations.** "Dependency resolution installs the wrong project" is rated medium likelihood, medium impact. Mitigations: catalog first; WoWInterface only when unique on folder shape or name, and recent; ambiguity becomes a warning with candidates; every install is still TOC-verified, recorded as a dependency and undoable. A second risk is drift between this module's satisfaction view and the engine's working view; the `DepView` trait makes the contract explicit and C4.1 implements it once. Confidence: high for the pure layer (table tests, no I/O); the engine rounds built on it are rated medium-high.

title: Epic: Dependency planning rounds in the engine
description:
## Background

This epic is the engine half of the M2 goal "complete installs": an addon whose loaded TOC requires another project gets that project in the same transaction, from a keyless source, verified like any other install, and nothing the TOC marks optional is installed without being asked for. The checkpoint case is `omaddons install littlewigs`: LittleWigs' TOC declares `## Dependencies: BigWigs` (verified live 2026-10-15), so BigWigs must come along, recorded as `reason: dependency, required_by: ["LittleWigs"]`, and one `undo` must revert both.

Today the planner cannot do this (code at commit `e902d36`, current `main`; line numbers drift, symbol names do not): `try_candidate` computes each folder's required dependencies and the primary folder and then drops them (`Winner` keeps only `Loadable`, `src/engine/plan.rs:596-611`); `plan()` fetches once, up front (`plan.rs:291`); `EngineCtx` (`src/engine/tx.rs:102-117`) has no catalog or default channel; `install --no-deps` is accepted and ignored; the warning `missing_dependency` is registered and never emitted.

The plan sized this work as one L task, "one engine flow: rounds, fetch-once across rounds, working-view integration, locks and failure semantics; splitting it would leave a half-resolving planner". It is split in two below without splitting that flow.

## Goals

- Planning rounds per target: round 0 plans the explicit requests; each later round collects the unsatisfied required dependencies of the needed folders of every planned install, resolves them through C3's pure chain (catalog, Tukui, WoWInterface), fetches the new refs once through B1's `ReleaseCache`, and plans them as `Install { reason: Dependency, pin: Keep, channel: default_channel }`, until a fixpoint bounded by `DEPENDENCY_MAX_DEPTH` (4) and `DEPENDENCY_MAX_ADDONS` (32).
- Satisfaction rules that install nothing for `Blizzard_*`, same-archive, present (managed, unmanaged, linked, protected) and same-transaction folders, with managed owners gaining `required_by` through reversible `AddRequiredBy` edits.
- Failure semantics: a resolved dependency that fails makes the run partial while the requester installs; an unresolvable one is a `missing_dependency` warning.
- `--no-deps` on `install` and `update`, a dependency-lock input for `sync --locked`, offline `rejudge` replay that drops dependency work whose requesters dropped.
- Bridge dependencies reported (never installed), with a first-install marker, for C5 to render.

## Success Criteria

When both children are closed:
- `install littlewigs` installs LittleWigs and BigWigs in one transaction, BigWigs recorded `reason: dependency, required_by: ["LittleWigs"]`; `undo` removes both.
- An unmanaged `BigWigs` folder satisfies the dependency (hint `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged`, later `adopt`); a managed explicit BigWigs gains `required_by` through a `required_by_add` history edit and stays `explicit`.
- `OptionalDeps` never install; chains install; cycles install once and list each other.
- A failing dependency makes the run partial and the requester installs; `--no-deps` installs only the requester and warns.
- `update` of a requester whose new release adds a dependency installs it in the same transaction; a dependency removed earlier is re-installed with `reason: dependency`; `update --no-deps` works.
- `net.log` shows each distinct ref fetched once across rounds, on install and update; a chain past `DEPENDENCY_MAX_DEPTH` stops with a warning naming the limit.
- Bridge dependencies are computed after the last round against the final working view.

## Non-Goals

- Rendering dependency results in command output (item fields, dependency items, `bridge_dependency` warnings, install hints): C5.
- Bookkeeping on remove and update (`RemoveRequiredBy`, `still_required`, `orphaned_dependency`, `status` orphans): C6.
- WoWInterface and Tukui lookups in the chain: C7 fills the optional lookups this epic adds.
- Filling dependency locks from `addons.toml`: F3.2.
- Installing `OptionalDeps`, repairing a managed record whose folder is missing, judging wrong-flavor presence (an M4 doctor finding).

## Considerations

- Decisions: M2-D7 (only the primary folder's required dependencies, and those of same-archive folders it requires, are installed; bridges are reported once; `OptionalDeps` never), M2-D8 (catalog, then Tukui, then WoWInterface only when unique and recent, else a warning), M2-D9 (resolved-but-failed is partial, unresolvable is a warning), M2-D33 (dependencies use `default_channel`, never the requester's), M2-D35 via A4.2 (`required_by` edits undo in place). The rationale comment carries the reasons and rejected alternatives.
- `src/engine/plan.rs` is the busiest file in M2 (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x): small commits, file lists in claims, rebase before every gate run.
- Confidence: medium-high, like all engine work; M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites are the regression net.
- If B6 is already on `main` when C4.1 lands, land C4.2 soon after: in between, `update` already resolves dependencies, but a failing dependency may not yet make `update` partial (that mapping is C4.2's).

## Children

| Key | Id | Title | Scope in one line | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C4.1 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` | Dependency rounds on install: collect, resolve, plan, fixpoint, failure semantics and --no-deps | The whole resolving loop inside engine planning for every planned install, limits, locks input, rejudge, `install --no-deps` | A3, A4.2, A5, A10, B1, C3 |
| C4.2 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.2` | Dependencies on the update path, update --no-deps and bridge dependencies | `update --no-deps`, update acceptance and failure mapping, bridge dependencies with the first-install marker | B6, C4.1 |

## How this was split

- **C4.1 keeps the whole loop.** Collection, satisfaction, resolution, rounds, fetch-once across rounds, the out-of-date guard, limits, failure semantics, the lock input and `rejudge` replay all land together, so no commit leaves a planner that resolves only part of a graph. The rounds run inside engine planning for **every** planned install, not only for the `install` command. `update` turns `Update { addon }` into an `Install` work through `want()`, so update gains dependency resolution automatically once B6 and C4.1 are both on `main`.
- **C4.2 adds only what is update-specific, plus a report-only pass.** The `--no-deps` flag on `update` (it can only land with `update` itself, and vision rule DEC-1 forbids a flag without behaviour), the update acceptance tests, the mapping that keeps B6's `skipped/blocked` from hiding dependency failures, and bridge dependencies, which install nothing and only feed C5.
- **`main` stays consistent after each lands.** After C4.1: installs are complete; nothing exposes a field or flag that does nothing; bridges have no output key yet, so nothing is half-reported. After C4.2: update is complete and the report holds everything C5 renders.
- **Edges moved from the original single C4 task.** C4.1 waits for A4.2 (it emits `required_by_add` edits, which must be reversible) and A5, but no longer for B6. C4.2 waits for B6 and C4.1. C7, E5.3, F3.1, F4 and H5 need only the loop, so they wait for C4.1. C5 (bridge data and first-install marker), C6 (update-side bookkeeping) and H2 (crash coverage of dependency transactions) wait for C4.2.
acceptance_criteria: C4.1 and C4.2 are closed; install littlewigs installs BigWigs in the same transaction as reason dependency with required_by ["LittleWigs"] and undo removes both; satisfied, optional, chained, cyclic, failing and --no-deps cases behave as the children specify on install and on update; each distinct ref is fetched once across rounds; the depth limit warns; bridge dependencies are computed after the last round for C5 to render
close_reason: All children completed

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this epic.** M1 made installs correct per folder: every folder is verified against the client's own TOC load rules before anything is written. It could not make them complete. An addon that needs another project installs alone and fails to load in game, and the user only finds out there. Dependency rounds close that hole inside the same transaction engine, so a dependency is fetched, verified, journaled, snapshotted, attributed and undone exactly like what the user asked for. This serves the project's thesis (omaddons is the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons) and the M2 goal "complete installs". The engine work also pays off later: `sync` (F3) and `copy` (F4) get dependency resolution for free, and multi-addon transactions are the shape M3's "Update all" and M4's repairs build on.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D7:** install only the required dependencies of the primary folder and of same-archive folders it requires; report bridge-folder dependencies once; never install `OptionalDeps`. Why: user intent, no surprise installs (Masque for everyone installing Dominos). Rejected: following every folder's dependencies.
- **M2-D8:** catalog, then Tukui, then WoWInterface (unique, recent, not out of date), else `missing_dependency`; a managed record whose folder is missing is reported, not repaired. Why: deterministic and conservative; WoWInterface has 781 folder names shared by several projects and stale projects such as the 2020 Details!. Rejected: the most-downloaded WoWInterface project.
- **M2-D9:** a resolved dependency that fails makes the run partial and the requester still installs; an unresolvable one is a warning. Why: partial means "retryable work failed". Rejected: failing the requester; skipping silently.
- **M2-D33:** dependencies use `default_channel`. Why: a beta addon must not drag its dependencies onto beta. Rejected: inheriting the requester's channel.
- **M2-D10** (a departure from the vision): the checkpoint uses LittleWigs → BigWigs instead of BugSack → !BugGrabber, because BugSack v12.1.7 lists `!BugGrabber` under `OptionalDeps` (which must never auto-install) and `!BugGrabber` has no official GitHub release (verified 2026-10-15). Rejected: auto-installing optional dependencies.
- **M2-D35** (via A4.2): `required_by` edits undo in place and are ignored by conflict detection, from the plan's third review pass. Without it, installing LittleWigs and then updating BigWigs would make the LittleWigs install impossible to undo.

**Why the split is safe.** The plan kept C4 whole to avoid a half-resolving planner. The split keeps the entire resolving loop in C4.1, which runs for every planned install, so no state of `main` resolves only part of a graph. C4.2 holds only what cannot exist before `update` does (its flag, its tests, its failure mapping) and the report-only bridge pass. C4.1 no longer waits for B6, so the dependency lane can proceed while the update lane finishes, which shortens the critical path (A3 → A4 → A5 → C4 → F3 → H2/H5 → H7).

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`): `Winner` (`src/engine/plan.rs:596-611`), `fetch_once` once (`plan.rs:291`), `EngineCtx` without a catalog (`src/engine/tx.rs:102-117`), `InstallArgs.no_deps` unused, `WarningCode::MissingDependency` unused, built-in catalog entries for BigWigs and LittleWigs. Live, 2026-10-15: `LittleWigs.toc` has `## Dependencies: BigWigs`.

**Risks and mitigations.** Medium-high confidence (the plan's rating for all engine work). Wrong-project installs are bounded by the conservative chain, TOC verification and undo. Regressions in install, remove and undo are caught by M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites, which must pass unchanged, and H2 adds crash coverage for dependency transactions. Many agents editing `plan.rs` is a high-likelihood collision; small commits and file-list claims mitigate it.

title: Dependency rounds on install: collect, resolve, plan, fixpoint, failure semantics and --no-deps
description:
## Background

M2 goal "complete installs": an addon whose loaded TOC requires another project gets that project in the same transaction, from a keyless source, verified like any other install; nothing the TOC marks optional is installed unasked. Today `omaddons install littlewigs` installs an addon the game will not load: LittleWigs' TOC says `## Dependencies: BigWigs` (verified 2026-10-15) and nothing installs BigWigs.

Why the engine cannot (line numbers as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- `try_candidate` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1018-1093`) computes each folder's required dependencies (`FolderVerdict.dependencies`, `src/engine/inspect.rs:840-847`, from `Toc::dependency_folders()`, `src/toc.rs:323`) and the primary folder (`primary_folder`, `plan.rs:1318`), then drops both: `Winner` keeps only `Loadable` (`plan.rs:596-611`).
- `plan()` calls `fetch_once` once, up front (`plan.rs:291`).
- `EngineCtx` (`src/engine/tx.rs:102-117`) and `PlanCtx` (`plan.rs:93-108`) have no catalog and no default channel.
- `install --no-deps` is accepted and ignored (`src/app/install.rs:54-56`, help "Accepted; dependencies arrive in a later release").
- Warning `missing_dependency` is registered (`src/error.rs:249`) but never emitted.

This bead adds dependency rounds inside engine planning. They run for every planned install, so any `Install` work gets them, `update`'s included (C4.2 adds update's flag, tests and bridge dependencies).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/engine/plan.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs` (`EngineCtx`, `TxRequest.no_deps`, `TxTarget.dependency_locks`, `PlanCtx` in `locked()`, rejudge), `src/app/engine.rs`, `src/app/install.rs`, `src/limits.rs` (two limits, `REGISTRY` rows, `LIMIT_NAMES` test list, `src/snapshots/omaddons__limits__tests__limit_registries.snap`), `src/toc.rs` (only if C1 has not landed), new `tests/deps.rs`.

### What counts (M2-D7)
- Required: `Dependencies`, `RequiredDeps`, any directive whose lowercased key starts with `dep`. `OptionalDeps` are never installed or warned about. `LoadWith`/`LoadManagers` are ignored.
- Only **needed folders** are followed: the primary folder plus every same-archive folder it transitively requires (C3 `needed_folders`). Bridge folders are C4.2's.
- Per-folder lists are C1's `DepList { required, optional, unknown_condition }` in `FolderVerdict.dependencies`. If C1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.1`) has not landed, add that type to `src/toc.rs` and fill `required` from `Toc.dependency_folders()`, `optional` from `Toc.optional_deps`, `unknown_condition` empty; C1 later switches the fill. An `unknown_condition` dependency is never installed; it is reported unresolved.

### 1. Keep the inputs
- `Winner` and `AddonWork` keep `primary: Option<FolderName>` (C3's name hint) and `deps: BTreeMap<FolderName, DepList>` for installed folders, plus which folders verified `Compatible { out_of_date: true }`.
- `EngineCtx`/`PlanCtx` gain `catalog: &Catalog`, `default_channel: Channel` (config, else stable), `tukui: Option<&dyn TukuiDirs>` and `wowi: Option<&dyn WowiDirs>` (`None` until C7). `app::engine::Engine` loads the catalog once; `locked()` (`tx.rs:444`) passes the fields.
- B1's `ReleaseCache` replaces `fetch_once`; its run-scoped map makes rounds fetch-once per command.

### 2. Rounds, per target
1. **Round 0:** explicit requests in A5's order (ownership judged after every round-0 work is inspected).
2. **Collect.** For each planned install, take its needed folders' required dependencies, drop the satisfied ones (part 3 below), resolve the rest (part 4), and collect new `Wanted` refs not already planned or fetched (visited set by ref and folder), sorted by ref identity (`Ref`'s `Ord`).
3. **Round N:** one `ReleaseCache::get` for the new refs, then plan each as `RequestedChange::Install { reason: Dependency, pin: Keep, channel: default_channel, channel_explicit: false, version: <lock or None>, name: <resolution name>, reinstall: false, … }` with the requesters (sorted, de-duplicated) in the work's `InstallIntent.required_by_add` (A3 gives `RequestedChange::Install` no `required_by` field; the engine builds these works itself). Never the requester's channel (M2-D33). Apply the out-of-date guard.
4. **Repeat** until no new refs, at most `DEPENDENCY_MAX_DEPTH` rounds (new limit, 4) and `DEPENDENCY_MAX_ADDONS` dependency installs per target (new limit, 32), not configurable. Past either, each remaining dependency is a `missing_dependency` warning naming the limit.
5. **Cycles** are harmless: the visited set stops re-planning, and both records list each other in `required_by`.
6. Order is deterministic (round 0 in argument order, then resolution order). Dry runs run rounds too.

### 3. Satisfied: nothing installed
A required folder `D` is satisfied when:
1. it starts with `Blizzard_` (case-insensitive);
2. it is a folder of the same archive this target installs;
3. a folder with `D`'s key exists in AddOns. **3a managed:** the owner gains the requester via `Edit(AddRequiredBy(requester))`, folded into the owner's work when it has one (one work per addon, A4.1); nothing when already listed. **3b unmanaged, linked or protected:** no record change; when unmanaged, the command adds the hint `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged` (action `list_unmanaged`; E5.3 makes it `adopt`);
4. another work in this transaction installs `D` (A5's working view): its record gains the requester.

Wrong-flavor or out-of-date presence is not judged here (M4 doctor).

### 4. Resolution chain (C3, pure)
`resolve(missing, target, &DepLookups { managed, catalog, tukui, wowi }) -> DepResolution` gives `Resolved { ref, via, name }`, `Ambiguous { candidates, reason }` or `Missing { reason }`, first unique hit winning (M2-D8): a record listing `D` while it is absent → `Missing { managed_folder_missing }` (never auto-repaired); catalog `by_folder(D)` filtered to the target's family (empty families match), name tie-break, else `Ambiguous { several_catalog_entries }`; Tukui list directories → `tukui:<slug>`; WoWInterface `UIDir` only when unique and recent (`DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE`, 730 days), else `Ambiguous { wowi_ambiguous | wowi_abandoned }` with the top three; else `Missing { no_source }`. Only the catalog is live here.

### 5. Guard and failures (M2-D9)
- **Out-of-date guard:** a dependency whose required folder verifies `Compatible { out_of_date: true }` is not installed; `missing_dependency` names the candidate and "out of date for this client".
- **Resolved but failed to plan** (no compatible release, network, verification, ownership): a `PlanFailure` for the dependency ref with `details.required_by`; the run is `partial`; the requester still installs.
- **Resolved to nothing** (missing, ambiguous, guard, limit): a `missing_dependency` warning, not partial. Message: requester, folder, why, top candidates. Fix: `omaddons install <top candidate> -t <id>`; `managed_folder_missing` → `omaddons install <owner> --reinstall -t <id>` once B9 has landed, else `omaddons list -t <id> -v`; `no_source` → `omaddons search <D>` once G1 has landed, else the text "no keyless source ships <D>; it may only be on CurseForge or Wago, which arrive in M5" (never a hint for a command that does not exist yet).
- Decided: dependency works are judged with `force: false`; `--force` is a deliberate act on the folders the user named.

### 6. Report for commands
`TargetPlan.dependencies: BTreeMap<String /*requester*/, DepReport>`, `#[serde(skip)]`, with `installs: Vec<(FolderName, String)>`, `unmanaged: Vec<FolderName>`, `unresolved: Vec<Unresolved { folder, reason, candidates: Vec<Ref> /*≤3*/ }>`, `failed: Vec<(FolderName, Ref)>`. `reason` wire values: C3's `no_source`, `managed_folder_missing`, `several_catalog_entries`, `wowi_ambiguous`, `wowi_abandoned`, plus `unknown_condition`, and (decided here, since no wire value was specified for these cases) `out_of_date` and `limit_reached`. C4.2 adds `bridge_dependencies` and `first_install`; C5 renders.
- `install`: `partial()` (`install.rs:196`, failed items only) also counts dependency failures, each mirrored as `Warning::item` naming the dependency and requesters; one `list_unmanaged` hint for 3b folders. `build_items` (`install.rs:725`) still lists positionals only (dependency items are C5's).
- The target-defaulting probe (`install.rs:592-605`) plans with `no_deps: true`: requested refs alone decide the target.

### 7. `--no-deps` and locks
- `TxRequest.no_deps` → `PlanRequest.no_deps` skips resolution and rounds; satisfaction is still judged and unresolved required dependencies still warn. Decided: 3a edits are still planned (they record a fact, install nothing). Install help: "Install only the named addons, not the ones their TOCs require".
- `TxTarget.dependency_locks: BTreeMap<Ref, String>` (→ `TargetRequest`), default empty: a dependency whose resolved ref equals a key (ref identity) is fetched at that version; a lock matching nothing is ignored; a lock never pins. F3.2 fills it.

### 8. Under the lock
`rejudge` replays planned works (dependency works and edits included) in order, offline (A5), never resolving or fetching. A dependency work or `AddRequiredBy` edit whose every requester dropped out is dropped too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Checkpoint:** `install littlewigs` (LittleWigs requires `BigWigs`, provided by `gh:o/bigwigs` through a test override in `<config>/omaddons/catalog.d/`) installs both in one transaction; BigWigs is `reason: dependency, required_by: ["LittleWigs"]`; `undo` removes both.
- `BigWigs` present unmanaged: nothing extra installs; `commands` holds `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged`.
- BigWigs managed and explicit: it gains `required_by: ["LittleWigs"]` in the same transaction (history `edit: required_by_add`); `reason` stays `explicit`.
- `OptionalDeps: X` never installs X, and X's ref is never fetched.
- A chain A → B → C installs all three; a cycle A ↔ B installs both once, each listing the other.
- A dependency with no compatible release: the requester installs, the run is `partial`, the failure names the dependency and `details.required_by`.
- `--no-deps` installs only the requester and warns `missing_dependency`.
- `net.log`: each distinct ref fetched once across rounds (a diamond shares one fetch).
- A chain longer than `DEPENDENCY_MAX_DEPTH` stops with a warning naming the limit.
- `Blizzard_*` and same-archive dependencies install nothing; the guard installs nothing and warns; a dependency of an `--channel beta` install uses `default_channel`; an engine-API lock fetches that version, unpinned.
- Existing install, crash, concurrency and undo suites pass unchanged.

## Test Plan

- E2E `tests/deps.rs`, one test per criterion: A10's `release_graph` (TOCs with `## Dependencies`/`## OptionalDeps`) and `gh_release` fixtures, `net_log` counters, record and history readers; undo of the checkpoint byte-for-byte; `--dry-run` lists both changes and writes nothing.
- Engine API: dependency locks; `DEPENDENCY_MAX_ADDONS` with 33 dependencies (or the rounds loop taking limits as parameters).
- Unit: rejudge drop rule, collection order, `DepReport` per case.

## Considerations

- Rounds start from planned installs only: an already-current requester has no work and resolves nothing.
- Install side of the bookkeeping: an explicit `install` of an addon recorded as a dependency promotes it (`reason: Explicit` through A3's carry-over; a records-only `SetReason` edit through A4.3 when current). Rule 3a only adds requesters and never changes `reason`.
- A5's working view must see dependency claims, so two dependencies shipping one folder fail `ownership_conflict` (`within_transaction`).
- An `AddRequiredBy` edit on an addon with no other change in the transaction is recorded with A4.2's reversible `edit` op, never snapshot restore. Folded into a work that also changes that addon (an update of the owner in the same transaction), it rides that addon's ordinary snapshot-restore undo, as A4.2 rules.
- When the resolved archive does not ship `D` for this client, warn and record nothing (report, don't act); record it with `decided:`.
- Emit A9 progress events per round when A9's sink exists.
- Collision hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x), `src/error.rs` and `src/limits.rs` (several). Claim with file lists; rebase before each gate run.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.3` (Record carry-over rules and the extended RequestedChange): dependency installs use `Install`'s `reason`, `pin` and `channel_explicit` and `carry_over`'s `required_by` rules.
- A4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.2` (Reversible required_by edit ops): rule 3a emits `AddRequiredBy` edits, which must undo in place before production code may produce them.
- A5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.5` (Per-target working view): satisfaction rule 4, conflicts between dependency works, rejudge replay order.
- A10 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.10` (M2 test helpers): `release_graph` fixtures, `net_log` counters.
- B1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.1` (The release memo and ReleaseCache): rounds call `ReleaseCache::get` again, fetch-once across rounds.
- C3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.3` (The dependency resolver): `needed_folders`, `is_satisfied`, `resolve`, name-hinted `primary_folder`.

Unblocks:
- C4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.2` (Dependencies on the update path, update --no-deps and bridge dependencies): builds on the rounds and the report.
- C7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.7` (Wire the WoWInterface and Tukui indexes): fills the lookups added here.
- E5.3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3` (Adopt hints and fixes): rewrites the unmanaged-dependency hint to `adopt`.
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): resolves dependencies as install does and passes `no_deps`.
- F4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.4` (The copy command): dependencies resolve on the destination.
- H5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.5` (Real-machine smoke tests): `install littlewigs -t retail`, then undo.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** It is the heart of the "complete installs" goal. M1 verifies every folder against the client's own TOC rules, but it cannot see that an addon needs another project, so `install littlewigs` succeeds and the game then refuses to load LittleWigs. With rounds in the engine, the dependency is fetched, selected, downloaded, verified and committed in the same journaled transaction as its requester, recorded as a dependency, and undone with it. That keeps the project's thesis intact: the extra install is a transaction like any other, not a side effect.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D7:** auto-install only the required dependencies of the primary folder and the folders it transitively requires in the same archive; bridge folders are reported (C4.2); `OptionalDeps` are never installed. Why: it matches user intent and avoids surprise installs (Masque for everyone installing Dominos). Rejected: following every folder's dependencies.
- **M2-D8:** resolution chain catalog, then Tukui, then WoWInterface (unique, recent, not out of date), else `missing_dependency`; a managed record with a missing folder is reported, not repaired. Why: deterministic and conservative; WoWInterface has 781 folder names shared by several projects and stale projects (Details! from 2020). Rejected: taking the most-downloaded WoWI project, which would install stale builds.
- **M2-D9:** a resolved dependency that fails to install makes the run partial and the requester still installs; an unresolvable one is a warning. Why: partial means "retryable work failed", which an agent can act on; the requester is harmless without its dependency. Rejected: failing the requester; skipping silently.
- **M2-D33:** dependency installs use `default_channel`, never the requester's channel. Why: a beta-channel addon should not drag its dependencies onto beta. Rejected: inheriting the channel.
- **M2-D35** (via A4.2): `required_by` edits are history ops with an `edit` field that undo reverses in place and conflict detection ignores. Why: otherwise installing LittleWigs and then updating BigWigs makes the LittleWigs install impossible to undo, and a snapshot restore would roll BigWigs' record back under its new folders. Rejected: snapshot restore for every records-only change. This came from the plan's third review pass ("undo of `required_by` edits").
- **M2-D10:** the checkpoint uses LittleWigs → BigWigs, not BugSack → !BugGrabber: BugSack v12.1.7 lists `!BugGrabber` under `OptionalDeps`, which must never auto-install, and `!BugGrabber` has no official GitHub release.
- Order independence (review pass 3, A5): ownership is judged only after every round-0 work is inspected, so dependency rounds always plan against a settled working view.

**Staging decisions taken in this bead** (record each with a `decided:` comment when implementing): dependency works never inherit `--force`; `--no-deps` still plans rule-3a `AddRequiredBy` edits; the install target-defaulting probe plans with `no_deps`; `unresolved` reasons `out_of_date` and `limit_reached` (the plan names none); fixes for `reinstall` and `search` wait for B9 and G1 (the plan's own rule: never hint a command that does not exist yet).

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`): `Winner` keeps only `Loadable` (`src/engine/plan.rs:596-611`); `FolderVerdict.dependencies` is filled and then unused (`src/engine/inspect.rs:840-847`); `fetch_once` runs once (`plan.rs:291`); `EngineCtx` has no catalog (`src/engine/tx.rs:102-117`); `InstallArgs.no_deps` is never read; `WarningCode::MissingDependency` is never constructed; install's `partial()` counts failed positional items only (`src/app/install.rs:196`); the built-in catalog lists BigWigs (12 folders) and LittleWigs. Verified live on 2026-10-15: `BigWigsMods/LittleWigs` `LittleWigs.toc` has `## Dependencies: BigWigs` and `## LoadOnDemand: 1`.

**Risks and mitigations.** The plan rates the engine changes (A4, A5, C4, A12) medium-high confidence: they touch the most delicate code. The regression net is M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites, which must pass unchanged. Wrong-project installs are bounded by the conservative chain, TOC verification and undo. `plan.rs` is the busiest file in M2: keep commits small.

**Relation to siblings.** C4.2 adds `update --no-deps`, the update acceptance tests and bridge dependencies (`bridge_dependencies`, `first_install` on the report). C5 renders the report (item fields, dependency items, `bridge_dependency` warnings, install hints). C6 does the remove and update bookkeeping (`RemoveRequiredBy`, `still_required`, orphans). This bead must not add any of those, but its rounds already run for update's `Install` works, so update resolves dependencies the moment both B6 and this bead are on `main`.

comments.text:
**decided (3.4.1 implementation):**

- **No `DepList` yet.** C1 (3.1) has not landed. `FolderVerdict.dependencies` stays the required list (`Toc::dependency_folders()`), so optional dependencies are never collected and `unknown_condition` is never produced. Why: `FolderVerdict` is serialized, so changing its shape is a wire change that C1 owns. C1 introduces `DepList` and switches the fill; `UnresolvedReason::UnknownCondition` already exists with its warning text.
- **Needed folders** use C3's `needed_folders(primary, verdicts)`, computed in `try_candidate` over the folders this client installs. With no primary, every installed folder counts as the addon.
- **Dependency works are judged without `--force`.**
- **`--no-deps` still plans rule-3a `AddRequiredBy` edits.** Folders still unresolved warn `missing_dependency` with reason `not_requested`.
- **Plans with `no_deps: true`:**
  - install's target-defaulting probe: the requested refs alone pick the target;
  - `outdated --verify`: it verifies the updates themselves, and their dependencies download at update time.
- **Unresolved reasons beyond C3's** (wire values on `Unresolved.reason`):
  - `out_of_date`: the guard;
  - `limit_reached`: the message names `DEPENDENCY_MAX_DEPTH` or `DEPENDENCY_MAX_ADDONS`;
  - `not_requested`: `--no-deps`;
  - `not_shipped`: the resolved archive does not ship the folder for this client. It warns and records nothing.
- **Fixes:**
  - `managed_folder_missing` → `omaddons list -t <id> -v` (B9's `--reinstall` has not landed);
  - `no_source` → the text "no keyless source ships <D>; it may only be on CurseForge or Wago, which arrive in M5" (G1's `search` has not landed);
  - ambiguous, abandoned, out_of_date and limit → `omaddons install <top candidate> -t <id>`.
- **One outcome per ref.** A ref met earlier in the rounds is never planned again:
  - a ref planned by any round, round 0 included, gives a later requester whose folder is still absent `not_shipped`;
  - a failed ref adds the requester to `DepReport.failed`;
  - a skipped ref repeats its reason.
  - Round-0 failures seed this set as failed, so a dependency resolving to a ref the user named, which failed, is not planned twice.
- **Fetch-once is per command.** Each command revalidates, as install always has. The checkpoint test asserts one `releases/latest` per ref per command and one asset download overall.
- **Rejudge drop rule.** A dependency work or `AddRequiredBy`-only edit is dropped under the lock only when every requester was planned in this transaction and none still commits. A requester outside the transaction keeps it. A rejudge error still fails the whole target, as before.
- **Warnings that belong to no work go into `unchanged_warnings` as well,** so the commit keeps `missing_dependency`.
- **`require()` failures carry the owner's ref.** Install reads a ref-less failure as a target failure.
- **Progress:** `ProgressSink::grow(phase, n)` raises the Fetch, Download and Verify totals for each round.

title: Dependencies on the update path, update --no-deps and bridge dependencies
description:
## Background

M2 goals "current by default" and "complete installs" meet here: when a requester's new release starts requiring another project, `omaddons update` must install it in the same transaction, recorded as a dependency and undone with the update.

After C4.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1`), dependency rounds run for every planned install, and `update`'s `Update { addon }` becomes an `Install` work through `want()` (`src/engine/plan.rs:465-504`; line numbers as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter). So update already resolves dependencies. Still missing:
- `update --no-deps`. B6 left it out of `UpdateArgs` on purpose (vision rule DEC-1: a flag lands only with its behaviour).
- Proof of the update path, and two B6 mappings that would hide dependency failures: B6 turns planning-time `no_compatible_release`/`wrong_flavor` into `skipped/blocked` (decision M2-D41), and A6's `build(outcomes, run, requested)` maps failures to requested items only, so a failed dependency would make no item and no `partial`.
- Bridge dependencies, which C5 needs with a first-install marker.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/app/update.rs`, `src/engine/plan.rs` (bridge pass, `DepReport` fields), `tests/deps.rs`.

### 1. `update --no-deps`
`UpdateArgs.no_deps: bool` (help "Update only the named addons, not the ones their TOCs require"), passed as `TxRequest.no_deps`. As on install: no resolution or rounds, satisfaction still judged, rule-3a `AddRequiredBy` edits still planned, each unresolved required dependency warns `missing_dependency`.

### 2. Dependency failures on update (decision M2-D9)
A resolved dependency that fails to install makes the run partial and the requester still updates. B6's `blocked` mapping applies only to works the user's request produced (`Update { addon }`, `--channel` installs), never to a dependency's failure. For each `DepReport.failed` entry, pass `ItemRequest { request: <required folder>, target: <id>, addon: None }` to A6's `build`, so the `PlanFailure` becomes a failed item. Successful dependency items and the dependency item fields are C5's.

### 3. Re-installing a removed dependency
No new code: D absent with no record means the rounds install it as `Install { reason: Dependency, pin: Keep, channel: default_channel }` with `required_by: [requester]`. Dependencies never take the requester's channel, even under `update X --channel beta` (M2-D33).

### 4. Bridge dependencies
Rule (M2-D7): only the primary folder and the same-archive folders it transitively requires are followed. Required dependencies of **other** folders (bridge or plugin folders, such as a `Masque_<Addon>` integrating with an optional third-party addon) are **reported, not installed**, because following them would install addons nobody asked for (Masque for everyone installing Dominos); the TOC author means "works with X if present".
- **When:** after the last round (straight after round 0 under `--no-deps`), for every planned install work, requested and dependency works alike.
- **What:** C3's `bridge_dependencies(...)`: required external dependencies of installed folders outside the needed set, minus those satisfied against the **final** working view (`Blizzard_*`; same archive; present in AddOns in any class; installed by another work in this transaction). A bridge whose target installs in the same transaction is not reported.
- **Where:** C4.1's `DepReport` (keyed by addon name on `TargetPlan.dependencies`) gains `bridge_dependencies: Vec<BridgeDep { folder, requires }>` (both `FolderName`, sorted by folder then requires; wire shape `[{folder, requires}]`) and `first_install: bool`, true when the target had no record for the addon's ref before the transaction.
- **Use:** C5 adds the item field and the informational warning `bridge_dependency` only when `first_install` is true; updates keep the list and never repeat the warning.
- Bridges never add a round, fetch or install, and `rejudge` does not recompute them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `update` of a requester whose new release adds a required dependency installs it in the same transaction (one history line; dependency `reason: dependency, required_by: [<requester>]`); `undo` reverts both.
- A dependency the user removed earlier is re-installed with `reason: dependency` when the requester's new release requires it.
- `update --no-deps` installs only the requester and warns `missing_dependency`.
- `net.log`: each distinct ref fetched once across rounds on update.
- A dependency with no compatible release during update is a failed item (`request` = the folder), not `skipped/blocked`; the run is `partial`; the requester is updated.
- Dependencies of `update X --channel beta` use `default_channel`.
- Bridges: primary `Foo` plus `Foo_Masque` (requires absent `Masque`) reports `[{folder: "Foo_Masque", requires: "Masque"}]` with `first_install: true`; `Masque` is never fetched; a later update reports the same list with `first_install: false`; with `Masque` on disk or installed in the same transaction, nothing is reported.

## Test Plan

- E2E `tests/deps.rs`: A10's `Home::installed_behind` and `release_graph` (a newer release adding `## Dependencies`), `net_log` counters, record and history readers, undo.
- Engine API (`engine::run` in-process): bridge cases asserting `TxOutcomes.plan.targets[].dependencies`, unserialised until C5.
- Contract: an `update --no-deps` row.

## Considerations

- A pinned or current requester has no work and resolves nothing; intended.
- Collision hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x); `src/app/update.rs` (B6, E5.3).

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): `UpdateArgs`, the update flow and its A6 item mapping are what this bead extends.
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (Dependency rounds on install): the rounds, `TxRequest.no_deps` and the `DepReport` extended here.

Unblocks:
- C5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.5` (Dependency results in command output): renders `bridge_dependencies`, warns on `first_install`.
- C6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.6` (Dependency bookkeeping on update and remove): its update-side `RemoveRequiredBy` edits build on this update path.
- H2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` (Crash and concurrency coverage): crashes a dependency transaction once install and update both resolve dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: update of a requester whose new release adds a required dependency installs it in the same transaction, recorded reason dependency with the requester in required_by, and undo reverts both; a dependency the user removed earlier is re-installed with reason dependency when the requester's new release requires it; update --no-deps installs only the requester and warns missing_dependency; net.log shows each distinct ref fetched once across rounds on update; a dependency with no compatible release during update is a failed item whose request is the required folder, never skipped/blocked, the run is partial and the requester is still updated; dependency installs under update X --channel beta use default_channel; bridge dependencies are computed after the last round against the final working view and attached to the addon's dependency report as bridge_dependencies [{folder, requires}] with first_install true only on the addon's first install, a bridge requirement is never fetched or installed, and nothing is reported when the required folder is on disk or installed in the same transaction
close_reason: update resolves dependencies with --no-deps and failures as items; bridge dependencies reported; gate green

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Updates are the most-used M2 command, and publishers do add dependencies between releases. Without this bead an `update` could leave an addon that silently stops loading, the same failure "complete installs" removes for `install`. It also finishes the dependency report that C5 renders: bridge dependencies, which tell the owner that a plugin folder works with something not installed, without installing it. Both serve the thesis that every change is a verified, undoable transaction, with the reasons visible to humans and agents.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D7:** only the primary folder's required dependencies (and those of the same-archive folders it requires) are installed; bridge-folder dependencies are reported once; `OptionalDeps` never install. Why: user intent, no surprise installs. Rejected: following every folder's dependencies. The separate `bridge_dependency` warning code keeps "optional integration" distinct from `OptionalDeps` (never warned) and from `missing_dependency` (needed and absent).
- **M2-D9:** a resolved dependency that fails makes the run partial, the requester still updates; an unresolvable one is a warning. Why: partial means retryable work failed. Rejected: failing the requester; skipping silently.
- **M2-D41** (B6): a newer release of a *requested* addon that does not load on a client is `skipped/blocked`, not failed, because that is information. This bead keeps it from swallowing dependency failures, which M2-D9 says are failures.
- **M2-D33:** dependencies use `default_channel`, never the requester's channel, so a beta addon does not drag its dependencies onto beta. Rejected: inheriting the channel.
- **M2-D4** (B6): bare `update` means `--all`, so dependency resolution runs across every client by default; fetch-once across rounds keeps that cheap.

**Staging decision.** The plan sized C4 as one L task because splitting it "would leave a half-resolving planner". The split keeps the whole resolving loop in C4.1, which runs for every planned install. This bead adds only what is update-specific (the flag, the failure mapping, the tests) and the report-only bridge pass. Decided here: dependency failures reach A6 as `ItemRequest`s whose `request` is the required folder, the same string C5 uses for dependency items, so C5 extends rather than replaces it.

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`): `want()` resolves `Reinstall { addon }` (A3 renames it `Update`) to an install of the recorded ref and channel (`src/engine/plan.rs:485-502`); the plan's `rejudge` never resolves anything new; `RequestedChange` has no flag for dependency handling today. Live, 2026-10-15: `LittleWigs.toc` declares `## Dependencies: BigWigs`; BugSack v12.1.7 lists `!BugGrabber` only under `OptionalDeps`.

**Risks and mitigations.** Medium-high confidence, as for all engine work. The main risk is double-reporting or losing dependency failures between B6's mapping and A6's builder; the acceptance criterion on a failing dependency during update pins it. Bridge computation against the final working view must run after the last round, or bridges satisfied in the same transaction would be reported falsely; a test covers it.

**Relation to siblings.** C4.1 owns rounds, satisfaction, resolution, limits, locks and `install --no-deps`; do not re-implement any of it here. C5 turns `bridge_dependencies` and `first_install` into item fields and the `bridge_dependency` warning. C6 adds the update-side `RemoveRequiredBy` bookkeeping and orphan warnings when a new release stops requiring a dependency.
