title: Dependency results in command output
description:
## Background

Users must see which installs were dependencies and who needed them, and agents need the same facts in JSON (M2 goals "complete installs" and "no regression of M1 guarantees": the JSON contract stays one additive envelope). After C4.1 and C4.2 the engine installs dependencies, but nothing shows it:
- `InstallItem` (`src/app/install.rs:109-125`; line numbers as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter) has no `reason` or `required_by`, and `build_items` (`install.rs:725`) lists positional arguments only, so BigWigs installed for LittleWigs appears in history but not in `items`.
- C4.1's `DepReport` (`TargetPlan.dependencies`: installs, unmanaged, unresolved, failed) and C4.2's `bridge_dependencies` and `first_install` are `#[serde(skip)]`.
- The warning `bridge_dependency` does not exist.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/app/install.rs`, `src/app/outcome.rs` (A6's `ItemResult`, `build`, renderer), `src/error.rs` (`bridge_dependency`; the `WarningCode::ALL` count at `src/error.rs:746`), `tests/snapshots/install__*.snap`, `tests/deps.rs`, `tests/contract/matrix.rs`.

### Item fields (install and multi-target items)
- `reason`: `explicit` | `dependency` (`null` when no record is known, such as a parse failure);
- `required_by`: requester names;
- `bridge_dependencies`: `[{folder, requires}]`;
- `unresolved`: `[{folder, reason, candidates}]` for missing, ambiguous, `unknown_condition`, `out_of_date` and `limit_reached` entries (reasons as C4.1 serialises them; `candidates` are ref strings, at most 3, best first).
- Decided: all four are always present on install items (empty arrays when there is nothing), so the schema is stable. Under `-v` only, items add `optional_dependencies: [folder]`, the needed folders' `OptionalDeps`, which are never installed or warned about (omitted otherwise, like `asset_url`).
- `request` keeps its M1 type, `String`. Everything is additive; existing keys and their order are unchanged.

```json
"items":[
 {"request":"littlewigs","ref":"gh:BigWigsMods/LittleWigs","name":"LittleWigs","status":"installed","reason":"explicit","required_by":[],"bridge_dependencies":[],"unresolved":[]},
 {"request":"BigWigs","ref":"gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs","name":"BigWigs","status":"installed","reason":"dependency","required_by":["LittleWigs"],"bridge_dependencies":[],"unresolved":[]}]
```

### Dependency items
- One item per dependency install, built from `DepReport.installs` and `.failed`. **`request` is the required folder name** (`"BigWigs"`), so the M1 type is unchanged.
- Placed right after its first requester's item; dependencies of dependencies follow their own requester (resolution order).
- `status` is `installed`, or `failed` with the `PlanFailure`'s error (`details.required_by`). `partial()` now counts these items, replacing C4.1's extra count. Failures stay mirrored in `warnings`, as for every partial item.
- Records-only `required_by` edits on already-installed addons do not get items; they appear in the engine `Plan`'s `changes` (and `--dry-run` output) as `edit`.
- Human output appends `(dependency of LittleWigs)` (`(dependency of A and B)` for several). The design sketch is `retail: installed 2 addons (tx …)`, then `LittleWigs v12.1.3 (requested)` and `BigWigs v428 (dependency of LittleWigs)`; the layout is free, that information is binding.

### Warnings and commands
- `missing_dependency` comes from C4.1 with its fix (top candidate install argv; reinstall for `managed_folder_missing`; the no-source fix). If G1 (`search`) has landed and C4.1 used the text fix, switch it to `omaddons search <folder>`; if not, leave it: G1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7.1`) switches every interim no-source fix already on `main` when it lands (its own switch list names C4.1 and C5), so no follow-up bead is needed.
- **`bridge_dependency`** (new warning code), informational, one per `{folder, requires}`, **only when `first_install` is true**: "Masque_Dominos works with Masque, which is not installed", fix argv `omaddons install <arg> -t <id>`, where `<arg>` is the required folder when the catalog answers it by name or alias, else the ref C3's `resolve` finds; with neither, the fix is the no-source fix and no hint is added. Updates keep `bridge_dependencies` in the item and never repeat the warning.
- `commands`: the undo hint first (unchanged), C4.1's `list_unmanaged` hint, then at most three `install <candidate> -t <id>` hints (action `install`): unresolved candidates in item order, then bridge requirements.

### Multi-target items (A6)
`ItemResult` gets the same four fields. A6 already declares `reason` and `required_by` on `ItemResult` (filled from the planned record, omitted for items without one); this bead adds `bridge_dependencies` and `unresolved` and fills all four for dependency data. A6's `build` emits dependency items after their requester per target, extending C4.2's failed-dependency `ItemRequest`s to every `DepReport.installs` entry. The renderer uses the same suffix. `update` shows them now; `sync` and `copy` inherit them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Insta snapshots, JSON and human: an install with one dependency (two items as above, `(dependency of LittleWigs)`); a missing dependency with candidates (`unresolved` entry, warning fix argv for the top candidate, at most three install hints); a missing dependency without candidates (no-source fix); a bridge dependency (item field, warning, hint).
- A second install or update of the same addon keeps `bridge_dependencies` and emits no `bridge_dependency` warning.
- A failed dependency is a `failed` item whose `request` is the folder; the run is `partial`.
- `update` items carry the four fields, with dependency items after their requester.
- Existing install snapshots change only by additive keys; the contract matrix passes; `bridge_dependency` is registered (count updated) and every new fix argv runs or is listed text.

## Test Plan

- E2E snapshots in `tests/deps.rs` on A10's `release_graph` fixtures; reviewed `tests/snapshots/install__*.snap` updates; contract rows for install with a dependency and with a missing one; unit tests for item ordering.

## Considerations

- M1 consumers of `install --json` must keep working: add, never rename or reorder.
- Collision hot spots: `src/error.rs` (several beads add codes); `src/app/outcome.rs` (created by A6, used by every multi-target command).

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.6` (Shared multi-target outcome): `ItemResult`, `build` and the renderer that multi-target items extend.
- C4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.2` (Dependencies on the update path and bridge dependencies): the complete `DepReport`, with `bridge_dependencies` and `first_install`.

Unblocks:
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): records the new item fields and the `bridge_dependency` warning.
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit): audits the new item fields, the warning and its fixes.
acceptance_criteria: install items and multi-target items gain reason (explicit|dependency), required_by, bridge_dependencies [{folder, requires}] and unresolved [{folder, reason, candidates}], always present on install items, with optional_dependencies only under -v; request stays a string and every change to install's JSON is additive; each dependency install is its own item whose request is the required folder name, placed right after its requester, rendered in human output as (dependency of LittleWigs); a failed dependency is a failed item with details.required_by and the run is partial; bridge_dependency is a new registered warning emitted only on the addon's first install, with an install fix argv, and a later install or update keeps bridge_dependencies without repeating the warning; commands keep the undo hint first and add at most three install <candidate> -t <id> hints; insta snapshots (JSON and human) cover an install with one dependency, a missing dependency with candidates, a missing dependency without candidates and a bridge dependency; update items carry the same fields with dependency items after their requester; existing install snapshots change only by additive keys and the contract matrix passes
close_reason: dependency items after their requester, item dependency fields, bridge_dependency on first install, install hints; install and multi-target outputs; gate green

**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

- **M2-D7:** only required dependencies of the primary folder (and same-archive folders it requires) are installed; bridge-folder dependencies are reported once; `OptionalDeps` never install. Why: user intent, no surprise installs. Rejected: following every folder's dependencies. Hence `bridge_dependency` warns only on the first install, and `OptionalDeps` appear only under `-v`.
- **M2-D9:** a failed resolved dependency is a failed item (partial); an unresolvable one is a warning. Why: partial means "retryable work failed". Rejected: failing the requester; skipping silently.
- **M2-D32:** contract additions are additive (one deliberate type change elsewhere, in dry-run plan output); `schema_version` stays 1.0 until the M4 freeze. Why: that is M1's practice (DEC-4: contract additions are allowed before the freeze and recorded on the vision bead). Rejected: bumping the schema now. Hence `request` stays a string and dependency items use the required folder name as their `request`.
- Default from the plan's rules for unanswered questions: verbose material goes behind `-v`; short enumerations may stay in default output. `unresolved` reasons and `bridge_dependencies` are short; optional dependencies are verbose.
- Default: never emit a hint for a command a later task adds. Hence the `search` fix waits for G1.

**Staging decisions taken here** (record with `decided:` when implementing): the four item fields are always present on install items; `optional_dependencies` is a `-v`-only item key (the plan says optional dependencies are "listed only under -v" without naming a key); the bridge hint's argument is the catalog name when the catalog answers the folder, else the resolved ref; at most three install hints in total.

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`): `InstallItem` has `request, ref, name, status, from_version, to_version, version_confidence, channel, folders, error` and `-v`-only `asset_url` (`src/app/install.rs:109-125`); `build_items` iterates positional arguments only (`install.rs:725-843`); `install`'s `partial()` counts failed items (`install.rs:196`); `Warning` has `code, message, fix` and no details (`src/error.rs:561-565`); `WarningCode::ALL.len()` is asserted at 22 (`src/error.rs:746`); four install snapshots exist (`install__install_{success,unchanged,partial,ambiguous}.snap`).

**Risks and mitigations.** Low technical risk: it is output over data C4.1 and C4.2 compute. The risk is contract drift (a renamed key, a reordered item list, a fix that does not run). Mitigations: reviewed snapshots, the contract matrix, and H1's audit that every fix argv runs.

**Relation to the C4 split.** C5 waits for C4.2, not only C4.1, because bridge dependencies and the first-install marker exist only after C4.2. C4.1 already counts failed dependencies as partial for `install` and C4.2 does so for `update` through failed-dependency `ItemRequest`s; this bead turns those into full items and removes C4.1's extra count.

title: Dependency bookkeeping on update and remove; orphans
description:
## Background

Without bookkeeping, `required_by` rots. Removing a requester leaves dependencies nothing needs, and removing a dependency silently breaks its dependents. This bead keeps `required_by` true on remove and update, warns when a removal breaks or orphans something, and makes orphans visible in `status`, `list` and `info`. It serves the M2 goals "complete installs" (a broken dependency is announced, not silent), "sole authority" (the tool knows which addons are only there for others) and "no regression of M1 guarantees" (every edit is undoable).

Today (line numbers as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- `TargetPlanner::remove` (`src/engine/plan.rs:861-898`) plans folder removals for the named addon and touches no other record.
- `build_install` copies `required_by` from the existing record unchanged (`plan.rs:828`), so an update never drops a requester.
- `AddonRecord.reason` and `required_by` exist (`src/model.rs:536-538`) and nothing reads them.
- `StatusTarget` (`src/app/status.rs:57-87`) has no orphan count; `recommendations()` (`status.rs:353`) has no remove hint; `ListAddon` (`src/app/list.rs:66-82`) and `InstalledInfo` (`src/app/info.rs:65-79`) show neither field.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/engine/plan.rs` (remove and update bookkeeping), `src/engine/tx.rs` (fix filled after commit), `src/app/remove.rs`, `src/app/status.rs`, `src/app/list.rs`, `src/app/info.rs`, `src/error.rs` (two warnings; the `WarningCode::ALL` count at `src/error.rs:746`), `tests/deps.rs`, `tests/status.rs`, `tests/list.rs`, their snapshots.

An **orphan** is a record with `reason: dependency` and an empty `required_by`. Explicitly installed addons are never orphans.

### Remove X
- If `X.required_by` is non-empty (ignoring requesters this same transaction removes), the remove **still succeeds** (the vision's rule) with the new warning **`still_required`**: "BigWigs is required by LittleWigs, which will not load without it". Its fix is `omaddons undo <tx>` as a command with argv, filled in after commit. Decided for `--dry-run` (no tx exists): the text fix "nothing is removed under --dry-run; after the remove, `omaddons undo <tx>` restores it".
- Every record whose `required_by` contains X gets `Edit(RemoveRequiredBy(X))` in the same transaction, folded into that record's work when it has one (one work per addon, A4.1). Records this transaction removes get none. History records each as a `record` op carrying `edit: {"required_by_remove": "X"}` (A4.2) when that record has no other change in the transaction; folded into a work that also changes it, the edit rides that addon's ordinary snapshot-restore undo, as A4.2 rules.
- A record orphaned by that adds the new warning **`orphaned_dependency`**, fix argv `omaddons remove <names…> -t <id>`: one command naming every addon this transaction orphaned on the target.
- The transaction kind stays `remove` (A4.1: in a mix, edits are ignored when choosing the kind). The edit's guard is "still recorded, at any release", so an unrelated concurrent update of the dependency does not abort the remove.

### Update (any planned install of an addon that already has a record)
- When the requester R's new release's **needed folders** (primary plus same-archive folders it transitively requires; C4.1 keeps `primary` and per-folder `deps` on the work) no longer require any folder of a record D that lists R in `required_by`, plan `Edit(RemoveRequiredBy(R))` on D, folded into D's work when it has one.
- If D's `required_by` becomes empty and `D.reason == dependency`, add `orphaned_dependency` with fix `omaddons remove D -t <id>`.
- Decided: these edits are planned under `--no-deps` too (bookkeeping installs nothing; C4.1 decided the same for `AddRequiredBy`).
- Conversely, updating a requester whose new release requires a dependency the user removed earlier re-installs it with `reason: dependency`; C4.2 covers that.
- A requester with no planned work (current, pinned) changes nothing.

### Explicit install of a dependency promotes it
The install carries `reason: Explicit` (A3's carry-over table), as a records-only `SetReason` edit when the release is already current (A4.3). Promoted addons are never orphans. No new code; test it.

### Fix after commit
`commit_target` (`src/engine/tx.rs:288`; the tx id is created at `tx.rs:297`) fills `still_required`'s fix. E3 needs the same hook for `local_changes_replaced`: reuse it if E3 has landed, else add a small generic one both can use.

### `status`, `list`, `info`
- `StatusTarget` gains `orphans: n`, counted from the record, also under `--cached` (no I/O beyond the record it already reads):

  ```json
  "updates": {"available": 2, "pinned": 1, "blocked": 0, "failed": 0, "unchecked": 0, "checked_at": "2026-10-15T20:01:02Z", "stale": false},
  "drift": [{"addon": "Plater", "state": "modified", "files": 2}],
  "adoptable": 3,
  "orphans": 0
  ```
  (`updates` and `adoptable` are B8's, `drift` is E3's.)
- `recommendations()` adds **`remove_orphans`**: `omaddons remove <names…> -t <id>`, one per target with orphans, `destructive: true`. Order: (1) existing journal and state fixes; (2) `reinstall` (E3); (3) `update` (B8); (4) `adopt` (E5.3); (5) `check_updates` (B8); (6) `remove_orphans`; (7) existing `forget_target` and `inspect`. Orphans are only reported and recommended, never removed automatically.
- `list`: a `dep` marker for `reason: dependency` (`dependency of LittleWigs` under `-v`) and an `orphan` flag. JSON per addon gains `reason`, `required_by`, `orphan` (bool).
- `info <addon>`: per installed target, `reason`, `required_by`, `orphan`.

### Undo (A4.2 semantics, relied on)
Undoing the remove restores X from the snapshot and applies the inverse edit (`AddRequiredBy(X)`) to D's **current** record, so `required_by` comes back exactly even if D was updated in between, with no `undo_conflict`. Ops carrying `edit` are excluded from undo's conflict check, touched folders and index changes; snapshot restores drop `required_by` names no longer recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Removing BigWigs while LittleWigs requires it succeeds, with `still_required` naming LittleWigs and fix argv `omaddons undo <tx>`.
- Removing LittleWigs makes BigWigs (`reason: dependency`) an orphan: `orphaned_dependency` with fix argv `omaddons remove BigWigs -t <id>`; one history line of kind `remove` whose ops include a `record` op with `edit: {"required_by_remove": "LittleWigs"}`; `status` shows `orphans: 1` and a `remove_orphans` recommendation; running that argv clears it.
- An update whose new release drops a dependency plans the `RemoveRequiredBy` edit and warns `orphaned_dependency`.
- An explicitly installed (or promoted) addon never becomes an orphan.
- Undoing the remove restores `required_by` exactly, also when the dependency was updated in between.
- `remove LittleWigs BigWigs` raises neither warning.
- `list` and `info` show `reason`, `required_by` and `orphan`; `status --cached` shows `orphans`.
- Both warnings are registered (count updated) with fixes; contract snapshots are reviewed.

## Test Plan

- E2E in `tests/deps.rs`: install LittleWigs (with its BigWigs dependency, C4.1 fixtures), then each remove, update (`Home::installed_behind` with a release dropping `## Dependencies`), promote and undo sequence above; A10's record and history readers.
- `tests/status.rs` and `tests/list.rs`: snapshot updates, `--cached` included; info JSON assertions.
- Unit: orphan counting; the update-side edit computation over synthetic records and `DepList`s.

## Considerations

- `still_required` names only dependents that remain after the transaction.
- Keep `status --cached` under its 5 ms budget: the count is one pass over records already loaded.
- Collision hot spots: `src/app/status.rs` (A2, B8, C6, E3, E5.x), `src/engine/plan.rs` (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x), `src/error.rs` (several), `src/engine/tx.rs` (E3 fills fixes after commit too).

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.2` (Reversible required_by edit ops): `required_by_remove` edits must undo in place without conflicts before remove and update may produce them.
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): the update path where requester releases change.
- B8 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.8` (status update counts, adoptable count, hints): the `StatusTarget` additions and recommendation order this bead extends.
- C4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.2` (Dependencies on the update path): dependency records exist, and update works carry `primary` and per-folder `DepList`s.

Unblocks:
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit): runs the `remove_orphans` recommendation and checks both warnings.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): documents `still_required`, orphans and the new keys.
acceptance_criteria: removing BigWigs while LittleWigs requires it succeeds with the new warning still_required naming LittleWigs and fix argv omaddons undo <tx> filled in after commit (a text fix under --dry-run); removing LittleWigs plans Edit(RemoveRequiredBy(LittleWigs)) on BigWigs in the same remove-kind transaction, recorded as a record op with edit required_by_remove, and because BigWigs is reason dependency with an empty required_by it raises the new warning orphaned_dependency with fix argv omaddons remove BigWigs -t <id>; status shows orphans 1 per target (also under --cached) and a destructive remove_orphans recommendation placed after check_updates and before forget_target, and running it clears the orphan; an update whose new release's needed folders no longer require a dependency plans the RemoveRequiredBy edit and warns orphaned_dependency; an explicitly installed or promoted addon never becomes an orphan; undoing the remove restores required_by exactly, also when the dependency was updated in between, with no undo_conflict; removing requester and dependency together raises neither warning; list and info show reason, required_by and orphan per addon and target; orphans are never removed automatically; both warning codes are registered with fixes and snapshots are reviewed
close_reason: required_by kept true on remove and update; still_required and orphaned_dependency; orphans in status (remove_orphans), list and info; gate green

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Dependency installs are only half a feature if the records go stale afterwards. Once C4.1 records BigWigs as `reason: dependency, required_by: ["LittleWigs"]`, every later remove and update must keep that true, or two things go wrong: removing BigWigs silently breaks LittleWigs in game, and removing LittleWigs leaves BigWigs installed forever for nobody. This bead makes both visible (`still_required`, `orphaned_dependency`), keeps `required_by` correct across updates, and gives `status` an `orphans` count with a one-command cleanup that a human or agent runs deliberately. It is also the vision's dependency checkpoint, as amended by M2-D10: "Removing BigWigs warns `still_required`, and removing LittleWigs reports BigWigs as `orphaned_dependency`." And it pre-builds the orphan detector that the M4 doctor wraps as a finding: M2 ships the detectors as library functions with typed results, not a doctor command.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D35:** `required_by` edits are history ops with an `edit` field that undo reverses in place on the current record, and that conflict detection ignores. Why: otherwise undoing a remove after the dependency was updated would raise `undo_conflict` on the dependency's folders, or a snapshot restore would roll its record back to the pre-update release while the new folders stay on disk. Rejected: snapshot restore for every records-only change. This is the plan's third review pass finding on "undo of `required_by` edits"; it is why this bead waits for A4.2.
- **M2-D6:** records-only work is first-class in the engine, so the `RemoveRequiredBy` edits ride in the same journaled, snapshotted, undoable transaction as the remove or update. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature.
- The vision's rule that removing a needed addon still succeeds: omaddons warns and offers undo, it does not refuse.
- Orphans are never removed automatically (vision rule): the owner may want BigWigs for itself. The `remove_orphans` recommendation is `destructive: true` so agents know.
- Same reasoning as **M2-D27** (B8: status attention means health, so pending updates are not attention and `status --check` is not permanently red; rejected: treating updates as attention): orphans are a count and a recommendation, never an attention string. The plan's only new attention values are `addon_modified` and `addon_folder_missing`.
- Carry-over rules (A3): `update` passes the recorded reason, so an updated dependency stays a dependency; an explicit `install` promotes it. Without that, orphan detection would break on the first update.

**Staging decisions taken here** (record with `decided:`): the dry-run text fix for `still_required`; `RemoveRequiredBy` bookkeeping also under `--no-deps`; `still_required` names only dependents that survive the transaction; the after-commit fix hook is shared with E3.

**Facts verified during planning** (code at `e902d36`): `TargetPlanner::remove` touches only the named addon (`src/engine/plan.rs:861-898`); `build_install` copies `required_by` unchanged (`plan.rs:828`); `next_record` lets the last work for an addon win (`src/engine/tx.rs:661-674`), which is why edits fold into an existing work; undo adds every op's folder to `touched` (`src/engine/undo.rs:638`) and writes old index entries back for touched folders (`undo.rs:840-846`), which A4.2's exclusion fixes; `recommendations()` already emits `forget_target`, `inspect` and `list_unmanaged` hints (`src/app/status.rs:353-401`); the warning count is asserted at 22 (`src/error.rs:746`).

**Risks and mitigations.** Medium-high confidence: the engine side is small once A4.2 exists, and the status, list and info parts are additive. Risks: double edits on one addon (mitigated by folding into the existing work), a status budget regression (the count reads records already loaded), and recommendation drift (H1 runs every recommendation on a fresh copy of each scenario home, destructive ones included).

**Relation to the C4 split.** C6 waits for C4.2, not only C4.1: the update-side bookkeeping needs the update path with dependencies, and the per-work `primary` and `DepList` that C4.1 keeps. C4.2 owns the converse case (re-installing a removed dependency when a new release needs it again).

comments.text:
**done:** `required_by` now stays true on remove and update. A removal that breaks a dependent warns, a dependency left required by nothing is an orphan, and orphans show in `status`, `list` and `info`. `argc gate` passes: 1178 tests, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical.

**Engine (`src/engine/plan.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs`):**
- **`TargetPlanner::unrequire`** runs after the dependency rounds and handovers, before bridges.
  - **Removed X** (a folder remove or a forget): every record listing X drops it with `Edit(RemoveRequiredBy(X))`, unless that record is removed in the same transaction.
  - **Updated requester R** (a folder work with `inspected` on an addon already recorded): a record D listing R drops R when none of D's folders is in R's new `deps.requires`. D's folders are taken from D's own planned work, else from its record. This is planned under `--no-deps` too.
  - A requester with no work (current or pinned) changes nothing.
  - Edits go through `bookkeep`, which `require` now shares (the old `AddRequiredBy` path with the same failure handling). They fold into the owner's work when it has one.
  - The kind stays as before. A remove plus edits is a `remove` (A4.1), an update plus edits an `update`.
  - `RemoveRequiredBy`'s guard is A4's "still recorded", so a concurrent update of the dependency does not abort the remove.
- **`plan::bookkeeping_warnings(record, works, target, tx)`** is pure.
  - **`still_required`:** one per removed addon whose `required_by` names addons that stay after the transaction. The message reads "On retail, BigWigs is required by LittleWigs, which will not load without it". The fix is `omaddons undo <tx>`, or the text "nothing is removed under --dry-run; after the remove, `omaddons undo <tx>` restores it".
  - **`orphaned_dependency`:** one per target, naming every addon this transaction turned into an orphan (it was not an orphan before and is one after). The fix argv is `omaddons remove <names…> -t <id>`, with names sorted ignoring case.
  - **Plan time:** the warnings are pushed to `tp.warnings` (dry runs show them).
  - **Commit:** `locked()` raises them again after the commit, from the committed works and the record read under the lock, with `Some(tx)`. This is the same post-commit hook E3 uses for `local_changes_replaced`; no new hook was needed.
- **`AddonRecord::is_orphan()`** (`src/model.rs`): `reason == dependency` and `required_by` empty.

**Surfaces:**
- **`status`:**
  - `StatusTarget.orphans` (a count from the record, `--cached` too; 0 for a missing client).
  - `orphan_names` is kept off the wire.
  - The text line shows `· N orphan(s)`.
  - `recommendations()` adds `remove_orphans` = `omaddons remove <names…> -t <id>`, `destructive: true`, one per target, after `check_updates` and before the attention fixes (`inspect`, `forget_target`). The order is reinstall, update, check_updates, remove_orphans, attention fixes, list_unmanaged; E5.3's adopt is not on `main` yet.
- **`list`:** each addon gains `reason`, `required_by` and `orphan`. The table flags `orphan`, `dep`, or `dependency of X, Y` under `-v`.
- **`info`:** each installed record gains `reason`, `required_by` and `orphan`, and the text line gains "· dependency of X" or "· a dependency nothing requires".
- **README:**
  - `remove`'s Dependencies paragraph;
  - install's bookkeeping paragraph;
  - `status` `orphans` and the recommendation list;
  - list/info fields;
  - both warning rows;
  - the "What works today" dependencies row.
- `TEXT_FIXES` adds the `still_required` dry-run text.

**Tests:**
- **Unit, `plan::tests::bookkeeping_warns_once_per_still_required_removal_and_once_for_every_orphan`:** synthetic records and works.
  - Removing a requester orphans Ace and Lib in one warning (with fix `remove Ace Lib -t retail`), while Big (still required by Plater) and Promoted (explicit) are not orphans.
  - Removing Big with Plater warns `still_required` naming Little only, with the undo argv, or the text fix without a tx.
  - Removing everything together warns nothing.
- **Unit, `status::tests::orphans_are_recommended_after_the_update_check_and_before_attention`.**
- **`tests/deps.rs` (+6):**
  - **Removing BigWigs while LittleWigs requires it:** the dry run gives a text fix and changes nothing. The real remove warns `still_required` with fix argv `omaddons undo <tx>`, and LittleWigs is untouched. Undo restores BigWigs as a dependency of LittleWigs.
  - **Removing LittleWigs:**
    - warns `orphaned_dependency` with fix argv `omaddons remove BigWigs -t retail`;
    - BigWigs becomes reason dependency with `required_by: []`;
    - the history line is a `remove` with a `required_by_remove: LittleWigs` op on BigWigs;
    - `status` and `status --cached` show `orphans: 1` and a destructive `remove_orphans` with that argv;
    - `list` and `info` show reason, required_by and orphan;
    - running the recommendation leaves `orphans: 0` and no hint.
  - **Undo after an update:** after removing LittleWigs and updating BigWigs to v2, `undo <remove tx>` restores LittleWigs and BigWigs v2 with `required_by: [LittleWigs]`, with no `undo_conflict`.
  - **Removing together:** `remove littlewigs bigwigs` raises neither warning and records no edit ops.
  - **An update dropping a dependency:** a LittleWigs v2 that requires nothing makes `update --refresh`, with and without `--no-deps`, drop LittleWigs from BigWigs. It warns `orphaned_dependency`, and the history line is an `update` with the `required_by_remove` op.
  - **Promotion:** after installing LittleWigs then `install bigwigs` (explicit, still required by LittleWigs), removing LittleWigs warns no orphan, and `status` shows 0.
- **Contract snapshots** `status_ok`, `status_check_failed` and `list_ok` were reviewed: they add only `orphans: 0` and `orphan`/`reason`/`required_by`.

**Wire names:**
- warning codes `still_required` and `orphaned_dependency` (WarningCode::ALL is now 33);
- status key `orphans`;
- recommendation action `remove_orphans`;
- list and info keys `reason`, `required_by`, `orphan`;
- text flags `dep` and `orphan`.

**Constants:** none.

title: Wire the WoWInterface and Tukui indexes into dependency resolution
description:
## Background

C3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.3`) defines dependency resolution as a pure chain over lookup traits (`DepLookups { managed, catalog, tukui: Option<&dyn TukuiDirs>, wowi: Option<&dyn WowiDirs>, … }`). C4.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1`) runs the rounds with the catalog only; its `EngineCtx`/`PlanCtx` index-lookup fields stay `None` until this bead fills them (`Engine::new` in `src/app/engine.rs` builds the `EngineCtx`, `src/engine/tx.rs:102`; line numbers as of `e902d36`, symbol names are what matter).

Without this bead, a dependency only Tukui or WoWInterface distributes (an ElvUI plugin when the catalog lacks ElvUI, a WoWInterface-only library) ends as `missing_dependency` (`no_source`) although a keyless source has it. This serves the M2 goals **complete installs** and **more keyless sources**.

## Technical Approach

### The two resolution steps this bead enables

After the catalog step misses, in order (the first unique hit wins):
- **Tukui.** The list's `directories` contain `D`, giving `tukui:<slug>` (`via: tukui`).
- **WoWInterface.** Projects whose sanitised `UIDir` contains `D` are ranked by: (1) single-folder project (`UIDir == [D]`); (2) `UIName` normalised equals `D` normalised; (3) `UICompatibility` maps to the target's family (a hint only); (4) `UIDownloadTotal`; (5) `UIDate`. Auto-resolve only when the top candidate is strictly better than the second on criterion 1 or 2, **and** its `UIDate` is within `DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE` (730 days). Otherwise the result is `Ambiguous { reason: wowi_ambiguous | wowi_abandoned }` with the top three as candidates.

C3 ranks; this bead supplies the data. C4.1 plans resolved refs like any install (D3/D4 fetch, MD5 verification), and its out-of-date guard still applies.

### Tukui lookup

- A `TukuiDirs` adapter over `TukuiIndex` (id, slug, name, author, version, patch, directories, last_update; this lookup reads `slug`, `name` and `directories`), the memo's `tukui_list`, read through D4's `ReleaseCache::tukui_list()` with `Window` freshness: free inside `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 min), else one `GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addons` (purpose `tukui-list`).
- It SHOULD read or fetch on its first call only; the chain reaches Tukui only after a catalog miss, so a catalog-resolved dependency costs no `tukui-list` request.

### WoWInterface lookup, loaded lazily

- Load `WowiIndex` **lazily, only when the catalog and Tukui lookups missed**, so most installs never touch the 1.5 MB index. Load at most once per command, shared across targets and rounds (for example a `OnceLock` inside the adapter that `app::engine::Engine` owns).
- Loading is D2's `WowiIndex::load_or_refresh(paths, http, policy)`: refresh when the stored index (`<cache>/omaddons/wowi/index.json`) is older than `max(WOWI_FILELIST_MIN_AGE, server max-age)` (1 h and `max-age=3600` today) or on `--refresh`, purpose `wowi-filelist`, gzip-encoded. An online refresh failure falls back to the stale index with `stale_check`; no index at all gives `None`.
- The adapter maps `by_folder(D)` hits to C3's project shape: uid, `name`, sanitised `dirs`, families from `compat[].version` via `RulesTable::family_for(version, InstallKind::Battlenet)` (`src/rules.rs:625`; a hint, since `UICompatibility` lags), `downloads`, `date_ms`.

### Enabled sources

- `[sources.wowi] enabled = false` or `[sources.tukui] enabled = false` (`SourceConfig`, `src/state/config.rs:141`; D3 wires the flags for every source) makes that lookup `None`, and the step is skipped. Disabling `wowi` also means no filelist refresh.
- When a dependency ends `no_source` while a step was skipped (disabled, no index, offline without a cached index), the `missing_dependency` message names the skipped source and why. No new data key.

### Offline

- Use the cached indexes regardless of age and warn `stale_check` **once per command**, not once per dependency.
- **Never trigger a filelist download just to resolve a dependency under `--offline`.** With no cached index, skip WoWInterface; with no `tukui_list` in the memo, skip Tukui.

**Files:** `src/app/engine.rs` (building the adapters and passing them into the lookup fields C4.1 added), `src/engine/plan.rs` (handing them to `DepLookups`), `tests/deps.rs` (new cases), dependency fixtures built with D2's `wowi_filelist`/`wowi_details` and D4's Tukui builders (`tests/common/wowi.rs`, `tests/common/tukui.rs`) and A10's `release_graph`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An ElvUI plugin fixture whose TOC requires `ElvUI` resolves to `tukui:elvui` when the catalog has no hit, and installs it in the same transaction with `reason: dependency` and the plugin in `required_by`.
- A WoWInterface-only dependency (a synthetic index with a unique, recent single-folder project) resolves to `wowi:<id>` and installs with MD5 verification.
- An abandoned WoWInterface project (`UIDate` older than 730 days) is not auto-installed: the run carries a `missing_dependency` warning with the candidate, and is not partial.
- An install whose dependencies all resolve from the catalog makes no `wowi-filelist` request (`net.log` count by purpose). Two WoWInterface-only dependencies in one command, with a stale index, cost one `wowi-filelist` request (loaded once per command).
- `--offline` with a cached index resolves the dependency from it, warns `stale_check` once and makes no request (the dependency's install then follows the offline rules: memo and blob cache, else an `offline` item failure); with no cached index it makes no request and reports `missing_dependency`.
- `sources.wowi.enabled = false` makes a WoWInterface-only dependency `missing_dependency` without any `wowi-filelist` request; `sources.tukui.enabled = false` likewise skips the Tukui step.

## Test Plan

E2E in `tests/deps.rs`: a pre-written WoWInterface index (aged via its `fetched_at`), Tukui list/addon/download fixtures (zip MD5 as `ETag`), `release_graph` archives with `## Dependencies`; requests asserted with A10's `net_log(home).count(host, purpose)`.

## Considerations

- ElvUI is in the built-in catalog (C2), so the Tukui-step test must drop it with a `catalog.d` override (`remove = true`); with the entry present, the catalog step resolves the same ref first.
- Lookups are local: no dependency name is ever sent to a service. WoWInterface's compatibility tags never exclude a build (M2-D11); TOC verification decides.
- `src/engine/plan.rs` is a collision hot spot (A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x); keep this bead's change there to passing the lookups through.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- C3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.3` (The dependency resolver (pure)): defines `DepLookups`, `TukuiDirs`, `WowiDirs` and the WoWInterface ranking this bead feeds.
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (Dependency rounds on install): adds the `EngineCtx`/`PlanCtx` lookup fields and the rounds that call `resolve`. Only C4.1 is needed, not C4.2: the update path and bridge dependencies do not change how lookups are built.
- D2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.2` (The WoWInterface index): `WowiIndex::load_or_refresh`, `by_folder` and the sanitised index this bead reads.
- D3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.3` (The WoWInterface source): a resolved `wowi:` dependency must install, and the source enable flags exist from D3.
- D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4` (The Tukui source): the memo's `tukui_list`, `ReleaseCache::tukui_list()`, and installable `tukui:` refs.

Unblocks:
- H7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7` (M2 checkpoint verification): the "complete installs from keyless sources" checkpoint covers dependencies that only Tukui or WoWInterface provide.
acceptance_criteria: An ElvUI plugin fixture whose TOC requires ElvUI resolves to tukui:elvui when the catalog has no hit (ElvUI dropped with a catalog.d remove override) and installs it in the same transaction with reason dependency and the plugin in required_by; a WoWInterface-only dependency (a synthetic index with a unique, recent single-folder project) resolves to wowi:<id> and installs with MD5 verification; an abandoned WoWInterface project (UIDate older than DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE, 730 days) is not auto-installed and yields a missing_dependency warning carrying the candidate without making the run partial; an install whose dependencies all resolve from the catalog makes no wowi-filelist request; the WoWInterface index is loaded at most once per command and only after catalog and Tukui lookups missed; --offline resolves from cached indexes, warns stale_check once and never triggers a filelist download (the dependency then installs only from the memo and blob cache, else fails offline), and with no cached index reports missing_dependency without any request; sources.wowi.enabled = false or sources.tukui.enabled = false skips that lookup and makes no request to it
close_reason: Dependencies resolve from the Tukui list and the WoWInterface index after the catalog, each loaded once per command and only when reached

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** The dependency engine (C4.1) can land and prove the LittleWigs → BigWigs checkpoint with the catalog alone, which keeps the critical path short. Two keyless ecosystems still matter for completeness: Tukui (ElvUI and its plugins) and WoWInterface (thousands of projects, many libraries). This small task plugs their indexes into the resolver C3 defined, so "complete installs" covers dependencies that only those sources distribute, without making ordinary installs any slower or chattier.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D8:** resolution chain catalog → Tukui → WoWInterface (unique, recent, not out of date) → `missing_dependency`. WoWInterface's 781 shared folder names and stale projects (Details! from 2020) make blind lookups dangerous. Rejected: taking the most-downloaded WoWInterface project, which would install stale builds.
- **M2-D11:** WoWInterface's `UICompatibility` never excludes a build; it lags the game by patches (no 5.x and nothing past 12.1.0, verified). In ranking it is only a hint; TOC verification decides. Rejected: treating it as release metadata.
- **M2-D12:** the WoWInterface index is cached by `max-age` only and stored slim, because the service sends no validators and ignores conditional requests (verified). Rejected: conditional GET (impossible) and keeping the raw 5.6 MB body.
- **M2-D13:** Tukui assets are deferred tokens; only version metadata (including `directories`) is memoised as `tukui_list`. That is what this bead reads. Rejected: storing the list's `url`, which expires within seconds.
- **M2-D37:** batch-style lookups use the 15-minute `Window`; the Tukui list follows it, so a run of installs costs at most one `tukui-list` request per window.
- **Lazy index rule** (from the task itself): load the WoWInterface index only when catalog and Tukui missed, so most installs never read the 1.5 MB index; never download the filelist to resolve a dependency under `--offline`.
- **Edge choice:** C7 waits for C4.1 only, not for all of C4. C4.2 (update path, bridge dependencies) does not change how lookups are built, so waiting for it would only delay this task.
- Staging decisions made when writing this bead: the Tukui adapter is lazy too (first call only), and a `no_source` result names skipped sources in its message rather than in a new data key.

**Facts verified during planning** (live, 2026-10-15; line numbers as of `e902d36`):
- WoWInterface `filelist.json`: 5,619,970 bytes decoded, 659,496 gzipped, 8,218 entries, `max-age=3600`, no ETag or Last-Modified, conditional headers ignored; `UIDir` arrays up to 74 entries; 4,297 entries carry `UICompatibility`, none 5.x and none past 12.1.0.
- `!BugGrabber`, LibStub, ElvUI and Auctionator are not on WoWInterface.
- Tukui `GET /v1/addons`: 2 entries with `directories` (ElvUI: `ElvUI, ElvUI_Libraries, ElvUI_Options`), `no-store`, no ETag.
- `SourceConfig { enabled, credential }` is parsed (`src/state/config.rs:141`) and read by nothing yet; `WOWI_FILELIST_MIN_AGE` (1 h) and `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 min) exist in `src/politeness.rs`; `Paths::wowi_cache_dir()` is reserved (`src/state/paths.rs:273`).

**Risks and mitigations.** "Dependency resolution installs the wrong project" (medium likelihood, medium impact) is mitigated by C3's guards; this bead must not weaken them, for example by mapping compatibility into a filter. "WoWI API drift" (medium/medium) is mitigated by D2's tolerant decoder and stale-index fallback; here a missing index just skips the step. A lookup that silently costs a 0.66 MB download on every install would undo M2's request economy, which is why the lazy rule has its own acceptance test. Confidence: high (adapters over indexes D2 and D4 build and test).

title: Epic: M2 sources (WoWInterface, Tukui) and changelogs
description:
## Background

Area epic of the M2 milestone `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp` (Updates, dependencies, adoption, desired state). It adds the two largest missing keyless ecosystems and makes release notes readable.

**What is missing today** (commit `e902d36`):
- **WoWInterface (thousands of addons) and Tukui (ElvUI) are refused.**
  - `wowi:` and `tukui:` refs and pasted links parse (`src/sources/refs.rs`), but every fetch fails `source_disabled` "… arrives in M2" through `SourceId::later()` (`src/sources/mod.rs:73`).
  - The hosts are already allowlisted (`api.mmoui.com`, `cdn.wowinterface.com`, `api.tukui.org`).
  - `Paths::wowi_cache_dir()` is reserved, and `WOWI_FILELIST_MIN_AGE` and `WOWI_DETAILS_BATCH_SIZE` are defined but unused.
- **No MD5 and no gzip.** `ExpectedHash` is SHA-256 only. ureq is built without gzip, and every response, JSON included, shares the 512 MiB download cap.
- **No release notes.** `Release.changelog_url` exists, but no source returns note text. The Atom decoder ignores `<content>`, and `info` still says "No changelog until M2".
- **Source switches do nothing.** `config.toml` parses `[sources.<id>] enabled`, and nothing reads it.

**What upstream really does** (verified live 2026-10-15; the full fact list is in this epic's rationale comment):
- WoWInterface sends no validators, so its file list can be cached by `max-age` only. Its `UIMD5` equals the MD5 of the downloaded bytes, and its compatibility tags lag the game.
- Tukui's download URLs are tokens that die within seconds, and the download's `ETag` is the zip's MD5.
- GitHub's `releases.atom` carries full release notes as escaped HTML.

**Who needs this.** This area serves milestone goal **G-M2-3, more keyless sources**: "WoWInterface and Tukui install, update and verify like GitHub (MD5 where the source provides one). Their changelogs are readable." It also feeds:
- dependency resolution (C7: WoWInterface and Tukui lookups);
- adoption (E5.1: `UIDir` evidence, `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, exactness checks);
- search (G1: local WoWInterface index, Tukui list).

**Line numbers** are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Goals

- gzip for API responses through omaddons' own decoding layer, a 64 MiB decoded cap for JSON, and `wire_bytes` in `net.log` (D1, M2-D14).
- A slim, cached WoWInterface index by folder and by project, refreshed at most every `max(1 h, max-age)` and parsed in under 40 ms (D2, M2-D12).
- `wowi:` refs and pasted WoWInterface links install, update and verify by MD5, with content identity `wowi:<id>@<md5>`, release notes, and working `sources.<id>.enabled` switches for every source (D3, M2-D11).
- `tukui:` refs install ElvUI on every client its TOC supports, with late-resolved, never-stored, redacted token URLs, `ETag` MD5 checks, case-insensitive slugs, and the Tukui list in the memo (D4, M2-D13).
- Bounded, markup-free plain text from HTML and BBCode (D5).
- `info --changelog` and `outdated --changelog` across GitHub (Atom, zero REST), WoWInterface (free notes), Tukui and git on GitHub (D6).

## Success Criteria

True when every child is closed:
- **Checkpoint 8 (WoWInterface).** A `wowi:` ref and a pasted WoWInterface link both install with MD5 verification, and a tampered fixture fails with `hash_mismatch`.
- **Checkpoint 7 (Tukui).** ElvUI installs from Tukui into retail and Classic targets (and every other family its TOC declares), with the download's MD5 checked against the response `ETag`. No token appears in any log, state file, plan, memo, envelope or stderr.
- **Checkpoint 10 (changelogs).** `info <gh addon> --changelog` shows release notes from the Atom feed with zero `api.github.com` requests. `outdated --changelog --json` attaches `latest.changelog.entries[]`.
- The WoWInterface file list arrives gzipped, with `wire_bytes` far below `bytes` in `net.log`. A gzip bomb is refused at the 64 MiB cap.
- Disabling any source in `config.toml` makes its refs fail `source_disabled` with the argv fix `omaddons config set sources.<id>.enabled true`.
- The new fuzz targets (`wowi_filelist`, `wowi_details`, `tukui_addons`, `html_text`, `bbcode_text`, `atom_feed`) each run 10 minutes clean, and the H4 live probes for WoWInterface, Tukui and the Atom feed pass.

## Non-Goals

- CurseForge and Wago sources and their `auth` commands (M5). `cf:` and `wago:` refs keep failing `source_disabled` "… arrives in M5".
- The GitHub GraphQL batch path (M5, M2-D22).
- Any query to a WoWInterface or Tukui search endpoint. Search stays local for those sources (M2-D21, owned by G1).
- Historical WoWInterface files. The API serves only the current file, so `--version` can only match it.
- Using WoWInterface `UICompatibility` or Tukui `patch[]` to exclude a build. They are hints, and TOCs decide (vision D5).
- Wiring the indexes into dependency resolution, adoption or search. C7, E5.1 and G1 own that, and this area provides the lookups.
- Brotli or deflate decoding. The layer refuses unknown encodings so they can be added later.

## Considerations

- **Volunteer-run services.** Batch WoWInterface details 50 ids per request, refresh the file list at most hourly, never send HEAD to Tukui, and never store Tukui response bodies (`no-store`).
- **Tokens are secrets for their short life.** Redaction lives in one helper used by `net::redact` and the guard's logged path, and D4's grep test covers every output.
- **Never emit a fix for a command that does not exist yet.** The `omaddons search …` fixes the design gives for unknown WoWInterface ids and Tukui slugs stay `omaddons help install` until G1 lands and upgrades them.
- **Follow reality.** If an upstream fact turns out different from what was verified on 2026-10-15: adjust the decoder, add a fixture and a live-probe assertion, and record the change with its date on the vision bead.
- **Collision hot spots inside this area:**
  - `src/net/mod.rs` and `src/net/guard.rs` (D1 and D4);
  - `src/sources/mod.rs` (D3, D4, D6);
  - `src/model.rs` (D3, D4, plus A7 and A8).
- **Fixtures are public.** Trim contributor names from recorded changelogs, and exclude recorded Tukui fixtures (which hold dead tokens) from leak greps.
- **Parallel start.** D1 and D5 have no blockers and start in wave 1. D2 follows D1. D3, D4 and D6 wait for engine and update work (A7, A8, B1, B5, C3).

## Children

**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this area.** Without WoWInterface and Tukui, the owner downloads zips by hand, and omaddons cannot be the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons. This area makes `wowi:` and `tukui:` refs first-class (MD5-verified, same evaluator, same engine) and makes release notes readable. It serves G-M2-3, and through C7, E5.1 and G1 also dependencies, adoption and search.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D11 (departs from the vision).** WoWInterface release identity is `wowi:<id>@<md5>`, the version is `UIVersion`, and `UICompatibility` never excludes a build. Rejected: tags as metadata.
- **M2-D12 (departs from the vision).** The WoWInterface index is cached by `max-age` only, and stored slim. Rejected: conditional GET (impossible), and the raw body.
- **M2-D13.** Tukui assets are deferred, re-resolved on retry, never persisted, redacted, with the `ETag` MD5 verified. Rejected: storing the list's `url`.
- **M2-D14.** gzip goes through our own API-only decoding layer, with a decoded cap and `wire_bytes`. Rejected: ureq `gzip`, which bypasses fixtures, hides wire bytes, defeats the `Content-Length` check and compiles dead backends.

**Verified external facts (live, 2026-10-15). These are the foundation of D2–D4 and D6. If reality later differs, follow it, adjust the decoder, add a fixture and a live probe, and record the change with its date on the vision bead.**

*WoWInterface (MMOUI v3, keyless).*
- **`GET https://api.mmoui.com/v3/game/WOW/filelist.json`:**
  - 5,619,970 bytes decoded, 659,496 gzipped; 8,218 entries, no duplicate UIDs;
  - `cache-control: max-age=3600`. **No ETag and no Last-Modified; If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since are ignored** (200).
- **Filelist fields:**
  - `UID`, `UICATID`: strings;
  - `UIVersion`: a free-form string; 5 are empty;
  - `UIDate`: a number, epoch ms;
  - `UIName`, `UIAuthorName`, `UIFileInfoURL`;
  - `UIDownloadTotal`, `UIDownloadMonthly`, `UIFavoriteTotal`: strings;
  - `UICompatibility`: an array of `{version, name}` or null. 4,297 are non-null, with 77 distinct versions, none 5.x and none past 12.1.0;
  - `UIDir`: an array, never empty, up to 74 entries;
  - `UIIMG_Thumbs`, `UIIMGs`; `UISiblings` (2 non-null).
- **Shared folder names:** 781 `UIDir` names belong to more than one project (775 case-insensitively). Junk includes `__MACOSX` (119), `""` (56), `Interface` (60) and `WTF` (23).
- **`GET …/filedetails/5995,7032,24910.json`:** comma batching works; `cache-control: max-age=3600`, no ETag.
  - Fields: `UID, UICATID, UIVersion, UIDate, UIMD5, UIFileName, UIDownload, UIPending, UIName, UIAuthorName, UIDescription, UIChangeLog, UIHitCount, UIHitCountMonthly, UIFavoriteTotal`.
  - **No `UIDir`, no `UICompatibility`, no `UIFileInfoURL`.** `UIDescription` and `UIChangeLog` are BBCode with CRLF.
- **Downloads:**
  - `UIDownload = https://cdn.wowinterface.com/downloads/getfile.php?id=<UID>&d=<UIDate/1000>&minion`;
  - served directly: 200, no redirect, `content-disposition` naming the file;
  - **the MD5 of the bytes equals `UIMD5`** (BugSack: `683278e9d6e1cbc1514c3066d3d347b2`).
- **TOC ids:** BugSack's TOC has `## X-WoWI-ID: 5995`, `## X-Curse-Project-ID: 6273`, `## X-Wago-ID: rkGrrgGy`. On the owner's machine, BigWigs' TOC has `## X-WoWI-ID: 5086` and Bartender4's `## X-WoWI-ID: 11190`, both GitHub catalog entries.
- **Gaps:** `!BugGrabber`, LibStub, ElvUI and Auctionator are not on WoWInterface (only "Auctionator ClassicFix" is). Details! (UID 23056) is stale, from 2020 (`DetailsRetail-v8.2.5…`).

*Tukui (keyless).*
- **`GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addons`:** 2 entries, `cache-control: private, no-store`, no ETag.
  - Fields: `id, slug, name, author, version, url, patch[], directories[], last_update (date), changelog_url, git_url, web_url`, plus images and descriptions.
  - ElvUI: id −2, version `16.00`, patch `[12.1.0, 5.5.4, 1.15.9, 2.5.6]`, directories `[ElvUI, ElvUI_Libraries, ElvUI_Options]`, last_update `2026-10-13`, changelog_url `https://api.tukui.org/v1/changelog/elvui`, git_url `https://github.com/tukui-org/ElvUI`.
  - Tukui: id −1, version `20.463`.
- **`GET /v1/addon/elvui`** returns the same 20 keys. **`url` = `https://api.tukui.org/v1/download/<slug>/<50-char token>`**, fresh on every call. One token was refused with 403 about 20–40 s after issue. HEAD returns 404.
- **The download** comes straight from `api.tukui.org`, no redirects: `content-type: application/zip`, `content-disposition: attachment; filename=elvui-16.00.zip`, **`etag` = the MD5 of the bytes**.
- **The ElvUI zip:**
  - three top-level folders, each with a single TOC carrying `## Interface: 11509, 16001, 20506, 38002, 50504, 120100, 120105`;
  - `## X-Tukui-ProjectID: -2` and `## X-Tukui-ProjectFolders: ElvUI, ElvUI_Libraries, ElvUI_Options`;
  - per-game-type titles via `[AllowLoadGameType …]` (standard, camelot, wrath, tbc, vanilla).

*GitHub Atom (for changelogs).*
- **`releases.atom`:**
  - 10 entries, each with **the full release notes as `<content type="html">`** (escaped HTML, 312–5,003 characters);
  - `id` is `tag:github.com,2008:Repository/<n>/<tag>`, `title` is the tag, plus `updated`;
  - weak `ETag`; `cache-control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate`.

**Risks.** API drift is covered by tolerant decoders, six fuzz targets and H4 probes. Token leaks are covered by one redaction helper and a grep test. Confidence is **high**: every fact above was verified live.

title: gzip decoding for API responses and an API response cap
description:
## Background

WoWInterface's file list (`GET https://api.mmoui.com/v3/game/WOW/filelist.json`) is 5,619,970 bytes of JSON decoded and 659,496 bytes gzipped (verified live 2026-10-15), about 8.5 times less traffic compressed. D2 refreshes it at most hourly wherever search, dependency resolution or adoption need it.

Today omaddons cannot request or decode compressed responses, and one cap guards every response:
- `Cargo.toml` builds ureq with `default-features = false, features = ["rustls"]`, so ureq neither sends `Accept-Encoding` nor decodes `Content-Encoding`.
- `src/net/mod.rs` builds `Limited<Retrying<Validating<Redirecting<Guarded<transport>>>>>` through `stack()` (`:274`), `stack_with()` (`:331`) and `core_stack_with()` (`:343`). The transport is `UreqTransport`, `ReplayTransport` or `RecordTransport`, chosen by `select_transport` (`:303`).
- `Guarded::new(…, config.download_max_bytes)` holds one limit for every response: `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB, `src/limits.rs:33`) or `limits.download_max_bytes`. Past it, `LoggingReader` (`guard.rs`, around line 200) fails with `archive_too_large` (exit 4) and the fix "raise download_max_bytes under [limits] in config.toml" (`guard::too_large`, `guard.rs:231`). 512 MiB is far too generous for JSON.
- `NetLogEntry` (`src/net/log.rs:31`) logs `bytes` and nothing about the wire.

**Why not ureq's own `gzip` feature (M2-D14).** It has four problems:
1. replay fixtures would bypass the decoder, because `ReplayTransport` replaces ureq below `Guarded`, so nothing could test it;
2. ureq strips `Content-Length`, so `net.log` could not show wire bytes and the guard's up-front size check would never fire;
3. every request, downloads included, would advertise gzip;
4. dead flate2 backends would be compiled in.

This serves G-M2-3 (more keyless sources: WoWInterface and Tukui install, update and verify like GitHub) and the request economy of G-M2-1. Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

**Decision M2-D14:** gzip goes through omaddons' own decoding layer, for API requests only (`flate2` with zlib-rs), with a decoded-size cap and `wire_bytes` in `net.log`.

**1. Dependency.** Add `flate2 = { version = "<the Cargo.lock version>", default-features = false, features = ["zlib-rs"] }`. flate2 is already in the tree through `zip` (`deflate-flate2-zlib-rs`) with the same backend. Run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny), and record the release binary's size change in the close comment.

**2. The `Decoding` layer** (new `src/net/decode.rs`), directly above the transport (real, replay or record) and below `Guarded`. `core_stack_with` becomes `Guarded::new(Box::new(Decoding::new(transport)), …)`, so the stack is `Limited<Retrying<Validating<Redirecting<Guarded<Decoding<transport>>>>>>`. Update the module docs that list the layers.

- **Send.** Add `Accept-Encoding: gzip` when `req.timeout == TimeoutKind::Api` and no such header is set. `TimeoutKind::Download` requests (`Request::download()`) are untouched, because archives must never advertise gzip.
- **Response, `Content-Encoding` absent or `identity`:** pass through unchanged.
- **Response, `gzip`:**
  - wrap the body as a counting reader feeding a streaming `flate2::read::GzDecoder`;
  - remove `content-encoding` from the headers handed upward, so `Validating` caches a plain body and nothing decodes twice;
  - **keep `content-length`** (the wire length), so the guard's up-front check still fires; comparing it with the decoded cap is a safe early refusal.
- **Response, any other value** (`br`, `deflate`, `zstd`, lists): fail without passing compressed bytes upward. Use the existing code `network` with `.retryable(false)` (as the redirect-limit error does), message "<host> answered with Content-Encoding <value>, which omaddons does not decode", text fix "retry later; if it persists, report the source's response". Corrupt gzip maps through `body_error` to `network`, as any broken body does.
- **Wire bytes:** `Guarded` writes the log line, but only `Decoding` knows the compressed count. Add a crate-private handle on `Response` (for example `pub(crate) wire_bytes: Option<Arc<AtomicU64>>`) that `LoggingReader` reads when the body ends or is dropped.

**3. Two caps in `Guarded`.**
- New limit **`API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` = 64 MiB** in `src/limits.rs`, not configurable: a `REGISTRY` row (`Bytes`, `config_key: None`, note "Largest decoded API response: a decompression-bomb guard"), its name in `LIMIT_NAMES`, and the `limit_registries` snapshot reviewed.
- `Guarded` keeps `max_bytes` for downloads and gains `api_max_bytes`, a constructor argument so tests can pass small caps.
- Pick the cap from `req.timeout` before the request moves into `inner.send`, and use it for both checks. Because `Decoding` sits below, `LoggingReader` counts **decoded** bytes: the cap is a decompression-bomb guard.
- **Error wording.** The code stays `archive_too_large`. `SizeCapExceeded` and `too_large` learn which limit tripped:
  - downloads keep today's message and fix;
  - API responses get "the response from <host> is larger than the 64 MiB API response limit" and a text fix that does not mention config.toml, for example "retry later; the source sent an unexpectedly large response";
  - `details` stays `{max_bytes}`.

**4. `net.log`.**
- `NetLogEntry` gains `wire_bytes: Option<u64>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`), after `bytes`, set only when it differs from `bytes`.
- `bytes` stays "body bytes read", now decoded. Old lines still parse.
- Update the literals at `src/net/log.rs`, `src/net/guard.rs:108` and `src/app/net_log.rs:161`. The human `net-log` view (`net_log.rs:102`) MAY show the wire size.

**5. Replay and record.**
- **Replay:** a fixture with `content-encoding: gzip` serves its gzipped `.body`, and `Decoding` decodes it, so tests use the real path. Add `gzip_bytes(&[u8]) -> Vec<u8>` to `tests/common/http.rs` for D2's builders.
- **Record:** `RecordTransport` sits below `Decoding`, so it stores the compressed body with its `content-encoding` header. It keeps every response header except `set-cookie` (`record.rs:122-137`), and never stores request headers.

**Files:** `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, new `src/net/decode.rs`, `src/net/mod.rs`, `src/net/guard.rs`, `src/net/log.rs`, `src/app/net_log.rs`, `src/limits.rs`, `src/snapshots/omaddons__limits__tests__limit_registries.snap`, `src/net/tests.rs`, `tests/net_replay.rs`, `tests/common/http.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- API requests send `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, and `Request::download()` requests send none.
- A replay fixture with `content-encoding: gzip` decodes transparently: the caller reads the original bytes, without a `content-encoding` header. Its `net.log` line has `bytes` (decoded) and `wire_bytes` (compressed). Identity responses have no `wire_bytes`.
- A gzip bomb fails `archive_too_large`, with the API wording naming the cap, and reading stops at the cap.
- API responses are capped at `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` and downloads at `download_max_bytes`, each enforced per request kind.
- An unsupported `Content-Encoding` fails with the non-retryable `network` error and never passes compressed bytes up.
- A gzip 200 with an ETag, then a 304, through `Validating`, returns the same decoded body.
- `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` has a `REGISTRY` row and no config key, and the snapshot is reviewed.
- `cargo deny check` passes, and the binary size change is recorded.
- Existing net, replay, record and install tests pass, apart from the new field.

## Test Plan

- **Unit (`src/net/decode.rs`, `src/net/tests.rs`):** a fake inner `Http` that records headers. Cover header insertion per `TimeoutKind`, identity pass-through, gzip read in 1-byte chunks, an unknown encoding, a truncated stream, and the wire counter.
- **Guard unit tests:** both caps with small injected values, the announced-length refusal, and `wire_bytes` written only when it differs from `bytes`.
- **Replay (`tests/net_replay.rs`):** a gzipped fixture through `stack_with`, with `net.log` read by `tests/common/netlog.rs`.
- **Bomb:** build it at test time (for example 80 MiB of zeros, about 80 KB compressed) rather than committing it.
- **Live (H4):** the real filelist arrives gzipped, with `wire_bytes` around 0.66 MB.

## Considerations

- Never decode or advertise gzip for downloads.
- The layer must stream. Never `read_to_end` inside `Decoding`, or the guard cannot protect.
- Document on `bytes` that traffic sums should use `wire_bytes` when present.
- **Collision hot spot:** D4 edits `src/net/mod.rs` (`redact`) and `src/net/guard.rs` (the logged path). Keep the guard diff small.
- If the contract suite reaches the API cap error, add its text fix to `TEXT_FIXES`.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: none (can start immediately).

Unblocks:
- D2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.2` (The WoWInterface index): the hourly filelist refresh depends on gzip (5.6 MB down to 0.66 MB) and on the 64 MiB API cap as its bomb guard, and D2's fixture builders serve gzipped bodies through this layer.
acceptance_criteria: API requests send Accept-Encoding: gzip and Request::download() requests send none; a replay fixture with content-encoding: gzip decodes transparently through a new Decoding layer between the transport and Guarded, the caller gets the original bytes without a content-encoding header, and its net.log line carries bytes (decoded) and wire_bytes (compressed) while identity responses have no wire_bytes; a gzip bomb fails archive_too_large with the API-response wording naming the cap and stops reading at the cap; API responses are capped by the new non-configurable API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES (64 MiB, REGISTRY row, snapshot reviewed) and downloads keep download_max_bytes; an unsupported Content-Encoding fails with a non-retryable network error and never passes compressed bytes up; a gzip 200 then 304 through Validating returns the same decoded body; flate2 is added with only the zlib-rs backend, cargo deny passes and the binary size change is recorded; existing net, replay, record and install tests pass

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** WoWInterface is one of the two keyless ecosystems M2 adds (goal G-M2-3). Its only folder-level index is a 5.6 MB JSON file that shrinks to 0.66 MB gzipped. Search (G1), dependency resolution (C7) and adoption (E5.1) refresh that file at most hourly. Without gzip, every refresh costs about 8.5 times the traffic, on the owner's machine and on a volunteer-run service. The same change gives JSON its own size cap: today a 512 MiB download limit guards every API response, which is no guard at all against a decompression bomb. Decoding happens in a layer omaddons owns, below the guard and above the transport, so the replay fixtures exercise it. That keeps the project's rule that every network behaviour is testable offline.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D14: gzip through our own layer, for API requests only.** flate2 uses the zlib-rs backend `zip` already compiles. The cap is checked on decoded bytes, and `net.log` gains `wire_bytes`. Rejected: ureq's `gzip` feature, for four reasons.
  1. Replay fixtures replace ureq below `Guarded`, so the decoder would never run in tests.
  2. ureq strips `Content-Length`, so `net.log` could not show wire bytes and the guard's up-front size check would never fire.
  3. Every request, downloads included, would advertise gzip.
  4. It compiles dead flate2 backends.
- **Staging decisions made while writing this bead** (none changes the plan's intent):
  - the decoded response drops `content-encoding` but keeps the wire `content-length`, so the guard's early check still works;
  - an unsupported encoding fails as a non-retryable `network` error (prefer an existing code);
  - the API-cap error keeps the code `archive_too_large` and only changes its message and text fix, because the limit is not configurable.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- Live, 2026-10-15: `GET https://api.mmoui.com/v3/game/WOW/filelist.json` is 5,619,970 bytes decoded and 659,496 gzipped, with 8,218 entries and `cache-control: max-age=3600`.
- Code at `e902d36`:
  - `Cargo.toml` builds ureq with `default-features = false, features = ["rustls"]`;
  - `Cargo.lock` already contains `flate2` with `zlib-rs` through `zip`;
  - `core_stack_with` (`src/net/mod.rs:343`) builds `Redirecting<Guarded<transport>>` with the single cap `config.download_max_bytes`;
  - the guard's size error is `archive_too_large` with a config-oriented fix (`src/net/guard.rs:231`);
  - `NetLogEntry` has `bytes` and no wire count (`src/net/log.rs:31`);
  - `RecordTransport` keeps response headers except `set-cookie` and never stores request headers (`src/net/record.rs:122-137`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *A layer that buffers defeats the bomb guard.* The decoder must stream, and the guard counts decoded bytes as the caller reads. The bomb test asserts that reading stops at the cap.
- *`bytes` changes meaning for gzip lines.* It becomes the decoded size. `wire_bytes` is additive, and the field doc says which to sum for traffic.
- *A server that ignores `Accept-Encoding`, or sends another coding.* Identity passes through. Anything else fails loudly instead of corrupting data.
- *Collision with D4.* D4 edits the same two files for Tukui token redaction. Keep the guard diff small.

The plan rates the WoWInterface and Tukui source work **high confidence**: every API fact was verified live on 2026-10-15. This task is small (size-S) and has no blockers, so it can start in wave 1 on the sources lane (A7 → D5 → D1 → D2 → …).
