title: Adoption evidence and precedence per folder (pure)
description:
## Background

M2 goal G-M2-4 ("sole authority") says that folders installed before omaddons, or by another addon manager, can be brought under management without being replaced, and only on confident identification. The vision's adoption checkpoint (vision bead §7, M2) adds two rules: a WoWInterface `UIDir`-only match whose Title and Author disagree is never `identified`, and no fixture is adopted under the wrong source.

Nothing identifies an unmanaged folder today. Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.
- `inventory()` reads each folder's loaded TOC at `Depth::Full` (`src/inventory.rs:168`, `read_details` at `:259`). `TocSummary` (`:84`) keeps only `file, title, version, author, interfaces, x_ids`, and `x_ids` keeps only `X-` keys ending in `id` (`:287-293`). `X-Website` and `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders` never reach a caller; C1 widens the struct.
- `Toc` already has accessors for every id adoption reads (`curse_project_id`, `wowi_id`, `wago_id`, `tukui_project_id`, `tukui_project_folders`, `website`, `src/toc.rs:337-360`). `Catalog::by_folder` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:150`) returns every entry listing a folder, with no family filter, and `by_name` (`:145`) matches a name or alias, ignoring ASCII case.
- `refs::parse_user_ref` (`src/sources/refs.rs:67`) cannot be applied to `X-Website` as is: it makes `url:` refs of unknown hosts (`:299`), makes `git:` refs of `github.com/<o>/<r>/tree/<branch>` (`:229-236`), and refuses `http://` (`:80-87`).
- The only way to take over an unmanaged folder is `install --force`, which replaces it (`src/engine/ownership.rs:358`: "rerun with `--force` until `adopt` exists").

Real TOCs make this hard (verified 2026-10-15). They carry several ids: BugSack's has `X-WoWI-ID: 5995`, `X-Curse-Project-ID: 6273` and `X-Wago-ID: rkGrrgGy`. WoWInterface lists 8,218 projects, 781 of its `UIDir` names belong to more than one project (775 ignoring case), and junk names are common: `__MACOSX` (119 projects), `""` (56), `Interface` (60), `WTF` (23).

This bead is the first half of the pure identification module: for one folder, collect every piece of evidence about its source, each with its precedence. E4.2 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4.2`) groups the claims into addons with tiers, and E5.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1`) is the first caller.

## Technical Approach

**Module.** New `src/resolve/adopt.rs`, declared `pub mod adopt;` in `src/resolve/mod.rs`. It is pure: no filesystem, network, clock or environment access. Lookups are in-memory trait objects that E5.1 builds before calling. Nothing here fetches.

**Candidates.** A candidate is an `AddOns/` entry of class `Unmanaged` with a valid name that is not `case_duplicate`. Symlinks (`Linked`) are never adopted; `Protected`, `Invalid` and `Managed` entries are never candidates. Put the rule in one constructor so E5.1 cannot drift from it:

```rust
pub struct CandidateFolder { pub folder: FolderName, pub toc: Option<TocSummary> } // loaded TOC, None if none loads
impl CandidateFolder { pub fn from_entry(entry: &FolderEntry) -> Option<Self>; }
```

Fields read from `TocSummary`: `title_plain`, `website`, `dependencies` and `tukui_project_folders` (all from C1), plus `author`, `version` and `x_ids`. Look `x_ids` keys up ignoring ASCII case. A candidate with `toc: None` can still match by folder name.

**Lookups.**

```rust
pub struct AdoptLookups<'a> {
    pub family: Family,                     // target family, for the catalog filter
    pub catalog: &'a dyn AdoptCatalog,
    pub tukui: Option<&'a dyn AdoptTukui>,  // None: list unavailable
    pub wowi: Option<&'a dyn AdoptWowi>,    // None: no index, or source disabled
}
pub trait AdoptCatalog { fn by_folder(&self, f: &FolderName) -> Vec<&Entry>; fn by_name(&self, n: &str) -> Option<&Entry>; }
impl AdoptCatalog for Catalog { /* delegates to Catalog::by_folder / by_name */ }
pub trait AdoptTukui { fn by_id(&self, id: i64) -> Option<TukuiProject>; fn by_slug(&self, s: &str) -> Option<TukuiProject>; }
pub struct TukuiProject { pub id: i64, pub slug: String, pub name: String, pub directories: Vec<FolderName> }
pub trait AdoptWowi {
    fn by_folder(&self, f: &FolderName) -> Vec<u64>;   // uids whose sanitised UIDir lists f
    fn by_uid(&self, uid: u64) -> Option<WowiProject>;
    fn by_name(&self, normalised: &str) -> Vec<u64>;    // uids whose normalise(UIName) equals
}
pub struct WowiProject { pub uid: u64, pub name: String, pub author: String,
                         pub dirs: Vec<FolderName>, pub downloads: u64, pub date_ms: i64 }
```

`dirs` are sanitised as D2 stores them: entries that are empty, start with `.`, or are `__MACOSX`, `Interface` or `WTF` (ignoring case) are dropped, entries failing `FolderName::new` are dropped, and the rest are de-duplicated ignoring case. Test fakes MUST model the same.

**Wire enums.** Both derive `Serialize + JsonSchema` with `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`:

```rust
pub enum Evidence { CatalogFolder, TocTukuiId, TocWebsite, TocWowiId, WowiDirCorroborated,
                    WowiDir, NameMatch, TocCurseId, TocWagoId }
pub enum Strength { Catalog, TocId, Corroborated, NameOnly, CfOnly }
```

Wire values: evidence `catalog_folder`, `toc_tukui_id`, `toc_website`, `toc_wowi_id`, `wowi_dir_corroborated`, `wowi_dir`, `name_match`, `toc_curse_id`, `toc_wago_id`; strengths `catalog`, `toc_id`, `corroborated`, `name_only`, `cf_only`. Add `Evidence::rank() -> u8` (the row below) and `Evidence::strength()`.

**Precedence (M2-D40), strongest first.**

| Rank | Evidence | Gives | Strength |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Catalog `by_folder`, family-filtered | the entry's ref; the entry's `folders` give the group | `catalog` |
| 2 | `## X-Tukui-ProjectID: N` | `tukui:<slug>` via the Tukui list, or the built-in map −1→`tukui`, −2→`elvui`; folders from `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders` | `toc_id` |
| 3 | `## X-Website` that parses to `gh:<owner>/<repo>` (both parts present), a WoWInterface `info<id>` link, or a Tukui link | that ref. Any other host is ignored, never turned into a `url:` ref | `toc_id` |
| 4 | `## X-WoWI-ID: N` | `wowi:N` | `toc_id` |
| 5 | WoWI `UIDir` contains the folder, the project is unique after sanitising (or the top single-folder project), **and** TOC Title (colour-stripped, normalised) ≈ `UIName` **or** TOC Author ≈ `UIAuthorName` | `wowi:<uid>` | `corroborated` |
| 6 | WoWI `UIDir` match without corroboration, or folder name = catalog name or alias, or folder name = WoWI `UIName` | that ref | `name_only` |
| 7 | `## X-Curse-Project-ID` / `## X-Wago-ID` only | none (CurseForge and Wago arrive in M5) | `cf_only` |

Rows 2–4 share the wire strength `toc_id` but keep distinct ranks, because M2-D40 orders Tukui id before `X-Website` before `X-WoWI-ID`. E4.2 decides contests by rank, so "equal strength" there means equal rank.

**Why the catalog wins.** Real TOCs carry several ids. BigWigs' `X-WoWI-ID: 5086` and Bartender4's `X-WoWI-ID: 11190` sit in TOCs of curated `gh:` catalog entries that `install bigwigs` resolves to. Adoption must pick the source `install` would, or the next `update` would swap the user's build for a different distribution. A TOC id that disagrees with a stronger claim is still returned here. E4.2 lists it in the group's `evidence` and `alternatives` and never chooses it.

**Claims.**

```rust
pub struct Claim {
    pub evidence: Evidence,
    pub r#ref: Option<Ref>,        // None only for toc_curse_id / toc_wago_id
    pub folders: Vec<FolderName>,  // proposed set, always including the candidate, sorted by key
    pub name: Option<String>,      // the source's name: catalog name, Tukui name or WoWI UIName
}
pub fn evidence(candidate: &CandidateFolder, lookups: &AdoptLookups<'_>) -> Vec<Claim>;
```

`name` lets E5.2 apply the record-name rule (catalog name, else Tukui name, else WoWI `UIName`, else the primary folder) without repeating lookups. For candidate folder `f` (a WoWI folder set is the project's `dirs`, a Tukui one its `directories`, each ∪ {f}, falling back to {f} when the lookup lacks the project):
1. Each `catalog.by_folder(f)` entry whose `families` is empty or contains `lookups.family`, with its `folders` ∪ {f}. Several entries give several rank-1 claims, and E4.2 turns that tie into a `guess`.
2. `X-Tukui-ProjectID` parsed as `i64`. Slug and name come from `tukui.by_id`, else `TUKUI_BUILTIN = [(-1, "tukui", "Tukui"), (-2, "elvui", "ElvUI")]`, else no claim. Folders are the valid `tukui_project_folders` ∪ {f}, else the project's `directories`.
3. `website_ref(website)`, with the WoWI or Tukui folder set for those refs, and {f} for `gh:`.
4. `X-WoWI-ID` parsed as a positive `u64` gives `wowi:N` (no index needed).
5. Needs a WoWI lookup. With `P = by_folder(f)`, the unique project is `P[0]` when `P` has one element, else the only project whose `dirs` are exactly `[f]`, else none. A unique project passing `names_match(title_plain, UIName)` or `names_match(author, UIAuthorName)` gives `wowi_dir_corroborated`.
6. A unique project without corroboration gives `wowi_dir`. With no unique project, each project in `P` gives a `wowi_dir`. `catalog.by_name(f)` gives `name_match` with the entry's folders and **no** family filter, because it is only ever a guess. `wowi.by_name(normalise(f))` gives one `name_match` per uid.
7. Only when rows 1–6 gave nothing: a numeric `X-Curse-Project-ID` gives `toc_curse_id`, and a non-empty alphanumeric `X-Wago-ID` gives `toc_wago_id`, each with `r#ref: None` and {f}.

Remove duplicate `(evidence, ref)` pairs. Sort by rank, then ref identity (`Ref: Ord`), then evidence order.

**`website_ref(raw) -> Option<Ref>`.**
- Accept `https://` and `http://` only. The scheme carries no identity, and nothing is fetched. Lowercase the host and strip `www.`, the port and any userinfo.
- `github.com`: the first two path segments are owner and repo. Both must be present and valid GitHub names. A trailing `.git` is stripped, and anything after the repo is ignored. The result is always `gh:`, never `git:`. Reject the non-account first segments `sponsors`, `orgs`, `users` and `topics`.
- `wowinterface.com`: a last segment `info<id>` (optionally followed by `-<name>` and `.html`) gives `wowi:<id>`. Every other WoWInterface page gives `None`.
- `tukui.org`: `/addon/<slug>`, `/addons/<slug>` or a `ui=<slug>` query parameter gives `tukui:<slug, lowercased>` when the slug is `[a-z0-9-]+`. A bare `tukui.org/<page>` gives `None`, because it matches any page on the site.
- Any other host gives `None`. Never return `url:`, `git:` or `file:`.
- Make `is_github_owner`, `is_github_repo` and `is_slug` in `src/sources/refs.rs` `pub(crate)` and reuse them. Do not copy them.

**Normalisation and the match rule.**
- `normalise(s)`: apply `toc::plain_title` (C1 strips `|c`+8 hex and `|r` colour codes, `|T…|t` textures and `|A…|a` atlases). Then lowercase, drop every character that is neither alphanumeric nor whitespace, collapse whitespace runs to one space, and trim.
- `names_match(a, b)`: both normalised strings are non-empty, and either they are equal, or the shorter is a prefix of the longer with at least `NAME_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS` (5) characters. Corroboration uses it; row 6 uses equality (`Entry::answers_to`, normalised `UIName`).
- `NAME_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS` and `TUKUI_BUILTIN` are documented constants in `adopt.rs`. Algorithm thresholds belong in their pure module, not in `src/limits.rs`.

**Files:** `src/resolve/adopt.rs` (new: types, `evidence`, `website_ref`, `normalise`, `names_match`, tests). `src/resolve/mod.rs` (`pub mod adopt;`). `src/sources/refs.rs` (`pub(crate)` on three helpers, no behaviour change).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Evidence` and `Strength` serialise to exactly the nine and five wire values above. `rank()` and `strength()` follow the table.
- `CandidateFolder::from_entry` is `Some` only for `Unmanaged`, non-`case_duplicate` entries.
- Row 1: an entry for the target family, or with empty `families`, gives `catalog_folder` with its folders plus the candidate. An entry only for other families gives none. Two qualifying entries give two rank-1 claims.
- Row 2: `X-Tukui-ProjectID: -2` with no Tukui lookup gives `tukui:elvui` with the `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders` folders, and invalid names in that list are dropped. An unknown or non-numeric id gives nothing.
- Row 3: `https://github.com/o/r`, `http://github.com/o/r/releases`, `https://www.github.com/o/r.git` and `https://github.com/o/r/tree/main` give `gh:o/r`. `https://github.com/o`, `https://github.com/sponsors/o` and `https://deadlybossmods.com` give nothing, never `url:`. `…/downloads/info5995-BugSack.html` gives `wowi:5995`, and `https://www.tukui.org/addon/elvui` gives `tukui:elvui`.
- Row 4: `X-WoWI-ID: 5086` gives `wowi:5086` with or without a WoWI lookup.
- Rows 5–6: a unique `UIDir` project with a matching Title, or only a matching Author, gives `wowi_dir_corroborated`; with both mismatched, `wowi_dir`. Two multi-folder projects give two `wowi_dir` claims. A sole single-folder project among several counts as unique. A catalog alias as folder name gives `name_match`, whatever the entry's families.
- Row 7: `X-Curse-Project-ID` alone gives `toc_curse_id` (no ref), and `X-Wago-ID` alone gives `toc_wago_id`. A TOC that also has `X-WoWI-ID` gives no `cf_only` claim.
- No claim ever carries a `url:`, `git:`, `file:`, `cf:` or `wago:` ref, across every test case.
- `normalise("|cff33ff99Details!|r Damage Meter")` is `details damage meter`. `names_match` accepts equality and a prefix of 5 or more characters, and rejects a 4-character prefix and empty strings.
- Claim order is deterministic. `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests in `src/resolve/adopt.rs`, table-driven, with fake `AdoptCatalog`/`AdoptTukui`/`AdoptWowi` structs over `BTreeMap`s. Build `catalog::Entry` and `TocSummary` values directly (public fields).
- One table per row, each asserting the full `Vec<Claim>`, so precedence order is checked too.
- A `website_ref` table over every link form above. A `normalise`/`names_match` table covering colour codes, textures, atlases, punctuation, Unicode letters and empty input.
- A `proptest` (already a dev-dependency): `website_ref` never panics on arbitrary input and returns only `gh:`, `wowi:` or `tukui:` refs.
- Fixture TOC sets and the grouping acceptance table are E4.2's.

## Considerations

- **Missing lookups degrade, never fetch.** Without WoWI, rows 5–6 (WoWI) are skipped and row 4 still works. Without Tukui, row 2 uses the built-in map. E5.1 reports skipped sources.
- **No CurseForge or Wago refs** (M2-D18). M2 reports CurseForge-only folders as `cf_only` with a `--ref` fix, because `auth curseforge` arrives in M5. Never construct `cf:` or `wago:` refs.
- **Family filter.** WeakAuras' catalog entry lists no `mainline` (`catalog/catalog.toml:21`), so a WeakAuras folder on retail gets no `catalog_folder` claim, only weaker ones. That is the intended conservative outcome.
- **Decisions made here, to restate in the close comment:** `http://` is accepted; bare Tukui pages and GitHub non-account pages are rejected; catalog name matches are not family-filtered; `cf_only` claims appear only when no ref-bearing evidence exists; `AdoptWowi::by_name` exists for the `UIName` rule. The plan's default for open questions applies: when in doubt, produce the weaker claim.
- **C3** (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.3`) defines similar lookup traits for dependencies in `src/resolve/deps.rs`. It is not a dependency. Share a trait only if both have landed and the shapes match exactly. B8's `adoptable` count is a separate name-only rule and does not call this module.
- **Collision hot spots:** `src/resolve/mod.rs` (B1, B4, C3 and G1 also add `pub mod` lines) and `src/sources/refs.rs` (D3 adds WoWI URL forms).
- **Not here:** grouping, tiers, `identify`, `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` and the fixture TOCs belong to E4.2. No clap subcommand and no output (DEC-1: no stubs).

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- C1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.1` (TOC conditional directives and plain titles): adds `TocSummary.title_plain`, `website`, `dependencies` and `tukui_project_folders`, and `toc::plain_title`. Corroboration, `X-Website` evidence, Tukui folder sets and `normalise` read them.

Unblocks:
- E4.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4.2` (Adoption grouping, tiers and alternatives (pure)): groups this bead's per-folder claims into addons and assigns tiers.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Adoption is how omaddons becomes the *sole* authority over a client that already has addons. Without it, the only way to manage a folder installed by hand or by another manager is `install --force`, which destroys it. For the owner, adoption must never be wrong in the one way that hurts: recording a folder under a different distribution than `install` would choose, because the next `update` would then silently replace a working build. This bead puts every "where did this folder come from" rule in one pure function with table tests, so the report (E5.1), the transaction (E5.2) and every later reader agree. It serves G-M2-4 (sole authority, confident identification only) and G-M2-7 (no regression: identification never touches disk or network).

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D40, evidence precedence.** The order is catalog, then Tukui id, then `X-Website` (GitHub, WoWInterface or Tukui links only), then `X-WoWI-ID`, then corroborated WoWI `UIDir`, then name. Why: adopt must pick the source `install` would, and real TOCs carry several ids (BigWigs: `X-WoWI-ID: 5086`). Rejected: TOC ids first, the vision's literal order, which would adopt catalog addons under WoWInterface.
- **M2-D18, departs from the vision.** CurseForge-only folders are `cf_only` with a `--ref` fix, not "adoptable, fix `auth curseforge set`", because `auth curseforge` arrives in M5 and a fix must name a command that exists. `exact` needs per-file SHA-256 equality with the newest release's verified install set (E5.1 decides it). Rejected: fingerprinting (CurseForge's method, M5) and matching version strings.
- **Review-round fix folded in.** The plan's second review pass (as a fresh implementer) found wrong-source adoption. Its fix is catalog-first precedence, `X-Website` limited to three hosts and never a `url:` ref, and disagreeing ids listed but never chosen. This bead implements the per-folder half.
- **Plan defaults.** Choose the conservative outcome when unsure: a weaker claim, never a stronger one. Algorithm thresholds such as the 5-character title prefix are named constants in their pure module.
- **Decided while writing the bead** (restate in the close comment):
  - Rows 2–4 share the wire strength `toc_id` but rank 2 > 3 > 4, as M2-D40 orders them.
  - `http://` websites are accepted; bare `tukui.org/<page>` and GitHub `sponsors`/`orgs`/`users`/`topics` pages are rejected.
  - Catalog name matches (row 6) skip the family filter, because they only ever yield a guess.
  - `cf_only` claims appear only without ref-bearing evidence.
  - `AdoptWowi::by_name` serves the `UIName` rule.
  - `CandidateFolder::from_entry` holds the candidate rule so E5.1 cannot drift from it.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- Code at `e902d36`: `TocSummary` (`src/inventory.rs:84`) lacks website, title_plain, dependencies and Tukui folders, and `x_ids` filters to keys ending in `id` (`:287-293`). `Toc` id accessors exist (`src/toc.rs:337-360`). `Catalog::by_folder` is unfiltered (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:150`). `parse_user_ref` falls back to `url:`/`git:` and refuses `http://` (`src/sources/refs.rs:80-87, 229-236, 299`). The catalog's WeakAuras entry lists no `mainline`.
- Live on 2026-10-15 (Appendix A.1): 8,218 WoWI projects. 781 `UIDir` names are shared (775 ignoring case). Junk names: `__MACOSX` 119, `""` 56, `Interface` 60, `WTF` 23. BugSack's TOC: `X-WoWI-ID: 5995`, `X-Curse-Project-ID: 6273`, `X-Wago-ID: rkGrrgGy`. BigWigs' and Bartender4's TOCs on the owner's `forever` client carry `X-WoWI-ID` 5086 and 11190. ElvUI's TOCs carry `X-Tukui-ProjectID: -2` and `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders`.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *Heuristic false positives* from shared `UIDir` names. They only ever produce `name_only` claims, which E4.2 turns into `guess` and E5 never applies without an explicit folder. Title/Author corroboration is required for anything stronger.
- *Odd `X-Website` values.* The parser is a whitelist of three hosts and is property-tested never to return another ref kind.
- *Missing indexes.* The lookups are optional and degrade without fetching.
- Plan confidence for adoption is **medium-high**. It is heuristic by nature, and conservatism bounds a wrong call to "a record that `undo` or `adopt --ref` corrects".

**Relation to siblings.** E4.1 delivers types and per-folder claims only, as public items with unit tests and no caller. It must not group folders, assign tiers, compute `alternatives`, add `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` or write fixture TOC sets. E4.2 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4.2`) adds `identify`, `Group` and the tier enum (including `exact` for E5.1), the alternatives cap and the full acceptance table over trimmed real TOCs. Nothing outside the module uses it until E5.1.

title: Adoption grouping, tiers and alternatives (pure)
description:
## Background

E4.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4.1`) answers "what does the evidence say about this one folder". Adoption records addons, not folders: one `AddonRecord` per ref, listing every folder it owns. Multi-folder addons are the norm. The catalog lists 8 folders for DBM and 12 for BigWigs (`catalog/catalog.toml:30`, `:37`), and the ElvUI zip ships `ElvUI`, `ElvUI_Libraries` and `ElvUI_Options` (verified 2026-10-15). Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

Grouping decides most of what can go wrong:
- **A partial group** (adopting `DBM-Core` but leaving `DBM-GUI` unmanaged) makes the next `update` of DBM fail with `unmanaged_folder` on the leftover.
- **A module grouped under a different ref than its parent** would be replaced by the wrong distribution on update.
- **A guess shown as confident** breaks the vision's adoption checkpoint (vision bead §7, M2). That checkpoint requires that a `guess` is never applied without an explicit folder argument (E5 enforces it from the tiers computed here), that a `UIDir`-only match with a mismatched Title and Author is never `identified`, and that no fixture is adopted under the wrong source.

This bead adds `identify`, the pure function that turns every candidate folder's claims into addon groups with a tier, the winning ref, the evidence behind it and the alternatives. It serves M2 goal G-M2-4: folders installed before omaddons are brought under management without being replaced, and only on confident identification. E5.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1`) calls it per target, then upgrades groups to `exact` by comparing downloads.

## Technical Approach

All code goes in `src/resolve/adopt.rs`, next to E4.1's types. Still pure: no I/O, and the lookups are the in-memory `AdoptLookups` from E4.1.

**Types.** All derive `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and enums are `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`:

```rust
pub enum Tier { Exact, Identified, Guess, CfOnly, Unknown }  // wire: exact, identified, guess, cf_only, unknown
pub struct GroupClaim {
    pub r#ref: Option<Ref>,       // None only when strength is cf_only
    pub strength: Strength,
    pub evidence: Vec<Evidence>,  // sorted by rank, de-duplicated
    pub name: Option<String>,     // the source's name (catalog, Tukui, WoWI UIName)
}
pub struct Group {
    pub folders: Vec<FolderName>,          // sorted by key
    pub primary: FolderName,
    pub tier: Tier,
    pub claim: Option<GroupClaim>,         // None only for unknown
    pub alternatives: Vec<Ref>,            // never claim.ref; at most ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES
    pub unloaded_folders: Vec<FolderName>, // always empty here; E5.1 fills it
}
pub fn identify(candidates: &[CandidateFolder], lookups: &AdoptLookups<'_>) -> Vec<Group>;
```

`identify` never yields `Tier::Exact`. The variant exists so E5.1 reuses this enum for its report, where `exact` means the files equal the newest release's verified install set. E5.1 renders each group per the report shape (keys binding, values illustrative):

```json
{"folders":["BigWigs","BigWigs_Core","…"],"primary":"BigWigs","tier":"identified","strength":"catalog",
 "ref":"gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs","name":"BigWigs","evidence":["catalog_folder","toc_wowi_id"],
 "alternatives":["wowi:5086"],"unloaded_folders":[]}
{"folders":["TradeSkillMaster"],"tier":"cf_only","strength":"cf_only","ref":null,"evidence":["toc_curse_id"]}
{"folders":["MyMacros"],"tier":"unknown","strength":null,"ref":null,"evidence":[]}
```

**The grouping rules (authoritative).**
1. Each piece of evidence proposes `(ref, folder set)`. The folder set comes from the catalog entry's `folders`, from `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders`, from the WoWI project's sanitised `UIDir`, or is just the folder itself. It is intersected with the unmanaged folders present.
2. A folder claimed by several refs goes to the strongest evidence (table order). At equal strength, the folder becomes a `guess`, with the others in `alternatives`.
3. A folder with no evidence of its own **joins** a group when the group's folder set lists it, **or** when it requires (or is required by) a grouped folder *and* shares that folder's name prefix. The prefix is the folder name up to its first `-` or `_`, compared case-insensitively, and must be at least 3 characters (`DBM-`, `BigWigs_`).
4. A group's tier is the weakest claim among the members that have **their own evidence for the group's ref**. Members that joined by rule 3 inherit the group's claim and do not lower it: `catalog`, `toc_id` or `corroborated` → `identified`; `name_only` → `guess`; `cf_only` → `cf_only`; no claim → `unknown`.

A TOC id that disagrees with a stronger claim is listed in the group's `evidence` and `alternatives`. It is never chosen.

**Algorithm.** `K` is the set of candidate folders (by key; keep the first of any duplicate key). "Strength" in rule 2 is E4.1's precedence rank (1–7). M2-D40 sets the order: catalog folder index, then `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, then `X-Website`, then `X-WoWI-ID`, then a corroborated WoWI `UIDir`, then name, then CurseForge/Wago only. That way adoption picks the source `install` would. Rows 2–4 share the wire strength `toc_id` but rank 2 > 3 > 4, so equal strength means equal rank.
1. **Claims.** Call E4.1's `evidence(c, lookups)` per candidate. Every claim with a ref (ranks 1–6) is a *proposal* covering `claim.folders ∩ K`. Its *source* is the candidate that produced it.
2. **Rank rounds (rules 1–2).** For rank `k` = 1..6, a proposal at rank `k` is *valid* when its source is unassigned at the start of the round, or already assigned to the same ref. For every still-unassigned folder covered by a valid rank-`k` proposal, let `W` be the distinct refs covering it, in tie order (below). Assign the folder to `W[0]`. If `W` has more than one ref, mark the folder *contested* and remember `W[1..]` as tied refs. Compute every assignment of a round before applying any, so the result never depends on input order. A proposal whose source went to another ref in an earlier round is discarded: its ref is a disagreeing claim. Evidence-less folders listed in a valid set are assigned here (rule 3's first clause).
3. **Ref groups.** All folders assigned to one ref (`Ref` identity) form one group.
4. **`cf_only` groups.** Each still-unassigned folder with a rank-7 claim seeds its own group: claim `{ref: None, strength: cf_only, evidence: its rank-7 values}`.
5. **Joining (rule 3, second clause).** A still-unassigned folder with no claim at all joins a group when it requires a member, or a member requires it, and both have the same prefix. Requirements come from `TocSummary.dependencies` (C1: required dependencies of the loaded TOC for this client), compared ignoring ASCII case. The prefix is the name up to the first `-` or `_` (the whole name if neither appears), compared ignoring ASCII case, with at least `GROUP_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS` (3) characters. Repeat in key order until nothing joins, so chains join. When several groups qualify, take the strongest winning rank, then ref identity, then primary key. Joiners inherit.
6. **`unknown` groups.** The remaining evidence-less folders form groups by connected components of the same require-plus-prefix relation, so `MyAddon` and `MyAddon_Config` stay together for a later `adopt --ref`. They get claim `None` and tier `unknown`.
7. **Per ref group:**
   - *Strength.* For each member with its own claims for the group's ref, take its best (lowest) rank for that ref. The group's rank is the weakest of those, and `strength` is that rank's `Strength`. With no such member, use the rank of the proposals that assigned the members.
   - *Tier.* `guess` when any member is contested, or when no member has its own evidence for the ref (every member got there through another folder's proposal). Otherwise `catalog`, `toc_id` or `corroborated` give `identified`, and `name_only` gives `guess`.
   - *Alternatives* (de-duplicated, never the group's ref, capped at `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES`): first the tied refs of contested members, in tie order. Then the refs of members' own claims at rank ≤ 5 that name a different ref (disagreeing TOC ids and corroborated WoWI projects), ordered by rank, then tie order. A disagreeing `name_only` claim appears only as a tied ref, so WoWI's shared folder names do not flood confident groups.
   - *Evidence.* Each member's own evidence values for the ref at that member's best rank, plus the evidence values of the claims whose refs are listed in `alternatives`. Sort by `Evidence` order. For BigWigs this gives `["catalog_folder","toc_wowi_id"]`.
   - *Name.* The `name` of the best-ranked own claim for the ref (ties by member key), else of the proposal that assigned the members.
8. **Primary.** For ref groups, use `crate::engine::plan::primary_folder(&ref, &folders)` (pure, `src/engine/plan.rs:1318`): the repo-named folder, else the folder the others extend, else the single `*-Core`/`*_Core`, else the shortest. If C3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.3`) has added its `name_hint` parameter, pass `claim.name`. For groups without a ref, move the ref-independent part of that function into `pub fn primary_by_shape(folders: &[FolderName]) -> Option<&FolderName>`, have `primary_folder` call it after its repo-name check, and use it.
9. **Order.** Groups are sorted by primary folder key, and folders within a group by key. Every candidate lands in exactly one group.

**Tie order** (picks `W[0]` and orders tied alternatives):
1. More covered candidates first: the proposal whose folder set ∩ `K` is larger explains more of what is present.
2. Two `wowi:` refs: normalised `UIName` equal to the contested folder's normalised name first, then more downloads, then newer `date_ms`.
3. Two catalog entries: the entry whose name equals the folder, ignoring ASCII case, first.
4. Ref identity ascending (`Ref: Ord`).

**Constants.** Add `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES: usize = 3` to `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row (not configurable). It bounds data the function returns. Update the registry name list test and review the `limit_registries` snapshot. E5.2 also uses it for the report's `adopt_with_ref` commands (one per alternative). `GROUP_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS = 3` is a documented constant in `adopt.rs` (why: `DBM-` and `BigWigs_` join, while `UI_` would join unrelated addons).

**Fixtures.** `tests/fixtures/adopt/<set>/<Folder>/<Folder>.toc`. Trimmed: `## Interface`, `## Title`, `## Author`, `## Version`, `## Dependencies` and the `X-` lines that matter. No such TOCs exist in the repository today: `tests/fixtures/http/catalog/` holds `release.json` metadata and Atom feeds only, so write them from the publishers' TOCs. Values that are not verified facts must be obviously synthetic.
- **DBM:** all 8 catalog folders. `DBM-Core` carries `## X-Website: https://deadlybossmods.com`; the others `## Dependencies: DBM-Core`. A separate stray `DBM-Extra` requires `DBM-Core` and has no ids; only the joining case adds it.
- **BigWigs:** `BigWigs` with `## X-WoWI-ID: 5086` (verified on the owner's `forever` client), plus `BigWigs_Core`, `BigWigs_Options` and `BigWigs_Plugins`.
- **ElvUI:** three folders, each with `## Interface: 11509, 16001, 20506, 38002, 50504, 120100, 120105`, `## X-Tukui-ProjectID: -2` and `## X-Tukui-ProjectFolders: ElvUI, ElvUI_Libraries, ElvUI_Options`.
- **BugSack:** `## X-WoWI-ID: 5995`, `## X-Curse-Project-ID: 6273`, `## X-Wago-ID: rkGrrgGy`, `## OptionalDeps: !BugGrabber, Ace3, LibSharedMedia-3.0, LibDBIcon-1.0`.
- **Details:** `Details` with `## Title: |cff33ff99Details!|r Damage Meter`, plus `Details_DataStorage`. WoWI project 23056 (stale, 2020) appears in the fake index.
- Small synthetic sets for the other cases below.

**Files:** `src/resolve/adopt.rs` (`Tier`, `GroupClaim`, `Group`, `identify`). `src/limits.rs` (`ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` and its `REGISTRY` row) plus the limit-registry snapshot. `src/engine/plan.rs` (extract `primary_by_shape`, no behaviour change). New `tests/adopt_identify.rs` and `tests/fixtures/adopt/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

Table tests MUST cover:
- BigWigs with both a catalog entry and a conflicting `X-WoWI-ID: 5086` → `identified` as `gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs`, strength `catalog`, evidence `["catalog_folder","toc_wowi_id"]`, alternatives `["wowi:5086"]`.
- `X-WoWI-ID` only → `identified` `wowi:<id>`, strength `toc_id`.
- `X-Tukui-ProjectID: -2` with three listed folders → one group `tukui:elvui`.
- `X-Website: https://github.com/o/r` → `gh:o/r`. `X-Website: https://deadlybossmods.com` is ignored and is **not** a `url:` ref.
- DBM's folder set via the catalog → one 8-folder `identified` group, primary `DBM-Core`. With the stray `DBM-Extra` added (requires `DBM-Core`, shares the `DBM` prefix), it joins as a ninth folder without lowering the tier. `XYZ-Thing` requiring `DBM-Core` does not join (prefix differs).
- A unique WoWI `UIDir` with a matching Title (colour codes stripped) → `identified` (`corroborated`). With a mismatched Title **and** Author → `guess`.
- A folder name equal to a catalog alias only → `guess`.
- `X-Curse-Project-ID` only → `cf_only`, claim ref `null`.
- Two equal-strength conflicting claims (two catalog entries listing one folder, or two WoWI projects sharing `Details`) → `guess`, with the other ref in `alternatives`.
- A stray folder that requires a grouped folder and shares its prefix → joins the group.
- Nothing → `unknown`, claim `None`, empty evidence.
- BugSack with a catalog entry `gh:funkydude/BugSack` (fake) → `identified` as that ref with `wowi:5995` in `alternatives`, and no `cf_only` evidence.
- **No case adopts under a source other than the winning evidence names.** A helper asserts, for every case, that each group's ref is the rank-round winner for its members, that `alternatives` never contain the group's ref, and that no group carries a `url:`, `git:`, `file:`, `cf:` or `wago:` ref.

Invariants, asserted over every case:
- every candidate is in exactly one group;
- `unloaded_folders` is empty and no tier is `exact`;
- `alternatives.len() ≤ ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` (a folder listed by five WoWI projects yields 3);
- permuting the candidate order gives an identical result.

Also: `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` is registered and the registry snapshot is reviewed, and `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- **`tests/adopt_identify.rs` (new).** For each fixture set, build a synthetic client the way `tests/inventory.rs` does (`common::trees::BattlenetRoot`, its `battlenet_target` helper pattern) and copy the set into `AddOns/`. Run `inventory::inventory(&target, None, &RulesTable::builtin(), Depth::Full)`, map entries through `CandidateFolder::from_entry`, and call `identify`. This exercises real loaded-TOC selection and C1's `TocSummary`.
- **Lookups.** Use `Catalog::builtin()` for DBM and BigWigs; DBM's 8 folders come from the real catalog, so a catalog change correctly fails the test. Use fakes for everything else. ElvUI, Tukui and BugSack enter the builtin catalog only with C2 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.2`), so use fake catalogs, with and without an ElvUI entry: with one it is `tukui:elvui` at strength `catalog`, without it `toc_id`. The fake WoWI index holds sanitised `dirs`.
- **Unit tests in `src/resolve/adopt.rs`** for the pieces: rank rounds with crafted claims (round independence, discarded proposals, contested folders), joining chains, the prefix function, and tie order.
- **`proptest`** over random claim sets: every candidate in exactly one group, order independence, and alternatives never containing the group's ref.

## Considerations

- **Never fetch inside `identify`.** Exactness (`exact`), downloads, `unloaded_folders`, `reason` and report rendering are E5.1's. The `adopt` transaction is E5.2's. This bead adds no command and no output (DEC-1).
- **Conservative by construction** (the plan's default for open questions): a tie or a borrowed claim yields `guess`, and `guess` is never applied without an explicit folder. A WoWI compilation listing many folders can pull evidence-less folders into a `guess` group. That is acceptable, because nothing is applied implicitly.
- **Decisions made while writing this bead** (restate them in the close comment):
  - rank-based rounds, with proposals discarded once their source goes elsewhere;
  - a group whose members have no evidence of their own for its ref is a `guess`;
  - `unknown` folders group by connected components, while `cf_only` folders are one group each;
  - `name_only` disagreements appear only as ties;
  - coverage first in tie order;
  - `Tier::Exact` lives here, but `identify` never produces it;
  - E4.2 owns `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES`;
  - `primary_by_shape` is extracted.
- **Collision hot spots.** `src/engine/plan.rs` is edited by A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3 and C4.x. Keep the `primary_by_shape` extraction minimal: C3 changes `primary_folder`'s signature, and whichever lands second keeps both. `src/limits.rs` gains rows from many M2 beads; rebase before regenerating the registry snapshot.
- **B8's `status.adoptable`** is a cheaper name-only count and does not call `identify`.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- E4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4.1` (Adoption evidence and precedence per folder (pure)): provides `CandidateFolder`, `AdoptLookups`, `Claim`, `Evidence`, `Strength` and `evidence()`, which this bead groups. C1's `TocSummary.dependencies`, used for joining, arrives through it.

Unblocks:
- E5.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1` (adopt report mode): calls `identify` per target, upgrades groups to `exact`, fills `unloaded_folders` and renders the groups.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** The owner's clients hold addons that span many folders: DBM ships 8, BigWigs 12 and ElvUI 3. Adoption only helps if it records whole addons under the source `install` would choose. A half-adopted addon breaks the next `update` with `unmanaged_folder`. A module recorded under a different ref gets replaced by the wrong distribution. A guess presented as confident puts a wrong record behind an "Apply" button. This bead makes grouping and tiers one pure, exhaustively tested function, so `adopt` (E5) and agents reading `groups[].tier` see the same answer. It serves G-M2-4 (sole authority, confident identification only) and is the second half of the vision's adoption checkpoint: guesses are never applied implicitly, a `UIDir`-only match with mismatched Title and Author is never `identified`, and no fixture is adopted under the wrong source.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D40, evidence precedence.** The order is catalog, then Tukui id, then `X-Website` (GitHub, WoWInterface or Tukui links), then `X-WoWI-ID`, then corroborated WoWI, then name. Why: adopt must pick the source `install` would, and real TOCs carry several ids (BigWigs: `X-WoWI-ID: 5086`). Rejected: TOC ids first, which would adopt catalog addons under WoWInterface. Here it decides contests: the strongest rank wins, an equal rank gives a `guess`, and disagreeing ids are listed but never chosen.
- **M2-D18, departs from the vision.** CurseForge-only folders are `cf_only` with a `--ref` fix, not "adoptable with `auth curseforge set`", because that command arrives in M5. `exact` needs per-file SHA-256 equality with the newest release's verified install set, decided later by E5.1. Rejected: fingerprinting (M5) and version-string matching. This is why `identify` never yields `exact`.
- **Review-round fix.** The plan's second review pass found wrong-source adoption; the fix is source precedence, and the "no case adopts under a source other than the winning evidence names" property test guards it.
- **Plan defaults.** Conservative when unsure; deterministic key order. `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` (3) bounds returned data, so it goes in `src/limits.rs`. `GROUP_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS` (3) is a threshold, so it stays in the module.
- **Decided while writing the bead** (the plan leaves these open; restate them in the close comment):
  - Rank-based rounds. "Equal strength" means equal rank, because rows 2–4 share the wire strength `toc_id`.
  - A proposal is discarded once its source folder is assigned to a different ref.
  - A group with no member holding its own evidence for its ref is a `guess`.
  - Evidence-less leftovers group by require-plus-prefix components as `unknown`.
  - `name_only` disagreements appear in `alternatives` only as ties.
  - Tie order starts with coverage of the present folders.
  - `Tier::Exact` is defined here for E5.1 but never produced.
  - `primary_by_shape` is extracted from `primary_folder`.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- Code at `e902d36`: `catalog/catalog.toml` lists DBM's 8 folders (`:30`) and BigWigs' 12 (`:37`). `engine::plan::primary_folder` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1318`) picks `DBM-Core` for DBM by its single-core rule. `FolderName` compares by case-folded key. `inventory()` with `Depth::Full` gives each folder's loaded TOC.
- The repository has **no** DBM, BigWigs, ElvUI, BugSack or Details TOC fixtures. The plan assumed "real TOCs copied from fixtures", but `tests/fixtures/http/catalog/` holds only `release.json` and Atom bodies, so they are written trimmed by hand.
- Live on 2026-10-15: ElvUI's three folders carry `X-Tukui-ProjectID: -2`, `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders` and interfaces `11509, 16001, 20506, 38002, 50504, 120100, 120105`. BigWigs' `X-WoWI-ID: 5086` and Bartender4's `11190` were seen on the owner's `forever` client. BugSack's ids are `5995`, `6273` and `rkGrrgGy`. WoWI project 23056 (Details!) is a stale 2020 upload. 781 `UIDir` names are shared across projects.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *Over-grouping* by a WoWI compilation's `UIDir` set. Such claims are `name_only`, so the group is a `guess`, which E5 never applies without an explicit folder.
- *Under-grouping* of modules without ids. The require-plus-prefix join handles it, and E5.1's `folder_set_differs` reason catches the rest before anything is applied.
- *Order dependence:* round-wise assignment, plus a permutation test.
- Plan confidence for adoption is **medium-high**. It is heuristic by nature, and conservatism bounds a wrong call to a record that `undo` or `adopt --ref` corrects.

**Relation to siblings.** E4.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4.1`) must have landed: this bead consumes its `Claim`s and never re-derives evidence. Do not download, compare files, fill `unloaded_folders`, compute `reason` or render output: those are E5.1's (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1`). The record name rule and the transaction are E5.2's. Nothing outside the module calls `identify` until E5.1 lands.

    - Ref groups are the folders assigned to one ref.
    - Each still-unassigned folder with only rank-7 claims seeds its own `cf_only` group.
  - **Joining:**
    - An evidence-less folder joins a group when it requires a member, or a member requires it (`TocSummary.dependencies`, ignoring case), and both share a name prefix of at least `GROUP_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS` (3).

- `elvui`: 3 folders, Tukui −2 and the project folders;
- `bugsack`: WoWI 5995, Curse 6273, Wago `rkGrrgGy`, OptionalDeps;
- `details`: the coloured title, and `Details_DataStorage`.

Real ids are the bead's verified ones; the rest are synthetic. I chose one TOML file over 20 `.toc` files for reviewability.

**Tests:**
- **`tests/adopt_identify.rs` (11, plus a 64-case proptest):** each case writes the folders into a synthetic retail client, reads them through `inventory(Depth::Full)` and `CandidateFolder::from_entry`, then calls `identify`. The lookups are the builtin catalog or fakes; the WoWI fake sanitises dirs with `sanitize_dirs`. Every case runs `check`:
  - each candidate is in exactly one group, with no folder twice;
  - nothing is `exact` and `unloaded_folders` is empty;
  - alternatives are ≤ 3 and never the group's ref;
  - refs are only `gh:`, `wowi:` or `tukui:`;
  - the group's ref is named by some evidence for one of its folders;
  - the claim's presence matches the tier;
  - the result is identical reversed and rotated.
- **Cases:**
  - BigWigs: `identified` `gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs`, `catalog`, evidence `[catalog_folder, toc_wowi_id]`, alternatives `[wowi:5086]`, 4 folders, primary `BigWigs`.
  - `X-WoWI-ID` only gives `wowi:777` (`toc_id`). `X-Website` GitHub gives `gh:o/r`. `deadlybossmods.com` gives `unknown`, never `url:`.
  - ElvUI: one `tukui:elvui` group of 3 folders, `toc_id`; with a catalog entry it is `catalog`.
  - DBM: one 8-folder `identified` group, primary `DBM-Core`. With the strays, `DBM-Extra` joins (9 folders, still `identified`) and `XYZ-Thing` is `unknown`.
  - A unique `UIDir` with a matching coloured title, or the author only, is `identified` (`corroborated`). With both mismatched it is a `guess` (`name_only`).
  - A catalog alias only gives a `guess`. `X-Curse-Project-ID` only gives `cf_only` with a null ref. No evidence gives `unknown` with no claim.
  - Two catalog entries on one folder: a `guess` with the other in alternatives. Two WoWI projects sharing `Details`: the one covering more present folders wins, as a `guess` with the other in alternatives.
  - BugSack with a catalog entry: `identified` `gh:funkydude/BugSack`, alternatives `[wowi:5995]`, no cf evidence.
  - Five projects listing one folder: 3 alternatives.
  - All sets together: each addon in its group. Details is a `guess` because `Details_DataStorage`'s own `UIDir` match is not corroborated: the weakest member decides (rule 4).
- **The proptest:** random subsets of every fixture folder, in seeded random order, with a WoWI index that includes a contested project.
- **Unit (`resolve::adopt`, 2 new):**
  - the prefix rule (`DBM`, `BigWigs`, `UI_` rejected);
  - a discarded proposal: `Lib` is the catalog's, so its Tukui project-folder proposal, which also lists evidence-less `Mod`, is discarded. `Mod` stays `unknown`, and `Lib` lists `tukui:elvui` as an alternative.

**decided** (as the bead lists):
- rank-based rounds, with proposals discarded once their source goes elsewhere;
- a group without own evidence for its ref is a `guess`;
- `unknown` folders group by components, and `cf_only` folders are one group each;
- `name_only` disagreements appear only as ties;
- coverage comes first in tie order;
- `Tier::Exact` lives here but is never produced;
- E4.2 owns `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES`;
- `primary_by_shape` is extracted.

Also:
- The tie key orders ref classes in identity order, so mixed-class ties (for example a catalog name match against a WoWI dir match at rank 6) resolve as ref identity does. The GitHub catalog-name rule applies within the GitHub class.
- When joining, a group's "winning rank" is its members' best assignment rank (7 for `cf_only`).

**Wire names:**
- `Tier`: `exact`, `identified`, `guess`, `cf_only`, `unknown`.
- `Group` keys: `folders`, `primary`, `tier`, `claim` (`ref`, `strength`, `evidence`, `name`), `alternatives`, `unloaded_folders`.

**Constants:** `ADOPT_MAX_ALTERNATIVES` (3, new).

title: Epic: The adopt command
description:
## Background

The owner arrives with folders installed by hand or by another addon manager, and M1 can only replace them. `install` refuses such a folder with `unmanaged_folder`, whose fix (`unmanaged_fix`, `src/engine/ownership.rs:358`, "rerun with `--force` until `adopt` exists (M2)") overwrites it with a fresh download. `status` can only point at `list -t <id> --unmanaged` (`src/app/status.rs:393-399`). `TxKind::Adopt` (`src/model.rs:413`) exists but is never produced. Line numbers are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

This epic delivers `omaddons adopt`. It classifies every unmanaged folder and brings the confident ones under management (updates, drift checks, undo) without changing a byte under AddOns. It serves M2 goal G-M2-4, "Sole authority": folders installed before omaddons, or by another manager, come under management without being replaced, and only on confident identification. That is what makes omaddons the sole, safe, undoable authority over a client.

The identification rules are pure and belong to the split epic E4 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.4`). E4.1 collects per-folder evidence in the precedence M2-D40 fixed so that adoption picks the source `install` would: catalog folder index, `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, an `X-Website` GitHub/WoWInterface/Tukui link, `X-WoWI-ID`, a WoWInterface `UIDir` match corroborated by Title or Author, then a name match. E4.2 groups folders into addons with a tier. This epic is the command around them: inventory, lookups, downloads and hashing, the exactness check, the records-only `adopt` transactions, and hints in other commands.

```
$ omaddons adopt -t retail
retail: checking 14 identified addons against their newest releases (≈ 63 MB, 9 already cached)
retail: 41 unmanaged folders → 17 addons
  exact       DBM (8 folders)        gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods  12.1.15
  identified  BugSack                gh:funkydude/BugSack (catalog)    v12.1.6 (from TOC; update available)
  guess       Details (7 folders)    wowi:23056 (name only)            — not applied; choose with --ref (or wowi:25068)
  cf_only     TradeSkillMaster (2)   X-Curse-Project-ID only           — CurseForge arrives in M5; pass --ref
Apply exact + identified: omaddons adopt --apply -t retail
$ omaddons adopt --apply -t retail
retail: adopted 14 addons (31 folders), tx 01M5… — no folder was changed
```

## Goals

- A read-only report grouping every unmanaged folder into addons with a tier (`exact`, `identified`, `guess`, `cf_only`, `unknown`), evidence, alternatives and unloaded folders, writing nothing outside `<cache>/omaddons/`, `net.log` and `<state>/omaddons/inflight/`.
- An objective `exact` tier: the folders are byte-identical (per-file SHA-256) to the newest release's verified install set for this client (M2-D18).
- `--apply`, `<folder>…`, `--ref R` and re-pointing: one records-only transaction of kind `adopt` per target, all sharing one run id, writing records, index entries and history `record` ops, with no stage and no swap. Undo removes the records and leaves every folder byte-identical.
- Adopted addons update like installed ones, but a newer build adopted from another distribution is never downgraded (M2-D42: compare the candidate's primary interface and `out_of_date` verdict with the installed TOC; B4 and B6 implement it, E5.2 proves it end to end).
- Hints that today say `install`, `--force` or `list --unmanaged` offer `adopt` where it is the right next step, with an argv that runs.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- Fixture installs identical to the release come out `exact` (recorded with `release_id`, `version_confidence: release`); one version behind comes out `identified` (`toc`) and the next `update` replaces it.
- A `guess` is never applied without an explicit folder argument, and a guess with alternatives needs `--ref`.
- A WoWInterface `UIDir`-only match whose Title and Author both disagree is never `identified`.
- No fixture is adopted under a source other than its winning evidence. BigWigs, whose TOC carries `## X-WoWI-ID: 5086`, adopts as the catalog's `gh:` ref.
- `adopt --apply` changes no file under AddOns (tree hashes equal before and after). `undo` removes the records, and the folders stay byte-identical.
- A folder modified between `adopt --apply`'s planning and its lock fails with `plan_stale` (retryable).
- `status` recommends `adopt -t <id>` only when `adoptable > 0`, and `install X` onto an unmanaged `X` fails with the fix argv `omaddons adopt X --ref <ref> -t <id>`, which then succeeds.

## Non-Goals

- CurseForge and Wago adoption. Fingerprint matching and `auth curseforge` are M5. A CurseForge-only folder is reported `cf_only` and can be adopted only with an explicit keyless `--ref` (M2-D18).
- Changing, moving or deleting any folder. Adoption never stages, swaps or prunes. Leftover modules stay unmanaged.
- `adopt --force`, or adopting `Blizzard_*`, symlinked (`linked`), invalid or case-duplicate folders.
- Detecting two targets that share one AddOns directory through a symlink (adopt would double-manage it): a known limitation, filed for the M4 doctor (`target-addons-shared`) by H6.

## Considerations

- Adoption is heuristic. Conservatism bounds the damage of a wrong call to "a record that `undo` or `adopt <folder> --ref R` corrects": catalog-first precedence, `guess` never applied implicitly, exactness by hash, and the planning-time downgrade guard. Planning rated adoption confidence medium-high for this reason.
- Adoption never calls the write-oriented `ownership::check`; it reads inventory classes directly.
- Report mode may use the network, as a command whose job is to look upstream: always through `ReleaseCache` (`Window` freshness) and the WoWI index's max-age.
- Real-machine tests (H5) run report mode only, with `--no-verify`; `forever` stays read-only while `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` is open.
- Collision hot spots: `src/app/status.rs` (A2, B8, C6, E3, E5.x), `src/engine/plan.rs`, `src/error.rs`.

## Children

| Key | Id | Title | Scope in one line | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E5.1 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.1` | adopt report mode: classify unmanaged folders and verify exactness | `adopt [-t T] [--no-verify] [--refresh]`: inventory, lookups, `identify`, exactness check, report data, progress | A1, A2, A9, A10, B1, B3, D2, D3, D4, E1, E4.2 |
| E5.2 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2` | adopt --apply, named folders, --ref and repoint as records-only adopt transactions | `--apply`, `<folder>…`, `--ref`, repoint; the adopt transaction; report-mode `commands` | A4.1, A6, B5, B6, E5.1, F1 |
| E5.3 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3` | Adopt hints and fixes across status, outdated, update, pin, remove, install and dependencies | `adopt` recommendations and fixes in other commands, the ownership fix, C4's dependency hint | B7, B8, C4.1, E5.2 |

## How this was split

Planning sized `adopt` as one large (L) task, because its report, apply, named-folder, `--ref` and repoint modes share one pipeline (identify, then verify exactness, then plan records-only transactions) and each mode is thin over it. The split keeps that pipeline whole in one subtask and layers the rest on top:

- **E5.1** builds the pipeline and the read-only report: full-depth inventory, candidates, lookups, `identify`, the exactness check with its up-front download announcement, `unloaded_folders`, the offline and `--no-verify` rules, candidate facts, report data and progress. Its subcommand has only the report flags (`--no-verify`, `--refresh`; `-t` is global). Its `commands` stay empty and its human output names no `--apply` or `--ref`, because those do not exist yet (DEC-1: no flag before its behaviour; and M2's rule that a task never hints at a command a later task adds). After E5.1, `main` has a complete read-only `adopt`.
- **E5.2** adds the mutating modes over the same pipeline: `--apply`, `<folder>…`, `--ref` (resolved through F1's `src/app/resolve_args.rs`) and re-pointing; the adopt transaction (spec, record fields, naming, guard to `plan_stale`, commit with no stage or swap, undo); item failures with fixes; A6 output; and the report-mode `commands`, whose argv now runs. Other commands still emit their earlier hints (`install`, `--force`, `list --unmanaged`), which are valid, so nothing is half-supported.
- **E5.3** rewires hints in other commands: `status`, `outdated`, `update`, `pin`, `remove`, the engine's `unmanaged_folder` fix and C4.1's dependency hint. It edits those commands' code, so they must exist first. That is why it waits for B7 (`pin`), B8 (`status` `adoptable`), C4.1 (the dependency hint) and E5.2.

Dependents attach to the subtask that provides what they need: H5 (real-machine smoke tests) runs report mode only and waits for E5.1; H2 (crash and concurrency) needs the adopt transaction and waits for E5.2; H1 (contract audit) and H6 (docs and vision records) need every hint and wait for E5.3.
acceptance_criteria: E5.1, E5.2 and E5.3 are closed; fixture installs identical to the release adopt as exact with release_id and version_confidence release, and one-version-behind installs adopt as identified (toc) and are replaced by the next update; a guess is never applied without an explicit folder argument; a UIDir-only match with mismatched Title and Author is never identified; no fixture is adopted under a source other than its winning evidence (BigWigs with X-WoWI-ID adopts as the catalog gh: ref); adopt --apply changes no file under AddOns and undo removes the records with folders byte-identical; a folder modified between planning and lock gives plan_stale; status recommends adopt only when adoptable > 0; install onto an unmanaged folder offers an adopt --ref fix whose argv succeeds
close_reason: All children completed

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this epic, and how it serves M2.** Adoption is one of the two features (with `sync`) that make omaddons the *sole* authority over a client, which is the project's thesis. Without it, a migrating user's only path is `install --force`, which destroys and re-downloads every folder. With it, existing folders come under management (updates, drift, undo) without a byte changing, and only on confident identification (goal G-M2-4). Every adopt is a journaled, snapshotted, undoable records-only transaction, so no M1 guarantee weakens (G-M2-7).

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D18 (departs from the vision).** CurseForge-only folders are reported `cf_only` with a `--ref` fix, not "adoptable, fix `auth curseforge set`", because `auth curseforge` arrives in M5 and a fix must name a command that exists. `exact` needs per-file SHA-256 equality with the newest release's verified install set. Rejected: fingerprinting (CurseForge's method, M5) and matching version strings, which cannot prove the bytes are the release's.
- **M2-D40.** Evidence precedence is catalog, then `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, then `X-Website` (only GitHub, WoWInterface or Tukui links), then `X-WoWI-ID`, then corroborated WoWInterface `UIDir`, then name. Reason: adopt must pick the source `install` would, or the next `update` swaps the user's build for another distribution; real TOCs carry several ids (BigWigs `X-WoWI-ID: 5086`, Bartender4 `11190`, both curated `gh:` catalog entries). Rejected: TOC ids first, which would adopt catalog addons under WoWInterface.
- **M2-D42.** Identified (TOC-version) adoptions are protected from downgrades by comparing the candidate's primary interface and its `out_of_date` flag with the installed TOC. Rejected: trusting `release_id: None` as "anything is newer", which would "update" an adopted newer CurseForge build to an older keyless one.
- **M2-D6.** Records-only work is first-class in the engine (A4.1), so adopt needs no hand-rolled state write. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature, which would not be journaled or undoable.
- **Review-round fixes folded in.** Wrong-source adoption (second review) produced the catalog-first precedence and the `X-Website` host limit. The planning-time `older_than_installed` guard (third review) covers adoptions made with `--no-verify` or after memo eviction, where no fact exists yet.

**Facts verified during planning.** `src/engine/ownership.rs:358` (`unmanaged_fix`) appends `--force` and says it waits for `adopt`; `src/app/status.rs:393-399` emits `list_unmanaged`; `src/app/remove.rs:396-402` gives `not_managed` the fix `list --unmanaged`; `TxKind::Adopt` (`src/model.rs:413`) and `FolderOp::Record` exist unused (all as of `e902d36`). Live facts (2026-10-15): BugSack's TOC carries `X-WoWI-ID: 5995`, `X-Curse-Project-ID: 6273` and `X-Wago-ID`; the WoWInterface filelist has 781 folder names shared by several projects; Details! (`wowi:23056`) is a stale 2020 upload; the ElvUI zip carries `X-Tukui-ProjectID: -2` and `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders`.

**Risks and mitigations.** Adoption under the wrong source, or an "update" that replaces an adopted newer build with an older one: low likelihood after M2-D40 and M2-D42, high impact. Mitigations: catalog-first precedence, the `X-Website` host limit, Title/Author corroboration, `guess` never applied implicitly, the exactness hash, the downgrade guard, `adopt --ref` re-pointing and undo. Two targets sharing one AddOns directory through a symlink would be double-managed; documented as a known limitation and filed for the M4 doctor by H6. Planning rated adoption medium-high confidence: heuristic by nature, but conservatism bounds a wrong call to a record that undo or `--ref` corrects.

**Why the split.** One pipeline, three subtasks: E5.1 builds it read-only, E5.2 adds the transactions, E5.3 rewires other commands' hints once those commands exist. Each leaves `main` consistent.
