title: The addons.toml model and parser
description:
## Background

This bead serves M2 goal G-M2-5, **declarative sets**: the addon set of every client can be exported to one reviewable TOML file, reproduced exactly (`--locked`) or loosely, kept in sync idempotently, and copied between compatible clients. Vision bead §5.9 ("Desired state") fixes only the outline: per-family sections apply to every `live` target of that family, `[target.<id>]` sections are the only way to address `test` targets, and entries are refs with optional pins and versions. This bead makes that a precise format with a line-accurate parser, the merge rule and a deterministic renderer. It adds no command.

Facts in the code today (line numbers are as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- `Paths::addons_toml()` (`src/state/paths.rs:131`) returns `<config>/omaddons/addons.toml` ("Desired state for `sync` (M2)"). Nothing reads or writes it.
- `toml` 1.1.8 is a dependency; it exports `toml::Spanned` and `toml::de::DeTable::parse(text)`, which keeps a byte span on every key and value.
- The install argument resolver is `parse_ref` (`src/app/install.rs:497-538`, `pub(super)`): `sources::refs::parse_user_ref` plus two lookups, installed addons (record name or folder, case-insensitive, over **every** target's records) and catalog names and aliases. `src/app/info.rs:16` imports it. Install names a new catalog addon after its entry (`install.rs:380-385`).
- `Family` (`src/rules.rs:149`) serialises kebab-case; `Family::from_name` parses case-insensitively. `TargetKind` is `Live | Test` (`src/rules.rs:289`).
- `ErrorCode::ALL` has 38 codes and `WarningCode::ALL` 22 (asserted at `src/error.rs:702-703`, `:746`).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** new `src/state/desired.rs`; new `src/app/resolve_args.rs`; `src/app/install.rs`, `src/app/info.rs`; `src/error.rs` (`desired_state_invalid`; warnings `desired_unknown_key`, `desired_unknown_target`); new fuzz target `desired_toml` (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/`, its `[[bin]]` row, three or more seeds with one `malformed*`, `TARGETS` in `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`); new `tests/desired.rs`; `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.

### The format (authoritative)

The default path is `<config>/omaddons/addons.toml` (`Paths::addons_toml()`). Any path can be given to `sync`.

```toml
# Desired addon sets for omaddons. `omaddons sync` makes each client match this file.
schema_version = "1.0"

[family.mainline]                       # every live mainline client
addons = ["WeakAuras", "DBM", "wowi:5995", "LittleWigs"]

[[family.mainline.addon]]               # table form when options are needed
name = "BigWigs"
ref = "gh:BigWigsMods/BigWigs"
dependency = true                       # a lock for LittleWigs' dependency, not a request
version = "v428"

[[family.mainline.addon]]
name = "Plater"
version = "Plater-v661"
pinned = true

[family.vanilla]
addons = ["Questie", "DBM"]

[target."wotlk"]                        # one client by id; the only way to address test clients
addons = ["git:https://github.com/fondlez/GroupBulletinBoard#main"]
```

**Sections.**
- `family.<family>` uses the family wire names of `src/rules.rs`, including `vanilla-legacy` and its siblings. `family.unknown` and unknown family names are `desired_state_invalid`.
- `target.<id>` uses target ids; quote ids containing `@`. Unknown target ids are the warning `desired_unknown_target`, because a dotfile may list clients this machine lacks. `sync --prune` refuses while one exists (F3.3).

**Entries.**
- A string is a name or a ref, resolved the way `install` resolves its arguments: canonical ref, pasted URL, catalog name or alias, or a name installed on that target.
- A table has: `name` (required unless `ref` is given); `ref`; `channel` (`stable|beta|alpha`; **absent means `stable`**, not `default_channel`, so changing that config never invalidates a file); `version`; `pinned` (bool, absent means `false`); `dependency` (bool, absent means `false`); `sha256`, the blob hash, which `export` writes for `--locked` offline reproduction.

**The desired set of a target T** is the family section for `T.family` when `T.kind = live`, unioned with the `target.<T.id>` section. A target entry with the same identity (resolved ref, else name) overrides the family entry. Family sections **never** apply to `test` targets.

**Duplicates** are `desired_state_invalid`, citing both lines. Two layers: `parse` rejects *textual* duplicates in one section (the same name or the same ref string); `sync` (F3.1) rejects *resolved* duplicates per target (two entries resolving to the same ref) as an item failure for that target.

**Unknown targets** (`desired_unknown_target`) are reported by a separate `validate` step, because `parse` has no registry.

**Dependency entries** (`dependency = true`) are *version locks*, not requests: installed only when something on that target requires them, then at the locked version under `--locked`; matched to a dependency by **resolved ref identity** (a lock that matches nothing is ignored); and they protect a required dependency from `--prune`. F1 only parses the flag; C4.1 and F3.x act on it.

**Validation.** Unknown keys are the warning `desired_unknown_key`, with the line. Bad values are `desired_state_invalid` (new error code, exit 2, not retryable), citing the line and the key. A missing `schema_version` is treated as 1.0 (hand-written files). A newer major is `desired_state_invalid`, with fix "upgrade omaddons".

**Parsing** uses the `toml` crate with spans. `toml_edit` is not needed, because export writes a fresh document. User files are inputs, never migrated or rewritten in place.

### Types

`DesiredState { schema_version, families: BTreeMap<Family, Section>, targets: BTreeMap<String, Section> }`; `Section { entries: Vec<Entry> }`; `Entry { name: Option<String>, r#ref: Option<String>, channel: Channel /* default stable */, version: Option<String>, pinned: bool, dependency: bool, sha256: Option<String>, span }`, `span` being the byte range (reported as a 1-based line).

### `parse(text, path) -> Result<(DesiredState, Vec<Warning>)>`

- Accepts `addons = [...]` lists and `[[…addon]]` tables in one section. Walk the spanned document by hand (no `deny_unknown_fields`). Known keys: `schema_version`, `family`, `target`; per section `addons`, `addon`; per table the seven entry keys.
- Every `desired_state_invalid` carries `details: {path, line, key, reason}` with `reason` one of `bad_value` (wrong type or value, a table with neither `name` nor `ref`, `sha256` not 64 lowercase hex digits, and TOML syntax errors, decided), `unknown_family`, `newer_schema` or `duplicate` (names compare ASCII-case-insensitively; a bare string also collides with another entry's name or ref string; `details.line` is the later line). Its text fix starts with a fixed phrase registered in `TEXT_FIXES`. F2 and F3.3 add the reasons `edited`, `empty` and `unknown_target_section`.
- Ref syntax and names are **not** checked here: `resolve_entry` resolves them per target, and its `ref_invalid`, `not_found` and `ref_ambiguous` become sync item failures, so one typo never blocks a whole file (decided).

### `validate(state, known) -> Vec<Warning>`

`desired_unknown_target` (fix argv `omaddons targets`) for each `target.<id>` matching no known id, compared ASCII-case-insensitively as `discover::registry::resolve` does. Known ids are `world.resolved.targets` (registered or provisional) plus `world.resolved.missing`; the `Registry` alone would make every section unknown on a fresh machine.

### `desired_for(target, resolve) -> Vec<Desired>`

The merge rule: the family section only for `TargetKind::Live`, plus the `target.<id>` section. Each `Desired` holds the entry, its layer and its resolution; a target-layer entry replaces every family-layer entry with the same identity (hence the resolver parameter). Duplicates left after the merge are F3.1's.

### The extracted resolver and `resolve_entry(entry, target, records, catalog) -> Result<Ref>`

- Move `parse_ref`, its lookups and the catalog-name helper into `src/app/resolve_args.rs`, with the records to consult as a parameter. `install` and `info` pass every target's records: a pure move, guarded by their existing tests.
- `resolve_entry` uses `ref` when present, else `name`, and consults **only that target's record** for installed names.
- Relative `file:` paths resolve against the directory holding the desired-state file, so a file means the same thing wherever `sync` runs (decided).

### `render(state) -> String`

Deterministic TOML for F2: the header comment above, `schema_version = "1.0"`, sections in `Family` declaration order then target id, entries sorted by name, table form only, `channel` and `pinned` only when not the defaults, `dependency = true` only when set, every target id quoted. Format values with the `toml` crate, never by hand.

### Decisions applied

- **M2-D19** (departs from vision): `export` prints to stdout; `--write` writes only the config path, protected and with a `.bak`, under `Writer::Config`; no `--output` (fsx writes only inside its scope table). `render` serves both.
- **M2-D20**: `sync` never moves an addon to a newer release by itself; an unpinned entry's `version` matters only under `--locked`, and absent `channel` is a fixed `stable`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The example above parses with no warning. Family sections apply only to the live targets of that family (never to a test target), and target sections override family entries with the same identity.
- An unknown family, and `family.unknown`, are `desired_state_invalid` (exit 2) with `details.line` and `reason: "unknown_family"`.
- An unknown key at any level warns `desired_unknown_key` with the line; parsing continues.
- `validate` reports an unknown target id as `desired_unknown_target`, but not a discovered-unregistered or missing registered target.
- The same name twice in one section, in either form, is `desired_state_invalid` (`duplicate`), citing both lines.
- A missing `schema_version` means 1.0; `"2.0"` is `desired_state_invalid` (`newer_schema`), fix "upgrade omaddons".
- Absent `channel` is `stable` even with `default_channel = "beta"`; absent `pinned` and `dependency` are `false`.
- `render(parse(render(x))) == render(x)` holds as a proptest property; `render` is deterministic.
- `resolve_entry` resolves a catalog alias, a canonical ref, a pasted URL and a name installed on that target, not one installed only elsewhere.
- The fuzz target `desired_toml` runs 10 minutes clean and is listed in `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`.
- `install`'s and `info`'s existing tests pass unchanged after the extraction; the registries include the three new codes (`ErrorCode::ALL` 39).

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/state/desired.rs`): a table test per rule, with `details.line`; `desired_for` for live and test targets and both override paths; `render` ordering and default elision; the round-trip property.
- `tests/desired.rs`: `resolve_entry` on a fixture `Home` with two targets and a catalog override (target-only installed names, a relative `file:` path).
- Fuzz `parse` (seeds: the example, an empty file, a malformed one). Regression: `tests/install.rs`, `tests/info_netlog.rs`, the contract suite.

## Considerations

- User files are inputs, not state: never migrate or rewrite one in place. Keep `parse` free of I/O, registry and catalog access.
- A release-URL string's tag is not a pin: `resolve_entry` returns only the ref; pins come only from `version` plus `pinned = true` (document it).
- Collision hot spots: `src/error.rs` (codes from several M2 beads); `src/app/install.rs` (also edited by A3, A6, B9, C4.1, C5), so land the extraction as a small behaviour-free commit.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: none (can start immediately).

Unblocks:
- E5.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2` (adopt --apply, named folders, --ref and repoint): `--ref` resolves through `src/app/resolve_args.rs`.
- F2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.2` (The export command): builds a `DesiredState` and writes it with `render`.
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): uses `parse`, `validate`, `desired_for` and `resolve_entry`.
acceptance_criteria: The documented addons.toml example parses with no warning; family sections apply only to live targets of that family and never to test targets, and target sections override family entries with the same identity (resolved ref, else name); an unknown family or family.unknown is desired_state_invalid (exit 2) with details.line and reason unknown_family; an unknown key at any level warns desired_unknown_key with the line; validate reports unknown target ids as desired_unknown_target but not discovered-unregistered or missing registered targets; the same name or ref string twice in one section is desired_state_invalid (reason duplicate) citing both lines; a missing schema_version means 1.0 and "2.0" is desired_state_invalid with the fix "upgrade omaddons"; absent channel means stable regardless of default_channel and absent pinned/dependency mean false; render(parse(render(x))) == render(x) holds as a property test and render is deterministic; resolve_entry resolves catalog aliases, canonical refs, pasted URLs and names installed on that target only, through the resolver extracted to src/app/resolve_args.rs; install and info tests pass unchanged after the extraction; the desired_toml fuzz target runs 10 minutes clean and is listed in tests/fuzz_seeds.rs; error and warning registries include the three new codes
close_reason: addons.toml model, parser, merge rule, renderer and per-target resolver; gate green, fuzz 10 min clean

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** The owner's addon set lives only in per-target state files today, so it cannot be reviewed, kept in dotfiles, or reproduced after a reinstall. A small, strict, hand-editable format is the precondition for `export`, `sync` and part of `adopt`. It serves the project's thesis (omaddons as the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons) by giving that authority a declarative input that every later mutation still runs through the transaction engine. It is the first step of goal G-M2-5 (declarative sets). The format is pure and round-trip tested, which is why the M2 plan rates the desired-state format **high** confidence.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D19** (departs from vision): `export` prints to stdout; `--write` writes only `<config>/omaddons/addons.toml`, protected and with a `.bak`, under `Writer::Config`. Why: fsx only writes inside its scope table, and a shell redirect already writes anywhere under the user's own authority. Rejected: `--output <path>`, which would widen the write scopes. F1 supplies the one renderer both paths use.
- **M2-D20**: `sync` reconciles presence, channel, pins and locks, and never moves an addon to a newer release by itself. Why: idempotent, offline when nothing changed, predictable; freshness is `update`'s job. Rejected: making `sync` also update, which would hit the network and change things on every run. The format supports this: an unpinned entry's `version` is only used under `--locked`.
- **Absent `channel` means `stable`, never `default_channel`.** This is the format-side half of the "sync convergence" finding from the second review round: a file whose meaning shifted with config would make `sync` report differences forever.
- **Two duplicate layers.** Textual duplicates are a parse error (the user can fix the file); resolved duplicates depend on records and the catalog, so `sync` reports them per target as item failures.
- **`validate` is separate from `parse`.** `parse` has no registry, which keeps it pure and fuzzable; unknown targets are warnings because a dotfile may name clients this machine lacks.
- **Resolver extraction.** `sync` entries and `adopt --ref` must mean exactly what `install` means by the same string. One function in `src/app/resolve_args.rs` guarantees it.

**Decisions made while writing this bead** (record each with a `decided:` comment when implementing): ref syntax and names are resolved per entry by `resolve_entry`, not by `parse`, so one typo fails one item instead of the file; a TOML syntax error uses `details.reason: "bad_value"`; known target ids for `validate` include discovered-unregistered and missing-registered targets; relative `file:` entries resolve against the file's directory; installed-name lookup for an entry is limited to that target's record, while `install`/`info` keep their all-target lookup; every target id is quoted by `render`.

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `e902d36`): `Paths::addons_toml()` at `src/state/paths.rs:131`; `parse_ref` at `src/app/install.rs:497-538`, also used by `src/app/info.rs:16`; `toml` 1.1.8 exposes `toml::Spanned` and `toml::de::DeTable::parse` with spans; `Family::from_name` and kebab-case family wire names in `src/rules.rs`; the catalog parser uses `deny_unknown_fields`, which F1 must not copy because unknown keys here are warnings; `ErrorCode::ALL` is 38 and `WarningCode::ALL` 22 today; `TEXT_FIXES` already contains "upgrade omaddons".

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Moving `parse_ref` could change `install` behaviour subtly (installed-name lookup across targets). Mitigation: a pure move with the record set as a parameter, landed alone, guarded by the existing `install` and `info` suites.
- Span-to-line conversion for values inside inline arrays is easy to get wrong. Mitigation: table tests assert `details.line` for each rule.
- Hand-written files are messy. Mitigation: unknown keys warn instead of failing, and the fuzz target runs for 10 minutes at the checkpoint.

comments.text:
**decided (6.1 implementation):**

**Parsing**
- **Names and refs are not checked by `parse`.** `app::resolve_args::resolve_entry` resolves each entry per target, so one typo fails one item rather than the whole file.
- **Broken TOML** is `reason: bad_value`, with `key: ""` and the line the TOML parser points at (where the broken construct starts).
- **A bare string that is a canonical ref** (it parses as a `Ref`: `gh:o/r`, `wowi:5995`, `git:…`) is kept in `ref`; any other bare string is kept in `name`. This classifies syntax only and rejects nothing. It makes `render` write `ref = "wowi:5995"` instead of `name = "wowi:5995"`.
- **Duplicates** compare names and ref strings, both ignoring ASCII case (a bare string collides with another entry's name or ref).
  - `details.line` is the later line; `details.first_line` carries the earlier one.
  - The same family twice in different case, or the same target id ignoring case, is also `duplicate`.
- **Target section ids must fit the target id grammar** (letters, digits and `@._-`, starting with a letter or digit, ignoring ASCII case); otherwise `bad_value`. An id no client can ever have is a typo, not a client this machine lacks. This also keeps `render`'s quoting trivial.

**Types**
- **`Entry` and `Section` carry `line`** (1-based; 0 when built in code) instead of the byte span. Every consumer reports lines.
- **`DesiredState` is not `Serialize`/`JsonSchema` yet:** nothing puts it on the wire. F2 adds that if export's JSON includes it.

**Validation and resolution**
- **Known ids for `validate` come from the new `Resolved::known_ids()`:** discovered targets (registered or provisional) plus registered ones discovery did not find.
- **`resolve_entry`:**
  - looks installed names up in that target's record only (`install` and `info` keep the all-target lookup through `parse_ref`);
  - resolves relative paths and `file:` refs against the desired-state file's directory;
  - returns only the ref (a release link's tag is not a pin).

**Rendering**
- **Every target id is quoted** (`[target."wotlk"]`), formatted by the `toml` crate.
- **An empty section** renders as its bare header, which round-trips.

**Known issue:** the `./` component that `file:` refs keep (omad-ex35) shows through `resolve_entry` too. The test compares normalised paths and cites the bead.

title: The export command
description:
## Background

This bead serves M2 goal G-M2-5, **declarative sets**: the addon set of every client can be exported to one reviewable TOML file, reproduced exactly (`--locked`) or loosely, kept in sync idempotently, and copied between compatible clients. Reproducing a set starts with writing down the current one. Vision bead §5.9 says only "`export` writes the file"; this bead makes export print by default and write the config path only on request, with protections for hand edits (M2-D19, M2-D43).

The workflow it enables ("make my new machine look like my old one", the dotfiles user):

```
old$ omaddons export > dotfiles/wow/addons.toml          # or: omaddons export --write
new$ omaddons sync dotfiles/wow/addons.toml --locked --dry-run
retail: would install 12 addons · era: would install 5 · wotlk: would install 2
new$ omaddons sync dotfiles/wow/addons.toml --locked
…
new$ omaddons sync dotfiles/wow/addons.toml
nothing to do (3 clients match addons.toml)
```

- `[family.mainline]` applies to every live mainline client. `[target."wotlk"]` addresses one client by id; test clients (PTR, beta) are reachable only through target sections.
- `--locked` installs the recorded versions, from the blob cache when present. One `sync` transaction runs per target. The second run is a pure local comparison: zero requests, exit 0, no transaction, every item `unchanged`.

Facts in the code today (line numbers are as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- There is no `export` command; `Paths::addons_toml()` (`src/state/paths.rs:131`) is reserved. The `Config` scope row admits `Writer::Config` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:23`, documented "`config set`"), `Auth` and `Doctor` (`:99`); the `Cache` row admits every writer (`:104`).
- `config set` (`src/app/config.rs:285-326`) is the config-dir write pattern: `GlobalLock::acquire`, `ScopeTable::new`, `WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Config, …)`, `ensure_dir_all`, `mutate(…, Op::WriteFile { content, mode })` (atomic: temp file, fsync, rename).
- `World::records()` (`src/app/world.rs:108`) covers only discovered, registered targets. Registered targets whose client dir is gone are in `world.resolved.missing` (`RegistryEntry`, `src/state/registry.rs:34`), with key, id and paths but **no family and no kind**.
- `AddonRecord` (`src/model.rs:528`) has `version_confidence` (`release|toc`), `channel`, `pinned`, `reason`, `required_by` and optional `blob_sha256`.
- Human-mode stdout carries only rendered data; warnings go to stderr (`src/output/mod.rs:96-127`), so `omaddons export > file` yields a clean document.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** new `src/app/export.rs`; `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs` (`Export` in the Look help group, A1); `src/state/paths.rs` (`export_memo()` → `<cache>/omaddons/export.json`); `src/fsx/scope.rs` (doc only: `Writer::Config` covers `config set` and `export --write`); `src/error.rs` (warnings `export_missing_target`, `export_local_source`); new `tests/export.rs`; contract matrix rows and `TEXT_FIXES`; `README.md` (commands table, "What it does today").

**Synopsis:** `omaddons export [-t T] [--write] [--overwrite]`; `ExportArgs { write: bool, overwrite: bool }`. `--overwrite` without `--write` is `usage`, fix argv adding `--write` (decided).

### Selecting targets

`World::select_many` (A2): all targets by default; `-t vanilla` exports every vanilla client. Export is the one exception to "missing targets are excluded from fan-out": with no `-t` every registered target whose client dir is missing is exported too; with `-t`, one is included when the selector equals its id or key, as `World::history_key` matches missing entries (decided). Load their records with `load_record(&paths, &entry.key)`.

### Building the document (authoritative rules)

From records for the selected targets (default: all):
- **Live targets:** for each family, the family section is the intersection of the explicit addon sets of all live targets of that family, matched by ref with equal channel, pin **and version**. Each target's remainder goes in its `target.<id>` section.
- **`version` is written only for records with `version_confidence: release`.** Identified adoptions carry a TOC version, which is not a fetchable release. Equality for the intersection compares the written form (no version for `toc` records).
- **`file:` and directory records are skipped,** because they are machine-specific paths, with the warning `export_local_source` naming them. `url:` records are exported like any other.
- **Test targets** get target sections only.
- **Dependency records** are exported with `dependency = true` and their version, **in the same section as their requester**. If requesters sit in different sections, the lock goes in each. Decided: a family-section lock only when every live target of that family records the same dependency ref and version, else per target section; a dependency with no exported requester (orphaned, or required by a skipped local source) goes in its own target section.
- **Registered targets whose client dir is missing** (an unmounted drive) are exported from their state records, with the warning `export_missing_target` (fix argv `omaddons targets`), so a backup taken while a drive is unplugged is still complete. Their family and kind are unknown (the registry entry has neither), so their entries go in their `target.<id>` section only (decided).

**Entry form.** Every entry is written as a table with `name`, `ref`, `version`, `sha256` (only when `blob_sha256` is recorded **and** the blob still exists), and `channel` and `pinned` only when not the default. Tables are sorted by name, so the file diffs cleanly. A family entry gets `sha256` only when every member records the same blob hash (decided). Export builds the `DesiredState`; F1's `render` writes it.

### Output

**Default output** is the TOML document on stdout in human mode: redirect it anywhere, for example `omaddons export > dotfiles/addons.toml`. Under `--json` it is `data: {path, backup, targets, entries, content}`, field order as shown:

```json
"data":{"path":null,"backup":null,"targets":["retail","era","wotlk"],"entries":19,"content":"# Desired addon sets for omaddons…\nschema_version = \"1.0\"\n…"}
```

`targets`: exported ids, sorted; `entries`: entries across sections; `commands` stays empty. With `--write`, human output is one summary line (file, entry count, backup) instead of the document (decided).

### `--write`

`--write` writes `<config>/omaddons/addons.toml` with `Writer::Config`, following the `config set` pattern (global lock held for the read-compare-write). It protects hand edits:
1. If the existing file's SHA-256 differs from the hash omaddons recorded when it last wrote that file (kept in `<cache>/omaddons/export.json`), the file was edited by hand or by another tool. `--write` then refuses with `desired_state_invalid` (exit 2, `details.reason: "edited"`) and the fix `omaddons export --write --overwrite` (argv: the original argv plus `--overwrite`). **A missing hash record counts as edited.** No existing file means nothing to protect.
2. An export with **zero entries** refuses `--write` (`desired_state_invalid`, `details.reason: "empty"`), so a fresh machine cannot overwrite a real file with nothing. Its text fix is registered in `TEXT_FIXES`.
3. With `--overwrite`, or when the file is unedited, the previous content is first copied to `addons.toml.bak` (a `WriteFile` of the old bytes, atomic).
4. Then the new file is written (`WriteFile`, atomic). There is no moment without an `addons.toml`.
5. Then the new hash is recorded in `<cache>/omaddons/export.json` (a versioned cache file, kind `export_memo` 1.0; tolerant read: missing or corrupt means "no record"). If this write fails, the next `--write` asks for `--overwrite`: the safe direction.

`data.path` and `data.backup` name the files (null when not written). Identical content with a matching hash writes nothing, so an older `.bak` survives; `--dry-run` runs every check and writes nothing (both decided).

**Why no `--output <path>`?** fsx only writes inside its scope table, and arbitrary paths would mean widening it. A shell redirect already writes anywhere, under the user's own authority (M2-D19, M2-D43).

### Decisions applied

- **M2-D19** (departs from vision): stdout by default; `--write` writes the config path (protected, `.bak`) as `Writer::Config`. Keeps fsx scopes tight.
- **M2-D43**: refuse hand-edited or non-omaddons files without `--overwrite`, and empty exports: the config dir is not snapshotted, so a lost hand-edited `addons.toml` is unrecoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `retail` and `retail@steam` both having DBM and Plater at equal ref, channel, pin and version but differing in one addon, export puts the shared two in `[family.mainline]` and the difference in a target section.
- Test targets appear only as target sections. A dependency record appears as a lock (`dependency = true`, with its version) in its requester's section.
- `version` appears only for `version_confidence: release` records; `sha256` only when the blob exists; `channel` and `pinned` only when not the defaults.
- A `file:` or directory record is skipped with `export_local_source`.
- Two `--write` runs leave the previous content in `addons.toml.bak`. A hand edit followed by `--write` refuses (`details.reason: "edited"`, fix argv with `--overwrite`), and `--overwrite` then succeeds. A pre-existing file with no hash record also refuses.
- `--write` with zero entries refuses (`details.reason: "empty"`).
- Output is deterministic: repeated runs are byte-identical, and `omaddons export > f` produces a file F1's `parse` accepts with no warning.
- With an unplugged target (registered, client dir gone), its addons are still exported, in its target section, with `export_missing_target`.
- Without `--write`, export makes no request and writes nothing (dirs hashed before and after, apart from discovery's own cache).
- The JSON envelope matches the shape above; contract rows pass.

## Test Plan

- `tests/export.rs` (E2E): two mainline clients (a Battle.net root plus a custom root) with records from fixture installs or a `tests/common` state builder; a PTR target; a seeded dependency record; a `file:` install; a registered target whose client dir the test moves away.
- `--write` sequences: first and second write, hand edit then refusal, `--overwrite`, empty export, missing hash record, `--dry-run --write`.
- An insta snapshot of the document, a determinism check, a parse-back through F1, and contract rows (`export`, and `export --write` refused as `edited`).

## Considerations

- Unpinned entries carry `version` too; `sync` uses it only under `--locked`, because it never moves an addon to a newer release by itself (M2-D20). Do not drop it.
- Export never touches the network. Deleting `<cache>/omaddons/` stays safe: the only effect is that the next `--write` asks for `--overwrite`.
- Collision hot spots: `src/error.rs` (warning codes from several beads), `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs` (every command bead).

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1` (Grouped bare help with a command group registry): `export` joins the Look group in the same commit as its clap variant, and bare help must stay under 30 lines.
- A2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.2` (Multi-target selection with World::select_many): `-t` must fan out (`-t vanilla` exports every vanilla client) instead of failing `target_ambiguous`.
- F1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.1` (The addons.toml model and parser): export builds F1's `DesiredState` and writes it with F1's `render`.

Unblocks:
- F3.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.2` (sync --locked): its acceptance criterion is "`export` then `sync --locked` into an empty target reproduces refs and versions".
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit for M2): audits export's rows, codes, text fixes and determinism.
- H5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.5` (Real-machine smoke tests for M2): runs `export --json` read-only on every client and `export` then `sync --dry-run`.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): records the command, its warnings and the `Writer::Config` scope note.

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** "Make my new machine look like my old one" is the dotfiles user's canonical intent, and it starts with writing down what is installed. Export turns per-target state records into one reviewable, diffable file that `sync` can reproduce exactly. That keeps omaddons the sole authority over the clients (the project's thesis) even across machines and reinstalls, and it serves goal G-M2-5 (declarative sets). It is read-only by default, so an agent can run it freely.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D19** (departs from vision): export prints to stdout; `--write` writes only the config path (protected, with a `.bak`); the writer is `Writer::Config`. Why: fsx only writes inside its scope table, and shell redirection already reaches any destination under the user's authority. Rejected: `--output <path>`, which widens the write scopes for no gain. Consequence: `Writer::Config`'s documented scope grows from "`config set`" to "`config set` and `export --write`", which H6 records on the vision bead.
- **M2-D43**: `--write` refuses a hand-edited or non-omaddons file unless `--overwrite`, and refuses empty exports. Why: the config dir is not snapshotted, so a lost hand-edited `addons.toml` is unrecoverable, and a fresh machine must not overwrite a real file with nothing. Rejected: a single `.bak` as the only protection, which a second `--write` silently overwrites. The last-written hash lives in the cache dir because it is derived data; losing it errs on the safe side (the next `--write` asks for `--overwrite`).
- **M2-D20** (via F1): `sync` never moves an addon to a newer release by itself, so export writes `version` for unpinned entries too; `sync` only uses it under `--locked`.
- **Family sections as intersections, matched on ref, channel, pin and version.** That makes a family entry exact for every member, so `sync --locked` on another machine reproduces each client, and differences stay visible in target sections.

**Decisions made while writing this bead** (record with `decided:` comments): missing targets go in target sections only, because `RegistryEntry` carries no family or kind; `-t` can select a missing target by exact id or key, as `history_key` does; family-level locks only when every family member agrees, else per target; family `sha256` only when every member shares the blob; locks without an exported requester go in their own target section; identical content skips the write so an older `.bak` survives; `--dry-run --write` checks without writing; `--overwrite` without `--write` is `usage`; the hash memo is a cache file of kind `export_memo` 1.0 (a new wire name for H6).

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `e902d36`): `Writer::Config` and the scope rows at `src/fsx/scope.rs:23,99,104`; the `config set` write pattern at `src/app/config.rs:285-326`; `World::records()` covers only discovered registered targets (`src/app/world.rs:108`); `RegistryEntry` (`src/state/registry.rs:34`) has no family or kind; human-mode warnings go to stderr, so stdout carries only the document (`src/output/mod.rs:96-127`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A redirect of human output must be valid TOML. Mitigation: the test parses `export` stdout back through F1 with zero warnings.
- Intersection logic can silently drop an addon. Mitigation: every explicit record lands in exactly one of the family or target sections; a test counts records against entries.
- Confidence: the desired-state format and its export are pure functions over records, rated high confidence by the M2 plan.

comments.text:
**done:** `omaddons export [-t T] [--write] [--overwrite]` writes every client's addon set as one `addons.toml`. It goes to stdout by default; `--write` writes the config path, keeping the previous file as `.bak` and protecting hand edits. `argc gate` passes: 1109 tests, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical.

**What landed:**
- **`src/app/export.rs`** (new):
  - The types are `ExportArgs { write, overwrite }`, `ExportData { path, backup, targets, entries, content }` (wire order) and `ExportOutcome`. In human mode, the outcome prints the document alone, or with `--write` one summary line.
  - **Selection:**
    - `World::select_many`, plus registered clients whose dir is gone: all of them without `-t`, else the one `-t` names by id or key.
    - A `-t` matching only a missing client exports just that client.
    - Records come from `World::records()`; missing clients use `load_record`.
  - **`build`** (pure, unit tested):
    - `Ref::File` records (zips and directories) are left out, each with `export_local_source`.
    - A family is shared only when every discovered live client of it is exported. Its section holds the explicit entries every member has alike, keyed by ref identity, channel, pin and written version. The name comes from the first member by id; `sha256` is kept only when every member has the same existing blob.
    - The family section also gets the dependency locks every member records alike, where on each member something exported requires the lock.
    - Everything else goes in the client's own section; test clients and missing clients get only their own.
    - Empty sections are not written. Rendering is F1's `render`.
  - **`item`:** `version` only for `version_confidence: release`; `sha256` only while `paths.blob(sha)` exists; `dependency` from `reason`.
  - **`write`:**
    1. An empty export refuses (`desired_state_invalid`, `details.reason: "empty"`).
    2. Then the global lock (unless `--dry-run`), and a read of the existing file.
    3. A file whose SHA-256 differs from the memo's, or has no memo record, refuses (`reason: "edited"`, fix argv + `--overwrite`) unless `--overwrite`.
    4. Our own unchanged file with identical content writes nothing.
    5. `--dry-run` stops there.
    6. Otherwise a `Writer::Config` session writes `addons.toml.bak` (the old bytes), then the file (atomic `WriteFile`), then records the hash. A memo write failure is a `-v` note.
- **`src/state/export_memo.rs`** (new): `ExportMemo { written: path → sha256 }`, kind `export_memo` 1.0, with a KINDS row. Missing, corrupt or newer reads as empty. Written at `Paths::export_memo()` = `<cache>/omaddons/export.json`.
- **`src/error.rs`:** the warnings `export_missing_target` (fix argv `omaddons targets`) and `export_local_source`; the count test is now 29.
- **`src/fsx/scope.rs`:** `Writer::Config` is documented as `config set` and `export --write`.
- **CLI:** the `Export` variant; `COMMANDS` puts `export` in Look after `info`; name mapping and dispatch with `-v` notes. Bare help stays under 30 lines (Look: status list outdated info export history net-log).
- **README:** a new `### export` section, "What works today" rows, the limitations row, the status line, the `desired_state_invalid` row (`edited`/`empty`), and two warning rows.

**Tests:**
- **Unit (`app::export`):** shared entries form the family section (a different version is a different entry; the PTR gets its own); locks follow requesters (an orphaned lock stays per client) and local sources are left out; `version` and `sha256` are written only when they hold.
- **`tests/export.rs` (5):**
  - **Family layout:** retail, a custom mainline client renamed `steam`, and a PTR. DBM and Plater are shared, Foo and Lib are retail-only (Lib seeded as Foo's dependency), DBM is on the PTR, and DBM is pinned. The result:
    - `[family.mainline]` holds DBM (pinned, v1, sha256) and Plater;
    - the PTR section has DBM;
    - retail has Foo and Lib (a `dependency = true` lock at v1);
    - there is no `channel` key, the local zip gives `export_local_source`, `targets` are sorted, `entries` is 5 and `path`/`backup` are null.
    - The document snapshot (`export_document`) is reviewed. Human stdout equals the content and repeats byte-identically, the parse-back has no warning, and no request is made.
  - **No writes:** without `--write`, the state and config trees are unchanged and there is no `export.json`.
  - **`--write`:**
    - the first write sets `path`; the same export again writes nothing and leaves no `.bak`;
    - a new addon means the next write keeps the previous file as `.bak`;
    - a hand edit is refused with `edited` and fix `["omaddons","export","--write","--overwrite"]`, the file untouched; `--overwrite` keeps the edited file as `.bak`;
    - a deleted `export.json` means `edited`;
    - `--write --dry-run` writes nothing.
  - **Empty and usage:** an empty `--write` fails `empty`; `--overwrite` alone is usage with fix argv adding `--write`.
  - **Unplugged:** the dir is renamed away, the client is exported in its own section with `export_missing_target`, and `-t drive` exports only it.
- **Contract:** the `export` row (snapshot `export_ok`), `--write`, then a hand edit refused (snapshot `export_edited`), and `--overwrite` alone as usage. The help snapshots `bare_help_human` and `bare_help_json` are reviewed.

**decided:**
- A family section is written only when every discovered live client of the family is exported. A `-t` subset that leaves one out gets client sections, so `sync` never applies them to a client that was not exported.
- An unregistered discovered client counts as a member with nothing installed.
- Dependency locks go in the family section only when every member records the same lock (ref, channel, pin, version) and something exported on each member requires it. Otherwise they go in their client's section, and a lock nothing exported requires stays there.
- A family entry takes its name from the first member by id.
- Clients with nothing exported are still listed in `data.targets`; empty sections are not written.
- `data.path` is null under `--dry-run` and when the file already holds this export. The human summary is "wrote <path> (N entries); the previous file is <bak>", "<path> is up to date (N entries)" or "would write <path> (N entries)".
- The memo is keyed by the file's absolute path. A failure to save it is a `-v` note, never an error: the next `--write` asks for `--overwrite`.
- The empty-export fix is a text that does not start with `omaddons`, so it needs no `TEXT_FIXES` row.

**Wire names:**
- the command `export` and the flags `--write`, `--overwrite`;
- the data keys `path`, `backup`, `targets`, `entries`, `content`;
- the warnings `export_missing_target` and `export_local_source`;
- the `desired_state_invalid` `details.reason` values `edited` and `empty`;
- the persisted kind `export_memo` 1.0 (`<cache>/omaddons/export.json`, `written`).

No new error codes and no constants.

title: Epic: The sync command
description:
## Background

`omaddons sync` makes every WoW client on the machine match a desired-state file, `addons.toml`. It is the vision's "restore a fresh machine" intent and the dotfiles-friendly alternative to scripting installs (vision decision D32: declarative `sync` with per-family and per-target sections instead of a one-shot import). The workflow it serves:

```
old$ omaddons export > dotfiles/wow/addons.toml          # or: omaddons export --write
new$ omaddons sync dotfiles/wow/addons.toml --locked --dry-run
retail: would install 12 addons · era: would install 5 · wotlk: would install 2
new$ omaddons sync dotfiles/wow/addons.toml --locked
new$ omaddons sync dotfiles/wow/addons.toml
nothing to do (3 clients match addons.toml)
```

`[family.mainline]` applies to every live mainline client; `[target."wotlk"]` addresses one client by id and is the only way to reach test clients (PTR, beta). The second plain run is a pure local comparison: zero requests, exit 0, no transaction.

Today nothing of this exists (line numbers as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter). `Paths::addons_toml()` (`src/state/paths.rs:131`) is reserved and documented "Desired state for `sync` (M2)". `TxKind::Sync` (`src/model.rs:414`, wire `sync`) exists, but nothing produces it. The planner rebuilds a record from scratch on every install (`src/engine/plan.rs:730-732`) and reports "unchanged" when the release is already installed even if the record should change (`plan.rs:659-667`), so a naive "install everything listed" loop could neither keep pins nor converge.

`sync` composes other beads' work: the `addons.toml` parser and resolver (F1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.1`), `export` (F2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.2`), carry-over and records-only engine work (A3, A4.1, A4.3), the working view (A5), the multi-target outcome and run ids (A6, A12), dependency rounds (C4.1) and blob-cache installs (B9). Because these interact, the plan sized it L; it is split into three children.

It serves M2 goal G-M2-5, "Declarative sets": the addon set of every client can be exported to one reviewable TOML file, reproduced exactly (`--locked`) or loosely, kept in sync idempotently, and copied between compatible clients. It keeps G-M2-7 (no regression of M1 guarantees): every sync change is a journaled, snapshotted, undoable transaction.

## Goals

- `omaddons sync [<file>] [-t T] [--locked] [--prune] [--strict] [--dry-run] [--no-deps]` reconciles each selected target with its desired set: presence, pin flags, channels and, under `--locked`, exact versions.
- Idempotent: a re-run with nothing to change makes zero network requests and no transaction. `sync` never moves an installed addon to a newer release by itself (M2-D20: freshness is `update`'s job).
- One `sync`-kind transaction per target with every change for that target in it, all sharing one run id, so bare `omaddons undo` reverts the whole run.
- `--locked` reproduces exact versions, with no network when the blobs are cached.
- `--prune` removes only unlisted managed addons, keeps required and locked dependencies, never touches unmanaged folders, and refuses while a `target.<id>` section names an unknown target.
- Family sections apply to live clients only.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed, the vision's desired-state checkpoint holds (H7 records the evidence):
- `export` followed by `sync --locked` into an empty target reproduces refs and versions.
- Re-running `sync` immediately is a no-op with zero `net.log` lines and no transaction, including straight after a channel-only change that the first run recorded as a records-only `SetChannel` edit.
- `--prune` removes only unlisted managed addons and refuses on an unknown target section. Family sections never touch test targets.
- An entry pinned at another version installs that version; an unpinned entry against a locally pinned addon unpins it with a records-only edit and no request. `--locked --offline` with cached blobs succeeds.
- `--strict` turns a partial run into exit 6. Bare `omaddons undo` reverts a multi-target sync exactly. One sync transaction can mix install, remove and edit changes (H2 crashes it).

## Non-Goals

- Updating. `sync` never installs a newer release of an installed addon unless a pin, a lock or an explicit channel change says so. That is `update` (B6).
- Writing or migrating `addons.toml`. User files are inputs; `export --write` (F2) is the only writer.
- `copy --from --to` (F4) and the parser itself (F1).
- Separate addon sets per game mode: Classic Era, Hardcore and Season of Discovery share one AddOns folder.
- Re-pointing an addon to another source (`adopt --ref`, E5.2) and repairing drifted files (`install --reinstall`, B9).
- Stored plans: `--dry-run` keeps returning `plan_id: null` until M4.

## Considerations

- **Network economy is a requirement, not an optimisation.** The diff is a local comparison of records and entries. Only targets with changes reach the engine, and only planned installs fetch. Tests count `net.log` lines, never time.
- **Pins protect.** A pin-flag difference is always a records-only `SetPinned` edit and never moves the release. An explicit channel change is the one case where `sync` may install an older release without a pin or lock (the amended vision rule: no downgrades unless pinned, locked, or explicitly switched to another channel).
- **Prune is the dangerous flag.** A typo in a target section, a hand-written file that omits dependencies, or an empty section can remove real addons. F3.3 refuses the typo case, keeps required and locked dependencies, and every removal is undoable. `--dry-run` shows it first.
- **Shared files.** All three children edit `src/app/sync.rs` and `tests/sync.rs`; F3.2 and F3.3 may run in parallel after F3.1, so each rebases on the other. `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs` and `tests/contract/*` are edited by every command task.
- **Confidence.** High for the format and the diff (pure, table-tested); medium-high for the engine paths `sync` composes.

## Children

| Key | Id | Title | Scope in one line | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F3.1 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` | sync core: diff desired sets against records into one transaction per target | The command, file loading, entry resolution, the diff (install, `SetPinned`, channel, pinned version), one `sync` transaction per target, `--strict`, `--no-deps`, output | A1, A2, A3, A4.1, A4.3, A5, A6, A9, A10, C4.1, F1 |
| F3.2 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.2` | sync --locked: exact versions from locks and the blob cache | `--locked`: versions for every entry, the local-blob candidate with `sha256` verification, `not_locked`, dependency locks into C4.1's lock input | B9, F2, F3.1 |
| F3.3 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.3` | sync --prune with dependency, lock and unknown-target safety | `--prune`: removals for unlisted managed addons with the dependency and lock exceptions, and the unknown-target-section refusal | F3.1 |

## How this was split

- **F3.1 is the whole diff engine and convergence.** It ships the command with `[<file>] [-t T] [--strict] [--dry-run] [--no-deps]`, the resolution and duplicate rules, every diff row that needs neither flag (install what is missing, `SetPinned` for pin differences, an `Install` on the new channel that A4.3 turns into `SetChannel` when its newest release is installed, an `Install { version }` for a pinned entry at another version), one `sync` transaction per target, and the A6 output. After F3.1 a re-run is already a zero-request no-op, family sections already skip test targets, and undo already reverts a multi-target sync. `main` is consistent: there is no flag that does nothing (DEC-1, no stubs: each command adds its subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour).
- **F3.2 adds `--locked`** over the same diff, with its help text and contract row (as does F3.3 for its flag): versions apply to unpinned entries too, `sha256` entries use B9's local-blob candidate after verifying the blob, entries without a version install the newest with `not_locked`, and `dependency = true` locks feed C4.1's lock input by resolved ref identity. It waits for B9 (the local-blob candidate) and F2 (the export-then-`sync --locked` criterion), so the F2 edge moved here from the unsplit task.
- **F3.3 adds `--prune`** as a flag over the same diff: `Remove` changes for unlisted managed addons, with the dependency and lock exceptions and the unknown-target refusal. It needs only F3.1, because `Remove` and the records-only `Forget` come from M1 and A4.1, which F3.1 already requires.
- **Dependents attach to the subtask that provides what they need:** H5 (real-machine `export` then `sync --dry-run`) waits for F3.1. H1 (contract audit), H2 (crash coverage, including the mixed install-remove-edit sync transaction) and H6 (README, help and vision records) wait for both F3.2 and F3.3, because they audit the finished surface.
acceptance_criteria: export followed by sync --locked into an empty target reproduces refs and versions; re-running sync is a no-op with zero net.log lines and no transaction, including straight after a channel-only change recorded as a records-only SetChannel edit; sync never updates an installed addon to a newer release without a pin, lock or explicit channel change; --prune removes only unlisted managed addons, keeps required and locked dependencies, never touches unmanaged folders and refuses on an unknown target section; family sections never touch test targets; --locked --offline with cached blobs succeeds; one sync transaction per target under one run id, undone together by bare undo; --strict turns partial into exit 6

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this epic, and how it serves M2 and the project.** The project's thesis is that omaddons is the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons. Adoption (E5) brings existing folders under that authority; `sync` keeps it there declaratively. Today the owner's addon set exists only in per-target state files, so a reinstalled machine or a new client means retyping installs one by one. With `export` (F2) and `sync`, the set lives in one reviewable, diffable file in the owner's dotfiles, and one command reproduces it, idempotently, with every change a journaled, undoable transaction. It is goal G-M2-5 ("Declarative sets") and the vision's desired-state checkpoint, and it must not weaken G-M2-7 (every mutation is a transaction, every write goes through fsx, every request is logged).

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D20.** `sync` reconciles presence, channel, pins and locks, and never moves an addon to a newer release by itself. Why: idempotent, offline when nothing changed, predictable; freshness is `update`'s job. Rejected: making `sync` also update, which would hit the network and change things on every run, so a re-run could never be a no-op.
- **M2-D37.** Per-command freshness: `sync` uses the 15-minute memo window (`SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL`), like `outdated`, `update` and `copy`; `install` revalidates. Rejected: one window for every command, which would make a fresh `install` miss a release published minutes ago.
- **M2-D6.** Records-only work, a per-target working view and folder handover are first-class in the engine. `sync` needs all three: pin and channel edits without touching folders, several addons in one transaction, and a sync whose install comes before an update that drops a folder. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature, which would be neither journaled nor undoable.
- **M2-D38.** History lines carry a run id, and bare `undo` reverts the most recent run. A multi-target sync is undone by one command. Rejected: reverting only the last transaction, which would revert one client out of three.
- **The amended "never downgrades" rule (M2-D10's second half).** Neither `update` nor `sync` installs an older release unless a version is pinned or locked, or the user explicitly switches the channel. An entry's `channel` differing from the record is such an explicit switch.
- **DEC-1 (no stubs: a command adds its subcommand and flags only with their behaviour)** shaped the split: `--locked` and `--prune` arrive with their behaviour in F3.2 and F3.3, never as accepted-but-ignored flags.

**Review-round fixes folded in.** The fresh-implementer review pass found a sync-convergence gap: a record-only difference (for example a channel change whose newest release is already installed) came back "unchanged" and would be re-planned on every run. The fix folded in is A4.3's conversion of record-only differences into records-only edits (`SetChannel`, `SetPinned`), plus the acceptance criterion "a re-run straight after a channel-only change makes zero requests". The consistency pass fixed pin-kind derivation (a sync's `sync` kind override wins over the pinned-only `pin` rule) and made folder handover order-independent, so a sync that lists an install before an update dropping the same folder behaves like the reverse order.

**Facts verified during planning** (commit `e902d36`): `Paths::addons_toml()` is reserved at `src/state/paths.rs:131`; `TxKind::Sync` exists at `src/model.rs:414` and is never produced; the planner overwrites `channel`, `pinned` and `reason` on every install (`src/engine/plan.rs:730-732`) and reports unchanged for a same-release install (`plan.rs:659-667`); the engine's ownership fixes append `--force` to the running argv (`src/engine/ownership.rs:256-264`, `:358-363`), which `sync` must rewrite because it has no `--force`; the `toml` crate is already a dependency.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- `--prune` removing wanted addons: the unknown-target-section refusal, the dependency and lock exceptions, `--dry-run`, and undo.
- Sync silently updating or re-fetching: the diff is local; acceptance counts `net.log` lines on re-runs and on installed-behind addons.
- Mixed transactions (install, remove, edit) in delicate engine code: A4.x and A5 own the engine semantics, and H2 crashes a mixed sync transaction with the folder and record oracles.

**Confidence in the plan:** high for the desired-state format and diff, which are pure and round-trip tested; medium-high for the engine paths underneath, mitigated by M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites.

title: sync core: diff desired sets against records into one transaction per target
description:
## Background

`omaddons sync` makes each WoW client match a desired-state file, `addons.toml` (vision decision D32: declarative `sync` instead of a one-shot import), idempotently.

Today (line numbers as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; symbol names are what matter):
- No `sync` subcommand exists (`cli::Command`, `src/cli.rs:122`). `Paths::addons_toml()` (`src/state/paths.rs:131`) is reserved for it. `TxKind::Sync` (`src/model.rs:414`, wire `sync`) is never produced.
- The planner rebuilds a record on every install (`src/engine/plan.rs:730-732`) and returns "unchanged" when the release is installed (`plan.rs:659-667`), so a naive "install every entry" loop would unpin addons, never record a channel switch, and fetch every ref on every run.
- Ownership refusals append `--force` to the running argv as their fix (`src/engine/ownership.rs:256-264`, `:358-363`); `sync` has no `--force`.

It serves G-M2-5, "Declarative sets" (every client's set in one reviewable file, kept in sync idempotently), and G-M2-7 (every change a journaled, undoable transaction). `--locked` (F3.2) and `--prune` (F3.3) come later.

## Technical Approach

**Command.** `omaddons sync [<file>] [-t T] [--strict] [--no-deps]` plus global flags (`--dry-run`, `--offline`). `SyncArgs { file: Option<PathBuf>, strict, no_deps }`; no `--locked`/`--prune` yet (DEC-1). Add `Command::Sync`, `sync` in the Change help group (A1), `command_name`/`dispatch` arms.

**The file.** Default `<config>/omaddons/addons.toml`; a relative `<file>` joins the current directory. Missing default: `not_found` (exit 3) with the **text** fix "pass the file: `omaddons sync <path>`, or run `omaddons export --write` on the machine that has your addons" (add to `TEXT_FIXES`); a missing given path is `not_found` naming it (decided). F1's `parse`: `desired_state_invalid` (exit 2, `details {path, line, key, reason}`) fails the command before any change; warnings pass through. F1's `validate` adds `desired_unknown_target` for unknown `target.<id>` sections; sync proceeds.

**Format rules** (F1's): `[family.<family>]` applies to **live** clients only; `[target."<id>"]` is the only way to reach test clients. Entries: a string (name or ref) or a table (`name`, `ref`, `channel` default `stable`, `version`, `pinned` default false, `dependency`, `sha256`). A target entry overrides a family entry with the same identity (resolved ref, else name). `dependency = true` entries are version locks, never requests: no change here.

**Per run.**
1. `World::load()`, `select_many(ctx)` (A2). A selected target with no applicable section is untouched: `no_section: true`, no items.
2. **Resolve** with F1's `desired_for(target, resolve)`, passing `resolve_entry` (the install resolver, `src/app/resolve_args.rs`): it applies the override and returns each `Desired` with its resolution. A resolver error (`not_found`, `ref_ambiguous`, `ref_invalid`, `source_disabled`) is a failed item whose message names the file and line.
3. **Resolved duplicates:** two non-lock entries on a target resolving to one ref both fail: `desired_state_invalid`, `details.reason: "duplicate"`, own `line`, message citing the other. Nothing is planned for that ref (decided: they may disagree, so act on neither).
4. **Diff**, a pure `fn diff(entries, record) -> Vec<DiffItem>`. For entry E (ref R, channel Ce, version Ve, pinned Pe), `rec` is the record whose ref has R's identity. First matching row wins, so an addon gets at most one change (one work per addon per transaction):

| Situation | Change |
|---|---|
| no `rec` | `Install { ref: R, channel: Ce, channel_explicit: true, version: Pe ? Ve : None, pin: Pe ? Pin : Keep, reason: Explicit, file: None, reinstall: false, name }` |
| Pe, Ve set, Ve ≠ `rec.version` | `Install { version: Ve, pin: Pin, channel: Ce, channel_explicit: true, reason: Explicit }` |
| Ce ≠ `rec.channel` | `Install { version: Pe ? Ve : None, pin: P, channel: Ce, channel_explicit: true, reason: Explicit }` |
| only Pe ≠ `rec.pinned` | `Edit { addon: rec.name, edit: SetPinned(Pe) }`, records-only, no fetch |
| otherwise | nothing; item `unchanged` |

   `P` = `Keep` if Pe equals `rec.pinned`, `Pin` if Pe, else `Unpin`. `name` = the catalog name for a catalog ref (as `install`), else the entry's `name`, else `None` (decided). Versions compare as exact strings (`export` writes them verbatim).
5. **Carry-over** (A3, A4.3 implement it): `pinned` Pin → true, Unpin → false, Keep → existing; `channel` and `reason` as passed (`Explicit` promotes a dependency); `required_by` kept. **A pin intent never moves the release by itself**: Pin/Unpin without a version keeps the installed release. **Record-only differences are changes**: the same release (folders present) with differing `pinned`, `channel` or `reason` becomes a records-only work. So row 3 installs the new channel's newest release, or records `SetChannel` (plus `SetPinned`) when that release is installed or a pin intent keeps it; the next run sees no difference.
6. **Sync never updates (M2-D20).** An unpinned entry never moves an installed release; its `version` matters only under `--locked` (F3.2).
7. **Transactions.** One `TxRequest { kind: Some(TxKind::Sync), run }` (A4.1 override, A12 run id), one `TxTarget` per target with changes, `default_kind: Sync`, changes ordered family entries then target entries in file order. The override beats every kind rule: a sync that only unpins is kind `sync`. Set C4.1's `TxRequest.no_deps` from `--no-deps` (its rounds resolve dependencies as for `install`); leave `TxTarget.dependency_locks` empty. **With no changes on any target, build no engine and call neither `engine.run` nor `ReleaseCache::get`.**
8. **Freshness.** `Window` (M2-D37); `--offline` gives `OfflineOnly`: memo of any age with one `stale_check`, archives only from the blob cache, uncached items fail `offline`. Records-only edits need no network. No stale fallback on network errors.
9. **Fix rewrite.** `ownership_conflict` and `unmanaged_folder` items get fix `omaddons install <ref> --force -t <id>` instead of the argv plus `--force` (as B6 does for `update`). Rewrite only a fix (or alternative) that is the running argv plus `--force`: E5.3 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3`, unordered with this bead) makes the engine's `unmanaged_folder` fix `omaddons adopt <folder> --ref <ref> -t <id>` with the `--force` retry as an alternative, and that adopt fix must pass through unchanged, with only its `--force` alternative rewritten.
10. **Output** via A6 (abridged below): item `request` = the entry's `name`, else its ref string; statuses `installed, updated, pinned, unpinned, edited, unchanged, failed`; `unchanged` hidden unless `-v`, counted in `summary`. Pre-engine failures and `no_section` targets go in through A6's `push_item`/`push_target`, the footer lines through `notes`. `commands`: `undo --run <run>` first when more than one transaction committed, then `undo <tx>` each. Human output: "nothing to do (N clients match <file>)" when nothing changed; "sync does not update; run `omaddons update`" whenever an item is `unchanged`. `--strict`: partial → exit 6 `check_failed`, data kept. Progress events (A9).

```json
"targets": [{"target": {"id": "ptr"}, "tx": null, "kind": null, "no_section": true, "items": []},
 {"target": {"id": "retail"}, "tx": "01M…", "kind": "sync", "no_section": false, "items": [
   {"request": "DBM", "status": "unpinned", "from_version": "12.1.14", "to_version": "12.1.14",
    "folders": {"added": [], "replaced": [], "removed": [], "recorded": ["DBM-Core", "DBM-GUI"]}}]}],
"summary": {"targets": 2, "changed": 1, "unchanged": 4, "skipped": 0, "failed": 0}
```

**Files:** new `src/app/sync.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs`, `src/app/help.rs`, new `tests/sync.rs`, `tests/common/` (`write_desired` helper), `tests/contract/{matrix,main}.rs`, snapshots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `sync <file>` installs every missing desired addon in one `sync`-kind transaction per target, all under one run id.
- An immediate re-run MUST log zero `net.log` lines, commit nothing, report every item `unchanged` and exit 0, also straight after a channel-only change recorded as `SetChannel`.
- An installed addon behind its newest release with an unpinned entry (with or without `version`) MUST NOT be updated: no request, folders byte-identical.
- Family sections never touch test targets (a PTR stays byte-identical, `no_section: true`); `[target."ptr"]` installs there.
- A pinned entry at another version installs that version, `pinned: true`. An unpinned entry against a pinned addon unpins it with a records-only edit (kind `sync`), no update, no request.
- A channel change records `SetChannel` without touching folders when its newest release is installed, else installs that release.
- A target entry overrides a family entry with the same resolved ref.
- An unresolvable entry fails its item (`partial: true`, exit 0; `--strict` exit 6). A resolved duplicate fails both entries.
- Missing default file → `not_found` with the text fix; invalid file → exit 2 before any change; unknown target section → `desired_unknown_target`.
- A required dependency installs in the same transaction; `--no-deps` skips it and warns.
- An `ownership_conflict` item's `fix_argv` is `omaddons install <ref> --force -t <id>`.
- Bare `omaddons undo` after a two-target sync reverts both transactions exactly.
- `--dry-run` writes nothing outside `<cache>/omaddons/`, `net.log` and `<state>/omaddons/inflight/`.
- Help group, contract rows and progress events are in place.

## Test Plan

- **Unit:** `diff` table test over every row and intent combination, locks, duplicates, the override, change order.
- **E2E** (`tests/sync.rs`, A10 helpers: `gh_release_v`, `installed_behind`, `net_log`, `record`/`history`, `release_graph`): `Home::new(&["wow", "wowt"])` gives retail plus the PTR (id `ptr`, kind test); `Home::with_custom` adds a second live mainline target. One test per criterion; tree hashes around every no-touch claim. Offline: an unpin works; an uncached install fails `offline`.
- **Contract:** matrix rows, a snapshot, deterministic `--dry-run`.

## Considerations

- Sync never repairs vanished folders (B9's job).
- A listed dependency record is promoted only when another difference plans an `Install`; no separate `SetReason`.
- A different ref for an installed addon counts as not installed and fails `ownership_conflict`; re-pointing is `adopt --ref` (E5.2).
- An explicit channel change may install an older release (allowed, like pins and locks).
- Hot spots: `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs`, `tests/contract/*` (every command task); F3.2 and F3.3 extend `src/app/sync.rs`. Avoid engine edits: `src/engine/plan.rs` is shared by A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3, C4.x.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1` (grouped help): `sync` joins the Change group within the 30-line bound.
- A2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.2` (select_many): `-t` fans out over family, mode and product selectors.
- A3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.3` (carry-over): `Install` gains `channel_explicit`, `pin`, `reason`; pins survive installs.
- A4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.1` (records-only work): `Edit(SetPinned)`, the `sync` kind override, `record` ops for undo.
- A4.3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.3` (record-only differences): `SetChannel` conversion, so a channel change converges in one run.
- A5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.5` (working view): many addons per transaction, order-independent claims and handover.
- A6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.6` (multi-target outcome): shape, `no_section`, renderer, undo commands with A12's run ids.
- A9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.9` (progress): events for a long command.
- A10 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.10` (test helpers): the fixtures and readers used.
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (dependency rounds): dependencies, `--no-deps`, the lock input; brings `ReleaseCache` (B1) and its `Window` freshness into planning.
- F1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.1` (addons.toml parser): `parse`, `validate`, the merge rule, `resolve_entry`.

Unblocks:
- F3.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.2` (sync --locked): adds `--locked` over this diff.
- F3.3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.3` (sync --prune): adds `--prune` over this diff.
- H5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.5` (real-machine smoke): runs `export` then `sync --dry-run` on real clients.
