comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead, and how it serves M2 and the project.** It turns `addons.toml` into the owner's addon set on every client with one command, and makes the second run free. That is the core of G-M2-5 ("Declarative sets") and the vision's desired-state checkpoint ("re-running `sync` is a no-op", "family sections never touch test targets"). It extends the thesis that omaddons is the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons from "one install at a time" to "the whole set at once", without weakening G-M2-7: every change is a transaction of kind `sync`, undone as a run by bare `omaddons undo`.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D20.** `sync` reconciles presence, channel, pins and locks, and never moves an addon to a newer release by itself. Why: idempotent, offline when nothing changed, predictable. Rejected: making `sync` also update, which would hit the network and change things on every run.
- **M2-D37.** `sync` uses the memo window (`Window` freshness, 15 minutes); `install` revalidates. Rejected: one window for every command.
- **M2-D6.** Records-only work, the per-target working view and handover are engine features, so sync's pin and channel edits are journaled, snapshotted and undoable. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes.
- **M2-D5.** Pin and unpin are records-only transactions of kind `pin`; but a sync's `TxRequest.kind` override (`sync`) wins, so a sync that only unpins is recorded as `sync`. Rejected for pins in general: plain state writes (not undoable) and reusing other kinds (misleading history).
- **M2-D24.** Multi-target commands fan out family, mode and product selectors through `select_many`; single-target commands keep `resolve_one`. Rejected: changing `resolve_one` globally.
- **M2-D38.** A run id on every history line; bare `undo` reverts the latest run. Rejected: reverting only the last transaction.
- **M2-D9 and M2-D33** come with C4.1's rounds: a resolved dependency that fails to install makes the run partial while the requester still installs (rejected: failing the requester, or skipping silently); dependency installs use `default_channel` (rejected: inheriting the requester's channel).
- **The amended "never downgrades" rule:** no older release unless pinned, locked, or explicitly switched to another channel. An entry's differing `channel` is an explicit switch.

**Decisions made while writing this bead** (each recorded as "decided" in the body): resolved duplicates fail every entry of the set rather than the second only, because the entries may disagree on options; a new install is named after the catalog entry, else the entry's `name`; a missing explicit file path is `not_found` like the default; no engine is built when nothing changed, so a no-op run cannot touch the network; ownership fixes are rewritten to `install <ref> --force -t <id>`, because the engine appends `--force` to the running argv and `sync` has no such flag (found in the code, not in the plan).

**Review-round fixes folded in.** Sync convergence (fresh-implementer pass): a channel change whose newest release is installed would otherwise come back "unchanged" forever; A4.3's records-only `SetChannel` fixes it, and a re-run straight after it MUST make zero requests. Pin-kind derivation and order-independent handover (consistency pass): the kind override rule order, and A5 releasing folders before any claim is judged, so the order in which a file lists entries never changes the outcome.

**Facts verified during planning** (commit `e902d36`): `Paths::addons_toml()` at `src/state/paths.rs:131`; `TxKind::Sync` at `src/model.rs:414`, never produced; record rebuild at `src/engine/plan.rs:730-732`; same-release "unchanged" at `plan.rs:659-667`; `--force` appended to fixes at `src/engine/ownership.rs:256-264` and `:358-363`; the PTR's target id is `ptr` (kind test, `src/rules.rs`), and `tests/common/trees.rs` builds it from product `wowt`.

**Risks and mitigations.** A silent update or a hidden fetch would break idempotency: acceptance counts `net.log` lines on re-runs and on installed-behind addons. Order-dependent outcomes in multi-addon transactions: A5's working view, plus a determinism test. Confidence: high for the pure diff; medium-high for the engine paths it composes, covered by M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites and by H2.

**Relation to siblings.** This bead MUST NOT add `--locked` or `--prune` (DEC-1). Keep `diff` open for them: F3.2 adds a "locked" input that makes unpinned versions count and fills C4.1's dependency-lock input; F3.3 adds removals for unlisted records after the entry changes.

**decided (6.3.1 implementation):**

**The file**
- **Missing-file fixes.** `export` does not exist yet, so the default-file fix does not name it: "pass the file: `omaddons sync <path>`, or write <default path> (see `omaddons help sync`)". - **Long help.** `omaddons help sync` carries a short example of the file (`after_long_help`).

**Entries and items**
- **New-install name:** the catalog name for a catalog ref, else the entry's `name` only when the entry also gives a `ref`. A bare string or a name-only entry is what the user typed, which `install` never names an addon after.
- **An existing addon is re-planned under its recorded ref and name,** so a ref written in another case or as a pasted link still finds it.
- **Lock entries (`dependency = true`) are skipped entirely:** no item and no duplicate check. F3.2 reads them.
- **Resolved duplicates:** each entry fails with `desired_state_invalid`, `details: {path, line, key: "", reason: "duplicate", other_line}`, fix "keep one of the entries on lines A and B of <path>". Nothing is planned for that ref.
- **Items are listed in file order,** dependencies last.

**Engine results**
- **A dependency that resolved but failed** (a failure carrying `details.required_by`) becomes a failed item of its own, so the run is `partial` (M2-D9). Otherwise `TargetsData::build` would drop it, since nobody requested it by name.
- **Fix rewrite:** a fix argv that is exactly the running argv plus `--force` becomes `omaddons install <ref> --force -t <id>`. `ItemError` carries no alternatives, so there is nothing more to rewrite until E5.3 adds them.

**Footer lines (human output)**
- "nothing to do (N clients match <file>)" when nothing changed or failed, where N counts the selected targets with a section.
- "sync does not update; run `omaddons update`" whenever an item is unchanged.

**Dry run.** A dry run leaves an empty `<state>/omaddons/trash/`. Cleanup prunes the plan's in-flight lock file into trash: the same root cause as omad-gfoq, which owns removing both, and this bead avoids engine edits. The dry-run test allows `inflight/` and `trash/`; everything else (records, history, config, AddOns) is compared byte for byte.

title: sync --locked: exact versions from locks and the blob cache
description:
## Background

`omaddons sync <file> --locked` reproduces the exact versions an `addons.toml` records, which restoring a fresh machine from dotfiles needs (`old$ omaddons export > dotfiles/wow/addons.toml`, then `new$ omaddons sync dotfiles/wow/addons.toml --locked`). The M2 checkpoint (and the vision's) says: "`export` followed by `sync --locked` into an empty target reproduces refs and versions". Without `--locked`, F3.1's `sync` ignores the `version` of unpinned entries and installs the newest release: refs are reproduced, versions are not.

What exists today (line numbers as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; symbol names are what matter):
- Planning always fetches release metadata first (`plan::plan` calls `fetch_once`, `src/engine/plan.rs:266-288`), even when the archive is already in `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/`.
- A local archive gets a content id, `<ref>@sha256:…` (`file_candidate`, `plan.rs:1241-1252`), so a cached blob cannot stand in for a known release without B9's local-blob candidate.
- B1's memo keeps only the newest release per ref and never memoises pinned-version fetches, so a locked version costs a metadata request unless a B3 candidate fact names it. WoWInterface serves only its current file, so an old WoWI version cannot be fetched at all.

This bead adds `--locked` to `sync` (F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1`). It serves G-M2-5, "Declarative sets", whose first promise is "reproduced exactly (`--locked`)", and G-M2-1's economy: a same-machine restore from cached blobs needs no network.

## Technical Approach

**Flag.** Add `locked: bool` to `SyncArgs` (`--locked`: "install the versions the file records, from the blob cache when cached"), update `help sync`, and add a contract row in the same commit (DEC-1).

**The diff under `--locked`.** F3.1's pure `diff` gains a `locked` input. Every rule of F3.1 stays; the version column changes (E = entry with ref R, channel Ce, version Ve, pinned Pe; `rec` = the record with R's identity; `P` = `Keep` if Pe equals `rec.pinned`, `Pin` if Pe, else `Unpin`):

| Situation | Without `--locked` (F3.1) | With `--locked` |
|---|---|---|
| no `rec` | `version: Pe ? Ve : None` | `version: Ve` (any entry with a version) |
| `rec`, Ve set, Ve ≠ `rec.version` | change only when Pe | `Install { version: Ve, pin: P, channel: Ce, channel_explicit: true, reason: Explicit }` |
| `rec`, Ce ≠ `rec.channel` | `version: Pe ? Ve : None` | `version: Ve` |
| no `rec`, no Ve | newest | newest, plus warning `not_locked` |

- **Pins are not implied by locks.** An unpinned entry installs its locked version unpinned (`pin: Keep` on a new install records `pinned: false`), so a later `update` may move it. Re-running `sync --locked` moves it back; plain `sync` never does.
- **An installed entry without a version** is left as F3.1 leaves it; `not_locked` is raised only when something is actually installed without a version.
- Rows apply in F3.1's order; one change per addon.

**Entries with a `sha256`** (written by `export` only when the blob still existed). B9 provides one builder for the **local-blob candidate**: given `(ref, release_id, version, channel, sha256)`, if `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/<sha256>` exists and its streamed SHA-256 matches, it returns a candidate with `location: AssetLocation::LocalZip(<blob>)` and the given `release_id` and `version` (overriding the `<ref>@sha256:` identity); otherwise it reports "not cached". B9 leaves the request-side input to this bead. So:
1. Add an optional, internal `blob_sha256: Option<String>` to `RequestedChange::Install` (default `None`, carried on `AddonWork`, never on the wire), and set it from the entry for every `--locked` install that names Ve.
2. In planning (`want()` and the `to_fetch` list), an install with `blob_sha256` looks up the memo candidate fact whose `sha256` equals it (B3 facts: `{release_id, asset, sha256, size, verdicts}`). Fact found and blob present: call the builder with the fact's `release_id` and skip the source entirely.
3. No fact but blob present: fetch the exact version as a pinned `Wanted { ref, channel, version: Some(Ve) }` (metadata only), then call the builder with the fetched release's `release_id`; no download.
4. Builder says "not cached" (blob missing or its bytes do not hash to the entry's `sha256`, logged under `-v`): fetch and download the exact version, as any pinned install.
5. The candidate is inspected and TOC-verified against the current client; the blob cache is trusted for integrity, never for compatibility. B9's rank fallback applies: if an unannotated local-blob candidate is refused, the exact-release fetch is used, and B3's facts still spare the download.

A freshly downloaded archive is verified by the source's own hash rules and not compared with the entry's `sha256` (decided: the plan verifies only the cached blob against the entry, so bytes are reproduced exactly only from the cache; versions always are).

**A version the source no longer serves** (WoWInterface keeps only the current file; a deleted GitHub tag) makes the pinned fetch fail. The item fails `not_found`, and sync replaces its fix with the invocation's argv minus `--locked` (`omaddons sync <file> [-t T]`, as `fix_argv`), meaning "sync to the newest instead".

**`not_locked`** (new warning code, registered in `src/error.rs` with the `WarningCode::ALL` count and expected table updated): one warning per target listing every entry installed without a version (decided: one per target keeps the output frugal for string-form entries, which never carry a version). Text fix: "add `version = \"…\"` to those entries, or regenerate the file with `omaddons export`" (add to `TEXT_FIXES`).

**Dependency locks.** Under `--locked`, take each target's applicable `dependency = true` entries (with a `version`), resolve them through F1's `desired_for`, and fill C4.1's `TxTarget.dependency_locks: BTreeMap<Ref, String>` (resolved ref → version; ref identity). C4.1's round N then plans `Install { reason: Dependency, pin: Keep, channel: default_channel, version: <lock> }` for a dependency whose resolved ref matches; a lock never pins, and one matching nothing is ignored. Locks carry versions only, so a locked dependency costs one metadata request; B3's facts still spare the download when its blob is cached (decided: no blob-hash input for dependency locks). A dependency already installed is satisfied and keeps its release (C4.1's satisfaction rule), so a lock fixes only the version of a dependency `sync --locked` installs. Without `--locked`, `dependency_locks` stays empty.

**Offline.** `--locked --offline` uses `OfflineOnly` freshness. A pinned-version fetch is impossible offline, so an explicit entry needs a memo fact and a cached blob (step 2); otherwise the item fails `offline`. A locked dependency always needs its metadata, so offline it fails `offline` like any unreachable dependency (the requester still installs and the run is partial, per C4.1's failure rule). With blobs and facts from an earlier install on the same machine and no dependency to install, the run makes zero requests.

**Idempotency.** After `sync --locked`, every locked entry matches its record, so an immediate re-run of `sync --locked` (and of plain `sync`) logs zero `net.log` lines and commits nothing.

**Files:** `src/app/sync.rs` (flag, `diff` locked input, lock collection, fix rewrite, `not_locked`), `src/engine/plan.rs` (`RequestedChange::Install.blob_sha256`, the fact lookup in `want()`/`to_fetch`, calls to B9's builder), `src/engine/tx.rs` (`AddonWork` carries the hint), `src/app/help.rs`, `src/error.rs` (`not_locked`), `tests/sync.rs`, `tests/contract/{matrix,main}.rs`, snapshots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Checkpoint:** `export` followed by `sync --locked` into an empty target reproduces refs and versions. Fixture: install older releases on home A, switch the scenario so newer releases are latest, `export`, then `sync --locked` on a fresh home B with the same clients. Every record has the exported ref, version and `release_id`; unpinned entries stay unpinned.
- Plain `sync` of the same file into an empty target installs the newest releases instead.
- `--locked --offline` with the blobs cached (and the facts recorded by the original install) succeeds with zero `net.log` lines.
- With the blob cached but no memo fact, the run makes exactly the metadata request and no `asset` download.
- A cached blob whose bytes do not hash to the entry's `sha256` is not used: the version is fetched and downloaded.
- A locked version the source no longer serves fails its item `not_found`, with `fix_argv` = the argv without `--locked`; the run is partial.
- An entry without a version installs the newest release and raises one `not_locked` warning for its target, with the text fix.
- An installed, unpinned addon at a version other than its entry's moves to the entry's version under `--locked` and stays unpinned; without `--locked` it is unchanged.
- A dependency lock: under `--locked`, installing a requester installs its dependency at the lock's version with `reason: dependency`; a lock that matches nothing is ignored.
- Re-running `sync --locked` immediately logs zero `net.log` lines and commits nothing.
- `--locked` appears in `help sync`, the contract row passes, and `not_locked` is registered.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (`src/app/sync.rs`): the `diff` table with `locked` on and off over every row; `not_locked` grouping; the fix rewrite (argv without `--locked`, other flags kept).
- **E2E** (`tests/sync.rs`, A10 helpers): `gh_release_v`/`gh_latest` sequences, `Home::installed_behind`, `home.scenario(...)` to switch latest, `net_log(home)` counts by host and purpose (`asset`, `release-json`), `record(home, target)`. The export-then-locked checkpoint across two homes; same-machine restore (install, `export`, `remove`, `sync --locked --offline`); blob present without fact; corrupted blob (overwrite the cached file in the test's tempdir); a fixture whose pinned-version fetch answers 404, standing in for WoWInterface's current-file-only rule (D3 is not a dependency); `release_graph` with a `dependency = true` lock.
- **Contract:** matrix row for `sync --locked`; `TEXT_FIXES` entry for `not_locked`.
- H2 later crashes a sync transaction that installs from the blob cache.

## Considerations

- A lock never implies a pin; `pinned` comes only from the entry. Locked installs may be downgrades, which the amended vision rule allows ("unless a version is pinned or locked").
- Pinned-version fetches bypass the memo by design: with uncached blobs, each locked entry costs one metadata request; blobs plus facts make it free.
- `git:` and `url:` records usually carry no `sha256` and take the plain pinned-version path.
- Hot spots: F3.3 edits `src/app/sync.rs` and `tests/sync.rs` in parallel (rebase on it); `src/error.rs` gains codes from several beads; keep the `src/engine/plan.rs` and `tx.rs` change to the hint and the fact lookup, since A3, A4.x, A5, A8, B3, B9, C3 and C4.x share them.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- B9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.9` (install --reinstall and installs from the blob cache): provides the local-blob candidate that plans a known release from `blobs/<sha256>` with its own `release_id` and `version`, and the exact-release fetch path; it also brings B3's candidate facts.
- F2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.2` (The export command): the checkpoint criterion starts from `export`, which writes `version` for release-confidence records and `sha256` only when the blob exists.
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): the command, the `diff` this flag extends, and the transaction and output path.

Unblocks:
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit): audits the finished `sync` surface, including `--locked` and `not_locked`.
- H2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` (Crash and concurrency coverage): crashes sync transactions in their final shape, including installs from the blob cache.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): documents `--locked` and records `not_locked`.
acceptance_criteria: export followed by sync --locked into an empty target reproduces refs, versions and release ids even when newer releases exist, and unpinned entries stay unpinned; plain sync of the same file installs the newest instead; --locked --offline with the blobs and facts of an earlier install succeeds with zero net.log lines; a cached blob without a memo fact costs exactly the metadata request and no asset download; a cached blob whose bytes do not hash to the entry's sha256 is not used and the version is fetched and downloaded; a locked version the source no longer serves fails its item not_found with fix_argv equal to the argv without --locked; an entry without a version installs the newest with one not_locked warning per target and a text fix; an installed unpinned addon at another version moves to the entry's version under --locked and is unchanged without it; a dependency lock installs the dependency at the locked version with reason dependency and an unmatched lock is ignored; re-running sync --locked logs zero net.log lines and commits nothing; --locked is in help sync, the contract row passes and not_locked is registered
close_reason: sync --locked: recorded versions, blob-cache installs by entry sha256 (offline with facts), not_locked, dependency locks, unlocked fix for unserved versions; gate green

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead, and how it serves M2 and the project.** A dotfile that can only say "these addons" restores a machine to today's releases, not to the setup that worked. `--locked` makes `addons.toml` a lock file: `export` then `sync --locked` reproduces refs and versions, the vision's desired-state checkpoint and the first promise of G-M2-5 ("reproduced exactly"). On the same machine, cached blobs and memo facts make the restore free of network, which serves G-M2-1's economy and lets `--offline` restores work. Every locked install is still a TOC-verified, journaled, undoable transaction (G-M2-7).

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D20.** `sync` never moves an addon to a newer release by itself; locks are one of the explicit exceptions. Rejected: making `sync` also update.
- **The amended "never downgrades" rule (from M2-D10):** neither `update` nor `sync` installs an older release unless a version is pinned or locked, or the channel is explicitly switched. A lock is such an explicit version, so a locked downgrade is intended.
- **M2-D28.** Per-command download de-duplication plus blob facts in the memo: each distinct archive downloads once per command and not at all when cached. `--locked` is a main beneficiary. Rejected: re-downloading per target, as M1 does.
- **The memo rules (M2-D1, M2-D37):** the memo is derived data in `<cache>/omaddons/`; pinned-version fetches are never memoised because they must see the exact release; offline runs answer from the memo and may install only what is already in the blob cache. Rejected: an update-result file in state, and one freshness window for every command.
- **M2-D19 and M2-D43 (export side):** `export` writes `sha256` only when the blob still exists, and `--write` never overwrites a hand-edited file. Rejected: `--output <path>` (widens fsx scopes) and a single `.bak` as the only protection.
- **M2-D33 (via C4.1):** dependency installs use `default_channel`; a lock supplies only the version. Rejected: inheriting the requester's channel.

**Decisions made while writing this bead.**
- Locks never imply pins: an unpinned locked entry installs unpinned. The plan's diff sets `version` under `--locked` but takes the pin intent from the entry.
- A freshly downloaded archive is not compared with the entry's `sha256`. The plan verifies the cached blob against the entry and is silent on downloads; adding a failure there would invent behaviour, so bytes are reproduced exactly only from the cache.
- One `not_locked` warning per target, not per entry, because string-form entries never carry a version.
- B9 builds the local-blob candidate and leaves the request-side input to this bead, so an internal `blob_sha256` hint on `RequestedChange::Install` (never on the wire) carries the entry's hash, and the memo-fact lookup for its `release_id` lives in planning.
- Dependency locks carry versions only, matching C4.1's `TxTarget.dependency_locks: BTreeMap<Ref, String>`; a locked dependency therefore costs one metadata request, and offline it fails like any unreachable dependency.
- The `not_found` fix for a version no longer served is the invocation's own argv minus `--locked`.

**Facts verified during planning.** Code at commit `e902d36`: planning always fetches first (`plan::plan` calls `fetch_once`, `src/engine/plan.rs:266-288`); a local archive's id is `<ref>@sha256:…` (`file_candidate`, `plan.rs:1241-1252`), which is why B9's local-blob candidate must override it. Live fact verified 2026-10-15: WoWInterface's `filedetails` describes only the current file (one `UIVersion`, one `UIMD5`, one `UIDownload` URL), and the plan's WoWI source therefore answers any other `--version` with `not_found` ("WoWInterface serves only its current file").

**Risks and mitigations.** A corrupted cached blob installing wrong bytes: the blob is re-hashed against the entry before use. A lock that the source can no longer serve: a clear `not_found` with an executable fix to sync loosely. Locks silently moving installed dependencies: they apply only to dependencies `sync --locked` installs. Confidence: high for the diff column (pure); medium-high for the blob path, which rests on B9 and B3.

**Relation to siblings.** F3.1 owns the command, the diff and the transaction; this bead only adds the `locked` input, the blob path, `not_locked` and dependency locks. F3.3 (`--prune`) is independent and may land first or in parallel; both edit `src/app/sync.rs`, so rebase on each other. Combining `--locked --prune` needs no extra rule: locks keep dependency records from pruning in F3.3 either way.

title: sync --prune with dependency, lock and unknown-target safety
description:
## Background

`omaddons sync --prune` completes "make this client match the file": it also removes managed addons the file no longer lists. The M2 checkpoint (and the vision's) says "`--prune` removes only unlisted managed addons". Without the flag, F3.1's `sync` (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1`) only adds and edits, so an addon dropped from a dotfile stays installed forever.

Pruning is the one destructive part of `sync`. Three hazards shape it: a typo such as `[target."retial"]` leaves the real target's extra addons out of its desired set, so a naive prune would remove them; a hand-written file may list LittleWigs without BigWigs (only `export` writes dependencies as `dependency = true` locks), and removing BigWigs breaks LittleWigs; and unmanaged folders are never omaddons' to remove.

What exists today (line numbers as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; symbol names are what matter): `RequestedChange::Remove { addon }` (`src/engine/plan.rs:83`) removes a managed addon's folders through a normal transaction, and undo restores them. A remove whose folders are already gone writes `ops: []` to history (latent defect 1); A4.1 turns it into a records-only `Forget` with `record` ops, which F3.1 already depends on.

This bead adds `--prune`. It serves G-M2-5 ("Declarative sets": every client kept in sync with the file) and G-M2-7: every removal is a journaled, undoable transaction, and unmanaged folders are untouched.

## Technical Approach

**Flag.** Add `prune: bool` to `SyncArgs` (`--prune`: "also remove managed addons the file does not list"), with help text stating the safety rules below and a contract row, in the same commit (DEC-1).

**Refusal first.** Before resolving or planning anything, if F1's `validate` reported any `desired_unknown_target` (a `target.<id>` section naming no known target), `--prune` fails the whole command with `desired_state_invalid` (exit 2) and `details {path, line, key: "target.<id>", reason: "unknown_target_section"}`. The message names the section and its line and says that `sync` without `--prune` is allowed. Fix: `omaddons targets` as argv, which lists the valid ids (decided). The refusal applies whatever `-t` selects, because the file as a whole is suspect. Nothing is changed. Registered targets whose client dir is missing are known, not unknown.

**Which records are removed.** Prune applies only to selected targets **with a desired set**. A target with no applicable section stays untouched and reports `no_section: true`, so a PTR reached by no target section is never pruned. For each such target, build the keep set K from the target's records:
1. every record whose ref has the identity of a resolved, desired, non-lock entry;
2. every record matched by a `dependency = true` lock of that target (resolved ref identity);
3. every record a failed entry may mean: the ref of a resolved duplicate, and each candidate ref a `ref_ambiguous` entry lists (decided: never prune what the file might name);
4. then, repeated to a fixpoint, every record whose `required_by` names a record already in K, so chains A → B → C survive.

Every other record becomes `Remove { addon: record.name }`, appended after F3.1's changes for that target, sorted by addon name (case-insensitive). The removals join the target's single `sync` transaction, so one transaction can mix install, remove and edit changes, and bare `omaddons undo` reverts the run.

**The dependency rule, decided.** The plan states the exception as "unless the record is `reason: dependency` and still required by a desired addon, or matches a `dependency = true` lock", and its acceptance criterion says prune "never removes a dependency that a listed addon requires". Rule 4 applies whatever the recorded `reason`: an explicitly installed BigWigs that a listed LittleWigs requires is kept too, and it is transitive. That is the conservative reading of both sentences. A `required_by` name that is no longer recorded protects nothing.

**Engine behaviour reused.** A record whose folders are all absent becomes A4.1's records-only `Forget`. Removals follow the running policy like `remove`. When C6 lands, its `RemoveRequiredBy` bookkeeping and `still_required`/`orphaned_dependency` warnings apply to prune removals too; this bead does not depend on it.

**Output** via A6: removed items have `status: "removed"`, `request` = the record's name, `from_version` set, `to_version: null` and `folders.removed`; records kept only by rules 2–4 produce no item. `--dry-run --prune` lists the removals and changes nothing. Re-running `sync --prune` right after finds nothing to remove and makes zero requests.

**Files:** `src/app/sync.rs` (flag, refusal, keep set, removals), `src/app/help.rs`, `tests/sync.rs`, `tests/contract/matrix.rs`, snapshots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `sync --prune` removes exactly the managed addons that are unlisted and unprotected on each target with a desired set; listed addons are untouched.
- It MUST NOT remove a record a listed addon requires (directly or through a chain) or a record matching a `dependency = true` lock, and MUST NOT touch an unmanaged folder (AddOns tree hash of unmanaged folders equal before and after).
- With any `target.<id>` section naming an unknown target, `--prune` refuses with `desired_state_invalid`, `details.reason: "unknown_target_section"`, exit 2, nothing changed, even when `-t` selects another target; plain `sync` of the same file proceeds with a `desired_unknown_target` warning.
- Targets without an applicable section are untouched under `--prune` and report `no_section: true` (a PTR fixture).
- One sync transaction that installs one addon, removes another and unpins a third commits as kind `sync`; its history line has `add`, `remove` and `record` ops; bare `omaddons undo` restores the previous folders and records exactly.
- `--dry-run --prune` lists the removals and writes nothing outside the cache, `net.log` and `<state>/omaddons/inflight/`.
- Pruning a record whose folders are gone records `record` ops, and undo restores the record.
- Re-running `sync --prune` immediately logs zero `net.log` lines and commits nothing.
- `--prune` is in `help sync`, and the contract matrix has a row for the refusal.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (`src/app/sync.rs`): keep-set table test: listed, locked, required directly, required through a chain, required only by a non-kept record, stale `required_by` name, duplicate and ambiguous entries, explicit record required by a listed one.
- **E2E** (`tests/sync.rs`, A10 helpers): `release_graph` for a LittleWigs → BigWigs pair; a hand-written file listing only the requester; a lock entry; an unmanaged folder beside managed ones; a typo'd target section; `Home::new(&["wow", "wowt"])` for the PTR; the mixed install-remove-edit transaction plus undo; `delete_managed` for the forget case; `net_log(home)` for the re-run.
- **Contract:** refusal row with its `fix_argv`.
- H2 later crashes the mixed install-remove-edit sync transaction with the folder and record oracles.

## Considerations

- An empty section (`addons = []`) is an explicit empty desired set: prune removes every managed addon on the targets it applies to. `--dry-run` shows it first, and undo restores it.
- `file:` and directory records are pruned like any other when unlisted. `export` skips them with `export_local_source`, so pruning with a file fresh from `export` on the same machine removes local installs; the export warning names them, and undo restores them.
- Never prune by folder: prune reads records only, so linked, protected and unmanaged folders are out of reach by construction.
- F3.2 (`--locked`) edits the same files in parallel; rebase on it. Hot spots shared with every command task: `src/app/help.rs`, `tests/contract/*`.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- F3.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.1` (sync core): the command, entry resolution, the per-target desired set, the transaction and output path this flag extends. `Remove` comes from M1 and `Forget` from A4.1, which F3.1 already requires.

Unblocks:
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit): audits the finished `sync` surface, including the prune refusal.
- H2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` (Crash and concurrency coverage): its `SyncMixed` op crashes an install, remove and edit in one sync transaction, which only `--prune` can produce.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): documents `--prune` and its safety rules and records `unknown_target_section`.
acceptance_criteria: sync --prune removes exactly the unlisted, unprotected managed addons on each target with a desired set and leaves listed addons untouched; it never removes a record a listed addon requires, directly or through a chain, or a record matching a dependency = true lock, and never touches an unmanaged folder; with any target section naming an unknown target it refuses with desired_state_invalid reason unknown_target_section, exit 2 and nothing changed, even when -t selects another target, while plain sync proceeds with a desired_unknown_target warning; targets without an applicable section stay untouched with no_section true; one sync transaction that installs, removes and unpins commits as kind sync with add, remove and record ops, and bare undo restores folders and records exactly; --dry-run --prune lists removals and writes nothing outside the cache, net.log and inflight; pruning a record whose folders are gone records record ops and undo restores it; an immediate re-run logs zero net.log lines; --prune is in help sync and the refusal has a contract row
close_reason: sync --prune: removes unlisted managed addons, keeps listed, locked and required (transitively), section-scoped, refuses unknown target sections; gate green

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead, and how it serves M2 and the project.** Without `--prune`, `sync` can only grow a client's addon set, so "make this client match my file" is half true: an addon removed from the dotfile lingers forever. `--prune` closes that gap and completes G-M2-5 ("Declarative sets", kept in sync idempotently) and the vision's checkpoint "`--prune` removes only unlisted managed addons". Because it is the only destructive part of `sync`, it is also where the project's thesis (omaddons as the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons) is tested hardest: every removal is a journaled, snapshotted transaction that bare `omaddons undo` reverts, and nothing unmanaged is ever in reach (G-M2-7).

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D20.** `sync` reconciles presence, channel, pins and locks; removal of unlisted addons is presence reconciliation, opt-in through `--prune`. Rejected (for `sync` in general): making it also update.
- **Dependency entries as locks** (the desired-state format): `dependency = true` entries are not requests, but they protect a required dependency from `--prune`, matched by resolved ref identity.
- **The unknown-target refusal.** `--prune` refuses with `desired_state_invalid` (`details.reason: "unknown_target_section"`) while any `target.<id>` section names an unknown target, because a typo such as `[target."retial"]` would otherwise prune the real target's addons. Plain `sync` only warns (`desired_unknown_target`), because a dotfile may legitimately list clients this machine lacks.
- **M2-D6 and A4.1's `Forget`.** A removal whose folders are already gone becomes a records-only `Forget` with `record` history ops, which fixes latent defect 1 (a remove of vanished folders wrote `ops: []`, so undo restored nothing). Rejected (for records-only changes in general): ad-hoc state writes.
- **Vision rule on orphans:** dependencies nobody needs are reported, never removed automatically. Prune removes only what the user's file leaves out, and C6's warnings still apply.

**Decisions made while writing this bead.**
- The `required_by` protection applies whatever the record's `reason` and is transitive. The plan's design sentence names `reason: dependency` records, but its acceptance criterion says prune "never removes a dependency that a listed addon requires"; an explicitly installed BigWigs that a listed LittleWigs needs, or a chain A → B → C, must survive, so the conservative reading wins.
- Records a failed entry may mean (a duplicate's ref, the candidates of a `ref_ambiguous` entry) are kept, following the plan's default "report and recommend rather than act" for ambiguity.
- The refusal's fix is `omaddons targets` (argv), which lists the valid ids; the message also says plain `sync` is allowed.
- `file:` and directory records are pruned like any other when unlisted. The plan exempts nothing, `export` warns about them with `export_local_source`, and undo restores them.

**Facts verified during planning** (commit `e902d36`): `RequestedChange::Remove { addon }` exists (`src/engine/plan.rs:83`); history ops are `add`, `replace`, `remove` and `record` (`FolderOp`, `src/state/history.rs:63`); the PTR's target id is `ptr` with kind `test`, so a family section can never reach it and prune leaves it alone unless its own target section exists.

**Risks and mitigations.** Removing wanted addons is the main risk: the refusal, the lock and dependency rules, `--dry-run`, and undo bound it. An empty section prunes everything it applies to; that is explicit user intent, and `--dry-run` shows it. Mixed install-remove-edit transactions are new to the engine; H2's `SyncMixed` op crashes one with the folder and record oracles. Confidence: high for the keep-set rule (pure, table-tested); medium-high for the mixed transaction, which rests on A4.1 and A5.

**Relation to siblings.** F3.1 owns the command, the diff and the transaction; this bead only appends removals and adds the refusal. It must not change F3.1's install and edit rows. F3.2 (`--locked`) is independent and may land in parallel; both edit `src/app/sync.rs`, so rebase on each other. A `dependency = true` lock protects its record from prune with or without `--locked`.

**done:** `sync --prune` removes the managed addons a target's desired set does not list. It keeps everything the file names or may name, everything a lock names, and everything those require through any chain. It touches only targets with a section, and it refuses a file with a section for no known client. `argc gate` passes: 1167 tests, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical.

**What landed (`src/app/sync.rs`):**
- `--prune`, whose help states the safety rules; `SYNC_HELP` explains it.
- **Refusal first:** before anything is resolved, a `[target."<id>"]` section naming no known id (`known_ids`, which include registered clients that are gone) fails the command. The error is `desired_state_invalid`, exit 2, `details {path, line, key: "target.<id>", reason: "unknown_target_section"}`, fix argv `omaddons targets`. It applies whatever `-t` selects. Plain `sync` is unchanged and keeps its `desired_unknown_target` warning.
- **`keep_set(record, refs)`** (pure, public): records whose ref identity one of `refs` names, then, to a fixpoint, every record whose `required_by` names a kept one, whatever its `reason`. A stale requester name protects nothing.
- **`target_work`:**
  - It now takes `&SyncArgs`.
  - It collects `named`: every resolved non-lock entry, every lock (`dependency = true`, with or without `--locked`), duplicates (resolved before the duplicate check), and each candidate a `ref_ambiguous` entry lists (`ambiguous_refs`, from `details.candidates[].ref`).
  - Under `--prune`, every record outside `keep_set` becomes `RequestedChange::Remove { addon: name }`. Removals are sorted by name ignoring case, appended after the entries' changes, and requested as `request = name`. They join the target's single `sync` transaction.
- Targets without an applicable section keep `no_section: true` and are never pruned.
- The engine is reused as it is: a record whose folders are all gone becomes A4.1's records-only `Forget` with `record` ops, the running policy applies as for `remove`, and undo restores.
- **README:** the `--prune` flag row, a paragraph with the keep rules, the refusal and the empty-section warning, the "What works today" and limitations rows, and `unknown_target_section` in the `desired_state_invalid` row.

**Tests:**
- **Unit, `sync::tests::prune_keeps_what_the_file_names_and_everything_that_requires`:**
  - kept: a listed ref in another case, the chain Little → Big → Lib, a locked ref, a duplicate's ref, an ambiguous candidate;
  - pruned: a stale requester, and a record required only by a pruned one.
- **`tests/sync.rs` (+4):**
  - **Unlisted only:** on retail with LittleWigs (pulling BigWigs as a dependency), Foo and Bar, plus Foo on the PTR, and a file listing LittleWigs and Foo, `--prune` removes exactly Bar. BigWigs is kept (required), the unmanaged `Mine` folder's tree is unchanged, and the PTR is `no_section` and untouched. A re-run makes 0 `net.log` lines and 0 transactions.
  - **Refusal:** with `[target."retial"]`, `--prune` and `--prune -t ptr` both fail `unknown_target_section` with key `target.retial` and fix `omaddons targets`, changing nothing. Plain `sync` proceeds with `desired_unknown_target`.

- **Contract:** the `sync` row adds the refusal (snapshot `sync_prune_refused`, reviewed).

**decided:**
- Duplicate entries keep both refs.
- Locks keep their records even without `--locked`.
- The refusal names the first unknown section, in id order.
- Removals use the record's name as `request`.

**Wire names:** the flag `sync --prune`; the `desired_state_invalid` `details.reason` value `unknown_target_section` (with `key: "target.<id>"`). No new codes, warnings or constants.

title: The copy command
description:
## Background

This bead serves M2 goal G-M2-5, **declarative sets**: the addon set of every client can be exported, reproduced, kept in sync, and **copied between compatible clients**. People who play several Classic flavors want the same addons on each, where builds exist. The owner's machine has Classic Era (`era`, family `vanilla`), Anniversary (`anniversary`, family `tbc`) and Mists Classic (`classic`, family `mists`). Vision bead §5.9 says: "`copy --from --to` installs the same refs where compatible and reports skips."

The intended interaction:

```
$ omaddons copy --from era --to anniversary
anniversary: installed 4 addons (tx 01M5…)
  skipped: pfUI-turtle (no build for tbc), ClassicHealPrediction (already installed)
```

Facts in the code today (line numbers are as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- There is no `copy` command. Today the owner would run `install <ref> -t anniversary` per addon, by hand, after reading `list -t era`.
- `discover::registry::resolve_one` (`src/discover/registry.rs:711`) resolves a selector to exactly one target, with `target_ambiguous` fixes per candidate. `copy` uses it for both sides, so a family selector never fans out here.
- `install` already treats `no_compatible_release` and `wrong_flavor` as client-specific failures (`client_specific`, `src/app/install.rs:677-682`). Copy reuses that classification to turn them into skips.
- `RequestedChange::Install` (`src/engine/plan.rs:71`) gains `channel_explicit`, `pin: PinIntent`, `reason` and `reinstall` in A3; dependency rounds (C4.1) run inside engine planning for every planned install; A6 provides the shared per-target outcome (`TargetsData`, `ItemResult` with `skip_reason`, undo commands, run id).

Without this bead, a multi-flavor player repeats every install per client, and nothing reports which addons have no build for the destination.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** new `src/app/copy.rs`; `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs` (the `Copy` subcommand, in the Change help group per A1); new `tests/copy.rs`; `tests/contract/matrix.rs`; `README.md` (commands table and "What it does today", in the same commit, as the delivery rules require).

**Synopsis (authoritative):** `omaddons copy --from T1 --to T2 [<addon>…] [--strict] [--dry-run] [--no-deps]`

`CopyArgs { from: String, to: String, addons: Vec<String>, strict: bool, no_deps: bool }`.

### Rules

- Both sides go through `resolve_one`. `--from` equal to `--to` is `usage`. The global `-t` is not used by `copy`; passing it is `usage` with a text fix to name the clients with `--from` and `--to` (decided).
- For each **explicit** record on T1 (`reason: explicit`), or each named one:
  - already installed on T2 (judged by ref identity, so `gh:` owner and repo compare case-insensitively): `skipped` with `skip_reason: already_installed`;
  - a `file:` record, or a directory install (also a `file:` ref): `skipped` with `skip_reason: local_source`, because local paths are machine-specific;
  - otherwise plan `Install { ref, channel: record.channel, reason: Explicit, pin: Keep }`, with `channel_explicit: false`, `version: None` and `reinstall: false`. The recorded name follows install's rule (the catalog name for catalog refs, else derived from the archive). `url:` records copy like any other.
- **Pins are not copied,** because versions are flavor-specific. The new record on T2 is unpinned even when T1's is pinned.
- **Dependencies resolve on T2 as usual** (C4.1): the engine's rounds find what the destination's loaded TOC requires, from the catalog first. `--no-deps` passes through to C4.1's switch: rounds are skipped, unresolved required dependencies still warn.
- **One transaction on T2** (kind `install`: the request's `default_kind` is Install, and every change is an install). It carries a run id like every committing command.
- **After planning,** items that end in `no_compatible_release` or `wrong_flavor` are `skipped` with `skip_reason: no_build_for_target`. **These are not failures.** Other errors are failures, and the run is partial (M2-D30).
- Named addons match T1's record names case-insensitively. A name with no record on T1 is a failed item `not_managed` with fix argv `omaddons list -t <T1 id>` (decided). Naming a dependency record copies it as explicit, because the user asked for it.

### Output (A6)

- `data` is the shared multi-target shape with one target (T2): `dry_run`, `run`, `targets[]` (`target`, `tx`, `kind`, `no_section: false`, `items`, `reload_required`, `atomic_swap`, `creates_addons_dir`, `error`), `summary {targets, changed, unchanged, skipped, failed}`.
- Items: `installed` for copied addons (dependency installs carry `reason: dependency` and `required_by` once C5 adds those fields), `skipped` with `skip_reason` `already_installed`, `local_source` or `no_build_for_target`, `failed` with `error`. Items are sorted by name; `unchanged` items are hidden unless `-v`.
- Human rendering follows the example above: a header line per target, then one `skipped:` line listing each skip with its reason in words (`no build for tbc`, `already installed`, `local source`).
- `commands`: `undo <tx>` when the transaction committed.
- `--strict` turns partial success (a real failure) into exit 6. Skips never count.
- `--dry-run`: `tx: null`, items show what would happen.
- The running-client policy applies to T2 exactly as for `install`.
- Progress: copy fetches one release per ref, so it emits progress events through `Context.progress` (A9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.9`, a blocker added during bead creation because the plan had missed it).

### Decisions applied

- **M2-D30**: `copy` skips for a missing compatible build are not failures. Incompatibility across flavors is expected, not an error. Rejected: counting them as partial, which would make nearly every cross-flavor copy partial and `--strict` useless.
- **M2-D34**: only explicitly installed addons count in `copy`; dependency records follow by resolution on the destination. Dependencies may differ per flavor. Rejected: copying dependency records verbatim, which could install a dependency the destination's TOC does not require, or the wrong project for that flavor.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Era → anniversary with one addon lacking a tbc build: the rest install in one transaction, the skip is listed with `skip_reason: no_build_for_target`, and the run exits 0 with `partial: false`.
- A network failure on one item makes the run partial (exit 0, `partial: true`); with `--strict` the same run exits 6. A run whose only non-installs are skips exits 0 even with `--strict`.
- Dependencies resolve on the destination: copying a requester whose destination TOC requires a catalog addon installs that dependency in the same transaction, recorded `reason: dependency`. Dependency records on T1 are not copied unless named. `--no-deps` installs only the requested addons and warns.
- `file:` and directory records are skipped with `local_source`; an addon already on T2 (by ref identity) is skipped with `already_installed`.
- A pinned record on T1 arrives unpinned on T2.
- `--from` equal to `--to` is `usage`; an ambiguous `--from` is `target_ambiguous` with one fix per candidate.
- `omaddons undo <tx>` from `commands` reverts the copy byte-for-byte.
- `copy` emits progress events through `Context.progress` (A9) for its fetches and downloads.
- `copy` appears in the Change help group, and the contract matrix has success and failure rows.

## Test Plan

- `tests/copy.rs` (E2E, binary): a Battle.net root with a Classic Era and an Anniversary client; fixture releases built with `tests/common` helpers: one addon with builds for both families, one whose release only verifies on vanilla, one recorded `file:` install, one pinned record, one ref whose fixture answers 500 (the network failure), and a requester/dependency pair from A10's `release_graph` with a catalog override for the dependency.
- Cases: the mixed copy above; `--strict` with and without a real failure; named addons, including an unknown name and a named dependency record; `--no-deps`; `--dry-run` (no state written, `tx: null`); undo of the committed transaction.
- Contract rows for `copy` (success, partial, usage).

## Considerations

- Copy never fans out: each side must be exactly one client, consistent with M1's "never guess the client" rule for single-target mutations (M2-D24).
- A `gh:` record installed with `--file` copies as a normal `gh:` install from the source; only `file:` refs are local.
- Copy does not promote a dependency record already on T2 to explicit (it is `already_installed`); `install` does that.
- Collision hot spots: `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs` (every command bead); copy reads A6's `src/app/outcome.rs` but should not need to change it.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1` (Grouped bare help with a command group registry): `copy` joins the Change group in the same commit as its clap variant.
- A6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.6` (Shared multi-target outcome and multi-target commit coverage): copy renders through the shared item shape, `skip_reason` values, summary buckets and undo commands instead of a private renderer.
- A9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.9` (Progress plumbing for long commands): copy needs one network round trip per ref, so it emits progress events through `Context.progress`.
- C4.1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1` (Dependency rounds on install): "dependencies resolve on the destination" is the engine's dependency rounds, and `--no-deps` is C4.1's switch.

Unblocks:
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit for M2): audits copy's rows, exits and skip reasons.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): documents the command and records its skip reasons.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** The owner plays several Classic flavors on one machine. Today each addon must be installed per client by hand, and nothing reports which ones have no build for the destination flavor. `copy` turns that into one command whose result is one undoable transaction on the destination, with every skip explained. It completes goal G-M2-5 (declarative sets: "copied between compatible clients") and keeps the thesis intact: the copy is a normal engine transaction, TOC-verified for the destination client, journaled and undoable.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D30**: skips for a missing compatible build are not failures. Why: incompatibility across flavors is expected, not an error, and it is consistent with M2-D41 (an update whose newest release does not load on a client is `skipped/blocked`, not failed). Rejected: counting them as partial, which would make most cross-flavor copies partial and make `--strict` meaningless.
- **M2-D34**: only explicitly installed addons count; dependency records follow by resolution on the destination. Why: dependencies may differ per flavor, and the destination's own loaded TOC is the authority for what it requires. Rejected: copying dependency records verbatim, which could install projects the destination does not need. This is why the bead waits for C4.1: without engine dependency rounds, a copied requester would arrive without its dependency and fail to load in game.
- **Pins are not copied** (versions are flavor-specific), and **copy never fans out** (M2-D24: single-target commands keep their ambiguity errors, because "never guess the client" is an M1 safety rule).
- `url:` records copy like any other; `file:` and directory records are machine-specific and skipped with `local_source`.

**Decisions made while writing this bead** (record with `decided:` comments): the global `-t` is `usage` for `copy`; a named addon with no record on `--from` is a failed `not_managed` item with fix `omaddons list -t <from>`; naming a dependency record copies it as explicit; new records take install's naming rule.

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `e902d36`): `resolve_one` at `src/discover/registry.rs:711`; install's `client_specific` classification of `no_compatible_release` and `wrong_flavor` at `src/app/install.rs:677-682`; install renders only `outcomes.first()` today (`src/app/install.rs:423`), which A6 replaces with the shared multi-target outcome that copy uses.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Cross-flavor builds are the common failure mode. Mitigation: every candidate is TOC-verified for the destination client before anything is staged, and verification failures become explicit skips.
- A dependency that resolves but fails to install makes the run partial while the requester installs (M2-D9, owned by C4.1); the item names the dependency, so a retry is obvious.
- A9 (progress plumbing) is a blocker, an edge added at bead creation because the plan had missed it, so copy emits progress events from its first commit and no follow-up bead is needed.
- Confidence: copy is a thin composition over A6 and C4.1. The engine work it relies on is rated medium-high confidence by the M2 plan, guarded by M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites.

title: Epic: M2 search and GitHub auth
description:
## Background

Area epic G of milestone M2 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp`). It delivers M2 goal G-M2-6, **findable**: addons can be searched for across every keyless source, and every result carries an install command. It also delivers the one GitHub account feature M2 keeps, an opt-in REST token, which raises the limits that search, beta and alpha channels, and repos without `release.json` run into.

Today "what was that addon called?" means opening a browser. M1 has a catalog with `by_name` lookups and a Levenshtein helper for mistyped commands (`src/cli.rs:538`, as of commit `e902d36`), and nothing else. Vision bead §5.4 ("Search", M2) asks for search over the catalog, the WoWI index, Tukui and GitHub repo lookups, ranked exact or alias match first, then downloads and recency, with per-target compatibility flags and source attribution.

The intended search interaction:

```
$ omaddons search damage meter -t retail
  Details! Damage Meter   wowi:23056   WoWInterface · 515k downloads · updated 2020 · retail: abandoned
  Recount                 wowi:…       WoWInterface · 2.1M downloads · updated 2026 · retail: likely
  Skada                   gh:…/Skada   GitHub · ★412 · retail: unknown
Install: omaddons install wowi:… -t retail        (abandoned results are never suggested)
```

Only GitHub sees the query string; WoWInterface and Tukui are searched locally from data omaddons already holds. Compatibility is a hint, and `install` still verifies TOCs.

**The token.** Vision decision D12 makes the GitHub token opt-in: omaddons never reads the user's `gh` credentials or `GITHUB_TOKEN` silently, and the main GitHub path (`release.json` publishers on the stable channel) needs no token at all. Today the only token source is the `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` variable (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:34`, `:270-276`). `config.toml` already parses `[sources.github] credential` and `resolve_credential` exists (`src/state/config.rs:755`), but nothing calls it at runtime, and `Writer::Auth` is still labelled "(M5)" (`src/fsx/scope.rs:24-25`). Unauthenticated REST allows 60 requests an hour and search 10 a minute (verified live on 2026-10-15, with search on its own `x-ratelimit-resource: search` budget); a token raises them to 5,000 an hour and 30 a minute.

## Goals

- **`omaddons search <query…>`** (G1, alias `find`): hits from the catalog, the WoWI index, the Tukui list and GitHub repository search; tiered ranking with catalog-first ordering, per-source popularity and recency; catalog de-duplication; per-target compatibility (`yes|no|likely|unlikely|unknown|abandoned`); `sources_skipped` objects with reasons; up to three ready-to-run `install` commands, never for `no`, `unlikely` or `abandoned` results.
- **`omaddons auth github [status | set | clear | --from-gh]`** (G2): stores a token in `<config>/omaddons/credentials/github` (mode 0600, `Writer::Auth`), reports what is configured and the REST quota, and clears it by truncation. One resolution order for every REST caller: `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN`, then `[sources.github] credential`, then the credentials file.

## Success Criteria

When both children are closed:
- `search` returns ranked hits from the catalog, the WoWI index, Tukui and GitHub, with per-target compatibility hints; `--offline` works from cached indices and lists GitHub as skipped.
- A rate-limited GitHub search degrades: other sources still return, `sources_skipped` carries `reset_at`, and the run is not partial.
- `commands[0].argv` from a search runs successfully; abandoned projects never appear in `commands`.
- Only `api.github.com` receives a search query (`net.log`).
- `echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set` stores the token with mode 0600 in a 0700 directory; `status` reports its source and quota without ever printing the token or calling identity endpoints; `clear` leaves a zero-byte file.
- With a token configured, REST and search requests carry it to `api.github.com` only, a 401 is `auth_rejected` with an executable fix, and the token never appears in `net.log`, envelopes, stderr, history, state files or child-process argv.

## Non-Goals

- The GitHub GraphQL batch path (moved to M5, M2-D22), and `auth curseforge|wago` (their sources arrive in M5).
- Sending the query to WoWInterface or Tukui search endpoints (M2-D21).
- Reading `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or `gh`'s credentials without an explicit `--from-gh` (D12).
- Treating compatibility hints as verdicts: `install` verifies TOCs; search never excludes a build on lagging WoWI tags.
- Caching GitHub search results or persisting rate-limit state between runs.

## Considerations

- **G1 and G2 have no edge between them.** Whichever lands second wires search to G2's shared token resolution; until then search reads `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` exactly as `GithubRest` does.
- **Separate rate-limit budgets.** GitHub tracks search separately from core REST; search keeps its own budget instance so neither starves the other.
- **G1 waits for the sources lane** (D2 WoWI index, D3 WoWI source, D4 Tukui source) and B1's memo, so it lands late (wave 5). G2 only waits for A1 and can land any time after it.
- **Privacy is a product promise.** README's privacy section must say that search sends the query to GitHub only and that the token is used for REST only (H6 makes the final pass; each bead updates README in its own commit).
- **Collision hot spots:** `src/sources/mod.rs` and every `SourceRegistry::builtin` caller (G2 and D3), `src/sources/github_rest.rs` (G2 and B2), `src/politeness.rs`/`src/limits.rs` registries (G1), `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs` (every command bead).

## Children

| Key | Id | Title | Scope in one line | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7.1` | The search command across the catalog, WoWInterface, Tukui and GitHub | Four sources, tiered ranking and merging, compat hints, `sources_skipped`, install `commands`, own search budget, alias `find` | A1, A2, A9, B1, D2, D3, D4 |
| G2 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7.2` | auth github: an opt-in REST token with set, status and clear | Credentials file via `Writer::Auth`, `--from-gh`, status with the core quota, one token resolution for every REST caller, `auth_rejected` on 401 | A1 |
acceptance_criteria: G1 and G2 are closed; search returns ranked catalog, WoWI, Tukui and GitHub hits with per-target compatibility hints, works offline from cached indices, degrades on a GitHub rate limit with sources_skipped and reset_at, and only GitHub receives the query; search commands run and never suggest abandoned results; auth github set stores a 0600 token through Writer::Auth, status never prints it or calls identity endpoints, clear truncates; one token resolution (env, config, file) serves every REST caller and the token reaches api.github.com only

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this epic.** Finding an addon is the step before every install, and agents need it to end in an executable command: "find and install" is two commands (`search Q --json`, then `commands[0].argv`). The token removes the one quota that can make beta-channel checks and search fail for a heavy user, without weakening the privacy promise. Both serve the thesis: search only suggests, `install` verifies and records every change as an undoable transaction, and the token's single source and single destination are testable facts. Goals: G-M2-6 (findable) and, for REST-backed update checks, G-M2-1 (current by default).

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D22** (departs from vision): the GitHub GraphQL batch path moves to M5; `auth github` (an opt-in REST token) stays in M2. Why: GraphQL needs `Method::Post` (the net layer has only GET and HEAD today), request bodies, body-keyed replay fixtures, a new decoder and retry changes, for a small gain once B2's tag-first probe makes an unchanged stable release cost one `github.com` request with no REST at all. M5 is already the accounts milestone (CurseForge, Wago). Rejected: building POST support now. Consequence: in M2 the token only raises REST limits (beta and alpha channels, repos without `release.json`, search), where the vision had also tied it to one GraphQL query for all tracked repos.
- **M2-D21**: search sends the query only to GitHub; WoWInterface and Tukui are searched locally, from the slim WoWI index (D2) and the memo's Tukui list (D4). Why: verifiable privacy (vision goal G5), disclosing as little as possible. Rejected: querying a WoWI search endpoint, which would send every query to a second service.
- **M2-D23**: `auth github clear` truncates the credential file to zero bytes, keeping `fsx::prune()` the only deletion path with fixed call sites. Rejected: a new prune call site.
- **M2-D39** (departs from vision timing): `find` is a visible alias of `search`, pulled forward from M4 because it is a likely first guess outside the Levenshtein-2 suggestion range.
- **Vision D12**: the token is explicit, never implicit. `GITHUB_TOKEN` is never read; `gh auth token` runs only on `--from-gh`.

**Facts verified during planning.** Live on 2026-10-15: `GET https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=…` works unauthenticated with `x-ratelimit-limit: 10`, `x-ratelimit-resource: search` and a one-minute window; Details! on WoWInterface (UID 23056) dates from 2020; WoWI compatibility tags lag (no 5.x values, nothing past 12.1.0). In the code at `e902d36`: the single core REST budget in `GithubRest` (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:40-82`); `token_from` reads only `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN`; `resolve_credential` exists with no runtime caller; `Redirecting` drops credential headers on cross-host hops (`src/net/guard.rs:19`); `auth_rejected` and `auth_required` are registered codes.

**Risks and confidence.**
- Search ranking quality is rated **medium** confidence by the M2 plan; its failure mode is a worse ordering, never a wrong install.
- GitHub's unauthenticated search allows 10 requests a minute; search makes one request per run and degrades to local results with `reset_at` when limited.
- A token leak would break the privacy promise; G2's grep tests cover every output, and the token is carried as a redacting `Secret`.
- Auth is not rated separately; it wires existing, tested pieces, so its risk is low.
