title: The search command across the catalog, WoWInterface, Tukui and GitHub
description:
## Background

This bead serves M2 goal G-M2-6, **findable**: addons can be searched for across every keyless source, and every result carries an install command. Vision bead §5.4 ("Search", M2) asks for the catalog, the WoWI index, Tukui and GitHub repo lookups, ranked exact/alias first, then downloads and recency, with per-target compatibility flags and source attribution. Today "what was that addon called?" means opening a browser.

The intended interaction:

```
$ omaddons search damage meter -t retail
  Details! Damage Meter   wowi:23056   WoWInterface · 515k downloads · updated 2020 · retail: abandoned
  Recount                 wowi:…       WoWInterface · 2.1M downloads · updated 2026 · retail: likely
  Skada                   gh:…/Skada   GitHub · ★412 · retail: unknown
Install: omaddons install wowi:… -t retail        (abandoned results are never suggested)
```

Search consults the catalog, the local WoWI index, the cached Tukui list, and GitHub's search API (unauthenticated, 10 requests per minute). Only GitHub sees the query string (M2-D21). Compatibility is a hint; install still verifies TOCs.

Facts (line numbers are as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- No search exists. The catalog has `Catalog::by_name` and `entries()` over `Entry { name, aliases, ref, families, folders, notes }` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:25-33`).
- `GithubRest` keeps one **core** rate-limit `Budget { remaining, reset }` per run, from `x-ratelimit-*` headers (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:40-82`); search must not share it.
- The retry layer turns a 403/429 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` into `rate_limited` at once, reset time in `details.reset_at` (`src/net/retry.rs:177-180`). `api.github.com` is allowlisted.
- The only token source today is `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` (`github_rest::token_from`, `:270-276`); `GITHUB_TOKEN` is never read (vision D12: the token is opt-in, never taken silently).
- `RulesTable::family_for(&ClientVersion, InstallKind)` (`src/rules.rs:625`) maps a version to a family.
- Verified live on 2026-10-15: unauthenticated `search/repositories` works with `x-ratelimit-limit: 10`, `x-ratelimit-resource: search`, a one-minute window. WoWI's filelist has `UIName`, `UIAuthorName`, `UIDate` (epoch ms), `UIDownloadTotal`, `UIDir` and a lagging `UICompatibility` (no 5.x, nothing past 12.1.0); Details! (UID 23056) dates from 2020. Tukui's list has `patch[]` and `last_update`.
- Consumed: D2's `WowiIndex::load_or_refresh` (slim entries with `name, author, date_ms, downloads, dirs, compat`); D4's `ReleaseCache::tukui_list()`; D3's `sources.<id>.enabled` flags; C3's `DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE` (730 days).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** new `src/app/search.rs`; new `src/resolve/search.rs` (pure scoring, merging, compatibility; `now` injected); new `src/sources/github_search.rs` (request, own budget, decoding); `src/politeness.rs` (`GITHUB_SEARCH_PER_PAGE` = 20); `src/limits.rs` (`SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS` = 50, `SEARCH_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` = 200, plus the registry name lists and `limit_registries` snapshot); `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs` (Look group, `visible_alias = "find"`); new `tests/search.rs`; a GitHub-search fixture builder in `tests/common/http.rs`; contract rows; `README.md` (commands table; privacy: only GitHub receives the query).

**Synopsis (authoritative):** `omaddons search <query…> [-t T] [--source catalog|wowi|tukui|github]… [--limit N] [--refresh]`, alias `find` (M2-D39: pulled forward from M4, a likely first guess outside the Levenshtein-2 suggestion range). `SearchArgs { query: Vec<String>, sources: Vec<SourceFilter>, limit: Option<usize>, refresh }`.

### Sources

- **The catalog** (offline): name, aliases, notes.
- **The WoWI index** (local): `UIName`, `UIAuthorName`, folder names.
- **The Tukui list** (memo, `Window` freshness).
- **GitHub:** `GET https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=<query>+(wow OR warcraft OR addon) in:name,description,topics&sort=stars&per_page=GITHUB_SEARCH_PER_PAGE` (purpose `github-search`, an API-timeout request with the same `Accept` and API-version headers as `GithubRest::api_request`).
  - Unauthenticated search allows 10 requests a minute; the token is used when configured (30 a minute).
  - Search has its **own** rate-limit budget, separate from `GithubRest`'s core budget, because GitHub tracks `x-ratelimit-resource: search` separately. Reuse the `Budget` type as a separate instance; a search response never updates the core budget and vice versa.
  - Skipped when `--offline`, when rate-limited, or when `--source` excludes it.
- **Token wiring order with G2:** whichever of G1 and G2 lands second wires search to G2's shared token resolution (env, config, credentials file). Until then search uses `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` via `token_from`, like `GithubRest`. The token goes to `api.github.com` only.
- `--refresh` bypasses the WoWI and Tukui windows; GitHub results are never cached.

### Ranking

One score per hit, then a stable sort.
1. **Tier 0:** the whole query exactly matches a catalog name or alias, or a WoWI or Tukui project name.
2. **Tier 1:** prefix match. **Tier 2:** all query tokens present in the name or folders. **Tier 3:** tokens in the author or description.
3. **Within a tier:** catalog first; then popularity normalised per source (WoWI downloads, GitHub stars, log-scaled); then recency (WoWI `UIDate`, GitHub `pushed_at`, Tukui `last_update`).
4. **De-duplication:** a WoWI or GitHub hit whose ref equals a catalog entry's ref is merged into the catalog hit.

Notes: compare lowercased, whitespace-collapsed text; drop hits that reach no tier. Popularity is `ln(1+n) / ln(1+max n of that source in this result set)`. Break remaining ties by name, then ref. A merged catalog hit keeps the catalog's name, ref, source and compat, and takes popularity and `updated_at` from the merged hit (decided). Apply `--limit` last.

### Compatibility per selected target

All targets by default (`World::select_many`, A2); `-t` narrows.
- catalog `families` → `yes` or `no` (an entry with no families → `unknown`, decided);
- Tukui `patch[]` → `likely` or `unlikely` (each patch version mapped through `family_for`);
- WoWI `compat` mapped through `family_for` → `likely` or `unknown` (never `no`, because it lags);
- a WoWI project older than `DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE` (by `UIDate`) → `abandoned`;
- GitHub → `unknown`.

The human output says compatibility is a hint and install verifies. D4's `TukuiIndex` entries carry `patch` and `last_update` for exactly this (B1's `tukui_list` slot lists them), so search adds no memo field.

### Output

- `results: [{name, ref, source, author, summary, popularity, updated_at, compat: {<target id>: yes|no|likely|unlikely|unknown|abandoned}}]`, `compat` a `BTreeMap`. `popularity`: `{downloads}` (WoWI), `{stars}` (GitHub), else `null`; `summary`: catalog notes or GitHub description, `null` for WoWI.
- `sources_skipped: [{source, reason: offline|rate_limited|disabled|no_index, reset_at?}]` (objects everywhere; `reset_at` only with `rate_limited`). Sources excluded by `--source` are not listed. Offline: GitHub `offline`; WoWI from a cached index (`stale_check` when stale) or `no_index`; Tukui from the memo or `offline`. Disabled sources: `disabled`.
- `commands`: `install <ref> -t <target>` (action `install`) for up to three top results whose compat on that target is `yes`, `likely` or `unknown`. Never `no`, `unlikely` or `abandoned`. The target is the first selected target, in id order, with the best compat for that result (`yes` over `likely` over `unknown`). With no eligible result there are no commands, and the human output says why.
- **Privacy:** only GitHub receives the query. The README privacy section says so (M2-D21).
- **Limits:** `SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS` (50); the default `--limit` is 20; a larger value or 0 is `usage` with the fix argv using the bound (decided). Summaries are capped at 200 characters (`SEARCH_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS`).
- A rate-limited GitHub search is not a failure (`partial: false`). Any other GitHub or Tukui failure (network, 5xx; with G2, a 401 is `auth_rejected`) skips that source, mirrors the error as a warning and sets `partial: true` (decided).
- Progress events (A9) for the WoWI refresh, the Tukui list and the GitHub request.

Example data:

```json
"data":{"query":"damage meter","results":[
  {"name":"Details! Damage Meter","ref":"wowi:23056","source":"wowi","author":"…","summary":null,
   "popularity":{"downloads":515870},"updated_at":"2020-…","compat":{"retail":"abandoned","era":"unknown"}}],
 "sources_skipped":[{"source":"github","reason":"rate_limited","reset_at":"2026-10-15T20:02:00Z"}]}
```

### Switch interim fixes that wait for `search`

A fix must name a command that exists, so beads that land before this one use an interim fix where the design says `omaddons search <folder>`. When this bead lands, switch each one that is already on `main`:
- the `missing_dependency` warning for a dependency that resolved to nothing (`Missing { reason: no_source }`, a result of C3's pure resolver, `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.3`), built with its interim text fix by C4.1 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.4.1`) and rendered by C5 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.5`): final fix argv `omaddons search <folder>`; its message keeps saying the folder may only be distributed on CurseForge or Wago, which arrive in M5. This bead owns that switch whenever C4.1 is already on `main`;
- the `not_found` fixes of the WoWInterface and Tukui sources (D3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.3`, D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4`), which use the interim `omaddons help install` until `search` exists: final fix argv `omaddons search <name>`;
- any other emitter whose bead text says it waits for G1 (grep the code for the interim fix).

If one of those beads is still open when this lands, it emits the final form directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `search weakauras` ranks the catalog entry first, with the WoWI duplicate merged into it.
- `search damage meter` returns WoWI and GitHub hits ranked by tier, then popularity. The 2020 Details! project is `abandoned` and never appears in `commands`.
- `--offline` returns catalog and cached-index hits, makes no request, and lists GitHub in `sources_skipped` with `offline`.
- A rate-limited GitHub search adds `sources_skipped` with `reset_at`; other sources still return, and the result is `partial: false`. The core REST budget is unaffected (a following beta-channel fetch in the same process still sends).
- `commands[0].argv` runs successfully against fixtures (a WoWI ref install).
- `omaddons find X` behaves as `search X`. `--source wowi` consults only the index. A disabled source appears as `disabled`.
- Results, compat values and `sources_skipped` follow the shapes above; repeated runs with the same fixtures are byte-identical apart from `meta`.
- Only the GitHub request contains the query (`net.log` shows no other host receiving it). Progress events are emitted with `--progress json`.
- Where C4.1/C5 landed first, a dependency with no source now carries the fix argv `omaddons search <folder>`, and that argv runs successfully.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/resolve/search.rs`): each tier, catalog-first ordering, log-scaled popularity per source, recency, tie-breaks, merging, every compat rule including `abandoned` with an injected `now`, summary capping.
- `tests/search.rs` (E2E): catalog plus an override; a WoWI index fixture (D2's `wowi_filelist`) with a 2020 Details! and a recent meter; a Tukui list fixture (D4); GitHub fixtures for success and for a 403 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`; `--offline` with a pre-written index and seeded memo; `--source`; `find`; running `commands[0].argv`; contract rows. H4 adds the live probe.

## Considerations

- Never send the query to WoWI or Tukui (M2-D21).
- Only the endpoint was verified live, not the grouped `(wow OR warcraft OR addon)` qualifier. If GitHub rejects or ignores it, follow reality: adjust the query, add a fixture and a live-probe assertion, and record the change with its date on the vision bead.
- Collision hot spots: `src/politeness.rs`/`src/limits.rs` registries, `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs`, and G2's token wiring.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1` (Grouped bare help with a command group registry): `search` and its alias join the Look group in the same commit as the clap variant.
- A2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.2` (Multi-target selection with World::select_many): compatibility columns are per selected target, and `-t vanilla` must mean every vanilla client.
- A9 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.9` (Progress plumbing for long commands): search makes several round trips (index refresh, Tukui list, GitHub) and must emit progress.
- B1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.1` (The release memo and ReleaseCache): the Tukui list comes from the memo with `Window` freshness.
- D2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.2` (The WoWInterface index): the WoWI source of hits, with `no_index` when absent.
- D3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.3` (The WoWInterface source): `commands[0].argv` is usually a `wowi:` install, which must run; D3 also wires the source enable flags behind `disabled`.
- D4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.4` (The Tukui source): provides `TukuiIndex` and `ReleaseCache::tukui_list()`.

Unblocks:
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit for M2): audits search rows, determinism and the alias.
- H4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.4` (Live probes for M2): adds the live GitHub search probe.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): records the command, alias, constants and the privacy statement.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Users and agents need to find an addon and get a command that installs it, without leaving the terminal. Search closes goal G-M2-6 (findable) and the agent intent "find and install" in two commands (`search Q --json`, then `commands[0].argv`). It strengthens the thesis without adding risk: search is read-only, every suggestion goes through `install`, which TOC-verifies, journals and can be undone, and results the tool knows to be stale (`abandoned`) are never suggested.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D21**: search sends the query only to GitHub; WoWI and Tukui are searched locally from the index and list omaddons already holds. Why: verifiable privacy (vision goal G5: hard host allowlist, `net.log`, disclose as little as possible). Rejected: querying a WoWI search endpoint, which would disclose every query to a second service for little gain over the local index.
- **M2-D39** (departs from vision timing): the alias `find` is pulled forward from M4, with `upgrade` and `check`. Why: a likely first guess that falls outside the Levenshtein-2 suggestion range, and cheap as a clap `visible_alias`. Rejected: waiting for M4's intent inference.
- **Separate search budget.** GitHub tracks `x-ratelimit-resource: search` apart from core, so sharing `GithubRest`'s budget would let a search response block REST fetches (or the reverse) for the wrong reason.
- **Search degrades rather than fails.** A rate-limited GitHub source becomes `sources_skipped` with `reset_at`, and the run stays `partial: false`, so an agent still gets local results.
- **Compatibility is a hint.** WoWI tags lag the game (no 5.x, nothing past 12.1.0, verified), so they can say `likely` or `unknown` but never `no`; install verifies TOCs (vision D5: TOCs are the ground truth).
- **Token wiring order (G1 and G2 have no edge between them):** whichever lands second wires search to G2's shared token resolution; until then search reads `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` like `GithubRest`. Neither bead blocks the other, and neither ships a half-wired token path.

**Decisions made while writing this bead** (record with `decided:` comments): catalog entries without families give `unknown`; a merged catalog hit takes popularity and recency from the merged WoWI or GitHub hit; `--limit` above 50 or 0 is `usage`; non-rate-limit failures of GitHub or the Tukui list skip that source, mirror the error as a warning and make the run partial; sources excluded with `--source` are not listed in `sources_skipped`. Tukui hints and recency read the `patch` and `last_update` fields that D4's `TukuiIndex` and B1's `tukui_list` slot already carry.

**Facts verified during planning.** Live on 2026-10-15: GitHub repository search works unauthenticated with `x-ratelimit-limit: 10`, `x-ratelimit-resource: search`, a one-minute window; Details! on WoWI (UID 23056) is from 2020; the WoWI filelist's `UICompatibility` has no 5.x values and nothing past 12.1.0; the Tukui list carries `patch[]` and `last_update`. In the code at `e902d36`: `GithubRest`'s single core `Budget` (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:40-82`); the retry layer's immediate `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at` on a 403/429 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` (`src/net/retry.rs:177-180`); `Catalog::by_name`/`entries` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs`); `RulesTable::family_for` (`src/rules.rs:625`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Ranking quality is subjective; the M2 plan rates search ranking **medium** confidence. Its failure mode is a worse ordering, never a wrong install. Mitigation: pure, table-tested scoring with deterministic tie-breaks, and a live probe at the checkpoint.
- The grouped OR qualifier is designed, not verified live. Mitigation: H4's live probe; follow reality if GitHub disagrees.
- GitHub's unauthenticated search limit is 10 a minute. Mitigation: one request per search, its own budget, and graceful `sources_skipped` with `reset_at`.

comments.text:
**done:** `omaddons search <query…> [-t T] [--source catalog|wowi|tukui|github]… [--limit N] [--refresh]`, alias `find`, in the Look group. It searches the catalog, the WoWInterface index, the Tukui list and GitHub's repository search, gives a ranked result list with a compatibility hint per selected client, and up to three install commands. Only GitHub receives the query. `argc gate` passes: 1221 tests, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical.

**Pure part (`src/resolve/search.rs`):**
- **`tier`:**
  - 0: the exact name or alias of a catalog hit, or the exact name of a WoWInterface or Tukui hit. GitHub never reaches tier 0.
  - 1: a name or alias prefix.
  - 2: every word in the name, aliases or folders.
  - 3: every word anywhere, author and description included.
  - Text is lowercased with whitespace collapsed.
- **`rank`:**
  - Merges duplicates into catalog hits, drops hits that reach no tier, then sorts by tier, then catalog first, then per-source log-scaled popularity `ln(1+n)/ln(1+max)` in thousandths, then the newest, then name, then ref.
  - A merged catalog hit keeps its name, ref, source and compat, and takes the best popularity, the newest date and the best tier of its duplicates.
- **`compat`:**
  - catalog families: `yes`/`no`, or `unknown` with no families;
  - Tukui patches through `family_for`: `likely`/`unlikely`, or `unknown` with no patches;
  - WoWInterface declared versions: `likely`/`unknown`, or `abandoned` past `DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_MAX_AGE` by `UIDate`, with `now` injected;
  - GitHub: `unknown`;
  - `Compat::suggestible` is true for yes, likely and unknown.
- **`cap_summary`:** cuts to `SEARCH_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` with `…`.

**GitHub (`src/sources/github_search.rs`):**
- `GithubSearch` has its own `Budget` instance, never `GithubRest`'s.
- The request is `GET https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=<query> (wow OR warcraft OR addon) in:name,description,topics&sort=stars&per_page=GITHUB_SEARCH_PER_PAGE`: purpose `github-search`, the API timeout, the same Accept and API-version headers, and a Bearer token from `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` when set. G2 is not on `main`, so `token_from` is used as `GithubRest` uses it.
- A spent budget is refused without a request. When the retry layer turns a 403 or 429 into `rate_limited`, the budget is recorded as spent with its `reset_at`.
- **Live check (2026-10-16):** GitHub accepted the grouped qualifier. "damage meter" gave 19 repositories, Details-Damage-Meter first with 228 stars.

**Command (`src/app/search.rs`):**
- Every source is optional (`--source`). A source that is off is `disabled`; sources left out by `--source` are never listed.
- **WoWInterface:** `WowiIndex::load_or_refresh`. An absent index gives `no_index`.
- **Tukui:** `cache.tukui_list()` with `Window` freshness, and `remember` once at the end, so the list is reused offline.
- **GitHub:** skipped under `--offline`.
- **Failures:**
  - Rate-limited or offline: `sources_skipped` (with `reset_at`), not partial.
  - Any other GitHub or Tukui failure: skipped, mirrored as a warning, `partial: true`.
- **Progress:** one `fetch` event per network source consulted.
- **Compat** per selected client (`select_many`, by id).
- **Commands:** `install <ref> -t <client>` for up to 3 results, each on the first client, by id, with the best suggestible hint. Never `no`, `unlikely` or `abandoned`.
- **`--limit`:** default 20, bound `SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS`. Outside 1..=50 it is `usage`, with fix `… --limit 1` for 0 and `--limit 50` above 50.
- **Human output:** the results table, why each source was skipped, `Install: …` with the hint note, or why nothing is suggested.

**Interim fixes switched:**
- `missing_dependency` for `no_source`: fix argv `omaddons search <folder>`. The message keeps "it may only be on CurseForge or Wago, which arrive in M5".
- C5's `bridge_dependency` with no source: `omaddons search <requires>`.
- Tukui `not_found`: `omaddons search <slug>`.

**decided:**
- WoWInterface's `not_found` keeps `omaddons help install`: it knows only the numeric id, which no search can use.
- Duplicates merge on the same ref, or on the same name plus a superset of the entry's folders. That is how the built-in catalog's WeakAuras (a GitHub ref) merges with its WoWInterface project.
- Tukui hits merge too.

**Tests:**
- **Unit:** tiers; ordering (catalog, popularity across sources, recency, name and ref ties); merging (same ref, same name and folders, a namesake with other folders kept apart); every compat rule; summary capping; the encoded GitHub URL and the token header.
- **`tests/search.rs` (8):**
  - **`weakauras`:** the catalog first, its WoWInterface project and GitHub repo merged (downloads 9M), compat `{era: yes, retail: no}`, hint `install gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2 -t era`.
  - **`damage meter -t retail`:** ranked Recount (likely), Details! 2020 (abandoned), then Skada (GitHub, tier 3, unknown). The hints are Recount and Skada, never Details!, and the first one runs: a `wowi:` install from fixtures.
  - **Privacy:** only `api.github.com` `github-search`, `api.mmoui.com` `wowi-filelist` and `api.tukui.org` `tukui-list` are contacted, and no path carries the query. 3 `fetch` progress events.
  - **`--offline`:** no request; the catalog and stored index answer; `github: offline`. A fresh home gives `github offline`, `wowi no_index` and `tukui offline`.
  - **Spent GitHub search:** `sources_skipped` with `reset_at`, the rest answers, not partial.
  - **In-process budgets:** the search budget is spent while the REST budget still `allows()`, and a second search sends nothing.
  - **Alias and filters:** `find` gives the same data as `search`; `--source wowi` gives only WoWInterface hits and no GitHub request; `sources.github.enabled false` gives `disabled`.
  - **Limits and determinism:** the bounds' fix argvs, `--limit 1`, and two runs with identical data and commands.
- **Other updated tests:**
  - `deps.rs`: the no-source fix is the search argv, and it runs (`--offline`).
  - `sources_tukui.rs`: the search fix.
- **Contract:** `search` row, snapshot `search_ok` (the catalog plus its merged GitHub duplicate), `find --offline`, and `--limit 99` as usage. Reviewed.
- **Reviewed snapshots:** `limit_registries` (3 new rows), `bare_help_human` and `bare_help_json` (search in Look, alias find), `install_dependencies`, and `deps__install_missing_no_source`.

**README:**
- the `search` section;
- the "What works today" and limitations rows;
- the Network and privacy host row and a Search paragraph (only GitHub receives the query);
- the `missing_dependency` and `bridge_dependency` rows.

**Wire names:**
- command `search`, alias `find`;
- data `{query, results: [{name, ref, source, author, summary, popularity: {downloads}|{stars}, updated_at, compat: {<id>: yes|no|likely|unlikely|unknown|abandoned}}], sources_skipped}`;
- `source` values: catalog, wowi, tukui, github;
- `net.log` purpose `github-search`;
- command action `install`.

**Constants:** `GITHUB_SEARCH_PER_PAGE` 20 (`politeness.rs`), `SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS` 50 and `SEARCH_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` 200 (`limits.rs`), with REGISTRY rows and name lists. The default `--limit` 20 and the 3 install hints are local display constants.

title: auth github: an opt-in REST token with set, status and clear
description:
## Background

The keyless path covers `release.json` publishers on GitHub with no REST at all. Three things still use GitHub's REST API: the beta and alpha channels (they need a release's `prerelease` flag), repos without `release.json` (asset listing), and search (G1). Unauthenticated REST allows 60 requests an hour (search: 10 a minute). An opt-in token raises that to 5,000 an hour (search: 30 a minute). Vision decision D12 makes the token **explicit, never implicit**: omaddons never reads the user's `gh` credentials or `GITHUB_TOKEN` silently, and the main GitHub path needs no token. This bead gives the owner one supported way to store a token, see what is configured, and remove it. It serves M2 goal G-M2-6 (findable: search at 30 a minute) and goal G-M2-1 (current by default: beta-channel and non-`release.json` repos stay checkable without exhausting 60 requests an hour).

Facts in the code today (line numbers are as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- `GithubRest::from_env()` (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:86-88`) reads only `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` through `token_from` (`:270-276`: trimmed, blank or control characters rejected; `GITHUB_TOKEN` never read). `SourceRegistry::builtin()` (`src/sources/mod.rs:127-136`) calls it, and `src/app/engine.rs:55` and `src/app/info.rs:294` build that registry. `api_request` adds `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (`github_rest.rs:103-112`).
- `config.toml` already parses `[sources.<id>] enabled` and `credential` (`src/state/config.rs:142-145`); `CredentialRef` is `Env { env } | File { file } | Command { command }` (`:150-160`). `resolve_credential` (`:755-795`) returns a redacting `Secret` plus warnings: `credential_file_mode` for a file readable by group or others; commands run as argv, no shell, stdin closed, stderr discarded, under `CREDENTIAL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` (10 s). **Nothing calls it at runtime today.**
- `Paths::credential_file(source)` (`src/state/paths.rs:125`) gives `<config>/omaddons/credentials/<source>`. `Writer::Auth` exists (`src/fsx/scope.rs:24-25`, documented "`auth` (M5)"); the `Config` row admits it (`:99`).
- `Op::WriteFile { content, mode }` (`src/fsx/op.rs:12-15`) sets the temp file's mode before the atomic rename (`src/fsx/sys.rs:136-160`), so a token never sits in a world-readable file. `Op::CreateDir` and `Op::Chmod` exist.
- `Redirecting` drops `authorization` and `x-api-key` when a redirect changes host (`src/net/guard.rs:19`, `:288`; tested in `src/net/tests.rs:281-291`). Record mode never stores request headers (`src/net/record.rs`).
- `auth_required` and `auth_rejected` are registered error codes (exit 1, not retryable). A 401 today surfaces as `http_status` through `error_for_status` (`github_rest.rs:150`, `:189`).
- `Context::new` already receives `stdin_is_tty`, but only for actor resolution (`src/cli.rs:169-181`, computed at `:230`).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** new `src/app/auth.rs`; `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs` (`Auth` subcommand in the Setup help group, A1); `src/sources/github_rest.rs` (token resolution order, 401 mapping); `src/sources/mod.rs` (`builtin` takes the resolved token); `src/app/engine.rs` and `src/app/info.rs` (pass it, and its warnings, through); `src/state/config.rs` (wire `resolve_credential`); `src/fsx/scope.rs` (drop "(M5)" from `Writer::Auth`'s doc); new `tests/auth.rs`; `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and `TEXT_FIXES`; `README.md` (commands table; privacy: the token is used for REST only).

**Synopsis (authoritative):** `omaddons auth github [status | set | clear | --from-gh]`. Bare `auth github` means `status`. `AuthArgs { source: AuthSource /* github only in M2 */, action: Status | Set | Clear, from_gh: bool }`. `--from-gh` alone means `set --from-gh`; with `status` or `clear` it is `usage` (decided). `curseforge` and `wago` are not values yet (DEC-1, no stubs).

### The design

- **`set`** reads the token from **stdin** (one line, trimmed). Control characters are rejected, and it never comes from argv.
  - When stdin is a TTY, `set` refuses with `usage` and the text fix `echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set`. It never blocks waiting for input.
  - It writes `<config>/omaddons/credentials/github` with mode 0600, through fsx `WriteFile { mode: 0o600 }` and `Writer::Auth`. The `credentials/` directory is created with mode 0700.
- **`--from-gh`** runs `gh auth token` as argv with no shell, under `CREDENTIAL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`, then stores the result as `set` does.
  - This is the only time omaddons reads `gh`'s credentials, and only on explicit request (D12).
  - Without `gh` on `PATH`, it fails with fix text naming `set`.
- **`clear`** overwrites the file with zero bytes (mode 0600). An empty file means "no token", and no new deletion path is needed (M2-D23).
- **`status`** reports `{configured, source: env|file|config|none, rate_limit: {limit, remaining, reset_at} | null}`.
  - Online, it makes one `GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit` (purpose `rate-limit`), which does not count against the core quota. `--offline` skips it.
  - It never prints the token, and never calls endpoints that reveal the account's identity.
- **Token resolution order:**
  1. `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN`;
  2. `config [sources.github] credential` (a `CredentialRef env|file|command`, already parsed);
  3. `<config>/omaddons/credentials/github`.

  `GITHUB_TOKEN` is never read (D12). The token goes only to `api.github.com`, and `Redirecting` already drops credential headers on cross-host hops. G2 makes this resolution the single source for every REST caller (`GithubRest`, search) and wires `resolve_credential`, so `credential_file_mode` fires when the file is readable by others.
- **A rejected token** (401 from `api.github.com`) is `auth_rejected`, with fix `omaddons auth github clear` and alternative `omaddons auth github set`.
- **What it enables in M2:** 5,000 REST requests an hour for beta and alpha channels, repos without `release.json`, and search (30 a minute instead of 10). The GraphQL batch path is M5 (M2-D22).

`status` data:

```json
"data":{"configured":true,"source":"file","rate_limit":{"limit":5000,"remaining":4987,"reset_at":"2026-10-15T21:00:00Z"}}
```

### Implementation notes

- **Shared resolution** in `src/sources/github_rest.rs`, e.g. `github_token(paths, config) -> TokenResolution { token: Option<Secret>, source, warnings }`. Env keeps `token_from`'s validation; config goes through `resolve_credential`; the file counts only when it exists and is non-blank, read through `resolve_credential(&CredentialRef::File { … })` so the mode warning fires. Carry the token as `Secret`.
- **A configured credential that fails to resolve** (unset variable, unreadable file, failing command) must not fall through silently to the file. Keep its error and raise it on the first REST request of the run, not at startup, so commands that need no REST are unaffected; `status` reports it as its error (decided).
- `SourceRegistry::builtin()` takes the resolved token instead of calling `from_env()`. D3 changes the same function to take `&SourceConfigView`; whichever lands second merges both signatures and updates every caller (`grep -rn 'SourceRegistry::builtin' src tests`). Resolution warnings reach the outcome of every command that builds the registry.
- **401 mapping** lives in `GithubRest::send` (and G1's search request), only when a token was sent. When the token came from the environment or config, `clear` would not help, so the fix names that source as text and `auth github clear` stays the alternative (decided).
- **TTY check:** keep `stdin_is_tty` on `Context` (it is already computed for actor resolution), so the refusal is decided before any read and is testable in-process through the existing `run_with` seam (decided).
- **Reading stdin:** the first line only, bounded by a new `src/limits.rs` constant (with a `REGISTRY` row) so a stream without a newline cannot grow memory. Blank input is `usage` with the same fix.
- **Writing:** follow `config set`'s pattern (`src/app/config.rs:285-326`): global lock, `ScopeTable`, `WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Auth, …)`, `ensure_dir_all` for the config dir, `CreateDir` then `Chmod { mode: 0o700 }` for `credentials/` (also tighten an existing directory that group or others can read; decided), then `WriteFile { mode: Some(0o600) }`.
- **`--from-gh`:** reuse `resolve_credential(&CredentialRef::Command { command: ["gh", "auth", "token"] })`. Check `PATH` for `gh` first; missing is `auth_required` with the text fix naming `set`; a failing or empty `gh auth token` is `auth_required` with a text fix to run `gh auth login` or use `set` (decided codes).
- **`set`, `--from-gh` and `clear` return the status shape** describing the state after the change, with `rate_limit: null` (no network). Human output names the file and says when `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` shadows it (decided).
- `status` reads `resources.core` from the `rate_limit` response for `{limit, remaining, reset_at}`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `echo tok | omaddons auth github set` writes the file with mode 0600 inside a 0700 directory, and `status` shows `configured: true, source: file`.
- `omaddons auth github set` with a TTY stdin fails `usage` at once and never blocks.
- With a token configured, REST requests carry `Authorization: Bearer` to `api.github.com` only. A cross-host redirect drops it (a new regression test).
- The token never appears in `net.log`, child-process argv, envelopes, stderr, history or state files (a grep test over all outputs).
- `clear` leaves a zero-byte file, and `status` then shows `configured: false, source: none`.
- `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` overrides the file and the config credential; a config `credential` overrides the file; `GITHUB_TOKEN` is ignored.
- A credentials file readable by others raises `credential_file_mode` on commands that resolve the token.
- A fixture 401 yields `auth_rejected` with the clear fix.
- Without `gh` installed, `--from-gh` fails with a fix naming `set`; with a fake `gh` that prints a token, the token is stored as `set` stores it.
- `status --offline` makes no request and reports `rate_limit: null`; online `status` makes exactly one request, to `/rate_limit`.
- `auth` appears in the Setup help group; contract rows pass.

## Test Plan

- `tests/auth.rs` (E2E, isolated HOME): `set` from piped stdin, file and directory modes; `status` online (fixture `api.github.com/rate_limit`) and offline; `clear`; precedence env over config over file; `GITHUB_TOKEN` ignored; `credential_file_mode` after a chmod; a 401 fixture; `--from-gh` with a fake `gh` script on `PATH`, and with no `gh`.
- Header assertions at the `Http` layer with a recording fake (as the existing `github_rest.rs` unit tests check `api_request`), plus the cross-host redirect regression test beside `src/net/tests.rs:281-291`.
- TTY refusal in-process through `run_with` with `stdin_is_tty = true`.
- Leak grep: run every form with a distinctive token; grep stdout, stderr, `net.log`, history and the state dir; fake `gh` and `git` executables that log their argv prove the token never reaches a child's argv.

## Considerations

- `auth github status` never calls identity endpoints (such as `/user`), for privacy.
- The GraphQL batch path is M5 (M2-D22: it needs POST support, request bodies and body-keyed fixtures for a small gain once tag-first probes exist). `auth curseforge|wago` arrive with their sources in M5.
- An empty or blank credentials file means "no token". Never delete it; `prune()` stays the only deletion path (M2-D23).
- G1 may land before or after this bead: whichever lands second wires search to this shared resolution.
- Collision hot spots: `src/sources/mod.rs` and every `SourceRegistry::builtin` caller (D3), `src/sources/github_rest.rs` (B2), `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs`.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1` (Grouped bare help with a command group registry): `auth` joins the Setup group in the same commit as its clap variant, and bare help must stay under 30 lines.

Unblocks:
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit for M2): audits the auth rows, `auth_rejected` fixes and the new text fixes.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records): records the command, the `Writer::Auth` scope note, the privacy statement and the GraphQL departure.

close_reason: auth github: an opt-in GitHub token with status, set, clear and --from-gh; one resolution for every REST caller

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** Beta-channel addons, repos without `release.json`, and search all go through GitHub's REST API, which allows 60 requests an hour unauthenticated. An owner tracking several beta builds can exhaust that in one `update`. A stored, opt-in token raises the limit to 5,000 an hour without ever reading credentials the owner did not hand over. It serves goals G-M2-1 (current by default) and G-M2-6 (findable), and the project's privacy promise (vision goal G5: verifiable privacy), because the token's single source, single destination host and redaction become testable facts.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D22** (departs from vision): the GitHub GraphQL batch path moves to M5; `auth github` (a REST token) stays in M2. Why: GraphQL needs `Method::Post`, request bodies, body-keyed fixtures and retry changes, for a small gain once tag-first probes exist (B2 makes an unchanged stable release cost one `github.com` request with no REST); M5 is already the accounts milestone. Rejected: building POST support now. The vision tied the token to a GraphQL query for all tracked repos; in M2 it only raises REST limits.
- **M2-D23**: `auth github clear` truncates the credential file to zero bytes. Why: keeps `fsx::prune()` the only deletion path, with fixed call sites, and an empty file already means "no token". Rejected: adding a new prune call site for one file.
- **Vision D12** (token opt-in, never implicit): `GITHUB_TOKEN` is never read, and `gh`'s credentials are read only by an explicit `--from-gh`.
- **One resolution for every REST caller** (env, then config `sources.github.credential`, then the credentials file), wired through `resolve_credential`, so the dormant `credential_file_mode` warning finally fires and search (G1) cannot drift to a different rule. G1 and G2 have no edge between them; whichever lands second does the wiring.
- **`set` reads stdin only, and refuses a TTY.** Argv leaks into shell history and process listings; a blocking prompt would hang agents.

**Decisions made while writing this bead** (record with `decided:` comments): a configured credential that fails to resolve is raised on the first REST request, never silently skipped; the 401 fix names the token's actual source (env or config as text, the file as `auth github clear`); `stdin_is_tty` is carried on `Context`; `--from-gh` failures are `auth_required`; `set`/`clear` return the status shape with `rate_limit: null`; an over-permissive `credentials/` directory is tightened to 0700; the stdin read bound is a new `src/limits.rs` constant.

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `e902d36`): `token_from` and `GithubRest::from_env` (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:86-88`, `:270-276`) and their only caller `SourceRegistry::builtin` (`src/sources/mod.rs:130`); `CredentialRef` and `resolve_credential` (`src/state/config.rs:150-160`, `:755-795`) with no runtime caller; `Writer::Auth` labelled M5 (`src/fsx/scope.rs:24-25`) and admitted by the Config row; `Paths::credential_file` (`src/state/paths.rs:125`); cross-host credential-header stripping (`src/net/guard.rs:19`); atomic writes set the mode on the temp file before rename (`src/fsx/sys.rs:136-160`); `auth_rejected` and `auth_required` already registered. Live on 2026-10-15: unauthenticated search allows 10 requests a minute on its own `search` resource.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A token leak through logs, errors or fixtures. Mitigation: `Secret` redacts in `Debug`/`Display`; record mode stores no request headers; `net.log` logs no headers; a grep test runs every form with a distinctive token over stdout, stderr, `net.log`, history and state, and fake `gh`/`git` executables log their argv.
- `SourceRegistry::builtin` is changed by D3 too. Mitigation: whichever lands second merges both signatures; the compiler finds every caller.
- Confidence: the M2 plan does not rate auth separately; it wires existing, tested pieces (`resolve_credential`, `Writer::Auth`, `WriteFile` with a mode, the redirect guard), so risk is low.

title: Epic: M2 checkpoint verification and docs
description:
## Background

M2 adds ten commands (`outdated, update, pin, unpin, adopt, export, sync, copy, search, auth`), two keyless sources (WoWInterface, Tukui), records-only and multi-target transactions, dependency planning rounds, adoption, drift checks and a desired-state file. Each feature bead tests its own behaviour. Some guarantees only show when the whole surface is checked together:
- the CLI contract across every command, alias and recommendation;
- the crash invariant across every new transaction shape;
- the timing and request-economy targets;
- the behaviour of the live upstream services;
- the owner's six real clients, left exactly as they were found.

M1 closed the same way. Its checkpoint bead (`omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.7.10`) ran every vision checkpoint and put the evidence for each criterion in its close reason: test names, timings, `net.log` counts, command output with home paths replaced by `<home>`. "Done" was a recorded fact, not an impression. M2 does the same, and this epic holds that work.

Its tasks run last (delivery wave 6). Each one starts when the features it verifies have landed. They add tests, benchmarks, docs and tracker records. Product code changes only when a task finds a defect: the defect is filed as a bug with `--deps discovered-from:<task id>`, fixed, and checked again.

The epic serves every M2 goal through evidence, and G-M2-7 most of all: no regression of M1 guarantees. Every new mutation is a journaled, snapshotted, undoable, attributed transaction. Every write goes through fsx (`src/fsx/`, the single writer). Every request is allowlisted and logged. Every error has a fix, and the JSON contract stays one envelope.

Placeholders used by this epic and its children: `<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>` are the XDG config, state and cache homes (`<config>/omaddons/` and so on); `<client dir>` is the directory holding a client's `Interface/` and `WTF/`.

## Goals

- **H1:** audit the contract across the whole M2 surface: matrix rows for every command and alias, registries (39 error codes, 34 warning codes), text fixes, determinism, exit codes, and every `status` recommendation actually run.
- **H2:** extend the cross-process crash matrix and the concurrency suite to every new transaction shape (multi-addon update, dependency install, mixed sync, folder handover, adopt, pin, forget), with the folder oracle, the record oracle and the mixed-transaction checks.
- **H3:** `argc bench` (hyperfine recipes) and release-mode budget tests for the four timing targets, plus `net.log` request-economy assertions in the normal gate.
- **H4:** live probes for WoWInterface, Tukui, the GitHub Atom feed, GitHub search and `outdated` economy, and the catalog × declared-flavor matrix extended to `tukui:` entries.
- **H5:** real-machine smoke tests for M2 on the owner's six clients: read-only everywhere, mutating only with explicit `-t` on retail and the Classic clients, everything undone by transaction id, the Forever stress-test set untouched.
- **H6:** README, help text and vision-bead records: contract additions, constants, departures, write scope, the M3 handoff and the known `target-addons-shared` limitation.
- **H7:** run the twelve M2 checkpoint criteria, paste the evidence into its close reason, tick M2 on the vision bead and close the milestone.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- H7's close reason holds evidence for each of the twelve M2 checkpoint criteria: update speed and economy, zero-REST checks, dependencies (LittleWigs → BigWigs), adoption fixtures, drift, desired state, Tukui, WoWInterface, status, changelogs, search, and gate and probes.
- `argc gate --all` passes. Every fuzz target (the 9 from M1 and the 7 M2 adds) ran 10 minutes without a crash.
- The contract suite covers every M2 command, alias and new flag, on success and failure, and every `status` recommendation in the scenario set executes successfully.
- Every new crash-matrix op crashes at 10 or more failpoints with its oracle holding, and every commit, multi-addon ones included, holds the lock under 50 ms.
- The release-mode budget tests pass, and `argc bench` prints medians that meet the targets.
- Every live probe passes on the checkpoint date, including the catalog × declared-flavor matrix with `tukui:` entries.
- The real-machine suite passes and leaves every AddOns folder and `WTF/` tree byte-identical. The Forever stress-test set keeps its record generation and its tree hash.
- README.md describes exactly what exists, and its Status says M2 is done.
- The vision bead carries the M2 comments (contract additions, constants, departures, write scope, M3 handoff, "[x] M2").
- `br epic close-eligible` has closed the area epics and the milestone epic.

## Non-Goals

- No new features. A gap a task finds becomes a bug bead, not scope added to the task.
- The wire-names golden file, `capabilities`, `robot-docs` and the `doctor` surface are M4.
- No CI (vision D16: a local gate before every code-change commit, no CI). Timing assertions never enter the per-commit gate; budgets and benchmarks run at the checkpoint.
- No mutation of the `forever` client while `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` is open.
- No GitHub GraphQL path (M5, M2-D22).

## Considerations

- **Order.** H1 to H6 run in parallel once their blockers close. H7 runs last and depends on all of them, plus C2 and C7, which nothing else in this epic waits for.
- **Edges re-pointed by the split of large tasks.** H1 and H6 wait for E5.3, F3.2 and F3.3, the last subtasks of `adopt` and `sync`. H2 waits for A4.4, C4.2, E5.2, F3.2 and F3.3, the subtasks that make the transaction shapes it crashes final. H5 waits for E5.1 (adopt report mode) and F3.1 (sync core): it only runs `adopt` read-only and `sync --dry-run`.
- **Evidence is public-safe.** Replace home paths with `<home>` in pasted output. Never paste hostnames, account, realm or character names.
- **A failing criterion** gets a bug bead (`--deps discovered-from:<H7>`), a fix, and a re-run. Close with a known gap only when the deviation is recorded and justified in a vision comment, as M1 did for WeakAuras on retail.
- **Volunteer-run services.** WoWInterface and Tukui are run by volunteers. Probes and benchmarks make the minimum number of requests, and repeatable timing runs use fixtures.
- **Forever.** The owner's `forever` client holds the stress-test set: transaction `01M50WBAPCN7YWGFFK8EB48RN8`, 12 managed folders across 5 addons. It stays installed until `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` closes (deferred to 2026-10-20). Only read-only commands may touch `forever`.
- **Collisions.** `tests/engine_crash.rs` is also edited by A4.4. `README.md` is updated by every wave that ships a command (in the same commit or the next one), so H6 is the final consistency pass, not the first mention. `src/error.rs` is touched by several feature beads.

## Children

| Key | Id | Title | Scope in one line | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` | Contract conformance audit for M2 | matrix rows for every M2 command and alias, registries 39/34, text fixes, determinism, recommendations run on fresh homes | B5, B6, B7, C5, C6, D6, E3, E5.3, F2, F3.2, F3.3, F4, G1, G2 |
| H2 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` | Crash and concurrency coverage for M2 transactions | new crash ops with folder, record and mixed oracles; three races; lock hold under 50 ms | A4.4, B6, C4.2, E5.2, F3.2, F3.3 |
| H3 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.3` | Performance budgets and bench recipes | `argc bench`, release budget tests in `tests/perf.rs`, `net.log` economy assertions in the gate | A8, B2, B3, B5, B6, B8, D2, E2, E3 |
| H4 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.4` | Live probes for M2 | WoWI, Tukui, Atom, search and `outdated` economy probes; catalog matrix with `tukui:` entries | B2, B5, C2, D3, D4, D6, G1 |
| H5 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.5` | Real-machine smoke tests for M2 | six real clients: read-only everywhere, explicit-`-t` mutations undone by id, Forever untouched | B6, B7, C4.1, E3, E5.1, F2, F3.1 |
| H6 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` | README, help text and vision-bead records for M2 | README pass, help strings, vision comments, `target-addons-shared` filed for M4 | B5, B6, B7, C2, C5, C6, D3, D4, D6, E3, E5.3, F2, F3.2, F3.3, F4, G1, G2 |
| H7 | `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7` | M2 checkpoint verification | twelve criteria with evidence, fuzz-all, "[x] M2" comment, close-eligible | C2, C7, H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6 |
acceptance_criteria: All seven children (H1-H7) are closed; H7's close reason holds evidence for each of the twelve M2 checkpoint criteria; argc gate --all passes and every fuzz target (9 M1, 7 M2) ran 10 minutes without a crash; the contract suite covers every M2 command, alias and recommendation; every new crash op crashes at 10 or more failpoints with its oracle holding and lock hold stays under 50 ms; budgets and live probes pass, including the catalog matrix with tukui: entries; the real-machine suite leaves every AddOns folder and WTF/ byte-identical and the Forever set untouched; README.md describes exactly what exists; the vision bead carries the M2 comments; br epic close-eligible closed the milestone
