comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this epic.** M2 changes the most delicate code (records-only work, handover, dependency rounds, multi-target commits) and adds the first commands that fan out across clients. Per-feature tests cannot show that the whole surface keeps M1's promises; an evidence-based checkpoint can, as in M1.

**Testing strategy for M2, recorded here so it survives in the tracker.**

Layers (what · where · when):
- Pure unit: evaluator, resolver, identifier, scorer, parsers, text renderers, carry-over · `src/**` `#[cfg(test)]` · every gate.
- Engine: records-only work, working view, handover, rounds, multi-target commit, run undo · `tests/plan.rs`, `tests/deps.rs`, `tests/engine_multi_target.rs`, `tests/undo_history.rs` · every gate.
- E2E (binary): every command, with HTTP fixtures, synthetic trees and a fake `/proc` · `tests/<command>.rs` · every gate.
- Contract: envelope, exits, fixes, determinism; recommendations actually run · `tests/contract/` · every gate.
- Crash and concurrency: folder and record oracles per op; races · `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs` · every gate.
- Request economy: `net.log` counts (fetch-once, download-once, zero-REST, warm zero) · inside E2E · every gate.
- Fuzz: 7 new targets plus the 9 existing · `fuzz/` · checkpoint, 10 min each.
- Budgets: `status --cached`, drift, WoWI index parse · `tests/perf.rs` (`#[ignore]`, release) · checkpoint.
- Benchmarks: hyperfine over `update` and `outdated`, warm and cold · `argc bench` · checkpoint.
- Live probes: WoWI, Tukui, Atom, search, catalog matrix, `outdated` economy · `tests/live_probes.rs` · checkpoint.
- Real machine: six clients, every change undone, Forever read-only · `tests/real_machine.rs` · checkpoint.

Fixtures: replay files at `tests/fixtures/http/<scenario>/<host>/<stem>.{json,body}`, keyed by method plus normalised URL. New scenarios `wowi/`, `tukui/`, `github-feed/`, `github-search/`, `deps/`, `adopt/`, plus one gzip body with `content-encoding: gzip`. `fixture_seq` sequences restart in every CLI process, so multi-command scenarios switch fixture sets with `home.scenario(...)`. Time is injected into pure functions. End-to-end freshness tests pre-seed `fetched_at` (`Home::seed_memo`) or write a pre-aged index file; there is no clock seam.

Request economy (`net_log(home)` counters by host and purpose): a cold `outdated` on N refs across T targets logs at most N `release-latest` lines; a warm re-run inside the window logs zero; after the window, unchanged tags log exactly N `release-latest` lines and no `release-json`, and a changed tag adds one `release-json` fetch (two lines with the redirect hop); `update` across targets sharing an asset logs one `asset` fetch per distinct asset; a `sync` re-run logs zero; a `release.json` publisher on stable logs zero `api.github.com` lines.

Crash oracles: the folder oracle (M1): each folder wholly old or wholly new by tree hash, consistent with generation and history after recovery, lock inode unchanged. The record oracle (A4.4): after an abort and a recovery command, the record has the edit if and only if `history.jsonl` has the transaction, the generation matches, and every AddOns folder is byte-identical. Mixed transactions: the folder oracle per folder, plus records reference only existing folders, `required_by` edits are present if and only if committed, and after a handover exactly one record owns the folder.

Must never happen (negative tests): a token, Tukui download URL or credential in `net.log`, records, plans, history, envelopes or stderr; `status` writing anything; `outdated` (no `--verify`), `search`, `adopt --no-verify` or `export` (no `--write`) writing outside `<cache>/omaddons/`, `net.log` and planning's `<state>/omaddons/inflight/<tx>.lock`; an adopt changing any byte under AddOns; an optional dependency installed; `sync` moving an addon to a newer release without a pin or lock; `update` installing an older release without an explicit `--channel` switch; `export --write` overwriting a hand-edited file without `--overwrite`; any M2 path touching a `Blizzard_*` folder.

Real-machine discipline: explicit `-t` on every mutation; undo by own transaction ids in reverse order; AddOns and `WTF/` tree hashes equal before and after; running clients skipped; `forever` read-only until `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` closes; fan-out commands without `-t` forbidden.

**Decisions applied.** Vision D16 keeps timing out of the per-commit gate. M2-D10 swaps the BugSack → !BugGrabber checkpoint for LittleWigs → BigWigs: BugSack lists !BugGrabber under `OptionalDeps`, and it has no official GitHub release (verified 2026-10-15). Rejected: auto-installing optional dependencies.

**Confidence.** Timing targets: medium until measured (M1 evidence: `status --cached` 1.3 ms, lock hold 2 ms, a 2,529-file stat walk about 3 ms). Economy and contract claims: high, asserted from `net.log` and envelopes.

title: Contract conformance audit for M2
description:
## Background

Each M2 command task adds its own contract matrix rows, registers its own codes and reviews its own snapshots. Nothing checks the M2 surface as a whole, and the gaps fall between tasks: a code registered by one task and emitted by another, a recommendation whose argv only works once a later command exists, an alias without a row, a text fix the harness has never seen. This task audits the whole surface once every command has landed.

The contract suite today (line numbers are as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- **`tests/contract/main.rs`**, the `support::check` harness, asserts for every `--json` run:
  - exactly one stdout envelope, keys in wire order (`ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, partial, data, error, warnings, commands, meta`);
  - `exit_code` equals the process exit and the error code's registered exit;
  - every `fix`/`fix_argv` (on errors, alternatives and warnings) is an `omaddons` argv that round-trips through shell-words, or a text fix;
  - every `commands[]` entry has an `action`, an argv starting with `omaddons` whose shell-words join equals `command`, and a boolean `destructive`;
  - stderr is NDJSON (`progress`, `log`, `warning`, `error` events) with exactly one `error` event per failure.
  A null-argv fix passes when it starts with a `TEXT_FIXES` prefix (`tests/contract/main.rs:49`) **or** does not start with `omaddons`.
- **`tests/contract/matrix.rs`**: one test per M1 command (`bare_and_help, status, targets, list, info, install, remove, undo, history, config, net_log`), success and failure, with envelope snapshots (meta removed, ULIDs, times and the tempdir redacted).
- **`tests/contract/special.rs`**: `locked`, panic, `--offline`, CI and dumb terminals, format spellings, `repeated_runs_are_byte_identical` (today: `list`, `status`, `history`, `info`, `remove`), human failures.
- **`tests/contract/exit_sites.rs`**: every `ErrorCode::<Variant>` used in `src/` is registered; codes are unique snake_case with exits in the 0–6 dictionary; the process exits only through `Exit`.
- **`src/error.rs` tests**: `error_registry_matches_the_table` asserts `ErrorCode::ALL.len() == 38` against a hand-written `EXPECTED` table of `(wire, exit, retryable)` (`src/error.rs:702`); `wire_names_are_unique_and_snake_case` asserts `WarningCode::ALL.len() == 22` (`src/error.rs:746`).
- **`status` recommendations** come from `recommendations()` (`src/app/status.rs:353`): `forget_target` (`omaddons targets rm <id>`, destructive), `inspect` (`omaddons list -t <id> -v`), `list_unmanaged` (`omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged`), and `status` when `--cached` finds no discovery cache. Nothing runs them.

Without the audit, an agent that follows M2's own hints can hit a fix that does not run. The M4 wire-name freeze would also start from an unrecorded surface, and H6 would have no reliable list of new wire names to put on the vision bead. This task serves G-M2-7 (no regression of M1 guarantees: every error has a fix, and the JSON contract stays one envelope) and the agent workflows of every other goal, where each intent must be reachable in at most two commands with argv hints.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `tests/contract/main.rs` (`TEXT_FIXES`, helpers), `tests/contract/matrix.rs`, `tests/contract/special.rs`, `tests/contract/exit_sites.rs`, `tests/contract/snapshots/`, `src/error.rs` (tests only), `tests/common/home.rs` or a new `tests/common/scenarios.rs` (scenario-home builders, DEC-8).

### 1. Matrix rows for the whole M2 surface

Every M2 command and alias gets at least one success row and one failure row through `support::check`, each with a reviewed snapshot. Many rows already exist from the feature tasks; audit them rather than duplicate them, and add what is missing:
- `outdated` and its alias `check`; `outdated --check` (exit 6 with `data`) and `outdated --changelog`;
- `update` and its alias `upgrade`; `update --all` with names (`usage`, argv fix without `--all`); `update --channel` without names (`usage`, the `TEXT_FIXES` text fix `omaddons update <addon> --channel <C>`); `update --version V` (`usage`, fix argv `omaddons install … --version V`, alternative `omaddons pin <addon> --version V`);
- `pin`, `unpin` (`not_managed` as a failure row);
- `adopt` (report), `adopt --apply`, `adopt <folder> --ref <ref>`;
- `export`, `export --write` (and its `desired_state_invalid` refusals `edited` and `empty`);
- `sync` (and its missing-default-file `not_found` text fix), `sync --dry-run`, `sync --locked`, `sync --prune`;
- `copy` (`--from` equal to `--to` is `usage`);
- `search` and its alias `find`;
- `auth github` (`status`, `set` from stdin, `clear`; `set` with a TTY stdin is `usage`);
- the new flags on M1 commands: `undo --run`, `history --run`, `history --by`, `install --reinstall`, `install --refresh`, `status --deep`, `list --deep`, `info --changelog`, `info --refresh`;
- the usage-error special case: `omaddons reinstall X` gets `fix_argv` `omaddons install X --reinstall`.

The bare-help row (`bare_and_help`) must show the grouped layout (Look, Change, Setup) with every command in exactly one group, and the `--json` help entries carry `group`.

### 2. Registries

After M2 the registries are:
- **Errors: 39** (M1's 38 plus `desired_state_invalid`: exit 2, not retryable, `details: {path, line, key, reason}`, `details.reason` one of `edited`, `empty`, `unknown_target_section`, `duplicate`, `bad_value`, `unknown_family`, `newer_schema`). F1 registers it; H1 checks that the `EXPECTED` row and the count are right.
- **Warnings: 34** (M1's 22 plus 12): `addon_pinned`, `still_required`, `orphaned_dependency`, `bridge_dependency`, `local_changes_replaced`, `stale_check`, `adopt_name_changed`, `export_missing_target`, `export_local_source`, `desired_unknown_key`, `desired_unknown_target`, `not_locked`. `missing_dependency` is already registered (M1) and is emitted for the first time by C4.1.
- Every new warning must carry a fix: an argv, or a text fix the harness accepts. Write a test that triggers each new warning in a fixture scenario and runs it through `support::check`; the harness checks the fix shape.
- Any count that differs from 39 and 34 means a feature task added an unrecorded code, or a planned one is missing. Find which, and record it in the close comment.

### 3. Text fixes

A null-argv fix passes the harness when it does not start with `omaddons`, so most M2 text fixes already pass: `echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set`, "pass the file: `omaddons sync <path>`, or run `omaddons export --write` on the machine that has your addons", and "the replaced files are kept in the transaction snapshot; `omaddons undo` restores them" (`local_changes_replaced` under `--dry-run`). Add to `TEXT_FIXES` only fixes that begin with `omaddons` and carry no argv (a placeholder such as `<path>`). Keep the list small and explicit.

### 4. Determinism

Extend `repeated_runs_are_byte_identical` (or add a sibling) with fixture-backed runs of `outdated`, `status` (with `updates`, `drift`, `adoptable` and `orphans` populated), `export` and `search`. Two runs must produce byte-identical stdout once `meta` is removed. The ordering rule for M2 output: when order carries no meaning, sort by target id, then addon name (case-insensitive), then folder key.

### 5. Exit codes

Every new error path must exit with its code's dictionary exit (the matrix rows check `exit_code`). `exit_sites` must still pass after every M2 code is used in `src/`. `--check` and `--strict` exits: `outdated --check` exits 6 when any update is available, and still 6 when the run is also partial. `status --check` exits 6 on drift (`addon_modified`, `addon_folder_missing`). `--strict` turns partial success into exit 6 on `update`, `sync` and `copy`. Exit 6 keeps `data`.

### 6. Recommendations actually run

`status` recommendations come in this order. Each is a `CommandHint` with argv.
1. existing journal and state fixes;
2. `reinstall`: `omaddons install <name> -t <id> --reinstall`, one per drifted or missing addon, at most 5;
3. `update`: `omaddons update` when several targets have updates, else `omaddons update -t <id>`;
4. `adopt`: `omaddons adopt -t <id>`, only when `adoptable > 0`;
5. `check_updates`: `omaddons outdated` when any target with checkable records is unchecked or stale;
6. `remove_orphans`: `omaddons remove <names…> -t <id>`, one command for all orphans on that target;
7. existing `forget_target` and `inspect`.

M1's `list_unmanaged` hint stays when a target has unmanaged folders and `adoptable` is 0, and `status` (the uncached run) stays for `--cached` without a discovery cache.

Build a scenario set of fixture homes that, together, make `status` emit every action at least once:
- a managed addon edited with A10's `edit_managed` (`reinstall`);
- one addon installed behind on two targets, after an `outdated` (`update`);
- an unmanaged folder whose name is a catalog entry's folder (`adopt`);
- records with no memo entry, and a memo older than `check_interval_hours` (`check_updates`);
- LittleWigs with its dependency BigWigs, then `remove LittleWigs` (`remove_orphans`);
- a registered target whose client directory was removed (`forget_target`);
- a degraded addon after an `install --force` takeover (`inspect`);
- unmanaged folders that match no catalog entry (`list_unmanaged`).

For each scenario, run `status --json`, then run each recommended argv in the order given, **each on a fresh copy of the home**, through `support::check`:
- non-destructive commands MUST exit 0;
- destructive ones (`remove_orphans`, `forget_target`) MUST exit 0 **and** leave the state the hint promised. After `remove_orphans`, `status` shows `orphans: 0` for that target and the explicit addons are untouched. After `forget_target`, the target is gone from `targets`.
- `reinstall` MUST clear the drift finding, and `update` MUST leave `updates.available` at 0.

**Fresh copies, decided:** rebuild each copy from its scenario builder in a new tempdir instead of copying directories. The registry stores absolute `install_root` and `client_dir` paths (`RegistryEntry`, `src/state/registry.rs:34-40`), so a recursive copy at another path would still point at the original's clients, and a destructive hint would act on the wrong home. Builders are deterministic, so a rebuild is an exact copy. Scenario homes use HTTP fixtures (`OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`), so every argv runs offline-deterministically.

### 7. What the M2 surface should contain

These are the contract additions recorded on the vision bead (H6). The audit checks that each exists and that nothing else changed shape:
- `TxKind` `pin` (records-only). `ChangeKind` `adopt`, `edit`, with `fields` from `pinned|channel|reason|required_by|ref`.
- Item statuses `adopted`, `pinned`, `unpinned`, `edited`, `skipped`, beside M1's `installed`, `updated`, `removed`, `unchanged`, `failed`. Skip reasons `pinned`, `ahead`, `blocked`, `static`, `unchecked`, `already_installed`, `no_build_for_target`, `local_source`, `duplicate`. Summary buckets `changed`, `unchanged`, `skipped`, `failed`.
- Attention strings `addon_modified`, `addon_folder_missing`.
- Additive data keys: `status` `updates`, `drift`, `adoptable`, `orphans`; install and multi-target items `reason`, `required_by`, `bridge_dependencies`, `unresolved`, `skip_reason`, `duplicate_of` (A5, only on a `skipped`/`duplicate` item), and `optional_dependencies` under `-v` only (C5); folders `recorded`; bare `--json` help entries `group` (`look|change|setup`, A1); `list --unmanaged`/`list -v` TOC summaries `title_plain`, `website`, `dependencies`, `optional_deps`, `tukui_project_folders` (C1); `list` addons `latest`, `reason`, `required_by`, `orphan`, `drift`; `info` per target `reason`, `required_by`, `orphan`, `drift`; `info` top level (with `--changelog`) `changelog`, `changelog_unavailable`; `outdated` items `status`, `confidence`, `blocked_reason`, `unchecked_reason`, `error`, and with `--changelog` `latest.changelog`, `latest.changelog_unavailable`; `history` `run`, `changes.recorded`; `undo` `run`, `reverted_run`, `transactions[]` (`status` `undone|failed`); error `details` `within_transaction`, `required_by`, `cause`, `reason`.
- Enum spellings: update statuses `current, update_available, pinned, ahead, blocked, failed, unchecked, static`, confidences `verified, declared, likely, unlikely`, blocked reasons `verified_not_loading, older_than_installed`, unchecked reasons `never_checked, source_disabled, offline, no_eligible_release` (B4); adoption tiers `exact, identified, guess, cf_only, unknown`, the nine evidence and five strength values (E4.1, E4.2), group reasons `files_differ, folder_set_differs, not_verified, not_verified_offline, source_error` and per-folder `failed` reasons `unindexable, limit_exceeded, already_managed` (E5.1); `unresolved` reasons `several_catalog_entries, wowi_ambiguous, wowi_abandoned, no_source, managed_folder_missing` (C3) plus `unknown_condition, out_of_date, limit_reached` (C4.1); drift states `clean, modified, missing, unindexed` (E2); compatibility hints `yes, no, likely, unlikely, unknown, abandoned` (G1); `changelog_unavailable` reasons `not_supported, offline, fetch_failed, no_releases` (D6); `sources_skipped` reasons `offline, rate_limited, disabled, no_index` (D2's `SourceSkipped`); `desired_state_invalid` `details.reason` as in section 2. The contract comment on the milestone epic `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp` lists each with its owning bead.
- One type change: the dry-run plan's `releases[].expected_hash`, from a string to a tagged `{"md5": "…"}` or `{"sha256": "…"}` (M2-D32: plans are not stored until M4, so only dry-run output changes).
- History `run` (ULID) and `ops[].edit` (`required_by_add`, `required_by_remove`).
- `net.log` purposes `wowi-filelist`, `wowi-details`, `tukui-list`, `tukui-addon`, `tukui-changelog`, `github-search`, `rate-limit` (and `asset` for WoWI and Tukui downloads), and the field `wire_bytes`.
- Progress events keep M1's shape (`{"event":"progress","phase":…,"message":…,"current":n,"total":m}`, A9) with phases `fetch`, `download`, `verify`, `stage`, `commit`.
- Recommendation and command actions: `update`, `check_updates`, `adopt`, `adopt_folder`, `adopt_with_ref`, `reinstall`, `remove_orphans`, `install`, `undo`, `undo_run`.
- `schema_version` stays `"1.0"` everywhere (DEC-4 practice until the M4 freeze).
- **M1 consumers keep working.** `install`'s JSON is unchanged except for the additive item fields and the item status `skipped` (`skip_reason: duplicate`). `undo` keeps every M1 key (`dry_run, reverted, tx, folders, saved_variables, reload_required, atomic_swap`), describing the first reverted transaction.

### 8. Close comment

List every wire name the audit saw that is new in M2, grouped as above, and flag any that differ from section 7. H6 copies the list into the vision comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The contract suite passes.
- Every M2 command, alias and new flag in section 1 has at least one success row and one failure row through `support::check`, with reviewed snapshots.
- Every new code is registered with its exit code and retryable flag: 39 error codes (`desired_state_invalid` exit 2, not retryable) and 34 plain warning codes; `src/error.rs` tests assert both counts.
- Every new warning has a fix, either an argv or a text fix the harness accepts. A test triggers each of the 12 new warnings plus `missing_dependency`.
- `outdated`, `status`, `export` and `search` are byte-identical across repeated fixture runs, apart from `meta`.
- Every new error path exits with its dictionary exit, and `exit_sites` passes.
- Every `status` recommendation in the scenario set executes successfully, in order, each on a freshly built home. Destructive hints leave the promised state, and `reinstall` and `update` clear their findings.
- `install` and `undo` keep their M1 keys (additive changes only).
- The close comment lists the new wire names for H6.

## Test Plan

- `cargo test --test contract` (matrix, special, exit_sites) and `cargo test --lib error` (registry tables).
- The recommendation runner over the scenario set, through `support::check`.
- `argc gate`. Review every new or changed snapshot in `tests/contract/snapshots/` before accepting it.

## Considerations

- The wire-names golden file is M4. This audit records the names; it does not freeze them.
- **D6 is a blocker of this task** (an edge added during bead creation; the plan had missed it). `info --changelog` and `outdated --changelog` come from D6 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.6`), and the audit covers every M2 flag, so it waits for D6.
- This task does not change behaviour. A hint that does not run, a missing fix or an unregistered code is a bug in the owning feature task's area: file it with `--deps discovered-from:omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1`, fix it, and note it in the close comment.
- Scenario homes must not use the network. Recommendations such as `update` and `check_updates` fetch, so their homes carry fixture scenarios. `reinstall` from a cached blob makes zero requests.
- `src/error.rs` is edited by several feature tasks (new codes). Rebase before the gate, and never renumber or reorder existing `EXPECTED` rows.
- `tests/contract/` snapshots are shared with every command task. Review diffs; never accept blindly.
- `destructive` flags: `forget_target` is `true` today. Check that `remove_orphans` is marked destructive and that read-only hints are not.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- B5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.5` (The outdated command): `outdated`/`check` rows, its `--check` exit and its determinism run.
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): `update`/`upgrade` rows and the `update` recommendation's argv.
- B7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7` (pin and unpin): `pin`/`unpin` rows and the `pin` transaction kind.
- C5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.5` (Dependency results in command output): the additive item fields and the `missing_dependency`/`bridge_dependency` fixes the audit checks.
- C6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.6` (Dependency bookkeeping; orphans): `still_required`, `orphaned_dependency` and the destructive `remove_orphans` recommendation.
- D6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.6` (Changelogs): the `info --changelog` and `outdated --changelog` rows and the `changelog_unavailable` reasons.
- E3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.3` (Drift in status, list and info): `addon_modified`, `local_changes_replaced` and the `reinstall` recommendation.
- E5.3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.3` (Adopt hints and fixes): the `adopt` recommendation and the adopt-based fixes are the last changes to `status` hints and `not_managed` fixes; auditing before them would audit superseded hints. This edge replaces the plan's whole-E5 edge.
- F2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.2` (The export command): `export` rows, `--write` refusals and determinism.
- F3.2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.2` (sync --locked): `sync --locked` rows and the `not_locked` warning.
- F3.3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.3.3` (sync --prune): `sync --prune` rows and the `unknown_target_section` refusal. With F3.2, the last sync subtasks, so the sync surface is final.
- F4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.6.4` (The copy command): `copy` rows and its skip reasons.
- G1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7.1` (The search command): `search`/`find` rows and determinism.
- G2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.7.2` (auth github): `auth github` rows, its TTY `usage` text fix and `auth_rejected`.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** The contract is what lets an agent drive omaddons without reading code: one envelope, a registered exit per code, a fix with argv on every error, executable `commands`. M2 roughly doubles the command count, and ten tasks add codes, warnings and hints independently. A task can only test what exists when it lands. Some hints are written before the command they name (a task emits the nearest existing command until the later task upgrades it), so only an audit after the last hint-changing task (E5.3) can prove every hint runs. The audit also produces the authoritative list of new wire names that H6 records on the vision bead before the M4 freeze. Serves G-M2-7 and the "at most two commands per intent, every hint executable" design of the agent workflows.

**Decisions applied.**
- **DEC-4 and M2-D32:** contract additions are additive and recorded on the vision bead; `schema_version` stays `"1.0"` until the M4 freeze. The one deliberate type change is the dry-run plan's `expected_hash` (string to tagged object), allowed because plans are not stored until M4. Rejected: bumping the schema now, which would churn every consumer before the freeze.
- **Recommendations must run.** The plan's `status` design says each recommendation is added only by the task that ships its command, and that this audit asserts every one executes successfully. Rejected alternative: checking only argv shape, as the M1 harness does, which cannot catch a hint whose command refuses in that state.
- **A fresh home per recommendation**, so an earlier hint (a destructive `remove_orphans`, say) cannot change what a later one sees. Decided here: "fresh copy" means rebuilding the scenario from its builder, because the registry stores absolute `install_root` and `client_dir` paths (`src/state/registry.rs:34-40`) that a directory copy would not rewrite.
- **The plan's defaults for open questions, applied:** prefer an existing code with a precise message over a new code; additive keys only, with verbose material behind `-v`; deterministic order by target id, then addon name, then folder key; a hint never names a command that does not exist yet.

**Facts verified during planning** (commit `e902d36`): `ErrorCode::ALL.len() == 38` asserted at `src/error.rs:702` with an `EXPECTED` `(wire, exit, retryable)` table; `WarningCode::ALL.len() == 22` at `src/error.rs:746`; `TEXT_FIXES` at `tests/contract/main.rs:49` (12 prefixes); the harness accepts a null-argv fix that does not start with `omaddons`, so most M2 text fixes need no list entry; `repeated_runs_are_byte_identical` covers `list`, `status`, `history`, `info`, `remove`; `recommendations()` at `src/app/status.rs:353` emits `forget_target` (destructive), `inspect`, `list_unmanaged`.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *Snapshot churn* from ten tasks touching `tests/contract/snapshots/`: review each diff, and rebase before the gate.
- *Count mismatch* (39/34) means an unplanned or missing code. Trace it to its task and record it rather than adjusting the count to fit.
- *Scenario homes that need the network* would make the runner flaky: every scenario carries fixtures.
- Confidence: high. The harness exists and is proven by M1. The work is coverage, not new machinery.

title: Crash and concurrency coverage for M2 transactions
description:
## Background

M1's crash matrix proves the folder invariant: at every instant an AddOns folder is either the complete old version or the complete new version, and the next command that takes the lock finishes or rolls back an interrupted transaction. M2 adds transaction shapes that must hold the same guarantee and that M1 never ran:
- multi-addon updates;
- dependency installs that edit another record's `required_by`;
- mixed `sync` transactions;
- folder handover between two addons;
- records-only adopts, pins and forgets.

The harness today (line numbers are as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- `tests/engine_crash.rs`: `support::Op` has `Install`, `FirstInstall` (no `Interface/`), `Update` (drops folder `FooOld`) and `Remove`. `matrix(op)` loops over every name in `omaddons::engine::FAILPOINTS` (24 failpoints, `src/engine/tx.rs:56`, from `engine.plan.fetched` to `engine.recover.step`). Each run aborts the command with `<failpoint>=abort`: a real crash with no unwinding, after which the kernel releases the flocks. It then checks:
  - each folder is wholly old or wholly new;
  - `status` reports `journal_pending` exactly when a journal is pending, and writes nothing;
  - the next lock-taking command (an install of `Bar`) reports `journal_recovered`, leaves no journal and no stray AddOns entry;
  - all folders sit on one side, consistent with the record generation and the history kinds;
  - the lock file keeps its inode.
  It asserts at least 10 failpoints actually crash on the path.
- `tests/common/engine.rs`: `Scene` builds a retail client and installs fixture zips with `--file … --offline`. A `--file` release is recorded as `<ref>@sha256:<hex>` (`local_identity` in `src/engine/plan.rs`). The M2 update evaluator treats such records as `static`, so `update`-, dependency- and sync-based ops cannot use `--file` installs.
- `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`: a reader during a live swap, recovery only under the lock, two concurrent installs (same addon, different addons), and `every_commit_holds_the_lock_under_50_ms` (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs:220`). That test parses `lock_held_ms` from the `-v` log of 20 commits and asserts each is under 50 ms (M1 measured max 2 ms).

A4.4 adds `Op::Pin` and `Op::Forget` with the **record oracle**: records-only transactions never change a folder, so the folder oracle alone proves nothing for them. This task covers the remaining M2 shapes, after the features that produce them have landed. It serves G-M2-7 (no regression of M1 guarantees): every new mutation must be as crash-safe and recoverable as M1's.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, `tests/common/engine.rs` (scene support for HTTP-fixture releases and the new ops' baselines).

### 1. New ops and the beads that provide them

| Op | What it runs (one transaction on retail) | Provided by | Oracle |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Pin` | A4.4's engine-API child: `Edit(SetPinned(true))` under the `pin` kind override (records-only). Switch it to `pin <addon> -t retail` only if B7 (`omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.7`) is already on `main`; H2 does not wait for B7 | A4.4 (exists when H2 starts; keep it) | record |
| `Forget` | `remove` of an addon whose folders were deleted out-of-band (`Forget` edit, `record` history ops) | A4.4 (exists; keep it) | record |
| `UpdateMany` | `update -t retail` over three addons installed one release behind | B6 (the `update` command) | folder plus record consistency |
| `InstallWithDep` | `install` of a requester whose loaded TOC requires one dependency that is not installed (planned in a dependency round) and one that is already managed and explicit (gains the requester through a `required_by_add` edit) | C4.1 (rounds on install), with A4.2 (reversible `required_by` edit ops) | folder per folder plus record consistency |
| `SyncMixed` | one `sync --prune` transaction holding an install, a remove and a records-only edit (a pin-flag difference) | F3.3 (prune), on F3.1 (sync core) | folder per folder plus record consistency |
| `Handover` | one transaction in which addon A's new release drops folder `Old` and addon B's release ships `Old`: one `SwapOp::Replace` owned by B, plus a transfer with `handover: true` | A5 (working view and handover), driven through `update` (B6) or `sync` (F3.1) | folder plus "exactly one record owns `Old`" |
| `Adopt` | `adopt --apply -t retail` over unmanaged folders (records-only, no stage, no swap) | E5.2 (`adopt --apply`) | record |

Each op implements `kind()` (the expected history kind: `pin`, `remove`, `update`, `install`, `sync`, `update` or `sync`, `adopt`) and `prepare()` (baseline plus argv). `expected_new(op)` runs it once without a failpoint. Follow the existing pattern: the matrix runs every failpoint in `FAILPOINTS`, and the next command that takes the lock (an install of `Bar` through `--file`) recovers.

**Fixtures.** Ops that update, resolve dependencies or sync need real release metadata. Use A10's helpers through `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`:
- `gh_release_v`, `gh_latest` and `Home::installed_behind(base, (old_tag, old_assets), (new_tag, new_assets), targets)` for "one release behind";
- `release_graph` for archives whose TOCs carry `## Dependencies` (the requester and its dependencies);
- `home.scenario(...)` to switch fixture sets between the baseline command and the crashed command (replay sequences restart in every CLI process);
- a test catalog override that maps the dependency folder to its ref, as C4.1's checkpoint test does.

The crashed command runs offline-deterministically from fixtures. Extend the stray-entry allowlist in `matrix` (today `Foo`, `FooOld`, `Bar`) with each op's folder names.

### 2. Oracles

- **Folder oracle (M1).** Each folder is wholly old or wholly new by tree hash at every instant. After recovery, all folders sit on one side, consistent with the generation and history, and the lock inode is unchanged.
- **Record oracle (A4.4) for `Pin`, `Forget`, `Adopt`.** After an abort at failpoint F and the recovery command:
  - the target record contains the transaction's edits **if and only if** `history.jsonl` contains the transaction;
  - the generation equals the old value plus that (plus one for the recovery install);
  - every AddOns folder is byte-identical to before, because records-only transactions never touch folders.
  - `Adopt` additionally: the files index has the adopted folders' entries if and only if the transaction committed.
- **Mixed transactions** (`InstallWithDep`, `SyncMixed`, `Handover`, and `UpdateMany`, which changes several records): the folder oracle per folder, **and** record consistency:
  - records reference only folders that exist;
  - `required_by` edits are present if and only if the transaction committed (for `InstallWithDep`: the existing dependency's record lists the requester exactly when the history has the transaction);
  - after a handover, exactly one record owns the folder, and no record is marked `degraded` (a handover is not a `--force` takeover);
  - one consistent side: "went new" is judged from folders and records together; a mix of new folders and old records is a failure.

### 3. Concurrency scenarios (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs`)

Cross-process, as the M1 races are. Order the two processes with a `sleep:` failpoint at `engine.plan.done`, as A3's and E5.2's concurrency tests do.
- **`update` against `install` of a different addon on the same target:** both commit, with no `locked`. Both history lines exist, and each record is consistent.
- **`adopt --apply` against an `install` touching an adopted folder:** one of them gets a clean `plan_stale` (retryable) or `ownership_conflict`, and nothing is half-applied. No record may point at a folder whose files the other transaction replaced without that record changing, and no folder may be owned by two records.
- **Two `outdated` processes writing the memo** (`<cache>/omaddons/releases.json`): afterwards the file parses as a valid memo (schema `1.0`). Completeness is not asserted, because the memo is a merge-on-write cache where a lost entry costs one request.

### 4. Lock hold

Extend `every_commit_holds_the_lock_under_50_ms` (or add a sibling) so the measured commits include multi-addon transactions: an `UpdateMany`-style update of three addons, an install with a dependency, and a mixed sync. Every commit must stay under 50 ms. The commit window holds only revalidate, journal, snapshots, swap and record writes; downloads, inspection and staging stay outside the lock.

### 5. Runtime

Each new op's matrix should add less than 5 s to the suite. Keep the archives tiny (a few small files per folder), reuse the `Scene` per failpoint pattern, and avoid network-shaped waits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/engine_crash.rs` has `UpdateMany`, `InstallWithDep`, `SyncMixed`, `Handover` and `Adopt` ops beside A4.4's `Pin` and `Forget`, each new op driven through the real CLI with `=abort` at every failpoint in `FAILPOINTS`.
- Every new op crashes at 10 or more failpoints, and its oracle holds at each one: the folder oracle for folder-touching ops, the record oracle for records-only ops, and folder-per-folder plus record consistency for mixed transactions.
- After a crashed handover and recovery, exactly one record owns the handed-over folder, and none is `degraded`.
- After a crashed dependency install and recovery, the existing dependency's `required_by` lists the requester if and only if the transaction is in history.
- The three concurrency scenarios pass: `update` against `install` both commit; `adopt --apply` against `install` ends with a clean `plan_stale` or `ownership_conflict` and nothing half-applied; two `outdated` writers leave a valid memo.
- The lock-hold test still shows every commit under 50 ms, now including multi-addon transactions.
- M1's crash, concurrency and undo suites pass unchanged.
- Each new op's matrix adds less than 5 s to the suite.

## Test Plan

- `cargo test --test engine_crash` and `cargo test --test engine_concurrency`, cross-process with `=abort`. Print per op "crashed at N of 24 failpoints" with the list, as M1 does, and paste the lines into the close reason.
- `cargo test --test engine_undo` and `--test undo_history` as the regression net.
- `argc gate`.

## Considerations

- **Fixtures, not `--file`, for the M2 ops.** `--file` releases are `static` to the update evaluator and carry `version_confidence: toc`, so they cannot drive `update` or dependency rounds. The recovery command can stay a `--file` install of `Bar`.
- **Handover in both argument orders** is A5's acceptance test. The crash matrix needs one order. Choose the order where the claiming addon is planned first, which is the harder case.
- **The `sleep:` failpoint** only orders processes. It is not a crash; keep `=abort` for the matrix.
- **`tests/engine_crash.rs` is shared with A4.4.** Generalise its harness (an oracle per op) only if A4.4 has not already done so; reuse what it built.
- **Records-only ops never change the folder trees.** A "wholly old or wholly new" folder assertion passes trivially for them, so the record oracle is the real check. Never weaken it to make an op pass.
- **Engine bugs found here** (a half-applied state, a wrong recovery) are filed with `--deps discovered-from:omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` against the engine area and fixed before this closes. Do not relax an oracle to make a case pass.
- Collision hot spots: `src/engine/plan.rs` and `src/engine/undo.rs` change only if a defect is found.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A4.4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.4.4` (Records-only crash matrix with the record oracle, and records-only concurrency): provides `Op::Pin`, `Op::Forget` and the record oracle that `Adopt` reuses.
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): `UpdateMany` and the `update`-against-`install` race run through `update`.

The edge points at C4.2, the last dependency-planning subtask (C4.1's rounds and A4.2's edit ops come before it), so the dependency transaction shape is final when the matrix is written.

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** The project's thesis is that omaddons is the sole, safe, undoable authority over every client's addons. "Safe" rests on the crash invariant: an interrupted run never leaves a half-installed addon, and the next run finishes or rolls back. M1 proved it for single-addon installs, updates and removes. M2 routinely puts several addons, other records' edits and records-only work into one transaction. If any of those shapes can be split by a crash, `update --all` across three clients becomes the dangerous operation the owner stopped trusting in other managers. This bead proves the invariant for every new shape before the checkpoint claims it.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D6:** records-only work, a per-target working view and folder handover are first-class engine features, so one crash matrix covers adopt, pin, dependency bookkeeping, sync and M4's future repair. Rejected: ad-hoc state writes per feature, which would each need their own (and usually missing) crash story.
- **M2-D35:** `required_by` edits are history ops with an `edit` field, reversed in place and ignored by conflict detection. That is why `InstallWithDep` checks "edit present iff committed" on the other record, not a snapshot comparison. Rejected: snapshot restore for every records-only change, which rolls a dependency's record back under new folders.
- **Handover merged into one `Replace` plus a transfer** (A5): a separate remove and add cannot work, because `swap()` runs adds before removes and undo refuses a `remove` whose folder is live. The crash case checks the merged form leaves exactly one owner. The third review pass of the plan made handover independent of argument order (releases are judged before any claim). The matrix uses the claimant-first order, the case that fix addressed.
- **A record oracle for records-only ops** (A4.4): the folder oracle cannot see a records-only transaction at all, because no folder changes.

**Facts verified during planning** (commit `e902d36`): `FAILPOINTS` has 24 names (`src/engine/tx.rs:56`); the matrix asserts at least 10 crash on the path; `Scene` installs `--file` zips offline (`tests/common/engine.rs`), whose release ids are `<ref>@sha256:<hex>` (`local_identity` in `src/engine/plan.rs`), and which the M2 evaluator treats as `static`, hence HTTP fixtures for the new ops; `every_commit_holds_the_lock_under_50_ms` measured M1 commits at min 1, median 1, max 2 ms.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *Suite runtime* grows with every op × 24 failpoints. Tiny archives and a budget of under 5 s per op keep the gate usable.
- *Flaky races*: order processes with the `sleep:` failpoint at `engine.plan.done`, never with timing guesses.
- *Temptation to weaken an oracle* when an op fails: forbidden. A failure here is an engine defect, filed with `discovered-from` and fixed.
- Confidence for this area (the engine changes A4, A5, C4, A12): medium-high. The changes touch the most delicate code. The mitigations are exactly this suite, M1's regression suites, and the multi-target tests that land before any feature depends on them.

title: Performance budgets and bench recipes
description:
## Background

The M2 checkpoint has four timing targets and several request-economy targets. Timing must be repeatable, so it is measured against fixture-backed homes with local replay, plus one live run that is recorded but not asserted. Economy is cheaper to prove than timing: it is a count of `net.log` lines, so it belongs in the normal gate, where every commit keeps it true.

The timing targets, as the checkpoint states them:
- **Checkpoint item 1, update speed and economy.** `update --all` across about 30 managed addons on three targets takes under 2 s warm and under 10 s cold (hyperfine, release build, fixture-backed for repeatability, plus one live run). `net.log` shows each distinct ref fetched once and each distinct asset downloaded once per run. A single `omaddons undo` then reverts every client's transaction from that run.
- **Checkpoint item 5, drift.** A check over 5,000 managed files takes under 30 ms warm (release build). A touched-but-identical file produces no finding. Modified, deleted and added files are named. `install <addon> --reinstall` repairs drift from the blob cache with no network.
- **Checkpoint item 9, status.** `status --cached` runs in under 5 ms, with update counts populated from the memo, and makes no network I/O.

This task measures the timing parts. The functional parts (undo of the run, `--reinstall` repair, drift findings) are the feature tasks' tests, which H7 cites.

What exists today (line numbers are as of commit `e902d36`, current `main`; the symbol names are what matter):
- `Argcfile.sh` has `gate`, `fmt`, `lint`, `test`, `fuzz` and `fuzz-all`, and no `bench` command. There is no `tests/perf.rs`.
- M1 measured `status --cached` at 1.3 ms with hyperfine (re-measured 2026-10-15) and the longest lock hold per commit at 2 ms. A stat walk of a 2,529-file real client takes about 3 ms.
- **Release builds ignore the test hooks.** `select_transport` honours `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` only when `cfg!(debug_assertions)` (`src/net/mod.rs:276-292`), per DEC-7 (test-only hooks work in debug builds only). A plain `--release` binary therefore cannot replay fixtures.
- Several feature tasks write budget tests, ignored in debug: B8 (`status --cached` under 5 ms), E2 (drift Stat over 5,000 files under 30 ms with at most 1% re-hashed) and D2 (WoWI slim-index load and parse under 40 ms).

Without this task the checkpoint's timing claims would be anecdotes, and the economy claims could regress silently between checkpoints. The M3 widget's polite background checks rely on them. Serves G-M2-1 (current by default with the minimum number of requests: one fetch per distinct ref per run, one download per distinct archive per run, a free re-check inside `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 minutes), and no GitHub REST for `release.json` publishers) and G-M2-4 (drift is visible cheaply).

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `Argcfile.sh` (new `bench` command), `tests/perf.rs` (B8 creates it with its `status --cached` budget; this task extends it), `Cargo.toml` (one bench profile, see below), optionally `scripts/bench.sh` if the recipe outgrows the Argcfile.

### 1. `tests/perf.rs`: budgets (ignored) and the bench-home generator

Budget tests, `#[ignore]` in every build and run at the checkpoint with `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored`:
- **`status --cached` under 5 ms**, B8's test: 100 records and a 200-entry memo of **realistically sized sets**. The sets are copied from recorded DBM, BigWigs and WeakAuras fixtures. DBM's per-interface `release.json` metadata is about 3 KB once trimmed to one release, so 100 refs is about 300 KB. Seed with B1's `Home::seed_memo`.
- **A 5,000-file drift check under 30 ms warm, with `files_rehashed` at most 1%.** Build the tree by installing through the engine, 5,000 files across 20 folders, so mtimes and `recorded_at_ns` are real. Then run Stat immediately afterwards.
- **WoWI index load and parse under 40 ms** (the slim index is about 1.5 MB).

Decided: `tests/perf.rs` is the single place for budgets. If B8, E2 or D2 left their budget test in their own test file, move it here unchanged, so one command runs every budget and nothing timing-based remains anywhere else.

**Budget tests must not depend on HTTP fixtures**, because `--release` disables them. Install through `--file` archives (local, no network) and seed the memo directly.

**The bench-home generator** is a committed `#[ignore]` test in `tests/perf.rs`. It builds the benchmark home at a directory given by an environment variable that only the test reads (never the binary, so DEC-7's hook list does not grow):
- three synthetic targets (for example retail, era and classic, from `BattlenetRoot`);
- about 30 managed addons across them, sharing some refs across targets so fetch-once and download-once are visible;
- 5,000 managed files in total;
- every addon installed one release behind (A10's `installed_behind`, `gh_release_v`, `gh_latest`), with a fixture scenario serving the newer releases.

It then deletes `<cache>/omaddons/` (always safe to delete) so the pristine home starts cold, with no memo and no blobs.

### 2. `argc bench`

A new Argcfile command (`# @cmd`, `# @meta require-tools hyperfine`):
1. Build the release binary. Also build an optimised binary that honours fixtures (see below).
2. Generate the bench home through the generator test, at a fixed working path W. Then snapshot it with `cp -a W W.pristine`. Restoring `W` from the snapshot at the **same path** keeps the registry's absolute `install_root` and `client_dir` paths valid. A copy to another path would still point at the original clients.
3. Run hyperfine and print the medians:
   - `status --cached` (release binary; no network by design);
   - `outdated` cold (`--prepare` restores W) and warm (after one run, inside the 15-minute window);
   - `update --all --dry-run` warm. Use one `--warmup` run with the fixture-honouring binary so the memo is fresh and blobs and candidate facts are cached; the timed release-binary runs then make zero requests;
   - `update --all` cold, with a fresh home per run (`--prepare` restores W from `W.pristine`), using the fixture-honouring binary;
   - `status` (drift Stat over the 5,000 managed files).
4. Check that the warm runs added **no** `net.log` lines (compare the line count before and after), and print that alongside the medians.

**Decided: an optimised binary that replays fixtures.** Release builds ignore `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` (`src/net/mod.rs:292`), and the cold runs need fixtures for repeatability. Add one Cargo profile that inherits `release` and turns `debug-assertions` on (for example `[profile.bench-fixtures]`, `inherits = "release"`, `debug-assertions = true`). Build it only for `argc bench`'s fixture-backed runs. `debug_assert!`s make it slightly slower, which errs on the safe side for a budget. Warm runs, `status --cached` and drift need no network and use the true release binary. Record which binary each median came from. The profile adds no crate; run `argc gate` (Cargo.toml changed).

**One live run (recorded, not asserted).** On a throwaway HOME with three synthetic clients, as `tests/live_probes.rs` builds them, and never on the owner's real clients (H5's rules):
- install catalog addons with the release binary until about 30 records exist across the three targets (the same addon on several targets counts once per target, and shares its fetch and download);
- time `outdated` cold (memo removed) and warm, and `update --all --dry-run` warm, with `hyperfine --runs 3`;
- paste the medians into the close reason with the date.

Keep live runs to that minimum: warm runs make no requests, and cold runs reach upstream services.

### 3. Request-economy assertions (normal gate, not timing)

These assertions are the cheapest proof of the performance claims. They read `net.log` through A10's `net_log(home)` counters (by host and purpose: `count(host, purpose)`). The purposes are `release-latest`, `release-json` and `asset`.
- **Cold check:** `outdated` on N distinct refs across T targets logs at most N `release-latest` lines.
- **Warm re-run** inside the window logs zero lines.
- **After the window,** unchanged tags log exactly N `release-latest` lines and no `release-json` fetches. A changed tag adds one `release-json` fetch: two lines, counting the redirect hop to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`.
- **`update` across targets** sharing an asset logs one `asset` fetch per distinct asset.
- **`sync` re-run** logs zero lines.
- **Any `release.json` publisher** on stable logs zero `api.github.com` lines.

Most of these already exist in the feature tasks' E2E tests (B2, B5, B6, A8, F3.1). Audit the set. Add each missing assertion to `tests/perf.rs` **without** `#[ignore]`, so the normal gate runs it. List in the close reason where each of the six lives. The `sync` re-run assertion is F3.1's own acceptance test; F3.1 is not upstream of this task, so if it has not landed, H7 verifies that assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `argc bench` runs end to end on the development machine and prints the medians for `status --cached`, `outdated` warm and cold, `update --all --dry-run` warm, `update --all` cold and `status` (drift), naming the binary used for each.
- The recorded medians meet the targets: `update --all` under 2 s warm and under 10 s cold; drift over 5,000 files under 30 ms warm; `status --cached` under 5 ms. A miss is a bug bead (`discovered-from`), not a silent pass.
- The warm runs add no `net.log` lines.
- The budget tests pass with `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored`: `status --cached` under 5 ms with realistically sized memo sets; 5,000-file drift under 30 ms with at most 1% re-hashed; WoWI index parse under 40 ms.
- The six request-economy assertions run in the normal gate (not `#[ignore]`), and the close reason says where each lives. The `sync` re-run assertion is F3.1's; if F3.1 has not landed when this task closes, the close reason says so and H7 verifies it.
- No timing assertion runs in the per-commit gate.
- One live run's medians are recorded in the close reason with the date.

## Test Plan

- `argc bench` on the development machine. Paste the hyperfine medians into the close reason.
- `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored` (budgets) and `argc gate` (economy tests, debug).
- The live run on a throwaway HOME, recorded.

## Considerations

- **Hardware varies.** Vision D16 keeps benchmarks at checkpoints, so budgets are `#[ignore]` and the gate asserts counts, never times.
- **D2 is a blocker of this task** (an edge added during bead creation; the plan had missed it). The WoWI index parse budget needs D2's slim index, so H3 cannot assert all three budgets before D2 closes.
- **If a budget is at risk,** measure before optimising. The designed fallback for `status --cached` is a per-entry `brief` in the memo, precomputed at write time (newest `release_id`, version, date, and candidate rank per family), which the evaluator uses without re-running `select`. Derived data goes in `<cache>/omaddons/` with a schema version and tolerant reads.
- **`--prepare` must restore the same path** (registry paths are absolute). Never point hyperfine at a home copied to another directory.
- **The bench home is synthetic.** It never touches the owner's clients.
- **The memo window is wall-clock** (15 minutes). Run warm measurements right after their warmup, or reseed `fetched_at`.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- A8 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.8` (Deferred asset locations and per-command download de-duplication): "each distinct asset downloaded once per run" exists only with its per-command download memo.
- B2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.2` (GitHub tag-first probe and conditional feeds): the after-window economy (one `release-latest` per unchanged ref, no `release-json`) is its probe.
- B3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.3` (Candidate facts: verdicts and blob hashes in the memo): warm `update` skips downloads only through candidate facts.
- B5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.5` (The outdated command): benchmarked warm and cold; cold and warm economy assertions.
- B6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.6` (The update command): the `update --all` timing target and the asset-once assertion.
- B8 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.2.8` (status update counts, adoptable count, hints and the list latest column): `status --cached` with update counts from the memo, and its budget test.
- D2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.4.2` (The WoWInterface index): the slim index whose load and parse must stay under 40 ms in a release build; its budget test moves into `tests/perf.rs`.
- E2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.2` (The drift detector): the drift budget test over 5,000 files.
- E3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.3` (Drift in status, list and info): plain `status` runs the Stat drift check that `argc bench` times.

Unblocks:
- H7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7` (M2 checkpoint verification): the medians and budgets are the evidence for checkpoint items 1, 5 and 9, and the economy assertions for items 1 and 2.

close_reason: argc bench end to end (status --cached 1.6 ms, drift 7.3 ms, update --all warm 0.3 s / cold 3.5 s, zero warm requests); budgets in tests/perf.rs pass in release; six economy assertions located (one added); live run recorded 2026-10-16; gate green

comments.author: GildedLedger
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** M2's daily-use promise is that `update` and `outdated` are fast and nearly free: a warm `outdated` makes zero requests, and a cold one costs one request per ref. That is what makes the M3 widget's background checks polite enough to run every few hours, and it keeps the project a good citizen toward volunteer-run services. `status --cached` under 5 ms is what lets the widget paint an update badge without touching the network. These are claims about speed and request counts, so they need measurement (checkpoint timing) and enforcement (economy assertions in every gate). Serves G-M2-1 and G-M2-4.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D1:** update-check results live in a release memo in the cache dir, and `status --cached` derives counts from it with the pure evaluator. Rejected: an `outdated.json` result file in state, which needs a mutating writer for a read command and goes stale the moment `update` commits. The `status --cached` budget measures exactly this design, with realistically sized memo sets.
- **M2-D2:** tag-first GitHub probe. A stale entry costs one `releases/latest` request, and `release.json` is fetched only when the tag changed. Rejected: always re-fetching `release.json`, and the Atom feed, which cannot tell prereleases apart. Asserted by the after-window economy check.
- **M2-D28:** per-command download de-duplication plus blob facts in the memo. Each distinct archive downloads once per command, and not at all when already cached. Rejected: re-downloading per target, as M1 does. Asserted by the asset-once check and by "warm runs add no `net.log` lines".
- **M2-D16:** a per-folder `recorded_at_ns` taken after the folder's files are synced, with filesystem-aware racy slack (20 ms on nanosecond filesystems, 2 s on coarse ones), so a fresh install is not re-hashed on every `status`. Rejected: the index-wide `written_at_ns`. The drift budget's "at most 1% re-hashed right after an install" is the check against a re-hash storm, a problem found in the plan's second review pass.
- **Vision D16:** timing stays out of the per-commit gate; budgets and hyperfine run at checkpoints.
- **Decided here (not in the plan):** an optimised Cargo profile with `debug-assertions = true` for the fixture-backed cold runs. Release builds ignore `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` (DEC-7, `src/net/mod.rs:276-292`), so "release build, fixture-backed" is otherwise impossible. Rejected: timing cold runs only live (not repeatable, and it loads upstream services), or widening DEC-7 to release builds (it would put test hooks in shipped binaries).
- **Decided here:** `tests/perf.rs` collects every budget test (B8, E2, D2), so one command runs them all.

**Facts verified during planning:** M1's hyperfine `status --cached` is 1.3 ms (2026-10-15), M1's lock hold max is 2 ms, and a 2,529-file real client stat walk takes about 3 ms. A DBM-sized memo set is about 3 KB once trimmed to one release (100 refs is about 300 KB). There is no `bench` command in `Argcfile.sh` and no `tests/perf.rs` at `e902d36`. The registry stores absolute client paths, so hyperfine's `--prepare` must restore the bench home at the same path.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *`status --cached` budget creep* (memo read plus evaluator): realistic set sizes in the test. The designed fallback is a precomputed per-entry `brief` in the memo.
- *Drift false positives or re-hash storms:* filesystem-aware slack, `recorded_at_ns` taken after sync, and undo writing fresh index entries. The 1% bound catches regressions.
- *Machine variance:* medians are recorded with the binary and date; misses become bug beads rather than adjusted targets.
- Confidence: medium for the exact timings on the owner's hardware, which look achievable from M1's numbers but are confirmed only at the checkpoint. High for the economy claims, which are counted, not timed.
