title: M2 checkpoint verification
description:
## Background

M1 closed with a checkpoint bead (`omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.7.10`) whose close reason held the evidence for every criterion: test names, timings, `net.log` counts, live-probe and real-machine output, and fuzz runs, with home paths replaced by `<home>`. "Done" was a recorded fact rather than an impression. A comment on the vision bead then ticked M1 in its §10 "Milestone status" and listed the deviations (comment 341). M2 closes the same way, and this is that bead.

The twelve criteria below amend the vision's §7 M2 checkpoint list. Item 3 replaces BugSack → !BugGrabber with LittleWigs → BigWigs (M2-D10). The others extend the list with the economy, MD5, WoWInterface, changelog, search and probe criteria M2 adds. H6 records the amendments on the vision bead.

Everything here is verification and recording. The work that produces the evidence lives in H1 to H6 and in the feature beads. This task runs the checkpoint, collects the evidence, fixes nothing silently, and closes the milestone. It serves all seven M2 goals by proving each one.

Line numbers, where cited, are as of commit `e902d36` (current `main`); the symbol names are what matter.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `README.md` (the Status section only); the vision bead (one comment); no code unless a criterion fails (then a bug bead does the change).

### 1. The twelve M2 checkpoint criteria

Run each one and paste its evidence into the close reason as `[x] <criterion>: <evidence>`.

1. **Update speed and economy.** `update --all` across about 30 managed addons on three targets takes under 2 s warm and under 10 s cold (hyperfine, release build, fixture-backed for repeatability, plus one live run). `net.log` shows each distinct ref fetched once and each distinct asset downloaded once per run. A single `omaddons undo` then reverts every client's transaction from that run.
2. **Zero-REST checks.** A full `outdated` across every `release.json` publisher in the catalog makes zero `api.github.com` requests. A second `outdated` inside 15 minutes makes zero requests of any kind. After the window, an unchanged release costs exactly one `github.com` request per ref. Exhausting REST on beta-channel or non-`release.json` repos returns `rate_limited` with `details.reset_at`.
3. **Dependencies** *(amended: LittleWigs replaces BugSack, M2-D10)*. Installing LittleWigs also installs BigWigs in the same transaction, with BigWigs recorded as `reason: dependency, required_by: ["LittleWigs"]`. Undoing that transaction removes both. `OptionalDeps` never auto-install: BugSack does not pull `!BugGrabber`. `Blizzard_*` dependencies count as satisfied. Removing BigWigs warns `still_required`, and removing LittleWigs reports BigWigs as `orphaned_dependency`.
4. **Adoption fixtures.** Current installs come out `exact`. One-version-behind installs come out `identified` and are replaced by the next `update`. A `guess` is never applied without an explicit folder argument. A `UIDir`-only match with a mismatched Title and Author is never `identified`. No fixture is adopted under the wrong source. Undo of an adopt removes the records and leaves every folder byte-identical.
5. **Drift.** A check over 5,000 managed files takes under 30 ms warm (release build). A touched-but-identical file produces no finding. Modified, deleted and added files are named. `install <addon> --reinstall` repairs drift from the blob cache with no network.
6. **Desired state.** `export` followed by `sync --locked` into an empty target reproduces refs and versions. Re-running `sync` is a no-op with zero network requests. `--prune` removes only unlisted managed addons. Family sections never touch `test` targets.
7. **Tukui.** ElvUI installs from Tukui into retail and Classic targets (and every other family its TOC declares). The download's MD5 is checked against the response `ETag`.
8. **WoWInterface.** A `wowi:` ref and a pasted WoWInterface link both install with MD5 verification. A tampered fixture fails with `hash_mismatch`.
9. **Status.** `status --cached` runs in under 5 ms with update counts populated from the memo, and makes no network I/O.
10. **Changelogs.** `info <gh addon> --changelog` shows release notes from the Atom feed with zero `api.github.com` requests.
11. **Search.** `search` returns ranked hits from the catalog, the WoWI index, Tukui and GitHub, with per-target compatibility hints. `--offline` works from cached indices.
12. **Gate and probes.** `argc gate --all` passes. Every new fuzz target runs 10 minutes without a crash. Live probes pass, including the catalog × declared-flavor matrix extended to Tukui entries. The real-machine suite passes and leaves every AddOns folder as it found it, including the untouched Forever stress-test set. README.md describes exactly what exists.

### 2. Where each criterion's evidence comes from

| # | Evidence to paste |
|---|---|
| 1 | H3's `argc bench` medians (warm `update --all --dry-run`, cold `update --all`, with the binary used) and its live-run medians; the `net.log` excerpt with counts from B6's and A8's economy tests (refs once, assets once); the test name of the run-level undo (A12 and B6: one bare `undo` reverts every target's transaction of the run) |
| 2 | H4's three-way `outdated` probe output (first run zero `api.github.com`, second run zero requests, aged memo one `github.com` `release-latest` per unchanged ref); B2's REST-exhaustion test (`rate_limited` with `details.reset_at`) |
| 3 | C4.1's checkpoint test (LittleWigs plus BigWigs in one transaction, recorded fields, undo removes both); C4.1's `OptionalDeps` test, plus an `install bugsack --dry-run` (fixtures or live) whose items contain no `!BugGrabber`; C3's `Blizzard_*` satisfied case; C6's `still_required` and `orphaned_dependency` tests; H5's live `install littlewigs -t retail` on the real retail client |
| 4 | E4.2's identification table and E5.2's adoption tests by name (exact, identified then updated, guess not applied, `UIDir`-only mismatch is a guess, no wrong-source adoption, undo leaves folders byte-identical) |
| 5 | H3's drift budget (time and `files_rehashed`) and hyperfine `status` median; E2's tests (touched-identical, modified, deleted, added); B9's and E3's `--reinstall` from the blob cache with zero `net.log` lines |
| 6 | F3.2's export-then-`sync --locked` test; F3.1's zero-`net.log` no-op re-run (also straight after a channel-only change); F3.3's prune tests; F3.1's family-sections-never-touch-test-targets test |
| 7 | D4's fixture installs on `-t retail`, `-t classic` and `-t era`; H4's live Tukui probe (`ETag` equals MD5, three folders with single TOCs); the ElvUI row of the catalog matrix |
| 8 | D3's tests (`wowi:5995`, the pasted `info5995-BugSack.html` link, tampered body gives `hash_mismatch`); H4's live `filedetails` and MD5 probe |
| 9 | H3's `status --cached` budget and hyperfine median; B8's test that `status --cached` leaves `net.log` byte-identical |
| 10 | D6's `info weakauras --changelog` test with zero `api.github.com`; H4's live Atom probe |
| 11 | G1's tests (ranking, compatibility hints, `--offline` with `sources_skipped`); H4's live search probe |
| 12 | `argc gate --all` output; the fuzz runs (below); H4's full live-probe output **with the catalog matrix pasted in** (vision comment 370 rule); H5's real-machine output; H1's and H2's results; the README check |

Also record, as M1 did (vision §5.12's checkpoint-only checks): the lock hold over the H2 multi-addon commits (min, median, max), and the coverage summary from `cargo llvm-cov --summary-only` (no threshold).

### 3. Gate and fuzz

- `argc gate --all`: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, the full test suite, `ubs` on changed files, and `cargo deny` even when dependency files did not change. Paste the summary (tests passed and ignored, cargo deny results).
- `argc fuzz-all --time 600`: it runs every target in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` for 600 s each, which covers the 9 M1 targets (`archive, bottles, bpsv, heroic, lutris, product_db, ref_parse, steam_vdf, toc`) and the 7 M2 targets (`wowi_filelist, wowi_details, tukui_addons, html_text, bbcode_text, desired_toml, atom_feed`). That is about 2 h 40 min.
  - The default `nightly` must be at least the crate's `rust-version` (1.97); otherwise pass `--toolchain nightly-<date>`, as M1 did with `nightly-2026-08-31`.
  - `fuzz/artifacts/` must be empty afterwards. Paste runs per target.
  - `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs` `TARGETS` must list all 16.
  - A crash becomes a regression unit test in the owning parser, then a fix, then a re-run.

### 4. Recording

- **README.md Status:** say M2 is done, with the date (H6 prepared the rest of the README). Commit it with `.beads/`.
- **Vision comment ticking M2,** in the style of comment 341: "**§10 Milestone status: M2 — Updates, dependencies, adoption, desired state is done (<date>).** [x] M2." Then a short evidence summary per criterion, and "Deviations from the body:" listing every deviation (each must also have its own justification on the vision bead). Never edit the vision body.
- **Close reason:** every criterion as `[x] …` with its evidence, the checkpoint-only checks, the commit hash, and the bugs the checkpoint found and fixed (with bead ids).
- **Close the milestone:** run `br epic close-eligible`. Split epics (A4, C4, E4, E5, F3) close first, then the area epics A to H, then the milestone. Run it again until it closes nothing more, then confirm with `br show omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp` that the milestone epic is closed. Then `br sync --flush-only`, commit `.beads/` and README together, and push.

### 5. When a criterion fails

File a bug bead with `--deps discovered-from:omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.7`, fix it (or let its owner fix it), and re-run that criterion. Never close with a known gap unless the deviation is recorded and justified in a vision comment, as M1 did for WeakAuras on retail (its release published no mainline build, so the guard refusing it was correct behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every one of the twelve criteria has evidence in the close reason, marked `[x]`, with test names, medians, `net.log` counts or command output (home paths as `<home>`).
- `argc gate --all` passes at the closing commit.
- `argc fuzz-all --time 600` ran all 16 targets with no crash, and `fuzz/artifacts/` is empty.
- The catalog × declared-flavor matrix, with `tukui:` entries, is pasted into the close reason.
- The real-machine output shows every AddOns folder and `WTF/` unchanged and the Forever stress-test set untouched.
- README's Status says M2 is done, and README describes exactly what exists.
- The vision bead has the "[x] M2" comment with deviations.
- `br epic close-eligible` has closed the split epics, the area epics and the milestone epic.
- Every failed or deferred item has a bead filed with `discovered-from`.

## Test Plan

The checkpoint itself: H3's bench and budgets, H4's live probes, H5's real-machine suite, H1's and H2's suites inside `argc gate --all`, fuzz-all, coverage. Each is run on the development machine, with its output logged in full and summarised in the close reason.

## Considerations

- **Forever.** Check `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6`. While it is open or deferred, the `forever` client stays read-only, and the Forever stress-test set (transaction `01M50WBAPCN7YWGFFK8EB48RN8`, 12 managed folders across 5 addons) must be untouched by the checkpoint. If `.6` has closed, record its outcome in the M2 comment. `omad-wez` (re-verify Forever after the 2026-11-04 launch) stays deferred and is not part of M2.
- **Upstream changes since the fixtures** (new releases, changed catalog data) are expected. Live criteria assert behaviour, not versions.
- **Timing on the owner's hardware** is what counts. If a target is missed, measure first. The designed fallbacks (the precomputed memo `brief`, caching derived data in `<cache>/omaddons/`) go through a bug bead, not a quiet target change.
- **Public-safe evidence:** no hostnames, account, realm or character names, or home paths.
- **Do not start before H1 to H6, C2 and C7 are closed.** The criteria depend on all of them.

**Common rules for every M2 bead.**
- `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, fixtures, snapshots or embedded assets (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). After adding a crate, run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny). Run `ubs` on the changed files.
- Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). Commands never print: they return an `Outcome` rendered by `src/output/`. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`.
- New constants live in `src/politeness.rs` or `src/limits.rs` with a `REGISTRY` row.
- Every struct that reaches the wire, state files or plans derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, field order is wire order, and maps are `BTreeMap` (DEC-3). Each command adds its own clap subcommand and flags only together with their behaviour (DEC-1: no stubs). New commands join a help group (A1) and emit progress events (A9) when they need more than one network round trip.
- Every error carries a `fix`, plus `fix_argv` when the fix is a command. Text-only fixes are listed in `TEXT_FIXES` in `tests/contract/main.rs`.
- New wire names (codes, keys, kinds, enum spellings) and new or changed constants are listed in the close comment, so H6 can record them on the vision bead (DEC-4, D21, D22). New or changed snapshots are reviewed, not blindly accepted.
- Test-only hooks (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, `OMADDONS_RECORD`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`) work in debug builds only (DEC-7). Fixture builders live in `tests/common/` (DEC-8).
- Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. Treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. No script-based code edits. File work found along the way with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- C2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.2` (Catalog additions for M2: ElvUI, Tukui and BugSack): criterion 7 installs `elvui` through the catalog, and criterion 3 uses BugSack's catalog entry to show `!BugGrabber` is never pulled.
- C7 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.3.7` (Wire the WoWInterface and Tukui indexes into dependency resolution): completes the dependency resolution chain (catalog, then Tukui, then WoWInterface) that criterion 3 and G-M2-2 claim. No other H task waits for it, so the checkpoint does.
- H1 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1` (Contract conformance audit for M2): the contract evidence behind criterion 12 and G-M2-7.
- H2 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.2` (Crash and concurrency coverage for M2 transactions): the crash, concurrency and lock-hold evidence.
- H3 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.3` (Performance budgets and bench recipes): the timing and economy evidence for criteria 1, 2, 5 and 9.
- H4 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.4` (Live probes for M2): live evidence for criteria 2, 7, 8, 10, 11 and the catalog matrix for 12.
- H5 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.5` (Real-machine smoke tests for M2): the real-machine evidence for criterion 12.
- H6 `omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.6` (README, help text and vision-bead records for M2): README accuracy for criterion 12 and the vision records the "[x] M2" comment builds on.

Unblocks: none. Closing this bead, through `br epic close-eligible`, closes the milestone.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M2 plan, 2026-10-15).**

**Why this bead.** A milestone is done when its criteria have evidence, not when its beads are closed. M1 set the pattern: one checkpoint bead, every criterion re-run on the closing commit, the evidence in the close reason, a vision comment ticking the milestone and naming each deviation. That record is what lets the owner trust `update` across every client before WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04. It also lets M3 start from facts: the widget relies on `status --cached` being fast and network-free, and on `--progress json`. It proves the project's thesis for M2: every new mutation is a transaction, the tool is the sole authority over each client's addons, and it stays polite to the services it uses.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M2-D10 (a checkpoint amendment):** item 3 uses LittleWigs → BigWigs. BugSack v12.1.7 lists `!BugGrabber` under `OptionalDeps` (verified 2026-10-15), so the vision's checkpoint contradicted its own "OptionalDeps never auto-install" rule, and `!BugGrabber` has no official GitHub release. `LittleWigs.toc` declares `## Dependencies: BigWigs`. Rejected: auto-installing optional dependencies. The same decision adds "unless pinned, locked, or explicitly switched to another channel" to "`update` never downgrades".
- **Twelve criteria instead of the vision's eight:** four are new (WoWInterface, changelogs, search, and gate and probes), covering M2 scope the vision listed without a checkpoint. Several existing ones are extended: asset-once and run-level undo (1), the after-window cost (2), the shared undo, `still_required` and orphans (3), undo of an adopt (4), added files and `--reinstall` repair (5), the `ETag` MD5 and every declared family (7), and update counts from the memo (9). Each is checkable from `net.log`, envelopes or timing.
- **Vision comment 370:** every milestone checkpoint runs the catalog × declared-flavor probe and pastes its matrix here. M2 extends it to `tukui:` entries (H4).
- **Vision D16:** the gate is local; fuzz, budgets, benchmarks, live probes and the real-machine suite are checkpoint-only checks, all run here.
- **M1 precedent for deviations:** close with a known gap only when it is recorded and justified on the vision bead, as with WeakAuras on retail in M1.

**Facts verified during planning.** M1's close reason format at `omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.7.10`, and its vision comment 341 ("§10 Milestone status: M1 — Working slice is done"). `argc fuzz-all` iterates `fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs`, so the 7 new targets are picked up automatically; M1 ran it with `--toolchain nightly-2026-08-31`, because the default nightly must be at least `rust-version` 1.97. `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs` lists the 9 M1 targets in `TARGETS`. `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` is deferred to 2026-10-20, and the Forever stress-test set (transaction `01M50WBAPCN7YWGFFK8EB48RN8`, 12 folders, 5 addons) stays installed until it closes.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- *A timing target misses on the owner's hardware:* measure, file a bug, apply the designed fallback (the precomputed memo `brief`, derived caches in `<cache>/omaddons/`), re-run. Never quietly move the target.
- *A live criterion fails because upstream changed:* follow reality. Adjust the decoder, add a fixture and a probe assertion, and record the change with its date on the vision bead.
- *The Forever set is disturbed during the checkpoint:* H5's absolute rules, and this bead re-checks `forever`'s generation and hash in its evidence.
- *Closing the milestone with open children:* `br epic close-eligible` only closes epics whose children are all closed; re-run it until nothing more closes, then confirm the milestone's status.
- Confidence (from the plan): high for the update path, the economy claims, the WoWI and Tukui facts, drift and the desired-state format; medium-high for the engine changes and adoption; medium for search ranking quality and the exact timings, which are confirmed only here.

title: Epic: M3 — The Omarchy widget, Lua errors and WTF backups
description:
## Background

M3 is the third milestone of omaddons (vision bead `omad-vision-8qa`, §7 M3, as amended by the comments added after body revision 2, including the M2→M3 handoff comment). It was planned on 2026-10-21 against `main` at `af10e34` (clean tree, about 1,590 tests listed by `cargo test -- --list`), revised the same day after a third, external review of 23 proposed revisions, and decomposed into these beads the same day.

**M1 made omaddons correct and M2 made it useful from a terminal.** It finds every WoW client on the machine with no configuration, verifies every archive against the client's own TOC load rules before writing anything, and runs every change through a journaled, crash-safe, undoable transaction engine behind a strict machine-readable CLI. M2 added `outdated`/`update` with run-level undo, dependencies, WoWInterface and Tukui, adoption, drift, `addons.toml` with `export`/`sync`/`copy`, and `search`.

**What M1 and M2 leave unprotected and unseen:**
- Nothing on the desktop says that updates are waiting, that an addon is broken, or that a client is running. Every answer needs a terminal.
- "Why is my UI broken?" is the most common addon question, and the answer sits in BugGrabber's SavedVariables, which nothing reads outside the game. BugGrabber itself has no keyless release anywhere omaddons can fetch from.
- The things omaddons protects today are the things a manager can re-download. The things players actually lose, their settings in `WTF/`, are protected only by undo's per-transaction SavedVariables snapshots, which retention prunes after a week and which exist only around omaddons' own changes.
- `status` reports attention reasons as bare enums with no severity and says nothing about history, so a bar cannot decide how urgent it is or what "Undo last" would undo.

### What M3 delivers

M3 makes omaddons **visible, diagnosable and safe for the data players actually lose**:

1. **An Omarchy bar widget** (`omaddons omarchy install`). One gamepad icon in the bar shows how many updates are waiting, turns urgent when something is broken or an addon threw Lua errors in the last session, and opens a keyboard-driven panel with five views: Updates, Installed, Issues, Backups, Search.
   - Every button runs the omaddons CLI as an argv array with `--actor widget`, under the exact `HOME`/XDG context the widget was installed for. The widget holds no logic of its own and never writes a file.
   - Destructive buttons show a dry-run preview first, and the real run is bound to that preview by a precondition token: if anything changed in between, nothing happens and a fresh preview appears (M3-D46).
   - "My WeakAuras settings are gone" is two keys in the panel: restore one addon's settings from a chosen backup, previewed, undoable.
   - It reacts within about a second to changes made from a terminal or by an agent (a doorbell file), and to a game client starting or exiting (Hyprland window events). All its commands go through one small scheduler, so at most one change runs at a time and a stale answer never lands in the wrong view.
2. **`omaddons errors`.** It reads BugGrabber's SavedVariables read-only with a bounded, fuzzed Lua-literal parser. It handles every BugGrabber schema in the wild (modern 2026 integer times, 2023–2026 string times, the 3.3.5a r152 chunked format) and both SavedVariables file formats the client writes (modern no-indent CRLF, legacy tab-indented with `-- [n]` comments).
   - It names the addon that most likely caused each error, not the shared library that happened to dispatch it, says how it decided (and how sure it is), and groups by managed addon with "an update is available" next to each one.
   - **Strict privacy by default.** Default output holds only structured, code-derived text: the addon, the file and line, Lua's own message templates, counts and an opaque fingerprint. Custom error strings, locals and user-written code appear only with `--raw-details`, which says plainly that it promises no anonymity.
   - Errors that other players sent through BugSack are kept apart and never make this machine's bar urgent.
   - `errors dismiss` records the dismissal as durable user state, never in a cache.
   - `status` gains a per-client Lua error count, and the widget turns urgent on new errors.
3. **Keyless BugGrabber.** A small `wowace:` source fetches upstream tags from WowAce's public SVN (no account, no key), each pinned to one immutable repository revision, and refuses any project that needs a packaging step it does not implement. Then `omaddons install buggrabber` works on every modern client, and on 3.3.5a through the last 3.3.5-era revision (r152, GPL). Without it, `errors` would depend on a browser download.
4. **`omaddons backup`**: `create`, `list`, `verify`, `restore`, `prune`, `export`, `import`.
   - A backup is a reflinked copy of a client's whole `WTF/` under `<meta>/backups/<id>/`, plus a small record of which addon versions produced it. On btrfs the copy initially shares all file data with the live tree, so it takes milliseconds and almost no space until the game rewrites files.
   - Each backup states what it proves: whether the tree was observed stable during the copy, and whether its content was verified against hashes (`backup verify`) or only its metadata checked.
   - `backup restore` is an undoable transaction. A whole restore swaps `WTF/` with one atomic `RENAME_EXCHANGE`, and refuses on a filesystem that cannot do that. `--addon` restores only one addon's SavedVariables, the common case ("my WeakAuras/ElvUI settings are gone"), using the folders that addon owned when the backup was taken.
   - `backup export` streams a `.tar.zst` straight to its destination for off-disk safety, and `backup import` brings one back after an exact manifest check.
   - **Automatic backups** take a checkpoint before the day's first change that touches folders or SavedVariables, and another after each play session that changed settings. They skip when nothing changed, prune themselves by day, and stop before the disk runs low. **M3 flips `auto_backup`'s default from `off` to `daily`** (copy-on-write filesystems only). That is the one README promise M3 changes (M3-D30, owner-visible).
5. **Triage the widget and agents can share.** `status` gains a `summary` block; per-client `issues[]`, shaped like the M4 doctor's findings (stable `fm-…` ids, P0–P3 severities, an argv remediation); `errors` and `backups` blocks; `last_change`, with the exact `undo --run <run>` argv for "Undo last"; and a `widget` block. One `status --cached --json` call (≤ 5 ms median) answers everything the bar shows. It reads small derived projections, never whole backup trees or the whole history, and says "unknown" rather than guess when a projection is stale.
6. **Safer persisted formats.** Journal and history readers fail closed: a journal this binary cannot fully read is never pruned, and undo refuses when history it cannot read might hide a conflict (M3-D45). That also closes a latent M2 hazard, where an undecodable `prepared` line made recovery delete the journal and the transaction's snapshots.

None of this weakens an M1 or M2 guarantee. Every new mutation runs through fsx and the journal, every new request is allowlisted and logged, every new error carries an executable fix, and the JSON contract stays one envelope with `schema_version` "1.0".

### Why this is the right M3

- **The vision assigns exactly this scope to M3**, and the M2→M3 handoff (vision comment 606) left two open items M3 closes: BugGrabber has no keyless source, and the widget's progress/status inputs. The M2 contract is stable enough to build a view on, and the M4 contract freeze is next. Building the widget now exposes every contract wart while it is still cheap to fix.
- **Backups close the real data-loss gap** at almost no cost on btrfs, which is what Omarchy installs.
- **`errors` turns the most common addon question into one command** with an update suggestion, for humans and agents alike.
- **Humans need a surface that fits the desktop they live in.** The owner runs Omarchy with five house widgets in the bar. A sixth that follows the house pattern (CLI as authority, doorbells, keyboard-first panel) is the natural home for "3 updates, one click".

### The decisions that shape the milestone

The full decision log (M3-D1 to M3-D48: decision, reason, rejected alternatives, implementing beads) is in five comments on this epic.

| Decision | One line |
|---|---|
| M3-D2 | The widget runs only argv arrays: fixes and recommendations come from CLI output, and row actions come from a fixed, test-validated template table whose slots hold only identifiers the CLI returned. Free text goes into read-only templates only. |
| M3-D4 | One doorbell, `<cache>/doorbell.json`, rung by every write that can change `status --cached`. The widget watches its directory with `inotifywait` (atomic renames), with a fallback poll. `status.json` stays as it is. |
| M3-D5 | The widget is a `service` + `bar-widget` plugin, so one shared service runs per shell even with two monitors (the development machine has two). |
| M3-D9, M3-D46 | Stored plans stay in M4. Destructive widget actions show a `--dry-run` preview, and the confirmed run carries that preview's precondition token (`--if-match`). The CLI refuses with `plan_stale` if the selection or observed state changed. |
| M3-D15 | BugGrabber comes from WowAce's public SVN through a new `wowace:` source. Every file of a tag is fetched at the tag's own last-changed revision, and only the packaging subset BugGrabber needs is supported. Rejected: GitHub mirrors (one is bcc-only, another re-tags several times a day), CurseForge's website API, and manual downloads. |
| M3-D21 | `errors` output is strict by default: structured location, addon, Lua's message templates, counts and fingerprints. Free-form text needs `--raw-details`. The same path sanitizer covers every channel: JSON, human output, progress, warnings and notifications. |
| M3-D24 | A whole-`WTF/` restore is one journaled `RENAME_EXCHANGE` of the `WTF` directory, kind `restore`, undoable, refused while the client runs, and refused outright where exchange is unavailable. A crashed one rolls back only once the game is not running. Anything displaced is preserved through a journaled, resumable intent before any cleanup. A state recovery cannot recognize is left pending, never guessed at. |
| M3-D27 | `backup restore --addon X` is a SavedVariables-only transaction whose snapshot layout is exactly the one undo already restores from, so undo needs no new code path for it. The folders come from the backup's own addon record. |
| M3-D30 | **Owner-visible:** `auto_backup` defaults to `daily` (copy-on-write only; `daily-copy` opts into byte copies; `off` disables). `status` reports the configured mode and the observed capability separately. |
| M3-D45 | Persisted formats fail closed: journal versions are checked, an unreadable journal line never leads to pruning, and undo's conflict analysis refuses when relevant history is unreadable. |

### Structure

Seven area epics and 47 leaf beads (7 size-S, 34 size-M, 6 size-L), wired with 102 `blocks` edges between leaves: the plan's 101, plus D6 ← A4, added when the beads were filed because D6 extends A4's undo precondition and cannot close without it (it does not move either critical path). Epics connect to their children by `parent-child` only and carry no blocking edges. The six size-L leaves (A2, D1, D3, D5, D14, F2) each say in their Considerations why they are not split: each is one invariant or one policy whose halves would leave the tree unsafe or half-wired in between.

| Area | Epic id | Leaves | What it delivers |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1` | A1–A5 | Contract foundations: the doorbell and its ring sites; `status` triage (`summary`, `issues[]`, `last_change`) with the history projection; persisted formats that fail closed; preview binding with `--if-match` and precondition tokens; the shared privacy redactor |
| B | `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2` | B1–B8 | Lua errors: the SavedVariables parser, synthetic BugGrabber fixtures, decoders, frames and attribution, bounded location and the strict privacy renderer, the `errors` command, errors in `status`, durable `errors dismiss` |
| C | `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3` | C1–C3 | Keyless BugGrabber: `wowace:` refs, listing and packaging parsers; the WowAce source with pinned revisions; catalog variants with disjoint family selectors |
| D | `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4` | D1–D14 | Backups and restore: the store and shared primitives, `create`, automatic checkpoints, retention and `prune`, the whole-`WTF/` restore engine, undo of restores, per-addon restore, the `restore` command, `export`, `import`, backups in `status`, integration crash/concurrency/perf evidence, `verify`, recovery preservation |
| E | `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5` | E1–E4 | Widget packaging: embedded assets, the renderer and validator, `omarchy install`, `omarchy status` and `omarchy remove`, the widget in `status` |
| F | `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6` | F0–F9 | The Omarchy widget: the Quickshell spike, scaffold and model, the service core, the bar button, the panel frame and its five views, desktop signals, security and contract checks |
| G | `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7` | G1–G3 | README final pass, vision comments, the M3 checkpoint |

Leaf ids follow the area epic: A1 is `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.1`, D14 is `.4.14`. The one exception is F0, the spike, which is `.6.10` so that F1–F9 keep matching numbers `.6.1`–`.6.9`. The first comment on this epic is the full key → id table.

**Labels.** Every leaf carries exactly one size label (`size-S`, `size-M`, `size-L`), the milestone label `m3`, and its delivery slice (`slice-1` to `slice-4`). The four slices are the milestone's progress measure (Considerations).

### How to read the M3 beads

**Placeholders.** Bead text never contains home paths (house rule: beads may go public). The M3 beads use these placeholders:

| Placeholder | Means | Default on Linux |
|---|---|---|
| `<config>` | omaddons' config dir | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omaddons` |
| `<state>` | omaddons' state dir | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/omaddons` |
| `<cache>` | omaddons' cache dir | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/omaddons` |
| `<client dir>` | the directory holding a client's `Interface/` and `WTF/` | for example `…/World of Warcraft/_retail_` |
| `<meta>` | `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons` | |
| `<config-omarchy>` | Omarchy's user config dir (holds `shell.json`) | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omarchy` |
| `<plugins>` | Omarchy's third-party plugin dir | `<config-omarchy>/plugins` |
| `<omarchy>` | Omarchy's install | the system share dir for Omarchy (also linked from the user's data dir) |

**Words.** A *target* is one WoW client (one flavor folder or one private-server root). *Managed* means omaddons has a record for it. The *widget* is the Omarchy bar plugin this milestone builds; the *bar button* is its icon in the bar; the *panel* is the keyboard-driven popup it opens. A *doorbell* is a signal that tells the widget to re-read the authority (the CLI); a doorbell is never a source of state (house plugin rule, vision §4.6).

**Plan keys and section labels.** Beads refer to each other by plan key (A1 … G3), resolved by the key → id table. Decisions are `M3-D1` to `M3-D48`. Where a bead cites a plan section label (`§x.y`), the section is carried, with its number, by one of the comments on this epic:

| Label | Comment on this epic (its title starts with) |
|---|---|
| §2 | "Ground truth (§2)" |
| §4 | "User workflows (§4)" |
| §5 | "Decision log, part 1 of 5" … "part 5 of 5" (each decision keeps its id) |
| §6.1–§6.4, §6.6 | "Architecture (§6)" |
| §6.5, Appendix C | "File map (§6.5) and new test files" |
| §7.1–§7.5 | "Contract additions, part 1 (§7.1–§7.5)" |
| §7.6–§7.11 | "Contract additions, part 2 (§7.6–§7.11)" |
| §11 | "Delivery (§11)" (the §11.1 table is the first comment, "Bead key → id map") |
| §12 | "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol (§12)" |
| §13 | "Rationale and confidence (§13)" |
| Appendix F | "Planning record (Appendix F)" |

§0, §1 and §3 are this body. §8–§10 are the leaf beads themselves (§8.0, the common rules, is copied into every leaf; §9.1–§9.3 are inlined into B1, B3 and B4; §10.1 is the comment "The widget at a glance (§10.1)" on the F epic). Appendix D (README changes) is inlined into G1 and Appendix E (vision comments) into G2. Code references `file.rs:123` are as of `af10e34`; line numbers drift, symbol names do not.

## Goals

- **G-M3-1 Glanceable.** One bar icon tells a player, without opening anything, whether addons need updating, whether something is broken, and whether a client is running. It is always current within about a second of any change, whoever made it: terminal, agent, or the widget itself. Opening the panel costs no network request.
- **G-M3-2 One-click common actions, none of them surprising.** Update all, update one, check now, undo the last change, back up now, restore a whole `WTF/` or one addon's settings, install from search, fix an issue.
  - Each one is an omaddons command line the user could have typed, recorded with `--actor widget` and undoable like any other change.
  - It is confirmed first when it removes something or rewrites `WTF/`. The confirmed run is bound to the preview the user saw.
- **G-M3-3 Lua errors become actionable.** `omaddons errors` answers "which addon is most likely throwing errors, how often, since when, and is there an update?" from BugGrabber's data, on every client including 3.3.5a.
  - Its default output contains no free-form text from the error data, so it cannot leak a name that some addon wrote into an error string.
  - Errors other players sent are kept apart.
  - BugGrabber itself installs keylessly, from a pinned upstream revision.
- **G-M3-4 Settings survive.** Every client's `WTF/` gets a checkpoint before the day's first omaddons change and after each play session that changed it, without filling the disk.
  - A whole-`WTF/` or single-addon restore is one undoable command, refused while the game runs.
  - Every backup says honestly what it proves: stable while copied or best effort; content-verified or metadata-only.
  - An export survives a disk failure, and an import brings it back exactly.
- **G-M3-5 The contract carries the widget.** Everything the widget shows comes from documented `--json` output: `status --cached` (one call for the bar), `list`, `errors`, `backup list`, `search`, `info`. Agents get the same triage blocks, and the same preview tokens. Contract additions stay additive (DEC-4), and `schema_version` stays "1.0".
- **G-M3-6 No new risk to the engine's guarantees.**
  - Every new mutation goes through fsx and the journal.
  - A whole restore replaces `WTF/` only by one atomic exchange, so every crash leaves `WTF/` wholly old or wholly new.
  - Recovery never deletes a displaced version of the user's settings before that version has a durable home. A state it cannot recognize stays pending, with its evidence intact.
  - The global lock is held only for the commit window, also for a 500 MB `WTF/`.
  - SavedVariables are never written while the client runs, as far as process detection can tell. Detection refuses; it cannot stop a launch.
  - Journal and history readers fail closed on what they cannot read.

## Success Criteria

The M3 checkpoint. G3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3`) runs each criterion and records the evidence in its close reason, in the M2 format `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>`, with commit hash, test names, timings and every `SKIP` line quoted. These criteria amend vision §7 "M3 checkpoints"; each amendment is marked and explained in the decision log. The four slice demos are recorded on this epic as each slice lands (Considerations).

**Pre-accepted `SKIP`s.** The plan's approval accepted exactly these `SKIP`s in advance, so G3 never needs an owner bead or an owner decision at close:
- a running game client, when no client can be launched by an agent (criterion 2's running-state check, F0);
- the bind-mount and size-limited-tmpfs sandbox tests (`unshare -rm`), where unprivileged user namespaces are unavailable on the machine running them;
- the af10e34 characterization's build, if that commit no longer builds with the installed toolchain (D12 records the error);
- `keyless_installs_forever`, which M2 already allows through `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` until the Forever client's guard lifts.

Any other `SKIP` means the criterion is not met. Then G3 defers itself with `NEEDS OWNER: accept SKIP <name> · <why no agent can run it> · <what accepting changes>`, as the project rules allow for an existing bead.

1. **Widget install.**
   - The embedded plugin passes `omarchy-plugin-validate` and omaddons' own validator.
   - `omaddons omarchy install` on the development machine produces a working, enabled widget on both monitors, with exactly one service instance and one registered IPC handler (`omarchy-shell a44.omaddons state` answers).
   - A reinstall swaps atomically. Every install stages in its own hidden `<plugins>/.omaddons.stage-<ulid>`, so the registry never loads it. Two installers racing each other never mix or delete each other's stage.
   - Every omaddons process the widget starts runs under the `HOME`/XDG context stamped at install, checked by a test that launches the widget under different roots.
   - `omaddons omarchy remove` leaves `<plugins>` and the bar layout as they were before install, apart from the history line.
   - *(Amended: enable is the default; two monitors.)*
2. **Doorbell latency.**
   - A change made from a terminal shows in the widget's IPC `state()` within 1 s, at the 95th percentile of 20 trials. The harness runs `backup create` and `backup prune` on retail 10 times each (checkpoint protocol, §12.3). Both ring, neither touches AddOns or `WTF/`, and nothing is left behind. Forever is never touched.
   - An update check run from a terminal (`outdated`) changes the badge within 1 s.
   - A window opening or closing triggers a refresh within 1 s.
   - The running state follows a real client starting and exiting. The agent launches the 3.3.5a client to its login screen; if no client can be launched, the criterion records a `SKIP` from the pre-accepted list above.
   - *(Amended: the vision checked only mutations and window events.)*
3. **Opening the panel performs no network I/O.** `net.log` is unchanged across 10 panel opens and view switches.
4. **Widget states.** Each state renders correctly, checked through `qmltestrunner` scenarios and on the real machine through IPC `state()` plus a `grim` screenshot of the bar: updates pending; a P0/P1 issue; new Lua errors; a client running (update labels say "then /reload"; a refused action shows its reason); no targets; binary missing; widget outdated or incompatible (read-only: actions disabled, only Retry and Reinstall offered); an action in progress, showing progress from NDJSON; an action failed, showing its fix; a preview gone stale (`plan_stale`), showing the fresh preview instead of running.
5. **Argv-only execution.**
   - Every argv the widget can run comes from CLI output or from the template table, which `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` validates. That includes parsing with hostile slot values: spaces, `!`, `$(…)`, a leading `-`.
   - The argv validated in Rust are exactly the ones `Model.buildArgv` emits in bun, produced fresh in the same gate run, never substituted a second time in Rust.
   - CLI-provided argv pass the same classifier as templates (a known command path, no standard flag overridden, previews for destructive ones), not merely an `omaddons` prefix.
   - No `bash -c` and no `Util.execDetached` appears in the widget, checked by a source scan.
   - Every source-derived string renders through the shared plain-text component (`PlainLabel.qml`), checked by a source scan.
6. **`errors`.**
   - It parses synthetic fixtures for every BugGrabber era: integer time, string time first-seen, string time last-seen, r152 chunked, and an embedded `BugGrabberDB` in another addon's file.
   - It parses both file formats (modern no-indent CRLF; legacy tabs with `-- [n]`). It attributes each error to the right managed addon, including the library-dispatch, WeakAuras-chunk, `ADDON_ACTION_FORBIDDEN` and truncated-path cases (B4's attribution table), and it reports the attribution method and confidence.
   - **Privacy:** default and `-v` output contain only code-derived text: recognized Lua and Blizzard message templates, locations, function names, counts and fingerprints; custom messages, locals and chunk contents appear only with `--raw-details`; no output on any channel prints an account, realm or character name, including progress, warnings and errors (`assert_private`, with adversarial names planted in messages, chunks, paths and symlink targets).
   - Received reports are listed apart and never count as new, never notify and never cause an update recommendation.
   - Filtered reads (`--addon`, `--since`, `--limit`) never change the memo or `status`'s counts. `--since` reports uncertain matches instead of silently dropping them.
   - A dismissal survives deleting `<cache>`. It never acknowledges errors the user was not shown: the widget binds it to the shown observation.
   - Parsing stays within its time and memory budgets on adversarial files (fragment floods, tiny-token tables, deep skipped globals, many candidate files). An over-budget file is reported as incomplete and not retried on every doorbell.
   - The `savedvariables` fuzz target runs ≥ 30 min without a crash.
   - A 4 MB BugGrabber file parses in under 20 ms (release build).
7. **BugGrabber installs keylessly.**
   - `omaddons install buggrabber` installs the newest WowAce tag on synthetic retail, Mists Classic, Era, Anniversary and Forever clients, and r152 on the 3.3.5a client (real machine, then undone).
   - Every file of the tag is fetched at one recorded revision. A tag moved mid-fetch cannot mix revisions, an unrelated upstream commit never shows as an update, and a locked reinstall fetches the same revision again.
   - A project that needs a packaging step omaddons does not implement (externals, moves, keywords other than `@project-version@`, build-type blocks) is refused, not installed half-built.
   - `net.log` shows only allowlisted hosts and zero GitHub REST requests.
   - *(Added: the handoff required a source.)*
8. **Backups.**
   - `backup create` of a 500 MB synthetic `WTF/` in 5,000 files on btrfs completes in under 1 s (release build, median of 5). That is the vision's budget, at a realistic file count: SavedVariables trees hold few, large files. 20,000 files is measured and reported without a budget.
   - In clone-only mode (`daily`), a filesystem that cannot clone costs zero copied payload bytes. A tree that changes during capture is retried once, then marked `best_effort`, never reported as stable.
   - `backup verify` detects same-size corruption in a backup whose hashes were recorded at capture or import, and says so when it can only set a first baseline.
   - A whole restore and an `--addon` restore are each undoable and refused while the client runs. A whole restore is refused, before anything is copied, where `WTF/` cannot be exchanged atomically (a mount point, a cross-mount stage, a filesystem without `RENAME_EXCHANGE`).
   - The global lock hold of a restore is under 50 ms with that same tree.
   - `backup export` → `backup import` → `backup restore` reproduces a `WTF/` that is byte-identical (`tree_hash`, exact modes included). Import accepts only an exact manifest-to-payload match.
   - No output names an account, realm or character.
   - **Auto backups:** a pre-change checkpoint at most once per local day, and a post-session checkpoint after each play session that changed settings (also caught up at widget start); no capture when nothing changed since the newest qualifying capture; never on a dry run, and never failing a transaction; an imported, partial or best-effort backup never counts as today's checkpoint; below `limits.backup_min_free_mb` of free space, automatic capture first reclaims eligible automatic backups, then skips with a visible reason, and never deletes a manual, imported or recovered backup; concurrent due checks on one target make one backup, and a backup being restored or exported is never pruned under it.
9. **Crash safety.**
   - Every engine failpoint, armed as a real `abort` during a whole restore, a partial restore and an undo of each, leaves the change wholly old or wholly new. A whole restore is judged by the `WTF/` `tree_hash`. A partial restore is judged per touched file, plus an unchanged hash of the rest of `WTF/`.
   - The next change command recovers it. Recovery direction follows the durable journal phase: backward before `swapped`, forward from it.
   - A crashed restore rolls back once its client is not running. Every displaced version that differs from a copy still held elsewhere is preserved as a `recovered` backup, through a journaled intent that a crash during recovery resumes with the same backup id (`restore_rolled_back`). A file the game replaced stays as the game wrote it.
   - Recovery is itself crash-tested at every preservation transition, and under injected I/O failures and disk-full. An unrecognized state or an incomplete preservation leaves every tree, the stage and the journal in place (`journal_pending`, manual repair as in M2); it never cleans up to finish.
   - With the client running or its state unknown, a crashed restore's journal stays pending and nothing under `WTF/` moves. It rolls back once the client exits. In-process recovery makes the same fresh check.
10. **`status --cached` stays under 5 ms** (median of 21, release build), with p95 and cold-start times recorded, with the new `summary`, `issues`, `errors`, `backups`, `last_change` and `widget` blocks. The home is the realistic one of `tests/perf.rs`, plus: 4 backups per target and one target with 200 manual backups; a 2 MB BugGrabber file per target and 16 accounts on one target; a 20 MB history of interleaved runs. A missing or stale projection reports "unknown", never a guess.
11. **Gate and checkpoint runs.**
    - `argc gate --all` passes, including the new widget tests (`bun test`, `qmltestrunner`), from a clean checkout with no generated artifacts.
    - Every fuzz target runs for 10 minutes; `savedvariables` and `wowace_listing` run 30 minutes.
    - Live probes and real-machine tests pass, with every `SKIP` quoted.
    - Line coverage is recorded.
12. **README describes exactly what exists**, and the vision has M3 comments for decisions, contract additions, constants, scope changes and departures (G2's list).
13. **Destructive previews are binding.** For `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`, a test changes state between `--dry-run` and the real run with `--if-match`. The real run refuses with `plan_stale` and changes nothing: no newly selected object is deleted or overwritten. *(Added: M3-D46.)*
14. **Persisted formats fail closed.**
    - A journal with an unreadable `prepared` line, an unknown step or a newer major version is left pending with its stage and snapshots, never pruned.
    - Undo refuses with `undo_conflict` when an unreadable history line on the same target might hide a conflict.
    - The af10e34 binary, run against committed and interrupted M3 restores, is characterized: what it refuses, what it would do, and where, recorded in D12's close comment and README Limitations. *(Added: M3-D45.)*

## Non-Goals

- **Stored plans** (`--dry-run` → `plan_id` → `apply`). They stay in M4 (M3-D9). The widget runs commands directly. M3 brings forward only the small, stateless part a confirm dialog needs: a precondition token (M3-D46), which M4's `apply` can reuse.
- **`doctor`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, the agent skill, completions, the wire-names golden file.** All M4. M3's `issues[]` uses the doctor's finding ids, so M4 extends it rather than replacing it.
- **Editing or parsing SavedVariables for any purpose other than reading `BugGrabberDB`.** Backups copy bytes and never parse. Partial restore selects files by name, using the folder ownership recorded with the backup, never by content.
- **Schema compatibility checks between addon versions.** A backup records which addon versions produced it, and restore shows the difference, but omaddons never judges whether an old profile suits a new addon version.
- **A GUI or TUI outside Omarchy, a daemon, an MCP server.** The widget is an Omarchy plugin and nothing else.
- **In-widget settings editing.** Widget settings change with `omarchy bar set a44.omaddons <key> <value>`, the Omarchy way. Product settings change with `omaddons config set`.
- **Export, import and verify from the widget.** They are CLI only in M3. The widget offers back up now, whole restore, single-addon restore and prune.
- **Protecting against pre-M3 binaries.** An M2 build run against state that M3 has written can still misread it (ground truth §2.9). M3 documents this and fails closed from M3 on. It cannot change binaries that already exist (M3-D45).
- **CurseForge and Wago** (M5).
- **Capturing Lua errors without BugGrabber.** The client writes no error log, so BugGrabber is the source.
- **Backups of anything but `WTF/`**, and a restore mode without atomic exchange.

## Considerations

- **One owner-visible change.** `auto_backup` defaults to `daily` (copy-on-write only; `daily-copy` opts into byte copies; `off` disables; M3-D30). It is the one README promise M3 changes; README and the vision record it.
- **Design gates.** A3 (fail-closed readers), A4 (precondition tokens), B8 (durable dismissal), C2 (pinned WowAce trees), D5 (the whole-restore transaction and its recovery) and D14 (preservation intents) introduce new protocols. Each closes only when its own adversarial matrix is green (common rule 14). Expect them to take longer than their size label.
- **Critical paths** (weighting S = 1, M = 2, L = 3 over the wired edges; sequencing guidance, not a delivery estimate). Two paths of 20 units each:
  - the widget and its installer: A2 → F1 → F2 → F3 → E1 → E2 → E3 → G1 → G2 → G3;
  - restore safety: D1 → D5 → D14 → D8 → D7 → F9 → F7 → G1 → G2 → G3.
  The second path is the restore protocol itself. That is deliberate: the third review showed that the recovery and preservation semantics, not the copying, carry the schedule risk. Near-critical (slack 1): A1, A3, D6, D12, F4, F5, F6. To shorten the path, staff F2 with the strongest QML agent and D5/D14 with the engine specialist, and start E1's validator and renderer against a fixture plugin tree while F2/F3 run.
- **Roots.** A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B4, C1, D1 and F0 have no blockers and can start at once on parallel agents. Six agents in the lanes of the delivery comment finish at the critical-path length; five take about 15% longer, four about 35% longer.
- **Delivery slices.** Progress is judged by four slices, each with a demonstrable exit. When a slice's last leaf closes, the agent closing it runs the slice's demo and records it as a comment on this epic in the `[x] … : evidence` style. A slice whose demo fails reopens the leaf responsible (`--deps discovered-from`). Nothing waits for G3 to discover that two halves do not fit.
  - **`slice-1` See and update from the bar** (A1, A2, A4, F0, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, E1, E2, E3, E4): `omarchy install` on the desktop; the badge follows a terminal `update` within 1 s; update one addon from the panel, undo it; a `remove` preview gone stale gives `plan_stale`; reinstall swaps atomically. Pre-checks criteria 1, 2 (the terminal-change part), 3, 4 (update states), 5, 13 (`remove`, `undo`).
  - **`slice-2` Capture and diagnose** (A5, B1–B8, C1–C3, D1–D4, D11, D13, F6, F8): `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal. Pre-checks criteria 6, 7, 8 (create, auto, verify), 13 (`errors dismiss`, `backup prune`).
  - **`slice-3` Recover** (A3, D5, D6, D14, D8, D7, F9): whole and `--addon` restores from the CLI and from the bar's chooser, each undone; the crash matrices of D5, D6, D7 and D14. Pre-checks criteria 8 (restore), 9, 13 (`backup restore`), 14.
  - **`slice-4` Portability and close** (D9, D10, D12, F7, G1, G2, G3): export → import → restore byte-identical; integration scenes; the af10e34 characterization; perf; gate from a clean checkout; README. Pre-checks criteria 8 (export, import), 9 (integration), 10, 11, 12, 14 (the characterization).
- **The Forever stress-test set stays untouched.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client: its stress-test addon set is guarded by `forever_guard()` in `tests/real_machine.rs` until `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` closes (deferred to 2026-11-05).
- **Real-capture validation is a documented limitation, not a bead.** No BugGrabber data exists on the development machine, so `errors` is validated on synthetic fixtures that follow BugGrabber's public structure. The project rules forbid a bead whose next step belongs to a person, so no "play a session" bead exists. G3's close reason and README Limitations state the limitation. If a leaf ever genuinely cannot finish without a real capture, that leaf is deferred with `NEEDS OWNER: …`; a new owner bead never is.
- **The contract stays additive** (DEC-4: additions are allowed before the M4 freeze if recorded). `schema_version` stays "1.0". Error codes go from 39 to 41 and warning codes from 41 to 49 (`widget_outdated`, reserved in M1, becomes emitted). Every leaf lists its new wire names in its close comment so G2 can record them on the vision bead.
- **Collision hot spots** for parallel agents on one `main`: `src/app/status.rs` (A2 first, then B7, D11, E4 append), `src/app/undo.rs` and `src/engine/undo.rs` (A2, A3, A4, D3, D6, D7), `src/engine/tx.rs` (A1, A3, D3, D5), `src/engine/journal.rs` (A1, A3, D5, D14: A3 first, then D5, then D14), `src/error.rs` (additive rows plus count bumps in nine leaves), `src/cli.rs`/`src/app/mod.rs`/help tests (twelve leaves), `src/limits.rs` and its snapshot (fifteen leaves), `tests/engine_crash.rs` (D3, D5, D6, D7, D14, D12), `omarchy/Service.qml` (F2, then F8), `README.md` (everyone, each in its own section; G1 reconciles), `Cargo.toml` (D9 only: `tar` and `zstd`). Claim with file lists, keep commits small, rebase before each gate run, coordinate through `SendMessage`, and treat unrecognised working-tree changes as a peer's work. The delivery comment has the per-file rules.
- **README is the product contract.** Each leaf that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit, so README never lags `main`. G1 is the final consistency pass, not the first mention; it is also the one that changes README's status line to "Milestones 1, 2 and 3 are done".
- **House rules** (from the project's CLAUDE.md; every leaf repeats the M3-specific ones in its "Common rules for every M3 bead" block): `argc gate` before code commits (D16, no CI); one writer (`src/fsx/`); commands never print; no `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and no `unsafe`; constants in `src/politeness.rs`/`src/limits.rs`; tokio, reqwest, native-tls, openssl and aws-lc are banned; DEC-1 (each command adds its own subcommand, no stubs), DEC-3 (`Serialize + JsonSchema`, `BTreeMap`), DEC-4 (additive), DEC-7 (test hooks in debug builds only); privacy on every channel; bounded work on untrusted input; previews bind; public-safe bead text; work on `main`. M3 adds exactly two crates (`tar`, `zstd`, D9).
- **G3 leaves the widget installed and enabled** on the development machine: it is M3's deliverable.
- **Planning record.** The plan was reviewed in three rounds before decomposition: two independent internal reviews (42 findings with 3 blockers, then 20 with 1 blocker) and one external review of 23 proposed revisions (19 adopted, one of them extended, and 4 adapted, keeping the goal with a different mechanism; none rejected outright). The integrated text was then checked by two consistency reviews (41 findings, then 17), all fixed. The comments on this epic carry everything the plan held that is not specific to one leaf: the key → id table, the decision log, ground truth, architecture, workflows, delivery, risks, rationale and confidence, contract additions, the file map and the planning record (with the outcome of each of the 23 revisions).
acceptance_criteria: All seven area epics (A-G) and their 47 leaves are closed; G3 records evidence for each of the fourteen checkpoint criteria in its close reason as [x] N <criterion>: <evidence>, with only the pre-accepted SKIPs (no launchable client, no user namespaces for unshare tests, af10e34 not building, keyless_installs_forever): (1) the embedded widget validates, installs enabled on both monitors with one service and one IPC handler, reinstalls atomically through per-operation stages, runs every child under the stamped context, and removes cleanly; (2) terminal changes reach the widget within 1 s at p95 of 20 trials, update checks and window events within 1 s, and the running state follows a real client or is a pre-accepted SKIP; (3) opening the panel performs no network I/O; (4) every widget state renders, in qmltestrunner and on the real machine; (5) only template or classified CLI argv run, the Rust validator parses exactly what Model.buildArgv emits in the same gate run, no bash -c or Util.execDetached, and every source string renders through PlainLabel.qml; (6) errors decodes every BugGrabber era and both file formats, attributes with method and confidence, prints no free-form text or name by default on any channel, keeps received reports apart, never shrinks the memo on filtered reads, keeps dismissals across a cache wipe bound to the shown observation, stays within its budgets on adversarial files, fuzzes 30 min clean and parses 4 MB in under 20 ms; (7) install buggrabber works keylessly on every modern client and r152 on 3.3.5a, with every file at one recorded revision, unsupported packaging refused, only allowlisted hosts and zero GitHub REST; (8) a 500 MB, 5,000-file backup takes under 1 s on btrfs, clone-only copies zero bytes where it cannot clone, verify detects same-size corruption, whole and --addon restores are undoable, refused while the client runs and refused where exchange is impossible, the restore lock hold is under 50 ms, export-import-restore is byte-identical with an exact manifest, no output names an account, realm or character, and automatic backups follow their trigger, coalescing, qualification, free-space and reservation rules; (9) every failpoint during whole and partial restores and their undos leaves the change wholly old or new, recovery follows the journal phase, rolls back only once the client is not running (pending, with nothing under WTF/ moved, while it runs or its state is unknown), preserves displaced versions through a resumable journaled intent, is itself crash-tested, and leaves unrecognized states pending; (10) status --cached stays under 5 ms median on the heavy home with all new blocks and reports unknown rather than guess; (11) argc gate --all passes from a clean checkout including bun test and qmltestrunner, every fuzz target runs 10 min (savedvariables and wowace_listing 30 min), live probes and real-machine tests pass, coverage is recorded; (12) README describes exactly what exists and the vision carries the M3 comments; (13) remove, undo, backup restore, backup prune and errors dismiss refuse a stale --if-match with plan_stale and change nothing; (14) unreadable or newer journals are left pending, undo refuses over unreadable same-target history, and the af10e34 binary's behaviour against M3 restores is characterized in D12 and README; the four slice demos are recorded on the milestone epic; the widget is left installed and enabled.
