comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** Without it, the widget would have to invent severity in QML, count errors and backups itself, and guess what "Undo last" means, which is logic in the view and a way for the bar and the terminal to disagree. After it, one `status --cached --json` call of a few milliseconds answers "how bad is it?", "anything to do?" and "what exactly would Undo last revert?", with the same run selection `undo` uses. Agents gain the same one-key triage (`summary.state`) and doctor-shaped findings (`issues[]` with `fm-…` ids), so the M4 doctor extends this instead of breaking it. It is the first task on the widget critical path: F1's model reducers, and B7, D11 and E4's status blocks, are all written against the structs it creates.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D37: `status` grows triage blocks the widget and agents share.** `summary` (with `state` in the priority attention > errors > updates > idle), `targets[].issues[]` (vision D20 failure-mode ids, P0–P3, argv remediation), `last_change` with `last_change_state`. `attention[]` stays unchanged; `issues[]` is its structured twin. Why: the bar needs severity, error counts and "undo last" in one ≤ 5 ms call; agents benefit equally; using the doctor's ids now avoids a breaking change at the M4 freeze. Rejected: severities on `attention` strings (a type change); computing severity in QML (logic in the view, vision D2); a database or daemon for these summaries.
- **M3-D37 (bounded work): `status --cached` reads projections, never unbounded authority.** `<cache>/history_tail.json` holds every line back to the 16th newest run with an undoable entry (backup and settings runs never count), at most 1 MiB, with `covers {from, bytes, last_line_sha256}`; it is maintained inside `history::append_line` under the caller's lock, rebuilt only from the dispatch epilogue after the lock is released, read with the same pure `undo::select`, and answers "unknown" on any doubt. Why: a bounded tail read cannot prove it holds a whole interleaved run, and a fast but incomplete answer is worse than an explicit "unknown". Rejected: the first draft's 64 KiB tail read.
- **M3-D1 (context):** triage blocks are one of the three enabling pieces M3 adds beyond the vision's list, because the bar needs them in one cheap call. M3's `issues[]` uses the doctor's ids, which is enough for the widget; the doctor itself stays in M4.
- **M3-D9 (context):** "Undo last" is a destructive widget action, previewed and bound by A4's token; `last_change.undo.argv` names the run, never "most recent".

**Review-round changes folded in.** The projection replaced a tail read (third review, revision 15): it counts only runs with an undoable entry, so 40 backups and 20 settings lines can never evict the last undoable update; it is maintained in `history::append_line`, the one function both appenders use, rather than at new call sites; its full rebuild runs outside the lock from one call site, `app::dispatch`'s epilogue, after every `mutates: true` path, because a 20 MB history read would break the 50 ms lock-hold budget; `Nothing` is reported as `ok` only when the projection covers the whole history (`covers.from == 0`); the run selection was extracted into a pure function shared with `undo`, so the size grew to L.

**Facts verified during planning.** `StatusData` is `{cached, targets[], journal, needs_attention}` (`src/app/status.rs:65-171`) with an enum `attention[]` and no severity, error, backup or history information; `status --cached` measured 3 ms on seven targets and the perf test asserts a median under 5 ms (`tests/perf.rs:300-410`); `attention_fixes` is at `src/app/status.rs:830-891`; `undo`'s run selection is `src/app/undo.rs:355-416` and gathers every entry with the run key across the whole file; history lines from concurrent runs interleave because each target's transaction appends inside its own lock (`src/engine/tx.rs:705`, `:936`, `:1005`); `history::append` (`src/state/history.rs:180`) and `append_setting` (`:186`) both call `append_line` (`:218`); dispatch is the exhaustive match at `src/app/mod.rs:292-485`; settings kinds are `SettingEntry` lines (`src/state/history.rs:72-90`) and `TxKind::Backup` is not undoable (`src/model.rs:412-453`) (all as of `af10e34`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- `status --cached` regresses past 5 ms (medium/medium): projections instead of scans; the perf test with a 20 MB interleaved history at the median and p95, extended by B7 and D11 with the heavy checkpoint home.
- The projection disagrees with `undo`: one shared `select`, plus a 1,000-case property test of projection-select against full-history select; any `covers` mismatch reports "unknown".
- A rebuild under the lock would break the lock-hold budget: the rebuild has exactly one call site, after unlock; the incremental update inside the lock touches only the 1 MiB projection.
- `status.rs` is the busiest hot spot of the milestone: A2 lands first and the others append.

**Confidence.** High: additive, contract-tested keys over existing data, with the projection's correctness pinned by a property test against the full-history selection (milestone confidence: "the doorbell and the contract additions").

title: Persisted formats fail closed
description:
## Background

M3 adds journal fields and line kinds (`writes_wtf`, `staged_stamp`, `staged_files`, `source_backup`, `preserve`, `preserved`), history op values (`wtf`, `saved_variables`) and fields (`backup`, `from`, `files`, `sv_restored`), history kinds (`widget`, `dismiss`) and several state files. Each of those becomes a way to lose data across binary versions if a reader treats what it cannot read as "nothing there". The widget makes mixed binaries more likely than before (it stamps one binary path at install, while a terminal may run another build). **M3-D45** therefore makes every reader M3 touches **fail closed**, and this task lands those readers before D5 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.5`) writes the first new journal, so no build in the tree ever prunes a journal it cannot read.

What the code does today (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.9; as of `af10e34`):

- **Journals** (`src/engine/journal.rs`):
  - `Prepared.schema_version` (`:82`, `CURRENT = 1.0` at `:38`) is written and **never compared**.
  - Unknown fields are ignored, because no journal type uses `deny_unknown_fields`.
  - An unknown enum value (`TxKind`, `StepOp`, `StepPurpose`, line `type`) fails its whole line, which is counted in `unknown_lines` and skipped (`:363-366`). Nothing reads that count.
  - **A skipped `prepared` line is the dangerous case.** The phase stays `Unprepared`, so recovery rolls nothing back. It prunes the journal and the in-flight lock (`:737`, `:767-776`), and the dead-snapshot sweep removes that transaction's state-side snapshots (`:781-794`). A journal this binary cannot fully read is treated as one with nothing to recover. **That is a latent M2 hazard**, independent of M3: any future journal change would trigger it.
  - A torn final line (a crash mid-append) is already tolerated: the tests `roll_forward_finds_its_own_line_that_lost_only_its_newline` and the next one cover it. The journal is write-ahead, so the step a torn line would have recorded never ran.
- **State files** (`src/state/store.rs:1-12`) carry `schema_version` `"MAJOR.MINOR"`; a newer file "is read only if it still decodes and is never written". The refusal is enforced inside `store::save` (`:230-243`, error `state_too_new`, exit 4), only for target records, files indexes and `registry.json`. **It fires late:** in a commit, `store::save` of the record runs after the swap and after undo's SavedVariables restore (`src/engine/tx.rs:904-913`, `src/engine/undo.rs:343-357`). Nothing refuses a newer record before staging, so a newer record stops a binary only after it has moved folders and written SavedVariables, leaving a pending journal behind.
- **History** (`src/state/history.rs:5-9`, `:318-330`, `:381`): an unreadable line is counted, and `history` and `undo` warn `history_lines_skipped`. `undo` then plans and checks conflicts over the readable entries only (`src/app/undo.rs:287-290`, `src/engine/undo.rs:162`, `:271`, `:700`). Conflict detection sees only folder ops (`check_conflicts`, `src/engine/undo.rs:704`). With the default `--saved-variables auto`, undo restores **every** SavedVariables file whose hash differs from the reverted transaction's manifest (`undo.rs:1339-1383`), whoever changed it. So an undo that cannot read a newer line may silently put old SavedVariables back over settings that line restored.
- **Scope already stops an older binary at the `WTF/` boundary.** `Scope::Wtf` admits only `Writer::BackupRestore` and `Scope::SavedVariables` only `Writer::Undo` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:117-118`), while recovery always writes as `Writer::Mutating` (`journal.rs:731`). An M2 binary that tries to recover an M3 restore journal is refused at its first `WTF/` rename.

This serves **G-M3-6 No new risk to the engine's guarantees** ("journal and history readers fail closed on what they cannot read") and checkpoint criterion 14 (persisted formats fail closed: an unreadable `prepared` line, an unknown step or a newer major version leaves the journal pending with its stage and snapshots; undo refuses with `undo_conflict` when an unreadable history line on the same target might hide a conflict). The af10e34 characterization half of criterion 14 belongs to D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`).

## Technical Approach

### The decision this task implements (M3-D45, operative rules)

- **Journal version.** `recover_parsed` compares `Prepared.schema_version` with `journal::CURRENT`.
  - A newer **major** version is never recovered by this binary. The journal, its stage and its snapshots stay, the target reports `journal_pending` with `details.reason: "journal_too_new"`, and the fix is prose: "a newer omaddons started this change; finish it with that version".
  - A newer **minor** is recovered, ignoring unknown fields as today.
  - M3 writes journal `1.1`: `writes_wtf` journals and preservation lines are additive, and an M2 binary reading them is refused by scope at its first `WTF/` rename.
- **Unreadable lines are not "nothing to do".** A journal whose `prepared` line does not decode, or that holds any other complete line `parse` could not decode, is **never** treated as `Unprepared`. Recovery leaves the journal, its in-flight lock, its stage and its state-side snapshots in place, with `journal_pending` and `details.reason: "journal_unreadable"`, which is manual repair as in M2.
  - **A torn append is not unreadable.** A final fragment without its newline is a crash mid-append, already tolerated by M2. It is ignored exactly as today. A journal that is nothing but a torn `prepared` fragment is pruned as today, because nothing ran.
  - `parse` therefore counts two things separately: `torn_tail` (0 or 1, tolerated) and `unknown_lines` (any complete undecodable line, fail closed).
- **History.** `history` and `list` keep skipping unreadable lines with `history_lines_skipped`. **Undo's conflict analysis fails closed** instead (M3-D28 rule 5, below).
- **Early refusal of newer state.** Before planning any mutation of a target, the engine loads that target's record and files index, and the registry for a registration. If any is `VersionStatus::Newer`, it refuses with `state_too_new` **before staging**. That is the barrier every binary from M3 on honours.
- **What M3 cannot fix, stated honestly.** An M2 binary (`af10e34` or older) has neither guard: run against state M3 wrote, it can read history without seeing restores, and its undo with `--saved-variables auto` would put an old transaction's SavedVariables copies back over restored ones; it fails only late, at the record save, if the record is newer; it is refused by scope if it tries to recover an M3 restore journal. There is no pre-mutation structure M2 already refuses, so M3 **does not claim a downgrade barrier against M2**: README Limitations documents the limit, and D12 characterizes the real af10e34 binary.

### M3-D28 rule 5: unreadable history fails closed (the operative text)

A history line this binary cannot decode, newer than the transaction T being undone, **is assumed to touch everything it might**:
- When the line is valid JSON, its raw `target` and `ops[].folder` strings are read as `serde_json::Value`. A line on another target is ignored. A line on T's target is treated as writing **all** SavedVariables of that target and the folders it names. It is treated as writing every folder when it names none, or names `WTF`.
- A line that is not even JSON is treated as touching every target.
- The ordinary rules then apply. A SavedVariables restore is refused with `undo_conflict`, `details.reason: "history_unreadable"` and the line count. The alternative is `--saved-variables keep`, offered only when the line's folders are disjoint from T's. A folder overlap is refused outright. The fix is prose: "a newer omaddons wrote that history; undo it with that version".

(Rules 1–4 of M3-D28, the `wtf` and `saved_variables` op conflicts, are D6 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.6` and D7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.7`; rule 5 is a separate function here so they compose.)

### Contract touched (milestone epic comment "Contract additions, part 2 (§7.6–§7.11)", §7.6–§7.8)

- **Reused error codes, new uses:** `state_too_new` (exit 4, not retryable): "a mutation refused up front because the target's record, files index or the registry is newer (M3-D45)"; `undo_conflict` with `details.reason: "history_unreadable"` (M3-D28 rule 5).
- **`journal_pending`** (existing) gains the `details.reason` values `journal_unreadable` and `journal_too_new` here (`unexpected_state` and `preservation_incomplete` come from D5 and D14). A2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.2`) maps all four to the "needs manual repair" issue title.
- **Journals become version `1.1`.** New `Prepared` keys stay `#[serde(default)]` (M2-D36, additive optional fields). This task only raises `CURRENT` and adds the readers; D5 adds the `Prepared` keys (`writes_wtf`, `staged_stamp`, `staged_files`, `source_backup`) and D14 the `preserve`/`preserved` line kinds.

### Steps

1. **Journal reading (`src/engine/journal.rs`).**
   - `parse` (`:339`) returns `torn_tail: bool` (a final fragment without its newline, tolerated as today) separately from `unknown_lines: usize` (complete lines that do not decode).
   - `recover_parsed` (`:703`):
     - `prepared.schema_version.major > CURRENT.major` → leave everything (journal, in-flight lock, stage, both snapshot halves); `journal_pending` with `details.reason: "journal_too_new"`;
     - `prepared` missing or undecodable while the file has any complete line → leave everything; `journal_unreadable`;
     - `unknown_lines > 0` → leave everything; `journal_unreadable`;
     - only a torn `prepared` fragment and nothing else → prune as today (nothing ran).
   - `CURRENT` becomes `1.1`. New `Prepared` keys stay `#[serde(default)]` (M2-D36).
   - The own-target rule is unchanged: a pending journal on the command's own target fails the command with its `journal_pending` details. Other targets continue (vision comment 667).
   - "Leave everything" also means the dead-snapshot sweep (`:781-794`) must not treat that transaction's snapshots as dead: a kept journal keeps its snapshots.
   - The README `journal_pending` troubleshooting paragraph ("`journal_pending` that does not clear", around line 1837 as of `af10e34`) gains the new manual-repair reasons, and keeps naming the M4 `doctor` as what will automate the repair.
2. **Early refusal of newer state (`src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/engine/undo.rs`).** Before `prestage_saved_variables` and before staging, load the target record and files index, and the registry when registering. If any `Loaded.status == VersionStatus::Newer`, return `state_too_new` (fix prose: "upgrade omaddons; a newer version wrote this client's state"). It costs one small read per file, already done later anyway, now done first. The late `store::save` check stays as a backstop. Because it sits on the shared engine path, every transaction kind gets it, including `backup restore` once D8 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.8`) exists.
3. **History for undo (`src/engine/undo.rs`, `src/state/history.rs`).**
   - `history::read` (`src/state/history.rs:335`) keeps the raw text of each unreadable line, bounded to `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` per line, beside `skipped_lines` (common rule 15: a bounded read of untrusted input).
   - `check_conflicts` implements M3-D28 rule 5. A raw line is parsed as `serde_json::Value` for `target` and `ops[].folder`; anything else counts as touching everything.
   - `history` and `list` keep their skip-and-warn behaviour.
4. **README.**
   - Limitations: "Do not run a pre-M3 omaddons build to change state that M3 has written. Reading with it (`status`, `list`, `history`) is safe. A pre-M3 `undo` cannot see M3 restores."
   - Safety model: the new journal rules (version checked; an unreadable complete line never leads to pruning; a torn tail is tolerated; newer state refused before staging; undo fails closed on unreadable history).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Planted journals give exactly the documented outcome, with every file (journal, in-flight lock, stage, both snapshot halves) left in place where "leave everything" is stated:
  - newer major → `journal_pending`, `details.reason: "journal_too_new"`;
  - an undecodable `prepared` → `journal_unreadable`;
  - an unknown `StepOp` → `journal_unreadable`;
  - an unknown line type → `journal_unreadable`;
  - an unknown field → recovered normally;
  - a newer minor version → recovered normally;
  - a torn final step line → recovered normally (both existing roll-forward tests stay green);
  - only a torn `prepared` → pruned.
- A pending unreadable journal on the command's own target fails that command with its `journal_pending` details; other targets continue.
- A newer target record makes `install`, `update`, `remove` and `undo` fail with `state_too_new` before any file under the client dir changes (hashes before and after). `backup restore` gets the same check through the shared engine path, tested by D8 once the command exists.
- With a planted, unreadable, newer history line on the same target naming folder `Foo`:
  - `undo` of an older transaction with a SavedVariables manifest is `undo_conflict` (`details.reason: "history_unreadable"`, with the line count);
  - with `--saved-variables keep`, it is allowed when T's folders exclude `Foo`, and refused when they include it;
  - with the same line on another target, the undo is allowed;
  - with a non-JSON line, it is refused.
- `history` and `list` still skip unreadable lines with `history_lines_skipped`.
- `journal::CURRENT` is `1.1`; README carries the Limitations sentence and the new journal rules.

## Test Plan

- **Unit (`src/engine/journal.rs`):** `parse` and `recover_parsed` with planted lines: every row of the planted-journal table, each asserting the outcome and that the journal, in-flight lock, stage and snapshots are (or are not) left in place; `torn_tail` vs `unknown_lines` counting; the existing `roll_forward_finds_its_own_line_that_lost_only_its_newline` tests unchanged.
- **E2E (`tests/undo_history.rs`):** rule 5: same-target JSON line naming `Foo` (refused; `keep` allowed or refused by folder overlap), another-target line (allowed), non-JSON line (refused); `details.reason` and the prose fix asserted.
- **E2E (early refusal):** a planted newer target record (and files index; a newer registry for a registration) makes `install`, `update`, `remove` and `undo` fail `state_too_new` with the client dir's tree hash unchanged.
- **Contract:** the `state_too_new` and `undo_conflict` (`history_unreadable`) failure rows.
- The early-refusal E2E and the contract rows were added while writing this bead, beside the planned unit tests on `parse` and `recover_parsed` and the rule-5 E2E, to cover the acceptance criteria; their file is the implementer's choice.
- **Not here:** the af10e34 characterization (`tests/compat_m2.rs`, ignored, run at the checkpoint) needs real M3 restores, so it belongs to D12. The milestone's new-test-files table lists it on the fail-closed-formats row next to this task's tests; D12 owns it, as the milestone testing strategy also says.

## Considerations

- **This changes M2 behaviour in one place:** a journal with an undecodable complete line was pruned and is now kept. That is a strict safety improvement, recorded on the vision by G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`). List the new `details.reason` values and the journal version in the close comment (common rule 6).
- **Why not a downgrade barrier against M2.** The third review asked for one "in a format older binaries already honour". Checking af10e34 showed none exists: `store::save`'s refusal fires after the swap and after undo's SavedVariables restore. Rejected (M3-D45): bumping the target record version as an M2 barrier (M2 would still write folders and SavedVariables before failing, then leave a stuck journal); making M3 journal lines undecodable to M2 on purpose (M2 would treat the journal as `Unprepared` and prune it, the very hazard above); a marker file M2 ignores.
- **Design gate.** This task introduces a new protocol: fail-closed persisted formats, a deliberate change of M2 behaviour (milestone epic comment "Rationale and confidence (§13)", §13.2). Where the risk lies (reasoning added while writing this bead): in the edges. A rule that is too strict blocks every change on a client with a harmless torn tail, and one that is too lax reintroduces the pruning hazard. It closes only when its adversarial matrix (every planted-journal row, every rule-5 case, the early refusal with tree hashes) is green (common rule 14). Expect it to take longer than its letter.
- **Risks.**
  - Milestone risk 18: a pre-M3 binary mutates state M3 wrote (two builds on one machine; likelihood low–medium, impact medium–high). M3 cannot change existing binaries; it fails closed from now on (journal versions, unreadable lines, history in conflict analysis, early `state_too_new`); D12 characterizes af10e34; M2's scope refusal stops it recovering M3 restore journals.
  - Milestone risk 7: restore breaks the engine's crash guarantees (likelihood low–medium, impact high). The milestone mitigation: directory steps reuse proven journal identity; exchange-only whole and partial restores; each shape lands with its own crash matrix; D14's preservation protocol is crash-, I/O- and disk-full-tested at every transition; unrecognized states keep everything. A3's readers are the first layer under that: no binary from M3 on prunes a journal it cannot fully read (an M2 binary is stopped by scope instead, not by these readers).
- **Collision hot spots** (coordinate through `SendMessage` and claim comments listing files):
  - `src/engine/journal.rs` (A1, A3, D5, D14): **A3 first (readers)**, then D5 (writer selection, waits, conservative stop), then D14 (preservation).
  - `src/engine/tx.rs` (A1, A3, D3, D5): A1's ring is one line; A3's early refusal is one call before staging; D3's hook sits before `stage_all`; D5 adds failpoints. Rebase carefully.
  - `src/engine/undo.rs`, `src/app/undo.rs` (A2, A3, A4, D3, D6, D7): A2's `select` refactor first; A3's rule 5 is a separate function; lane 6 owns D6, lane 5 owns D7.
  - `src/state/history.rs`: A2 edits `append_line`; A3 edits the reader.
- **Delivery.** Slice `slice-3` ("Recover"). Exit demo: whole and `--addon` restores from the CLI and from the bar's chooser, each undone; the crash matrices of D5, D6, D7 and D14. A3 is the format layer under all of them. **Near-critical (slack 1):** D5 needs A3 at t=3 on the restore critical path (D1 → D5 → D14 → D8 → D7 → F9 → F7 → G1 → G2 → G3), so lane 6 ("Formats, archives and integrity") takes it first.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- none
**Unblocks:**
- D5 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.5` (The whole-`WTF/` restore transaction in the engine): restore journals add `Prepared` fields (and, with D14, line kinds) that every reader must treat safely; D5 writes the first `1.1` journal only once these readers exist.
- D6 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.6` (Undo of a whole restore, and the conflict rules): undo's conflict analysis gains M3-D28 rule 5 here; D6 adds rules 1, 2 and 4 beside it.

Inherited relations (not list entries): D7 and D14 inherit the readers and rule 5 through D5 and D6; D12 characterizes the af10e34 binary against what these readers protect.

Parent: the A epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1`. Delivery slice: `slice-3`.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** Today a journal whose `prepared` line this binary cannot decode is treated as "nothing ran": recovery prunes it, its in-flight lock and its snapshots. M3 is about to add journal fields, line kinds and history ops, so without this bead every future format change could make some binary throw away the only record of an interrupted change, and an undo that cannot read a newer history line could silently overwrite restored settings. After it, every binary from M3 on refuses what it cannot read: the journal stays pending for manual repair, newer state is refused before any folder moves, and undo assumes an unreadable line touched everything it might. That keeps the thesis honest: omaddons stays the safe, undoable authority even when two builds share one machine, which the widget (one stamped binary path) makes more likely. D5 and D6 build on these readers.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D45: persisted formats fail closed.** The journal version is compared (a newer major is never recovered: `journal_too_new`); a complete undecodable line is never "nothing to do" (`journal_unreadable`, everything kept), while a torn tail is tolerated as today; history stays skip-and-warn for `history` and `list` but fails closed in undo's conflict analysis; newer state is refused with `state_too_new` before staging. M3 writes journal `1.1`. Why: no barrier "in a format older binaries already honour" exists at `af10e34`, because `store::save` refuses only after folders and SavedVariables were written; what M3 can do is make itself and every later binary refuse up front, and say precisely what remains. Rejected: bumping the target record version as an M2 barrier (M2 would still write first, then leave a stuck journal); making M3 journal lines undecodable to M2 on purpose (M2 would prune them, the very hazard); a marker file M2 ignores.
- **M3-D28 rule 5: unreadable history fails closed in undo.** A same-target valid-JSON line is treated as writing all of that target's SavedVariables and the folders it names (every folder when it names none or names `WTF`); a non-JSON line touches every target; a SavedVariables restore is then `undo_conflict` (`history_unreadable`), with `--saved-variables keep` offered only for disjoint folders. Why: an M2-style blind undo would put an old install's SavedVariables back over a restore, exactly the data loss backups exist to prevent.
- **M2-D36 (context): additive journal keys stay `#[serde(default)]`**, so a newer minor still recovers.
- **A change of M2 behaviour, not a vision departure:** a journal with an undecodable complete line was pruned and is now kept. M3-D45 carries no departure mark; G2 records the change in the vision comment on journal and recovery ("a strict change from M2").

**Review-round changes folded in.** This task is new in the third review (revision 21, adapted): fail-closed journal and history reading and the early `state_too_new` were adopted as proposed, and the latent M2 pruning hazard was found while checking the claim; the requested downgrade barrier was not adopted, because it does not exist at `af10e34`, and the af10e34 characterization went to D12 instead. `parse` counts `torn_tail` separately from `unknown_lines`, so the existing torn-append tolerance (and its two roll-forward tests) survives, and only a journal that is nothing but a torn `prepared` fragment is still pruned.

**Facts verified during planning.** `Prepared.schema_version` (`src/engine/journal.rs:82`, `CURRENT = 1.0` at `:38`) is never compared; an unknown enum value fails its whole line, counted in `unknown_lines` and skipped (`:363-366`), and nothing reads the count; a skipped `prepared` leaves the phase `Unprepared`, so recovery prunes the journal and in-flight lock (`:737`, `:767-776`) and the dead-snapshot sweep removes the state-side snapshots (`:781-794`); `store::save` refuses `state_too_new` (`src/state/store.rs:230-243`) only after the swap and undo's SavedVariables restore (`src/engine/tx.rs:904-913`, `src/engine/undo.rs:343-357`); history skips unreadable lines and undo checks conflicts over readable entries only (`src/state/history.rs:318-330`, `src/app/undo.rs:287-290`, `src/engine/undo.rs:162`, `:271`, `:700`, `check_conflicts` at `:704`); `--saved-variables auto` restores every SavedVariables file whose hash differs (`undo.rs:1339-1383`); recovery writes as `Writer::Mutating` (`journal.rs:731`) and `Scope::Wtf`/`Scope::SavedVariables` admit only `BackupRestore`/`Undo` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:117-118`), so an M2 binary is refused at its first `WTF/` rename of an M3 restore journal (all as of `af10e34`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Too strict a reader blocks every change on a client: torn tails stay tolerated, unknown fields and newer minors still recover, and only the command's own target fails on a pending journal.
- Too lax a reader reintroduces pruning: the planted-journal table covers every line class, with file-presence assertions.
- A pre-M3 binary mutating M3 state (milestone risk 18): documented in README Limitations, characterized by D12; M3 cannot change existing binaries.
- Hot spot `journal.rs`: A3 lands first; D5 and D14 rebase onto it.

**Confidence.** (The milestone's confidence list does not grade this task by name; this grade was set while writing this bead, within its design-gate framing.) High in the rules (each is a narrow, fail-closed check on an existing code path, and the planted matrix pins every outcome), but this is a design gate: it closes only with its adversarial matrix green.

comments.text:
Landed: persisted formats fail closed (M3-D45). The journal is version 1.1.

**Journals (`src/engine/journal.rs`).**
- `parse` never fails. It counts `torn_tail` (a last line without its newline, or a last line that is not JSON) apart from `unknown_lines` (any complete line it cannot decode, including a non-JSON line before the last).
- It reads the `prepared` line's raw `schema_version` and `target_key` even when that line does not decode.
- `Parsed::unrecoverable()` gives `TooNew` for a newer major version, and `Unreadable` for unknown lines or for complete lines without a `prepared` one.
- `recover_parsed` returns before touching anything (journal, in-flight lock, stage, both snapshot halves).
- `pending()` carries the reason; `unfinished()` and therefore `cleanup` keep such a journal; `status` passes the reason to `issues_for` ("needs manual repair").

**Early refusal.**
- `store::refuse_newer` plus `tx::refuse_newer_state` check the record and files index, or the registry for a registration.
- It runs at the start of `commit_target` (before the in-flight lock and staging) and in `undo` after its dry run.
- It runs again under the lock in both paths (after registration and recovery).
- The late `store::save` check stays as a backstop.

**Rule 5 (`src/engine/undo.rs`).**
- `history::parse` keeps each unreadable line's raw text (bounded by `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES`) and its position (`after`, adjusted for `--limit`).
- `check_unreadable` runs in `plan` after the SavedVariables plan. A folder overlap is refused outright; a SavedVariables restore is refused with `undo <tx> --saved-variables keep` as the alternative.

**Decided.**
- A complete last line that is not JSON stays a torn tail. Every writer writes JSON, so such a line is a fragment that recovery's `committed` append closed off. This is M2's tolerance, kept.
- A non-JSON line before the last was an internal error that left the journal. It is now `journal_unreadable`: same outcome, typed reason.
- `roll_forward` no longer appends `committed` after a torn tail. Otherwise a crash before the prune turns the merged line into a mid-file unreadable line, a manual repair caused by a harmless tear. Roll-forward is idempotent, so it simply runs again.
- An unrecoverable journal fails its own target's command as `state_too_new` (exit 4, `journal_too_new`) or `state_corrupt` (exit 1, `journal_unreadable`). Details are `{journal_pending, reason, target}`, with a prose fix.
- For other targets it is one `journal_pending` warning naming the reason, identical from the reader and from recovery, so a run says it once.
- A committed journal that holds an unknown line is also left, and reported pending.
- In rule 5, only a `target` that parses as another key rules a line out. A null, missing or unparseable target is assumed to be T's. An op without a folder string means every folder.
- In rule 5, "restores" means the policy is not `keep` and the snapshot manifest has an entry in scope, unchanged ones included (the bead's "with a SavedVariables manifest").
- The `history_lines_skipped` fix now also names "written by a newer omaddons".

**New wire names (DEC-4).**
- `journal_pending` reasons `journal_too_new` and `journal_unreadable`, on `state_too_new` and `state_corrupt` errors (`details.journal_pending`, `details.reason`, `details.target`) and in warning messages.
- `undo_conflict` `details.reason: "history_unreadable"` with `details.lines`.
- `state_too_new` as an up-front refusal.
- The journal `schema_version` is 1.1.

**This changes M2 behaviour in one place**, for G2 to record: a journal with an undecodable complete line was pruned, and is now kept. `tests/list.rs::a_pending_journal_is_reported_not_recovered` planted a lone `swapped` line. Its reader warning now names `journal_unreadable` with a prose fix; the test was updated to say so.

**Note for later beads (ubs).** The token-comparison rule taints variables file-wide through identifiers inside string literals: a `(s)` in a message became the identifier `s`. That tainted `let message`/`let error`, then `tx` and `at` across `undo.rs`. The fix was at the source (no `(s)`, and the error built under a unique name), with no `ubs:ignore` needed.

**Evidence.**
- `argc gate` green.
- Unit matrix in `engine::journal`, five fail-closed rows: newer major, undecodable `prepared`, unknown step op, unknown line type, and non-JSON before the last. Each asserts the own-target error and details, the other-target warning, `pending`, `unfinished` and the reader warning, with all five artifacts present after repeated recovery.
- Four may-ignore rows: unknown field, newer minor, torn step, older version.
- A torn `prepared` line is pruned, and the torn-tail roll-forward never appends.
- A planted mutation (the guard disabled) fails the matrix.
- E2E `tests/fail_closed.rs`: install, update, remove and undo against a newer record, each with the client tree hash unchanged; a newer files index; a newer registry; planted journals that fail their own target, let the other go on, and show "needs manual repair" in `status`.
- E2E rule 5 in `tests/undo_history.rs`: a line naming Foo is refused with and without `keep`; a line naming Bar offers `keep`, and running it succeeds with SavedVariables kept; another target's line, an older line and an older non-JSON line are allowed; a newer non-JSON line is refused; `history` warns.
- Contract: `undo_history_unreadable` and `install_state_too_new` snapshots.
- The crash (34), concurrency, fallbacks, engine undo and preconditions suites are unchanged and green.

title: Preview binding: `--if-match` and precondition tokens
description:
## Background

A confirm dialog is only honest if the confirmed run is the previewed one. The widget (and an agent following the same pattern) previews every destructive action with `--dry-run`, shows the result, and runs the real command on "Yes". Between preview and confirm, a terminal or an agent can change the target, the restore source, the prune selection or undo's conflicts. The dialog then no longer describes what will happen: a `backup prune --keep N` could delete a different set than shown, and prune is not undoable; undo is not a substitute for confirming a deletion. **The concerning case is not a new release** (as the first draft argued); it is a concurrent change.

Stored plans (`--dry-run` → `plan_id` → `apply`) would fix this, but they are an M4 deliverable with their own contract (`plan_id`, `PLAN_TTL`, `plan_stale`) and freeze; pulling them forward would double the risk of both milestones (M3-D9). **M3-D46** brings forward only the small, stateless part a dialog needs: a **precondition token**. Every `--dry-run` of the five destructive commands (`remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `errors dismiss`) returns `data.precondition`; the real run with `--if-match <token>` recomputes the token from its own plan before staging anything and refuses with `plan_stale`, changing nothing, if any covered part differs. The token is opt-in: commands typed without `--if-match` behave exactly as today, so no script breaks.

What exists today (as of `af10e34`): `ErrorCode::PlanStale` and `PlanStaleSource::{Replan, Apply}` (`src/error.rs:494-555`): `Replan` is engine step 6 re-planning (retrying replans against the new state); `Apply` is "the stored plan can never apply; the fix is its dry-run argv", which is exactly the non-retryable semantics this needs. The engine already checks target generations under the lock. `remove` and `undo` already have `--dry-run`. Nothing binds a run to a preview.

This task builds the token function, the global flag, and the binding for the two destructive commands that exist now (`remove`, `undo`). B8, D4 and D8 compute their own parts with the same function when they add `errors dismiss`, `backup prune` and `backup restore`; F2's runner passes `--if-match` on confirm. It serves **G-M3-2** (destructive actions "confirmed first … the confirmed run is bound to the preview the user saw") and checkpoint criterion 13 ("destructive previews are binding": for `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`, a test changes state between `--dry-run` and the real run with `--if-match`; the real run refuses with `plan_stale` and changes nothing).

## Technical Approach

### The decision this task implements (M3-D46, operative rules)

- **A new global flag, `--if-match <TOKEN>`**, and a `precondition` key in the `--dry-run` data of the five commands it applies to: `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`. Elsewhere `--if-match` is a usage error naming those five.
- **The token** is `pc1:` plus four 16-hex-digit fields: the first 64 bits of a SHA-256 of each canonical part, namely the command path, `targets` (`[{key, generation}…]`), `selection` and `observed`. Keys are sorted, arrays sorted where order carries no meaning. Separate fields let a refusal say which part changed without any stored state. It is computed by one function, `app::precondition`, from the **same plan** the command executes:

  | Command | `selection` | `observed` | Task |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `remove` | addon names and the exact folders to delete, per target | nothing beyond `targets` (the record generation covers the selection's inputs) | A4 |
  | `undo` | the exact tx ids reverted; the folder plan; the SavedVariables files it would restore | the conflict verdict; for an undo of a whole restore, the live `WTF/` stamp digest (added by D6) | A4 (D6 extends) |
  | `backup restore` | backup id, mode, resolved folders and files | the source backup's `backup.json` digest; the live `WTF/` stamp digest (whole) or the candidate files' stamps (`--addon`). The generation is in `targets` | D8 |
  | `backup prune` | the exact backup ids it would delete, per target | each victim's `backup.json` digest | D4 |
  | `errors dismiss` | each database key it would acknowledge | each database file's stamp and session. Its `targets` part holds target keys **without** generations, because an addon update between reading and dismissing does not change what was shown. `--if-match` requires exactly the token's target set; the widget dismisses one target per call | B8 |

- **Applying.** With `--if-match`, the real run computes the token from its own plan, **before staging anything**. A different token fails with `plan_stale`, **not retryable** (`PlanStaleSource::Apply`). Retrying the same argv with the same token could only fail again, and README's rule that a retryable `plan_stale` reruns its own `fix_argv` would loop.
  - `details.changed` names the parts that differ, from the fixed set `command`, `targets`, `selection` and `observed`.
  - `fix_argv` is the same command with `--dry-run` in place of `--if-match <token>`: preview again. Nothing is changed.
  - Under the lock, the engine's existing generation check then compares against the plan's generations, which equal the token's, so a commit that sneaks in between plan and lock is caught too. **With `--if-match`, that refusal is not retryable either.**
  - Without `--if-match`, every command behaves as today: the token is an opt-in for previews, never a new requirement for typed commands.
- **Where tokens come from.** Every `--dry-run` of the five commands. `errors` (the read) also returns `targets[].dismiss.precondition` for the observation it shows (B6/B8), so dismissing what you just looked at needs no extra dry run.
- **Stateless.** Nothing is stored; a token is valid for exactly as long as the world it describes is unchanged. M4's `plan_id` can embed it.

### Contract (milestone epic comment "Contract additions, part 1 (§7.1–§7.5)", §7.1, and milestone epic comment "Contract additions, part 2 (§7.6–§7.11)", §7.6)

- **Global flag:** `--if-match <TOKEN>`, accepted by `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`; a usage error elsewhere. The token comes from those commands' `--dry-run` data (`data.precondition`) or, for `errors dismiss`, from `errors`' `targets[].dismiss.precondition`. A changed plan gives `plan_stale` and changes nothing.
- **`plan_stale`** (reused code): with `--if-match` it is **not retryable** (`PlanStaleSource::Apply`), `details.changed` is a subset of `command`, `targets`, `selection` and `observed`, and `fix_argv` is the `--dry-run` form of the same command.
- **Dry-run data key:** `precondition`, a `pc1:` token string. Where a command's dry-run and real data share one struct, the real run carries `precondition: null`, as the `backup restore` and `backup prune` shapes do (applying that to `remove` and `undo` was decided while writing this bead).

### Steps

1. **`src/app/precondition.rs` (new).**
   ```rust
   pub struct Precondition { command: &'static str, targets: Vec<(TargetKey, Option<u64> /* generation; None only for errors dismiss */)>, selection: serde_json::Value, observed: serde_json::Value }
   impl Precondition { pub fn token(&self) -> String /* "pc1:" + four 16-hex fields */ }
   pub fn check(expected: Option<&str>, actual: &Precondition, dry_run_argv: &[String]) -> Result<()>   // plan_stale (PlanStaleSource::Apply, not retryable) with details.changed and fix_argv = dry_run_argv
   ```
   - **Token layout:** `pc1:` followed by four 16-hex-digit fields (64 hex digits in all). Each is the first 64 bits of a SHA-256: of the command path, of the canonical `targets`, of `selection` and of `observed`, in that order. `check` can therefore name which part changed (`details.changed: ["observed"]`) without storing anything. 64 bits per part is ample for detecting staleness; **the token is not a security credential**.
   - **Canonical JSON:** keys sorted, arrays of ids sorted, numbers as integers, no floats. A test pins the bytes of a fixture token, so the format never drifts silently.
   - A token for another command path is `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["command"]`. `details.changed` only ever holds `command`, `targets`, `selection` and `observed`.
   - `check(None, …)` is a no-op: without `--if-match`, nothing changes.
   - The module declares the list of the five command paths that bind (`remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `errors dismiss`) as one public constant. Dispatch's usage check reads it, and F1's always-on Rust test checks `omarchy/Model.js`'s `CLI_PATHS[].binds` against it.
   - Keep the type independent of the widget, so M4's `plan_id` can embed the same `Precondition`.
   - **For B8 (decided when the beads were filed):** `errors dismiss`'s `targets` part holds target keys **without** generations (M3-D46). So the generation is an `Option<u64>`: every other command passes `Some(generation)`; `errors dismiss` passes `None`, which canonicalizes as a key-only entry (`{"key": …}` with no `generation` field), so B8 computes its token through this one function rather than a second encoding. A unit test pins both canonical forms.
2. **`src/cli.rs`:** a global `--if-match <TOKEN>` (`global = true`, value pattern `^pc1:[0-9a-f]{64}$`, else `usage`). `app::dispatch` rejects it with `usage` for every command path except the five of M3-D46. The usage message names the five commands of M3-D46 (`remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `errors dismiss`), read from the module's constant, which lists all five from the start; a path that does not exist yet simply cannot be dispatched.
3. **`remove` and `undo`** (the two that exist now):
   - their `--dry-run` data gains `precondition`;
   - their real path computes the same `Precondition` from its own plan, right after planning and before staging, and calls `check`;
   - the engine's lock-time generation check compares against the plan's generations, which equal the token's, so a commit between plan and lock still gives `plan_stale` (not retryable when `--if-match` was given);
   - `selection` and `observed` per the table above. For `undo`, `observed` covers the conflict verdict and the current state (stamps) of the SavedVariables files it would restore, so a SavedVariables file changed between preview and run moves the token; the whole-restore `WTF/` stamp digest is added by D6. Decided while writing this bead: M3-D46's table lists those files under `selection`, while this task's acceptance criterion names `observed` for a SavedVariables file changed in between; the file list stays in `selection` and their current stamps go into `observed`, which satisfies both (a rewritten file that was already going to be restored changes no list, only its stamp).
4. **Contract and README.** `precondition` (dry-run data), `--if-match`, `plan_stale`'s `details.changed`. README: a "Previews and --if-match" paragraph under the JSON contract (preview with `--dry-run --json`, then run with `--if-match <data.precondition>`; `plan_stale` means preview again), and the global options table.

### How it is used downstream (for context)

- **The widget runner (F2):** for `confirm` templates and destructive CLI argv, the dry run runs in the mutation lane, the dialog keeps `data.precondition`, and Yes runs the real argv with `--if-match <token>` when the path binds (and plainly when it does not, such as `targets rm`). A `plan_stale` answer reruns the dry run and replaces the dialog with "changed since you looked: …". `--if-match` is inserted with the other standard flags right after the binary, only with a validated token (`^pc1:[0-9a-f]{64}$`).
- **`errors dismiss` (B8):** bound without a dialog; the token is the `dismiss.precondition` of the `errors` read the Issues view shows, so a session that ended in between is never acknowledged unseen.
- **Agents:** `<command> --dry-run --json`, then `<command> --if-match <data.precondition>`; `plan_stale` means preview again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `remove X --dry-run` returns a token. `remove X --if-match <it>` succeeds unchanged. After a concurrent `install Y` on the same target (generation moved), the same token gives `plan_stale` (`details.changed: ["targets"]`, `retryable: false`, `fix_argv` = `remove X --dry-run …`) and nothing is removed.
- `undo --dry-run` then `--if-match`: a later commit on the target in between gives `plan_stale`. So does a SavedVariables file changed in between, when the undo would restore it (`observed`).
- A token for another command path gives `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["command"]`.
- `--if-match` on `update` is `usage`, naming the five commands (`remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `errors dismiss`). A malformed token (not `^pc1:[0-9a-f]{64}$`) is `usage`.
- Tokens are identical across two dry runs of an unchanged home, and differ when any covered input changes (unit table). A pinned fixture token's bytes never change.
- Commands without `--if-match` behave exactly as before (existing `remove` and `undo` tests and snapshots unchanged apart from the new `precondition` key in dry-run data).
- README documents "Previews and --if-match" and the new global option.

## Test Plan

- **Unit (`src/app/precondition.rs`):** canonicalization (sorted keys, sorted id arrays, integers only); the pinned fixture token; `check` naming each changed part (`command`, `targets`, `selection`, `observed`, and combinations); `check(None, …)` a no-op; the error's `retryable: false` and `fix_argv`.
- **E2E (`tests/preconditions.rs`, new):** the `remove` scenario with a concurrent `install Y`; the `undo` scenarios (a later commit; a SavedVariables file changed in between); a cross-command token; `--if-match` on `update`; a malformed token. B8, D4 and D8 extend this file for their commands.
- **Contract:** rows for `plan_stale` (with `details.changed` and the `--dry-run` `fix_argv`) and the usage error; `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` and help snapshots for the new global flag.

## Considerations

- **Commands typed without `--if-match` behave exactly as today.** The token is opt-in, so no existing script breaks.
- **M4's `plan_id` can embed the same `Precondition`.** Keep the type independent of the widget.
- **Why a token and not something else** (M3-D46 and M3-D9): rejected stored plans in M3 (an M4 deliverable with its own freeze); a per-command `--expect-*` flag set; a time-limited token (staleness is about state, not time); no preview at all; a preview with no binding (the first draft); binding by target generation alone (the game and external tools change `WTF/` and BugGrabber files without moving any generation, so restore and dismissal tokens also cover the files the preview observed).
- **Departure from the vision.** Vision §5.11 says "Mutating buttons first fetch a plan and then call apply". That arrives with M4; M3 brings only preview binding forward. G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) records both. List `--if-match`, `precondition` and `details.changed` in the close comment (common rule 6).
- **Design gate.** This task introduces a new protocol: preview binding, a small stateless contract that M4 can grow into stored plans (milestone epic comment "Rationale and confidence (§13)", §13.2). Where its risk lies (reasoning added while writing this bead): a canonical form that drifts (tokens that differ for an unchanged world break every confirm) or covers too little (a stale preview that still matches). It closes only when its adversarial tests (the unit table of covered inputs, the pinned token, and every state-change-between-preview-and-run scenario) are green (common rule 14).
- **Risk (milestone risk 21): a preview no longer describes what a confirmed action does** (likelihood medium, impact medium–high). Mitigation: precondition tokens on every destructive command; `plan_stale` refreshes the dialog; exact ids for prune and undo (M3-D46). Owners: A4, D4, D8, B8, F2.
- **Collision hot spots** (coordinate through `SendMessage` and claim comments listing files):
  - `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs` (dispatch), help tests: **A4's global flag first**; command tasks add their variants afterwards.
  - `src/app/remove.rs`, `src/app/undo.rs`: A2 refactors `select` in `undo.rs`; land A2's refactor first, or rebase. A4's token is a separate function.
- **Delivery.** Slice `slice-1` ("See and update from the bar"). Exit demo: `omarchy install` on the desktop; the badge follows a terminal `update` within 1 s; update one addon from the panel, undo it; **a `remove` preview gone stale gives `plan_stale`**; reinstall swaps atomically. A4 supplies the `plan_stale` part. Lane 2 takes A4 right after A2, because F2 needs it at t=5.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- none
**Unblocks:**
- B8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.8` (`errors dismiss`, durable acknowledgement): computes its precondition (database keys; file stamps and sessions; target keys without generations) through `app::precondition` and honours `--if-match`, binding a dismissal to the shown observation.
- D4 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.4` (Backup retention, space reclamation and `backup prune`): `backup prune` tokens (exact victim ids; each victim's `backup.json` digest).
- D8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.8` (The `backup restore` command): `backup restore` tokens (backup id, mode, resolved folders and files; source digest and live stamps).

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** The widget makes destructive actions two keystrokes away, and a confirm dialog that describes yesterday's world is worse than none: a `backup prune` could delete a different set than shown, and prune cannot be undone. This bead makes "Yes" mean "do exactly what I was shown, or nothing": the dry run returns a stateless token, and the real run refuses with `plan_stale` if the target, the selection or the observed files changed. Agents get the same guarantee with the same two calls. It costs one hash per destructive command, stores nothing, and changes nothing for commands typed without `--if-match`. B8, D4, D8 and the widget runner (F2) all build on it, and M4's stored plans can embed the same `Precondition`.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D46 (departs from the vision): destructive previews bind to a precondition token.** `--if-match <TOKEN>` on `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` (a usage error elsewhere); `pc1:` plus four 16-hex fields (command path, `targets` with generations, `selection`, `observed`), computed by one function from the same plan the command executes, before staging; a mismatch is `plan_stale`, not retryable (`PlanStaleSource::Apply`), with `details.changed` and the `--dry-run` form as `fix_argv`; the engine's lock-time generation check catches a commit between plan and lock. Why: it is the smallest contract that makes a confirm dialog mean what it says, and it reuses `plan_stale` and the existing generation check; generations alone miss changes the game and other tools make to `WTF/` and BugGrabber files. Rejected: stored plans in M3; a per-command `--expect-*` flag set; a time-limited token (staleness is about state, not time).
- **M3-D9 (departs from the vision): stored plans stay in M4; the widget previews destructive actions and binds the run to the preview.** Every row action uses exact identifiers (backup ids for prune, `undo --run <run>`), never "newest" or a count. Rejected: pulling stored plans forward (doubles the risk of two milestones); no preview; a preview with no binding (the first draft); binding by generation alone. Vision §5.11's "fetch a plan, then apply" arrives with M4; G2 records both departures.

**Review-round changes folded in.** This task is new in the third review (revision 7, adopted as proposed: stateless four-part tokens). As designed, `plan_stale` under `--if-match` is non-retryable, both at the token check and at the lock-time generation check, with the `--dry-run` form as `fix_argv`, because README's rule that a retryable `plan_stale` reruns its own `fix_argv` would otherwise loop on a stale token; and `details.changed` only ever holds the four part names.

**Facts verified during planning.** `PlanStaleSource::{Replan, Apply}` exists (`src/error.rs:494-555`), with `Apply` documented as "the stored plan can never apply; the fix is its dry-run argv"; the engine re-checks target generations under the lock; `remove` and `undo` have `--dry-run`; dispatch is one exhaustive match (`src/app/mod.rs:292-485`), so a per-path flag check has one home; `undo`'s run selection is `src/app/undo.rs:355-416`, which A2 makes a pure function first (all as of `af10e34`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A preview no longer describes the confirmed action (milestone risk 21, medium/medium–high): tokens on every destructive command, refreshed dialogs on `plan_stale`, exact ids.
- Canonical-form drift makes every token differ: canonical JSON with sorted keys and ids and integers only, a pinned fixture token, and an "identical across two dry runs" test.
- Covering too little: each command's `selection`/`observed` follows the M3-D46 table, and each binding task adds a test that changes state between preview and run.
- Hot spot `cli.rs`/`app/mod.rs`: A4's global flag lands before the command tasks add their variants.

**Confidence.** High: a small, stateless, contract-tested addition that reuses an existing error code and the engine's generation check; it is still a design gate and closes only with its adversarial tests green.

comments.text:
**Done: preview binding, `--if-match` and precondition tokens (A4).** Gate passed (fmt, clippy -D warnings, 1,636 tests with 0 failed and 53 ignored, ubs 0 critical on 23 changed files; cargo deny skipped, no dependency change). The design gate's adversarial tests are green: the unit table of covered inputs (each part moves only its own field, combinations, malformed tokens), the pinned fixture token (its four fields recomputed independently with `sha256sum` over the expected canonical texts), "identical across two dry runs", and every state-change-between-preview-and-run scenario.

**What landed**
- `src/app/precondition.rs` (new): `Precondition`, `Part`, `token()`, `check()`, `stale()`, `preview_argv()`, `is_token()`, `BINDING_COMMANDS`; `of_remove(&Plan)` and `of_undo(&[UndoPlanned])`; `RemoveBinding` and `UndoBinding`.
- Engine: `Binding` trait (`plan`, `undo`, `moved`) in `EngineCtx.binding`. `engine::run` asks `plan` after planning, before staging; the commit window refuses with `moved` when the target's generation moved since planning (before re-judging). `engine::undo` asks `undo` before staging and again with the plan made under the lock, before the journal. `UndoOutcome.plan: UndoFacts {generation, ops, saved_variables}` (not on the wire). `app::Engine::run_bound` / `undo_bound`.
- `FileStamp::fingerprint()` (dev, inode, type, mode, size, mtime, ctime) for observed SavedVariables.
- CLI: global `--if-match <TOKEN>`, `Context.if_match`, validated in `Context::new`.
- `remove` and `undo`: `data.precondition` (token under `--dry-run`, `null` otherwise); bound real runs.
- Tests: 7 unit tests in `precondition.rs`; `tests/preconditions.rs` (10 E2E: remove as previewed; a concurrent install before the run; a commit between plan and lock (pause at `engine.snapshot.prestaged`) for remove and for undo; bare undo after a later commit; `undo <tx>` after an unrelated commit; a SavedVariables file rewritten since the preview (`observed`); a cross-command token; usage errors; `--dry-run` with `--if-match`); contract rows `if_match_stale` and `if_match_unbound_command`; `remove_ok`, `undo_ok`, `undo_run` and `bare_help_json` snapshots re-accepted (only `precondition: null` and the new flag).
- README: global options row, "Previews and `--if-match`" under the JSON contract, the `plan_stale` row, `remove` and `undo` sections, the agents block.

**Wire names (DEC-4, for G2):** global flag `--if-match <TOKEN>`; data key `precondition` in `remove` and `undo` data (token `pc1:` + 64 lowercase hex under `--dry-run`, `null` on real runs); `plan_stale` under `--if-match`: `retryable: false`, `details.changed` (subset of `command`, `targets`, `selection`, `observed`), `fix_argv` = the `--dry-run` form; usage error for `--if-match` off the binding commands or with a malformed token. Constant `app::precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS` for F1's `CLI_PATHS[].binds` test.

**Decided while doing it**
- *Engine stays below app.* The token code is in `src/app/precondition.rs` as the bead says; the engine only knows a `Binding` trait, which the app implements, so no engine module depends on `app`.
- *Bound undo plans first.* With `--if-match`, `undo` plans every selected transaction as its preview did, checks the run's token before staging anything, then binds each transaction's undo to its own per-transaction token (re-checked under the lock against the plan made there).
- *Undo's parts:* `selection` = each transaction's id, folder operations (its history ops) and the SavedVariables paths it restores; `observed` = each transaction's verdict (`ok` or the error code that stops it) and the stamps of those files now. So a newer commit that changes what bare `undo` selects gives `selection` (with `targets` and `observed`), a commit on the target alone gives `targets`, a SavedVariables file rewritten since the preview gives `observed`.
- *Lock-time refusal for `remove`:* a generation that moved between plan and lock refuses before re-judging (without `--if-match` the old behaviour, re-judge and commit, is unchanged and tested). It reaches the envelope through the item path, so its `details` also carry `items` (the all-failed convention).
- *`--dry-run` with `--if-match`* previews afresh and returns the current token (no check).
- *Usage fixes:* off a binding command, a command that changes something gets `omaddons help <command>` and a read-only one gets its argv without the flag (a fix never hands over a changing command); a malformed token's fix is the preview.
