title: The `errors` command
description:
## Background

`omaddons errors` is the command that answers "**which addon is most likely throwing errors, how often, since when, and is there an update?**" from BugGrabber's data, on every client including 3.3.5a, for humans and agents alike (G-M3-3). Today that answer means opening `WTF/Account/<account>/SavedVariables/!BugGrabber.lua` by hand, or installing BugSack and reading it in game. Nothing in omaddons reads BugGrabber's data.

This task builds the command over the pieces the earlier B tasks provide: the SavedVariables parser (B1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.1`), the decoders (B3, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.3`), frames and attribution (B4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.4`), and the bounded locator and strict renderer (B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`). It writes **only** the derived errors memo in `<cache>` (M3-D20), so it stays a Look command (`mutates: false`).

**Its structure is the fix for three review findings** (review round 3, revision 9):
- one **canonical observation** per target is built first, from **every** local entry;
- the memo, the counts, `--check` and `status` derive from that observation;
- only then do the output filters apply, so a filtered or truncated view can never shrink what the bar knows (`errors --addon DBM --limit 1` must not make the widget think the other addons are clean).

**Ground truth this task relies on** (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.6, as of `af10e34`):
- **Write model.** The client writes SavedVariables only at logout, `/reload` and disconnect. A session's errors therefore reach the file when that session ends, and the next UI load starts with a higher `session` number. A running client's errors since its last `/reload` are not on disk yet.
- **Modern BugGrabber v12.1.0:** entries `{message, session, time = time(), counter, stack?, locals?}`; a repeat bumps `counter`, moves `time` to the latest occurrence, updates `session` and moves the entry to the end; `MAX_BUGGRABBER_ERRORS = 500`; DB keys `session` (+1 per UI load, reset to 1 by `/bugsack reset`), `errors`, `lastSanitation`, `stopnag`, and sometimes leftover `save`, `limit`, `throttle`.
- **`time` has four meanings and two types, with no version field:** v10.1–v12.0.2 a local-time string of the first capture; v12.0.3–v12.0.9 a string of the last occurrence; v12.0.11+ a unix integer of the last occurrence; r152 (3.3.5a) a string of the first capture in the session.
- **r152 (3.3.5a):** `message` is a string or up to 7 chunks of ≤ 980 bytes plus `type` (`error`/`event`); no `stack` or `locals` key (both embedded in `message` after `"\nLocals:|r\n"`, with a trailing `"\n  ---"`); duplicates merge only within one session, so it writes one entry per session and duplicate.
- **Received reports.** BugSack's `OnBugComm` (`core.lua:177-200`) stores errors another player sends through the addon channel into `BugGrabberDB.errors`, with `source = sender` and `session` set to the **current local session**, keeping the sender's `time` and `counter`, with no duplicate check. BugGrabber itself never sets `source`. Without filtering, a friend's error would count as "new on this machine" and suggest updating a local addon.
- `Remembered`, the release-memo evaluator that knows each managed addon's latest version offline, is `pub(super) struct Remembered` in `src/app/status.rs:599` (used at `:392`, evaluated over `:599-688`).
- `history::parse_since(s, now)` (`src/app/history.rs:381`) already parses `--since` values (`30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `2w`, or an RFC 3339 time) for `history`.
- `tests/status.rs::status_writes_nothing` (`tests/status.rs:154`) hashes state, cache and client dirs across `status` runs; `status` must stay write-free, which is why the memo lives in `<cache>` and is written by `errors`, never by `status`.
- The bare-help Look line is 72 columns today; adding `errors` makes it wrap (`render_groups` supports continuation lines; `src/app/help.rs:145-171`, test `:404-444`).

**Checkpoint criterion 6** (milestone epic body) is mostly this task's:
- it parses synthetic fixtures for every BugGrabber era and both file formats, and attributes each error to the right managed addon with method and confidence;
- default and `-v` output contain only code-derived text; custom messages, locals and chunk contents appear only with `--raw-details`; no output on any channel prints an account, realm or character name;
- received reports are listed apart and never count as new, never notify and never cause an update recommendation;
- filtered reads (`--addon`, `--since`, `--limit`) never change the memo or `status`'s counts; `--since` reports uncertain matches instead of silently dropping them;
- parsing stays within its budgets on adversarial files, and an over-budget file is reported as incomplete and not retried on every doorbell.

**Decisions that shape it, in one line each** (full text in the milestone epic's decision log):
- **M3-D18:** attribute to the first non-library addon frame, with `method` and `confidence`; say "likely source", never "caused by"; offer an update as "may fix it".
- **M3-D19:** "new" is decided per database against a baseline (memo first-read baseline, later the durable acknowledgement), an age limit against the clock, and never for received reports.
- **M3-D20:** the memo is derived, written only from the complete observation, only when its content changed, and holds no message text.
- **M3-D21:** strict output by default; `--raw-details` for free text; privacy on every channel; received reports apart.
- **M3-D22:** `errors` exits 0 whether or not errors exist; `--check` exits 6 on new local errors or an incomplete read, judged before `--limit`.
- **M3-D44:** the bounded lookup (B5), plus the per-invocation byte budget enforced here.
- **M3-D39:** Look gains `errors` after `search`; the line wraps.
- **M3-D4 (via A1):** `errors` rings the doorbell when it changed the memo.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/app/errors.rs`: arguments and command surface

```text
omaddons errors [-t T] [--since D] [--addon A] [--limit N] [--received] [--raw-details] [--check]
```

`ErrorsArgs { since: Option<String>, addon: Option<String>, limit: Option<usize>, received: bool, raw_details: bool, check: bool }`.
- Global `-t` selects many (M2's `World::select_many`); the default is **every** target.
- `--since D` takes what `history --since` takes: parse with `history::parse_since(s, crate::clock::now())` (A1's clock seam, so tests can freeze time with `OMADDONS_NOW`). A bad value is a `usage` error with fix argv `omaddons errors --since 1d` (decided while writing this bead, mirroring `history`'s own error at `src/app/history.rs:257-264`).
- `--limit N` defaults to 10 addons per target; `--limit 0` is a `usage` error.
- `errors dismiss` is B8's subcommand (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.8`); this task leaves room for it (an optional subcommand under `errors`, so bare `errors` is the read).

### 2. Per target: the canonical observation (`errors::Observation`)

Built from every local entry, **before** any filter:
1. **`locate`** (bounded, B5): candidate files, `capture`, `skipped` counts, `coverage`, listing fingerprints.
2. **Read** each file with `lua::read_bounded` (B1), within the invocation's `ERRORS_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` (256 MiB across every target of one invocation).
   - A file over `SAVEDVARIABLES_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB, `InputTooLarge`), or past the remaining invocation budget, gives the warning `errors_partial` with read outcome `over_budget` (and its `FileStamp`, so the unchanged file is reported as incomplete rather than re-read on every doorbell).
   - A read error gives `errors_partial` with `io` text (the message names no path below `WTF/Account/`; use `account N` labels).
3. **Parse** with `parse_saved_variables(bytes, &["BugGrabberDB"])` (skip mode: no other global is built). `!complete` (EOF inside a value: a file being written at logout) gives `errors_partial`, outcome `partial`, and keeps the entries read before the cut.
4. **Decode** (B3): one **database** per file, with id `db-<n>`, the account ordinal (B5's 1-based label `account N`), the provider folder (`!BugGrabber` or the embedding addon), `shape` (`modern`/`legacy`), the DB `session`, and the read state (`complete`, `partial`, `over_budget`).
5. **Attribute** each entry (B4): `attribute(message, stack, entry.entry_type == EntryType::Event, &installed_folders, legacy)` gives `target` (`Addon`/`Library`/`Blizzard`/`Unknown`), `method` and `confidence`. The `FolderSet` comes from the target's inventory (every AddOns folder, case-insensitive like `FolderName::key()`). The folder then maps to the managed addon that records it (`TargetRecord`; DBM-Core and DBM-GUI both map to DBM); an unmanaged folder is listed under its folder name with `managed: false`.
6. **Split by `origin`.** `Received` entries (a `source` key was present; B3's `Origin` keeps no value) go to a separate, counted list and **never** enter the local groups, the new counts, `--check`, `commands[]` or the memo's addon counts.
7. **Group the local entries:**
   - group key `(addon or folder, kind)`, where `kind` is `addon`, `library` (attributed to a library folder only), `blizzard` or `unknown`;
   - inside a group, merge entries with the same **normalized message** within one database. Normalizing means: the first line only (r152's `\n  ---` tail and embedded stack removed); UI escape codes stripped; for BugGrabber ≤ v12.0.2 data, library version suffixes undone (`AceAddon-3.0-13` → `AceAddon-3.0`). Line numbers are kept. r152's per-session duplicates merge this way;
   - the aggregates, for each merged error and for each addon group (the JSON carries `count`, `new`, `entries` and `last_seen` on the addon, and `count`, `sessions`, `new` and `last_seen` on each error): `count = Σ counter`, `entries = n`, `sessions` = distinct `(database, session)` pairs, `last_seen` = the aggregate time evidence keeping the **weakest** meaning of what it combined (§9.2), and `new` (below);
   - each error gets its strict rendering (B5: `message_kind`, `message` or `message_chars`, `location`, strict `stack`), its `fingerprint` (B5, over the normalized message and location) and its `database` id;
   - the decoder never merges; merging is this step's job.
8. **Sort** addons by `new` count, then `count`, then name, descending.

**The "new" rule in this task** (M3-D19, inlined; B8 later adds the acknowledgement and its time clause through one shared function, `errors::session_is_new`):
- "New" is decided **per database**: one BugGrabber file of one account, or one embedding provider's file. Sessions are counted per database and never compared or merged across databases (a target with two accounts, or with an embedded copy, has independent counters).
- **The first-read baseline** is an observation kept in the memo. It is set when `errors` first reads a database with no memo entry: to `DB session − 1`, so that only the latest UI session's errors count as new (B8 changes this to the acknowledged session when a valid acknowledgement exists). Afterwards it never moves on its own: errors from every later session, including several `/reload`s in one evening, stay new until dismissed.
- **Reset and replacement.** When a read observes a database whose `session` is **below** the memo's first-read baseline (`/bugsack reset`, a restored `WTF/`, a copied file), the baseline cannot belong to this database's history: rewrite it to 0 in the memo, so everything since the reset is new. That stays true after the reset database passes the old number again (the rewrite is sticky).
- **An entry is new** when it is local, its database's file mtime is within `ERRORS_NEW_MAX_AGE` (7 days) **at the time of the read** (judged against `crate::clock::now()`), and its `session` is greater than the baseline.
- r152 writes one entry per session and duplicate, so the same rules apply per entry.

**Time evidence** (decoded by B3, used here; inlined from the decoding rules):
- meaning: `last` (an integer time, the last occurrence), `first_or_last` (a string time: the first capture in ≤ v12.0.2 and r152, the last occurrence in v12.0.3–v12.0.9; the file cannot say which), or `unknown`;
- tz: `explicit` (a unix time) or `system_assumed` (a local string read in this machine's time zone, which may not be the zone that wrote it, for example an imported `WTF/`);
- a `first_or_last` time is a **lower bound** on the last occurrence: it is never labelled as the last occurrence, and it can never prove that an entry is older than a cutoff;
- `TimeEvidence::at_or_after(cutoff)` is `Yes` when a time proves the entry occurred at or after the cutoff (any meaning: even a first capture after the cutoff proves it), `No` only for a `last` time before it, and `Uncertain` for a `first_or_last` time before it or no time at all.

### 3. The memo (`src/errors/memo.rs`)

`<cache>/errors.json`, kind `errors_memo` 1.0 (`Versioned`, with a `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` row). It is written **from the complete observation only** (step 2), before any filter. Per target key and per database it stores (M3-D20):
- each file's path relative to the client dir (local only) and its `FileStamp`;
- each `SavedVariables/` dir's listing fingerprint (B5);
- the DB `session` and the first-read baseline (M3-D19), with the reset rewrite above;
- per-session counts of local entries, `{session: {entries, occurrences, newest_time}}`, where `newest_time` is that session's newest time evidence (meaning and tz included). `new` can then be recomputed against the baseline, a later acknowledgement and the clock without the file (B7 does this in `status --cached`);
- totals per database (entries and occurrences of local entries);
- `received` (a count only);
- per-addon counts (`addon`, `folder`, `count`, `new`, `last_seen` with its time meaning). **Decided while drafting this bead:** keep the per-addon counts broken down by session within each database, so B7 can recompute `targets[].errors.top[].new` exactly as it recomputes the database totals, and the widget's toast never names an addon whose errors aged out or were dismissed;
- the read outcome per database: `complete`, `partial` (with its reason) or `over_budget` (with its stamp);
- the target's `capture` (`buggrabber`, `none`) and its probe coverage (accounts and files examined against the bounds, M3-D44).

**It stores no message, stack or locals text.** Deleting it deletes observations only; dismissals live in `<state>` (B8).

It is written through `WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Derived, …)`, **only when its encoding changed**, and then the doorbell rings (`doorbell::ring(paths, "errors", ctx.actor)`, A1). A write failure is ignored (derived and best effort, like the release memo); it never fails the command. Any new stamp or listing fingerprint changes the encoding, so a `stale` state in `status` always converges after one `errors` run.

### 4. The view (`Observation → ErrorsData`), after the memo

- **`--since D`:** each local entry is partitioned by `TimeEvidence::at_or_after(cutoff)` into `matched` (`Yes`), `uncertain` (`Uncertain` with a `first_or_last` time before the cutoff) and `no_time` (no usable time). Only `matched` entries are listed, and every count is reported (`summary.matched`, `summary.uncertain`, `summary.no_time`). The human footer names the others: `2 older first-seen errors may have recurred since then (string times cannot tell); 1 has no time`.
- **`--addon A`:** by addon name or folder, case-insensitive.
- **`--limit N`** (default 10 addons per target): `summary.matched` and `summary.shown` always say what was cut. Totals never depend on `--limit`.
- **`--received`** also lists received entries, in their own addon groups marked `"origin": "received"`, never counted as new. Without it, received entries appear only as the per-target `received` count.
- **`--raw-details`** adds each error's `raw` block (B5's `raw_details`, with the client's `WtfPathRedactor`) and sets `data.raw_details: true`. The human output prints the warning line "raw details may contain other players' names and your own code; share with care".
- **`-v`** adds the full frame list (up to `ERRORS_STACK_LINES_VERBOSE` = 40) and `files[].path`, relative to the client dir with the account folder replaced by `account N`.

### 5. `--check` (M3-D22)

`errors` exits 0 whether or not errors exist: errors are status, not failure. A target without BugGrabber is listed with `capture: "none"` and an install hint in `commands`, which is not an error.

`--check` evaluates the **observation** with only the selection filters (`-t`, `--addon`, and `--since`, with `uncertain` counting as matching because a check must not pass by dropping an error that may be recent), **never** `--limit`. It exits 6 (`check_failed`, `data` kept) when, for any selected target:
- it has new local errors; **or**
- its observation is incomplete: a selected database is `partial` or `over_budget`, every candidate file failed to read (`unreadable`), or the walk hit a bound (`coverage: truncated`). The error's `details.reason` is `"incomplete"`. A check cannot certify what it could not read.

### 6. `latest` without the network

Managed addons get `version` and `latest: {version, status}` from `Remembered`, the release-memo evaluator, with no network I/O. Move `Remembered` from `src/app/status.rs:599-688` (`pub(super)`) to a new `src/app/remembered.rs` (`pub(crate)`), shared by `status`, `list` and `errors`. This is a **pure move**, with no behaviour change; its tests move with it.

### 7. `dismiss.precondition` (added by B8)

Per target, B8's token over the observed databases (file stamp and session per database), computed with `app::precondition` (A4) once B8 lands. Until then the key is absent; B8 adds it, and its contract snapshot.

### 8. `commands[]`

- Per target, **`update <addons with new local errors and update_available> -t <id>`**, one argv for all of them, action `update`, `destructive: false`. Received entries never contribute.
- `errors dismiss -t <id>` (action `dismiss_errors`) when `new > 0`: added by B8.
- When `capture == None`: `search buggrabber` (action `install_buggrabber`). C3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3`) later replaces it with `install buggrabber -t <id>`, and "no BugGrabber build for this client is known" when no catalog variant covers the target's family.
- Every argv parses (contract rule), and the update argv updates exactly the listed addons.

### The data flow this command is part of (milestone epic comment "Architecture (§6)", §6.3)

```text
game exits ─► Hyprland closewindow ─► Service: debounce 500 ms ─► status --cached
   status: targets[retail].running=false (was true); errors.state="stale" (BugGrabber file stamp changed)
   Service: mutation lane  ← backup create --auto -t retail   (post-session; "unchanged" if nothing was played)

      errors: locate files (bounded) → lua::parse (skip mode, BugGrabberDB only) → decode
              → canonical observation (every local entry; received ones apart) → attribute → group
              → write errors memo from the complete observation if changed → ring doorbell
              → apply --since/--addon/--limit to the view only
   Service: doorbell → status --cached → errors.state="ok", errors.new=4 (recomputed: ack, clock)
            summary.state="errors" → bar urgent; notifyErrors → one toast (addon names, counts)
```

- **Strict privacy:**
  - the `personal` and `custom_names` scenarios print no `FakeChar`, `FakeRealm`, GUID, chunk text or custom message by default or with `-v`, while runtime messages appear in full;
  - `--raw-details` shows the custom message with the client's own names replaced and GUIDs redacted, sets `data.raw_details: true`, and prints the warning line;
  - `assert_private_all` passes over stdout and stderr (with `--progress json`) for every test home, with and without `-v`, and with `--raw-details`.
- **Canonical observation:**
  - `errors --addon DBM --limit 1` followed by `status --cached` reports the same totals and new counts as a plain `errors` run would;
  - with 12 affected addons, `--limit 10` shows 10, `summary.matched` is 12, and `status`'s counts include all 12;
  - `--check --limit 1` fails when the eleventh addon has new errors.
- **Received:** the `received` scenario's entries are not new, are absent from `commands`, appear only as a count without `--received`, and as marked groups (`origin: received`) with it.
- **Time:** in `mixed_times`, `--since 1d` lists the integer-time entry that is newer than a day, and reports the old string-time entry as `uncertain`, not dropped. `--check --since 1d` fails when that uncertain entry is new.
- **Databases:** `two_accounts` reports two databases with independent sessions and baselines.
- The first read marks the latest session's errors new. A second `errors` run keeps the same new flags, and errors from two later sessions (a `/reload` in between) are both new.
- A DB `session` reset to 1 (simulated `/bugsack reset`) voids the old baseline, so everything since the reset is new (M3-D19). After the reset database passes the old first-read baseline again, with no dismissal, its errors are still new (the memo baseline was rewritten to 0).
- A file older than 7 days has no new errors (the mtime is set in the test, the clock frozen with `OMADDONS_NOW`).
- A truncated file (EOF mid-entry) gives `errors_partial` and the entries before the cut. An over-budget file is recorded as `over_budget` with its stamp, and `--check` fails on it with `details.reason: "incomplete"`; truncated coverage also fails `--check` as incomplete.
- A target without BugGrabber is listed with `capture: "none"`, exit 0, and a `search buggrabber` hint (action `install_buggrabber`); `errors --addon <A> -t <id>` on such a target gives `not_found` (§7.6).
- `status_writes_nothing` still passes. `errors` writes only `<cache>/errors.json`, and only when something changed (a second run leaves its mtime unchanged), and rings the doorbell only when it wrote.
- Every argv in `commands` parses. The update argv updates exactly the listed addons.
- `errors` is in `COMMANDS` (Look, `mutates: false`), appears after `search` in bare help (which stays under 30 lines and 80 columns), has its `special.rs` read-only row, and its contract matrix rows (success, `--check` exit 6, `--check` incomplete, unknown `-t`, `--limit 0`) pass with snapshots.
- `Remembered` lives in `src/app/remembered.rs` and `status`/`list` behave exactly as before (their tests and snapshots unchanged).
- `ERRORS_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` and `ERRORS_NEW_MAX_AGE` are registered; `errors_partial` is registered and counted; `errors_memo` has a `KINDS` row.

- **Contract:** matrix rows with snapshots (success, `--check` exit 6, `--check` incomplete, unknown `-t`, `--limit 0`), `special.rs` read-only invocation, bare-help snapshots and `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` literals, the `help.rs` layout test.
- **Unit (`src/errors/mod.rs`, `src/app/errors.rs`):** grouping and the normalized-message merge (r152 per-session duplicates, ≤ v12.0.2 library suffixes); observation-before-view (filters never touch the memo input); the `--since` partition table; the new-flag rules per database (first read, reset rewrite, age); `commands` building (received never contribute).
- **Moved tests:** `Remembered`'s tests move to `src/app/remembered.rs` unchanged.
- **Perf** stays B1's (4 MB parse under 20 ms); B7 adds the `status --cached` budget with a memo present.

## Considerations

- **Observation first, view second.** Every count the bar or `--check` uses comes from the complete observation. Never compute a count after a filter.
- **No stale fallback in the memo.** The memo is written only from a complete observation; a partial or over-budget read is recorded as such with its stamp, never as zero errors.
- **Running clients.** Errors since the last `/reload` are not on disk while a client runs; the human output says so. `errors` never reads or touches anything the game holds open beyond a read.
- **Attribution is a heuristic.** A stack shows where an error surfaced, not proof of its root cause; method and confidence are always shown (risk 6, mitigated by B4's table tests and this wording).
- **Risk 13 (personal data leaks; L, H):** strict output on kinds of text; free text only with `--raw-details`; one path redactor for progress, warnings and errors; `assert_private_all` with adversarial names; no message text in the memo. This task owns the command-level enforcement.
- **Risk 5 (BugGrabber changes its schema or write model; M, M):** the tolerant decoder (B3) ignores unknown keys; a mid-session write model would break M3-D19's session watermarks, and C2's live probe of upstream `BugGrabber.lua` is the tripwire.
- **Collision hot spots** (coordinate with `SendMessage` and claim comments listing files):
  - `src/error.rs` (B6, B8, D2, D3, D5, D8, D9, E2, E4): additive rows plus count bumps; merge conflicts are trivial, but the counts must be right;
  - `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs`, help tests (A4, B6, B8, D1, D2, D4, D8, D9, D10, D13, E2, E3): one `Command` variant per top-level command (`errors`); B8 adds the `dismiss` subcommand variant;
  - `src/limits.rs` and its snapshot: re-accept the snapshot in each task;
  - `src/app/status.rs` (A2, B7, D11, E4): this task only moves `Remembered` out; coordinate with A2's restructure (land after A2 or rebase).
- **Lane and slack.** Lane 3 (Errors): A1 → B1 → B3 → **B6** → B8 → B7 → F6 → E4. The errors lane has about 3 units of slack; not on either critical path.
- **Delivery slice `slice-2` (S2, "Capture and diagnose").** Exit demo: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal. Pre-checks checkpoint criteria 6, 7, 8 (create, auto, verify) and 13 (`errors dismiss`, `backup prune`). This task is the "`errors` on every client" part.
- **Real machine.** At G3, `errors` runs read-only on every client (no BugGrabber data exists on the development machine, so the real-machine run proves the `capture: none` path and the bounds; synthetic fixtures prove decoding, a documented limitation recorded at G3).

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- A1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.1` (The doorbell file and its ring sites): `doorbell::ring` after a changed memo write, and the `crate::clock::now()` seam (`OMADDONS_NOW`) for the age rule and `--since`.
- B2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.2` (Synthetic BugGrabber fixtures): every E2E scenario, in both writer formats, and `tests/common/privacy.rs` names.
- B3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.3` (BugGrabber decoders): `decode`, `BugEntry`, `Origin`, `EntryType`, `TimeEvidence` and `at_or_after`.
- B4 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.4` (Frames and attribution): `attribute` with `method` and `confidence`, and `FolderSet`.
- B5 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5` (Locating `BugGrabberDB` within bounds, and the strict privacy renderer): `locate`, listing fingerprints, the strict renderer, `fingerprint` and `raw_details`.

**Unblocks:**
- B7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7` (Errors in `status`): the memo (per-session counts, stamps, fingerprints, read outcomes) that `status --cached` validates and recomputes from, and the live observation plain `status` runs.
- B8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.8` (`errors dismiss`, durable acknowledgement): the observation it acknowledges, the memo it rewrites, and the read whose `dismiss.precondition` it adds.
- C3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3` (BugGrabber in the catalog: disjoint family variants): the `install_buggrabber` hint it replaces with `install buggrabber -t <id>`.
- F8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.8` (`Service.qml`, part 2: Hyprland, auto-check, post-session triggers, notifications): the `errors_target` template it adds calls this command.

B7 inherits B2's fixtures through this task. Parent: the B epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2`. Delivery slice: `slice-2`.

comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** Today "my UI is broken" means opening `!BugGrabber.lua` by hand or reading BugSack in game. After this bead it is `omaddons errors`: which addon most likely threw errors, how often, since when, whether an update exists, with the update command attached and the attribution evidence shown, on every client including 3.3.5a, and without printing a name. Agents get the same answer as JSON (`errors --since 1d --json`, then `commands[]`). It is the read side of the whole errors feature: B7 makes the bar urgent from its memo, B8 dismisses what it showed, C3 makes its install hint a one-command BugGrabber install, F6 renders it in the Issues view, and F8 runs it after every play session. It keeps the thesis true: omaddons is the one authority over every client's addons, and now it can also say which of them is failing.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D18: attribution with evidence.** First non-library addon frame, else the first library frame's folder, else `blizzard` or `unknown`; every result carries `method` and `confidence`; output says "likely source" and offers updates as "may fix it". Why: a "first library frame" rule blames whichever addon's CallbackHandler copy won LibStub's race (Questie issue 7959). Rejected: the message location only (truncated, often a library).
- **M3-D19: what counts as new.** Per database; the first-read baseline (`DB session − 1` on first read) never moves on its own; a session below the baseline (reset, replaced database) rewrites it to 0, stickily; a file older than 7 days at the time of the read has no new errors; received reports are never new. B8 adds the acknowledgement and its time clause. Rejected: time windows (the meaning of `time` varies by version); no dismissing (a permanent urgent state); storing dismissals in the cache (the first draft).
- **M3-D20: the errors memo is derived; `status` stays write-free.** Written by `errors` only from the complete observation, only when its encoding changed, with no message text; per-session counts with newest times so `status --cached` can recompute `new` against the clock. Rejected: `status --cached` parsing on every call (2–20 ms per file breaks the 5 ms budget); letting `status` write the memo (breaks the read-only invariant).
- **M3-D21: privacy on every channel.** Strict output by default, `--raw-details` for free text with a warning line and `raw_details: true`, received reports apart and never counted, `assert_private_all` over both streams. Rejected: pattern redaction of first lines (cannot recognize names); hiding templates too (loses diagnostic value); `-v` as the free-text switch.
- **M3-D22: exit codes.** `errors` exits 0 whether or not errors exist; `--check` exits 6 on new local errors or an incomplete observation (`details.reason: "incomplete"`), counting `uncertain` as matching and ignoring `--limit`. Why: it matches `outdated --check` and the exit dictionary.
- **M3-D44: the bounded lookup** (B5) plus the 256 MiB per-invocation budget, enforced here.
- **M3-D39: help layout.** `errors` joins Look after `search`; the line wraps.
- **M3-D4 (via A1): the doorbell.** `errors` rings it only when the memo changed, so the bar follows.

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 3, revision 9 (adopted): the canonical observation is built first from every local entry, and the memo, counts, `--check` and `status` derive from it; filters apply only to the view; received reports are excluded everywhere; attribution evidence and "likely" wording; freshness recomputed against the clock.
- Round 3, revision 14 (adopted): time meaning and zone evidence, the `--since` partition with `uncertain`, and `databases[]` with per-database sessions.
- Round 3, revision 11 (adopted): per-invocation byte budget; over-budget files remembered with their stamp, not re-read on every doorbell.
- Round 3, revision 8 (adapted, completed by B8): per-database session watermarks rather than per-fingerprint ones, because BugGrabber writes only when a UI session ends.
- Round 1: the memo converges (listing fingerprints), and "new" uses a per-file baseline session.
- Decided while drafting this bead: the memo keeps per-addon counts broken down by session within each database, so B7 can recompute `top[].new` exactly; `--check` treats truncated coverage and an all-unreadable target as incomplete, as M3-D22 lists.

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`:
- `Remembered` is `pub(super)` at `src/app/status.rs:599` (evaluator over `:599-688`); moving it is a pure refactor.
- `history::parse_since` (`src/app/history.rs:381`) parses `30m`/`12h`/`1d`/`2w` or RFC 3339.
- `COMMANDS` is at `src/app/mod.rs:109-138` with `search` in Look; `target_not_found` is exit 3 (`src/error.rs:155`); `check_failed` exits 6.
- `tests/status.rs:154` (`status_writes_nothing`) guards the read-only invariant.
- BugSack's `OnBugComm` (`core.lua:177-200`) stores received reports with `source` and the current local session (ground truth comment, §2.6); the client writes SavedVariables only at logout, `/reload` and disconnect.
- 41 warning codes exist today (`src/error.rs:239-312`, count asserted at `:809`); `errors_partial` is one of the eight M3 adds.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk 13, personal data leaks (L, H): strict renderer, raw only on request, one redactor, adversarial-name tests on both streams, no text in the memo.
- Risk 6, wrong attribution (M, M): evidence always shown; "likely source"; library and Blizzard fallbacks named by `kind`.
- Risk 5, BugGrabber schema or write-model change (M, M): tolerant decoding; C2's live probe of upstream field names; a mid-session write model would show up there before it misleads users.
- A filtered read shrinking the bar's knowledge: designed out by observation-before-view, with an explicit E2E test.
- Plan confidence: the memo's per-addon-per-session breakdown is a drafting decision; if it proves heavy, the alternative is to zero `top[].new` for databases whose recomputed `new` is 0, which is exact for aging and dismissal but not for the time clause.

**Confidence.** High: the parser and decoder handle a regular input format, fuzzed and resource-tested, with synthetic fixtures for every documented shape; the command layer follows M2's `outdated` patterns (derived memo, offline `latest`, `--check` exit 6). Attribution accuracy on rare stack shapes stays medium (§13.3, B4's), which is why every error shows its method and confidence.

Handoff from B3 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.3, landed), for the `errors` command.

What: the decoder is
`errors::buggrabber::decode(&parsed.globals["BugGrabberDB"]) -> BugDb { session, shape, entries (oldest to newest), dropped }`.
Why: each `BugEntry` carries `message`, `stack`, `locals`, `session`, `time: Option<BugTime>`, `counter ≥ 1`, `entry_type` and `origin`. `origin == Received` entries are BugSack's received reports: exclude them by origin, never by session.
How:
- `evidence(entry.time.as_ref(), &TimeZone::system())` gives the `TimeEvidence` the wire calls `last_seen`; it already serializes as `{at, meaning, tz}`.
- Aggregate with `TimeEvidence::weakest`.
- `at_or_after(cutoff)` gives `Tri::{Yes, No, Uncertain}` for the `--since` partition: matched, or uncertain / no_time.
- `--check` counts `Uncertain` as matching (M3-D22).
Risks: `BugDb`, `BugEntry` and `BugTime` do not derive `Serialize`. Map them into the `errors` data structs, with the field `entry_type` on the wire as `type`.
Done when: the `errors` data carries these values with the contract's wire names.

Handoff from B4 and B5 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.4 and .2.5, landed). The inputs B6 composes, per target:

title: Errors in `status`
description:
## Background

The bar's urgent state, the widget's after-session errors refresh and its "Lua errors in your last session" toast all hinge on one thing: `status` knowing about Lua errors **cheaply** (inside the 5 ms budget of `status --cached`), **correctly as time passes** (an error that was new yesterday may not be new today, without anyone rereading the file), and **honestly** when a read was incomplete (a file the game was still writing is never a clean zero).

`status` knows nothing about Lua errors today (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.2, as of `af10e34`):
- `StatusData` is `{cached, targets[], journal, needs_attention}` (`src/app/status.rs:65-171`); `StatusTarget` carries running, missing, folders, addons, `updates{…}`, drift, adoptable, orphans and `attention[]`. There is no severity, no Lua error count, no backup info and no "last change".
- `status --cached` measured 3 ms on the development machine with seven targets; `tests/perf.rs:300-410` asserts a median under 5 ms.
- `status` changes no state: `tests/status.rs:154-163` (`status_writes_nothing`) hashes state, cache and client dir across `status`, `status --cached` and `status --cached --offline`. So `status` may read the errors memo but must never write it (M3-D20).

This task adds `targets[].errors` and fills A2's `summary.errors` (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.2` created the `summary` struct with a zero `errors` block for this task to fill). It reads two files: the derived errors memo `<cache>/errors.json` that `errors` writes (B6, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6`), and the durable acknowledgement `<state>/errors_ack.json` that `errors dismiss` writes (B8, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.8`).

**Why it needs both B6 and B8.** The memo holds observations (stamps, per-session counts, newest times, first-read baselines); the acknowledgement holds the user's dismissals. `new` must be **recomputed on every call** from the two, plus each file's age against the clock, through the one function B8 defines, `errors::session_is_new`. That is what makes `status --cached` and `errors` always agree, and what lets a dismissal survive `rm -r <cache>`.

**Goals and checkpoints served.**
- G-M3-1 (glanceable: the bar is current within a second; opening the panel costs no network) and G-M3-5 (the contract carries the widget: one `status --cached --json` answers everything the bar shows).
- Checkpoint criterion 4 (widget states: "new Lua errors" renders), criterion 6 (filtered `errors` reads never change `status`'s counts; received reports never count; an over-budget file is not retried on every doorbell) and criterion 10 (`status --cached` stays under 5 ms at the median, with p95 and cold start recorded, on a heavy home with a 2 MB BugGrabber file per target and 16 accounts on one target).

**Decisions that shape it, in one line each:**
- **M3-D20:** the memo is derived and written only by `errors`/`errors dismiss`; `status --cached` validates it with lstats and bounded listings, recomputes `new`, and reports `stale`, `unchecked` or `partial` honestly; plain `status` parses live and writes nothing.
- **M3-D19:** the baseline and new rule, the acknowledgement's time clause, and the 7-day age limit recomputed against the clock on every call.
- **M3-D21:** received reports never count in `status`.
- **M3-D37:** `status` grows triage blocks shared by the widget and agents; `summary.state` priority `attention > errors > updates > idle`.
- **M3-D44:** the probe stays within `ERRORS_MAX_ACCOUNTS` account dirs, and hitting it is `coverage: "truncated"`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `StatusTarget.errors: TargetErrors` (new key, after the existing ones; wire order is declaration order)

The contract (milestone epic comment "Contract additions, part 1", §7.2):

```json
"errors":{"capture":"buggrabber","state":"ok","coverage":"complete","new":4,"total":11,"addons":3,"received":1,
          "top":[{"addon":"DBM","folder":"DBM-Core","new":3,"count":7}],
          "last_session_at":"2026-10-21T18:40:02Z","dismissed_at":null}
```

- **`capture`:** `buggrabber` or `none`. For `none` the state is `ok` with zero counts.
- **`state`:**
  - `ok`;
  - `stale`: a recorded BugGrabber file's stamp changed, or a `SavedVariables/` dir's listing fingerprint (its sorted file names) changed since the memo;
  - `unchecked`: no memo entry for this target (while `capture` is BugGrabber);
  - `partial`: the last read was incomplete, because the file was being written, over a cap or bound, or damaged. The counts are what was read, **never presented as a clean zero**;
  - `unreadable`: every candidate file failed to read.
- **`coverage`:** `complete` or `truncated` (an `ERRORS_MAX_*` bound was hit, M3-D44).
- **`new`:** recomputed on every call from the memo's per-session counts, the acknowledgement and each file's age against the clock (M3-D19). Never a `new` count frozen into the memo.
- **`total`**, **`addons`** (affected local addons), **`received`** (reports from other players, which are never new). The plan does not define `total`. §7.2's example `total: 11` equals §7.3's `summary.entries: 11` for the same home, not its `occurrences: 23`, so `total` counts local entries, the number `errors`' human header calls "11 errors" (decided while reviewing this bead; record it in the close comment). Whatever unit is chosen, `new`, `total` and `top[].count` use the same units as `errors`' `summary.new`, `summary.entries` and `addons[].count`, so the acceptance criterion "counts matching `errors`' own" holds.
- **`top`:** per-addon `{addon, folder, new, count}` for the target's local errors, in `errors`' order (new desc, count desc, name). `new` per addon is recomputed with the same rule, from the memo's per-addon counts kept per database and session (B6). Nothing in the contract fixes a length for `top`; F8's toast names its addons and F6 shows it. Choose a small fixed bound (a display choice, not a safety limit, so a local `const` rather than `limits.rs`) and record it in a `decided:` comment.
- **`last_session_at`:** the newest BugGrabber file's mtime (the client writes it at logout and `/reload`), or `null`.
- **`dismissed_at`:** the newest `acked_at` among this target's acknowledged databases (from `<state>/errors_ack.json`), or `null`. The plan shows only `null`; this definition is decided while writing the B beads and matches B8's `targets[].dismissed` in the `errors` read.

### 2. `--cached`: validate the memo, recompute `new`

Read the errors memo and the acknowledgement file **once per run**. Then, for each target:
1. **Probe cheaply.** `lstat` each file the memo recorded for this target, and `read_dir` up to `ERRORS_MAX_ACCOUNTS` (32) accounts' `SavedVariables/` dirs to recompute their listing fingerprints (SHA-256 of sorted file names, B5's definition). That spots a new account, a new embedded file or a deleted file without reading any file content. More account dirs than the bound gives `coverage: "truncated"`.
2. **Stamps and fingerprints match:** the memo's observations are still valid. Then:
   - `new` is **recomputed now** with `errors::session_is_new` (B8) for each `(database, session)` from the per-session counts and newest times: the baseline rule (memo first-read baseline, the acknowledgement and its time clause) and each file's mtime against `ERRORS_NEW_MAX_AGE` (7 days) and the current clock (`crate::clock::now()`, A1). Matching stamps validate the **observations**, not time-dependent freshness (a review finding: a memo written while a file was 6 days old must stop reporting new errors two days later with no file change);
   - a first-read baseline above the database's current session is treated as 0 **for this call** (`status` writes nothing; the next `errors` run rewrites it, M3-D19);
   - `state` is `ok`, or `partial` when the memo recorded a `partial` or `over_budget` outcome for any of the target's databases, or `unreadable` when every recorded candidate file failed to read.
3. **Any difference** (a stamp or a fingerprint): `state: "stale"`, with the memo's counts and `new` recomputed by the same rule (so dismissals and aging still apply to what is known). A new file that turns out not to hold `BugGrabberDB` still changes the fingerprint once; the next `errors` run records the new fingerprint, so the state converges.
4. **No memo entry:** `state: "unchecked"` with zero counts when `capture` is BugGrabber (decided by the same cheap probe as B5's `locate`: `!BugGrabber` installed or a candidate file present); else `capture: "none"`.

**The new rule, inlined** (M3-D19; `session_is_new` is B8's single implementation, used by `errors`, `status` and the memo writer):
- `baseline = max(first-read baseline, valid acknowledged session)`. A value above the database's current `session` is void (a reset or replaced database); a first-read baseline above it counts as 0.
- A session is new when its database's file is within the age limit **and either** its number is above the baseline, **or** an acknowledgement exists and the session's newest time evidence proves it occurred after `acked_at` (`TimeEvidence::at_or_after(acked_at) == Yes`). The time clause is decided per `(database, session)`, which is exactly what the memo keeps, so `status --cached` and `errors` agree.
- Received reports are never new and never counted in `new`, `total`, `addons` or `top`.

**Reading the acknowledgement is tolerant.** A missing file means no acknowledgement. A corrupt file is treated as "no acknowledgement" (B8's rule). B8's spec says `errors` and `status` do so "with a warning", but §7.7's warning table adds no code for it and no existing code fits; decided while writing the B beads (B8 says the same): surface it as a human/`-v` note; a newer-version file is read only if it still decodes and otherwise treated as absent with the existing `state_version_newer` warning. M3 adds no warning code for this (the M3 warning set is fixed at eight new codes), so do not invent one here.

### 3. Not cached: the live observation

Plain `status` runs B6's observation live for each target (bounded, typically under 10 ms per file) **without writing the memo**, and fills the same block from it. `state` is `ok`, `partial` or `unreadable`; never `stale` or `unchecked`. `new` uses the same `session_is_new` with the memo's first-read baseline when one exists (read-only), else the first-read rule (`DB session − 1`).

### 4. `summary.errors` and `summary.state`

- `summary.errors` is `{new, targets}`: the sum of local, recomputed `new` counts across targets, and the ids of targets with `new > 0`. Received reports never count.
- `summary.state` uses it through A2's priority rule: `attention` when any P0/P1 issue exists; else `errors` when `summary.errors.new > 0`; else `updates` when updates are available; else `idle`. So `summary.state` is `errors` when only errors are new, and **not** when only received reports exist.

### 5. The recommendation

`commands[]` gains `errors` (action `check_errors`, argv `["omaddons","errors"]`, `destructive: false`) when any target's `errors.state` is `stale` or `unchecked`. **Not** on `partial` (rereading an unchanged over-budget file would not help) and not on `unreadable`. The widget follows the same rule (F8): it reruns `errors` for a target on `stale` or `unchecked`, never on `partial`. The `check_errors` action is one of M3's new `commands[]` actions (DEC-4); add the scene to `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`, which parses and runs the argv on a fresh home.

### 6. Human `status`

One line per target with errors, under that target:
- `  errors: 4 new (DBM 3, WeakAuras 1) · omaddons errors -t retail`;
- `  errors: incomplete read (file was being written) · 2 new so far` for `partial`;
- `stale` and `unchecked` say so and point at `omaddons errors -t <id>` (wording decided while writing this bead; the plan gives only the two lines above).

A2's one-line summary is computed from `summary`; once `summary.errors` is filled, include the new-error count in that line in the same style as its other parts (choose the wording and record it in a `decided:` comment). The lines name addons and counts only; no message text appears in `status` (M3-D21).

### 7. Performance

A2's perf test (`tests/perf.rs::status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo`, release, median of 21 with p95 and cold start recorded) gains: a 2 MB BugGrabber file per target, 16 accounts on one target, an errors memo and an acknowledgement. `--cached` must stay under 5 ms. It only lstats recorded files and lists bounded dirs; it never opens a SavedVariables file.

### 8. Contract and README

- Re-accept the `status` snapshots (new keys only; `attention[]` unchanged for every existing fixture).
- README's `status` section: the errors line, the `errors` block keys and states, and the `check_errors` recommendation.

**Files:** `src/app/status.rs` (`TargetErrors`, `summary.errors`, the recommendation, human lines); `src/errors/memo.rs` (a read-only loader if B6 did not expose one); `src/errors/ack.rs` (read side, from B8); `tests/status.rs`; `tests/perf.rs`; `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`; `status` snapshots; README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `errors`, `status --cached` reports `state: ok` with counts matching `errors`' own (`new`, `total`, `addons`, `received`).
- After the fixture rewrites the BugGrabber file (a simulated logout), `--cached` says `stale`, and plain `status` reports the new counts live.
- A new file appearing in a `SavedVariables/` dir (a new account or embedded copy) makes `--cached` say `stale` through the listing fingerprint; after the next `errors` run it is `ok` again.
- **Aging:** with the memo written while a file was 6 days old, and `OMADDONS_NOW` (A1's clock seam) moved 2 days later with no file change, `--cached` reports `new: 0` without any `errors` run.
- **Dismissal:** after `errors dismiss`, `--cached` reports `new: 0` with the memo deleted too. The acknowledgement in `<state>` is enough (the target shows `unchecked`, with zero counts, and `new: 0`; after the next `errors` run the dismissed errors stay not-new).
- An over-budget file gives `state: partial`, no `check_errors` recommendation, and no `errors` rerun by the widget (F8 test).
- A target whose every candidate file fails to read reports `unreadable`, never `ok` with zeros.
- More than 32 account dirs report `coverage: "truncated"`.
- `status` writes nothing (the existing `status_writes_nothing` test, with a memo and an acknowledgement present).
- `summary.state` is `errors` when only errors are new, and not when only received reports exist; `summary.errors.targets` lists exactly the targets with new local errors.
- The `check_errors` recommendation appears exactly when a target is `stale` or `unchecked`, and its argv parses and runs on a fresh home.
- `targets[].errors.top[].new` agrees with `errors`' per-addon `new` for the same home and clock.
- The budget holds: `status --cached` under 5 ms at the median (release, median of 21, p95 and cold start recorded) with a 2 MB BugGrabber file per target, 16 accounts on one target, a memo and an acknowledgement.
- `attention[]` is unchanged for every existing fixture; the `status` snapshot diff is limited to new keys.

## Test Plan

- **E2E, `tests/status.rs`** (extended): `ok` after `errors`; `stale` after a simulated logout (file rewritten), live counts from plain `status`; `stale` after a new file in a `SavedVariables/` dir, converging after `errors`; aging with `OMADDONS_NOW`; dismissal with the memo deleted; `partial` (truncated file) and `over_budget`; `unreadable`; `unchecked` (BugGrabber installed, no memo) and `capture: none`; truncated coverage with 33 account dirs; `summary.state` with only errors new, and with only received reports; `status_writes_nothing` with a memo and an acknowledgement present. All homes use `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` and `assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr.
- **Property** (shared with B8): `errors`' and `status --cached`'s new counts (totals and per addon) are equal over random session and time layouts, with and without an acknowledgement.
- **Perf, `tests/perf.rs`:** A2's `status --cached` test with the heavy home above.
- **Recommendations, `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`:** the `check_errors` scene (stale and unchecked), and its absence on `partial`.
- **Contract:** re-accept the `status` snapshots (new keys only).
- **Widget side** (F8's QML test, not this task): a `partial` state triggers no rerun.

## Considerations

- **`status` stays write-free.** Never write the memo or the acknowledgement from `status`, not even to rewrite a void baseline; treat it as 0 for the call instead.
- **Freshness is recomputed, not stored.** The age rule and the acknowledgement's time clause are evaluated against the clock on every call; a frozen `new` in the memo would leave the bar urgent forever.
- **Honest states.** `partial`, `unreadable` and `truncated` are never collapsed into `ok` with zeros; the widget shows "incomplete read (the game may be writing)" for `partial`.
- **Risk 15 (`status --cached` regresses past 5 ms; M, M):** only lstats and bounded `read_dir`s; the perf test with 16 accounts and 2 MB files per target guards it at the median and p95.
- **Risk 13 (personal data; L, H):** `status` carries addon names, counts and times only; no message text, no paths, no account names.
- **Collision hot spot: `src/app/status.rs`** (A2, B7, D11, E4). A2 lands first and owns the restructure; this task appends `TargetErrors` and fills `summary.errors`. D11 (backups) and E4 (widget) append their own blocks; rebase before each gate run.
- **Lane order.** Lane 3 (Errors): A1 → B1 → B3 → B6 → B8 → **B7** → F6 → E4. B8 lands before B7 because `status` reads the acknowledgement to compute `new`.
- **Delivery slice `slice-2` (S2, "Capture and diagnose").** Exit demo: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal. This task is what makes the bar urgent after a bad session and calm after a dismissal.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- A2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.2` (`status` triage: `summary`, `issues[]`, `last_change`, and the history projection): the `summary` struct with `SummaryErrors`, the `summary.state` priority rule and the perf test this task extends.
- B6 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6` (The `errors` command): the errors memo (stamps, listing fingerprints, per-session counts and newest times, per-addon counts, read outcomes, coverage) and the live observation plain `status` runs.
- B8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.8` (`errors dismiss`, durable acknowledgement): `<state>/errors_ack.json` and `errors::session_is_new`, so cached and live counts honour dismissals and agree with `errors`.

**Unblocks:**
- F6 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.6` (The Issues and Search views): `summary.state: "errors"` and the per-target `errors` block the Issues view reads.
- F8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.8` (`Service.qml`, part 2: Hyprland, auto-check, post-session triggers, notifications): its triggers and toasts read `errors.state`, `summary.errors.new` and `targets[].errors.top`.
- G1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1` (README final pass): the `status` errors line and recommendation it reconciles.

Parent: the B epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2`. Delivery slice: `slice-2`.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** The bar can only turn urgent after a bad play session, and calm down after a dismissal, if `status --cached` knows about Lua errors in under 5 ms without ever writing anything. This bead gives `status` a per-client `errors` block and fills `summary.errors`, from the memo `errors` wrote and the user's dismissals, with `new` recomputed against the clock on every call. Agents get the same block, so "is anything broken?" is one `status --json` call. It keeps the M3 promise that the widget is a view of the CLI, never a second source of truth: the widget's urgent state, its errors refresh (F8) and its Issues view (F6) all read what this bead computes.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D20: the errors memo is derived; `status` stays write-free.** `status --cached` reads the memo and the acknowledgement, lstats the recorded files, lists up to `ERRORS_MAX_ACCOUNTS` accounts' `SavedVariables/` dirs, and reports `stale`, `unchecked`, `partial` or `truncated` honestly; plain `status` parses live and writes nothing; the widget reruns `errors` on `stale`/`unchecked`, never on `partial`. Rejected: parsing in `status --cached` on every call (2–20 ms per file breaks the 5 ms budget); letting `status` write the memo (breaks the read-only invariant guarded by `tests/status.rs:154`).
- **M3-D19: the new rule.** Baseline = max(first-read baseline, acknowledged session), void when above the current session; the acknowledgement's time clause per `(database, session)`; the 7-day age limit judged at the time of the call. `status --cached` treats a void first-read baseline as 0 for that call because it writes nothing. Rejected: trusting a `new` count frozen into the memo.
- **M3-D21: received reports never count** in `status`, `summary.errors` or notifications.
- **M3-D37: triage blocks.** `summary.errors` feeds `summary.state` (`attention > errors > updates > idle`), so agents and the bar share one answer. Rejected: computing severity or state in QML (logic in the view).
- **M3-D44: bounded probes**, reported as `coverage: "truncated"`.

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 3, revision 9 (adopted): freshness is recomputed against the clock; matching stamps validate observations, not time-dependent freshness. This is why `status --cached` recomputes `new` from per-session counts and newest times instead of reading a stored `new`.
- Round 3, revision 8 (adapted, via B8): dismissals are durable user state in `<state>`, so `status` reads them directly and a cache wipe never makes the bar urgent again about dismissed errors.
- Round 3, revision 15 (adopted): bounded cached status; this block only lstats and lists bounded dirs; the heavy perf home (16 accounts, 2 MB files) is part of the budget.
- Round 1: the memo converges through listing fingerprints, so a new file not holding `BugGrabberDB` changes the state to `stale` exactly once.

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`:
- `StatusData` is `{cached, targets[], journal, needs_attention}` at `src/app/status.rs:65-171`, with no errors, severity, backups or last change.
- `status --cached` measured 3 ms on seven targets; `tests/perf.rs:300-410` asserts a median under 5 ms.
- `tests/status.rs:154-163` hashes state, cache and client dir across `status` variants.
- The client writes SavedVariables only at logout, `/reload` and disconnect, so a file's mtime is the end of its last session (`last_session_at`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk 15, `status --cached` past 5 ms (M, M): lstats and bounded listings only, measured at median and p95 on the heavy home.
- A stale-but-ok answer: designed out by stamps plus listing fingerprints; any difference is `stale`, and the widget reruns `errors`.

**Confidence.** High: a read-only validation over a small derived file, following the M2 release-memo pattern that `status --cached` already uses within budget.
