title: `errors dismiss`, durable acknowledgement
description:
## Background

After a bad play session the bar turns urgent, and it must be able to calm down again: the player looks at the errors, perhaps updates the addon, and says "I've seen these". That is a **dismissal**. Without it, one old error keeps the icon red forever; with a careless one, the bar goes quiet about errors the player never saw.

**A dismissal is the user's decision** (M3-D19), so:
- it belongs in `<state>`, not `<cache>`: `<cache>` is documented as safe to delete, and deleting it must never make the bar urgent again about errors the user already dismissed;
- it is attributed in history (`--actor`, `--reason`), like every other settings change;
- it must **never acknowledge errors the user was not shown**: a session can end (the game writes BugGrabber's file at logout and `/reload`) between the moment the Issues view showed the errors and the moment the user pressed "dismiss";
- it is a **subcommand**, `errors dismiss`, because mutation is classified per command path, not per flag: `app::mutates(path)` reads the `COMMANDS` row, so a `--dismiss` flag on the read command would make `app::mutates("errors")` false for a write (ground truth comment, §2.1).

**Ground truth this task relies on** (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", as of `af10e34`):
- `Scope::State` and `Scope::History` already admit `Writer::Mutating` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:102-111`), so writing `<state>/errors_ack.json` and appending a history line needs no scope change.
- Settings changes are `SettingEntry` history lines (`src/state/history.rs:72-90`: `{schema_version, tx, kind, at, target, actor, reason, argv, ops: [], result, run}`), written by `app::record_setting` (`src/app/mod.rs:42`). `TxKind::is_setting()` is `src/model.rs:447`. Settings lines are not undoable; `undo` steps over them.
- `store::save` (`src/state/store.rs:230`) refuses to overwrite a newer-version state file with `state_too_new` (M3-D45 relies on this for every M3 state file).
- `GlobalLock::acquire(paths, command)` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:72`). Vision comment 723: every lock acquisition for a change recovers first. Every history appender holds the global lock (ground truth comment, §2.4 item 14).
- `plan_stale` exists with `PlanStaleSource::{Replan, Apply}` (`src/error.rs:492-555`); `Apply` makes it not retryable.
- The client writes SavedVariables only when a UI session ends (logout, `/reload`, disconnect), and the next UI load has a higher `session` number. Modern BugGrabber moves a recurring entry's `session` forward; r152 adds a new entry per session. `/bugsack reset` sets `session` back to 1 (ground truth comment, §2.6).

**Goals and checkpoints served.** G-M3-2 (one-click common actions, none of them surprising; the confirmed run is bound to what the user saw) and G-M3-3. Checkpoint criterion 6 ("a dismissal survives deleting `<cache>`; it never acknowledges errors the user was not shown: the widget binds it to the shown observation") and criterion 13 (for `errors dismiss`, a test changes state between the preview and the real run with `--if-match`; the real run refuses with `plan_stale` and changes nothing).

**Decisions that shape it, in one line each:**
- **M3-D19:** per-database session watermarks, baseline = max(first-read baseline, acknowledged session), a per-session time clause after `acked_at`, reset handling, durable acknowledgement in `<state>/errors_ack.json`.
- **M3-D46:** destructive and binding previews carry a `pc1:` precondition token; `errors dismiss`'s token covers each database's file stamp and session, with target keys **without** generations.
- **M3-D9:** the widget binds the dismissal to the `errors` read the Issues view shows, without a confirm dialog.
- **M3-D20:** the errors memo is derived; this task rewrites its per-database `new` counts after a dismissal.
- **M3-D45:** the acknowledgement is written through `store::save`, so a newer file is never overwritten.
- **M3-D4 (via A1):** `errors dismiss` rings the doorbell.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/errors/ack.rs` (new): the durable acknowledgement

`<state>/errors_ack.json`, kind `errors_ack` 1.0 (`Versioned`, with a `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` row):

```json
{"schema_version":"1.0",
 "targets":{"<target key>":{"databases":{"<db key>":{"acked_session":48,"acked_at":"2026-10-21T19:02:11Z"}}}}}
```

- **The database key** is the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the file's path **relative to the client dir**, never the path itself (the path names an account folder). It stores no diagnostic text: per target key and database key, only `{acked_session, acked_at}`.
- **Reading is tolerant:** a corrupt file is `state_corrupt` for `errors dismiss` (which refuses to overwrite what it cannot read; the prose fix wording, naming the file `errors_ack.json` in the state directory and saying that deleting it brings dismissed errors back as new, is decided while writing this bead), and is treated as "no acknowledgement" by `errors` and `status`. The spec says "with a warning", but §7.7's warning table adds no code for it and no existing warning code fits; decided while writing the B beads (B7 says the same): surface it as a human/`-v` note and add no warning code (M3's warning set is fixed at eight new codes, 41 → 49). A newer-version file is read only if it still decodes (the store's rule) and is never written.
- **Writing** goes through `store::save` (so a newer file is refused, M3-D45), in an untracked `WriteSession` with `Writer::Mutating`, under the global lock.

### 2. Wire the acknowledgement into the new rule (B6's code, `src/errors/mod.rs`)

One function decides newness everywhere, so the cached and live counts always agree:

```rust
pub fn session_is_new(db: &DbState, session: u32, newest_time: Option<&TimeEvidence>, ack: Option<&Ack>, now: Timestamp) -> bool
```

Every reader uses it: `errors` (B6), `status` both modes (B7, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7`) and the memo writer. The rules, from M3-D19:
- **Per database.** One BugGrabber file of one account, or one embedding provider's file. Received reports are never new.
- **The baseline** is the larger of:
  - the **acknowledged session** `acked_session` (with `acked_at`), from `<state>/errors_ack.json`;
  - the **first-read baseline** from the memo. When `errors` first reads a database with no memo entry, it is set to `acked_session` when a valid acknowledgement exists, otherwise to `DB session − 1`. **A missing first-read baseline is initialized from the acknowledgement**, so wiping `<cache>` never hides an error the user did not dismiss and never resurrects one they did.
- **An entry is new** when it is local, its database's file mtime is within `ERRORS_NEW_MAX_AGE` (7 days) at the time of the read, **and either** its `session` is greater than the baseline, **or** an acknowledgement exists and its session's newest time evidence proves that session occurred after `acked_at` (`TimeEvidence::at_or_after(acked_at) == Yes`).
  - The time clause is decided **per `(database, session)`**, not per entry, so `errors` and `status --cached` (which keeps only per-session counts and newest times) always agree.
  - An integer time proves occurrence. A string time (`first_or_last`) proves it only when it is after `acked_at`, because a first capture after the dismissal implies the error happened after it.
  - A session that ended after the dismissal yet carries a number at or below the acknowledged one can only come from a reset or replaced database; all its entries postdate the dismissal, and the time clause catches them.
- **Reset and replacement.** An acknowledgement or a first-read baseline above the database's current `session` cannot belong to this database's history (after `/bugsack reset`, a restored `WTF/`, a copied file); that value is void while it is above the session.
  - The first-read baseline is made **sticky by its writer**: when `errors` or `errors dismiss` observes a database whose `session` is below the memo's first-read baseline, it rewrites that baseline to 0. `status --cached`, which writes nothing, treats such a baseline as 0 for that call.
  - Voiding an acknowledgement by session alone is not sticky: once a reset database passes the old number, a stale acknowledgement would apply again. The time clause makes that harmless: every error that occurred after the dismissal is new whatever its session number, so a revived acknowledgement can only hide errors that predate the dismissal itself.

**Why session watermarks, not per-fingerprint ones** (M3-D19). The client writes SavedVariables only when a UI session ends, and the next session starts with a higher number, so an error that occurs after a dismissal always lands in a session above the acknowledged one, even "the same error again". A per-session watermark is exact for BugGrabber's write model and needs no message-derived state. The real race is a dismissal acknowledging a session the user never saw, which the token (step 3.2) closes. If a future BugGrabber writes mid-session, the observed session would stop advancing per write; C2's live probe of upstream `BugGrabber.lua` is the tripwire.

### 3. The subcommand `errors dismiss [-t T]…`

`src/app/errors.rs`: `ErrorsAction::Dismiss`; path `errors dismiss`, group Look, `mutates: true`.

1. **Observe.** Build each selected target's observation (B6, with no view filters).
2. **Precondition** (A4, `app::precondition`, M3-D46):
   - `command` = `errors dismiss`;
   - `targets` = the target keys **without** generations (an addon update between reading and dismissing does not change what was shown). A4's `Precondition` declares `targets: Vec<(TargetKey, Option<u64>)>`, and `errors dismiss` passes `None` for every target, which canonicalizes as a key-only entry (decided when the beads were filed; A4 says the same);
   - `selection` = the database keys it would acknowledge;
   - `observed` = each database file's `FileStamp` and DB `session`.

   The token is `pc1:` followed by four 16-hex fields, the first 64 bits of a SHA-256 of each canonical part (command path, targets, selection, observed; keys sorted, id arrays sorted, integers only). `--if-match <token>` compares **before anything is written**, and requires **exactly the token's target set** (one `-t`, as the widget sends). A mismatch is `plan_stale` with `PlanStaleSource::Apply` (**not retryable**), `details.changed` naming the differing parts from `command`, `targets`, `selection`, `observed`, and `fix_argv` = the same command with `--dry-run` in place of `--if-match <token>` (preview again). Nothing is acknowledged.
3. **Lock.** `GlobalLock::acquire` (recover first, vision comment 723). If any database's stamp moved since step 1, rebuild the observation **under the lock** and, with `--if-match`, compare the token again. That closes the window between the first comparison and the write.
4. **Acknowledge.** For each **complete** database: `acked_session = DB session`, `acked_at = crate::clock::now()`. Incomplete databases (`partial`, `over_budget`, `unreadable`: `errors_partial` on the read) are skipped and listed; the result is `partial: true` and names them.
5. **Write and record.** Write `errors_ack.json`. Append a **settings** history line of the new kind `TxKind::Dismiss` (`is_setting() == true`, wire `dismiss`), carrying the target and the counts `{databases: n, errors: n}` (databases acknowledged; new local errors cleared) and **no message text**. Decided while writing this bead (the plan names the fields, not their encoding): `SettingEntry` gains these counts as optional keys (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = …)]`), so every other settings line is unchanged. Release the lock.
6. **Derive.** Rewrite the memo's per-database `new` counts (derived, best effort) and ring the doorbell (`doorbell::ring(paths, "errors dismiss", ctx.actor)`, A1).

- **`--dry-run`** reports what would be acknowledged, with `precondition`, and writes nothing (state, cache and history unchanged).
- **Without `--if-match`** the command acknowledges what it observes now, exactly like a typed command; the token is opt-in (M3-D46).
- **Decided while drafting:** when no selected database is complete, nothing is written, no history line is appended, and the result is `partial: true` with every database in `skipped`. A target with `capture: none` has nothing to acknowledge and is reported with empty lists.

### 4. The contract (milestone epic comment "Contract additions, part 1", §7.1, §7.3; additive, DEC-4)

`errors dismiss` returns:

```json
{"data":{"targets":[{"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M4…"},
                     "acknowledged":[{"database":"db-1","session":48}],
                     "skipped":[{"database":"db-2","reason":"partial"}]}]},
 "partial":true}
```

with `partial: true` when anything was skipped. Its `--dry-run` adds `data.precondition`.

**B6's read gains** (this task adds them, with their contract snapshot):
- `targets[].dismiss = {precondition, databases}`: the token over the observation the read shows (each database's stamp and session), and the number of complete databases a dismissal would acknowledge. Dismissing what you just looked at needs no extra dry run;
- `targets[].databases[].acknowledged`: the database's valid acknowledged session, or `null`;
- `targets[].dismissed`: the newest `acked_at` among the target's acknowledged databases, or `null`.

The plan shows these keys (§7.3: `"dismiss":{"precondition":"pc1:5be1…","databases":1}`, `"acknowledged":null`, `"dismissed":null`) without defining `dismiss.databases`, `acknowledged` or `dismissed`; the three meanings above are decided while writing the B beads (B6 and B7's `dismissed_at` agree).
- the `commands[]` recommendation `errors dismiss -t <id>` (action `dismiss_errors`, `destructive: false`) when the target has `new > 0`.

The global flag `--if-match <TOKEN>` (A4) accepts `errors dismiss` as one of its five paths (`remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `errors dismiss`); it is a usage error elsewhere.

### 5. `history`

- `history` renders a dismiss line as `dismiss · retail · 4 errors in 1 database`.
- `undo` steps over it like other settings lines (not undoable). An M2 binary cannot decode the new kind (an unknown `TxKind` fails its line, ground truth §2.9) and skips the line with `history_lines_skipped`; the line touches no folder, so that is harmless (an analysis made while writing this bead).

### 6. Registry and contract (DEC-1 touch points)

- `src/cli.rs`: the `dismiss` subcommand under `Command::Errors` (doc comment = about; `after_long_help`: "a dismissal only removes the 'new' mark; the errors stay listed; it cannot be undone").
- `src/app/mod.rs`: `COMMANDS` row `entry("errors dismiss", Group::Look, true)`; `command_name` arm (`"errors dismiss"`); `dispatch` arm.
- `src/model.rs`: `TxKind::Dismiss` (wire `dismiss`, `is_setting() == true`, not undoable), with the model's kind tests updated.
- `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows with snapshots: success; `--dry-run`; `plan_stale` (with `--if-match` after a rewrite); a partial database.
- `tests/contract/special.rs` gains **no** read-only row for it (it mutates).
- `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS`: the `errors_ack` row.
- `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` and the help layout test, if the subcommand appears in help.
- `tests/preconditions.rs` (A4's file): the `errors dismiss` binding cases.
- Once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed: the `CLI_PATHS` row `errors dismiss` in `omarchy/Model.js` with `mutates: true`, `destructive: false`, `binds: true`. The widget template that uses it (F6 adds it) is `"dismiss_errors": { "argv": ["errors", "dismiss", "-t", "{target}"], "mutates": true, "bind": true }`; the runner appends `--if-match <dismiss.precondition>` from the shown read, and a `plan_stale` refreshes the Issues section with "new errors arrived; review them".

### 7. README

- `errors dismiss` under `### errors` (what it acknowledges, that it cannot be undone and only removes the "new" mark, `--if-match`).
- The history kinds table: `dismiss`.
- Files and state: `<state>/errors_ack.json` ("your dismissals; deleting it brings dismissed errors back as new").
- The "deleting the cache forgets which older errors were new" note under `errors.json`, now qualified: dismissed errors stay dismissed.

**Files:** new `src/errors/ack.rs`; `src/errors/mod.rs` (`session_is_new`); `src/errors/memo.rs` (rewrite after dismiss; initialize the first-read baseline from the acknowledgement); `src/app/errors.rs` (subcommand, `dismiss` block in the read); `src/cli.rs`; `src/app/mod.rs`; `src/model.rs`; `src/state/history.rs` (`SettingEntry` counts, rendering); `src/state/store.rs`; new `tests/errors_dismiss.rs`; `tests/preconditions.rs`; contract matrix and snapshots; README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `errors dismiss -t retail` clears `new` in `errors` and `status`, appends one `dismiss` history line (no message text), rings the doorbell, and survives deleting `<cache>`.
- **Binding:** take the `dismiss.precondition` from an `errors` read, rewrite the BugGrabber file (a session ended), then `errors dismiss -t retail --if-match <it>` → `plan_stale` (`retryable: false`, `details.changed` includes `observed`, `fix_argv` is the `--dry-run` form), and nothing is acknowledged. Without the rewrite, it acknowledges exactly what was shown.
- `--if-match` with a target set other than the token's (no `-t`, or two `-t`) is refused before anything is written.
- **Later errors stay new:** after a dismissal, a later session's errors are new, including a recurrence of a dismissed error (its `session` moved forward).
- **Reset:** a DB session reset to 1 after a dismissal at 48 voids the acknowledgement; the errors since the reset are new. After the reset database passes session 48 again (simulated), errors from those later sessions are still new, by the time clause, and a stale acknowledgement hides nothing that occurred after the dismissal.
- **Cache wipe:** after a dismissal and two more sessions, deleting `<cache>` keeps exactly those two sessions' errors new (the first-read baseline is rebuilt from the acknowledgement).
- **Two dismissers:** two `errors dismiss` at once (a pause failpoint in one) serialize under the lock, and the file holds both targets' acknowledgements.
- **Partial:** a database read incompletely is not acknowledged, and the result is `partial: true` naming it.
- `errors dismiss --dry-run` writes nothing (state, cache and history hashes unchanged) and returns `precondition`.
- The `errors` read carries `targets[].dismiss.precondition` and the `dismiss_errors` recommendation when `new > 0`; that argv parses.
- A corrupt `errors_ack.json` makes `errors dismiss` fail with `state_corrupt` (prose fix, no runnable command named) and leaves `errors` and `status` working with no acknowledgement applied.
- `history` renders the line as `dismiss · <target> · N errors in M database(s)`, and `undo` steps over it.
- `errors dismiss` is in `COMMANDS` (Look, `mutates: true`); its contract rows (success, `--dry-run`, `plan_stale`, partial) pass with snapshots; `errors_ack` has a `KINDS` row; `TxKind::Dismiss` is a settings kind.
- `assert_private_all` passes over stdout and stderr for every case (the acknowledgement file and history line hold no names or paths).

## Test Plan

- **E2E, `tests/errors_dismiss.rs`** (new), on B2 fixture homes: dismiss then `errors` and `status --cached`; cache wipe; binding with and without a file rewrite between read and dismiss; wrong target set with `--if-match`; later sessions and recurrence; reset to 1 and passing 48 again; two dismissers with a pause failpoint in one process (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>=pause` with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR` markers, `src/fsx/failpoint.rs:3`, debug builds only), placed after the lock is taken and before `errors_ack.json` is written (the plan names no new failpoint for this; the fsx primitive's own `fsx.<primitive>.before` hit on the acknowledgement write sits there, decided while writing this bead); partial database; `--dry-run` hashes of state, cache and history; corrupt acknowledgement file; history rendering and `undo` stepping over the line.
- **Unit, `session_is_new`'s table:** memo baseline only, acknowledgement only, both, neither, reset, reset passing the old number with and without an acknowledgement, string and integer times, the age limit.
- **Property:** `errors`' and `status --cached`'s new counts (totals and per addon) are equal over random session and time layouts, with and without acknowledgements and resets.
- **Contract:** matrix rows (success, `--dry-run`, `plan_stale`, partial) with snapshots; the `errors` read snapshot with `dismiss`, `acknowledged` and `dismissed`.
- **Preconditions:** `tests/preconditions.rs` gains the `errors dismiss` cases (token stable across two reads of an unchanged home; differs when a stamp or session changes; `details.changed`).
- **Privacy:** `assert_private_all` over both streams for every case, and a scan of `errors_ack.json` and the history line for `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm`, `FakeChar`.

## Considerations

- **A dismissal cannot be undone.** Settings lines are not undoable. It only removes the "new" mark; the errors stay listed. Say so in the help text.
- **Design gate: this task introduces a new protocol** ("durable acknowledgement: user state, not cache", one of the six design gates with A3, A4, C2, D5 and D14). It is risky because it moves a decision from a rebuildable cache into durable state that every reader must honour identically, and because its correctness rests on BugGrabber's session-end write model plus a time clause for resets. It closes only when its adversarial matrix is green (common rule 14): the binding race, the reset-then-pass case, the cache wipe, concurrent dismissers and the cached-versus-live property test.
- **Lock discipline.** The global lock is held only to recheck stamps, write the small acknowledgement file and append one history line; no parse of a large file happens under it unless a stamp moved (then the observation is rebuilt under the lock, bounded as always).
- **Risk 21 (a preview no longer describes what a confirmed action does; M, M–H):** the token binds the dismissal to the shown observation; `plan_stale` refreshes the view.
- **Risk 5 (BugGrabber changes its write model; M, M):** a mid-session write model would break session watermarks; C2's live probe is the tripwire.
- **Risk 13 (personal data; L, H):** database keys are hashes, the file holds no text, the history line holds counts only.
- **Collision hot spots:** `src/error.rs` (no new code here, but `plan_stale` details), `src/cli.rs` and `src/app/mod.rs` (the subcommand variant under `errors`), help tests, `src/state/history.rs` (`SettingEntry` keys; A2 and A3 also edit this file: A2's `append_line` projection, A3's reader), `tests/preconditions.rs` (A4, D4, D8 extend it too).
- **Lane order.** Lane 3 (Errors): A1 → B1 → B3 → B6 → **B8** → B7 → F6 → E4. B8 sits between B6 and B7 because `status` reads the acknowledgement to compute `new`.
- **Delivery slice `slice-2` (S2, "Capture and diagnose").** Exit demo: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and **a bound dismissal**. Pre-checks checkpoint criterion 13 for `errors dismiss`.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.

6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".

The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).

They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** An urgent bar that can never calm down is worse than no bar, and one that calms down about errors the player never saw is dangerous. This bead makes "I've seen these errors" a real, durable user decision: `omaddons errors dismiss`, recorded in `<state>`, attributed in history, surviving a cache wipe, and bound to exactly the observation the player (or agent) looked at. The widget's Issues view dismisses with one key (`d`), and a session that ended in between gives `plan_stale` instead of a silent acknowledgement. B7 reads the acknowledgement so `status` and the bar honour it, and F6 wires the key. It serves the M3 thesis directly: every change, even a dismissal, goes through the CLI, is attributed, and does exactly what the preview showed.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D19: what counts as new, and dismissal as durable user state.** Per-database baselines combining the acknowledged session and the memo's first-read baseline (the larger wins); a missing first-read baseline initialized from the acknowledgement; a per-session time clause after `acked_at`; values above the current session void, with the first-read baseline rewritten to 0 stickily by its writers; a subcommand with `mutates: true`, the global lock, an untracked `Writer::Mutating` session, a settings history line of the new kind `dismiss`, the doorbell; not undoable. Why session watermarks: BugGrabber's file changes only when a UI session ends and the next session is numbered higher, so a session watermark is exact; the time clause covers resets. Rejected: (i) time windows (the meaning of `time` varies by version); (ii) no dismissing (a permanent urgent state); (iii) `errors --dismiss`, a flag on a read command (it would make `app::mutates("errors")` false for a write); (iv) storing the dismissal in the cache memo (the first draft); and per-fingerprint occurrence watermarks (the review's proposal: extra state and identity rules for a case BugGrabber's write model cannot produce).
- **M3-D46: previews bind.** The `errors dismiss` token covers each database's stamp and session, with target keys without generations, and requires exactly the token's target set; a mismatch is a non-retryable `plan_stale` whose fix is the `--dry-run` form. Rejected: stored plans in M3; per-command `--expect-*` flags; time-limited tokens. Departure from the vision (part of vision §5.11's "plan, then apply" brought forward); G2 records it.
- **M3-D9: the widget binds the dismissal to the shown read, without a dialog.** The token comes from `errors`' `targets[].dismiss.precondition`.
- **M3-D20: the memo is derived.** The dismissal rewrites the memo's per-database `new` counts after the durable write; deleting the memo loses nothing the user decided.
- **M3-D45: fail closed on newer state.** The acknowledgement is written through `store::save`.

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 3, revision 8 (adapted): durable state, a subcommand, history, locking and binding to the shown observation were adopted; per-fingerprint watermarks were not, for the write-model reason above. The real race, acknowledging an unseen session, is closed by the token.
- Round 3, revision 7 (adopted): destructive and binding actions carry stateless four-part tokens; `errors dismiss` is one of the five paths.
- Not traced to a specific review round in the planning record, but part of M3-D19 as approved: the first-read baseline is sticky (rewritten to 0 on reset) and is initialized from the acknowledgement; the time clause is decided per session (`errors::session_is_new`) so cached and live counts agree.
- Decided while drafting this bead: when no database is complete, nothing is written and no history line is appended; `SettingEntry` gains the counts as optional keys; `dismissed` in the read is the newest `acked_at`.

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`:
- `Scope::State` and `Scope::History` admit `Writer::Mutating` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:102-111`): no scope change.
- `SettingEntry` (`src/state/history.rs:72-90`) carries `target`, `argv` and empty `ops`; `record_setting` is `src/app/mod.rs:42`; `is_setting` is `src/model.rs:447`.
- `store::save` refuses newer files (`src/state/store.rs:230`).
- `GlobalLock::acquire` is `src/fsx/lock.rs:72`; vision comment 723: lock acquisitions for changes recover first.
- `plan_stale` with `PlanStaleSource::Apply` is not retryable (`src/error.rs:492-555`).
- The pause failpoint exists (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>=pause`, `src/fsx/failpoint.rs:3`).
- BugSack's received reports carry `source` and the current session (ground truth comment, §2.6); B6 keeps them out of every count, so they can never be acknowledged as "new" in the first place.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk 21, a preview no longer describing the action (M, M–H): the token, rechecked under the lock after a stamp move.
- Risk 5, BugGrabber's write model changes (M, M): C2's live probe; the time clause limits the damage of a revived acknowledgement to errors that predate the dismissal.
- A cache wipe resurrecting or hiding errors: the first-read baseline is rebuilt from the acknowledgement; tested.
- Divergent counts between `errors` and `status`: one function, and a property test over random layouts.

**Confidence.** Medium-high: the mechanics (a small state file under the lock, a settings line, a token) are well-trodden in this codebase, but it is one of the six design gates because the newness rules must hold across resets, cache wipes and concurrent writers, which only its adversarial matrix can show.

title: Epic: M3 keyless BugGrabber (the wowace: source)
description:
## Background

Area C of M3 (milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`): keyless BugGrabber.

`omaddons errors` is only useful if BugGrabber is installed, and BugGrabber has no keyless release anywhere omaddons already fetches from: not on GitHub (one mirror is bcc-only, another re-tags several times a day), not on WoWInterface, not on Tukui (ground truth §2.6). Its upstream is WowAce's public SVN at `repos.wowace.com`: keyless, with modern tags, and r152 as the last 3.3.5-era revision for 3.3.5a (GPL). Without a source, `errors` would depend on a browser download.

A small `wowace:` source makes `omaddons install buggrabber` work (M3-D15):
- It lists tags with one `PROPFIND` that returns every tag's `version-name` (its last-changed revision).
- It fetches every file of a tag through `!svn/bc/<tagrev>/`, so the whole tree comes from one immutable revision: a tag moved mid-fetch cannot mix revisions, an unrelated upstream commit never shows as an update, and a locked reinstall fetches the same revision again.
- It builds a deterministic zip that is TOC-verified like any other archive.
- It supports only the packaging subset BugGrabber needs and refuses anything else by name (`packaging_unsupported`): the `.pkgmeta` keys `externals`, `ignore`, `plain-copy`, `move-folders`, `enable-toc-creation: yes` and any unlisted key; any `@word@` keyword in a `.toc`, `.lua` or `.xml` file other than `@project-version@` in a `.toc`; and build-type block markers.

The catalog then needs same-name variants: the modern BugGrabber and the 3.3.5a r152 build are both "BugGrabber". The catalog collapses entries with the same name today, so C3 adds variants selected by disjoint client families (`name#variant`), merged by identity with user overrides (M3-D16).

## Goals

- **C1** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.1` (`wowace:` refs, listing parsers and the packaging scanner): ref parsing, the `PROPFIND` and directory-listing parsers (fuzzed, `wowace_listing`), and the `.pkgmeta`/keyword scanner that decides what is supported.
- **C2** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.2` (The WowAce source): pinned trees, the deterministic zip, TOC verification, the allowlisted host, caching and the live probe.
- **C3** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3` (BugGrabber in the catalog: disjoint family variants): variants with disjoint family selectors, `name#variant`, merge by identity, and the `errors` hint switched to the keyless install.

## Success Criteria

- `install buggrabber` installs the newest WowAce tag on synthetic retail, Mists Classic, Era, Anniversary and Forever clients, and r152 on the 3.3.5a client (real machine, then undone).
- Every tree URL is pinned to one revision; a tag moved mid-fetch cannot mix revisions; unrelated upstream commits show no update; a locked reinstall fetches the same revision.
- Unsupported packaging is refused by name, never installed half-built.
- `net.log` shows only allowlisted hosts and zero GitHub REST requests.
- User catalog overrides keep variants intact.
- The `wowace_listing` fuzz target runs at least 30 minutes clean at G3; the live probe `wowace_bug_grabber_decodes` passes.

## Non-Goals

- WowAce projects that need packaging steps (externals, moves, ignores, build keywords).
- Changelogs from WowAce.
- A general CurseForge/WowAce integration (CurseForge and Wago are M5).

## Considerations

- **`repos.wowace.com` joins the always-allowed host list.** `HEAD` returns 401 there, so the source uses `GET` and `PROPFIND` only.
- **C2 is a design gate** (source pinning: every file fetched at one revision) and closes only with its adversarial tests green: a tag moved mid-fetch, an unrelated commit, a locked reinstall.
- **Slack.** The WowAce lane has 5 to 7 units of slack against the critical paths. C1 is a root; the six-lane schedule fills the widget agent's early gap with it.
- **C3 waits for B6**, because it changes the hint `errors` emits for a client without BugGrabber (action `install_buggrabber`: B6's `search buggrabber` becomes `install buggrabber -t <id>`, or no command where no variant covers the client's family).
- **External host risk** (risk 4). WowAce SVN may go down, change its listing format or refuse `PROPFIND`. Mitigations: recorded fixtures, three response formats parsed, a live probe at checkpoints, the blob cache serving reinstalls offline, the `--file` fallback, and the M5 CurseForge source as a second route. A refused `PROPFIND` would need the `OPTIONS` (`svn-youngest-rev`) plus content-digest fallback, which is designed but not built in M3.
- **Slice.** All three leaves belong to `slice-2` (capture and diagnose).
acceptance_criteria: C1-C3 are closed; install buggrabber installs the newest WowAce tag on synthetic retail, Mists Classic, Era, Anniversary and Forever clients and r152 on the 3.3.5a client (real machine, then undone); every tree URL is pinned to one revision, a tag moved mid-fetch cannot mix revisions, unrelated upstream commits show no update, and a locked reinstall fetches the same revision; unsupported packaging is refused by name; net.log shows only allowlisted hosts and zero GitHub REST requests; user catalog overrides keep variants intact; the wowace_listing fuzz target runs at least 30 min clean at G3 and the wowace_bug_grabber_decodes live probe passes.

title: `wowace:` refs, listing parsers and the packaging scanner
description:
## Background `omaddons errors` (B6, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6`) reads BugGrabber's SavedVariables. It is only useful if BugGrabber itself can be installed the way every other addon is: keylessly, verified, undoable. BugGrabber has no keyless release anywhere omaddons already reads (facts as of 2026-10-21): - **GitHub:** `hippuli/BugGrabber` is byte-identical to upstream, but since v11.2.7 every build it publishes is bcc-only. `curseforge-mirror/bug-grabber` is re-tagged several times a day (100 releases in three weeks), has no `release.json`, needs GitHub REST to list assets, and is a third party. - **BugSack's GitHub release does not bundle `!BugGrabber`**; the catalog's BugSack note says today "install it yourself" (`catalog/catalog.toml:115-119`). - **WoWInterface** lists BugGrabber only as discontinued. **Tukui** does not have it. - **Its upstream is WowAce SVN**, public and keyless: `https://repos.wowace.com/wow/bug-grabber/tags//` with 98 tags, the newest `v12.1.0` (trunk r401), and r152 (2010, Interface 30300, GPL v2+), the last 3.3.5-era revision, at the peg path `!svn/bc/152/trunk/`. Plain `GET` works; `HEAD` returns 401. M3-D15 therefore adds a new keyless source, `wowace:`, for WowAce projects. This task builds its **pure half**: the ref grammar and pasted-link parsing, and four parsers that read untrusted server responses and project files. C2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.2`) builds the source on top of them. Because every parser here reads bytes a server or a project author controls, all four are fuzzed. What the parsers read, as observed against the live server (Apache 2.4.18, Subversion 1.9.3, mod_dav_svn): - **`PROPFIND` with `Depth: 1` on `tags/`** returns every tag with its `version-name` in one `207 Multi-Status` response of about 32 KB (for example `v12.0.9/` → 369, `v12.1.0/` → 401). `version-name` is the tag directory's **last-changed revision**. That one number is both the immutable fetch root and the update identity C2 uses. - **`GET …/!svn/bc//tags//`** serves a file, or a directory listing, **as of that revision**, immutable even if someone later edits or re-creates the tag. mod_dav_svn serves directory listings as an HTML index (`
  • name/
    • `) or an XML index (``, ``). - **`.pkgmeta`** is the packager's project file. BugGrabber's (in tags and trunk, unchanged since r134) is only `package-as: "!BugGrabber"`. - **Keywords.** The packager (the BigWigs packager, per its README) can substitute keywords (`@project-version@`, `@project-revision@`, `@localization(…)@`, build dates) and comment out or remove build-type blocks (`--@debug@`, `--@alpha@`, `--@do-not-package@`, `--@retail@`, `--@version-*@`, each with `non-` forms). It can also apply `.pkgmeta` directives: externals, ignore, plain-copy, move-folders, package-as, license-output, changelogs, nolib or per-flavor TOC creation. Dotfiles are never packaged. BugGrabber's only keyword is the TOC's `## Version: @project-version@`; `BugGrabber.lua` and `load.xml` contain no `@` at all, so it has no debug or alpha blocks. **Why a packaging scanner at all (M3-D15).** "No externals" alone would not make a source tree installable: packaging can move, ignore, substitute and comment out code. Shipping an unbuilt tree that happens to load would be a silent correctness bug. The source supports exactly the **source-ready subset** BugGrabber needs, verified against its tree, and refuses everything else by name. The scanner is what makes that refusal possible. This task serves goal **G-M3-3** ("BugGrabber itself installs keylessly, from a pinned upstream revision") and checkpoint criterion 7 (BugGrabber installs keylessly; unsupported packaging is refused, not installed half-built), and checkpoint criterion 11 (every fuzz target runs 10 minutes; `wowace_listing` runs 30 minutes at G3). Decisions that shape it: - **M3-D15** (departure from the vision handoff, comment 606): BugGrabber comes from WowAce's public SVN through a new `wowace:` source that fetches every tree at one immutable revision and supports only the verified packaging subset. - **M3-D16** (context): the catalog (C3) will name `wowace:bug-grabber` and `wowace:bug-grabber#r152` as two disjoint-family variants, so both ref forms this task parses must round-trip. Code facts this task builds on (as of `af10e34`): - `Ref` is defined in `src/model.rs:653` (variants `GitHub`, `Wowi`, `Tukui`, `CurseForge`, `Wago`, `Git { url, rev }`, `Url`, `File`), with `RefKind` at `src/model.rs:603` (`pub const ALL: [Self; 8]`, `prefix()` is the canonical prefix without the colon). - User input is parsed by `parse_user_ref` in `src/sources/refs.rs:68` (canonical refs, pasted URLs, local paths, `owner/repo` shorthand, installed and catalog names); `ParsedRef { ref, version_hint, asset_hint, matched_by }`. - `SourceId::of(&Ref)` (`src/sources/mod.rs:108-118`) maps every ref to its source exhaustively, and `SourceId::ALL` is `[Self; 8]` (`:97`) with wire names at `:121-132`. - An unregistered source makes `SourceRegistry::disabled`/`unavailable` (`src/sources/mod.rs:446-480`) return `source_disabled` ("the … source is not available", fix `omaddons help install`). - `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` is 64 MiB (`src/limits.rs:85`). - Fuzz targets live in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` (17 today: `archive`, `atom_feed`, `bbcode_text`, `bottles`, `bpsv`, `desired_toml`, `heroic`, `html_text`, `lutris`, `product_db`, `ref_parse`, `steam_shortcuts`, `steam_vdf`, `toc`, `tukui_addons`, `wowi_details`, `wowi_filelist`); their seeds are listed and checked in `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`. M3 adds three (`savedvariables`, `wowace_listing`, `backup_tar`), so README's count goes 17 → 20 (G1). ## Technical Approach ### 1. Refs and links **The ref type** (`src/model.rs`, parsed in `src/sources/refs.rs`): - `Ref::WowAce { slug: String, rev: Option }`, with `enum WowAceRev { Tag(String), Revision(u32) }`. - It displays as `wowace:[#|#r]`: - `wowace:`: the newest stable tag; - `wowace:#`: a pinned tag; - `wowace:#r`: a trunk peg revision. - **Grammar:** - the slug rule is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` (the contract summary in the milestone epic's "Contract additions, part 2" comment, §7.8, writes it without the length bound, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; this task's 64-character bound is the specific rule and wins); - a tag is `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,64}$`; - `#r` is `r` followed by a decimal `u32` revision (`r152`). Decided while writing this bead: a `#` value of the form `r` is always read as a revision, never as a tag. WowAce tags are version names (`v12.1.0`), so this is unambiguous in practice; help says so. - **`RefKind::WowAce`** (prefix `wowace`) joins `RefKind::ALL` (8 → 9). `SourceId::of` must stay exhaustive, so this task also adds **`SourceId::Wowace`** (wire `wowace`, display name "WowAce") to `SourceId::ALL` (8 → 9) and `wire()`. The `Source` implementation and its registration are C2's. Until C2 registers it, a parsed `wowace:` ref fails at resolution with the existing `source_disabled` "the WowAce source is not available" path (`SourceRegistry::unavailable`), never with a panic or an unknown-ref error. - **Pasted links** (in `parse_user_ref`'s URL branch, `matched_by: Url`): | Input | Ref | |---|---| | `https://repos.wowace.com/wow//` (with or without the trailing slash, or `…/trunk/…`) | `wowace:` | | `https://repos.wowace.com/wow//tags//` (and any path below it) | `wowace:#` | | `https://repos.wowace.com/wow//!svn/bc//tags//` (and below) | `wowace:#` | | `https://repos.wowace.com/wow//!svn/bc//trunk/` (and below) | `wowace:#r` | | `https://www.wowace.com/projects/` (and below) | `wowace:` | | any `http://` form of the above | the existing `ref_invalid`, with the https suggestion (vision comment 815) | The spec lists the root forms only. Decided while writing this bead: the trailing slash is optional; a live `…/trunk/…` link without a `!svn/bc//` peg maps to `wowace:`, because an unpinned trunk path names no revision to pin; and any path below a tag or a peg root maps as that root does. A `!svn/bc//tags//` link maps to the tag, not the revision: C2 resolves the tag's own last-changed revision through `PROPFIND`, which is the immutable root. The pasted revision is only where the user happened to browse. - **`--version` on a `wowace:` ref** takes a tag or `r`. When it disagrees with a `#` already in the ref, that is a `usage` error (the git rule, vision comment 313), with the fix that drops one of the two. - Round-trip: `Ref::WowAce` → `Display` → `parse_user_ref` gives the same ref for every form; serde uses the same canonical string. ### 2. The listing parsers, `src/sources/wowace/listing.rs` (new) ```rust pub struct Entry { pub name: String, pub dir: bool } pub struct TagRev { pub tag: String, pub rev: u32 } pub fn parse_listing(body: &[u8]) -> Result, ListingError> // mod_dav_svn HTML or XML index pub fn parse_tag_revs(body: &[u8]) -> Result, ListingError> // PROPFIND Depth:1 multistatus on tags/ pub fn newest_stable_tag(tags: &[TagRev]) -> Option<&TagRev> pub struct PkgMeta { pub package_as: Option, pub unsupported: Vec /* keys outside the subset */ } pub fn parse_pkgmeta(body: &str) -> PkgMeta pub fn scan_keywords(path: &str, body: &[u8]) -> KeywordScan // { project_version_lines, unsupported: Vec } ``` All five functions are pure: bytes in, values out, no I/O, no allocation proportional to anything but the (already capped) input. None of them panics on any input (the fuzz target and property tests check this). **`parse_listing`** accepts both index formats mod_dav_svn serves: - the HTML index: `
  • name/
    • ` (a trailing `/` marks a directory); - the XML index: `` and ``. Rules: - **Names are rejected** when they contain `/`, `..`, a control character, or start with `.`. Dotfiles are the one exception to "rejected": they are **skipped silently**, because the packager never packages them. `.pkgmeta` is read separately (C2 fetches it by name, then parses it with `parse_pkgmeta`); every other dotfile is skipped. Decided while writing this bead: the HTML index's parent link (`..`) is skipped as navigation, not rejected. - **Duplicates.** A listing with two names that are equal after case folding fails with `ListingError::DuplicateName` (`duplicate_name`). (WoW loads folders case-insensitively, and the archive inspector would reject the collision later anyway; failing here names the problem.) - **Bounds.** The body is bounded by `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB, enforced by the net layer's response cap before the parser sees it). The entry count is bounded too, so a hostile listing fails as `ListingError::TooManyEntries` instead of building an unbounded vector. The spec names the error but not the cap. Decided while writing this bead: the per-listing cap is `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_FILES` (2,000; the milestone epic's "Contract additions, part 2" comment, §7.11, names C2 as its owner); because C1 lands first, C1 adds that constant to `src/limits.rs` with its `REGISTRY` row (common rule 7) and C2 reuses it for the tree walk. - `ListingError::{NotAListing, TooManyEntries, DuplicateName}`. `NotAListing` covers a body that is neither index format (an error page, a login page, a truncated document). **`parse_tag_revs`** reads the `PROPFIND Depth: 1` multistatus of `tags/`: - each `` element gives `` (the tag directory) and `` (a decimal revision); - it skips the `tags/` collection itself (the response whose href is the requested directory); - it rejects names exactly as `parse_listing` does, and is bounded the same way; - it is a **tolerant, hand-written scanner** for the few elements it needs, with **no XML crate** (no new dependency). It matches the `D:` and `lp1:` prefixes the server sends today; matching on element local names, so another prefix for the same element still parses, is a reasonable hardening the implementer may add; - decided while writing this bead: a response without a parseable `version-name` is skipped, not guessed; a body with no usable response is `NotAListing`. **`newest_stable_tag`:** - parse each tag with `^v?(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))*(?:[-_+]?([A-Za-z]+\d*))?$`; - a suffix of `alpha|beta|rc|pre` (case-insensitive, decided while writing this bead) is **not stable**; tags that do not parse are not candidates; - compare the numeric components numerically, component by component (`v12.1.0` > `v12.0.9`, `v9.9.9` < `v12.0.9`); - ties (for example `v12.1` and `v12.1.0`) go to the **shorter string**; - the revision does not decide "newest": a re-tag of an old version can have a high revision. **`parse_pkgmeta`:** a tolerant line reader, with **no YAML crate**. - It reads `package-as:` (quoted or bare value, decided while writing this bead). The value is **validated by C2** with `FolderName::new`; this parser only extracts it. - It collects every other **top-level** key into `unsupported`, except the metadata-only allowlist of M3-D15: - `manual-changelog`, `changelog-title`, `license-output`, `required-dependencies`, `optional-dependencies`, `tools-used`, `wowi-*` (any key with that prefix), and `enable-nolib-creation: no`. - **Refused keys** therefore include `externals`, `ignore`, `plain-copy`, `move-folders`, `enable-toc-creation: yes`, `enable-nolib-creation` with any value other than `no`, and any key not listed. Decided while writing this bead (what "top-level" means to a line reader): nested lines (indented, or list items) belong to their top-level key and are not keys themselves. - Comments (`#`) and blank lines are ignored (decided while writing this bead). **`scan_keywords`** runs over `.toc`, `.lua` and `.xml` files (the caller decides which files; the function takes the path to know the extension): - it finds `@word@` and `@word(…)@` tokens anywhere in a line; - it finds build-type block markers at line start: `--@` (Lua), ``, `#@no-lib-strip@` at line start (with leading whitespace); `@project-revision@` and `@localization(locale="enUS")@` tokens; `@project-version@` in a `.lua` reported as unsupported; a lone `@` not a token. - **Property (`proptest`, as M2's parsers use it):** none of the four parsers panics on arbitrary bytes; every returned name satisfies the name rules. - **Fuzz:** `wowace_listing` with the seven seeds; `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs` asserts the seeds exist and are listed. ## Considerations - **Hand-written scanners, no XML or YAML crate.** The inputs are small, the needed elements are few, and a new parser crate would grow the binary (11.1 MB today, M5 target under 10 MB) and the dependency surface. Tolerance matters more than completeness: an unknown element is ignored, never a reason to fail, as long as the needed ones are found. - **The scanner must refuse by name.** C2 turns `unsupported` entries into `packaging_unsupported` reasons inside `no_compatible_release`'s `details.tried[]`, naming the key or the file and line. Keep the strings stable and human-readable; they are what a user reads when a project is refused. - **Risk 4 (the milestone epic's "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol" comment, §12.1): WowAce SVN down, its listing format changes, or `PROPFIND` refused** (likelihood L–M, impact M). Mitigation here: the parsers accept the three response formats observed (HTML index, XML index, multistatus) and are fuzzed; C2 adds recorded fixtures, the live probe, the blob cache for reinstalls, and documents the `OPTIONS` + content-digest fallback (designed, not built). CurseForge in M5 is the second route. - **No user-visible advertising before C2.** DEC-1 forbids stubs. C1 lands the grammar and parsers, but README's Sources row, help examples and the network host table change in C2, once the source is registered, so no build advertises a ref it cannot install. Until then a `wowace:` ref fails with the honest `source_disabled` "not available" message. - **Not on a critical path.** The WowAce lane (C1 → C2 → C3) has 5 to 7 units of slack. In the suggested lanes, the widget agent takes C1 (t=1–3) while A2 lands; C2 and C3 follow on the contract-and-sources lane. - **Delivery slice `slice-2` ("Capture and diagnose").** Its exit demo: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal. This task contributes the parsing the keyless install rests on. The agent closing the slice's last task runs the demo and records it on the milestone epic. - **Collision hot spots:** `src/limits.rs` and its snapshot (A2, A5, B1, B3, B5, B6, C2, D1, D2, D3, D4, D10, D11, E2 and E3 all add constants there): re-accept the snapshot in this task and review the diff. `src/model.rs` and `src/sources/mod.rs` gain one variant each; rebase before each gate run. **Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`. 1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed. 2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry. 3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`. 4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`): 1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples); 2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm; 3. `src/app/.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string); 4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`; 5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations; 6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots; 7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test; 8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation; 9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file; 10. README's command reference section; 11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there. 5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`. 6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0". 7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff). 8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.** 9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21). - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`). - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`. 10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before. 11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit. 12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update --claim --transition-comment "claim: "`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:`. Run `br lint --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``) defined in the milestone epic body. 13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`). 14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works. 15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result. 16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46). ## Dependencies **Blocked by:** - none **Unblocks:** - C2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.2` (The WowAce source): the `wowace:` ref and its links, `SourceId::Wowace`, and the five pure functions (`parse_listing`, `parse_tag_revs`, `newest_stable_tag`, `parse_pkgmeta`, `scan_keywords`) that the source's fetch, pinned-tree walk and packaging-subset checks are built from. Parent: the C epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3`. Delivery slice: `slice-2`. C3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3`) depends on this task through C2: its catalog variants name `wowace:bug-grabber` and `wowace:bug-grabber#r152`.
acceptance_criteria: Refs and links round-trip: wowace:bug-grabber, wowace:bug-grabber#v12.1.0 and wowace:bug-grabber#r152 parse, display and re-parse identically, each pasted repos.wowace.com and www.wowace.com/projects link form maps to its ref, and an http:// link gives ref_invalid with the https suggestion; --version on a wowace: ref accepts a tag or r<rev>, and disagreeing with the ref's # is a usage error with a fix; a slug or tag outside its grammar is ref_invalid; RefKind::ALL and SourceId::ALL list wowace with their count and wire-name tests updated, and a wowace: ref before C2 registers the source fails with source_disabled, not a panic; listings and multistatus bodies parse hand-written copies of the documented shapes (C2 records the real fixtures and re-runs these parsers over them); parse_listing rejects names with /, .. or control characters, skips dotfiles, fails DuplicateName on names equal after case folding, TooManyEntries past its cap and NotAListing on a non-listing body; newest_stable_tag over [v12.0.9@369, v12.1.0@401, v12.1.0-beta1@399, v9.9.9@100] is v12.1.0@401; BugGrabber's .pkgmeta (package-as: "!BugGrabber") gives package_as !BugGrabber and no unsupported key, one with externals:, move-folders: or ignore: lists each, and the metadata-only allowlist keys are not listed; BugGrabber's v12.1.0 files give only the supported @project-version@ in the TOC, and a planted --@debug@ block or @project-revision@ is reported with its file and line; the wowace_listing fuzz target and its seeds exist and are listed in tests/fuzz_seeds.rs, run 10 minutes without a crash at close (recorded) and at least 30 minutes at G3; WOWACE_TREE_MAX_FILES (2,000) is in src/limits.rs with its REGISTRY row and the limit_registries snapshot re-accepted; the close comment lists the new wire names (ref prefix and source id wowace, the limit WOWACE_TREE_MAX_FILES)
