comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** `omaddons errors` is only as useful as the BugGrabber install behind it, and today the only way to get BugGrabber is a browser download: no keyless source omaddons reads carries it. This bead is the pure, fuzzed foundation of the new `wowace:` source: the ref grammar and pasted links, and the four parsers for what WowAce's SVN server and a project's packaging files say. C2 builds the network source on it, and C3 makes `omaddons install buggrabber` work on every client from it. Keeping these parsers pure and separate means the untrusted-input half of the source is fuzzed and unit-tested before any request is made, which is how M1 and M2 built every other source (TOC, BPSV, WoWInterface and Tukui parsers each have their own fuzz target). It serves the thesis directly: omaddons stays the sole, keyless, verified authority over every addon, including the one that makes errors visible.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D15 (departure from the vision's M2→M3 handoff, comment 606): BugGrabber comes from WowAce's public SVN through a new `wowace:` source**, with three ref forms (`wowace:<slug>`, `#<tag>`, `#r<rev>`) and pasted links, every tree fetched at one immutable revision, and only the verified packaging subset supported. Why: it is BugGrabber's real upstream (byte-identical to the GitHub mirror, official tags), keyless, and it serves both modern BugGrabber and r152 for 3.3.5a (GPL). Rejected: `hippuli/BugGrabber` (bcc-only since v11.2.7); `curseforge-mirror/bug-grabber` (re-tagged several times a day, which means phantom updates, no `release.json`, REST to list assets, a third party); CurseForge's undocumented website API (terms risk, contrary to vision D4); `--file` only (a poor experience, kept as a fallback); bundling BugGrabber (modern BugGrabber is "All Rights Reserved"); and advertising every no-externals project as supported. The handoff listed a git mirror, CurseForge in M5, or a manual `--file`; this is a fourth option chosen with evidence, which G2 records with the new host.
- **M3-D15, the packaging subset, is why `parse_pkgmeta` and `scan_keywords` exist.** "No externals" alone would not make a source tree installable, because packaging can move, ignore, substitute and comment out code. The metadata-only `.pkgmeta` keys are allowed (`manual-changelog`, `changelog-title`, `license-output`, `required-dependencies`, `optional-dependencies`, `tools-used`, `wowi-*`, `enable-nolib-creation: no`), `package-as` is honoured, and everything else is refused by name; `@project-version@` in a TOC is the only keyword.
- **M3-D16 (context): disjoint catalog variants.** C3 ships `BugGrabber#modern` as `wowace:bug-grabber` and `BugGrabber#r152` as `wowace:bug-grabber#r152`, so both forms must round-trip exactly.
- **Common rule 15, bounded work:** every parser reads untrusted bytes, so each is bounded (the response cap, an entry cap) and reports exhaustion as an error, never a clean partial result.
- **Decisions made while writing this bead:** a `#r<digits>` value is always a revision, never a tag; the HTML index's parent link is skipped, not rejected; the per-listing entry cap is `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_FILES`, which C1 adds to `src/limits.rs` because it lands before C2 (the contract table names C2 as its owner; C2 reuses it); keyword tokens are `@[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*@` and `@word(…)@`, erring towards reporting, with block markers allowed after leading whitespace and each finding reported as `<path>:<line>: <token>`; the link table's optional trailing slash, unpinned `…/trunk/…` → `wowace:<slug>` and paths below a root; a multistatus response without a parseable `version-name` skipped; case-insensitive pre-release suffixes; `.pkgmeta` comments ignored and nested lines not counted as keys; and C1 adds `SourceId::Wowace` alongside `Ref::WowAce` because `SourceId::of` is an exhaustive match, leaving the `Source` implementation and its registration to C2.

**Review-round changes folded in.** Review round 3, revision 12 ("immutable WowAce trees; a narrow packaging promise"), was adopted: the first draft fetched live tag paths and zipped them with sorted, timestamp-fixed entries, which is deterministic serialization of a tree that may itself be mixed. The design now uses `PROPFIND` (`Depth: 1`) on `tags/` to learn each tag's last-changed revision, which serves both as the immutable fetch root and as the update identity, so this bead gained `parse_tag_revs`. The same revision added the packaging allowlist and the keyword scanner, so this bead gained `parse_pkgmeta`'s allowlist semantics and `scan_keywords`. The `OPTIONS` + content-digest fallback for a refused `PROPFIND` is designed, not built.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- WowAce SVN at `https://repos.wowace.com/wow/bug-grabber/` serves 98 tags, the newest `v12.1.0`; plain `GET` works and `HEAD` returns 401; r152 is at `!svn/bc/152/trunk/` (Apache 2.4.18, Subversion 1.9.3, mod_dav_svn).
- `PROPFIND` `Depth: 1` on `tags/` returns every tag's `version-name` in one 207 response of about 32 KB (`v12.0.9/` → 369, `v12.1.0/` → 401); `GET …/!svn/bc/<rev>/tags/<tag>/<path>` serves a file or listing as of that revision; the third review fetched `!svn/bc/401/tags/v12.1.0/!BugGrabber.toc`. SVN tags are ordinary directories and can change after creation.
- BugGrabber's `.pkgmeta` (tags and trunk, unchanged since r134) is only `package-as: "!BugGrabber"`; its only keyword is the TOC's `## Version: @project-version@`; `BugGrabber.lua` and `load.xml` contain no `@`.
- The BigWigs packager's documented directives, keywords and build-type blocks are as listed in the Background.
- `Ref` is at `src/model.rs:653` and `RefKind` at `src/model.rs:603` (`ALL: [Self; 8]`); `parse_user_ref` at `src/sources/refs.rs:68`; `SourceId::of` at `src/sources/mod.rs:108-118` (exhaustive), `SourceId::ALL: [Self; 8]` at `:97`; an unregistered source gives `source_disabled` through `SourceRegistry::unavailable` (`src/sources/mod.rs:446-480`); `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` is 64 MiB (`src/limits.rs:85`); 17 fuzz targets exist today, with seeds checked by `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- **Risk 4 (the milestone epic's "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol" comment, §12.1): WowAce SVN down, its listing format changes, or `PROPFIND` refused** (L–M likelihood, M impact). The parsers accept all three observed formats and are fuzzed; C2 adds recorded fixtures, a live probe at checkpoints, offline reinstalls from the blob cache, and the documented `OPTIONS` fallback; `--file` stays; CurseForge in M5 is a second route.
- **A scanner false negative installs a half-built project.** The token rule errs towards reporting, and refusal is by name, so a false positive is visible and fixable while a false negative is not.
- **Hand-written XML and YAML readers miss an edge case.** They read only a few elements and keys, ignore everything else, and are property-tested and fuzzed for no panic.

**Confidence.** High: pure parsers over a small, observed input format, fuzzed and table-tested; the external-host risk sits in C2, not here.

title: The WowAce source
description:
## Background

`omaddons errors` reads BugGrabber's data, but BugGrabber has no keyless release anywhere omaddons already reads: GitHub's `hippuli/BugGrabber` has been bcc-only since v11.2.7, `curseforge-mirror/bug-grabber` re-tags several times a day and has no `release.json`, BugSack's GitHub release does not bundle `!BugGrabber`, WoWInterface lists it only as discontinued, and Tukui does not have it. Its upstream is **WowAce SVN**, public and keyless. This task turns `wowace:` refs (parsed by C1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.1`) into installable, TOC-verified releases through the same fetch → select → verify pipeline as every other source (vision D28). Without it, `errors` would begin with "download this in a browser", which contradicts vision G2 (keyless by default) in the one feature that most needs a dependency.

**The two properties that make this source safe** (M3-D15):
1. **Every tree is fetched at one immutable revision.** SVN tags are ordinary directories and can change after creation, so fetching files through live `tags/<tag>/` paths can mix revisions. Instead, one `PROPFIND` (`Depth: 1`) on `tags/` returns each tag's `version-name`, the revision at which that tag directory last changed, and every listing and file is fetched through `!svn/bc/<rev>/tags/<tag>/…`, the tag as of that revision. The same number is the update identity: a commit elsewhere in the repository never moves it, so it never shows as a phantom update.
2. **Only the verified packaging subset is supported.** WowAce projects are normally built by a packager that can move, ignore, substitute and comment out code. "No externals" alone would not make a source tree installable; shipping an unbuilt tree that happens to load would be a silent correctness bug. This source assembles the zip deterministically, as the packager would build a project that needs nothing but `package-as` and `@project-version@`, and refuses everything else by name.

Facts as observed on 2026-10-21 against the live server (Apache 2.4.18, Subversion 1.9.3, mod_dav_svn):
- `https://repos.wowace.com/wow/bug-grabber/tags/<tag>/`: 98 tags, the newest `v12.1.0`. Plain `GET` works; **`HEAD` returns 401**.
- `PROPFIND` with `Depth: 1` on `tags/` returns every tag with its `version-name` in one `207` response of about 32 KB (`v12.0.9/` → 369, `v12.1.0/` → 401).
- `GET …/!svn/bc/<rev>/tags/<tag>/<path>` serves a file or a directory listing as of that revision, immutable even if someone later edits or re-creates the tag. The third review fetched `!svn/bc/401/tags/v12.1.0/!BugGrabber.toc`.
- `OPTIONS` with a `<D:options><D:activity-collection-set/></D:options>` body returns `svn-youngest-rev` (the basis of a fallback that is designed, not built; see Considerations).
- r152 (2010, Interface 30300, GPL v2+), the last 3.3.5-era revision, is at the peg path `!svn/bc/152/trunk/`.
- **BugGrabber's packaging:** `.pkgmeta` (tags and trunk, unchanged since r134) is only `package-as: "!BugGrabber"`. Its only keyword is the TOC's `## Version: @project-version@`; `BugGrabber.lua` and `load.xml` contain no `@` at all. The v12.1.0 tree is 5 files and the r152 tree 4 files, so a stable install costs 7 requests.
- **Modern BugGrabber's entry schema** (the live probe's tripwire): entries are `{message, session, time = time(), counter, stack?, locals?}`; a repeat bumps `counter`, moves `time` to the latest occurrence, updates `session`, and moves the entry to the end. The client writes SavedVariables only at logout, `/reload` and disconnect.

This task serves goal **G-M3-3** (BugGrabber installs keylessly, from a pinned upstream revision) and is the core of checkpoint criterion 7: `omaddons install buggrabber` installs the newest WowAce tag on synthetic retail, Mists Classic, Era, Anniversary and Forever clients and r152 on 3.3.5a; every file of the tag is fetched at one recorded revision; a tag moved mid-fetch cannot mix revisions; an unrelated upstream commit never shows as an update; a locked reinstall fetches the same revision again; unsupported packaging is refused, not installed half-built; `net.log` shows only allowlisted hosts and zero GitHub REST requests. It also feeds criterion 11 (live probes at G3) and the slice-2 demo.

Decisions that shape it: **M3-D15** (the source, its identity, immutability and packaging subset; a departure from the vision handoff that G2 records together with the new host in the vision D13 allowlist), **M3-D16** (C3's catalog variants name `wowace:bug-grabber` and `wowace:bug-grabber#r152`), and the M3 decision recorded in this task's close comment that a WowAce download carries **no `download_unverified` warning** (TLS plus TOC verification, the same posture as GitHub's no-REST path).

Code facts this task builds on (as of `af10e34`):
- The `Source` trait is `src/sources/mod.rs:237` (`fn id`, `fn fetch(&self, wanted: &[Wanted], http: &dyn Http) -> Vec<Result<ReleaseSet>>`, an optional `fn probe`). Sources are registered in `SourceRegistry`; an unregistered or disabled source gives `source_disabled` through `SourceRegistry::disabled`/`unavailable` (`:446-480`), whose disabled-in-config fix is `omaddons config set sources.<id>.enabled true` (`:461`). Config accepts `sources.*.enabled` (`src/state/config.rs:300`).
- `AssetLocation` (`src/model.rs:962-984`) has `Url`, `LocalZip`, `LocalDir`, `GitCheckout { url, rev, sha }` and `Deferred { source, key }`. `Deferred` resolves to **one URL** right before each attempt (`Source::resolve_asset`; `src/sources/mod.rs:254`, `:337-344`) and cannot fetch a tree.
- The planner's `GitCheckout` arm (`src/engine/plan.rs:4025-4027`) calls `TargetPlanner::checkout` (`:4173-4191`), which materializes the checkout into `paths.cache_tmp(&tx).join("git")/<n>/<name>` through `WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Derived, …)` and `ensure_dir_all`, and then inspects it in place with `inspect_dir` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:501`). **At `af10e34` the git path does not pack a checkout into the blob cache**: the arm returns no downloaded blob, and the download path treats `GitCheckout` as "not downloaded" (`plan.rs:4302-4307`).
- Cached archives are reused through `local_blob_candidate` (`src/engine/plan.rs:4473-4500`), which turns a cached blob (looked up by SHA-256) into a `LocalZip` candidate carrying the release's identity: reinstalls use it, and `sync --locked` does when the `addons.toml` entry carries a `sha256` (`src/app/sync.rs:145-173`). Blobs are stored through `BlobCache::store_stream`/`store_checked` (`src/engine/blobs.rs:157-185`), content-addressed by SHA-256.
- `Release` (`src/model.rs:929-945`) has `release_id`, `version`, `channel`, `published_at`, `assets`, `changelog_url`, `notes`, `name_hint`; it has no revision. `AddonRecord` (`src/model.rs:557-575`) has `release_id: Option<String>` and `version`; the `addons.toml` entry (`src/state/desired.rs:77-97`) has `version`, `pinned`, `dependency`, `sha256`.
- The net layer has only `Method::{Get, Head}` (`src/net/mod.rs:46-58`); `Request` has no body (`:80-108`); `UreqTransport::send` matches the two methods (`src/net/client.rs:64-79`); `src/net/retry.rs:8` documents "the net layer only has GET and HEAD, so every retried request is idempotent". Fixtures are keyed by `request_key(method, url)` (`src/net/replay.rs:66-67`), and record mode names files `<method>-<slug>-<hash>` (`src/net/record.rs:49-66`).
- The always-allowed HTTP host list is `ALWAYS` in `src/net/allowlist.rs:8`; git hosts are a separate, disjoint list (test `git_hosts_and_http_hosts_are_disjoint`, `:133`).
- Politeness (`src/politeness.rs`): `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST = 3` (`:18`), `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` 15 min (`:35`), connect 10 s, `API_READ_TIMEOUT` 30 s, up to 3 retries with jittered backoff capped at 8 s, `Retry-After` honoured up to 60 s. Limits: `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` 512 MiB (`src/limits.rs:33`), `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` 64 MiB (`:85`).
- Dependencies already present: `ureq` 3.4.2 (rustls), `zip` 9.0.3 with Deflate (`Cargo.toml:34-35`). No new crate is needed.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/sources/wowace.rs` (new), implementing `Source`

The source id is `wowace` (`SourceId::Wowace`, added by C1 with the ref). This task registers the implementation in `SourceRegistry`, honouring `sources.wowace.enabled`.

**`fetch`**, per ref form (`Ref::WowAce { slug, rev }`):

| Ref | Requests | Release |
|---|---|---|
| `wowace:<slug>` (no rev) | `PROPFIND https://repos.wowace.com/wow/<slug>/tags/`, `Depth: 1`, a `version-name` prop body, purpose `wowace-tags`; then `newest_stable_tag` (C1) | `release_id = wowace:<slug>@<tag>`, `version = <tag>`, `revision = <tag rev>`, base `…/!svn/bc/<rev>/tags/<tag>/` |
| `wowace:<slug>#<tag>` | the same `PROPFIND`, to learn that tag's revision; an absent tag is `not_found` | as above, for that tag |
| `wowace:<slug>#r<rev>` | none at fetch time | `release_id = wowace:<slug>@r<rev>`, `version = r<rev>`, `revision = <rev>`, base `…/!svn/bc/<rev>/trunk/` |

- The `PROPFIND` body is fixed, for example `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?><D:propfind xmlns:D="DAV:"><D:prop><D:version-name/></D:prop></D:propfind>`. The response is parsed with C1's `parse_tag_revs`.
- `Release` gains **`revision: Option<u32>`** (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, additive), so "a resolved release records `revision`".
- Each release has **one asset of a new location, `AssetLocation::WowAceTree { base, revision }`**. `Deferred` cannot be used: it resolves to one URL and cannot fetch a tree. Decided while writing this bead: the enum's `snake_case` would spell the variant `wow_ace_tree`, so it carries `#[serde(rename = "wowace_tree")]` to match the source id.
- The new location follows **`AssetLocation::GitCheckout`'s path end to end**: the planner materializes the tree into `<cache>/tmp/<tx>/wowace/<slug>/` (`Writer::Derived`, through fsx, exactly as `TargetPlanner::checkout` does for git), inspects it as a local directory with `inspect_dir`, and from then on archive inspection, TOC verification and staging are unchanged.
- **Caching the archive for offline reinstalls.** The spec intends the tree's archive to be cached "the way git checkouts are cached", so reinstall and undo work offline. At `af10e34` git checkouts are **not** packed into the blob cache (see Background), so this task does the packing itself, in the planner arm for `WowAceTree` (the steps below are decided while writing this bead; confirm them in the close comment):
  - after materializing, pack the tree into the **deterministic zip** described below and store it with `BlobCache::store_stream` (content-addressed by SHA-256);
  - treat that blob as the candidate's download, so `TargetPlanner::learn` records its SHA-256 and the `loads` verdict in the release memo's candidate facts, exactly as for a URL asset;
  - key the facts by the **blob-cache key `wowace:<slug>/tags/<tag>@r<rev>`** (trunk pegs: `wowace:<slug>/trunk@r<rev>`), so a re-tag of the same tag never reuses the old tree's facts or blob;
  - later reinstalls (`install --reinstall`) and `sync --locked` with the entry's `sha256` then reuse the blob through `local_blob_candidate` with no network. Undo works offline too: it restores from the transaction's snapshots and never needs the blob.
- **The lock entry records `revision`, so `sync --locked` fetches exactly that revision.** Decided while writing this bead (the spec says what must be recorded, not where): `AddonRecord` gains the same optional `revision: Option<u32>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, no schema bump; older binaries ignore the unknown field, as M2's optional `recorded_at_ns` showed), carried from the release at install; `export` writes it into the `addons.toml` entry as `revision = 401` (a new optional key in `src/state/desired.rs`'s `Entry`); `sync --locked` fetches that tag at the recorded revision directly, with base `…/!svn/bc/<recorded rev>/tags/<tag>/` (the tag as of that revision, not trunk, and no `PROPFIND` needed), so the tree is the recorded one whether or not the tag has moved since. Without a cached blob, `sync --locked` still fetches the recorded revision, never the tag's current state.

**Materializing the tree** (in the planner arm, using the shared HTTP pool):
- **Every listing and file is fetched under `base`**, the pinned `!svn/bc/<rev>/…` path, **never** a live `tags/<tag>/` path. A tag that changes mid-fetch therefore cannot mix revisions.
- The walk issues purpose `wowace-tree` per directory listing (parsed with C1's `parse_listing`) and `wowace-file` per file, through the shared pool (`MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST` 3, the standard retries).
- It is bounded by:

  | Constant (`src/limits.rs`, non-config) | Value | Purpose |
  |---|---|---|
  | `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_FILES` | 2,000 | Files fetched per tag tree. C1 adds it to `src/limits.rs` (with its `REGISTRY` row) as `parse_listing`'s per-listing entry cap, because C1 lands first; this task reuses it for the walk (a choice recorded in C1's bead; the contract table names C2 as its owner) |
  | `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_DIRS` | 200 | Directory listings fetched per tag tree |
  | `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_DEPTH` | 8 | Directory depth fetched |
  | `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_REQUESTS` | 2,500 | Requests per tree, retries included |

  plus `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB) in total over all files. Each constant this task adds (the other three) gets a `REGISTRY` row and a `LIMIT_NAMES` entry; re-accept the `limit_registries` snapshot (common rule 7). Exceeding any bound fails the candidate cleanly, before anything is staged, and leaves no partial install.
- **Collisions.** Paths that collide after case folding, or a directory listed twice on one walk (a cycle), fail the candidate with `bad_archive`, `details.reason: "tree_collision"`.
- **`.pkgmeta`.** Read it if present (`parse_pkgmeta`). `package-as` must pass `FolderName::new`, else the candidate fails with `packaging_unsupported`. Any `unsupported` key fails the candidate with reason `packaging_unsupported`, which `no_compatible_release` lists in `details.tried[]` with the key.
- **Keywords.** Run `scan_keywords` on every `.toc`, `.lua` and `.xml`. Any unsupported token or block marker fails the candidate the same way (`packaging_unsupported`), naming the file and line.
- **Writing the tree.** Write each file under the root `<package-as or slug>/` (BugGrabber: `!BugGrabber/`), dotfiles excluded, replacing `@project-version@` in `.toc` files with the tag name (or `r<rev>` for a trunk peg). For v12.1.0 the TOC's version line then reads `## Version: v12.1.0`.
- **Deterministic packing.** Pack the tree for the blob cache the way a checkout would be packed, as a **deterministic zip**: entries sorted by path, every timestamp `1980-01-01T00:00:00`, Deflate, fixed permissions (the permissions are decided while writing this bead, for determinism). The same pinned revision always yields the same blob SHA-256. (`zip` 9 with `SimpleFileOptions`'s default `DateTime` gives the 1980 epoch.)

**Changelog:** `changelog_unavailable: not_supported` (the existing `ChangelogUnavailable::NotSupported`, `src/sources/changelog.rs:49`). No changelog is read from WowAce in M3.

**Updates** (how `outdated`, `update` and `status` see a WowAce addon):
- The release memo caches the `PROPFIND` result like other sources' listings: `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` (15 min). The server sends no validators, so a refetch after the window is a full request of about 32 KB.
- **An update exists when the newest stable tag's name differs from the installed one, or when the same tag's revision moved** (shown as "v12.1.0 (re-tagged upstream)"). Because `release_id` is `wowace:<slug>@<tag>` for both, the update evaluator (`src/resolve/updates.rs`) compares the recorded `revision` as well for `wowace` records: same release id and a different revision is `update_available`.
- **Commits elsewhere in the repository move neither**, so they never show as an update. That is why the repository's youngest revision is never used as identity (M3-D15, rejected alternative vii).
- A `#r<rev>` ref is pinned by construction: it never shows an update.

**Error and item mapping** (all existing codes; the milestone epic's "Contract additions, part 2" comment, §7.6 and §7.8):

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| `#<tag>` not in the `PROPFIND` listing | `not_found` |
| No stable tag at all | `no_compatible_release` (empty selection) |
| `.pkgmeta` key outside the subset, a `package-as` that fails `FolderName::new`, or an unsupported keyword or block marker | the candidate fails; `no_compatible_release` lists it in `details.tried[]` with reason `packaging_unsupported` and `details` naming the key, or the file and line (`externals_unsupported` is folded into `packaging_unsupported`) |
| Case-fold collision or a directory cycle in the tree | `bad_archive`, `details.reason: "tree_collision"` |
| A tree bound exceeded | the candidate fails cleanly (the bound's name in the message), no partial install |
| The newest tag does not load on this client (3.3.5a without a pin) | `no_compatible_release`, the TOC guard working |
| `--offline` with nothing cached | `offline` |
| `sources.wowace.enabled = false` | `source_disabled`, with the fix `omaddons config set sources.wowace.enabled true` |
| A non-listing or malformed response | the C1 parser's error, surfaced as a source failure for that ref (retryable only where the transport says so) |

The spec settles the `not_found`, `packaging_unsupported`, `tree_collision`, TOC-guard, `offline` and `source_disabled` rows. Decided while writing this bead: the empty-selection `no_compatible_release` for a project with no stable tag, the malformed-response row, and naming the exceeded bound in the message (the spec says only "fails cleanly, without a partial install").

### 2. Net

- **Host.** `repos.wowace.com` joins the always-allowed list (`ALWAYS`, `src/net/allowlist.rs:8`), **never** the git host list (the disjointness test stays green). Each redirect hop is still checked.
- **`PROPFIND`** becomes an allowed method **for this source only**: idempotent, retried like a GET, with a fixed request body and `Depth: 1`, through the same pool, politeness and response cap. The net layer gains it as a **typed request kind, not a free-form method string**:
  - add `Method::Propfind` (`as_str` → `"PROPFIND"`) whose body is the fixed `version-name` propfind document; a constructor such as `Request::propfind_version_names(url, purpose)` sets `Depth: 1` and `Content-Type: text/xml` and is the only way to build one;
  - `UreqTransport::send` (`src/net/client.rs:64-79`) builds it as an `http::Request` with `http::Method::from_bytes(b"PROPFIND")` and the fixed body, sent through the same agent. Check what ureq 3.4.2 requires for a non-standard method with a body (its agent config may need non-standard methods allowed) and cover it with a transport test;
  - update `src/net/retry.rs`'s module doc (`:8`): GET, HEAD and PROPFIND are all idempotent, so every retried request still is;
  - replay and record already key by method and URL (`request_key`), so a `PROPFIND` fixture is `PROPFIND <url>`; because the body is fixed, no body-keyed fixtures are needed.
- **Purposes** (in `net.log`): `wowace-tags` (the `PROPFIND` of `tags/`), `wowace-tree` (pinned directory listings), `wowace-file`.
- **`HEAD` returns 401**, so only `GET` and `PROPFIND` are used. Nothing in the source may issue a `HEAD` (the shared download path's optional HEAD probe, if any, must be skipped for this source).
- No GitHub request of any kind is made, so a BugGrabber install shows zero `api.github.com` requests.

### 3. Config

- `[sources.wowace] enabled` (default `true`, bool), a `KEYS` row via the existing `sources.<id>.enabled` mechanism (`src/state/config.rs:300`). Disabled → `source_disabled`, with the fix that re-enables it.

### 4. Fixtures

- `OMADDONS_RECORD=1` records `tests/fixtures/http/wowace-bug-grabber/`: the `PROPFIND` response, the v12.1.0 tree at its revision (5 files), and the r152 tree (4 files), with query secrets stripped (there are none).
- Hand-edited replay variants for the tests below: a `PROPFIND` where only an unrelated tag's `version-name` changed; one where `v12.1.0`'s moved; a tree with `externals:`/`move-folders:` in `.pkgmeta`; a tree with a `--@debug@` block; a tree with a case-fold collision and one with a repeated directory; a tree over `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_DIRS` and over `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_REQUESTS`; a fixture in which the **live** `tags/v12.1.0/` path serves different bytes (it must never be requested).
- Run C1's parsers over the recorded bodies too (a test in `tests/sources_wowace.rs`), so the hand-written shapes C1 tested against are confirmed against the real server's.
- Replay tests: `tests/sources_wowace.rs` (new).

### 5. Live probe `live_probes::wowace_bug_grabber_decodes` (`OMADDONS_LIVE=1`)

In `tests/live_probes.rs` (beside `catalog_matches_declared_flavors`, `:139`):
- fetch the tags `PROPFIND` and the newest tag at its revision, assemble it, and verify its TOC lists modern interfaces;
- fetch r152, and verify `## Interface: 30300`;
- read the newest tag's `BugGrabber.lua` and assert it still builds entries with `message =`, `session =`, `time = time()` and `counter = 1`. **This is the schema-drift tripwire for risk 5**: a changed `errorObject` or a mid-session write model would break B3's decoders and M3-D19's session watermarks;
- assert the newest tag still passes the packaging subset (no new `.pkgmeta` key, no new keyword).

### 6. README (same commit, common rule 11)

- the Sources table row (`wowace:`, pinned revisions);
- the Network host table row (`repos.wowace.com`: "WowAce SVN tags (BugGrabber); used");
- the `net.log` purposes (`wowace-tags`, `wowace-tree`, `wowace-file`; `PROPFIND` for tags);
- the "What a stable install costs" paragraph for WowAce: 1 `PROPFIND` plus the tree's directories plus its files, which is 7 requests for BugGrabber; a repeat check within 15 minutes costs nothing, after it one ~32 KB `PROPFIND`;
- the Configuration section: `sources.wowace.enabled`;
- Limitations: "WowAce projects that need packaging steps (externals, moved folders, build-time keywords) are not supported".

### Files

- `src/sources/wowace.rs` (new); `src/sources/mod.rs` (registration).
- `src/model.rs` (`AssetLocation::WowAceTree`, `Release.revision`, `AddonRecord.revision`).
- `src/engine/plan.rs` (the `WowAceTree` arm: materialize, inspect, pack, store, learn).
- `src/net/mod.rs`, `src/net/client.rs`, `src/net/retry.rs` (doc), `src/net/allowlist.rs`.
- `src/resolve/updates.rs` (re-tag detection), `src/state/desired.rs` and `src/app/export.rs`/`src/app/sync.rs` (`revision` in the lock entry).
- `src/state/config.rs` (`KEYS` row), `src/limits.rs` (+ snapshot).
- `tests/sources_wowace.rs` (new), `tests/fixtures/http/wowace-bug-grabber/` (recorded), `tests/live_probes.rs`, contract snapshots touched by the new `AssetLocation` variant in dry-run output.
- README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Replayed install:** `install wowace:bug-grabber -t retail` installs `!BugGrabber` from v12.1.0 at revision 401, TOC-verified, with the TOC's version line reading `v12.1.0`. Every `net.log` line of the run is a `repos.wowace.com` request with a `wowace-*` purpose, and every tree URL contains `!svn/bc/401/`. No `HEAD` and no `api.github.com` request appears.
- **Immutability:**
  - two assemblies of the same pinned tree produce the same blob SHA-256;
  - a replay in which the live tag path serves different bytes mid-fetch cannot change the result, because no live path is requested;
  - a `PROPFIND` replay where only an unrelated tag's revision changed reports no update;
  - one where `v12.1.0`'s revision moved reports a re-tag update ("re-tagged upstream");
  - `sync --locked` refetches the recorded revision (the `addons.toml` entry carries `revision`), and with the blob cached it reinstalls with no network.
- `-t wotlk` with `#r152` installs the r152 folder. `wowace:bug-grabber` on wotlk without a pin is `no_compatible_release`, because the newest tag does not load on 3.3.5a: the guard working.
- A project with `externals`, `move-folders` or a `--@debug@` block is refused with `packaging_unsupported` in `tried`, naming the key or the file and line. A `package-as` that fails `FolderName::new` is refused the same way.
- A tree with a case-fold collision or a repeated directory fails with `bad_archive` and `details.reason: "tree_collision"`.
- A tree exceeding `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_DIRS` or `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_REQUESTS` fails cleanly, without a partial install.
- `--offline` gives `offline`. A disabled source gives `source_disabled` with the re-enable fix.
- `info wowace:bug-grabber --changelog` reports `changelog_unavailable: not_supported`; no `download_unverified` warning is emitted for a WowAce install.
- The four `WOWACE_TREE_*` constants have `REGISTRY` rows (C1 added `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_FILES`; this task adds the other three) and the snapshot is re-accepted; `sources.wowace.enabled` is a config key with default `true`.
- README carries the Sources row, host row, purposes, the cost paragraph, the config key and the limitation.
- The live probe `wowace_bug_grabber_decodes` passes at G3 (the spec's criterion); running it at close too, with the result in the close comment, is decided while writing this bead.
- The close comment lists the new wire names: source id `wowace`, asset location `wowace_tree`, release and record key `revision`, `addons.toml` key `revision`, purposes `wowace-tags`/`wowace-tree`/`wowace-file`, host `repos.wowace.com`, `tried[]` reason `packaging_unsupported`, `bad_archive` reason `tree_collision`, config key `sources.wowace.enabled`, the three limits this task adds, and the "no `download_unverified`" decision.

## Test Plan

- **E2E replay, `tests/sources_wowace.rs` (new):**
  - `install wowace:bug-grabber -t retail` from the recorded fixtures: folder, TOC version line, `net.log` hosts and purposes, every tree URL pinned at `!svn/bc/401/`;
  - `-t wotlk` with `#r152`; `-t wotlk` without a pin → `no_compatible_release`;
  - determinism: assemble the same pinned tree twice (two homes) → same blob SHA-256;
  - live-path poisoning fixture: the live `tags/v12.1.0/` path serves other bytes; the result is unchanged and the path never appears in `net.log`;
  - update identity: `outdated` after a `PROPFIND` where an unrelated tag moved (no update) and where `v12.1.0` moved (a re-tag update);
  - `export` then `sync --locked` into a fresh target: the recorded revision is fetched; with the blob cached and `--offline`, it reinstalls with no request;
  - packaging refusals: `externals`, `move-folders`, `ignore` keys; a `--@debug@` block; a bad `package-as`; each in `details.tried[]` as `packaging_unsupported` with its key or file and line;
  - `tree_collision` (case fold; repeated directory);
  - bounds: over `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_DIRS`, over `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_REQUESTS` (retries counted); no staged folder left behind;
  - `--offline` → `offline`; `config set sources.wowace.enabled false` → `source_disabled` with the fix;
  - C1's parsers over the recorded bodies.
- **Unit:** the deterministic zip writer (sorted entries, fixed timestamps, stable hash); the `@project-version@` substitution only in `.toc`; the re-tag rule in the update evaluator; `Method::Propfind` round-trip through the replay transport (`request_key`), and a transport-level test that the method and body are sent.
- **Net:** the allowlist test gains `repos.wowace.com` in `ALWAYS` and keeps `git_hosts_and_http_hosts_are_disjoint` green; a test that a `HEAD` is never issued by this source.
- **Contract:** dry-run snapshots that include a WowAce candidate (the new `AssetLocation` variant); `source_disabled` and `no_compatible_release` rows if the matrix gains a WowAce case.
- **Live:** `wowace_bug_grabber_decodes` (`OMADDONS_LIVE=1`, ignored by default).
- **Crash:** no new journal shape or recovery rule; the existing install crash matrix covers the commit, because staging and commit are unchanged. The materialized tree under `<cache>/tmp/<tx>/` is swept like a git checkout's.

## Considerations

- **SVN availability is outside our control.** The memo and blob cache make reinstalls offline-safe, and the M5 CurseForge source becomes a second route. `--file` remains a manual fallback.
- **If `PROPFIND` is ever refused** (a server change), the fallback would be pinning at the `svn-youngest-rev` from `OPTIONS`, with a content-digest identity. It is **not built in M3**. The live probe detects the change, and risk 4 tracks it.
- **The 15-minute window** keeps `outdated` polite: about 32 KB per check per project after the window, nothing within it.
- **No hash comes from the server.** The transfer is TLS-protected and the TOCs are verified, the same posture as GitHub's no-REST path, so no `download_unverified` warning. This is an M3 decision, recorded in this task's close comment.
- **Why `GitCheckout`'s path and not `Deferred`** (review round 1): `Deferred` resolves one URL per attempt for short-lived token downloads (Tukui) and cannot fetch a tree; the git path already materializes a directory under the transaction's temp dir and inspects it with the same rules as a local directory.
- **The blob-cache packing is new code** (the spec assumed the git path already packs checkouts; at `af10e34` it does not). Keep it local to the `WowAceTree` arm so the git path's behaviour does not change in this task.
- **Design gate.** This task introduces a new protocol (the milestone epic's "Rationale and confidence" comment, §13.2: "source pinning: every file fetched at one revision"). It is new because no existing source fetches a multi-file tree over plain HTTP, where the server offers no atomic snapshot and the only immutability is the `!svn/bc/<rev>/` path discipline plus the tag's `version-name` as identity. A single live-path request, or the repository's youngest revision used as identity, would silently reintroduce mixed trees or phantom updates. It closes only when its adversarial matrix is green (common rule 14 in spirit, and the design-gate rule in the milestone epic's "Delivery" comment, §11.3): the live-path poisoning fixture, the unrelated-tag and re-tag `PROPFIND` fixtures, the determinism check, `sync --locked` at the recorded revision, every packaging refusal, the collision and cycle cases and both bounds.
- **Risk 4 (the milestone epic's "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol" comment, §12.1): WowAce SVN down, its listing format changes, or `PROPFIND` refused** (likelihood L–M, impact M). Mitigation: recorded fixtures; three response formats parsed (C1); the live probe at checkpoints; the blob cache serves reinstalls; `--file` fallback; CurseForge in M5; the designed-not-built `OPTIONS` + content-digest fallback.
- **Risk 5 (the milestone epic's "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol" comment, §12.1): BugGrabber changes its DB schema or write model again** (M, M). Mitigation here: the live probe reads upstream `BugGrabber.lua` and checks that entries are still built with `message`, `session`, `time = time()` and `counter = 1`. A mid-session write model would break M3-D19's session watermarks, and this probe is the tripwire. B3's tolerant decoders are the other half.
- **Collision hot spots:** `src/limits.rs` and its snapshot (A2, A5, B1, B3, B5, B6, C1, D1, D2, D3, D4, D10, D11, E2 and E3 also add constants there): re-accept the snapshot in this task and review the diff. `src/engine/plan.rs` is shared with many tasks; keep the `WowAceTree` arm self-contained and rebase before each gate run.
- **Not on a critical path.** The WowAce lane has 5 to 7 units of slack. In the suggested lanes the contract-and-sources agent takes C2 at t=5–7, after A2 and A4.
- **Delivery slice `slice-2` ("Capture and diagnose").** Exit demo: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal. This task delivers the keyless install that demo runs (through C3's catalog name). The agent closing the slice's last task runs the demo and records it on the milestone epic.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- C1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.1` (`wowace:` refs, listing parsers and the packaging scanner): the `Ref::WowAce` grammar and links, `SourceId::Wowace`, `parse_tag_revs` and `newest_stable_tag` for the `PROPFIND`, `parse_listing` for the pinned tree walk, and `parse_pkgmeta`/`scan_keywords` for the packaging subset.

**Unblocks:**
- C3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3` (BugGrabber in the catalog: disjoint family variants): a working `wowace:` source, so the catalog's `BugGrabber#modern` (`wowace:bug-grabber`) and `BugGrabber#r152` (`wowace:bug-grabber#r152`) variants install, and the recorded fixtures C3's replayed install tests use.

Parent: the C epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3`. Delivery slice: `slice-2`.

Through C3, this task also feeds F6 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.6`, the Issues view's "Install BugGrabber" action) and G1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1`, the README final pass), and G3's real-machine test `buggrabber_installs_then_undo` on retail and wotlk.
