comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** It makes BugGrabber, the addon that captures Lua errors, installable the way every other addon is: keyless, verified against the client's TOC rules, journaled and undoable. Without it, M3's `errors` feature would open with "download this in a browser", and the bar's Issues view could not offer a one-key install. It is also the first source that fetches a multi-file tree over plain HTTP from a server with no atomic snapshot, so it carries the milestone's "source pinning" protocol: every file at one revision, and one revision number as update identity. C3 puts it in the catalog as `omaddons install buggrabber`, F6 renders that install in the bar, and G3's real-machine test installs and undoes it on retail and wotlk. It serves the thesis directly: omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over every addon, now including the one that makes failures visible.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D15 (departure from the vision's M2→M3 handoff, comment 606): BugGrabber comes from WowAce's public SVN through a new `wowace:` source.** One `PROPFIND` (`Depth: 1`) on `tags/` gives every tag's `version-name` (its last-changed revision); every listing and file is fetched through `!svn/bc/<rev>/…`; the display version is the tag name (the TOC says `@project-version@`); the release id is `wowace:<slug>@<tag>` (or `@r<rev>`), with the revision recorded in the release, the lock entry and the blob-cache key; a re-tag is an update, an unrelated commit is not; `sync --locked` and reinstalls fetch the recorded revision. Why: it is BugGrabber's real upstream (byte-identical to the GitHub mirror, official tags), keyless, and serves both modern BugGrabber and r152 (GPL). Rejected: (i) `hippuli/BugGrabber`, bcc-only since v11.2.7; (ii) `curseforge-mirror/bug-grabber`, re-tagged several times a day (100 releases in three weeks, phantom updates), no `release.json`, REST to list assets, a third party; (iii) CurseForge's undocumented website API, terms risk and contrary to vision D4; (iv) `--file` only, a poor experience, kept as a fallback; (v) bundling BugGrabber, which is "All Rights Reserved"; (vi) live tag paths with a sorted, timestamp-fixed zip, which is deterministic serialization of a tree that may itself be mixed; (vii) the repository's youngest revision as identity, which would turn every unrelated commit into an update; (viii) advertising every no-externals project as supported. G2 records the departure and the new host (vision D13 allowlist).
- **M3-D15, the packaging subset.** `package-as` honoured (validated by `FolderName::new`); metadata-only keys ignored; every other `.pkgmeta` key refused; `@project-version@` in a `.toc` replaced with the tag name; every other keyword or build-type block refused; dotfiles skipped. Why: packaging can move, ignore, substitute and comment out code, and an unbuilt tree that happens to load would be a silent correctness bug.
- **M3 decision recorded in the close comment: no `download_unverified` warning for WowAce.** No hash comes from the server, but the transfer is TLS-protected and the TOCs are verified, the same posture as GitHub's no-REST path.
- **Vision D28 (context): one fetch → select → verify pipeline.** The source adds a location, not a new install path: inspection, TOC verification, staging and commit are unchanged.
- **Common rule 15, bounded work:** four tree bounds (files, directories, depth, requests with retries) plus `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES`, each a named constant, each failing cleanly.
- **Decisions made while writing this bead:** the revision lives on `AddonRecord` and the `addons.toml` entry as an optional `revision` key (additive, no schema bump), because the spec requires the lock entry to record it and re-tag detection needs the installed revision; the update evaluator compares `revision` for `wowace` records because the release id names only the tag; the facts and blob key include the revision so a re-tag never reuses the old tree; the asset location serializes as `wowace_tree`; the error table's no-stable-tag, malformed-response and bound-naming rows and the zip's fixed permissions; `sync --locked` fetching `!svn/bc/<recorded rev>/tags/<tag>/` directly; and the packing into the blob cache is new code local to the `WowAceTree` arm (see the next paragraph).

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- **Round 1:** WowAce trees follow the `GitCheckout` path (materialize under the transaction's temp dir, inspect as a directory), not `Deferred`, which resolves to one URL per attempt and cannot fetch a tree.
- **Round 3, revision 12, adopted:** immutable trees and a narrow packaging promise. `PROPFIND` gives each tag's last-changed revision, which serves both as the immutable fetch root and as update identity; the packaging allowlist and keyword scanner replaced the first draft's "no externals" rule; the `OPTIONS` + content-digest fallback is designed, not built. Risk 5's live-probe tripwire (upstream `BugGrabber.lua` still builds `message`, `session`, `time = time()`, `counter = 1`) was added to this task's probe.
- **Found while writing this bead:** the plan says the WowAce archive is cached "the way git checkouts are cached", but at `af10e34` git checkouts are inspected in place and never packed into the blob cache (`src/engine/plan.rs:4025-4027`, `:4302-4307`). This bead therefore specifies the packing (deterministic zip, `BlobCache::store_stream`, facts via `TargetPlanner::learn`, reuse via `local_blob_candidate`) as new code, which is what the offline-reinstall acceptance criterion needs.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- Live server (2026-10-21): 98 tags, newest `v12.1.0`; `GET` works, `HEAD` returns 401; `PROPFIND` `Depth: 1` on `tags/` returns every tag's `version-name` in one ~32 KB 207 (`v12.0.9/` → 369, `v12.1.0/` → 401); `GET …/!svn/bc/<rev>/tags/<tag>/<path>` is immutable (the review fetched `!svn/bc/401/tags/v12.1.0/!BugGrabber.toc`); `OPTIONS` returns `svn-youngest-rev`; r152 at `!svn/bc/152/trunk/`. Eleven sequential requests were made during review round 3.
- BugGrabber's `.pkgmeta` is only `package-as: "!BugGrabber"` (unchanged since r134); its only keyword is the TOC's `@project-version@`; `BugGrabber.lua` and `load.xml` contain no `@`.
- Code (as of `af10e34`): `Source` trait `src/sources/mod.rs:237`; `source_disabled` paths `:446-480`; `AssetLocation` `src/model.rs:962-984`; `TargetPlanner::checkout` `src/engine/plan.rs:4173-4191`; `local_blob_candidate` `:4473-4500`; `BlobCache::store_stream` `src/engine/blobs.rs:157`; `Release` `src/model.rs:929-945` (no revision); `AddonRecord` `:557-575`; `addons.toml` `Entry` `src/state/desired.rs:77-97` (`sha256` used by `sync --locked`, `src/app/sync.rs:145-173`); `Method::{Get, Head}` only (`src/net/mod.rs:46-58`), no request body (`:80-108`), `UreqTransport::send` `src/net/client.rs:64-79`; fixtures keyed by method and URL (`src/net/replay.rs:66-67`); `ALWAYS` hosts `src/net/allowlist.rs:8` with the git/HTTP disjointness test at `:133`; politeness constants `src/politeness.rs:18`, `:35`; `ureq` 3.4.2 and `zip` 9.0.3 already declared.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- **Risk 4 (the milestone epic's "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol" comment, §12.1): WowAce SVN down, its listing format changes, or `PROPFIND` refused** (L–M, M): recorded fixtures, three parsed formats, the live probe at checkpoints, offline reinstalls from the blob cache, `--file`, CurseForge in M5, and the designed-not-built `OPTIONS` fallback.
- **Risk 5 (the milestone epic's "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol" comment, §12.1): BugGrabber changes its DB schema or write model** (M, M): this task's live probe is the tripwire, paired with B3's tolerant decoders.
- **A mixed-revision tree or a phantom update** would be silent: the adversarial fixtures (live-path poisoning, unrelated-tag move, re-tag) are the gate.
- **`PROPFIND` through ureq 3** needs a non-standard method with a body; a transport test pins it, and the method is a typed kind so nothing else can send free-form methods.

**Confidence.** Medium, with the risk named (the milestone epic's "Rationale and confidence" comment, §13.3): WowAce availability over time is an external host omaddons does not control, mitigated by caching, the live probe and M5's second route. The pinning protocol itself was verified against the live server and every step is replay-tested; it is a design gate (the milestone epic's "Rationale and confidence" comment, §13.2: source pinning), so expect it to take longer than its size letter.

title: BugGrabber in the catalog: disjoint family variants
description:
## Background

After C2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.2`), BugGrabber installs from `wowace:bug-grabber` (the newest stable tag, every modern client) and `wowace:bug-grabber#r152` (the last 3.3.5-era revision, Interface 30300, GPL v2+). Nobody should have to know either ref. This task makes the obvious command work on every client:

```text
$ omaddons errors -t retail
retail: no Lua errors are captured: BugGrabber is not installed
fix: omaddons install buggrabber -t retail
$ omaddons install buggrabber bugsack -t retail
retail: installed BugGrabber v12.1.0 (1 folder)
retail: installed BugSack v12.1.7 (1 folder)
```

On the 3.3.5a server the same command installs r152. The catalog holds one `BugGrabber` **variant** per set of client families, the sets never overlap, and the name resolves against the target's actual family (M3-D16). A family with no verified build, such as 1.12.1 unless this task's probe finds one, gets "no BugGrabber build for this client is known", never another family's build. Users perceive it as "I didn't have to find a download".

**Why the catalog needs a new concept.** Today the catalog cannot hold two entries with the same name at all, and it fails silently rather than loudly (the milestone epic's "Ground truth" comment, §2.1; as of `af10e34`):
- `Catalog::apply` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:173-205`) upserts an entry over any existing entry with the same name, ignoring case (`:180-184`), and only then checks names and aliases for uniqueness (`:194-202`).
- The embedded catalog goes through the same `apply` (`Catalog::builtin`, `:98-101`), so two same-name entries collapse silently, **even inside the shipped catalog**, before any validator could see them.
- Lookup is `by_name` (`:161-162`), the first entry that answers to a name or alias (`Entry::answers_to`, `:41-44`).
- The catalog's entry struct is `Entry` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:29-37`: `name`, `aliases`, `ref`, `families: Vec<Family>`, `folders`, `notes`). `Entry::declares` (`:46-49`) treats **an empty `families` list as "claims every family"**.
- The catalog has 62 entries today (`catalog/catalog.toml`). Its BugSack entry (`catalog/catalog.toml:115-119`) says "!BugGrabber is an optional dependency with no official GitHub releases; install it yourself if you want it".
- `info` reports the entry as `InfoData.catalog: Option<CatalogInfo>` (`src/app/info.rs:62-89`; `CatalogInfo { name, aliases, families, folders, notes }`), found by ref or by `by_name` (`:391-395`).
- `Family` (`src/rules.rs:149-164`) has 14 values, with wire names `vanilla`, `forever`, `tbc`, `wrath`, `titan`, `cata`, `mists`, `mainline`, `vanilla-legacy`, `tbc-legacy`, `wrath-legacy`, `cata-legacy`, `mists-legacy`, `unknown`; `Family::ALL` (`:175-190`) is the family order.

The first draft of this design allowed duplicates only across generations (modern vs `*-legacy`). The plan's own TBC, Cata and Mists legacy builds are all one generation, so its validator would have rejected them; and the merge would have collapsed them before any validator ran (review round 3, revision 13). Disjoint family sets are the smallest rule that is both correct and checkable, and they guarantee a vanilla-legacy client is never offered a build that only some other legacy family has.

This task also changes the hint `errors` emits. B6 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6`) ships the interim hint for a target with `capture: "none"`: `search buggrabber` with action `install_buggrabber`. C3 replaces it with `omaddons install buggrabber -t <id>` when a variant covers the target's family, and with the "no build known" prose (no command) when none does.

This task serves goal **G-M3-3** (Lua errors actionable on every client; BugGrabber keyless and pinned) and checkpoint criterion 7 (`omaddons install buggrabber` installs the newest WowAce tag on synthetic retail, Mists Classic, Era, Anniversary and Forever clients, and r152 on the 3.3.5a client, on the real machine and then undone), and checkpoint criterion 11 (live probes, including the catalog × flavor probe with the BugGrabber variants). G3's real-machine test `buggrabber_installs_then_undo` runs on retail and on wotlk.

Decisions that shape it:
- **M3-D16:** same-name catalog variants select by pairwise-disjoint client families, with a stable identity `name#variant`; merge works on identities; one `Catalog::resolve(name, family)` serves every lookup.
- **M3-D15:** the variants' refs are `wowace:` refs, fetched at a pinned revision.
- **M3-D22 / M3-D2 (context):** `errors` exits 0 whether or not errors exist, and a target without BugGrabber is listed with `capture: "none"` and an install hint in `commands[]`; the widget runs that hint's argv exactly as the CLI returned it (F6's Issues view: "BugGrabber is not installed: Install").

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/resolve/catalog.rs`

**Identity.**
- The catalog entry (`Entry`; the spec calls it `CatalogEntry`) gains **`variant: Option<String>`**, required when a name has more than one entry. An entry's identity is `name` (no variant) or `name#variant`.
- TOML key: `variant = "modern"` in `catalog/catalog.toml` and in `catalog.d` files.

**`apply` merges by identity, not by name** (today `:173-205` upserts by name, `:180-184`):
- an override naming `name` **and** `variant` replaces or removes only that variant;
- an override naming only `name` replaces **all** variants of that name with itself, or removes them all with `remove = true`.

The embedded catalog goes through the same `apply`, so its own variants survive.

**Validation**, after the embedded catalog and after each `catalog.d` file:
- the family sets of one name's variants are **pairwise disjoint**;
- variant keys are present and unique per name (a name with two or more entries needs a `variant` on every one of them);
- no alias is claimed by two different names. Aliases shared between variants of the **same** name are allowed (both BugGrabber variants carry `!buggrabber` and `bug-grabber`).
- A violation in the embedded catalog is a build bug (a unit test asserts the shipped catalog loads). In a `catalog.d` file it skips that file whole with `catalog_override_invalid` (the existing warning, `src/error.rs:268`), as today.
- Decided while writing this bead: because `Entry::declares` reads an empty `families` list as every family, a variant with `families = []` overlaps every other variant of its name and fails the disjointness check. A single entry with no variants keeps today's meaning.

**One resolver**, `Catalog::resolve(name, family: Option<Family>) -> Option<&Entry>`:
- **with a family:** the variant whose `families` contains it, or `None` (the catalog has no entry for that target; `install` reports it as it reports any uncatalogued name);
- **without one, for `info` and `search`:** the variant covering `mainline`, else the first in family order (`Family::ALL`), plus the other variants' family sets in `InfoData.catalog.variants` (additive).
- **Without `-t`**, commands resolve with the default target's family (M3-D16). With no default target, `info` shows the variant covering `mainline` and lists the others.
- TOC verification remains the final compatibility check for whatever is resolved.

It is used by `by_name`'s callers in install, search, info and dependency resolution, and by `errors`' hint. The `by_name` callers at `af10e34`, each of which moves to `resolve` (the spec names the callers by command; the file-level list and the "With variants" column are decided while writing this bead, so confirm each row in the close comment):

| Caller | What it does | With variants |
|---|---|---|
| `src/app/resolve_args.rs:103-108` (the `RefContext.catalog` closure used by `parse_ref`/`parse_among`, i.e. `install`, `info`, `sync`, `adopt --ref`) | turns a catalog name or alias into a ref | must resolve against each selected **target's** family (see "Per-target resolution" below) |
| `src/app/info.rs:391-395` | finds the entry to show | by ref first (each variant has its own ref), else `resolve(name, default target family or None)`; fills `variants` |
| `src/app/world.rs:295-301` (`names_addon`, used by `update`, `pin`, `unpin`) | matches a typed name to an installed addon by catalog ref identity | must accept **any** variant of the name whose ref identity equals the record's, so `pin bug-grabber -t wotlk` matches the r152 record |
| `src/resolve/adopt.rs:82` and `:360` (adoption's name-match guess, step 6) | proposes a catalog ref for an unmanaged folder named like an entry | resolve with the target's family, so a 3.3.5a `!BugGrabber` folder is never guessed as the modern variant; no variant for the family → no catalog guess |
| `src/app/adopt/hints.rs:64` | the ref in an adopt fix | same as above, with the hint's target family |
| `src/resolve/search.rs` (catalog hits) | catalog hits and their compatibility hints | one hit per catalog name, from `resolve(name, None)`; the implementer may compute each target's compatibility hint from the variant that target resolves to, so 3.3.5a is not shown incompatible with BugGrabber (record the choice in the close comment) |
| `src/engine/plan.rs:2043` (`TargetPlanner::bridge_warning`, the dependency-resolution caller: the fix for a bridge dependency whose folder is missing) | offers `install <requires> -t <id>` when the catalog knows the name, else the dependency resolver's ref, else `search` | resolve with `Some(target.family)`: offer the catalog install only when a variant covers this target's family; otherwise fall through to the resolver and `search` exactly as for an uncatalogued name |

**Per-target resolution** (found while writing this bead). At `af10e34`, `install` parses each request once, before fanning out to targets (`src/app/install.rs:415` calls `parse_ref` over all records). A catalog name can now mean a different ref per target family, so a catalog match must be resolved per target: for example, the parse step yields a catalog-name match, and each target's plan resolves it with `Catalog::resolve(name, Some(target.family))`. A target whose family no variant covers gets the uncatalogued-name result for that target only; the other targets proceed. `catalog_name(catalog, r)` (`src/app/resolve_args.rs:121-128`), which names a record after its catalog entry by ref, keeps working: both variants carry the name `BugGrabber`.

**Unchanged:** dependency and adoption **folder** matching. They already never cross generations (vision comment 790), and with disjoint families they never cross variants either. `src/resolve/deps.rs:287` already filters catalog entries by the client's family.

### 2. `catalog/catalog.toml`

```toml
[[addon]]
name = "BugGrabber"
variant = "modern"
aliases = ["!buggrabber", "bug-grabber"]
ref = "wowace:bug-grabber"
families = ["mainline", "vanilla", "tbc", "wrath", "titan", "cata", "mists", "forever"]
folders = ["!BugGrabber"]
notes = "Lua error capture used by omaddons errors and BugSack (WowAce SVN, keyless)"

[[addon]]
name = "BugGrabber"
variant = "r152"
aliases = ["!buggrabber", "bug-grabber"]
ref = "wowace:bug-grabber#r152"
families = ["wrath-legacy"]
folders = ["!BugGrabber"]
notes = "r152, the last 3.3.5a revision (GPL v2+)"
```

- The modern families list must match what v12.1.0's TOC declares, checked against C2's recorded fixture (`tests/fixtures/http/wowace-bug-grabber/`) by the catalog probe.
- The file's verification header (`catalog/catalog.toml:3-…`) gains a line saying how and when the BugGrabber entries were verified (the WowAce `PROPFIND`, the pinned trees, the TOC interfaces), matching how every other entry is documented.
- `catalog/**` is an embedded asset: changing it requires `argc gate` (common rule 1).

### 3. Other legacy revisions

- A one-off live probe walks the trunk log (`!svn/bc/<rev>/trunk/!BugGrabber.toc` for candidate revisions) to find the **last** revision whose `## Interface` is 20400 (2.4.3), 40300 (4.3.4) and 50400 (5.4.8). Each verified revision also passes C2's packaging subset.
- Add one variant per verified revision: `variant = "r<rev>"`, `ref = "wowace:bug-grabber#r<rev>"`, families `["tbc-legacy"]`, `["cata-legacy"]` or `["mists-legacy"]`, `folders = ["!BugGrabber"]`. Record the revisions, and how each was verified, in the close comment.
- Whether any revision declares 11200 (1.12.1) is **UNVERIFIED**. The probe decides. If none does, `errors` on a vanilla-legacy client says "no BugGrabber build for this client is known" instead of offering an install. **No other family's variant is ever offered.**
- Keep the probe's request count small and sequential (politeness: it is a one-off walk, not a test that runs on every gate); record the request count in the close comment.

### 4. The `errors` hint (replacing B6's interim hint)

- For each target with `capture: "none"`: when `catalog.resolve("buggrabber", Some(target.family))` finds a variant, the hint is `omaddons install buggrabber -t <id>` (`commands[]` entry with action `install_buggrabber`, `destructive: false`, full `argv`); the human line is `fix: omaddons install buggrabber -t <id>`.
- Otherwise the human output and the target's message say "no BugGrabber build for this client is known", with **no command** (and no `commands[]` entry). This is prose, so it must not name a runnable omaddons command (`PROSE_COMMANDS`/`names_a_command`, common rule 8).
- B6's interim `search buggrabber` hint is removed. Update `tests/errors.rs` and the `errors` snapshots and contract rows that show it.
- The install argv must parse and work: the test runs it (replayed).

### 5. BugSack

- Keep the BugSack entry. Its note changes to: "its `!BugGrabber` is now in the catalog; `install bugsack` does not pull it, because it is an optional dependency (`OptionalDeps` never install)".
- README recommends `omaddons install buggrabber bugsack`.

### 6. Probes

- `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` (`tests/live_probes.rs:139`) gains the `wowace` variants. The legacy ones run against the synthetic legacy clients.
- The probe must check each variant against the families it claims (not the name as a whole), so a variant's families are proven by its own TOC.

### 7. README (same commit, common rule 11)

- **Catalog section:** the count changes (62, plus the BugGrabber variants, plus any verified legacy ones); variants and `catalog.d` override semantics (a whole name vs `name#variant`; `remove = true` on a bare name removes every variant); the BugSack note.
- The `errors` section's "no Lua errors are captured" fix shows `omaddons install buggrabber -t <id>`, and the "no BugGrabber build for this client is known" case.
- Recommend `omaddons install buggrabber bugsack`.

### Wire changes

- `InfoData.catalog` (`CatalogInfo`) gains `variant: Option<String>` (the chosen variant) and `variants: Vec<{variant, families}>` (the others), both additive.
- The `catalog.d` file format gains the `variant` key.
- `commands[]` action `install_buggrabber` keeps its name (B6 introduced it) with the new argv.

### Files

- `src/resolve/catalog.rs` (variant, merge by identity, validation, `resolve`), `catalog/catalog.toml`.
- Callers: `src/app/resolve_args.rs`, `src/app/install.rs` (per-target resolution), `src/engine/plan.rs` (`TargetPlanner::bridge_warning`), `src/app/info.rs`, `src/app/world.rs` (`names_addon`), `src/resolve/adopt.rs`, `src/app/adopt/hints.rs`, `src/resolve/search.rs`, `src/app/errors.rs` (the hint).
- Tests: `tests/catalog.rs` (extended), the merge-and-validate unit table in `src/resolve/catalog.rs`, `tests/errors.rs`, `tests/live_probes.rs`, snapshots touched by `info` and `errors`.
- README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `install buggrabber -t retail` installs v12.1.0 (`wowace:bug-grabber`) and `install buggrabber -t wotlk` installs r152 (`wowace:bug-grabber#r152`) (replayed with C2's fixtures).
- `install buggrabber` with no `-t` on a home with only legacy clients picks the default target's family variant.
- A multi-target install whose targets have different families gets each target its own variant; a target whose family no variant covers reports the uncatalogued-name result for that target while the others install.
- `errors` on a client without BugGrabber offers the install argv (`install_buggrabber`), which parses and works (replayed). On a vanilla-legacy client with no variant, it offers no install and says "no BugGrabber build for this client is known".
- The catalog accepts disjoint TBC, Wrath, Cata and Mists legacy variants (a test catalog), rejects two variants whose families overlap, and rejects a missing or repeated variant key. A variant with an empty family list is rejected as overlapping.
- **Overrides:**
  - a `catalog.d` file overriding only `BugGrabber#r152` leaves `#modern` intact;
  - one overriding bare `BugGrabber` replaces both;
  - `remove = true` on bare `BugGrabber` removes both;
  - one that would create an overlap is skipped with `catalog_override_invalid`.
- The shipped catalog loads (unit test), with both BugGrabber variants present after the embedded `apply`.
- `info buggrabber` shows the chosen variant and lists the other variants' families.
- `update`, `pin` and `unpin` match an installed BugGrabber by its name or either alias on both a modern and a wotlk target.
- Adoption never guesses the modern variant for an unmanaged `!BugGrabber` folder on a 3.3.5a client.
- The modern variant's families match v12.1.0's TOC (checked against the recorded fixture); every legacy variant added was verified by the trunk-log probe, and its revision is in the close comment.
- `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` covers the `wowace` variants and passes (at close when run, and at G3).
- README's Catalog section, BugSack note and `errors` fix text are updated.
- The close comment lists the new wire names: catalog key `variant`, `InfoData.catalog.variant` and `.variants`, the changed `install_buggrabber` argv, and the verified legacy revisions.

## Test Plan

- **Unit, `src/resolve/catalog.rs` (a merge-and-validate table):** embedded variants survive `apply`; identity override of one variant; bare-name override replaces all; bare-name `remove` removes all; overlap rejected (embedded → error, `catalog.d` → file skipped with `catalog_override_invalid`); missing and repeated variant keys rejected; empty-family variant rejected; shared aliases within one name allowed, across names rejected; `resolve` with each family (including an uncovered one → `None`) and without a family (mainline, else first in `Family::ALL` order).
- **`tests/catalog.rs` (replayed):** `install buggrabber -t retail`, `-t wotlk`, no `-t` on a legacy-only home, a mixed-family multi-target install; the four override scenarios through real `catalog.d` files; `info buggrabber` (variant and variants); `pin`/`unpin`/`update` by alias on wotlk.
- **`tests/errors.rs`:** the hint on a modern client without BugGrabber (argv parses and runs, replayed); a vanilla-legacy client (no command, the prose); snapshot updates replacing B6's interim `search` hint.
- **Adoption:** a unit or E2E case with an unmanaged `!BugGrabber` folder on a synthetic 3.3.5a client: no modern-variant guess.
- **Dependency fix:** a bridge dependency named like a two-variant test-catalog entry offers the catalog `install` only on a target whose family a variant covers, and otherwise the resolver's ref or `search`, as for an uncatalogued name.
- **Live:** `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` with the variants (the legacy ones against the synthetic legacy clients); the one-off trunk-log probe for legacy revisions.
- **Contract:** `errors` and `info` snapshots re-accepted (new keys only, plus the replaced hint).

## Considerations

- **Why disjoint families and not something else** (M3-D16): a distinct name (`BugGrabber-335`) is one users would not guess; generation as the selector is too coarse (the TBC, Cata and Mists legacy builds are one generation); a general rule engine over interface numbers is speculative.
- **The merge change is the risky part, not the TOML.** Today's upsert-by-name silently collapses same-name entries; every existing override behaviour (single-entry names) must stay exactly as it is. The merge-and-validate table must include the existing override cases unchanged.
- **Per-target resolution touches install's argument parsing.** Keep the change narrow: resolve catalog names per target only when the name has variants, so every existing single-entry name behaves byte-for-byte as before (snapshots unchanged).
- **Unverified 1.12.1.** If the probe finds no 11200 revision, vanilla-legacy gets the "no build known" prose. Never offer a family a variant it does not declare; TOC verification would refuse it anyway, but the hint must not promise it.
- **Not on a critical path.** The WowAce lane has 5 to 7 units of slack; C3 can start at t=6 (after B6 and C2). In the suggested lanes the contract-and-sources agent takes it at t=8–10.
- **Collision hot spots:** `src/app/errors.rs` is B6's file (C3 changes only the hint); `src/app/install.rs`, `src/app/info.rs` and `src/app/world.rs` are shared with other commands; rebase before each gate run.
- **Delivery slice `slice-2` ("Capture and diagnose").** Exit demo: `errors` on every client, read-only; **`install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk**; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal. This task delivers the `install buggrabber` part of the demo and the Issues view's install action. The agent closing the slice's last task runs the demo and records it on the milestone epic.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- B6 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6` (The `errors` command): the `errors` command and its interim `install_buggrabber` hint (`search buggrabber`), which this task replaces with the real install argv; C3 changes a hint that must already exist.
- C2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.2` (The WowAce source): a working `wowace:` source and its recorded fixtures, so `wowace:bug-grabber` and `wowace:bug-grabber#r152` install in the replayed tests and the catalog probe can check the modern families against v12.1.0's TOC.

**Unblocks:**
- F6 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.6` (The Issues and Search views): the Issues view shows "BugGrabber is not installed: Install" and runs that target's `commands[]` `install_buggrabber` argv, or shows "no BugGrabber build for this client is known"; it needs the final hint shape and the catalog name.
- G1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1` (README final pass): the Catalog section's new count, variants and override semantics, and the BugSack note, which G1 reconciles.

Parent: the C epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3`. Delivery slice: `slice-2`.
acceptance_criteria: install buggrabber -t retail installs v12.1.0 (wowace:bug-grabber) and install buggrabber -t wotlk installs r152 (wowace:bug-grabber#r152), replayed; install buggrabber with no -t on a home with only legacy clients picks the default target's family variant; a multi-target install across families gets each target its own variant, and a target no variant covers gets the uncatalogued-name result while the others install; errors on a client without BugGrabber offers the install_buggrabber argv omaddons install buggrabber -t <id>, which parses and works (replayed), and on a vanilla-legacy client with no variant offers no install and says no BugGrabber build for this client is known; the catalog accepts disjoint TBC, Wrath, Cata and Mists legacy variants (a test catalog), rejects overlapping families, a missing or repeated variant key, and an empty-family variant; overrides: a catalog.d file overriding only BugGrabber#r152 leaves #modern intact, one overriding bare BugGrabber replaces both, remove = true on bare BugGrabber removes both, and one that would create an overlap is skipped with catalog_override_invalid; the shipped catalog loads with both BugGrabber variants after the embedded apply; info buggrabber shows the chosen variant and lists the other variants' families; update, pin and unpin match an installed BugGrabber by name or either alias on modern and wotlk targets; adoption never guesses the modern variant for an unmanaged !BugGrabber folder on a 3.3.5a client; the modern variant's families match v12.1.0's TOC (recorded fixture) and every legacy variant added was verified by the trunk-log probe with its revision in the close comment; catalog_matches_declared_flavors covers the wowace variants and passes; README's Catalog section, BugSack note and errors fix text are updated; the close comment lists the new wire names (catalog key variant, InfoData.catalog.variant and variants, the new install_buggrabber argv) and the verified legacy revisions
