comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** C2 makes BugGrabber installable from two refs nobody would guess. This bead turns them into the one command everyone would: `omaddons install buggrabber`, on retail, Classic, Era, Anniversary, Forever and the 3.3.5a server alike, and it makes `omaddons errors` offer exactly that command on a client that has no BugGrabber. To do that safely it fixes a latent catalog bug: today two entries with the same name silently collapse into one, even inside the shipped catalog, before any validator could notice. The bar's Issues view (F6) runs this hint as its "Install" action, and the README final pass (G1) documents the new catalog semantics. It serves the thesis: the obvious name works everywhere, resolution is exact per client, and omaddons never offers a client a build it does not declare.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D16: same-name catalog variants select by pairwise-disjoint client families.** Each variant has a stable identity `<name>#<variant>`; `variant` is required whenever a name has more than one entry; overlapping family sets for one name, an alias claimed by two names, and a missing or repeated variant key are errors in the embedded catalog and after every `catalog.d` file; a name resolves against the target's actual family, and no covering variant means the catalog has no entry for that target; `catalog.d` merges on identities (a `name#variant` override touches one variant, a bare-name override replaces or removes all) and is re-validated, a breaking file being skipped whole with `catalog_override_invalid`; merge, `by_name`, `search`, `info`, `install` and dependency resolution all go through one `Catalog::resolve(name, family)`. Why: `install buggrabber -t wotlk` must just work; the first draft's "duplicates only across generations" rule would have rejected the plan's own TBC, Cata and Mists legacy builds (one generation), and today's merge collapses same-name entries before any validator runs; disjoint sets are the smallest rule that is correct and checkable, and they keep a vanilla-legacy client from ever being offered another legacy family's build. Rejected: a distinct name such as `BugGrabber-335` (users would not guess it), generation as the selector (too coarse), a general rule engine over interface numbers (speculative).
- **M3-D15 (context):** the variants' refs are `wowace:` refs pinned to a revision; `#r152` is pinned by construction.
- **M3-D22 and M3-D2 (context):** `errors` exits 0 with or without errors, and a target without BugGrabber is listed with `capture: "none"` and an install hint in `commands[]`, which the widget runs exactly as the CLI returned it.
- **Decisions made while writing this bead:** a variant with an empty `families` list is rejected as overlapping, because `Entry::declares` reads an empty list as every family; catalog names are resolved per target in `install` (it parses each request once before fanning out today), so a mixed-family install gets each target its own variant; `names_addon` (update, pin, unpin) accepts any variant of the name; adoption's name-match guess, adopt hints and the bridge-dependency fix (`bridge_warning`) resolve with the target's family; `search` shows one hit per name from `resolve(name, None)`, with per-target compatibility hints from each target's own variant left to the implementer to record.

**Review-round changes folded in.** Review round 3, revision 13 ("disjoint family selectors"), was adopted, including merge by variant identity, because the re-verification at `af10e34` found that `Catalog::apply` upserts by name before validating, so same-name entries collapse silently. The first draft's generation-based duplicate rule was replaced by pairwise-disjoint family sets.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- `Catalog::apply` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:173-205`) upserts by name ignoring case (`:180-184`) and validates names and aliases only afterwards (`:194-202`); the embedded catalog goes through the same `apply` (`:98-101`); `by_name` returns the first entry answering to a name or alias (`:161-162`); `Entry` (`:29-37`) has no variant field; `Entry::declares` (`:46-49`) treats an empty family list as all families.
- `catalog/catalog.toml` has 62 entries; BugSack's note (`:115-119`) tells users to install `!BugGrabber` themselves.
- `by_name` callers: `src/app/resolve_args.rs:103-108` (via `parse_ref`, used once per request by `install`, `src/app/install.rs:415`), `src/app/info.rs:391-395`, `src/app/world.rs:295-301` (`names_addon`), `src/resolve/adopt.rs:82` and `:360`, `src/app/adopt/hints.rs:64`, and the dependency-resolution caller `TargetPlanner::bridge_warning` (`src/engine/plan.rs:2043`); `src/resolve/deps.rs:287` already filters by family.
- `Family` has 14 values (`src/rules.rs:149-190`); `CatalogInfo` (`src/app/info.rs:82-89`) has no variant fields; `catalog_override_invalid` exists (`src/error.rs:268`); `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` is `tests/live_probes.rs:139`.
- Upstream: r152 declares Interface 30300; v12.1.0 is the newest tag; which legacy revisions declare 20400, 40300, 50400 or 11200 is to be found by this task's probe (11200 is UNVERIFIED).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- **A merge change regresses existing overrides.** The merge-and-validate table keeps every single-entry override case, and per-target resolution applies only to names that have variants, so existing snapshots stay unchanged.
- **The wrong build offered to a client.** Disjointness is validated at load; `resolve` returns `None` for an uncovered family; TOC verification remains the final check; the probe proves each variant against its own families.
- **No legacy revision exists for some family.** The "no build known" prose is the designed outcome, never another family's build.

**Confidence.** High: a pure catalog change with an exhaustive unit table, replayed installs and a live probe; the only external dependency, C2's source, is already a blocker.

title: Epic: M3 backups and restore (omaddons backup)
description:
## Background

Area D of M3 (milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`): `omaddons backup` and the restore transactions.

**Settings are the data players lose.** Addon folders can be re-downloaded; a client's `WTF/` (SavedVariables, layouts, keybindings, WeakAuras, profiles) cannot. Today it is protected only by undo's per-transaction SavedVariables snapshots, which exist only around omaddons' own changes and which retention prunes after a week.

M3 makes a backup a reflinked copy of a client's whole `WTF/` under `<meta>/backups/<id>/`, plus a small `addons.json` record of which addon versions and folders produced it (M3-D23). On btrfs, which Omarchy installs, the copy initially shares all file data with the live tree, so it takes milliseconds and almost no space until the game rewrites files. Each backup states what it proves: capture consistency (`stable` or `best_effort`) and integrity (`metadata_only`, `verified` or `damaged`, with a baseline from `capture`, `import` or `later`; M3-D47).

Restores are journaled, undoable transactions:
- **A whole restore** swaps `WTF/` with one atomic `RENAME_EXCHANGE` of the `WTF` directory (kind `restore`), refused while the client runs and refused outright where the exchange is impossible (a mount point, a cross-mount stage, a filesystem without `RENAME_EXCHANGE`; `filesystem_unsupported`). A crashed one rolls back only once the game is not running. Anything displaced is preserved through a journaled, resumable intent before any cleanup, and a state recovery cannot recognize stays pending, never guessed at (M3-D24). Before staging, a whole restore also keeps the current `WTF/` as a `before_restore` backup where the filesystem can reflink, and warns `before_restore_skipped` elsewhere (M3-D26).
- **A partial restore** (`--addon X`) is a SavedVariables-only transaction whose snapshot layout is exactly the one undo already restores from, using the folders that addon owned when the backup was taken (M3-D27). Partial restores are exchange-only too.
- Undo and restores conflict where they would overwrite each other (M3-D28); restores never run while the client runs (M3-D29).

**Automatic backups** take a checkpoint before the day's first change that touches folders or SavedVariables, and another after each play session that changed settings; they skip when nothing changed since the newest qualifying capture, prune themselves by day, and stop before the disk runs low (M3-D31, M3-D32, M3-D48). **`auto_backup` defaults to `daily`** on copy-on-write filesystems (M3-D30, owner-visible). `backup export` streams a `.tar.zst` to a new file for off-disk safety (M3-D34), and `backup import` accepts only an exact archive (M3-D35).

## Goals

- **D1** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1` (The backup store, `backup list`, and the shared primitives): the store layout, `backup list`, the inventory projection, and the shared primitives (`ClonePolicy::{Required, Preferred}`, `StampDigest`, `DirLock`, the `backup::fs` seams with `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE`/`OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB`, `busy` in listings).
- **D2** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.2` (`backup create`): manual captures with consistency checks, the addon record, and the history line.
- **D3** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.3` (Automatic backups: two triggers, qualifying checkpoints, the space guard): pre-change and post-session triggers, coalescing, qualifying captures, the free-space guard, the `daily-copy` byte budget and the scheduling lock.
- **D4** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.4` (Backup retention, space reclamation and `backup prune`): per-day retention, reclamation, reader reservations, and the bound `backup prune`.
- **D5** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.5` (The whole-`WTF/` restore transaction in the engine): the scope root rename, writer selection by `writes_wtf`, the statx and exchange preflight, the journal 1.1 `Prepared` keys (A3 moves the version to 1.1), the recovery rules with their conservative stop, and the crash matrix.
- **D6** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.6` (Undo of a whole restore, and the conflict rules): undo of `restore` transactions and the restore/undo conflict rules.
- **D7** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.7` (Partial restore, `backup restore --addon`): the SavedVariables-only transaction in undo's layout, exchange-only, with its crash matrix.
- **D8** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.8` (The `backup restore` command): the user-facing command over D5/D6/D14, previews bound with `--if-match`.
- **D9** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.9` (`backup export`): streaming `.tar.zst` to a new file, never replacing one; the only crate additions of M3 (`tar`, `zstd`).
- **D10** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.10` (`backup import`): exact manifest-to-payload acceptance, hostile-archive rejection, the `backup_tar` fuzz target.
- **D11** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.11` (Backups in `status`): the per-target `backups` block from `backups.json`, cheap enough for `status --cached`.
- **D12** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12` (Integration crash matrices, concurrency and performance checkpoints): cross-feature scenes, the full failpoint sweep, concurrency, the 500 MB budget and the af10e34 characterization.
- **D13** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.13` (`backup verify` and integrity states): opt-in content verification against recorded hashes, and honest integrity labels.
- **D14** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.14` (Recovery preservation: unexpected identities and the journaled intent): recognized versus unrecognized identities, `preserve`/`preserved` journal lines with a reserved backup id, resumable, crash-tested inside recovery itself.

## Success Criteria

- A 500 MB `WTF/` in 5,000 files backs up in under 1 s on btrfs (release, median of 5); 20,000 files is measured and reported.
- Clone-only mode copies zero payload bytes where it cannot clone; a tree that changes during capture is retried once, then marked `best_effort`.
- A restore holds the global lock under 50 ms with that tree.
- Every failpoint leaves `WTF/` wholly old or wholly new (whole restore: `tree_hash`; partial: per touched file plus the rest of `WTF/`).
- Nothing displaced is pruned before it has a durable home, also across crashes inside recovery; unrecognized states stay pending with their evidence.
- Restores are refused while the client runs and where exchange is impossible, before anything is copied.
- `export` → `import` → `restore` is byte-identical with an exact manifest match.
- Automatic backups are bounded by day and by free space, never fail a transaction, never run on a dry run, and never delete a manual, imported or recovered backup.
- `backup verify` detects same-size corruption where hashes exist and says so when it can only set a first baseline.
- `backup restore` and `backup prune` previews are binding (`plan_stale` on change).
- No personal data on any channel.
- The af10e34 binary, run against committed and interrupted M3 restores, is characterized (what it refuses, what it would do, and where), recorded in D12's close comment and README Limitations.

## Non-Goals

- Parsing or editing SavedVariables (backups copy bytes; partial restore selects files by name and recorded ownership, never by content).
- Backups of anything but `WTF/`.
- A restore mode without atomic exchange.
- Judging whether an old profile suits a new addon version (restore shows the version difference only).
- Export, import and verify from the widget (CLI only in M3).

## Considerations

- **The restore critical path.** D1 → D5 → D14 → D8 → D7 → F9 → F7 → G1 → G2 → G3 is one of the two 20-unit critical paths. That is deliberate: the recovery and preservation semantics, not the copying, carry the schedule risk. Staff D5 and D14 with the engine specialist. D6 and D12 are near-critical.
- **Design gates.** D5 (the whole-restore transaction and its recovery) and D14 (preservation intents) are new protocols in the most sensitive place in the code, and close only with their own crash matrices green (common rule 14). D12 integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
- **Why D5, D14 and D8 are separate.** D5 stops conservatively wherever preservation would be needed, keeping everything, so it is safe alone. D14 turns those stops into the preservation protocol. D8 waits for both, so no user ever runs a restore whose crash recovery cannot yet preserve a played-on tree. D6 runs in parallel with D14 (undo of a restore needs D5's transaction, not D14's protocol). D7 comes after D8: partial restore adds a flag to the command D8 creates and shares `restore.rs` with D5 and D6, and ordering it last among the restore tasks avoids three-way edits of `undo.rs`.
- **Engine changes needing vision comments (G2).** The scope root rename, writer selection by `writes_wtf`, the WTF rollback rules, preservation intents, journal 1.1 and the retention guards.
- **Collision hot spots.** `src/engine/journal.rs` (A1, A3, D5, D14: A3 first, then D5, then D14), `src/engine/tx.rs` (D3's hook before `stage_all`, D5's failpoints), `src/fsx/sys.rs`/`mutate.rs`/`lock.rs` (D1 adds `ClonePolicy`, `StampDigest`, `DirLock`; D5 the exchange probe; D9 the directory fsync after persist), `src/fsx/scope.rs` (D5, D9), `src/fsx/prune.rs` and `tests/single_writer.rs` (D2, D4, D10), `src/engine/undo.rs` (D3, D6, D7), `tests/engine_crash.rs` (D3, D5, D6, D7, D14, D12), `src/app/status.rs` (D11 appends after A2), `src/error.rs` (D2, D3, D5, D8, D9 add codes), `Cargo.toml` (D9 only).
- **Real machine.** The development machine's `WTF/` dirs are tiny (232–596 KB, 31–104 files) and all on btrfs, so the 500 MB budget is measured on a synthetic tree (D12). Real-machine tests never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before; they never touch the Forever client.
- **Slices.** D1–D4, D11 and D13 belong to `slice-2`; D5, D6, D7, D8 and D14 to `slice-3` (recover); D9, D10 and D12 to `slice-4` (portability and close).
acceptance_criteria: D1-D14 are closed; a 500 MB, 5,000-file WTF/ backs up in under 1 s on btrfs (release, median of 5) and 20,000 files is reported; clone-only mode copies zero payload bytes where it cannot clone and a changing tree is retried once then marked best_effort; a restore holds the global lock under 50 ms; every failpoint leaves WTF/ wholly old or wholly new; nothing displaced is pruned before it has a durable home, also across crashes inside recovery, and unrecognized states stay pending with their evidence; restores are refused while the client runs and where exchange is impossible, before anything is copied; export-import-restore is byte-identical with an exact manifest match; automatic backups are bounded by day and by free space, never fail a transaction, never run on a dry run and never delete a manual, imported or recovered backup; backup verify detects same-size corruption where hashes exist and says so when it can only set a first baseline; backup restore and backup prune previews bind; no personal data appears on any channel; the af10e34 binary run against committed and interrupted M3 restores is characterized in D12's close comment and README Limitations.

title: The backup store, `backup list`, and the shared primitives
description:
## Background

Every M3 backup feature reads and writes **one on-disk model**, and two of them copy whole `WTF/` trees: `backup create` (live tree → stage) and `backup restore` (backup → stage). This task defines that model, the read-only `backup list` command, and **one** tree-clone primitive, so create, restore, export, import and prune can proceed in parallel against a single copy routine that is made fast and correct once.

Three more primitives are shared just as widely, and they belong with the model:
- the **clone policy** that makes "clone-only" real (M3-D30): today a caller that wants "reflink or nothing" has already paid for a full byte copy before it learns the clone failed;
- the **directory locks** behind reader reservations and the per-target scheduling lock (M3-D48);
- the **backup inventory projection** that keeps `status --cached` bounded no matter how many backups exist (M3-D37).

**Why it matters.** Settings (`WTF/`, SavedVariables) are the data players actually lose. Today they are protected only by undo's per-transaction SavedVariables snapshots, which retention prunes after about a week and which cover only omaddons' own changes. M3 adds reflinked copies of the whole `WTF/` that cost milliseconds and almost no space on btrfs (which Omarchy installs). This task serves goal **G-M3-4 "Settings survive"** (checkpoints within a disk bound, every backup honest about what it proves) and **G-M3-6 "No new risk to the engine"** (fsx only, the global lock only for commit windows), and the contract goal **G-M3-5** (everything the widget shows is documented `--json`). It pre-checks **checkpoint criterion 8** (clone-only copies zero bytes where it cannot clone; the 500 MB / 5,000-file budget, measured here first) and feeds **checkpoint criterion 10** (`status --cached` under 5 ms with 200 manual backups on one target, through the inventory projection).

**Ground truth this task builds on** (all anchors as of `af10e34`; symbols matter more than lines):
- `ClientPaths::backups()` returns `<meta>/backups` (`src/state/paths.rs:410-413`) and has no callers. `ClientPaths::wtf()` resolves an existing `wtf/` spelling (`:415-419`).
- `Writer::{Backup, BackupRestore, Omarchy, Skill, Doctor}` exist (`src/fsx/scope.rs:19-42`). `Scope::ClientMeta` admits `Backup` and `BackupRestore`, so `<meta>/backups/` is writable by them. `Scope::Wtf` (the whole `WTF/` tree) admits only `BackupRestore` (`scope.rs:118`).
- `PruneReason::BackupPrune` exists and may delete exactly one entry below `<meta>/backups/` (`src/fsx/prune.rs:25-46`, `:311-315`).
- **`CloneFile`** tries `FICLONE` and falls back to a byte copy on `EOPNOTSUPP|EXDEV|EINVAL|ENOTTY|ENOSYS` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:207-259`). **The fallback happens inside the same call**: `clone_file(from, to, durability)` swallows the "unsupported" error (`reflink_unsupported`, `sys.rs:253-259`) and copies every byte into a temp sibling (`:231-249`), and only then returns `CloneKind::ByteCopy`. There is no parameter to forbid the fallback; the only knob is the `fsx.reflink.unsupported` test failpoint (`:218`). FICLONE is atomic per file with respect to concurrent writes (`ioctl_ficlone(2)`); a sequence of per-file clones is **not** a snapshot of a tree. Shared extents need new space when either side is later rewritten: a reflinked backup is cheap when made, not free forever.
- **Deferred durability** (one `syncfs` instead of an fsync per file) is allowed only under `<meta>/stage/<tx>/` in untracked sessions (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:277-289`). A transaction session hashes every renamed directory and every cloned file (`mutate.rs:595-618`), so copying a large `WTF/` must happen in an untracked staging session and must not hash.
- `stage_trees` (`src/engine/stage.rs:198-203`) copies trees with reflinks but SHA-256s every file it copies (`:272-279`): right for AddOns, too slow for a 500 MB `WTF/`. That is why this task adds a separate tree clone rather than reusing `stage_trees`.
- `keep_dir_mode` (`src/engine/stage.rs:297-312`) chmods a staged directory to `(mode & 0o777) | 0o700` once its children are in, so a `0500` source cannot block them. That keeps staged trees prunable at the cost of not reproducing a `0500` directory exactly. This task records **exact** modes in the manifest and applies them only when a restore stages the tree (M3-D23).
- `TreeDigest` always renders `tree:sha256:` (`mutate.rs:177-180`); M3-D25 needs a separate `StampDigest` type that renders `stamp:sha256:`.
- `InflightLock` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:193-275`) is a `create_new` + `try_lock` file per transaction; stage dirs are orphaned only when their transaction's lock is free or missing.
- Progress phases today are `fetch|download|verify|stage|commit` (`src/output/stderr.rs:32-58`; the `Phase` enum at `:35-46`). There is no `copy` phase.
- Local time is used in exactly one place, `src/app/history.rs:464-469` (`TimeZone::system()`); tests set no `TZ`.
- On the development machine every client path is on btrfs (`compress=zstd:3`), so reflinks work; real `WTF/` dirs are tiny (232–596 KB, 31–104 files, no symlinks), so the 500 MB budget must be measured on a synthetic tree.

**Decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic):
- **M3-D23 (what a backup is):** a backup is `<meta>/backups/<id>/` holding `backup.json`, `manifest.json`, `addons.json` and `WTF/`, built in an untracked `Writer::Backup` stage with deferred durability, directories kept owner-writable with exact modes in the manifest, one `syncfs`, then `RENAME_NOREPLACE`. Capture consistency is measured (stamps, root identity, inventory recheck), never assumed.
- **M3-D25:** whole-tree renames record **stamp digests** (`stamp:sha256:`, over sorted `(path, kind, size, mode, mtime_ns)`), never content hashes, so no `WTF/` is content-hashed under the lock. This task adds the `StampDigest` type.
- **M3-D30 (owner-visible):** `daily` automatic backups are clone-only through `ClonePolicy::Required` **at the fsx primitive**; capability is observed per attempt and recorded in the inventory projection; `statfs` is only an eligibility hint.
- **M3-D37:** `status --cached` reads small, validated projections, never unbounded authority; `<cache>/backups.json` is one of them, and `backup list` reads only `backup.json` files.
- **M3-D40:** a new progress phase `copy`, whose message is a fixed label, never a path.
- **M3-D47:** integrity is explicit (`metadata_only|verified|damaged`, with `baseline` `capture|import|later`); listing never walks or hashes a tree.
- **M3-D48:** directory `flock`s (`DirLock`) for reader reservations and the scheduling lock; no lock files; apparent sizes are labelled, with free space next to them.
- **M3-D21:** no account, realm or character name on any channel; progress carries counts and a fixed label.
- **M3-D39:** help layout: the Change group gains `backup` after `undo`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The model, `src/backup/mod.rs` (new)

Types:
- `pub struct BackupId(Ulid)`, using the `ulid_id!` macro pattern (`src/model.rs:222-299`).
- `pub enum BackupKind { Manual, Auto, BeforeRestore, Imported, Recovered }` (wire: `manual`, `auto`, `before_restore`, `imported`, `recovered`) and `pub enum Trigger { PreChange, PostSession }` (wire: `pre_change`, `post_session`; automatic backups only).
- `pub enum Consistency { Stable, BestEffort }` (`stable`, `best_effort`), `pub enum Integrity { MetadataOnly, Verified, Damaged }` (`metadata_only`, `verified`, `damaged`) and `pub enum Baseline { Capture, Import, Later }` (`capture`, `import`, `later`).
- `pub struct BackupMeta { … }`: the fields of M3-D23, `Versioned` kind `backup` 1.0, with a `store::KINDS` row (`src/state/store.rs:107`). The fields, in wire order:
  - identity: `id`, `target` (target key), `target_id`, `family`;
  - times: `created_at` (when this backup was published here) and `captured_at` (when its content was captured; for an import, the source's capture time);
  - `kind`, plus `trigger` (`pre_change|post_session`, automatic backups only), `actor`, `reason`;
  - `client_version`, `client_running`;
  - counts `files`, `dirs`, `symlinks`, `skipped`; `bytes` (apparent); `reflinked` (`all|some|none`); `unsettled`;
  - `consistency` (`stable|best_effort`);
  - `integrity` (`metadata_only|verified|damaged`) with `verified_at` and `baseline` (`capture|import|later`);
  - `tool_version`, `source` (imports only: `{id, target_id, family, created_at, captured_at, tool_version}`) and `partial` (true only for a `recovered` backup holding some files; it then restores only with `--addon`).
- `pub struct ManifestEntry { path: String, kind: EntryKind /* file|dir|symlink */, size: u64, mode: u32, mtime_ns: i64, link: Option<String>, sha256: Option<String> }`: the list is `Versioned` kind `backup_manifest` 1.0 with a `KINDS` row. `path` is relative to `WTF/`, as spelled on disk. `mode` is the **exact source mode**. `link` is a symlink's target. `sha256` is set only by `create --verify` (D2), import (D10) or `backup verify` (D13). The manifest is local only, because its paths contain account names.
- `pub struct AddonProvenance { name, folders: Vec<FolderName>, version: Option<String>, source: SourceNote }` where `SourceNote` is `{kind, ref, release_id}`. The list is `Versioned` kind `backup_addons` 1.0 with a `KINDS` row. It is copied from the target record at capture (D2 writes it; no SavedVariables is parsed). Addon names are not personal data, so `backup list -v` may show them.
- `pub struct BackupRef { id, meta, dir: PathBuf, restorable: bool, qualifying: bool, busy: bool }`, where:
  - `restorable` means `backup.json` and the manifest are readable **and** `integrity != Damaged` (and, per the `backup list` contract, the backup's client `WTF` is not a symlink out of the client dir, which D2 records);
  - `qualifying` is the predicate of M3-D31, defined here and shared with D3, D4 and D11: kind ∈ {`manual`, `auto`, `before_restore`}, **not** `partial`, `consistency: stable`, captured on this machine (not imported). Imported, recovered and best-effort backups never qualify. Scheduling and the stale recommendation use the qualifying capture's `captured_at`, never a directory's age, a publish time or an imported source's date;
  - `busy` is a non-blocking `DirLock::try_exclusive` on the backup's dir, released at once: true when a reader holds a reservation (item 4). It is best effort, a snapshot of that instant.

Functions:
- `pub fn list(client: &ClientPaths) -> (Vec<BackupRef>, Vec<Warning>)` reads `<meta>/backups/*/backup.json` (each bounded by `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES`, 1 MiB, `src/limits.rs:65`) and checks that `manifest.json` **exists**. **It never walks or hashes a tree** (M3-D47). Order: newest `captured_at` first. A dir without readable metadata is listed with `restorable: false` and never fails the listing.
- `pub fn resolve(client, prefix) -> Result<BackupRef>`: a prefix of **8 or more** characters selects one, as undo's prefixes do; 7 or fewer is a `usage` error. `not_found` lists the newest 3 ids as alternatives (argv `omaddons backup list -t <id>`); `ref_ambiguous` gives one alternative per candidate (each a complete argv that parses).
- `pub fn check_structure(b: &BackupRef) -> Result<TreeCheck>` compares the manifest with the tree (entry set, kinds, sizes; **no hashing**). D5 and D13 call it. Listing does not.

### 2. The command, `src/app/backup.rs` (new)

- The `Backup` clap command with `BackupAction::{List, Create, Verify, Restore, Prune, Export, Import}`. **Only `List` is wired here**; every other subcommand is added by its own task with its own variant, registry row and contract rows (DEC-1: no stubs). The variants above name the final shape only; do not declare unwired variants.
- **Bare `backup` = `backup list`.** `--limit N` bounds the backups shown per target, newest first (the widget passes 50); `shown` and `total` are always reported. `backup list` has no default limit.
- `-t` selects many (`World::select_many`). With no `-t`: every target that has `<meta>/backups/`.
- **Data** (the `backup list` part of the contract, additive, DEC-4; field order is wire order):
  ```json
  {"data":{"targets":[{"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M4…"},
    "auto":{"mode":"daily","capability":"supported","last":{"at":"…","result":"created"}},
    "backups":[{"id":"01M6Q…","created_at":"…","captured_at":"…","kind":"auto","trigger":"post_session",
                "actor":"widget","reason":null,"files":412,"bytes":15937536,"reflinked":"all",
                "client_running":false,"unsettled":0,"consistency":"stable",
                "integrity":"metadata_only","verified_at":null,"baseline":null,
                "restorable":true,"qualifying":true,"busy":false}],
    "bytes":63963136,"snapshot_bytes":0,"free_bytes":227633266688,"shown":5,"total":5}]}}
  ```
  - `backup list -v` adds per backup: `"addons":[{"name":"WeakAuras","folders":["WeakAuras","WeakAurasOptions"],"version":"5.19.2"}]`.
  - `restorable: false` marks a backup that is `damaged`, whose recorded structure is incomplete (a missing manifest), or whose client's `WTF` is a symlink out of the client dir. Listing reads metadata only; a full tree check is what `backup verify` (D13) and a restore's staging (D5) do.
  - `qualifying` says whether the backup counts as a checkpoint (M3-D31).
  - `busy` is true while another process holds a reader reservation (a restore, export or verify). Prune (D4) retries a busy victim once after 50 ms, so this listing's own probe never makes a backup look busy to prune. The widget disables its prune key on a busy backup.
  - `integrity`, `verified_at` and `baseline` are as M3-D47 defines them. Human output never prints "verified" for `metadata_only`.
  - `auto` is `{mode, capability, last}` from config and the inventory projection (D3 fills `capability` and `last`; until then `capability: "unknown"`, `last: null`). `bytes` is the target's backups' apparent total; `snapshot_bytes` the apparent size of `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/WTF.previous` undo trees (0 until D5 creates them); `free_bytes` is `statvfs` free space for unprivileged users on `<meta>`'s filesystem (item 6).
- **Human output:**
  ```text
  retail (12.1.5, mainline) · 5 backups · 61.0 MB apparent, initially shared copy-on-write · 212 GB free
    01M6Q2VA…  today 18:02       auto (after play)   412 files  15.2 MB  stable
    01M5Z1KB…  2026-10-18 21:15  manual              412 files  15.1 MB  stable · verified  "before the raid"
  ```
  - Ids are shown at 16 characters, as history does (vision comment 823).
  - Times are local `captured_at` (`jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`).
  - "verified" is printed only for `integrity: verified`; `best_effort` and `damaged` are always printed.
  - Apparent sizes overstate real usage on btrfs, so the header says "apparent, initially shared copy-on-write" whenever any backup has `reflinked != none`, and shows free space beside it (M3-D48). omaddons never claims a backup's exclusive physical size, which reflinks make unknowable without a full extent walk.
- **`commands[]`:** `omaddons backup create -t <id>` (action `backup_create`, `destructive: false`) for a target with no **qualifying** capture from the last 7 days. This hint uses `Timestamp::now()` and its tests seed `captured_at` relative to the real clock, because A1's clock seam is not a blocker of this task; D2 later switches the `backup` module to `crate::clock::now()`.
- **Inventory rebuild.** `backup list` rewrites the inventory projection (item 5) when it is stale. That is a derived cache write, like `outdated`'s release memo, which is why `backup list` is `mutates: false` yet may write `<cache>/backups.json`. D2 makes every projection write that changed it ring the doorbell (A1 is D2's blocker, not D1's, which keeps D1 free to start on day one).

### 3. The tree clone, `src/backup/tree.rs` (new, `pub(crate)`)

Used by D2 (live → stage) and D5/D6 (backup or snapshot → stage). (D7's partial restore copies single files with `CloneFile`, not this tree clone.)

```rust
pub struct CloneOpts { pub settle: bool, pub policy: ClonePolicy, pub max_entries: usize, pub max_depth: usize, pub exact_modes: bool /* restore staging */ }
pub struct TreeCopy { pub files: u64, pub dirs: u64, pub symlinks: u64, pub skipped: u64, pub bytes: u64, pub copied_bytes: u64 /* payload byte-copied, not cloned */, pub reflinked: Reflinked /* all|some|none */, pub unsettled: u64, pub consistency: Consistency, pub changes: InventoryDelta /* changed, added, removed */, pub stamp_digest: StampDigest, pub manifest: Vec<ManifestEntry> }
pub fn clone_tree(s: &mut WriteSession<'_>, from: &Path, to: &Path, opts: &CloneOpts, progress: &ProgressSink) -> Result<TreeCopy, CloneError>
```

- **Contract.** The caller passes an **untracked** session whose `to` lies under a `<meta>/stage/<tx>/` dir. That is the only place deferred durability is allowed (`mutate.rs:277-289`).
- **Walk.** It reads with `std::fs` (reads are allowed outside fsx; only writes go through fsx) and **never follows symlinks**. It stops at `max_entries` or `max_depth` with `CloneError::TooLarge { limit }`, which callers map to `archive_too_large` (`details.limit`). The bounds are new non-config constants this task adds to `src/limits.rs`:

  | Constant | Value | Purpose |
  |---|---|---|
  | `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_ENTRIES` | 200,000 | Entries walked in one `WTF/` |
  | `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_DEPTH` | 16 | Directory depth walked |

  Each gets a `REGISTRY` row and a `LIMIT_NAMES` entry; re-accept the `limit_registries` snapshot (review the diff).
- **The clone policy, at the fsx primitive** (`src/fsx/sys.rs`, `src/fsx/mutate.rs`):
  - `Op::CloneFile { from, policy: ClonePolicy }` and `sys::clone_file(from, to, durability, policy)`, with `pub enum ClonePolicy { Required, Preferred }`.
  - `Preferred` is today's behaviour. **Every existing caller passes it explicitly**, a mechanical change made **by hand** at each call site (CLAUDE.md forbids scripted code changes). As of `af10e34` the five production call sites are the `Op::CloneFile` constructions at `src/engine/stage.rs:272`, `src/engine/swap.rs:331`, `src/engine/swap.rs:603` and `src/engine/undo.rs:1526`, and the direct `sys::clone_file(source, &copy, Durability::Immediate)` call at `src/fsx/mutate.rs:649` (the transaction's copy of a file it is about to overwrite). Beyond those five: the `Op::CloneFile` dispatch at `mutate.rs:698` (match arm `:522`) passes the op's own policy through to `sys::clone_file`, and the test call sites (`mutate.rs:978`, the `sys.rs` unit tests at `:693-730`) gain the argument too. Grep for `Op::CloneFile` and `clone_file(` before starting, since lines drift.
  - `Required` returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` straight from the failed FICLONE (the `reflink_unsupported` check, `sys.rs:253-259`) and **never enters the byte-copy branch** (`:231-249`). `clone_tree` maps it to `CloneError::NotReflinkable` at the first file, leaving no partial destination file.
  - `TreeCopy.copied_bytes` counts bytes written by the byte-copy branch, so a test can assert it is 0.
- **Per entry:**
  - directories: `Op::CreateDir` with mode `0o700`. After its children are in, `Op::Chmod` to `(recorded & 0o777) | 0o700`, so a stored backup stays prunable (an exact `0500` directory could not be emptied by a recursive delete). With `exact_modes` (restore staging), it goes to **exactly** the recorded mode instead, children first, so the restored `WTF/` matches the source exactly, a `0500` directory included (M3-D23);
  - regular files: `Op::CloneFile` with `Durability::Deferred` and `opts.policy`;
  - symlinks: `Op::SymlinkAtomic`, never followed, with `link` recorded in the manifest;
  - devices, FIFOs and sockets: counted as `skipped`, never copied.
- **Capture consistency** (M3-D23). A tree is not captured atomically, so the copy measures what happened:
  - **Per file:** a `FileStamp` is read before and after each file's copy. With `settle`, a mismatch is copied once more; a second mismatch counts as `unsettled`.
  - **Root:** the root's identity (device, inode, birth time) is read before the walk and after the copy. A change is `CloneError::Changed { path: "WTF" }` (the tree was replaced: a concurrent restore, a sync tool).
  - **Inventory:** after the copy, a second stat walk of the source is compared with `manifest`: entry set, kinds, sizes, mtimes. Differences go to `changes` (`changed`, `added`, `removed` counts). This catches a file added, removed or changed **after** its own copy.
  - `consistency` is `Stable` only when `unsettled == 0` and `changes` is empty; otherwise `BestEffort`. Retrying is the caller's choice (`BACKUP_CAPTURE_ATTEMPTS`, D2). `stable` means **observed quiescent during capture**, not a filesystem snapshot.
- **Hashing.** No file content is hashed here.
  - `manifest` records the **source** entries' stats (path, kind, size, mode, mtime, link). Restore diffs and export mtimes come from it, because copies get new mtimes.
  - `stamp_digest` is a `StampDigest` taken by a stat walk of the **destination** after the copy.
  - This task adds the `StampDigest` type to `src/fsx/mutate.rs`: SHA-256 over the sorted `(rel, kind, size, mode, mtime_ns)` tuples, displayed `stamp:sha256:<hex>` (M3-D25). `TreeDigest` keeps rendering `tree:sha256:`. D5 adds `MutateOpts.stamp_before/stamp_after` that consume it.
- **Vanished entries.** An entry that vanishes or changes type mid-walk is an error (`CloneError::Changed { path }`), **never a silent skip**: a restore must not stage a partial backup, and a create reports it (callers map it to `io`, retryable). The path stays **relative** to `WTF/`, and callers redact it with A5's `WtfPathRedactor::rel` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`) before it reaches any output. D1 itself never prints it.
- **Finish.** One `fsx::sync_filesystem(to)` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:433`). There is **no mount check** here: a backup create may read from another filesystem with byte copies (`daily-copy`). D5 adds its own `statx` topology preflight, because a restore must swap by rename.
- **Progress.** `ProgressSink::event(Phase::Copy, total, "WTF/ files")` every 256 files. The label is fixed and **never a path** (M3-D21: every path below `WTF/Account/` names an account, a realm and a character). This task adds `Phase::Copy` (wire `"copy"`) to `src/output/stderr.rs`: the enum variant, the `wire()` arm, and the phase-list test (`:462-472` as of `af10e34`) (M3-D40). Its `current`/`total` count files. The progress event shape stays `{"event":"progress","phase","message","current","total"}`.
- **Unit tests (in `tree.rs`):**
  - a fixture tree (2 accounts, 3 characters, 50 files, a symlink, an empty dir, a `0500` dir) clones with content and manifest equal to a fresh stat walk of the source. The stored `0500` dir is `0700`, and an `exact_modes` clone of the stored copy reproduces the source's `tree_hash` exactly;
  - `ClonePolicy::Required` with the `fsx.reflink.unsupported` failpoint returns `NotReflinkable` at the first file, with `copied_bytes == 0` and no partial destination file. `Preferred` gives `reflinked: none`;
  - a file rewritten between its two stamps (a pause failpoint) is re-copied;
  - a file rewritten **after** its own copy, while a later file copies, shows in `changes` and gives `BestEffort`; so do an added file and a deleted file. A root exchanged during the walk (the test renames another tree into place) is `Changed`;
  - a FIFO is skipped; both bounds trip with `TooLarge`;
  - no progress event contains `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm` or `FakeChar`.
- **Performance, measured here, not at the end.** An `#[ignore]` release test, `clone_tree_500_mb`, clones `Wtf::big(500 MiB, 5,000 files)` on a btrfs dir under `target/`, with the inventory recheck included; it prints `SKIP` without btrfs. The checkpoint budget is **< 1 s** (checkpoint criterion 8: "500 MB in realistic file counts (5,000) under 1 s"; SavedVariables trees hold few, large files). Record the median in the close comment. 20,000 files is measured and reported without a budget.
  - If it misses, or 20,000 files take over 2 s, this task adds the cheaper per-file path **before** D2 and D5 build on it: one `canonicalize` per directory instead of per file, and the clone without `mutate`'s precondition re-stat (its own scope check once per dir).

### 4. Directory locks, `src/fsx/lock.rs`

Add `pub struct DirLock`:
- `shared(dir)` and `try_exclusive(dir) -> Option<DirLock>`, each a `flock` on an `O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY` fd, released on drop and by the kernel on process death (a crashed reader never pins a backup);
- `same_dir(&self, path) -> bool`, which compares the fd's `fstat` with the path's `stat`, so a reader can detect a backup that was moved or deleted under it (it is then `not_found`).

**No lock file is created** (M3-D48: directories are locked directly; lock files under `<cache>` were rejected because a cache wipe would silently break exclusion). The lock order rule, which D3, D4, D5, D8, D9 and D13 rely on: backup directory locks are taken **before** the global lock and are **never waited on while holding it**.

How later tasks use it (for orientation; they implement their own parts):
- **reader reservations:** a restore (plan to commit, D8), an export (the whole stream, D9) and a verify (D13) hold `DirLock::shared` on the backup's own dir, then re-check `same_dir`;
- **deletions:** prune and retention take `DirLock::try_exclusive` on each victim before moving it to trash; a held one is skipped and reported `busy` (D4);
- **scheduling lock:** automatic due check, capture and publication hold `DirLock::try_exclusive` on the target's `<meta>/backups/` dir; a second automatic attempt that finds it held skips as `in_progress` (D3). Manual creates do not take it.

Unit tests: a shared lock blocks `try_exclusive`; a dropped one frees it; a forked child that dies frees it.

### 5. The inventory projection, `src/backup/inventory.rs` (new)

- File `<cache>/backups.json`, kind `backup_inventory` 1.0, with a `KINDS` row, written through fsx as `Writer::Derived` (untracked). Per target key it holds:
  `{covers: {backups: [ids], wtf_previous: [tx ids]}, counts_by_kind, bytes, snapshot_bytes, latest, latest_qualifying, auto: {capability, last}}`.
- `pub fn load_validated(paths, client, key) -> Inventory { fresh | stale(listing_count) | missing }`. It does one `read_dir` of `<meta>/backups/` and one of `<meta>/snapshots/` (an `lstat` of `<tx>/WTF.previous` per entry, a handful), compared with `covers`. A `WTF.previous` that transaction retention pruned therefore makes the projection stale, never falsely current. This is what `status --cached` calls (D11 renders it): the same id set means current; a different set gives the projection's numbers marked `stale: true` with the listing's count.
- `pub fn rebuild(paths, client, key)` reads every `backup.json` (bounded) and sums the apparent sizes of the `WTF.previous` trees (a bounded stat walk). It runs in commands, **never** in `status --cached`. **`auto.capability` and `auto.last` have no other authority**, so a rebuild carries them over from the old projection when it is readable, and starts at `unknown`/`null` only when it is not.
- `pub fn record(paths, key, change)` applies one known change cheaply, falling back to `rebuild` on any mismatch.
- Every call is **best effort**: a failed write never fails its command (the release-memo pattern). A projection is derived: deleting it costs one "stale/unknown" until the next writer, never correctness.
- Callers: D2, D3, D4, D10, D13 and D14 call `record`. D3 records automatic-attempt outcomes there (`auto.capability` `supported|unsupported`, `auto.last {at, result}`; M3-D30).
- The status block it feeds (D11 renders it, for orientation):
  ```json
  "backups":{"count":5,"stale":false,
             "latest":{"id":"01M6Q…","captured_at":"…","kind":"auto","trigger":"post_session"},
             "latest_qualifying":{"id":"01M6Q…","captured_at":"…"},
             "auto":{"mode":"daily","capability":"supported","last":{"at":"…","result":"created"}},
             "bytes":63963136,"snapshot_bytes":15937536,"free_bytes":227633266688}
  ```

### 6. Filesystem hints, `src/backup/fs.rs` (new)

Every later backup task reads these instead of probing on its own:
- `clone_hint(meta) -> CloneHint { Capable, Incapable }` from `statfs` magic numbers: btrfs `0x9123683E` and xfs `0x58465342` → `Capable`; anything else (ext4 `0xEF53`, tmpfs, FUSE, NTFS) → `Incapable` (M3-D30). It is only an **eligibility hint**: capability is observed per attempt (D3). In debug builds, `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE=yes|no` overrides it (a DEC-7 test seam that release builds ignore), and `TestEnv` sets `no` by default (`tests/common/env.rs`), so the default `daily` mode skips with no write in every existing scene on any `TMPDIR`.
- `free_bytes(meta) -> u64` from `statvfs` (`f_bavail × f_frsize`, the space for unprivileged users). In debug builds, `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB=<n>` overrides it.
- Users: D2 (dry run and `backup_space_low`), D3 (automatic decisions), D8 (`before_restore`), D11 (`status`), and D1's own listing (`free_bytes`).

### 7. Registry and help

- `COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:109-138`): an entry `backup` (group Change, `mutates: true`, because the tree's subcommands mutate) and `backup list` (Change, `mutates: false`). One entry per nested path.
- `command_name` arm and `dispatch` arm; `pub mod backup`.
- Help layout (M3-D39): the Change group gains `backup` after `undo`. Bare help stays under 30 lines and 80 columns. Update `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals, the bare-help snapshots and the `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test.
- The `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocation for `backup list`.
- Contract matrix rows (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`) with snapshots: one success, one `not_found` (an unknown id prefix of 8+).
- There are no new verb aliases. The typo machinery already maps `backups` → `help backup`.

### 8. Fixtures

- `tests/common/wtf.rs` (new): `Wtf::at(client_dir)` with `.account("FAKEACCT")`, `.realm("FakeRealm")`, `.character("FakeChar")`, `.saved_variables(folder, bytes)`, `.config_wtf(text)`, `.file(rel, bytes)`, `.symlink(rel, target)`, `.mode(rel, mode)`, `.big(total_bytes, files)` (for perf), and `.build()`. `common_selftest` covers it.
- `tests/common/backups.rs` (new): `seed_backup(client, kind, captured_at, files)`, plus `seed_many(client, n)` for the 200-backup perf home (checkpoint criterion 10).
- `TZ=UTC` set in `TestEnv` (`tests/common/env.rs`; common rule 13), and `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE=no` as its default (item 6).
- These are the shared builders listed for D1 in the new-test-files table: `tests/common/wtf.rs`, `tests/common/backups.rs` (`seed_backup`, `seed_many`); E2E in `tests/backup_list.rs`.

### 9. README

- A new `### backup` section skeleton (list only, at this point; later tasks add their subcommands).
- Files table rows: `<meta>/backups/` (0700, with `backup.json`, `manifest.json`, `addons.json`, `WTF/`) and `<cache>/backups.json` (derived, safe to delete).
- `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE` and `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB` in the debug-hook sentence (debug builds only).

### Wire names this task adds (list them in the close comment, common rule 6)

Command paths `backup`, `backup list`; `--limit` on `backup list`; data keys of `backup list` above; the `backup_create` `commands[]` action; progress phase `copy`; state kinds `backup`, `backup_manifest`, `backup_addons`, `backup_inventory`; backup kinds `manual|auto|before_restore|imported|recovered`; `trigger`, `consistency`, `integrity`, `baseline`, `reflinked` values; debug seams `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE`, `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB`; constants `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_ENTRIES`, `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_DEPTH`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `backup list` lists seeded backups newest first, with kind, trigger, counts, apparent bytes, local capture times, `consistency`, `integrity`, `restorable`, `qualifying` and `busy`, and free space per target; bare `backup` gives the same data.
- A damaged backup (deleted manifest, unreadable `backup.json`) lists as `restorable: false` and never fails the command.
- Listing 200 backups reads only their `backup.json` files and the manifests' presence (a counting test fixture asserts no tree walk and no hashing).
- `--limit N` bounds the backups shown per target; `shown` and `total` are always correct.
- A prefix of 8 resolves; 7 is `usage`; an ambiguous prefix is `ref_ambiguous` with alternatives that parse; an unknown prefix is `not_found` with the newest three ids as alternatives.
- The `Required` clone policy copies zero payload bytes on a filesystem that cannot clone (`fsx.reflink.unsupported`: `NotReflinkable` at the first file, `copied_bytes == 0`, no partial destination file); `Preferred` gives `reflinked: none`.
- Every existing `CloneFile` caller (the four `Op::CloneFile` constructions and the direct `sys::clone_file` call in `mutate.rs`) passes `ClonePolicy::Preferred` explicitly, and the existing engine, crash and undo suites stay green.
- The tree clone reproduces content, symlink targets and a manifest equal to a fresh stat walk of the source; stored directories are owner-writable; an `exact_modes` clone of the stored copy reproduces the source `tree_hash` exactly, a `0500` dir included.
- Capture consistency: a file rewritten between its stamps is re-copied; a change after its own copy, an added file, a deleted file each give `best_effort`; a replaced root gives `Changed`; FIFOs are skipped; both tree bounds trip with `TooLarge`.
- `DirLock`: a shared lock blocks `try_exclusive`; dropping frees it; a dead child process frees it; `same_dir` detects a moved or deleted dir; no lock file is created.
- No output (human, JSON or stderr progress) contains `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm` or `FakeChar`. D1 checks that with plain substring asserts, because A5's `assert_private_all` may land after D1 starts; D2 switches the backup tests to the shared helper.
- The inventory projection validates, goes stale when a backup dir (or a `WTF.previous`) is added or removed behind its back, rebuilds on `backup list`, carries `auto.capability`/`auto.last` across a rebuild, and a failed projection write never fails the command.
- `clone_tree_500_mb` (release, `#[ignore]`) runs on btrfs and its median is recorded in the close comment against the < 1 s budget (or the cheaper per-file path is added); without btrfs it prints `SKIP`.
- `Phase::Copy` serializes as `"copy"` and is covered by the phase-list test.
- The new constants have `REGISTRY` rows and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted; the four new state kinds have `KINDS` rows.
- The contract rows (success and `not_found`) are snapshotted; `backup list` has its `special.rs` read-only invocation; bare help stays under 30 lines and 80 columns with `backup` after `undo` in Change.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (in `src/`): `BackupId` parsing and prefix resolution (8 resolves, 7 usage, ambiguous, unknown); `check_structure` against complete and incomplete trees; `ClonePolicy` at `sys::clone_file` (both policies, with the failpoint); `StampDigest` (sorted input, stable rendering `stamp:sha256:`); `DirLock` (shared vs exclusive, drop, child death, `same_dir`); the tree clone cases listed under item 3; inventory `load_validated` (fresh, stale after an added dir, stale after a pruned `WTF.previous`, missing), `rebuild` carry-over of `auto`, `record` fallback to rebuild; `clone_hint` and `free_bytes` with and without the debug seams.
- **E2E** (`tests/backup_list.rs`, new): seeded backups of each kind via `seed_backup`; damaged entries; `--limit`; `-t` with several targets; no `-t`; human output (apparent-size wording, 16-character ids, local times with `TZ=UTC`); the `backup_create` hint for a target with no qualifying capture in 7 days; plain-substring privacy asserts over stdout and stderr with `--progress json`.
- **Counting fixture:** 200 seeded backups (`seed_many`) with a test hook that counts opened files, asserting only `backup.json` reads and manifest existence checks.
- **Contract:** `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows (success, `not_found`) with snapshots; `special.rs` read-only row; `cli_skeleton` and help-layout updates.
- **Perf:** `clone_tree_500_mb` (`#[ignore]`, release, btrfs under `target/`), 5,000 and 20,000 files, median recorded.
- **`common_selftest`:** the `Wtf` builder and `seed_backup`.

## Considerations

- **Size L, kept as one task on purpose.** The primitives (clone policy, `DirLock`, inventory, fs hints) were added here deliberately. Splitting them out would make D2, D4, D5 and D9 each wait on several small tasks.
- **Critical path.** D1 is the first task on the restore-safety critical path (20 weighted units): D1 → D5 → D14 → D8 → D7 → F9 → F7 → G1 → G2 → G3. It has no slack: start it on day one (lane 5, "restore engine", the engine specialist, t=0–3, owns `journal.rs`, `restore.rs`, `preserve.rs` afterwards).
- Apparent sizes overstate real usage on btrfs. The human line says "apparent, initially shared copy-on-write" whenever `reflinked != none`, and shows free space beside it (M3-D48).
- The `ClonePolicy` change touches five existing `CloneFile` call sites (`stage.rs:272`, `swap.rs:331`, `swap.rs:603`, `undo.rs:1526`, and the direct `sys::clone_file` call at `mutate.rs:649`), plus the dispatch at `mutate.rs:698` and the test call sites. Each passes `Preferred` explicitly, made by hand (CLAUDE.md: no scripted code changes). Find them by symbol; lines drift.
- The capture-consistency rules make a torn copy visible rather than impossible: `stable` is "observed quiescent", not a snapshot. README must say so in those words (D2 writes that paragraph).
- `busy` in the listing is a best-effort snapshot. D4's one retry after 50 ms exists precisely so this probe never makes a backup look busy to prune.
- D1 may start before A1 lands. Neither its 7-day hint nor D11's stale recommendation needs a frozen clock; both use `Timestamp::now()` with tests seeded relative to the real clock. D2 switches the module to `crate::clock::now()`.
- **Risks (from the milestone risk table):** risk 9, backups filling the disk (SavedVariables churn on btrfs, `daily-copy` on ext4): mitigated by the per-day retention (D4), the free-space guard and byte-copy budget (D3), and free space shown next to apparent sizes (here). Risk 13, personal data leaking on any channel: progress carries only a fixed label; paths stay relative and are redacted by callers. Risk 15, `status --cached` regressing past 5 ms: the inventory projection validated by one `read_dir` instead of tree scans.
- **Collision hot spots:** `src/fsx/sys.rs`, `mutate.rs`, `lock.rs` (D1, D5, D9: D1 adds `ClonePolicy`, `StampDigest`, `DirLock`; D5 the exchange probe; D9 the directory fsync after persist); `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs` and the help tests (one `Command` variant per top-level command: D1 adds `backup` with `list`, later tasks add subcommand variants; A4's global flag first); `src/limits.rs` and its snapshot (re-accept in each task); `README.md` (edit only your own section). Claim with a file list and rebase before each gate run.
- **Delivery slice:** `slice-2` ("Capture and diagnose"). Its exit demo: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 6, 7, 8 (create, auto, verify) and 13 (`errors dismiss`, `backup prune`). D1 supplies the model, listing and copy routine underneath every backup part of that demo.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- none

**Unblocks:**
- D2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.2` (`backup create`): writes this model (`BackupMeta`, manifest, `addons.json`) using `clone_tree` with `ClonePolicy`, the capture-consistency result, `StampDigest`, `inventory::record` and `fs::free_bytes`.
- D4 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.4` (Backup retention, space reclamation and `backup prune`): reads `list`/`BackupRef` and the shared `qualifying` predicate, takes `DirLock::try_exclusive` on victims, records deletions in the inventory.
- D5 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.5` (The whole-`WTF/` restore transaction in the engine): reads the model, calls `check_structure`, takes reader reservations with `DirLock::shared`/`same_dir`, stages with `clone_tree` (`exact_modes`), and uses `StampDigest` for M3-D25.
- D9 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.9` (`backup export`): reads the model and manifest under a `DirLock::shared` reservation.
- D11 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.11` (Backups in `status`): reads the inventory projection through `load_validated` and `fs::free_bytes`.

Inherited through those: D3, D8, D10 and D13 use these primitives through D2, D4, D5 and D9; D14 records recovered backups through `inventory::record`.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** The settings players lose (`WTF/`, SavedVariables) are the one thing omaddons does not yet protect beyond a week of undo snapshots. Every M3 backup feature (create, automatic checkpoints, prune, restore, export, import, verify, the bar's Backups view) stands on one model, one listing, one tree-clone routine and three shared primitives, and this bead builds all of them. Putting them in one place means there is exactly one copy routine to make fast (500 MB under 1 s on btrfs) and correct (honest about consistency, never following symlinks, never hashing), one clone policy that makes "clone-only" true at the fsx primitive, one lock type for reservations, and one projection that keeps `status --cached` at 5 ms with hundreds of backups. It keeps the thesis intact: every write still goes through fsx, nothing here takes the global lock, and every backup says truthfully what it proves. It is the first task of the restore-safety critical path, so D5, D14 and D8 cannot start until it lands.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D23: what a backup is.** `<meta>/backups/<id>/` (0700) with `backup.json`, `manifest.json` (exact source modes, optional hashes, local only), `addons.json` (addon provenance copied from the record) and `WTF/`, built in an untracked `Writer::Backup` stage with deferred durability and one `syncfs`, published by `RENAME_NOREPLACE`. Directories stay owner-writable in the store; exact modes are applied only at restore staging. Capture consistency is measured by per-file stamps, a root-identity check and an inventory recheck. Why: same filesystem as `WTF/` (reflinks, atomic exchange), the only fsx path that allows deferred durability, and honest evidence at two lstats per file. Rejected: per-file SHA-256 at every create (0.5–1 s per 500 MB, breaks the budget; opt-in instead), a tar inside the client dir (no reflinks, slow), timestamp ids (collisions), storing exact `0500` modes in the store (unprunable backups).
- **M3-D25: stamp digests, not content hashes, for whole-tree renames.** This bead adds the `StampDigest` type (`stamp:sha256:` over sorted `(path, kind, size, mode, mtime_ns)`), taken from a stat walk of the destination. Why: a transaction session would otherwise content-hash a 500 MB `WTF/` twice under the lock (seconds against a 50 ms budget); journal identity uses inodes and birth times anyway. Rejected: content digests before the lock (0.5–1 s per restore for no safety gain).
- **M3-D30 (owner-visible; departs from the vision's `off` default): clone-only is enforced at the primitive.** `ClonePolicy::Required` returns `Unsupported` from the failed FICLONE and never enters the byte-copy branch; capability is observed per attempt and stored in the inventory; `statfs` magic is only a hint, with a debug seam for deterministic tests. Why: "a clone-only policy that can still pay for a full byte copy of a large first file is not clone-only" (review finding), and a mode reported "on" that never succeeds would be a lie. Rejected: aborting after seeing `ByteCopy` (the copy is already paid for).
- **M3-D37: projections, not unbounded reads, for `status --cached`.** `<cache>/backups.json` holds per-target counts, apparent bytes, latest and latest qualifying capture and the `auto` capability/last attempt, with `covers` validated by one `read_dir` of `backups/` and of `snapshots/`. Why: a directory listing holds no sizes, and summing 200 backups' trees in 5 ms is impossible. Rejected: a database or daemon for summaries.
- **M3-D40: a new progress phase `copy`**, with a fixed label (`"WTF/ files"`), never a path. Rejected: reusing `stage`, which means archive staging and would mislead.
- **M3-D47: integrity is explicit.** The model carries `integrity` (`metadata_only|verified|damaged`), `verified_at` and `baseline`; `restorable` (kept for DEC-4) now means "structurally restorable and not damaged"; listing never walks or hashes trees. Rejected: hashing every automatic capture; claiming "verified" from a first verification.
- **M3-D48: directory locks, honest accounting.** `DirLock` is a `flock` on a directory fd (shared for readers, non-blocking exclusive for deleters and the scheduling lock), released by the kernel on process death; no lock files; directory locks before the global lock, never waited on while holding it. Sizes are apparent and labelled, shown next to measured free space. Rejected: lock files under `<cache>` (a cache wipe silently breaks exclusion); an apparent-byte budget for reflinked backups (it measures the wrong thing).
- **M3-D31 (shared predicate): qualifying captures.** The predicate (manual, auto or before_restore; not partial; stable; local) lives in `backup/mod.rs` so D3, D4 and D11 cannot drift apart.
- **M3-D21 (context): privacy on every channel.** Progress carries counts and a fixed label; `CloneError::Changed` paths stay relative for callers to redact with A5's redactor.
- **M3-D39 (context): help layout**: `backup` joins the Change group after `undo`.

**Review-round changes folded in.** Review round 1 moved the 500 MB performance measurement into this bead (it had been at the end), set the budget at a realistic 5,000 files, and introduced `statfs` capability detection. Review round 2 added the `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE` test seam so suites are deterministic on any `TMPDIR`. Review round 3 (revision 3) made clone-only real with `ClonePolicy::Required` at `sys::clone_file`, added the root-identity and inventory rechecks with `stable` versus `best_effort`, and turned `statfs` into a hint with observed capability; revision 5 added `integrity`/`baseline` and `addons.json`; revision 15 added the `backups.json` projection validated by `read_dir`; revision 23 added `DirLock` reservations, the scheduling lock and honest apparent-size accounting; revision 22 fixed the directory-mode inconsistency (owner-writable store, exact modes at restore). The primitives were put in this bead on purpose, so D2, D4, D5 and D9 each wait on one bead, not on several small ones.

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`:
- `sys::clone_file` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:207-259`) swallows the unsupported error and byte-copies in the same call; `reflink_unsupported` is at `:253-259`; the only knob is the `fsx.reflink.unsupported` failpoint (`:218`).
- The five production clone call sites: `Op::CloneFile` at `src/engine/stage.rs:272`, `src/engine/swap.rs:331` and `:603`, `src/engine/undo.rs:1526`, and a direct `sys::clone_file` call at `src/fsx/mutate.rs:649`; the `Op::CloneFile` dispatch is at `mutate.rs:698`, and an fsx test constructs one at `:978`.
- Deferred durability only under `<meta>/stage/<tx>/` in untracked sessions (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:277-289`); transaction sessions hash every renamed dir and cloned file (`:595-618`).
- `stage_trees` hashes every copied file (`src/engine/stage.rs:272-279`); `keep_dir_mode` keeps staged dirs owner-writable (`:297-312`).
- `TreeDigest` renders `tree:sha256:` (`mutate.rs:177-180`); `fsx::sync_filesystem` exists (`mutate.rs:433`).
- `ClientPaths::backups()` exists with no callers (`src/state/paths.rs:410-413`); `ClientPaths::wtf()` resolves a `wtf/` spelling (`:415-419`).
- `Scope::ClientMeta` admits `Backup` and `BackupRestore`; `Scope::Wtf` admits only `BackupRestore` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:99-122`, `:118`).
- `PruneReason::BackupPrune` deletes exactly one entry below `backups/` (`src/fsx/prune.rs:25-46`, `:311-315`).
- `ulid_id!` is at `src/model.rs:222-299`; `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB) at `src/limits.rs:65`.
- Progress phases are `fetch|download|verify|stage|commit` (`src/output/stderr.rs:32-58`).
- The development machine's clients are all on btrfs, and their `WTF/` trees are tiny (232–596 KB), so the perf budget needs a synthetic tree.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- The 500 MB budget might miss: it is measured here, before D2 and D5 build on the clone, with a named fallback (per-directory canonicalize, no per-file precondition re-stat).
- Touching every `CloneFile` call site could regress AddOns staging, swaps or undo: each passes `Preferred`, which is byte-for-byte today's behaviour, and the existing crash and undo suites are the regression net.
- A projection could report stale numbers as current: `covers` is validated against `read_dir` of both `backups/` and `snapshots/` on every read, and a mismatch is reported `stale`, never hidden.
- Personal data in progress: fixed labels only, asserted in unit and E2E tests.
- Disk fill (risk 9) and `status --cached` regressions (risk 15) are mitigated by the projection and the honest accounting here, and by D3/D4 policy.

**Confidence.** High: backup creation and listing, and the clone policy, are small, directly tested, and the budget is measured early in this very bead.
