Handoff from A2 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.2, landed).

What: `src/app/status.rs` now has `data.summary`, per-target `issues[]` and `data.last_change` / `last_change_state`. Append the backups block after these keys (DEC-3: additive, declared after existing keys).
Why: backup lines (`TxKind::Backup`) never count as the last change and never push it out of the history projection. `newest_run` skips them, and `tests/status.rs` `backups_and_settings_changes_never_push_the_last_change_out` runs 40 real `backup create`s plus 20 `config set`s after an update.
How:
- A backup finding that should reach the widget's Issues view becomes an `Issue` with an id added to `app::issues::ids` (one table), ranked by `issues_for`'s severity/id/addon order.
- `tests/perf.rs` `status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo` now has a second phase with a 20 MB interleaved history: median 4.1 ms, p95 4.3 ms, first run 4.9 ms, and the change that rebuilt the projection 30 ms. Add the 200-backups, 16-accounts phase there, as milestone risk 15 says.
Risks: about 0.9 ms of headroom remains under the 5 ms budget.
Done when: the perf phase is in and the README `### status` section names the backups keys.

title: Integration crash matrices, concurrency and performance checkpoints
description:
## Background

Goal **G-M3-6 (no new risk to the engine's guarantees)** and checkpoint criteria **8 (backups)**, **9 (crash safety)**, **10 (`status --cached` under 5 ms)** and **14 (persisted formats fail closed)** need the same kind of evidence the M1 and M2 engines carry: crash matrices armed as real aborts, concurrency tests, release-build performance budgets, and an honest account of what older binaries do.

**What D12 is not.** Each protocol-changing task already lands its **own** crash and recovery matrix before it closes (common rule 14):
- D5 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.5`): the whole restore (`Op::Restore`, its `restore_matrix`, its failpoints, its journaled renames, repeated recovery, running-client deferral, the conservative stop);
- D6 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.6`): the undo of a whole restore (`Op::UndoRestore`);
- D14 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.14`): recovery preservation (crashes, I/O failures and disk-full inside recovery, at every preservation transition);
- D7 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.7`): the partial restore and its undo (`Op::RestoreAddon`, `Op::UndoRestoreAddon`);
- D3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.3`): the `daily-copy` scene that arms `engine.autobackup` as an abort.

D12 never discovers whether any of those works. **It owns what crosses features:** cross-shape scenes that need two tasks' work at once, concurrency between features, the release performance checkpoints, and the **af10e34 characterization**, whose scenes need every restore shape (whole and partial, committed and interrupted) and A3's (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.3`) fail-closed readers.

**Why the characterization exists** (M3-D45, and the ground truth on persisted formats, §2.9, in the milestone epic's "Ground truth" comment). An M2 binary (`af10e34` or older) has no guard against state M3 wrote:
- Journals: `Prepared.schema_version` is written and **never compared** (`src/engine/journal.rs:82`, `CURRENT = 1.0` at `:38`). An unknown enum value fails its whole line, which is counted in `unknown_lines` and skipped (`:363-366`), and nothing reads that count. A skipped `prepared` line leaves the phase `Unprepared`, so M2 recovery rolls nothing back, prunes the journal and in-flight lock (`:737`, `:767-776`), and the dead-snapshot sweep removes that transaction's state-side snapshots (`:781-794`).
- History: an unreadable line is counted and `history`/`undo` warn `history_lines_skipped` (`src/state/history.rs:5-9`, `:318-330`, `:381`); `undo` then plans and checks conflicts over the readable entries only (`src/app/undo.rs:287-290`, `src/engine/undo.rs:162`, `:271`, `:700`). An M2 binary cannot read an M3 `wtf` or `saved_variables` op, because `FolderOp` gains variants.
- M2's undo with the default `--saved-variables auto` restores **every** SavedVariables file whose hash differs from the reverted transaction's manifest (`src/engine/undo.rs:1339-1383`), whoever changed it. So an M2 binary that undoes an old install after an M3 restore would silently put the install-time copies back over the restored settings: **the blind SavedVariables undo**.
- The newer-record refusal (`store::save`, `src/state/store.rs:230-243`, `state_too_new`, exit 4) **fires late**: after the swap and after undo's SavedVariables restore (`src/engine/tx.rs:904-913`, `src/engine/undo.rs:343-357`).
- What does protect M3 restore journals: `Scope::Wtf` (the whole `WTF/` tree) admits **only** `Writer::BackupRestore` and `Scope::SavedVariables` admits only `Undo` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:117-118`), while M2 recovery always writes as `Writer::Mutating` (`journal.rs:731`). So an M2 binary that tries to recover an M3 restore journal is refused by scope at its first `WTF/` rename.

There is no pre-mutation structure that M2 already refuses, so M3 **does not claim a downgrade barrier**. Instead D12 characterizes the real af10e34 binary against committed and interrupted M3 restores, records exactly what it refuses and what it would do, and README Limitations quotes it.

Decisions that shape it, one line each (full text in the milestone epic's decision-log comments):
- **M3-D45**: persisted formats fail closed from M3 on; M3 documents and characterizes, rather than claims to prevent, what M2 binaries do.
- **M3-D24**: a whole restore is one journaled `RENAME_EXCHANGE` of `WTF`; recovery direction follows the durable journal phase (backward before `swapped`, forward from it); `writes_wtf` journals wait while the client runs; unexpected identities are ambiguous; displaced versions get a durable home through a journaled, resumable intent before anything is pruned.
- **M3-D27 / M3-D28**: a partial restore uses undo's SavedVariables layout; undo and restores conflict where they would overwrite each other.
- **M3-D31 / M3-D48**: automatic captures are serialized per target by a scheduling lock (`DirLock::try_exclusive` on `<meta>/backups/`); readers (restore, export, verify) hold `DirLock::shared` reservations; prune skips busy backups; lock order is backup directory locks first, never waited on while holding the global lock.
- **M3-D23 / M3-D25**: the 500 MB budget at a realistic 5,000-file count; whole-tree renames record stamp digests so nothing hashes a 500 MB tree under the lock (lock-hold budget 50 ms).
- **M3-D37**: `status --cached` reads projections; the heavy home of criterion 10 proves the bound.
- **M3-D47**: verification timing is reported, not budgeted (`--verify` is opt-in).

## Technical Approach

### 1. `tests/engine_crash.rs`: cross-feature scenes

These build on the shapes and oracles the earlier tasks committed: D5's `Op::Restore` and `restore_matrix`, D6's `Op::UndoRestore`, D7's `Op::RestoreAddon` and `Op::UndoRestoreAddon`, D14's preservation matrix, and D3's `daily-copy` autobackup scene. The existing harness is `support::{Op, Shape, matrix, recovery_matrix, rename_matrix, shape_matrix, …}` over `common::engine::Scene`, arming each failpoint as a real `abort` in a child process (as of `af10e34`, `tests/engine_crash.rs:31` and the `support` module).

1. **Played-on undo-of-restore** (needs D6's shape and D14's protocol): a crash after an undo-of-restore's exchange, a simulated play session on the tree it put in place (a SavedVariables file rewritten), then recovery.
   - Expected: the tree from before the undo is live again, and the played tree is a `recovered` backup (byte-identical to the played tree), with `restore_rolled_back` naming it.
   - **The same with a crash inside that preservation** (abort at `engine.preserve.intent`, `engine.preserve.moved`, `engine.preserve.published`): the next recovery resumes with the **same** backup id; exactly one `recovered` backup exists.
2. **An automatic capture racing a restore:**
   - a widget-style `backup create --auto` from a second process while a restore is paused at `engine.restore.staged`;
   - the same with `engine.autobackup` armed as an abort in the capturing process.
   - Expected: the capture takes the scheduling lock and copies the live, pre-restore tree, or skips; the restore's reader reservation and journal are unaffected; lock order holds (no deadlock); and no half-made backup is ever listed (`backup list` between steps shows only complete backups).
3. **Recovery of several targets** with one deferred (its client running, fake proc) and one preserving (a played-on interrupted restore): the other target recovers and preserves, and the deferred one stays pending (`journal_pending`, "… waits for the game to exit", nothing under its `WTF/` moved). After that client "exits", it rolls back.
4. **The full sweep:** every `FAILPOINTS` entry (34) armed once in each M3 shape, with the oracle of each shape's own matrix, to catch a failpoint that a later task moved. This is a loop over the shapes D5, D6, D7 and D14 defined, **not new oracles**.
   - The 34 engine failpoints are the 27 of `af10e34` (`src/engine/tx.rs:67-95`: `engine.plan.fetched`, `engine.plan.downloaded`, `engine.plan.done`, `engine.stage.begin`, `engine.stage.file`, `engine.stage.synced`, `engine.snapshot.prestaged`, `engine.lock.acquired`, `engine.recovered`, `engine.registered`, `engine.revalidated`, `engine.journal.prepared`, `engine.addons_dir.created`, `engine.snapshot.sv`, `engine.snapshot.state`, `engine.swap.before_rename`, `engine.swap.after_exchange`, `engine.swapped`, `engine.record.written`, `engine.history.appended`, `engine.committed`, `engine.unlocked`, `engine.cleanup.done`, `engine.retention`, `engine.recover.step`, `engine.recover.sv`, `engine.recover.forward`) plus seven new ones:
     - `engine.autobackup` (D3, just before the automatic capture);
     - `engine.restore.staged` (after the clone), `engine.restore.exchanged` (after step 1), `engine.restore.snapshotted` (after step 2) (D5);
     - `engine.preserve.intent`, `engine.preserve.moved`, `engine.preserve.published` (D14).
   - The existing rule for off-path failpoints applies: a failpoint a scene never reaches must let it succeed.

The oracles, restated so this task can check them without reopening the earlier beads:
- **Whole restore:** every crash leaves `<client dir>/WTF` wholly old or wholly new, judged by its `tree_hash` (exact modes included); the next change command recovers it; direction follows the durable phase (backward before `swapped`, forward from it), and the rename having executed does not, by itself, select roll-forward.
- **Partial restore:** each touched file is wholly old or wholly new, and the `tree_hash` of the rest of `WTF/` is unchanged.
- **Preservation:** every displaced version that differs from a copy still held elsewhere ends up as a `recovered` backup, resumed with the same id after a crash; a file the game replaced stays as the game wrote it; an unrecognized state or an incomplete preservation leaves every tree, the stage and the journal in place (`journal_pending` with `details.reason` `unexpected_state` or `preservation_incomplete`), and never cleans up to finish.
- **Running client:** a crashed restore's journal stays pending and nothing under `WTF/` moves while the client runs or its state is unknown; it rolls back once the client exits; in-process recovery makes the same fresh check.
- **Repeated recovery** is idempotent (run it more than once after each scene).

### 2. `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`: concurrency between features

- A concurrent `install` completes while a restore is paused at `engine.restore.staged` (the restore holds no global lock while staging). A `backup create` paused mid-copy blocks nothing (a concurrent commit completes; the `engine_concurrency` pattern).
- Two `backup create --auto` on one target at once make **one** backup; the second reports `skipped: in_progress` (D3's scheduling lock).
- A `backup prune` racing a paused export and a paused restore reports both sources `busy` (D4's reservation-aware deletion: `DirLock::try_exclusive`, one retry after 50 ms, then `busy`), and neither reader fails.
- A `backup verify` racing a prune of the same backup: one of them reports `busy` or `not_found`, **never a crash or a partial delete** (D13's shared reservation and `same_dir` check).

### 3. `tests/perf.rs`: release performance checkpoints (`#[ignore]`, release build)

- **`backup_create_500_mb_under_1_s`**: `Wtf::big(500 MiB, 5,000 files)` (D1's builder), with realistic file sizes (D1 measured the primitive first with `clone_tree_500_mb`), the capture consistency recheck included. Budget: under 1 s, median of 5.
  - Test homes are temp dirs on tmpfs (`TestEnv::new()` uses `tempfile::tempdir()`, `tests/common/env.rs:21`), so this test builds its home under a btrfs dir in the repo's `target/` (`target/` is on btrfs on the development machine).
  - When `statfs` says that dir is not reflink-capable, it prints `SKIP` and fails unless allowed, per `tests/common/checkpoint.rs` (`OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP`). This `SKIP` is **not** one of the checkpoint's pre-accepted `SKIP`s, so on the development machine it must run.
  - It also reports 20,000 files, as information, without a budget.
- **`backup_create_verify_500_mb`**: `--verify` timing on the same tree, reported without a budget (documented as roughly 0.5–1 s per 500 MB).
- **`restore_lock_hold_under_50_ms`** with the same tree: the global lock hold of a whole restore stays under 50 ms (measured with the existing `common::engine::lock_held_ms` helper, as `commits_hold_the_lock_under_50_ms` does at `tests/perf.rs:417`). D5's gate test keeps a debug-build sanity ceiling of 2 s; this is the release budget.
- **`status_cached_under_5_ms_with_m3_blocks`** (A2's test, extended again; D11 adds the 200-backup target, so extend D11's version when it has landed):
  - 4 backups per target and one target with 200 (`seed_many`);
  - a 2 MB BugGrabber file per target and 16 accounts on one (B2's `tests/common/buggrabber.rs` builder);
  - a 20 MB interleaved history (A2's generator of runs from two simulated terminals).

  It reports the median of 21 (budget 5 ms), the p95, and a cold first call. A missing or stale projection must report "unknown"/`stale`, never a guess.
- The 500 MB fixture takes disk space and time to build. Build it **once per test run** in a cached dir under `target/` (the `bench_home` pattern, `tests/perf.rs:119`), not in the gate.

### 4. README

Development → "Crash testing": failpoint counts 27 → 34 (`engine.autobackup`, three restore points, three preservation points). There are **two README mentions** of "27" as of `af10e34`: the Safety model's "Crash testing" paragraph (line 1427, "All 27 engine failpoints are armed …") and the test-suite table row for `tests/engine_crash.rs` (line 1919). Update both. Decided while writing this bead: also extend the paragraph's list of crashed shapes with the restore, undo-of-restore, partial-restore and preservation scenes, so the count and the list agree.

### 5. The af10e34 characterization (`tests/compat_m2.rs`, `#[ignore]`; M3-D45)

It runs when this task closes and again at G3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3`). It lands here because its scenes need committed and interrupted whole and partial restores (D5, D7, D8) and A3's fail-closed readers.

- **Build.** Build `af10e34` once in a scratch worktree under `target/compat/` (`git worktree add`, `cargo build --release`), cached by commit hash. The test skips with a `SKIP` line when it cannot build. That is one of the checkpoint's **pre-accepted `SKIP`s**: the build error goes in the close comment, README Limitations keeps A3's general warning, and D12 closes.
- **Scenes**, each on a fixture home that the **current** binary prepared:
  1. a committed whole restore, then the M2 binary's `undo <older install>` with the default `--saved-variables auto`;
  2. a committed partial restore (`backup restore --addon`), then the same undo;
  3. an interrupted whole restore (failpoint abort after the exchange, `engine.restore.exchanged=abort`), then any M2 change command on that target;
  4. an interrupted partial restore, the same;
  5. an M3 `dismiss` and `widget` history line, then M2 `history` and `undo`. (These lines come from `errors dismiss` and `omarchy install`, B8 and E2, which are not upstream of D12. Decided while writing this bead: if they have not landed when this task runs, plant literal lines of the documented shape, a `SettingEntry` of kind `dismiss` and one of kind `widget`, and say so in the close comment.)
- **Record, for each scene:** the exit code; the error code; which files under `WTF/` changed (hashes before and after); whether the journal, stage and snapshots survived; and what the M3 binary's next recovery did.
- **The assertions are about what must hold:**
  - an interrupted M3 restore journal is **never deleted** by M2 (scope refuses its first `WTF/` rename);
  - the M3 binary afterwards recovers it or reports it.
- **What M2 is expected to get wrong**, the blind SavedVariables undo of scenes 1 and 2, is **asserted as observed**, so a change in it is noticed, and copied verbatim into README Limitations (which A3 opened with the general warning "do not run a pre-M3 build against state M3 has written; reading with it is safe").
- **The table goes in the close comment** of this bead (one row per scene with the recorded columns), and G3 reruns it (`cargo test --release --test compat_m2 -- --ignored`) and puts the table in its close reason.
- Building an old commit in a test is heavy, so the characterization is ignored by default and its binary is cached by commit hash under `target/compat/`.

### Files

`tests/engine_crash.rs` (scenes and sweep), `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, `tests/perf.rs`, new `tests/compat_m2.rs`, README (crash-testing counts; Limitations quote). No production code changes are expected; a defect found here is filed, not patched here (Considerations).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every cross-feature scene passes: the played-on undo-of-restore (with and without a crash inside its preservation, resuming with the same id); the automatic capture racing a paused restore (also with `engine.autobackup` aborted), with no deadlock and no half-made backup ever listed; recovery of several targets with one deferred and one preserving.
- The full sweep arms each of the 34 `FAILPOINTS` once in each M3 shape (D5, D6, D7, D14) and every scene meets its own shape's oracle; off-path failpoints let their scenes succeed.
- Every concurrency test passes: install during a paused restore; nothing blocked by a paused backup copy; two `--auto` captures make one backup (`in_progress`); prune reports a paused export's and a paused restore's sources `busy`; verify racing prune gives `busy` or `not_found`, never a crash or a partial delete.
- The perf tests meet their budgets on the development machine (release build), with timings recorded in the close comment, p95 included: `backup_create_500_mb_under_1_s` (median of 5 under 1 s; 20,000 files reported), `backup_create_verify_500_mb` (reported), `restore_lock_hold_under_50_ms`, `status_cached_under_5_ms_with_m3_blocks` (median of 21 under 5 ms; p95 and cold start reported).
- README's failpoint counts (both mentions) say 34, and the crash-testing paragraph names the new shapes (the latter decided while writing this bead).
- The af10e34 characterization ran; its table (exit code, error code, `WTF/` changes, journal/stage/snapshot survival, the M3 binary's next recovery, per scene) is in the close comment; an interrupted M3 restore journal was never deleted by M2; the M3 binary recovered or reported it; README Limitations quotes the observed behaviour, the blind SavedVariables undo included.
- If af10e34 no longer builds with the installed toolchain, that is one of the checkpoint's pre-accepted `SKIP`s: the build error goes in the close comment, README Limitations keeps A3's general warning, and D12 closes.

## Test Plan

- **Crash** (`tests/engine_crash.rs`): the three cross-feature scenes and the full sweep, as real `abort`s in child processes, with repeated recovery after each.
- **Concurrency** (`tests/engine_concurrency.rs`): the four scenes, using `tests/common/pause.rs` (`<name>=pause` failpoints with `Pause::reached`/`resume`) for deterministic interleavings and the fake proc (`tests/common/procfs.rs`, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`) for running clients.
- **Perf** (`tests/perf.rs`, release, `#[ignore]`): the four tests above, built once per run in a cached dir under `target/`; `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home` runs them.
- **Compatibility** (`tests/compat_m2.rs`, `#[ignore]`): `cargo test --release --test compat_m2 -- --ignored`; the five scenes against the cached af10e34 build.
- **Privacy**: any output these tests capture from the M3 binary goes through `assert_private_all` (A5's helper) where a `WTF/` with `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` is involved.

## Considerations

- **Scope discipline.** If a shape's own matrix (from D5, D6, D7 or D14) is missing a case that D12 finds, D12 files a bug with `--deps discovered-from:omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12` against that task's code. **It does not patch around it here.**
- **Disk and time.** The 500 MB fixture takes space and time; build it once per run in a cached dir under `target/` (the `bench_home` pattern), never in the gate. The characterization builds an old commit; it is ignored by default and its binary cached under `target/compat/` by commit hash.
- **Heavy-home inputs from tasks that are not D12 blockers** (decided while writing this bead). The `status_cached_under_5_ms_with_m3_blocks` home uses B2's BugGrabber builder and measures A2's triage blocks and history projection, D11's backups block, B7's errors block and E4's widget block; A2, B2, B7, D11 and E4 are not upstream of D12. If any has not landed when this task closes, the test covers the blocks that exist, and **G3's perf run, which follows every leaf, is the binding measurement for checkpoint criterion 10**. Say so in the close comment.
- **Risks** (milestone risk table, §12.1):
  - *#7, restore breaks the engine's crash guarantees* (L–M likelihood, H impact): mitigated by per-shape matrices in their own tasks; D12 adds the cross-feature scenes and the full sweep so a moved failpoint is caught.
  - *#23, the recovery protocol has a gap only a crash during recovery reveals* (L–M, H): D14's per-transition crash injection; D12's played-on undo-of-restore and multi-target recovery scenes extend it across shapes.
  - *#18, a pre-M3 binary mutates state M3 wrote* (L–M, M–H): M3 cannot change existing binaries; the characterization documents exactly what af10e34 does, and README Limitations says not to run a pre-M3 build against state M3 wrote.
  - *#15, `status --cached` regresses past 5 ms* (M, M): the heavy-home perf test with p95 and cold start.
  - *#9, backups fill the disk*: not measured here, but the concurrency scenes prove the scheduling lock prevents duplicate automatic backups.
- **Collision hot spots** (coordinate through claim comments): `tests/engine_crash.rs` is touched by D3, D5, D6, D7, D14 and D12: each task adds its own shape and matrix, and D12 adds cross-feature scenes and the sweep only; rebase before each gate run. `README.md`: edit only the crash-testing counts and the Limitations quote; G1 reconciles.
- **Schedule.** D12 is **near-critical (slack 1)**. In the six-lane schedule it runs in lane 6 at t=13–15, after D13; it gates G1 and G3 on both critical paths. Start the 500 MB fixture build and the af10e34 worktree build early.
- **Delivery.** Slice `slice-4` (S4, "Portability and close"). S4's exit demo: export → import → restore byte-identical; integration scenes; the af10e34 characterization; perf; gate from a clean checkout; README. This task supplies the integration scenes, the characterization and the perf numbers; when S4's last task closes, its demo is recorded as a comment on the milestone epic in the `[x] … : evidence` style.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- D3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.3` (Automatic backups: two triggers, qualifying checkpoints, the space guard): `engine.autobackup`, `backup create --auto` and the per-target scheduling lock, for the capture-racing-restore scene, the two-`--auto` concurrency test and the perf lock-hold baseline.
- D7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.7` (Partial restore, `backup restore --addon`): the partial-restore shapes (`Op::RestoreAddon`, `Op::UndoRestoreAddon`) for the full sweep and the characterization's partial scenes.
- D8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.8` (The `backup restore` command): the end-to-end `backup restore` command (with D5's transaction, D6's undo and D14's preservation behind it), used by the cross-feature scenes, the restore lock-hold perf test and the characterization's whole-restore scenes.
- D10 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.10` (`backup import`): the import path that completes the export → import → restore chain, and (through D9) the paused-export reader for the prune-busy concurrency test.
- D13 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.13` (`backup verify` and integrity states): `backup verify` for the verify-racing-prune scene and the `backup_create_verify_500_mb` timing.

**Unblocks:**
- G1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1` (README final pass): the failpoint counts, the characterization's observed behaviour for Limitations, and the recorded perf numbers.
- G3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3` (The M3 checkpoint): the crash, concurrency and perf evidence for checkpoint criteria 8, 9, 10 and 14, and the characterization G3 reruns.

Through D8, D12 also depends on D5, D6, D14, A3 and A4; through D3 on D2 and D4; through D10 on D9. Those are inherited relations, not list entries.

Parent: the D epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4`. Delivery slice: `slice-4`.
acceptance_criteria: Every cross-feature scene in tests/engine_crash.rs passes: the played-on undo-of-restore leaves the pre-undo tree live and the played tree as a recovered backup, also with a crash inside that preservation resuming with the same id; an automatic backup create --auto racing a restore paused at engine.restore.staged (and with engine.autobackup aborted) takes the scheduling lock and copies the live pre-restore tree or skips, leaves the restore's reservation and journal unaffected, never deadlocks and never lists a half-made backup; recovery of several targets with one deferred (client running) and one preserving recovers the other and leaves the deferred one pending; the full sweep arms each of the 34 FAILPOINTS once in each M3 shape (D5, D6, D7, D14) and every scene meets its own shape's oracle, with off-path failpoints letting scenes succeed; every concurrency test in tests/engine_concurrency.rs passes (install completes during a paused restore; a paused backup copy blocks nothing; two backup create --auto on one target make one backup and the second reports in_progress; prune racing a paused export and a paused restore reports both busy; verify racing prune gives busy or not_found, never a crash or a partial delete); the release perf tests meet their budgets on the development machine with timings and p95 recorded in the close comment (backup_create_500_mb_under_1_s, median of 5 under 1 s, 20,000 files reported; backup_create_verify_500_mb reported; restore_lock_hold_under_50_ms; status_cached_under_5_ms_with_m3_blocks, median of 21 under 5 ms with p95 and cold start reported); both README failpoint mentions say 34 and the crash-testing paragraph names the new shapes (decided while writing this bead); the af10e34 characterization ran, its per-scene table is in the close comment, an interrupted M3 restore journal was never deleted by M2, the M3 binary recovered or reported it, and README Limitations quotes the observed behaviour including the blind SavedVariables undo; if af10e34 no longer builds with the installed toolchain, that pre-accepted SKIP is recorded with the build error in the close comment, README Limitations keeps A3's general warning, and D12 closes

comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** M3 changes the most sensitive code in omaddons: it lets the engine exchange a player's whole `WTF/`, roll it back after a crash, and preserve anything a crash displaced. Each of those protocols is crash-tested in its own task. What no single task can test is how they behave together (an automatic capture during a restore, an undo of a restore that the game played on before it crashed, two clients recovering at once), whether every failpoint still sits where its matrix expects after later tasks moved code, whether the budgets the vision promises (500 MB in under 1 s, a 50 ms lock hold, a 5 ms `status --cached`) hold on a release build, and what the M2 binary still installed on the machine would do to state M3 wrote. This bead produces that evidence for checkpoint criteria 8, 9, 10 and 14, and the honest README Limitations text that M3 promises instead of a downgrade barrier it cannot build. It is the proof behind G-M3-6, "no new risk to the engine's guarantees".

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D45: persisted formats fail closed; M2 is characterized, not guarded.** The review asked for a downgrade barrier "in a format older binaries already honour"; checking af10e34 showed none exists, because `store::save`'s refusal fires after the swap and after undo's SavedVariables restore. So M3 makes itself and every later binary refuse up front (A3), and D12 records exactly what af10e34 refuses and does. Rejected: bumping the record version as an M2 barrier (M2 would still write folders and SavedVariables first and leave a stuck journal); making M3 journal lines undecodable to M2 on purpose (M2 would treat the journal as `Unprepared` and prune it); a marker file M2 ignores.
- **M3-D24: one journaled exchange, rollback by durable phase, waits while running, ambiguous identities, preservation through a resumable intent.** D12's oracles are these rules restated: `WTF/` wholly old or new by `tree_hash`, direction from the durable phase, nothing moved while the client runs, a `recovered` backup with the same id after a crash inside preservation. Rejected in the decision: "the game's writes win" (inferring a change's author from an inode mismatch) and a fresh backup id per recovery attempt (it cannot be resumed); review round 2 had already dropped roll-forward recovery for restores (it needed planned steps recorded in the journal, and the dead-snapshot sweep would have deleted its snapshots).
- **M3-D27 / M3-D28:** partial restores land in undo's SavedVariables layout, and undo and restores conflict where they would overwrite each other; the sweep and the characterization's partial scenes cover them.
- **M3-D31 / M3-D48:** automatic captures are serialized per target by `DirLock::try_exclusive` on `<meta>/backups/`; readers hold shared reservations; prune skips busy backups; backup directory locks are taken before the global lock and never waited on while holding it. The concurrency scenes prove these, including no deadlock.
- **M3-D23 / M3-D25:** the 500 MB budget is set at a realistic 5,000 files (SavedVariables trees hold few, large files), and stamp digests keep whole-tree renames from hashing under the lock, which is what makes a 50 ms restore lock hold possible.
- **M3-D37:** `status --cached` reads projections; the heavy home (200 backups on one target, 16 accounts, a 20 MB interleaved history) is the proof.
- **M3-D47:** `--verify` costs about 0.5–1 s per 500 MB, so its timing is reported without a budget.

**Review-round changes folded in.** Round 3 changed this task's job. Revision 22 (protocol tests in their tasks) moved every shape's own crash matrix into the task that creates the shape (common rule 14), so D12 integrates and sweeps instead of discovering. Revision 21 (persisted-format compatibility) added the af10e34 characterization in place of a claimed barrier. Revision 1 (restore recovery as a durable protocol) added the played-on undo-of-restore and multi-target recovery scenes. Revision 23 (storage pressure; scheduling lock; reader reservations) added the busy and two-`--auto` concurrency scenes. Revision 15 (bounded cached status) made the perf home heavy and added p95 and cold-start reporting. Round 1 set the 500 MB budget at a realistic file count and had D1 measure the primitive early instead of finding out here.

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`:
- `FAILPOINTS` lists 27 engine failpoints (`src/engine/tx.rs:67-95`), each armed as an `abort` in a child process by `tests/engine_crash.rs`; README says "27" in two places (the crash-testing paragraph at line 1427 and the test table at line 1919).
- Test homes are temp dirs (`tests/common/env.rs:21`), so the btrfs-dependent perf test builds under `target/`, which is on btrfs on the development machine; `tests/common/checkpoint.rs` prints `SKIP` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names the test.
- The lock-hold helper `common::engine::lock_held_ms` and the 50 ms tests exist (`tests/perf.rs:412-503`); `bench_home` is the cached-home pattern (`tests/perf.rs:119`).
- M2 journal and history readers: `Prepared.schema_version` never compared (`journal.rs:82`, `:38`); undecodable lines counted and skipped (`:363-366`); an `Unprepared` journal pruned with its snapshots (`:737`, `:767-776`, `:781-794`); history skips unreadable lines and undo plans over the rest (`src/state/history.rs:318-330`, `src/app/undo.rs:287-290`, `src/engine/undo.rs:162`, `:271`, `:700`); the SavedVariables undo restores every differing file (`src/engine/undo.rs:1339-1383`); `store::save`'s refusal fires late (`src/state/store.rs:230-243`, `src/engine/tx.rs:904-913`, `src/engine/undo.rs:343-357`).
- M2 recovery writes as `Writer::Mutating` (`journal.rs:731`), and `Scope::Wtf` admits only `BackupRestore` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:118`), so M2 is refused at its first `WTF/` rename when it meets an M3 restore journal.
- The development machine's real `WTF/` trees are tiny (232–596 KB, 31–104 files), so the 500 MB budget must be measured on a synthetic tree.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A cross-feature gap that no per-task matrix sees (risks 7 and 23): the three cross-feature scenes and the full 34-failpoint sweep.
- A failpoint moved by a later task, silently testing nothing: the sweep reuses each shape's oracle, and the off-path rule makes an unreached failpoint visible as a success that must be explained.
- A pre-M3 binary mutating M3 state (risk 18): characterized and documented; the assertions pin the one property that must hold (M2 never deletes an interrupted M3 restore journal).
- Perf numbers that depend on the machine: release build, cached fixtures under `target/`, medians with p95 and cold start recorded; G3 reruns them.
- Heavy-home inputs from non-blocking tasks (A2, B2, B7, D11, E4) may land after D12: G3's perf run is the binding measurement, stated in the close comment.

**Confidence.** Medium-high: the scenes reuse oracles and harnesses that already exist, but the restore protocol they exercise is new code in the most sensitive place (the plan's one "medium" area), and this task is where a cross-feature defect would surface.

title: `backup verify` and integrity states
description:
## Background

A backup that only had its metadata checked must never be presented as intact (M3-D47). Same-size corruption passes a size check, and a hash computed at export time proves only what was on disk at export time, not what was captured. Before the third review, the plan's `restorable: true` meant only "paths, kinds and sizes match the manifest", and export hashed whatever bytes were there; neither established that the bytes were the ones captured. A label that overstates evidence is worse than no label.

So every backup carries an explicit `integrity` (added to the model by D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`):
- **`metadata_only`**: paths, kinds and sizes were checked against the manifest. **Same-size corruption is not detected**, and output never implies otherwise.
- **`verified`**: every file was hashed against manifest hashes that exist. `baseline` records when those hashes were established:
  - `capture`: `backup create --verify` hashed the staged copy (D2, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.2`);
  - `import`: `backup import` checked every hash (D10, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.10`);
  - `later`: the first `backup verify` of a backup that had no hashes. A `later` baseline proves the content has not changed **since then**, not that it equals what was captured, and the output says exactly that.
- **`damaged`**: a check failed. `backup list` shows why, and `backup restore` refuses with `state_corrupt`.

This task adds the command that establishes or checks that evidence: `omaddons backup verify <ID>… [-t T]`, and it says which of the two it did. Automatic captures do not hash (it would break the 1 s budget for 500 MB; hashing costs about 0.5–1 s per 500 MB on the development machine), so `verify` is how a user turns a cheap reflinked checkpoint into one with content evidence.

It serves **G-M3-4 (settings survive)**: "every backup says honestly what it proves: … content-verified or metadata-only", and **checkpoint criterion 8**: "`backup verify` detects same-size corruption in a backup whose hashes were recorded at capture or import, and says so when it can only set a first baseline."

Decisions that shape it (full text in the milestone epic's decision-log comments):
- **M3-D47**: integrity is explicit; `backup verify` hashes under a reader reservation, compares or records a `later` baseline, updates `integrity`, `verified_at` and the manifest atomically, rings the doorbell, appends no history line, runs without the global lock, and reports per backup (a damaged backup makes the run `partial` with exit 0). `--dry-run` hashes and reports without recording.
- **M3-D48**: reader reservations: a verify holds a shared `flock` on the backup's own directory (`DirLock::shared`), re-checks that the path still names the same inode, and a concurrent prune skips the backup as `busy`.
- **M3-D23**: the manifest `[{path, kind, size, mode, mtime_ns, link?, sha256?}]` carries `sha256` only when content was hashed at capture (`--verify`), at import, or by `backup verify`; it is local only (it contains account names).
- **M3-D21**: no output names an account, realm or character; a mismatch message's path goes through the redactor.
- **M3-D40**: long operations report `Phase::Copy` progress with a fixed label, never a path; verify uses the label `"verifying"`.
- **M3-D4**: `backup verify` rings the doorbell when it recorded a result (it can change what `backup list` and the widget show).

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/backup/verify.rs` (new)

```rust
pub enum VerifyOutcome { Verified { against: Baseline }, BaselineRecorded, Mismatch { files: u64, first: String /* redacted */ }, Structure(TreeCheck) }
pub fn verify(paths, scopes, client, b: &BackupRef, record: bool, progress: &ProgressSink) -> Result<VerifyOutcome>
```

The steps, in order:
1. **Reservation.** Take `DirLock::shared(<meta>/backups/<id>)` and check `same_dir` (D1's `fsx::lock::DirLock`: a `flock` on an `O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY` fd, released on drop and by the kernel on process death; `same_dir(&self, path)` compares the fd's `fstat` with the path's `stat`). A backup moved or deleted under the reader is `not_found`. The reservation is held until the result is recorded (or reported, for a dry run). Backup directory locks are taken **before** the global lock and never waited on while holding it (M3-D48 lock order); this command takes no global lock at all.
2. **Structure.** `check_structure` (D1: compares the manifest with the tree's entry set, kinds and sizes; no hashing). A structural difference sets `integrity: damaged` and stops (`Structure(TreeCheck)`).
3. **Hash** every regular file with D2's hashing helper (the one `backup create --verify` uses), reporting `Phase::Copy` progress (`ProgressSink::event(Phase::Copy, total, "verifying")`; the message is a fixed label, never a path, M3-D40).
4. **With manifest hashes:** compare them. Any difference sets `damaged` (`Mismatch { files, first }`, where `first` is the first differing path passed through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor::rel`, A5 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`). Otherwise the backup is `verified`, **keeping its existing `baseline`** (`capture` or `import` or `later`), with a new `verified_at`.
5. **Without manifest hashes:** record them, set `verified` with `baseline: later`, and say: "no hashes existed; recorded a baseline (this cannot prove the capture was intact)" (`BaselineRecorded`).
6. **Recording** (`record == true`, the non-dry-run case) writes through fsx (`Writer::Backup`, `Scope::ClientMeta`, which already admits `Backup`), each file atomically, **manifest first, then `backup.json`**.
   - `backup.json`'s `integrity` is the commit point. A crash between the two writes leaves new hashes in the manifest with the old `integrity`; the next verify simply compares against those hashes.
   - Then record the change in the inventory projection (D1's `inventory::record`; since D2, every projection write that changed it rings the doorbell) and ring the doorbell (A1's `doorbell::ring`, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.1`, reached through D2).
   - A `damaged` result is recorded the same way: `integrity: damaged` in `backup.json` (manifest hashes unchanged).

### 2. The command, `backup verify <ID>… [-t T]`

- `BackupAction::Verify` joins the `backup` clap command (D1 created `BackupAction::{List, …}`; DEC-1: this task adds its own variant). Ids are resolved with D1's `backup::resolve(client, prefix)`: a prefix of 8 or more characters; `not_found` lists the newest 3 ids as alternatives (argv `backup list -t <id>`); `ref_ambiguous` gives one alternative per candidate.
- Per backup, a result as in the contract (milestone epic comment "Contract additions, part 1", §7.4):

  ```json
  {"data":{"dry_run":false,"targets":[{"target":{…},"backups":[{"id":"01M6K…","integrity":"verified","baseline":"later",
    "files":410,"checked":410,"mismatched":0,"note":"no hashes existed; recorded a baseline (this cannot prove the capture was intact)"}]}]}}
  ```

- A **damaged** backup makes the run `partial: true`, still **exit 0**, because the verification itself succeeded.
- **`--dry-run`** hashes and compares but records nothing (`backup.json` and manifest hashes unchanged). It still establishes no baseline, and says so.
- **No history line** (a check, not a change of settings). **No global lock.**
- **Registry and docs:**
  - `COMMANDS` row `backup verify` (group Change, `mutates: true`; it records integrity);
  - help: M3-D39 needs no top-level change (`backup` already sits in the Change group after `undo`); the `backup` subcommand help lists `verify`; `after_long_help` examples;
  - contract matrix rows: one success and one failure (`not_found` for an unknown id), with snapshots;
  - README: `### backup verify`, plus the integrity vocabulary in `### backup list`;
  - once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js`: `backup verify`, `mutates: true`, `destructive: false`, `binds: false` (verify is CLI only in M3; the widget offers no verify action).

### 3. `backup list` shows integrity with its baseline

- Human output shows `verified (capture)`, `verified (import)`, `verified (later)`, or nothing for `metadata_only`, and `damaged` in the warning color.
- It **never prints "verified" without its baseline.**
- JSON already carries `integrity`, `verified_at` and `baseline` from D1; `restorable: false` for a `damaged` backup (D1: "structurally restorable and not damaged").

### Contract additions (DEC-4)

- Command path `backup verify`; its data shape above (`targets[].backups[]` with `id`, `integrity`, `baseline`, `files`, `checked`, `mismatched`, `note`).
- No new error codes. Reused: `not_found` (unknown id; backup moved or pruned under the reader), `ref_ambiguous` (prefix matches two), `state_corrupt` (a backup whose `backup.json` or manifest is unreadable).
- No new constants.

### Files

New `src/backup/verify.rs`; `src/app/backup.rs` (the `Verify` subcommand and its outcome); `src/app/mod.rs` (`COMMANDS` row); `src/backup/mod.rs` (list rendering of integrity, if not already there from D1); new `tests/backup_verify.rs`; `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and snapshots; README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `--verify` backup with one byte flipped in a file (same size): `backup verify` reports `Mismatch`, the backup becomes `damaged`, the run is `partial: true` with exit 0, and `backup list` shows it `damaged` and `restorable: false`. `backup restore` of it refuses with `state_corrupt` (asserted here once D8 has landed; D8's own acceptance also covers the refusal of a damaged backup).
- A backup without hashes: the first verify records a `later` baseline, with the wording "no hashes existed; recorded a baseline (this cannot prove the capture was intact)". A byte flip after that is caught by the second verify.
- An imported backup verifies against its import hashes and keeps `baseline: import`.
- `--dry-run` writes nothing: `backup.json` and the manifest hashes are unchanged, and no baseline is established (the output says so).
- A concurrent `backup prune <id>` during a verify reports the backup `busy`, and the verify completes.
- No path in a mismatch message contains `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm` or `FakeChar`; no output on any channel does (`assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr with `--progress json`).
- `backup list` prints `verified (<baseline>)` only for `integrity: verified`, nothing for `metadata_only`, and `damaged` when damaged.
- No history line is appended; no global lock is taken; the doorbell rings after a recorded result and not after a dry run.
- A crash between the manifest write and the `backup.json` write leaves a backup that the next verify compares against the new hashes (no false `damaged`).
- Contract rows (success and `not_found`) are snapshotted; README documents `backup verify` and the integrity vocabulary.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** (`src/backup/verify.rs`): outcome selection over the table {hashes present / absent} × {match / mismatch / structure difference} × {record / dry run}, including "verified keeps its existing baseline".
- **E2E, `tests/backup_verify.rs`** (new), with D1's `tests/common/wtf.rs` (`FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar`) and `tests/common/backups.rs`:
  - create with `--verify`, flip one byte in place (same size), verify → `Mismatch`, `damaged`, `partial: true`, exit 0;
  - create without `--verify`, verify → `BaselineRecorded` with the exact note; flip a byte; verify → `Mismatch`;
  - an imported backup: produced through `backup import` once D10 has landed, otherwise seeded with `seed_backup` as kind `imported` with manifest hashes and `baseline: import`; verify → `verified`, `baseline: import`;
  - `--dry-run` on a hashless backup: hashes on disk byte-identical before and after;
  - **busy:** pause the verify while it holds its reservation (for example `fsx.write_atomic.before=pause` at its first record write, through `tests/common/pause.rs`), then run `backup prune <id>` from another process → `busy`; resume → verify completes. If D4 has not landed when this task is implemented, assert instead that `backup list` reports `busy: true` for that backup during the pause; D12's concurrency scene covers prune against verify end to end;
  - **crash between the two writes:** abort at the `backup.json` write (`fsx.write_atomic.before=abort@2`, or the equivalent hit count), then verify again → compares against the recorded hashes, result `verified`;
  - doorbell: rings after a recorded result, untouched after `--dry-run`;
  - privacy: `assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr with `--progress json`.
- **Contract**: success and `not_found` rows in `tests/contract/matrix.rs`, snapshots.
- **Perf** (informational, owned by D12): `backup_create_verify_500_mb` reports hashing time without a budget.

## Considerations

- **Cost.** Hashing 500 MB takes about 0.5–1 s on the development machine. That is fine for an explicit command, which is why automatic captures do not hash (M3-D47) and `--verify` is opt-in on `create`.
- **Commit point.** Writing the manifest first and `backup.json` second makes `integrity` the commit point; never reverse the order.
- **What "verified (later)" means.** It proves the content has not changed since the baseline, not that the capture was intact. Every surface (JSON `note`, human output, README) says so. Never upgrade a `later` baseline to `capture`.
- **Dependencies not on this task's blocker list** (decided while writing this bead). `backup restore` (D8), `backup import` (D10) and `backup prune` (D4) are not upstream of D13. The acceptance cases that use them run once they exist; until then the tests use seeded backups and the `busy` listing probe, as described in the Test Plan, and D12 (which follows D4, D8, D10 and D13) integrates them.
- **Open details with a recommended default** (not specified by the plan; record with a `decided:` comment when implementing): an unknown id among several named ids is reported per backup (`not_found` for that id, `partial: true`), and the command fails with `not_found` only when every named id is unknown, mirroring `backup create`'s per-target semantics.
- **Collision hot spots** (coordinate through claim comments):
  - `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs` and the help tests are touched by every command task; add only the `Verify` variant and its row;
  - `src/app/backup.rs` is shared by D1, D2, D4, D8, D9, D10 and D13; keep the subcommand in its own function;
  - `README.md`: edit only the `backup` sections; G1 reconciles.
- **Delivery.** Slice `slice-2` (S2, "Capture and diagnose"); its exit demo includes "`backup verify`" (alongside `errors` on every client, keyless BugGrabber, automatic checkpoints, and the Issues view). In the six-lane schedule D13 runs in lane 6 at t=11–13 and has about 7 units of slack ("verification 7").

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- D2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.2` (`backup create`): the shared hashing helper and the `--verify` capture baseline this task builds on, manifests written with `sha256`, the inventory writes that ring the doorbell, and (through D2) D1's model, `resolve`, `check_structure`, `DirLock` and A5's redactor.

**Unblocks:**
- D12 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12` (Integration crash matrices, concurrency and performance checkpoints): the verify-vs-prune concurrency scene and the `backup_create_verify_500_mb` timing.
- G1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1` (README final pass): `### backup verify` and the integrity vocabulary in `### backup list`.

Parent: the D epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4`. Delivery slice: `slice-2`.
acceptance_criteria: A --verify backup with one byte flipped in a file (same size): backup verify reports Mismatch, the backup becomes damaged, the run is partial: true with exit 0, backup list shows it damaged and restorable: false, and backup restore of it refuses with state_corrupt (asserted here once D8 has landed; D8's acceptance also covers it); a backup without hashes: the first verify records a later baseline with the note "no hashes existed; recorded a baseline (this cannot prove the capture was intact)", and a byte flip after that is caught by the second verify; an imported backup verifies against its import hashes and keeps baseline: import; --dry-run writes nothing (backup.json and manifest hashes unchanged) and establishes no baseline, saying so; a concurrent backup prune <id> during a verify reports the backup busy and the verify completes; no path in a mismatch message, and no output on any channel, contains FAKEACCT, FakeRealm or FakeChar (assert_private_all over stdout and stderr with --progress json); backup list prints verified (<baseline>) only for integrity: verified, nothing for metadata_only, and damaged when damaged; no history line is appended, no global lock is taken, and the doorbell rings after a recorded result but not after a dry run; a crash between the manifest write and the backup.json write leaves a backup the next verify compares against the new hashes with no false damaged; contract rows (success and not_found) are snapshotted and README documents backup verify and the integrity vocabulary

comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** A reflinked backup is cheap because nothing is hashed, which also means nothing proves its bytes are the ones captured: same-size corruption passes every size check. Before this bead a backup could only say "metadata checked". After it, `omaddons backup verify <id>` either checks the content against hashes recorded at capture or import, or records a first baseline and says plainly that a first baseline cannot prove the capture was intact. Every surface (`backup list`, restore, export, the widget's Backups rows) then shows exactly what has been established, and a damaged backup is refused by restore instead of silently restoring corrupt settings. This keeps the M3 promise "every backup says honestly what it proves", and it is what makes the "settings survive" goal trustworthy rather than merely likely.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D47: integrity is explicit; `backup verify`.** `integrity` is `metadata_only | verified | damaged`, with `baseline` `capture | import | later` and `verified_at`; `restorable` stays (DEC-4) and means "structurally restorable and not damaged"; listing never walks or hashes trees. Verify compares when hashes exist and records a `later` baseline otherwise, updates the manifest and `backup.json` atomically, rings the doorbell, appends no history line, runs without the global lock, and reports per backup (damaged → `partial`, exit 0). Why: the first draft's `restorable: true` meant only "paths, kinds and sizes match", and export hashed whatever was there at export time; a label that overstates evidence is worse than none. Rejected: hashing every automatic capture (it breaks the 1 s budget for large trees, on the common path); claiming "verified" from a first verification.
- **M3-D48: reader reservations.** Verify holds `DirLock::shared` on the backup's directory and re-checks `same_dir`; prune and retention skip a held backup as `busy`; the kernel frees the lock if the reader dies; no lock files. Lock order: backup directory locks before the global lock, never waited on while holding it. Rejected: lock files under `<cache>` (a cache wipe would silently break exclusion).
- **M3-D23: the manifest carries `sha256` only when content was hashed** (`--verify`, import, or verify), and it is local only, because its paths contain account names.
- **M3-D21: privacy on every channel.** The first mismatching path is redacted (`WtfPathRedactor::rel`); progress labels are fixed text.
- **M3-D40: `Phase::Copy`** progress with the label `"verifying"`, never a path.
- **M3-D4: the doorbell** rings when verify recorded a result, because it changes what `backup list` and the widget show.
- **M3-D39 (context):** help layout needs no top-level change; `backup` already sits in the Change group.

**Review-round changes folded in.** Round 3, revision 5 (explicit verification; addon provenance) created this task: `integrity` with baselines, `backup verify`, `create --verify`, and restores and exports that check hashes when present. Revision 23 (storage pressure; reader reservations) gave verify its shared directory lock, so a concurrent prune reports `busy` instead of deleting a backup mid-hash.

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`:
- Nothing reads or writes `<meta>/backups/` today: `ClientPaths::backups()` has no callers (`src/state/paths.rs:410-413`); `Scope::ClientMeta` admits `Backup` and `BackupRestore` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:99-122`), so the record writes need no scope change.
- fsx writes are temp file plus rename (`src/fsx/sys.rs:132-160`), so each of the two record writes is atomic on its own; the order of the two is what makes `integrity` the commit point.
- `pause` failpoints and their test-side helper exist (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs` `parse_action`: `abort`, `error`, `panic`, `pause`, `sleep:<ms>`, with `@N`; `tests/common/pause.rs`), so the busy scene needs no new failpoint and the engine `FAILPOINTS` count (34 after M3) is unaffected.
- Hashing 500 MB costs about 0.5–1 s on the development machine (btrfs, `compress=zstd:3`).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A first baseline mistaken for proof of capture: the `later` baseline's wording is fixed and tested; human output always prints the baseline next to "verified".
- A crash between the two writes producing a false `damaged`: manifest first, `backup.json` second, and a crash test between them.
- A prune deleting a backup mid-verify: the shared reservation, tested with a paused verify.
- Acceptance cases that need D4, D8 or D10, which are not upstream of this task: seeded fixtures and the `busy` listing probe until they land; D12 integrates the end-to-end versions.

**Confidence.** High: a small, read-mostly command over D1's model and D2's hashing helper, with the evidence semantics fixed by M3-D47 and directly testable with byte flips.

- `backup::tree::hash_files(root, entries, progress) -> Result<Vec<Option<String>>, CloneError>` in `src/backup/tree.rs` hashes each regular file the manifest lists below `root` (lowercase hex SHA-256; `None` for dirs and symlinks). `backup create --verify` stores them as `ManifestEntry.sha256` with `integrity: verified`, `baseline: capture`, `verified_at`.
