comments.text:
**Handoff from A4 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`, closed): preview binding as landed.**

- `src/app/precondition.rs`: `Precondition::new(command, targets: Vec<(TargetKey, Option<u64>)>, selection: Value, observed: Value)`, `.token()` (`pc1:` + four 16-hex fields), `check(expected: Option<&str>, &actual, preview_argv) -> Result<()>`, `stale(command, &[Part], preview_argv)`, `preview_argv(&ctx.argv)` (the same command with `--dry-run` for `--if-match <token>`), `is_token`, and `BINDING_COMMANDS` (all five paths; your path is already in it, so `Context::new` lets `--if-match` through for it and checks the token's shape). `Option<u64>` generation `None` is the key-only form (`errors dismiss`).
- `ctx.if_match: Option<String>` is set only on a binding path with a well-formed token. Compute your `Precondition` from the plan you execute, before anything is staged or written, and call `check(ctx.if_match.as_deref(), &p, &preview_argv(&ctx.argv))`; under `--dry-run` put `p.token()` in `data.precondition` (and `null` on the real run when dry-run and real data share a struct). `--dry-run` with `--if-match` previews afresh (no check).
- Canonical JSON is explicit (sorted keys), but sort arrays whose order carries no meaning yourself and use integers only.
- Engine-run commands bind through `crate::engine::Binding` (`plan`, `undo`, `moved`) carried in `EngineCtx.binding` (`Engine::run_bound` / `undo_bound`): the engine asks it after planning (before staging) and refuses under the lock when the target's generation moved (`moved`), or, for undo, re-checks the plan made under the lock. A command outside the engine (`backup prune`, `errors dismiss`) re-checks its own selection under its lock the same way. A refusal is `plan_stale`, `PlanStaleSource::Apply` (not retryable), `details.changed` from `command`, `targets`, `selection`, `observed`.
- Add your scenarios to `tests/preconditions.rs` (state changed between preview and run: refusal, nothing changed).

title: `backup export`
description:
## Background

Every M3 backup lives under `<meta>/backups/`, on the same filesystem as the client's `WTF/`. That is what makes them cheap (reflinks) and what makes a restore atomic (one exchange), but it also means a disk failure takes the backups with the settings. The vision promises off-disk copies (vision §5.8). This task adds `omaddons backup export <ID> <FILE>`: a deterministic `tar` streamed through `zstd` straight into a hidden temporary file next to the destination and published without ever replacing an existing file. Together with D10's `backup import` (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.10`) it makes "survive a disk failure, or move to a new machine" a two-command story; with `omaddons export > addons.toml` plus `sync --locked` for the addons themselves, it is a full machine restore.

It serves **G-M3-4 (settings survive):** "an export survives a disk failure, and an import brings it back exactly", and checkpoint criterion 8 (`backup export` → `backup import` → `backup restore` reproduces a byte-identical `WTF/`, exact modes included; no output names an account, realm or character).

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`):
- **M3-D34:** export writes a new file and never replaces one; it streams with no intermediate copy; it gets a **runtime single-path write scope**; an existing `<file>` is the new error `file_exists`; stdout (`-`) is refused because binary data would break the one-envelope rule under `--json`.
- **M3-D36:** the `tar` (default features off) and `zstd` crates, added here, with `argc gate --all` (cargo deny).
- **M3-D47:** when the local manifest has hashes, every streamed file is checked against them, and the archive records where its hashes came from (`verified_against`).
- **M3-D48:** the export holds a reader reservation on its backup for the whole stream, so a concurrent prune reports it `busy` instead of deleting it mid-read.
- **M3-D21:** progress carries a fixed label, never a path; a mismatched path in an error goes through the redactor.
- **M3-D40:** long backup operations report the `copy` progress phase.

**Facts this task relies on** (as of `af10e34`):
- **There is no write scope for a user-chosen destination.** The scope rows (`src/fsx/scope.rs:66-94`) are all fixed roots under the XDG dirs, the home or a registered client dir; anything else is refused as "outside every write scope" (`scope.rs:333-337`). `export --write` writes only `<config>/addons.toml` (§2.3).
- fsx already writes from a streaming reader: `Content::Reader(&mut dyn Read)` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:62-65`, handled at `:150`).
- fsx already publishes with no clobber and fsyncs the parent in `clone_file` (`temp.persist_noclobber(to)`, `sys.rs:245`, then `fsync_dir`, `:247`; `fsync_dir` at `:277`). `MutateOpts { expect: Some(Expect::Absent) }` refuses an existing path (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:85`, `:542`).
- **But the `WriteFile` path does not publish with no clobber.** `Op::WriteFile` goes to `sys::write_atomic` (`mutate.rs:671`), which persists with `temp.persist(path)` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:161`), a rename that replaces whatever is there; it already fsyncs the directory afterwards under `Durability::Immediate` (`sys.rs:162-164`). `Expect::Absent` is only a check before the write (`mutate.rs:542`), so it cannot catch a destination another process creates mid-export. (Verified while reviewing this bead; the module map lists "`WriteFile` no-clobber persist from a streaming reader" under `src/fsx/mutate.rs`, `sys.rs` for D9.)
- The release binary is 11.1 MB; the M5 target is under 10 MB (§2.7).
- `deny.toml`'s license allow-list includes `MIT`, `Apache-2.0` and `BSD-3-Clause` (the C zstd library is BSD-licensed); `Cargo.toml` has `flate2`, `zip` and `tempfile`, and no `tar` or `zstd`.
- The error-code registry asserts its size (`ErrorCode::ALL.len()` and `EXPECTED.len()` both 39, `src/error.rs:765-766`).

## Technical Approach

### What the user sees

```text
$ omaddons backup export 01M6Q8PN <usb drive>/retail-wtf.tar.zst
exported backup 01M6Q… (retail, today 18:02) to <usb drive>/retail-wtf.tar.zst: 412 files, 15.2 MB → 1.9 MB
```

An interrupted export leaves nothing behind but its own hidden temporary file, which it removes. An existing destination is never overwritten (`file_exists`).

### 1. Crates

- `tar = { version = "<current>", default-features = false }` and `zstd = "<current>"` (default features; it compiles the C zstd library through `cc`, as `ring` already compiles C). These are the only crate additions in M3.
- `argc gate --all` must pass (cargo deny: licenses, bans). Both licenses are on the `deny.toml` list. `ruzstd`'s encoder is not mature, which is why `zstd` is chosen (M3-D36).
- **Measure the release binary** before and after, and record both sizes in the close comment (risk #12: 11.1 MB today, M5 target < 10 MB). M3-D36 says `zstd` with default features, while risk #12's mitigation says "`zstd` with minimal features": start with the defaults and trim the features if the measured growth is large, recording which was kept in the close comment (this reconciliation was decided while writing this bead).

### 2. `src/backup/export.rs` (new)

- **Reservation.** Take `DirLock::shared(<meta>/backups/<id>)` and check `same_dir` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`): after locking, a moved or deleted backup is `not_found`. Hold the lock until the file is published (M3-D48). The kernel releases it if the process dies.
- **One streaming write, straight to the destination.** `mutate(<file>, Op::WriteFile { content: Reader(producer), mode: Some(0o600) })` in a `Writer::Backup` untracked session, with `MutateOpts { expect: Some(Expect::Absent), … }`.
  - The reader is a small adapter (DEC-11) that runs the tar+zstd producer (**level 3**) on a scoped thread and hands bytes over a bounded channel. Memory stays flat for any backup size.
  - fsx writes into its hidden temporary sibling of `<file>`, which is on the destination's own filesystem.
  - It finishes the encoder, fsyncs the file, persists with no clobber (`tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist_noclobber` inside `fsx::sys`), then fsyncs the destination directory. **If `fsx::sys`'s reader-content `WriteFile` path lacks the directory fsync after a persist, this task adds it** (it exists for `clone_file`, `sys.rs:245-247`, and, at `af10e34`, in `write_atomic` under `Durability::Immediate`). **This task adds the no-clobber publish to the `WriteFile` path** (module map: "`WriteFile` no-clobber persist from a streaming reader", D9): when `expect` is `Absent`, `write_atomic` publishes with `persist_noclobber` instead of `persist` (`sys.rs:161`), and an `EEXIST` there maps to `file_exists`. Without it, the "destination created by another process mid-export" acceptance case would silently replace that file. The exact shape (a flag on `write_atomic` or a sibling function) is left to the implementer.
  - A producer error (a vanished file, a hash mismatch), a write error or disk-full drops the reader and fails the `mutate`. fsx removes **only** that operation's unpublished temporary sibling. The destination never appears half-written.
- **Nothing is written under `<cache>`.** An export needs no cache capacity and writes the compressed bytes once. (The first draft wrote to `<cache>/tmp` and then copied, which doubled the I/O.)
- **Entries, in this order:**
  1. `backup.json`, with `verified_against` (`capture | import | later`, or `computed_at_export` when the local manifest had no hashes; M3-D34) and **no export timestamp**, so exports stay deterministic;
  2. `addons.json`, when the backup has one;
  3. `WTF/…`, sorted, each entry with its **recorded source mode and mtime from the manifest** (copies have new mtimes and owner-writable dirs; the manifest is the truth), uid/gid 0, and no user or group names. Symlinks are kept as symlinks with their recorded `link` targets;
  4. `manifest.json` **last**, with the `sha256` of every regular file, computed while it streamed (M3-D34). Import stages everything first and verifies against it before anything leaves the stage.
- **Checked against recorded hashes.** When the local manifest has hashes (a `--verify` capture, an import, or a `backup verify` baseline; M3-D47), each streamed file's hash is compared with its recorded one. A mismatch aborts with `hash_mismatch` ("backup … is damaged; run omaddons backup verify", the spec's message; if D13's `backup verify` has not landed when this task does, keep "backup … is damaged" until it has, decided while writing this bead so that no message names a command that does not exist), the temporary file is removed, and the offending path goes through `WtfPathRedactor::rel` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`).
- **Progress:** `Phase::Copy` (M3-D40), label `"exporting"`, counting files. **Never a path** (M3-D21): every path below `WTF/Account/` names an account, a realm and a character.

### 3. Runtime scope (`src/fsx/scope.rs`)

- `ScopeTable::with_export_file(&mut self, file: &Path) -> Result<()>` canonicalizes the parent (it must exist; else `io`) and refuses:
  - a parent inside any client dir in the table;
  - inside a Wine prefix (an ancestor holding both `drive_c/` and `dosdevices/`);
  - inside `<config>`, `<state>` or `<cache>`.
- It admits only `Writer::Backup`, for exactly that path and fsx's temporary siblings of it.
- Scope tests cover each refusal, and that no other writer and no other path is admitted.
- **Vision comment required** (G2, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`): the scope table is vision territory. It keeps the single-writer and scope guarantees in the M2-D19 spirit (no general `--output`).

### 4. Errors

| Code | Exit | Retryable | When | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file_exists` (**new**, §7.6) | 4 | no | the destination exists, at the start or when another process created it mid-export (the no-clobber persist fails) | prose: "choose another file name, or delete that file yourself" |
| `scope_denied` | 4 | no | a destination inside a client dir, a Wine prefix, `<config>`, `<state>` or `<cache>` | prose, naming why |
| `usage` | 2 | no | `<FILE>` is `-` ("write the export to a file") | as usage errors do |
| `io` | | | the destination's parent does not exist | prose |
| `not_found` | | | unknown backup id, or the backup moved or was deleted under the reservation | D1's `backup list -t <id>` alternatives |
| `hash_mismatch` | | | a streamed file differs from its recorded hash; message "backup … is damaged; run omaddons backup verify" (see section 2 for before D13), path redacted | as D8 decides (`fix_argv` `omaddons backup verify <id> -t <target>` once D13 exists; see Considerations) |

`file_exists` joins `ErrorCode` as an additive macro row (exit 4, `Refused`, not retryable); the registry size asserts (`src/error.rs:765-766`) and the `EXPECTED` table move by one. (D5 adds `filesystem_unsupported`; together they take the registry from 39 to 41.)

### 5. The command, `backup export <ID> <FILE> [-t T]`

- `BackupAction::Export { id: String, file: PathBuf }` in `src/app/backup.rs`.
- `-t` resolves one target; with no `-t`, the target that owns the backup id (scan every target's `<meta>/backups/` with D1's `resolve`), as `backup restore` resolves it. Whichever of D8 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.8`) and this task lands second moves that owning-target scan into one shared function in `src/app/backup.rs`. (The spec gives only `[-t T]`; resolving without `-t` like `backup restore`, and the shared function, were decided while writing this bead.)
- `<FILE>` is a path; `-` is `usage`.
- **`--dry-run`** (every mutating subcommand takes it, §7.1): resolve the backup, take and release the reservation, run `with_export_file` and the existence check, and report what would be written (files, apparent bytes, `verified_against`), writing nothing. The spec is silent on export's dry run; this behaviour was decided while writing this bead.
- **No history line:** a read of a backup plus a file the user named, and the vision lists export as not a transaction. **The doorbell does not ring** (nothing `status --cached` reports changed).
- **Data** (§7.4):
  ```json
  {"data":{"backup":{"id":"01M6Q…","captured_at":"…","kind":"auto","…":"(the backup list entry)"},
    "file":"<usb drive>/retail-wtf.tar.zst","files":412,"bytes":15937536,"compressed_bytes":1988123,"sha256":"…",
    "verified_against":"capture"}}
  ```
  `file` is the destination path; `files` and `bytes` are the backup's file count and apparent bytes streamed; `compressed_bytes` is the archive's size; `sha256` is read here as the archive file's own digest, computed as it is written (the contract shows the key without defining it: confirm and document it in README when implementing); `verified_against` repeats the archive's `backup.json` value.
- **Human output** as shown above.
- **Registry touch points** (common rule 4): `COMMANDS` row `backup export` (Change, `mutates: true`: it writes a file); `command_name` and dispatch arms; contract rows (success, `file_exists`); once F1 has landed, `CLI_PATHS` `backup export` = `{mutates: true, destructive: false, binds: false}`. Export is CLI only in M3: the widget offers no export (a non-goal).
- **README:** `### backup export` (what the archive holds, determinism, no overwrite, the destination rules, that it is not a transaction), the Files note that an export writes only the destination and its hidden temporary sibling, and the "off-disk safety" workflow paired with `backup import`.

**Files:** `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `src/backup/export.rs` (new), `src/backup/mod.rs`, `src/fsx/scope.rs`, `src/fsx/sys.rs` and `src/fsx/mutate.rs` (the no-clobber `WriteFile` publish; the directory fsync after persist, if missing), `src/error.rs` (`file_exists`), `src/app/backup.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs`, `tests/backup_export.rs` (new), contract matrix rows and snapshots, README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The export of a fixture backup reproduces, when listed with `tar --zstd -tvf`, every file with its recorded mode, no owner names, uid/gid 0, sorted, with `backup.json` first and `manifest.json` last.
- `manifest.json` hashes match the files.
- An existing destination is refused with `file_exists` and left untouched.
- Destinations inside a client dir, a Wine prefix or `<state>` are refused (`scope_denied`); so are `<config>` and `<cache>` (scope unit tests); `-` is `usage`; a missing parent is `io`.
- Two exports of the same backup produce identical bytes (determinism).
- **No intermediate copy:** `<cache>` is unchanged after an export (a hash of the dir), and the destination filesystem sees the compressed bytes written once (a byte-counting test writer).
- **Failure cleanup:**
  - a producer failure (a backup file deleted mid-stream), a planted hash mismatch and a disk-full destination (a size-limited tmpfs in an `unshare -rm` sandbox, `SKIP` where unprivileged user namespaces are unavailable, a pre-accepted SKIP; plus `fsx.write_atomic.after=error` for a deterministic case) each leave no file at `<file>` and no temporary sibling;
  - a crash (`abort` failpoint) leaves at most the hidden temporary sibling, never `<file>`;
  - a destination created by another process mid-export makes the persist fail with `file_exists`, and that file is untouched.
- A concurrent `backup prune <id>` during the export reports the backup `busy`, and the export completes.
- A backup with recorded hashes exports with `verified_against` equal to its baseline; one without hashes exports with `computed_at_export`.
- No output on any channel (human, JSON, stderr progress, the mismatch error) names an account, realm or character (`assert_private_all`, `--progress json`).
- `argc gate --all` passes with the two crates; the release binary size before and after is in the close comment.
- The error registry counts `file_exists` (exit 4, not retryable); contract rows for success and `file_exists` are snapshotted.

## Test Plan

- **E2E** `tests/backup_export.rs` (new): listing with `tar --zstd -tvf`; manifest hashes; `file_exists` (before, and mid-export through a pause failpoint and a second process); refused destinations; determinism (byte-equal twice); the `<cache>` hash and the byte-counting writer; the four failure-cleanup cases (deleted file mid-stream, planted mismatch, disk-full in the sandbox with `SKIP`, `fsx.write_atomic.after=error`, `abort`); the busy prune from a second process; `assert_private_all` with `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` trees from `tests/common/wtf.rs`.
- **Unit** (`src/fsx/scope.rs`): each `with_export_file` refusal (client dir, Wine prefix with `drive_c/` and `dosdevices/`, `<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, missing parent), admission of exactly the path and its temp siblings, `Writer::Backup` only.
- **Unit** (`src/backup/export.rs`): entry order, header fields from the manifest, `verified_against` selection.
- **Unit** (`src/fsx/sys.rs`, `mutate.rs`): a `WriteFile` with `Expect::Absent` whose destination appears between the temp write and the publish (the `fsx.write_atomic.after` failpoint as a pause, then a planted file) fails, leaves the planted file untouched and removes the temp sibling; without `Expect::Absent`, today's replacing behaviour is unchanged.
- **Contract:** matrix rows and snapshots (success, `file_exists`).
- `argc gate --all` (cargo deny).

## Considerations

- **Binary size.** A `zstd` C build adds compile time and binary size. Measure the release binary before and after, and record it in the close comment (M5 target < 10 MB). This is risk #12 (likelihood H, impact L now): M5 owns the target; this task owns the measurement.
- **`hash_mismatch` retryability.** The registry default is retryable (`src/error.rs:186`), tuned for downloads. A damaged backup does not heal on retry. Follow D8's recorded choice (recommended: this instance not retryable, with the `backup verify` fix once D13 exists); whichever of D8, D9 and D13 lands first decides and records it, the others match.
- **Why no stdout.** `--json` promises one envelope on stdout; binary data there would break it. `<file>` must be a path.
- **Why a runtime scope, not `--output` everywhere.** A narrow single-path scope keeps the single-writer guarantee checkable (M2-D19's spirit). It requires an existing parent dir, so a typo cannot create directory trees.
- **Exports contain account names** inside the archive (paths under `WTF/Account/`), as any copy of `WTF/` must. Only output channels are covered by the privacy rule; the archive is the user's data, written mode 0600.
- **Not a transaction.** No history line, no undo: it creates a new file only, never touches the client, and the user can delete the file.
- **Collision hot spots:** `src/fsx/scope.rs` (D5, D9, E2: each adds a row or case with its own scope test); `src/fsx/sys.rs`, `mutate.rs`, `lock.rs` (D1 adds `ClonePolicy`, `StampDigest`, `DirLock`; D5 the exchange probe; D9 the directory fsync after persist and, per the module map, the no-clobber `WriteFile` persist); `src/error.rs` (additive rows plus count bumps; get the counts right); `src/cli.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs` and the help tests; `Cargo.toml` (D9 only: the only crate additions in M3).
- **Schedule.** Off the critical path, with about 7 units of slack ("export and import 7"). Suggested lane 6, formats, archives and integrity (D9 at t=5–7, after D2).
- **Delivery slice `slice-4`, "S4. Portability and close"** (D9, D10, D12, F7, G1, G2, G3). Exit demo: export → import → restore byte-identical; integration scenes; the af10e34 characterization; perf; the gate from a clean checkout; README. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 8 (export, import), 9 (integration), 10, 11, 12 and 14 (the characterization).

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- A5 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5` (The shared privacy redactor): `WtfPathRedactor::rel` for the path in a `hash_mismatch` or vanished-file error, and `assert_private_all` for the tests.
- D1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1` (The backup store, `backup list`, and the shared primitives): the backup model (`BackupRef`, `resolve`, `backup.json`, `manifest.json` with recorded modes and mtimes, `addons.json`), `DirLock::shared` and `same_dir` for the reader reservation, `Phase::Copy`, and the `backup` command tree.

**Unblocks:**
- D10 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.10` (`backup import`): the archive format import accepts exactly (entry order, `manifest.json` last with per-file `sha256`, recorded modes and links, `backup.json` with `verified_against`), the `tar` and `zstd` crates, and real exports to round-trip.
- G1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1` (README final pass): the `backup export` documentation to reconcile.

Parent: the D epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4`. Delivery slice: `slice-4`.

The hashes it checks come from D2's `--verify` (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.2`), D10's import and D13's `backup verify` (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.13`); export works without any of them (`computed_at_export`). The busy prune in its tests needs D4 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.4`); if D4 has not landed yet, that test lands with whichever of D4 and D9 comes second. None of these is a direct edge.
acceptance_criteria: The export of a fixture backup, listed with tar --zstd -tvf, reproduces every file with its recorded mode, no owner names, uid/gid 0, sorted, with backup.json first and manifest.json last; manifest.json hashes match the files; an existing destination is refused with file_exists and left untouched; destinations inside a client dir, a Wine prefix or <state> are refused with scope_denied (and <config>, <cache> in scope unit tests), - is a usage error and a missing parent is io; two exports of the same backup produce identical bytes; no intermediate copy: <cache> is unchanged after an export and the destination filesystem sees the compressed bytes written once (byte-counting test writer); a producer failure (a backup file deleted mid-stream), a planted hash mismatch and a disk-full destination (size-limited tmpfs in an unshare -rm sandbox, SKIP where unavailable, plus fsx.write_atomic.after=error) each leave no file at <file> and no temporary sibling, a crash (abort failpoint) leaves at most the hidden temporary sibling and never <file>, and a destination created by another process mid-export makes the persist fail with file_exists and leaves that file untouched; a concurrent backup prune <id> during the export reports the backup busy and the export completes; a backup with recorded hashes exports with verified_against equal to its baseline and one without exports with computed_at_export; no output on any channel (human, JSON, stderr progress, the mismatch error) names an account, realm or character (assert_private_all with --progress json); argc gate --all passes with the tar and zstd crates and the release binary size before and after is recorded in the close comment; the error registry counts file_exists (exit 4, not retryable) and contract rows for success and file_exists are snapshotted

comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** Backups under `<meta>/backups/` are cheap and atomic to restore precisely because they share the client's filesystem, which also means one disk failure loses both the settings and their backups. `omaddons backup export <id> <file>` is the off-disk half of the promise: a deterministic, compressed, self-verifying archive written once, straight to where the user wants it, never overwriting anything, and failing without leaving a half-written file. With D10's import it turns "new machine" or "dead disk" into two commands, and with `omaddons export` plus `sync --locked` for the addons it is a full machine restore. It keeps the single-writer guarantee intact by adding the narrowest possible write scope: exactly one path the user named.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D34: export writes a new file and never replaces one, streaming with no intermediate copy.** A producer thread feeds tar+zstd (level 3) through a bounded channel into fsx's reader-content `WriteFile`, which writes the destination's hidden temporary sibling, fsyncs, publishes with no clobber and fsyncs the directory. `manifest.json` goes last with a SHA-256 per file computed while streaming. Rejected: staging the archive in `<cache>` and copying it (doubled I/O and a cache-capacity requirement, the first draft); stdout output (it would break the one-envelope `--json` rule); a general `--output` scope (M2-D19: keep scopes narrow).
- **M3-D36: `tar` (default features off) and `zstd`.** The vision named them, they are the standard choices, and `ruzstd`'s encoder is not mature. Both licenses are on the deny list.
- **M3-D47: integrity is explicit.** Export compares each streamed file with the manifest's hashes when they exist and records their provenance as `verified_against` (`capture`, `import`, `later`, or `computed_at_export`), so an archive never implies more than was established. Rejected: hashing whatever bytes are present at export and calling them verified.
- **M3-D48: a reader reservation for the whole stream,** so a concurrent prune reports the backup `busy` rather than deleting it under the reader. Rejected: lock files under `<cache>` (a cache wipe would silently break exclusion).
- **M3-D21 and M3-D40:** progress uses `Phase::Copy` with the fixed label `"exporting"`, never a path; error paths go through the redactor.

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 3, revision 6: **direct streaming to the destination's temporary sibling** replaced the first draft's `<cache>/tmp` archive plus copy, so the compressed bytes are written once and an export needs no cache space.
- Round 3, revision 5: hashes are checked against the local manifest when present, and `verified_against` records where they came from.
- Round 3, revision 23: the reader reservation.

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`: No write scope exists for a user-chosen path: the rows are fixed roots (`src/fsx/scope.rs:66-94`), and anything else is "outside every write scope" (`scope.rs:333-337`), §2.3. fsx already supports `Content::Reader` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:62-65`, `:150`), already publishes with `persist_noclobber` and fsyncs the parent in `clone_file` (`sys.rs:245-247`, `fsync_dir` at `:277`), and already refuses an existing path with `Expect::Absent` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:85`, `:542`). That check runs only before the write, and `WriteFile`'s `write_atomic` publishes with a replacing `temp.persist(path)` (`sys.rs:161`, directory fsync after it at `:162-164`), so the no-clobber `WriteFile` publish the module map assigns to D9 is new fsx code (verified while reviewing this bead). The release binary is 11.1 MB against M5's under-10 MB target (§2.7). The error registry asserts 39 codes (`src/error.rs:765-766`). `deny.toml` allows MIT, Apache-2.0 and BSD-3-Clause; `Cargo.toml` has no `tar` or `zstd` yet.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk #12, binary size grows past M5's target (likelihood H, impact L now): measured before and after in this task, `zstd` with minimal features, recorded in the close comment; M5 owns the target.
- A half-written archive on failure: fsx removes only its own unpublished temporary sibling, and a crash leaves at most that hidden sibling; tested with a vanished file, a hash mismatch, a size-limited tmpfs and an abort failpoint.
- Writing somewhere dangerous (inside a client dir, a Wine prefix, omaddons' own dirs): the runtime scope refuses each, with unit tests, and admits only `Writer::Backup` for exactly that path.
- Personal data: the archive holds the user's own `WTF/` (mode 0600, by design); every output channel stays name-free.

**Confidence.** High. It composes proven pieces (fsx's reader-content write and directory fsync, `clone_file`'s no-clobber persist pattern, D1's model and reservation) with two standard crates, and every failure path is deterministic to test; the one new fsx primitive, a no-clobber `WriteFile` publish, is small and directly tested; the binary-size cost is measured, not guessed.

title: Epic: M3 widget packaging (omaddons omarchy)
description:
## Background

Area E of M3 (milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`): packaging and controlling the widget from the CLI.

The widget ships inside the omaddons binary and is rendered at install time. The installer stamps three things into the plugin's `Build.js` (M3-D7):
- the absolute path of the binary that installed it, so the widget always runs the binary it was built for and CLI and widget never skew (vision D10);
- the data context (`HOME` plus the four XDG roots), so every omaddons process the widget starts acts on the same state that installed it, whatever environment the shell was started with;
- a content hash, so `status` can say when the installed widget no longer matches the binary (`widget_outdated`, reserved since M1 and emitted from M3).

Omarchy's own tools enable and disable plugins (they write `shell.json`); omaddons validates the plugin with Omarchy's validator and its own, stages it in a hidden per-operation directory (`<plugins>/.omaddons.stage-<ulid>`, invisible to Omarchy's registry), swaps it in atomically, enables it by default (M3-D8), and records the install in history (M3-D38). A first install is one no-replace rename; a replacement is one `RENAME_EXCHANGE` of the stage with `<plugins>/omaddons`, with a fallback of two renames through a hidden `.omaddons.old-<ulid>` where exchange is unavailable. Any write under `<plugins>` reloads the whole bar, so nothing is written into the live plugin dir in place, and the widget itself never writes there (M3-D3). The content hash covers the other rendered files, the context and the tool version but excludes the binary path, so a `settings.binary` override or a differently-pathed build of the same assets is not reported as outdated (an install still compares the full rendered bytes, `Build.js` included, so a moved binary is restamped on reinstall).

## Goals

- **E1** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.1` (Embedded assets, the renderer and the validator): the embedded asset table (`include_str!` of every widget file, with a set-equality test), the renderer that stamps `Build.js` (binary path, `CONTEXT`, `PLUGIN_ID`, content hash), and omaddons' own validator.
- **E2** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2` (`omaddons omarchy install`): per-operation stages `<plugins>/.omaddons.stage-<ulid>`, validation, the atomic swap, enable by default, the history line, the doorbell ring; a reinstall that changes nothing is `unchanged`.
- **E3** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.3` (`omaddons omarchy status` and `omaddons omarchy remove`): reporting install state, hash and context match; removal that restores `<plugins>` and the bar layout.
- **E4** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.4` (The widget in `status`): the `widget` block and `summary.widget_outdated`, with `context_matches` reported separately.

## Success Criteria

- Install validates (Omarchy's validator and omaddons'), swaps atomically, enables and records.
- Two installers racing each other never mix or delete each other's stage; the registry never loads a stage.
- A reinstall is `unchanged` when nothing changed, and swaps atomically when something did.
- `omarchy remove` restores `<plugins>` and the bar layout as they were before install, apart from the history line.
- `widget_outdated` fires on a hash mismatch; a context mismatch is reported separately (`context_matches`) without a reinstall recommendation.
- Every omaddons process the widget starts runs under the stamped context (checkpoint criterion 1).

## Non-Goals

- Writing Omarchy's `shell.json` directly (Omarchy's `enable`/`disable` do it).
- In-widget settings (widget settings change with `omarchy bar set a44.omaddons <key> <value>`).

## Considerations

- **`omarchy plugin remove a44.omaddons` cannot work**, because it assumes the plugin directory name equals the plugin id (the folder is `<plugins>/omaddons/`, id `a44.omaddons`, M3-D6). `omaddons omarchy remove` is the supported path, and README says so.
- **Critical path.** E1 → E2 → E3 is on the widget critical path (A2 → F1 → F2 → F3 → E1 → E2 → E3 → G1 → G2 → G3). E1 waits for F3 because the asset table can only `include_str!` files that exist and the plugin is valid only once its two entry points exist (F2's service, F3's bar widget). E1's validator and renderer can start against a fixture plugin tree while F2/F3 run; only its asset table needs F3's files, so E1 can land in two commits.
- **Collision hot spots.** `src/fsx/scope.rs` (E2 adds a row with its own scope test), `src/fsx/prune.rs` and `tests/single_writer.rs` (E2, E3 add their entries, and the `omarchy-*` subprocesses need allowlist entries with reasons), `src/error.rs` (E2, E4), `src/limits.rs` (E2, E3), `src/app/status.rs` (E4 appends after A2).
- **Tests** run against stub `omarchy-*` scripts on a temp `PATH` and a fake `<config-omarchy>` (`tests/omarchy.rs`), including two-installer races.
- **Slice.** All four leaves belong to `slice-1` (see and update from the bar).
acceptance_criteria: E1-E4 are closed; omarchy install validates with Omarchy's and omaddons' validators, stages in its own hidden per-operation directory, swaps atomically, enables and records a history line; two racing installers never mix or delete each other's stage and the registry never loads a stage; a reinstall is unchanged when nothing changed and swaps atomically when something did; omarchy remove restores <plugins> and the bar layout as they were before install, apart from the history line; widget_outdated fires on a content-hash mismatch and context_matches is reported separately without a reinstall recommendation; every omaddons process the widget starts runs under the stamped HOME and XDG context.

title: Embedded assets, the renderer and the validator
description:
## Background

The Omarchy widget is a directory of QML and JavaScript files (`omarchy/` in the repository) that the Omarchy shell loads from `<plugins>/omaddons/`. This task makes those files part of the omaddons binary and gives the binary three pure functions over them: an embedded asset table, a renderer that stamps per-install facts into a generated `Build.js`, and a validator. E2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2`) uses all three to install the widget, E3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.3`) and E4 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.4`) use the renderer's hash to tell whether an installed widget still matches the running binary.

Why the files are embedded and stamped (M3-D7, vision D10):
- **No skew between CLI and widget.** The project version-locks the widget to the binary (vision D10). If the widget's files came from anywhere but the binary that installs them, a newer CLI could meet an older template table, and the same argv could mean something else. Embedding with `include_str!` makes the widget's code exactly the code of the build that installed it.
- **omaddons is not on the shell's PATH.** On the development machine the binary is run from `target/release/`, and the user's cargo bin directory does not hold it (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.5). So the widget must know the absolute path of the binary that installed it: `Build.BINARY`.
- **The data context must travel with the widget.** `Paths::from_env` (`src/state/paths.rs:37-65` as of `af10e34`) derives every omaddons directory from `HOME` and the four XDG variables, falling back to defaults under `HOME`; there is no flag and no `OMADDONS_*` variable that overrides the roots wholesale (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.4 item 17). A session manager can give graphical apps different XDG values than a terminal has. A widget that only knew a cache dir would watch cache A while its commands read and wrote state B: the badge would never update, or the widget would act on a second, empty omaddons state (review round 3, revision 17). Stamping the whole context (`HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, absolute, defaults written out) lets F2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2`) overlay it on every omaddons process it starts, so the widget always acts on exactly the state the installing command used.
- **A content hash catches rebuilds.** During development the binary is rebuilt constantly with the same version number. Comparing version strings would miss that. The hash covers the context, the version and every rendered file except `Build.js`'s own `BINARY` line, so a moved binary or a `settings.binary` override is not "outdated", while another build or other assets are. A different context also changes the hash, but `status` and `omarchy status` recompute the hash for the **installed** context (read back from `Build.js`), so another context alone is never "outdated": it shows as `context_matches: false` (M3-D7).
- **Omarchy's validator may be absent.** `omarchy-plugin-validate` is a bash script that uses `jq` and `find`; it is not guaranteed outside Omarchy, and a build machine may not have it. omaddons therefore ports its rules to Rust so the rendered plugin is always validated, and E2 runs the bash validator as well when it is on `PATH`.

Ground truth this task relies on (as of `af10e34`):
- `Paths` already exposes `home()`, `config_home()` and `data_home()` (`src/state/paths.rs:92-104`), but stores the state and cache roots only joined with `omaddons` (`with_roots`, `:74-89`); `state_home()` and `cache_home()` (the roots before `/omaddons`) are new.
- The plugin dir is `config_home/omarchy/plugins/omaddons` (`Paths::omarchy_plugin_dir`, `paths.rs:151-158`); `<config-omarchy>` is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omarchy`, and `<plugins>` is `<config-omarchy>/plugins`.
- Omarchy's manifest contract (from `omarchy-plugin-validate`, read-only): `schemaVersion` must be the number `1`; `id`, `name`, `version`, `kinds` and `entryPoints` are required; the id matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`, contains no `..` and does not start with `omarchy.`; entry points are relative, contain no `..` and exist; there is exactly one entry point per kind (`bar-widget` → `barWidget`, `service` → `service`); **no symlinks** anywhere inside the plugin dir.
- Discovery loads `<plugins>/*/manifest.json`; the glob skips dot-directories, so hidden stages are invisible to the registry. Any file event under a plugin dir hot-reloads every bar widget, so the widget must never write into its own dir; generated files are written only at install time, by omaddons.
- Omarchy 4.0.6 ignores manifest `defaults` and `schema` (nothing renders or applies them), so the manifest's `version` is informational. Omarchy compares nothing.

This task serves G-M3-5 (the contract carries the widget) and G-M3-6 (no new risk), and checkpoint criterion 1 (the embedded plugin passes `omarchy-plugin-validate` and omaddons' own validator; every omaddons process the widget starts runs under the stamped `HOME`/XDG context, checked by a test that launches the widget under different roots). It sits on the widget critical path: A2 → F1 → F2 → F3 → **E1** → E2 → E3 → G1 → G2 → G3.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/omarchy/assets.rs`: the embedded asset table

```rust
pub const ASSETS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("manifest.json", include_str!("../../omarchy/manifest.json")),
    ("Model.js", include_str!("../../omarchy/Model.js")),
    // … one row per runtime file under omarchy/
];
```

- The table lists exactly the runtime files under `omarchy/`, excluding `omarchy/tests/` and `Build.js` (which is generated at install, never committed). A test lists `omarchy/` from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and asserts **set equality** with the table, so a file added later by F4 (`PanelView.qml`), F5, F6, F8 or F9 must be embedded in the same commit, or the test fails. The test belongs in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (the file F1 created; F1's spec reserved this one assertion for E1).
- The full runtime set of the finished widget, for reference (the set grows as F-tasks land; the test enforces whatever exists):

  | File | Role | Task |
  |---|---|---|
  | `manifest.json` | Plugin manifest (`version` stamped at install) | F1 |
  | `Model.js` | Pure helpers, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, the `COMMANDS` template block, `CLI_PATHS` and the argv classifier, the scheduler's pure parts, reducers, widget constants; `require`-able | F1 |
  | `Store.js` | `.pragma library` holder of the service (fallback lookup) | F1 |
  | `PlainLabel.qml` | The one text component for CLI-provided strings (`Text.PlainText`) | F1 |
  | `Service.qml` | The one service | F2, F8 |
  | `BarWidget.qml` | The bar button and its `KeyboardPanel` | F3, F4 |
  | `PanelView.qml` | The panel frame | F4 |
  | `views/UpdatesView.qml`, `views/InstalledView.qml` | Views | F5 (F9 adds Installed's restore key) |
  | `views/IssuesView.qml`, `views/SearchView.qml` | Views | F6 |
  | `views/BackupsView.qml`, `RestoreChooser.qml` | Backups view and restore-scope chooser | F9 |
  | `Build.js` | Generated at install by this task's renderer; not in the repo | E1 |
  | `tests/*.test.js`, `tests/qml/…` | bun and qmltestrunner tests; **not embedded** | F1, F2, F7, F8, F9 |

- `src/omarchy/mod.rs` declares the modules (`assets`, `render`, `validate`; E2 and E3 add `install`, `status`, `remove`, `shell`).

### 2. `src/omarchy/render.rs`: the renderer and the context

```rust
pub struct Context {
    pub home: PathBuf,
    pub xdg_config_home: PathBuf,
    pub xdg_state_home: PathBuf,
    pub xdg_cache_home: PathBuf,
    pub xdg_data_home: PathBuf,
}
impl Context { pub fn of(paths: &Paths) -> Self }   // the effective roots Paths::from_env resolved, defaults written out
pub struct Rendered { pub files: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>, pub content_sha256: String }
pub fn render(binary: &Path, ctx: &Context) -> Rendered
```

- **`Paths` accessors.** `Paths` gains the accessors `Context::of` needs: `home()`, `config_home()`, `state_home()`, `cache_home()`, `data_home()` (the first, second and fifth exist; add `state_home()` and `cache_home()`). They are the roots before `/omaddons`, exactly as `from_lookup` computes them (`paths.rs:37-65`), including the fallback when an `XDG_*` value is unset or relative (a relative value falls back to the default under `HOME`). A unit test asserts that `Paths::from_lookup(Context::of(p).as_env())` equals `p`, where `as_env()` yields the five `(name, value)` pairs. That equality is what guarantees a widget child given `CONTEXT` resolves the very same `<config>`, `<state>` and `<cache>`.
- **Manifest version stamp.** Stamp the manifest's `version` with `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, using a structured JSON edit (`serde_json::Value`, re-serialized pretty with a trailing newline). Never a string replace.
- **`content_sha256`.** SHA-256 over the context, the version and the sorted `(path, bytes)` of every rendered file other than `Build.js`. **Not the binary path** (M3-D7): an install compares the full rendered bytes, `Build.js` included, to decide whether anything must be written (so a moved binary is restamped), while `status` compares this narrower hash to decide "outdated" (so a `settings.binary` override or a differently-pathed build of the same code is not called outdated). Define the hash input encoding once (for example length-prefixed fields) so that no two different inputs can collide by concatenation (an encoding detail decided while writing this bead; planning fixed only the inputs).
- **`Build.js`**, rendered last:

  ```js
  .pragma library
  var BINARY = "…"; var TOOL_VERSION = "…"; var PLUGIN_ID = "a44.omaddons";
  var CONTEXT = {"HOME": "…", "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": "…", "XDG_STATE_HOME": "…", "XDG_CACHE_HOME": "…", "XDG_DATA_HOME": "…"};
  var CACHE_DIR = "…/omaddons"; var CONTENT_SHA256 = "…"
  ```

  - `BINARY` is the canonical `std::env::current_exe()` of the installing run (E2 passes it in; `render` takes it as an argument so tests can vary it).
  - `TOOL_VERSION` is `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`; F2 compares each envelope's `tool_version` with it (M3-D42).
  - `PLUGIN_ID` is `a44.omaddons` in every normal install (see the debug seam below). Every QML use of the id derives from it.
  - `CONTEXT` is the five absolute roots; it feeds the content hash.
  - `CACHE_DIR` is `<CONTEXT.XDG_CACHE_HOME>/omaddons`, derived from `CONTEXT`; F2's `inotifywait` watches it for `doorbell.json` (M3-D4).
  - `CONTENT_SHA256` is `Rendered.content_sha256`.
  - **Every value is JSON-escaped** (`serde_json::to_string` of the string), so a path with quotes, backslashes or non-ASCII cannot break out of the literal.
- **Reading back an installed widget:**
  - `pub fn installed_sha256(dir: &Path) -> Option<String>` reads `Build.js` (bounded read; the file is small) and extracts `CONTENT_SHA256` with a strict line match (exact `var CONTENT_SHA256 = "<64 hex>"` form). Anything else is `None`. The exact matched form is decided while writing this bead: the sample above shows `CACHE_DIR` and `CONTENT_SHA256` sharing one line, so whatever layout the renderer emits, the matcher accepts exactly that rendered form and nothing looser.
  - `pub fn installed_context(dir: &Path) -> Option<Context>` extracts `CONTEXT` the same way (strict match, parsed as JSON), for `omarchy status`'s and `status`'s `context_matches`, and so that E4 can compute "the hash this binary would stamp **for the installed context**".
- **A debug-only checkpoint seam** (DEC-7: test hooks exist in debug builds only; release builds ignore the variable):
  - `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID=<suffix>`, pattern `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`, makes the plugin id `a44.omaddons-<suffix>` and its directory `<plugins>/omaddons-<suffix>`.
  - It reaches the manifest `id`, `Build.PLUGIN_ID` (from which every QML use of the id derives: the service lookup `serviceFor`, the IPC target, `Panel`'s `moduleName`/`ipcTarget` and `summon` arguments, in F2, F3 and F8, checked by F7's scan 8) and every `Paths` widget path, which E2's scope rows follow.
  - G3 uses it to install an isolated second widget for screenshots and the context check (G3's checkpoint protocol, milestone epic comment "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol (§12)", §12.3 step 3.4: a temporary plugin id `a44.omaddons-checkpoint`, installed by a debug build run with `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID=checkpoint` and fixture `HOME`/`XDG_*` values, removed afterwards). Nothing else uses it.
  - A value that fails the pattern must never reach a path or an id. Planning did not say what an invalid value does; this bead decides it is ignored (the normal id and dir are used), to be confirmed in the close comment.

### 3. `src/omarchy/validate.rs`: the validator

`pub fn validate(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String>`, a port of `omarchy-plugin-validate`. Each returned string is one violation; empty means valid. Rules:
- `schemaVersion` is the JSON number `1` (not the string);
- required keys: `id`, `name`, `version`, `kinds`, `entryPoints`;
- the id matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`, contains no `..`, and does not start with `omarchy.`;
- entry points are relative, contain no `..`, and exist inside the dir;
- one entry point per kind: each declared kind has its entry-point key (`bar-widget` → `entryPoints.barWidget`, `service` → `entryPoints.service`);
- `barWidget.defaultSection`, when present, is one of `left`, `center`, `right`;
- **no symlinks** anywhere in the dir (walk with `symlink_metadata`, never following links).

Read from the installed Omarchy 4.0.6 script while reviewing this bead (port these too, and re-read the script when porting): `kinds` must be a non-empty array and `entryPoints` an object; an empty `id` fails; an entry point may not be empty or contain a newline; the kind table is `bar` → `bar`, `bar-widget` → `barWidget`, `menu` → `menu`, `overlay` → `overlay`, `panel` → `panel`, `service` → `service` (a kind not in the table is left alone); and the symlink walk skips a `.git` directory. The script does **not** check that two kinds use different files.

Unit tests use fixture plugin trees (built in a temp dir in the test), one per violation, plus a test that the rendered plugin (`render` written to a temp dir) validates clean.

### 4. Constants

None. `Build.js` is small, and the asset files are bounded by the binary itself.

### 5. Landing in two commits

E1 can be split to shorten the widget critical path (delivery note): the renderer, the context and the validator can be written and tested against a fixture plugin tree while F2 and F3 are still in progress. Only the asset table (and its set-equality test) needs F3's `BarWidget.qml` to exist, because `include_str!` can only embed files that exist and the plugin is valid only once both entry points exist (F2's `Service.qml`, F3's `BarWidget.qml`). Views added later (F4, F5, F6, F9) append rows to the table; the set-equality test forces them to.

### Files

- New: `src/omarchy/mod.rs`, `src/omarchy/assets.rs`, `src/omarchy/render.rs`, `src/omarchy/validate.rs`.
- Changed: `src/state/paths.rs` (`state_home()`, `cache_home()`, the widget id seam feeding `omarchy_plugin_dir`), `src/lib.rs` or `src/main.rs` module declaration, `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (the asset-set assertion).
- No command surface: E2 adds `omaddons omarchy install`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `render` is deterministic: two renders with the same inputs produce byte-identical files and the same `content_sha256`.
- Two renders under different XDG roots differ in `CONTEXT` and in `content_sha256`.
- Two renders under different binary paths differ only in `Build.js`'s `BINARY` value; every other file and `content_sha256` are identical.
- `Paths` built from a rendered `CONTEXT` equals the installing `Paths`, including non-default roots and a relative `XDG_*` value that fell back to the default.
- The rendered manifest's `version` equals `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, and the manifest stays valid pretty JSON with a trailing newline.
- Every `Build.js` value is JSON-escaped: a context path containing `"`, `\` and non-ASCII renders to a file that `installed_context` reads back exactly.
- Validation fails on each planted violation (string `schemaVersion`, a missing required key, a bad id, an `omarchy.` id, an entry point with `..`, a missing entry file, a declared kind without its entry-point key, a bad `defaultSection`, a symlink anywhere in the tree), and passes on the rendered plugin.
- `installed_sha256` and `installed_context` round-trip what `render` wrote, and return `None` for a missing, truncated or hand-edited `Build.js`.
- The asset-set test fails when a runtime file under `omarchy/` is not embedded (a table row naming a missing file already fails the build, through `include_str!`).
- In a debug build, `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID=checkpoint` yields the id `a44.omaddons-checkpoint` in the manifest and in `Build.PLUGIN_ID`, and the plugin dir `<plugins>/omaddons-checkpoint`; a release build ignores it.

## Test Plan

- **Unit, `src/omarchy/render.rs`:** determinism; context variation changes `CONTEXT` and the hash; binary variation changes only `BINARY`; manifest stamping through `serde_json::Value`; escaping of hostile path characters; `installed_sha256` and `installed_context` round trips and strict-match rejections (extra spaces, wrong hex length, a second `CONTENT_SHA256` line; cases chosen while writing this bead); the `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` seam (valid suffix, invalid suffix ignored, as decided above).
- **Unit, `src/state/paths.rs`:** `Paths::from_lookup(Context::of(p).as_env()) == p` for default roots, explicit non-default roots, and a relative `XDG_STATE_HOME` that fell back to the default.
- **Unit, `src/omarchy/validate.rs`:** one fixture tree per rule violation, built in a temp dir, plus the clean rendered tree.
- **`tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (always on):** the embedded asset set equals the runtime files under `omarchy/` (excluding `tests/` and `Build.js`).
- **Contract:** none (no command yet). E2's tests exercise `render` and `validate` through the command.

## Considerations

- **The hash deliberately excludes `BINARY`.** E2 compares full rendered bytes (so a moved binary is restamped on reinstall), and E4/E3 compare `CONTENT_SHA256` (so a different binary path is never "outdated"). Do not merge the two comparisons.
- **`CONTEXT` is in the hash on purpose.** A widget installed for another context is outdated *for that context* only when the assets differ; E4 computes `render(current_exe, installed_context).content_sha256` and compares it with the installed hash, so a terminal running under another context does not see "outdated" merely because its own context differs (it sees `context_matches: false`, without a reinstall recommendation, M3-D7).
- **Determinism matters for idempotence.** E2 reports `installed: unchanged` and writes nothing when every rendered file already matches the installed bytes; any nondeterminism (map ordering, timestamps) would make every install a replacement and hot-reload the bar for nothing.
- **The `Model.js` constants and templates are part of the hashed assets,** so any change to the template table makes an installed widget outdated, which is exactly the version lock the project wants.
- **Risks (from the risk register: milestone epic comment "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol (§12)", §12.1):** risk 22, the widget acting on a different omaddons state than the terminal (an XDG difference), is mitigated here by stamping the full context, and in F2 and E4 by using and reporting it. Risk 1, Omarchy changing its plugin API, is registered against F0 and F2–F4 (mitigation: F0's live verification, a small API surface, IPC `state()`, a fallback poll); it touches this task only through the validator, whose rules copy Omarchy's and must be re-read if Omarchy changes them (this bead's reading, not the register's).
- **Collision hot spots:** the delivery plan's hot-spot table (§11.4) lists no file for E1. Files shared with other tasks, noted while writing this bead: `src/state/paths.rs` (E2 also edits the widget paths; land E1 first), `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (F1 owns it; E1 adds one assertion).
- **Critical path.** E1 is on the widget critical path; its successor E2 waits on it. Start the renderer and validator early against a fixture tree (section 5).
- **Delivery slice `slice-1` (see and update from the bar).** Exit demo, run by whoever closes the slice's last task and recorded as a comment on the milestone epic: `omarchy install` on the desktop; the badge follows a terminal `update` within 1 s; update one addon from the panel and undo it; a `remove` preview gone stale gives `plan_stale`; reinstall swaps atomically. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 1, 2 (the terminal-change part), 3, 4 (update states), 5 and 13 (`remove`, `undo`).

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- F3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.3` (`BarWidget.qml`, the bar button): the asset table can only `include_str!` files that exist, and the plugin is valid only once both entry points exist (`Service.qml` from F2, `BarWidget.qml` from F3). The renderer and validator may be built earlier against a fixture tree.

**Unblocks:**
- E2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2` (`omaddons omarchy install`): renders, validates and stages the embedded plugin, and compares rendered bytes for idempotence.
- E4 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.4` (The widget in `status`): `installed_sha256`, `installed_context` and `render(current_exe, installed_context)` decide `outdated` and `context_matches`.

E3 (`omarchy status` and `remove`) uses these functions too, through E2. F1's `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` gains this task's asset-set assertion.

Parent: the E epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5`. Delivery slice: `slice-1`.

comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** Without it there is no widget to install: the QML lives in the repository, but nothing ships it, nothing tells it which binary and which omaddons state it belongs to, and nothing can tell a stale install from a current one. After this bead the binary carries its own widget, byte for byte, and can render it for one exact context: the binary path, the five XDG roots and a content hash. That is what makes the version lock between CLI and widget real (vision D10), and what keeps the widget acting on the same state as the terminal that installed it. E2 installs what this renders, E3 and E4 compare against it, and G3's isolated checkpoint widget exists only because of this task's debug seam.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D7: the binary path, the data context and a content hash are stamped at install.** `Build.js` holds `BINARY`, `TOOL_VERSION`, `PLUGIN_ID`, `CONTEXT` (absolute `HOME` and the four XDG roots, defaults written out), `CACHE_DIR` and `CONTENT_SHA256`; `BINARY` is not hashed. Why: omaddons is not on the shell's PATH, a cache dir alone would let the widget watch one state while acting on another, and a hash catches same-version rebuilds. Rejected: relying on PATH (fails on the development machine today); comparing version strings only (misses rebuilds); a manifest `x-omaddons` block (Omarchy does not hand the manifest to bar widgets, while a `.js` the widget imports is directly usable); a new `--home`/`--state-dir` CLI flag (a contract addition for one caller, when environment variables are what `Paths` already reads).
- **M3-D5 and M3-D6 (context): one shared service, plugin folder `<plugins>/omaddons/`, id `a44.omaddons`.** Every QML use of the id derives from `Build.PLUGIN_ID`, never a literal, so the debug `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` seam yields a truly separate widget (its own service, IPC handler and panel). Rejected for the folder: naming it `a44.omaddons/` so Omarchy's own remove works (it breaks the house convention and the existing scope rows).
- **DEC-7: test hooks in debug builds only.** The widget-id seam is ignored by release builds.
- **Vision D10 (version lock).** The widget is from exactly one build; E4 and F2 turn a mismatch into a visible, read-only state (M3-D42).

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 1 took `BINARY` out of the content hash, so a moved binary or a `settings.binary` override is not reported as outdated.
- Round 3 (revision 17, the installed filesystem context) replaced a stamped `CACHE_DIR` alone with the whole `CONTEXT`, added the `Paths` round-trip test, and introduced `installed_context` for `context_matches`.
- The plugin-id rule (every QML use of the id comes from `Build.PLUGIN_ID`, never a literal: M3-D5, checked by F7's scan 8) is not attributed to a numbered review revision in the planning record; it exists so this task's debug seam yields a truly separate checkpoint widget.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- `Paths::from_env`/`from_lookup` read `HOME` (must be absolute) and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, falling back to defaults under `HOME` (`src/state/paths.rs:37-65` as of `af10e34`); there is no wholesale override.
- `home()`, `config_home()` and `data_home()` exist (`paths.rs:92-104`); state and cache roots are stored only joined with `omaddons` (`with_roots`, `:74-89`).
- `Paths::omarchy_plugin_dir` is `config_home/omarchy/plugins/omaddons`, and today's `omarchy_plugin_stage` is a single fixed `.omaddons.stage` (`paths.rs:151-158`), which E2 replaces.
- `omarchy-plugin-validate` is a read-only bash script (`jq`, `find`) whose rules are listed in the body; discovery skips dot-directories; any write under a plugin dir hot-reloads every bar widget; Omarchy 4.0.6 ignores manifest `defaults` and `schema` (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.5).
- omaddons is run from `target/release/` on the development machine and is not on the shell's PATH.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk 22 (the widget acts on a different state than the terminal): the full context is stamped and round-trip-tested here; F2 overlays it on every child; E4 reports `context_matches`.
- Risk 1 (Omarchy changes its plugin API; registered against F0 and F2–F4, mitigated by F0's live verification and a small surface): it reaches this task only through the validator, whose rules copy Omarchy's; E2 also runs the bash validator when present (this connection is the bead's reading, not the register's).
- Nondeterministic rendering would turn every reinstall into a replacement and a bar reload: determinism is an acceptance criterion.

**Confidence.** High: pure, deterministic functions over embedded files, fully unit-testable; the only external input is the validator's rule set, which is small and was read from source.

title: `omaddons omarchy install`
description:
## Background

`omaddons omarchy install` puts the bar widget on the desktop: it renders the embedded plugin (E1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.1`), validates it, swaps it into `<plugins>/omaddons/` atomically, records the install in history, rings the doorbell and places the widget in the bar. It is the first command a user runs to get the widget (user workflow "first run": within a second a gamepad glyph appears on both monitors' bars, and hovering shows "omaddons · 6 clients · 3 updates · checked 2 h ago"), and the command the widget itself runs, detached, to reinstall itself when it finds it is from another build (M3-D42).

Four properties make it safe, each from a decision:
- **Atomic and validated (M3-D6, M3-D7).** The plugin is assembled in a hidden stage (Omarchy's discovery glob `<plugins>/*/manifest.json` skips dot-directories, so the registry never sees a half-written plugin), validated by omaddons' Rust validator and, when present, by `omarchy-plugin-validate`, then published with one `RENAME_EXCHANGE` (replacement) or `RENAME_NOREPLACE` (first install). Any file event under a plugin dir hot-reloads every widget on the bar, so writing in place would reload the bar once per file.
- **Visible at once (M3-D8, a departure from the vision's opt-in `--enable`).** The first command a user guesses should work (vision D17). A user who installs a bar widget wants it in the bar. Enabling uses Omarchy's own `omarchy-bar put`, which leaves an already-placed widget where the owner put it.
- **Recorded (M3-D38).** Every change is attributed (vision §5.9): the install appends a `widget` settings line to history, so the widget's self-reinstall shows as `actor: widget`.
- **Safe against a second installer (M3-D38, review round 3 revision 16).** The terminal and the widget's own self-reinstall can run at the same time. A fixed shared stage dir assembled outside the lock let two installers delete or mix each other's files before either reached the atomic swap. The engine already solved this for transactions with in-flight locks, so each install owns its stage under an `InflightLock`, and only a process that can take a stage's lock may reclaim it. Elapsed time is never ownership evidence.

Ground truth this task relies on (as of `af10e34`):
- `Scope::Omarchy` covers `<plugins>/omaddons/` and a single fixed `<plugins>/.omaddons.stage/` (`src/state/paths.rs:151-158`; scope rows at `src/fsx/scope.rs:404-405`; admits `Writer::Omarchy` and `Writer::Doctor`, `scope.rs:119`).
- A scope root accepts only `CreateDir` (`scope.rs:343`), so without new rules every swap and every prune at those roots is refused.
- `Scope::History` admits `Writer::Backup` but **not** `Writer::Omarchy` (`scope.rs:99-122`).
- Settings kinds (`config`, `target`, `auth`, `export`) are `SettingEntry` lines (`src/state/history.rs:72-90`); `TxKind` has no `Widget` kind yet (`src/model.rs:412-453`).
- `InflightLock` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:193-275`) is a `create_new` + `try_lock` file per transaction (`<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock`, or `<cache>/inflight/<tx>.lock` for scratch work); stage dirs and temp blobs are orphaned only when their transaction's lock is free or missing. `fsx::prune` re-checks liveness itself only for lock-file victims (`prune.rs:140`); for stage victims it relies on its callers. `LockUse::Own` restricts victims to the caller's own transaction (`prune.rs:101-112`).
- `prune.rs`'s `location()` (`src/fsx/prune.rs:264-338`) only classifies known kinds; an unknown victim is refused as not prunable. `PruneReason` today is `Retention`, `PostCommitCleanup`, `PlanExpiry`, `BackupPrune`, `DoctorGc` (`prune.rs:25-46`).
- Subprocesses may be started only from `src/sources/git_hosts.rs` and `src/state/config.rs` (the allowlist in `tests/single_writer.rs`).
- `omarchy-bar put <id> --section <s>` prints `<id> is on the bar` whether or not it had to place the widget, and **exits 0 even when the shell is not running** (it prints "omarchy-shell is not running …" to stderr). While the shell is still rescanning plugins it reports `is not a known widget` on stderr; its own `ask_to_put` loop retries. A separate `enablePlugin` call would race the asynchronous `rescanPlugins` (`shell.qml:1607`).
- Omarchy's tools need the desktop environment: `OMARCHY_PATH` (`omarchy-shell:40`), the Wayland and Hyprland variables and the D-Bus session.
- `omarchy plugin enable` writes only `{ "id": "<id>" }` into `<config-omarchy>/shell.json`; omaddons never writes `shell.json` itself.

This task serves G-M3-1 (glanceable: the icon exists), G-M3-6 (no new risk: fsx, scope rows, in-flight ownership) and checkpoint criterion 1 (a working, enabled widget on both monitors; a reinstall swaps atomically; every install stages in its own hidden `<plugins>/.omaddons.stage-<ulid>`; two racing installers never mix or delete each other's stage). It is on the widget critical path: … → E1 → **E2** → E3 → G1 → G2 → G3.

## Technical Approach

### The command surface

```text
omaddons omarchy install [--no-enable] [--section left|center|right]
```
