comments.text:
**The widget at a glance (§10.1): files, the manifest, the `COMMANDS` template block, the key map (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).** Each F and E leaf inlines the parts it builds; this comment is the whole picture in one place.

Section labels (`§x.y`) and plan keys (A1 … G3) are resolved by the milestone epic body ("How to read the M3 beads") and the key → id comment. Code references are as of `af10e34`.

### 10.1 The widget at a glance

**Files** in `omarchy/`. Each one is embedded in the binary except `tests/`; E1's asset table must list exactly this set, and a test checks it:

| File | Role | Task |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | Plugin manifest (`version` stamped at install) | F1 |
| `Model.js` | Pure helpers, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, the `COMMANDS` template block, `CLI_PATHS` and the argv classifier, the scheduler's pure parts, reducers from envelopes to view models, widget constants; `require`-able | F1 |
| `Store.js` | `.pragma library` holder of the service (the fallback lookup) | F1 |
| `PlainLabel.qml` | The one text component for CLI-provided strings: `textFormat: Text.PlainText`, elided, never rich text | F1 |
| `Service.qml` | The one service: scheduler and process runner, compatibility gate, confirmations, IPC (F2); doorbells, Hyprland, auto-check, post-session triggers, notifications (F8) | F2, F8 |
| `BarWidget.qml` | The bar button and its `KeyboardPanel`; binds to the service | F3, F4 |
| `PanelView.qml` | The panel frame: hero, target switcher, view switcher, footer, cards, confirm dialog | F4 |
| `views/UpdatesView.qml`, `views/InstalledView.qml` | Views | F5 (F9 adds Installed's restore key) |
| `views/IssuesView.qml`, `views/SearchView.qml` | Views | F6 |
| `views/BackupsView.qml`, `RestoreChooser.qml` | The Backups view and the restore-scope chooser | F9 |
| `Build.js` | **Generated at install** (E1); not in the repo | E1 |
| `tests/*.test.js`, `tests/qml/…` | bun and qmltestrunner tests | F1, F2, F7, F8, F9 |

**The manifest** (F1):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "id": "a44.omaddons",
  "name": "omaddons",
  "version": "0.0.0-unstamped",
  "author": "a44",
  "description": "World of Warcraft addons on every client: updates, Lua errors and WTF backups, from the omaddons CLI.",
  "kinds": ["service", "bar-widget"],
  "entryPoints": { "service": "Service.qml", "barWidget": "BarWidget.qml" },
  "barWidget": {
    "displayName": "omaddons",
    "description": "One gamepad for every WoW client: a badge for pending addon updates, urgent when something is broken or an addon threw Lua errors, and a keyboard panel to update, undo, back up and restore. Every action is an omaddons command line, recorded and undoable.",
    "category": "Games",
    "aliases": ["omaddons", "wow", "warcraft", "addons"],
    "allowMultiple": false,
    "defaultSection": "right",
    "defaults": { "binary": "", "panelWidth": 540, "autoCheck": "On", "notifyUpdates": "Off", "notifyErrors": "On", "refreshIntervalSec": 300 },
    "schema": [
      { "key": "binary", "type": "path", "label": "omaddons binary", "defaultValue": "", "description": "Empty runs the binary that installed the widget (omaddons omarchy install stamps its path). Set a path to run another build." },
      { "key": "panelWidth", "type": "integer", "label": "Panel width", "min": 400, "max": 800, "step": 20, "defaultValue": 540 },
      { "key": "autoCheck", "type": "enum", "label": "Check for updates when due", "options": ["On", "Off"], "defaultValue": "On", "description": "Run omaddons outdated in the background when a client's last check is older than check_interval_hours in omaddons' config.toml." },
      { "key": "notifyUpdates", "type": "enum", "label": "Notify about new updates", "options": ["On", "Off"], "defaultValue": "Off" },
      { "key": "notifyErrors", "type": "enum", "label": "Notify about Lua errors after a session", "options": ["On", "Off"], "defaultValue": "On" },
      { "key": "refreshIntervalSec", "type": "integer", "label": "Fallback refresh (seconds)", "min": 30, "max": 3600, "step": 30, "defaultValue": 300, "description": "Safety-net refresh behind the doorbell; 15 s while the panel is open." }
    ]
  }
}
```

**The `COMMANDS` template block** (F1). It lives in `Model.js` between marker comments, and its JSON-compatible literal is checked by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (M3-D2):

```js
// BEGIN COMMANDS: checked by tests/omarchy_widget.rs; every entry must parse as an omaddons command line
// F1 ships the entries for commands that exist at F1 time; F8 adds errors_target and backup_auto (B6, D3);
// F6 adds errors, errors_raw and dismiss_errors (B6, B8); F9 adds backups, backup_target, backup_all,
// restore, restore_addon and prune_backup (D2, D4, D7, D8).
var COMMANDS = {
  "status":         { "argv": ["status", "--cached", "-v"],                         "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "status_full":    { "argv": ["status", "-v"],                                     "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "list":           { "argv": ["list", "-v"],                                       "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "errors":         { "argv": ["errors", "--limit", "10"],                          "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "errors_target":  { "argv": ["errors", "--limit", "10", "-t", "{target}"],        "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "errors_raw":     { "argv": ["errors", "--raw-details", "-t", "{target}", "--addon={addon}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "dismiss_errors": { "argv": ["errors", "dismiss", "-t", "{target}"],              "mutates": true,  "bind": true },
  "backups":        { "argv": ["backup", "list", "--limit", "50"],                  "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "changelog":      { "argv": ["info", "-t", "{target}", "--changelog", "--", "{addon}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "network" },
  "search":         { "argv": ["search", "--limit", "20", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{query}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "network" },
  "check":          { "argv": ["outdated"],                                         "mutates": false, "lane": "network" },
  "update_all":     { "argv": ["update"],                                           "mutates": true },
  "update_target":  { "argv": ["update", "-t", "{target}"],                         "mutates": true },
  "update_addon":   { "argv": ["update", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],        "mutates": true },
  "reinstall":      { "argv": ["install", "-t", "{target}", "--reinstall", "--", "{addon}"], "mutates": true },
  "remove":         { "argv": ["remove", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],        "mutates": true, "confirm": true },
  "pin":            { "argv": ["pin", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],           "mutates": true },
  "unpin":          { "argv": ["unpin", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],         "mutates": true },
  "install":        { "argv": ["install", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{ref}"],         "mutates": true },
  "backup_target":  { "argv": ["backup", "create", "-t", "{target}"],               "mutates": true },
  "backup_all":     { "argv": ["backup", "create"],                                 "mutates": true },
  "backup_auto":    { "argv": ["backup", "create", "--auto", "-t", "{target}"],     "mutates": true, "silent": true },
  "restore":        { "argv": ["backup", "restore", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{backup}"], "mutates": true, "confirm": true },
  "restore_addon":  { "argv": ["backup", "restore", "-t", "{target}", "--addon={addon}", "--", "{backup}"], "mutates": true, "confirm": true },
  "prune_backup":   { "argv": ["backup", "prune", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{backup}"],   "mutates": true, "confirm": true }
}
// END COMMANDS
```

**Two templates added when the beads were filed** (each decided in its bead): `search_all` (F6), `["search", "--limit", "20", "--", "{query}"]`, read-only, network lane, for the All filter, because `search` with `-t` reports hints only for the selected client; and `backups_detail` (F9), `["backup", "list", "-v", "-t", "{target}", "--limit", "50"]`, read-only, local lane, view-bound, for the restore chooser's per-backup addon versions. Both pass the same Rust argv validation as every other template.

- **Running a template.** `argv[0]` (`omaddons`) is implicit.
  - `Model.buildArgv` returns `{ argv: [binary, "--json", "--actor", "widget", "--reason", <label>, ("--progress", "json")?, ("--dry-run")?, ("--if-match", <token>)?, ...template], env: Build.CONTEXT }`. The standard flags go **right after the binary**, before the command words. They are global flags, and anything after the template's `--` is a positional (M3-D2).
  - `--progress json` is added for mutating templates and `check`. `--if-match` is added only when the caller passes a validated token (`^pc1:[0-9a-f]{64}$`).
  - CLI-output argv get the same insertion after their `omaddons`, once `classifyCliArgv` accepts them.
- **Slots as option values** are written `--opt={slot}`, in one argv element, so a value beginning with `-` is still that option's value and never a flag. Positional slots follow `--` (M3-D2). `{target}` never needs either, because its pattern cannot start with `-`.
- **`lane`** names the scheduler lane of a read (M3-D11); every `mutates: true` template runs in the mutation lane.
- **`confirm: true`**: the runner first runs the same argv with `--dry-run`, shows the dialog from its result, and on confirm reruns with `--if-match <data.precondition>`. A `plan_stale` answer reloads the dialog with a fresh dry run (M3-D9).
- **`bind: true`** (`dismiss_errors`): no dialog. The token is the `dismiss.precondition` of the `errors` read the view shows, and a `plan_stale` answer refreshes the view instead (M3-D19).
- **Undo and fixes** come from CLI output, never from templates (`last_change.undo.argv`, `fix_argv`, `remediation.argv`, `commands[].argv`), after the classifier (M3-D2). Undo always goes through the confirm flow (M3-D9). The widget's reinstall is a detached `omarchy install` (M3-D42).
- **`errors dismiss`** writes `<state>`, so its template is `mutates: true`, in the mutation lane, and recorded in history (M3-D19).
- **`silent: true`** (`backup_auto`) runs in the **same** mutation lane at background priority, and shows no result line unless it fails (M3-D11).

**The panel's key map** (F4). It respects `PanelKeyCatcher`'s reserved keys (§2.5):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `j`/`k`, ↓/↑ | Move the row cursor |
| `h`/`l`, ←/→ | Previous/next view: Updates · Installed · Issues · Backups · Search |
| Enter | The row's primary action (update / reinstall / fix / restore / install) |
| `x` | The row's removal (remove addon, prune backup), with confirm |
| Esc | Cancel a confirm, leave the search field, or close the panel |
| Tab / Shift-Tab | (Omarchy) neighbouring bar panel |
| `u` | Update all (or the selected target's updates, when a target is selected) |
| `c` | Check now |
| `z` | Undo last (`last_change.undo`), with confirm |
| `b` | Back up now (selected target, or all) |
| `d` | Dismiss errors (selected target, or each target with new errors), bound to the shown observation |
| `r` | Restore settings: on an Installed or Issues addon row, that addon's settings from a backup; on a Backups row, that backup (the restore chooser, F9) |
| `s` | Show the selected error's raw details (`errors --raw-details`, labelled "may contain names") |
| `i` | Toggle the selected update's release notes (network, on demand) |
| `p` | Pin/unpin the selected addon |
| `o` | Open the selected target's AddOns folder (`xdg-open <client_dir>/Interface/AddOns`) |
| `t` | Cycle the target filter: All → each target |
| `/` | Go to Search and focus the field |
| `1`–`5` | Jump to view N |

Space behaves as Enter: `PanelKeyCatcher` maps it to `activateRequested` (`Ui/PanelKeyCatcher.qml`).

title: The widget scaffold: manifest, `Model.js`, `Store.js`, `PlainLabel.qml`, tests, the gate pipeline
description:
## Background

The M3 widget is an Omarchy bar plugin under `omarchy/` in this repository, embedded in the binary (E1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.1`) and installed by `omaddons omarchy install` (E2, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2`). Its rule, from the vision (D2, §5.11) and M3-D2/M3-D3, is that **the CLI is the authority and the widget holds no product logic**: it reduces `--json` envelopes into view models, runs omaddons as argv arrays, and never writes a file. Some logic is unavoidable even so: reducing envelopes to view models, choosing labels, validating command templates and CLI-provided argv, and the scheduler's decisions about which request runs next and which late result may be applied. This task puts all of that logic into one **pure, `require`-able JavaScript file, `omarchy/Model.js`**, so bun can test it against envelopes the real binary produces (M3-D41), and builds the pipeline that runs those tests in every gate.

The template table and the classifier in `Model.js` are **the widget's safety boundary** (M3-D2): every argv the widget can ever run comes either from that fixed table, filled only with identifiers the CLI returned, or from CLI output that the classifier accepts. Nothing is shell-parsed, and nothing destructive runs without a preview the user saw.

What exists today (as of `af10e34`):
- There is **no `omarchy/` directory** yet. `Paths` already has `omarchy_plugin_dir()` = `<config-omarchy>/plugins/omaddons` and a reserved stage path (`src/state/paths.rs:151-158`), and `WarningCode::WidgetOutdated` is reserved (`src/error.rs:259`, no other reference).
- **The command registry** is `COMMANDS` in `src/app/mod.rs:109-138` (`CommandEntry { name, group: Look|Change|Setup, mutates }`), and `app::mutates(path)` (`src/app/mod.rs:142-147`) treats a path the registry does not list as mutating. Mutation is classified **per command path, not per flag**, which is why `CLI_PATHS` can mirror the registry exactly.
- **The envelope** is `schema_version` "1.0" (`src/output/envelope.rs:10-38`), written as **one compact line** on stdout (`serde_json::to_vec`, `src/output/mod.rs:266`). Progress events are NDJSON on stderr, shape `{"event":"progress","phase","message","current","total"}` (`src/output/stderr.rs:312-329`), opted into with `--progress json` even under `--json` (`src/output/term.rs:124-157`).
- **Every global flag is `global = true`** (`src/cli.rs:49-111`), and README says every global option works before the command. Appending standard flags at the **end** of a template would put them after `--`, where clap reads them as positionals: `pin … -- Foo --json` was reproduced as a usage error in review round 1.
- **Network politeness** (`src/politeness.rs:20-33`): `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` 10 s, `API_READ_TIMEOUT` 30 s, `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` 300 s, `MAX_RETRIES` 3 (4 attempts), `BACKOFF_MAX` 8 s, `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` 60 s. One request can legitimately take about 4 × 30 s + 3 × 60 s ≈ 5 minutes, so a widget deadline shorter than that would kill healthy update checks (M3-D11).
- **The gate** is `scripts/gate.sh` (fmt, clippy, `cargo test --locked`, `ubs` on changed files, `cargo deny` on dependency changes), run by `argc gate` from `Argcfile.sh`.
- **The house harness for QML exists on this machine**: the 37signals.hey plugin ships a `require`-able `Model.js` tested with node, and `qmltestrunner -import tests/qml/imports` with mock `Quickshell/Io/{Process,StdioCollector,SplitParser}.qml` under `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`. omaddons uses `bun` instead of node (house rule).
- **Manifest `defaults` and `schema` are inert in Omarchy 4.0.6** (milestone ground-truth comment, §2.5): nothing renders or applies them, and `omarchy plugin enable` writes only `{ "id": "<id>" }` into `<config-omarchy>/shell.json`. So the defaults must also live in code.

This task serves G-M3-2 (one-click actions, argv-only, never surprising), G-M3-5 (everything the widget shows comes from documented `--json` output) and G-M3-1 (the bar model), and it is the base of checkpoint criteria 4 (widget states, through the reducers), 5 (argv-only execution: the template table, the classifier and the exact-argv validation) and 11 (the gate runs the widget tests from a clean checkout).

- **M3-D10:** six widget settings, with defaults duplicated in `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` because Omarchy ignores manifest defaults.

- **M3-D41:** widget tests run in the gate in one ordered pipeline, with every artifact generated fresh into `$OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT`.
- **M3-D42:** `compatible(env, build)` decides the read-only incompatible state.

### 2. `omarchy/Model.js`

No `.pragma`, so each importer gets its own copy. It ends with a guarded export so bun can `require` it: `if (typeof module !== "undefined") module.exports = {…}`. Engine-neutral JavaScript only: no QML globals, ES2017 at most (Qt 6's V4 supports it), and `var`/`function` style like the house plugins. It holds:

#### 2.1 Settings and constants

- `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, equal to `manifest.json`'s `barWidget.defaults` (a test asserts it).
- `setting(settings, key)` with the house fallback rules, plus `intSetting(settings, key, def, min, max)`, `boolSetting(…)` and the `On`/`Off` enum convention. A missing, wrong-typed or out-of-range value falls back to `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`. (The exact signatures and the fallback detail are decided while writing this bead. F4 calls the panel width as `intSetting("panelWidth", 540, 400, 800)` from `BarWidget.qml`, so that call is a thin QML wrapper that passes the widget's `settings` into `Model.intSetting`.)
- **The widget constants** (QML cannot read `src/limits.rs`, so they live here; values from the constants table in the milestone epic's contract comment, §7.11):

  | Constant | Value | Basis |
  |---|---|---|
  | `WIDGET_LOCAL_DEADLINE_SEC` | 20 | Plain UI choice: deadline of a local read from its start; pinned only by `model.test.js` |
  | `WIDGET_NETWORK_DEADLINE_SEC` | 600 | An **inactivity** deadline for network reads, reset on every NDJSON progress line. `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` checks it is at least `(MAX_RETRIES + 1) × API_READ_TIMEOUT + MAX_RETRIES × RETRY_AFTER_CAP` from `src/politeness.rs` (4 × 30 + 3 × 60 = 300 s today) |

#### 2.2 The `COMMANDS` template block

- **F1 ships** the entries for commands that exist at F1 time (status, list, outdated, update, install, remove, pin, unpin, info, search): `status`, `status_full`, `list`, `changelog`, `search`, `check`, `update_all`, `update_target`, `update_addon`, `reinstall`, `remove`, `pin`, `unpin`, `install`.
- **F8** (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.8`) adds `errors_target` and `backup_auto` (once B6 and D3 exist).
- **F6** (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.6`) adds `errors`, `errors_raw` and `dismiss_errors` (B6, B8), and `search_all` (the All filter's search without `-t`; decided when the beads were filed).

**Template semantics** (the runner, F2, implements the behaviour; `Model.js` encodes the rules):
- `argv[0]` (`omaddons`) is implicit; the binary path is substituted.
- **Slots** (M3-D2):
  - `{target}`: a target id or key from `status`. `buildArgv` refuses any value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@-]*$`, which every id and key satisfies. It cannot start with `-`, so it never needs `--` or the `=` form;
  - `{addon}`: an addon name from `list`;
  - `{ref}`: a ref from `search`;
  - `{backup}`: a backup id from `backup list`;
  - `{query}`: free text, allowed **only** in read-only templates.
- **Positional slots follow a `--` separator; a slot used as an option's value is written `--opt={slot}` in one argv element**, so a value beginning with `-` is still that option's value and never a flag.
- **`lane`** names the scheduler lane of a read (M3-D11): `local` or `network`. Every `mutates: true` template runs in the mutation lane.
- **`confirm: true`**: the runner first runs the same argv with `--dry-run`, shows the dialog from its result, and on confirm reruns with `--if-match <data.precondition>`. A `plan_stale` answer reloads the dialog with a fresh dry run (M3-D9).
- **`bind: true`** (`dismiss_errors`): no dialog. The token is the `dismiss.precondition` of the `errors` read the view shows, and a `plan_stale` answer refreshes the view instead (M3-D19).
- **`silent: true`** (`backup_auto`): runs in the **same** mutation lane at background priority and shows no result line unless it fails (M3-D11). "Silent" changes presentation only, never concurrency.
- **Undo and fixes come from CLI output, never from templates** (`last_change.undo.argv`, `fix_argv`, `remediation.argv`, `commands[].argv`), after the classifier (M3-D2). Undo always goes through the confirm flow (M3-D9). The widget's own reinstall is a detached `omarchy install` (M3-D42, F2).
- `errors dismiss` writes `<state>`, so its template is `mutates: true`, in the mutation lane, and recorded in history (M3-D19).

#### 2.3 `CLI_PATHS`

`CLI_PATHS` is `{ "<path>": { "mutates": bool, "destructive": bool, "binds": bool } }`, **one row for every `app::COMMANDS` path** (nested paths such as `targets rm` included), also between marker comments so the Rust test can extract it.
- `mutates` equals `app::mutates(path)` for every path; the always-on Rust test asserts the path set and the flags are identical to the registry.
- `destructive` marks `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `targets rm`.
- `binds` marks the five paths that accept `--if-match` (M3-D46): `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`. The Rust test checks `binds` against the list of binding paths that A4's `app::precondition` declares (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`, owns that list; `app::dispatch` rejects `--if-match` with `usage` on every other path).
- **At F1 time** only the paths that exist are listed (so `binds` is set on `remove` and `undo`). Every later command task adds its own `CLI_PATHS` row in the same commit as its registry row (common rule 4.11); the always-on test fails otherwise.
- **Ordering with A4** (decided while writing this bead; confirm in the close comment). F1 is not blocked by A4, and in the six-lane schedule both run at t=3–5, so A4's `--if-match` and its binding list may not exist yet when F1 lands. If A4 has not landed, the test checks `binds` against M3-D46's five paths restricted to the paths the registry has; the switch to `app::precondition`'s list is made by whichever of F1 and A4 lands second.

#### 2.4 `buildArgv(name, slots, opts) -> {argv, env}`

- Fills the template's slots. **Throws** on:
  - an unknown slot, or a template slot left unfilled;
  - a `{target}` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@-]*$`;
  - `{query}` in a mutating template;
  - a token that fails `^pc1:[0-9a-f]{64}$`, or a token for a path that does not `bind` (the CLI would reject `--if-match` there as `usage`).

  (The plan names the unknown slot, the `{target}` pattern, `{query}` in a mutating template and the token pattern. Throwing on an unfilled slot and on a token for a non-binding path, instead of silently omitting `--if-match`, is decided while writing this bead.)
- **Inserts the standard flags right after the binary, before the command words** (M3-D2): `[binary, "--json", "--actor", "widget", "--reason", <label>, ("--progress", "json")?, ("--dry-run")?, ("--if-match", <token>)?, ...template]`, where `<label>` is `"<button label> (bar widget)"`.
  - `--progress json` is added when the template `mutates` or is `check`.
  - `--dry-run` is added when `opts.preview` is set.
  - `--if-match <token>` is added only when the caller passes a validated token and the path `binds`.
  - Example: `omaddons --json --actor widget --reason "Update (bar widget)" update -t retail -- DBM`.
- `env` is `opts.context`, which the service fills from `Build.CONTEXT` (M3-D7): the installing run's effective, absolute `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME`. These are exactly the inputs `Paths::from_env` reads (`src/state/paths.rs:37-65`): there is no flag and no `OMADDONS_*` variable that overrides the roots wholesale, so a child started under a different environment would see a different omaddons. Overlaying the context makes every widget command act on the state that installed it.

#### 2.5 `classifyCliArgv(argv) -> {ok, path, mutates, destructive, binds, reason}` and `cliArgv(argv, opts)`

(The plan's signature returns `{ok, path, mutates, destructive, reason}`. Adding `binds` is decided while writing this bead, because F2's runner adds `--if-match` to a confirmed CLI argv only when its path binds.)

The rules of M3-D2 (a). CLI output supplies argv in `error.fix_argv`, `error.alternatives[].argv`, `warnings[].fix_argv`, `commands[].argv`, `issues[].remediation.argv` and `last_change.undo.argv`. An entry qualifies only when the classifier accepts it:
- `argv[0]` is `omaddons`;
- the leading command words (every token before the first flag or `--`) form a path in `CLI_PATHS`;
- **no standard flag the widget owns** (`--json`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--progress`, `--if-match`, `--format`) appears anywhere before `--`, so a CLI-provided argv can never re-attribute itself or bypass a preview;
- `destructive` is reported from `CLI_PATHS`, so the runner sends a destructive path (including an `issues[].remediation.argv` with `destructive: true`) through the same preview and confirm flow as a destructive template (M3-D9). A destructive path that does not `bind` (`targets rm`) is confirmed from its dry run, or from the CLI's own command text when it has none, and then runs without `--if-match`.

An argv that fails any rule is shown as text with its command line, never as a button. `cliArgv(argv, opts)` builds the runnable `{argv, env}` from an accepted argv, substituting the binary for `omaddons` and inserting the same standard flags right after it (a `fix_argv` may itself contain `--`). Rejected (M3-D2, from review): trusting any argv that starts with `omaddons`, because a prefix proves which program runs, not what the command does or whether it is destructive.

#### 2.6 Compatibility

- `envelopeOk(env)`: a parseable envelope object with `schema_version`, `ok`, `command` (the exact key check is decided while writing this bead).
- `compatible(env, build)`: `schema_version` major is `1`, `tool_version` equals `build.TOOL_VERSION`, and `data.widget.outdated` is false **when present** (E4 adds `data.widget`; asset drift means the widget's templates may no longer match the binary). A false result puts the service into the read-only incompatible state of M3-D42 (F2 applies it).

#### 2.7 The scheduler's pure parts (M3-D11)

Every omaddons process the service starts is a **request** `{id, contextGeneration, target, resource, kind, priority, selection}`, run in one of three lanes:
- **mutation lane** (one at a time): every command that `mutates`, including the silent `backup_auto`. Queued user actions run before queued background ones, but nothing preempts a running mutation. The queue holds at most one background request per (resource, target), and at most one queued user mutation (a third replaces the queued one);
- **local read lane** (one at a time): `status`, `list`, `errors`, `backup list`. Requests coalesce by (resource, target): at most one queued per key, the newest replacing an older queued one. `status --cached` has priority and jumps the queue, because the bar depends on it and it takes milliseconds while an `errors` read can take seconds;
- **network read lane** (one at a time, at most 4 queued): `outdated`, `search`, `info --changelog`. A newer search replaces a queued older one.

The pure functions, which F2's QML only applies:
- `nextRequest(queues, lanesBusy)`: which queued request starts next in each free lane, by the rules above.
- `coalesceKey(request)`: the (resource, target) key used for coalescing and for "newer than the last applied".
- `acceptResult(request, lastApplied, currentSelection, contextGeneration)`: every result needs a current `contextGeneration`. Beyond that:
  - **data results** (`status`, `list`, `backup list`, and `errors` used for the bar) are applied when newer than the last result applied for the same key, by request id. A newer answer is never discarded just because an even newer request is still queued, so a busy lane cannot starve the bar;
  - **view-bound results** (`search`, `changelog`, an `errors` read for an expanded row) are applied only if their `selection` (the query text, the target filter, the expanded row) still equals the view's current one. A slow search for target A can never fill target B's view, or supply B's install buttons.
- `outcomeOf(exitCode, started, stdout, timedOut, cancelled)`: one of `ok`, `failed` (an envelope with `ok:false`), `timeout`, `cancelled`, `missing` (never `started`), `incompatible` (M3-D42), `malformed` (no parseable envelope) and `oversized` (stdout over `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`).

#### 2.8 Reducers (envelopes to view models)

`reduceStatus(env) -> { bar, targets, summary, lastChange, widget }`, with `bar = { badge, urgent, dimmed, spinning, tooltip[] }`:
- `badge` is `summary.updates.available` (hidden at 0);
- `urgent` is `summary.state` `attention` or `errors`;

## Considerations

- **`Model.js` must stay engine-neutral JS:** no QML globals, ES2017 at most (Qt 6 V4 supports it), and `var`/`function` style like the house plugins. Its only exports are pure functions and data, so bun and QML get identical behaviour.
- **The template table is the safety boundary, and it is deliberately small.** Per-row argv arrays in every list (the literal reading of vision §5.11) were rejected: roughly 3 actions × 200 addons of JSON on every refresh, frozen at M4, for no safety gain. Building argv freely in QML was rejected as untestable, and a `omarchy commands --json` endpoint as one more contract surface for no gain (the template file is embedded in the same binary). M3-D2 refines vision §5.11 and is recorded as a departure by G2.
- **Templates land with their commands**; F1 must not pre-add `errors`, `backup` or `restore` templates, because the registry check fails on unknown paths by design. The same holds for `CLI_PATHS` rows.
- **Collision hot spots.** No row of the §11.4 table (milestone epic delivery comment) names F1 except `README.md` (everyone; each task edits only its own section, G1 reconciles). Other shared files: `scripts/gate.sh` and `Argcfile.sh` are changed only here in M3 (module map, §6.5); `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` is extended by E1 (asset set) and F7 (scans). Any command task landing after F1 must add its `CLI_PATHS` row, so coordinate with B6, B8, D1, D2, D4, D8, D9, D10, D13, E2 and E3 (each adds a path).
- **Risks** (milestone risks comment, §12.1): risk 22, "the widget acts on a different omaddons state than the terminal (an XDG difference)" (L–M / M), is mitigated here by `buildArgv` always returning the stamped context as `env`; risk 14 (a keyboard slip runs a mutation) by the `confirm` flags that route destructive templates through the preview; risk 2 (duplicate processes on two monitors) is F2's, but the scheduler's pure parts are tested here first.
- **Critical path.** F1 is on the widget critical path, A2 → F1 → F2 → F3 → E1 → E2 → E3 → G1 → G2 → G3 (20 weighted units; S=1, M=2, L=3). Earliest start is t=3 (after A2, an L, and F0); F2 starts at t=5 when F1 ends. Unit arithmetic is sequencing guidance, not a delivery estimate. 14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

acceptance_criteria: bun test passes over real-binary fixtures for status (attention, updates, idle; F6 adds errors), list, search and a failure envelope; the pipeline (write_widget_fixtures, bun test, validate_built_argv, then qmltestrunner over a copy with the fixture Build.js when omarchy/ changed or with --all) passes from a clean checkout with no generated files present, nothing generated is committed, and .gitignore guards omarchy/tests/fixtures/ except the hand-written Build.js; the Rust validation parses exactly the argv bun emitted and fails when a template is broken (a template flipped to ["updat"] locally), when a flag lands after -- (planted), and when a hostile {addon} given as --addon {addon} in two elements is read as a flag (planted); classifyCliArgv rejects the planted argv (--actor agent, --json after the path, an unknown path, a destructive path without preview) and the Rust side agrees; a clap flag rename in src/cli.rs that a template uses fails the gate even though nothing under omarchy/ changed; CLI_PATHS equals the registry's paths and mutates flags and binds equals A4's list of --if-match paths (always-on test); WIDGET_NETWORK_DEADLINE_SEC passes its check against politeness.rs and WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES bounds every shipped template's worst-case fixture output; DEFAULT_SETTINGS equals manifest.json's defaults and setting falls back on missing, wrong-typed and out-of-range values; a missing bun, or a missing qmltestrunner when the QML step runs, fails the gate with the install message, and argc widget-test runs the same pipeline; manifest.json is exactly the specified manifest and the literal a44.omaddons appears in no other QML or JS file under omarchy/, the fixture Build.js included

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** The widget is how most people will meet omaddons from now on, and its credibility rests on one property: it never runs anything the user did not see and the CLI did not offer. This bead builds that boundary first, as data and pure functions that a test can exhaust: the fixed command templates, the classifier for CLI-provided argv, the flag placement, and the scheduler's decisions about which late answer may be shown. It also wires the widget tests into every gate, so a clap flag rename or an envelope change that would silently break the bar fails before commit instead of on the owner's desktop. Everything F2 to F9 build is a caller of this file, and checkpoint criteria 4, 5 and 11 are proven through it. It keeps the thesis honest on the desktop: the widget is a view of the CLI, with no logic of its own that could drift from the authority.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D2 (departure: refines vision §5.11): the widget runs argv arrays from two sources only.** CLI output (`fix_argv`, alternatives, `commands[]`, `issues[].remediation.argv`, `last_change.undo.argv`) qualifies only through `classifyCliArgv` (a known `CLI_PATHS` path, no widget-owned standard flag before `--`, destructive paths routed through the preview); everything else comes from the fixed `COMMANDS` table with typed, validated slots, positionals after `--` and option slots in the `--opt={slot}` single-element form. Standard flags go right after the binary. Why: vision §5.11 literally asks for per-row argv in every list, about 3 actions × 200 addons on every refresh, frozen at M4, for no safety gain; the real property is "nothing is shell-parsed, and nothing the user did not see runs". Rejected: per-row argv arrays; building argv freely in QML (untestable, drifts); a `omarchy commands --json` endpoint (one more surface for no gain); trusting any argv that starts with `omaddons` (a prefix proves the program, not the command or whether it is destructive).
- **M3-D10 (departure): six widget settings, defaults duplicated in `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`.** Omarchy 4.0.6 ignores manifest defaults. `checkIntervalHours` and `defaultTarget` were dropped from the vision's list because `config.toml` already owns them; two knobs for one interval would disagree.
- **M3-D11: the scheduler's lanes, coalescing, request identity and acceptance rules,** written here as pure functions so bun covers the state machine's decisions. Why: request identity is what keeps a keyboard UI honest when results arrive late; data results are applied when newer, view-bound results only when they still match the selection. Rejected: a separate background lane for silent mutations; a general job system or daemon.
- **M3-D41: widget tests run in the gate as one ordered pipeline** (envelopes, bun, Rust argv check, QML over a copy with a fixture `Build.js`), with every artifact generated fresh into `$OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT`. Steps 1–3 run on every gate because a CLI change can break the widget. Rejected (review): running the Rust argv check inside `cargo test` before bun produced its input, and re-substituting slots in Rust, which tests a second implementation instead of the real one.
- **M3-D42: `compatible(env, build)`** (schema major 1, `tool_version` match, `widget.outdated` false) defines the read-only incompatible state F2 enforces.
- **M3-D46: `binds` marks the five `--if-match` paths,** checked against A4's list; `buildArgv` inserts a token only for those. Why: a stateless token is the smallest contract that makes a confirm dialog mean what it says. Rejected (M3-D46): stored plans in M3; a per-command `--expect-*` flag set; a time-limited token (staleness is about state, not time).
- **M3-D7: `buildArgv` returns the stamped context as `env`,** so every omaddons child resolves the installing run's `<config>`, `<state>` and `<cache>`. Rejected: relying on PATH or the shell's own XDG environment (the badge would never update, or the widget would act on a second, empty state).
- **M3-D37 (context):** the reducers consume `summary`, `issues[]`, `last_change` and `last_change_state` from A2; an `unknown` last change is shown as unknown, never as "nothing to undo".

**Review-round changes folded in.** Round 1 moved the standard flags before the command words (appended after `--`, clap read them as positionals; reproduced). Round 2's reviewer ran every widget template against the debug binary with hostile slot values; all parsed, with values arriving as positionals, which this bead's tests now pin permanently. Round 3: revision 19 added the CLI argv classifier (replacing trust in an `omaddons` prefix) and the single plain-text component `PlainLabel.qml`; revision 18 adopted the three-lane scheduler with request identity, whose pure decisions this bead holds, and bounded output size on the CLI side because Quickshell cannot cap a single line as it arrives; revision 22 ordered the widget pipeline so the Rust check reads exactly what bun built, from a clean checkout (M3-D41 records the first draft's two faults). The `--opt={slot}` single-element form for option slots and the planted two-element `--addon {addon}` case are part of the final design; the planning record does not attribute them to a specific revision.

**Facts verified during planning.** `COMMANDS` registry at `src/app/mod.rs:109-138` and `app::mutates` treating unknown paths as mutating (`src/app/mod.rs:142-147`); global flags `global = true` at `src/cli.rs:49-111`; the envelope is one compact line (`src/output/mod.rs:266`); progress NDJSON shape (`src/output/stderr.rs:312-329`) and `--progress json` under `--json` (`src/output/term.rs:124-157`); politeness constants (`src/politeness.rs:20-33`: `API_READ_TIMEOUT` 30 s, `MAX_RETRIES` 3, `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` 60 s); `Paths::from_env` reads `HOME` and the four XDG roots with no override flag (`src/state/paths.rs:37-65`); `scripts/gate.sh` structure and README's stated gate prerequisites; the hey plugin's `require`-able `Model.js` and `qmltestrunner` harness on this machine; Omarchy 4.0.6 ignores manifest defaults (all as of `af10e34` and the 2026-10-21 desktop).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- A template silently stops parsing after a CLI change: the Rust check parses bun's exact output on every gate, and a planted broken template proves the check bites.
- A hostile slot value is read as a flag: positionals after `--`, option slots in one element, and planted hostile cases in both bun and Rust.
- The widget acts on another omaddons state (risk 22): `env` is always the stamped context.
- A CLI-provided fix re-attributes itself or skips a preview: the classifier forbids widget-owned flags and reports `destructive`.
- `Model.js` grows QML-only code and breaks bun: the engine-neutral, ES2017, `var`/`function` rule and the guarded export.

**Confidence.** Medium-high: the logic is small, pure and tested against envelopes the real binary emits in every gate (milestone rationale comment, §13.2: "the widget holds no product logic"), and the harness is proven on this machine; the residual risk is Qt's V4 engine differing from bun on an edge of ES2017, which the QML step's smoke test catches.

comments.text:
Handoff from A2 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.2, landed): the wire the widget reads from `status --cached --json`.

What:
- `data.summary.state`: `attention | errors | updates | idle`, the bar icon's state.
- `data.summary.issues.{p0,p1,p2,p3}`, `updates.{available,targets}`, `running[]`, `check_due`.
- `data.targets[].issues[]`: `{id, severity: "P0".."P3", title, addon|null, remediation: {command, argv|null, destructive}}`. `argv: null` means advice: show `command` as text and offer no button. `destructive: true` needs confirmation.
- `data.last_change` (`run, kind, at, actor, reason, targets[], changes{added,replaced,removed,recorded,restored}, undo{command, argv}`) and `data.last_change_state: ok | unknown`.
Why: under `--cached`, `unknown` never means there is nothing to undo. The history projection was missing or stale, or could not tell.
How:
- Show "last change unknown" and offer no "Undo last". The next changing command rebuilds the projection and rings the doorbell when it rewrote it, so the next doorbell refresh resolves it.
- "Undo last" runs `last_change.undo.argv`. It names the run (`undo --run <id>`), so it reverts what was shown even if another run committed in between (E2E-tested).
Risks: `null` `last_change` with `ok` is a fresh or undo-less home, and should look idle rather than unknown.
Done when: `Model.js` maps these keys, with a fixture taken from a real `status --cached --json`.

title: Spike, verifying Quickshell facts on the development machine
description:
## Background

The M3 widget is an Omarchy bar plugin (a Quickshell QML plugin) that renders the omaddons CLI. Its whole architecture rests on facts about Omarchy 4.0.6, Quickshell 0.3.2, Qt 6.12.0 and Hyprland 0.56.2 that the planning agent gathered by **reading Omarchy's and Quickshell's source** on the development machine, plus one headless `Process` probe. Nothing has yet been observed on the live shell. Eight of those facts decide how F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) and F2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2`) are built, and each is cheap to check before any production QML exists. If one of them is wrong, finding out now costs a 100-line throwaway plugin; finding out after F2 (an L-sized state machine) costs a redesign.

The facts, as recorded in the milestone epic's ground-truth comment (§2.5, "The Omarchy plugin system on the development machine"), plus the placement rule of M3-D8 (last bullet, which is a decision, not a §2.5 fact):

- **The development machine has two monitors**, so the bar, and every bar-widget item, exists twice. A `service` plugin entry is mounted **once** per shell and receives `shell`, `manifest` and the registries but **no settings**; bar widgets receive `bar` (a `PluginBarApi` facade), `moduleName` and `settings`, and find the service with `bar.shell.serviceFor(id)`, falling back to a `.pragma library` store (the notification-center, hey and ntfy plugin pattern).
- **Only one `IpcHandler` per target works.** A second one logs "Handler was registered but will not be used". With two monitors, a per-widget handler is only half-registered, which is why the shared service owns IPC (M3-D5).
- **Hot reload.** Omarchy runs `inotifywait -m -r` on `<plugins>`; any file event under a plugin dir reloads every plugin widget on the bar (built-ins included); only top-level dot-entries and `.git` are excluded. So `inotifywait` is guaranteed present on Omarchy, and a plugin must never write runtime files into its own dir (M3-D3).
- **Every omaddons write is a temp file plus rename** (`src/fsx/sys.rs:132-160`, as of `af10e34`), so a watcher on the doorbell file's inode loses it after the first write; a **directory** watch is needed (M3-D4). Whether Quickshell's `FileView { watchChanges: true }` survives external renames is UNVERIFIED.
- **Processes.** `Quickshell.Io.Process` takes an argv array; `environment` merges with the inherited environment (`clearEnvironment` exists too). A missing binary emits **no `exited`**, only `runningChanged(false)` and a log warning. `running = false` sends **SIGTERM and nothing more**: there is no kill escalation, `signal(9)` kills the pid only (not its group), and destroying the object (a reload) kills with SIGKILL, so "stopped" is not "exited". `startDetached()` applies `environment` and the working directory, sends stdio to the null device, and gives no pid or exit status. `Quickshell.execDetached([...])` takes an argv only. A `SplitParser` on stderr delivers NDJSON line by line (verified headless). **Neither collector is bounded**: `StdioCollector` appends everything to one buffer, and a `SplitParser` grows without limit until its delimiter arrives.
- **Hyprland raw events.** `openwindow>>ADDR,WS,CLASS,TITLE` and `closewindow>>ADDR` arrive through `Quickshell.Hyprland`'s `rawEvent` (the first-party idle service uses them). Omarchy's Battle.net rule says every window of that Proton prefix has class `steam_app_battlenet`, UNVERIFIED for the game window itself.
- **Notifications.** The shell is the notification daemon (no mako, dunst or swaync). `omarchy-notification-send [--app-name A] [-g glyph] [-u low|normal|critical] <title> [body] [--exec program args…]` sets an `omarchy-exec-argv` hint, so a click on the toast runs an argv. Panels are opened from outside with `omarchy-shell shell toggle <id>`; the plan uses `summon` (opens, never closes) for toasts (M3-D14).
- **The keyboard panel** (`qs.Ui` `KeyboardPanel` + `PanelKeyCatcher`) reserves Esc, Tab/Shift-Tab (Tab moves to the neighbouring bar panel), `j`/`k`/`h`/`l` and the arrows (`moveRequested(dx,dy)`), Enter, Space and `x` (`deleteRequested`); other letters arrive as `textKey`. In-panel views must switch on `h`/`l`, as the first-party agents panel does.
- **Manifest `defaults` and `schema` are inert** in Omarchy 4.0.6; `omarchy plugin enable` writes only `{ "id": "<id>" }` into `<config-omarchy>/shell.json`, and disabling deletes the entry, inline settings included.
- **Placement.** M3-D8 enables the widget with Omarchy's own `omarchy-bar put <id> --section <s>`, which retries while the shell is still rescanning (its `ask_to_put` loop), instead of a racy `enablePlugin` that can hit an unknown-widget error during the asynchronous `rescanPlugins` (`shell.qml:1607`).

This task is a spike: it observes each fact on the live desktop and records the evidence before F1 and F2 start. It serves G-M3-1 (glanceable: the widget must be right on two monitors) and G-M3-2 (one-click actions that are never surprising), and it de-risks checkpoint criteria 1 (one service instance and one IPC handler on two monitors), 2 (doorbell latency and running-state tracking) and 4 (widget states). It also establishes whether an agent can launch the 3.3.5a client to its login screen, which decides whether checkpoint criterion 2's running-state check runs or records one of the pre-accepted `SKIP`s.

Decisions this spike verifies or feeds:
- **M3-D4** (one doorbell file, `<cache>/doorbell.json`, watched by directory with `inotifywait`): the spike proves a directory watch delivers one line per fsx-style write, and records whether `FileView` would also work (it stays an option; M3-D4 uses `inotifywait` either way).
- **M3-D5** (one shared `service` + `bar-widget` plugin, so one service per shell even with two monitors): the spike proves there is one instance and one working `IpcHandler`.
- **M3-D11** (the scheduler's deadlines: SIGTERM, then `signal(9)` after a grace period, with the lane kept busy until `runningChanged(false)`; completion on `exited` **and** stream end): the spike measures the real timings and ordering.
- **M3-D13** (Hyprland `openwindow`/`closewindow` are a doorbell, no class filter): the spike confirms the events arrive.
- **M3-D14** (toasts carry `--exec omarchy-shell shell summon a44.omaddons {}`): the spike records the exact `summon` payload form that opens, not toggles.
- **M3-D7** (every omaddons child gets the stamped `HOME`/XDG context through `Process.environment`, and the self-reinstall uses `startDetached()` with it): the spike observes `environment` overlay on both `Process` and `startDetached()`.

## Technical Approach

Build a **throwaway plugin** at `<plugins>/omaddons-spike/` with id `a44.omaddons-spike`, kinds `service` + `bar-widget` (entry points `Service.qml` and `BarWidget.qml`), about 100 lines in total. It is never committed to the repository; keep it in scratch and copy it into `<plugins>` only for the session. Check each of the following eight facts and record evidence for each.

1. **Service singleton.**
   - With two monitors there is exactly one service instance (log a counter or a creation timestamp from `Component.onCompleted`).
   - `bar.shell.serviceFor("a44.omaddons-spike")` returns that instance in **both** bar widgets (log an identity from each).
   - One `IpcHandler` registers, with **no** "Handler was registered but will not be used" line in `qs log`.
   - `omarchy-shell a44.omaddons-spike ping` answers.
2. **The doorbell.**
   - Run `inotifywait -m -q -e close_write,moved_to --format %f <cache dir of a throwaway HOME>` in a `Process` with a `SplitParser`, and show it delivers **one line per fsx-style write** (temp + rename). Produce the writes by running `omaddons` against a throwaway `HOME`/`XDG_*` (for example a `backup`-free read that rewrites the discovery cache, or any command that writes `<cache>`), so the owner's real state is untouched.
   - Also test whether `FileView { watchChanges: true }` on the file survives renames. Record the result. M3-D4 uses `inotifywait` either way; a working `FileView` only remains an option.
3. **Process behaviour.**
   - A missing binary gives `runningChanged(false)` **without** `exited`, so detection by "no `started`" or "no `processId`" works.
   - NDJSON on stderr arrives line by line through a `SplitParser`.
   - A 1 MB stdout is collected whole by `StdioCollector`.
4. **Hyprland.**
   - `Connections { target: Hyprland; function onRawEvent(e) { … } }` delivers `openwindow` and `closewindow` for a terminal window (log `e.name` and the payload).
   - If an agent can start the 3.3.5a client to its login screen (the same umu launch command used for the observation in vision bead comment 903), record the **class and title** of its window as `rawEvent` reports them, and whether `closewindow` fires on exit (the `closewindow` check is added while writing this bead). This decides whether checkpoint criterion 2's running-state check can run for real.
5. **Notifications.**
   - `omarchy-notification-send --app-name omaddons-spike -g … -u low "title" "body" --exec omarchy-shell shell summon a44.omaddons-spike {}` shows a toast.
   - Clicking it **opens (not toggles)** the spike's panel on the focused monitor, also when the panel is already open (the already-open case is added while writing this bead; it is what distinguishes `summon` from `toggle`).
   - Record the exact `summon` payload form that works (`{}` or otherwise). F2's IPC `show(view)` fallback and F8's toasts copy it.
6. **`PanelKeyCatcher`.** Whether `h`/`l` reach `moveRequested(dx)` with a `Flickable` inside the panel (F4's `PanelView.qml` is a `Flickable`). Also record that Space arrives as `activateRequested` and that `x` arrives as `deleteRequested` (these two observations are added while writing this bead; F4's key map relies on them).
7. **Bar placement.** `omarchy-bar put a44.omaddons-spike --section right` places it right after a `rescanPlugins`, retrying while the shell rescans. Also (added while writing this bead, because E2 parses these strings) record its stdout (M3-D8 expects exactly `a44.omaddons-spike is on the bar`), its stderr while the shell is still rescanning (M3-D8's retry trigger is stderr containing `is not a known widget`), and its exit code when the shell is not running (M3-D8 expects 0 with "omarchy-shell is not running …" on stderr). E2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2`) relies on these exact strings.
8. **Process environment and termination.** These facts were read from Quickshell's source during the third review; the spike observes them live:
   - a `Process` with `environment: {"XDG_CACHE_HOME": "<throwaway>"}` runs `env` with that value overlaid and everything else inherited;
   - `startDetached()` with the same `environment` applies it too (the child writes `env` to a throwaway file, since detached stdio goes to the null device);
   - `running = false` on a child that **traps SIGTERM** leaves it alive, and `signal(9)` then kills it. Record how long `runningChanged(false)` takes after each;
   - a **4 MB single-line** stdout arrives whole through `StdioCollector`, and `streamFinished` fires after `exited`, or record the order if it is the reverse (F2's completion rule is "`exited` **and** `streamFinished`, order-independent").

**Cleanup.**
- Before installing the spike, copy `<config-omarchy>/shell.json` to scratch.
- Afterwards, disable the spike (`omarchy-shell shell setPluginEnabled a44.omaddons-spike false`) and delete `<plugins>/omaddons-spike/`.
- Confirm that `shell.json` is **semantically** equal to the copy: same bar layout, same plugins, same settings (for example `jq -S` of both with the `version`/`plugins` bookkeeping keys compared separately). Omarchy re-serializes the file and may add `version`/`plugins` keys (`shell.qml:111-116`), so bytes can differ. Record the comparison.

**Recording.** One bead comment on this bead lists each of the eight facts as `fact N: <observed> · evidence: <log lines, IPC output, screenshot file names>`. Screenshots stay in scratch and are never committed. Then, for every fact that differs from the description above, add a `decided:` comment on F1 or F2 (whichever builds on it) **before** it is claimed, naming what changes in its design. Fact 5's payload form and fact 8's timings and ordering are always copied onto F2 as a comment, whether or not they differ (decided while writing this bead: F2's runner and `show(view)` fallback are written "per F0's finding", so F2 needs the recorded values, not only the differences).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A bead comment records each of the eight facts with evidence: log lines, IPC output, and screenshot file names (screenshots kept only in scratch, never committed).
- Any fact that differs from the description in this bead is filed as a decision update (`decided:` comment) on F1 or F2 before they start; fact 5's working `summon` payload form and fact 8's measured SIGTERM/SIGKILL timings and stream ordering are copied onto F2 in any case (decided while writing this bead).
- Whether an agent can launch the 3.3.5a client to its login screen is recorded, with the window's class and title when it can.
- `<config-omarchy>/shell.json` is semantically equal afterwards (bar layout, plugins, settings), and the comparison is recorded.
- `<plugins>/omaddons-spike/` no longer exists, and the spike id is disabled; nothing under `<plugins>` or the repository was left behind.

## Test Plan

This is a spike; its "tests" are the eight live observations, each scripted so it can be repeated:
- **Singleton and IPC:** `qs log` captured across a shell reload with the spike enabled, filtered for the spike's creation lines and for "will not be used"; `omarchy-shell a44.omaddons-spike ping` output.
- **Doorbell:** a loop that runs a cache-writing omaddons command against a throwaway `HOME`/`XDG_*` N times, counting `SplitParser` lines (expect N lines naming the file); a second run with a `FileView { watchChanges: true }` counting change signals.
- **Process:** a `Process` on a nonexistent path (log `started`, `exited`, `runningChanged`); a `Process` on a script that emits NDJSON lines with sleeps on stderr; a `Process` on a script that prints 1 MB, then 4 MB on a single line; a script that traps SIGTERM, with timestamps for `running = false`, `signal(9)` and each `runningChanged(false)`.
- **Environment:** `env` run through `Process` and through `startDetached()` with one overlaid variable, diffed against the shell's own environment.
- **Hyprland:** open and close a terminal; optionally launch the 3.3.5a client.
- **Notifications:** send a toast with `--exec … summon …`; click it with the panel closed and with it open.
- **Keys:** press `h`/`l`, Space and `x` in a panel containing a `Flickable`, logging the received signals.
- **Placement:** `omarchy-bar put` right after enabling (during rescan), after rescan, and with the shell stopped, capturing stdout, stderr and exit code.
- **Cleanup check:** a `jq -S` comparison of `shell.json` before and after.

## Considerations

- **This is a real-desktop change on the owner's machine.** It stays scoped to the spike id `a44.omaddons-spike` and the folder `omaddons-spike/`, and it is always cleaned up, even when a check fails partway. It never touches the owner's real omaddons state: every omaddons run uses a throwaway `HOME`/`XDG_*`.
- **If the shell cannot be reached** (no Wayland session available to the agent), the spike defers itself with `br defer <this id> --transition-comment "NEEDS OWNER: a desktop session · the spike observes the live Omarchy shell, which no agent can reach without one · the answer confirms or corrects the facts F1 and F2 are built on"`. That is the only way it blocks; while it is deferred, F1 (and everything after it on the widget path) stays blocked.
- **Launching the 3.3.5a client** is optional. If it cannot be done by an agent, record that; checkpoint criterion 2's running-state check then records a `SKIP` from the plan's pre-accepted list ("a running game client, when no client can be launched by an agent"). Never launch or touch the Forever client.
- **Risks addressed** (from the risks comment on the milestone epic, §12.1):
  - Risk 1, "Omarchy changes its plugin API (it ships often; 4.0.6 today)" (likelihood M, impact H): this spike verifies on the live shell; the widget then uses a small surface (`Panel`, `WidgetButton`, `KeyboardPanel`, `PanelKeyCatcher`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Button`, `BorderSurface`; `serviceFor`, `summon`), IPC `state()` makes breakage detectable by an agent, and a fallback poll covers a dead watcher.
  - Risk 16, "`PanelKeyCatcher` reserved keys differ from the reading of Omarchy's source" (L/L): fact 6 verifies them; F4 keeps the key map in one function.
  - Risk 2, "duplicate processes or toasts with two monitors" (H if done naively): fact 1 proves the one-service model before F2 relies on it.
- **Delivery.** Slice `slice-1` ("See and update from the bar": A1, A2, A4, F0, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, E1, E2, E3, E4). The slice's exit demo is `omarchy install` on the desktop; the badge following a terminal `update` within 1 s; updating one addon from the panel and undoing it; a `remove` preview gone stale giving `plan_stale`; and a reinstall swapping atomically. This spike is not on a critical path (it runs at t=0–1 in the widget lane, and F1 waits for A2 until t=3), so it can run first thing; lane 1 (the widget agent) then takes C1 while A2 lands.
- **No code, fixture or snapshot changes** land from this task, so the gate does not apply to it; it still follows the bead rules.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- none

**Unblocks:**
- F1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1` (The widget scaffold: manifest, `Model.js`, `Store.js`, `PlainLabel.qml`, tests, the gate pipeline): F1's scheduler pure functions (`outcomeOf`, completion on exit and stream end), its process-environment model (`buildArgv` returns `env: Build.CONTEXT`) and its manifest (one `service` + `bar-widget` plugin) rest on facts 1, 3 and 8; any difference is recorded on F1 before it starts.

F2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2`) inherits these facts through F1: its runner (deadlines, TERM then KILL, completion), its doorbell watcher, its IPC owner and its `summon` fallback all use what this spike records, and facts 5 and 8 are copied onto F2 directly.

Parent: the F epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6`. Delivery slice: `slice-1`.
acceptance_criteria: A bead comment records each of the eight facts (service singleton and one IpcHandler on two monitors; the directory doorbell watch delivering one line per temp-plus-rename write, and whether FileView survives renames; missing binary gives runningChanged(false) without exited, NDJSON stderr arrives line by line, 1 MB stdout collected whole; Hyprland openwindow/closewindow; the toast --exec summon payload that opens rather than toggles; PanelKeyCatcher h/l with a Flickable; omarchy-bar put placement after rescanPlugins with its stdout, stderr and exit code; Process environment overlay for Process and startDetached, SIGTERM-trapping child survives running = false and dies on signal(9) with runningChanged timings, a 4 MB single-line stdout arrives whole and the exited/streamFinished order) with evidence (log lines, IPC output, screenshot file names kept only in scratch); any fact that differs from this bead's description is recorded as a decided: comment on F1 or F2 before they start, and fact 5's payload form and fact 8's timings and ordering are copied onto F2 in any case (decided while writing this bead); whether an agent can launch the 3.3.5a client to its login screen is recorded, with its window class and title when it can; <config-omarchy>/shell.json is semantically equal afterwards (layout, plugins, settings) and the comparison is recorded; the spike folder is deleted and its id disabled, leaving nothing under <plugins> or in the repository
