comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** These two views are where the badge turns into action: see which addons are behind on which client, update one or all, read the release notes on demand, pin, repair a modified addon, remove one with a preview that cannot drift from what runs. They are what makes "3 updates, one click" true, and they do it without a line of product logic: rows are reduced envelopes, actions are tested templates, text is plain. Every change is an omaddons command line the user could have typed, attributed `--actor widget`, undoable from the same panel. The slice-1 demo (update from the panel, undo it, a stale `remove` preview refused) runs through this task.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D2: argv from two sources only** (classified CLI output, or the `COMMANDS` templates with typed slots), standard flags first, positionals after `--`. Why: nothing is shell-parsed, and nothing the user did not see runs; templates are visible, tested and tiny. Rejected: per-row argv arrays in every `list` (heavy contract, frozen at M4); building argv freely in QML (untestable, drifts); a `omarchy commands` endpoint (one more surface for no gain); trusting any argv that starts with `omaddons`.
- **M3-D9: destructive actions preview first; updates, installs and pins do not.** `remove` deletes folders, so it is previewed; updates are undoable and expected. Rejected: stored plans in M3; no preview; a preview with no binding; binding by target generation alone.
- **M3-D46: the confirmed `remove` is bound to its preview** with `--if-match`, and `plan_stale` reloads the dialog. Rejected: a per-command `--expect-*` flag set; a time-limited token (staleness is about state, not time).
- **M3-D11: lanes and view-bound results.** `list` on the local read lane, `changelog` on the network lane and applied only if the selection still matches; mutations one at a time.
- **M3-D3: the widget never writes a file;** external links open only through `omarchy-launch-browser` behind `isSafeUrl`.

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 1: the standard flags moved before the command words (appended after `--`, clap read them as positionals; reproduced).
- Round 3 (revision 7): `remove` from the panel is bound to its preview by a token; (revision 18) results are applied by request identity, so a late changelog cannot land under another row; (revision 19) `PlainLabel` for every CLI string.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- `--json`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--progress`, `--dry-run` are `global = true` (`src/cli.rs:49-111` as of `af10e34`), and README says every global option works before the command.
- `PanelKeyCatcher` reserves Esc, Tab/Shift-Tab, `j`/`k`/`h`/`l` and arrows, Enter, Space and `x` (`deleteRequested`); other letters arrive as `textKey` (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.5).
- `Quickshell.Io.Process` takes an argv array and merges `environment` with the inherited environment.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk 14 (a keyboard slip runs a mutation): `remove` and undo are confirmed and bound; everything else is undoable and attributed.
- A stale view after a terminal change: the doorbell (A1, F2) refreshes `status` and the open view within about a second.
- Untrusted changelog text: plain text, 400 characters, safe-URL links only.

**Confidence.** Medium, as the plan rates widget polish across Omarchy updates (an external API, mitigated by F0 and a small surface). The views themselves are straightforward, over F1's tested reducers and F2's runner.

title: The Issues and Search views
description:
## Background

The **Issues** view answers "what is wrong, and what do I do about it?" in one place: structured problems from `status` (`issues[]`, with severities and remediations), the Lua errors of the last sessions from `omaddons errors`, and the run warnings of the last status. The **Search** view finds and installs addons. Together they deliver the "after a play session: my UI is broken" workflow from the bar:

```text
Lua errors (retail, last session)
  DBM            3×  new   likely source · 12.1.14 → 12.1.15 available (may fix it)   [Update DBM]
    DBM-Core/DBM-Core.lua:1234: attempt to index a nil value (field 'x')
  WeakAuras      1×  new   likely source (custom code) · current
    WeakAuras/RegionTypes/Text.lua:88: custom error message (46 characters, hidden)   [Show details]
  1 error received from another player · not counted
[Dismiss]  (or press d)
```

- The DBM line is a Lua runtime template whose only variable part, `x`, is an identifier from DBM's code, so the CLI shows it in strict output. The WeakAuras message is free text an addon wrote and might hold anything (a player's name); it stays hidden until the user asks with **Show details** (`s`), which runs `errors -t retail --addon=WeakAuras --raw-details` and labels the result "may contain names; share with care".
- **Update DBM** runs the update. **Dismiss** runs `omaddons errors dismiss -t retail --if-match <token>`, where the token comes from the `errors` read the view shows, so a session that ended in between is never dismissed unseen: the CLI answers `plan_stale` and the view refreshes ("new errors arrived; review them"). The icon calms down. The dismissal lives in `<state>`, so clearing the cache does not bring the errors back as new.
- Users should feel: "It told me which addon, and the likely fix, without showing my friends' names."

The view renders what the CLI decided; it never decides privacy, attribution, newness or ownership itself:
- **Strict privacy by default** (M3-D21) is the CLI's contract on *kinds of text*: default output holds only code-derived text (the addon, file and line, Lua's and Blizzard's message templates whose variable parts are identifiers, counts, an opaque fingerprint). Custom messages, locals and chunk contents appear only with `--raw-details`. The widget shows strict output by default and raw details only on `s`, under an explicit label.
- **Received reports** (errors other players' BugSack sent, M3-D21) are listed apart, never counted as new, never notify and never cause a recommendation. The view shows only their count, with no action.
- **Attribution** (M3-D18) is "likely source" with a method and a confidence; the view shows the confidence as a dot and says "update available (may fix it)", never a promise.
- **Dismissal** (M3-D19) is durable user state, bound to the shown observation by the `errors` read's `dismiss.precondition` token (M3-D46).
- **Search installs only into a target the user chose.** In the All filter, Enter opens a target chooser listing the targets whose hint is `yes` or `likely`, preselecting none, so a compatibility hint is never silently promoted to a destination (review round 3, revision 20).

This task serves G-M3-2 (one-click fix, update, dismiss, install), G-M3-3 (Lua errors actionable, strict privacy by default), and checkpoint criteria 4 (the P0/P1 issue and new-Lua-errors states render), 6 (in the widget: no custom message text until `s`, received reports never counted, a dismissal bound to the shown observation), 7 (install BugGrabber from the Issues view) and 13 (`errors dismiss` binding). It is near-critical (slack 1).

## Technical Approach

### Inputs (all read-only reads, local lane unless noted)

- `status --cached -v` / `status -v` (from F2): `targets[].issues[]`, `targets[].errors` (B7: `capture`, `state`, `coverage`, `new`, `total`, `received`, `top[]`), `warnings[]`, `commands[]`.
- `errors --json` (template `errors`, or F8's `errors_target` for one target). Its data, per target, as B6 and B8 define it:

  ```json
  {"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M4…"},"capture":"buggrabber","coverage":"complete",
   "databases":[{"id":"db-1","account":"account 1","provider":"!BugGrabber","shape":"modern","session":48,"state":"complete","baseline":47,"acknowledged":null}],
   "summary":{"entries":11,"occurrences":23,"addons":3,"new":4,"matched":11,"shown":11,"uncertain":0,"no_time":0,"received":1},
   "addons":[{"addon":"DBM","managed":true,"folders":["DBM-Core"],"kind":"addon","version":"12.1.14",
              "latest":{"version":"12.1.15","status":"update_available"},"count":7,"new":3,"entries":2,
              "last_seen":{"at":"…","meaning":"last","tz":"explicit"},
              "errors":[{"fingerprint":"e:3f9a0c7d21b4e8aa","database":"db-1","origin":"local","message_kind":"lua_runtime",
                         "message":"attempt to index a nil value (field 'x')","location":"DBM-Core/DBM-Core.lua:1234",
                         "attribution":{"method":"first_addon_frame","confidence":"high"},
                         "stack":["DBM-Core/DBM-Core.lua:1234: in function 'X'"],"count":5,"sessions":2,"new":true,
                         "last_seen":{"at":"…","meaning":"last","tz":"explicit"},"type":"error"}]}],
   "dismiss":{"precondition":"pc1:5be1…","databases":1},"dismissed":null}
  ```

  - `kind` is `addon`, `library` (attributed to a library folder only), `blizzard` or `unknown`.
  - `message_kind` is `lua_runtime`, `blizzard` or `custom`; for `custom`, `message` is `null` and `message_chars` gives its length.
  - `type` is `error`, `event` (protected-call) or `warning` (`LUA_WARNING`).
  - `origin` is `local` or `received`; received entries appear only with `--received`, so the view uses the per-target `summary.received` count.
  - `--raw-details` adds `errors[].raw: {message, stack, locals, chunks}` (bounded, sanitized) and sets `data.raw_details: true`.
- `search --json` (template `search`, network lane).

### Templates this task adds (now that `errors` and `errors dismiss` exist, B6 and B8)

```js
"errors":         { "argv": ["errors", "--limit", "10"],                          "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
"errors_raw":     { "argv": ["errors", "--raw-details", "-t", "{target}", "--addon={addon}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
"dismiss_errors": { "argv": ["errors", "dismiss", "-t", "{target}"],              "mutates": true,  "bind": true },
```

Templates it uses from F1: `update_addon`, `search`, `install`:

```js
"search":         { "argv": ["search", "--limit", "20", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{query}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "network" },
"install":        { "argv": ["install", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{ref}"],         "mutates": true },
"update_addon":   { "argv": ["update", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],        "mutates": true },
```

- **Slots as option values are one element**, `--addon={addon}`, so an addon name beginning with `-` is still that option's value and never a flag (M3-D2). Positionals follow `--`. `{query}` is free text and allowed only in read-only templates (F1's `buildArgv` throws otherwise). `{ref}` is a ref from `search` output.
- **`bind: true`** (`dismiss_errors`): no dialog. The token is the `dismiss.precondition` of the `errors` read the view shows for that target, and F2's runner adds `--if-match <token>` (only for paths that `bind`). A `plan_stale` answer refreshes the view instead of retrying.
- **`errors dismiss` writes `<state>`**, so its template is `mutates: true`, runs in the mutation lane and is recorded in history (a `dismiss` settings line, M3-D19).
- **Reads this task adds to F2's sequence:** the `errors` read after `status_full` and `list` when the panel opens, and as the Issues view's switch-in read (if older than 10 s or stale after a doorbell). Templates land with their commands (M3-D2): `app::mutates` treats an unknown path as mutating, so an `errors` template added before `errors` existed would fail F1's check by design.

### 1. `omarchy/views/IssuesView.qml`

**Section 1, Problems.** `targets[].issues` from `status`, sorted by severity. Each row shows a P0–P3 chip, the title and the target. Enter runs `remediation.argv` through F2's `runCliArgv`: `Model.classifyCliArgv` first, then the confirm flow when the path is `destructive`. A prose remediation (argv `null`), or an argv the classifier rejects, shows as text with its command line, never as a button. The issue table the CLI emits (A2, E4):

| Attention / condition | Issue id | Severity | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `journal_pending` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` | P0 | prose ("quit the game if it is running, then run any change command"), or the README troubleshooting pointer for manual repair (argv null) |
| `state_version_newer` | `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` | P0 | prose: "upgrade omaddons" |
| `addon_folder_missing` (per addon) | `fm-state_files-record-folder-missing` | P1 | `install <addon> -t <id> --reinstall` |
| `addon_modified` (per addon) | `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` | P2 | `install <addon> -t <id> --reinstall` |
| `addon_degraded` (per target, with count) | `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` | P2 | `list -t <id> -v` |
| `target_missing` | `fm-userland_state-target-vanished` | P2 | `targets rm <id>` (destructive: confirmed; it does not bind, so it runs without `--if-match`) |
| widget hash mismatch | `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` | P3 | `omarchy install` |

The classifier's rules (M3-D2 (a)): `argv[0]` is `omaddons`; the leading command words form a path in `CLI_PATHS`; no standard flag the widget owns (`--json`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--progress`, `--if-match`, `--format`) appears before `--`; a `destructive` path goes through the preview and confirm flow (a destructive path that does not bind, `targets rm`, is confirmed from its dry run, or from the CLI's own command text when it has none, and then runs without `--if-match`).

**Section 2, Lua errors** (from `errors --json`):
- per target, addon rows with `count`, a `new` chip, "likely source" with the attribution's confidence as a dot (`high`, `medium`, `low`), and "update available (may fix it)" when `latest.status` is `update_available`;
- each error's line shows the `location` and, for `lua_runtime`/`blizzard`, the `message`; for `custom`, "custom message (N characters)" from `message_chars`. Everything goes through `PlainLabel`;
- Enter → `update_addon` when an update is available, else expand the row to its strict stack lines (`stack`, at most 6 by default from the CLI);
- `s` → `errors_raw` for that addon (target and addon slots), shown in an expander headed "raw details: may contain other players' names and your own code". This read is **view-bound** (M3-D11): applied only if the same row is still expanded when it returns;
- `d` → `dismiss_errors` for the selected target (or, with no target selected, for each target with new errors, one call per target, because `--if-match` requires exactly the token's target set), bound to the shown observation (`bind: true`). A `plan_stale` refreshes the section with "new errors arrived; review them";
- a target with `capture: none` shows "BugGrabber is not installed: Install", where Enter runs that target's `commands[]` entry with action `install_buggrabber` (through the classifier), or, when the catalog knows no build for that client family (C3's disjoint variants), "no BugGrabber build for this client is known" with no action;
- a per-target "N errors received from other players (not counted)" line, with no action;
- a target in `partial` state (`errors.state: "partial"`) shows "incomplete read (the game may be writing)". The view never reruns a read for `partial` (F8's refresh rule).

**Section 3, run warnings** from the last status (`journal_pending` and similar), with their `fix_argv` through the classifier. A manual-repair reason (`details.reason` `unexpected_state`, `journal_unreadable`, `journal_too_new` or `preservation_incomplete`) shows its README pointer as text.

### 2. `omarchy/views/SearchView.qml`

- A `TextField`; Enter runs `search` on the network lane (a newer search replaces a queued older one, M3-D11). Results show name, source, popularity and the per-target hint (`yes`, `likely`, …).
- **The search result is view-bound:** applied only if the query text and target filter still match the view's current selection, so a slow search for target A can never fill target B's view or supply B's install buttons.
- **Enter installs into the explicitly selected target** (template `install`, `{ref}` from the result). In the "All" filter, Enter first opens a target chooser listing the targets whose hint is `yes` or `likely` (others greyed, with their hint), **preselecting none**, so a hint is never promoted to a destination silently.
- Results with hint `no`, `unlikely` or `abandoned` show the hint and no install action for that target. That matches the CLI's own `commands` rule.
- **The All filter searches every client with a second template (decided when the beads were filed).** The `search` template (above, from F1's table) always passes `-t {target}`, and `search` reports hints only for the clients it selected (`world.select_many`, `src/app/search.rs:285` as of `af10e34`); without `-t` it selects every target. So this task adds one read-only template, `"search_all": { "argv": ["search", "--limit", "20", "--", "{query}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "network" }`, used when the target filter is All; a single-target filter keeps `search`. One request instead of one per client keeps the network lane free and gives every client's compatibility hint in one envelope. The template extends the `COMMANDS` table, so F1's Rust test parses it with hostile `{query}` values, F7's checks cover it, and `search_all` is a wire name to list for G2.
- `/` (F4's key map) focuses the field; while it has focus, `PanelKeyCatcher` is blocked (`blocked: searchField.activeFocus`); Esc leaves it.

### 3. Fixtures

Regenerate the bun fixtures, through F1's `write_widget_fixtures` (generated into `$OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT/fixtures/`, never committed), for: `errors` strict, raw, received and partial; `errors dismiss` with `plan_stale`; and a `status` whose `summary.state` is `errors`. F1's template test covers the new templates unchanged (hostile slot values for `{addon}` and `{target}`).

### 4. QML tests

In `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_views.qml` (the views' QML test file; mocks under `omarchy/tests/qml/imports/`). For each section, including the stale dismissal, the raw-details expander label, the received line with no name, the `capture: none` Install row, the `partial` line, a classifier-rejected remediation shown as text, a destructive remediation going through the confirm flow, and the All-filter target chooser (no preselection; greyed targets).

### 5. README

The Omarchy widget section documents the Issues and Search views, `s` and `d`, and the "may contain names" label (common rule 11; the section is created by E2, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2`, and G1 reconciles. The spec names no README step for this task; this item is decided while writing this bead).

### Files

New: `omarchy/views/IssuesView.qml`, `omarchy/views/SearchView.qml`, QML tests in `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_views.qml`. Changed: `omarchy/Model.js` (the four templates: `errors`, `errors_raw`, `dismiss_errors` and `search_all`; any reducer additions in `reduceErrors`/`reduceSearch` with bun tests), `omarchy/Service.qml` (the `errors` read in the panel-open and switch-in sequences), `src/omarchy/assets.rs` (two embedded files), `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (fixture scenarios), README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At G3: dismiss errors from the panel on a fixture home (a `HOME`-isolated shell run, or real errors if available).
- At G3: install BugGrabber from the Issues view on a non-Forever client, choosing the target explicitly from the All view, then undo.
- On a fixture home, the Issues view shows no custom message text until `s` is pressed, and never a name in the received line.
- A dismissal after a new session ended (the observation changed between read and dismiss) gives `plan_stale`, refreshes the section with "new errors arrived; review them", and acknowledges nothing.
- The raw-details expander is labelled "raw details: may contain other players' names and your own code", and a late raw read for a row no longer expanded is dropped.
- A remediation argv the classifier rejects is shown as text, never as a button; a destructive one runs only through the confirm flow.
- Search in the All filter never picks a target implicitly; hints `no`, `unlikely` and `abandoned` offer no install.
- The three new templates pass F1's Rust argv validation with hostile slot values (`--addon={addon}` arrives as the option's value even for a leading `-`).
- QML and bun tests pass in the gate; the two view files are embedded.
- In the All filter, a search runs the `search_all` template (no `-t`) once and renders every client's hint from that one envelope; with one target selected it runs `search` with `-t`. Both templates parse in F1's Rust test with hostile `{query}` values.

## Test Plan

- **QML (qmltestrunner, the gate's step 4; `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_views.qml`):** the cases in section 4, with F2's mocks; the `Process` mock asserts each built argv (template, slots, `--if-match` only for `dismiss_errors`).
- **bun (`omarchy/tests/model.test.js`):** `reduceErrors` over the strict, raw, received and partial fixtures (no custom text in the strict model; received only as a count); `reduceSearch` hints; the All-filter chooser's eligible targets.
- **Rust (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs`):** new fixture scenarios in `write_widget_fixtures`; `validate_built_argv` covers `errors`, `errors_raw`, `dismiss_errors` unchanged.
- **Privacy:** the fixture home plants adversarial names (`FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm`, `FakeChar` and names inside custom messages and chunks); the reduced view models and the rendered strict rows contain none of them until `s`.
- **Real machine (G3):** the dismiss and install-then-undo passes above, on a non-Forever client.
- QML (`tst_views.qml`): the All filter dispatches `search_all` exactly once per query and a single-target filter dispatches `search`; a stale result for a superseded query is dropped (request identity, M3-D11).

## Considerations

- **The view never sees what it must not show.** It renders the strict envelope; free text arrives only in the `errors_raw` result, displayed under its label. No error-model field ever reaches a notification (F8, M3-D14) or a template slot other than `{addon}`/`{target}`.
- **`d` with no target selected** issues one `dismiss_errors` per target with new errors, each with its own target's token, because a token covers exactly its target set.
- **Search `{query}` is free text**, so it is confined to the read-only `search` template, positional after `--`.
- **Risks (from the risk register: milestone epic comment "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol (§12)", §12.1):** risk 13 (personal data leaks through `errors` or any channel): strict output by default, raw details only on `s` with a label, received reports as counts. Risk 6 (attribution blames the wrong addon): the view shows "likely source", the confidence dot and "may fix it". Risk 21 (a preview no longer describes what runs): the dismissal is bound to the shown observation. Risk 14 (a keyboard slip): `d` is bound, installs are undoable.
- **Collision hot spots:** `README.md` (everyone: each task edits only its own section; G1 reconciles); `omarchy/Service.qml` (the milestone's table lists F2 and F8 with the rule "F2 first; F8 adds signal handlers and templates only"; this task also edits it, adding only the `errors` read to the open and switch-in sequences, so coordinate with F8). Also shared, though not in that table: `omarchy/Model.js` (`COMMANDS` entries are added by F6, F8 and F9; append within the marked block); `omarchy/views/IssuesView.qml` is later edited by F9 (adds `r`).
- **Near-critical** (slack 1): F7 waits on this task.
- **Delivery slice `slice-2` (capture and diagnose).** Exit demo, recorded on the milestone epic when the slice's last task closes: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; **the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal**. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 6, 7, 8 (create, auto, verify) and 13 (`errors dismiss`, `backup prune`). This task supplies the bolded step.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- B7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7` (Errors in `status`): `targets[].errors` (`capture`, `state`, `new`, `received`, `top`) and `summary.errors`, which the Issues view and its `summary.state: errors` fixture render.
- B8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.8` (`errors dismiss`, durable acknowledgement): the `errors dismiss` command, its `--if-match` binding and `plan_stale` refusal, and the `errors` read's `dismiss.precondition`, which `d` runs.
- C3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3` (BugGrabber in the catalog: disjoint family variants): the `install_buggrabber` recommendation for `capture: none` targets and the "no BugGrabber build for this client is known" case.
- F4 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.4` (The panel frame, `PanelView.qml`): the content `Loader`, the key dispatch, the footer, the confirm dialog and the read-only state.

**Unblocks:**
- F7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.7` (Widget security and contract checks): its rendering, provenance, slot and preview scans run over these views and templates.

The `errors` command itself (B6) reaches this task through B7 and B8. F9 later edits `IssuesView.qml` to add `r`.

Parent: the F epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6`. Delivery slice: `slice-2`.
acceptance_criteria: At G3, dismiss errors from the panel on a fixture home (a HOME-isolated shell run, or real errors if available); at G3, install BugGrabber from the Issues view on a non-Forever client, choosing the target explicitly from the All view, then undo; on a fixture home the Issues view shows no custom message text until s is pressed and never a name in the received line; a dismissal after the observation changed gives plan_stale, refreshes the section with "new errors arrived; review them" and acknowledges nothing; the raw-details expander is labelled "raw details: may contain other players' names and your own code" and a late raw read for a row no longer expanded is dropped; a remediation argv the classifier rejects is shown as text, never as a button, and a destructive one runs only through the confirm flow; Search in the All filter never picks a target implicitly and hints no, unlikely and abandoned offer no install; the errors, errors_raw and dismiss_errors templates pass F1's Rust argv validation with hostile slot values (--addon={addon} arrives as the option's value even with a leading -); QML and bun tests pass in the gate and both view files are embedded; in the All filter a search runs the search_all template (no -t) once and renders every client's hint from that envelope, while a single-target filter runs search with -t.
