comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** "Why is my UI broken?" is the most common addon question, and the answer sits in a file nobody reads. B1–B8 turn it into `omaddons errors`; this view puts it in the bar, next to every other problem `status` knows, each with its fix one key away: update the likely culprit, install BugGrabber where it is missing, dismiss what was seen, or look at raw details only when the user asks and is told what they may contain. Search adds the other half of a manager's job, finding and installing, without ever choosing a client on the user's behalf. Nothing here decides privacy, attribution or newness; it renders what the CLI decided.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D21: privacy is a contract on kinds of text, on every channel.** Strict output by default; free text only via `--raw-details`, labelled; received reports apart and never counted. Rejected: the first draft's first-line-plus-pattern-redaction (cannot recognize names); hiding all message text (loses most diagnostic value); making `-v` the free-text switch.
- **M3-D19 and M3-D46: dismissal is durable user state, bound to the shown observation.** The `errors` read's `dismiss.precondition` is the token; `plan_stale` refreshes the view. Rejected: storing the dismissal in the cache memo; a `--dismiss` flag on a read command; per-fingerprint watermarks (BugGrabber writes only at session end, so session watermarks are exact).
- **M3-D18: attribution is "likely source" with method and confidence;** the view shows the confidence and "may fix it".
- **M3-D2: templates land with their commands; option slots are `--opt={slot}` in one element; CLI remediations pass the classifier.** Rejected: trusting any argv that starts with `omaddons` (a prefix proves which program runs, not what it does).
- **M3-D9: destructive remediations go through the preview flow.**
- **M3-D11: view-bound results** (search, raw details) apply only to the selection they were made for.
- **M3-D16 (context): disjoint BugGrabber variants;** a family with no verified build is told so, never offered another family's build.
- **M3-D20 (context): `partial` is never re-read on every doorbell.**

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 3 (revision 8): dismissal bound to the shown observation; (revision 9) received reports kept apart in every surface; (revision 10) the strict/raw split with templates kept in default output; (revision 19) the classifier for CLI argv and `PlainLabel`; (revision 20) explicit targets in Search's All view; F6 was split from F9 (the Backups view and restore chooser).

**Facts verified during planning.**
- BugSack stores errors received from other players in the same database, marked with a `source` key, so they land in the user's own current session unless separated (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.6).
- `PanelKeyCatcher` delivers other letters (`s`, `d`, `/`) as `textKey`; its `blocked` property disables keys while a text field has focus (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.5).
- `app::mutates` reads the `COMMANDS` row per path, which is why `errors dismiss` is a subcommand with its own `mutates: true` template.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk 13 (personal data leaks): the view consumes strict envelopes; raw text only on request, labelled; privacy fixtures with adversarial names.
- Risk 6 (wrong addon blamed): "likely" wording, a confidence dot, "may fix it".
- Risk 21 (a stale dismissal): the token; `plan_stale` refreshes rather than retries.
- Risk 14 (keyboard slip): `d` is bound; installs are undoable; destructive remediations are confirmed.

**Confidence.** Medium, as the plan rates widget polish across Omarchy updates (an external API, mitigated by F0 and a small surface). The view logic is thin over B6–B8's tested contract; real BugGrabber captures from a played session are not attempted (fixtures follow the public structure), which G3 records as a limitation.

title: Widget security and contract checks
description:
## Background

The widget's safety rests on a few structural rules, each enforced by one shared mechanism:
- **Argv only, from two sources** (M3-D2): every command the widget runs is either a `COMMANDS` template built by `Model.buildArgv`, or a CLI-provided argv (`fix_argv`, `alternatives[].argv`, `commands[].argv`, `remediation.argv`, `last_change.undo.argv`) accepted by `Model.classifyCliArgv`. Nothing is shell-parsed, and nothing the user did not see runs. Besides omaddons, exactly four literal tools run.
- **No file writes** (M3-D3): no `FileView.setText`, no `Util.execDetached` of shell strings; any write under the plugin dir would hot-reload every bar widget, and the CLI is the authority.
- **The stamped context** (M3-D7): every omaddons process gets `environment: Build.CONTEXT`, so the widget acts on exactly the state that installed it; the self-reinstall uses `startDetached()` with it.
- **Plain text for CLI strings** (M3-D21, M3-D2): every source-derived string renders through `PlainLabel.qml` (`Text.PlainText`), so an addon name or a release note can never inject rich text or links.
- **Previews for destructive actions** (M3-D9, M3-D46): `confirm` templates and destructive CLI paths run only through the preview flow.
- **Notifications carry names and counts only** (M3-D14, M3-D21).
- **One plugin id source** (`Build.PLUGIN_ID`, E1's debug `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` seam): a literal id in QML would make G3's isolated checkpoint widget share the real widget's service and IPC.

F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) built the mechanisms (the template table, the classifier, `PlainLabel`, the Rust argv validation over exactly the argv bun emitted). This task adds **scans that catch regressions**: lints over the widget's source that fail when any code path bypasses those mechanisms. The real guarantees come from the shared component and the classifier; the scans check that nothing goes around them. It runs last among the widget tasks, after every view and signal handler exists (F5, F6, F8, F9), so the scans cover the finished widget.

This task serves G-M3-2 (no surprising actions) and is the core evidence for checkpoint criterion 5 (argv-only execution: every argv from CLI output or the validated template table; CLI-provided argv pass the same classifier, not merely an `omaddons` prefix; no `bash -c` and no `Util.execDetached` in the widget, checked by a source scan; every source-derived string through `PlainLabel.qml`, checked by a source scan). It is on the restore critical path: … → F9 → **F7** → G1 → G2 → G3.

## Technical Approach

`omarchy/tests/security.test.js` (bun; the pattern of the hey plugin's `panel-security.test.js`, which scans plugin source files as text), plus checks in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`. The spec does not split the checks between the two files; putting the plugin-id literal (and the `Build.CONTEXT` rule, if easier to express there) in Rust is decided while writing this bead. The scans read every runtime file under `omarchy/` (`*.qml`, `*.js`, excluding `tests/`).

### The template table the scans cover (for reference; F1, F6, F8 and F9 built it)

```js
var COMMANDS = {
  "status":         { "argv": ["status", "--cached", "-v"],                         "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "status_full":    { "argv": ["status", "-v"],                                     "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "list":           { "argv": ["list", "-v"],                                       "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "errors":         { "argv": ["errors", "--limit", "10"],                          "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "errors_target":  { "argv": ["errors", "--limit", "10", "-t", "{target}"],        "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "errors_raw":     { "argv": ["errors", "--raw-details", "-t", "{target}", "--addon={addon}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "dismiss_errors": { "argv": ["errors", "dismiss", "-t", "{target}"],              "mutates": true,  "bind": true },
  "backups":        { "argv": ["backup", "list", "--limit", "50"],                  "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
  "changelog":      { "argv": ["info", "-t", "{target}", "--changelog", "--", "{addon}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "network" },
  "search":         { "argv": ["search", "--limit", "20", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{query}"], "mutates": false, "lane": "network" },
  "check":          { "argv": ["outdated"],                                         "mutates": false, "lane": "network" },
  "update_all":     { "argv": ["update"],                                           "mutates": true },
  "update_target":  { "argv": ["update", "-t", "{target}"],                         "mutates": true },
  "update_addon":   { "argv": ["update", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],        "mutates": true },
  "reinstall":      { "argv": ["install", "-t", "{target}", "--reinstall", "--", "{addon}"], "mutates": true },
  "remove":         { "argv": ["remove", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],        "mutates": true, "confirm": true },
  "pin":            { "argv": ["pin", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],           "mutates": true },
  "unpin":          { "argv": ["unpin", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{addon}"],         "mutates": true },
  "install":        { "argv": ["install", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{ref}"],         "mutates": true },
  "backup_target":  { "argv": ["backup", "create", "-t", "{target}"],               "mutates": true },
  "backup_all":     { "argv": ["backup", "create"],                                 "mutates": true },
  "backup_auto":    { "argv": ["backup", "create", "--auto", "-t", "{target}"],     "mutates": true, "silent": true },
  "restore":        { "argv": ["backup", "restore", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{backup}"], "mutates": true, "confirm": true },
  "restore_addon":  { "argv": ["backup", "restore", "-t", "{target}", "--addon={addon}", "--", "{backup}"], "mutates": true, "confirm": true },
  "prune_backup":   { "argv": ["backup", "prune", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{backup}"],   "mutates": true, "confirm": true }
}
```

- `CLI_PATHS` marks `destructive`: `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `targets rm`; and `binds` (accepts `--if-match`): `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `errors dismiss`.
- The classifier (M3-D2 (a)): `argv[0]` is `omaddons`; the leading command words (every token before the first flag or `--`) form a path in `CLI_PATHS`; no standard flag the widget owns (`--json`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--progress`, `--if-match`, `--format`) appears before `--`; a `destructive` path goes through the preview and confirm flow (a destructive path that does not bind, `targets rm`, is confirmed from its dry run or the CLI's command text, then runs without `--if-match`). An argv that fails any rule is shown as text, never as a button.
- The four literal tools (M3-D2): `inotifywait -m -q -e close_write,moved_to --format %f <Build.CACHE_DIR>`; `omarchy-notification-send …` (text as argv elements); `xdg-open <client_dir>/Interface/AddOns`, where `client_dir` comes from `status -v`; `omarchy-launch-browser <url>`, only when `Model.isSafeUrl` accepts it (`https:`; hosts `github.com`, `www.wowinterface.com`, `www.tukui.org`, `www.wowace.com`).

### The eight checks

1. **Rendering.** No `Text`, `Label` or `TextEdit` outside `PlainLabel.qml` binds to `modelData`, `svc.*`, `row.*` or `entry.*`. CLI-provided strings may reach the screen only through `PlainLabel`. `PlainLabel.qml` itself is checked to set `textFormat: Text.PlainText` and to expose no `textFormat` override.
2. **Process launching.**
   - No `Util.execDetached`, `bar.run`, `"bash"`, `"-c"`, `"sh"` or `execDetached("` string forms anywhere. Every `Quickshell.execDetached(` call takes `[`: the text after the opening parenthesis is an argv array literal (F8's notification calls are written `Quickshell.execDetached(["omarchy-notification-send", …])`), so the rule stays checkable as text.
   - Every `Process` whose `command` starts with the omaddons binary sets `environment: Build.CONTEXT` (M3-D7), and the self-reinstall `Process` uses `startDetached()` with it.
3. **Argv provenance.** Every `Process` `command:` and `Quickshell.execDetached` argv comes from one of three places:
   - `Model.buildArgv(...)`;
   - `Model.cliArgv(...)`, which applies `classifyCliArgv`;
   - one of the four literal tools above.
4. **Files and URLs.** No `FileView` with `setText`, and no `Qt.openUrlExternally` except through `Model.isSafeUrl`.
5. **Slots.** Every `{query}` substitution goes only into read-only templates (re-asserted from F1: scan the table for `{query}` in a `mutates: true` entry, and the call sites for `buildArgv` with a `query` slot on a mutating name).
6. **Previews.** Every `confirm` template (`remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`) and every destructive `CLI_PATHS` entry reaches the runner only through the preview flow: a scan for `run(` calls with those names outside `Service.qml`'s confirm path fails.
7. **Notifications.** The notification argv builder takes only `{names, counts, targets}`. The scan forbids passing any error-model field into it (for example `message`, `stack`, `locals`, `raw`, `location`, `path`) (M3-D21).
8. **The plugin id.** The literal `a44.omaddons` appears in no QML or JS file under `omarchy/` except `manifest.json`. Every `serviceFor`, IPC target, `moduleName`, `ipcTarget` and `summon` argument uses `Build.PLUGIN_ID`, so E1's debug `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` seam yields a truly separate widget (its own service, IPC handler and panel).

The parenthetical scan methods in checks 5 and 6 and the example field names in check 7 are decided while writing this bead; the rules themselves are the spec's.

### Self-tests

Each check self-tests with a temporary planted string: the scan function runs over an in-memory copy of a real file with one violation inserted, and must fail; then over the unmodified file, and must pass. Required planted cases (the spec names the three for checks 1, 2 and 8; the other six, one per remaining check, are decided while writing this bead so that every check has one):
- a rich-text `Text` bound to `svc.errors` planted in a view fails check 1;
- an omaddons `Process` without `environment` fails check 2;
- a `Quickshell.execDetached("omarchy-notification-send …")` string form fails check 2;
- a `Process` whose `command` is a hand-built array of the binary and `"update"` fails check 3;
- a `FileView { … setText(…) }` fails check 4;
- a `{query}` slot passed to `update_addon` fails check 5;
- a `run("remove", …)` outside the confirm path fails check 6;
- a notification builder call passing `entry.message` fails check 7;
- a planted `serviceFor("a44.omaddons")` fails check 8.

### Where it runs

`bun test omarchy/tests` is step 2 of the gate's ordered widget pipeline (F1's `scripts/gate.sh`, M3-D41), on every gate; the Rust checks are always-on `cargo test` tests in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`. A missing `bun` fails the gate with "install bun … to run the widget tests". Nothing generated is committed.

### Files

New: `omarchy/tests/security.test.js`. Changed: `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (the Rust-side checks, if any), README (the widget's safety rules in the Architecture or widget section, one paragraph naming the scans; the spec names no README step, so this item is decided while writing this bead, under common rule 11).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The eight scans pass on the finished widget source.
- Each scan fails on its planted violation (the self-tests above), including: a rich-text `Text` bound to `svc.errors` planted in a view fails check 1; an omaddons `Process` without `environment` fails check 2; a planted `serviceFor("a44.omaddons")` fails check 8.
- The scans run in the gate (bun step on every gate; Rust checks under plain `cargo test`) from a clean checkout.
- The scans cover every runtime `*.qml` and `*.js` file under `omarchy/` (a test asserts the scanned set equals E1's embedded asset set minus `manifest.json`; this criterion is decided while writing this bead, so a new file cannot escape the scans).

## Test Plan

- **bun, `omarchy/tests/security.test.js`:** one `test()` per check over the real files, and one per planted violation over an in-memory modified copy.
- **Rust, `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`:** the plugin-id literal scan (and any check expressed more robustly in Rust), with its own planted case; the scanned-set equality with the asset table.
- **Gate:** the full pipeline from a clean checkout (`argc gate` and `argc widget-test`).

## Considerations

- **Scans are lints, not proofs.** They are text-level and can be fooled by deliberate obfuscation; they exist to catch accidental regressions. The guarantees are `PlainLabel`, `buildArgv`, `classifyCliArgv`, and the Rust parse of exactly the argv bun emitted (F1). Keep the scans simple and their failure messages specific (file, line, rule).
- **Avoid false positives in tests and mocks.** Exclude `omarchy/tests/` from the source scans; the mocks legitimately contain `Process` stubs, and the hand-written fixture `omarchy/tests/fixtures/Build.js` may hold an id literal. This matches E1's asset-set test, which also lists `omarchy/` without `tests/` and `Build.js` (the exclusion is decided while writing this bead).
- **The id literal is allowed in `manifest.json` only.** E1 stamps the manifest's `version` at install, and under its debug `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` seam it also rewrites the manifest `id` and `Build.PLUGIN_ID` to `a44.omaddons-<suffix>`; the generated `Build.js` is not in the repo, so it is never scanned.
- **Two argv in F2 sit outside check 3's three sources** (noted while reviewing this bead). One is the self-reinstall `Process` command `[binary, "--actor", "widget", "--reason", "reinstall from the bar widget", "omarchy", "install"]` (M3-D42, a fixed literal that check 2 already names). The other, used only if F0 found the `shell.summon` facade unusable, is `show()`'s fallback `Quickshell.execDetached(["omarchy-shell", "shell", "summon", Build.PLUGIN_ID, "{}"])`; `omarchy-shell` is not one of M3-D2's four literal tools. Allow each as a named, exact exception in the scan (or route the reinstall argv through a `Model.js` builder the scan accepts), so the exceptions cannot widen, and record the choice in the close comment.
- **User-visible text that names the id counts too** (noted while reviewing this bead). The binary-missing card's command `omarchy bar set a44.omaddons binary <path>` (F2 and F4) must be built from `Build.PLUGIN_ID`, or check 8 fails on that string literal, and an isolated checkpoint widget would print the wrong id.
- **Risks (from the risk register: milestone epic comment "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol (§12)", §12.1):** risk 13 (personal data leaks through any channel): checks 1 and 7. Risk 22 (the widget acts on another state): check 2's `environment` rule. Risk 21 (a preview no longer describes what runs): check 6. Risk 14 (a keyboard slip runs a mutation): check 6 keeps destructive paths behind confirmation.
- **Collision hot spot:** `README.md` (everyone: each task edits only its own section; G1 reconciles), if this task adds its paragraph.
- **Critical path.** F7 is on the restore critical path (after F9) and gates G1 and G3.
- **Delivery slice `slice-4` (portability and close).** Exit demo, recorded on the milestone epic when the slice's last task closes: export → import → restore byte-identical; integration scenes; the af10e34 characterization; perf; **gate from a clean checkout**; README. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 8 (export, import), 9 (integration), 10, 11, 12 and 14. This task contributes the widget scans to the clean-checkout gate run.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- F5 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.5` (The Updates and Installed views): view source the rendering, provenance and preview scans cover.
- F6 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.6` (The Issues and Search views): view source and the `errors`, `errors_raw`, `dismiss_errors` templates the scans cover.
- F8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.8` (`Service.qml`, part 2: Hyprland, auto-check, post-session triggers, notifications): the notification builder (check 7), its `execDetached` calls (check 2) and `summon` ids (check 8).
- F9 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.9` (The Backups view and the restore-scope chooser): the last views and the remaining `confirm` templates (check 6).

**Unblocks:**
- G1 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1` (README final pass): the finished widget, its last task closed, so the README pass describes the widget as it ships (including the gate's widget pipeline and any safety paragraph this task adds).
- G3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3` (The M3 checkpoint): criterion 5 (argv-only execution, the source scans) is recorded from these tests.

F1's mechanisms (template table, classifier, `PlainLabel`, the Rust argv validation) and F2's runner reach this task through F5, F6, F8 and F9.

Parent: the F epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6`. Delivery slice: `slice-4`.
acceptance_criteria: The eight scans (rendering only through PlainLabel with PlainLabel.qml fixed to Text.PlainText; no Util.execDetached, bar.run, bash, -c, sh or execDetached string forms and every Quickshell.execDetached taking [ (an argv array literal); every omaddons Process setting environment: Build.CONTEXT and the self-reinstall using startDetached with it; every Process command and execDetached argv from Model.buildArgv, Model.cliArgv or one of the four literal tools; no FileView setText and no Qt.openUrlExternally except through Model.isSafeUrl; {query} only in read-only templates; confirm templates and destructive CLI_PATHS reaching the runner only through the preview flow; the notification builder taking only names, counts and targets; the literal a44.omaddons only in manifest.json with every serviceFor, IPC target, moduleName, ipcTarget and summon argument using Build.PLUGIN_ID) pass on the finished widget source; each scan fails on its planted violation, including a rich-text Text bound to svc.errors (check 1), an omaddons Process without environment (check 2) and a planted serviceFor("a44.omaddons") (check 8); the scans run in the gate from a clean checkout (bun on every gate, Rust checks under plain cargo test); the scanned file set equals the embedded runtime QML and JS files

comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** The widget runs commands that delete folders and rewrite `WTF/`, and it renders strings that come from addon authors and other players. Its safety comes from a handful of shared mechanisms, and the cheapest way to keep them load-bearing is a test that fails the gate the moment any code path goes around them: a rich `Text` bound to error data, a hand-built argv, a shell string, a process without the stamped context, a destructive action outside the preview flow, error text in a toast, a literal plugin id. It is small, it runs last so it sees the whole widget, and it is the evidence G3 records for checkpoint criterion 5.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D2: argv from two sources only, plus four literal tools,** with the classifier deciding what CLI output may run. Rejected: trusting any argv that starts with `omaddons` (a prefix proves which program runs, not what the command does or whether it is destructive); building argv freely in QML.
- **M3-D3: the widget never writes a file;** no `setText`, no `execDetached` of strings, no `bash`.
- **M3-D7: every omaddons child runs under `Build.CONTEXT`;** the self-reinstall uses `startDetached()`.
- **M3-D9 and M3-D46: destructive actions only through the preview flow.**
- **M3-D14 and M3-D21: notifications carry names and counts only;** a toast is a privacy channel.
- **M3-D41: widget tests run in the gate,** bun on every gate, from a clean checkout.
- **E1's plugin-id rule:** every QML use of the id derives from `Build.PLUGIN_ID`, so the debug checkpoint widget is truly separate.

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 3 (revision 19): the classifier for CLI argv (not a prefix check) and `PlainLabel` for every CLI string, with scans for both; (revision 17): the `Build.CONTEXT` rule on every omaddons `Process`. Check 8 (the plugin-id literal) pairs with E1's debug `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` seam, which G3 uses for its isolated checkpoint widget, so that widget gets its own service, IPC handler and panel.
- Round 2's reviewer ran every widget command template against the debug binary with hostile slot values (all parse, values arriving as positionals); F1 made that a gate test, and this task keeps call sites from bypassing it.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- `Quickshell.execDetached([...])` takes an argv only, while the house `Util.execDetached` takes shell strings (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.5).
- Any write under a plugin dir reloads every bar widget, which is why no `FileView.setText` may exist.
- The hey plugin ships a working source-scan security test (`panel-security.test.js`) that this task follows.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risks 13, 14, 21, 22 (privacy, keyboard slips, preview drift, another state): each has a scan that catches a regression of its mechanism.
- Text scans can miss deliberate obfuscation: accepted; the scans guard against accidents, and the mechanisms (classifier, `buildArgv`, `PlainLabel`, Rust parse) are the guarantees.
- False positives from mocks: test files are excluded from the source scans.

**Confidence.** High: small, deterministic text scans with a planted self-test per rule.

title: `Service.qml`, part 2: Hyprland, auto-check, post-session triggers, notifications
description:
## Background

F2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2`) built the service's core: the scheduler with its three lanes, the process runner, the compatibility gate, confirmations, IPC, and freshness through the doorbell and the fallback poll. This task adds the service's inputs **from the desktop** that go beyond plain freshness (M3-D12, M3-D13, M3-D14, M3-D31):
- **Hyprland window events** as a doorbell: a game client starting or exiting shows within about a second.
- **Post-session work**: when a client stops running, take the post-session settings checkpoint (`backup create --auto`) and refresh its Lua errors, so "after a play session" protection and diagnosis happen without the user asking.
- **Startup reconciliation**: on service start, queue the post-session checkpoint for every stopped target, so protection does not depend on the shell having seen the transition (a reboot, a crashed shell, a session played with the bar off).
- **The errors refresh** when `status` says a target's errors are stale or unchecked.
- **Background update checks** when `status` says a check is due.
- **Notifications** for new Lua errors (default on) and new updates (default off), and for a panel action that finished while no panel is open.

Each of these **only adds requests** to F2's scheduler, so it can land after the core without changing its rules. It needs `errors` (B6, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6`) and `backup create --auto` (D3, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.3`) to exist, because its templates call them (templates land with their commands, M3-D2), and `status`'s errors block (B7, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7`), because its triggers and toasts read `errors.state`, `summary.errors.new` and `targets[].errors.top`.

The after-session workflow this delivers:
1. The player quits the game. Hyprland reports the window closing; the widget refreshes. `status` sees the client stopped, and notices BugGrabber's file changed since `errors` last read it (`errors.state: "stale"`).
2. The service queues `omaddons backup create --auto -t retail` in the mutation lane (the CLI decides whether a backup is due and skips an unchanged tree), then `omaddons errors -t retail` in the local read lane.
3. That finds 4 new errors; one received from a guildmate does not count. The icon turns urgent. With `notifyErrors` On (the default), a toast reads "Lua errors in your last session · DBM 3 · WeakAuras 1": addon names and counts only, never message text. Clicking it opens the panel.

Ground truth this task relies on (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.5, Omarchy 4.0.6, Quickshell 0.3.2, Hyprland 0.56.2):
- Hyprland raw events `openwindow>>ADDR,WS,CLASS,TITLE` and `closewindow>>ADDR` arrive through `Quickshell.Hyprland`'s `rawEvent` (the first-party idle service uses them). Omarchy's Battle.net rule gives every window of that Proton prefix class `steam_app_battlenet`; whether the game window itself has that class is UNVERIFIED, which is why there is no class filter (M3-D13).
- The shell is the notification daemon (no mako, dunst or swaync). `omarchy-notification-send [--app-name A] [-g glyph] [-u low|normal|critical] <title> [body] [--exec program args…]` sets an `omarchy-exec-argv` hint, so a click on the toast runs an argv. `summon` opens a panel where `toggle` would close an open one; F0 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.10`) recorded the exact `summon` payload form that works.
- `Quickshell.execDetached([...])` takes an argv only, inherits the desktop environment, and gives no exit status.
- Running detection is the CLI's job (`/proc`, failing closed when unreadable); window events are only a hint that it may have changed, and a `status --cached` refresh costs about 3 ms.
- A Wine game process can outlive its window, which is why follow-up refreshes run after a `closewindow`.

This task serves G-M3-1 (glanceable: current within a second of a client starting or exiting), G-M3-3 (errors noticed after a session), G-M3-4 (post-session checkpoints, caught up at widget start), and checkpoint criteria 2 (doorbell latency: a window opening or closing triggers a refresh within 1 s; the running state follows a real client starting and exiting), 6 (notifications carry no error text), and 8 (a post-session checkpoint after each play session that changed settings, also caught up at widget start).

## Technical Approach

### Templates this task adds (now that B6 and D3 exist)

```js
"errors_target":  { "argv": ["errors", "--limit", "10", "-t", "{target}"],        "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
"backup_auto":    { "argv": ["backup", "create", "--auto", "-t", "{target}"],     "mutates": true, "silent": true },
```

- `silent: true` (`backup_auto`) runs in the **same** mutation lane as user actions, at background priority, and shows no result line unless it fails (M3-D11). "Silent" changes only presentation, never concurrency: queued user actions run before queued background ones, nothing preempts a running mutation, and the queue holds at most one background request per (resource, target), so a second `backup_auto` for the same target replaces the first.
- `errors_target` runs on the local read lane, coalesced per (resource, target).
- Both are built by `Model.buildArgv` with the standard flags first (`--json --actor widget --reason "<label> (bar widget)"`, plus `--progress json` for the mutating one), and run with `environment: Build.CONTEXT` (M3-D7). F1's Rust validation covers them unchanged.

### 1. Hyprland (M3-D13)

```qml
Connections {
    target: Hyprland
    function onRawEvent(e) { if (e.name === "openwindow" || e.name === "closewindow") windowDebounce.restart() }
}
```

- `windowDebounce`: 500 ms, then a `status` request (`status --cached`, which jumps F2's local queue).
- **After a `closewindow` while any target was running,** follow-up refreshes run at +2 s, +5 s and +15 s, because a Wine game process can outlive its window.
- **While any target runs,** F2's fallback poll is shortened to 30 s, so the running→stopped transition is never missed for long.
- No class filter: filtering by window class (unverified for Proton game windows) adds risk for no gain.

### 2. Post-session work (F2's `onStatus` hook)

On each running→stopped transition of a target, observed between two compatible statuses (the "compatible" qualifier is decided while writing this bead, from M3-D42's rule that automatic work stops while incompatible):
1. queue `backup_auto` for it (mutation lane, background priority; M3-D31 (b): the CLI decides whether a backup is due, skips a target whose client still runs or whose running state is unknown, and coalesces unchanged trees as `unchanged`);
2. then queue the errors refresh, `errors_target` (local lane).

Order and lanes are part of the contract (tests assert them).

### 3. Startup reconciliation (M3-D13)

On the **first compatible status** after the service starts, queue `backup_auto` for every target that is not running. The CLI's coalescing makes each a no-op unless settings changed since the newest qualifying capture. These background requests queue behind nothing user-initiated: a user action queued meanwhile runs first.

### 4. The errors refresh (M3-D20)

After any status where a target's `errors.state` is `stale` or `unchecked` (**never** `partial`, which records an incomplete read that must not be retried on every doorbell), queue `errors_target` for it, coalesced per target. The read rings the doorbell when it changes the memo, and the next status shows the new counts.

### 5. Auto check (M3-D12)

**When it is evaluated:** with `autoCheck` On, a 15-minute timer and every status refresh look at `status --cached` (its `commands[]`, summarized as `summary.check_due`). The widget has no update schedule of its own, so a shell restart causes no burst of checks.

If `autoCheck` is On, `summary.check_due` is true (A2: true when `commands[]` holds `check_updates`, which `status` adds when a client was never checked or its check is stale against `check_interval_hours` in `<config>/config.toml`), and the last automatic check started more than 15 minutes ago, queue `check` (`outdated`) on the network lane. It never disables buttons; its progress shows only in the panel footer. **Check now** (`c`, F4) runs it unconditionally. A healthy `outdated` waiting out `Retry-After`s keeps emitting progress and is never killed (F2's inactivity deadline, `WIDGET_NETWORK_DEADLINE_SEC` = 600 s, reset on each progress line).

### 6. Notifications (M3-D14), plus action completion

Every trigger checks `phase == "ok"` first: a missing or incompatible binary sends nothing (the bar is dimmed instead, M3-D42).
- **Action completion:** when a mutating action started from the panel finishes while no panel is open, send one low-urgency toast with `Model.resultLine` (for example "Updated 3 addons on 2 clients · /reload in game"). Clicking it opens the panel.
- **Updates** (`notifyUpdates`, default Off): when `summary.updates.available` > `lastNotifiedUpdates`, and this is not the first status since start, send a toast with the counts.
- **Errors** (`notifyErrors`, default On): on the first status where `summary.errors.new` rose above the previous value, after a running→stopped transition or an errors refresh, send a toast with the addon names from `targets[].errors.top` and their counts. **Only names, target ids and counts**: no message, path or other error text (M3-D21). Received reports never count (they are not in `new`).
- **Nothing fires on the first status after the service starts.**
- Both use an argv array:

  ```js
  Quickshell.execDetached(["omarchy-notification-send", "--app-name", "omaddons", "-g", <glyph>, "-u", "low"|"normal",
                           <title>, <body>, "--exec", "omarchy-shell", "shell", "summon", Build.PLUGIN_ID, "{}"])
  ```

  so a click opens rather than toggles (the payload form per F0). No `Util.execDetached`; every value is an argv element. The plugin id comes from `Build.PLUGIN_ID`, never a literal (F7 scan 8).
- **The notification argv builder takes only `{names, counts, targets}`** (a small pure function in `Model.js`), so no error-model field can reach it; F7's scan 7 forbids passing any.
- The single shared service (M3-D5) means one toast per event even with two monitors.

### 7. QML tests (`omarchy/tests/qml/tst_signals.qml`)

With F2's mocks plus a `Quickshell/Hyprland` mock (a `Hyprland` singleton with a `rawEvent` signal):
- `closewindow` → one status after the debounce; a burst of events → one status;
- after `closewindow` with a running target, the +2 s, +5 s and +15 s refreshes;
- running→stopped → `backup_auto` then `errors_target`, in that order and in their lanes;
- startup with two stopped targets → two `backup_auto` requests, queued behind nothing user-initiated (a user action queued meanwhile runs first);
- a `partial` errors state does not trigger a rerun; `stale` and `unchecked` do, once per target;
- update and error notifications fire on rises, never on the first status, never while incompatible or missing, and the error toast's argv contains no message text from the fixture (assert every element against the fixture's message, path and locals strings);
- auto check fires only when `check_due`, at most once per 15 minutes (evaluated on the 15-minute timer and on each status refresh);
- the action-completion toast fires only when no panel is open.

Add the fixture scenarios these need (a `status` with a running target, then stopped; `errors.state` `stale`, `unchecked`, `partial`; `summary.errors.new` rising; `check_due` true) to F1's `write_widget_fixtures`.

### 8. README

The Omarchy widget section documents the automatic behaviour: after-play checkpoints and errors refresh, startup catch-up, background checks when due, and the two notification settings (common rule 11; the section is created by E2, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2`, and G1 reconciles. The spec names no README step for this task; this item is decided while writing this bead).

### Files

Changed: `omarchy/Service.qml` (signal handlers, hooks and timers only; F2's state machine is not restructured), `omarchy/Model.js` (the two templates, the notification argv builder and any pure trigger decisions, with bun tests), `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_signals.qml` and the `Quickshell/Hyprland` mock under `omarchy/tests/qml/imports/`, `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (fixture scenarios), README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every QML test in section 7 passes under `qmltestrunner` in the gate.
- On the real machine at G3, the doorbell latency criterion passes: a terminal change, an update check and a window opening or closing each show in IPC `state()` within 1 s (95th percentile of 20 trials for the terminal case), and the running state follows a real client starting and exiting (the agent launches the 3.3.5a client to its login screen; if no client can be launched, the pre-accepted `SKIP` is recorded).
- Running→stopped queues `backup_auto` then `errors_target`, in that order and lane; startup queues `backup_auto` for each stopped target behind any user action.
- No notification fires on the first status, while incompatible, or while the binary is missing; the error toast carries only addon names, target ids and counts.
- `errors_target` and `backup_auto` pass F1's Rust argv validation.
- Automatic work stops while the widget is incompatible (`phase` checked by every trigger).

## Test Plan

- **QML (`tst_signals.qml`):** the cases in section 7.
- **bun (`model.test.js`):** the notification argv builder (only names, counts, targets; no other parameter), any pure trigger decisions moved into `Model.js` (transition detection, the 15-minute auto-check rule, the rise detection excluding the first status).
- **Rust (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs`):** the new templates in `validate_built_argv`; fixture scenarios.
- **Real machine (G3):** the doorbell latency harness (a script in scratch that runs `backup create -t retail --reason "doorbell latency check"` and `backup prune <id> -t retail` 10 times each, timing each ring until IPC `state()` changes; both ring and neither touches AddOns or `WTF/`; afterwards `backup list` shows no leftover and the AddOns hash is unchanged; Forever is never touched); window open/close timing; the client start/exit check.

## Considerations

- **Only additions.** F8 adds handlers, timers, hooks and templates; it does not change F2's lane rules, deadlines or acceptance rules. If a trigger seems to need a scheduler change, that is a finding against F2, filed with `--deps discovered-from`.
- **`backup_auto` competes for the one mutation lane.** It is background priority and silent; a user action queued after it still runs first, and a running user action is never preempted. The CLI's coalescing (`unchanged`), its scheduling lock (`in_progress`) and its running check (`running`) make repeated triggers cheap and safe (D3).
- **No timer of its own for backups.** There is no daemon; the triggers are the widget's own doorbells (M3-D31). A user who never runs the shell still gets the CLI's pre-change checkpoint (D3).
- **Toast text is a privacy channel** (notifications persist in the notification center), so the builder accepts names and counts only.
- **Risks (from the risk register: milestone epic comment "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol (§12)", §12.1):** risk 2 (duplicate processes or toasts with two monitors): one shared service. Risk 20 (Hyprland event floods): the 500 ms debounce, a 3 ms status, bounded coalesced queues. Risk 13 (privacy): the restricted builder and F7's scan. Risk 9 (backups fill the disk): the CLI's space guard and per-day retention bound what `backup_auto` does (D3, D4). Risk 3 (`inotifywait` missing or the cache dir deleted): Hyprland events and the shortened poll are a second path to freshness.
- **Collision hot spots:** `omarchy/Service.qml` (F2 first; F8 adds signal handlers and templates only; F6 and F9 also add their panel-open reads there). `README.md` (everyone: each task edits only its own section; G1 reconciles). Also shared, though not in the milestone's hot-spot table: `omarchy/Model.js`'s `COMMANDS` block is also extended by F6 and F9; append within the markers.
- **Delivery slice `slice-2` (capture and diagnose).** Exit demo, recorded on the milestone epic when the slice's last task closes: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; **automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced**; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 6, 7, 8 (create, auto, verify) and 13 (`errors dismiss`, `backup prune`). This task supplies the after-session trigger of the bolded step.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- B6 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6` (The `errors` command): the `errors -t <target>` read behind the `errors_target` template, which rings the doorbell when it changes the memo.
- B7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7` (Errors in `status`): `targets[].errors.state` (`stale`, `unchecked`, `partial`), `summary.errors.new` and `targets[].errors.top`, which the refresh rule and the error toast read.
- D3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.3` (Automatic backups: two triggers, qualifying checkpoints, the space guard): `backup create --auto`, with its due check, coalescing, running skip, scheduling lock and space guard, behind the `backup_auto` template.
- F2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2` (`Service.qml`, part 1): the scheduler and lanes, the `onStatus` hook, the fallback poll, `phase`, and the mocks these QML tests extend.

**Unblocks:**
- F7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.7` (Widget security and contract checks): its process, notification-builder and plugin-id scans cover this task's handlers.

Parent: the F epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6`. Delivery slice: `slice-2`.
acceptance_criteria: Every QML test in tst_signals.qml passes under qmltestrunner in the gate (closewindow gives one status after the 500 ms debounce, a burst gives one, the +2 s/+5 s/+15 s follow-ups after a closewindow with a running target, running to stopped queues backup_auto then errors_target in that order and lane, startup with two stopped targets queues two backup_auto requests behind any user action, partial never triggers a rerun while stale and unchecked do once per target, update and error notifications fire on rises only and never on the first status or while incompatible or missing, the error toast argv holds no message text from the fixture, auto check fires only when check_due and at most once per 15 minutes, the action-completion toast fires only with no panel open); on the real machine at G3 the doorbell latency criterion passes (terminal change, update check and window open or close each reach IPC state() within 1 s, the terminal case at the 95th percentile of 20 trials) and the running state follows a real client starting and exiting, or the pre-accepted SKIP is recorded when no client can be launched; the error toast carries only addon names, target ids and counts; errors_target and backup_auto pass F1's Rust argv validation; automatic work stops while the widget is incompatible
