comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** It is what makes the widget feel alive without a daemon: the bar notices a game starting or stopping, and the moment a session ends it takes the post-session settings checkpoint and reads the session's Lua errors, then says so in a toast that names addons and counts only. It catches up at startup, so protection does not depend on the shell having watched the session. It checks for updates only when the CLI says a check is due, so a shell restart causes no burst. Every one of these is a request in F2's one scheduler, attributed to the widget, and every one is a no-op when nothing changed.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D13: Hyprland window events are a doorbell,** with no class filter, plus post-session work on running→stopped and startup reconciliation. Why: running detection is the CLI's job; events are a hint; a refresh costs about 3 ms; window classes of Proton game windows are unverified.
- **M3-D31 (b): the post-session checkpoint is `backup create --auto`,** triggered by the widget on each running→stopped transition and for every stopped target at startup; the CLI skips running targets and coalesces unchanged trees. Rejected: a timer in the widget; post-session captures while the client runs; one automatic backup per day of any trigger.
- **M3-D11: one mutation lane for everything that mutates, `backup_auto` included.** "Silent" changes presentation only; user actions queue first; one queued background request per (resource, target). Rejected: a separate background lane for silent mutations (an automatic backup copying `WTF/` while a user's restore stages it would make the capture's meaning unclear).
- **M3-D12: background update checks follow `status`'s `check_due`,** at most once per 15 minutes; Check now is unconditional. Why: staleness comes from the user's config; the widget needs no schedule of its own.
- **M3-D14: notifications on transitions only,** names and counts only, `summon` so a click opens, nothing on the first status, nothing when missing or incompatible; `notifyErrors` default On, `notifyUpdates` default Off. Why: errors are rare and actionable; updates are frequent and already a badge; the toast persists in the notification center, so the privacy rule covers it.
- **M3-D20: the errors refresh runs on `stale` or `unchecked`, never on `partial`.**
- **M3-D21: notifications are a privacy channel.**
- **M3-D42: automatic work stops while incompatible.**
- **M3-D2: templates land with their commands** (`errors_target`, `backup_auto`).

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 3 (revision 18) split the desktop signals out of F2 into this task, because they only add requests and need commands (`errors`, `backup create --auto`) that F2 does not wait for; (revision 4) added startup reconciliation and the two-trigger model; (revision 10) restricted toasts to names and counts through a builder that cannot see error fields.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- `rawEvent` delivers `openwindow>>ADDR,WS,CLASS,TITLE` and `closewindow>>ADDR`; the Battle.net Proton prefix's windows have class `steam_app_battlenet`, unverified for the game window (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.5).
- `omarchy-notification-send … --exec program args…` makes a click run an argv; the shell is the notification daemon; `Quickshell.execDetached` takes an argv only.
- A Wine game process can outlive its window.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk 2 (duplicate processes or toasts on two monitors): the single shared service.
- Risk 20 (event floods): debounce, cheap status, coalesced queues.
- Risk 13 (privacy via toasts): the restricted builder, F7's scan 7, tests that assert no fixture text reaches the argv.
- Risk 9 (disk filled by automatic backups): bounded by D3's space guard and D4's per-day retention, not by the widget.
- A missed running→stopped transition: the shortened 30 s poll while a client runs, follow-up refreshes after `closewindow`, and startup reconciliation.

**Confidence.** Medium: the logic is small and fully QML-tested with mocks, but it meets real Quickshell timing, Hyprland events and Proton process lifetimes; F0's observations and G3's real-machine latency checks are the evidence.

title: The Backups view and the restore-scope chooser
description:
## Background

"My WeakAuras settings are gone" is the most persuasive reason for M3's backups, and the widget must make the **safest** fix the easiest one: restoring **one addon's settings** from a chosen backup, previewed and undoable, in two keys. A whole-`WTF/` restore also rolls back keybindings, macros, chat settings and every other addon's settings; offering only that in the bar would invite the wrong fix (review round 3, revision 20; risk 11). M3 already implements partial restore in the CLI (D7, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.7`), so this task is UI over existing commands, with no new engine scope.

The workflow it delivers (from the bar):
- In the Installed view, select WeakAuras and press `r`, or press `r` on a WeakAuras row in Issues. A chooser lists that target's backups, newest first, with age, kind and "WeakAuras 5.19.2". Picking one runs the same dry run the CLI would (`backup restore <id> --addon=WeakAuras -t retail --dry-run`) and shows its counts and the version note ("settings written by WeakAuras 5.19.2; installed now: 5.20.0"; "6 files: 4 replaced, 1 restored (absent now), 1 created since (moved aside)"). Confirming runs the restore bound to that preview (`--if-match`, M3-D46). Whole-`WTF/` restore is the second choice in the same chooser, labelled with what else it changes.
- While the game runs, the restore choices are disabled with "quit the game first" (the CLI would refuse with `game_running`: SavedVariables are never written while the client runs, because it overwrites them on logout, M3-D29).
- Users should feel: "It saved my profile and didn't touch anything else."

What the CLI decides, and the widget only shows (D7, D8, M3-D27, M3-D24):
- **Which folders.** A partial restore uses the folders the addon owned **when the backup was taken** (the backup's `addons.json`), so it works after the addon was removed, renamed a folder or changed version. A folder another managed addon owns now is refused with `ref_ambiguous`, whose alternatives name each folder as an `--addon <folder>` argv; the user picks. A folder the addon owns now but did not own at capture is left alone and listed as "not in this backup; left as it is". **The QML never decides ownership or scope.**
- **Atomicity.** A whole restore swaps `WTF/` with one `RENAME_EXCHANGE`; a partial restore exchanges each file. Where that is impossible (a `WTF/` mount point, a stage on another mount, a filesystem without `RENAME_EXCHANGE`, such as FUSE or network shares) the restore refuses before copying anything with `filesystem_unsupported`, for whole and `--addon` restores alike. Its fix is prose, and `details.backup_dir` names the backup's plain `WTF/` folder for a manual copy with the game closed.
- **Safety nets.** A whole restore keeps the current `WTF/` as a `before_restore` backup (on filesystems that can reflink, M3-D26) as well as in the transaction snapshot; every restore is undoable; the source backup holds a reader reservation, so a concurrent prune skips it as busy (M3-D48).
- **Integrity.** Each backup says what it proves: `stable` or `best_effort` capture, `metadata_only`/`verified`/`damaged` integrity with a `baseline` (M3-D47); a restore whose source has hashes checks them and refuses `hash_mismatch` on a difference.

This task serves G-M3-2 (one-click restore of a whole `WTF/` or one addon's settings, confirmed and bound), G-M3-4 (settings survive), and checkpoint criteria 4 (a client running: restore choices disabled with the reason; a stale preview shows the fresh one), 8 (whole and `--addon` restores, each undoable, refused while running) and 13 (`backup restore` and `backup prune` previews are binding). It is on the restore critical path: D1 → D5 → D14 → D8 → D7 → **F9** → F7 → G1 → G2 → G3.

## Technical Approach

### Templates this task adds (now that `backup create`, `prune`, `restore` and `--addon` exist: D2, D4, D7, D8)

```js
"backups":        { "argv": ["backup", "list", "--limit", "50"],                  "mutates": false, "lane": "local" },
"backup_target":  { "argv": ["backup", "create", "-t", "{target}"],               "mutates": true },
"backup_all":     { "argv": ["backup", "create"],                                 "mutates": true },
"restore":        { "argv": ["backup", "restore", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{backup}"], "mutates": true, "confirm": true },
"restore_addon":  { "argv": ["backup", "restore", "-t", "{target}", "--addon={addon}", "--", "{backup}"], "mutates": true, "confirm": true },
"prune_backup":   { "argv": ["backup", "prune", "-t", "{target}", "--", "{backup}"],   "mutates": true, "confirm": true }
```

- `{backup}` is a backup id from `backup list`; `{addon}` an addon name from `list` (or a folder name taken from a `ref_ambiguous` alternative); `{target}` an id or key from `status`. The option slot is one element (`--addon={addon}`) and positionals follow `--`, so a hostile value beginning with `-` is never a flag (M3-D2).
- **`confirm: true`**: F2's runner first runs the same argv with `--dry-run` (inserted with the standard flags, right after the binary), shows the dialog from its result, keeps `data.precondition`, and on Yes reruns with `--if-match <token>` (all three paths bind, M3-D46). A `plan_stale` answer reloads the dialog with a fresh dry run and "changed since you looked: …" (`Model.staleText`, from `details.changed`), and Yes needs a fresh press.
- `backup_auto` is F8's, not this task's.
- **Reads this task adds:** the `backups` read in F2's panel-open sequence (after `status_full`, `list` and F6's `errors`), and as the Backups view's switch-in read. `backup list --limit 50` bounds the output; `shown` and `total` say how many exist.

### Data consumed (`backup list`, `backup restore --dry-run`)

```json
{"data":{"targets":[{"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M4…"},
  "auto":{"mode":"daily","capability":"supported","last":{"at":"…","result":"created"}},
  "backups":[{"id":"01M6Q…","created_at":"…","captured_at":"…","kind":"auto","trigger":"post_session",
              "actor":"widget","reason":null,"files":412,"bytes":15937536,"reflinked":"all",
              "client_running":false,"unsettled":0,"consistency":"stable",
              "integrity":"metadata_only","verified_at":null,"baseline":null,
              "restorable":true,"qualifying":true,"busy":false}],
  "bytes":63963136,"snapshot_bytes":0,"free_bytes":227633266688,"shown":5,"total":5}]}}
```

- `backup list -v` adds per backup `"addons":[{"name":"WeakAuras","folders":["WeakAuras","WeakAurasOptions"],"version":"5.19.2"}]`, which the chooser uses to show "WeakAuras 5.19.2" per backup. **The chooser reads versions through a second, per-target template (decided when the beads were filed).** The `backups` template above has no `-v` and no `{target}` slot, so it carries no per-backup addon versions; adding `-v` to it would multiply the bar's every backups read by the addon lists of every backup on every client (one target may hold 200 manual backups). So this task adds one read-only, view-bound template (M3-D11), `"backups_detail": { "argv": ["backup", "list", "-v", "-t", "{target}", "--limit", "50"], "mutates": false, "lane": "local" }`, run when the restore chooser opens for a target and dropped if the view changes before it returns. Its worst-case fixture (50 backups, each with its addon list) must stay under `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`, checked by F1's output-cap test. The dry run's version note is still shown once a backup is picked. `backups_detail` is a wire name to list for G2.
- `busy` is true while another process holds a reader reservation (a restore, export or verify); it is best effort, a snapshot of that instant.
- `restorable: false` marks a `damaged` backup, one whose recorded structure is incomplete, or one whose client's `WTF` is a symlink out of the client dir.
- `integrity` is `metadata_only`, `verified` or `damaged`; `baseline` is `capture`, `import` or `later`. **Never print "verified" for `metadata_only`.**
- Restore dry-run data:

  ```json
  {"dry_run":true,"target":{…},"tx":null,"kind":"restore","mode":"whole",
   "backup":{"id":"01M6K…","captured_at":"…","kind":"auto","integrity":"verified"},
   "files":{"restored":410,"differed":37,"created_since":3,"unchanged":373},
   "addons":null,"before_restore":null,"reload_required":"restart","precondition":"pc1:…","exchange":"unverified"}
  ```

  A dry run creates no `before_restore` backup: it reports counts and the `precondition`, and its human text says "would keep the current WTF/ as a backup (before restore)" (D8). The real run's data carries `"before_restore":{"id":"01M6S…"}` and the `tx`. The `null` values for `tx` and `before_restore` in this dry-run sketch are assumed while writing this bead; D8's dry-run snapshot is authoritative.

  With `--addon`: `"mode":"addons","addons":[{"addon":"WeakAuras","folders":["WeakAuras","WeakAurasOptions"],"captured_version":"5.19.2","installed_version":"5.20.0","not_in_backup":[],"files":{"replaced":4,"restored":1,"created_since":1}}]`. A dry run runs the `statx` mount checks but writes no exchange probe, so it reports `exchange: "unverified"`; the real run probes before copying.

### 1. `omarchy/views/BackupsView.qml`

- **Per target:**
  - the automatic-backup status from `backups.auto` (`{mode, capability, last}`), labelled with the spec's four labels "daily, working", "daily, but this filesystem cannot clone", "skipped: low disk space" and "off". Which field values select each label is decided while writing this bead:

    | Condition | Label |
    |---|---|
    | `mode` `daily` (or `daily-copy`) and `capability` `supported` | "daily, working" |
    | `capability` `unsupported` (last result `no_reflink`) | "daily, but this filesystem cannot clone" |
    | `last.result` `space_low` | "skipped: low disk space" |
    | `mode` `off` | "off" |

    Other `last.result` values (`created`, `unchanged`, `done_today`, `in_progress`, `running`, `failed`, `no_wtf`) show as their plain meaning with the time. The mapping is a pure `Model.js` function with bun tests.
  - free space (`free_bytes`), next to the apparent size (`bytes`, labelled apparent);
  - then rows: `when · kind (trigger) · files · size · stable/best effort · verified (baseline)`, all through `PlainLabel`. "verified" appears only for `integrity: verified`, with its baseline; `damaged` shows as damaged.
- **Keys:**
  - `b` → `backup_target` for the selected target, or `backup_all` in the All filter (no confirmation: creation is undoable and expected, M3-D9);
  - Enter (or `r`) on a row → the restore chooser for that backup;
  - `x` → `prune_backup` for that backup id (confirm, bound by token). **Busy backups show "in use", and `x` is disabled** on them;
  - restore actions are disabled with "quit the game first" while the target runs (or its running state is unknown).
- Every row action uses the exact backup id, never "newest" or a count (M3-D9).

### 2. `omarchy/RestoreChooser.qml`

A `ConfirmDialog`-style overlay, opened from Backups, Installed or Issues.
- **Inputs:** a target and either a backup or an addon. Opened from an addon row, the addon is preselected and the backup list is that target's backups, newest first, from `backups`, each with age, kind and the addon's captured version where known.
- **Two scopes, in this order:**
  1. **"<addon>'s settings"** (template `restore_addon`). Opened from a Backups row, it reads "one addon's settings…" and lists that target's managed addons from `lists`;
  2. **"Whole WTF/"** (template `restore`), labelled "also restores keybindings, macros, chat settings and every other addon's settings".
- **Choosing a scope runs its dry run**, and the dialog shows `Model.confirmText(name, dryRunEnv)`:
  - the counts (`files.replaced`, `restored`, `created_since` for an addon; `restored`, `differed`, `created_since` for whole);
  - the version note: "settings written by WeakAuras 5.19.2; installed now: 5.20.0" (from `captured_version`/`installed_version`);
  - `not_in_backup` folders ("not in this backup; left as it is");
  - for a `ref_ambiguous` refusal (ownership changed since capture), the choices, each a button for `--addon <folder>`. The CLI names them in `error.alternatives[].argv`; the button reruns the chooser's dry run for that folder, either by running the alternative argv after `classifyCliArgv` accepts it (a destructive path, so it takes the preview flow) or through `restore_addon` with the folder as `{addon}` (`--addon=<folder>`). Which of the two is decided in this task and recorded in the close comment;
  - for whole: "the current WTF/ is kept as a backup" (`before_restore`), or, if the dry run reports it, the `before_restore_skipped` warning when the filesystem cannot clone (the transaction snapshot still holds the old tree until retention).
- **Confirm** runs the real restore with `--if-match <precondition>` (F2's flow). A refusal shows its message and fix: `game_running` ("quit the game client, then rerun"), `filesystem_unsupported` (the prose fix, and the backup's folder from `details.backup_dir` as text), `hash_mismatch`, `state_corrupt` (a damaged backup).
- The result line carries the Undo button from `commands[]`; undo goes through the confirm flow (M3-D9).
- **The QML never decides ownership or scope:** folders, files, versions and ambiguity all come from the CLI's dry run (D7).

### 3. `r` in the Installed and Issues views

- Installed view (F5's file): `r` on an addon row → the chooser with that addon preselected.
- Issues view (F6's file): `r` on an error's addon row → the chooser with that addon preselected.
- F9 adds both `r` bindings, so no key exists before its action does (DEC-1).

### 4. Fixtures

Through F1's `write_widget_fixtures` (generated into `$OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT/fixtures/`, never committed): `backup list` with stable, best-effort, verified and busy backups and each `auto` state; an `--addon` dry run with a version note and `not_in_backup`; a `ref_ambiguous` refusal with alternatives; a whole dry run (which says it would keep the current `WTF/` as a `before_restore` backup); a `plan_stale` answer; and the refusals `game_running` and `filesystem_unsupported`.

### 5. QML tests

In `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_views.qml` (the Backups view and the two `r` keys) and `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_chooser.qml` (the restore chooser), mocks under `omarchy/tests/qml/imports/`. For the view and the chooser: opening from each entry point (Backups row, Installed `r`, Issues `r`); scope order and labels; the version note; an ambiguous-ownership dialog producing the folder argv; a stale preview replaced with "changed since you looked"; a refused restore showing its fix; `x` disabled on a busy backup; restore disabled while the target runs; `b` choosing `backup_target` or `backup_all` by filter; the All filter never picking a target implicitly.

### 6. README

The Omarchy widget section documents the Backups view, the restore chooser (addon first, whole second, with what whole also changes), `b`, `r` and `x`, and that restores are disabled while the game runs (common rule 11; the section is created by E2, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2`, and G1 reconciles. The spec names no README step for this task; this item is decided while writing this bead).

### Files

New: `omarchy/views/BackupsView.qml`, `omarchy/RestoreChooser.qml`, QML tests (`tst_chooser.qml`, and cases in `tst_views.qml`). Changed: `omarchy/views/InstalledView.qml` and `omarchy/views/IssuesView.qml` (`r`), `omarchy/Model.js` (the seven templates: `backups`, `backups_detail`, `backup_target`, `backup_all`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`; `reduceBackups`, the auto-status labels and `confirmText` cases, with bun tests), `omarchy/Service.qml` (the `backups` read in the open and switch-in sequences), `src/omarchy/assets.rs` (two embedded files), `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (fixture scenarios), README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At G3, on a fixture home or a non-Forever client (then undone): create a backup from the panel; restore **one addon's settings** from the Installed view with the chooser; undo from the panel; restore the whole `WTF/` from the Backups view; undo again. `WTF/` hashes identical to the start.
- A test restores one addon's settings through the chooser on a fixture home and shows that unrelated settings (another addon's file, `Config.wtf`) are unchanged.
- From the All filter, no action ever picks a target implicitly.
- The chooser lists "<addon>'s settings" first and "Whole WTF/" second with its label; choosing a scope runs its dry run and shows counts, the version note and `not_in_backup`; a `ref_ambiguous` refusal offers one button per alternative folder, and each produces that folder's `--addon` dry run (the folder argv).
- Confirm runs with `--if-match <token>`; a state change between preview and confirm gives `plan_stale` and a refreshed dialog, and nothing is restored.
- `x` is disabled on a busy backup; `prune_backup` is confirmed and bound; restore choices are disabled with "quit the game first" while the target runs.
- "verified" is never shown for a `metadata_only` backup.
- The seven templates pass F1's Rust argv validation with hostile slot values; QML and bun tests pass in the gate; the two new files are embedded.
- Opening the restore chooser for a target runs the `backups_detail` template (`backup list -v -t <target> --limit 50`), view-bound, and shows each backup's addon version from it; its worst-case fixture stays under `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`.

## Test Plan

- **QML (qmltestrunner, the gate's step 4; `tst_views.qml` and `tst_chooser.qml`):** the cases in section 5 with F2's mocks; the `Process` mock asserts each built argv (template, slots, `--dry-run` then `--if-match`).
- **bun (`model.test.js`):** `reduceBackups` over the fixtures (rows, labels, busy, integrity wording), the auto-status label mapping, `confirmText` for addon and whole dry runs (version note, `not_in_backup`, `before_restore`, `before_restore_skipped`), `staleText`.
- **Rust (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs`):** the seven templates in `validate_built_argv`; fixture scenarios in `write_widget_fixtures`.
- **E2E on a fixture home** (a `HOME`-isolated run of the CLI the chooser drives): one addon's settings restored; another addon's SavedVariables and `Config.wtf` unchanged (tree hashes).
- **Real machine (G3):** the create → addon restore → undo → whole restore → undo pass, with `WTF/` hashed before and after, on a non-Forever client.
- QML (`tst_chooser.qml`): opening the chooser dispatches `backups_detail` for that target; a result that returns after the view changed is dropped; the version column renders from it, and the dry-run version note still appears once a backup is picked. Rust: the `backups_detail` worst-case fixture passes the output-cap check.

## Considerations

- **Addon first, by design.** The order of scopes is the safety feature; do not reorder for symmetry.
- **Exact ids only.** Prune and restore take the row's backup id; undo takes the `undo --run <run>` argv from the CLI.
- **Busy is a snapshot.** `busy` comes from a non-blocking probe at listing time; prune itself retries a busy victim once after 50 ms and reports what it skipped, so a stale "in use" label is harmless.
- **Running state comes from `status`.** The disable is a convenience; the CLI's own refusal (`game_running`, checked at plan time, under the lock and before in-process recovery) is the guarantee. A launch in the last milliseconds cannot be prevented by any check, and README says so (M3-D29).
- **Risks (from the risk register: milestone epic comment "Risks, testing strategy and checkpoint protocol (§12)", §12.1):** risk 11 (a user restores the whole `WTF/` when they meant one addon): the chooser offers one addon's settings first, the dry-run counts, the label on whole, a `before_restore` backup, and undo. Risk 21 (a preview no longer describes what runs): every restore and prune is bound by token. Risk 14 (a keyboard slip): restore and prune are confirmed; creation is undoable. Risk 8 (SavedVariables written while the client runs): the CLI refuses; the widget disables.
- **Collision hot spots:** `README.md` (everyone: each task edits only its own section; G1 reconciles); `omarchy/Service.qml` (the milestone's table lists F2 and F8, "F2 first; F8 adds signal handlers and templates only"; this task adds only the `backups` read, so coordinate with F8). Also shared, though not in that table: `omarchy/views/InstalledView.qml` (F5's) and `omarchy/views/IssuesView.qml` (F6's) gain one key case each; `omarchy/Model.js`'s `COMMANDS` block (append within the markers).
- **Critical path.** F9 is on the restore-safety critical path; F7 waits on it.
- **Delivery slice `slice-3` (recover).** Exit demo, recorded on the milestone epic when the slice's last task closes: **whole and `--addon` restores from the CLI and from the bar's chooser, each undone**; the crash matrices of D5, D6, D7 and D14. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 8 (restore), 9, 13 (`backup restore`) and 14. This task supplies the bar half of the bolded step.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- D7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.7` (Partial restore, `backup restore --addon`): `--addon` with capture-time folder resolution, `ref_ambiguous` alternatives, the version context and `not_in_backup`, behind the `restore_addon` template and the chooser's first scope.
- D8 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.8` (The `backup restore` command): the whole restore with `--dry-run`, `precondition`, `--if-match`, `before_restore` and its refusals (`game_running`, `filesystem_unsupported`, `hash_mismatch`), behind the `restore` template.
- D11 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.11` (Backups in `status`): `targets[].backups` (`auto` with `{mode, capability, last}`, counts, free space) for the view's per-target header.
- F4 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.4` (The panel frame, `PanelView.qml`): the content `Loader`, the key dispatch, the `ConfirmDialog` pattern the chooser follows, the footer and the read-only state.

**Unblocks:**
- F7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.7` (Widget security and contract checks): its rendering, provenance and preview scans run over the Backups view and the chooser, the last views to land.

`backup create` (D2) and `backup prune` (D4), behind `backup_target`, `backup_all` and `prune_backup`, reach this task through D8 (which depends on both). F5's and F6's view files are edited here for the `r` key.

Parent: the F epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6`. Delivery slice: `slice-3`.
acceptance_criteria: At G3, on a fixture home or a non-Forever client (then undone): create a backup from the panel, restore one addon's settings from the Installed view with the chooser, undo from the panel, restore the whole WTF/ from the Backups view, undo again, and WTF/ hashes identical to the start; a test restores one addon's settings through the chooser on a fixture home and shows that unrelated settings (another addon's file, Config.wtf) are unchanged; from the All filter no action ever picks a target implicitly; the chooser lists "<addon>'s settings" first and "Whole WTF/" second with its label, choosing a scope runs its dry run and shows counts, the version note and not_in_backup, and a ref_ambiguous refusal offers one button per alternative folder, each producing that folder's --addon dry run (the folder argv); confirm runs with --if-match <token>, and a state change between preview and confirm gives plan_stale, a refreshed dialog and no restore; x is disabled on a busy backup, prune_backup is confirmed and bound, and restore choices are disabled with "quit the game first" while the target runs; "verified" is never shown for a metadata_only backup; the seven templates pass F1's Rust argv validation with hostile slot values, QML and bun tests pass in the gate, and the two new files are embedded; opening the restore chooser runs the view-bound backups_detail template (backup list -v -t <target> --limit 50) and shows each backup's addon version from it, within WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** Players lose settings, not addons, and "my WeakAuras are gone" should be two keys in the bar: pick the addon, pick a backup, see exactly what will change, confirm. The chooser puts the narrow fix first and labels the broad one with everything else it rolls back, so the widget steers people to the restore that does the least damage. Every choice is the CLI's dry run, every confirm is bound to it, every result is undoable from the same panel, and nothing runs while the game could overwrite it. The slice-3 demo (restores from the bar, each undone) and G3's `WTF/`-hash round trip run through this task.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D27: a partial restore is a SavedVariables-only transaction undo already understands,** scoped by capture-time ownership; ambiguity refuses with `ref_ambiguous` and folder alternatives; the version context is shown, never judged. The widget renders these; it decides nothing. Rejected (for the CLI): restoring files directly with roll-forward payload semantics.
- **M3-D24: a whole restore is one journaled `RENAME_EXCHANGE` of `WTF/`,** refused outright (`filesystem_unsupported`) where exchange is impossible, for partial restores too. Rejected: a silent two-rename fallback (a moment with no `WTF/`; a missing file reads as "reset this addon").
- **M3-D26: a whole restore keeps the current `WTF/` as a `before_restore` backup** on filesystems that can reflink.
- **M3-D29: restores never run while the client runs;** the widget disables the choices, the CLI refuses, and README states the residual launch race.
- **M3-D9 and M3-D46: destructive actions preview, then run bound to the preview** (`restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`); `plan_stale` reloads the dialog.
- **M3-D47: integrity is explicit;** "verified" only for `verified`, with its baseline.
- **M3-D48: reader reservations make a restore's source busy;** the widget disables prune on busy backups.
- **M3-D30 (context): `backups.auto` reports mode, observed capability and the last result separately,** which the view's labels follow.
- **M3-D2: templates land with their commands;** exact ids in slots; `--addon={addon}` as one element.

**Review-round changes folded in.**
- Round 3 (revision 20, single-addon recovery in the widget) created this task (split from F6), the restore-scope chooser with addon first, the `r` key in Installed and Issues, and the "no implicit target" rule; (revision 2) made partial restores exchange-only, which is why `filesystem_unsupported` applies to both scopes; (revision 5) added the version context and capture-time folders the chooser shows; (revision 7) bound restore and prune to their previews; (revision 23) added `busy`.

**Facts verified during planning.**
- `PanelKeyCatcher` maps `x` to `deleteRequested` and Space to `activateRequested`; `r` and `b` arrive as `textKey` (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.5).
- Running detection fails closed when `/proc` is unreadable, and `PolicyOp::RestoreSavedVariables` refuses unconditionally while the client runs (`src/engine/running.rs:143-157` as of `af10e34`).
- Rename across mounts fails with `EXDEV` even on the same filesystem, and renaming a mount point fails with `EBUSY`; FUSE and network filesystems generally lack `RENAME_EXCHANGE` (milestone epic comment "Ground truth (§2)", §2.4 item 16).

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Risk 11 (whole restore when one addon was meant): addon scope first, counts, the whole-scope label, `before_restore`, undo.
- Risk 21 (preview drift): tokens on restore and prune.
- Risk 8 (writes while the client runs): the CLI's refusal at plan time, under the lock and before recovery; the widget's disable.
- Ownership confusion after an addon changed folders: the CLI's capture-time resolution and `ref_ambiguous`; the widget only offers the CLI's alternatives.

**Confidence.** Medium, as the plan rates widget polish across Omarchy updates (an external API, mitigated by F0 and a small surface). The task is UI over D7 and D8's tested commands, with no engine scope of its own (the restore protocol underneath is the plan's medium-confidence part, owned by D5 and D14); the risk here is presentation and keyboard flow, checked by QML tests and G3's real-machine round trip.

title: Epic: M3 docs and checkpoint
description:
## Background

Area G of M3 (milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`): docs, vision records and the checkpoint.

README.md is the product contract: it must describe exactly what exists, no more and no less. The vision bead `omad-vision-8qa` records decisions, and its body lets later comments supersede it, so every M3 decision that departs from or adds to the vision, every contract addition and every new constant must be written there as a comment. The checkpoint proves the milestone: each of the fourteen success criteria on the milestone epic is run and its evidence recorded, in the M2 format `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>`.

## Goals

- **G1** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1` (README final pass): reconcile every section the M3 leaves edited, through G1's README checklist (the status line, "What works today" and the Roadmap; every count; the Files table, the Safety model, Network and Configuration, including the `auto_backup` default; the FAQ and "For coding agents"; Limitations, including synthetic-only `errors` validation, the pre-M3-binary note and the restore filesystem requirement), so README describes exactly what exists.
- **G2** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2` (Vision comments): the M3 comments on the vision bead: decisions and departures, contract additions and the wire-name glossary, constants, scope changes.
- **G3** `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3` (The M3 checkpoint): run all fourteen criteria and record evidence, commit hash, test names, timings and every `SKIP` line in the close reason; leave the widget installed and enabled.

## Success Criteria

- G1's README checklist is complete, each item checked off with a line number, and README matches `main`, including the `auto_backup` `daily` default and the documented limitations; `rumdl check README.md` reports no new findings compared with `af10e34`.
- G2's vision comments are written and each departure, addition and constant is recorded; `br lint` is clean on every bead touched.
- Every one of the fourteen milestone criteria is `[x]` with evidence; any `SKIP` outside the pre-accepted list makes G3 defer itself with `NEEDS OWNER: accept SKIP …` instead of closing.
- The real-capture limitation is stated in G3's close reason and in README, and the widget is left installed and enabled.

## Non-Goals

- New features.
- Owner beads: limitations that need a person (real BugGrabber captures from a played session) are documented instead.

## Considerations

- **These are the last three steps of both critical paths** (… → G1 → G2 → G3). G1 waits on every leaf that ships a user-visible surface or evidence (B7, C3, D7, D8, D9, D10, D11, D12, D13, E3, E4, F7); G3 also waits on D12, E3, E4 and F7 directly.
- **G3 leaves the widget installed and enabled** on the development machine: it is M3's deliverable.
- **README's status line** becomes "Milestones 1, 2 and 3 are done …", naming the widget, `errors` and `backup`, with Milestone 4 next, in G1's pass (its README checklist). The vision's "M3 is done" comment (vision §10, with deviations) is G3's last step, followed by `br epic close-eligible`.
- **Slice.** All three leaves belong to `slice-4` (portability and close).
acceptance_criteria: G1-G3 are closed; G1's README checklist is complete with a line number for each item and README describes exactly what exists on main, including the auto_backup daily default and the documented limitations, with rumdl check reporting no new findings against af10e34; the vision bead carries the M3 comments for decisions and departures, contract additions and wire names, constants and scope changes, and br lint is clean on every bead touched; G3's close reason records [x] evidence for all fourteen checkpoint criteria with every SKIP quoted and only pre-accepted SKIPs; the real-capture limitation is stated in the close reason and README; the widget is left installed and enabled.

title: README final pass
description:
## Background

README.md is the product contract (project CLAUDE.md: "README.md is the product contract: where it answers, that is the answer"). Every M3 feature task updates its own README section in the same commit as the code (common rule 11), so by the time this task starts each section is individually right. What no single feature task can do is make the **whole** document true and consistent at once: the status line, "What works today", the comparison table, every count (error and warning codes, failpoints, fuzz targets, tests, catalog entries), the Files table, the Safety model, Network, Configuration, the FAQ, "For coding agents", Troubleshooting and Limitations. M3 adds three command trees (`errors`, `backup`, `omarchy`), a widget, a new source, new state files, new safety rules and one owner-visible default change, which touches nearly every section.

This task is the final consistency pass, not the first mention. It serves **checkpoint criterion 12**: "README describes exactly what exists, and the vision has M3 comments for decisions, contract additions, constants, scope changes and departures" (the vision half is G2, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`). It also carries the user-facing statements several decisions require README to make:
- **M3-D30 (owner-visible):** `auto_backup` now defaults to `daily` (copy-on-write only), with the new value `daily-copy`; README previously promised "default `off`; used from milestone 3". Plan approval approved this change; README must state it. If the owner ever rejects it, D3 changes one constant and this section's default sentence.
- **M3-D29 / M3-D24:** the restore launch race (process detection is a refusal check, not exclusion; a launch in the last milliseconds cannot be prevented; the consequence README must state is that the game may then write its in-memory settings over the restored files at logout, and that the undo snapshot keeps the pre-restore tree), and the requirement that restores need atomic exchange (a plain `WTF/` on the same mount as `Interface/`, on a filesystem with `RENAME_EXCHANGE`: btrfs, ext4, xfs, tmpfs), with the manual-copy workaround from `<meta>/backups/<id>/WTF/`.
- **M3-D45:** "do not run a pre-M3 build against state M3 has written; reading with it is safe", plus D12's (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) characterization of what af10e34 actually does. The note itself comes from A3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.3`), which opened README Limitations with: "Do not run a pre-M3 omaddons build to change state that M3 has written. Reading with it (`status`, `list`, `history`) is safe. A pre-M3 `undo` cannot see M3 restores." D12 copies its observed behaviour (the blind SavedVariables undo, asserted as observed) into the same section. G1 checks both are there and agree.
- **M3-D21:** the strict privacy contract for `errors` and `--raw-details`, which promises no anonymity.
- **M3-D6:** `omarchy plugin remove a44.omaddons` cannot work for house plugins (it assumes directory == id); `omaddons omarchy remove` is the supported path.
- **The real-capture limitation** (recorded, not filed): `errors` was validated on synthetic fixtures that follow BugGrabber's public structure, not on a capture from a played session, because no agent can play the game.

## Technical Approach

### Method

1. Read README.md top to bottom against `main`. For every claim M3 touched, check it against the code or a command's actual output, not against a bead: `omaddons help <cmd>` and `--json` envelopes for the command reference, `src/error.rs` for code counts (the count asserts at `src/error.rs:763-777` for errors and `:809` for warnings, as of `af10e34`), `src/engine/tx.rs` `FAILPOINTS` for the failpoint count, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` for the fuzz-target count (17 at `af10e34`), `cargo test -- --list` for the test count (about 1,590 at `af10e34`), `catalog/catalog.toml` for the catalog count.
2. Work through the checklist below, ticking each item with the README line number where it now lives. Record the ticked list in the close comment.
3. Run the house prose checks (the `de-slopify` skill's checks) on every new or rewritten paragraph.
4. Run `rumdl check README.md` (rumdl is installed; the repo has a `.rumdl_cache`) and compare with the findings at `af10e34`: no new findings.
5. README-only commits may skip `argc gate` (project CLAUDE.md), but if any doc test or snapshot embeds README text, run the gate.

### The "done" flips are prepared here and committed by G3

The status line, the "What works today" M3 row and the Roadmap's M3 entry say M3 is **done**. As in M2 (README said M2 was done only at its checkpoint), those three flips land in the commit that records the M3 checkpoint, G3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3`; the checkpoint protocol's "Record" step: "the README status line flipped (G1 prepared it)"). G1 writes everything else, and puts the **exact replacement text** for the three flips in its close comment, so G3 applies them verbatim with the checkpoint date. (The checkpoint protocol names only the status line as "prepared by G1"; holding back the "What works today" M3 row and the Roadmap entry the same way, because they also say M3 is done, is decided while writing this bead.)

### The checklist (README change checklist; line numbers as of `af10e34`)

- [ ] **Status line (41).** "Milestones 1, 2 and 3 are done …", naming the widget, `errors` and `backup`, with Milestone 4 next. *(Prepared here; committed by G3.)* At `af10e34` the line says Milestones 1 and 2 are done and "Milestone 3, the Omarchy widget, is next".
- [ ] **"What works today" (123–152).**
  - The M3 row flips to ✅ *(prepared here; committed by G3)*.
  - New rows: the widget (with the restore chooser); `errors` and `errors dismiss`; BugGrabber via `wowace:`; `backup` (create/list/verify/restore/prune/export/import); automatic checkpoints; `status` triage blocks; preview tokens.
- [ ] **Design philosophy 4 (166).** "the Omarchy widget renders the same envelope without logic of its own" (drop "future").
- [ ] **How omaddons compares (174–191).** Add rows: "Lua error triage", "Settings backups and restore".
- [ ] **Sources and refs table (484–498).** Add the `wowace:` row (pinned revisions): ref forms `wowace:<slug>`, `wowace:<slug>#<tag>`, `wowace:<slug>#r<rev>`, and pasted `repos.wowace.com/wow/<slug>/…` and `www.wowace.com/projects/<slug>` links.
- [ ] **Catalog (521–586).**
  - The count changes: 62, plus the BugGrabber variants, plus any verified legacy ones.
  - Variants and `catalog.d` override semantics (whole name vs `name#variant`).
  - The BugSack note (538).
- [ ] **Command reference.** New `### errors` (with `dismiss`, `--received`, `--raw-details`), `### backup` (each subcommand, `verify` included), `### omarchy`. Under `### status`: summary, issues, errors, backups (auto mode and capability, free space), last_change (and `last_change_state`), widget.
- [ ] **Global options.** `--actor widget` is real (623). `--if-match` is new (accepted by `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`; a usage error elsewhere).
- [ ] **The JSON contract.**

### Reference values to check against (from the contract)

- **Error codes** (39 → 41): new `file_exists` (exit 4, not retryable, prose fix "choose another file name, or delete that file yourself") and `filesystem_unsupported` (exit 4, not retryable, `details.reason` `wtf_is_mount_point|stage_cross_mount|no_rename_exchange`, `details.backup_dir`).

Help groups: Look gains `errors` after `search`; Change gains `backup` after `undo`; Setup gains `omarchy` before `help` (M3-D39).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every checklist item above is checked off with the README line number where it now lives, recorded in the close comment; the three "done" flips (status line, the "What works today" M3 row, the Roadmap entry) are prepared as exact replacement text in the close comment for G3 to commit.
- Every count in README matches the code on `main` (error codes 41, warning codes 49, failpoints 34 in both mentions, fuzz targets 20, the current test count, the catalog count).

- `rumdl check README.md` reports no new findings compared with `af10e34`.
- The house prose checks (`de-slopify`) were run on every new or rewritten paragraph.
- README gains no personal data: no real usernames, hostnames, emails or machine-specific absolute paths (the house rule on names; the generic home-relative default locations README already uses stay). This criterion is added while writing this bead.

## Test Plan

- `rumdl check README.md` on `main` and on `af10e34` (for example from a worktree), compared finding by finding.
- Cross-checks: `omaddons help` and `omaddons help <cmd>` for each new command against the command reference; `--json` envelopes from the contract snapshots (`tests/contract/snapshots/`) against the JSON-contract section; the code registries for counts (`src/error.rs` count asserts, `FAILPOINTS`, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/`, `cargo test -- --list | wc -l`).
- If any test embeds README text (for example help-text or link checks), `argc gate` passes.

## Considerations

- **Feature beads own their sections; G1 reconciles.** If a section is wrong because a feature shipped differently, fix README to match the code, and if the code is wrong rather than README, file a bug with `--deps discovered-from:omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1` instead of documenting a defect as a feature.
- **Owner-visible change (M3-D30).** The `auto_backup` default sentence is the one README promise M3 changes; plan approval approved it. Risk 10 (the owner rejects the flip) is mitigated by one constant in D3 plus this sentence.
- **Risk 17 (the Forever launch on 2026-11-04 lands mid-M3).** M3 changes neither discovery nor rules; if README's Forever notes need an update after launch, that is `omad-wez`'s work, not this task's.
- **Collision hot spot:** `README.md` is edited by every M3 task (each its own section); G1 runs last, after all of them, and reconciles. Rebase before editing.
- **Schedule.** G1 is on **both critical paths** (the widget path A2 → F1 → F2 → F3 → E1 → E2 → E3 → G1 → G2 → G3 and the restore path D1 → D5 → D14 → D8 → D7 → F9 → F7 → G1 → G2 → G3); earliest start t=16 in the six-lane schedule (lane 2).
- **Delivery.** Slice `slice-4` (S4, "Portability and close": D9, D10, D12, F7, G1, G2, G3). Its exit demo, run by whoever closes the slice's last task and recorded as a comment on the milestone epic: export → import → restore byte-identical; integration scenes; the af10e34 characterization; perf; gate from a clean checkout; README. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 8 (export, import), 9 (integration), 10, 11, 12 and 14 (the characterization). G1 supplies the README part.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**

- D11 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.11` (Backups in `status`): the `status` backups block (auto mode and capability, free space) and its recommendations.
- D12 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12` (Integration crash matrices, concurrency and performance checkpoints): the failpoint counts (27 → 34), the af10e34 characterization quoted in Limitations, and the measured numbers.
- D13 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.13` (`backup verify` and integrity states): `### backup verify`, the integrity vocabulary, and the agents' `backup verify` line.
- E3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.3` (`omaddons omarchy status` and `omaddons omarchy remove`): `### omarchy`, the supported removal path, and the `omarchy plugin remove` troubleshooting entry.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** README is the product contract: for a person it is the manual, and for an agent it is the specification it codes and scripts against. M3 touches almost every section of it (three new command trees, a widget, a new source, new state files, new safety rules, a changed default), and each feature task only edits its own section. Without a final pass the document ends up individually right and collectively wrong: stale counts, a status line that says M3 is next, Limitations that still say "no backups", a troubleshooting guide with no entry for the new refusals. This bead makes the whole of it true at once, and checkpoint criterion 12 cannot pass without it. It also carries the honest statements M3 owes its users: the restore launch race, the atomic-exchange requirement, the pre-M3-binary warning, the synthetic-fixture limitation of `errors`, and the `auto_backup` default change.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M3-D30 (owner-visible): `auto_backup` defaults to `daily`.** The one README promise M3 changes ("default `off`; used from milestone 3"); by the house rules a change to a README promise needs the owner, and approving the plan approved it. If rejected, D3 changes one constant and this sentence. Rejected (in the decision): keeping `off` (the protection would not reach the users who need it), `daily` with byte copies everywhere, a separate `auto_backup_copy` boolean.
- **M3-D45: formats fail closed; pre-M3 binaries are characterized, not guarded.** README Limitations says "do not run a pre-M3 build against state M3 has written; reading with it is safe" and quotes D12's observed af10e34 behaviour. Rejected: claiming a downgrade barrier that does not exist.
- **M3-D29 / M3-D24: restores never run while the client runs, and need atomic exchange.** README states that process detection is a refusal check, not exclusion, and names the manual-copy workaround for filesystems without `RENAME_EXCHANGE`. Rejected (in M3-D24): a silent two-rename fallback and an `--allow-gap` mode.
- **M3-D21: privacy is a contract on kinds of text.** README documents strict default output and `--raw-details`, which promises no anonymity.
- **M3-D6: the plugin folder is `<plugins>/omaddons/`, id `a44.omaddons`.** README says `omaddons omarchy remove` is the supported removal and that `omarchy plugin remove a44.omaddons` does not work for house plugins.
- **M3-D39: help layout** (Look gains `errors`, Change gains `backup`, Setup gains `omarchy`), reflected in the command reference.
- **DEC-4 and the contract counts:** error codes 39 → 41, warnings 41 → 49 (`widget_outdated` no longer reserved), failpoints 27 → 34, fuzz targets 17 → 20.
- **Checkpoint protocol (M2 precedent): "done" is said only at the checkpoint.** Not an M3-Dn decision: the protocol's Record step says the README status line is flipped at the checkpoint, prepared by G1. This bead extends that to the What-works-today and Roadmap flips (its own choice); G3 commits all three with the checkpoint date.

**Review-round changes folded in.** Round 3 added several Limitations and Troubleshooting items this pass must carry: revision 21 (the pre-M3-binary note and D12's characterization), revision 2 (exchange-only restores, partial restores included, and the stated launch race), revision 10 (strict privacy and `--raw-details`), revision 23 (apparent vs free space in the FAQ and "Automatic backups"), and revision 22's removal of the owner bead, which turned the real-capture gap into a documented limitation instead of a task.

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`:
- README's status line (line 41) says Milestones 1 and 2 are done and "Milestone 3, the Omarchy widget, is next"; the checklist's other line anchors (123–152 What works today, 166, 174–191, 484–498, 521–586, 623, 1349, 1420–1427, 1549, 1580, 1652, 1837, 1845–1868, 1883, 1956, 2002–2035) were read at `af10e34`.
- README mentions "27" engine failpoints twice (lines 1427 and 1919).
- 17 fuzz targets exist (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/`); about 1,590 tests are listed by `cargo test -- --list`; 39 error and 41 warning codes are asserted in `src/error.rs` (`:763-777`, `:809`); the catalog has 62 entries.
- `rumdl` is installed and the repo has a `.rumdl_cache`.
- Project CLAUDE.md lets README-only commits skip `argc gate`.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Documenting what was planned instead of what shipped: every claim is checked against `main` (help output, envelopes, registries), and feature close comments win over the planning text.
- Saying "done" before the checkpoint passes: the three flips are prepared, not committed, until G3.
- Owner rejection of the `auto_backup` default (risk 10): one sentence here and one constant in D3.

**Confidence.** High: a bounded documentation pass with an explicit checklist and mechanical checks (counts, `rumdl`).
