**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** The vision bead is how every future agent learns what omaddons is. Its body is frozen at revision 2, and the design moves forward only through comments. M3 departs from the vision in eleven places, changes two §5.5 engine rules (write scopes; journal and recovery), fills in §5.8 and §5.11 with real designs, adds about a hundred wire names before the M4 contract freeze, and observed facts that supersede UNVERIFIED notes. Unless those are recorded where the design lives, M4's contract freeze and doctor will be built against a vision that no longer describes the code. This bead writes them from what actually shipped (close comments, code, README), which is what checkpoint criterion 12 asks for and what DEC-4 requires before the freeze.

**Decisions applied.**
- **The departures themselves** (each recorded by this bead, per the decision log): M3-D1 (three enabling additions: doorbell, triage blocks, `wowace:`); M3-D2 (argv-only execution from classified CLI output and a validated template table); M3-D4 (the doorbell file replaces `status.json` as the widget's signal; rejected: watching `status.json` plus caches, ringing from every command, a socket); M3-D8 (enable by default; rejected: the vision's opt-in `--enable`); M3-D9 with M3-D46 (stored plans stay in M4; previews bound by stateless precondition tokens; rejected: pulling stored plans into M3, previews without binding); M3-D10 (widget settings trimmed to six); M3-D15 (BugGrabber from WowAce SVN, pinned per tag revision, narrow packaging subset; rejected: GitHub mirrors, CurseForge's website API, manual downloads); M3-D19 (dismissal as a subcommand and durable state, session watermarks; rejected: a flag on a read command, storing it in the cache, per-fingerprint watermarks); M3-D30 (owner-visible: `auto_backup` default `daily`); M3-D35 (`backup import`); M3-D47 (`backup verify`).
- **M3-D45 (a strict change from M2, recorded on the vision):** a journal with an undecodable complete line was pruned by M2 and is now kept; readers fail closed; no downgrade barrier against M2 is claimed.
- **Scope-table and doctor-contract changes the decision log says must be recorded:** the `Wtf` root renamable by `BackupRestore` (M3-D24 (a)); `Scope::History` admitting `Omarchy` and the Omarchy stage/old/trash rows (M3-D38); `stamp:sha256:` digests and `MutateOpts::stamp_before/after`, which touch the doctor's `before_hash` semantics (M3-D25); `WTF.previous` outside `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES`, reported in `snapshot_bytes` (M3-D48).
- **DEC-4, D21, D22:** additive contract recorded before the freeze; the wire-names golden file is M4, so the vision comments are the record; constants recorded as shipped.

**Review-round changes folded in.** Round 3 added the topics of comments 2 and 3 that did not exist before (reader reservations and `DirLock`, per-operation widget stages, the preservation protocol, journal 1.1 and fail-closed readers, the exchange-only rule for partial restores, early `state_too_new`), and the af10e34 characterization and BugSack's received-report semantics in comment 9. Revision 8's adaptation (session watermarks, not per-fingerprint ones) is why comment 5 must say "and why not fingerprints".

**Facts verified during planning.**
- The vision bead `omad-vision-8qa` has body revision 2 and 93 comments as of 2026-10-21; its recent comments use the "§x.y Title (bead ids). What · Why · How · Contract" style and say what they supersede ("the body is not edited").
- Project CLAUDE.md: "its body is authoritative, and comments added after body revision 2 supersede it."
- The vision's statements M3 departs from: §5.11's `status.json` doorbell and "mutating buttons first fetch a plan and then call apply"; §5.6's `auto_backup` default `off`; the backup command list (create, list, restore, export, prune); vision comment 606's options for BugGrabber (a git mirror, CurseForge in M5, or a manual `--file` install); the opt-in `--enable`.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- Recording the plan instead of what shipped: close comments and code win; differences are named.
- Missing a wire name: comment 7 is reconciled against the registries and the contract snapshots, not only against the plan's list.
- Public text: every comment file is scanned for paths and names before it is added.

**Confidence.** High: writing comments from an explicit list against shipped, close-commented code.

title: The M3 checkpoint
description:
## Background

This is the M3 checkpoint: the task that proves the milestone, records the evidence, and closes it. It amends vision §7 "M3 checkpoints" with fourteen criteria (below). It follows every other M3 leaf (directly D12, E3, E4, F7 and G2; transitively all 46 others), so when it starts, every feature exists and every task's own tests have passed.

It runs each criterion and records the evidence in its close reason in the M2 format, `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>`, with commit hash, test names, medians and p95, `net.log` counts, screenshot names (scratch only, never committed), the IPC `state()` outputs, `shell.json` diffs, and every `SKIP` line quoted. It then writes the vision's "M3 is done" comment, commits README's three "done" flips that G1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1`) prepared, and closes the epics.

Two things make this checkpoint different from M2's:
- **Pre-accepted `SKIP`s.** Approving the M3 plan accepted exactly four `SKIP`s in advance, so G3 never needs an owner bead or an owner decision at close (project CLAUDE.md, "Blocked on a Human": no owner beads). Any other `SKIP` means the criterion is not met, and G3 then **defers itself** (an existing bead may be deferred; a new owner bead is never filed).
- **A documented limitation instead of an owner session.** No agent can play the game, so `errors` is validated on synthetic fixtures that follow BugGrabber's public structure, not on a capture from a played session. G3's close reason and README Limitations say so plainly.

**The widget stays installed and enabled** at the end: it is M3's deliverable.

## Technical Approach

### Step 0: freeze

- Every leaf is closed.
- The four slice demos are recorded on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx` as comments in the `[x] … : evidence` style (each recorded by the agent who closed that slice's last task; a missing one is run and recorded now):

  | Slice | Tasks | Exit demo |
  |---|---|---|
  | **S1. See and update from the bar** | A1, A2, A4, F0, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, E1, E2, E3, E4 | `omarchy install` on the desktop; the badge follows a terminal `update` within 1 s; update one addon from the panel, undo it; a `remove` preview gone stale gives `plan_stale`; reinstall swaps atomically |
  | **S2. Capture and diagnose** | A5, B1–B8, C1–C3, D1–D4, D11, D13, F6, F8 | `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and wotlk; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a simulated session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal |
  | **S3. Recover** | A3, D5, D6, D14, D8, D7, F9 | whole and `--addon` restores from the CLI and from the bar's chooser, each undone; the crash matrices of D5, D6, D7 and D14 |
  | **S4. Portability and close** | D9, D10, D12, F7, G1, G2, G3 | export → import → restore byte-identical; integration scenes; the af10e34 characterization; perf; gate from a clean checkout; README |

- `br epic close-eligible` shows the M3 epic ready apart from this task.

### Step 1: gate and checkpoint runs, in this order

1. `argc gate --all` **from a clean checkout** with no generated artifacts (the widget pipeline included: real-binary envelopes → `bun test omarchy/tests` → `validate_built_argv` → `qmltestrunner` on a copy with a fixture `Build.js`; M3-D41).
2. Perf: `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home` (medians and p95).
3. `argc bench`.
4. Fuzz: `argc fuzz-all --time 600 --toolchain <nightly>` (every target 10 minutes), plus `argc fuzz savedvariables --time 1800` and `argc fuzz wowace_listing --time 1800`.
5. The af10e34 characterization: `cargo test --release --test compat_m2 -- --ignored` (D12's, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`, rerun; its table goes in the close reason).
6. Live probes: `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored` (with `catalog_matches_declared_flavors`, the new WowAce probe `wowace_bug_grabber_decodes`, and the BugGrabber upstream field check).
7. Real machine: `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=keyless_installs_forever cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1`, with the new M3 real-machine tests:
   - `errors_reads_every_client_read_only`;
   - `backup_create_list_prune_on_retail` (the backup is pruned afterwards);
   - `restore_addon_then_undo_on_classic` (`WTF/` hash identical after);
   - `buggrabber_installs_then_undo` on retail and on wotlk.
8. `qmllint` on a **rendered** copy of the plugin (E1's `render` into scratch, so `Build.js` exists), with `-I <omarchy>/shell`: zero errors; warnings recorded.
9. Coverage: `cargo llvm-cov` line coverage, recorded.

Real-machine rules hold throughout (common rule 10): never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`; its stress-test set stays guarded until `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` closes, deferred to 2026-11-05), undo every change before asserting, record every `SKIP` line, and never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.

### Step 2: on the desktop

1. `omaddons omarchy install`.
2. Record `omarchy-shell a44.omaddons state` before and after each scripted change.
3. **The doorbell latency harness:** a script in scratch that runs `omaddons backup create -t retail --reason "doorbell latency check"` and `omaddons backup prune <id> -t retail` 10 times each, timing each ring until IPC `state()` changes.
   - Both ring, and neither touches AddOns or `WTF/`.
   - Not a pin/unpin loop: that would leave records that block undoing the install (`undo_conflict`) on the owner's real client.
   - Afterwards: `backup list` shows no leftover, and the AddOns hash is unchanged. Forever is never touched.
4. **`grim` screenshots of each bar state**, forced through fixture homes run by a **second, isolated widget** when real states cannot be produced.
   - Isolated means a temporary plugin id `a44.omaddons-checkpoint`, installed by a **debug** build run with E1's `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID=checkpoint` seam (DEC-7; release builds ignore it; pattern `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`, giving id `a44.omaddons-<suffix>` and directory `<plugins>/omaddons-<suffix>`) and fixture `HOME`/`XDG_*` values. The stamped context (M3-D7: `Build.CONTEXT` overlaid on every omaddons child) then sends every command it runs to the fixture state, with no wrapper script.
   - **The context check (criterion 1):** through the checkpoint widget's IPC `state()` and its own cache's doorbell, show that its commands reach only the isolated state.
   - It is removed afterwards with the same seam (`omarchy remove`).
5. The real widget **stays installed and enabled**. Record the final `shell.json` diff.

### Step 3: the known limitation, recorded, not filed

No agent can play the game, so `errors` has been validated on synthetic fixtures that follow the public structure, not on a real capture from a played session. The close reason and README Limitations say so plainly.
- Per the project rules (CLAUDE.md, "Blocked on a Human"), **no new bead is filed for the owner**.
- If a real capture is ever indispensable to an existing task, that task is deferred with `NEEDS OWNER: …`, as the rules allow. Otherwise the limitation simply stays documented.

### Step 4: record

- The close reason, in the M2 format: one `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>` line per criterion (below), with every `SKIP` quoted.
- The vision comment on `omad-vision-8qa`: "vision §10 Milestone status: M3 … is done (date)", with deviations, in the G2 style ("**Title (bead ids).** What · Why · How · Contract"). This is comment 10 of the M3 vision set; G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) wrote 1–9.
- README: commit the three "done" flips G1 prepared in its close comment (the status line "Milestones 1, 2 and 3 are done …", the "What works today" M3 row ✅, and the Roadmap's "M3 ✅" with its date). The checkpoint protocol names only "the README status line flipped (G1 prepared it)"; G1's bead holds back the other two flips the same way, because they also say M3 is done.

### Step 5: close

`br epic close-eligible` until nothing more closes (the area epics, then the milestone epic). The widget stays installed.

### Deferral rule for an unexpected `SKIP`

Any `SKIP` not in the pre-accepted list below means that criterion is not met. Then G3 defers **itself**:

```bash
br defer omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3 --transition-comment "NEEDS OWNER: accept SKIP <name> · <why no agent can run it> · <what accepting changes>"
```

### The M3 checkpoint criteria (these amend vision §7 "M3 checkpoints")

**Pre-accepted `SKIP`s.** Approving the plan accepted exactly these in advance:
- a running game client, when no client can be launched by an agent (criterion 2's running-state check, F0);
- the bind-mount and size-limited-tmpfs sandbox tests (`unshare -rm`), where unprivileged user namespaces are unavailable on the machine running them;
- the af10e34 characterization's build, if that commit no longer builds with the installed toolchain (D12 records the error);
- `keyless_installs_forever`, which M2 already allows through `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` until the Forever client's guard lifts.

1. **Widget install.**
   - The embedded plugin passes `omarchy-plugin-validate` and omaddons' own validator.
   - `omaddons omarchy install` on the development machine produces a working, enabled widget on both monitors, with exactly one service instance and one registered IPC handler (`omarchy-shell a44.omaddons state` answers).
   - A reinstall swaps atomically. Every install stages in its own hidden `<plugins>/.omaddons.stage-<ulid>`, so the registry never loads it. Two installers racing each other never mix or delete each other's stage.
   - Every omaddons process the widget starts runs under the `HOME`/XDG context stamped at install, checked by a test that launches the widget under different roots.
   - `omaddons omarchy remove` leaves `<plugins>` and the bar layout as they were before install, apart from the history line.
   - *(Amended: enable is the default; two monitors.)*
2. **Doorbell latency.**
   - A change made from a terminal shows in the widget's IPC `state()` within 1 s, at the 95th percentile of 20 trials. The harness runs `backup create` and `backup prune` on retail 10 times each (Step 2.3). Both ring, neither touches AddOns or `WTF/`, and nothing is left behind. Forever is never touched.
   - An update check run from a terminal (`outdated`) changes the badge within 1 s.
   - A window opening or closing triggers a refresh within 1 s.
   - The running state follows a real client starting and exiting. The agent launches the 3.3.5a client to its login screen; if no client can be launched, the criterion records a `SKIP` from the pre-accepted list above.
   - *(Amended: the vision checked only mutations and window events.)*
3. **Opening the panel performs no network I/O.** `net.log` is unchanged across 10 panel opens and view switches.
4. **Widget states.** Each state renders correctly, checked through `qmltestrunner` scenarios and on the real machine through IPC `state()` plus a `grim` screenshot of the bar:
   - updates pending;
   - a P0/P1 issue;
   - new Lua errors;
   - a client running (update labels say "then /reload"; a refused action shows its reason);
   - no targets;
   - binary missing;
   - widget outdated or incompatible (read-only: actions disabled, only Retry and Reinstall offered);
   - an action in progress, showing progress from NDJSON;
   - an action failed, showing its fix;
   - a preview gone stale (`plan_stale`), showing the fresh preview instead of running.
5. **Argv-only execution.**
   - Every argv the widget can run comes from CLI output or from the template table, which `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` validates. That includes parsing with hostile slot values: spaces, `!`, `$(…)`, a leading `-`.
   - The argv validated in Rust are exactly the ones `Model.buildArgv` emits in bun, produced fresh in the same gate run, never substituted a second time in Rust.
   - CLI-provided argv pass the same classifier as templates (a known command path, no standard flag overridden, previews for destructive ones), not merely an `omaddons` prefix.
   - No `bash -c` and no `Util.execDetached` appears in the widget, checked by a source scan.
   - Every source-derived string renders through the shared plain-text component (`PlainLabel.qml`), checked by a source scan.
6. **`errors`.**
   - It parses synthetic fixtures for every BugGrabber era: integer time, string time first-seen, string time last-seen, r152 chunked, and an embedded `BugGrabberDB` in another addon's file.
   - It parses both file formats (modern no-indent CRLF; legacy tabs with `-- [n]`). It attributes each error to the right managed addon, including the library-dispatch, WeakAuras-chunk, `ADDON_ACTION_FORBIDDEN` and truncated-path cases (the attribution cases of B4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.4`), and it reports the attribution method and confidence.
   - **Privacy:**
     - default and `-v` output contain only code-derived text: recognized Lua and Blizzard message templates, locations, function names, counts and fingerprints;
     - custom messages, locals and chunk contents appear only with `--raw-details`;
     - no output on any channel prints an account, realm or character name, including progress, warnings and errors (`assert_private`, with adversarial names planted in messages, chunks, paths and symlink targets).
   - Received reports are listed apart and never count as new, never notify and never cause an update recommendation.
   - Filtered reads (`--addon`, `--since`, `--limit`) never change the memo or `status`'s counts. `--since` reports uncertain matches instead of silently dropping them.
   - A dismissal survives deleting `<cache>`. It never acknowledges errors the user was not shown: the widget binds it to the shown observation.
   - Parsing stays within its time and memory budgets on adversarial files (fragment floods, tiny-token tables, deep skipped globals, many candidate files). An over-budget file is reported as incomplete and not retried on every doorbell.
   - The `savedvariables` fuzz target runs ≥ 30 min without a crash.
   - A 4 MB BugGrabber file parses in under 20 ms (release build).
7. **BugGrabber installs keylessly.**
   - `omaddons install buggrabber` installs the newest WowAce tag on synthetic retail, Mists Classic, Era, Anniversary and Forever clients, and r152 on the 3.3.5a client (real machine, then undone).
   - Every file of the tag is fetched at one recorded revision. A tag moved mid-fetch cannot mix revisions, an unrelated upstream commit never shows as an update, and a locked reinstall fetches the same revision again.
   - A project that needs a packaging step omaddons does not implement (externals, moves, keywords other than `@project-version@`, build-type blocks) is refused, not installed half-built.
   - `net.log` shows only allowlisted hosts and zero GitHub REST requests.
   - *(Added: the handoff required a source.)*
8. **Backups.**
   - `backup create` of a 500 MB synthetic `WTF/` in 5,000 files on btrfs completes in under 1 s (release build, median of 5). That is the vision's budget, at a realistic file count: SavedVariables trees hold few, large files. 20,000 files is measured and reported without a budget.
   - In clone-only mode (`daily`), a filesystem that cannot clone costs zero copied payload bytes. A tree that changes during capture is retried once, then marked `best_effort`, never reported as stable.
   - `backup verify` detects same-size corruption in a backup whose hashes were recorded at capture or import, and says so when it can only set a first baseline.
   - A whole restore and an `--addon` restore are each undoable and refused while the client runs. A whole restore is refused, before anything is copied, where `WTF/` cannot be exchanged atomically (a mount point, a cross-mount stage, a filesystem without `RENAME_EXCHANGE`).
   - The global lock hold of a restore is under 50 ms with that same tree.
   - `backup export` → `backup import` → `backup restore` reproduces a `WTF/` that is byte-identical (`tree_hash`, exact modes included). Import accepts only an exact manifest-to-payload match.
   - No output names an account, realm or character.
   - **Auto backups:**
     - a pre-change checkpoint at most once per local day, and a post-session checkpoint after each play session that changed settings (also caught up at widget start);
     - no capture when nothing changed since the newest qualifying capture;
     - never on a dry run, and never failing a transaction;
     - an imported, partial or best-effort backup never counts as today's checkpoint;
     - below `limits.backup_min_free_mb` of free space, automatic capture first reclaims eligible automatic backups, then skips with a visible reason, and never deletes a manual, imported or recovered backup;
     - concurrent due checks on one target make one backup, and a backup being restored or exported is never pruned under it.
9. **Crash safety.**
   - Every engine failpoint, armed as a real `abort` during a whole restore, a partial restore and an undo of each, leaves the change wholly old or wholly new. A whole restore is judged by the `WTF/` `tree_hash`. A partial restore is judged per touched file, plus an unchanged hash of the rest of `WTF/`.
   - The next change command recovers it. Recovery direction follows the durable journal phase: backward before `swapped`, forward from it.
   - A crashed restore rolls back once its client is not running. Every displaced version that differs from a copy still held elsewhere is preserved as a `recovered` backup, through a journaled intent that a crash during recovery resumes with the same backup id (`restore_rolled_back`). A file the game replaced stays as the game wrote it.
   - Recovery is itself crash-tested at every preservation transition, and under injected I/O failures and disk-full. An unrecognized state or an incomplete preservation leaves every tree, the stage and the journal in place (`journal_pending`, manual repair as in M2); it never cleans up to finish.
   - With the client running or its state unknown, a crashed restore's journal stays pending and nothing under `WTF/` moves. It rolls back once the client exits. In-process recovery makes the same fresh check.
10. **`status --cached` stays under 5 ms** (median of 21, release build), with p95 and cold-start times recorded, with the new `summary`, `issues`, `errors`, `backups`, `last_change` and `widget` blocks. The home is the realistic one of `tests/perf.rs`, plus:
    - 4 backups per target and one target with 200 manual backups;
    - a 2 MB BugGrabber file per target and 16 accounts on one target;
    - a 20 MB history of interleaved runs.

    A missing or stale projection reports "unknown", never a guess. (Noted while writing this bead: D12's perf run may predate B7 or E4; this run, after every leaf, is the binding measurement.)
11. **Gate and checkpoint runs.**
    - `argc gate --all` passes, including the new widget tests (`bun test`, `qmltestrunner`), from a clean checkout with no generated artifacts.
    - Every fuzz target runs for 10 minutes; `savedvariables` and `wowace_listing` run 30 minutes.
    - Live probes and real-machine tests pass, with every `SKIP` quoted.
    - Line coverage is recorded.
12. **README describes exactly what exists**, and the vision has M3 comments for decisions, contract additions, constants, scope changes and departures (G1 and G2).
13. **Destructive previews are binding.** For `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`, a test changes state between `--dry-run` and the real run with `--if-match`. The real run refuses with `plan_stale` and changes nothing: no newly selected object is deleted or overwritten. *(Added: M3-D46.)*
14. **Persisted formats fail closed.**
    - A journal with an unreadable `prepared` line, an unknown step or a newer major version is left pending with its stage and snapshots, never pruned.
    - Undo refuses with `undo_conflict` when an unreadable history line on the same target might hide a conflict.
    - The af10e34 binary, run against committed and interrupted M3 restores, is characterized: what it refuses, what it would do, and where, recorded in D12's close comment and README Limitations. *(Added: M3-D45.)*

### Where each criterion's evidence comes from

Compiled while writing this bead from the task specs, as a guide to where each criterion's evidence is produced; it adds no criterion.

| Criterion | Evidence produced by |
|---|---|
| 1 | E1's validator, E2 and E3 (`tests/omarchy.rs`, two-installer races), the context test that launches the widget under different roots (F2's QML `Process` mock records `environment`); Step 2 on the desktop and the checkpoint widget's context check |
| 2 | F2/F8 QML tests; Step 2.3's latency harness (p95 of 20); the 3.3.5a launch or its pre-accepted `SKIP` |
| 3 | the panel-open read sequence (F2, F4), which runs local reads only; `net.log` before and after 10 opens and view switches |
| 4 | F3–F6, F9 `qmltestrunner` scenarios; IPC `state()` and `grim` screenshots (checkpoint widget where real states cannot be produced) |
| 5 | F7 (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs` `validate_built_argv`, the source scans), M3-D41's pipeline in the gate |
| 6 | B1–B8 tests, the `savedvariables` 30-minute fuzz run, the 4 MB perf test, `errors_reads_every_client_read_only` |
| 7 | C1–C3 tests, `wowace_bug_grabber_decodes`, `buggrabber_installs_then_undo` on retail and wotlk |
| 8 | D1–D4, D7–D10, D13 tests; D12's perf tests; `backup_create_list_prune_on_retail`, `restore_addon_then_undo_on_classic` |
| 9 | D5, D6, D7, D14 matrices; D12's scenes and full sweep |
| 10 | the perf run in Step 1 |
| 11 | Step 1 |
| 12 | G1's checklist, G2's comments |
| 13 | `tests/preconditions.rs` (A4, extended by B8, D4, D8) |
| 14 | A3's planted-journal and planted-history tests; D12's characterization rerun in Step 1.5 |

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every one of the fourteen criteria above is `[x]` in the close reason with its evidence (commit hash, test names, medians and p95, `net.log` counts, screenshot names, IPC `state()` outputs, `shell.json` diffs), or carries a `SKIP` from the pre-accepted list, quoted verbatim.
- Any other `SKIP` defers G3 with `NEEDS OWNER: accept SKIP <name> · <why no agent can run it> · <what accepting changes>`; no new bead is filed for the owner.
- The four slice demos are recorded on the milestone epic before the freeze.
- The af10e34 characterization table is in the close reason.
- The real-capture limitation is stated in the close reason and in README Limitations.
- The vision has the "M3 is done" comment with deviations; README's status line, "What works today" M3 row and Roadmap entry say M3 is done, with the date.
- `br epic close-eligible` closes the area epics and the milestone epic; nothing M3 remains open.
- The widget is installed and enabled on the development machine at the end, with the final `shell.json` diff recorded; the isolated checkpoint widget is removed; Forever was never touched; every real-machine change was undone (`WTF/` and AddOns hashes as before).

## Test Plan

The runs of Step 1, in order, and the desktop checks of Step 2. Specifically:
- `argc gate --all` from a clean checkout (a fresh worktree or `git clean -xdf` equivalent in a scratch clone), so no generated widget artifact is present.
- Perf (release, `#[ignore]`), `argc bench`, fuzz (10 minutes each; 30 for `savedvariables` and `wowace_listing`), `compat_m2`, live probes, real machine with `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=keyless_installs_forever` and `--test-threads=1`, `qmllint` on a rendered copy with `-I <omarchy>/shell`, `cargo llvm-cov`.
- Desktop: IPC `state()` transcripts, the doorbell latency harness (20 trials, p95), `grim` screenshots (kept in scratch, named in the close reason), the checkpoint widget's context check, `shell.json` diffs.

## Considerations

- **Forever.** The Forever client's stress-test set stays guarded until `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` closes (deferred to 2026-11-05). WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04 and may land mid-M3 (risk 17); M3 changes neither discovery nor rules, real-machine tests never touch Forever, and `omad-wez` re-probes after launch.
- **Omarchy changes its plugin API** (risk 1; it ships often, 4.0.6 at planning). F0 verified the surface the widget uses; IPC `state()` makes breakage detectable by an agent. If the shell version on the desktop has moved since F0, record the version in the close reason and rerun F0's checks before the desktop step (a step added while writing this bead).
- **Do not leave residue on the owner's clients.** Every real-machine change is undone before asserting; the doorbell harness uses backup create/prune (no records left), not pin/unpin.
- **Screenshots and transcripts stay in scratch**, never committed, and the close reason names them only.
- **Public-safe close reason:** no home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders.
- **Schedule.** G3 is the last node of **both critical paths** (… → G1 → G2 → G3); t=18 → done at t=20 in the six-lane schedule (lane 2).
- **Delivery.** Slice `slice-4` (S4, "Portability and close"); this task records S4's demo if no earlier closer did.

**Common rules for every M3 bead.** Every M3 leaf carries this same block. Plan keys (A1 … G3) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`). A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's subprocess allowlist, with its reason. A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry.
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command task adds its own clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, dispatch arm, help-layout update, contract matrix rows (one success and one failure, with snapshots), and the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path. The full list of touch points (line numbers as of `af10e34`):
   1. `src/cli.rs` `Command` variant (doc comment = about; `after_long_help` examples);
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod`, `COMMANDS` entry (one per nested path), `command_name` arm, `dispatch` arm;
   3. `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (`Args`, `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema`, `impl Outcome` with `command()` equal to the `command_name` string);
   4. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows and `tests/contract/snapshots/`;
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs:317-372` read-only invocations;
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:119-143` literals and the bare-help snapshots;
   7. `src/app/help.rs:404-444` planned-layout test;
   8. `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` when `status` gains a recommendation;
   9. `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS` for any new `Versioned` file;
   10. README's command reference section;
   11. once F1 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1`) has landed, the `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js` (path, `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`). The always-on test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` fails when a registry path is missing there.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
6. **DEC-4, additive contract.** List every new wire name (codes, keys, actions, purposes, kinds) in the close comment, so G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`) can record them on the vision bead. Never rename or remove an existing key. `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a name-list entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. Prose fixes may not name a runnable omaddons command. The guard is `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs:48-81`. **There is no `TEXT_FIXES` list; do not copy that sentence from M2 beads.**
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character: not JSON, not human text, not stderr progress, not warning or error details, not notifications (M3-D21).
   - A task that prints or reports a path below `WTF/` passes it through `privacy::WtfPathRedactor` (A5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.5`; the strict errors renderer is B5, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.5`).
   - Tests that create `WTF/` use the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names and `assert_private` (pattern: `tests/undo_history.rs:21-23`, `:118-124`; A5 moves them to `tests/common/privacy.rs` and adds `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`). They run it over stdout **and** stderr, with `--progress json`.
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, and record every `SKIP` line. They never write under a `WTF/` except through a restore under test, which they undo, after which `WTF/` must hash as before.
11. **README is the product contract.** A task that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.** Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`. File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`. Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean. Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`. Bead text never contains home paths, hostnames or names; use the placeholders (`<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`, `<meta>`, `<config-omarchy>`, `<plugins>`, `<omarchy>`) defined in the milestone epic body.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time (auto backups, display) takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` through `TestEnv` (D1, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1`, adds it to `tests/common/env.rs`).
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A task that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule or a preservation step closes only when its own crash and recovery matrix passes. That matrix covers every failpoint it adds, every journaled rename, repeated recovery, injected I/O failure and disk-full where it writes. D12 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12`) integrates and extends across features; it never discovers whether a task's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A task that reads an untrusted or user-sized input (SavedVariables, a server listing, an archive, a backup tree, history) bounds it with a named constant and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.
16. **Previews bind.** A task that adds a destructive command, or a destructive path to an existing one, computes its `precondition` through `app::precondition` (A4, `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4`) and honours `--if-match`, with a test that changes state between preview and run (M3-D46).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**
- D12 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12` (Integration crash matrices, concurrency and performance checkpoints): the crash, concurrency and perf evidence for criteria 8, 9 and 10, and the af10e34 characterization this task reruns for criterion 14.
- E3 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.3` (`omaddons omarchy status` and `omaddons omarchy remove`): `omarchy remove` (criterion 1's remove-restores-the-bar check, and removing the checkpoint widget) and `omarchy status`.
- E4 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.4` (The widget in `status`): the `status` widget block and `widget_outdated` for criteria 4 and 10.
- F7 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.7` (Widget security and contract checks): criterion 5's argv-only evidence and the finished widget with every view.
- G2 `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2` (Vision comments): criterion 12's vision half; this task's "M3 is done" comment follows comments 1–9.

**Unblocks:** none. This is the last M3 task; closing it lets `br epic close-eligible` close the area epics and the milestone epic.

Transitively every other M3 leaf blocks this task (through D12, E3, E4, F7 and G2); those are inherited relations, not list entries.

Parent: the G epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7`. Delivery slice: `slice-4`.
