comments.author: HazyMaple
comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M3 plan, 2026-10-21).**

**Why this bead.** A milestone is done when its promises are demonstrated on the real machine, not when its beads are closed. This bead runs every checkpoint criterion against `main` and the owner's desktop, records the evidence in a form the next agent can audit (`[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>`, every `SKIP` quoted), writes the vision's "M3 is done" record, flips README's status, and closes the epics. It leaves the bar widget installed and enabled, because the widget is what M3 delivers. It is also where the milestone's honesty rules meet: only the four `SKIP`s the owner pre-accepted by approving the plan are allowed, anything else defers this bead with a precise `NEEDS OWNER` line, and the one thing no agent can do (play a session that produces a real BugGrabber capture) is stated as a limitation rather than filed as an owner bead.

**Decisions applied.**
- **Pre-accepted `SKIP`s (the M3 success criteria's preamble; the owner bead they make unnecessary was removed in review round 3, revision 22).** Approving the plan accepts exactly four `SKIP`s (no launchable client for criterion 2's running-state check; no unprivileged user namespaces for the `unshare -rm` sandbox tests; af10e34 not building; `keyless_installs_forever` while Forever is guarded), so G3 never needs an owner decision at close. Why: project CLAUDE.md forbids owner beads; an existing bead may be deferred. Rejected: an owner bead for the real-capture session (the earlier plan's version, removed in round 3).
- **M3-D41: widget tests in the gate, one ordered pipeline, from a clean checkout;** `qmllint` at checkpoints with zero errors on a rendered copy (so `Build.js` exists). Rejected (in the decision): running the Rust argv check before bun produced its input, and substituting slots a second time in Rust.
- **M3-D7: the binary, data context and content hash stamped at install.** The checkpoint widget (`OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID=checkpoint`, a debug-only DEC-7 seam) proves every command the widget runs reaches only its stamped state, with no wrapper script.
- **M3-D8: enable by default** and **M3-D5: one shared service per shell** (two monitors on the development machine): criterion 1 checks both bars and exactly one service and IPC handler.
- **M3-D4: the doorbell** (criterion 2's latency harness uses backup create/prune because both ring and neither touches AddOns or `WTF/`; a pin/unpin loop would leave records that block undoing the install on the owner's client).
- **M3-D45:** the af10e34 characterization is rerun here and its table goes in the close reason.
- **M3-D30 (owner-visible):** the `auto_backup` default ships as approved; G3 records it among the deviations in the "M3 is done" comment.
- **Checkpoint protocol (M2 precedent; not an M3-Dn decision):** README says M3 is done only in the checkpoint commit; G1 prepared the text (the protocol names the status line; G1's bead extends the hand-off to the What-works-today row and the Roadmap entry).

**Review-round changes folded in.** Round 3, revision 22 (protocol tests in their tasks; gate ordering; slices): the gate runs from a clean checkout with the ordered widget pipeline; the four delivery slices are demonstrated as they land and recorded on the milestone epic before the freeze; the owner bead was replaced by pre-accepted `SKIP`s and a documented limitation. Criteria 13 (binding previews, M3-D46) and 14 (fail-closed formats, M3-D45) were added in round 3; criterion 7 was added because the handoff required a keyless BugGrabber source; criteria 1 and 2 were amended (enable by default, two monitors; terminal-driven latency, not only mutations and window events).

**Facts verified during planning.** As of `af10e34`:
- The development machine runs Omarchy 4.0.6, Quickshell 0.3.2, Qt 6.12.0 and Hyprland 0.56.2 with **two monitors**; `qmltestrunner`, `qmllint`, `grim`, `bun` and `cargo llvm-cov` are installed.
- Seven targets exist (retail, classic/Mists, era, anniversary, forever, the 3.3.5a private server, and a Warcraft III folder that HEAD skips); every path is on btrfs; real `WTF/` trees are tiny (232–596 KB), so the 500 MB budget is measured synthetically.
- `tests/real_machine.rs` has `forever_guard()` and `keyless_installs_forever` (allowed through `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP`); `tests/common/checkpoint.rs` prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` and fails unless allowed.
- `argc fuzz` and `argc fuzz-all --time` exist (`Argcfile.sh`); 17 fuzz targets exist before M3 (20 after).
- omaddons is not on the shell's PATH (it runs from `target/release/`), which is why the widget stamps an absolute binary path.
- The Forever stress-test set stays guarded until `omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6` closes (deferred to 2026-11-05); WoW: Forever launches on 2026-11-04.

**Risks and mitigations.**
- An unexpected `SKIP` at the last step: only the four pre-accepted ones pass; anything else defers G3 with a precise `NEEDS OWNER` line instead of closing on weaker evidence.
- Omarchy's plugin API moved since F0 (risk 1): record the shell version; rerun F0's checks before the desktop step.
- Residue on the owner's clients: every change undone and hashed; latency harness without records; Forever untouched (risk 17).
- Real states that cannot be produced on demand (for example "binary missing"): the isolated checkpoint widget on fixture homes.

**Confidence.** Medium-high: every criterion has a named producer and a scripted run, but the desktop steps depend on the live shell and on whether an agent can launch the 3.3.5a client (pre-accepted as a `SKIP` if not).

title: Single-file archives are refused whole when one side folder lists only another client's interface (ArkInventory, Titan Panel)
description:
## Background

README "How omaddons decides what loads" promises the following. Without a publisher `release.json` that declares the client, the addon's own folder must load. Every skipped folder must also rule itself out: a game-type gate, TOCs only for other clients, or a dependency on such a folder. "A folder that merely lists another client's interface marks a build for another client, and the whole archive is refused." `accepts` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:964`) implements this.

The keyless-coverage study (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7, 2026-10-20) found the rule refusing archives whose main addon loads, from sources that offer exactly one file:

- **ArkInventory 3.12.17** (`wowi:6488`) on Mists Classic, Classic Era and Forever. ArkInventory, ArkInventoryConfig, ArkInventoryRules and ArkInventorySearch load and are current. `ArkInventoryRules_Example` is an example rules module whose plain TOC lists only 120105, so the whole archive is refused. The publisher's GitHub repository has no releases, which leaves WoWInterface as its only keyless source.
- **Titan Panel 9.3.5** (`wowi:8092`) on Anniversary. Titan and 14 plugins load and are current. `TitanAmmo` lists `11509, 16001, 205056`, where 205056 is a typo for a 2.5.x interface, so the archive is refused. No other keyless source was found.

The game client would load these addons and show the odd folder as incompatible. WoWInterface and Tukui serve one file per project, so the refusal leaves the user nothing to install. The rule exists to keep a build for another client out: a retail zip of a per-flavor project whose shared main TOC lists every interface.

## Technical Approach

The decision is the owner's, because it changes a README promise. Options:

1. Keep the rule, and say in the refusal which folder caused it and that the rest would load.
2. For sources with a single candidate per release (`wowi:`, `tukui:`, `url:`, `--file`, local), skip a folder that lists only other clients' interfaces when nothing that loads requires it. Report it in `folders.skipped` and warn.
3. Apply option 2 everywhere, keeping the refusal only when a better-ranked candidate exists for this client in the same release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The chosen option is recorded in README "How omaddons decides what loads", and `accepts` follows it.
- Under options 2 and 3, fixtures shaped like ArkInventory 3.12.17 and Titan Panel 9.3.5 install on the clients above, with the odd folder in `folders.skipped`. A per-flavor retail zip whose main TOC lists every interface is still refused when the release offers a classic zip.

## Test Plan

- Engine fixtures for both archives and for the per-flavor case.
- `argc gate`.

## Considerations

- 4 of the 700 WoWInterface × client cells in the study were lost to this rule. The data is in the study's report on omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7.
acceptance_criteria: the owner's chosen option is recorded in README 'How omaddons decides what loads' and implemented in accepts; under options 2/3, ArkInventory 3.12.17- and Titan Panel 9.3.5-shaped fixtures install with the odd folder skipped while a per-flavor retail zip is still refused when a classic zip exists; argc gate passes

comments.author: CosmicKettle
comments.text: NEEDS OWNER: whether a single-file source's archive (WoWInterface, Tukui, url:, local) may skip a side folder that lists only another client's interface instead of being refused whole · README 'How omaddons decides what loads' promises the refusal, and changing a README promise is the owner's call · the answer picks option 1, 2 or 3 in the body: 1 keeps the rule with a clearer message, 2 or 3 let ArkInventory install on Mists Classic, Classic Era and Forever and Titan Panel on Anniversary

title: `auth github set` and `clear` record a history line when the stored token does not change
description:
## Background

The closing check of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz) found that `auth github set` and `auth github clear` record a history line on every run, even when the stored token does not change.

README's history section says settings changes (`config set`, `targets add`/`rm`/`rename`/`default`, `auth github set` and `clear`, `export --write`) each record a line of kind `config`, `target`, `auth` or `export`, and: "A dry run, or a change to nothing, records none."

The other settings commands keep that promise:

- `config set` compares the new file text with the old and writes and records only when they differ (src/app/config.rs:324-335, `changed && !ctx.dry_run`).
- `targets add` records one line per client it actually registered, none when every one already was (src/app/targets.rs:403-412); the other `targets` changes have the same no-op paths (src/app/targets.rs:560-597).
- `export --write` returns "is up to date" without writing or recording when the file already holds the same content (src/app/export.rs:442-445).

`auth` does not. `run` (src/app/auth.rs:166-175) calls `write` for every `set` and `clear`, and `write` (src/app/auth.rs:298-334) always rewrites the credentials file and always calls `super::record_setting(..., TxKind::Auth, None)`, which appends a history line and rings the doorbell. Clearing an already empty (or missing) credentials file, or storing the token that is already stored, adds an `auth` line each time. History then shows settings changes that did not happen, and the doorbell wakes listeners for nothing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh HOME (an empty directory), `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`.
2. `omaddons auth github clear --json` twice.
3. `echo -n ghp_abcdef0123456789 | omaddons auth github set --json` twice (same token).
4. `omaddons history --json`: `data.entries` holds four entries of kind `auth`, two with argv `auth github clear` and two with `auth github set`. Only one of the four (the first `set`) changed the stored token.

## Technical Approach

- In `write` (src/app/auth.rs), after taking the global lock and recovering journals (both must still happen: README lists `auth github set` and `clear` among the commands that recover under the lock even when they change nothing), read the current credentials file.
- Treat a missing file and an empty file as the same state, "no token" (README: "an empty file is no token").
- When the current content equals the content to write, skip the `WriteFile` and skip `record_setting` (no history line, no doorbell). Still apply the 0700 `Chmod` on the credentials directory when it exists, since that tightening is a safety repair, not a settings change.
- Reading the file is a read, so it may use `std::fs::read`; the single-writer rule (only src/fsx/ writes) is unaffected.
- The outcome stays the same shape (`{configured, source, rate_limit, dry_run}`); the human line may say "already stored" / "already clear" if the renderer distinguishes it, but that is optional.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `auth github clear` on a missing or empty credentials file records no history line and leaves the file as it was (or absent).
- `auth github set` with the token already stored records no history line and does not rewrite the file.
- `auth github set` with a different token, and `clear` of a stored token, each record exactly one `auth` line, as today.
- Both still take the global lock and recover a pending journal first.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- E2E (tests/auth.rs): in a fresh HOME, `clear`, `clear`, `set T`, `set T`, `set U`, `clear`; `history --json` holds exactly three `auth` entries (set T, set U, clear) in that order.
- E2E: a no-op `clear` with a journal pending still recovers it (`journal_recovered` warning), with no `auth` history line.
- Unit (if `write` gains a helper): equal content → no write, no record; different content → write and record.

## Considerations

- Compare bytes exactly. A token with a trailing newline in the file versus none on stdin would count as a change; `set` already strips input through `checked`/`valid`, so stored tokens have no trailing whitespace.
- A credentials file with loose permissions (`credential_file_mode` warning) and unchanged content: the fix leaves its mode to the existing warning's `chmod 600` fix rather than silently rewriting it, unless the implementer decides the no-op path should also re-apply 0600 through `Op::Chmod`. Either is fine; record the choice in the close reason.
- `--dry-run` already writes and records nothing; keep that.
acceptance_criteria: clear of a missing or empty credentials file and set of the already stored token record no history line and do not rewrite the file; a real change records exactly one auth line; both still take the global lock and recover journals; argc gate passes

title: `outdated` human footer says "to install them" for an adopt hint when no update is available
description:
## Background

The closing check of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz) found a wrong human footer on `outdated`.

`OutdatedOutcome::render_human` (src/app/outdated.rs:264-268) ends with:

```rust
if let Some(hint) = self.commands.first() {
    writeln!(w, "Run `{}` to install them.", hint.command())?;
}
```

It assumes the first command hint is the update hint. But `commands` is built as the update hint (if any) followed by adopt hints (src/app/outdated.rs:561-562: `hints(&out_targets)` then `super::status::adopt_hints(...)`). `hints` returns nothing when no target has an update (src/app/outdated.rs:800-818), and `adopt_hints` (src/app/status.rs:707-733) adds `omaddons adopt -t <id>` for each client that manages nothing yet and holds an adoptable folder. In that case the only hint is the adopt hint, and the footer tells a human to "Run `omaddons adopt -t retail` to install them." after a summary that says there are no updates. tests/adopt_hints.rs:249-265 (`outdated_and_update_hint_adopt_only_where_nothing_is_managed_yet`) covers this exact state in JSON, where `commands` holds only the adopt hint; the human render was never checked.

The JSON contract is right (each hint has its own `action`); only the human sentence is wrong. `assertion_failure` (`--check`, src/app/outdated.rs:211-224) also uses `commands.first()`, but only when `update_available > 0`, where the update hint is always first, so it is correct.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh HOME with one synthetic retail client (a Battle.net root with `.build.info`, `_retail_/.flavor.info`, `_retail_/WoW.exe`, `_retail_/Interface/AddOns/`), no managed addons.
2. Add a catalog.d override naming a folder (`[[addon]] name = "Foo", ref = "gh:o/foo", folders = ["Foo"]`) and create `Interface/AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc`.
3. `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 omaddons outdated --format human` prints:
   ```
   No updates on 1 client · nothing checked
   Run `omaddons adopt -t retail` to install them.
   ```
4. `--json` shows `commands` = `[{"action":"adopt","command":"omaddons adopt -t retail",...}]`.

## Technical Approach

- In `render_human`, find the hint whose action is `update` (`self.commands.iter().find(|c| c.action() == "update")`, adding an accessor on `CommandHint` if none exists) and print "Run `…` to install them." only for it.
- For adopt hints, either print nothing extra (the adopt suggestion stays in JSON `commands`), or print a separate line that says what it does, e.g. "Run `omaddons adopt -t retail` to bring folders installed by hand under management." Pick one and keep it to one line per hint; `status`'s human render may already have wording for `adopt` to reuse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With no update and an adopt hint, the human output never says "to install them" and never presents the adopt command as an install.
- With an update available (one or several clients), the footer is unchanged: "Run `omaddons update[ -t <id>]` to install them."
- With both an update and an adopt hint, the update footer names the update command (not the adopt command).
- JSON output is unchanged.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- E2E (tests/adopt_hints.rs): extend `outdated_and_update_hint_adopt_only_where_nothing_is_managed_yet` to run `outdated --format human` (or the suite's human-output helper) and assert the output does not contain "to install them".
- E2E (tests/outdated.rs): an existing update scenario still prints the update footer; add a scenario with both an update on one client and an adoptable folder on another client and assert the footer names `omaddons update`.
- If human output is snapshotted, update the snapshot.

## Considerations

- `CommandHint` keeps `action` private (src/error.rs:405-410); add a read accessor rather than matching on the argv.
- At 7fb0a2c this is the only "to install them" footer in src/app/; `update` also gets adopt hints but has no such footer. The other `commands.first()` users (src/app/undo.rs:201, src/app/search.rs:179) build their own `commands` and are not affected.
acceptance_criteria: with no update and an adopt hint the human output never says "to install them"; with updates the footer names the update command (also when an adopt hint exists); JSON unchanged; argc gate passes

title: A target-level planning error is reported as an unchanged item with ok:true
description:
## Background

`plan()` in `src/engine/plan.rs` fails a whole target when the target's inventory cannot be read: it pushes one `PlanFailure` with `ref: None` and `addon: None`, and plans none of that target's changes. `build_items()` in `src/app/install.rs` only maps a ref-less failure onto items that were planned (that path exists for commit-time failures). An item that was never planned and has no failure of its own falls through to `status: unchanged`, with `name: null`. Nothing else reports the error: it is not in `warnings` and not in `error`.

So an agent sees `ok: true`, exit 0 and "unchanged" for an install that never happened, and the real error (`io`, with its fix) is lost. That breaks the contract's promise that every failure carries a code and a fix (vision G4, §5.9).

Found while fixing omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.2 (install into a never-launched client).

## Steps to Reproduce

Verified 2026-10-15 in a throwaway HOME with a synthetic Battle.net tree (`wowf` in `.build.info`, an empty `_forever_/Wow.exe`):

1. Make `_forever_/Interface/AddOns` a regular file instead of a directory (any unreadable AddOns works).
2. `omaddons install plater -t forever --json`.
3. Result: `{"ok":true,"exit_code":0,"partial":false,"error":null}`, with one item `{"name":null,"status":"unchanged","error":null}` and no warnings.
4. Human output: `forever: plater unchanged (?)`, exit 0.

## Technical Approach

1. **Fail each item, not the target.** When `inventory()` fails in `plan()`, push one `PlanFailure` per requested change on that target, each with its `ref` (and `addon` for removes), all carrying the same error. Then `build_items()` marks every item failed through its existing per-ref path. Commit-time failures keep `ref: None`, since they apply to planned items.
2. **Check the other consumers.** `src/app/remove.rs` and `choose_target()` in `src/app/install.rs` read `failures` the same way. A remove on an unreadable AddOns must fail too. The probe must treat the error as non-client-specific (`io` is not `no_compatible_release`), so it is reported rather than skipped.
3. **No silent fall-through.** In `build_items()`, an item that was neither planned nor failed, while a ref-less failure exists for its target, is a bug. Make it a failed item with that error, as a safety net.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `install <ref> -t <id>` on a target whose AddOns is a regular file exits 1 with `error.code` `io` and a fix. It is never `ok: true` or `unchanged`.
- With two refs on such a target, both items fail, and the command returns the first item's error with `details.items` listing both.
- `remove <addon> -t <id>` on such a target fails the same way.
- A commit-time failure still marks only the planned items failed; unchanged items stay unchanged.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- **E2E** (`tests/install.rs`): AddOns as a regular file, with one ref and with two refs: assert exit code, `error.code`, per-item errors, and that nothing is reported unchanged.
- **E2E** (`tests/remove.rs`): the same for remove.
- **Unit** (`src/app/install.rs` tests): `build_items` with a plan-time ref-less failure and unplanned items yields failed items.

## Considerations

- `PlanFailure.target` names the target, so per-item failures stay attributable.
- Keep the error's own code (`io`, `state_too_new`, ...); do not wrap it.
- The inventory error path is rare (permissions, a file where a folder belongs, I/O errors), which is why no test caught it.
acceptance_criteria: install on a target whose AddOns cannot be read exits 1 with the io error (never ok:true/unchanged); two refs both fail with details.items; remove fails the same way; commit-time failures still only fail planned items; argc gate passes
close_reason: plan() now fails every change of a target whose inventory cannot be read, each under its own ref and addon, instead of one ref-less failure that build_items could not attach to an unplanned item. install reports each item failed with the io error (exit 1, details.items listing every request); remove already matched ref-less failures and now matches by addon too; commit-time failures are untouched, so unchanged items stay unchanged.

comments.author: RustyDolphin
comments.text: claim: src/engine/plan.rs (per-change failures when the inventory fails), tests/install.rs, tests/remove.rs

comments.author: RustyDolphin
comments.text: done: argc gate passes; tests/install.rs an_unreadable_addons_folder_fails_every_item (AddOns a regular file: one ref exits 1 with io; two refs list both with io; nothing unchanged) failed before the fix with ok:true/unchanged; tests/remove.rs an_unreadable_addons_folder_fails_the_removal guards remove. decided: no build_items safety net for unplanned items, because a commit-time ref-less failure must leave genuinely unchanged items unchanged · found: none

title: `help auth github` and `auth github --help` fail with a cut-off usage error; install REF help and git log purposes are incomplete
description:
## Background

The closing check of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz) compared README.md with the code at 7fb0a2c. README presents `auth github` as a command: it has its own section under "Command reference" (`### auth github`), and `### help [COMMAND]` says `omaddons help targets add` shows "a subcommand by its path; the same as omaddons targets add --help". An agent that follows that pattern for `auth github` gets a usage error instead of help, and the error message is cut off mid-sentence.

Two causes, one per spelling:

- `omaddons help auth github`: `help::for_command` (src/app/help.rs:248-290) walks the words of the name one clap subcommand at a time. `github` is not a subcommand of `auth`; it is the value of `auth`'s first positional `SERVICE` (an `AuthService` value enum, src/app/auth.rs:36-43). The walk fails on `github`, and because `auth` has no subcommands at all, the message is built as `there is no command "auth github": auth has ` followed by an empty list.
- `omaddons auth github --help` (and `auth github set --help`): the global help flag parses, and `dispatch` (src/app/mod.rs:316-321) calls `help::for_command(Some(name))` with the command's envelope name, which `command_name` gives as `"auth github"` (src/app/mod.rs:205). The same walk then fails the same way.

`omaddons help auth` and `omaddons auth --help` work, so the help text exists; only the path `auth github` does not resolve.

Two small text defects found by the same check are folded in here, since each is a one-line change:

- `install`'s `REF` help (src/app/install.rs, the doc comment on `InstallArgs::refs`, around line 53) lists the canonical refs as "gh:, git:, url:, file:". `wowi:` and `tukui:` are canonical refs too: src/sources/refs.rs parses `wowi:5108` and `tukui:elvui` as `MatchKind::Canonical`, and README's ref table lists both. `omaddons help install` therefore under-documents what `install` accepts.
- The doc comment on `GitLogEntry::purpose` (src/net/log.rs:64) says the purpose is "`ls-remote`, `clone` or `fetch`". src/sources/git_hosts.rs also runs and logs `init`, `checkout` and `rev-parse` (in `materialize`, lines 403-470), and every run goes through `run_watched`, which writes a net.log line with that purpose. A reader of the type (or of net.log) is told three values when there are six.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a fresh HOME (an empty directory), with `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`, run `omaddons help auth github --json`.
2. Observe exit 2 and `error.message` = `there is no command "auth github": auth has ` (the sentence ends after "has"), fix `omaddons help auth`.
3. Run `omaddons auth github --help` and `omaddons auth github set --help`: the same usage error, exit 2.
4. Run `omaddons help install --format human`: the `REF` line names "gh:, git:, url:, file:" and neither `wowi:` nor `tukui:`.
5. Read src/net/log.rs:64 against the `purpose` strings passed in src/sources/git_hosts.rs (`init`, `fetch`, `checkout`, `clone`, `rev-parse`, `ls-remote`).

## Technical Approach

- In `help::for_command`, when a word is not a subcommand of the command walked so far, check whether it is a possible value of that command's first positional argument (clap's `get_arguments()` → positional → `get_possible_values()`). If it is, stop walking and render that command's help: `help auth github` and `auth github --help` show `auth`'s help. Words after the value (`auth github set`) are values of later positionals; accept them the same way rather than failing.
- Make the error message never end in an empty list: when the command walked so far has no subcommands, say so (`auth takes no subcommands`) instead of `auth has `.
- Keep the fix (`omaddons help auth`) and the alternatives as they are for a word that is neither a subcommand nor a positional value (`help auth gihub` stays a usage error).
- Add `wowi:` and `tukui:` to the `REF` doc comment in src/app/install.rs, keeping the comment's style ("a canonical ref (gh:, git:, url:, file:, wowi:, tukui:)").
- Change the doc comment in src/net/log.rs:64 to list every purpose git runs log: `ls-remote`, `init`, `fetch`, `checkout`, `clone` or `rev-parse`.
- If the help-text snapshots under tests/ change (the `install` help), update them in the same commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons help auth github`, `omaddons auth github --help` and `omaddons auth github set --help` exit 0 and show `auth`'s help (usage `omaddons auth [OPTIONS] <SERVICE> [ACTION]`).
- `omaddons help auth gihub` is still a usage error, and its message is a complete sentence (no trailing "has ").
- No usage-error message from `help` ends with an empty list.
- `omaddons help install` names `wowi:` and `tukui:` among the canonical refs.
- The `GitLogEntry::purpose` doc comment lists all six purposes git runs log.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (src/app/help.rs tests): `for_command(Some("auth github"))` and `for_command(Some("auth github set"))` return `auth`'s help; `for_command(Some("auth gihub"))` is `usage` with a message that does not end in "has ".
- E2E (tests/cli_skeleton.rs or the contract suite): `auth github --help --json` exits 0 with `command` `help`; `help auth github --json` likewise.
- Contract: add `["auth", "github", "--help"]` to whichever corpus checks that every documented help path resolves, if one exists; otherwise the E2E case above covers it.
- The `install` help snapshot (if any) shows the two added schemes.

## Considerations

- `auth` is the only command whose envelope name (`auth github`) holds a positional value, so the `--help` path through `command_name` breaks only here today. A later command with the same shape (a service or kind as its first word) would break the same way; resolving positional values in `for_command` covers it generically.
- Do not make `github` a real clap subcommand: that changes the parse tree, the usage-fix corpus entries for `auth gihub` / `auth github st` (tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs), and the envelope `command` name.
- README.md is being updated separately; this bead changes only code and doc comments.
acceptance_criteria: help auth github, auth github --help and auth github set --help exit 0 with auth help; help auth gihub stays a usage error with a complete message (no trailing "has "); install REF help names wowi: and tukui:; GitLogEntry::purpose doc lists ls-remote, init, fetch, checkout, clone, rev-parse; argc gate passes

title: An install from another ref silently replaces a same-named managed addon and reports a fresh install
description:
## Background

Folders owned by another addon are protected: installing over them is `ownership_conflict` (exit 4) unless `--force` is given. `--force` marks the old owner degraded with an `ownership_transferred` warning (`src/engine/ownership.rs`).

Addon identity, however, is the lowercased addon name (`src/state/records.rs` around lines 40-42, `src/engine/ownership.rs` around lines 172-178). So an install whose ref differs from the record's ref, but whose addon has the same name, is treated as the same addon:

- `install ./Bar-2.1.0.zip` then `install ./Bar-2.2.0.zip` (two different `file:` refs);
- `install gh:demo/bar --file Bar-2.2.0.zip` over a `Bar` installed from a `file:` ref;
- in principle, a second repository whose addon folder happens to be named like an installed one.

In each case the folder and record are replaced without `--force` and without a warning. The item reports `status: "installed"` and `from_version: null`, as if nothing had been there. The record's ref silently switches to the new one, so future updates come from a different source than the user chose.

Found while exercising install, remove and undo for the README rewrite, and confirmed by the README fact-check. README.md lists it under Known issues.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `omaddons install ./Bar-2.1.0.zip -t retail` (Bar becomes managed from `file:…/Bar-2.1.0.zip`).
2. `omaddons install gh:demo/bar --file ./Bar-2.2.0.zip -t retail --offline --json`
3. Result: exit 0, item `installed`, `from_version: null`, folder Bar replaced, the record's ref now `gh:demo/bar`.

The same happens with `omaddons install ./Bar-2.2.0.zip -t retail` in step 2.

## Technical Approach

- Decide the identity rule and record it with `decided:`. The sensible default:
  - the same ref is the same addon (update, no `--force`);
  - a different ref whose folders another record owns is a takeover, so `ownership_conflict` unless `--force`;
  - two `file:` refs are the exception, because a local update is just a newer zip of the same addon. Either treat any local ref as replaceable by another local ref of the same name, reported as `updated`, or require `--force`. Pick one and document it.
- Repointing an addon to another ref on purpose belongs to `adopt --ref` / repoint in M2 (omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.5.5.2). This bead only makes the implicit switch explicit.
- Whatever the outcome, report the real `from_version`, `status: "updated"` where it is one, and the folder under `folders.replaced`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Installing a different (non-local) ref over an addon managed from another ref needs `--force`, and the forced install emits `ownership_transferred`.
- The chosen local-zip rule is implemented and documented in README.md and `install --help`.
- `from_version`, `status` and `folders.replaced` are correct for every replacement.
- Undo of the forced install restores the original record, ref and folder.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/install.rs`: both reproductions, unforced and forced, asserting the item fields and the warning.
- `tests/engine_undo.rs`: undo after the forced transfer restores the original ref and bytes.

## Considerations

- Same-ref reinstalls and updates must stay free of `--force`.
- `gh:` and `git:` refs of the same repository are different refs.
- Catalog names resolve to a ref first, so `install dbm` over a DBM installed as `gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods` is the same ref.
acceptance_criteria: a different non-local ref over a managed addon needs --force and the forced install warns ownership_transferred; the local-zip rule is decided and documented; from_version, status and folders.replaced are correct; undo restores the original ref and folder; argc gate passes
close_reason: same-name installs from another ref: local zip over local zip is an update; any other ref is a takeover needing --force (ownership_transferred, real from_version, undoable); documented; gate green

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text:
**done:** An install from another ref no longer silently replaces an addon of the same name. `argc gate` passes: 1194 tests, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical.

**decided (the identity rule):** an addon is installed from one ref at a time.
- **The same ref** is the same addon, as before: updates and reinstalls need no `--force`.
- **Another local archive of a local install** (`file:` over `file:`) is the same addon. It is reported `updated` from the old version (`folders.replaced`), carries over pin, channel and reason, and is recorded from the new archive. No `--force`, no warning: a newer zip of a local addon is its update.
- **Any other different ref under a name the client already manages** is a takeover:
  - Without `--force` it fails `ownership_conflict` (exit 4): "<name> on <id> comes from <old ref>; installing <new ref> would replace it". The fix is the same argv plus `--force`; the alternative is `omaddons remove <name> -t <id>`. The details are `folders[]` with `reason: "same_name_other_ref"`, `owner` and `ref`.
  - With `--force` it is an `updated` item from the replaced version, with `folders.replaced`, and the warning `ownership_transferred`: "<name> on <id> now comes from <new ref> instead of <old ref>", fix `omaddons list -t <id> --verbose`. The record switches to the new ref, and `undo` restores the original ref, version and folders.
- **Edge cases:** `gh:` and `git:` refs of one repository are different refs. Re-pointing on purpose stays `adopt <folder> --ref`.

**How (`src/engine/plan.rs`):**
- `build_install` finds the *namesake*: the record under the template's name key with another ref, when nothing matched by ref. It applies the rule before the carry-over, so planning and the under-lock rejudge agree.
- When the namesake is accepted it becomes `existing`, which gives the real `from_version`, kind `Update`, the dropped-folder diff and the carry-over.
- New helpers: `is_local`, `takeover_refused`, `takeover_warning`.

**Tests:**
- **`tests/install.rs::an_addon_of_the_same_name_from_another_ref_is_replaced_only_as_its_rule_says`:**
  - Bar-2.1.0.zip, then Bar-2.2.0.zip: `updated` 2.1.0 → 2.2.0, `replaced: [Bar]`, no warning, ref `file:<new>`. Undo restores the ref, version and tree.
  - `gh:demo/bar --file`: exit 4 `ownership_conflict`, the fix ends in `--force`, the alternative is the remove, and nothing changed.
  - Forced: `updated` from 2.1.0, `replaced: [Bar]`, `ownership_transferred`, ref `gh:demo/bar`.
  - Undo restores the original ref, version and AddOns tree hash. I tested this here rather than in `engine_undo.rs`: it exercises the same snapshot-restore path end to end.
- **`tests/engine_concurrency.rs::two_installs_of_different_addons_at_once`** had relied on the bug: it installed `gh:o/baz` from Bar's archive, then `gh:o/bar` from it. Baz now has its own archive, so the test truly installs different addons.
- **Docs:**
  - README: the "Same name, another ref" rule under install, and the Known issues entry removed.
  - `install --help`: an `after_long_help` stating the rule, and `--force`'s help naming the takeover.

**Wire names:** `ownership_conflict` `details.folders[].reason` value `same_name_other_ref` (with `owner` and `ref`). No new codes or constants.

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: claim: src/engine/plan.rs build_install identity rule; tests/install.rs; README; cli help

title: A `git:` commit the server refuses to send fails `download_failed` marked retryable
description:
## Background

The closing check of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz) found a `download_failed` error marked retryable although retrying can never succeed.

When a `git:` ref on a `git_hosts` host names an exact commit, `GitRunner::materialize` (src/sources/git_hosts.rs:397-470) runs `git init`, then `git fetch --depth 1 -- <url> <sha>`. Some servers refuse to send a commit that is not a branch or tag tip. The `map_err` at src/sources/git_hosts.rs:416-426 replaces the fetch's `download_failed` with:

```rust
Error::new(
    ErrorCode::DownloadFailed,
    format!("{url} refused to send commit {sha}; some servers only serve branches and tags"),
    Suggestion::text("name a branch or tag after # instead of a commit"),
)
```

`Error::new` takes the code's default retryability, and `download_failed` defaults to retryable (src/error.rs:182, `DownloadFailed = "download_failed", Failed, true`). So the envelope says `retryable: true`, while the fix itself says the same command cannot work: the user must change the ref. The error it replaces, from `failure()` (src/sources/git_hosts.rs:678-719), was explicitly `.retryable(false)` for `clone`/`fetch` failures; the rewrite throws that away. Every other `download_failed` built in that file sets `.retryable(false)` (the login-needed case and the clone/fetch case in `failure`).

`retryable` is the contract's signal to an agent or the widget that running the same command again may work (README's error table and the envelope's `error.retryable`). A `true` here invites pointless retries against the git host.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read src/sources/git_hosts.rs:416-426 and src/error.rs:182 at 7fb0a2c: the rewritten error has no `.retryable(false)`, so it serializes `retryable: true`.
2. Live reproduction needs a git host that refuses unadvertised commits (`uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant` off). A local bare repo served with that setting, used as a `git_hosts` host in a test, reproduces it: `omaddons install 'git:https://<host>/o/r#<sha-that-is-not-a-tip>' -t retail --json` fails `download_failed` with `retryable: true`.

## Technical Approach

- Add `.retryable(false)` to the `Error::new(ErrorCode::DownloadFailed, …)` in the `map_err` at src/sources/git_hosts.rs:416-426. Nothing else changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The "refused to send commit" `download_failed` error has `retryable: false` in the envelope.
- Its message and fix are unchanged.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (src/sources/git_hosts.rs tests): the existing git test harness builds local repositories (e.g. the fixture around line 1347 that runs `git init --initial-branch=main`); add a case that fetches a commit the served repo refuses to send (or stub the runner so the fetch fails with `download_failed`) and assert the mapped error has code `download_failed`, the "refused to send commit" message and `retryable == false`.
- If a unit-level stub is simpler than a real refusing server, assert on the mapping directly by factoring the `map_err` closure into a small function.

## Considerations

- A transient network failure during the same fetch does not reach this branch: timeouts and wait failures are `network` (src/sources/git_hosts.rs:854-880), which `map_err` passes through unchanged. So making this branch non-retryable does not hide a real transient failure.
- A repository that needs a login also returns `download_failed` from `failure()`; this branch currently rewrites that message to "refused to send commit" as well. Resolution (`ls-remote`) normally fails first for such a repository, so it is unlikely to reach here, but the implementer may narrow the rewrite to keep the login message if it does.
acceptance_criteria: the "refused to send commit" download_failed error has retryable false; message and fix unchanged; a test asserts it; argc gate passes

title: primary_by_shape picks DBM-Test over DBM-Core, so DBM's WoWInterface file is refused on Mists Classic and Anniversary
description:
## Background

The keyless-coverage study (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7, 2026-10-20) dry-ran WoWInterface's Deadly Boss Mods file (`wowi:8814`, DBM-Core-11.2.15.zip) on Mists Classic and Anniversary. omaddons refused it with `no_compatible_release`, though DBM-Core, DBM-GUI, DBM-StatusBarTimers and DBM-VPVEM all load there (`_Mists`/`_TBC` TOCs, out of date). Every folder that does not load has TOCs only for other clients (`no_loadable_toc`), which `accepts` allows.

The cause is the primary folder. `primary_by_shape` (`src/engine/plan.rs:4611`) ranks first the folder that other folders extend by name. The archive holds `DBM-Test` and `DBM-Test-WarWithin`, so `DBM-Test` is "extended" once and outranks `DBM-Core`. The single-core rule (`DBM-Core beside DBM-GUI`, from the doc comment) applies only when the top folder extends nothing. `DBM-Test` has no `_Mists` or `_TBC` TOC, so the primary does not load and `accepts` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:964`) refuses the whole archive.

It matters wherever no publisher `release.json` declares the client: WoWInterface files, GitHub zip-asset fallbacks, `url:` and local archives. `primary_folder` also feeds adoption grouping (`src/resolve/adopt.rs:749`, `:861`) and update checks (`src/resolve/updates.rs:197`, `:428`), where the same pick may name the wrong folder. Those two paths were not reproduced.

## Technical Approach

- In `primary_by_shape`, prefer the single `-core`/`_core` folder unless it extends the top-ranked folder itself. BigWigs keeps `BigWigs` (`BigWigs_Core` extends it). DBM gets `DBM-Core` (`DBM-Core` does not extend `DBM-Test`).
- Keep the rest of the order: the most-extended folder, then the shortest, then by name.
- Check every caller of `primary_folder`/`primary_by_shape` for a test that pinned the old pick.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `primary_by_shape` picks `DBM-Core` from the folders of DBM-Core-11.2.15.zip (DBM-Affixes, DBM-Brawlers, DBM-Core, DBM-GUI, DBM-KhazAlgar, DBM-Raids-WarWithin, DBM-StatusBarTimers, DBM-Test, DBM-Test-WarWithin, DBM-VPVEM).
- It still picks `BigWigs` beside `BigWigs_Core`/`BigWigs_Options`, `WeakAuras` beside `WeakAurasOptions`, and `DBM-Core` beside `DBM-GUI`.
- A fixture archive shaped like that DBM file, with `_Mists` TOCs on the core folders and `_Mainline`-only TOCs on the rest, installs on a mists target without `release.json` and skips the mainline-only folders.

## Test Plan

- Unit test in `src/engine/plan.rs` for `primary_by_shape` with the folder sets above.
- Engine test with a fixture archive: install on a mists target succeeds with `folders.skipped` listing the mainline-only folders. Before the fix it fails with `no_compatible_release`.
- `argc gate`.

## Considerations

- The WoWInterface DBM file is itself stale (2025-09-15), and the catalog's `gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods` is the better source. The pick is still wrong for any archive with `X-Core` beside an `X-Foo` that `X-Foo-Bar` extends.
- Adoption names the managed addon after its primary folder. If adoption picks `DBM-Test`, a user sees the wrong name. Check this while fixing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a throwaway HOME with a Mists Classic (`_classic_`, 5.5.4) or Anniversary (`_anniversary_`, 2.5.6) client, run `omaddons install wowi:8814 -t classic --dry-run --json`. That is DBM-Core-11.2.15.zip, WoWInterface file of 2025-09-15.
2. It fails with `no_compatible_release`. `error.details.tried[0].reason` shows DBM-Core, DBM-GUI, DBM-StatusBarTimers and DBM-VPVEM `compatible` (out of date), and every other folder `no_loadable_toc`.
3. Expected: it installs DBM-Core, DBM-GUI, DBM-StatusBarTimers and DBM-VPVEM, with the mainline-only folders in `folders.skipped`.
acceptance_criteria: primary_by_shape picks DBM-Core from DBM-Core-11.2.15.zip's folders and still picks BigWigs, WeakAuras and DBM-Core in the existing shapes; a DBM-shaped fixture installs on a mists target without release.json, skipping its mainline-only folders; argc gate passes

title: Doctor finding: two targets sharing one AddOns directory (target-addons-shared)
description:
## Background

Some players symlink one `Interface/AddOns` directory between Classic clients (for example Classic Era and Anniversary), so both clients load the same folders. omaddons keeps one record and one files index per target and never compares targets' AddOns paths. With a shared directory, each target's records are its own: an addon installed through one target shows up on the other as unmanaged folders, `status` there recommends looking at them, and `adopt` on the other target would record the same folders a second time. Two records owning one physical folder can then disagree, and an update through one target silently changes what the other's record claims.

M2 does not special-case this (recorded as a known limitation in README and on the vision bead, comment 606). The vision gives such machine-shape checks to M4's `doctor`.

## Technical Approach

- A doctor finding `target-addons-shared`: after discovery, canonicalize each target's `Interface/AddOns` (resolving symlinks) and group targets whose resolved directories are equal, or where one is inside another.
- Report each group once, naming the targets and the resolved path, with a fix that is advice, not a command: keep one target managing the directory (`omaddons targets rm <id>` for the other is the argv alternative), or stop sharing it.
- `status` may surface the same condition as an attention item; decide in this bead whether that is in scope (the finding is the minimum).
- No mutation: the finding only reports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two discovered targets whose AddOns directories resolve to the same directory produce exactly one `target-addons-shared` finding naming both targets.
- A target whose AddOns is not shared produces no finding; a symlink to a directory outside every target produces no finding.
- The finding's fix is a valid text fix or argv per the JSON contract, and the contract suite covers it.

## Test Plan

- Unit test over a synthetic layout: two Battle.net product folders whose `Interface/AddOns` is a symlink to one directory, and a control layout without the link.
- A contract row for the doctor command once it exists (M4).

## Considerations

- Discovered in the M2 documentation pass; belongs to M4 (the doctor). Not a blocker for any M2 or M3 bead.
- Resolving symlinks must not follow links out of the user's home in unexpected ways; reuse discovery's existing path rules.
close_reason: Shared AddOns directories are detected; status warns target_addons_shared

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: discover::shared::shared_addons(targets) canonicalizes each target's Interface/AddOns (read-only) and groups targets whose directories are equal or nested (outermost path; a missing AddOns shares nothing; a link to a directory no other target uses is no group). decided: with no doctor yet (M4 is not decomposed), status is the surface now: one target_addons_shared warning per group that includes a selected target, message naming the targets and the resolved path, fix a text instruction (manage those addons from one client, -t <first>, do not adopt them on the others, or stop sharing) since targets rm only unregisters and discovery would find the client again. M4's doctor reuses shared_addons for its finding and contract row (to note when M4 is decomposed). Tests: unit a_symlinked_addons_dir_is_one_group_and_the_rest_share_nothing, an_addons_dir_inside_another_is_shared; status clients_sharing_one_addons_directory_are_warned_once (era+anniversary symlinked, retail control; -t retail none; -t anniversary one). Real machine: status shows no such warning (nothing shared here). README: warnings table row; the Known-limitations line now says detected but not managed together. Gate green (1288).

title: `undo --last-by <typo>` usage fix drops every other argument and suggests a real undo by another actor
description:
## Background

The closing check of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz) found a usage-error fix that hands the user a different command that changes addons.

README's usage-fix rule ("Command reference"): "A mistyped command, flag or value is a usage error. Its fix is the corrected command when that command only reads, and `omaddons help <command>` when the closest command changes something: a typo never hands you a different command that changes addons. A mistyped flag or value of the command you typed is corrected in place (`--channel betaa` → `--channel beta`). Every suggested command parses."

`undo --last-by` breaks it. `--last-by` is a plain `Option<String>` (src/app/undo.rs:40-42) parsed inside `undo::run` (src/app/undo.rs:268-280). Any value other than human, agent or widget is a usage error whose fix is always the fixed argv `["omaddons", "undo", "--last-by", "agent"]`:

- every other argument the user typed is dropped: `-t <id>`, `--dry-run`, `--saved-variables`, `--reason`;
- the value is not the closest match: `humna` is "corrected" to `agent`, not `human`.

So `omaddons undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run` (a preview of undoing the human's last run on one client) suggests `omaddons undo --last-by agent`, which really undoes the agent's last run on every client. An agent that follows `fix_argv`, as the contract invites, changes addons the user never asked to touch, and possibly SavedVariables too.

Compare `--saved-variables`, which uses a clap `value_parser` (src/app/undo.rs:46-49) and goes through the general clap invalid-value correction: `undo --saved-variables restor -t retail --dry-run` suggests `omaddons undo --saved-variables restore -t retail --dry-run`, every argument kept.

The global `--actor` flag has a smaller version of the same defect. `Context::new` (src/cli.rs:245-253) answers an invalid `--actor` value with `fix_argv(&without_flag(argv, "--actor"))`: the flag is dropped instead of corrected in place. The suggested command is the one the user typed, so it changes the same addons, but it runs under a different actor: with no flag, the actor falls back to `OMADDONS_ACTOR`, then to human when stdin is a terminal and agent otherwise (src/model.rs:338-356). `omaddons install weakauras -t retail --actor humna` from a script suggests `omaddons install weakauras -t retail`, which would be recorded as `agent`, so a later `undo --last-by human` would not find it. That is not a different command on addons, but it is a mistyped value not corrected in place, and it changes what `undo --last-by` and `history` see. It is included here because the fix is the same.

tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs only checks that a fix runs the command path the user typed (`never_another_mutating_command`), so `undo --last-by agent` for a typo in `undo` passes it today.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh HOME with one synthetic retail client, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`.
2. `omaddons undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run --json`: exit 2, `error.fix_argv` = `["omaddons","undo","--last-by","agent"]` (no `-t`, no `--dry-run`, wrong value).
3. `omaddons undo --last-by xyzzy -t retail --dry-run --json`: the same fix.
4. `omaddons undo --saved-variables restor -t retail --dry-run --json`: fix `["omaddons","undo","--saved-variables","restore","-t","retail","--dry-run"]` (correct behaviour, for contrast).
5. `omaddons install weakauras -t retail --actor humna --json`: fix `["omaddons","install","weakauras","-t","retail"]` (the flag dropped, not corrected).

## Technical Approach

- `--last-by`: give the clap arg `value_parser = ["human", "agent", "widget"]` (as `--saved-variables` and `--channel` have), so a bad value goes through the existing clap invalid-value path that corrects the value in place and keeps every argument. Keep parsing the accepted string into `Actor` in `run`; the hand-built usage error there becomes unreachable and can be removed (or kept as an internal guard).
- If the clap path cannot be used (e.g. it must stay a free string for some reason), build the fix with the existing helper `with_flag_value(argv, "--last-by", <closest>)` (src/cli.rs:1060), choosing the closest of human/agent/widget by the same distance `suggest` uses; when nothing is close, the fix is `omaddons help undo` (a read), never a guessed value.
- `--actor`: correct the value in place the same way: `fix_argv(&with_flag_value(argv, "--actor", <closest>))` when a value is close, otherwise `omaddons help <command>` or a prose fix ("--actor is human, agent or widget"). A clap `value_parser` on the global flag would also work, but the env-variable path (`OMADDONS_ACTOR`) keeps its prose fix either way.
- Add the cases to the usage-fix corpus in tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs, and add an assertion there (or a new test beside it) that for a mistyped flag value the fix keeps every other argument: the fix argv equals the typed argv with only that value replaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run` suggests `omaddons undo --last-by human -t retail --dry-run`.
- `undo --last-by agnet ...` suggests `agent` with every other argument kept.
- A `--last-by` value with no close match suggests `omaddons help undo` (or a prose fix), never an `undo` that runs.
- A mistyped `--actor` value is corrected in place with every other argument kept, or answered with help/prose when nothing is close; the flag is never silently dropped.
- The usage-fix corpus covers both flags and fails if a value fix drops an argument.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Contract (tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs): corpus entries `["undo", "--last-by", "humna", "-t", "retail", "--dry-run"]`, `["undo", "--last-by", "xyzzy"]`, `["install", "x", "-t", "retail", "--actor", "humna"]`; assert the exact `fix_argv` for the first and third.
- Contract: a property over the value-typo corpus entries: the fix argv differs from the typed argv only at the mistyped value's position.
- Unit (src/cli.rs tests): `Context::new` with `--actor humna` yields a fix with `--actor human`; with `OMADDONS_ACTOR=humna` the prose fix is unchanged.
- E2E: `undo --last-by humna --dry-run` exits 2 and nothing in the client changes.

## Considerations

- README already states the rule; no README change is needed for this fix.
- `undo` is the most dangerous command to guess for: it can restore SavedVariables. Any fallback must prefer help over a guessed actor.
- clap's value-parser error text for `--last-by` will change the message wording; update any snapshot that pins the old message ("--last-by is human, agent or widget, not ...").
acceptance_criteria: undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run suggests undo --last-by human -t retail --dry-run; no close match suggests help undo or prose, never a running undo; a bad --actor value is corrected in place or answered with help/prose, never dropped; usage-fix corpus covers both and fails if a value fix drops an argument; argc gate passes
close_reason: --last-by goes through clap's in-place value fix; --actor is corrected in place or answered with help

title: TLS crates rustls-webpki 0.103.15 and webpki-roots 1.0.9 fail cargo deny (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, -0382)
description:
## Background

`argc gate --all` runs `cargo deny`. On 2026-10-21 it fails on two new RustSec advisories against the TLS stack that every omaddons request goes through (ureq 3.4.2 with rustls):

- RUSTSEC-2026-0382: `rustls-webpki` 0.103.15 may accept certificate paths through distrusted emSign intermediates, whose private keys are now public. Fixed in 0.103.16.
- RUSTSEC-2026-0381: `webpki-roots` 1.0.9 bundles `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, which allows the same paths. Fixed in 1.0.10, which removes that root.

README "Network and privacy" promises TLS through rustls with the bundled Mozilla root store (webpki-roots). With the affected versions, a certificate chaining through a distrusted emSign intermediate could be accepted for an allowlisted host. The plain `argc gate` runs `cargo deny` only when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` change, so it still passes at HEAD and hides the advisories. The post-M2 audit epic (omad-m2-audit-yegz) needs the gate to pass at its closing commit.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. At be0e16f, run `argc gate --all`.
2. The fmt, clippy and test stages pass. `cargo deny` reports `advisories FAILED` with RUSTSEC-2026-0381 and RUSTSEC-2026-0382, and the gate exits 1.

## Technical Approach

- `cargo update -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-roots`, which changes only `Cargo.lock`: rustls-webpki 0.103.15 to 0.103.16, webpki-roots 1.0.9 to 1.0.10. Both are semver-compatible patch releases, and no other crate moves.
- No `Cargo.toml` change and no code change. Do not ignore the advisories in `deny.toml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Cargo.lock` pins rustls-webpki 0.103.16 or newer and webpki-roots 1.0.10 or newer, and nothing else changes.
- `argc gate --all` passes, with `cargo deny` reporting advisories ok.

## Test Plan

- `argc gate --all`: the full test suite, including the recorded-HTTP replay tests, and cargo deny.
- No new test. The certificate path validation is the crates' own; the suite proves nothing else moved.

## Considerations

- Release builds embed the root store, so binaries built before this commit keep the affected roots until they are rebuilt.
- If a later advisory lands with no patched release, a `deny.toml` exception needs its own decision; it is not part of this fix.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo.lock pins rustls-webpki >= 0.103.16 and webpki-roots >= 1.0.10 with no other change; argc gate --all passes with cargo deny advisories ok
close_reason: Cargo.lock now pins rustls-webpki 0.103.16 and webpki-roots 1.0.10 (cargo update -p for both, nothing else moved). argc gate --all passes: 1592 tests passed, 0 failed, 53 ignored; cargo deny advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok.

title: Scaffold the Cargo package, toolchain pin, lint config, deny.toml and local gate
description:
## Background

The vision bead (omad-vision-8qa, §5.12 and §7 M1 "Project and contract core") fixes the shape of the repository: a single Cargo package with a library and an `omaddons` binary, a pinned stable toolchain, strict lints, `deny.toml`, and one local command that runs the full quality gate (D16: no CI; every commit that changes code runs the gate first). Nothing else in M1 can start until the crate compiles and the gate exists, so this bead lands first and every other M1 bead depends on it.

## Technical Approach

- `Cargo.toml`: package `omaddons`, edition 2024, `publish = false`, `rust-version` equal to the pinned toolchain. `[lib]` plus `[[bin]] name = "omaddons"`.
- Lints in `[lints]`: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; clippy `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `dbg_macro`, `print_stdout`, `print_stderr` denied. `clippy.toml` allows unwrap/expect inside `#[test]` code. Integration test crates that need unwrap in helpers add a crate-level `#![allow(...)]`. `print_stdout`/`print_stderr` enforce "commands never print": rendering goes through `src/output/` writing to locked handles via `std::io::Write`.
- Dependencies: every M1 crate from the §5.12 crate table is declared up front with the features the vision names (clap derive/env/wrap_help; serde; serde_json; toml; toml_edit; shell-words; ureq with rustls on the ring provider only; zip with deflate only; sha2; pelite; etcetera; fs4; rustix fs; reflink-copy; tempfile; ulid; jiff; thiserror; schemars). Dev-dependencies: insta, assert_cmd, predicates, proptest. Decided: declaring them once avoids parallel agents fighting over `Cargo.toml` and lets `cargo deny` vet the whole tree in one pass. Crates for later milestones (tar, zstd, sha1, md-5, clap_complete, clap_mangen) are added by the milestone that needs them.
- `rust-toolchain.toml`: pinned to an installed stable release with rustfmt and clippy. Decided: a pinned version instead of the floating `stable` channel so every agent builds with the same compiler.
- `rustfmt.toml` (style edition 2024) and `clippy.toml`.
- `deny.toml`: advisories, a permissive license allowlist (tuned until `cargo deny check` passes), crates.io as the only source, and bans that enforce D9 and the crate table: `openssl-sys`, `native-tls`, `aws-lc-rs`, `aws-lc-sys`, `reqwest`, `tokio`.
- Module skeleton: `src/lib.rs` declares the M1 modules from the §5.12 layout, each file holding only a `//!` doc comment stating its responsibility. Decided: declaring them now keeps parallel beads from colliding on `lib.rs`. `src/net/` is a directory rather than the single `net.rs` the layout shows, because it holds the Http trait, the ureq implementation, the allowlist, net.log, validators, retry and record/replay. Folder classification gets its own `src/inventory.rs`, which the layout does not list.
- The local gate: `Argcfile.sh` recipe `argc gate` calls `scripts/gate.sh`, which runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, `ubs` on changed files (staged, unstaged and untracked relative to HEAD, excluding `.beads/`), and `cargo deny check` only when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed (`--all` forces it).
- `.gitignore` for `target/`, fuzz outputs and coverage files.
- README.md v1 describing exactly what exists: the goal, the pre-alpha status, how to build, the gate, the layout, and where the plan lives.
- A "This Project" section in CLAUDE.md with the gate rule and the crate-level rules (fsx single writer, no printing outside `output`, no unwrap outside tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo build` produces `target/debug/omaddons`, and running it exits 0.
- `argc gate --all` passes: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, tests, ubs and cargo deny.
- `cargo tree -i aws-lc-rs`, `cargo tree -i openssl-sys` and `cargo tree -i tokio` find nothing.
- `rust-toolchain.toml` pins an installed stable toolchain; `cargo --version` inside the repository reports it.
- README.md describes only what exists, and CLAUDE.md has a "This Project" section.
- No `.github/` directory exists (D16).

## Test Plan

- Unit: none (no logic yet).
- E2E: `tests/smoke.rs` runs the built binary with `assert_cmd` and asserts exit 0. The CLI skeleton bead replaces it with the bare-help contract test.
- Gate: run `argc gate --all` and record the output in the close reason.

## Considerations

- ureq's default features may pull in a crypto provider other than ring. Verify with `cargo tree` and disable default features where needed.
- The deny license allowlist must be the minimum the tree actually needs; widen it only in response to a concrete `cargo deny` rejection.
- `cargo deny check` fetches the advisory database over the network; the gate runs it only when dependency files change.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build produces target/debug/omaddons and running it exits 0; argc gate --all passes (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, ubs, cargo deny); cargo tree finds no aws-lc-rs, openssl-sys or tokio; rust-toolchain.toml pins an installed stable toolchain; README.md describes only what exists and CLAUDE.md has a This Project section; no .github/ directory exists
close_reason: Crate scaffold landed: lib + bin, toolchain pinned to 1.97.1, lints, deny.toml with D9 bans, M1 crates declared, module skeleton, argc gate, README v1, CLAUDE.md This Project section

title: update --all with names: the usage fix drops the first name
description:
## Background

`update`'s usage error for `--all` with addon names (`src/app/update.rs`, `check_args`) builds its fix with `crate::cli::without_flag(&fix_argv(&ctx.argv), "--all")`. `without_flag` is for flags that take a value: it also drops the token after the flag. `--all` is a boolean, so `omaddons update --all Foo` gets the fix `omaddons update`, which drops `Foo` and updates everything: the opposite of naming addons. `omaddons update Foo --all` gets the right fix, `omaddons update Foo`. Found while writing `adopt --apply <folder>`'s usage fix, which filters the boolean flag out instead.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install any addon on a client (`omaddons install gh:o/foo -t retail`).
2. Run `omaddons update --all Foo --json`.
3. The error is `usage`, and its `fix_argv` is `["omaddons", "update"]`: the name is gone. With `update Foo --all` it is `["omaddons", "update", "Foo"]`.

## Technical Approach

Add `crate::cli::without_switch(argv, flag)`, which drops only the flag token (and `--flag=` forms are not valid for a switch), next to `without_flag` in `src/cli.rs`. Use it in `update::check_args` and in `adopt`'s `Mode::of` (`src/app/adopt/apply.rs`), which filters `--apply` by hand today. Grep for other `without_flag` calls on boolean flags and switch them too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons update --all Foo` fails `usage` with `fix_argv` `["omaddons", "update", "Foo"]`; `omaddons update Foo --all` gives the same.
- `adopt --apply Foo` keeps its fix `["omaddons", "adopt", "Foo"]`.
- `without_flag` keeps its meaning for valued flags (`--channel beta`).

## Test Plan

A unit test of `without_switch` in `src/cli.rs` (switch first, last, between names); an e2e assertion in `tests/update.rs` for both argument orders.
close_reason: update --all with names now suggests the names without --all

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: cli::without_switch removes a valueless flag only (without_flag removed --all and the word after it, the first name); update's check_args uses it. Unit test in cli.rs; contract row update_all_with_names shows fix_argv [omaddons, update, weakauras]. Found by the M2 contract audit (omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1).

title: In-source scanners stop at the first #[cfg(test)], as single_writer did
description:
## Background

omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.8 fixed tests/single_writer.rs, which stopped scanning a file at its first column-0 #[cfg(test)] and so never scanned src/net/mod.rs past its early `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` (line 20). Five unit tests inside src/ scan source text the same way, with `text.split("#[cfg(test)]").next()`:

- src/engine/tx.rs (~1829): every failpoint::hit("engine.…") name across src/engine/.
- src/state/store.rs (~345): every `impl Versioned for` across src/.
- src/fsx/lock.rs (~362, ~384): lock_file references across src/, and forbidden calls in lock.rs itself.
- src/resolve/select.rs (~642): banned std::fs/std::net use in select.rs itself.
- src/state/paths.rs (~650): create_dir/canonicalize calls in paths.rs itself.

They also match inside comments and string literals, and a `#[cfg(test)]` written in a string (as these very scanners do) cuts the scan short. No miss exists today: the only file with production code after its first #[cfg(test)] is src/net/mod.rs, which holds no engine failpoint, no Versioned impl and no lock_file reference.

## Technical Approach

Give these scanners the production view single_writer now has: a small shared helper under src/ (cfg(test), e.g. src/testing/source.rs) with the lexer (comments dropped, literals blanked across lines) and test-item skipping, ported from tests/single_writer.rs (code_lines, production_code), used by all five. Alternative if the helper is judged too heavy: move src/net/mod.rs's `mod tests;` to the end of the file and add a guard test that no src file has production code after its first column-0 #[cfg(test)].

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the five scanners sees production code after an early `mod tests;` (a self-test with an in-memory probe, as single_writer's net/mod.rs test does).
- argc gate passes.
close_reason: The five in-source scanners read a production view of the source (comments dropped, test items blanked wherever they sit), so code after an early mod tests; is seen.

title: Archive ratio guard rejects real textures just past the 1 MiB floor (Plater)
description:
## Background

The M1 checkpoint's live keyless install of Plater (gh:Tercioo/Plater-Nameplates, Plater-v660.zip) into retail failed with unsafe_archive: "Plater/images/transparent.tga expands 1048594 bytes from 1046, past the 200:1 compression ratio". The file is a legitimate 512x512 RGBA TGA (1 MiB of pixels plus an 18-byte header) that is almost entirely transparent, so it deflates about 1000:1. ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR (1 MiB) exempts only entries up to exactly 1 MiB, so ordinary textures trip the zip-bomb guard.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. omaddons install plater -t retail --dry-run --json
2. error.details.tried[0].reason is unsafe_archive for Plater/images/transparent.tga.

## Technical Approach

Raise ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR in src/limits.rs to 32 MiB: large enough for a 2048x2048 RGBA texture with its header, the largest texture an addon realistically ships uncompressed. Bombs stay bounded by ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED (1 GiB total, counted while decompressing) and ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES; the ratio still catches a bomb entry once it passes 32 MiB. Update the ratio-bomb fixture in tests/inspect.rs to expand past the new floor, and the limits registry snapshot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An archive holding a 1 MiB + 18 byte highly compressible texture inspects cleanly.
- A deflated entry of zeros larger than 32 MiB is still refused with unsafe_archive (ratio).
- Plater installs into the development machine's retail target.

## Test Plan

- Regression test in tests/inspect.rs with the Plater-shaped texture.
- The ratio bomb case in hostile_entries_are_refused uses 40 MiB of zeros.
- Unit test ratios_apply_past_the_floor follows the constant.

## Considerations

- A higher floor lets a single bomb entry expand to 32 MiB before the ratio stops it; that is within every other bound.
acceptance_criteria: A 1 MiB + 18 byte compressible texture inspects cleanly; a deflated zero entry past 32 MiB is still unsafe_archive; Plater installs into the development machine's retail target
close_reason: ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR raised to 32 MiB so real textures pass; bombs stay bounded

title: Discovery offers Warcraft III (product w3) in the Battle.net prefix as a WoW target, warning unknown_flavor on every command
description:
## Background

On the development machine (2026-10-20), the Battle.net prefix also holds Warcraft III: Reforged, at `drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Warcraft III/` (it has its own `.build.info` and a `_retail_` flavor folder whose `.flavor.info` names product `w3`). Discovery's scan treats it as a WoW install. Every command then lists an unregistered target `retail@battlenet`:
- `product: "w3"`, `version: "3.0.1.24371"`, `interface: 30001`, `family: "unknown"`, `found_by: "scan"`, label "retail (battlenet)";
- every command, `status` and `list -t <other>` included, emits `unknown_flavor`: "retail@battlenet: flavor folder _retail_ runs version 3.0.1.24371, which no family covers; it is usable with permissive modern rules", with a fix suggesting `config set targets.retail@battlenet.family <family>`.

That warning is noise on every run. Worse, its fix invites the user to give a Warcraft III folder a WoW family, after which omaddons would install addons into it. README's first line promises omaddons manages addons "for every client"; a non-WoW Blizzard game is not a client.

The cause: `src/discover/battlenet.rs:30-60`. `is_battlenet_root` accepts any directory with a `.build.info`, and `discover_root` makes a target of every flavor folder, whatever its product. A product unknown to the rules table still becomes a target, which is deliberate for future WoW products (a new `wow_*` code), but it also admits other Blizzard games.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a Battle.net prefix with WoW, install another Blizzard game that uses the `_retail_` layout (Warcraft III: Reforged; also likely Diablo IV, Hearthstone, Overwatch).
2. Run `omaddons targets --json`: a `retail@battlenet` entry with that game's product code (`w3`) appears, `registered: false`.
3. Run any command: `unknown_flavor` is warned for it.

Unit-level: a fake prefix with `Program Files (x86)/Warcraft III/.build.info` and `_retail_/.flavor.info` naming `w3` yields a discovered target today.

## Technical Approach

- In `discover_root`, skip a flavor folder whose product is known and is not a WoW product. Define "WoW product" in one place: a code in the rules table's product list, or matching the `wow` prefix (`wow`, `wow_classic`, `wow_classic_era`, `wow_anniversary`, `wowt`, `wowf`, ...). `w3`, `fenris`, `hs_beta`, `pro`, `osi` and the like are skipped.
- A folder with no readable product (no `.flavor.info`, no hint) keeps today's behaviour, so an unusual WoW layout is still found.
- Alternatively, or in addition, require a WoW executable (`Wow.exe`, `WowClassic.exe`, `WowT.exe`, ...; the table's exe names) in the flavor folder. Prefer the product check: it reads only the file discovery already reads.
- Skip silently: no warning for a non-WoW game.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Battle.net root whose flavor folders all name non-WoW products produces no target and no warning.
- A WoW root next to it is discovered exactly as before.
- A flavor folder with an unknown `wow*` product still becomes a target (with `unknown_flavor`), as today.
- On the development machine, `omaddons targets` no longer lists `retail@battlenet`, and `status` emits no `unknown_flavor`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/discover_*.rs`: a fake prefix with `World of Warcraft/` (`_retail_`, product `wow`) and `Warcraft III/` (`_retail_`, product `w3`): only the WoW target is discovered, no warning.
- Unknown `wow_future` product: still discovered, `unknown_flavor` warned.
- Unit test for the WoW-product predicate.
- The "nothing written" discovery assertions stay green.

## Considerations

- A user may already have run the suggested `config set targets.retail@battlenet.family …`. A registered or configured target must not vanish silently: if config names it, keep it and let the user remove it (or warn once that it is not a WoW product).
- The discovery cache may hold the stale target; check it is re-scanned.
- No personal data: product codes and folder names only.
acceptance_criteria: a Battle.net flavor folder whose product is known and not a WoW product yields no target and no warning; WoW roots beside it are discovered as before; unknown wow* products still become targets; configured targets do not vanish silently; discovery tests cover it
close_reason: discover_root skips a flavor folder whose readable product is not WoW's (RulesTable::is_wow_product: in the rules table, or a wow* code), silently; unreadable products stay targets; registered ones surface as target_missing; discovery cache PARSE_REVISION 3; README says so.

comments.author: ScarletThistle
comments.text: claim: src/rules.rs (WoW-product predicate), src/discover/battlenet.rs (skip non-WoW flavor folders), src/discover/cache.rs (PARSE_REVISION), tests/discover_*.rs

comments.author: ScarletThistle
comments.text: decided: skip by product, silently, in discover_root (src/discover/battlenet.rs), with the predicate in one place (RulesTable::is_wow_product: a product in the rules table, or any wow* code). What and why: a flavor folder whose product is readable and not WoW's is no client; a folder with no readable product stays a target, and a [rules] products entry can admit any code. How the bead's 'must not vanish silently' consideration is met: a target registered there by an earlier build is no longer discovered, so the registry keeps it and status raises target_missing with 'targets rm' as the fix (existing behaviour, tests/status.rs); a never-registered one only had a config family override at stake, and nothing installs without registering, so its override simply goes unused (no warning: README promises none for an unused override). Found while testing: on a fresh machine Warcraft III sorts before World of Warcraft and took the bare id retail, leaving WoW as retail@battlenet, so -t retail selected Warcraft III; the fix removes that too. Risk: a future WoW product whose code does not start with wow and is not in the table is skipped until a [rules] products entry or a release adds it. Discovery cache PARSE_REVISION bumped to 3 so cached w3 targets are re-parsed. README 'Where discovery looks' says so.
